action: Pass a new 'Freedom of Speech Protection Act'
background: Pass a new act which I believe could help define and protect lawful, non-violent, free speech from censorship by the state or tech companies in a broader, more detailed way than existing laws.
additional_details: I would like it to include protections for personal privacy related to speech and a review board to resolve complaints about infringements on free speech. I think it could help safeguard open dialogue, help prevent potential censorship, help ensure a true democracy, and help ensure accountability of digital platforms in moderating content. I think protecting lawful, non-violent speech strengthens society by allowing diverse ideas without fear of potential suppression or corporate overreach.

action: Review the NICs increase for not-for-profit public service providers
background: We call on the UK Government to review the increase of NICs and how to protect all not-for-profit providers of vital public services from the impact of these unexpected costs. This review should consider how to ensure a level playing field for all health and social care providers in particular.
additional_details: We think the NICs increase will put immense pressure on healthcare, social care, education, leisure and community public services providers, which are already stretched by funding and staffing issues. We think the impact of the rise will result in suppliers being forced to abandon contracts, freeze pay, freeze recruitment, and make redundancies, as well as the closure of some providers. We think this will impact those reliant on vital public services. We call for swift reassurance and clarity.

action: Improve the Financial Assistance Scheme for pensioners
background: We call on the Government to change the parameters of compensation set out in the Financial Assistance Scheme to end what we see as a miscarriage of justice inflicted on former workforces who lost their pensions when their pension schemes being lost due to employer insolvency.
additional_details: The current scheme only gives people 90% of their accrued pension. Increases linked to inflation are limited to 2.5%. We believe that these pensions should be increased to 100% of what was accrued and also that inflation adjustments should be matched at the actual inflation rate. We think these pensions should be fully restored with their schemes in full pre/post 1997 indexation and backdated to the date they were due to be paid.

action: Grant cats the same status under the Road Traffic Act 1988 as dogs
background: Grant cats the same status as dogs and other animals mentioned in the Road Traffic Act 1988. This would mandate the reporting of any accidents involving cats to the police and empower them to take legal action against motorists who neglect to report such incidents
additional_details: By including cats in the Road Traffic Act, the government would acknowledge their status as valuable family members, ensure greater accountability from drivers, and ultimately promote a more compassionate society that treats all animals with the respect and consideration they deserve.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700808

action: Raise the maximum weight limit for Light Goods Vehicles to 3750kg.
background: We would like the Government to increase the maximum weight of Light Goods Vehicles from 3500kg to 3750kg, as we think the regulations around weight limits were set decades ago, vehicles produced nowadays are safer and average curb weights have increased.
additional_details: We believe that increasing the maximum weight limit for Light Goods Vehicles to 3750kg could benefit businesses by reducing costs and red tape. We also believe that it would lead to more vehicles coming under the Light Goods Vehicle category, which could lead to more vehicle sales and cleaner commercial vehicles on the road.

action: Review the rules on suspending SIA licenses
background: We want the government to review the rules on suspending worker's SIA licenses following an allegation of assault. We believe that licences should not be suspended unless the holder is formally charged with any allegations.
additional_details: We believe the current SIA suspension guidelines can allow for suspensions that could deny innocent people their right to work. If the police do not charge the licence-holder for an alleged offence, we believe they should have the right to retain their licence, and to provide for themselves and/or their families.

action: Remove the Church of England's Bishops from the House of Lords
background: Currently there are 26 Bishops from the Church of England in the House of Lords. They should be removed, there should be a clear separation between the Church and the State. We shouldn't give individuals political power based on their religious status.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Remove the automatic right of bishops to sit in the House of Lords
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700563

action: Conscript all legal and illegal immigrants and migrants (including NI)
background: The government should conscript all illegal and legal immigrants and migrants (with the inclusion of Northern Ireland).
additional_details:
The crime stats have risen in conjunction with immigration statistics. Systems are at breaking point due to increasing number of people that are depending on them (housing, benefits, NHS etc.)
Many crossings to the UK have a high number of deaths due to the risks taken.
Conscription would deter many from the dangerous travel. Northern Ireland should be included as they could use Northern Ireland as the scapegoat to enjoy the rights and benefits of being in the UK without having to serve.
rejection_details: We can only publish a petition if we have the full name of the petition creator, which is published alongside the petition text.

action: Save the National Citizens Service
background: We would like the Government to reverse its decision to wind down the National Citizens Service Programme and close the trust. We believe it has been proven to help young people in the UK and so it should be conserved.
additional_details: With rising mental health issues amongst young people, we believe that the NCS is a vital scheme that connects communities, reduces stress, and empowers young people by building their confidence and developing important life skills.

action: Introduce breeder licences, a dog database & harsher punishments for dog abuse
background: We want meaningful reform in the areas of dog ownership, welfare and breeding practices. We propose a database to regulate dog purchases and limit the sale of certain breeds. We also want licences for all dog breeders to help ensure ethical practices.
additional_details: We think that current welfare rules lack clarity and enforcement, leading to lenient penalties for abuse and neglect. We want increased penalties for the mistreatment of dogs.

action: Repeal the Climate Change Act 2008 and Net Zero targets
background: We consider that Parliament must revoke The Climate Change Act 2008 and related Net Zero targets as since 2008 when The Climate Change Act became law many hundreds of scientists up to the highest Nobel Laureate level have jointly declared "There is no climate emergency".
additional_details: We believe the Climate Change Act 2008 and related Net Zero targets are both now in effect based on just one side of a two-sided scientific debate as we do not consider there to be a scientific consensus on the hypothesis of human emissions causing climate change. We consider that one side only of a two-sided scientific debate is not an acceptable basis for significant legislation that could have major impacts on the UK's economy and citizens. We want the issue of Climate Change to be reconsidered from scratch based on views and evidence from all sides.
government_response_summary: There is no ‘two-sided’ debate on anthropogenic climate change. The Government’s policy to support ambitious action on climate change reflects the overwhelming scientific consensus.
government_response_body: The Government’s policy to support ambitious action on climate change reflects the mainstream scientific consensus and thousands of studies, including the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) assessments. The IPCC is the authoritative source of information on climate science. The IPCC has established that human influence has warmed the climate at a rate that is unprecedented in at least the last 2000 years. This warming of the climate is attributed to the build-up of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere due to fossil fuel combustion and deforestation. The evidence for this is set out in chapters 2 and 3 of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Working Group 1 report. The IPCC Sixth Assessment reports can be accessed here: https://www.ipcc.ch/assessment-report/ar6/  As discussed in chapter 4 of the above report, if the CO2 concentration continues to rise unchecked the world could face a global surface temperature rise of about 3°C or more above pre-industrial levels by the end of this century. The serious consequences of this for human societies and ecosystems are set out in the IPCC Working Group report on impacts, vulnerability, and adaptation.  The Climate Change Act 2008 sets our commitment to reach net zero emissions by 2050 in law. The UK has halved its emissions, having cut them by around 53% between 1990 and 2023. We are absolutely committed to our targets. That is why making Britain a clean energy superpower is one of the five missions of this government — delivering clean power by 2030 and accelerating to net zero across the economy.  This transition will be one of the economic opportunities of the century – a chance to create hundreds of thousands of good jobs, drive investment into all parts of the UK, and protect the UK economy from future price shocks that reliance on fossil fuels create. Beyond growth and energy security, the transition to a net zero economy can deliver a range of social and health benefits for people right across the UK. As we act on how we heat our homes and buildings, fuel our transport, and protect our natural world, we can cut fuel poverty, clean up our air, increase access to nature and improve quality of life.  The net zero transition is critical to sustainable UK growth because of the economic costs of unmitigated climate change, and because global demand for low-carbon products and services is growing rapidly. The Office of Budget Responsibility (OBR) published its analysis of the cost of reaching net zero by 2050 in chapter 3 of the July 2021 edition of its UK Fiscal Risk Report. As the OBR has noted, “the costs of failing to get climate change under control would be much larger than those of bringing emissions down to net zero.” (https://obr.uk/frs/fiscal-risks-report-july-2021/#:~:text=This%20year%20we%20cover%20three,legacy%20for%20the%20public%20finances.)  We know many people are struggling with their bills and we want to do everything we can to help them. Without the shift to renewable energy, we will continue to be exposed to volatile fossil fuel markets and the cost-of-living crises households had to live through in the last Parliament.   We will be fighting for working families and businesses through establishing Great British Energy (GBE), a publicly owned national champion that will ensure British taxpayers, billpayers and communities reap the benefits of clean, secure, home-grown energy. GBE will work in lockstep with the National Wealth Fund (NWF). The NWF, capitalised with £27.8bn, will mobilise billions of pounds of investment in the UK’s world-leading clean energy and growth industries and support the delivery of the Industrial Strategy.  We have also created a Clean Power 2030 Unit led by former chief executive of the Climate Change Committee, Chris Stark, to act as a top team of industry experts and officials to troubleshoot, negotiate and clear the way for energy projects which drive growth.  The net zero transition will support the creation of hundreds of thousands of good jobs across the UK. There were 272,400 full-time equivalents (FTE) directly employed in the UK Low Carbon and Renewable Energy Economy in 2022, an 8% increase since 2021 – with up to 450,000 FTE employees when including the wider supply chain.  There are high levels of support for our net zero goals, and we know that people are willing to make choices to help reduce climate change. The most recent wave of the DESNZ Public Attitudes Tracker shows that 80% of the UK public are either fairly or very concerned about climate change (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/desnz-public-attitudes-tracker-winter-2023).  We are committed to ensuring that everyone has the opportunity to contribute to the transition, supporting people and communities to take action and realise the benefits.  We will set out our approach in a Public Participation Strategy to be published in 2025. This will include opportunities to ensure public views are considered in policy development.  Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

action: Ban ground rent on all leasehold properties.
background: I would like the government to introduce a bill which builds on the Leasehold Reform (Ground Rent) Act 2022 and Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024, extending the ground rent ban to all current leaseholds.
additional_details: A large proportion of flats and apartments are leasehold. This means that if people live in flats or apartments, they can often be faced with ground rents which can be an additional expense, one not faced by those in freehold properties. We believe they should be completely outlawed.

action: Include Wales in the Union Flag
background: I urge the Government and Parliament to recognize Wales's integral role within the UK by updating the Union Jack to include Wales. I am calling for an official review and redesign process that engages experts, stakeholders, and the public to ensure Wales's rightful place on our national flag.
additional_details: Currently, the flag incorporates elements of England, Scotland, and Ireland but overlooks the distinct identity and heritage of Wales, despite its status as one of the UK's four nations. I think this change would foster greater inclusivity, accurately reflect the unity of all UK nations, and promote a sense of equal representation and national pride. I am a firm believer that this change would be a positive one for the people of the United Kingdom.

action: Legalise marijuana. Introduce a tax and require a license to sell it.
background: Introduce license for growing, producing and selling marijuana plants and products. Tax it and sell it in dispensaries.
additional_details: The legalisation will minimise crimes and antisocial behaviour involving marijuana. It will require sensible and responsible individuals to have a license too sell and produce marijuana, stopping the need for people to commit crime to purchase it and become involved in gang crimes and activity surrounding the growing and selling of marijuana.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition which calls for a similar action: 

Reassess the classification of Cannabis and decriminalize it. 

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700385

action: Extend consumer protection laws on fast food orders
background: I would like consumer protection laws to be extended so that fast food companies more thoroughly check the items in the order before they are handed off to the customer.
additional_details: We believe this could help reduce food waste and improve overall wellbeing for the customers. We think both of these could be addressed by just having an employee spend a meagre amount of seconds to ensure that everything in the order is correct.

action: Create the Department of Government Efficiency
background: Create The Department of Government Efficiency (DGE) focused on optimising the operations of public services in the UK, ensuring that tax revenue is spent as effectively as possible and brings real benefits to British citizens.
additional_details: To optimise the operations of public services in the UK, ensuring that tax revenue is spent as effectively as possible. By identifying and eliminating waste, streamlining processes, and enhancing coordination between agencies, the DGE could help reduce bureaucracy, shorten service delivery times, and save taxpayer money.

action: Support year abroad students - re-establish our EU education opportunities
background: The UK needs to improve how they financially support year abroads, and give funding earlier. Embassies should 'fast-track' students on specific days during Spring/Summer months, to help students apply for the visas they need. The UK must re-establish higher education connections with EU countries.
additional_details: I am a university student, disappointed with the lack of support and help towards our year abroads, after Brexit. The additional costs that have been created because we left the EU, are not covered by The Turing Scheme, leaving year abroad students with difficulties at visa appointments, trying to evidence that they have sufficient funds to live/study/work abroad. Some countries expect us to have thousands of pounds in our own bank accounts as proof that we can afford our year abroad.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition which calls for a similar action: 

Negotiate a youth mobility scheme with the EU 

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700055

action: Reopen the maternity unit at Samuel Johnson Community Hospital
background: Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Integrated Health Board (ICB) should reopen the midwife-led maternity unit at Samuel Johnson Community Hospital in Lichfield. Currently, women in South-East Staffordshire and Derbyshire have to travel to sites much further away to access maternity care.
additional_details:
Accepting this proposal would help women access this vital service closer to home.

The maternity unit was available for mothers considered low-risk to give birth in, until the service was suspended in 2020. Antenatal and post-natal care continue to be provided in Lichfield, but women have to travel elsewhere to give birth.

This proposal would increase provision in an area with a rising population and free up capacity elsewhere, therefore it is in the best interests of mothers and the NHS.
rejection_details:
You may wish to contact your local councillor or MP. 

You can contact your local councillor here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

You can contact your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

action: Introduce scheme for reduced or free public transport fares
background: I believe that there should be a government scheme to make public transport fees reduced or free across the country, in addition to the existing bus fare cap.
additional_details: I think doing so could address climate change, cost of living, and urban accessibility. Public transport can help reduce global emissions, and it has been reported that some cities with free transport see higher ridership and lower congestion. We believe this policy could ease financial strain, improve air quality, create safer streets, and has the potential to lead to a more sustainable and inclusive society.

action: Amend the restrictions on the Disabled Persons Travel Pass
background: We want the government/parliament to lift the time restrictions on the Disabled Persons Travel pass
additional_details:
The fact you cannot use the travel pass before 9:30am is a problem for many people all over the United Kingdom.
Not being able to use the pass before 9:30am can prevent people from travelling to work, college, school, meetings etc. People whom have a disabled buss pass have so for a reason, the reason being they are disabled and in some way struggle or are not able to carry out every day activities to the ability that everyone else is able to.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Enable disabled bus pass users to travel during peak times across England
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701163

action: Change the house purchasing process to protect sellers
background: We believe that buyers should be legally required to cover the seller's legal costs if the buyer pulls out of a property purchase after an offer is accepted.
additional_details: In England and Wales there is no legal requirement for a buyer to cover a seller's costs if the buyer pulls out of a house purchase, even if the process has lasted many months. This can leave sellers with legal costs of hundreds of pounds to find.

action: Introduce the mandatory neutering of cats by 6 months of age.
background: We are calling on the government to introduce the mandatory neutering of cats by 6 months of age unless they are registered as licensed breeding cats. Some animal charities are being overwhelmed with abandoned cats and kittens.
additional_details: I am a volunteer Neutering Officer and see first-hand the problem the uncontrolled breeding of cats’ causes. Our branch is continually taking in unwanted cats and kittens because their owners can no longer afford to care for them. This can place a large financial burden on charities having to provide interim care and cover veterinary costs before rehoming. I believe that mandatory neutering before six months is the only way to tackle the current problem.

action: Keep Morley Post Office open
background: Morley is a market town and a civil parish within the City of Leeds metropolitan borough, in West Yorkshire, England. Morley is the largest town in the borough after Leeds with a population of approx 44,000 people.
additional_details:
Our post office is the hub of our community and is used by old and young alike. 
To close this post office will have a detrimental effect on the town and those people who live here. 
It is vital this service stays open.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. 
	
You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them here:
https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Legally require all secondary schools in England to teach financial education
background: Financial education should be made compulsory by statute for all secondary school students in England. This would be delivered by all schools to all students. Currently, it is included in the national curriculum, but not all schools (e.g. academies or free schools) have to follow it.
additional_details: We believe that finance has never been so important. Money plays a vital role in all young peoples' lives, and yet we believe we fail to arm them with the financial knowledge that they need to take into adulthood. In modern times, online fraud is common, many children have bank accounts, students face rising university costs, and some young people need to navigate car insurance. To us, it is clear that we need financial education that is statutory in all secondary schools in England.

action: Change the guidelines of Hand Foot & Mouth Disease
background: I would like the Goverment to change the guidelines of Hand Foot & Mouth Disease. If a child has HFM they should not be allowed in nursery or school for at least 5 days or until blisters have scabbed over to stop it spreading to other children.
additional_details: I would like the government to change this as  at the moment a child with HFM is allowed to go to Nursery or School with the disease infecting healthy children. Parents are having to keep their healthy children off nursery/school to stop them getting infected. If the infected child stayed home to get better the rest of the child’s class wouldn’t have to stay off for no reason and miss out on their education.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about this are a matter for the NHS, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Make it a legal requirement for individuals to report child sexual abuse
background: The previous government proposed making it a mandatory duty for those working or volunteering with children to report child sexual abuse. We would like the Government to make it a legal requirement for all individuals to report child sexual abuse.
additional_details: We believe that this will help protect vulnerable innocent children from child sex abusers and those who enable or actively protect them, by introducing requirements for everyone to report child sexual abuse.

action: Require e-bike riders to be licensed & regulated like mopeds
background: We call for e-bike riders to be required to hold a valid license in the same way as moped and light motorcycle drivers. We also call for e-bike riders to be treated equally to moped drivers for road offences under the Road Traffic Acts.
additional_details: We believe the growth in e-bikes, especially dockless hire bikes & delivery riders, has made some pavements & crossings very hazardous. E-bikes on pavements & jumping red lights are dangerous for pedestrians, especially the vulnerable such as young children, elderly & disabled people. Dangerous riding of mopeds risks penalty points & losing your licence; there is no similar deterrent for e-bikes. It is also difficult to punish e-bike drivers as they are not required to hold a license.

action: Hold an inquiry before transferring the Chagos Islands to Mauritius
background: We call for the Government to hold an open and transparent inquiry on the UK’s proposal to transfer sovereignty over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius before carrying it out.
additional_details: We want the process to hand over these islands to be delayed until an inquiry, and full and transparent, open debate have taken place, which includes ensuring that there has been no foreign or hostile influence.

action: Introduce basic UK political knowledge into secondary school curriculum
background: Introduce basic UK political knowledge into secondary school curriculum in PSHE / Citizenships and Values, with what each political party stands for, who people vote and why, and manifestos
additional_details: There are many young people who are highly uninterested in British politics, which a lot of the time can lead to wasted votes as people either do not vote or they vote based on how much they like the leader's character.
rejection_details:
The key stage 3 and 4 curriculums for Citizenship already include teaching about democracy, government and how laws are made and upheld. 

You can read more here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study-for-key-stages-3-and-4

If you would like Politics to be a compulsory subject in its own right, or the content of the curriculum to change, you could start a petition about that.

action: Increase funding for Early years providers.
background: Increase funding for early years settings. We believe early childcare is fundamental to all children and giving them the best start. Save our nurseries and Preschools. We believe early years education is crucial to set the foundations.
additional_details:
The Government wants the early years sector to support Working Parents. How can we when the sector is under pressure from wages, NI costs to the employer and business rates?
We believe settings will rely on Apprentices to staff them and have a skeleton core staff, which could lead to quality being compromised. Many settings, in our view, will be forced to put quantity over quality by maximising floor space with children.

action: Stop the closure of post offices
background:
Our local banks have closed , people use the post office instead of the bank ! Local businesses use it as well as the community ! 
Intervene and protect our high street , our community and our jobs
additional_details: The local community meet in local places , a post office Que is one of those! We see the same people behind the counter. The elderly recognise them and feel safe ! It’s a passport office too for mums to get photos done and fast tracked and so much more! Everyone will have to go into the city for a post office . Not good for the environment
rejection_details:
Decisions about closing individual post offices are a decision for the Post Office.

The Government set the minimum access criteria which states that 99% of the UK population are required to be within three miles of their nearest Post Office outlet.

You could start a petition to change that requirement, if that's what you'd like.

action: Limit the use of LED headlights in cars.
background: Research the change to LED lights in car headlights. They are blinding and cause headaches and restrict the use of driving at night. As SUV’s become more popular the headlights are higher and can blind drivers in front.
additional_details: Lower the max voltage or position of lights in order not to blind oncoming traffic.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition which calls for a similar action: 

Ban LED headlights 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701233

action: Declare a state of emergency to prioritise climate action
background: We believe that climate change poses an urgent and unprecedented threat to the UK's environment, economy, and public health. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events, and loss of biodiversity are already affecting our communities, and vulnerable groups can face the greatest risks.
additional_details: We think that declaring an emergency would help prioritise climate action and that it could enable faster policy changes and resource allocation to help mitigate impacts and protect future generations. It could also position the UK as a leader in global climate action. It could also lead to green job creation and drive more climate education in schools.

action: Change laws around amendments on birth certificates
background: I want the Government to change the law so that corrections to a birth registration are made to the relevant part of the full birth certificate, not in a marginal note.
additional_details: If a registrar makes a mistake in entering the sex of a child this cannot corrected on register itself, only in a note in the margin. This may affect the child's future making life difficult for them when getting married, applying for jobs and everything else they need a birth certificate for.

action: Introduce regulations for Hairdressers and Barbers
background: We call on the Government to introduce general licensing requirements for hairdressers and barbers to open salons and statutory requirements for hairdressers and barbers to hold specific qualifications.
additional_details: The UK hairdressing industry is currently unregulated. We are concerned by the current lack of rules or regulations on opening a salon and the lack of qualifications held by some barbers and hairdressers, which may result in potential harm to customers.

action: Proposal for Review of Smoking Policies for NHS Staff and Patients
background: Current smoking policies for both staff members and patients within hospital specifically related to smoking during working hours and the allowances for patients to smoke while admitted. I believe these practices may be having a negative impact on both patient care and the overall work environment.
additional_details:
Impact of Smoking Breaks on Staff and Patient Care:
In high-pressure environments like Accident & Emergency (A&E), smoking breaks, though essential for staff welfare, can disrupt patient care by causing delays and increasing wait times. These brief absences from duty may affect the timely response to urgent patient needs, reducing care efficiency. Additionally, non-smoking staff may feel disadvantaged, as they are expected to remain at their posts while colleagues take unscheduled breaks. This creates an imbalance in work-life equity, with non-smokers shouldering more continuous responsibility. Addressing this issue requires balancing staff wellbeing with maintaining a consistent, fair work environment for all team members.

action: Review the Access to Work Scheme
background: Investigate how the Access to Work scheme is operating. This review should ensure the scheme offers fair and timely support for all disabled people seeking employment.
additional_details: We believe that a system meant to promote equality could be perpetuating discrimination, inconsistent decisions and what we feel are unreasonable delays, potentially defeating the purpose of the scheme, which is to help disabled people stay in or enter employment. We believe these delays can cause significant financial and emotional distress, and in some cases, it has been reported that they are leading to job losses.

action: Review the Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme
background: We call on the Government to review the current Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme, as we believe it is not supporting those affected, is inefficient, out-dated, and is compounding harm.
additional_details: As of 25 September 2024, 15,804 claims have been received by the Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme relating to ill-effects from Covid-19 vaccinations. Of these, only 188 have been awarded a Vaccine Damage Payment. We believe that to rebuild trust from the general public, there needs to be a more effective, compassionate means of support for those adversely affected by vaccination. We believe it is time for change, and the UK needs a vaccine injury scheme of which it can be proud.

action: Base university home fee status on visa application date, not arrival date
background: The Government should revise the student finance rules for England so that the date a student applied for their visa, rather than the date they arrived in the UK, is used for determining whether they qualify for Home Fee Status.
additional_details: Some families who applied for UK residency before Brexit, such as under the Ankara Agreement, planned to settle in the UK permanently before Exit Day but due to visa processing delays arrived after 31 December 2020, disqualifying their children from home fee status. This policy may force students into unnecessary gap years or burden them with high international fees. We believe that adjusting the rule to consider application date would ensure fairer access to university fees for these families.

action: Vote against the Assisted Dying Bill
background: I would like MPs to vote against the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill. I believe it sets a dangerous precedent, devaluing life based on contribution, not inherent worth. I think it undermines our core principles & puts doctors in a conflicted position, challenging their oath to protect life.
additional_details: We urge the UK Government to reject the Assisted Dying Bill and instead prioritize initiatives that improve palliative care, mental health support, and resources for those experiencing end-of-life challenges. These alternatives could ensure dignity and support. I believe that relying on implementing assisted dying instead places vulnerable people at risk and does not uphold our societal commitment to valuing life.

action: Change the Law on which animals need to be reported in a road accident
background:
It is a legal requirement to stop and report the accident to Police Scotland when you hit a dog, goat, horse, cattle, donkey, mule, sheep or pig with your car.

This should be changed. Any Animal that has been hit by a car especially pet Cats...should be reported to Police Scotland.
additional_details: All Animals deserve respect and help the same as Humans do. They are helpless and voiceless. I am Their Voice
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action:  

Drivers who hit cats in their car should stop and take the cat to a vet
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700808

action: Keep Cross Gates Post Office Open
background:
Cross Gates Post Office has been identified as one of the remaining Crown Post Offices that could be transferred or closed altogether.

This must not be allowed to happen, and instead Post Office must invest in local branches that provide an essential set of services.
additional_details:
This is a busy and well used branch which provides essential services and support to residents in the area, which has seen the closure of many other banks and other services.

Many cannot travel to other nearby offices, and having the cash management services in our locality supports businesses around the area as well as residents.

Post Office services must stay open and accessible in Cross Gates.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise.

You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them here:
https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Fund a national checkup scheme at menopause in England
background: Around menopause a number of 'silent' changes occur that women may not be aware of but can increase their risk of osteoporosis, heart disease, diabetes & dementia, including changes in blood pressure, cholesterol & triglycerides. A health check at the time of menopause could improve long-term health
additional_details: Women may have a longer lifespan than men but our healthspan is not as good, with 25% more time spent in ill health. Many of the changes that increase the risk of these diseases occur without being noticed around menopause. I would like the Government to fund a checkup which tests for risk factors at this time. They should also advise on lifestyle or medications that could help reduce those risks & keep women healthy for longer.

action: Discard Non-Crime Hate Incident Laws pertaining to Social Media & Journalism.
background: Discard the Non-Crime Hate Incident Laws pertaining to social media & journalism. Rely on news & social media platform’s existing Public Safety Policies to deal with articles, posts, comments and interactions that are reported as offensive, hostile or prejudice to an individual, group or community.
additional_details: Discard the Non-Crime Hate Incident Law with regard to social media and journalism including articles, posts, comments and interactions. This is a law that many UK citizens do not support because of it’s ambiguous & subjective nature. There is public concern about  the potential of infringement on human rights with regards to freedom of speech, freedom of expression and the right to have a point of view which others may find offensive, but it not unlawful or a criminal offence.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Abolish Non-Crime Hate Incidents: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701051

action: Cap public electric vehicle (EV) charging station rates.
background: Current prices for public electric vehicle (EV) charging stations can be triple the cost of domestic electricity. This would make the cost per mile for many EV's higher than the diesel/petrol equivalent vehicle. The Government should set a maximum charge for public EV charging stations.
additional_details: We believe that the high price of electricity from EV charging stations will impact the conversion to electric from diesel or petrol. Simple caps could therefore help ensure that people looking to invest in changing from fossil fuels to electric vehicles can justify the expense.

action: Establish a statutory body to mediate disputes within the motor industry.
background: Set up a Statutory Body for mediation purposes for customers of the motor industry as a board that would act as a medium between parties. We think the panel of the board should be vetted and required to actively communicate with complainants throughout the process.
additional_details:
We think the National Conciliation Service has not accurately fulfilled this role and they provide an exceptionally bad service to the public.

We think we need a reliable statutory body instead, who would protect the customers and would genuinely step into the disputes.

action: Introduce licences, number plates and insurance requirements for cyclists
background: I would like the Government to introduce registration for cyclists so that they can be more easily punished when they do not obey the Highway Code.
additional_details: I believe that there are too many instances of cyclists who ride on pedestrian only pavements, go through red lights etc. I think it's about time that cyclists were brought into 'line' with 'other' road users. I think that many cyclists persistently disobey the Highway Code laws/rules, and this in turn, leads to accidents. I think that this will allow Police to clamp down 'harder' on cyclists.

action: Review the rules on complaint escalation to Ombudsmen/ADR in all industries
background: We think the review should consider whether businesses with "No resolution" offered to customers should pay a lumpsum for complaint escalation to the Ombudsman/ADR; and whether the time frame for businesses for complaint handling should be reduced to 4 weeks.
additional_details:
The review should also consider and whether the rule of rejection of repeat complaints should be demolished. 
 
We feel some businesses take large advantage on the existence of Ombudsmen/ADR and do not properly deal with complaints, leaving customers in a disadvantageous position with a lot of distress. We think the timeframe for businesses’ complaint handling, which is usually 8 weeks, is also very unreasonable to wait for "no viable outcomes". Currently if a problem is a repeat issue, Ombudsmen/ADR would reject dealing with the complaint, which we think causes further distress to customers. With a lumpsum paid to the Ombudsman/ADR by businesses each time, we think they would think twice.

action: Fund Medicinal Reviews for Patients Prescribed Highly Addictive Drugs
background: We ask Government to fund medicinal reviews for patients prescribed addictive drugs, ensuring regular assessments, informed consent, and accountability. Reviews would explore alternative treatments and monitor patient well-being to prevent dependency and foster safer prescribing practices.
additional_details: Unchecked prescriptions for addictive drugs may fuel a public health crisis. I believe that mandatory reviews would protect patients, reduce addiction cases, and show the Government’s commitment to safer, more responsible healthcare.

action: Create an ombudsman for online trading
background: We think the Government should set up an ombudsman to oversee consumers' reports about their experience on goods purchased online.
additional_details:
The ombudsman should have enforcement authority and able to take the necessary action for non-compliance based on consumers' statutory rights, and powers to ban the traders' portal from trading in the UK.

There is a pattern I observed with traders based overseas, who fail to accept returns of goods or fail to deliver, whilst they consistently fail to refund customers' money, thus we end up with no item and no money.
 
Currently, there is No enforcement body to tackle this, and if necessary ban a merchant's portal from trading in the UK if they notoriously fail to abide to statutory consumers' rights.

action: Change requirements for ILR for those who have graduated and worked for 3 years
background: We believe people who have studied on at least a year long programme in the UK in the past 5 years and graduated, and have then worked for at least three years in the UK should be allowed to apply for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) with their dependents.
additional_details: This is envisioned to retain highly skilled immigrants in the country, a valuable workforce, without burdening them with a 5-year sponsored visa route to obtain ILR. Completing a rigorous 1-year minimum course of study in the UK, paying the required fees and successfully completing the rigour of world-renowned British universities' academic curriculum; and then working diligently as skilled workers for 3 years is in our view sufficient.
government_response_summary: Settlement in the UK is a privilege. Those wishing to settle must show a contribution to the UK for a meaningful period, and we see no case to reduce the five year period required to demonstrate this.
government_response_body: Whilst we recognise and appreciate the work of skilled professionals, we must have a settlement process which is fair to all. Unless there are truly exceptional reasons, the expectation is that applicants should serve a probationary period with limited permission before being eligible to apply for settlement. The UK immigration system provides for people to settle in different circumstances, with different qualifying periods required to reach settlement, up to 10 years.  The Points-Based system has a number of benefits aimed at improving the process for sponsors and applicants. At present, individuals can apply for settlement after they have completed five years on the Skilled Worker visa.  Those coming to the UK should be aware that settlement is not guaranteed. The long-standing policy is that a person should be able to demonstrate they can contribute to the UK for a meaningful period of time and they are able to support themselves and their families.  There is a difference between temporary routes, designed to allow people to work and study for shorter periods of time, and work routes which can lead to settlement. The different purposes are also reflected in the rules which do not generally allow time spent on the shorter, temporary route to be counted as part of the current five years leading to settlement.  The Student and Graduate routes are temporary immigration routes. Students and Graduates are expected either to leave the UK prior to the expiry of their permission or, subject to meeting requirements, apply for another immigration route to remain in the UK, including to a route that leads to UK settlement. The Student and Graduate routes are not direct routes to UK settlement although the long residence rules allow time as a Student and as a Graduate to count toward the qualifying period for settlement. There are currently no plans to reduce the five year qualifying period, but we keep all of our policies under review.   Home Office

action: Abolish homework across all educational institutions
background: We believe assigning homework on topics already covered in class is counterproductive. If teachers can't complete lessons during school hours, it suggests they lack time or resources. Relying on extra assignments outside school creates unnecessary pressure on students, affecting their well-being.
additional_details: We ask the government and Parliament to take action to limit homework on topics already covered in class. This practice puts unnecessary strain on students, affecting their mental health and well-being. Teachers should be provided with enough time and resources to teach effectively during school hours. Reducing after-school work will create a more balanced education, giving students time for rest, extracurricular activities, and personal development, essential for their overall growth

background: Ban the use of Variable Direct Debit. We think this leaves consumers in an unfair position as they may get multiple bills and multiple amounts are taken from their bank account per month.

action: Change the requirements of how often MPs attend a Parliamentary sitting.
background: To set requirements for MPs to attend the House of Commons and to hold constituency surgeries on a minimum number of occasions throughout the year.
additional_details: I think public trust in MPs and the Parliamentary process could be strengthened if MPs were seen to be undertaking their duties according to a minimum set of standards: that is, by attending the House of Commons and holding constituency surgeries on a regular basis as a formal requirement of the role. background: We believe that parents should not be able to choose to be absent from the life of their child without clear and enforced legal consequences. I think that usually mothers, but sometimes fathers, can be left to raise the child on their own.
additional_details: We believe that a parent walking away from their parental responsibilities should be a legal offence.

background: We believe the benefits application system for cancer patients is not fit for purpose. We think it is over-complicated, upsetting, and adds high levels of stress. We would like the Government to create a fast-track system for all of those cancer patients who are seeking benefits.
additional_details: We think the system should be simplified, streamlined and cost-effective in a way that would benefit patients, medical professionals and the DWP. We believe that cancer patients should be focusing on getting through their treatment and not worrying about paying bills, mortgages or going back to work too soon as time taken for even an initial decision can be months.

action: Improve Access to Affordable, Safe Medical Cannabis for UK Patients
background: Approximately 63,000 patients in the UK rely on medical cannabis, with an average monthly cost of £272. We urge the government to allow patients to cultivate medical cannabis for personal use under a regulated framework, providing affordable, safe access and mitigating many issues we patients face.
additional_details:
Personal or collective cultivation would provide patients with steady, affordable access to medical cannabis, reducing stock shortages, quality issues, and high costs.Many cannot afford current prescription costs, depriving them of essential, life-changing medical relief.

In countries like Malta, Luxembourg, and Canada, patients can legally grow a small number of cannabis plants. A similar 'grow your own' scheme in the UK would grant patients more choice, autonomy, and critical financial relief

action: We are petitioning for a National Referendum on Assisted Dying
background: We believe that the decision to introduce assisted dying legislation in the UK, is a matter of such fundamental import to the future of our nation and to us as citizens, that it must be decided as a nation, not by Members of Parliament alone.
additional_details: It is also our view that the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill 2024-25, now before Parliament, requires far more scrutiny and time for deliberation than will be afforded by a Private Member’s Bill, as is the case in this instance. In the interests of reaching a rational and reasoned decision on the matter, we believe it is imperative that time is set aside to discuss and reflect upon the economic, political and cultural contexts in which assisted dying legislation would be exercised.
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to hold a referendum on assisted dying.
government_response_body: The Government has the utmost sympathy for anyone experiencing a life-threatening or degenerative condition, and the pain of watching a loved one deal with those circumstances.  The Government also understands that assisted dying is a deeply emotive issue, with strongly held views on all sides.  It remains the Government’s view that any change to the law in this sensitive area is a matter for Parliament to decide and an issue of conscience for individual parliamentarians, rather than one of policy. That is why, when the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill was debated on 29 November 2024, the Prime Minister set aside collective responsibility and allowed a free vote for MPs, allowing Parliament to decide independently of Government.  The Bill, which is a Private Members' Bills brought forward by Kim Leadbeater MP, is currently making its way through Parliament, providing MPs with an opportunity to address public concerns and to change the law.  If the will of Parliament is that the law on assisting dying should change, the Government would not stand in its way and would seek to ensure that the law could be implemented in the way that Parliament intended. action: Require parliamentary scrutiny of any proposal to amend the Royal Mail USO
background: We call on the Government to amend legislation to require parliamentary scrutiny on any change to the Royal Mail's Universal Service Obligation (USO).
additional_details: We also call on the Government to: insist any changes to the USO are dependent on Royal Mail meeting existing performance delivery targets for letters and cards; regulate the price of first class mail to avoid further above-inflation rises; and insist Royal Mail maintains a national, affordable, and reliable postal service that supports high streets and communities across the UK.
government_response_summary: The government’s priority is to ensure that Royal Mail can effectively serve its customers in the future. Legislation requires Ofcom to secure a sustainable and efficient universal postal service.
government_response_body: The government is committed to the provision of a reliable and affordable universal postal service. A postal service that works for customers, workers and communities is crucial to the UK businesses that help drive growth across the country.  Ofcom formally launched a consultation on the future of the UK’s postal services in January 2025, highlighting a significant decline in letter volumes and that users’ needs had changed. Ofcom set out that they have considered extensive evidence that the universal service obligation must change to secure its long-term future. Since January, Ofcom has consulted publicly on a package of potential reforms to the requirements for the delivery of second-class letters, to better reflect users’ preferences and support financial sustainability.  The consultation closed on 10 April and Ofcom expects to publish a Statement in the summer. Further information is available on Ofcom’s website: www.ofcom.org.uk/post/royal-mail/consultation-review-of-the-universal-postal-service-and-other-postal-regulation/.  Ofcom is required by Parliament (under the Postal Services Act 2011) to ensure the provision of the universal postal service and is permitted to make limited changes to its regulation accordingly. The changes that Ofcom has proposed in its consultation would not require parliamentary approval.  However, more significant reforms, such as changes to the minimum requirements set out in the Postal Services Act 2011, which include a six-days-a-week postal service at affordable prices, would need to be approved by Parliament. Ofcom remains accountable to Parliament through mechanisms such as select committee evidence sessions and its statutory obligation to lay its Annual Report and Accounts in parliament.  The government is clear that Royal Mail’s quality of service has not been good enough. Ofcom, as the independent regulator for the postal sector, has set Royal Mail enforceable targets each year to deliver 93% of First-Class letters next-day and 98.5% of Second-Class letters within three days. Ofcom takes compliance with its regulatory targets seriously and this involves conducting thorough investigations where failures have been identified. In December 2024, following its investigation of Royal Mail’s performance in the 2023-24 financial year, Ofcom fined the company £10.5m because of its failure to meet service levels. In January, Justin Madders, the minister with policy responsibility for postal services, met representatives of Ofcom who gave their reassurance that they are closely monitoring Royal Mail’s performance. The government expects that Ofcom will continue to closely monitor Royal Mail’s performance and regularly press it on this issue to improve service levels as a matter of urgency.  With regards to stamp prices, as an independent business, it is for Royal Mail’s management to set the prices for its services. The government does not have a role in the company’s day-to-day commercial or operational decisions.  In setting its prices however, Royal Mail must work within the regulatory framework set by Ofcom, the independent regulator.  In 2024, Ofcom reviewed its position on safeguard caps on certain 2nd class products and amended the cap accordingly. The purpose of the safeguard caps is to ensure an affordable service is available for all users. We are grateful for the widespread public interest in the postal service. The government recognises that the essential service provided by Royal Mail, and underpinned by its universal service obligation, is a vital part of the UK’s communications fabric. Customers, businesses and communities across the UK depend on a reliable and affordable postal service and the government remains committed to ensuring Royal Mail is able to effectively deliver for those users.  Department for Business and Trade

background: Introduce legislation to expand the rights of UK property owners against people who park on their property, such as the right to get the trespassers' vehicle towed or clamped and fined. additional_details: We feel there are many instances where motorists disrespect and trespass private lands for parking, despite it is usually very clearly marked. Sadly, this is currently considered as a civil dispute and residents are unable to seek protection from the authorities. background: Make vaping or smoking a criminal offence for people under 18. We think the punishment should be a fine, for example, a £90 fine, which is the same as buying a vape for an under 18.

action: Legalise/regulate cannabis to boost the economy, public safety, & social equity.

It ensures public safety through regulated sales, quality control, and education on responsible use. Decriminalisation reduces law enforcement costs and prevents unfair criminal records. Legal markets combat organised crime and protect communities. It aligns with modern public opinion, promotes social equity, and supports medical research and sustainability.

action: Switch Greenland and Iceland’s Names: Greenland to Iceland, Iceland to Greenland
background: I want the Government or Parliament to support renaming Greenland to Iceland and Iceland to Greenland. This would correct the historical misnomer, as Greenland is icy, and Iceland is greener. The name swap would improve geographical accuracy and reduce confusion in education and travel.
additional_details: The names Greenland and Iceland are historically misleading, causing confusion in education and navigation. Greenland is icy, while Iceland is greener.
