action: Reverse Cadet Forces Funding Cuts by Min of Defence and the Dept of Education.
background: The govt have recently halved funding to State School Cadet units and Cadet Force Adult Volunteer Allowances. This is leading to reductions in activities and we think having a highly destructive impact on young people across the UK. We think this particularly impacts those from poorest backgrounds.
additional_details:
The Cadets consist of the Sea Cadet Corps, the Army Cadet Force, the RAF Air Cadets and the school based Combined Cadet Forces.
 
A Uni. of Northampton Study highlights the enormous value of Cadet Forces.
 
https://www.northampton.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/social-impact-cadet-forces-uk-2020.pdf
 
It highlights return on investment from money spent on UK Cadet Activities (c£160m pa) results in savings of 3.8 times the amount invested.
 
Please sign this petition to get these cuts reversed.
government_response_summary: Resource constraints have impacted across all areas of Education and Defence including support to cadet activity. Cadet funding is kept under review and must be balanced against other priorities.
government_response_body: MOD Funding of Cadets: The general level of MOD funding for cadet activity has remained largely unchanged over the past 5 years and comes from numerous sources within Defence, including the single Services (Royal Navy, Army, and RAF).  Cadet Force Adult Volunteer allowance: adult volunteer remuneration comes from single Service budgets and whilst only a portion of activity delivered by adult volunteers attracts remuneration through the volunteer allowance, this nevertheless represents a significant component of the running costs for the delivery of their cadet activity. Defence seeks to preserve the quality of the cadet experience but there are financial and other constraints that have impacted across all areas, and this includes the delivery of the cadet experience, not just for school-based cadet activity (Combined Cadet Forces) but for community cadets too (Army Cadet Force, Air Training Corps, Sea Cadet Corps and Volunteer Cadet Corps). We recognise that adult volunteers are the cornerstone of the MOD Cadet movement, and we are alive to the challenges that they face in delivering their vital role, so we are seeking to ensure that they are properly supported.  Supporting Cadets in schools: recognising the benefits of cadet activity to young people and society, and in schools, the joint MOD/DfE the Cadet Expansion Programme (CEP) was launched in 2012. The programme has increased the number of cadet units in UK schools to over 500. Through the CEP more than 250 new units have opened in state schools with priority given to less affluent areas. Prior to CEP, 75% of school cadet units were in independent schools; now around 60% are in the state sector. In September 2018, the then Secretary of State announced an ambition to grow the number of cadets in schools from 46,000 to 60,000. We are currently at approximately 85% of that aspiration. Since FY 21/22 the level of investment by the MOD into the CEP has grown year on year (currently £3.6 million per year) so that more young people can enjoy the benefits of the cadet experience in schools. This commitment remains unchanged.  School Staff Instructors (SSI): the SSIs are considered a vital component for the successful delivery of school-based cadets and the MOD remunerates SSIs through the mechanism of Volunteer Allowance and this level of support has remained unchanged. As part of the initial CEP Phase 3 plan, the Department for Education agreed to match the funding for this SSI Volunteer Allowance, through the mechanism of SSI grant funding in state schools in England until the end of August 2023 but agreed to extend this for a further year until August 2024. However, they were unable to extend the SSI grant funding beyond that point into the 24/25 academic year. In light of the Strategic Defence Review recommendation – funded with an additional £70 million – that the MOD should expand in-school and community-based Cadet Forces across the country by 30% by 2030, the Government will consider reinstating the funding for SSIs as part of a wider growth strategy.  Ministry of Defence  This is a revised response. The Petitions Committee requested a response which more directly addressed the request of the petition. You can find the original response towards the bottom of the petition page (https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701884)

action: Stop members of the Government and Parliament from attending WEF meetings
background: We call on the Government to not allow any ministers or members of Parliament to engage with the World Economic Forum.
additional_details: We believe that Members of Parliament should not attend meetings of the World Economic Forum nor engage with its stated aims . The World Economic Forum is not the one who elects the government and it should have no influence over British politics or the Government.

action: Legally require unanimous jury verdicts for serious offences.
background: We believe majority jury verdicts can lead to miscarriages of justice.
additional_details: We think majority jury verdicts can risk unsafe convictions, which should always be proved "beyond reasonable doubt". We believe the principle of jury unanimity should be reinstated for indictable only offences.

action: Create a Law that protects children from being used as pawns during separations.
background: I wish for Parliament to enforce a law that helps protect innocent children from being emotional abused during separations between their parents. So, so many people, adult and child, are affected and it has such a huge negative impact on those involved.
additional_details:
This is something that has been happening for years and years. Namely mothers, using their children as some sort of weapon to cause malice or hurt in attempts to have control. The fact that a parent has to pay thousands and spend months and months going through courts in attempt to gain visitation to their own children, is an absolute disgrace and shouldn’t have to happen. 
So many children and young adults are not being supported enough. They’re the ones who are being damaged the most.
rejection_details: You may wish to submit your petition again, making clear exactly what actions you would like the Government or Parliament to take.

action: Lower the age that someone can be considered a victim of domestic abuse
background: The law defines domestic abuse as abusive behaviour by one person towards another, where both people are 16 or over. We think this should be changed. Our daughter Holly, aged 15, was murdered by her ex-boyfriend and we think this case should have been looked at in the context of domestic abuse.
additional_details: We need to safeguard children. We believe under 16s should be able to be considered victims of domestic abuse, and that kids need more education about domestic abuse within a relationship and access to domestic abuse services. I’d like the age to be lowered so under 16s can get the help they need if they find themselves in an abusive relationship.

action: Fund more school places for autistic children without learning disabilities
background: I would like the Government to fund more school places for children who have autism, but not learning disabilities. Mainstream school can be completely unsuitable due to sensory issues, social difficulties and anxiety, which could prevent these children being educated to their full potential.
additional_details: I believe most state special schools are geared towards pupils with learning disabilities and/or serious physical conditions and therefore deliver too few high level qualifications such as GCSEs and A-levels. As such, we feel that many autistic pupils cannot be suitably educated in the state special OR mainstream system. I think the private companies opening schools to fill this gap in provision turn large profits, which the Government could avoid by funding more school places.

action: Change the law on who can receive inheritance - Position of Power
background: We propose that individuals with a professional duty of care, such as carers, doctors, or bankers, be prohibited from inheriting or being beneficiaries in Wills to prevent conflicts of interest.
additional_details:
Change the law on 

We propose that individuals in positions of power or those with a professional duty of care—such as carers, doctors, bankers, or similar professionals—should not be permitted to inherit or be named as beneficiaries in a Will. This measure aims to prevent conflicts of interest and protect the integrity of such relationships.
rejection_details:
The petition does not clearly define who you mean by "individuals in positions of power" or "with a professional duty of care". As this is unclear, we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do and exactly who would be covered by it.

action: Tighter restrictions on fireworks
background: Fireworks are commonly purchased for 5th November for bonfire night however they are so easily accessible for many people, people who misuse them and don’t just use them on bonfire night. Fireworks can be extremely scary to some people and certainly to many many animals.
additional_details:
Recently a 3 month old red panda died in Edinburgh Zoo due to stress caused by fireworks. 

Veterans with PTSD may be triggered by fireworks.

Peoples pets stress and make themselves ill and sometimes run away due to fireworks.

Elderly people may be scared if they’re alone and have limited mobility.

We need tighter laws on fireworks. I feel that fireworks should only be available to businesses with licences and for organised controlled displays.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for a similar action: 

Limit the sale and use of Fireworks to licence holders only 

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700013

action: Review police pursuit rules to ensure proportionality and safety
background: We believe police pursuits can pose high risks of serious injury/death to drivers, passengers bystanders. One of the duties of the police is to prioritise the preservation of life. A review should investigate whether rules on police pursuits reflect this duty of care and commitment to public safety.
additional_details: We believe that fatalities, including among children, are alarming and devastating communities. The review should consider matters such as the prohibition of police pursuit use in response to non-violent offences and minor traffic offences; and mandatory camera activation. The review should consider what steps may be necessary to reduce casualties, especially among children.

action: build another water park in the former wet n wild Newcastle site
background: The wet n wild water park opened in 1992 has recently been demolished which shut in 2020 when covid started everyone in the north east loved this site and had a good time throughout the years of it being opened and people miss it and say they would like to see it reopen as it’s a childhood memories
additional_details: Build another water park similar and or as the new biggest water park site in the uk

action: Require car insurance companies to insure the car, not the driver
background: Car insurance companies primarily insure drivers, rather than cars. We believe that not only is this false advertisement, but it can also allow for discrimination, often affecting young people.
additional_details:
One price comparison firm said in January that on average 17-20-year-olds had seen insurance rise by more than £1,000 from the same time last year.
 
We believe that car insurance companies should be required to only insure cars, so any driver with a full and valid licence would be insured when driving an insured vehicle. This would base car insurance pricing on the car itself, and not driver demographics.

action: Free use of parking areas and drop-off and pick-up zones at airports for taxi's
background: Free use of parking areas and drop-off and pick-up zones at airports for any taxi drivers from any county.
additional_details: All taxis have the right to use airport areas without paying. Just like buses and trains. We also provide the same service. Airport transfers. And pick-ups. Keep an eye on illegal transporters. Taxi drivers try to survive with competition from unlicensed people who are dedicated to taking people to airports.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
Decisions about airport parking areas, drop-off and pick-up zones are a matter for airport authorities, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Ban sunbed use due to health risks + the large cost to the NHS from skin cancers
background: Ban sunbeds outright due to the high risk of health risks and the cost that skin cancers and related health complications cost the NHS in which sunbeds are a major contributor.
additional_details: There has been many previous calls for this. Many young people are attempting to seek a beauty standard which is costing people their lives through cancer in which sunbeds are a large contributor playing into that fact.

action: Review the Highways Act 1980 to allow safe EV charging cables across pavements
background: We urge the Government to review the Highways Act 1980 to permit the safe use of charging cables across pavements, under specific conditions. These include cables being placed under protectors, laid flat and straight from property to vehicle, and used during periods of low pedestrian traffic.
additional_details:
We believe current rules impact people living in urban areas, where off-street parking is rare. We think public charging points are often costly, insufficient, and frequently occupied by non-EV vehicles. We think this creates significant barriers to EV ownership, limiting efforts to meet environmental targets and reduce carbon emissions.

We think this change could enable more people to adopt EVs, make sustainable transport more accessible, and ensure safe, minimally disruptive charging solutions for those without off-street parking.

action: Create a licence to ensure safe use of smart devices like phones
background: Create a User and Digital Device Licensing Authority and a Mandatory Personal User License for smart devices which would ensure only trained users can operate Internet of things and Human Machine Interface devices, such as smartphones, to enhance safety and responsible use.
additional_details: We think current campaigns stigmatize children by seeking to ban their smartphone use, though misuse risks extend to untrained adults. We think a licensing system is a practical solution that addresses these risks broadly, promoting digital safety without unfair restrictions. The authority would oversee training, registration, and accountability, similar to driver licensing. We think these proactive measure ensures responsible device usage and protects both public safety and digital freedom.

action: Introduce stricter minimum penalties for acts of animal cruelty.
background: We want the Government to introduce stricter penalties for animal cruelty. Current punishments can often just result in suspended sentences or fines. We think the government should introduce stricter minimum penalties, including prison sentences, to help deter abuse and ensure justice for victims.
additional_details: We think current punishments for animal cruelty fail to reflect their severity. In our view, stricter laws, including minimum custodial sentences, would be vital to help deter cruelty and help ensure justice.

action: The UK needs to change the way sick animals are treated
background:
For the Government to look at an NHS like system to lower costs for animals in need of treatment via vets. These costs can run into thousands and more often than not need paying up front.

Aside from this, monthly insurance premiums are costly and not something everyone can afford.
additional_details:
Enact an NHS like system to lower fees for required treatment when it comes to animal care and any associated treatment.

I am asking the UK Government to look into manageable low cost alternatives that is universal to everyone so all animals are not left suffering and to make fee paying manageable to everyone.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign:

Fund a veterinary service for pets so people don’t have to pay vet fees
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700344

action: Make hedgehog highways mandatory on all new fencing.
background: Hedgehogs travel around one mile every night through our parks and gardens in their quest to find enough food and a mate. We can make their life a little easier by removing the barriers within our control. For example, by mandating the use of holes/hedgehog friendly gravel boards on all new fencing.
additional_details: Surveys in the latest ‘State of Britain's Hedgehogs’ report estimate that hedgehog numbers have decreased by up to 75% in rural areas since the turn of the century. Much of this decline can be attributed to human expansion and the erection of fencing which hedgehogs (and other treasured wildlife) cannot gain access through.

action: Scrap VAR in the Premier League!
background: Like many of us who live in the UK, the introduction of VAR was met with significant optimism. Correcting obvious refereeing mistakes, ruling out goals were clearly offside to name a couple. This appeared to be for the good of the game.
additional_details: Unfortunately, and it’s sad to say, but VAR has had the completely opposite impact and is ruining the beautiful game that so many of the British public love. We are constantly having to watch matches that are full of conservatory with VAR taking centre stage when it should be a relative bystander. The fans deserve better. We collectively pay huge sums to watch our teams, be that in stadiums or TV subscriptions. I think the government needs to seriously consider intervening. Thank you
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. This is a matter for the footballing authorities.

action: Institute a maximum cap for the interest rate on credit cards and personal loans
background: An interest rate cap should be introduced to ensure that people - especially young people at the start of a career - are not trapped in debt and can afford to thrive, not just survive.
additional_details:
We believe that in modern society, it is all but mandatory for people to use a credit card in order to build a credit rating. We also think that the UK has one of the highest interest rates in the world for loans and credit cards, with representative rates ranging from 35 to 50% depending on the provider.

We believe that research shows that even small debt has severe mental and physical health effects.

President elect Trump has also suggested a 10% cap on credit card interest rates.

action: UK Government to open talks with EU on rejoining Custom Union and Single Market
background: We think the government should seek to rejoin CU/SM as soon as possible to ensure seamless trade.
additional_details: We think our economy is suffering being so distanced from EU, our nearest trading partner.

action: Influence NHS Lothian to withdraw it's intention to close Veterans First Point.
background: The Scottish Government has provided it's share of the funding required to support psychological services for veterans in Lothian.  The NHS Lothian Board has decided to withdraw their funding forcing the service to close, this needs to change and NHS Lothian should fund the services to veterans.
additional_details: The NHS Board has not taken into account the impact that this will have on veterans or services.  They state that veterans will be seen by other services, when these are also being reduced leading to veterans having to waits of over 52 weeks for input which is not in accordance with the Covenant or Armed Forces act.
rejection_details: The NHS in Scotland is also a devolved matter that is not the responsibility of the UK Government or Parliament. You may wish to contact your local MSP, who can be found here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps

action: Exempt Commonwealth soldiers from the Life in the UK test after 6yrs Service.
background: We call on the Government to exempt Commonwealth soldiers in the British army from the Life in the UK test when applying for citizenship after 6 years and more continuous service.
additional_details:
We believe that due to the struggles, mental health and stress commonwealth soldiers go through in serving they find it hard sometimes to sit and pass the Life in UK test; and this has caused so many problems in the life of the serving soldiers. 

We have suggested inserting the reference to applying for citizenship because Commonwealth members of HM Forces are exempt from the test when applying for indefinite leave to remain.

action: Stop nurseries charging for bank holidays
background: Stop nurseries charging for bank holidays and any other days like the Christmas period where the nursery is closed.
additional_details: This is wrong to charge people for childcare where the nursery is not open. Whilst relatively small it should not be normal practice for this to be happening. Childcare can cost around £80 a day with government funding and if you have a child who is in on bank holidays that’s an extra £800+ per year that is charged for a service that is not provided.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

The pricing, and opening times, of privately provided childcare are matters for individual providers and parents, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Grant all asylum seekers the right to work
background: We believe that scrapping asylum support saves the taxpayer's money and budget; and that allowing asylum seekers to work would help asylum seekers to integrate into society.
additional_details: We think that a lot of money is wasted by denying asylum seekers the right to work while we have a shortage of workers; and this action would save the country's economy.

action: End Discrimination and Ensure Equal Treatment for All Nationalities
background: In R (on the application of LR (Afghanistan)) v SSHD (Ukrainian Family Scheme—discrimination, nationality) [2024] UKUT 00236 (IAC), the court ruled that refusing his application for failing to meet the requirement to be a Ukrainian national was direct discrimination on the grounds of nationality.
additional_details:
Equal Rights and Protection: We urge the government to ensure that all, regardless of nationality, are treated equitably under UK law. 
This includes fair and transparent processes for residency and protection.
Conduct a comprehensive review of current immigration policies to eliminate any form of bias or discrimination and establish safeguards to uphold equality for all.

action: Reopen the Footpath from Bottom Lane to Market Drayton nature reserve
background: Direct the local council to reopen the footpath from Bottom Lane through Market Drayton Nature Reserve to Salisbury Hill View, remove barriers restricting access, and provide a transparent explanation for the closure. Ensure community consultation for future changes.
additional_details: The footpath in question is a much-loved route within our community, frequently used by residents for walking, jogging, and particularly as a popular dog walking route. Its closure has significantly impacted local residents’ ability to enjoy outdoor activities and connect with nature. The path promotes physical health, mental well-being, and social interaction among residents. Reopening this footpath will restore these important benefits to the community and uphold our right to access public spaces.

action: Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal
background: We want all forms of geo-engineering to be illegal in the UK. We do not want any use of technologies to intervene in the Earth's natural systems.
additional_details: We think there is a potential for this to negatively impact humanity, flora and fauna in the future. It has previously been said that Greenhouse Gas Removal (GGR) is essential to meet climate targets. We believe that this, and all other forms of geo-engineering, should be made illegal in the UK.
government_response_summary: Greenhouse Gas Removals are important for achieving net zero emissions. The Government is not in favour of using Solar Radiation Modification and has no plans for deployment.
government_response_body: Making Britain a clean energy superpower is one of the five missions of this Government — delivering clean power by 2030 and accelerating to net zero across the economy. The government’s priority is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from human activities and to adapt to the unavoidable impacts of climate change.  Geo-engineering is a term commonly used to refer to two types of technologies: Greenhouse Gas Removals (GGRs) and Solar Radiation Modification (SRM).  GGR technologies will be important for reaching net zero – balancing residual emissions from hard-to-decarbonise sectors, as recognised by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and the UK’s independent Climate Change Committee. There are commercial scale GGR projects operating and being planned around the world.  GGR approaches fall broadly into two categories: 1) nature-based approaches, such as afforestation, and soil carbon sequestration, and 2) engineering-based approaches, such as Direct Air Carbon Capture and Storage, Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage, carbon in building materials, biochar, and enhanced rock weathering. Nature-based methods can play an important role in removing and storing carbon dioxide at scale while delivering a range of additional environmental benefits such as biodiversity gain, air quality and soil health. However, due to factors such as land constraints and timescales for sequestration, the evidence demonstrates that nature-based GGRs must be complemented by engineered solutions to remove carbon dioxide at the speed and scale needed to meet our targets.  In February, the government announced an Independent Review to consider how GGRs can assist the UK in meeting our net zero targets out to 2050. The review is not centred on any particular project and will consider all GGRs, with a focus on engineered GGR approaches. The review’s findings will be published.  The government supports the deployment of high integrity removals, and has committed to ensuring that GGRs provide measurable and verifiable removals of CO2 from the atmosphere. The government is currently working with the British Standards Institution to develop GGR methodologies. Some GGR technologies may use sustainable biomass and relevant GGR standards will also include biomass sustainability criteria. These criteria will build on the existing sustainability criteria for biomass to ensure they are based on the latest evidence base. The government plan to consult on the details of the sustainability actions set out in the Biomass Strategy published in 2023.   In March 2023, the government committed to launch a process to expand the Track-1 Carbon Capture Usage and Storage clusters: HyNet and East Coast Clusters. As of spring 2024, the Track-1 expansion HyNet process allows GGR and Power Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage projects to apply to the expansion of the HyNet cluster in the North West.  Applicants for Track-1 expansion HyNet were expected to complete an Environment Agency Guidance annex, as per the application guidance published in December 2023. This annex provides environmental considerations likely to be relevant to projects and steps they may need to take in relation to obtaining permits and consents. The Environment Agency Guidance aids the identification of key environmental risks associated with proposals and helps applicants to demonstrate awareness of potential control measures and environmental standards and regulations for the areas of risk that may be relevant to proposals.  SRM describes a set of technologies that could theoretically cool the Earth by reflecting some of the Sun’s energy back into space. However, the wider consequences of SRM are poorly understood, with significant uncertainty around the possible risks and impacts of deployment. As such, the government’s position is that it is not deploying SRM and has no plans in place to do so.  The government acknowledges that the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA), an independent research agency sponsored by the Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology, are funding some SRM research projects through their Exploring Climate Cooling Programme. This research aims to begin gathering critical missing scientific data to better understand potential Earth cooling approaches, conducting cautious, controlled research aimed at improving understanding of the risks and impacts associated with cooling technologies. The programme does not fund deployment. None of the approved ARIA projects involve the release of toxic materials to the environment. This research into cooling technologies in no way alleviates the urgent need for increased decarbonisation efforts.   Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

action: Introduce a cap for motorcycle insurance prices
background: We want the Government to introduce a cap on increases to motorcycle insurance prices. We believe recent increases in prices for motor cycle insurance are abusive, getting out of control and needs to be addressed.
additional_details:
We believe insurance companies need a limit on how much they can increase prices to standard inflation.
 
The government or parliament is the only entity able to make a change. We need to address this issue as we believe citizens are being affected by insurance companies.

action: Require companies put political party logo on all products if they fund a party
background: We think people will happily show their desire not to consume or purchase goods that have been made by a company with ties or donations to a political party they do not agree with.
additional_details: We think if companies want to put money towards a party they should be required to show this on all their products and take the hit if consumers boycott their product.

action: Offer injured veterans housing in surplus military accommodation
background: We call on the Government to protect injured veterans by providing housing for them in surplus military accommodation.

action: Scrap the APD increase for essential regional flights and consider a reform
background: Reverse the increases made in the Budget to Air Passenger Duty (APD) on regional air routes which are essential to connectivity in the UK, whilst also considering a reform which will safeguard these routes for future generations with lower APD offered on a case-by-case basis.
additional_details:
APD disproportionately affects regional flights as it is levied on both legs of a return journey. This means that regional airline operations become financially unsustainable.
 
Regional flights can massively benefit small communities where other modes of transport are not viable for day returns either for business or visiting friends and relatives.
 
APD is not and never has been an environmental tax. We believe that the UK regional sector is already at the forefront of decarbonisation efforts.

action: Introduce a new tax code for emergency workers and armed forces
background: The Government should introduce a new tax code system for those working as emergency service workers, in the armed forces and in the public sector at a discounted rate.
additional_details: We believe that workers in the above sectors have already made sacrifices both personally and professionally in order to provide an unattainable level of public service anywhere else in the world. Many workers have and continue to spend a copious amount of time away from their own lives, friends and families as well as risking their own lives and wellness both mentally and physically in order to provide a service to the rest of society.

action: Seek to secure trade deals with the US and Canada
background: We call on the Government to do more to seek to a free trade deal with the USA, and a new trade deal with Canada. We believe that that it makes complete sense to move towards free trade between these countries with who we share so much culture and history with.
additional_details: We already have free trade deals with Australia and New Zealand, so we believe it surely makes sense to do the same with Canada and the USA. Our histories are intrinsically linked. We believe that ever increasing ties with these countries can be achieved to the advantage of us all.

action: Create system for injured veterans to apply for disability benefits
background: We think veterans injured on active duty should not be passed to civilian benefit system to be dealt with, and there should be a special system for injured veterans to apply for disability benefits.
additional_details: We think the journey to obtain civilian health assessment and benefits can be a gruelling affair. We think that military and civilian medical assessments can contradict each other, which could create an environment of misinformation and confusion.

action: Require more time spent in physical education classes in primary schools
background: We would like an increase to the amount of weekly physical education sessions that primary schools deliver. We think this would help tackle the current obesity epidemic, improve mental health and improve confidence in children. We need to keep our kids moving and healthy.
additional_details: A 2022 study showed that the amount of children treated for type 2 diabetes in paediatric diabetes units in England and Wales had increased by over 50%. Children face a range of health issues. We think that more exercise in schools could help improve children’s health.

action: Give government time to debate the Prime Minister's resignation
background: An online petition was submitted demanding the resignation of PM Keir Starmer. (1) It has reached over 300,000 signatures. Given the rate at which it is gathering signatures this matter should be debated in parliament.
additional_details:
After the resignations of Boris Johnson & Liz Truss Labour demanded a general election. It is only right that should PM Starmer be forced to resign we have a general election.

(1) Demand Change: Keir Starmer, Step Down Now! https://www.change.org/p/demand-change-keir-starmer-step-down-now
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for elected representatives or public servants to resign or be removed from office. 

You may wish to sign the existing open petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700143

action: End Modern Slavery for International Qualified Care Workers in Nursing Homes
background: We call on Parliament to pass a law allowing international nurses working in UK nursing homes for three or more years as healthcare assistants, who have completed CBT and OSCE qualifications, to be eligible for NMC registration without requiring the SIFE document.
additional_details:
Qualified international healthcare workers in UK nursing homes face exploitation. 
Under Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) rules, international nurses can register as qualified nurses if their managers provide a Supporting Information from Employer (SIFE) document.
Many employers refuse to issue this certificate due to the low wages paid to qualified and experienced nurses working as healthcare assistants.
This practice blocks career advancement and perpetuates modern slavery-like conditions.

action: Ban advertisements on paid video/film streaming services
background: Many streaming services require a paid subscription but still force one to watch advertisements. This is an absolute joke!
additional_details: The government should put an end to this by creating a piece of legislation banning paid streaming platforms from showing advertisements.

action: No confidence in the government
background: The rural community has no confidence in the government and wants to call for a debate the issues caused by the chancellor’s recent budget that will damage the food security of the UK
additional_details: Allow a free vote on the decision of the chancellors budget that will directly affect the ability of the UK to ensure we have a strong and reliable supply of domestic food production in the UK
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the petition below relating to inheritance tax: 

Don't change inheritance tax relief for working farms
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700138

action: Make it a legal requirement that resale of event tickets must be face value
background: Endless fans are being priced out of events by touts using bots to buy tickets then reselling them on sites such as viagogo for heavily inflated prices. This should not be allowed and any resale should only be allowed at face value.
additional_details: Make it a legal requirement that all resale of event tickets are advertised and sold at face value only. There is no reason why this cannot be done. Should someone want/need to resell a ticket then the original purchase price should visable to people wanting to buy and the ticket should only be sold at this price. Sites and individuals should be punished for attempting to sell at inflated prices.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign the following petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702304

action: Child against parent violence to be recognised as domestic abuse & more support
background: I want the Domestic Abuse Act to be amended to recognise that child against parent violence by under 16’s is still a form of domestic violence.
additional_details:
I wish for more recognition and understanding of the issue & more funding for support for victims to access help during and after their experiences. 
 
For an issue that affects many parents or caregivers I believe there needs to be far more awareness & support for families during and in the aftermath. Currently there may be little to no consequences for the perpetrators, with blame often placed mainly on the parents.

action: Deploy the Royal Navy to help stop illegal immigrants entering the UK
background: We think that UK national security is the number one job of the UK government. We would like the Government to deploy the Royal Navy to help stop illegal immigrants entering the UK.
additional_details: We believe that there isn't enough of a deterrent in place and a speedy response is needed and needed now. We think we are totally exposed to an increasing number of undocumented migrants entering our country. The UK Government should get tough. We believe international agreements are a waste of UK tax payers money, and money better spent in UK defence could allow the Navy to help prevent illegal migration.

action: Stop giving homework to primary and secondary school students
background: I think that the government should ban all homework for children aged 4-16. This is because children go to school for an average of 6.5 hours a day and then get home and have to do more work, this being homework.
additional_details: Finland have some of the happiest and most academically successful students in the world. Finland also have almost no homework.

action: Scrap the Sugar tax on soft drinks
background: The Sugar Tax was brought in by the last Conservative government in 2018 partly to try and reduce childhood obesity. We believe it hasn't worked at all and has instead just provided the government more money for no reason.
additional_details: Instead of taking away people's freedoms of choice on what to eat and drink, we should be encouraging overweight people to live a healthier lifestyle and go to the gym. We think it's not fair how fit, healthy people can be affected by anti obesity measures including this sugar levy which we feel was a bad idea. In addition, some people with allergies to sweeteners may need full sugar drinks instead.

action: Stop the permitted development right to extend upwards
background: We urge the Government to stop the permitted development right to extend upwards. We think this policy benefits developers & freeholders, harming leaseholders & residents, causing financial, structural, & emotional strain. Meant to ease housing shortages, we think it is now a profit-driven scheme.
additional_details:
We think these developments could:
- Undermine building safety, creating both risks during building works and long-term risks.
- Devalue flats, leaving leaseholders financially trapped.
- Raise service charges.
- Disrupt daily life, causing noise, dust, and restricted access, ruining residents’ well-being.
- Prioritise profits over communities, neglecting local needs.
 
This petition urges the Government to protect leaseholders, property rights, and communities from exploitation and disruption.

action: Require drivers to retake their driving test at age 60.
background: We think at the age of 60 everyone should have to redo their driving test as many road accidents involve an older driver.
additional_details: I believe it would be safer for everyone if people redid they're driving test age 60 and dangerous drivers get taken off the roads.

action: Ban the teaching of inappropriate sexual content in schools to children
background: US President elect Donald J Trump has initiated the banning of teaching of inappropriate sexual content in schools. Whilst sex education is vitally important it must be done at an appropriate age, with full parental knowledge, consent and consultation on the content. We should do the same.
rejection_details: Government guidance indicates schools should consult parents. You can find more information here: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/62cea352e90e071e789ea9bf/Relationships_Education_RSE_and_Health_Education.pdf

action: Hold a national referendum on the UK’s diplomatic relationship with Israel.
background: We call on the Government to hold a national referendum on the UK's relationship with Israel. We think this would allow the British public to decide whether to continue current relations in light of the concerns many have about Israel’s actions.
additional_details: UK relations with Israel have come under scrutiny due to many being concerned about allegations of war crimes and compliance with international law. We think this raises ethical and legal questions regarding the UK's support and diplomatic relations with Israel. By holding a national referendum, we think we would empower British citizens to express their stance on whether these ties should continue, be revised, or severed entirely, helping to ensure that the UK's foreign policy aligns with values and will of its people.

action: Fund improvements to secondary care community mental health services
background: We think supporting patients with a qualified & compassionate workforce that have sufficient time & resources to provide effective support is essential & cost effective.
additional_details:
We think the government should not conflate primary & secondary care services. We think the NHS should better fund services, including the professional 'Care Coordinator' role (i.e. qualified mental health Nurses, Social Workers & Occupational Therapists).
 
We think the Government should provide NHS funding so qualified 'care coordinator' to patient ratios are a maximum of 1:12 and psychological therapists to patient ratio are maximum of 1:40. 
 
We think the Government should adequately fund and legislate to mandate these staff to patient ratios in every secondary care service.

action: Make autism training mandatory for teachers in schools to help understanding
background: We would like the Government to make autism training mandatory for all teachers.
additional_details: I believe that if teachers were made to complete autism training as a mandatory requirement, this would give them some understanding of how people living with Autism can struggle in school and how best they can support their students as currently there is very little understanding with in schools. I think that this may also help some children remain in mainstream schools instead of having to go to specialist schools, as the child may not actually need to attend a specialist school if mainstream ones could support.

action: Standardise Women’s Titles as "Ms" and Eliminate Titles Based on Marital Status
background: 1.       Update legal documents, government forms, and public records to include only the title "Ms" for women. 2. Eliminate "Miss" and "Mrs." as options on official forms, correspondence, and in public records. 3. Launch a public awareness campaign to educate citizens and organisations.
additional_details: The distinction originates from when a woman’s societal worth was tied to her relationship with a man. "Miss" is often used to denote divorced women, making their marital history public. We think this is problematic in settings like schools, where titles are displayed everywhere; and contradicts the Equality Act 2010, prohibiting discrimination on the grounds of sex, marital status, and other protected characteristics. France and Germany, have eliminated titles based on marital status for women.

action: Ban Fur Imports into the UK
background: We ask the Government to ban the import and sale of all fur products in the UK. Fur farming is banned here due to cruelty, yet imports support suffering abroad. We believe that this ban would align UK laws with ethical and environmental responsibility, closing the loophole that fuels the fur trade.
additional_details: Fur farming is banned in the UK, but we believe that importing fur allows cruelty abroad to thrive. Animals on fur farms endure lifelong confinement in tiny cages, suffering immense stress and horrific executions like gassing and electrocution. We hold that fur production pollutes water, air, and soil and involves toxic chemicals. With ethical and sustainable alternatives widely available, continuing to import fur contradicts UK values of compassion and environmental responsibility. We believe a ban would close this harmful loophole.

action: Create an Animal NHS
background: The cost of veterinary provision is rising exponentially.  If Parliament sets up an Animal NHS, if only for the animals of pensioners and those on means tested benefits, it will prevent pet owning from becoming the province of only the extremely wealthy.
additional_details:
Pet owners whose animals become ill or are injured and who are on limited financial means  face the choice of killing their animal or being prosecuted by the RSPCA if they wait until they have the money to pay for treatment.  

 If veterinary students who worked for an Animal NHS for 5 years when they qualified had their tuitions fees waived the scheme would pay for itself considering the heartbreak and stress that pet owners face. in these situations.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700344

background: Call a general election as the current government is not fit for purpose
additional_details: Because they are not fit for purpose and we think the general public feel they are not working for the good of the country
rejection_details:

background: I would like the government to make an exemption for the increased employer's national insurance contributions for micro companies (so called micro-entities).
additional_details: As an owner of a micro business, attempting to grow, the national insurance increase will make it impossible to employ new staff members and will also lead to layoffs. I have discussed this with multiple SME owners and they have all said they will be making staff cuts, due to the increases.

action: Increase tariffs on all imports
background: We believe that this would help to protect UK jobs and our economy.

action: Prohibit publishers irrevocably disabling video games they have already sold
background: The government should update consumer law to prohibit publishers from disabling video games (and related game assets / features) they have already sold without recourse for customers to retain or repair them. We seek this as a statutory consumer right.
additional_details: Most video games sold can work indefinitely, but some have design elements that render the product non-functional at a time which the publisher controls, with no date provided at sale. We see this as a form of planned obsolescence, as customers can be deprived of their purchase and cannot retain or repair the game. We think this practice is hostile to consumers, entirely preventable, and have concerns existing laws do not address the problem.  Thus, we believe government intervention is needed.
government_response_summary: There are no plans to amend UK consumer law on disabling video games. Those selling games must comply with existing requirements in consumer law and we will continue to monitor this issue.
government_response_body: The Government recognises concerns raised by video games users regarding the operability of purchased products. As the lead department for video games, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) regularly engages industry representatives and monitors how consumers interact with games. We work with the Department for Business and Trade (DBT) as the lead department for consumer protection more generally.  We are aware of issues relating to the life-span of digital content, including video games, and we appreciate the concerns of players of some games that have been discontinued. We have no plans to amend existing consumer law on digital obsolescence, but we will monitor this issue and consider the relevant work of the Competition and Market Authority (CMA) on consumer rights and consumer detriment.  Video games sellers must comply with existing consumer law – this includes the Consumer Rights Act 2015 (CRA) and Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs). We have provided details of relevant protections below. However, there is no requirement in UK law for software companies to support older versions of their products. Decision-making is for those companies, taking account of commercial and regulatory factors and complying with existing consumer law. There may be occasions where companies make decisions based on the high running costs of maintaining older servers for games with declining user bases.   The CRA gives consumers important rights when they make a contract with a trader for the supply of digital content, requiring it to be of satisfactory quality, fit for a particular purpose and as described by the seller. It may be difficult and expensive for businesses to maintain support for old software, particularly if it needs to interact with new technologies. However, if software is offered for sale that is not supported by the provider, then this should be made clear, for example on product webpages and physical packaging.   If digital content does not meet these quality rights, the consumer is entitled to a repair or replacement or, if not possible, some money back up to 100% of the cost of the digital content. These rights apply to intangible digital content like a PC game, as well as tangible content like a physical copy of a game. The CRA has a limit of up to six years after a breach of contract during which a consumer can take legal action.  A trader or third party can upgrade and improve the features of digital content so long as it continues to match any description given by the trader and conforms with any pre-contract information provided by the trader, unless varied by express agreement.   In addition, the CRA requires that the terms and conditions applied by a trader to a product they sell must not be unfair and must be prominent and transparent. If not, they may also be challenged and the question of fairness is a matter for the courts. Terms found to be unfair are not binding on the consumer.  The CPRs require information to consumers to be clear and correct and prohibit commercial practices which through false information or misleading omissions cause the average consumer to make a different choice. As such, the regulations prohibit commercial practices which omit or hide information which the average consumer needs to make an informed choice, and prohibits traders from providing material information in an unclear, unintelligible, ambiguous or untimely manner. If consumers are led to believe that a game will remain playable indefinitely for certain systems, despite the end of physical support, the CPRs may require that the game remains technically feasible (for example, available offline) to play under those circumstances.   The CPRs are enforced by Trading Standards and the CMA. If consumers believe that there has been a breach of these regulations, they should report it to the Citizens Advice helpline (or Advice Direct Scotland for those living in Scotland) which is a free service advising on rights and how to take their case forward. The helplines will refer complaints to Trading Standards and CMA where appropriate. Consumers can also pursue private redress through the courts where a trader has provided misleading information on a product.   The CPRs section of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers (DMCC) Act 2024 is expected to come into effect in April 2025. It restates and updates the CPRs into primary legislation, revokes the 2008 regulations and sets out rules around unfair trading. The Act: ●	Provides the Secretary of State with the power to add, amend, or remove a description of a commercial practice which are in all circumstances considered unfair  ●	Provides clarification that someone facilitating supply or promotion of a product is a ‘trader’ and must comply with consumer law  The use of this power will be kept under review – any amendments proposed are subject to a duty to consult with stakeholders and approval by both Houses of Parliament. Department for Culture, Media and Sport

action: Explain the Data (Use and Access) Bill thoroughly to the people of the UK.
background:
Let the people of the United Kingdom decide if this bill is as innocent as it is being made out to be.

For people's reading
 https://bills.parliament.uk/publications/56527/documents/5211
additional_details:
A bill of 262 pages of 14 far-reaching provisions with 8 main parts and 138 sub-parts. What does this bill mean for the people of the United Kingdom concerning data use and access?

The data (property) of the United Kingdom people is theirs, NOT anyone else's. First, talk to the people of the United Kingdom, be honest and transparent, and see if they agree with the proposals for the Data (Use and Access) Bill and the property of said child, woman, and man.
rejection_details:
