action: Review and mandate DNA testing to end honey fraud and protect real producers.
background: We urge the Government to bring forward regulations that mandate DNA testing to ensure honey purity. We believe that current tests fail to detect widespread adulteration.
additional_details:
Genuine honey deserves better protection. Let’s preserve its integrity. 

There are concerns that counterfeit honey floods the market, undercutting real beekeepers and deceiving consumers, and current sugar profiling tests fail to catch sophisticated fraud. We think that DNA testing could ensure authenticity, protecting livelihoods and maintaining fair competition. The Government should act decisively to mandate advanced testing to safeguard genuine honey, and uphold the integrity of the UK honey market for all.

action: Conduct a review into the merits of co-operative exams
background: I would like the Government to review the merits of introducing co-operative exams in school, where students work together to solve issues.
additional_details: I believe co-operation exams would allow students to learn teamwork and leadership more easily. They could also help create an efficient workplace for wherever students go and it could also help them get grades more easily by allowing them to show skills in other aspects

action: Require school to watch PMQs every Wednesday at midday
background: It is important for students at school to understand the skills of debate needed in parliament and understand politics and how parliament pass laws.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about what programmes children are shown at school are a matter for individual schools, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Change the earliest days of ILR application from 28days to 180days before 5years
background: I want the government to change the ILR application from 28days to 180 days before 5years. It is a great privilege to live here permanently. Applying earlier helps people in their plans and help to attain permanent stay before visas expire and reduces the tension of applying 28days before 5years.
additional_details: Most people take years to prepare and save up to apply. I believe that there's a lot of pressure and tension leading up to 28days and a lot of people might apply at the same time which increases the government's workload. 180 days before 5years is enough time to turn in applications and focus on work and family. I think getting the ILR early helps people with a great sense of belonging and pride.

action: Change the voting age from 18 to 16
background: The government should move the voting age from 18 to 16 in all elections.
additional_details:
16 year old have to pay National Insurance and Income Tax once they reach an income threshold, it only makes sense that the responsibility of paying taxes should come with the right to vote and decide where those taxes go.

Young people need the right to decide their own future, and it's clear that the future that is currently being created isn't the one young people deserve.

When people turn 16, they gain so many rights and responsibilities. Why is the right to vote not a part of that?
rejection_details: You may wish to sign the following petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700687

action: Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal.
background: We believe neither the Government, nor anyone else, should be able to use technologies to intervene in the Earth’s natural weather systems. WE WANT ALL FORMS of 'GEO-ENGINEERING' on LAND, SEA & AIR in the UK BANNED.
additional_details: The Govt has 'declared Geo-Engineering essential to meet its climate targets'. We strongly counter this claim. People, animals, plants are being harmed; because the atmosphere in which they exist is being polluted on a daily basis by a cocktail of dangerous, chemicals and heavy metals they should NOT be exposed to. More importantly WE WERE NOT ASKED for our opinion nor permission to put our health at risk for the sake of a 'globalist' Net Zero agenda. NOR SHOULD OUR GOVERNMENT IMPOSE IT!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign:

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701963

action: Reduce salary threshold of 38,700 for visa sponsorship requirements
background: We call on the Government to review and reduce the £38,700 minimum salary threshold for skilled worker visa sponsorship, as this figure is significantly above typical UK salaries and creates unnecessary barriers for both businesses and skilled migrants.
additional_details:
The current threshold:
- Far exceeds the UK median salary (approximately £30,000)
- Creates an artificial barrier for skilled workers in many legitimate professions
- Disproportionately affects small businesses and regions outside London
- May force current visa holders to leave the UK despite being valued employees
- Risks splitting families where the main visa holder cannot meet the new threshold.

This review is crucial for supporting business growth and family unity.

action: Expand the winter fuel allowance to other vulnerable people.
background: Instead of means testing the winter fuel payment for pensioners, we think all over 60s, those with cancer or long term sick patients should be entitled to £100 per month for each of gas and electricity from Oct to Jan paid directly to the energy company, or £200 per month for all electric homes.
additional_details: We believe this could help cut hospital admissions and the associated cost to the NHS.

action: Give Naturists More Freedom and Equal Rights in Public Spaces
background: Naturism is simply connecting with nature and rediscovery of ourselves without the need of clothes. Being nude is beneficial to our wellbeing and mental health. Naturists deserve the right to coexist in society with the clothed community.
additional_details: Naturists need the equal rights just like every other community within society. The evidence is out there that simply being nude makes us happier and more confident. It is good for every body, regardless of background, ethnicity, gender and sexual orientation.

action: We want a referendum on 7 changes to our voting system
background: We want a referendum on 7 changes to our voting system to maximise turnout and strengthen faith in our voting system. People should be allowed to say yes or no to the following.
additional_details:
1) Voting should be over 2 weeks to maximise voter turnout.

2) Only registered citizens should be allowed to vote.

3) Abolition of postal voting - I believe it's grossly open to abuse

4) Abolition of electronic voting - I believe it's grossly open to abuse.

5) Like some other countries it must be mandatory to vote & failure to vote should carry a fine.

6) Polling stations should be open 24 hours to maximise turnout.

7) Like in India once you have voted they should put an indelible mark on your finger which lasts two weeks so you can't vote more than once

action: Change the drinking age in pubs to 14 and alcohol purchasing age in pubs to 16
background: We believe that the drinking age in pubs should be lowered to 14. This should be accompanied with a meal and with parent supervision and permission. We would also like the Government to introduce legislation that allows people to purchase a small amount of alcohol in pubs from the age of 16.
additional_details: We think that pubs are a key part of British culture and with the financial difficulties some pubs are currently experiencing this could help give them a slight increase in revenue and allow our pubs to stay open. We think those aged 14 and older should also be able to partake in this vital part of British culture ensuring its preservation for many years to come and revitalising the British pub

action: Change the childcare policy in Scotland to align with that in England.
background: Align the Scottish childcare policy with that of England. So that all families with a child older than 9 months get 15 hours support with childcare costs.
additional_details: At the moment the current policy involves making parents wait until the child is 2 years of age (if receiving benefits) or 3 if not in receipt of benefits. This is too late and is negatively impacting on working families and children. It means working mother's have to put their careers on hold for longer in Scotland, despite Scotland having higher taxes than England. Scotland want to help more families in poverty but this help only starts from 2 years of age, England helps everyone from 9 months
rejection_details: Childcare in Scotland is a devolved matter. You may wish to get in touch with Scottish Parliament about this issue.

action: Ban horse racing
background: I think that horse racing causes too many horses to die. It is unnecessary for jockeys to force the horses to run so fast that there is a risk of death - which is what happens to some horses.
additional_details: I am asking the Government to ban horse racing.

action: Review the prescribing and sale of topical corticosteroids
background: We ask the government to review prescribing protocols and over-the-counter availability of topical corticosteroids. We believe that topical corticosteroids have been over-prescribed and irresponsibly prescribed for decades – leading to what is known as ‘Topical Steroid Addiction’.
additional_details:
This can cause the iatrogenic illness known as ‘Red Skin Syndrome’ – often misdiagnosed as ‘worsening eczema’. 

The recovery process - ‘Topical Steroid Withdrawal’ is brutal, highly debilitating, and often lasts for years. Healthcare professionals need to fully understand the potential serious side-effects of these medications before prescribing them to patients, to prevent unnecessary, preventable suffering.

action: Review regulation around hysterectomies in private hospitals
background: We believe there should be a review of the regulation around hysterectomies in private hospitals, to ensure that the hospitals have all necessary equipment and appropriately trained staff to deal with emergency complications. If they don't, they shouldn't be able to do it.

action: Make teaching BSL mandatory in all schools
background: There are about 50,000 deaf children in the UK. I would like the Government to make all schools introduce British sign language as a mandatory lesson in the curriculum.
additional_details: I think it’s disgusting that in 2024 BSL is not mandatory in schools.  When deaf children start school I want them to be able to communicate with other kids and thrive in a normal school environment, but until there’s a change it won't be possible. I believe it's about time it’s added to the curriculum!

action: lawmakers to implement measures fathers accountable for financial contributions
background:
Mandatory Financial Contributions
We call upon the government and Parliament to take decisive action to enforce the financial responsibilities of fathers towards their children. It is imperative that every child has access to the resources they need for a healthy and prosperous life,
additional_details: Child Welfare: Children are entitled to support from both parents to ensure their basic needs are met, including food, shelter, healthcare, and education. Government intervention can establish and enforce standards for child support that guarantee every child receives the financial resources necessary for a healthy upbringing.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you are concerned about fathers making financial contributions for their children, but we are not sure how you would like the government to enforce this.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may wish to sign the following petition:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701777

Requirements of child maintenance: 
https://www.gov.uk/child-maintenance-service

action: Change the rule for change visa from tier4 to tier2
background: Its need to change the rule for visa change. Because of many reasons students cannot complete there study. Because of that they have no any option to change there visa from tier4 to tier2.
additional_details: Previous government was change this rule and close the door for that people who want to start there career in uk. Because of rule change they have no option to start career. If this rule will dismiss so they have option to start there career in uk.
rejection_details:
It’s not clear what the petition is asking the UK Government or Parliament to do.

On 1st Dec 2020, the Tier 2 Visa was replaced by the Skilled Worker Visa.

action: Exemption from stamp duty changes if mortgage offers predate the Autumn budget
background: Waive stamp duty increases for buyers with mortgage offers predating the decision to increase stamp duty in the Autumn budget. We think that if buyers can prove that purchase offers and mortgage offers were agreed before these changes were announced, the higher rates of stamp duty should be waived.
additional_details: Many may now face unexpected costs, which could leave them unable to move. I want to support fairness for those who budgeted under previous rules and are now impacted by government changes. I think this could cause profound disruption to individuals and families who have reserved newbuild homes that won't be built/completed until after the changes come into effect.

action: Cabinet ministers to publish annual tax returns
background: I want all senior post holders in Government, i.e. all cabinet ministers, to publish their tax returns.
additional_details: I think it is appropriate for this action to be considered by this Government as I think they promote fair taxation and the idea that those who can afford to pay more should pay more. This could be an opportunity to demonstrate to the electorate that senior politicians who hold financially privileged positions embrace their mantra and shoulder their fair share of tax.

action: Abolish 'Non-Crime Hate Incidents' (NCHIs) in England & Wales.
background: We would like the Westminster government to abolish 'Non-Crime Hate Incidents' (NCHIs) in England & Wales. We are targeting England and Wales since the recording and retention of NCHIs in Scotland and Northern Ireland is devolved to them and not therefore a matter for the government in Westminster.
additional_details: The UK is rapidly turning into an Orwellian totalitarian state in which people are investigated and harassed by the police for their lawful ("Non-Crime") comments. According to Freedom of Information requests in 2019, the police had already recorded 119,934 NCHIs since 2014. That number has probably doubled since 2019. NCHIs are having a chilling effect on free speech, encouraging people to report those whose views they simply do not like, and diverting police resources from dealing with crime.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701051

action: Referendum on whether to abolish the Welsh Parliament
background: I believe a referendum in Wales is needed on whether to abolish the Welsh Parliament.
additional_details: I believe money in Wales is being wasted by the Welsh Government and it has become too costly and is no longer fit for purpose. I think that abolishing it would save money that could be put to better use.

action: Require licences to use air rifles
background: I would like for all air rifle owners to have to have a licence to use their weapon even if they are under 12foot/pound.
additional_details: Since 2020, there has been an increase of people being seriously injured with air weapons. These weapons are still lethal and no licence required so people are not tested to use.

action: Set limits on the length of lane closures for roadworks
background:
Set limits for roadworks on motorways and A roads including:
- Limiting lane closures to 3 miles maximum on motorways, 1 mile on A roads. 
- No roadworks or lane closures allowed within 20 miles of other works.
- All work areas resourced 24 hours a day in non-residential areas until completion.
additional_details:
We believe that continuous lane closure disruption may cause:
- Increased potential for accidents
- Reduced access for emergency vehicles
- Delayed business deliveries
- Difficulty planning journeys
- Increased journey times
- Personal stress
- Road rage
- Lateness for medical appointments, work, school, flights, etc.
- Damage to the environment due to pollution from concentrated stationary traffic

action: Abolish TV licence
background: The TV licence is outdated and should no longer be forced on people due to competitive law with subscription based companies and free TV with adverts from many different providers. The BBC TV licence must go,if the BBC doesn't want to show paid adverts then make them an optional subscription company
additional_details: Over 18000 people signed up for the TV license to be abolished under the previous government. The money presenters get paid is a ridiculous amount and if cheaper presenters were used, then the TV licence could be reduced. Freedom of the individual, should be able to choose what they want to watch, if one wants to watch live TV of the itv for example, that are self funded, then why does a TV licence need to be obtained from the BBC, those overseas can watch the BBC for free, so why are we paying!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Abolish the tv licence
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701068

action: Allow UK citizens to call for a referendum on confidence in the government.
background: Change the law allowing UK citizens to hold a referendum where there's widespread concern & confidence within the electorate over the governments performance, policies & conformance to their published manifesto. The referendum should be a yes/no vote followed by a general election if successful.
additional_details: I believe that the electorate should be given more say in the running of the country and that the current system of government with a fixed term of office can become undemocratic given the timescales between the electorate having a voice to raise their concerns between general elections. This allows for the ruling party to force unpopular decision onto the electorate without the electorate having the ability to respond.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition: 

Change the law, so that UK citizens can force an immediate General Election: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702341

action: Make children eligible for free childcare from the date of their 3rd birthday
background: I believe that parents of all 3 year olds should have access to free childcare from the day of the child's 3rd birthday, rather than from the start of the following term. I think otherwise this is discriminatory.
additional_details: Children do not currently become eligible for free childcare entitlements until the start of the nursery term following their third birthday. This means that some children must wait up to five months before they are eligible. Under this current system, some children can be losing up to five months of early learning and play because of their birth date.

action: Launch a Government Review on protecting UK democracy and China
background: We call on the Government to review how to protect the UK’s democracy in respect of its relationship with China and the UK Government’s engagement with the Chinese Government on trade issues.
additional_details: This is in the context of allegations that China has been monitoring criticism of its government overseas, including in the UK, and its sanctioning of UK Members of Parliament. We believe that such actions supress the freedom of expression in the UK.

action: Ensure needs of autistic people are met in any future pandemic response
background: Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, I believe many Autistic people struggled to process & understand information about the pandemic. If we were to have another pandemic, appropriate, autism-friendly advice should be provided.
additional_details: The mental health of many Autistic people has been negatively affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. A recent Insight Survey ‘The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Autistic Adults’ published in February 2021 stated: "72% of respondents reported some or significant deterioration in Mental Health during the pandemic” and said the most negative impacts were the result of “uncertainty and disruption of normal routine”. More should be done to prevent this in future.

action: Introduce a Statutory Levy on Bookmakers to Fund Greyhound Welfare
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce a statutory levy on bookmakers to secure reliable funding for greyhound welfare.
additional_details: We do not think current voluntary contributions adequately address welfare needs. We think we need a sustainable funding model to ensure that every greyhound receives proper care and support both during and after their racing careers. By legislating for this levy, the government could secure the future of greyhound welfare funding, ensuring that we continue to protect and care for these canine athletes for years to come.

action: Change fine rules so only one parent is charged for a child taken out of school
background: Currently both parents can be issued fines for a child being taken out of school. We believe it is unfair to get penalised twice for the same child being taken out of school.
additional_details: To make it fair, and help ensure that single parents and other families are being treated fairly, we would like the Government to change the rules around fines, so that both parents cannot be charged.

action: Change election rules so that only people who live in the area can stand
background: We think the rules for Parliamentary elections or by-elections need changing so that only people who have their primary home in a particular area and have lived in that areas for at least five years can stand in elections.
additional_details:
We want to change the laws about who can represent a particular area as we think this would ensure that only people who have a real interest in that particular area are able to stand to act for that area wanting the best for the area. We think this would stop people who are not local residents standing as a candidate just because they think it will be an easy seat to win. We think these candidates have no real connection to that area nor a real concern over what happens in that area.
 
We think making it so that only local people can represent their neighbours will restore some confidence in MPs because who knows the needs of an area better than someone who actually lives in that area.

action: Boost the UK economy & reduce unemployment by reducing corporation tax
background: I believe that lowering corporation tax to 1% could encourage foreign investment potentially boosting the UK economy and reducing unemployment.
additional_details: I believe we should lower corporation tax to encourage foreign investment.

action: Make overtime pay tax-free to support workers and boost the UK economy!
background: We urge the Government to make overtime pay tax-free. This would support workers facing rising costs, encourage part-time staff to take on extra hours, and help fill labour shortages. By allowing workers to keep their full overtime earnings, it would boost incomes and drive economic growth.
additional_details: Making overtime pay tax-free would provide financial relief to workers struggling with rising living costs, incentivise part-time staff to work extra hours, and address critical labour shortages. This policy would boost disposable incomes, increase productivity, and strengthen the UK economy overall.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign:

'Don’t tax people on any overtime they work.'
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701418

action: Allow other religions to solemnise weddings
background: Change the law so that any faith leader registered as such, has the right to conduct weddings equal to Anglican, Quaker and Jewish leaders.
additional_details:
We think the current rules regarding weddings are outdated and favour Anglican, Quaker and Jewish leaders over other religions or faiths, giving greater religious power to clergy from 3 faith groups over any other. We think that legal bias needs to end.

We believe a lot of the population feel let down by the rules some Churches have that say they cannot have a religious wedding. Other faith leaders may be willing to conduct the wedding for same-sex or mixed faith couples.

action: Change building regulations to enhance sustainability
background: To include solar panels, batteries, and rainwater reclamation systems as a minimum standard on all new buildings. I believe this will help reduce fossil fuel energy consumption and reliance on national water systems like reservoirs.
additional_details:
I believe it will help promote sustainability in the energy sector as spare energy could be sold to the national grid suppliers which may also lead to reduced energy costs and lower carbon footprint. And I believe the batteries will help during times when energy consumption is higher.

action: Don't introduce unique child identifier and increased home education regulation
background: We urge the government not to introduce a single unique identifier number for children and increased regulation of home education. We think its proposals would infringe on children’s privacy and parental rights, especially as elective home education is not in itself a safeguarding risk.
additional_details: We urge the rejection of proposals in the Keeping Children Safe, Helping Families Thrive paper to introduce a single unique identifier for children and more regulation of home education. We think these measures would infringe on children’s privacy and family rights, even though the paper acknowledges elective home education isn't in itself a safeguarding risk. We think these measures would also increase needless monitoring and could infringe on family freedoms and children’s rights.
government_response_summary: The government is committed to introducing a unique child identifier and register of children not in school to promote and support children’s education and welfare.
government_response_body: These proposals, which are included in the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill, are central to the government’s ambition to promote the welfare of children, facilitate the provision of support and ensure that all children can achieve and thrive. The introduction of a single unique identifier for children is a Manifesto commitment.   Concerns about privacy should not be a barrier to the legitimate collection and sharing of information that would keep children safe or promote their education. The Department takes children’s rights and privacy very seriously. We have undertaken several detailed Impact Assessments to ensure that the proposals in the Bill support and safeguard these rights including a Child’s Rights Impact Assessment and Equalities Impact Assessment. Further, we have published a European Convention of Human Rights memorandum.     Keeping children safe from harm is a multi-agency endeavour. Practitioners supporting children and families must find, receive and share relevant information to assess risks effectively. That is why the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill introduces provision in law now, paving the way for a Single Unique Identifier to be specified and the organisations required to use it, later, via regulations.  An identifier has potential to increase confidence that practitioners from different agencies are talking about the same child and increase the ease and possibility of linking data together across datasets. We want appropriate agencies and practitioners to spend less time chasing information and more time acting on the full picture of relevant information about the child. This will enable practitioners to provide the right services at the right time to meet the needs of children and families.  In regard to the Children Not in School measures included in the Bill, these are aimed at ensuring that all children are in receipt of a safe and suitable education, whether they are educated at school or otherwise. The introduction of these measures will also secure for the first time, a legal duty for local authorities to provide support and advice to home educating families should they request it.  Local authorities have an existing duty under Section 436A of the Education Act 1996 to identify children of compulsory school age in their areas who are not in school and not receiving a suitable education.  However, their ability to fulfil this duty is currently undermined by the fact that parents have no obligation to proactively inform their local authority that they are home educating. England and Wales are in the small minority of Western countries where there is no requirement for parents to register as home educators.  Therefore, the proposals for compulsory Children Not in School registers in each local authority and accompanying duties on parents and certain out-of-school education providers to give information for these registers, will simply ensure that local authorities have an accurate record of where children are being educated across England and Wales.   The mandatory information that parents will be required to give for the Children Not in School registers is limited to: their child’s name, date of birth, address, the parents’ names and addresses, and details of other individuals or organisations that are providing the child with education. This is the information that local authorities require to identify a child and to understand where and how they are receiving education.   If local authorities identify that a child is not in school and is not receiving a suitable education, it is essential that they can support that child into education as quickly as possible. That is why we are making improvements to the existing School Attendance Order process by introducing statutory timelines on certain parts of the process, for example.  We agree that safe and suitable home education is not a safeguarding risk and many parents and carers provide enriching experiences for their children. However, some children who have been withdrawn from school under the guise of home education have been seriously harmed or died due to abuse or neglect and action is needed to prevent this.  The proposal in the Bill to introduce a requirement for parents of children who are on child protection plans, subject to section 47 child protection enquiries, or at special schools to get permission from the local authority before they withdraw their child from school to home educate them is a proportionate check to ensure that home education is in the child’s best interests.  The consent requirement is not an automatic removal of a parent’s right to home educate, and the vast majority of parents will be able to continue to home educate without seeking permission to do so.  Department for Education

action: Change the law, so that UK citizens can force an immediate General Election

government_response_summary: It is a core principle of our constitution that the government of the day holds office by virtue of its ability to command the confidence of the House of Commons. There are no plans to change this.
government_response_body: The Prime Minister can call a general election at a time of their choosing by requesting a dissolution of Parliament from the Sovereign. The Government was elected by the British people on a mandate of change at the July 2024 general election.  It is a core constitutional principle that the government of the day derives its mandate to govern from its ability to command the confidence of the elected House of Commons. There are no plans to change this.  The Government is directly accountable to Parliament in a number of ways, such as Prime Minister’s Questions, opposition day debates, oral and written parliamentary questions, oral and written statements, debates in both Houses and select committee inquiries. The House of Commons is accountable to the people as its members are directly elected representatives from their respective constituencies.  This Government is securing Britain’s future through the Plan for Change, which is delivering security and renewal by kick-starting economic growth to put more money in working people’s pockets, rebuilding the NHS and strengthening our borders. This Government will continue to deliver the manifesto of change that it was elected on and serve the country in the national interest.  Cabinet Office

government_response_summary: There are already 20 Violence Reduction Units established in England and Wales, many of them based on Scotland’s model, and all of them integral to our mission to halve knife crime within a decade.
government_response_body: Violence Reduction Units (VRUs)  Established in 2019, VRUs are non-statutory partnerships operating in the 20 police force areas most affected by serious violence across England and Wales. They are leading and co-ordinating the local response to serious violence, many of which are based on the successful model of Scotland’s VRU.    Responsible for delivering a ‘whole system’ public health approach to tackling violence (like Scotland’s VRU), they bring together key partners to identify the local drivers and root-causes of serious violence and agree and implement a multi-agency response to them.   To this end, VRUs are delivering a range of early intervention and prevention programmes to divert people away from a life of crime. This includes a wide range of approaches including mentoring and trusted adult programmes, intensive behavioural therapies, and sports-based diversionary activities.    The Police Funding Settlement for 2025/26 includes £49.7m for the continuation of work to prevent serious violence, delivered via the VRU programme.   Serious Violence Duty   Introduced through the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 (PCSC 2022), the Serious Violence Duty requires a range of specified authorities, such as the police, local government, youth offending teams, fire, health, and probation services, to work collaboratively, analyse the local problem, and put in place a strategy to prevent and reduce serious violence within their local communities, enabled by new powers to share data and information.  This financial year (2025/26), the Government has allocated £14.4m to continue the implementation and delivery of the Serious Violence Duty across all 43 police force areas in England and Wales.  Sentencing  Anyone found carrying a knife can face the maximum penalty of 4 years of imprisonment.  In recognition of the seriousness of offences related to knives, the law already provides for minimum custodial sentences for repeat knife possession and offences that involve threatening with a weapon.  Adults face a minimum of 6 months of imprisonment whilst young people aged 16 or 17 face a four-month Detention and Training Order.  Where someone is harmed by a knife or offensive weapon, there are a range of offences that they may be charged with, such as causing grievous bodily harm.  These can result in lengthy sentences, up to life imprisonment.   Stop and Search Powers  Stop and search is a vital tool for tackling crime, and police officers in England and Wales have long-standing powers to stop and search an individual or vehicle if they have reasonable grounds to suspect that a person is carrying an offensive weapon, stolen goods, drugs or certain other items.  In addition, where serious violence has occurred, or where intelligence suggests it may occur, a senior police officer may authorise police to stop and search any individual or vehicles for offensive weapons or dangerous implements, with or without reasonable suspicion. These authorisations under section 60 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 are limited to a particular area for a specific period of time, usually no longer than 24 hours.  In the 12 months to March 2024, police in England and Wales conducted a total of 535,307 stop and searches, of which 16,066 resulted in an offensive weapon or firearm being found and taken off the streets. We will continue to support the police in the proportionate and effective use of these powers.  Young Futures Programme  The Government has also created the Young Futures Programme. This includes the establishment of Young Futures Prevention Partnerships, to intervene earlier to ensure that children and young people that are vulnerable to being drawn into crime are identified and offered support in a more systematic way.   As we continue to design Young Futures Prevention Partnerships, we want to ensure that they learn from and build on the work of the 20 VRUs in England and Wales to improve how we identify, reach, and support young people at risk of being drawn into violence.   Home Office

We think the key to effective wider change is freedom to make informed decisions.

action: Allow conjugal visits for prisoners in England and Wales
background: Allow prisoners to have conjugal visits with their partners. We think this will put less strain on relationships and might also help keep prisoners in check as they could lose rights for certain visits if misbehaving.
additional_details: The UK has one of the highest rates of re-offending in the western world. We think it could be beneficial for prisoners to be allowed time to de-stress with their partner. It could also help couples who are looking to start a family, especially if the prisoner has a long sentence.

action: Allow Ukrainians who are disabled to apply for immediate ILR
background: We call on the Government to allow Ukrainians who are disabled to be able to immediately apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain.
additional_details: We believe that Ukrainians with disabilities might find it more difficult to return to life in Ukraine. We think they should be granted Indefinite Leave to Remain in the UK.

action: Allow Visa applicants to pay health surcharge in instalments
background: If someone applies for a five-year visa, they currently must pay £1,035 per year upfront, totalling £5,175. We think applicants should have the option to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge in instalments instead of the full amount upfront for the entire visa duration.
additional_details: We think requiring applicants to pay upfront often results in a surge of fee waiver applications, creating backlogs, delaying visa processing, and increasing taxpayer costs. We believe some applicants exploit this system to extend their stay while transitioning to another visa. We think the high upfront cost, especially for families, leads to frequent fee waiver approvals, causing financial losses for the government. We think instalment payments could curb fee waiver abuse, ease the Home Office’s workload, and boost revenue.

action: Take action to prevent UK supplied missiles being fired into Russia
background: It has been reported that Ukraine have fired UK-supplied missiles into Russia. We call on the Government to take action to prevent UK supplied missiles being used in this way. We believe this will help avoid escalating the conflict and pulling the UK directly into the conflict.
additional_details: We are very concerned about reports of Russia's Oreshnik missile and the apparent lack of defence against them.

action: Bring back higher Right to Buy discounts make Right to Acquire discounts equal
background: Restore the original, higher discounts for Right to Buy and align Right to Acquire discounts with these levels to ensure fairness for all tenants, regardless of whether they live in council or housing association properties.
additional_details: The recent reduction in Right to Buy discounts has made home ownership less accessible for council tenants. Housing association tenants under Right to Acquire face even less support, creating an unfair gap. By restoring higher discounts and aligning the two schemes, the Government can give more families the chance to own their homes, promote equality between tenants, and support long-term housing security for low-income households.

action: Deduct private health care charges from NI contributions.
background: I would like the government to introduce the option for those people who are working to take out private healthcare cover. The charges they pay will be deducted from their national insurance contributions once it has been calculated.
additional_details: I believe it will save the NHS. People are waiting longer to see a GP/specialist or have diagnostic tests, resulting in delayed treatment. This results in them being more likely to have to access emergency care because they have become acutely unwell. An easily treated illness or disease can become more complex due to late diagnosis and treatment resulting in higher costs to the NHS. I believe that more people accessing private healthcare will reduce the pressure on the NHS waiting times, A+E admissions and inpatient ward stay.

action: Introduce differentiated energy pricing, tax breaks and a Transition Energy Fund
background: We urge the Government to establish a two-tier energy pricing system which requires lower tariffs for renewable energy and higher tariffs for fossil fuels. We also call the Government to establish a Transition Energy Fund which support vulnerable households and finances renewable infrastructure.
additional_details: We also urge the Government to introduce tax breaks for businesses investing in green technologies and discounts for consumers using certified renewable energy. We believe differentiating energy costs based on the source of production can accelerate the transition to clean energy. We also believe incentivising renewables and penalising fossil fuels will promote sustainability, reduce emissions, and support a low-carbon economy.

background: At present a vote of no confidence can only be called by parliament, leaving majority governments in an almost untouchable position. This means that governments can break promises or make decisions that are destructive to the country, and the electorate can do nothing until the next election.
additional_details: Citizens should be able to hold the government to account at all times, not just during General Elections. The law needs to be changed so that a petition of 'no confidence' to parliament, containing the signatures of at least 51% of the population means a General Election is immediately called.

action: Require food and drink companies to use Nutri-Score on their packaging
background: I think the government should require companies to use Nutri-Score as a mandatory front-of-pack label. I think this A–E system simplifies healthy choices while supporting those with eating disorders who find calorie counting harmful.
additional_details:
Used in France, I think Nutri-Score is effective and evidence-based, promoting informed, stigma-free decisions. I feel that current traffic light labelling often misrepresents foods, like avocados, due to their fat content. Nutri-Score (A–E) could offer a research-backed, simple alternative. 
 
Around 94% of French consumers support the Nutri-Score on the front of food packages and up to 57% of consumers reported in 2020 that they changed at least one purchasing habit due to Nutri-Score. 
 
Nutri-Score integrates fats, sugars, fibre, protein, and energy into one label, which could reduce confusion and stigma, especially for those with eating disorders.

action: Automatically disclose a violent offender’s history to a partner
background: We believe the law needs to be changed so that if the authorities (police and other bodies) know that a person is in a relationship with someone who has been imprisoned for sexual or other serious violence and is a known dangerous offender, then this is disclosed to the person automatically.
additional_details: At the minute we have Clare’s law that that allows you to do a background check on your partners previous history with domestic violence. We think the law should be changed so that information is automatically shared by agencies/ police should you be in a relationship with someone who has a history of serious violence or sexual violence, and the agencies/police are aware of this relationship. We believe disclosing this automatically without having to go through Clare’s law would help protect victims in the future.

background: We're calling on the government, to call on all councils and housing associations, to take control of the home swapping process. With their involvement, they can ensure that swaps are handled more efficiently, helping those in real need connect with suitable homes.
additional_details: Across the country, many people are desperately seeking a home swap—whether it's to gain an extra room for their growing family, downsize, move closer to support networks, or escape overcrowded conditions. However, the current home swapping system often gets hijacked by people who are not serious about making a real swap. These individuals can waste valuable time, resources and cause unnecessary delays for those who genuinely need to move.

action: Lift restrictions on prescribing puberty blockers to trans children.
background: We want the Government to reverse the restrictions it has introduced relating to the prescription of puberty blockers to children. The Government introduced legislation banning them from being prescribed by the private sector and NHS primary care to under 18s not already taking them.
additional_details:
We believe the ban on puberty blockers has caused untold suffering to trans children in the UK, and the suffering must not be allowed to continue. We think it goes against article 8 of The United Nations Convention On The Rights Of The Child.

Under the convention, children have the right to their own identity –  including their name, nationality and family relations. No one should take this away from them, but if this happens, the convention states that state parties must provide assistance and protection so children can quickly get their identity back.
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to reverse the legislation. It is backed by evidence from the Cass Review and independent recommendations by the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM).
government_response_body: The Government wants trans people and their families to feel safe and accepted in our society, and to be able to live with freedom and dignity. It is also essential that we ensure healthcare provision available to children and young people experiencing gender dysphoria and/or incongruence is safe, evidence-based and clinically appropriate.  These key values are at the heart of the Secretary of State’s decision to introduce an indefinite ban on puberty blocking medicines for new patients, with gender dysphoria and/or incongruence. This came into effect on 1 January 2025 and will be formally reviewed in 2027.   This legislation is available at https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2024/1319/made   The decision to implement this legislation was taken with great care and was informed by multiple strands of evidence, including, but not limited to:   I.	The ‘Independent review of gender identity services for children and young people’ (the ‘Cass Review’). Further information can be found at: https://cass.independent-review.uk/  II.	Independent expert advice from the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM). Further information can be found at: CHM's report on proposed changes to the availability of puberty blockers - GOV.UK - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/chms-report-on-proposed-changes-to-the-availability-of-puberty-blockers  III.	Responses to a targeted consultation to the ‘Proposed changes to the availability of puberty blockers for under 18s’. Further information can be found at: Government's response to the targeted consultation on proposed changes to the availability of puberty blockers - GOV.UK - https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/proposed-changes-to-the-availability-of-puberty-blockers-for-under-18s/outcome/governments-response-to-the-targeted-consultation-on-proposed-changes-to-the-availability-of-puberty-blockers  IV.	Constructive, open and honest in-person discussions between the Secretary of State and children, young people, and their families, with lived experience of gender dysphoria and/or incongruence   In his statement to the House of Commons 11 December 2024, quoting the CHM report, the Secretary of State set out that the current prescribing environment and care pathway for gender dysphoria and/or incongruence in some private settings, and those outside the UK, presents an ‘unacceptable safety risk’ for children and young people.  The CHM, as detailed in their report, observed evidence that information and healthcare provided to some children and young people by private practitioners appeared ‘unsafe from a prescribing medicine safety perspective’ and would ‘likely not be considered to have fulfilled Gillick competence, safe prescribing practice, or be consistent with General Medical Council (GMC) guidance’. They additionally noted that there was an ‘absence of long-term safety and efficacy data for this population’.   These are very serious conclusions which indicate that transgender young people were, uniquely, being exposed to unacceptable risks.  The CHM made recommendations that prescriptions for puberty blockers from prescribers registered overseas should be banned permanently. They further recommended that the prescribing environment in the UK should be made safer through additional safeguards. In particular, and in response to recommendation 3b, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has been asked to develop a quality standard for gender dysphoria services. Additionally, the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is considering how to introduce a risk acknowledgement form (RAF) which prescribers would complete with the patient and/or guardian, in response to recommendation 3a.  Over the last year, NHS England has opened three new gender services in the North West, London and the South West, that offer a fundamentally different clinical model, embedding multi-disciplinary teams in specialist children’s hospitals. This model includes a nominated paediatrician or psychiatrist with overall clinical responsibility for patient safety in these services. A fourth service will open in the East of England in Spring. NHS England is making progress towards its commitment for there to be a specialist children’s gender service in every region by 2026.   NHS England has also published a new service specification for the National Referral Support Service for Specialist Services for Children and Young People with Gender Incongruence. This means that a referral for the specialist Children and Young People’s Gender Service can be only made by an NHS-commissioned, secondary care-level paediatric service or a Children and Young Person mental health service. This will help ensure that healthcare professionals with the relevant expertise conduct the assessment and help determine any co-existing mental health or other health needs of these children and their onward care.  Recently, The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) have published details on the upcoming PATHWAYS: Puberty Suppression and Transitional Healthcare with Adaptive Youth Services clinical study. The study aims to build the evidence base on the care needs and development of children and young people. For further information regarding the trial please visit: https://fundingawards.nihr.ac.uk/award/NIHR167530.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Remove visa requirement: Albania, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia

- Improve the implementation of the Soft Power approach at which we believe the UK is a leader.

- Contribute to the UK economy through increased numbers of tourists.

- Help reduce illegal crossings through the channel.

action: A commission to investigate the feasibility & introduction of a Land Value Tax
background: In light of the recent Inheritance Tax changes, we call on the government to establish a commission to investigate the feasibility & implementation of a Land Value Tax (LVT) as a replacement for property taxes. We believe this could reduce the tax burden on people's work on their property.
additional_details: We believe a Land Value Tax, based on the unimproved value of land rather than property or income, may offer a fairer, more efficient, and sustainable way to generate public revenue. Unlike property taxes, which we think penalize homeowners for improving their properties, a LVT could incentivize the productive use of land while potentially discouraging land speculation and underutilization.

background: Windsor Post office is part of historic Windsor, tourists often going there after visiting the castle.  It is a key lifeline for many Windsor residents.  Windsor castle appears on stamps and it is the home to our Royal family.  Closing this Post office without considering other options is a mistake.

additional_details:

We believe that this would help nurture a greener, healthier future for our kids, as well as being a better use of the planet's resources.

background: The Government should introduce legislation to require all products, including those sold online, to show their origin of production.
additional_details: We think consumers have the right to know where a product is produced upon making a decision to purchase.

action: Increase the statutory paternity leave allowance for fathers of multiple births
background: We believe the Government should increase paternity leave allowance for fathers of multiple births, such as in the case of twins or triplets. We think it’s unfair that fathers are expected to return to work after two weeks in the event of multiple births.
additional_details: We believe the current policy of 2 weeks for statutory paternity leave is unfair for fathers and mothers and are concerned about the potential mental health impact on mothers. We believe that children from multiple births require a huge amount of care a devotion from both parents, not just one parent. We believe that statutory paternity leave should increase per child born.

action: Allow Scotland to hold another Independence referendum
background: Allow the Scottish people to have another independence referendum.
additional_details: Scotland is able to survive on its own, and the people of Scotland should be able to make their own mind up about if we should be. I don't think the way things have went the last 10 years would have been as bad if we voted for independence the first time. The Scots shouldn't have to go through it because the UK parliament decides everything.

action: Change building regulations to ensure more women's toilets in public buildings
background: We call on the Government to change building regulations whereby all new and renovated public buildings have twice as many women's toilets as men's toilets. We believe that women requiring more toilets has been overlooked in the male-dominated construction industry.
additional_details: We believe this measure will prevent excessive queueing and inconveniences for women in public spaces, and that the current situation is a subtle example of everyday sexism that the UK could pioneer in resolving.

action: Review the child maintenance service
background: Review the child maintenance service.
additional_details: Review how the child maintenance service is run. We think the child maintenance service makes it very difficult for paying parents to work, due to high calculations and unexpected arrears. Some parents may refuse to go into direct pay because of concerns about the system. Some parents feel forced to stay on benefits, as they may not be able to afford to pay the arrears within 2 years, and think the monthly payments if they were to work would be unaffordable.

action: Remove all benefits for immigrants that arrive illegally to the UK
background: I want to create a petition urging the government to remove incentives for illegal immigrants in the UK to ensure that public resources are allocated fairly to those here legally.
additional_details: I want the government and Parliament to take action to remove incentives for illegal immigrants because it is crucial for maintaining the integrity of our immigration system and ensuring that taxpayer resources are used efficiently and responsibly. When illegal immigrants have access to public services and welfare benefits, it places an undue burden on our economy and can strain essential services, which are meant for citizens and legal residents who contribute to society. Furthermore, by enforcing stricter regulations, we can deter illegal immigration, which not only helps to uphold the rule of law but also fosters a sense of fairness among those who have followed the legal immigration process.

Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

action: Stop MPs' perks and pay rises while public services face cuts.
background: We urge the Government to end unnecessary perks for MPs, including expense claims for energy bills, rent, and subsidised food and drinks. Additionally, all MP pay rises should be frozen to reflect the financial hardships faced by the public. MPs must lead by example and share the sacrifices.
additional_details: Millions of people in the UK face rising costs and cuts to vital support like the Winter Fuel Payment, forcing them to choose between heating and eating. Meanwhile, MPs benefit from taxpayer-funded perks and pay rises. This is unfair and creates a disconnect. Removing these perks and halting pay rises would show solidarity with the public, restore trust, and ensure that MPs face the same financial realities as those they represent
rejection_details:
Decisions about MPs' pay are the responsibility of the Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority, you can find out more information about IPSA here: https://www.theipsa.org.uk/

Additionally, catering services for the House of Commons are provided by an in-house team who do not provide a subsidised service, though the cost of running the service means that it runs at a loss. It is important to note that while in some venues the cost of providing the service exceeds the income received in sales, other venues in the Commons make a profit which contributes to reducing overall costs. The House of Commons publishes details of the cost of House of Commons catering services: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/foi/transparency-publications/hoc-transparency-publications/catering-services/transparency-reporting-catering-services/

Customers of the House of Commons Catering Services include some of the 650 MPs but also around 14,500 other pass-holders, many of whom are staff on lower wages that work irregular hours. In addition, members of the public and non pass holding visitors to Parliament also have access to these services. The irregular hours and the unpredictability of Parliamentary business contribute to increasing the net cost of providing a catering service. To offset this many of the restaurants, dining room facilities and their staff, are used to cater for private events at times when they are not required by the House. This is one of a number of measures used to reduce costs.

action: Launch a review into increasing speed limits on motorways and dual carriageways
background: I would like the Government to carry out a review into potentially increasing the speed limit to 100mph on motorways and 80mph on dual carriageways. The review should be carried out on 9 year old cars (the average age), testing their braking distance, safety features and sensors.
additional_details: This review could help ensure safety standards are met before implementing any changes and would be crucial to ensure vehicles could handle higher speeds without compromising road safety, protecting drivers and passengers. By analysing these factors, I think the Government could make informed decisions about any future potential speed limit changes while maintaining safety as a priority.

action: Seek to start peace talks between Russia and Ukraine
background: I would like the government to seek to facilitate peace talks between Russia and Ukraine to stop the war.
additional_details: We are concerned that without efforts to end the war, it could escalate. We think it is now time to bring Russia and Ukraine together and try to negotiate peace between the two. We want to stop further damage and loss of life, with the aftermath effect potentially taking decades to recover.

action: Change the capital city to Chester.
background: Change the capital city from London in the south to Chester in the north.

action: Review process for booking driving tests and ban the resale at inflated prices
background: I would like the government to review the process for booking driving tests and ban the resale of driving tests at inflated prices. I think there should be penalties for those caught doing so.
additional_details: I think the DVSA should upgrade the booking site so only one booking can be done per license, unless someone has failed a test. I believe the government should review the booking process so that it is closely monitored with heavy fines and ADI badges taken off people caught selling tests. I believe the online booking system is vulnerable to bots which can buy multiple tests. I believe that extending the validity of the driving theory test certificate to 3 years could help with this process.
government_response_summary: DVSA is reviewing its booking processes with the aim of improving this service for all users. A consultation regarding possible options for improvements has been fast-tracked to May 2025.
government_response_body: To ensure fairness for everyone wanting to book a practical driving test, the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) continues to work hard to combat the unscrupulous practice of reselling tests across the country and has announced further measures to review the driving test booking system.  The DVSA is aware of third-party websites selling driving test appointments and does not approve use of such applications. The DVSA encourages learner drivers to use only the official GOV.UK website to book and manage their driving test and has published advice aimed at learner drivers to warn of the risks of using third parties to book a practical driving test. Further information can be found on GOV.UK at learner drivers warned about the risks of driving test cancellation finders. (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/learner-drivers-warned-about-the-risks-of-driving-test-cancellation-finders?utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=govuk-notifications-topic&utm_source=7db74f10-2052-45bc-952e-2ce2d972f61b&utm_content=immediately)  It is not possible to block book car practical driving tests. A driving licence number can be assigned to only one car practical driving test within the booking system at a time.  DVSA deploys enhanced bot protection to help stop automated systems from buying up tests unfairly. These applications, however, are constantly evolving and changing, and DVSA’s work on this is ongoing.  On the 18 December 2024, DVSA launched a call for evidence (https://www.gov.uk/government/calls-for-evidence/experience-of-booking-and-managing-car-driving-tests/experience-of-booking-and-managing-car-driving-tests), seeking views on the current rules to book tests. This closed with just under 27,000 responses.   The DVSA have been analysing the evidence from this and has been developing proposals which will lead to consultation on improving processes, including any potential future legislative changes. On the 23 April the Secretary of State for Transport announced (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/transport-secretary-acts-to-make-thousands-of-extra-driving-tests-available-each-month?) that this consultation had been fast-tracked to May 2025.  In January 2023, the DVSA changed the terms and conditions for using the booking service to help prevent anyone from selling tests at profit. Between 9 January 2023 and 5 January 2025, the DVSA issued 350 warnings, 792 suspensions, and closed 813 business accounts for misuse of its booking service.  On 6 January 2025, the DVSA introduced a set of tougher terms and conditions that only allow driving instructors or businesses that employ driving instructors to use the booking service to book driving tests. The new terms and conditions make it clear that driving instructors and businesses must not book driving tests on behalf of learner drivers they are not teaching. They also stop driving instructors and businesses from using a learner driver’s details to book a driving test that they have no intention of that particular learner driver using.  If anyone breaks the terms and conditions, the DVSA can issue them with a warning notice, suspend their account and where necessary, close their account.    Since this change DVSA has issued 44 warnings, 120 suspensions, and closed 270 business accounts.  It is important road safety knowledge and hazard perception skills are up to date at the critical point a person drives unsupervised for the first time.  The maximum duration of two years between passing the theory test and a subsequent practical test is in place to ensure a customer’s road safety knowledge and ability to identify developing hazards is current. This validity period is set in legislation, and the Government has no current plans to lay further legislation to extend it.  Ensuring learner drivers have current relevant knowledge and skills is a vital part of the learning to drive process as new drivers are disproportionately casualties on our roads. Learners therefore need to pass another theory test if their two-year theory test certificate expires.  Department for Transport

action: Extend free bus travel for people over 60 in England
background: We call on the Government to extend free bus travel to all people over 60 years old in England outside London. We believe the current situation is unjust and we want equality for everyone over 60.
additional_details: Currently, people in England who do not live in London are not entitled to free bus travel until they reach the state pension age, which we believe has changed dramatically. government_response_summary: The English National Concessionary Travel Scheme costs around £700 million annually. Any changes to the statutory scheme must be carefully considered for their impact on its financial sustainability.
government_response_body: The government wants everyone to have access to public transport and is committed to improving services. We also recognise the importance of the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme (ENCTS) in supporting local bus travel, assisting with access to essential local services and helping those who use it to stay active and avoid isolation.  The ENCTS provides free off-peak bus travel to those with eligible disabilities and those of state pension age, currently sixty-six. The ENCTS costs around £700 million annually and any changes to the statutory obligations, such as lowering the age of eligibility, would therefore need to be carefully considered for its impact on the scheme’s financial sustainability.     Local authorities in England do have the power to offer concessions in addition to their statutory obligations, for example, by extending the age of eligibility for the older persons’ bus pass. These are additional local concessions provided and funded by local authorities from local resources, depending on the needs and priorities of each area.  At the Budget on 30 October, the government confirmed a £1 billion boost for buses, of which £712 million has been allocated to local authorities to support and improve bus services. Funding allocated to local authorities to improve services for passengers can be used in whichever way they wish. This could include extending the discretionary concessions available in the local area.  Concessionary travel is a devolved policy area and as such, the eligibility age for the bus pass differs between the devolved nations of the United Kingdom. This means, in effect, that there are different schemes in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, so the administrative arrangements are entirely separate.  Department for Transport

additional_details:

- state that police officers cannot be caused harassment, alarm or distress under section 4A
- remove the term "insulting" as a criteria variable
- explicitly state what qualifies as "abusive".
 
We believe that nobody should be arrested for being overheard, or for using swearwords in public.

action: Make political education compulsory in our secondary schools

action: Reform the Dangerous Dogs Act (DDA) 1991: keep the public safe
background: We urge the Government to reform the DDA 1991. Whilst S3 applies to all breeds, we believe it's discriminatory due to the existence of S1 which targets specific types based on appearance. We want this replaced with a behaviour-based approach, and to prioritise education for safety and fairness.
additional_details: We believe the DDA 1991 is flawed, and that both S1 and S3 are discriminatory. We think the former unfairly bans certain dogs based on looks, not behaviour, which can create stigma that we believe may affect enforcement of the latter. Some research suggests bans don’t reduce attacks. bans also do not address what we see as the underlying issues of aggression for all dogs: poor ownership and training. We believe we need fair, behaviour-focused laws with strong enforcement and public education.

action: Amend Children Act 1989 to presume grandchild-grandparent contact
background: Based on sound UK evidence, we ask to amend the Children Act 1989 to presume (unless there are safeguarding factors) that involvement of a grandparent in a grandchild's life will further their welfare.
additional_details:
We think this should apply to all grandchildren regardless of their age and family situations.

A 2022 survey estimates a sixth of 0-16yo UK grandparents are prevented from seeing their grandchildren. We believe grandchildren then often experience a sudden and traumatic end to the relationship, leaving many grandchildren unable to see their safe grandparents long-term. We think there are seven typologies that reflect the various grandchild experiences.
 
We believe that grandchildren's ongoing ambiguous grief following this living loss is an unidentified but significant component of the present children and young people's mental health crisis.

action: Reduce corporation tax for small businesses with profits under £50,000 to 13%

additional_details: I believe 19% is too much for small businesses, as the cost of living and inflation have led to many small businesses, earning less than £50,000 profit, to struggle to stay open. I believe the current tax rate is harming the World of business and people's ability to open up their own business.

action: To give more funding to Uniformed Youth Organisations to support young people.

additional_details: I would like the Government to implement this because there is evidence that youth organisations improve young people's life skills, general skills and helps reduce crime.

action: Independent Third-Party to handle and store NHS Health Records
background: We call upon the Government to introduce legislation that means NHS health records are handled by an independent third party to ensure transparency, accountability, and the highest standards of data protection.
additional_details: The NHS provides care to millions and collects and maintains an extensive repository of health records containing sensitive information. The NHS has control over the handling, sharing & storage of these records. We think this unilateral control can result in conflicts of interest, insufficient oversight, and diminished public trust.

action: Enforce that game developers provide a way for their releases to remain playable
background: With ever-increasing reliance on the internet and externally-hosted servers, the government should ensure that consumers have access to the product they paid for. This could take the form of ensuring games have an offline mode, or the ability for users to host their own servers for example.
additional_details: There have been too many cases of online-only games shutting down with no way to access them in recent memory. Perhaps most notably, Sony shut down their large-budget game Concord just two weeks after launch, despite significant marketing efforts, but a largely unsuccessful launch. Ensuring that these games remain playable in some form will protect developers from wasting years on a project with no future and perhaps reduce redundancies in the industry too.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702074

action: Make it illegal to smoke on hospital grounds
background: We want the government to make it against the law to smoke on hospital grounds, with fines for offenders.
additional_details: We think patients across the country are being subjected to second hand smoke when going to medical appointments. We think this should not be a risk when attending a hospital appointment, especially on an “smoke-free site”. We think the Tobacco & Vapes Bill 2024 has missed this vital point.

action: Require news outlets to publish clear, accurate headlines
background: I urge the Government to introduce regulations requiring UK news organisations to publish clear, accurate headlines that reflect article content. I think that misleading "clickbait" titles in media misrepresent articles, erode trust, and spread misinformation.
additional_details: I think this would promote responsible journalism, improve transparency and support public understanding. I don't think this would limit press freedom, but would encourage responsible journalism. For example, instead of "Shocking News About John Doe," a headline like "John Doe jailed for fraud" could promote transparency.

action: Repeal the vagrancy act of 1824 & introduce “leave no trace laws”
background: The Vagrancy Act criminalises the homeless and wild campers which adds to their hardship. I think recognising the humanity of the homeless is crucial. I think “leave no trace laws” should be introduced which require homeless people to leave no trace of their rough sleeping or wild camping.
additional_details: I think this outdated law criminalises people facing challenges. In the past five years, nearly 2,500 homeless individuals in England & Wales have been arrested under this Act for simply having no place to go. I think implementing "leave no trace" laws could protect the environment while allowing wild camping and rough sleeping without persecution. I think Scotland’s “free roam” laws are a good example of how it can be done.

action: Don’t consider bonus or overtime payments when calculating universal credit
background: Change the law so that people who claim universal credits & work, don't get penalised if they receive a bonus in work or if they work a small amount of overtime for a special occasion coming up i.e. a child's birthday, xmas.
additional_details: We believe this affects hundreds of thousands of families in the UK especially single parents who are doing their best to work and juggle parenting. If someone got a £300 bonus in work in most cases their UC would be reduced by 65% of the net payment. We think a change is needed to allow for these bonuses to not effect their usual monthly payments.

action: Require schools to allow students to wear their own clothes at least once a week
background: I call on the Government to require secondary schools to allow students to wear their own clothes at least once a week. additional_details: I believe this measure would benefit students as I think it would let them be who they want to be and allow them to show their true selves through their choice of clothing. I think it could also be beneficial because I believe it may improve student behaviour.

action: Save Crayford Greyhound Stadium

additional_details: Ofsted regulated children’s residential care homes support children with complex needs. Stability in staffing is crucial to their welfare. We think the April 2024 changes have left providers unable to fill critical roles, despite proving the necessity of these positions through inspections. We think this policy adds barriers for already stretched organisations. We think amending restrictions will help care homes recruit the skilled staff needed to protect vulnerable children.

action: Stop the use of non-hate crime orders immediately.

additional_details:
The use of non-hate crime orders undermines fundamental principles of justice and fairness. These orders allow individuals to be penalised for actions or speech that do not meet the legal definition of a hate crime, creating a slippery slope where subjective judgments can lead to overreach and potential misuse of authority.

They also create a chilling effect on free speech, where individuals may feel unable to express themselves out of fear of being unfairly penalised.

action: Improve benefits for veterans
