background: We ask the government to create a Department of Government Efficiency to reduce waste, streamline services, ensuring taxpayer money is spent effectively. By adopting innovative practices and technology, this department would modernize operations, cut bureaucracy, and improve public services for all.
additional_details: A DOGE would ensure taxpayer money is spent wisely by identifying waste, reducing unnecessary bureaucracy, and modernizing services. By adopting innovative practices, such as advanced tech and streamlined processes, the government can improve transparency, deliver better services, and build trust. This initiative would make the UK a leader in efficient governance, ensuring that every pound delivers maximum value for citizens while fostering innovation and responsiveness in public administration.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Create the Department of Government Efficiency: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701630

action: Make Freddos 10p.
background: Make Freddos 10p again. Can be a start to reducing prices of everything else.
additional_details: To make it easier for the poor to eat and have fun.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about food product prices are a matter for manufacturers and retailers, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Amend UNECE Regulation No. 79
background: We call on the Government to amend UNECE Regulation 79 to allow greater flexibility in the safe use of car’s remote driving features.
additional_details:
Extending the distance limits so UK drivers can fully utilise this technology, will, we believe, improve convenience and safety while aligning with standards in other countries.

Some car owners in the UK have paid extra for features that allow a car to be summoned remotely, but UNECE Regulation 79 restricts their use, limiting their range and effectiveness. We believe that this feature has been proven safe in other countries without these limits. We urge the UK Government to amend these restrictions, allowing drivers to use them fully as intended, which we believe is safe and will improve convenience and ensure fairness for those who have invested in this technology.

action: Stop MPs from Claiming Heating Allowance on Expenses.
background: Recently the Government stopped the Winter Fuel Allowance for pensioners who receive the full state pension or are not in receipt of pension credit. MPs earn significantly more annually. They can afford their own heating bills. Please make sure they pay their own bills.
additional_details: Since the Government allegedly inherited a £21 billion black hole, it doesn't seem fair to penalise pensioners and other members of the public without the Government being penalised too. After all it is the Government that mismanaged the nation's finances, not the general public. Politicians can contribute by paying their own heating bills.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA) is responsible for deciding on MPs' expenses and pay. IPSA is independent of both Parliament and Government.

You can find out more about IPSA here: http://www.theipsa.org.uk

You might wish to sign this petition on a similar matter: 

Review the system of expenses and allowances for MPs https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702821

action: Enable Northern Ireland residents  to have Labour representation at Westminster.
background: The local parliamentary MPs never form the UK government they are mere observers. If Labour wishes to implement its tax policies in Northern Ireland it cannot do so as Northern Ireland has no Labour representative MPs at Westminster. The principle of no taxation without representation applies here.
additional_details: The principle of "no taxation without representation" is foundational in democratic systems. In Northern Ireland, because no Labour MPs sit in Westminster, the policies Labour would advocate or enforce (such as tax rates or fiscal adjustments) wouldn't have direct representation for Northern Irish constituents. Many would argue that, absent a direct democratic voice, such policies shouldn't automatically apply to Northern Irish residents. The absence of Labour MPs (or Conservative MPs) from Northern Ireland in Westminster directly affects how policies like Inheritance Tax (IHT), income tax, and other fiscal policies apply—or fail to apply—to the people of Northern Ireland.
rejection_details: Decisions about whether to stand candidates in a particular constituency or part of the UK at an election are a matter for the indivdual political parties not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Third Child get universal credit as well because it’s unfair and injustice
background: Parliament should approve all children get same rights
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition calling for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703975

action: Create mobile phone picture alert scheme for missing children
background: We think if a child goes missing locally, everyone's phones should alert them with a picture of the child and contact details for the authorities in case the child is seen with an abductor.
additional_details: We believe it is a great tool for preventing children going missing and the technology to enable this is easily available.

action: Fund cannabis prescriptions for fibromyalgia and other pain conditions
background: I would like the government to fund the NHS to prescribe medical cannabis for people with fibromyalgia and other severe pain patients. Some people find that the prescription meds currently prescribed do not work.
additional_details: I think medical cannabis could give a better quality of life to those suffering from these sorts of debilitating conditions. I think that if the government prescribe medical cannabis, it could help people with chronic pain to get their lives back, enjoy family time and contribute positively to society.

action: Ban water company bonuses and dividend payments unless agreed KPI’s are met.
background:
Agree a set of environmental and business sustainability KPI’s.

Implement a total ban on water company executive bonuses where these KPIs are not met.

Implement a ban on shareholder dividend payments until these KPIs are delivered by executives and debt falls to viable and sustainable levels.
additional_details: Bonuses and dividends are being paid for failure. Failure to protect our environment which is essential to life, failure to deliver essential services which are value for money to the consumer and failure to invest adequately in future planning and infrastructure.
rejection_details:
The Government has recently introduced new legislation on water company bonuses. Ofwat, the water sector regulator, is now required to set rules to ensure water companies stop the payment of performance related pay to directors and chief executives where performance fails to meet specified standards. You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/water-special-measures-bill-policy-statement/water-special-measures-bill-policy-statement

If you'd like these provisions to change or be extended - for example to shareholder dividends - you could start a new petition setting out what changes you'd like. 

Information about Ofwat's regulation of dividends is available here: https://www.ofwat.gov.uk/households/your-water-company/returns-and-dividends/

action: Do not allow any private companies to be involved in delivering NHS care
background: We want the Government to protect the NHS. We believe giving profits to companies and shareholders is wasting valuable funds. The Government should put the NHS first.
additional_details: We believe the NHS is essential for the health of the nation. We think we need to fix what we have and bring it back to what it was.

action: Petition the Government to grant a Knighthood to Kevin Sinfield !
background: Due to Mr Sinfields devotion to raising awareness and Funds for Motor Neurone Disease it is high time he was rewarded with the highest award possible.
additional_details: Because if anyone does deserve a knighthood it is Mr Kevin Sinfield due to his tireless charity work and the love he has shown to his late friend and team mate Rob Burrow.
rejection_details:
The Government will only accept individual nominations, not petitions, so we can’t publish your petition.

To submit a nomination for an honour, visit: http://www.gov.uk/honours/

action: Encourage people to buy products manufactured in the UK.
background: Support British manufacturing.
additional_details: Help improve the economy
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you are concerned about people buying products manufactured in the UK, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do to encourage this.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Abolish Death Tax (IHT)We tax our citizens during a time of stress and loss
background: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Sweden, Norway and the list goes on all have no death tax. The USA has a 13million dollar threshold, before a penny of tax is paid. Why cant we make it that people want to stay here for there entire lives, instead of leaving so there hard work is not taken away.
additional_details:
I wish for the UK government to have a vote of the people on whether we should scrap Death Tax. I understand the need for taxation but this is double taxation and extremely stressful to our aging population.
The death tax is something that causes a great deal of stress and drives wealth out of this wonderful country.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Abolish inheritance tax
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703787

action: Make all households with income under £200,000 eligible for free childcare
background: Under current UK policy, families where each parent earns just under £100,000 totalling nearly £200,000 are eligible for 30 hours of free childcare. In contrast, a single-income family earning just over £100,000 does not qualify for this benefit.
additional_details: We believe the current rule unfairly excludes single-income families earning just over £100,000, while dual-income households earning £198,000 still qualify. We think that changing and allowing all households with income under £200,000 to be eligible for free childcare would encourage people to work harder without facing a financial penalty for exceeding the cap. It could also ensure they continue contributing more tax to the economy while receiving the same support as higher-earning dual-income families.

action: Taxes to pay for pet healthcare
background: Our pets are being neglected in their healthcare needs due to the ridiculous costs of vet treatment. I would like for our taxes to pay towards pet healthcase, as our taxes pay towards NHS treatment for humans.
additional_details: As this involves taxes and financials, it would be the government who would be responsible for working out the logistics.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700344

action: Regulate Psychotherapists and Counsellors.
background: It would a huge relief to me as well as anyone who has suffered maltreatment from a person without any training calling themselves a therapist if the government could work with the BACP (British Association for Counsellors and Psychotherapists) to regulate psychotherapists and Counsellors.
additional_details: Since the number of complaints against accredited counsellors has risen 24% since 2020 according to the BACP you can only imagine the amount of unheard complaints of abuse against ‘therapists’, who are not accredited nor trained. According to women who have spoken up to the guardian about their experiences being abused by people pretending to be trained therapists they feel “embarrassed, humiliated & under control of the therapists”.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Regulate all mental health Therapists: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/705247

action: Ask Bath & North East Somerset Council to provide Wheelchair Accessible Taxis
background: I am an adult wheelchair user. The list of wheelchair accessible taxis (WAV) on the council website is misleading. Only one operates in Bath and often tied up with school runs. This is an essential service to the disabled community. I've been left in the rain by regular taxis who refused to take me.
additional_details: I am currently applying for a WAV with Motabilty Foundation and in discussing my needs I have explained how frustrating it is to access a local WAV taxi. They have told me this is a nationwide problem. The Equality Act 2010 is meant to level up access to enable disabled people to be as independent as possible and have good quality of life as does the rest of the population.
rejection_details: You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Regulate the way that Gyms can increase the price in the middle of a contract.
background: The Government should establish consistent and fair rules for how gyms can apply a price rise mid contract. This should be similar to recent decisions for mobile phones, Pay TV & Broadband which banned inflation linked rises.
additional_details: We believe that this issue affects many in the UK and that with the uncertainty for the consumer and rising bills this has never been more important.

action: Equality Act 2010 - (Disability) NOT FIT FOR PURPOSE
background: The current Labour Government has recently announced that it wants those who are disabled to find employment and those on long term sick leave to return to work.
additional_details: I work for a large company, with many premises around the UK. In my location, there are over 200 employees, with over 100 that are employed to do the same job as me. My employer has a ‘Disability Aware’ award, yet, despite this, we are ALL expected to do the same. Reasonable adjustments, implemented in an empathetic way, with a view to the employees strengths, would certainly go a long way to levelling the uphill struggle many are experiencing daily, especially those in low paid manual jobs.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Stop child sex offenders from joining public court cases on child sex abuse
background: To stop convicted child sex abusers from going into the public gallery at court in another case of child sexual abuse and listening to all the evidence and descriptions of child sexual abuse/ assault.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about who can sit in the public gallery at court are a matter for HM Courts & Tribunals Service, not the UK Government or Parliament.

https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-courts-and-tribunals-service

action: Change requirement to get advice on transferring DB pension
background: We think you should only be required to get financial advice on transferring your defined benefit pension if the value of the scheme is more than £100,000. At the moment it is a requirement if the value is more than £30,000.
additional_details: Fees for advice can be thousands, and many find they are lucky if they can actually find an adviser. We think the Government is denying us freedom of choice regarding our pensions.

action: Enforce checks on people before allowing them to have animals.
background: Do background checks on people before they are allowed to have animals as pets. Stop animal abuse!
additional_details: Enforce background checks before people are allowed to buy animals. Too many animals are being abused and caused harm by their owners. This is unfair and inhumane. Animals should have more rights. It’s disgusting what they have to suffer from people who own them; people who they trust!! Why should they be treated differently to a child? They don’t get a say where they go or what happens them. More needs to be done to stop pain, hurt, harm and sadness!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stricter regulations on the breeding and sale/adoption of pets
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707248

action: Petition to stop sidiq Khan receiving a knighthood
background: Stop London mayor from getting a knighthood
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions that relate to honours and appointments, which includes calling for an honour to be removed or blocked.

action: Ban publishing information about people accused of crimes until proven guilty
background: I want the government to prevent the names and photos of people accused of crimes from being released until they are proven guilty. I do not think that newspapers should be allowed to put people’s jobs and safety at risk.
additional_details: People arrested for crimes may be innocent. I think their lives could be ruined if information is published about them. Their family and children could also be put in danger.

action: Abolish the Parliament Act 1911
background: We believe that this Act left the House of Lords unable to effectively challenge poorly thought-out legislation, allowing governments to force through unpopular laws. We think there is widespread discontent with government decisions and restoring a proper check on power is vital.
additional_details: Under the Act, the House of Lords cannot stop legislation, and we believe this leaves the government unchecked. We think the Government is losing public trust due to unpopular policies, and that this unchecked power undermines democracy. We believe that revoking the Act would restore a necessary balance, ensuring laws are scrutinised and not rushed through by a single-party majority. It's time Parliament prioritised the people's voices over political convenience and brought back real accountability to protect our future.

action: Do not allow people charged with rape to be released on bail
background: We think people accused of rape should not be released on bail. We think this will help keep the public safe.
additional_details: We think this needs to be sorted.

action: Decorate Christmas Tree in Trafalgar Square
background: I want the Parliament to decorate Trafalgar Square  Christmas Tree as that is the symbol of our cultural heritage and an integral part of the history and tradition
additional_details:
London is a cosmopolitan city and a tourist hub. People  travel from all over the world to visit the iconic monuments and relive the history of this city 
The present tree does not reflect and represent the true liveliness, diversity, harmony and beauty of our society. In it’s present display it depicts an adverse picture of our society to be a depressed and unhappy community
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

You may want to start a petition to the London Assembly, or write to the Mayor of London.

You can find more information about creating a petition to the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/who-we-are/what-london-assembly-does/petitions

action: CREATE A 4 DAY WORKING WEEK IN THE UK
background: I urge the UK Government to implement a four-day workweek with no loss of pay. This change boosts productivity, improves mental health, enhances work-life balance, reduces emissions, and supports economic growth. Countries like Iceland have proven its success, benefiting workers and businesses
additional_details: I urge the UK Government to implement a four-day workweek with no loss of pay. This change boosts productivity, improves mental health, enhances work-life balance, reduces emissions, and supports economic growth. Countries like Iceland have proven its success, benefiting workers and businesses alike. It's time for the UK to modernize its approach to work for a healthier, happier, and more sustainable society. Support this petition to make a positive change today.
rejection_details:
The government is not responsible for how many days people work. We could potentially accept a petition on something like 'Implement measures to support a 4-day work week' if you wanted to resubmit a new petition. We have accepted something like the below in the past:

https://petition.parliament.uk/archived/petitions/639885

action: Allow dependents to stay if someone switches to care visa
background: We want the Government to allow those on other visa routes to be able to switch to the Health and Care Visa and for their dependents to be able to stay, as there are many students on the graduate route who are experienced and work in the care sector but aren’t switching due to the dependent rule.
additional_details: I came here on a student visa and started a part time job in a care home. I completed my degree, and am now on the graduate route and still working in care. I have almost 2 years of experience and my employer is happy with my work. I love my job, but I can’t switch to a care visa as I have a dependent with me. There are many people in the same situation, and we want the Government to allow those who are already in the UK and have experience to be able to apply for a care visa and for their dependents to be able to stay.

action: Require Cyclists to adhere to the Road Traffic ACT & Highway Code
background:
Cyclists when using public roads should be subject to, and bound by the same Road Traffic Act and Highway Code that motorists are.    
ALL road users should be obliged to understand, recognise and adhere to traffic signals and signage and have Lighting and other forms of hi-visibility at night
additional_details: Government have for years promoted cycling and given cyclists greater priority on the roads, but have failed to address Cyclists lack of adherence to the Law or suitably considered the Duty of Care that is owed to their Health & Safety and that of other road users.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

The Highway Code already applies to cyclists.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Scrap the state pension and return some NI contributions
background: Scrap the state pension and return a proportion of NI contributions to people so they may use their money to enter into a private pension arrangement.
additional_details: We think if the Government are not able to sustain the pension system it should be scrapped or reformed allowing people the opportunity to make their own pension arrangements.

action: Hold UK Energy Companies Accountable for Fair Pricing
background: Stop energy companies profiteering while UK households face soaring bills. Reform the price cap, cap profit margins, tax excess profits, and enforce transparency. Use windfall taxes to aid vulnerable households and promote fair pricing. Protect consumers and ensure energy fairness now
additional_details: UK households are struggling with soaring energy bills, yet energy companies report £457 billion in profits, exploiting the energy price cap as a target rather than a limit. Vulnerable families are forced into fuel poverty while corporations prioritize shareholder gains. Reform the price cap, enforce transparency, and cap excessive profits. Windfall taxes on these profits should fund aid for low-income households and energy efficiency programs.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition: 
Introduce an annual Windfall Tax on the most profitable Energy Firms: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/704838

In addition, we can only accept petitions about matters which the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. Ofgem is the regulator for energy and sets the energy price cap. You can find out how to contact Ofgem here: https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/contact-us

You could also raise your concerns with your MP. You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

action: Immediate Action on Homeless Issues in Manchester
background: We urge the UK Government to act on the homelessness crisis in Manchester, where tents in St Peter’s Square tarnish the city’s global reputation. Despite a £100bn GDP, efforts fail to provide solutions. Demand transparency, investment in housing, and an end to this humanitarian failure.
additional_details: We urge the UK Government to address Manchester’s homelessness crisis, symbolized by tents in St Peter’s Square. Despite billions invested in the city’s growth and Manchester’s £100bn GDP, over 5,000 people remain homeless in the region. This failure harms tourism, damages the city’s reputation, and highlights systemic inequality. Images of these scenes are shared internationally, mocking the UK’s decline. We demand urgent investment in housing, mental health services, and long-term solutions.
rejection_details:
Tackling homelessness locally is the responsibility of the local council, Manchester City Council, not the UK Government or Parliament. We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: "Stop Black Market Driving Test Slots and Ensure Fair Access."
background:
Investigate and stop the black market sale of driving test slots.
Strengthen the DVSA booking system with anti-bot protections like CAPTCHA to prevent third-party agencies from monopolising slots.
Introduce penalties for reselling test slots and ensure fair access for genuine learners.
additional_details:
The black market sale of driving test slots has created a deeply unfair and inaccessible system for learner drivers in the UK. Despite their best efforts, many individuals are unable to book a test through the official DVSA website because third-party agencies exploit the system. These agencies use automated tools to grab available slots, which are then resold at inflated prices, often costing learners hundreds of pounds.

1. Unfair Disadvantage for Learners
2. Undermining Public Confidence
3. Negative Impact on Road Safety
4. Exacerbating Inequality
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Review process for booking driving tests and ban the resale at inflated prices: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702760

action: Recognise the Republic of Somaliland
background: To hold a debate in parliament to change the United Kingdom's international policy, on the recognition of the Republic of Somaliland
additional_details: The recognition of Somaliland by the United Kingdom is crucial for geopolitical and humanitarian reasons. Since declaring independence in 1991, Somaliland has maintained stability and democratic governance. Acknowledging its status would support its aspirations for self-determination and enhance regional stability in the Horn of Africa. Additionally, recognition could improve trade relations and aid initiatives, promoting development and reducing emigration pressures.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703233

action: Require employers to pay college students undertaking work placements
background: I think the Government should require employers to pay people who have to attend work placements for their college courses (education up to 18 is mandatory).
additional_details: I believe students should get paid for the hours they do. Especially considering it’s so difficult to get apprenticeships meaning people often can’t choose to learn and get paid.

action: Review medical care for those with temporomandibular disorders
background: People suffering can find they are passed from dentist to doctor without effective treatment, and that care guidelines aren't being followed. Many people battle for years to access the right care.
additional_details: We’d like for there to be a review to help ensure doctors have a more serious approach to this health condition. It can affect many people, including younger people and older people. People shouldn’t have to wait years to have results. People shouldn’t have to deteriorate due to waiting so long or not being heard. Doctors need to acknowledge the symptoms and send referrals, this doesn’t seem to always happen and it can be dismissed. We’d truly like this to be more recognised and for there to be more training. We believe England doesn’t know much about TMDs.

action: Review and seek changes to GPSR, and provide better support for small businesses
background: GPSR imposes stringent requirements many UK small businesses cannot afford, effectively barring them from trading in the EU. We urge the Government to review, provide financial support, streamline compliance and negotiate exemptions to help small businesses trade sustainably and safely in the EU.
additional_details: GPSR imposes stringent requirements that many UK small businesses cannot afford to meet, effectively barring them from trading in the EU. We believe that this not only threatens their survival but also undermines the UK economy by reducing exports and stifling growth. Small businesses are vital to innovation and employment; we consider that they need support to adapt to these regulations without incurring unsustainable costs. A review and tailored support can help ensure they remain competitive and thrive in international markets.

action: Introduce conveyancing laws similar to those in Scotland, across England & Wales
background: I urge the UK Government to introduce laws for the conveyancing process currently used in Scotland to be used across England and Wales. I believe this could speed up property sales and stimulate the economy while reducing the burden on conveyancers and the margin for errors.
additional_details:
I think this could also reduce stress, financial losses, and uncertainty. 
 
I want the Government to adopt Scotland's house buying and selling process in England and Wales as the current system can be archaic, slow, stressful, and often results in wasted time and financial losses due to the burden on conveyancers. 
 
Adapting the process could reduce uncertainty and make transactions quicker and more efficient. I think this change would minimize the risk of mishandling a large volume of cases, ensuring smoother property sales and boosting the economy through faster market turnover.

action: Require schools to teach pupils about physical & emotional abuse
background: I would like all children from an early age to be educated in schools about what is and what isn’t acceptable from their care givers. This would be a delicate area of education which would need to be addressed sensitively to not traumatise children.
additional_details:
I believe that if children had more knowledge about physical and emotional abuse and confidence in their schools, then they may be more likely to reach out before its too late. Story books could be introduced for the younger children and case studies for those who are older.
 
I believe that if children know how to seek help it might help take the pressure off social services.

action: Give children priority regarding preferred schools if their school gets closed
background: If a council decides to close a school, children needing to then look for a new school should be given priority so they can get their preferred new school.
additional_details: At the moment children who need to look for a new school because their school gets closed do not get priority when applying for a place at a new school. This is unfair! The children are going through enough trauma as it is so shouldn’t be made to suffer even more. Also, the parents will possibly encounter further problems if their child does not get into their preferred school (the new school given to them might be too far away or not easy to get to, for example).
rejection_details:
Decisions about school admission criteria and priority are a matter for local authorities and schools.

You can contact your local councillors who represent you to raise your concerns about this. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

You could also contact the Office of the Schools Adjudicator. You can find out more about their role here: https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/office-of-the-schools-adjudicator

action: Reverse the Ban on Puberty Blockers for Under-18s
background: The government needs to immediately reverse the ban on Puberty Blockers for Under-18s as it will have a detrimental effect on the trans youth community that already faces enough issues.
additional_details: The trans youth community already faces enough discrimination and issues each and every day. The government should be on their side, but instead, they are blocking an essential need many trans youth have. This has to stop.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Lift restrictions on prescribing puberty blockers to trans children: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702538

action: Stop spending taxpayers money on foreign countries without public consent.
background: Stop using our taxes to fund other countries problems before fixing our own issues first, our taxes must only be used in this country until everything is brought upto date
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action:

Stop all foreign aid
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700263

action: Create an independent Safeguarding Body.
background:
We urge the creation of an independent safeguarding body to:
 
Investigate institutional abuse objectively.
Review local authority decisions
Protect vulnerable adults effectively.
additional_details:
Without this body, we feel vulnerable adults have no higher authority to ensure safety.
 
We believe the system forces agencies to investigate themselves, creating conflicts of interest and leaving people unprotected. We think no effective independent body exists to oversee or intervene when local authorities fail to safeguard the vulnerable.

action: Introduce compulsory fee based licencing for deer stalking guides.
background: Any person who offers or provides services as a deer staking guide, or lets or sub-lets deer stalking in any commercial capacity, should be subject to paying for an annual renewable licence e.g. £2000 increasing based on number of clients. The funds raised to go to re-wilding projects.
additional_details: We think deer numbers in the UK are preventing reforestation and natural regeneration in many areas. One cause is deer stalking guides failing to reduce deer numbers as it is in their financial interests that paying guests have something to shoot. The government acknowledges the seriousness of the problem. The Scottish government for instance removed the close season for male deer. We think a fee to fund rewilding/deer fencing could offset the damage this causes and encourage more deer control.

action: Detain all migrants that enter the UK illegally
background: Detain all migrants that enter the UK illegally in detention centres. We think existing MOD bases could be used for this. Hotels are not to be used. Only process asylum applications for those arriving with documents and proof of no convictions.
additional_details: We think this would be a deterrent that does not reward migrants that have broken international border laws. We think undocumented migrants cost the tax payer too much.

action: Require online account deletion to be simple and clear
background: Creating online accounts is simple, but deleting them can be difficult. We would like the government to introduce a law requiring a clear, one-step “Delete Account” button, banning barriers, and ensuring users control their data.
additional_details:
We believe that some companies deliberately make it difficult to delete accounts by hiding the option in obscure menus or requiring unnecessary steps like contacting support or multiple email verifications.

We call for a law that mandates:
1. Easy navigation to account settings.
2. A clear, one-step “Delete Account” button.
3. A ban on unnecessary hurdles, ensuring user autonomy and data control.

We would like simpler, transparent account deletion for all.

action: Make political parties manifestos legally binding.
background:
An Independent panel should monitor that the new government follows through on its pre-election promises.  If after a period of time the panel decides that the promises are not being kept, then a warning should be issued
Following this if its still in breach then a new election must be called.
additional_details: It's too easy to make promises pre-election which when in power they don't follow up on, and at the moment there's no mechanism for holding them accountable other than waiting 5 years till the next election
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700035

action: Ban higher car insurance premiums for young and new drivers
background: We want the government to introduce regulations to require car insurance companies to reduce the cost of insurance for new drivers, particularly those under 25, by offering need-based pricing models.
additional_details:
We also want insurance companies to be required to offer a sliding scale of premiums that reward new drivers for maintaining a clean driving record over time.
 
We believe these reforms will lead to fairer, more affordable insurance rates, encourage safer driving practices, and make vehicle ownership accessible for all, regardless of age or experience.

action: Review powers of Child Maintenance Service regarding concealed income
background: We think there should be a review into how the Child Maintenance Service can tackle the issue of non-paying parents who are avoiding their responsibilities by working cash in hand.
additional_details: We think current CMS powers are insufficient to tackle this.

action: Public inquiry into the selling of Family Asset Protection Trusts.
background: We think some people are being mis-sold "Family Asset Protection Trusts". We think the Government needs to protect citizens, introduce harsher punishments for miss-selling, and support victims.
additional_details:
We think the Government is not doing enough at the moment, and that this could be the Next Big Miss-Selling Scandal.
 
We think vulnerable people - such as the elderly and the sick - may be being sold these without their effects being properly explained, and that they can leave people worse off.  We believe they are being promised protection from costs - such as care fees - but that what they are being sold may not actually protect them from these costs. We want to see the government hold a public inquiry on this.

action: Limit the public budget for memorials to former Monarchs.
background: The public funds for memorials to former Monarchs should be limited to £1-3 million and the rest allocated to what we think are far more benevolent and practical issues.
additional_details: We believe that the allocated budget is wasteful given the people who are facing high costs of living; having to use food banks; “heat or eat” choices; low wages and high rents; as well as the levels of child poverty and homelessness. We think that any additional requirements must be met by private donations and/or from the royal family themselves.

action: Make medication for mental health  free
background: Make all or most  mental medications available and free of charge to help people with disabilities and mental health issues
additional_details: Because the cost of living is a struggle for many and many people also need the support and can’t afford some because the medication is expensive
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund free regular prescriptions for mental health patients
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707406

action: Ban councils from offering 100% council tax reduction
background: We think everyone should be paying Council Tax. We all get some services from local councils but we don't all contribute to them.

action: Conduct a review into the long-term effect of section 28
background: We want the government commit to launching a full review into the impact of Section 28 on LGBTQ+ individuals. This could include its contribution to physical and mental health struggles, as well as the long-term harm caused to those raised under its enforcement.

action: Stricter Oversight and Safeguarding Measures for Home-Educated Children
background: The Government should introduce mandatory registration and welfare checks for home-educated children. Local authorities must assess their education and safety regularly. I believe these steps will help prevent abuse and neglect while supporting parents who choose to educate their children at home.
additional_details: Without mandatory registration and monitoring, I believe that vulnerable children can slip through the cracks, suffering abuse and neglect. I believe mandatory regular checks would ensure children’s safety, guarantee access to adequate education, and provide accountability for parents. I believe these measures could protect children and ensure they are not deprived of their right to education and safety. I think the government must act to prevent further tragedies.

action: Publish detailed data about offences committed by illegal migrants.
background: The majority of British people would like to see geographic, demographic and crime-type data on offences committed by illegal migrants. People are rightly concerned about the threat, harm and risk posed by illegal migrants entering the country, by whatever means. It is causing widespread unease.
additional_details: The new UK Labour Government has pledged to tackle the criminal gangs that are contributing to the huge influx in illegal migrants entering the country. These efforts are welcomed but the British people expect transparency from the government in reporting the effectiveness of this strategy. Measurement should not be limited to the number of criminal gang members arrested or vehicles and property seized, for example. It should include the crime data to evaluate the impact – the real outcomes.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Collect and Publish statistics on crimes committed by illegal immigrants
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709094

action: Help the homeless re-integrate into society, they have a right to basic survival
background: Provide urgent full-scale support, not pilot studies. Don't let them freeze to death on our streets this winter! Help them become self-reliant again! Canada provided $1B in their 2024 budget for the homless, Finland have been reducing their homeless since 2007. Follow their lead and commit similarly
additional_details: Provide low cost temporary housing and support so that the indigenous homeless(including children, 1.8M in the USA, how many here?) return to normal life and be able to find work and support themselves. Learn from  the success in Finland and commit fully to helping all that want help. There was a  ''Housing First feasibility study conducted in Liverpool in 2017.” with Crisis UK. Seven years ago and we still have a rising homeless problem and are not practicing what has been learnt.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.
We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.
You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, for instance which specific policy or boost to funding you would like to see

action: Protect our children - remove Migrant hotels from towns and cities!
background: Hundreds of asylum seekers are being boarded in hotels near schools and families. We don't know these people there background and yet they are protected but we aren't.
additional_details: Create asylum seekers centres away from schools families etc. Stop using the tax payers money to house potentially dangerous individuals.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

You mention towns and cities in the petition title, but then talk more generally about schools and families in the body of your petition.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Ban police from using lethal methods when dogs are out of control
background: We want the government to require police to use non-kill methods with out of control dogs. Stun not gun.
additional_details: We think that many dogs could have been brought under control without being killed and that this has caused a lot of distress.

action: The Home Office to urgently publish data on illegal migrant crime.
background: The British public demand clear, accurate, transparent and regular crime data from mass immigration and particularly illegal immigration. Publish this data publicly and also support our MPs when they directly request such from you. We want to see the true big picture and the details for ourselves.
additional_details:
We need to see the truth at a national and neighbourhood level regarding the enormous negative impact on our society and our people, particularly on women and girls, from the crimes committed by illegal migrants.
The Home Office refuse to provide this data, stating that the public doesn't want to see it nor have questions asked in Parliament regarding it. We need to challenge that incorrect assertion and we need to see the truth. You need to see the shocking truth.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Collect and Publish statistics on crimes committed by illegal immigrants
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709094

action: New rules on internal exclusions and independent body to be established
background: We think removing children from classrooms, sometimes called "internal exclusion", is misused. We think the Government needs to replace current advice with definitive rules. Introduce an independent body where complaints about internal exclusion, detention, and other exclusion are reviewed.
additional_details:
We think the excessive use of internal exclusion is having a detrimental effect on young people and limiting their education, frequently for the wrong reasons. Many children are fearful in school due to the sudden and volatile nature that detentions and internal exclusions are given. We think teachers are ill equipped or inexperienced so resort to bullish behaviours and the misuse of sanctions.
Schools need to be held to account.

action: Make it illegal for parents to smack children
background: We want the government to bring in legislation which prohibits the slapping, hitting and smacking of children.
additional_details: We feel that too many children are seriously injured both physically and mentally by parental abuse.

action: Make election manifestoes a legally-binding contract with the electorate.
background: Introduce an element of compulsion to ensure that manifestoes contain only clear and unambiguous promises which must be implemented exactly as stated and in full - with substantial financial penalties for failure to do so and possibly custodial sentences for deliberate non-fulfilment or dishonesty.
additional_details: We are heartily sick of manifestoes that contain promises which the party concerned either has no intention of keeping, or which include deliberately misleading statements about what is actually intended.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700035

action: Release the name of the judge who placed Sara Sharif with her abusive father
background: The judge and professionals who placed Sara Sharif with her killer are being protected from being named by order of the High Court. We want the government to release the name of the judge who made this decision to the public.
additional_details:
The failures of the family court played a large role in Sara's murder.

Protecting the name of the judge who made this decision puts more families at risk because no one knows if their children are at risk of serious negligence, having no debate and no review is not good enough.

Hundreds of thousands of children are at risk in the system, and not naming the judge at fault means they can continue to adjudicate on other cases where children are at risk of significant harm.
rejection_details:
The name of the judge was published following the recent Court of Appeal judgement on this issue. 

However, we could not have accepted a petition on this issue as these decisions are the responsibilty of the courts not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Publish data on illegal migrant crime
background: In recent years, we have seen an unprecedented explosion in illegal migration. The public has a right to understand the true implications of this migration and its impact on society and crime levels. Given the recent tensions, public transparency is now more critical than ever.
additional_details: The Home Office recently denied requests to publish the data, claiming the public doesn't want the information. A public petition would be a fair way to determine whether this is true.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Collect and Publish statistics on crimes committed by illegal immigrants
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709094

action: Fund measures to reduce traffic
background: We want the government to fund the creation of additional and larger roads as well as a more efficient system to open roads quickly after traffic collisions.
additional_details: In 2017, UK drivers wasted an average of 31 hours in rush-hour traffic. People rely on our roads to get to their work on time and earn the money to survive. We think we need better traffic systems.

action: Exempt all nurseries from Employer NI Contributions
background: We believe that if costs incurred from the planned increase to employer National Insurance Contributions and National Minimum wage are not mitigated, nurseries will have to increase fees parents pay, reduce staffing (and thereby the number of places offered), or close due to no longer being viable.
additional_details:
Private, voluntary and independent (PVI) providers will not be reimbursed for employer NICs & business rates whilst schools and public nurseries will. PVI nurseries receive some government funding, but they need to be sustainable.
 
The costs faced by PVI providers could mean that they will have no option but to increase parent fees.

action: Abolish Inheritance tax completely.
background: Abolish Inheritance tax on any item or estate that has already had tax of any kind deducted from it when passed on to beneficiaries.
additional_details: The items and estates passed down through inheritance are all taxed when over a certain value. The government taxes earnings, purchases from those earnings and then on the businesses. Everything is taxed, we should not be taxed on items already taxed in life. This causes estates to break up.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition: 

Abolish inheritance tax: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703787

action: Make the BBC go commercial and ban the controversial TV licence.
background: This licence I feel is out dated and not in the interest of the public having a licence forced upon us by law when generally TV is so commercialised. It's easy for them to go commercial. BBC break to show upcoming programs so in essence we are in fact watching adverts on BBC channels anyway.
additional_details: I have to pay for 2 licences. I pay my full licence in my property and contribute to a second licence owned by my Housing association on a TV that is in our common room should we need to watch TV in a function or personally when we visit the common room on site. Why? It's unfair and unjust that a housing association has to add charges of this sort just to watch a TV in a common room. It's impractical. So I'm looking for this licence to be barred  and decriminalised.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Abolish the tv licence
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701068

action: Don't allow absent parents to take children from primary care givers
background: Change the law so that absent parents can't take children away from their primary care givers.
additional_details: I believe the emotional damage done to children and parents in these cases can be long term. We believe no parent, father or mother, that is absent from the children's lives for a year or more should be allowed to use their parental responsibility to take the children away. We don't think this is beneficial to the child/children. We think allowing this to happen could potentially put a child/children at risk.

action: Stop the closure of Abbey House Museum.
background: Stop the closure of Abbey House Museum in Kirkstall.  And hopefully full fund it.
additional_details: Fund the museum. Through local or national funding
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about the museum are a matter for Leeds City Council, not the UK Government or Parliament.

You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Make it a legal requirement for all landlords to hold valid buildings insurance
background: Under current regulations, landlords who own properties outright are not obliged to hold buildings insurance. Require that all landlords who rent out properties, regardless of mortgage status, maintain valid buildings insurance as a legal condition of letting the property.
additional_details: We believe mandatory buildings insurance would ensure that necessary repairs are funded without placing tenants’ safety and financial security at risk. We think it would also protect local authorities and emergency services from shouldering undue burdens if uninsured damages lead to unsafe conditions. In our view, implementing this measure would improve tenant protection, property standards, and overall fairness in the rental market.

action: Change Delay compensation times on UK trains from 15 minutes to 10 minutes.
background: The Government should change the minimum time for delay repay to 10 minutes in train franchise contracts. We think this will force a change of operation from operators as it would eat into their share price.
additional_details:
We believe that we are exposed every day to a bad, overpriced, train service, and yet we have no say or option but to use these monopolies.

We consider that if you are clearly big on "green" then this needs to be sorted out as we think that this type of service just drives people insane and forces them to use a car rather than a train.

action: Hold a referendum on restoring the Death Penalty for murder
background:
We call on the Government to hold a referendum on restoring the death penalty for murderers.

We question why taxpayers should pay to keep convicted murderers in prison. We believe that justice betrayed is justice denied.
additional_details:
The death penalty was abolished in the 1960s.

The last free vote in Parliament was in the 1990s.

We believe it is time the people of our country had their say.

action: End the need for a fit note every 6 months for permanently disabled people.
background: End the need for a fit note every 6 months for permanently disabled people to reduce the time and cost on the NHS
additional_details: There are 16.1 million people in the UK Ringsted Disabled. Every 6 months they have to ask for a fit note from the NHS for there Universal Credit claim. Each case takes 1-5 minuets acuminating 1,333,330 Hrs of NHS Time. This would greatly cut back on wasted time and expense on the NHS.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

Fit notes are issued if a health condition or disability affects a persons capability to work for longer than 7 days. Fit notes are based on an assessment by a healthcare professional, who decide the length of a fit note based on their clinical judgement.

If a health condition or disability affects capability to work for longer than 28 days, a Work Capability Assessment can be carried out. 

You can find more information on Work Capability Assessments and Universal Credit at:

https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/benefits/universal-credit/if-youre-sick-or-disabled/going-to-your-universal-credit-medical-assessment/ 

https://www.gov.uk/health-conditions-disability-universal-credit

There is also a similar petition relating to PIP assessment which you may wish to sign: 

Stop DWP repeating PIP assessments for disabled people
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703827

action: Independent Review of HMRC: Accountability for Taxpayer Justice
background: The HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) plays a vital role in collecting taxes and ensuring compliance with the UK’s tax laws. However, many taxpayers have reported issues with HMRC’s processes, including unjustified demands for tax payments from years prior.
additional_details:
We, the undersigned, call on the UK Parliament to initiate an independent review of HMRC. This should focus on the following:
1. Transparency and Proof: Ensure that HMRC provides clear and sufficient evidence before issuing tax demands.
2. Fair Practices: Review cases of backdated tax claims to ensure they are lawful and substantiated.
3. Public Accountability: Identify any systemic issues within HMRC’s operations

action: Release the name of the judge and social workers in the Sara Sharif case.
background: I feel as though the judiciary and care-workers who failed to do their job in the case of Sara Sharif should not be allowed anonymity.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about what information to release in relation to individual family court cases are a matter for the courts, not the UK Government or Parliament.

The names of the judges involved in the previous proceedings have now been published.

action: Do not make any agreement with the EU on youth mobility
background: We do not the Government to make an agreement with the EU on youth mobility.
additional_details: We voted to leave the EU to regain control of our borders and we think to introduce a youth mobility scheme would be a reversal of what we voted for.

action: Stop schools refusing students access to toilets
background:
Stop schools taking away human rights

Access to sanitation and toilets is a human right in the UK

Schools
The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) states that children have the right to access clean, appropriately stocked toilets whenever they need to
additional_details:
Many schools - particularly secondary refuse students access to the toilet during lesson times. Going to the toilet is a human right and shouldn’t be refused.

Young females find this a particular challenge especially during menstrual cycles. Many schools including our own require you to go to the Drs and pay for a note from the gp to allow a child a ‘toilet pass’ - other schools even go to the length of locking toilets! Protect our kids and make it law in schools to use the toilet as needed.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703387

action: Hospital charges for Overseas visitors
background:
Ensure the Law is being used by Hospital Trusts to boost NHS funds.

Can the Government ensure that provision is made to recover these statutory charges within Hospital Trusts
additional_details:
The Statutory provisions which enable overseas visitors to be charged for NHS treatment are found in section 175 of the National Health Service Act 2006. Section 175 allows the Secretary of State for Health to make regulations for making and recovery of charges in relation to any person who is not ordinarily resident in the UK for NHS services provided to them.

The National Health Service (Charges to Overseas Visitors) Regulations 2020 place a legal obligation on the Trust to make and recover charges for NHS treatment provided by that relevant NHS body. The Trust
rejection_details:

action: Make suicide awareness mandatory for all secondary schools and sixth forms
background: We would like the Government to implement suicide awareness to make it a mandatory part of learning for all secondary schools as part of their timetabled, curricular learning. There could be group discussions and presentations about this as part of relationships, literary and humanities lessons.
additional_details: As someone working in education myself, in schools where I have worked and many others, learners only hear about these kinds of events from assembly or visitors. If we could bring this to the forefront and base lessons on this, we may be able to raise more awareness and save more lives in the long-term. If successful, we think there should be mandatory CPD training for teaching staff also, as to help them be more prepared when delivering lessons involving this topic.

action: Publish a detailed plan to tackle illegal migration and stop boat crossings
background: We want a clearer and more detailed plan from the Government to tackle illegal migration and stop the dangerous boat crossings. We want the Government to clearly set out what their strategy is. We think it's time for transparency and action. Sign this petition and hold them accountable!
additional_details: We believe they are not dealing with the issue effectively or telling us the public what can be done so we want the Government to set out what they plan to do.

action: Ban smartphones for under 14s.
background:
Bad smartphones in schools, ban children under 14 or 16 from owning smartphones. Protect children from dangerous content on the internet.
The Safer Phones Bill sets out to protect children when using the internet and digital devices.
additional_details:
A study by Channel 4 (Swiped) showed that smartphones are damaging to children's health and wellbeing, and affect children's education and ability to concentrate and learn.
The Smartphone Free Childhood (SFC) charity has also identified a number of issues with children owning smartphones.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/714201

action: Do not allow the taxpayers to fund a £46 million Queen Elizabeth statue.
background: I would like the Government to remove the current budget for a statue of Queen Elizabeth. The Windsor family can then pay for the statue themselves, and the £23-46 million should be spent investing in the NHS.
additional_details: The UK government has set out a provisional £23-46 million to spend on a statue of the late monarch. Considering that the Sovereign Grant already reaches nearly £100 million, and that the Windsors’ private estate collects tens of millions more from the taxpayer in the form of rented out space to the NHS and schools, I do not believe it right for us to fund more of their projects.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Limit the public budget for memorials to former Monarchs.

action: Bring back the death penalty for homicide of a child
background: I think the government need more serious punishments for those who commit homicide on children. I believe that those who take a child’s life should never get a second chance.
additional_details: To give justice to the innocent little souls taken by evil people.

action: Stop the labour party destroying the British countryside.
background: The labour party have extensive plans to build on green belt areas and completely disregard the views if the British people . They have already stated that wild life will not be allowed to get in the way of house building .
additional_details: This must be stopped.Apart from not having any infrastructure to support this huge increase in population, it will increase flooding and destroy unique habitats and decimate wildlife. It will also remove green spaces that are essential for well being and mental health.In addition, the net zero madness will see the remaining green spaces carpeted in solar panels. This  must be stopped. We cannot allow this wantondestruction of our green and pleasant land.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Ban all developments in high wildlife areas 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/705032

action: Remove labour in a vote of no confidence.
background: Labour are unfit to govern the uk.
additional_details: Labour lied about there plans and mislead votors
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

Call a General Election

action: Limit the number of terms an elected mayor can serve
background: With the increase in the number of elected mayors in England, we think we must ensure those elected do not become entrenched.
additional_details: We propose a limit of a maximum of two terms for each mayor. We think this will encourage democratic representation and prevent abuses of power.

action: Bring back hanging for child killers
background: Bring back hanging for child murderers ,as there is no place for them on this planet
additional_details: Please bring back hanging for child killers
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Bring back the death penalty for homicide of a child: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709710

action: Abuse/Violence to retail staff to be a standalone criminal offence.
background: To make violence or abuse against retail staff a standalone criminal offence. To reduce crime in the town/city centres and make a stand against criminals and give strong signals to the victims.
additional_details:
Looking at the stats on British Retail Consortium for 2022/23: survey shows a 50% increase in levels of retail violence and abuse, to 1300 incidents a day.

60% of respondents say police response is “poor” or “very poor”.

Putting retail abuse as a standalone criminal offence should in effect lower the amount of incidents per day with police having a better response.

Less employees will go off sick/stressed and fell safe on their working environment. Retail abuse can have a long term effect on people’s mental health.

Make the difference to make retail workers feel safe.
rejection_details:
In November 2024, the Policing Minister announced that the new specific offence of assaulting a shopworker would have a maximum prison sentence of six months. 

Perpetrators would also face an unlimited fine and a ban from the shop where they committed the offence.

action: Light Up Cemeteries During Christmas. Festive decorations can bring solace.
background: Christmas is a time for connection, and cemeteries should  reflect this spirit for those visiting loved ones. A well-lit and decorated cemetery shows respect for those who have passed and provides a space of dignity for families who come to grieve and find closure.
additional_details:
For many like me, Christmas intensifies the pain of losing a loved one. Therefore, decorated cemeteries provides a meaningful way to honour and include those we've lost in the celebrations, making the season a little easier for those in mourning.
Cemeteries can feel cold and desolate especially during winter. Adding lights and festive touches can transform them into peaceful and inviting spaces, symbolising the enduring light of love and memory.
rejection_details: I'm sorry to hear about your loss. Cemeteries are run either by local councils, churches or private companies so the government isn't directly responsible for them. You may wish to contact the cemetery manager about festive decorations if it is privately owned or your local council.

action: Reform the special educational needs system and properly fund it.
background: We wish the government to reform the special educational needs system and properly fund it  so that children and young people can have access to the specialistic help they urgently require.
additional_details: England’s SEN system is not delivering better outcomes for children and young people, it  is financially unsustainable and in urgent need of reform, according  to the National audit office. My grandson is on the autistic spectrum he has been let down by the system and has been unable to get the help he needs mainly because of a lack of funding and long waiting lists, families have to battle to get the help needed and are losing confidence in the system that is supposed to help them.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Increase funding for SEND in schools.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701409

action: Introduce Regulation of Private Parking Practices
background:
We call for legislation to regulate the practices of private parking firms, including:
- allowing pre-payment or payment at the time of departure
- offering free or discounted parking for Blue Badge holders
- exempting parking for medical emergencies from Penalty Charge Notices (PCNs).
additional_details: Private parking companies may impose strict time limits to pay, which I think is penalizing drivers for factors beyond their control, like malfunctioning machines or queues. Additionally, in my view, Blue Badge holders and those in medical emergencies face unfair fines. I believe that by regulating these practices, the Government could promote fairness, accessibility, and protect vulnerable individuals from potential exploitation, ensuring the system works in the public's best interest.

action: Provide funding for all schools to have a social worker
background: I think that all children deserve to have access to an independent person who they can share their worries and fears with as they need within their school days not having to wait to fit criteria set by others and disturbing their life creating differences between them and other children.
additional_details: I am a surviving school phobic and didn’t receive the right help. In 1981 whilst studying community and youth work and social work I went on an exchange to Berlin and found social workers in schools.

action: Release all migrant data.
background: I want all migrant data released to ensure transparency and accountability in immigration policies. The public deserves to know the full scope of migrant arrivals, impacts, and integration to make informed decisions and hold government actions to scrutiny.
additional_details: A migrant dashboard is crucial for transparency and effective policy making. It should track data in real time like other public services, allowing for government accountability on this key issue.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Collect and Publish statistics on crimes committed by illegal immigrants
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709094

action: Ban train companies from using vague terms to explain cancellations and delays.
background: Ban train companies from using terms such as “short notice change to the timetable” to explain cancellations and delays.
additional_details:
Train companies are increasingly using vague terminology such as “short notice change to the timetable” to explain cancellations and delays. This offers users no explanation of causes and is little consolation to those affected. It is, in fact, insulting to lack transparency.

Train operators should be made to give honest explanations in order to be held to account.

A cancellation is a ‘short notice change to a timetable’. Essentially, the reason they are currently providing is: Cancellation.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about this are a matter for train companies, not the UK Government or Parliament.

We could accept something calling for a review into rail operators' communications with customers, if that is what you would like.

action: Ban palm oil
background: I want the importation and use of palm oil to be banned. Palm oil production is one of the leading causes of deforestation.
additional_details:
Large areas of tropical rainforests are sometimes cleared to make way for oil palm plantations, which can contribute to habitat loss for endangered species like orangutans, tigers, and rhinos.

The palm oil industry has also sometimes been linked to human rights abuses, including poor working conditions, child labour, and land grabbing. Indigenous and local communities have lost their land to plantations without proper compensation.

	•	Ensure families can benefit from retirement savings as intended.
	•	Encourage long-term saving and financial security in retirement planning.
	•	Reduce the complexity and administrative burden of IHT.

IHT on pensions places an unfair burden on families. Abolishing it would protect hard-earned retirement savings and provide greater financial stability for future generations.

action: Make the state pension tax exempt

government_response_summary: Exempting the State Pension from income tax would be expensive and add complexity to the tax system.
government_response_body: The government has no current plans to make the State Pension tax exempt. When it comes to taxes, social security benefits are treated differently depending on why they are paid. Generally, benefits that replace income, like the State Pension, are taxable.  Exempting the State Pension from income tax would be expensive at a time when the Government has inherited a very challenging set of fiscal circumstances. Individuals earning above the higher rate threshold would benefit more than those with incomes below, and those earning below the Personal Allowance would not benefit at all.  The Government keeps all taxes under review as part of the policy making process. The Chancellor will announce any changes to the tax system at fiscal events in the usual way.
