The Governments figures show that between 2019-2022, 48,500 hectares in England had the usage changed to development.
 
We feel that once development begins, any historical items are then lost.
 
There were more than 53,000 archaeological finds and 1,300 Treasure cases in 2022, recorded with the Portable Antiquities Scheme at the British Museum.
 
We feel this shows to shear amount of historical items being found each year around the UK.
 
If this law was put in place, a non-profit organisation could be started to over see this, with any money gained being used to preserve the nations history.

action: Fund the RSV injection for people over 79, especially the vulnerable.
background: Provide funding to change the window of ages for those who are offered the vaccine, from between 75-79 , to include those over 79.
additional_details: We think that if this vaccine was available to every vulnerable person, it could help lessen, or indeed prevent them having to go to hospitals, thereby helping to lessen the burden on the NHS.

action: Review and reform child custody arrangements
background: Change the default child custody contact arrangements to be 50/50 shared contact and living. We feel that the current system leads to disputes and can leave children without access to one parent.
additional_details:
We would like the law changed to reflect the following:
Shared care/ live to be the default position
No primary carer
Emergency Court Hearings for cessation of contact
Stricter penalties for parents violating court orders and proven false allegations to result in contact ceasing 
Fund more contact centres

action: Make watching football on tv more affordable and let the UK watch 3pm games
background:
I want them to have blackout games on tv for all in the UK (3pm games for premier league) 
Amazon showed all games over the Boxing Day period and it was cheap and well done. Someone needs to have these rights (that aren’t Sky) and it should be affordable.
additional_details: I think it should be policed by parliament as the cost of watching sport should be capped and not monetised as Sky do. Make it a fee but an affordable one. The Amazon prime was a good example of how it can be done well and affordable.
rejection_details: Decisions about when to hold and broadcast football matches, and how much to charge for them, are a matter for the FA, the Premier League and the Football League, and broadcasters, not the Government or House of Commons.

action: Reopen the British embassy in Syria.
background: After closing the embassy in 2012 due to the conflict, we think the British Government should now reopen its embassy in Damascus. We think reopening the embassy and restoring diplomatic ties is crucial for fostering cooperation, ensuring British contribution to Syria’s reconstruction.
additional_details:
We think a British diplomatic presence would enable effective support for humanitarian efforts, promote stability, and strengthen the UK’s role in Middle East peacebuilding.
 
For Syrians, we think the reopening of the embassy would signal international recognition and support for rebuilding the country, creating opportunities for economic and educational exchanges, and facilitating visa processes for those seeking to travel or study in the UK.

action: Revoke the BBC's royal charter & right to charge a licence fee
background: Revoke the BBC's Charter and right to charge a licence fee.
additional_details: We think the BBC is no longer impartial as our national broadcaster should be.

action: Stop creating too many medical specialities. Combined many specialities as one.
background: Combined Cardiology and Pulmonology as one speciality. Combined Neurology, Psychiatry and PM&R as one speciality. Combined OB-GYN, Urology, Andrology, and Nephrology as one speciality. Combined Intensive care medicine and Emergency medicine as one speciality. Etc, etc.
additional_details: Gastroenterology should treat the whole gastrointestinal tract esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum and anus as well as the pancreas, liver, bile ducts and gallbladder, as one speciality. Combined ENT and Ophthalmology as one speciality, but only as clinical speciality not surgical, basically same speciality but separate, into clinical and surgical. Etc etc.
rejection_details: We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

action: Introduce a pink and blue sticker emblazoned with beautiful silver angel wings
background: For the purpose of sticking in the windows of our homes, our cars, our vans, and residencies, which can be purchased at government buildings throughout our constituencies at a minimal cost to cover the forming of a signature and address database signed by purchaser at these designated locations
additional_details: when signed by the sticker purchaser, an agreement is struck that upon their signature at no period of their knowing within their being present at their disclosed address, their vehicle, or therefore whilst alive will any child ever be subjected to any of the crimes which are currently related to and accepted to be crimes committed by pedophiles, and child Murderers and if such action be proven against them they are willing to accept an empty cell in prison and pray for and welcome their death
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Organising social campaigns is a matter for indivdual campaign groups.

action: Remove all electronic devices from paedophiles and child murderers' prison cells
background: Remove electronic games, Televisions and other entertainment technology. We think electronic devices should be removed they are in prison for the most heinous acts and deserve no such luxuries.
additional_details: I feel that the heinous crimes committed do not warrant recreational enjoyment. We believe that such prisoners should not have game consoles, televisions, music systems and other technological devices when many people outside prison don't have access to such things.

action: Change regulations for large monetary donations to uk political parties
background:
Disallow donations to any uk political party from any person or organisation which does not have close, strong and current uk citizenship/business origins.
Limit total annual donation amounts to any uk political party to a reasonable amount to be agreed by all parties.
additional_details: It is unacceptable that any uk political party should have massively inflated donations which could lead to an imbalance in political influence and functioning. Additionally, for this to originate from foreign sources could greatly affect uk stability, democracy, wealth and security in the world.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Tighten the rules on political donations: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707189

action: End Council Tax
background: Council tax has become a burdensome financial drain on householders. The basic responsibilities of councils such as refuse collection, libraries & education, have been cut back by councils to a large degree, whilst expensive employees, together with their pensions have become obvious beneficiaries.
additional_details: 25% of Council Tax that we pay is used to finance the pension pot of council employees, a luxury that most of us in the real World could never afford. It is time for a fairer system of paying for day to day services instead of paying for ever growing bloated councils, many of which cannot manage properly the vast amounts of money they obtain from Council Tax.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: 

Abolish council Tax

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707913

action: Transfer all child sex offenders and child murderers overseas
background: The Government should seek an agreement to transfer all prisoners serving sentences for child sexual abuse or murder of a child to serve their sentence overseas.
additional_details: I believe this would help reduce overcrowding, staff shortages and funding cuts. I believe it would be a remedy that should kill two with one stone as it would empty prison cells and should be of substantial financial benefit considering our prisons are currently operating at a cost of above fifty thousand United Kingdom pounds per prisoner per year.

action: Review the tax system
background: We think the tax system should be reviewed to reduce the percentage of tax on goods such as food, petrol/diesel, energy etc.
additional_details:
We think the review should also consider reducing the income tax rates and changing the rules to mean you do not have to pay tax once you are retired.

We think the government seems to have far too much of the British tax payers money. We think that if the government can afford to spend billions of pounds in foreign aid to foreign countries, and house, feed and clothe illegal immigrants, we are paying too much tax.

action: Provide an exact number of prisoners who have murdered children aged under 16
background: I want the figures to be published on a twice-a-year basis. The announcement should be presented in layman's terms and categorised as to whether sexual or non-sexual.
additional_details:
A format similar to the one below.
Total prisoners in English & Welsh prisons who have murdered a child with no sexual conduct or motivation. = 666
Total prisoners in English & Welsh prisons who have murdered a child with sexual conduct or motivation. = 666
 
I believe that releasing this simple data will provide the population with a transparent benchmark to the scale of these heinous crimes. Then I believe we can offer our ideas on how best to prevent such despicable actions and how to move forward with those already incarcerated.

action: Require electoral candidates to declare interests in their nomination papers
background: Require candidates to declare their current and past interests in their nomination papers. We think this change could enable voters to make more informed decisions and could better integrate the Nolan principles into our electoral process. We believe this could help enhance electoral transparency.
additional_details:
The declaration should include, but not be limited to:
 
Financial interests (investments, directorships, significant shareholdings)
 
Political affiliations and donations
 
Memberships of organisations or lobbying groups
 
Family connections to relevant industries or political entities
 
Professional qualifications
 
Disqualifications and criminal convictions
 
A standardised updateable format for declaring interests should be implemented to help ensure consistency and ease of comparison for voters.

action: Ensure the May 2025 local elections go ahead
background:
We the Public demand that the May 2025 local elections go ahead.
It is not acceptable for the current Labour Government to cancel these elections- the Public must be allowed to vote.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not postpone the local elections
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710155

action: Require AUTOMATIC by election if an MP changes party during a term of office
background: A petition to recall an MP is opened in three situations and a by-election forced so long as 10% of the electorate sign such a petition. However, if an MP changes party during a term of office there is nothing the constituents can do. We think there should be an automatic by election.
additional_details: The reason is that since the electorate voted that MP in as a representative of that party, if they stood for one.

action: Amend the British Museum Act 1963 to allow for the return of artefacts
background: Museums are facing calls to return artefacts to their places of origin. The British Museum Act holds that the Trustees of the British Museum shall not dispose of objects vested in them except in very limited circumstances.
additional_details: Some nations have called for the return of artefacts. We believe that other nations can preserve artefacts that are currently in British museums.

action: Hold an automatic general election on resignation of any Prime Minister.
background: When in opposition Labour demanded a general election following the resignations of PM, Theresa May, Boris Johnson and Liz Truss. We think it is only right now that they are in government they should legislate for this.

action: Introduce stricter penalties and enforcement for shoplifting.
background: We believe this country is going through a shoplifting crisis and appears in our view to be almost decriminalised. All cases need investigation by the police (no matter the value of the items). First offences should attract substantial community service and mandatory custodial sentences after that.
additional_details: The government, police and judiciary all need to work together to overcome this problem because we believe that it hits shop staff morale, that it grows a sense of lawlessness and that, ultimately, it costs the consumer.

action: Review how police deal with dogs, including using tranquiliser guns.
background: We think the government should review whether the police should use tranquiliser guns instead of real guns when dealing with dogs they think are a danger. We believe that the police need to be better trained in dog behaviour and learn to take time to assess a situation before acting on it.
additional_details: We think there have been xl bully's or other dogs shot and killed in front of there family's because of the lack of understanding of there behaviour and temperament instead of looking into a situation before acting. We think the repercussions of this mean an innocent dog may be shot and killed for being a loving kind big softie, that has a family that will forever will have there heart broken because of a gun instead of a tranquiliser. We think this review would give time to look into what could save a innocent life so please please save our dogs.

action: Sadiq khan should not be given a knighthood
background: We want parliament to petition the government to stop this knighthood.
additional_details: Sadiq Khan is a polarising figure and does not deserve this Knighthood. The taxpaying workers of Britain should9 get a vote on who should receive awards such as this.
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions that relate to honours and appointments, which includes calling for an honour to be removed or blocked.

action: Implement Proportional Property-Based Fines for Illegal Fox Hunting.
background: People convicted of offences under the Hunting Act 2004, including illegal fox hunting, should be liable for fines based on the market value of their main residence, even if they do not own it, as well as all properties they own or transferred to family members in the last 5 years.
additional_details:
Fines should escalate for repeat offenders and fund rural policing. 
We believe that illegal fox hunting continues despite legal restrictions, and that the current penalties are not sufficient to deter wealthy offenders. We think that tying fines to property value, including rental homes and transferred assets, would ensure accountability; create a stronger deterrent; fund wildlife protection, and ensure that those responsible are held financially liable in proportion to their wealth.

action: Make all cyclists, e bike and e scooter riders do a basic road test.
background: Cyclists and e bike riders are a danger to all other road uses snd should be required to do a road test and be responsible for any accident they cause and they should be insured.
additional_details: The government should make cyclists and e bike riders do a road test and ensure they are responsible for their vehicles. They should also be banned from operating them in pedestrian areas. They should suffer from similar liabilities as car drivers if they cause an accident.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701762

action: Stop the Labour Party stopping the local elections
background: I’d like the government removed for trying to stop the local elections, what part of Democracy don’t they understand !
additional_details: The government have no respect for its British ppl
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not postpone the local elections
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710155

action: Change the DVLA requirements for motor caravan conversions.
background: Change the DVLA requirements for motor caravan conversions. We think the current requirements are too stringent, meaning campervans that we think are suitable are rejected. We think the DVLA should remove the requirements for two windows on one side and a detachable table.
additional_details: In addition, we think the DVLA should be clear about what is meant by "a combination" of external features. We think the requirements limit design options such as one window on either opposite sides, or an alternative to a fixed table such as a completely free standing table or eating on your lap. We think that campervans with cooking, storage and beds are clearly not LGVs but feel the features required by the DVLA rule too many out.

action: Allow people to get a low taper fade for free at any barber in the uk
background: I want my haircut to be free
additional_details: Because people can’t afford it

action: Make vandalism and theft of vans a specific offence
background: We want stronger punishment for the vandalism and theft of vans. We'd also like to introduce victim compensation for van theft. We feel that it can affect hundreds of thousands of livelihoods and that vans are the backbone of small to medium businesses.
additional_details: We believe that this is a situation that is so common which is damaging to workers morale and mental health. We feel this issue is left with the victim to pick up the pieces, through business expense and increased insurance premiums.

action: Stop a Waste Transfer Station being built in the Centre of Bacup.
background: Prevent the construction of a waste transfer station inside the town of Bacup, East Lancashire.
additional_details:
The proposed Waste Transfer Station is to be built in close proximity to residential areas, supermarkets and local businesses.  

The impact upon the town's infrastructure will be devastating. 

It will create noise pollution, unpleasant odours, additional traffic from large vehicles and litter.

The station is to be built very close to two large supermarkets and the river irwell.  There is a risk of cross transmission from rats, vermin and other pathogens.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/ 

Alternatively, you could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Hold a referendum on the proposed ban on new ICE cars in 2030
background: I request a referendum regarding the proposed ban on the sale of new Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) cars by 2030. I think this referendum is crucial to ensure public opinion is considered in this significant transition, balancing environmental goals with economic and social impacts.
additional_details: I think key points to be considered include the economic impact, environmental benefits, infrastructure readiness, consumer choice, and technological advancements. I think a referendum with an open debate will help make an informed decision that balances environmental goals with economic and social considerations.

action: An Annual Day of Remembrance for children killed in wars, conflicts and violence
background: We think the Government should create an annual day of remembrance specifically for children killed in wars, conflicts, and acts of violence in the hope it might help todays young people find solutions to problems other than killing each other when they become adults.
additional_details: Schools across the country would be invited to hold two minutes silence on this day to remember all children who have died as an act of violence in the UK and across the world. Eventually schools across the world would be invited to do the same on this day.

action: All policies suggested for by unelected organisations to be put to referendum.
background: Putting to a referendum any policies impacting British citizens, suggested by unelected organisations, such as the UN,WEF or WHO
additional_details:
The UK GOVERNMENT is beholden to the citizens of the UK, NOT the W.H.O. , W.E.F of U.N., nor any other government or N.G.O. 
We vermently oppose ALL efforts by foreign entities, whether the UN, WEF or WHO or any other corporate organisations to impose policies on the national sovereignty of the UK.
rejection_details:
Furthermore, any policies suggested by external organisations are not the responsibility of the UK Government or Parliament. 

You could submit a petition based on a specific policy which you object to.

action: Change Art Galleries & Museums Opening Times to suit working people 12-8pm daily
background: I am hoping of changing public art gallery and museum opening times to suit working peoples schedules and thus raise more money for the exchequer: from higher wages and lower crime rates which come from a higher educated population.
additional_details:
Inquisitive working people will visit when convenient for them and their busy schedules.

Currently Art Gallery and Museum opening times are around 10am-4.30pm on average across the kingdom. Public galleries and museums were set up in the age of ennoblement - the mid 19th century.

I think we can increase education levels and tax receipts from the benefits that a higher educated population brings with it from Art Gallery and Museum opening hours that would suit the unennobled such as 12pm-8pm

action: Repeal the Hunting Act 2004
background: We believe that the Hunting Act 2004 constitutes an unjustifiable interference with the public's right to enjoy a private life. We further consider that the Act attempts to encroach centuries of traditions of hunting wild animals. We ask that the Act be repealed.
additional_details: The Act was passed under the Parliament Acts and we feel there was not strong support for stringent restrictions of hunting. We think most of the Act is any way legally ineffective and its prohibition of hunting is easily circumvented. We think the Act does not contain sufficient exemptions and extends to people's private land which undermines centuries of precedent.

action: The Labour government needs too STOP ilegal migrants coming into the UK.
background: Take action and stop it.
additional_details: I believe that our country values and believes are being diminished. Either Sir Keir Starmer STOPS it or steps down and resign.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: 

Publish a detailed plan to tackle illegal migration and stop boat crossings:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709678

action: Abolish Motorcycle license A2 to A test requirement
background: In the past (prior to 2013), an A2 license holder would be restricted to two years before achieving a full A category unrestricted motorcycle license without an additional test. We propose it returns to that scheme.
additional_details: We propose reinstating automatic upgrades from A2 to A motorcycle licenses after two years, as was the case pre-2013. This change reduces test centre backlogs, supports green transport by promoting motorcycle use, and eliminates redundant retesting that doesn’t improve safety. Riders gain sufficient experience in two years to handle larger bikes. It also highlights the benefits of post-EU regulatory flexibility, streamlining licensing while supporting environmental and public sector goals.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/706650

action: Introduce a legal minimum age for access to internet social media web sites.
background: Introduce a law which makes it illegal for young people under the age of 16 years to have unsupervised access to internet social media (or other harmful websites) using a smart phone or other smart device.
additional_details: There is increasing evidence confirming that young people under the age of 16 are being exposed to harmful content on social media sites and are spending many hours of unsupervised access. The so called age restrictions on using these web sites do not seem to be working at all. There is also increasing evidence of significant negative impact on the well-being of young people who spend a lot of time on social media sites, impacting their behaviour, sleep patterns and education.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700086

action: Change the ‘whole month’ approach to change of circumstances in Universal Credit
background: If a change in circumstance occurs at any point in the Universal Credit assessment period it counts for the whole month - which we think is unfair.
additional_details:
It can mean people receive less than they had expected and budgeted for. We think any changes in entitlement should be pro-rata.
 
For example if a child stops being a child 3 days before assessment period ends, the claimant is told they owe money for the whole month due to this change - not just the 3 days the child had stopped being a child. 
We feel the Government may push people in debt with this policy.
We think it would be better if the Government calculated entitlement to the day.

action: Mandate that all dentists provide minimum amount of NHS services
background: Millions lack NHS dental care. We demand a 50% NHS allocation mandate for all dentist practices, requirements to ensure all NHS treatment that is needed for a particular patient is carried out, and a rule requiring practices to accept new NHS patients in their area.
additional_details: We don't think dental care should be dependent on income. An estimated 13 million lack NHS dental care, with many unable to access treatment at all. Those who do can face inadequate care and struggle to get all the treatments they may need. Some practices only treat private patients, leaving locals excluded. A 50% mandate, requirements to ensure full and NHS treatment is carried out, and ensuring local NHS access could reduce inequality, tackle the dental crisis, and protect public health.

action: Increase funding for IVF & fertility treatments to increase access.
background: We believe that we are in a fertility crisis. We worry that many people may be being denied access to medical treatment for infertility due to inconsistent restrictions and criteria that we believe are unfair. We feel this level of inequality and inequity needs to be urgently addressed.
additional_details:
In 2021, 55k people had IVF or DI treatment. Despite NICE guidelines advising ICBs to offer 3 rounds of IVF per patient, subject to certain criteria, currently access to fertility treatment is dependent on factors including postcode, sexuality, age, parental status, miscarriage, BMI & Anti-mullerian hormone level.
 
In 2014 40% of IVF treatments were NHS-funded, but by 2022, this dropped to just 24%, despite growing demand for timely diagnoses and mental health support and decreasing total fertility rate.

action: To deport convicted dual national terrorists to their other country of origin.
background: I would like there to be a debate in Parliament about the feasibility of deporting convicted terrorists to their other country of residence if they have dual citizenship. On deportation to another country I would like their UK passport to be confiscated and their UK citizenship cancelled.
additional_details: Because there are currently tens of thousands of convixted terrorists residing in the UK who are on a goverment terrorist watch list. Unfortunately we do not have the resources to monitir all of these potential terrorists. Therefore if the UK government could deport convicted terrorists with dual citizenship to their second country that would make the UK safer as it would allow the Security Services to monitor the potential terrorist threat to the UK more effectively.
rejection_details:
You can find more information in this House of Commons Library briefing: 

Deprivation of British citizenship and withdrawal of passports
https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/sn06820/

action: Photograph all claimants for DWP Benefits
background: I think many unregistered people are claiming benefits. I think that people are claiming the same benefit several times using different names. Photographs should be taken of claimants and cross checked for previous claims.
additional_details: I think fraud is a major problem within the UK benefits system. In the 2023–2024 financial year, the UK government lost an estimated £7.4 billion due to fraud and error in the benefit system.

action: Reduce the interest on student loans and put a cap on the interest.
background: Place a cap on the interest that student loans companies can place on student loans. This should be applied to new and old student loans.
additional_details:
The interest on some student loans is extortionate which means that those who require loans are amassing huge depts. People will be charged for long periods of their lives, often paying back far more than they ever borrowed. 
Higher education should be accessible to all without the worry of being charge extortionate amounts for the rest of their lives.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. There is also already a cap in place on the interest rate on student loans. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: More investment in tidal energy generation
background: We think the government should reassess their priorities, away from sources of energy currently being promoted, (Wind and Solar), which we consider to be unreliable and ineffective, and increase investment in tidal energy generation, which we think is more reliable and efficient.
additional_details:
The UK has one of the longest coastlines in Europe, and the UK experiences one of the largest tidal variations, with up to a 15m variation in the Bristol Channel.
We consider that tides are more regular, reliable and consistent than wind or sun exposure. France have been benefitting from tidal power since 1966 and have a 240 Megawatt installation in Brittany that operates very well. Focusing on a small number of large tidal installations could make integration with the power grid simpler and we think could help save hundreds of miles of additional pylons.

action: Change the amount of redundancy from 20 years maximum to full employment term.
background: I would like parliament and the government to change the rules regarding redundancy pay entitlement to account for the full years of employment, and not a maximum of 20 years.
additional_details: I believe employers should be made by law to pay for every year of service. This could encourage the employer to look at other options to redundancy if the cost of doing it is increased.

action: Renew Holiday Activity Fund for pupil premium free school meals children.
background: Ask the government to renew the holiday activity fund to support children during school holidays and ensure they have safe childcare and a hot meal each day.
additional_details: The government has not announced what it is doing with the HAF, and with the fund due to end in January 2025, children are in danger of not being able to access childcare and a hot meal during the school holiday from Easter 2025. Providers and parents need time to plan and ensure this is delivered.
rejection_details:
Earlier this month, the Government announced that funding for this programme will continue for 2025-26. 

You can read more about this here: https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2025-02-11/debates/070f726f-9cab-4773-87ef-226722f15272/ChildrenSWellbeingAndSchoolsBill(ThirteenthSitting)#contribution-4115EBAB-C481-434E-9310-D24ABCF0239C

action: Ban fireworks to save the suffering and lives of our animals
background: Ban fireworks to save the suffering and lives of our animals
additional_details: I'm absolutely heartbroken to read a Facebook post this morning about a dog that is nearly 2 years old  that has lost his life due to fireworks, sadly the shock of the sound of the fireworks has made this dog very scared and he has had a seizure and has been paralysed from this. Sadly this morning the family has had to have him put to sleep.  I'm now hearing other animals have been affected too and I'm sure there are many more. These animals do not have a voice and we are there voices. This post has really touched my heart, its not only the poor animals that have suffered but the families too. This has left me so upset and heartbroken and I feel like I need to start this petition for every animal suffering and there families.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Ban fireworks

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700199

action: Halt plans to demolish Oastler shopping centre and kirkgate market in Bradford
background:
We want the government and parliament to take immediate action to halt the planned demolition of Oastler shopping centre and Kirkgate Market in Bradford. These sites hold significant historical cultural and economic value for our community. 
Encourage public consultations and involve the locals.
additional_details:
We believe that the government and parliament have a responsibility to protect and preserve the cultural historical and economic assets of our communities. Oastler 
Shopping centre and Kirkgate Market are more than just buildings. They are integral parts of Bradford’s identity and heritage. Here’s why we urge the government and parliament. We urge the government and parliament to recognize the importance of these sites and take steps to ensure their preservation for future generations.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.
 
You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.
 
You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP
 
And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Review the affordability of care homes
background: We want the government to investigate the affordability of care homes.
additional_details: I do not see how some care homes can justify charges of £5000 to £7000 per month. I think that most of the people in these homes who have to self fund have worked really hard to buy their own homes, only to have to sell them to pay for care costs. Their money can be gone in a matter of years. I feel that this is unfair to them.

action: Make income threshold for student loan repayments £60,000 and charge no interest
background: We propose the following change: Base repayments above £60,000 income are solely on the capital loan balance, charging no interest, allowing faster debt repayment and saving people that graduated after 1998 thousands.
additional_details: In 1998, the government introduced interest on student loans repayments. Before this, student loans were interest-free in real terms. For a graduate in 2022, the average student debt is £44,940, with interest accruing from the moment the loan is issued. Currently, most graduates are on Plan 2, where repayments begin once they earn above £27,295 per year. Above this threshold, a fixed percentage of income is deducted to repay the loan. However, there is no cap on the interest.

action: stop the UK government from using taxpayers' money
background: The United Kingdom is reportedly in debt by £22 billion, yet the government continues to allocate taxpayers' money to other countries.
additional_details:
This practice needs to stop. UK funds should prioritize addressing domestic needs, especially during times of financial strain. While international aid has its place, we must ensure that the nation's own challenges are resolved first. The UK is not a charity, and its resources should reflect the priorities of its citizens.
Perhaps the government should start a dedicated charity and ask for voluntary donations, rather than giving away money that doesn't belong to them.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions:

Only provide foreign aid for national disasters and emergencies: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/705222

action: Provide funding to preserve and protect cemeteries around the UK.
background: We feel that much more funding for cemeteries is needed to care, maintain, protect and preserve them now and in the years ahead.
additional_details:
We think this is important as babies, children, adults and those in the Armed Forces are resting in cemeteries, their forever home. We feel that these places are where we honour, remember and pay our respects to those we love and cherish with all our hearts. We feel that we all live on through our precious loved one's who have gone before us and the legacies left behind by millions of these people.

government_response_summary: Local authority cemeteries are managed by councils, who set budgets and make service decisions locally. Privately owned cemeteries operate independently and are maintained by their respective owners.
government_response_body: The government does not have day-to-day operational responsibility for burial grounds. However, we recognise the importance of cemeteries as places of remembrance, heritage, and community significance. Their preservation and upkeep matter deeply to families and communities across the UK.  Responsibility for the maintenance and funding of cemeteries depends on their ownership. Local authority cemeteries are managed by individual councils, who are responsible for setting their own budgets and making decisions about local services in line with community priorities. The majority of funding in the Local Government Finance Settlement is unringfenced recognising that local leaders are best placed to identify local priorities.   Privately owned cemeteries, including those operated by religious organisations, charities, or private businesses, are independently managed and do not receive government funding. Their maintenance and preservation are the responsibility of their owners.  The government has issued Guidance for Burial Gound Managers (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5a7e0743ed915d74e6223a35/burial-ground-managers.pdf) which aims to support good practice across the sector. It is designed to ensure that cemetery managers are familiar with the legal framework in which they operate and to encourage consistent standards of care.  The guidance sets out expectations around maintenance, including:  •	A general duty to keep burial grounds in good order and repair, including paths, boundaries, and communal areas. •	The need for sensitive and proportionate ground maintenance, balancing practical upkeep with respect for the bereaved and the cultural or environmental character of the site. •	Responsibilities for the maintenance of graves and memorials, including safety inspections and appropriate action where memorials pose a risk. •	Considerations around environmental and heritage preservation, such as biodiversity, landscape management, and the protection of historically significant features.  The guidance applies to all burial ground managers, regardless of ownership type, and aims to promote high standards across the sector.   The government is also considering longer-term reforms to burial law through the Law Commission’s “Burial, Cremation and New Funerary Methods” project. As part of this, the Commission is considering introducing a general duty for burial ground operators to maintain sites in good order, potentially supported by a statutory code of practice and periodic management plans to encourage consistent standards and enable enforcement where necessary.   The Law Commission anticipates publishing its report on the burial and cremation part of this project at the end of 2025 and the government looks forward to considering this.   Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs

action: Launch a Public Inquiry into Grooming Gangs
background: A taskforce has helped arrest hundreds of offenders since 2023. We believe abuse is large scale and ongoing. Yet we think the authorities refuse to acknowledge the background and motivation of abusers, the failures of police, social workers and local councillors, and potential cover-ups.
additional_details:
In August 2014, a ground breaking report by former senior social worker Alexis Jay revealed that an estimated 1,400 children had been sexually exploited in Rotherham from 1997 to 2013, and the majority of known perpetrators were of Pakistani heritage. It revealed the failures of leadership and staff fears of being considered racist in identifying the ethnic origins of perpetrators.

government_response_summary: Alexis Jay went on to conduct a 7-year national inquiry on child sexual abuse. Our priority now is to act on her findings and deliver justice for grooming victims, not order another national inquiry.
government_response_body: The Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse undertaken by former senior social worker Alexis Jay was a full national inquiry taking 7 years, which engaged over 7,000 victims and survivors, and had 15 separate strands, including a specific two-year inquiry into child sexual abuse by organised networks (or grooming gangs).   The Government is determined to act on its findings, working to protect more children from the horrors of grooming gangs and other forms of sexual abuse and exploitation, and to deliver justice for the victims of these appalling crimes. Full public inquiries can take years, while victims, survivors and experts, including Alexis Jay, have been clear that they want to see action now. That means protecting more children, finding more criminals, and getting justice for more victims and survivors.  Earlier this year, the Home Secretary announced a package of new measures and an investment of £10m that will allow us to do that, as well as drive change at a local level. The package includes the following:  •	More support and empowerment for victims. We are expanding the Child Sexual Abuse Review Panel mandate to include crimes which took place after 2013. This means that survivors who feel let down and unheard can ask the Panel to review their closed case even if it happened after 2013.  •	Baroness Louise Casey is leading a rapid audit of existing evidence on grooming gangs, examining existing data and evidence to uncover the true nature, scale and profile of group-based child sexual abuse offending being dealt with by forces in the UK today, including increasing our evidence base on the ethnicity of perpetrators; identifying gaps in existing knowledge; and making recommendations that can be applied both locally and nationally.  •	A renewed examination of all cases by police forces in England and Wales. The NPCC, at the Home Office’s request, is asking forces to reexamine both live and non-recent cases where no further action was taken. Police will be asked to work with the Child Sexual Abuse Police Taskforce to pursue new possible lines of inquiry and reopen investigations where appropriate to deliver justice for more victims and put more vile perpetrators behind bars.  •	An updated independent review of progress on the policing response to grooming gangs which the Home Secretary has commissioned from Her Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary, Fire and Rescue Services, following its December 2023 report.  •	A new, Government-developed, framework for victim-centred, local led inquiries. As we have seen in the likes of Telford and Rotherham, effective local inquiries can provide detailed, context-specific insight and recommendations, driving real change at the local level, using a framework developed in collaboration with experts experienced in establishing and delivering such inquiries, informed by established best practice and tailored to the specific needs of each community.  •	Stronger national backing for local inquiries, with the establishment of a £5m national fund for locally-led work to support both local areas which want to launch a full local independent inquiry, and those which want to deliver more bespoke work, e.g. through the establishment of local victims’ panels or conducting local-led audits into the handling of historic cases. This will enable more areas to conduct meaningful work to deliver the truth, justice and accountability that victims deserve.  •	A new Victims and Survivors Panel to ensure victims’ voices remain at the heart of policy-making, not just on the recommendations of the Jay report, but on wider work around child sexual exploitation and abuse.  •	Introducing a Duty of Candour, which will strengthen the accountability mechanisms underpinning local inquiries, to ensure that those who are complicit in cover-ups or who try to resist scrutiny are always robustly held to account, and that truth and justice are never denied.  •	 A new mandatory duty to report child sexual abuse, a key recommendation from Alexis Jay’s report.   These measures are set against a backdrop of continued investment in other work to strengthen law enforcement capacity and capability to tackle child sexual abuse and exploitation, including the Child Sexual Exploitation Police Taskforce which – since July 2023 – has supported the arrest of over 900 individuals and protected thousands of victims.  The work set out above remains the urgent priority of the Government and law enforcement when it comes to tackling child grooming gangs, and delivering justice for victims, and we believe that should remain the priority, rather than commissioning and waiting for the results of another national inquiry. additional_details:
Why This Matters:
Modern lifestyles with artificial light, screens, and irregular schedules have caused an epidemic of circadian rhythm disruption, linked to poor UK health outcomes. Melatonin, proven safe in low doses, supports sleep and synchronizes the body’s internal clock. Countries like the US, Canada, and the EU classify it as a supplement. Scientific advances highlight its critical role, and reclassification would empower proactive health management while easing NHS strain.

action: Allow motorcycles in bus lanes as default
background: We call on the Government to reverse its decision on the motorcycles in bus lanes consultation published 21 November 2024 and make the national default that motorcycles are allowed in bus lanes unless the local authority decides otherwise.
additional_details: The overwhelming majority of individual responses to the consultation were in favour of allowing motorcycle access. We believe that large amounts of real-world evidence proves the policy is safe with over 55 local authorities allowing motorcycle access to approximately half of the nation's bus lanes by length. Our view is that a default policy does not erode the authority to make local decisions.
government_response_summary: Local authorities are best placed to understand the needs of their road networks rather than central government. The consultation did not find enough evidence of the safety benefits for change.
government_response_body: The Department understands that the outcome of this consultation will have been a disappointment for some motorcyclists and associated organisations.   Local authorities are best placed to understand the needs of their local road networks, rather than central government. In the absence of robust data from the consultation, there is little justification for moving away from a position of local authority choice to one in which allowing motorcycles to use bus lanes is the default.   The safety benefits of allowing motorcycles into bus lanes are not clear. The consultation aimed to gather up to date, robust evidence, primarily from local authorities. While a very large number of individual responses was received, there were not enough from local authorities to provide the information needed. Although many individuals responded in favour, the vast majority did not provide any supporting evidence of the benefits or risks.   The Department acknowledges that some questions received a high number of responses, but whilst the number of responses illustrates the prevalence of each response, a consultation cannot be seen as a ‘vote’. Conclusions cannot and have not been drawn based solely on the number of people offering positive or negative comments about a particular suggestion.      Research on the potential safety impacts for cyclists, and the impact on bus services would be needed to form the evidence base for any change in policy. Whilst there is evidence of this working locally, this is quite different from a national policy of default access.   Furthermore, the cost to local authorities of new traffic signs and Traffic Regulation Orders mandating such a change for existing bus lanes would be considerable. Without strong evidence of the benefits, this cannot be justified. The existing policy of local authority discretion also aligns well with our policies on bus service improvements, encouraging walking and cycling, and devolving powers to local government, which is at the heart of our transport ambitions.  The Government remains committed to supporting efforts to improve the safety of motorcyclists and this policy will be kept under review.  Department for Transport

action: Do not restrict vape flavours
background: We want the Government to not give Ministers powers to restrict vape flavours in the Tobacco & Vapes Bill, as we believe it will undermine efforts to help smokers quit.
additional_details:
Some studies show flavoured vapes can help people stop smoking, and we think limiting options risks pushing users back to cigarettes or other products, endangering public health.
 
We believe flavoured vaping products already play a crucial role in helping smokers quit smoking cigarettes. We believe that restricting flavours would bring more harm, reversing smoking cessation progress and pushing users to dangerous black-market products.
government_response_summary: Further consultation will occur before introduction of any specific restrictions on vape flavours. To avoid unintended consequences on smoking rates, the any restrictions will be carefully considered.
government_response_body: Our health advice is clear, whilst vapes can be an effective quit aid for adult smokers, children should never vape.   Due to the branding and advertising of vapes to children, youth vaping has more than doubled in the last 5 years and one-in-four 11-15-year olds tried vaping in 2023. Due to nicotine content and the unknown long-term harms, vapes and nicotine products carry risk of harm and addiction; this is particularly acute for adolescents whose lungs and brains are still developing.   That is why this Government is committed to bringing about definitive and positive change to stop future generations from becoming hooked on nicotine – and the Tobacco and Vapes Bill includes landmark policies to achieve this.  The Tobacco and Vapes Bill includes measures and powers that will reduce the appeal and availability of all vapes and other nicotine products to children. Amongst the regulation making powers is one that will enable government to introduce future limits on flavours.    There are a vast and diverse variety of flavours on the UK market, many with attractive wording and names that entice children to try vaping. Evidence shows that children are attracted to the fruit and sweet flavours of vapes, both in their taste and smell, as well as how they are described. As stated in a recent ASH survey, the most frequently used vape flavouring for young people is “fruit flavour” with 59% of current child vapers using these flavours. 16% of children who vape also choose sweet flavours such as chocolate or candy.  The survey can be viewed here: www.ash.org.uk/uploads/Use-of-vapes-among-young-people-in-Great-Britain-2024.pdf.   It is the Government’s view that restricting flavours that appeal to children has the potential to reduce the number of children who are vaping. There is no reason that flavours like “gummy bear” and “cotton candy” should be available, flavours like these are not necessary for smoking cessation purposes and overtly appeal to children.     In considering the specific restrictions we bring forward, we are keenly aware that vaping is rightly used by adults as a tool to quit smoking. Vapes are less harmful than cigarettes, and vape flavours are an important consideration for adult smokers seeking to quit smoking.   We are conscious of the need to avoid unintended consequences on adult smoking rates, and therefore the scope and impact of any restrictions will be carefully considered and weighed against evidence. That is why we will be consulting further on these measures as soon as possible after Royal Assent of the Tobacco and Vapes Bill, and we would invite people to submit their views and evidence for consideration as part of that process.   Regulations on flavours that are subsequently drafted will be subject to parliamentary debate and vote before becoming law.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Decide on any change to the commission payable on the sale of a Park Home

additional_details:
The current legislation has been in place since 1983 and we feel it has become outdated and misleading in 2025. The maximum commission that the Park Owner can request was set in 1983 at 10% and remains the same today. 

The Government commissioned an independent survey on the subject in 2021 and the findings of that survey were submitted to the Government in June 2022. Since then there has been no decisions made to make changes to the 40 year old legislation or not. We feel that promises made have not been kept.

action: Create a public register of domestic abuse offenders

additional_details:
The police receive a domestic abuse-related call every 30 seconds.
On average, one woman is killed by an abusive partner or ex every five days in England and Wales. It is estimated that around 3 women a week die by suicide as a result of domestic abuse.
 
By making the information public, we think it could prevent many women and children having to endure the pain of domestic abuse, as well as saving police time having to disclose under Clare's Law and reduce domestic abuse related incidents and call outs.

action: Increase funding for people with Parkinson’s and implement the "Parky Charter"
background: We want the government to take the decisive five steps set out in the Movers and Shakers' "Parky Charter" and to fulfil the Health Secretary’s promises.
additional_details:
As a priority, we want to make sure that everyone referred for a possible Parkinson’s diagnosis sees a consultant within 18 weeks and at least once a year after that.
 
As set out in the Parky Charter, we want:
 
1. Speedy specialists
2. Instant information
3. Parkinson's passport
4. Comprehensive care
5. Quest for a cure
 
Parkinson’s is considered the fastest growing neurological condition in the world. We think it’s time for the government to respond to our grave concerns about what we consider systematic failings in Parkinson’s care.
 
The measures in the Parky Charter, which are supported by the three big Parkinson’s charities, require the government to deliver on their promises, ensuring timely diagnosis, comprehensive care, and dignity for all people with Parkinson’s.
government_response_summary: The Government is committed to improving health outcomes for people with neurological conditions, including Parkinson’s disease. Funding provision is subject to Spending Review decisions.
government_response_body: We acknowledge the challenges that neurology services have faced, particularly regarding workforce, delays to treatment and care, and a lack of information and support for patients. Nationally, there are initiatives supporting service improvement and better care for Parkinson’s patients, including the RightCare Progressive Neurological Conditions Toolkit and the Getting It Right First Time Neurology Programme. NHS England (NHSE) has established a Neurology Transformation Programme, which has developed a new model of integrated care to support integrated care boards to deliver the right service, at the right time for all neurology patients.  We have set up a UK-wide Neuro Forum, to bring together key stakeholders from across all four nations, to share learning, best practice examples and potential solutions.  NHSE commissions the specialised elements of Parkinson’s care that patients may receive from 27 specialised neurology centres across England. Within specialised centres, multidisciplinary teams ensure patients can access a range of health professionals and specialised treatment, according to their needs.  A central part of the 10-Year Health Plan will be our workforce and how we train and provide the staff the NHS needs to care for patients across our communities. This summer, we will publish a refreshed Long Term Workforce Plan aiming to treat patients on time again. We will ensure the NHS has the right people, in the right places, with the right skills to deliver the care patients need when they need it, including in neurology.  In January, NHSE published a new Elective Reform Plan, which sets out a whole system approach to hitting the 18-week referral to treatment target by 2029. We have achieved our pledge to deliver 2 million extra elective appointments. The additional appointments have taken place across a number of specialities, including neurology. We have made the commitment that 92% of patients will wait no longer than 18 weeks from referral to consultant-led treatment – in line with the NHS constitutional standard – by March 2029.  NICE guidance recommends that people with Parkinson's should be seen at regular intervals of 6-12 months. While NICE guidance is not mandatory, we expect commissioners to take it fully into account when designing services for their local population.  The Government currently has no plans to increase specific funding for people with Parkinson’s. However, at the Autumn Budget, DHSC received a £22.6 billion increase in resource spending from 2023-24 to 2025-26. How this is spent will be determined according to clinical priorities.  There are no plans to add to the list of conditions that give entitlement to free prescriptions. Around 89% of prescription items are currently dispensed free of charge and a wide range of exemptions from prescription charges are in place. People with Parkinson’s who are 60 years old or over are entitled to free prescriptions. For those that pay for prescriptions, the cost can be capped by purchasing a pre-payment certificate. Also, the NHS Low Income Scheme can provide help with health costs on an income-related basis.  The Government recently brought forward a Green Paper on the health and disability benefits system and the support we offer, entitled Pathways to Work: Reforming Benefits and Support to Get Britain Working. Within that, we consider how to improve the system for those with very severe health conditions and disabilities, including exploring ways to reduce the need for some people with very severe health conditions to undergo a full Personal Independence Payment functional assessment.  Eligibility for a Blue Badge is not condition specific. Blue Badge eligibility criteria in England were extended in 2019 to include more people with non-visible disabilities, to ensure that people with the greatest needs, whatever their disability or condition, all have the same access to a badge.  The Government spent £79.06 million on Parkinson’s research from 2019-20 to 2023-24, with research delivered via UK Research and Innovation and the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR). We are continuing to invest in Parkinson’s research. For example, the UK Dementia Research Institute, primarily funded by Government, is partnering with Parkinson’s UK to establish a new £10 million research centre dedicated to better understanding the causes of Parkinson’s and finding new treatments. The NIHR welcomes high-quality funding applications for research into any aspect of human health, including Parkinson's. Applications are subject to peer review and judged in open competition, with awards being made on the basis of the importance of the topic to patients and health and care services, value for money and scientific quality. Welcoming applications on Parkinson’s disease to all NIHR programmes enables maximum flexibility in terms of the amount of research funding a particular area can be awarded, and the type of research which can be funded.  Department of Health and Social Care  This is a revised response. The Petitions Committee requested a response which more directly addressed the request of the petition. action: Ensure plurality of political coverage across UK broadcast media at all times
background: We want to ensure that a plurality of views from all political parties in Westminster are represented and the nations parliaments are heard all year round, not just election times. The rules for coverage during elections should apply at all times.
additional_details:
We feel this is important as we deeply value democracy and the plurality of voices. We are very concerned about the perceived lack of fair political coverage outside of elections. 

We do not think that the current rules ensure equal or fair coverage of different political parties outside elections. We want ensure parties with representation are shown for the work they are performing all year round. We feel that this could result in citizens possessing a broader perspective on their representatives' activities, which we think is essential for an informed, functioning, democracy. We also want a review to look into how broadcasters ensure coverage never verges on propaganda for one political party or another.
government_response_summary: Ofcom rules ensure that broadcast news must be reported with due accuracy and impartiality. The Government is committed to a free media and has no plans to extend rules which apply during elections.
government_response_body: The Government is strongly committed to a free, sustainable, and plural media landscape, where diverse voices representing the breadth of views across our country can be heard. An independent media is a cornerstone of our democracy, and plays an essential role in helping citizens become more informed and support their decision making. Effective regulation is an essential part of this, helping to ensure that the highest standards are upheld, polemic is not presented as fact, and people can trust what they see. However, editorial decisions are a matter for individual broadcasters, not for the Government. It would not be proportionate or practical to mandate equal coverage for political parties outside of election and referendum periods. Doing so would place undue restrictions on broadcasters’ ability to freely report the news and undertake their critical role in holding the Government and political representatives to account. Therefore, the Government has no plans to extend broadcasting rules which apply during election or referendum periods to apply at all times.  Ofcom is the UK’s independent regulator for broadcasting, and by law carries out its duties independently of the Government. Ofcom’s Broadcasting Code includes rules which apply specifically during election periods, to ensure that due weight is given to the coverage of parties and independent candidates, based on evidence of past electoral support and/or current support. Broadcasters must also consider giving appropriate coverage to parties and independent candidates with significant views and perspectives. These rules are an important part of ensuring that audiences are informed about the range of political parties and candidates who are standing for elected office. They are designed to help secure the integrity of the democratic process, and the public’s trust in that process, by preventing unfair electoral advantage being afforded to a particular candidate.  The Broadcasting Code also includes rules to ensure that news is reported with due accuracy and presented with due impartiality. No politician may be used as a newsreader, interviewer or reporter in any news programme unless, exceptionally, it is editorially justified. In that case, the political allegiance of that person must be made clear to the audience. Ofcom is required by legislation and accountable to Parliament to keep the Broadcasting Code under review, and make changes to the Code if they consider it appropriate. Ofcom recently held a consultation on proposed changes to the rules around politicians acting as presenters. The proposed changes aim to make it clear to broadcasters that a politician cannot be used as a newsreader, news interviewer, or news reporter in any type of programme. Changes to the Broadcasting Code are rightly a matter for Ofcom, as the independent regulator, and Ofcom is expected to set out next steps following the consultation later this year.  Department for Culture, Media and Sport

action: Stop party leaders removing the whip when MPs vote in Parliament.
background: MPs are elected to represent their constituents in Parliament but this seems to have been forgotten with MPs often whipped to vote along the Party line and this is unacceptable in a democracy.

If MPs are not carrying out the will of those who elected them, then we no longer have a democracy and live under a dictatorship.
rejection_details:

action: Petition to Prohibit Serving Halal Meat to Non-Muslims Without Prior Consent.
background: We urge the Government to mandate clear labeling of halal meat, require education on its preparation (including non-stun slaughter), and prohibit serving halal meat to non-Muslims without their explicit consent. This ensures transparency, informed choice, and respect for individual dietary beliefs
additional_details: Halal meat, often prepared using non-stun slaughter, is served to non-Muslims in schools, restaurants, and institutions without their knowledge or consent. This denies individuals the right to make informed dietary choices and imposes religious practices on others. Non-stun slaughter also raises serious animal welfare concerns, as highlighted by the BVA and RSPCA. Requiring education and consent ensures transparency and protects consumer rights while addressing ethical concerns.

action: Require schools to allow students to use their phones at break and lunch
background: We think that students should be allowed to use their phones during break and lunch because it provides them with the opportunity to connect with people. Phones can allow students to stay in touch with family and friends, access helpful resources, and arrange group activities.
additional_details: Students could also use apps for relaxation, creativity, or even catching up on homework. We think that allowing responsible phone use fosters trust and teaches time management, preparing students for the real world where technology could be essential.

action: Fund a nationwide app for parking
background: Currently there are multiple different mobile apps used to collect payment for parking. When parking, the motorist needs to find the correct app and may not have it on their phone. This may lead to delay and possible errors.
additional_details:
We believe the Government should provide funding so there is one app for the whole country. When adding a vehicle to a user list, the app should connect with DVLA and affirm that the registration entered is valid and matches the vehicle identity. 

Many car parks use Automatic Number Plate Recognition. If a driver inadvertently inserts an incorrect registration that ANPR has not detected at the entrance, the payment collection system should alert the driver to this immediately.

action: Raise the personal tax allowance to £13750
background: The minimum living wage rises every year, yet the personal tax allowance does not. The minimum wage increases to help with the rising cost of living and inflation and we think the personal tax allowance should correlate to this.
additional_details: The average UK income is £37,000 a year. We think this would help out those earning on the lower end of the tax bracket who need it most. This has been fixed since 2021. In 2021, something costing £10 would now cost around £12.09.

action: Create a compensation scheme for businesses affected by rail strikes
background: We would like the government to do something concrete to stop rail strikes. They could create a compensation scheme for the businesses effected by strikes funded by the train companies and unions.
additional_details: We think that the strikes can have an adverse effect on the economy of communities serviced by lines subject to regular strikes and they cannot be left until franchise renewal. The business communities do not wish for the travel disruption to continue into the summer months and beyond, whilst they are still trying to recover from COVID 19.

action: Disqualify current or ex Solicitors, Barristers & Judges from becoming MPs
background: We believe that any prospective MP upon nomination should be required to declare if they are or have ever been a Solicitor, Barrister & Judge. If they have they would be disqualified from being an MP.
additional_details: We believe the aforementioned Solicitors, Barristers & Judges, do and have served a very important and valued position in society. However we think they are intrinsically linked to upholding and preserving the current legislation. In our view this could lead to a conflict of interest preventing them adequately representing the views of constituents wanting to change.

action: Review the police response to assaults on mental health nurses
background: We want more protection for mental health nurses in cases of assault. Review the official action taken after an assault, to ensure that the assault and abuse of mental health nurses is taken seriously. Review how Operation Cavell has been applied to mental health nurses.
additional_details: We believe that assaults on mental health nurses are often not taken seriously by the police with some officers taking the attitude that 'it's part of your job'. Assault towards MH nurses should be treated the same as abuse in public or of nurses in acute services.

action: Ask the Government to fund a mental health scheme for the British Army
background: We want Parliament to discuss the ongoing issue with regard to the funding, support, and recognition of mental health in the British Army. Once they are more aware of the statistics and the lack of funding, we would like them to establish a separate mental health fund specifically for the Army
additional_details: The British Army has been chronically underfunded for years. Once they receive their budget there is little left over for mental health concerns. The Government should show how much they respect our forces by creating a separate mental health scheme for soldiers.

action: To include hospitality as a key part of a single ministerial portfolio
background: Hospitality contributes £93bn annually and employs 3.5m people, yet it lacks dedicated representation in government. We urge the Government to include hospitality in a single ministerial portfolio, ensuring cohesive policies, support for recovery, and recognition of its vital role in the UK economy.
additional_details: The hospitality sector is critical to the UK economy, but fragmented oversight across multiple departments leads to inconsistent policies and missed opportunities. A dedicated ministerial portfolio would prioritise challenges like staffing shortages, rising costs, and sustainability. This unified approach would enable cohesive decision-making, better support businesses, and maximise the sector’s potential to create jobs, drive local economies, and strengthen communities across the UK.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. The Minister for Services, Small Business & Exports has hospitality in his portfolio.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Require hunting hounds to wear muzzles when on a trail or clean boot hunt
background: We ask that the government bring in a new law which requires mandatory wearing of humane, approved muzzles, such as basket muzzles, by all fox hunting hounds when trail or clean boot hunting. Basket muzzles made from rubber plastic or metal allow dogs to drink, breathe & pant.
additional_details:
In the trail hunting process foxes may still be caught & killed due to the hounds being in fox habitat.
Foxes, other wildlife, farm animals & domestic pets may be hurt & killed. We think this can be avoided by a legal requirement that all hunting hounds must wear muzzles when on a hunt.

action: Legalize and regulate cannabis for responsible medicinal and recreational use.
background: We ask the Government to legalize cannabis, regulate its sale and use, and decriminalize possession. Introduce strict licensing for production, ensure product safety, and tax sales to fund public services. Promote education on responsible use and reduce harm while addressing the illegal market.
additional_details: Legalizing cannabis will reduce illegal markets, provide safer products, and generate significant tax revenue to support public services like healthcare and education. Other countries have shown legalization can reduce crime, ease pressure on police and courts, and create jobs. It allows for better public health outcomes by regulating quality and promoting responsible use. The UK has an opportunity to adopt an evidence-based policy that benefits society and the economy.
rejection_details:

Legalise recreational cannabis & release those convicted of cannabis offences.

Reassess the classification of Cannabis and decriminalize it.
