action: Make the UK a state of the United States under Donald Trump’s leadership
background: I want the UK Government to begin discussions with the United States to make the UK a state of the US under Donald Trump’s leadership. This would strengthen ties, improve economic and political unity, and create a closer relationship between the two nations.
additional_details: Joining the United States as a state under Donald Trump’s leadership could bring economic growth, stronger international influence, and closer ties with one of our closest allies. This would unify our values and cultures, simplify trade, and enhance security cooperation between the two nations.
rejection_details: Joining of the United States of America would be a matter for the US Congress to decide, and not something the UK Government or Parliament could unilaterally do.

action: Ensure companies don't make excess profits to bring prices down to a fair amount
background: We think any profit margin above 30%is excessive. We want the government to negotiate with supermarkets and companies, who are making excessive profits, to use their profits to bring down prices. Alternatively, we'd like the Government to introduce a windfall tax on their profits.
additional_details: We feel this could help ease the cost of living crisis for millions of people. We believe this policy would show strong leadership and benefit the public.

action: Make post separation abuse a stand-alone offence
background:
Abuse usually escalates post separation and can be relentless for months and years.

We must hold abusers to account and prevent further abuse at the most dangerous time for those having escaped abusers. 

Our current system doesn't.
additional_details:
Escaping an abuser is proven to be the most dangerous time for any victim/survivor. It is well evidenced and recognised that abuse escalates in severity post separation and along with that the risks to the victim/survivor and their families is vast. 

Separation is a key indicator in femicide with 2 women a week murdered in the UK by a current or ex-partner.

Convictions for abuse post separation would validate and better protect victims who remain largely unheard or feel there is no escape
rejection_details:
Controlling or coercive behaviour is a crime in England and Wales under section 76 of the Serious Crime Act (2015). This law highlights that domestic abuse is often a purposeful pattern of behaviour.

The Domestic Abuse Act (2021) for England and Wales extended this offence to include post-separation abuse. This changed the law so that controlling or coercive behaviour can now potentially be prosecuted as a criminal offence even if the parties are no longer in a relationship and are not living together.

action: Close the child maintenance payment loophole for parents working abroad
background: We believe there is loophole for that allows non-resident parents who work abroad to avoid child maintenance payments and we want the Government to take action to stop this.
additional_details: We want the Government to put a policy in place to protect maintenance payments from parents who work abroad to protect children that may face poverty as a result of non-payment.

action: Fund offer of toxicology test for repetitive symptoms unexplained otherwise
background: I would like parliament to put in place funding, to ensure everyone is offered a toxicology blood test if they go to the doctor or A&E and are not getting any answers for their symptoms. For people who have attended more than once for symptoms unexplained otherwise.
additional_details: One singular blood test can let people know that something is very wrong. I want to put this in place so people do not suffer this way. This is not acceptable and we believe this small change WILL make a big difference.

action: Amend The Animal Welfare Act 2006 To Give Cats Better Protections On Roads
background: It is perfectly legal in the UK to hit a cat when driving and leave them scared, alone and in pain roadside. Cats are important, loved, valued family members and, as it does for dogs, the law should reflect this. We want legislation that recognises cats as a species worth helping if injured on roads
additional_details: We want section 4 of the Animal Welfare Act to include a direct amendment that holds drivers accountable if they fail to stop and report a collision involving a cat on the basis they left a cat to unnecessarily suffer. Asking a bit of decency is legislated for by asking drivers be made responsible for seeking help for an injured cat is a perfectly reasonable & simple ask. Legislation currently leans toward encouraging unnecessary suffering by allowing drivers to flee the scene. It must change.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions:

Protect Cats: Make Reporting Cat Accidents a Legal Requirement
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700990

Drivers who hit cats in their car should stop and take the cat to a vet
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700808

action: Make it mandatory for all disabled bays to be painted yellow
background: Currently, disabled parking bays can be painted either yellow or white. Yellow disabled bays are enforceable meaning that only disabled badge holders can park there. White disabled bays are only advisory, so technically anyone can park there.
additional_details: We urge the government to implement regulations for all local authorities that require all disabled parking bays to be painted yellow, not white. We think this change could help reduce parking misuse and could also better support our community members with disabilities.

action: For Government to continue the Listed Places of Worship Grant Scheme (LPWGS).
background: The Church of England’s Cathedral & Church Buildings team is increasingly concerned that this scheme, administered by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport and funded jointly with HM Treasury, may not be extended beyond its current end date of 31 March 2025. Parishioners are deeply concerned.
additional_details:
The LPW scheme allows listed places of worship of all faiths across the UK to reclaim the full amount of VAT they pay on repairs of over £1000. 
Removing it means 20% more needs to be raised by local people to pay VAT to the Government, this increases pressure on overstretched finances.  
LPW's provide a safe space for people to connect and belong in community. Studies have shown the high value of 'faith capital' which benefit the lives of old and young all over the country. LPW's are a lifeline
rejection_details: You can find further information about the scheme being extended to March 2026 here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/23-million-government-package-to-support-restoration-of-thousands-of-listed-places-of-worship

action: Stop Stubbington study centre from closing
background: Stubbington Study Centre is a Children’s Services facility available to schools and other pre-booked groups for residentials and more.  They want to change it to a specialist secure welfare home for 18 children.
additional_details:
Closing Stubbington to the amount of chidren that use this site would be detrimental to future children's learning. 
For a lot of children this maybe the only chance they get to have a holiday and the only chance they get to stay away from home without parents. 
Over 6000 children a year stay at Stubbington. They are proposing to close this site and turning it in to a welfare home for only 18 children. 
The centre has been running for 90 years. Offering so much to Hampshire schools.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Make our railways public: Say no to extortionate prices through privatisation.
background: Reverse the privatisation of the British railway system and bring it back under public ownership. This includes ensuring railway operations and infrastructure are unified under a public body, with revenues reinvested to improve services, lower ticket prices, and benefit the environment.
additional_details: Privatisation has failed passengers. Ticket prices have risen disproportionately, while services have become unreliable and overcrowded. Publicly owned systems in other countries show that affordable, efficient, and sustainable railways are achievable when profit is not the priority. A publicly owned railway will ensure accountability, affordability, and better service for all.
rejection_details:
Under the Passenger Railway Services (Public Ownership) Act 2024, passenger train operators with contracts with the Department for Transport (DfT) are to be brought into public ownership. Nationalisation will start in 2025 and is expected to finish in 2027.

You can find more information in this briefing from the House of Commons library: 
https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/when-will-my-local-train-operator-be-nationalised/

action: Make credit companies do more thorough security checks to help stop fraud
background: Enforce stricter security guidelines to help prevent identity theft and fraudulent activity
additional_details: I was recently a victim of identity theft where someone managed to take credit out in my name after learning my basic personal details from hacking my phone
rejection_details: The Financial Conduct Authority regulate financial services firms and financial markets in the UK, you can find more information here: https://www.fca.org.uk/

action: Allow communities in England and Wales to use beavers for flood management
background: Beavers, the greatest watercourse engineers on the planet, can help communities to slow the flow of water across river catchments, thereby protecting them from flooding, at very low cost. Beavers increase water storage protecting against drought, increase biodiversity and improve water quality.
additional_details: For more evidence of the benefits of beavers to communities in tackling the climate and nature crises, please see the River Otter Beaver Trial Science and Evidence Report available here:- https://www.devonwildlifetrust.org/what-we-do/our-projects/river-otter-beaver-trial
rejection_details:
You can find more information about the wild release and management of beavers here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/wild-release-and-management-of-beavers-in-england/wild-release-and-management-of-beavers-in-england

Environmental policy is a devolved and the Welsh Parliament has its own Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Welsh Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.senedd.wales/

action: Stop the Chagos Islands deal as it is not in the National Interest
background: Give the country a good reason as to how this is in the public interest and will enhance UK safety.
additional_details:
The people of the UK need the government to explain how this will enhance Western security and improve relations with our most powerful ally USA 
This needs a full debate in parliament  together with an explantion of the financial implications to our economy and where the money is coming from.

action: Climate policies: do more to engage and consider impacts on disabled people
background: I would like the Government to do more to explicitly consider and consult disabled people in its development of climate change policies.
additional_details:
They weren't mentioned in the Nationally Determined Contribution. I believe this is against international human rights laws.
 
I demand that the government includes and engages disabled people in the decision-making processes around climate change policy.
 
In the UK it’s estimated there are 16.1 million disabled people. Disabled people are more at risk in the climate crisis.
 
Neglecting including disabled people in climate mitigation policies means ignoring the meaningful contributions disabled people could make.

action: Give Wales the same funding per person for the rail network as England
background: We feel that the Welsh rail network is treated as second class compared to England. The nation has 11% of the entire UK's rail network, has 5% of the UK's population but receives just 1% of rail infrastructure funding.
additional_details:
The UK government could use the Railways Bill this year to create a mechanism to guarantee fair funding.

We feel that the rail network in Wales has so much potential to help address the challenges the nation and the world face. The nation has less electrified track than other developed countries. We believe that better investment - comparable with England and Scotland - could provide an economic boost, reduce carbon emissions, reduce congestion on busy roads and improve people's quality of life.
 
We want better and faster rail connection throughout Wales, not just to London.

action: Abolish Vehicle Excise Duty and add the cost to Fuel Duty
background: I would like Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) to be completely abolished. Instead, add the cost to Fuel Duty. I think this will mean that for more fuel-efficient vehicles which generally use less fuel and emit less CO2, drivers will pay less for fuel, and this change may help wider zero carbon policies.
additional_details:
Older, less efficient vehicles can disappear naturally without some families potentially feeling forced into rash decisions about vehicle use.
 
In my view, any attempt to fast-track carbon reduction by hiking certain taxes like VED may make the country poorer. I think the infrastructure needed to do the things government wants to do is decades behind. I believe that it should be the case that the more fuel you use, the more tax you pay.

action: We want to make a change to Pocklington School to make rugby not compulsory.
background: Since forcing kids to play rugby legally counts as child abuse and child abuse is very illegal we should not be forced to play rugby as we always get hurt and we end up hating thursdays because they force us to play rugby and it puts a bad note to the day thus ruining it.
additional_details: I think from the perspective of a 12 year old and his friends. (me) we always get hurt in rugby and we think you should not be forced to play it. Please make the school remove this and provide a substitute such as basketball.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about what sports to play at school are a matter for individual schools, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Review the legislation relating to asylum and refugees entering the UK
background: We would like the government to undertake a comprehensive review of the of the Asylum Act 1991, the 1951 UN Convention on refugees and any other legislation to ensure the legal frameworks for refugees and asylum seeks arriving in the UK are still for for purpose.
additional_details: We think the UK has a proud history of providing refuge to those in need. However, we think it is imperative to recognise that the world has changed significantly since these legal frameworks were established. We think that updating these laws could ensure the nation continues to uphold its humanitarian values whilst maintaining public confidence in our immigration system.

action: Deport people with dual nationality who are found guilty of raping children
background: We think the Grooming Gangs scandal is possibly the biggest scandal in our country's history. It is time for a tough approach. We are calling for foreign born nationals with dual nationality who are found guilty of raping children to be deported.

action: Scrap Council Tax
background: The current council tax is no longer fit for purpose and needs to end.
additional_details: To help those who are on a low income
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Abolish council Tax

action: Fund free British Sign Language Courses for deaf people and their friends/family
background: I am profoundly deaf. I have hearing aids and I can lipread. This is still not enough in circumstances like noisy environment and at home too when I choose to have hearing breaks, which many deaf people will do.
additional_details:
I and many others like myself, refuse to pay for BSL courses because we feel we should easily be entitled to them. As well as this, the friends and family of deaf individuals also need to learn to communicate via BSL.
 
I feel that the problem is that many people were never taught BSL growing up as it wasn’t well known.
 
BSL has become a well-known language. Why should we have to pay for in classroom courses when we think we should be eligible already?

action: Compensate the RHS for £6m charity losses caused by the A3/M25 roadworks
background: A3/M25 roadworks have disrupted access to RHS Wisley leading to £6m losses, £11m when the roadworks end. Since the roadworks started the garden has had 25% fewer visitors, loss of £1m income from membership and cancelled events. Less income means less charitable work for people and planet.
additional_details: The RHS is a charity that is not government funded and is urging Government to recognise there is a special case for compensation. With the £6m losses to date the RHS could have created 15 NHS wellbeing gardens, brought gardening and nature to hundreds more schools and communities across the UK, funded 110 horticultural apprenticeships or 38 science PhD students to find nature-based solutions to help pollution, flooding and the biodiversity and the climate crises.
rejection_details:

government_response_summary: The government has no plans to hold a referendum on changing the process by which the Mayor of London can be removed from office.
government_response_body: The Greater London Authority, the position of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly were established following a referendum held in Greater London on 7 May 1998 in which 72% of those voting expressed their support for the proposals. The government has no  plans to hold another referendum on the role of Mayor of London or the process by which they may be removed, and are proposing to grow the number and role of mayors across England over the coming years.  The government believes in devolution, moving power out of Westminster and to those who know their area best. Devolution in London has proved successful in maintaining the prosperity and success of London on a national and international level.  The Mayor of London is directly elected by the people of Greater London every 4 years and is scrutinised by the elected London Assembly. The Mayor is required to appear before the Assembly at least 10 times per year and host a public State of London Debate. The Assembly also conducts investigations on matters of importance to London through a series of themed committees.  Alongside other eligibility criteria, a person is disqualified from being the Mayor of London if they: •	are convicted of any offence and a sentence of imprisonment of at least 3 months has been imposed, •	are disqualified for illegal or corrupt practices at elections •	incur or authorise unlawful expenses •	fail to attend 6 meetings of the London Assembly when required More details on eligibility and disqualification criteria can be found here:  https://www.electoralcommission.org.uk/guidance-candidates-and-agents-greater-london-authority-elections/what-you-need-know-you-stand-a-candidate/qualifications-and-disqualifications-standing-election/disqualifications#footnote2_iaSbti  The Political Parties, Elections and Referendum Act 2000 sets out the regulatory framework for referendums in the UK. Our constitutional arrangements allow for referendums to take place and primary legislation is required. Parliament is the supreme legislative authority in the United Kingdom and it is for Parliament to decide whether a referendum should take place and to pass primary legislation to determine how the referendum would be conducted. The government has no plans to introduce such primary legislation.  Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

action: Reform the British Spouse Visa System
background: Many British citizens and their spouses face huge costs, with the initial visa application costing £4,951(including the healthcare surcharge), the extension application priced at £3,845.50, and the settlement (ILR) application at £2,885. Over five years, families may have to pay more than £11,000.
additional_details: I do not believe family unity should not come with an exorbitant price tag. I believe the current system places undue stress on families, penalising them for seeking the simple right to live together. I think reforming the spouse visa process is essential to uphold fairness, equality, and compassion in the UK’s immigration policies. I believe Ireland’s Spouse Immigration System offers a model of fairness and compassion. Spouses of Irish citizens are exempt from visa fees.

action: Require social housing providers to allow XL bullies with exemption certificate
background:
We think local authorities should not be allowed to exclude XL bully owners with a certificate of exemption from Social Housing.

additional_details:

Be told as homeless priority, to chose between a prospective home & euthanising their much loved pet.
Be threatened with eviction because they couldn't go through with euthanisation.
We think the current situation is torturous, unacceptable and needs to stop urgently. We believe it impacts on Human Rights & Animal Welfare

action: Fund Child Contact Centre visits for parents
background: Some individuals are ordered by the courts to attend a child contact centre for supervised or supported contact. We feel this should be funded by the Government.

Call a public inquiry into the grooming gangs, and provide the committee with full powers to prosecute indiscriminately, with a compulsion to do so.

action: Reform the processes of arranging a funeral / collecting ashes
background: I think that, as well as the green form, an additional step should be added to the process of requesting a cremation, collecting ashes and arranging a funeral. This should be to prove that the person arranging the funeral or collecting the ashes is the next of kin or executor of the will.
additional_details: I don't think that the green form and death certificate should be sufficient proof to confirm someone has the right to collect ashes or organise a funeral. This will prevent families being caused distress by not being able to rightfully collect and bury ashes of a loved one.

action: NHS dental nurses to be entitled to an NHS pension
background: Give all Dental nurses working within a practice with an NHS contract the same pension rights as other NHS workers.
additional_details: Dental nurses are working alongside Dentists whom have an NHS contract, this contract entitles them to an NHS pension. However, Dental nurses do not receive an NHS pension.

action: End the Immigration Health Surcharge for National Insurance payers
background: People may be struggling to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge, when they are renewing their residence permits. If they are working and paying national insurance and taxes, we think it's not fair that people have to then pay again for the Health Service Charge when they apply to renew their visa.
additional_details: I want the Government to end the Immigration Health Surcharge for those who are working and contributing towards national insurance and taxes. Because there are people who are struggling and under pressure, but also immigrants doing well to support the country.

action: Stop doritos from changing to square

action: Funding for Gastric Pacemaker Treatment for Gastroparesis Patients
background: I urge the government to fund gastric pacemaker treatment for gastroparesis patients.
additional_details: We think patients with gastroparesis deserve access to a gastric pacemaker, a treatment that may improve quality of life. Many suffer from persistent symptoms like nausea, vomiting, and malnutrition, with limited treatment options. We think this device could reduce hospital stays and improves nutrition. We think providing funding could ensure equitable healthcare access, reduce long-term NHS costs, and offer patients a chance at a better quality of life, free from constant hospital visits and severe symptoms.

action: Have more bins  and use more solar power instead of burning fossil fuels
background: Can you please spend a little more time on things like our planet so we can save it and a way to do that is to get more bins so less people litter and we could get  more solar panels to reduce the amount of fossil fuels being burned. action: Fund greater police presence in bike theft hotspots
background: There have been increased reports recently of violent bike theft in Richmond Park, Regents Park and other public spaces. The victims of such incidents may be fearful for their lives and may not have the courage to cycle again. This is abhorrent.
additional_details:
I do not think the current police response to these cases is acceptable; cases are not investigated sufficiently.

We would like to see more police present in known hotspots and more resources available to catch thieves and punish them appropriately.

action: Make machines, which take payment on exit, mandatory for parking operators.
background: I want the Government to legislate so that parking operators have to use machines which charge for parking on exit so that charges correlate to the amount of time that a person stays. Fixed penalties for overstaying should not be allowed.
additional_details: I think many parking operators charge extortionate penalties for overstaying. Occasionally people don't realise they have slightly overstayed or could not return to the parking place within the parking ticket time.

action: Apply the same energy efficiency legislation to all property - not just rentals
background: The UK government has announced plans to significantly increase energy efficiency standards for privately rented properties. Owner-occupied properties would not be required to meet the same requirements, which we think creates an unfair and illogical situation from an environmental standpoint.
additional_details:
We urge the UK government to introduce a level playing field by applying the same energy efficiency standards to both privately rented and owner-occupied properties.
We believe that a fair and equitable approach to improving energy efficiency with the same standards is applied across the board. We think it is illogical from an environmental point of view to only apply the rules to the private rental sector.

action: Expand laws around Intellectual Property Rights to ideas and intelligence.
background: IPR laws need modernising for the 21st century, expanding the scope of what can be defined as intellectual property to include ideas people or businesses have and new intelligence developed by people.
additional_details: The private sector, corporate world is broken, with a toxic culture. At the centre of this is the mamagement consultancy industry. The main problem is that there's no laws in place to protect businesses or people's ideas and creative intelligence - laws currently in place around other forms of intellectual like inventions. The result is a free for all where there's no incentive to create own ideas, only to steal from others, and spin as your own.

In some temporary accommodation, you are not allowed to stay out overnight and in some, residents have to sign a daily register to prove they have been in the property. Children may lose their social skills and bonds with family members and parents may lose jobs because they can’t get childcare, if they can’t have a someone such as a grandparent in the property to help.

background: Pensioners have worked all their life, paying their dues and diligently saving for a comfortable retirement; a right they have honestly earned. It is contrary to penalize them for their foresightedness by taxing their pensions which in essence, has already weathered taxation in its previous form.
additional_details:

By implementing tax exemption for pensioners or increasing the tax-free allowance, we are helpinging a significant group of people who have done their part for society through lifelong employment and contribution. action: Make it illegal for the media to shame victims of romance fraud
background: We believe it should be illegal for the media to use victim-shaming language in their headlines and news reports. We think that doing so is secondary victimisation, which includes harassment and discrimination, that the media should be held accountable for.
additional_details:
Romance fraud destroys lives. It is a cruel and devastating crime where fraudsters groom victims through coercive control, similar to domestic abuse.
 
However, we think that sections of the British press believe that victims of romance fraud are legitimate targets for ridicule. We believe this is completely unethical and this pure form of victim shaming will stop others coming forward to report crimes. We do not think that victims should have to live with the shame they are made to feel.

action: Prevent landlords from profiting from tenants, and extorting tenants
background:
We want the Government to make it illegal to operate a business that relies on people needing a safe place to live.

No landlord should be profiting from people needing a safe place to live

No landlord should be putting the rent up at every opportunity

Action will cause house prices to drop.
additional_details:
Landlords use the phrase "it's a business not a charity" while looking for the next best opportunity to increase the rent.

If action isn't taken to prevent landlords continued abuse of power, it will result in utter catastrophic widespread social unrest, protests, riots, vandalism, arson, and worse.

The British government needs to provide safe, affordable housing for the British people and prevent landlords from purchasing property to be used for taking advantage of the poor and working class.

action: Agree not to means test the triple lock on pensions now or into the future
background: Labour have today (18 January) not ruled out means testing of triple lock pensions. This is unacceptable. Former working people have paid into the system & the state pension is not a benefit to be viewed as a ‘free’ fund to be cut by governments.  Current/future pensioners need urgent assurances.
additional_details:
Pensioners face financial struggles when they retire and need confidence that the ruling government will not add to their concerns.

It’s unacceptable for governments to continue to pick the pockets of pensioners when there are better choices to limit commitments to overseas projects, improve efficiencies in the Civil Services, tax big business more fairly, reduce or eliminate subsidies and expenses in Parliament and concerns over the size, constitution and value from the House of Lords.

action: Scrap 100 Year Deal With Ukraine And Fund State Of The Art NHS Hospitals Instead
background: Instead of sending billions of UK taxpayers’ money to Ukraine, we think we should commit those billions over a 100-year deal to the NHS and fund state of the art hospitals, rather than exacerbate reported ‘black holes’ in our public finances.

action: Create an inclusive special envoy for home educating families
background: Create a special envoy for home educating families, who would be a mediator between Government, officials and the Home Education Community, and suggest amendments to the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill. This special envoy should include home educating parents.
additional_details:
We think this would benefit home educated children who we want to achieve their best potential.
 
We think Part 2, Sections 25 - 30 of the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill is not fit for purpose in its present state and should be amended because we think it:
- is poorly researched, lacks understanding of home education, may put additional children at risk, especially those from families who have experienced Domestic Violence or Child Abuse.
- is ambiguous, lacks straightforwardness and simplicity which may lend it easily to misuse of power.
- undermines children's rights as protected in UNCRC.

action: Remove the expensive car supplement for secondhand cars
background: We don't want the expensive car supplement to Vehicle Excise Duty rate to apply to secondhand cars to account for the depreciation of value.
additional_details:
We don't think its fair that under current policy, someone could save money to purchase a second hand car, which is no longer worth £40,000 and then have to pay £425 per annum on top of the standard VED. 

We think that cars depreciate in value and that people buying secondhand cars should not be penalised for trying to save money.

action: Introduce random alcohol & drug testing within the House of Commons
background: We want the government to introduce random alcohol and drug testing within the House of Commons
additional_details:
The Palace of Westminster is a place of Government. It is also the place that legislation is passed that governs us all.
 
Therefore, great responsibility and privilege is afforded to MPs. In the interests of the highest possible standards, we think random alcohol and drug testing needs to be introduced.

action: Ban balaclavas except for winter activity use
background:
We want the government to introduce legislation that clearly defines restrictions on wearing balaclavas in public, with exemptions for winter activities.
 
There could be penalties for non-compliance, and guidance issued to ensure public understanding and adherence.
additional_details: We think this action is necessary to enhance public safety and security. Balaclavas can be used to conceal identity, making it impossible for authorities to identify individuals in the event of criminal activities or public disturbances. By restricting their use to appropriate contexts, such as winter sports, we think the government could help reduce the potential for anonymity in situations that could compromise safety while allowing for personal freedom in legitimate circumstances.

action: Create English regional assemblies (regional governments)
background: We urge the Government to set up regional governments (e.g. a Midlands assembly, Northern Assembly) and shake up local outdated Council scheme to do this, as we believe more areas outside London would benefit, see growth, have someone closer to home to answer to and more resources and power.
additional_details: The UK economy is focused around London, and we believe other areas of the England cannot keep up. We believe that if other areas where given assembly-style regional governments and local councils were de-scaled to cost efficient sizes, then regions outside of London would see a boost in economic growth.

action: Require general elections at least every 3 years instead of 5
background: I want the government to be required to hold a general election every three years instead of every five years.
additional_details:
Due to the previous years of leadership changes, three years can show what a party is capable of.
 
I think this would allow the public to assess the actions of the government and determine if the current path is suitable for the country.

action: Install Speed Bumps
background:
Install speed bumps on Alcester Road, Studley, Warwickshire to prevent further damage to people's homes from speeding drivers.
Potential to save lives.
additional_details:
A large number of terrible road traffic accidents with considerable damage to people's properties and parked vehicles.

Four major accidents in the last 18 months alone.

action: Require pension providers to contact their customers every 5 years
background: We think pension providers should be made to contact the people who have pensions with them every 5 years.
additional_details:
We are automatically enrolled into a pension but if you change jobs and loose track of your pension you may not be contacted and you could loose that pension. They have many of your details and should be made to every five years.
 
Make it mandatory for pension providers to contact customers every 5 years through email or post so no one could lose their money if they have lost track of on especially if they have changed jobs multiple times.

action: Review how the legal system and police treat abuse cases
background: We're advocating for reforms in the British judicial system to ensure fairness for all involved in abuse cases. We think this means considering both defendants and victims and promoting transparent investigations.
additional_details: We think the review should consider reforms in police investigation methods, improved transparency, and the law on media coverage before trial. We think an independent inquiry into police practices is needed to prevent unfair outcomes for defendants, ensuring justice is upheld for all involved.

action: Provide funding for a review of the efficacy of Pineal Gland Surgery
background: We would like the government to fund a review to explore the extent to which surgical intervention can alleviate the symptoms experienced by individuals with pineal cysts.
additional_details:
We believe that such a review could provide valuable insights and inform future treatment options, ultimately benefiting those affected by this condition.

We propose an independent panel, composed of leading experts in the field to conduct this urgent review of the scientific literature related to pineal cysts and their management. This review would aim to provide recommendations based on the latest evidence.
 
Let us choose our destiny.

action: Provide funding for a national crime reference number system
background: We think that a better way to monitor crime would be to use prefixes to criminal reference numbers that would indicate the postcode area and the type of crime. We think this would make it easier to monitor crime throughout the country.

action: Remove the need for people to have gender dysphoria to legally change gender
background: As of now, one of the requirements for someone to legally change their gender is to have been diagnosed with gender dysphoria. Parliament should remove this requirement and allow people to legally change their gender, even without the diagnosis of gender dysphoria.
additional_details: The NHS's inability to provide support at acceptable speeds can and will result in a diagnosis taking a long time to actually be processed. This is not only unacceptable, but could also create mental health problems for the person wanting to change their legal gender, which is completely unnecessary. Furthermore, the idea that this diagnosis is needed to change their gender reinforces the discriminatory ideology that transgender people are "mentally ill", which keeps prejudice alive.

action: Give parent and child parking spaces the same legal status as a disabled space.
background: Change the law to make parking in a parent and child parking bay without a child under 12 illegal with a fine of up to £100 to give parity with disabled parking spaces.
additional_details: As a first time mother of a young baby it’s opened my eyes to how difficult it can be to get my baby and her accessories out of the car in a standard space. However I find many people park in parent and child bay without a child or a care. I have seen many heated arguments take place in the car park and on social media about this problem and it’s time we changed it. The spaces do not need to be closer to do the door just wider and have action taken against people who park there without children.

action: Include more sports options for GCSE PE
background: I feel that a lot of the sports chosen for GCSE PE are not available in more deprived areas, limiting the options for working class children to consider taking a GCSE in sport.
additional_details: I think that activities like weight-lifting and martial arts are much more accessible and many children partake in them from all backgrounds. I couldn’t believe the limitations of what students are allowed to chose. Why is it that a student can partake at competition level for certain sports, such as weightlifting, but can't do the activity for GCSE? I feel it's unfair that expensive, "for the masses" sports are on the list, but other, more accessible sports aren't.

action: Review the car insurance industry and car insurance premiums
background: We think the Government should review why car insurance companies change insurance policy quotes depending on seemingly unrelated factors. Eg start date in 4 weeks time, quote may be a lot cheaper than starting the next working day, and why a quote can vary depending on when you search.
additional_details: Car insurance is a legal requirement so we feel insurance Vehicle companies have too much power over UK drivers young and old. Want to drive ? Need insurance ? Then pay the price we think is extortionate for the privilege as its a legal requirement, unlike other insurance policies Eg Home Insurance, which are not required under UK Law.

action: Introduce minimum age and driving experience for emergency response drivers
background: Restrict the age of emergency response drivers (such as police officers) to person's over 25 with 3 years driving experience to prevent accidents involving police vehicles.
additional_details:
Police vehicles driven by young officers with limited experience and could cause harm to members of the public and damage to police vehicles that are subsequently replaced by tax payers money.
Currently a police officer can attend an emergency response driving course as long as they have a valid driving licence. This means in theory a driver could be expected to advanced standards with little driving experience. We think this is unfair to the officer.

action: Review assessment of and guidelines about ARFID in ASD children
background: We think how children with ASD are assessed for Eating Disorders such as Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) should be reviewed. We think the review should consider how weight loss is monitored and the guidelines followed in Schools & Hospitals, to identify issues beyond fussy eating.
additional_details: We think the currently guidelines for Schools or Hospitals to treat or manage ARFID are poor. Children could lose their lives to malnutrition when they could have been peg fed before deterioration got worse. Eating issues may be blamed on the disability / cognitive disorder (fussy Eating) and not treated as a separate medical condition. I have started this petition in Memory of Alfie who sadly passed away at aged 7.

action: Actively drive a decrease in the amount of ultraprocessed food eaten in UK.
background: I want the government to promote better health and to RESIST lobbying by powerful food industries who fool us all into eating ultra-processed foods which damage our health and increase levels of obesity, diabetes, heart disease, strokes and other harms. Food labelling needs improvement and honesty.
additional_details: Advertising is effective. It’s propaganda. Low in fat/sugar/salt!) are misleading and fool many people that they are doing the best for their health. Research has proved that high fat diets are NOT bad. High starch diets ARE. action: Cut the excessive announcements on train journeys.
background: Ensure that Train Operating Companies reduce the number of on-train announcements to the same level as they were in Year 2000 or earlier.
additional_details: The frequency and repetitive nature of on-board train announcements has now reached an intolerable level. Being told the same thing multiple times per journey is un-necessary and unwelcome noise pollution. It particularly affects older people who have less capacity to filter out unwanted noise. People should be left in peace during journeys.  At the very least, a quiet coach should be provided on every service where passengers can escape from the unwanted noise.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about how many announcements to give on individual train journeys are a matter for train companies, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Make Nakba education part of the national curriculum
background: I believe the recent war in Gaza is a wake up call to the dehumanisation of Palestinians and injustices they face. I propose to make teaching about the Nakba part of the national curriculum. I believe this will help ensure this never happens again and will help Palestinians to finally have justice.
additional_details: I think it is important for future generations to learn about injustices Palestinians have faced throughout history since the 1948 Nakba. By teaching this aspect of history to future generations, I believe it will hopefully stop the dehumanisation of Palestinians and Arabs/Muslims to an extent. I propose that Nakba education covers the 1947 UN partition of Palestine, Britain’s role in the Israeli Palestinian conflict and how many Jews living in Arab countries moved to Israel because of the Nakba.

action: Talk Up Britain
background:
Apolitical in ideology, and pragmatic in its expression, 'Talk Up Britain', aims to:

- Foster national pride and a collective identity
- Showcase the countries world-renowned capabilities
- Promote investment across the country and in education 

To improve confidence and growth in the U.K.
additional_details:
Parliament plays the central role in talking up Britain because it serves as the legislative and representative body that shapes public discourse, national policies, with the necessary reach to galvanise public support and actions.

This collective effort can help create a more resilient and optimistic society, ultimately benefitting the nation as a whole.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: The Sperrin Mountains (Northern Ireland) is a national park; preserve & protect.
background: By recognising The Sperrin Mountains as a national park opens up opportunities for local business, in an historically underfunded region, to develop, thrive and provide valuable insight to how to manage, preserve and protect similar ecosystems globally.
additional_details: I urge this government to define it's commitment to the natural environment. Nothing less.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Northern Ireland Executive and Northern Ireland Assembly is responsible for. 

In Northern Ireland, the designation of land as a National Park is the responsibility of the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (DAERA), which is advised by the Council for Nature Conservation and the Countryside. 

If you want to raise this issue you could raise it with the Northern Ireland Executive.

You can find contact details for the departments of the Northern Ireland Executive here: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/government-departments-in-northern-ireland

action: Fund the NHS to employ Blood Bikers
background: Currently, blood bikers, a much needed service, are in many areas funded by way of charity. If the NHS needs this service so much, then we think it should be delivered by the NHS, and funded by the tax payer.
additional_details: We think an NHS trust awarding a £14m contract for a private company  that included the same work in 2019 is not fair. It was estimated it saved the trust £100,000 a year to have volunteer blood bikers do this work, however we think it would be more beneficial to the economy if these workers were paid an hourly wage rather than be volunteer run. We think it would also benefit the NHS and it is unlikely to cost £14m in wages!

action: Hold local elections as planned and protect our democratic rights.
background: The unwritten nature of Britain's constitution places special responsibility upon Parliament to protect our democratic foundations. This petition urges Parliament to debate the critical issue of electoral timing to ensure our democratic institutions remain robust and protected from manipulation.
additional_details: A delay in scheduled elections undermines democratic principles and citizens' right to choose representatives. Leaders who can postpone elections may abuse this power when facing opposition or declining popularity. Electoral delays damage public trust and lead to civic disengagement. History shows such delays often precede democratic backsliding. While emergencies may require adjusting voting methods, the fundamental right to vote at scheduled intervals must be protected.

background: Require specific qualifications in Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) in order to work with children with SEND in schools. This includes contracted school staff and agency support staff. If currently working with SEND, school to provide appropriate training.
additional_details: Provide general training in basic SEND. Allocate funding for schools to provide appropriate training for staff. Allocate funding for agencies to provide training for staff.

If fines are in place for people who don't chip their dog people will think twice about not doing it! Random checks on the streets should be done by pcso's or police and carry a microchipping device

action: Regulate the housing market more strictly
background: We call on the Government to regulate the housing market and end predatory mortgage practices. Enact stricter laws, ensure fair mortgage practices, align housing prices with conditions and wages, provide rent subsidies or reduced mortgage rates for essential workers, and prevent exploitation.
additional_details: Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights guarantees respect for private and family life, including the home. We think current mortgage laws often undermine this right. We think landmark cases like Manchester CC v Pinnock recognized the need for protections, but inconsistencies remain. We think the housing crisis in London exacerbates the issue. We think we must ensure fair housing policies to prevent exploitation and support key workers. We think the government must address the unregulated real estate market, which has spiralled out of control, making it impossible for young people to afford decent living conditions or purchase property due to skyrocketing and unrealistic prices. We think these measures will uphold human dignity and provide a stable living environment.

action: Decrease the speed limit on country roads for the protection of animals
background: Decrease the speed limit on country roads to reduce the number of animals killed by cars, which could also reduce the number of accidents. This could also help the conservation of rare species that are frequently killed by vehicles, such as muntjacs and red squirrels.
additional_details: We think there are too many native species that are being killed due to the changing environment around roads and highways. We are concerned that that fast drivers could endanger certain species. We think slowing down vehicles would give animals/drivers more time to react and also reduce the amount of dangerous crashes caused by people driving fast on small roads.

action: Form a Special task force to irradicate the Grooming Gangs

They should prosecute the individuals irrespective of the Political Stature

Since this issue has been around for more than a decade, clearly there is some coverup going on by local agencies it may be due to corruption or political pressure. Hence existing agencies are not able to produce the results for benefit of the society especially in this regard. 

This task force should launch nationwide enquiry with the support of our Prime minister and the citizens who look up to our government to resolve such issues.

action: Give the Chagossians a referendum vote on their sovereignty.
background: The Chagossians should be able to decide what happens to their islands. They’ve not been given a chance to vote on becoming part of Mauritius. They have a right to self determination. The UK government should set up a referendum that asks islanders and descendants of islanders what they want.
additional_details: The Chagossians deserve the right to self determination. They should be able to choose what happens to their islands in a democratic referendum. They should be able to decide whether they want to be independent, become part of Mauritius, or remain a British Overseas Territory. So far they’ve not been given a choice on their future. Instead they’ve been forced to be a part of Mauritius without anyone asking the Chagossians if they’d like this. Many Chagossians have stated they don’t want this.

action: Require all social media companies to allow infinite scrolling to be turned off
background: We think the Government should require all social media companies currently providing services in the UK to provide users with a means of deactivating so called ‘infinite scrolling’.
additional_details:
Limitless scrolling is designed to ensure that social media users maintain their use for as long as possible.
We think there are many issues with this form of social media design including:
-Mental health issues
-Users losing productivity and track of time
- Decreases in attention span
- Physical health problems (poor posture and eye issues)
- Ethical issues including exploitation of users and influence of opinion by algorithms.
 
We think by allowing users to turn these functions off, users gain the control.

action: Regulate & License the Non-Surgical Cosmetic Sector
background:
To provide inclusive regulatory standards and licensing for non-surgical cosmetic professionals who offer treatments and services such as; 
dermal filler injections, toxin injections, fat dissolving injections, invasive cosmetic treatments - i.e laser treatments, chemical peels.
additional_details:
Introduce a licensing scheme which covers - recognised accreditation, best practice standards and mandatory business requirements, without excluding skilled practitioners and professionals. 
  
We think all individuals and businesses (medic and non-medic) should be held accountable to these regulatory requirements - To help minimise treatment related complications and inadequate standards from any unlicensed individuals or businesses who continue to performing invasive treatments and services unregulated.

action: Raise the age of digital consent from 13 to 16
background: Raise the age for digital consent from 13 to 16. GDPR contains specific protections for children – defined as under 16 years of age – such as stating that consent when processing a child’s data can only be obtained with parental authorisation.
additional_details: We do not believe that the majority of children, at the age of 13, appreciate the consent given to companies when granting permission to handle their data. As parents are legally responsible for their children's actions at this age, we believe it seems wholly inappropriate that children should be given the responsibility at such a young age. GDPR contains specific protections for children - defined as under 16 years - but the UK lowered this to the age of 13 when UK GDPR was introduced.

action: "Increase Sentences for Child Rapists to Protect Our Children"
background: "We call on the UK Government to significantly increase the minimum and maximum sentences for child rapists. This would ensure sentences reflect the severity of their crimes, provide justice for victims, and act as a strong deterrent to prevent further harm."
additional_details:
"Child sexual abuse is one of the most heinous crimes, causing lifelong trauma to victims and their families. However, current sentencing often fails to reflect the true gravity of these offenses, leaving survivors without the justice they deserve.
Raising the sentences for child rapists will send a clear message: Such crimes will not be tolerated in our society.We urge the Government to implement harsher sentencing guidelines to protect the most innocent members of our society—our children."
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/715556

action: Legal requirement to test and record blood group at birth for medical records
background: I would like there to be a legal requirement for blood group to be tested at birth. This would then be on our medical records for life. I would also like there to be an official card people could carry stating their blood type so it is easy to access along with our medical history.
additional_details: Many people don't know their blood group unless they need to for medical reasons or have given blood. In an emergency where someone needs a blood transfusion, blood has to be taken and tested. Valuable time and money is wasted in this process. Carrying a card (as diabetics do, for example) or accessing medical records with blood types recorded could save lives. A card could also be kept visible at home, as other medical emergency information often is, in case a medic/ambulance attends the home.

action: Review and reform Cafcass to address systemic failings and protect families
background: We think Cafcass fails children and families, showing a lack of balance, ignoring evidence, and enabling abusers. Section 7 reports may be inaccurate, professional assessments dismissed, and complaints ignored. Victims may face retraumatisation, while staff may make harmful decisions.
additional_details:
We think urgent reform is essential.
 
We think Cafcass consistently fails children and families with unbalance reports, dismissed evidence, and enabling abusers through recommending co-parenting. 
These failures may cause delays in support, trauma for victims, and emotional distress for families. We think the Government must reform Cafcass to enforce accountability, improve staff training, and prioritise children’s welfare. We think families deserve a system that safeguards their rights and well-being, not one that exacerbates conflict and harm.

action: Commit to continuing to fund the Employment Support Scheme
background: Commit to continuing to fund the Employment Support Scheme for people with disabilities. Guarantee that anyone receiving support via the scheme will continue to do so for the while they remain in their current role.
additional_details: The Employment Support Scheme is a vital scheme which supports disabled people in work. Without this scheme in place some of the most vulnerable people in society will be faced with losing their jobs through no fault of their own. The government should strive to ensure that disabled people currently in employment remain employed. The scheme has been closed to new participants since 2006 so the costs for the government will decline in future when existing participants leave the scheme

action: Remove people on the terror watch list from the UK
background: In 2020, the Home Office said there were over 40,000 people where MI5 judged there was some risk of them re-engaging in terrorist activity. We think people on this list who are in the UK should be deported, to keep people in the UK safe.
additional_details: People in the UK should be safe in their own country and we think having potential terrorists among us isn’t safe. We feel we are under threat. We think we should not have to live like this, and that the government has a duty to protect the people of this country.

action: Amend Article 6 of the Human Rights Act to ensure a fair trial for Victims
background: Unlike defendants, whose right to a fair trial is a Human Right with legal consequences when breached, breaches of the Victims’ Code carry no legal consequences. We think this leaves victims unsupported. We think equal rights are essential for fairness.
additional_details: Victims may face delays, mishandled evidence, and systemic failures that deepen their trauma. Without enforceable rights, we think they remain vulnerable and inadequately supported in a system designed to protect everyone. Amending Article 6 could ensure victims have a right to a fair trial and are treated equally, and with dignity. We think this critical change would restore trust, hold institutions accountable, and address the systemic imbalance that we feel silences victims while safeguarding offenders. We think equal rights are essential for justice.

action: Remove Permitted Development rights for HMO property up to 6 unrelated persons.

We believe neighbours have a right to know what is happening in their streets. In many cases there is currently NO consultation process for neighbours.

action: Stop the 30m mast in Headless Cross Protect our community & reject 24/01177/TEL
background: We urge the Government to stop the 30m mast in Headless Cross (24/01177/TEL) by National Grid, which offers no public benefit. action: Enforce maximum donation limits for individuals and corporations to any party
background: Too many billionaires are influencing the outcomes of elections for their own personal gain and profit. Maximum donation limits should be introduced for individuals and corporations so that the election and campaign processes remain democratic.
additional_details: Australia have been exploring the idea of donation limits and this proposal is inspired by these suggestions. Any individual may donate a maximum of £20,000 to a single candidate. An individual or corporation may not donate more than £600,000 per election cycle. Alongside this, any donations above £1000 should be openly and publicly recorded for transparency. This will ensure that no British political party is influenced by any one benefactor.

action: Give the Chagos Islands to the USA
background: Now Britain no longer has an Empire, we think we should gift the Chagos Islands to the USA. They already use the naval base there but we think they could potentially then also build a space-port for sending rockets to Mars. The islands are close to the Equator.
additional_details: The United States is our closest ally and we already share intelligence and cooperate on defence and much else. We believe space exploration is going to be very important this century and beyond. Working with America and perhaps sharing access to a new space port, we could participate in these developments. We believe this would benefit British and American industry. It could also create jobs in the Chagos Islands. We believe it would be a win-win situation all round.

action: Do not introduce digital driving licences
background: We do not want the Government to introduce digital driving licences, and we would like to preserve the card and paper form that already exists as we believe it is sufficient. We believe this could be a slippery slope to compulsory digital ID, etc.
additional_details: We want the Government to stop the introduction of digital driving licences and keep the existing system in place, which we think works well. We believe it would be a cost burden on an already burdened public, and could be the first steps on a slippery slope to compulsory digital ID.

action: Define what an MP’s job is.
background: I want the government to define what they are paid to do (other than making laws and applying taxes, particularly what a local MP is accountable for and what their actual job is.
additional_details:
An MP is elected to office and paid, paid to employ staff but with no job description and no compunction to assist their constituency at all.  

I believe there should be a basic job description to which an MP’s performance can be measured against eg responding to constituents’ requests, supporting local issues and acting in the benefit of their own constituents.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/713100

action: Stop Excluding Names Starting with Q, U, X, Y, Z: Name a Storm After Them
background: I want the government to update the storm naming system to include names starting with Q, U, X, Y, and Z, ensuring all letters of the alphabet are represented in the naming process. This would promote fairness, inclusivity, and diversity in storm naming conventions.
additional_details: Names starting with Q, U, X, Y, and Z are currently excluded, which feels unfair. Including them would make the process more balanced and ensure everyone feels represented. Updating the naming system to include all letters would show a commitment to fairness and equality, ensuring the process remains consistent.

action: End the UK’s membership of the World Health Organisation

action: Extend the closing date of the Plug-in Van and Truck Grant beyond 31 March 2025

action: Add the subject of post-partum mental illness to the national curriculum
background: Outline post partum depression, and other mental illnesses that can happen before, during and after pregnancy/birth. We think this could happen either at the end of sex education talks or through mental health awareness talks.
additional_details: We believe this could help reduce maternal suicide rates as suicide continues to be the leading cause of direct maternal death between 6 weeks and 12 months post partum. To raise awareness of this and to educate pupils on signs and symptoms, where to go for help, which services would help and lessen the burden and worry on new parents. action: Nationalize all utilities and public services currently owned privately.
background: I believe that the government should nationalize all utilities and public services currently owned privately. Through the process of asset forfeiture.

action: Stop airport expansion: halt all airport expansion plans across the UK
background: More than 20 airports across the UK have expansion plans, which will result in a combined increase of 60%+ capacity. More flights means more emissions, at a time when we should be doing everything we can to reduce emissions and avert climate catastrophe.
additional_details:
More flights also mean more noise and air pollution, which is linked to poor physical and mental health for those living near airports.
 
The Climate Change Committee says there should be no net airport expansion unless aviation is outperforming its emission baselines. Local people and politicians oppose airport expansion plans, but central government can overrule their decisions.
 
We think airports are big enough. Stop airport expansion.
government_response_summary: The Government supports airport expansion where it promotes economic growth, aligns with climate commitments, and meets strict air quality and noise pollution requirements.
government_response_body: UK connectivity is vital to supporting jobs, opportunity, and businesses across the length and breadth of the country. The government is committed to securing the long-term future of the UK’s aviation sector, and if the UK is to remain competitive as a global leader in aviation, it is crucial that aviation infrastructure remains world-class.  Capacity constraints are hindering the ability of UK aviation to grow – which means demand will outstrip supply. The Government therefore supports airport expansion where expansion proposals can demonstrate that they contribute to economic growth, can be delivered in line with the UK’s legally binding climate change commitments and meets strict environmental requirements on air quality and noise pollution.  Airports support regional and economic growth. This Government has granted additional capacity at Gatwick, London City and Luton, with other airports, such as Leeds Bradford and Stansted, also taking forward expansion plans.  Heathrow is operating at full capacity, putting UK connectivity, competitiveness, and the benefits of a hub airport at risk. A hub airport enables global connectivity, attracting international investment, boosting trade, and sustaining routes that would not be viable without transfer passengers – thereby amplifying the UK’s role in the global economy. As rivals like Istanbul and Frankfurt expand, the UK risks falling behind. To secure Heathrow’s future and support growth, the Government is therefore assessing proposals for a third runway.  Following the conclusion of the assessment process, the Climate Change Committee will be engaged throughout the review of the Airports National Policy Statement (ANPS), ensuring independent oversight and advice during the process.  We understand people will have environmental concerns. The Government is actively investing into innovation in making aviation more sustainable, to ensure that we can achieve net zero aviation by 2050. Key initiatives include the introduction of a Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, a Revenue Certainty Mechanism to encourage investment in UK SAF production, and £63 million in funding for 2025/26 through the Advanced Fuels Fund to support domestic SAF supply – with more funding committed across the next Spending Review period. The UK will also set out detailed plans for meeting legislated carbon budgets later this year as part of its wider approach to fulfilling climate obligations.  Efforts are also underway to deliver quicker, quieter and cleaner air travel through airspace modernisation. This includes consultations on designing more direct and efficient flight paths.  To support the transition to low and zero carbon aircraft, the Aerospace Technology Institute (ATI) Programme is backing innovation in next-generation sustainable technologies. As part of the Industrial Strategy, up to £2.3 billion has been allocated over 10 years to extend this programme.  In terms of noise reduction, measures such as noise abatement procedures and night flight restrictions are in place at major airports, including Heathrow. Alongside the use of more modern quieter aircraft, these steps have contributed to a reduction of up to 40% in areas affected by significant noise levels and a decrease in population exposure of up to 37%.  Sustainable aviation growth remains a priority. Airport expansion plays a key role in this, supporting job creation, attracting investment, and maintaining the UK’s position as a global leader in aviation.  Department for Transport

action: Raise statutory maternity/paternity pay to match the National Living Wage
background: Statutory maternity and paternity pay is £4.99 per hour for a full-time worker on 37.5 hours per week - approximately 59% less than the 2024 National Living Wage of £12.21 per hour for workers aged 21+, which has been set out to ensure a basic standard of living.
additional_details:
If the National Living Wage is £12.21 per hour to legally enforce and ensure a basic standard of living, why is statutory maternity or paternity pay just £4.99 per hour?

We feel that working parents, especially women, who contribute to the tax system are being pushed into poverty at their most vulnerable time. We believe this undermines family stability and suggests the Government does not prioritise childbirth or its economic value.
government_response_summary: Parental pay entitlements are intended to provide a measure of financial security to parents to care for their child(ren).  However, they are not intended to replace earnings.
government_response_body: The Government recognises the importance of parents having time away from work to care for a new child in their family. This is a key part of our plan to Make Work Pay, which aims to improve the quality and security of work. Parental leave and pay entitlements include Maternity, Paternity, Shared Parental and Neonatal Care Pay, as well as Adoption Leave and Pay, all of which are designed to support parents to take leave whilst retaining an attachment to the labour market so they can return to work when appropriate.  Maternity pay is primarily a health and safety provision for pregnant working women, providing a measure of financial security during this important time.  There are two types of maternity pay available to pregnant working women: Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), paid by employers and Maternity Allowance (MA), paid by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) to eligible women (including the self-employed and women in employment who are not eligible for SMP). The qualifying conditions for both SMP and MA are based on a woman's recent employment and earnings.  Both SMP and MA are paid for up to a maximum of 39 weeks. For SMP, the first six weeks are paid at a weekly rate equal to 90 per cent of the woman's average weekly earnings, with no upper limit, followed by up to 33 weeks at the lower of either the standard rate or 90 per cent of the woman's average weekly earnings. MA is paid at either the standard rate or 90 per cent of the woman’s average weekly earnings, whichever is the lower, for a maximum of 39 weeks.  Paternity Leave and Pay arrangements enable eligible employed fathers and partners to take up to two one-week blocks of leave, either consecutively or separately, during the first year following the birth of their child or placement for adoption. Paternity Pay is paid at the statutory rate.  The Government has set an aim to deliver a genuine living wage for every adult worker; the increase to the National Living Wage (NLW) to £12.21 is intended to make progress towards that. As this petition highlights, this payment is higher than the equivalent hourly rate of Maternity/Paternity Pay. However, Maternity and other types of Parental Pay are intended to provide a measure of financial security to support parents whilst they are away from the workplace; they are not a replacement of earnings and therefore are not directly comparable.  The Government understands the importance of ensuring statutory payments are set at the right level. The Secretary of State for Work and Pensions is required by law to undertake an annual review of benefits and State Pensions, including statutory pay. This is based on a review of trends in prices and earnings growth in the preceding year. From April these payments were uprated in line with the Consumer Prices Index of 1.7 per cent, with their standard rates increasing from £184.03 to £187.18 per week. This means that the benefits retain their value against inflation.  When considering calls to increase the level of parental benefits, the Government must balance a range of factors including the needs of parents, the impact on employers, and affordability for taxpayers. This is particularly true in today’s challenging economic climate. As such, any changes would need to be carefully considered, taking into account views from businesses and other stakeholders.  This petition has raised concerns that working parents, especially women (and by association, their child/children) are being pushed into poverty at their most vulnerable time. The Government recognises the financial pressures facing many pregnant women and new mothers and has measures in place to support them and their families. Maternity Pay is just one element of the support available. Indeed, depending on an individual’s circumstances, additional financial support, for example, Universal Credit, Child Benefit, and the Sure Start Maternity Grant (a lump sum payment of £500), may also be available. More information about benefits and financial support available to pregnant women and their families can be found on www.gov.uk via the Childcare and Parenting link on the home page.  Delivering the manifesto commitment to tackle child poverty is an urgent priority for this Government, and we will bring forward a Child Poverty Strategy as soon as possible.  In addition, this Government is taking a mission-based approach to raise the healthiest generation of children ever and ensure that every child has a healthy, happy start to life. Giving children the best start in life means delivering accessible, integrated maternity, baby and family support services through the 1,001 days from conception to age two.  The Government also committed in the manifesto to review parental leave to ensure that it best supports working families. Planning is underway and further details of the review will be announced in due course.  Department for Work and Pensions

action: Require pickup of packaging boxes by companies making repeat deliveries
background: We want the government to pass legislation that requires corporations/companies which deliver to the same addresses on a regular basis (defined as more than twice a month) to pick up and recycle their own packaging.
additional_details:
Nearly 4 billion packages were shipped in the UK in 2024, more than double the number shipped ten years earlier. The reason for this staggering increase is the growth of internet companies.
 
Many companies deliver regularly to the same addresses, and we think it would be easy for them to pick up and recycle their used packaging, as is already done by progressive companies.

action: Allow Gluten-Free applicants to join the British Army
background: Change the ruling on (otherwise fit and healthy) gluten-free applicants being classed as unfit in army applications.
additional_details: Gluten-Free ration packs aren’t available in the Armed Forces whilst other special dietary requirements (ie. Vegetarian) are being catered for. We think the Armed Forces should be able to accommodate the people who would be otherwise eligible to serve their country.

action: Introduce mandatory life sentences for child sex offences
background: I would like harsher sentencing introduced for what are the worst of all crimes in my opinion. I feel that child sex offenders are treated with leniency and this feels to me to be a grave injustice.
additional_details: I personally feel that sexual crimes against children are the most serious of all. I believe that Britain has a rich tradition of justice and leading the world in ethical matters.
