action: License all animal rescues in wales
background:
I want the Welsh government to review animal welfare in Wales and license un-registered rescue's to improve the care of these animals and prevent animal cruelty and neglect. 
Currently anybody can call themselves a rescue with no liscense, no checks and no conformity to animal welfare.
additional_details:
I would like to start this petition as this is a subject that has personally affected myself and family pet.
Sadly in Wales anybody can take animals in and call themselves a rescue with no regard to the animals welfare as there are no welfare checks in place for these animals.
I believe all rescues should be liscensed and have checks to prevent the growing problem of abuse and neglect along with financial 
transparency as many of these "rescues" abuse these animals for personal financial gain.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Welsh Government and Welsh Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.

The Welsh Parliament has its own Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Welsh Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.senedd.wales/

You may also wish to raise this issue with your local Members of the Senedd who represent you. You can find out who your Members of the Senedd are and how to contact them here: https://senedd.wales/find-a-member-of-the-senedd/

action: Stop Geo-Engineering Experiments to Dim the Sun
background: We want the government to stop experimentation, as we have not given consent.
additional_details: We did not vote for this or give consent.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701963

action: Require MPs & Councillors to have minimum 5 yrs employment in industry/commerce
background: Anyone standing to be elected as an MP or Councillor, including County Councillors, should be required to have a record of five years of employment in industry or commerce.
additional_details: We believe too many of them now come straight from school or university, and have little or no experience of industry or commerce. We think this is insufficient knowledge or experience to demonstrate their ability to make social or industrial/commercial decisions.

action: Introduce free bus passes at age 60 in England, like Scotland, Wales and NI
background: We want the Government to allow people in England to get a concessionary bus pass at age 60, as they do in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. This would improve fairness, support older people’s wellbeing, and encourage greater use of public transport.
additional_details: At 60, many people face health challenges, financial strain, and social isolation. In Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, free bus travel helps people stay connected and active. England’s older citizens deserve the same support and fairness. Providing free bus travel from age 60 would help people stay engaged, reduce isolation, ease financial pressure, and promote the use of greener, more sustainable transport, benefiting both individuals and communities, improving quality of life.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702845

action: Give licenced security officers specific powers under the law
background: We think licenced security officers should have powers to use force to retrieve stolen items and deny entry or evict persons from premises. We also think they should also have search powers to find items they believe to be stolen, in bags, pockets and inside clothes.
additional_details: We feel that the current powers that licenced security guards have are simply not enough. There has been an increase in shoplifting recently, and we think security officers do not have the powers to effectively deal with offenders. We think this common sense change in the law will help prevent shoplifting.

action: Make property transactions legally binding at the point of an accepted offer.
background: When purchasing a property in the UK the transaction should become legally binding when the seller accepts and signs a purchase agreement and returns it to the proposed buyer. The agreement may include contingencies, which can be negotiated and outlined in the contract.
additional_details:
In the UK, roughly one in three (approximately 35%) of property sales fall through. 

From working in the industry, I have seen how people place offers on multiple properties with no real intention of proceeding. Purchasers who do proceed have the right currently to walk away at the last minute, which can leave people in financial difficulty and, at worst, homeless. The decision to make such a large decision that affects more than one involved party should be regulated to minimise these effects.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721744

action: Legally classify the creation & use of sexual deep fakes as sexual assault
background: We think that if a person creates a pornographic deep fake it should be classified as sexual assault, as AI use is rising and the use of deep fakes to depict women and girls performing sexual acts is on the rise.
additional_details: We think sexual deep fakes should be classed as sexual assault because they violate a person's consent, autonomy, and dignity. In our view, victims experience real trauma, humiliation, and emotional harm, similar to physical sexual abuse. We think the intent is to sexually exploit or degrade without permission, weaponizing someone's body and identity. Even without physical contact, we think the psychological damage mirrors traditional forms of sexual violence and deserves equal legal recognition and protection.

action: Keep the fundamental protections for nature provided by the Habitats Regulations
background: Keep the Habitats Regulations and supercharges nature restoration protection. This is the most important and fundamental protections we have to safeguard our nature and wildlife, which is threatened by the new proposed Government bill. We should be protecting our natural habitat not destroy it.
additional_details: We are 89 seconds to midnight on the doomsday clock. We should be doing everything in our power to protect our natural environment, bees are on the decline, 30% of bird’s in the UK are at risk of extinction but the Government is continuing to destroy our habitat for profit, which we can all see. Climate change is the most important agenda for our survival and the Government is continuously threatening this. The UK has been stripped of its nature. Action is needed to protect our precious nature.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action: 

Stop the Planning and Infrastructure Bill 2025 to Protect Nature
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726174

action: Prohibit disclosure of pre-trial therapy notes in sexual assault investigations
background: We want the government to amend the law on disclosure to prohibit access to pre-trial therapy notes of sexual assault survivors. We think that for these survivors, usually women and girls, the justice system is appalling and extremely challenging to navigate and they face restrictive rules.
additional_details:
We feel they're unable to fully address trauma with therapists while an investigation is still ongoing.
 
We think survivors deserve the right to speak freely about their experiences, even as investigations are underway, and not risk having this used against them in the court of law. We believe the law fails to consider survivors' mental health and their emotional recovery, and that sharing stories is a crucial avenue for healing, that should not be used in the courtroom against women and girls.

action: Capital punishment for officials guilty of treason, corruption, misconduct
background: We believe for too long our government and institutions have had officials who don't have the country's or the public’s best interest at heart. We think serious action is needed to prevent treason, corruption, and misconduct in public office. Those found guilty should face capital punishment.
additional_details: We think people in positions of power face no consequences for their actions and they often get pay rises, knighted or peerages despite their failings. In our view, anyone in a position of power should face capital punishment if found guilty of treason, corruption, or misconduct in public office.

action: Abolish the Energy Profits Levy
background: We think this punitive tax is dismantling the UK’s offshore oil and gas industry, especially in Scotland, accelerating job losses and forcing early decommissioning, despite oil now trading at a lower level
additional_details: We think the EPL is fiscally reckless and industrially destructive. In our view, it was introduced during a short-lived price spike, it now persists even as oil trades at a lower level. Investment has collapsed, viable fields are being shut down, and many skilled UK jobs are vanishing. We think we are dismantling a world class industry for no gain. We think the tax is harming energy security, communities, and the economy. We think it must be abolished now, before more permanent damage is done.

action: Legislation that keeps the public safe from dangerous, out of control dogs.
background: Determine whether an individual dog poses a risk to the public, that MUST be based on their ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR not what they look like or measure . It defies logic to believe a dog’s appearance, shape of head, breath of chest has any influence on behaviour, temperament and propensity for aggression.
additional_details:
That flawed belief is dictating laws related to public safety. There is no evidence to support the existence of "inherently dangerous" dog breeds.
Would you feel safer living in a community that protected you from dogs that posed a real danger based on their actions or dogs or an invalidated stereotype? Actions of owners need to be held accountable. We should look at responsible ownership, education and strict penalties for owners of dogs that abuse them and purposely train aggression.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions which call for similar action:

Reform the Dangerous Dogs Act (DDA) 1991: keep the public safe
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702953

Reform Dog Laws: Licensing & Mandatory Training Instead of Breed Bans
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/716062

action: Require all phone numbers be added to a public register
background: All phone numbers, including those of mobile phones, should be added to a public register.
additional_details: We think this will help prevent spam calling and scamming, as people could report numbers and check for the history of any scam/spam numbers.

action: Immediate review and reform of the education system
background: We want an education system that is more student-centred and holistic, with a greater focus on mutual respect, socialising, mindfulness, freedom for teachers, individual strengths, emotional development, positive reinforcement not punishment, and equal opportunities.
additional_details:
We believe the current education system is outdated, performance led and test heavy, and provides a "one-size-fits-all" education, failing pupils, parents/carers, staff and communities. We think the current system fails to nurture the talents and abilities of a diverse range of individuals.

Schools should be inclusive, nurturing and confidence building institutions where needs and struggles are validated and children are able to express themselves

Put children first!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703964

action: Words Are Stronger Than Weapons: Diplomacy time, before another chance is lost.
background:
We call on the UK Government to strengthen its diplomatic engagement in support of a peaceful resolution to the conflict in Ukraine, using its global standing and moral authority to champion a shift toward negotiations. 

Diplomacy, pursued early or late, remains the only sustainable solution...
additional_details:
Let’s be honest — the current path isn’t working
This isn’t idealism. It’s realism

The perpetuation of conflict often serves political interests at others’ expense

When diplomatic solutions were within reach, they were delayed or dismissed. 

Future opportunities must not be missed again.

The broader context was never one that offered clean victories

Britain always has stood not only as an actor, but as a conscience — a voice willing to speak when silence is easier

This moment has come now!
rejection_details:
We understand that you're concerned about the war in Ukraine but we're not sure exactly what you'd like to happen.

You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the UK to seek to start peace talks with Ukraine and Russia: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702643

action: I call for halting of chemical weather experiments designed to "dim the sun"
background: I urge the Government and Parliament to enact legislation prohibiting all chemical solar dimming experiments. They must impose an immediate moratorium on proposed geoengineering trials, ensuring no chemicals are released until comprehensive, independent environmental+health assessments are completed
additional_details: I believe no large-scale geoengineering should proceed without explicit democratic consent. Dimming the sun through chemical spraying affects every community, ecosystem, and generation. Yet the public has not been informed, consulted, or given any say. Government has a duty to represent its citizens’ interests and guard against unilateral decisions by scientists or private entities.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701963

action: Reform Child Maintenance Laws to Close Loopholes  used by Non-Resident Parents
background: I want the government to reform the Child Maintenance Service by closing loopholes that let parents avoid paying. Support should reflect the real cost of raising a child, not just income. There must be minimum contributions, proper enforcement, and asset checks.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/717395

action: Allow a majority of the electorate to pass a vote of no confidence in Government
background: Parliament should debate and take a vote based on the will of the people as demanded by the number of signatures to the petition.
additional_details: Because a Government could obtain a General Election victory based on unfulfilled promises or simply could be incompetent in office.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

You might like to sign this petition:

Call a General Election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700143

action: Criticism of RELIGION must not be criminalised in a secular state.
background: In a secular society all religions must accept that their worldview will be examined and criticised in open dialogue and debate. This government must make a commitment to protect free speech as regards a citizen's right within a secular society to examine and criticise any religion or ideology.
additional_details: This petition is needed because the government is set on a course of action that could by default censor the British public's ability to openly examine or criticise a religion. This governement is creating a council that would draw up an official definition of ‘Islamophobia’ of which the next step would be the potential to impose a blasphemy law.  A secular society cannot allow critique of a religion to be branded as hate speech or racism. The government must protect free speech, not censor it.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

The Government have said that they are not going to introduce blasphemy laws:
https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2024-12-18/debates/ba455fa1-fb15-4e1b-b4c9-884dfdaeb83e/CommonsChamber#contribution-76ACDC1C-F8FF-4664-AA99-BE235577FE72

It is therefore unclear what further action you would like the Government or Parliament to take.

action: Fund more support for children with SEN & allow term-time holidays
background: I want the government to fund more schools for children with SEN, and activity provision. I want more school places. I want leave granted e.g. One weeks term time leave for SEN children. I want more places e.g. Play centres, activities for SEN children after school.
additional_details:
Children with SEN can find holidays too busy. They may not be able to access places in busy periods. We think there should be other options for children during term time to have a break and go on holiday. It’s not fair that other children have a break but SEN children may not have the same opportunities. 

Play centres can be miles away, and there isn’t enough school provision.

action: Change the working week to 30 hours full time
background: Establish full time hours as 30 hours per week instead of 37.5 hours with no penalty on pay.
additional_details: reduce full time hours from 37.5 hours to 30 hours per week
rejection_details: There is no legal minimum when deciding what constitutes "full time hours". It is up to individual employers to decide what is classed as a full or part time contract.

action: Establish a Public Portal for Victims of Mistaken Criminal Identity
background: Create a secure, voluntary portal for people wrongly linked to criminal records due to name confusion, allowing them to prove their innocence and protect themselves from harm, while ensuring privacy and data protection.
additional_details:
My life has been severely disrupted by being wrongly identified as a registered Sex Offender simply because of a shared name.
 
I have heard from others with similar stories and I believe a government solution would help protect innocent people from suffering such life-altering consequences.

action: Ban the sale of disposable BBQs during periods of high wildfire risk
background: We want to ban businesses from continuing to sell disposable BBQ equipment to the public while the business is located in an area with a high wildfire risk. At present, businesses sell these to consumers despite the real risk they can pose of starting wildfires when used irresponsibly.
additional_details: Disposable BBQs, when used irresponsibly, can cause wildfires during periods of low rainfall. Even though fire services across the country issue wildfire risk warnings of High or even Extreme, these BBQs continue to be sold, and they can spark avoidable wildfires. If a business is located in an area designated as high wildfire risk, they should be prevented from selling them until the risk has passed.

action: Ensure MP's provide clear and direct answers to questions, without evasion.
background: I’d like the Government or Parliament to make sure that MPs give clear and honest answers to questions at the dispatch box, rather than avoiding them or using vague language. The speaker must set standards and force them to answer.
additional_details: It’s important that the public can trust what’s being said and feel confident that politicians are being open and transparent.
rejection_details:
It’s about something that the UK Government or Parliament is not directly responsible for.

We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker personally, and the Prime Minister is responsible for answers to questions.

action: Ban Holiday Companies from charging Higher prices in the School Holidays!!!!!
background: The government needs to ban holiday companies from doubling and tripling their prices for trips and flights during school holidays. It is shocking that nothing has already been done about this. Families are struggling to afford to take their children on holidays especially abroad due to increases.
additional_details: Doing this will improve school attendance for many children as parents will no longer feel the need to have to take their children out of school during term time because of extortionate prices in school holidays. Holidays are beneficial for families mental health and wellbeing and therefore making them the same price as during term time will make it more accessible for all families and people. This includes for teachers as well as due to their work load they deserve holidays but can’t afford it.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban holiday companies raising prices in school holidays.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700540

action: Do not house illegal migrants in private rentals, deport them immediately
background: Don't house illegal migrants in private rental accommodation. Instead, I want the government to immediately return them to their home country or last safe country they travelled from. I think they've no right to enter via boats or other means without applying for and achieving a warranted visa.
additional_details: I believe not many people want illegal immigrants in the UK and that it's costing taxpayers when the country is already on its knees. I think there's not enough social housing for the British population as it is, many of whom may be forced to privately rent at extortionate prices, if they’re even able to afford it. Some veterans are living on the streets, and some are suffering with mental health after serving and giving their all for King/Queen and country. I believe that they deserve to be put before any illegal immigrant. I don't think it is fair that illegal immigrants receive the support and accommodation that they do, at taxpayers' expense.

action: Exclude pre-marriage assets from divorce settlements in England and Wales
background: In Scotland generally only assets acquired from the date of marriage up to the date of separation are considered in divorce settlements. This is not the case in England and Wales, where a spouse can be granted rights to assets - such as pensions - acquired before marriage. We want this to change.
additional_details: We believe it is unfair that people who are divorced in England and Wales, with financial assets acquired before their marriage, can be disadvantaged compared to people in Scotland when it comes to divorce settlements. We want pre-marriage assets to be excluded from divorce settlements in England and Wales, to mirror rules in Scotland.

action: Apply for the UK to rejoin the EU fully - do not just 'reset' the relationship
background: I think the UK needs to rejoin the EU fully for maximum economic benefit and to restore influence rather than merely 'reset' relations.
additional_details:
A 'reset', Customs Union or Single Market membership may offer some advantages but I think full EU membership alone can provide the growth, security and global standing we need.

As the UK faces economic challenges and global uncertainties, I think it is more important than ever to work jointly with European partners. I believe rejoining the EU would increase and strengthen the economy, enhance international cooperation, improve security, and help protect the UK against external pressures.

I think partial measures fall short of what is needed. Only full EU membership ensures stability, influence and security.
government_response_summary: Britain will stay outside the EU, but we must make Brexit work. In May, the Government announced a new strategic partnership with the EU which will deliver economic and security benefits for the UK.
government_response_body: Britain will stay outside the EU, and we will seize the opportunities of Brexit to make it work.  The Government was elected last year with a clear and emphatic mandate to strengthen our relationship with the EU but which committed to not rejoining the EU, the single market, customs union or returning to freedom of movement.  Since taking office, we have reset our relations with European partners to improve the lives of working people and make the people across the UK safer, more secure and more prosperous.   On 19 May, following the first ever Summit between the UK and the EU, the Prime Minister announced a deal with the EU and a renewed agenda for UK-EU cooperation, which will deliver on what the British public voted for last year. This deal is good for bills, good for jobs, and good for our borders. The package agreed at the Summit delivers for the public by providing greater security via a Security and Defence Partnership, which will allow for closer defence industrial collaboration by unlocking the opportunity to access the EU’s €150bn SAFE fund.  It will increase safety for UK citizens through strong borders: we have taken a significant step towards a comprehensive migration partnership and will boost our relationships with key EU agencies, supporting information sharing to tackle crime and working together on returns of irregular migrants.  Finally, the deal we have struck will boost prosperity through removal of trade barriers through an SPS agreement, energy efficiency through cooperation on electricity trading, and a cheaper transition to net zero through linking our Emissions Trading Schemes. The deal will reduce costs for businesses, meaning better prices and more choice to consumers.  The deal means the UK has unprecedented access to the EU market – the best of any country outside the EU or EFTA, and by 2040 the agreement will deliver a £9 billion boost to the UK economy.  Our new relationship will also ensure that we remain influential on the world stage in addressing global issues through e.g. our membership of NATO, G20 and G7.  Being outside the EU also allows the UK to agree economic and trade deals with other countries, as the Prime Minister announced in May with the US and India, which will provide further economic benefit to the UK.  Cabinet Office

action: Make Firms in receipt of public funds Subject to Freedom of Information Act 2000
background: To make it a legal requirement of firms who receive public funds to answer FOIs
additional_details: All money's spent by the government showed be accounted for to the public
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/717120

action: Establish an Independent Review of NHS Extraction-Based Orthodontics
background: We call on the Department of Health and Social Care to commission an independent review of any potential long-term health effects of extraction-based orthodontic treatment provided through the NHS, and to review clinical guidelines and consent protocols related to such treatment
additional_details:
Extraction of teeth can be part of orthodontic treatment. Some research has suggested links between this and the risk of long-term health effects.
 
We request a formal, independent investigation into the long-term health outcomes of NHS-funded extraction-based orthodontics, including a national patient registry and longitudinal study.

action: Create new background checks for jurors on sexual or domestic abuse trials
background: We urge the Government to change the law so that jurors on any trial for sexual assault, rape or domestic abuse undergo background checks. Any juror who has been a victim or know victims should be disqualified, as we think they may be biased when deciding the verdict.
additional_details: We feel that many innocent young men have been convicted of sexual assault and rape of ex-partners. We are concerned that the lives of some people and their families have been destroyed by false allegations.

action: Require companies to cap price increases to 20% during school holidays
background: We want the Government to make it law that holiday companies can only raise prices by a maximum of 20% during school holidays. We feel families are currently unfairly charged because they are limited to travelling in school holidays. We feel it would make access to holidays fairer.
additional_details: Families with school-age children are often forced to travel during school breaks and holiday companies raise prices, in our opinion by huge amounts. We think this makes holidays unaffordable for many, leaving only wealthier families able to go away. We think a 20% cap would stop such large price hikes, making sure all families have a fairer chance to enjoy a break together. We feel holidays are important for family time, rest, and creating memories, and they shouldn’t just be for those who can afford massive extra costs.

action: Ban nurseries charging fees when closed and cap fees
background: We want the Government to ban nurseries charging parents childcare fees when they are closed and cap daily fees.
additional_details: We feel that there are limited nursery places available, which means working parents must accept whatever the nursery dictates in their terms and conditions, even if they feel it is unfair. This includes paying for bank holidays when nurseries are closed and even general closures at nursery's discretion. We feel that childcare is so expensive that this could discourage many from working as they would be better off financially, by not working. We also want the Government to cap daily fees for private childcare so nurseries don't offset this limit by raising prices.

action: We call on Government to urgently revise the mobile phone in schools guidance
background: We believe schools cannot meet statutory safeguarding duties under ‘Keeping Children Safe in Education’ while allowing students to carry smartphones. Smartphones pose risks including distraction, sharing harmful content, cyberbullying, and non-consensual photos and recording of students and staff.
additional_details: We ask for a clear distinction between non-internet mobile phones and smartphones - with reference to smartphones the removal of the option d ‘never used, seen or heard’ as statutory guidance, unless a medical need. We ask that schools list smartphones as a prohibited item and allow only basic non-internet phones for parent contact where necessary. We believe the current guidance is unenforceable, compromises student safety and undermines a schools’ ability to uphold their legal duties.

action: Do not ban level 7 qualified non-medical aesthetic practitioners from practising
background: We want the Government to recognise level 7-qualified non-medical aesthetic practitioners as competent and safe when making decisions relating to the 2023 consultation on the licensing of non-surgical cosmetic procedures in England.
additional_details:
We don't want retrospective bans. We want regulation based on training and accountability. We also want there to be a transitional period before any changes commence and further consultation of all parts of the industry before any changes are implemented. 

Thousands of professionals—mostly women—trained under frameworks like the level 7, investing years of work and savings. They opened clinics, signed leases, and many are sole providers for children. We want to ensure they are not banned from practicing which we think would be unjust and negatively impact mental health and stability.

action: Introduce a Minister for Deportations at the Home Office
background: Introduce a dedicated Minister for Deportations at the Home Office, with their own team and budget, focused solely on deportations.
additional_details:
We believe our borders are out of control, that the volume of immigration is unsustainable, and that we need tough and decisive action.
We have had enough of what is, in our view, the Government's failure to deal with legal and illegal immigration.
We think we need a dedicated Minister for Deportations who will work solely in this area of Home Office policy.

action: Ban the ownership of smartphones and camera phones for children under 16
background:
I call for the government to ban the sale of, or provision of smartphones, or camera phones to under 16s. 
This would be punishable by a £2000 fine, to the adult who provided the child with the phone. 
I call for the government to make it illegal for under 16s to hold any social media accounts.
additional_details:
Smartphones and camera phones are having a devastating impact on young people in Britain. Children have access to huge amounts of material online, a lot of which is harmful to the child exposed to it. 
There is an epidemic of issues related to internet usage and social media; cyber bullying, issues around sending and receiving sexualised images, unrealistic expectations around body image and appearance. 
Smartphones are damaging the mental and physical health of our children and adolescents.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban the sale, ownership and access to smartphones for children 16 and under
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/714201

action: Make UK rape laws gender-neutral under one section.
background: We want the law to treat all rape equally, no matter who commits it. Right now, women can't be charged with rape, only assault. This isn't fair. We want a gender-neutral law that gives all victims equal justice and matches international human rights standards.
additional_details: The current law only allows men to be charged with rape, ignoring that women can also commit this crime. Instead, women are charged with assault by penetration, a term that sounds less serious and is grouped under general sexual assault. This downplays the offence and its impact. Rape should be defined by the act, not the gender. To promote true equality and justice, women must be held to same legal standard, with offences treated equally in name, charge and consequence.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/706166

action: Make any sexual contact with an animal a criminal offence
background: We think the government should recognise gap in current law regarding bestiality and change it. They should make it law that any sexual act with an animal is illegal.
additional_details: Under Section 69 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, a person commits an offence if they intentionally perform an act of penetration with their penis on the vagina or anus of a living animal. However, the law does not cover other forms of sexual contact with animals, such as oral sex or digital penetration. Any sexual act should be consensual and animals are unable to give consent. This is animal abuse and the law needs to change.

action: Exempt people from paying National Insurance Contributions after 35 years
background: I urge the Government to exempt people from paying National Insurance after reaching the 35 years of NI contributions required to receive the basic state pension. I believe we should be able to stop paying after we have reached 35 years of NI contributions.
additional_details: I believe it to be the unfair of people still paying NI after they have achieved the 35 years. I feel the situation has been made more unfair by raising the state pension age. By the time I retire at 67, I could have paid 16 years more than the 35 years for full pension - that's 51 years NI paid as I worked since the age of 16.

action: Construct special parks for dogs
background: We are very disturbed by dog owners bringing their dogs to park where families and children, it is also disliked by us and that it should have own park or spacious places for pets, this is my final call
rejection_details: Decisions relating to local parks and whether dogs are allowed in them are matters for local authorities, not the Government or Parliament.

action: Increase funding for more frequent bus services connecting rural areas
background: I would like increased funding to add more bus services, and at greater frequency, in rural areas so people in such areas don't have to rely on cars to get to places, e.g. the nearest town and city or the nearest village with a shop. I think this should be prioritised over increased buses in cities.
additional_details: I think this needs to be done as many people may feel trapped and unable to go out without spending money on an expensive taxi service. In my view, cities have lots of buses that are becoming more frequent than ever. Some major towns and cities have services run to other major places up to every 10 minutes. However, in rural places with bus services, they may only run every hour or 2 hours which I think makes them less accessible to those who want to use the services and is just not fair.

action: Introduce an elected Supreme Court
background: Introduce an elected Supreme Court, so that the public can vote to elect the Justices to the Supreme Court, rather than them being appointed.
additional_details: We believe this would open the door to wider political representation and suffrage for the people. We think that if the public can vote in a government, then they should be able to vote in the members of the Supreme Court.

action: Ensure GCSE students have access to formulae and equation sheets post 2027
background: In recent years, students have been given formulae and equation sheets for GCSE exams. We believe that future GCSE students deserve equal treatment during their GCSE exams as those who have sat their exams in recent years, as their education was also affected by the COVID 19 pandemic.
additional_details: We think there needs to be equal resources.

action: Minimum pay of £15/hour for Care Assistants in the private sector and care homes
background: Long hours with little pay. We are Carers, nurses, advisors, friends, family. We endure heartache when your loved one's pass but we have to be brave and carry on. We think minimum wage is not good enough and we need higher rates of pay.
additional_details:
We think we deserve more recognition and more money as it’s a tough role.

Give carers the recognition that's needed. Pay us what we deserve. We feel we work long hours for very little pay. We think care assistants in the private sector deserve more money. We think the healthcare sector cry out for carers to look after your loved ones and charge thousands to live in care homes but yet we feel they don’t pay their carers fairly! We need more pay. We think minimum wage is a disgrace. We think we need a minimum of £15 per hour

action: Ban Digital Billboards in Cities to Reduce Light Pollution/Adverts & Save Energy
background: We call on the Government to completely ban digital billboards in our cities.
additional_details: We believe these energy-intensive screens waste electricity, pollute our night skies with light, and force constant corporate advertising into public spaces. We feel that everyone deserves access to darkness, peace, and freedom from this marketing.

action: Ban Live Facial Recognition (LFR) in all public and private spaces
background: We call on the Government to ban the use of Live Facial Recognition (LFR) surveillance in all public and private spaces. This includes by private companies and in retail spaces unless strictly for national security or immediate prevention of terrorism, with strict oversight and judicial approval.
additional_details: We think LFR is a disproportionate response to everyday crime and is expanding with little oversight, risking mass surveillance and loss of privacy. It was recently reported permanent LFRs were being installed in Croydon. As Snowden said, "Arguing that you don't care about the right to privacy because you have nothing to hide is no different than saying you don't care about free speech because you have nothing to say." We believe we must avoid risking civil liberty as the price of public safety.

action: Ban all disposable barbecues from sale in the U.K
background: Place an outright ban on all disposable barbecues, especially those using tin foil containers, in order to dramatically lessen the chance of wildfires occurring.
additional_details: The climate changes we see are already happening too fast for a lot of wildlife to adapt to, not only due to diminishing habitats, but also due to indigenous species migrating around the country and becoming predators to native species where there were none before.Wildfires have devastating effects, further destroying habitats. We have a responsibility not to add to it.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726390

action: Call a general election, as local results demonstrate need for change.
background: I'd like the Government to call a General election, as the recent local election results clearly show the public's growing discontent and desire for change. This would allow the country to have a say in its future direction and ensure the government accurately represents the people's will.
additional_details: The current government's policies and actions no longer seem to align with the people's wishes. A General election would provide an opportunity for the public to reassess the government's mandate and potentially bring about a more representative and responsive government. This would help restore trust in the political system and ensure that it is working in the best interests of the country.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Provide fulsome scientific elucidation behind sun blocking
background: Cooling a portion of atmosphere the size of the UK will draw an equivalent mass of southerly warmer air to the UK and conversely a mass of cooler air from the UK to warmer countries, as temperatures equalise. This creates the potential for an extreme weather event, typically hurricanes and flooding.
additional_details:
What thought has the government given to the following?
What will less Sun have on the nation’s physical and mental health? (eg vitamin D and rickets, depression, family cohesion).
How will this effects crop production in the UK and adjacent countries?
Has the UK consulted other countries?
Is the UK government prepared to pay reparation damages?
What are the names of all those proposing and implementing the idea?
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may wish to sign the following petition on the subject matter: 

Make all forms of 'geo-engineering' affecting the environment illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701963

action: Require all public buildings to display the Union Jack flag
background: We believe in celebrating and honouring the rich history and heritage of the United Kingdom. We think displaying the Union Jack on public buildings will serve as a daily reminder of our collective history, fostering a sense of pride and belonging among citizens of all backgrounds.
additional_details: We think seeing the Union Jack flying proudly would inspire patriotism and remind us of the values and traditions that have shaped our nation. By visibly showcasing our flag, we think we could strengthen our national identity and ensure that future generations understand and appreciate the legacy of the United Kingdom. Therefore, we respectfully request the government to implement a policy that encourages the regular and respectful display of the Union Jack flag on public buildings.

action: Require all PIP assessments & reviews be conducted by doctors
background: Currently people we think are under-qualified are carrying out PIP assessments & reviews. We feel this is unfair as PIP claimants should be assessed by practising doctors and in complex cases, specialist doctors, not occupational therapists, nurses, physiotherapists, paramedics, or pharmacists.
additional_details: All applicants and recipients of PIP are under the care of doctors, and often specialist doctors. Even with training, we think a nurse (for example) is not qualified to make a life changing determination on how an applicant's disability affects them. These are complex questions, and due to the importance of the decision, it is vital that they are assessed appropriately, which we feel the current system fails to do. We think this failure could be discriminatory to the disabled community.

action: Add a 'None of the Above' Option on Ballot Papers
background: I would like the Government/Parliament to include a 'None of the Above' box on ballot papers, so that a) the electorate has a formal way to express dissatisfaction with the available candidates and b) the voice of disillusioned voters is both registered and reported.
additional_details: By including this option, politicians and parties would no longer be able to ignore the discontent among voters who feel there is no viable candidate worthy of their vote. It would offer clearer insight into voter sentiment, ultimately guiding future candidates to better represent their constituents, and boost the integrity of our democratic process. Most importantly, it would hold politicians and parties to greater accountability and encourage them to work harder to earn our trust and support.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/703780

action:
Dissolution!
Call a General Election now!
background:
On July 4 2024, Sir Keir Starmer was elected as Prime Minister.
Since then, his Labour Government has introduced measures that were not included in the Labour Party's manifesto.
additional_details:
We, the people, have no confidence in the way the Labour Government has acted.
Pensioners and farmers have been directly affected by policies that were not included in Labour's manifesto.
We were deliberately misled and the obfuscation and deceit has only got worse since Starmer took power.
It is time for action.

There needs to be a dissolution of Parliament and a General Election called now!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call a General Election

action: Help end homelessness in Leeds
background: Homelessness is getting worse in Leeds. More people are sleeping on the streets or staying in places that aren’t safe. It’s really upsetting to see people with no home, especially in the winter. We think the government should do more to help.
additional_details: We want the government to give more money to Leeds so the council can build more homes and help people who are homeless. This could mean more shelters, support for mental health, and help for young people and families who are struggling. Everyone deserves a safe place to live. As well as provide a land for homeless people or people struggling for home to be able to set up camps as a temporary shelter.
rejection_details: You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: A statue of David Attenborough in the middle of Isleworth.
background: David Attenborough has become the Grandfather the UK and the World has needed, including me.
additional_details: Sir David Attenborough has created a world that has become more aware of the wild and given us the opportunity to learn and grow with the understanding of nature.
rejection_details:

action: Introduce a government-backed motor vehicle insurance provider
background: The government should introduce their own insurance provider specifically for the motor vehicle market to compete with existing insurance companies. We believe this could help improve the insurance market.
additional_details: The government should introduce their own insurance provider to help introduce newer competition with existing private insurance providers. We think that currently, insurance providers are acting in oligopoly type behaviour which we feel is causing a disservice to UK citizens. We believe a lack of strong competition means that insurance companies can set their prices to a level that is significantly higher than what would be allocatively efficient.

action: Increase UK investment in renewable energy
background: I call on the Government to increase UK investment in renewable energy like wind energy, so we don't have to use fossil fuels and harm the environment.
additional_details: I want the Government to do this so that we don't have to rely on fossil fuels and cause harm to our environment. I think we can save our world if we do our part.

action: Fund Solar Panels for not-for-profit leisure centres
background: We urge the Government to fund solar panels for non-for-profit leisure centres. We are concerned that leisure centres struggle with the cost of electricity bills, heating swimming pools and the running studio, and gym air conditioning, as it can mean less money to spend on staff and equipment.
additional_details: Many centres have a very large roof, which can be ideal for a large number of solar panels. We believe solar panels would be a one-off cost rather than a monthly handout. We believe this initiative can help leisure centres stay open, which can ensure continued investment in our mental and physical health whilst also helping the government move towards its net zero goal.

action: Assess Impact on UK Reputation: Reconsider Forthcoming State Visit.
background: The government needs to ensure that all state visits uphold the values of respect, international cooperation, and democratic principles. We request that any planned state visit that risks undermining these values be reconsidered.
additional_details: We urge the UK government to reconsider any state visits from individuals whose public statements or actions may compromise international relations, undermine democratic values, or cause harm to the dignity of the United Kingdom. We believe that state visits should only be extended to those who demonstrate a commitment to these fundamental principles.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.
We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.
You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Increase engine power limit for motorcycle drivers on CBT license
background: Allow CBT license holders to ride motorcycles that have more than 15bhp while still maintaining the 125cc engine size. We think 25bhp should be the maximum power allowed on a CBT license for those aged 17 and older.
additional_details: We think that 15bhp is an unsafe amount of power for a motorcycle. We feel it can be dangerous when turning onto roads with a speed limit of more than 40mph+ as some motorcycles cannot reliably reach the speed limit in time to ensure the rider can safely enter the road. We feel that 25bhp is a more reasonable limit as it will allow the motorcycle to reach the desired speed in time and minimises the risk to the rider and other road users and is also still manageable for inexperienced motorcyclists.

action: Require all vets to open at weekends
background: I think all vets should be required to open weekends, not just a few. I think this would avoid unnecessary pet deaths like my puppy. I think it's not fair and we should think of other owners.
additional_details: I believe that unnecessary pet deaths could be avoided if all vets open Saturday and Sunday. Animals have feelings too and it hurts to see them go, We think they don't deserve such a fate, they deserve help just like us humans. I’m not asking for a pet NHS. I'm just asking for all vets to be required to be open at weekends.

action: Call for general election 2025
background: This petition urges the UK government to hold a general election in 2025 to allow the public to decide the future leadership of the country. With growing public dissatisfaction over key issues such as the economy, public services, and trust in political leadership.
additional_details:
The UK is facing a crisis of leadership and public trust. Over recent years, the government has been marked by instability, scandals, broken promises, and a failure to address key national issues effectively — from the cost-of-living crisis and NHS pressures to housing shortages and environmental concerns.
Many citizens feel that the current leadership no longer represents the will or interests of the public.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700143

action: Reduce the 7-Year Route for UK-born children to apply for ILR to 3 Years
background: We call on the Government to reduce the 7-year wait to apply for ILR to 3 years for UK-born children, allowing them to apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain sooner. We believe this will ensure stability, integration, and fairness in line with their best interests and human rights.
additional_details: We believe the current rule delays stability, which may hinder access to education and healthcare. We believe a 3-year route aligns with children’s best interests under human rights law, fosters integration, and supports their right to a secure life in the UK, which may be their only home. We believe this change could benefit thousands, ensuring compassion and fairness in the UK’s immigration policy.

action: Allow years worked under an ICT visa to count towards eligibility for ILR.
background: I urge the Government to review the current regulations and permit the years worked under an ICT visa to be counted towards eligibility for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR). At present, time spent on an ICT visa is not considered in ILR applications.
additional_details: Research has shown that, due to the relatively high salary thresholds for ICT migrants most ICT workers are net contributors to public finances and provide significant value to the UK economy. There are minimal differences between the ICT and the Skilled Worker visa, which does provide a pathway to ILR. Furthermore, the ICT visa has now been phased out. Given these factors, it would be reasonable to allow the years spent under the ICT visa to count toward eligibility for ILR.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/715704

action: For the Scottish Government to fund and legally protect Scottish wildcats.
background: The Government to increase funding for us to help the Scottish wildcat, and the many threats that it is under. By increasing funding we can help the many problems such as habitat loss, diseases, hybridisation and killing of them. There should be more severe punishment for killing of this animal
additional_details: I am currently studying the Scottish wildcats and am amazed by the beauty of this amazing animal. I just want to help prevent the awful decline of this animal, with your help too.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.  
 
The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here:  

https://www.parliament.scot/chamber-and-committees/committees/current-and-previous-committees/session-6-citizen-participation-and-public-petitions-committee

action: Do not make a deal with USA and Trump, stand up for human rights
background: Do not roll back human rights to get a deal with USA and Trump. Align with Europe and Canada.
additional_details: Labour is rolling back human rights laws to get a deal with Trump and the USA. Don't do it. Work with Europe and Canada. Drop trump and make a stand.
rejection_details:

Thank you for your petition.

We are unable to accept your petition as we're not exactly sure what UK human rights legislation you are referring to, and what you mean when you talk about rolling back human rights. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do in relation to the UK-US trade deal.

Kind regards,

The Petitions Team

action: Recognise the Rights of Legal Migrant Workers
background: We work, pay taxes, and follow the rules — yet all legal migrant workers have no say in UK policies that affect our lives. We’re part of this country. It’s time we were heard. This is about fairness, dignity, and a voice in decisions that matter.
additional_details:
We ask the UK Government to:
1. Stop treating legal migrant workers as a silent group to be managed.
2. Clearly separate legal migrants from illegal immigration in all policy and public messaging.
3. Involve legal migrant voices, especially those without citizenship, in political and policy changes that directly affects their lives.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand you're concerned about the rights of legal migrant workers, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Require mobile network operators to provide PAC codes for previous 07 numbers
background: We urge the Government to pass a law which requires mobile network operators to be legally required to provide customers with PAC codes for previous 07 numbers upon request.
additional_details: We believe a mobile number is a critical commodity as it’s not only used for voice calls and text messages but for accessing critical applications such as messaging apps, banking apps, the NHS app and 2-stage authentication for accessing much more. We believe losing access to mobile numbers is a huge issue across the UK, and may cause severe stress, anxiety and an inability to access services without a recovery text being sent to the mobile number.

action: Election Manifestos of political parties must become legally binding contracts
background: The Parties publicly declare their policies that they promise to deliver if elected into office this is the Election Manifesto. There is no legal mechanism in place besides general/local elections to hold parties to account. Election Manifestos should be made into legally binding contracts.
additional_details: If an elected government, local council, elected mayor or assembly breaks the contract they've delivered to the electorate. The party in question should be taken to the British Courts, if found guilty the punishment should be a fine. The payment would be from the parties own funding and not from the tax payer to deter uk parties from purposefully deceiving the electorate. If political parties can’t abide by their manifesto promises then this should automatically trigger another general election.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724417

action: We would like the County name of Devon, to be changed back too Devonshire.
background:
We would simply like the name of the county of Devon, to be changed back too it’s historic and heritage rich name of Devonshire.

Seeing that Devon is not the true name of the county Devon.

Also the name Devon in itself, falls too showcase some of the best qualities and features of Devonshire.
additional_details:
The county name of Devonshire was change too Devon ,due too the Local Government Act of 1972 which we recognise as an important bit of legislation.

however we believe it was unnecessary to change the county name of Devonshire to Devon.

Devonshire is the proper name of the County of Devon too not recognised it , is not only a failure  too celebrate Devonshire unique  culture and history , it’s also a failure too recognise a part of unique British history heritage culture and traditions.

We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.

action: Review & modernise the GCSE curriculum to teach life skills & support students
background: We think the GCSE curriculum is outdated and ignores real-life skills. Many students also face tough home lives, like being young carers. We call on the government to review and modernise the system to be more relevant, inclusive, and supportive for all.
additional_details: We believe some students may experience depression and anxiety due to the GCSE system that we think is outdated. Some lack support at home, with parents who do not care or cannot provide guidance. We think the current curriculum doesn’t reflect the challenges we face. We think we need a modern, inclusive education system that prioritizes mental health, life skills, and support for all students to help us build a better future.

action: Mandatory that all dogs in public must be on a lead.
background: We need it law that all dogs in a public place be on a lead. Not just under control which is how it is at the present.
additional_details: We are fed up of dogs being mauled, people being bitten and the same thing coming out of people's mouths. It's ok, he/she is friendly. Our dogs are on a lead for a reason. We need a law to protect our dogs and children from out of control dogs. If they want off lead running, hire a dog field, keep us safe.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710271

action: Call for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister
background: We, the general public of Great Britain call on our MPs to put forward a vote of no Confidence in our current Prime Minister Kier Starmer. We are sick and tired of his lies and broken promises. We asked for change but we did not ask for him to make this country worse. Help your people now!
additional_details: We, the general public of Great Britain call on our MPs to put forward a vote of no Confidence in our current Prime Minister Kier Starmer. We are sick and tired of his lies and broken promises. We asked for change but we did not ask for him to make this country worse. Help your people now before he runs this country even further into the ground
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister.

action: Knowsley Council to Accept DVLA MOTs for Private Hire Vehicles.
background: Issuing national guidance or policy, if needed, to allow all councils flexibility in accepting DVLA MOTs during periods of high demand or local service disruption — to prevent loss of income and hardship for drivers.
additional_details: The current MOT backlog in Knowsley is forcing private hire drivers to wait months for tests, making them unable to work legally. This is causing serious financial hardship, many are losing income, falling behind on bills, and even facing eviction. Other councils accept DVLA MOTs, which are safe and reliable. We ask the Government to step in, ensure fairness, and allow DVLA MOTs temporarily so drivers can keep working and providing for their families during this crisis.

We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.

action: The UK must not sign up to EU Military Unification without a referendum.
background: The UK should not sign any agreement that commits the UK to the European Defence Fund (EDF) or Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO). Control of the UK’s military must not be transferred to Brussels in any form without a referendum.
additional_details: The prospect of EU military unification has neither been properly debated in Parliament nor presented to the British public. The full implications of the European Defence Fund (EDF) and Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO) are not widely understood in the UK. Before any agreement is signed, the UK government must ensure a transparent, open debate and put the matter to a referendum.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/717489

action: Set a cap or reduce amount car insurance company’s can charge new drivers
background: Cap the amount insurance company’s can charge or reduce the cost to make it more affordable for normal people
additional_details:
Affordable car insurance is essential for economic mobility and access to work.
In many regions, especially where public transport is limited, owning and operating a car is a necessity—not a luxury. If insurance prices become unaffordable, people risk driving uninsured (which raises costs for everyone) or being unable to get to work, education, or healthcare. This deepens inequality and limits economic participation, especially for low-income families, young drivers, and rural residents.

So, capping or making insurance more affordable isn’t just consumer protection — it’s an investment in economic inclusion and social mobility.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709463

action: Oppose cuts to PIP and prevent the introduction of a voucher system.
background: We call on the Government to halt proposed cuts to PIP and the introduction of a voucher system. These changes would harm disabled individuals, limiting independence and access to vital support. PIP is a lifeline that must be protected.
additional_details: We urge Parliament to stop the proposed cuts to PIP, as it is a crucial lifeline for disabled people. PIP is not work-related, and many recipients are in employment. The 0% fraud rate, according to the DWP, shows there’s no issue with misuse. Cutting PIP would force many disabled people out of work, making them more dependent on the state. These cuts would harm the independence of those who rely on this support for essential services, mobility, and everyday needs.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action: 

Stop PIP Cuts: Protect Support for Disabled People
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721918

action: Bring in first aid training in to all schools.
background: Every school should learn about first aid training as this is one of the main things in life that is needed on a daily basis
additional_details: This could save a lot more lives, Younger generation should be trained in schools so they can act on it straight away
rejection_details:
First aid training is already part of the health curriculum for schools, which you can see on page 37 + 38 of the curriculum guidance here:

https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1090195/Relationships_Education_RSE_and_Health_Education.pdf

action: Fund off-road cycle paths linking every village, town and city in the country
background: We want the government to fund and construct a network of off-road cycle paths linking every town, village and city in the country.
additional_details: We think the construction of these paths will allow all short distance journeys to be cycled safely. We also think this will reduce traffic on the roads for those who need to use them.

action: Provide funding so refuge spaces are free for all
background: We want the Government to ensure refuge spaces are free to anyone in need, regardless of income to enable everyone to find a safe haven when they need it. We feel that victims should not have to pay rent.
additional_details: People are in danger if they cannot be fully supported in a safe caring environment. No one should be financially ruined while protecting their family or themselves from abuse.

action: Provide funding to make all asthma-related medication free on prescription
background: We call on the Government to provide funding to make all medication related to asthma free of charge on prescription. This would include inhalers, pacers, and breathing treatments.
additional_details: Asthma is classed as a long-term and potentially life-threatening condition that affects thousands of people every day. Asthma attacks alone can cause people to go into respiratory distress and more. Without medication, people may be unable to control their symptoms, which may lead to hospitalisation and more stress on NHS staff. We believe having asthma medication free and available can help to prevent this as asthma medication can cost up to £50 total each month.

action: Increase funding for EHCPs to help address funding gaps in schools
background: We want EHCP funding to be increased for schools. For some, funding doesn’t cover the support required in the EHCP. We think that funding shouldn’t be based on banding but actual costs. EHCPs must fully fund staff, therapies, equipment, and training to meet a child’s needs effectively and lawfully.
additional_details: We believe funding doesn't effectively cover the full cost of supporting a SEND child. In some cases, minimum-wage learning support staff can exceed funding offered, this is without extra costs like therapies, training, equipment, and resources. Some schools are left struggling to meet legal obligations without adequate support. We believe increased EHCP funding is urgently needed to ensure proper care and inclusion.

action: Criminalise breaking election promises for public office, no maximum sentence.
background: To make Politicians personally liable for their public statements and put no limit on the legal recourse should any political figure make promises then U-turn as soon as they assume office. In the real world this is often dealt with in the sales of goods and services act.
additional_details: To bring honesty back into British Politics. Think and analyse before you shout your mouth off at the electorates expense.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724417

action: Permit Private Hire Vehicles Access to Bus Lanes in North Somerset
background: Require all councils including North Somerset to allow all licensed private hire vehicles (PHVs), not just taxis or minibuses, access to bus lanes to ensure fairness, reduce congestion, and align with neighbouring authorities’ policies.
additional_details: North Somerset’s policy is discriminatory, outdated, and inconsistent, excluding standard PHVs from bus lanes while allowing others. This causes confusion, increases congestion and emissions, undermines trust, and may breach the Equality Act. It disadvantages disabled passengers, fragments transport, and ignores best practice seen in neighbouring councils. Immediate reform is essential for fairness and safety.
