action: Dogs should be on a lead in all public places.
background: To make it a law that dogs must be on a lead in all public places,there are secure fields available to hire to train dogs,the increase in dog attacks are awful and unfair as the police don’t do anything if there are no witnesses.
additional_details: My chihuahua was attacked while on a lead by 5 dogs who were off leads that the woman couldn’t control,it was terrifying I still have nightmares and had my two on a lead.i had turned round and was a good distance away and they attacked with no sniffing at all.this has traumatised me and the woman denied it and goes about her weakly life with her dogs as  if nothing has happened and the police and dog warden did nothing.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710271

action: Launch an inquiry into online disinformation on social media platforms
background: We call on the Government to launch a public inquiry into social media disinformation, focusing on foreign state influence. We want the inquiry to look into the impact that disinformation has on the views of the general public.
additional_details: We are concerned about social media’s influence, and a lack of transparency. We feel it may be leading to widespread disinformation that is altering the general public’s views.

action: Require energy companies to offer analogue meters
background: We want the Government to require energy companies to offer analogue meters for those who cannot have or do not want smart meters.
additional_details: Smart meters emit electro magnetic frequency radiation (EMFR), there have been reports about meters linked to fires, inaccurate data and we are concerned about cyber security. Some people report being too sensitive to EMFR to live with smart meters and others simply do not want them. It is not a legal requirement to have a smart meter but we feel energy companies don't offer a choice when replacing meters.

action: Provide transgender people with more gender options on their birth certificate
background: We urge the Government to give the transgender community the option to identify as TF or TM as well as F and M on their birth certificate.
additional_details: As a transgender woman, I embrace the label of transgender woman to me as I believe it is a big part of my identity, and I would like to embrace that in every part of my life, including on my personal documents.

action: Launch a public inquiry into business rates and small businesses
background: We urge the Government to launch a public inquiry into business rates, including valuations of premises, and the impact on small businesses. We want the inquiry to consider any changes that might be needed in order to support the wider public and the economy.
additional_details: We believe action is needed to protect a larger number of small businesses, and the families, towns and cities that rely on these up and down the country. Many smaller businesses are struggling to survive due to many reasons, and one of them has been business rates. We believe a public inquiry could look at possible changes to the system that could help businesses up and down the country, which can ultimately support the local and wider economy.

action: Ban CEOs from external positions till their company is rectified.
background: To ban all CEOs who hold positions in external companies ( that undertake public functions) such as Boards,Committees and Consultancy Work. Until their organisation is fit for purpose.
additional_details:
Currently there are a number of organisations which the Government has stepped in and put the Organisation in Supervision or Severe Maladministration. As well as failings in Complaints Handling or managing its Finances.
Whilst this is going on the CEO is elsewhere. On Boards, Committees or Consultancy Work picking up an additional income. This needs addressing where they should only be allowed on these positions when their own 'house' is in order.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Exempt first time buyers from stamp duty
background: We urge the Government to remove stamp duty for first-time buyers to allow them to get onto the property ladder. Many first-time buyers have to cope with inflation and rising costs of properties, which are extremely difficult, and then pay stamp duty on top of hard-earned money saved after tax.
additional_details: We believe doing this may not only mean that first time buyers will be able to finally purchase a property, but it could give them an incentive to start a family, which could help the economy in the long run.

action: Require all doctors to receive perimenopause training & GPs to have specialists
background: We urge the Government to require all doctors and UK medical students to take mandatory perimenopause training and ensure every GP practice has at least one senior medical staff member trained to support, listen to, and properly help women experiencing perimenopause.
additional_details: We believe more doctors must be educated on the symptoms of perimenopause. Affecting a significant amount of the population, perimenopause can place immense physical and mental strain on women. It can deeply impact relationships, careers, and every part of life—yet many women say they are not heard or helped. We believe this must change.

action: Petition to End Excessive Drop-Off Charges at UK Airports
background: We call on the UK Government to abolish excessive drop-off charges at all UK airports. Passengers already pay Air Passenger Duty in their ticket price—charging extra to access terminals is unfair, exploitative and must be stopped.
additional_details: Parliament should require the Department for Transport and the Civil Aviation Authority to regulate airport drop-off charges. This includes capping fees, mandating a minimum free drop-off period, and ensuring transparency. Airports must justify any charges and offer exemptions for disabled passengers and families. Legislation should prevent airports from using access fees as a hidden revenue source, ensuring fair treatment for all travelers already paying Air Passenger Duty.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: 

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724381

action: Scrap six-year time limit for claims in Overseas Operations Act
background: We feel this time limit unfairly discriminates against veterans who may need more time to come forward with claims — especially in cases involving PTSD, delayed diagnoses, or where evidence surfaces later.
additional_details:
We feel it discriminates against those who served in overseas operations compared to those who served at home or in non-combat roles abroad. We believe that tragically, and ironically, it targets the very people who put themselves in harm’s way to protect the rights of every other citizen. We feel that if it wasn’t so serious and disrespectful, it would be laughable.

We are calling for Part 2 of this Act to be scrapped — not amended, not delayed — scrapped. We believe that justice must be equal for all, or it is not justice at all.

action: Protect Online Privacy – Ban Charging Users to Reject Tracking Cookies
background: Make it illegal for websites to charge users for rejecting tracking cookies. Businesses should not exploit consent by forcing users to choose between paying or having their data tracked.
additional_details: We feel the rise of cookie paywalls undermines genuine consent, pressuring users into accepting invasive tracking to avoid payment. Data privacy should not come at a financial cost. People accessing information should not be penalised for protecting their personal data. Other models, such as exclusive content or website memberships, should be considered for generating revenue. If users do pay reject tracking cookies, we feel there is no guarantee that tracking cookies will not be used.

action: REMOVE IHS SURCHARGE FOR VISAS WITH A RIGHT TO WORK FULL TIME
background: For the IHS surcharge to be completely removed for individuals applying for, or granted visas that allow them work full time in the United Kingdom. I would like parliament to discuss and subsequently vote on completely removing this surcharge for the visas in question
additional_details: This is because as a current or prospective full time employee, this individual contributes or would contribute into the nations pot through PAYE and NI just like any other individual who works part time, full time, or for whatever reason is unemployed and yet not expected to pay an additional fee to access the NHS. The surcharge is a double tax for individuals with visas  or applying for visas that grant them a right to work full time
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/714377

action: Ban dim the sun experiments
background: Ban dim the sun experiments
additional_details: Because it’s simple biology , less sun( there’s very little sun as it is in the UK !) less photosynthesis! The govt is still encouraging the covering of huge amounts of agricultural land with solar panels to produce electricity with sunlight! And now they want to dim it! Stop this  madness!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701963

action: Create an Autumn Bank Holiday in England & Wales
background: We ask the Government to decide on an Autumn Bank Holiday date and implement it for England & Wales.
additional_details: With 121 days between the August Bank Holiday and Christmas Day (25th Dec), this is the longest stretch in the calendar year without a Bank Holiday break in England & Wales. Giving everyone an Autumn Bank Holiday would even the spread of holidays in the year. The Government could allow the public or Parliament to decide what the Bank Holiday could be for, whether for Guy Fawkes / Bonfire Night, for mental health or something else.

action: Require all employers to provide sanitary products at the workplace
background: We urge the Government to require employers to provide sanitary products at the workplace. Many workers are caught off guard at work or unable to afford sanitary products which means that they may not be able to do their job properly due to being unable to contain the bleeding.
additional_details: While working, we believe the employer has a responsibility for employees and if employees are unable to afford the products needed, we believe the employer should support their employees and provide them with these products so they can do their job.

action: Lower the cost of car insurance for young drivers
background: All that young people ask for is a bit of independence, this being the cars we buy are affordable to run and sustainable for us to use. Car insurance prices are extortionate leading to a small percentage being able to pay. This is also another reason as to why there are so many uninsured drivers.
additional_details: Action needs to be taken as we can no longer keep this up, it cause us to either rely on public transport or taking other modes of transport which can cause you to be late as you have no control of the transport stopping for example or a bus terminating randomly.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709463

action: Legalise Cannabis Fully: Medical, Sale, Growing, Recreational
background: Legalise cannabis fully by 2025 for medicinal & recreational use, including growing, production, sale & adult use (18+). Regulate for safety, taxes, reduced crime & medical relief. Unlike decriminalisation, legalisation ensures quality & revenue. Act now for a safer, united UK.
additional_details: Current UK cannabis laws force medical firms to irradiate crops and use poor growing methods, harming quality and patients. Restrictive regulations create a framework which in term is leading to a medical firm monopoly, stifling legal companies and fueling a new black market. Full legalization by 2025 will enable safe, high-quality cannabis production, open opportunities for all businesses, and reduce illegal trade, fostering a united, thriving UK community with economic and social benefits.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action: 

Legalise recreational cannabis & release those convicted of cannabis offences.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707970

Introduce 'Grow Your Own' Laws for Legal Medical Cannabis Patients (CBPM)
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700860

Make it easier to obtain a licence to produce/grow medical cannabis
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725168

action: Change speeding penalties to 1point for up to 25MPH on a 20MPH road
background: We feel that the current penalty of 3 points for speeding in 20mph areas is disproportionate. We think the current penalty treats these drivers the same as other drivers who speed at much higher limits.
additional_details: In areas like London, drivers can be penalised for doing 24mph in 20mph areas, which we feel is heavily punishing. We feel it's easy to collect multiple 3 points penalties if drivers are making many journeys. We would like the penalties reviewed. Penalties can impact drivers insurance costs and can affect their ability to work.

action: Fund free Meningitis B & ACWY vaccines on the NHS for all
background: I do not think that private medical companies should be able to charge hundreds of pounds for Meningitis B & ACWY vaccines. I think they should be provided free for everyone of any age on the NHS.
additional_details: I believe that no family/friends should ever have to go through the pain of children and adults dying prematurely and completely unnecessarily simply because of lack of means to immunise due to high costs or due to failures of past governments to immunise the adult population. I am concerned that immunisation remains a luxury of the rich. This must end.

action: Be proud, fly the Union Jack,
background:
I would like to see our Great world renowned Flag flown from all council and government buildings that the Tax payer contributes to
All UK airports and ports 
I have visited many countries around the world and they all fly their national flag with Pride
Put the Great back into Britain
additional_details:
I believe that the people of this great nation feel that we as a country has lost its identity.  We have embraced change but at the same time lost our way.
The Uk has rich and amazing history  envied by other nations, one that we should learn from not be ashamed of  
Men and women have died in defending 
Show the world wave our flag 
If we as a nation can be proud of flag we will endeavour to strive  to make this great nation a prosperous and peaceful place to live Representation  is everything
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require all public buildings to display the Union Jack flag
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726537

action: Keep the Union Jack flags up all year round, particularly in Regents Street
background: The government and Parliament should discuss this to inject patriotism into the country and to remind the country of our past and current struggles.
additional_details: Place more Union Jack flags around the UK, in particular streets such as Regents Street to make everyone proud of our country.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726537

action: 25% reduction in council tax for those living alone is not enough
background:
It carries the assumption that 4 adults live in each house.
Each person is a burden to services, (potholes, fire prevention, libraries, police, etc) not each household. Council tax should be per person not per house.
additional_details:
It should not be up to each council, but decided by the government. Council tax is used to pay for local services and repairs, like waste disposal, libraries and education, police and fire departments, transport and highways and so on.
Also, single people don't put the bin out each time there is a collection if not full.
Single people, widowed, etc should not have to pay a higher amount than other people. The reduction should be 50% as a min. It should be paid by every adult not every house.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707636

action: Add Martial Arts ( karate) to the GCSE Pe
background: Add Karate to Pe GCSE
additional_details: I think that activities like martial arts are much more  popular than ever at the minute children partake in them from all backgrounds. I couldn’t believe the limitations of what students are allowed to chose. Why is it that a student can partake at competition level for certain sports, such as karate but can't do the activity for GCSE? I feel it's unfair and some of the activities on the list are unreal, I feel myself karate (Martial Arts)is straight forward to assess for GCSE sports
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Add boxing and martial arts to the education curriculum
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/715681

action: Add birth sex to special category data under GDPR
background: Under UK GDPR, special category data is personal data that needs more protection because it is sensitive. It includes "sexual orientation", which can protect gay people; this does not protect transgender people. We urge the Government to add birth sex to the list.
additional_details: A Supreme Court judgement found that a person's sex for the purpose of the Equality Act is their "biological sex" and that this describes sex at birth. We are concerned about how that information will be recorded and verified for transgender people. We feel making vulnerable groups easy to identify can increase the risk of harassment and discrimination. As with sexuality or religion, we believe birth sex should be "need to know", and protected from potentially accidental/malicious disclosure.

action: Ban songs about knife crime and violence on social media and music apps
background: Social media platforms and music apps may allow children to listen to music talking about knives and crime. I want a ban on music that I think glamorises this lifestyle.

action: Review and strengthen mandatory allergy training for all food industry staff
background: We want the Government to review and strengthen allergy training for all food industry staff, including front-of-house and kitchen roles, to ensure safe handling, clear communication, and better protection for allergy sufferers.
additional_details: We want to make the UK safer for allergy sufferers. Over 2 million people in the UK have food allergies, and even tiny traces can trigger severe or life-threatening reactions. We believe that improving the training staff receive would raise awareness, reduce risks, and help prevent future tragedies.

action: Make paternity tests compulsory before registering a birth
background: I call on the Government to require fathers to undergo a paternity test before registering himself as the father of the child on a birth certificate, and to only grant exemptions for exceptional circumstances.
additional_details: I am concerned about the possible abuse by mothers against fathers expressing their parental responsibility, and an increase in expenses for father attempting to prove their PR. We have retained Art 7, rights of child and we feel it is difficult to prove parental alienation by the mother. We believe this change will prevent and reduce paternity fraud cases and the caseload in family courts. We feel that currently, in practice, mother and fathers are not equal.

action: End pick up and drop off fees at airports.
background: Legislate against the charges that airports are imposing on people dropping off and picking up from the airports. The airport operators are taking advantage by charging ridiculous rates to use the pick up and drop off zones. You wouldn’t pay to enter a bus station or train station.
additional_details: I want the government to pass a law that prevents charges being made to access a travel facility to pick up or drop off. This is not about parking but simply about the ridiculous and ever increasing charges Airports are charging to pick up or drop off. I believe there should be a 10 minute free period and by all means charge for overstaying. But charging for what is a basic necessity when using air travel is absurd.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724381

action: Require all social housing flats to have a personal balcony/garden
background: We urge the Government to require all existing and newbuild social housing to have a personal balcony if above ground floor, as it can help reduce depression or help with future house swaps, as some house swappers may not consider sites with no balcony or garden due to a lack of outside space.
additional_details: We believe we must discuss social housing matters that impact people on a regular basis. We believe that by requiring housing associations and councils to make sure their properties have a balcony, or garden may help with people’s mental health, and that this is a step they should take. As I live in a flat with no personal outside space, this is my last option as many people on sites like homeswapper don't consider properties that don't have balconies; making it harder to find a swap.

action: Mandate Local Hiring and Restrict Offshore Hiring of workers
background: We urge the Government to create a law which mandates that if no qualified UK workers are available, companies must provide proof if they want to hire from abroad. Additionally, we call the Government to tax companies who recruit overseas and use the revenue to support retraining affected workers.
additional_details: We are concerned that some UK companies may be hiring offshore to cut costs, leaving many skilled British workers redundant or struggling for jobs. We believe relying on cheaper offshore labour depresses wages and side-lines local talent. We believe that ensuring priority for domestic recruitment and taxing offshore hiring when unavoidable can protect our workforce, restore fair competition, and support a robust UK economy.

action: Review Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill’s impact on non-school settings
background: Ensure the Bill does not require full-time non-school settings, including youth clubs, enrichment programmes, and religious or cultural centres, to adhere to the Independent School Standards if they are not providing full-time academic education in place of a school.
additional_details: We feel the Bill could unfairly classify youth clubs, enrichment groups, and cultural centres as schools, restricting their freedom to operate. We believe this would be an overreach that could limit educational diversity, harm community life, and goes against British values of freedom, diversity, and voluntary learning choices.

action: Reject the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill's proposals on home education
background: Do not pass any part of the Bill that introduces mandatory registration, monitoring, or oversight for home-educating families. Home education should remain flexible and free from excessive government control or interference.
additional_details: Mandatory registration would undermine trust, interfere with home educators, and ignore why parents choose home education: the right to educate freely without interference. This is a basic human right and parental responsibility, and it infringes upon British values of educational freedom and diversity. We understand that if a child requires social services, the government could intervene, but for mainstream families, we want no interference.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action: 

Remove CWS Bill clauses and provide tangible support to home educating parents
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/716515

Don't introduce unique child identifier and increased home education regulation
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702270

action: Stop the importation of honey bees into GB from the EU via Northern Ireland
background: We want the Government to close what we see as a loophole potentially allowing unchecked honey bee imports from NI into Great Britain. We believe full inspections, destination tracking, bee inspectors in NI, and prioritising local bee breeding are needed to help protect UK bee health.
additional_details: Since Brexit, we believe honey bee imports via Northern Ireland have bypassed established biosecurity arrangements, risking the introduction of devastating pests like small hive beetle and tropilaelaps mites. Imports from countries such as Italy and Malta may now escape full checks. We believe this threatens UK beekeeping, native honey bees and ecosystems. We think action is needed to prevent potentially serious pest outbreaks.

action: Raise a no confidence vote on Kier Starmer and the Labour government
background: Have a review the policies implemented by the Labour government and Kier Starmer.
additional_details: Each policy introduced by the current Labour government  seems to be against the British people and the people that voted them into power and needs to be looked into.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

You might like to sign this petition:

Call a General Election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700143

action: Fraud, Error and Recovery powers to monitor MPs’ and Lords’ bank accounts.
background: Expand the surveillance powers in the Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Bill to include the bank accounts, investments and financial holdings of all MPs and members of the House of Lords.
additional_details: To ensure a level paying field where fraud detection is applied equally.
rejection_details:
The powers in the Bill already apply to MPs in the same way as any other person (there isn't a carve out for them in the Bill), so it isn't clear what additional powers you want to add.

MPs are already required to declare financial interests, which you can see here

https://www.parliament.uk/mps-lords-and-offices/standards-and-financial-interests/parliamentary-commissioner-for-standards/registers-of-interests/register-of-members-financial-interests/

The failure to register a relevant interest could be a breach of the Code of Conduct for Members, which you can read more about here:

https://www.parliament.uk/business/publications/commons/hoc-code-of-conduct/

action: UK must play its role in preventing war between India and Pakistan.
background: Intervene and help to de-escalate tensions between neighbouring South Asian nations which are nuclear powers.
additional_details: India and Pakistan are former British colonies and members of the Commonwealth. Since gaining independence, they have fought several wars. Recent events have led to heightened war hysteria and marginalisation of voices of peace and sanity. Any confrontation between the two can bring about a nuclear conflagration with catastrophic human and climate cost. Indian and Pakistani ethnicities make up 3.1% and 2.7% population of England and Wales, respectively, who will be inevitably affected.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what specific action you would like the Government or Parliament to take. 

The UK Government has said that it is in contact with both the Indian and Pakistani Foreign Ministers, and is working closely with partners such as the US and the Gulf. The Government has said "Our consistent message to both India and Pakistan has been to show restraint. They need to engage in dialogue to find a swift, diplomatic path forward."

You can read more about this by looking at a recent statement from the Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State (Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan): https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2025-05-07/debates/E63F112D-D5FA-41D4-9C8A-E16575620A60/India-PakistanEscalation

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what specific action you would like the UK Government or Parliament to take.

action: Referendum to let the people choose whether they want early elections.
background: Let the people of the country decide whether they want Labour to continue their journey or whether it's time for a new political party to come into power and fix this country's immense problems through a democratic referendum.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/702341

action: Expand menstrual health education & early screening for conditions
background: I feel too many people suffer in silence from conditions like endometriosis and adenomyosis without knowing what they are. Some data suggests that in the UK 1 in 10 women are affected by endometriosis, it takes on average 8 yrs 10 months to diagnose, and only 50% of 16-24-yr-olds know what it is.
additional_details:
I want to see two changes:

Expand menstrual health education in the National Curriculum for schools and colleges, including teaching about conditions like endometriosis and adenomyosis, and encourage universities to teach this too.

Introduce routine screening for such conditions from age 14 to help catch these conditions early. Early detection can help prevent years of pain, misdiagnosis, and damage.

action: I would like to improve public transport
background: I would like the government to put more funding into our buses and to have more frequent buses as buses in the greater Manchester area never stick to a schedule and just come as they like.
additional_details: This would improve the lives of many and also help with the environment.

action: Require fresh produce to be labelled with pesticides used
background: We want clear labelling on fruits & veg showing what pesticides were used during growing and what treatments were added after harvest. We feel that consumers deserve transparency to make informed choices about what they feed their families and that it’s time for more transparent labelling.
additional_details: We’re calling on the Government to take action because we feel consumers have a right to know what’s on their food. We believe that without clear labelling, families are unable to know what pesticides are used. We think that transparency allows informed choices and enables them to make decisions about their health. We think this is a basic right, not a luxury.

action: Force TFL to Slash Fares and Make London Transport Affordable
background:
1. Force TFL to cut Tube, DLR, Overground, and tram fares by 50%.
2. Cut all adult bus fares by 25%.
3. Introduce a £3 daily cap for unlimited travel across all zones.
4. Ensure fares are reviewed annually and adjusted based on the cost of living.
additional_details:
Londoners are being priced out of public transport during a cost-of-living crisis, forcing many to rely on cars or skip essential travel. This harms work, education, and daily life.
We demand that the Government take immediate action to compel TFL to lower fares and make travel affordable for all.
Fair, reliable public transport is not a luxury — it’s a necessity for equality, clean air, opportunity, and a strong, inclusive economy.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. It is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly. 

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Ban baled tyre exports to protect UK tyre recycling
background: According to reports each year the UK has 50 million waste tyres that need recycling and around half of those are exported to India. We believe this is harming the UK recycling industry.
additional_details:
This has led to toxic emissions and carbon black waste, often violating environmental rules due to poor regulation, outdated technology, and weak enforcement—posing a serious environmental threat.

If we don't act now many UK tyre recyclers will be forced to close. We believe if this happens there will be no alternative but to rely on these exports which we feel are poorly run and inadequate.

action: Specialist Hospital Units for Vulnerable Young Adults with learning disabilities
background: Fund specialist hospital units for young adults with learning disabilities and additional needs, including autism, which offer them paediatric care to age 18 where clinically appropriate. The units should be sensory-considerate, ease the eventual transition to adult care and minimise distress.
additional_details:
We would also like parents or carers to be able to remain in the units 24/7, and for consistent, inclusive, compassionate care to be ensured across all NHS hospitals.

We think care decisions should be based on developmental rather than chronological age, with an emphasis on individual needs.

We believe these young people deserve care that respects their unique challenges. We think they need understanding, not assumptions. We think they need protection, not policies that in our view fail them.

action: Grant automatic guardianship to parents of 18yr olds who lack mental capacity
background: Under existing law, if you have parental responsibility for a child and wish to extend this when they turn 18, for instance if they lack mental capacity, you have to apply for guardianship.
additional_details:
For those who've had parental responsibility for a child and advocated for the child's wellbeing and health throughout their life, I want them to be able to continue guardianship of their adult child automatically without having to apply for it.
 
I'd like this to apply only to parents who've been actively involved in supporting their child's health and wellbeing throughout their life. I think they should automatically be granted continued guardianship where their child lacks mental capacity.

action: Create a national register of wills & require all wills to be registered
background: We call on the Government to create a government-backed national register of wills and make will registration mandatory in the UK. We are concerned that without this, a valid will may not be followed. We register births, deaths and property — we believe wills should be no different.
additional_details: Each year, many families apply for probate without knowing whether a valid will exists. The risk of lost, hidden or disputed wills can cause delays, distress, and legal battles. As will writers & estate planners, we’ve seen this harm first-hand. We believe a national register could offer clarity, reduce fraud, and protect legacies.

action: Stop the buliding of new houses on green spaces in Bratton area!
background: Stop the 1500+ house development on Bratton Farm (B5063). Prioritize brownfield sites over green spaces, protect Bratton’s rural character, and prevent overcrowded roads, schools, and services. Choose sustainable growth, not urban sprawl. Preserve our community and environment.
additional_details: It will worsen traffic, overcrowd schools, and strain local services. Our precious green spaces will be lost, harming wildlife and removing vital recreational areas. Bratton’s rural character will vanish, replaced by urban sprawl. Nearby areas like Shawbirch and Allcott are already struggling with overdevelopment. Instead, the government should use brownfield sites, ensuring sustainable growth without destroying farmland and green spaces.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Stop Clause NC21 from Erasing Legal Recognition for Transgender People
background: We call on the UK Government to reject Clause NC21 of the Data (Use and Access) Bill. which would force public authorities to prioritise sex assigned at birth over legal gender, irrespective of whether a GRC is issued.
additional_details:
Clause NC21 would strip trans people of privacy, dignity, and recognition in essential services, records, and identification.

For many trans people — especially those awaiting or unable to obtain a GRC — this clause threatens to forcibly out them and deny them access to services, protections, and legal equality. 

It could impact our safety, our families, and our right to exist without surveillance or erasure.

This is not about data accuracy  it's about control, exclusion, and harm.
rejection_details: New Clause 21 of the Data (Use and Access) Bill was voted down on 7 May 2025: https://votes.parliament.uk/votes/commons/division/2016

action: Ban travel insurance premium hikes & refusals for people in clinical trials
background: Ban travel insurance companies vastly increasing premiums, or refusal to cover people who partake in clinical trials, which may make it impossible for them to travel without resulting in substantial additional costs.

action: Provide funding for a nationwide, nature-rich river corridor network.
background: Support farmers and landowners to make space for water with more, easily accessible funding schemes. We call on government to commit to providing financial incentives to help farmers create & maintain connected land along all river corridors (with buffers, wetlands, riparian tree planting) at scale.
additional_details: Many UK rivers are heavily altered from their natural state & can have difficulty handling our changing environment. This can have potentially disastrous consequences for people & nature. For rivers to provide us with essential benefits, we think they urgently need space to recover. Connected, natural areas of land along river corridors can offer this space, and could help to: restore rivers; improve water quality; offer flood/drought resilience; boost biodiversity and help safeguard food production.
government_response_summary: We are investing in ELM schemes, supporting buffers, wetlands, tree planting and river restoration. We are protecting or restoring 20,000 kilometres of watercourses and investing in flood protection.
government_response_body: As a result of the June 2025 Spending Review, Defra secured a strong financial settlement. We are directing over £7 billion directed into nature’s recovery. This includes environmental farming schemes, tree planting, and peatland restoration. We recently published our revised Environmental Improvement Plan 2025, on Monday 1 December, which is backed by newly announced funding of £500 million for Landscape Recovery (LR) projects. These will make a significant contribution to the Environment Act and statutory net zero targets, including improving water quality, air quality, and spaces for wildlife so biodiversity can thrive, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions.  Our Environmental Land Management (ELM) schemes include the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI), Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier (CSHT), and LR. SFI includes an explicit action (BFS6) that pays for establishing and managing a minimum of 6 metres up to 12 metres wide strip beside watercourses. This has detailed rules on eligibility, management and evidence and with advice on establishment and ongoing maintenance.   The CSHT provides a number of grants which support farmers/land managers to enhance their environmental habitats, including watercourses. This includes actions such as:  •	CSW25, which directly supports the management of riparian and water edge habitats.  •	CSW12, which allows rivers to flow naturally across the floodplain to deliver benefits for biodiversity, flood and drought management and climate adaptation and wetland actions on fen, reedbed and wetland mosaics.  •	CWT13, which supports management and restoration of fen, reedbed and wetland mosaics. CWT14, which supports the creation of fen, reedbed or wetland mosaics.   More information about CSHT actions and how to apply can be found here. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/countryside-stewardship-higher-tier-csht  For habitat strips next to watercourses, it is estimated that 550 kilometres of watercourse is protected by SFI action BFS6. A range of other buffering actions under schemes protects an additional 20,000 - 29,000 kilometres of watercourses.  Round 1 of LR is taking forward 22 projects and providing funding for them to develop their proposals for the long-term restoration of nature within their respective landscapes.   One of the core aims of Round 1 is to restore England’s streams and rivers. It aims to improve water quality, biodiversity, and adapt to climate change. Through long-term, bespoke agreements projects will restore water bodies, rivers, and floodplains to a more natural state, reduce nutrient pollution, benefit aquatic species, and improve flood mitigation and resilience to climate change. At the start of the Project Development Phase, round 1 projects proposed to restore more than 700 kilometres of rivers in England.  The first project to enter into a long term agreement from round 1 was Boothby Wildland. Boothby signed their implementation agreement in June 2025, with works beginning on the ground shortly afterwards. They have already started work to convert unproductive arable land into a diverse mosaic of habitats, focusing on the reconnection of the West Glen River to its natural floodplain.  Farming schemes are not the only way we are working to support rivers and tackle flooding. On 14 October, following consultation, the government announced major changes to its flood and coastal erosion funding policy. These reforms will simplify our funding rules, making it quicker and easier to deliver the right flood defences in the right places and to optimise funding between new flood projects and maintaining existing defence assets. The new approach will better support new schemes protecting rural communities by getting rid of the Partnership Funding calculator and by investing at least £300 million in natural flood management over ten years. Our upcoming White Paper will also form the basis of a new Water Bill, bringing in reforms which will secure better outcomes for customers, investors and the environment.   Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

action: Fund better Functional Neurological Disorder care, treatment and support
background: We urge the Government to increase funding to ensure better Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) care, including clear FND care pathways in health trusts, multidisciplinary teams trained in FND, more follow-up appointments for patients, and mandatory training for GPs, neurologists, and A&E staff.
additional_details: We are not just statistics. We are people living with a life-altering condition. We ask for dignity, proper care, and a system that recognises and supports us. We live with real, disabling symptoms from seizures and paralysis to chronic fatigue and cognitive challenges. We feel we deserve the same standards of care as patients with other neurological or chronic conditions.
government_response_summary: Improving health outcomes for people living with long-term conditions, including functional neurological disorder (FND), is a key part of the Government's ambition to build an NHS fit for the future.
government_response_body: The Government recognises that FND is a complex condition, involving a range of neurological symptoms without a clear cause, which can impact on an individual’s life significantly. FND can be difficult to diagnose, as well as to treat, as its wide variety of symptoms can make it hard to find effective interventions.  The Government recognises that there is a need to do more to improve access to services for people living with conditions such as FND. This is why improving care for people with long-term conditions is a key priority for this Government and the NHS, and we are committed to ensuring they receive high-quality care and support and access to the latest treatments. The recently published 10 Year Health Plan for England will ensure a better health service for everyone, regardless of condition or service area.  At a national level, there are a number of initiatives supporting service improvement and better care for patients with neurological conditions, including FND, such as the Getting It Right First Time Programme for Neurology and the Neurology Transformation Programme, which aim to improve care for people by reducing variation and delivering care more equitably across England.  In addition to this, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has developed guidance on rehabilitation for chronic neurological disorders. The guidance, which was published on 15 October 2025, emphasises a holistic approach and focuses on individual needs and promoting independence and well-being. Specifically, it recommends a multidisciplinary team approach, a single point of contact for coordination of care, and access to various therapies like physical therapy, occupational therapy and psychological support. More information on the guidance can be found at this link: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/NG252  NHS England has recently published a new service specification covering the provision of specialised neurology services for adults, which routinely diagnose and treat individuals aged 16 and older with suspected or confirmed neurological conditions. The new specification includes FND as a major area of adult specialised neurology activity that must be provided at each specialised neurology centre, including assessment, formulation, and treatment planning for patients who have not sufficiently benefited from first line management within core neurology services. A copy of the specification is available at the following link: https://www.england.nhs.uk/publication/specialised-neurology-services-adults/  The service specification emphasises a multidisciplinary approach by outlining a networked model of care where secondary and tertiary neurology services, alongside core services and community teams, work collaboratively to provide seamless, needs-based support for people with neurological conditions like FND. This includes collaboration with local authority services, community-based professionals, and other hospital services to deliver rehabilitation, reablement and disability management across all condition groups.  Service specifications are important in clearly defining the standards of care expected from organisations funded by NHS England to provide specialised care. Integrated care boards must follow the national standards for specialised services set by NHS England, and there are a number of mechanisms in place to assure compliance with these service specifications.  We have also set up a UK-wide Neuro Forum, facilitating formal, biannual meetings across the Department of Health and Social Care, NHS England, devolved governments and health services, and Neurological Alliances of all four UK nations. The new forum, which has met twice to date, brings key stakeholders together to share learnings across the system, discuss important neurology services transformation and workforce challenges, as well as best practice examples and potential solutions that will add both to the existing programmes of work and wider health plans.  The standard of training for GPs and other health care professionals is the responsibility of the independent statutory regulatory bodies, which set the outcome standards expected at undergraduate level and approve courses, and higher education institutions, which write and teach the curricula content that enables their students to meet the regulators’ outcome standards. Once qualified, healthcare professionals are responsible for ensuring their own clinical knowledge remains up to date, and for identifying learning needs as part of their continuing professional development. This should include taking account of any new research and guidance, to ensure that they can continue to provide high-quality care. To increase understanding of FND among GPs, the Royal College of General Practitioners has produced a learning course, which includes a module on recognising and explaining FND, which can be found at: https://www.rcgp.org.uk/learning-resources/courses-and-events/elearning-courses  Department of Health and Social Care
