action: Make stamp duty payable on the difference in cost of the current & new home
background: Facilitate families to progress to larger homes by only applying stamp duty to the difference between the cost of the current home and the price of their new home. We think this would effectively give families a ‘credit note’ of the stamp duty paid and help reduce this financial barrier.
additional_details: We think the current system is unethical, applies a significant tax burden to what is a necessity and increasingly confines progress to those fortunate families that can afford to spare tens of thousands of pounds in addition to the cost of moving home. By reducing this burden, applying a credit for stamp duty paid to use against a future home purchase, we think this would meet the needs of our diverse, increasingly transient population and encourage movement of the workforce.

action: Add a “None of the above” option to ballot papers for all elections
background: We urge the Government to pass a law which adds a “None of the above” option at the bottom of all ballot papers in local and general elections, which we would like to be counted alongside votes and published in the results.
additional_details: We believe this could make it easier to distinguish between people who may not vote out of a lack of interest, and people who may not vote because none of the options are meeting their needs. This policy could allow parties to see how many people want to participate but may not feel represented.

action: Update school uniform guidance to prioritise comfort for students in England
background: We urge the Government to update guidance on school uniforms in England, so that it prioritises comfort and addresses: breathable fabrics, flexible designs, and seasonal options. We believe comfortable uniforms help students focus, feel confident, and learn better in school.
additional_details: We want the Government to ensure school uniforms are comfortable and inclusive for all learners, including neurodivergent students who may struggle with restrictive fabrics or seams. We think current uniforms can affect focus and wellbeing. We propose updating the guidance to allow more flexible options, like PE kit-style clothing, made from breathable materials and branded with school logos to maintain identity. We believe this could support comfort, inclusivity, and confidence, helping all students engage better in their learning.

action: End concurrent sentencing for heinous crimes

action: Require drivers to stop and take cats to the vets if they hit them in their car
background: We want the government to make it law that if you hit a cat you must legally report it and take it to the nearest vets.
additional_details: I have recently had my pet cat run over and he was killed.
government_response_summary: The Government has no current plans to mandate that motorists report a collision involving a cat, or to grant Police powers to prosecute motorists who fail to report a collision involving a cat.
government_response_body: This Government understands how upsetting it is when a much-loved pet is killed on our roads and thank you for raising this issue.  This is a compassionate country and although there is no obligation to report all animal deaths on roads, drivers should, if possible, make enquiries to ascertain the owner of domestic animals, such as cats, and advise them of the situation.  Under section 170 of the Road Traffic Act 1988, a driver is required to stop and report an accident involving specified animals including horses, cattle, ass, mules, sheep, pigs, goats or dogs, but not cats or wild animals. This requirement arises from their status as working animals rather than as domestic pets. To introduce such a measure within the provision of section 170, would require primary legislation. (Note that certain legislation still uses the word ‘accident’, although the preferred terms are collision or crash.)  Because cats are much smaller than other specified animals, and often most active at dawn or dusk, in many cases drivers may not be aware they’ve hit them – particularly with larger vehicles. Because of that, it would be difficult to prosecute drivers if the law was changed.  In June 2024, the Government introduced compulsory cat microchipping to help reunite lost and stray cats. All cats in England over 20 weeks of age must be microchipped and registered on a compliant database, unless exempt or free-living. The legislation is intended to improve pet welfare by increasing the likelihood of reuniting lost or stray pet cats with their keepers. Defra works closely with stakeholders to communicate pet microchipping requirements to the public.  Defra has also commissioned a research project to understand the operational challenges that currently prevent some cats from being reunited with their keepers after a road traffic collision. The project will provide an evidence base to inform best practice for local authorities.   Department for Transport

action: Use Proportional Representation at the next General Election
background: Change the voting system to Proportional Representation instead of First Past the Post. We think this would eradicate disillusionment and encourage voter participation as people could start to believe that their votes actually matter.
additional_details: We think that First Past The Post only works when there are only two parties involved. We live in a more diverse society than ever. We think that if we want our politicians to truly reflect our population then we need Proportional Representation.
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to change the voting system for UK Parliamentary Elections.
government_response_body: There are 650 Members of Parliament (MPs) in the UK Parliament, each of whom represent a constituency.  Each MP is elected using a ‘First Past the Post’ system whereby electors vote once for a candidate in their constituency.  The candidate with the most votes is elected as the MP for the constituency.  This provides a robust and secure way of electing representatives that is well understood by voters.       While not perfect, the Government believes this to be the most appropriate voting method for UK Parliamentary General Elections.  MPs representing a range of views and parties are elected to the Parliament, supporting a range of views to be put forward and debated.  At the same time, the ‘First Past the Post’ system also ensures a clear link between MPs and their constituents, thereby ensuring strong and clear local accountability between elected representatives and their constituents.    The Government is committed to restoring trust in our democracy. In July 2025, the published policy paper, Restoring Trust in Our Democracy: Our strategy for modern and secure elections, set out our plans to simplify, protect and promote our democracy.   Through measures such as moving towards an increasingly automated electoral registration system and reforming voter identification we intend to remove barriers to democratic participation that we know individuals face so citizens can be encouraged to play their part in shaping our democratic future with confidence.   However, we recognise that improving processes, such as registration and voter ID, is only part of the solution. Research(https://www.electoralcommission.org.uk/research-reports-and-data/public-attitudes/attitudes-voter-registration-research-report) tells us that electors’ attitudes and motivation are arguably more important than procedural issues in determining whether they participate in the democratic process.  That is why the Government is listening to those already leading the way.  Across the UK, individuals and organisations are finding innovative ways to reduce and remove obstacles to democratic participation. We are learning from their successes and building on initiatives that are already making a difference. This work will help empower citizens to be active participants in our democracy.   To stay informed about the latest developments in electoral policy and practice, we recommend visiting www.electoralcommission.org.uk.  Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

action: Fund research using postural changes in SBP and HR to detect sepsis

This is not just an oversight,it's exclusion, With new playgrounds currently being built in places like Oldham centre, we have a real chance to do better

Play is more than just fun,it's essential to a child’s development, well-being, and sense of belonging. But many children are being left behind because of a lack of ramps, wheelchair-friendly surfaces, or inclusive equipment.We demand that:
new playgrounds be built with accessibility and inclusion as a requirement, Existing parks be reviewed/adapted to be accessible.Local councils consult with disabled individuals, parents, and advocates when designing these spaces.Accessibility is a basic right
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: We need an independent inquiry into Ffos y Fran to assess environmental impact
background: Government need to ascertain the roles and accountabilities that have led to Ffos Y Fran opencast not being properly reinstated as per the original plan.
additional_details: We also need to understand what environmental impacts this is and could cause in its current state
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

You may also wish to raise this issue with your local Members of the Senedd who represent you. You can find out who your Members of the Senedd are and how to contact them here: https://senedd.wales/find-a-member-of-the-senedd/

action: Ban the Ring Flying disc to Protect Our Seals
background: Young seals sometimes find lost or discarded flying rings (any type of throwing ring). Being inquisitive, they sometimes play with them, putting their heads through the hole & may become trapped. As they grow, the rings can cut into their necks, causing life threatening open wounds & sometimes death
additional_details: Seals around the UK are protected wild animals. Legislation does not allow any suffering, killing or injuring of our heritage seals. However, this may be caused by flying rings. Flying rings may be lost or discarded on beaches, and may end up in the sea. We think the use of existing solid discs, preferably biodegradable, are seal safe alternatives.

action: Block the Chagos Deal with the UK & Mauritius pending a vote of Chagos diaspora.
background: Parliament to scrutinise the agreement made; a referendum of residents and diaspora of the British Indian Ocean Territory (Chagos/Diego Garcia); the referendum being binding to require primary legislation to enact its result; the current treaty is suspended.
additional_details:
Publish full details to both Houses of Parliament on the details of negotiations between UK, Mauritius, the NATO allies and China and India. 

Detail through parliamentary libraries discussions with other Commonwealth Realms and Overseas Territories.

That An Humble Address is made to His Majesty the King to effect this.

Parliament is recalled as soon as possible with urgency to consider this treaty/agreement. 

Treaty ratification is placed in abeyance until an Act is passed or not approving
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/706882

action: Land aid directly into Gaza
background: We call on the British Government to break the blockade and land food and medical aid into Gaza.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700682

action: Provide funding to put up fences on all roads to protect wildlife
background: Provide funding to put up fences to protect wildlife as there’s often roadkill. We think animals deserve protection and help. We think it is disgraceful and disturbing to see many badgers, deers, foxes, pheasants, bunnies and many more that have been killed on roads.
additional_details: We think its shameful and disturbing how there are dead corpses of animals left on roads. We think the Government should provide funding to protect the vulnerable wildlife.

action: Reopen the Isle of Mull Railway
background: Reopen the former railway from Craignure to Torosay castle
additional_details:
1. It would be cool if it reopened 
2. It would also really help the nearby tourist industry 
3. Lots of people probably have fond memories of the railway

action: Regulate and oversee hair strand testing used in family court cases
background: Introduce regulation and independent oversight of hair strand testing companies used in family court. Require mandatory standards and accreditation to ensure accuracy, transparency, and fairness in decisions affecting children and families.
additional_details: We think hair strand test results may decide the outcome of court cases,—yet these tests are unregulated, may be erroneous and we think lack independent oversight. False positives can devastate families. There are no governing bodies to ensure accuracy, accountability, or fairness. We think this must change to protect families and children.

action: Introduce measures to protect women at risk of domestic violence
background: Mandatory Real-Time Domestic Violence History Checks: public bodies including the police, courts, probation services and local authorities must check for known domestic violence or coercive control histories before allowing shared housing, child contact, or release from custody.
additional_details:
Automatic Clare’s Law Disclosures: Instead of placing the burden on victims to ask, we think authorities must proactively inform individuals if their partner has a violent or abusive past.
 
Fast-Track Legal Protections for Pregnant or Vulnerable Women:  we think women who report feeling unsafe—especially during pregnancy or early motherhood—should get immediate access to protective orders, rehousing, and mental health support.
 
Education on Coercive Control: We think we must teach young people how to spot early signs of coercive, possessive, or manipulative behavior. We think that prevention begins with education.
 
A National Femicide Review Board; we think that every murder of a woman by a partner or ex-partner must be reviewed nationally.

action: Ban chemical castration in the criminal justice system
background: We urge the UK Government to ban chemical castration as a means of treating or rehabilitating sex offenders and enabling early release based on undergoing such procedures. We think this practice raises serious concerns about ethics, human rights, and public safety.
additional_details: We think that linking it to sentencing or early release risks public safety and weakens justice for victims. We are concerned it could pressure offenders into invasive treatment without full consent. We want the government to support ethical, rights-based rehabilitation. Justice must protect society without violating dignity.

action: Ban the sale and use of sunscreens containing ingredients that damage corals
background: Research suggests that many sunscreens containing chemicals like oxybenzone harm coral reefs, causing bleaching & death. Coral reefs support marine life and protect coastlines. We think the Government must act to ban harmful sunscreens to protect marine ecosystems and promote reef-safe alternatives.
additional_details: Coral reefs are essential for biodiversity, fisheries, and tourism but face threats from pollution and climate change. Research indicates that sunscreens that use mineral-based ingredients like zinc oxide do not harm marine life and are reef-safe. By banning certain sunscreens, we think the Government can reduce environmental damage and encourage eco-friendly products, setting a global example in ocean conservation.

action: A National Vote of No Confidence in the Prime Minister and his Government.
background: The current Government to be removed from office.
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

action: Keep the Graduate Route (PSW Visa) at 2 years for international students
background: We call on the UK Government to keep the full 2-year Graduate Route (3 years for PhDs), dependant rights for taught postgraduates, and consult student communities before future changes that could impact international education and mobility.
additional_details: We think the changes proposed in the immigration white paper would affect international students unfairly, harming the UK’s global reputation and competitiveness. We think post-study work and family rights are key factors in choosing where to study. We think not implementing the proposals in the immigration white paper would support inclusivity, education exports, and the UK’s relationship with key partner nations.

action: Increase the weight threshold on dual purpose vehicles
background: Increase the weight threshold on dual purpose vehicles. Increasing the weight threshold would mean they are not considered light goods vehicles and increase the speed limit that vehicles could drive on dual carriageway and single carriageway roads.
additional_details:
The additional emissions equipment required to achieve compliance with current guidelines, in addition to extra safety features has pushed the weight of some these vehicles to just above the now dated maximum of 2040kg.
We think this maximum should be increased to allow newer double cab pickup trucks to return to the class of dual purpose vehicles and be driven at 70 on dual carriageway, 60 on single carriageway. Like older ones can and in line with cars (as they are classed by HMRC).

action: Keep the 5-Year ILR pathway for the Skilled Worker visa holders and dependants
background: To keep the 5-Year ILR pathway for the Skilled Worker visa holders and dependants
additional_details: Skilled visa holders move to the UK for better opportunities and in they contribute to the UK economy, pay taxes, and support critical sectors like, accounting, finance, health, care, and engineering. Changing ILR rules seems unfair and causing stress for families already in UK and planning to come. Keep the rules and timeframe to ILR same as already, we would appreciate if this can be seriously considered.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Keep the 5-Year ILR pathway for existing Skilled Worker visa holders
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727360

action: Longer sentences and disqualification for drug/drink drivers who injure someone
background: The current law for serious injury by dangerous driving is a maximum of 5 years. I think that when this is caused by a drink and/or drug driver, the sentence should be made harsher, with an automatic disqualification for life to make our roads safer.

action: Count Post-Study Work (PSW) Visa Years Toward the 5-Year ILR Route
background: We ask the Government to count time spent on the Graduate (PSW) visa toward the 5-year ILR route. This will recognize the contribution of international graduates, support talent retention, and make the UK a more attractive place to study, work, and build a future.
additional_details: Many international graduates contribute to the UK economy during their PSW visa period but are not recognized in the ILR timeline. Excluding PSW time forces skilled individuals to start over, delaying settlement and discouraging long-term plans. Including it would promote fairness and help retain global talent.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/704940

action: Call for investigation into claims of irregularities in Poland's 2025 election
background: We urge the UK Government to advocate for an international investigation into claims of irregularities during Poland's 2025 Presidential Election. We think this would encourage accountability and reaffirm the UK’s support for free elections.
additional_details: Poland is a strategic UK ally, NATO and EU partner. There are over 1 million residents of Polish descent in the UK, and we believe many are deeply concerned. We think the UK should call for an investigation into these claims in order to defend democratic integrity, support rule of law and maintain regional stability in Europe.

action: Award the humanitarian medal to frontline personnel that served in the pandemic
background: The government should recognise the efforts and sacrifices made by members of the NHS, emergency services, armed forces, carers and any other front line workers that served during the COVID pandemic. The government should award all personnel with the humanitarian medal.
additional_details: Hundered of thousands of lives were saved by the efforts of the front line services during the pandemic. Thus-far no government has recognised, acknowledged or even thanked any of the frontline services for the efforts and sacrifices made. The Labour government being the party of compassion should award this medal as a sign of thanks and acknowledgment.
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions that ask for a person or a group of people to be given an honour, or have an honour taken away.

action: Do something about climate change
background: If we don't do something about climate change now, the world is going to get worse.
additional_details: We could slow climate change down by doing things like reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you're concerned about climate change but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Stop removal of SEND provision in Mainstream schools.
background: Ministers are planning to remove the legal right to SEND provision in mainstream schools. This would further oppress children who require support in mainstream schools preventing them from fulfilling their potential, impact mental well being and life chances. We cannot allow this.
additional_details: The government must not pursue the removal of SEND from mainstream schools this would be catastrophic for children. They need to seek further advice from those at grass roots level ie non statutory organisations run by parent professionals. Homeschooling has risen because of the lack of SEND provision. Child centred SEND provision must continue in mainstream schools not be prevented. It is necessary and without it children will be unable to secure an education they are capable of with support.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711021

action: Advocate for Policies to Mitigate AI Job Disruption and Losses
background: It is vital the government starts preparing for widespread AI job loss and disruption. By taking action now, we can mitigate the potential harms and help our communities thrive in the AI-driven era. Furthermore, incentives for industries to innovate responsibly and ethically.
additional_details: The impact of AI on jobs cannot be understated. Artificial intelligence technologies are reshaping industries at an unprecedented pace. According to a report by McKinsey Global Institute, up to 800 million jobs could be displaced by automation by 2030. These figures are alarming, and without adequate policy interventions, the repercussions on the global workforce could be severe, leading to increased unemployment rates and social unrest.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707509

action: Ban the release of balloons and sky lanterns
background: Sky lanterns and balloon releases present hazards to animals. While I am sympathetic to those who have lost a loved one, I believe there are many alternative and longer lasting ways to remember them, e.g. tree planting.
additional_details: Balloon and lantern releases can have a lasting environmental impact, not only through littering, but some wildlife, livestock, marine life and family pets may mistake them for food, which can lead to death. I believe we collectively have a responsibility to protect our wildlife.

action: Stop advertising alcohol on tv and stop showing celebrities on tv showing it
background: I want the government to stop putting alcohol on the tv like on celebrity gogglebox each celebrity has wine or a pint in plain sight would you allow them to inject heroin or snort cocaine ? Alcohol is poison and as a recovering alcoholic this is a trigger
additional_details: Stop advertising alcohol!! You wouldn’t advertise cocaine! Alcohol is poison and kills people i lmaost died due to being an alcoholic thankfully i seeked help and i am in recovery but watching tv and on gogglebox people casually drinking should be illegal it should be hidden like cigarettes in the convenience stores!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710852

action: Bring back the “Eat Out To Help Out” scheme
background: We call on the Government to bring back the “Eat Out To Help Out” scheme that gave 50 percent off for food and non-alcoholic drinks at participating businesses.
additional_details: We believe it could help businesses across the country.

action: Fund more bins, CCTV, enforcement staff and raise fines to prevent littering
background: I would like the Government to increase the minimum littering fine to £250. And to also invest in more bins and enforcement officers especially in popular walking areas and parks. I also think the government should provide funding for more CCTV.
additional_details: I believe that current fines are not enough to discourage people from littering. I am calling on the  Government to tighten litter laws and help protect our environment and wildlife. Surveys have found that 48% of people in the UK admit to dropping litter. The RSPCA gets over 5000 calls a year about animals being injured or killed by litter. Most litterers never get caught or face fines. I believe that if the laws were stricter people would be more reluctant to litter.

action: Fund Full NHS Bursaries for Nurses & Midwives to Help Secure Our Workforce
background: We call on the Government to reinstate fully funded tuition and maintenance bursaries for nursing and midwifery students. We believe this would reduce the burden on trainees, stop nurses paying to work, and cut NHS reliance on overseas staff by investing in homegrown talent.
additional_details: The removal of NHS bursaries in 2017 meant many nurses and midwives had to pay more for their own training. We think this drove many away from vital roles and has left the NHS with over 25,000 vacancies within the Registered Nursing Staff group in England. We think restoring full bursaries would help ensure a strong, homegrown workforce, help make training affordable, help reduce the NHS’s dependence on international recruitment, and alleviate pressure on other countries' healthcare systems.

action: Ban the use of aversive dog training tools
background: I would like the Government to ban the use of aversive tools such as electric shock collars, prong collars and invisible fencing due to the possible physical and mental harm caused to animals. I believe trauma and cruelty is unacceptable. Legislation on this topic has still not been enacted.
additional_details: Aversive techniques of "training" dogs may lead to many harmful side effects. I am concerned that animals, usually dogs, are being abused with these tools that cause pain to make them do as the person inflicting it wants. I believe this is not only abusive but can also prevent dogs communicating their needs and shutting down.

action: Do not change ILR qualification period, PSW duration for EXISTING IMMIGRANTS.
background: There is a similar petition for existing skilled workers which does not include all existing immigrants and students. This petition is more inclusive and hence we request that this be considered as well.please do not change the qualification period, immigration rules for existing immigrants midway!
additional_details: Changing the rules midway like extending the qualification period for ILR and reducing the PSW duration to 18 months effects a lot of careers and creates chaos for many including Children. Everyone who came here believed in the existing rules and made decisions (investing time,money) accordingly. It is understandable if the rules are for new immigrants, but changing them for existing ones who have already planned their lives around the current rules will effect their lives in many unwanted ways.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727372

action: Allow the release of wild boar and introduce a statutory close shooting season
background: Give wild boar (sus scrofa), an iconic British species, a close shooting season. Allow landowners to release boar onto their land (after assessing local opinions) to increase the hunting economy and eco-tourism.
additional_details: Wild Boar are an iconic, native, British species entwined with our culture and traditions. We think they have important ecological functions, and that tales of them being dangerous should be hushed by the fact we already live alongside red deer, a large wild animal. We don't believe this would be 'species reintroduction' given wild boar are already present in England.

action: Reform the Care System for Children, Adults, and Care Leavers
background: Reform the care system for children, adults, and care leavers. Improve safeguarding, staff training, accountability, and long-term support. Care-experienced people deserve protection, advocacy, and a voice in decisions that affect their lives.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you would like to reform the care system, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Review and increase the amount of support care leavers get post-18
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710233

action: Fund free public transport for all through an additional tax on income
background: Introduce a new tax on income to fund free public transport, such as free trains, buses, trams. We think it would encourage richer people to use public transport and help poorer people. We think this tax should be progressive so that you are taxed more if your income is more.

action: Automatically revoke spousal visas from abusive partners in the UK
background: We call on the Government to create a law that automatically revokes the spousal visa of any person who abuses their partner while on a spousal visa. We believe abusers should not benefit from UK residency. We feel immigration rules must protect victims and not shield abusers.
additional_details: I know many, especially minority women, who suffer in silence fearing no justice. I believe the law must protect victims and ensure abusers face immigration consequences.

action: Expand London’s Fare Zone 6 to Include More Stations
background: We ask the UK Government to work with Transport for London to add more stations to fare Zone 6 as train operators are nationalised.
additional_details:
Many residents and visitors on the outskirts of London would benefit from an expanded Zone 6 as it would simplify fares and support local economies by encouraging greater use of public transport.

Nationalisation provides the opportunity for the next round of Zone 6 stations to be established and implemented as quickly as possible.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Transport for London is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly. 

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Set legal deadlines for NHS to provide medical reports for DWP tribunals
background: We call for legal deadlines to be set for the NHS to provide medical reports for DWP tribunals. Delays can cause unfair outcomes. We think this would ensure efficiency and accountability in the tribunal process, and that this would promote just decisions and improved DWP practices.
additional_details: Petition for the Government to set legal deadlines for the NHS to provide medical reports for DWP tribunals. We think that delays can impede fair tribunal outcomes, and that this reform is essential to ensure justice, support vulnerable individuals, and uphold the integrity of tribunal processes. We believe it would promote efficiency, fairness, and accountability, which we think would foster a more equitable system for all.

action: Keep the5Year ILR Route for existing PSW Holders Switching to Skilledworker visa
background: The government should allow existing PSW holders transitioning to Skilled Worker Visas to qualify for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) after 5 years, instead of forcing them onto the 10-year route. This will ensure fairness, retain skilled workers, and support economic growth.
additional_details: The 10-year ILR route unfairly impacts PSW holders already living in the UK who will switch to Skilled Worker Visas. Many contribute to essential sectors like healthcare, education, and tech but now face extended settlement timelines. The government must restore the 5-year ILR pathway to retain skilled professionals, support economic growth, and ensure fairness for those who have invested in the UK’s future.we feel betrayed at this point.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728402

action: Hold a debate on AI automation, mass job loss, and Universal Basic Income
background: We ask Parliament to debate the economic impact of AI and automation, including projected job losses across sectors, and to explore Universal Basic Income (UBI) as a potential policy response to protect livelihoods and ensure economic stability in the years ahead.
additional_details: AI and automation are advancing rapidly, threatening millions of jobs in sectors from law to logistics. Many workers may soon find themselves without work, income, or prospects: not due to failure, but because machines can do it faster and cheaper. We believe Parliament must urgently address this reality and explore policies like UBI to ensure no one is left behind in the transition. Without action, the social and economic consequences could be severe and irreversible.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707509

action: Seek a UK-EU deal to scrap the Entry/Exit System for travel under 90 days
background: We ask the Government to work with the EU to seek a deal to prevent UK citizens needing ETIAS when visiting the EU for 90 days or less, and to drop the requirements for EU citizens needing an ETA as well for less than 90 days.
additional_details: We feel the UK government is keen to start a new era in strengthening the relationship with the EU. We believe this proposal would be a good way to bolster this commitment for a renewed relationship with our closest trading partner.

action: Grant 5 years ILR to current Graduate Visa Holders switch to Skilled Worker Visa
background: We urge the Government to reconsider the 10-year ILR rule for current Graduate Visa holders when making the switch to Skilled Worker Visa, given the initial 5-year promise when we arrived. Retrospective fairness is crucial.
additional_details:
Many of us have employer sponsorship promises pending our Graduate Visa expiration. The 10-year rule may lead employers to reconsider, causing setbacks. We request a 5-year ILR pathway to maintain stability

As significant contributors to UK's economy, healthcare, social care, energy, and other sectors, we believe our efforts warrant consideration. Granting 5-year ILR would recognise our value and support continued growth. 

We urge the government to consider this or the start date for a future date.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727360

action: Access to more comprehensive financial education within schools.
background: For the government to create a specified curriculum for financial education, built upon the national curriculum currently in place in secondary schools and expand it to be more comprehensive e.g., savings, taxes, and income expenditure. Whilst adding curriculums for primary schools and sixth forms.
additional_details: Financial illiteracy negatively affects a large percentage of the young adult population, and to prevent this from impacting more youth in the future, providing better financial education should be a higher priority. Many still lack the resources to learn—resources that could be provided by the education system. According to a report from Santander UK (2024), 1 in 4 young adults aged 18-21 report receiving any financial education at school. Change is necessary.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701663

action: Exempt Global Talent and 'highest skilled worker' visas from 10-year ILR rule
background: Exempt all existing TIER 1 high-skilled visa holders and their replacement visa types (including Global Talent, Investor, Innovator Founder, Entrepreneur), and their dependents from the 10-year ILR rule. Preserve 3 and 5-year ILR and 12-month citizenship timelines
additional_details:
Include grandfathering protections.
Keep attracting top talent to settle and grow the UK economy.
 
We are concerned that breaking promises to industry leaders who trusted the UK could trigger a catastrophic brain drain of top talent to rival nations. A Home Office survey of 4,025 Global Talent visa holders (published 28 March 2024) showed the top motivators were visa flexibility (66%) and the chance to settle (63%). Two-thirds surveyed planned to apply for ILR under the 3- and 5-year rules. We urge the Government to honour its commitment to fast-track ILR and citizenship for the brightest and best talent driving UK high growth.

action: Keep 5 year ILR pathway for  migrants & students who are already in UK legally.
background: Do not apply the proposed 10-year ILR rule to existing legal migrants  & international students in UK. who already contributing to UK economy.Keep the 5-year ILR route for those already in the UK on this visa. As government threshold are too high this will help in future economic contributions.
additional_details: Many international minds come to UK to learn and then apply great skills in UK Work sector for better opportunities. They have studied & worked on all odd and critical sectors like care, warehouse, food industry, science, technology, research and so on. We think changing ILR rules Mid-journey is unfare  & causing stress. Apply 10 year ILR rule to future entrances. also now government closed international care workers and in all visas Threshold are very high.so this people will backbone  economy.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action:  https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727360

action: Keep 5 year path of ILR for the immigrants on Post graduate visa  in the UK
background: Keep five year ILR path for the immigration are already in UK, The new rules only apply on the immigrants come in UK after implement
additional_details: The immigrants who are already in the UK, should we follow the five year ILR route
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728402

action: Increase New State Pension and pay to all, abolish the old Basic State Pension.
background: We think the government should put all our elderly onto the New State Pension, increase the New State Pension to a good percentage of average earnings and abolish the old 'Basic State Pension'.
additional_details:
We believe those on the Basic State Pension should be paid the difference accrued, since the New State Pension's introduction, between the Basic State Pension and New State Pension.

Britain's basic State Pension is currently £176.45 per week.
Britain's New State Pension is currently £230.25 a week.
Britain's average weekly earnings (AWE) were estimated at £722 in March 2025, by the Office for National Statistics.

action: Bring all Social Care into the Public Sector under the NHS & stop means testing.
background: We demand the government bring all Social and Community Care under the NHS, fully funded by general taxation. We believe neither Social Care, Community Care, nor the NHS should be for profit, but remain free at the point of use.
additional_details:
We want to reverse the changes to Social Care, made over decades, which have resulted in parts of it being transferred to local government, privatised and/or means tested.

We believe that trends in local authority budgets and Social Care funding since 2010 have harmed the sector and that immigration policies have contributed to staffing problems.

action: Require the regulation, watermarking, and labelling of generative AI content.
background: We call on the Government to require clear labelling and watermarking of all AI-generated content to prevent public deception, protect trust, and ensure transparency. Regulation is needed to balance innovation with accountability and safeguard democracy.
additional_details: AI-generated content is harder to spot, enabling enabling fraud, scams, identity theft, and misinformation. Without clear labelling, the public faces real harm. We urge regulation, with fines or sentencing for those who deliberately use AI to mislead, to protect democracy and ensure transparency. This is in order to protect people, uphold democracy, and ensure transparency and accountability, for both corporations and individuals.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/715706

action: Work to eliminate discrimination against trans people
background: Parliament, government and public authorities should follow the public sector equality duty to advance equal opportunity for trans people, minimising the disadvantages they suffer and encouraging them to participate in public life, promoting understanding and tackling prejudice.
additional_details: Trans people are under intense public scrutiny, suffering discrimination, misinformation and hostility. The presence of trans women in women’s services is portrayed in media as a threat to women’s privacy, dignity and safety. Trans people are ordinary diverse people wanting to live their lives in peace, knowing they are not their sex assigned at birth. Public authorities should work to foster good relations between trans and non-trans people and eliminate discrimination against trans people.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: The Government should block all trade with Israel including the blocking of arms
background: We think Israel's illegal settlements and disproportionate military actions against Palestinians violate international law and are widely condemned. We believe the UK must take stronger a position.

action: Protect Current International Students & PSW Visa Holders from ILR Rule Changes
background: We ask the UK Government to maintain the 5-year ILR eligibility for Skilled Worker visa holders and ensure proposed changes don’t apply to current international students and Graduate Route (Post Study Work visa) holders who planned their future in the UK based on the existing system.
additional_details: Many international students chose the UK based on the 5-year ILR route. Changing the rules now, before we move to Skilled Worker visas, is unfair and damaging. We’ve invested time, money, and trust in the UK. This change would impact our careers, families, mental wellbeing, and future stability. It may also discourage future students, harming universities and the economy. We ask for fairness, clarity, and a respectful transition that protects current visa holders and their future.

action: Consider Opening four motorcycle venues across the UK

action: Give State Pension to all at 60 and increase it to equal 48hrs of Living Wage
background: We want the Government to make the State Pension available from the age of 60 & increase this to equal 48hrs a week at the National Living Wage.
additional_details:
Hence from April 2025 a Universal State Pension should be £586.08 per week or about £30,476.16 per year as a right to all including expatriates, age 60 and above.
 
We think that Government policy seems intent on the State Pension being a benefit not paid to all, while ever increasing the age of entitlement. We want reforms to the State Pension, so that it is available to all including expatriates, from age 60, and linked to the National Living Wage, for security.
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to make the State Pension available from the age of 60 or for it to equal 48 hours a week at the National Living Wage.
government_response_body: The Government is committed to supporting current and future generations of pensioners and giving them the dignity and security they deserve in retirement. Our commitment to the Triple Lock through this Parliament will benefit over 12 million pensioners. From the end of this Parliament, spending on the State Pension as a result of our commitment to protect the Triple Lock is forecast to be around £31 billion more a year, compared with 2024/25.   Our system of state, private, and workplace pensions provides the basis for security in retirement. The new State Pension was introduced in 2016 to be a simpler, clearer, sustainable foundation for private saving, including workplace pensions supported through Automatic Enrolment.   The Government also takes seriously the need to ensure future retirees, have a decent standard of living. That is why the Government have recently launched the Pensions Commission to ensure our pensions system delivers this in the decades ahead.  Supplementary benefits provide additional support, including Pension Credit (which guarantees a minimum level of income for low-income pensioners). Pension Credit passports pensioners to receive other benefits (help with council tax, fuel bills and a free TV licence for those over 75).  The Government also announced that everyone over the State Pension age in England and Wales with an income of, or below, £35,000 a year will benefit from a Winter Fuel Payment this winter. This extends eligibility to the vast majority of pensioners, with over three quarters benefitting.  Other key supplementary benefits for low-income pensioners include the Warm Home Discount (rebate on energy bills); Housing Benefit (help with rent) and Discretionary Housing Payments.  Pensioners with a long-term health condition or disability may also be eligible for additional-costs disability benefits. In England and Wales these are Attendance Allowance, Disability Living Allowance and Personal Independence Payment. In Scotland, where this is a devolved matter, they are the Scottish Government’s Pension Age Disability Payment, Adult Disability Payment and, from March 2025, Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance.   In the past year, the Government has put the NHS on the road to recovery, delivering record investment to ensure it is there for pensioners when they need it. We promised 2 million extra appointments: we have delivered more than 5 million. We promised 1,000 new GPs on the frontline and we have recruited over 2,000. We have taken almost a quarter of a million people off waiting lists, cutting them to their lowest level in two years.   There are no plans to bring State Pension age back down to 60. Increases to State Pension age have been in legislation since the Pensions Act 1995 and there have since been a number of legislated increases to State Pension age introduced under successive Governments. As longevity has increased and our society aged, State Pension age rises have maintained fairness between generations and protected the public finances.    Department for Work and Pensions

action: Raise the standard tax-free Personal Allowance to £45,000.
background: The Personal Allowance is the amount of income a person can get before they pay tax. It stands at £12,570 in 2025. We would like the standard Personal Allowance raised to what we think is a more realistic figure of £45,000.
additional_details:
We think that the Personal Allowance, as termed by the government, has been kept unreasonably low for far too long, at the expense of the poorest, most needy people in our society.

We feel that the poorer majority should pay substantially less than the wealthy. We think that the tax system seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

action: Fund Free TV licences for all pensioners.
background: We want the Government to fund free TV licences for existing pensioners and those who reach the official retirement age. When people reach retirement age, we think they should receive a state-financed free TV licence.
additional_details:
Many pensioners live on the breadline with only the TV for company. With the cost of food soaring and utility bills ever higher, we feel there is a desperate need to provide all pensioners with at least this concession.

We feel it is a double outrage that those who have given their all to this country in taxes and raising children have to pay a TV licence fee and are only exempt if they receive means-tested Pension Credit. Meanwhile, some media figures draw huge salaries.
government_response_summary: There are a number of TV licence concessions available, including for over-75s in receipt of pension credit. There is no BBC concession to provide free TV licences for all pensioners at this time.
government_response_body: The BBC is a vital British asset and makes a huge contribution to lives up and down the country. It supports our democracy, brings our communities together, and helps to shape and define our nation through telling stories about the lives of people in all parts of the UK.  TV licence concessions are available to people who are registered blind or severely sight impaired, people over-75 and in receipt of pension credit, and people living in qualifying residential care who are disabled or over 60 years old. There are no further concessions available at this time.  While the Government strongly believes in public funding for the BBC given the public good it serves, we are aware of the financial difficulties faced by some households. For this reason the Government has announced a significant extension to the Simple Payment Plan (SPP). This will allow unlicensed households experiencing financial difficulty to split up the annual payment into more manageable fortnightly and monthly instalments. The BBC’s analysis suggests that the expansion could double the number of households using the SPP to around 500,000 by the end of 2027.   The Government is committed to the current licence fee for the remainder of this Charter and, as such, will not be changing the available concessions at this stage. The BBC remains responsible for the over-75s concession, including the decision to provide free TV licences for over-75s in receipt of pension credit. Given the existing BBC concession, we have no plans to introduce a new Government concession for all pensioners at this time.  However, the Government is absolutely committed to supporting pensioners and giving them the dignity and security they deserve in retirement. That’s why, through our commitment to protect the Triple Lock, over 12 million pensioners will benefit. From the end of this Parliament, spending on the State Pension as a result of our commitment to protect the Triple Lock is forecast to be around £31 billion more a year, compared with 2024/25. This will see pensioners’ yearly incomes rising by up to £1,900. The basic and new State Pensions increased by 4.1% in April, benefitting over 12 million pensioners by up to £470.  Looking further ahead, the Secretary of State has been clear that the BBC must be funded by a model that is sustainable and fair to all those that are paying it. The forthcoming Charter Review is a key opportunity to set the BBC up for success long into the future. It will consider a range of options for funding the BBC, including how they can support the BBC in a way that is sustainable and fair. We are thinking creatively about options for the future, to ensure we future-proof our national broadcaster for many years to come.  In taking this work forward, the Government will take into account a range of factors such as affordability and fairness when considering the future funding model of the BBC, and what obligations should continue to be placed on members of the public. In doing so the Government will consider existing concessions and whether any new concessions may be justified.   As we progress Charter Review we will work closely with the BBC, and engage with other broadcasters, stakeholders across the creative industries as well as the British public to inform our thinking. This will include the opportunity for stakeholders and audiences across the country to respond to the Charter Review public consultation before the new charter comes into effect in 2028.  Department for Culture, Media & Sport

action: Funding so all infants are offered Type 1 Diabetes Testing in routine care
background: Fund mandatory offer of testing for Type 1 Diabetes in babies, toddlers, and young children as a routine part of medical assessments at the point of care.
additional_details: We believe that lives could be saved by doing this. Too many children are misdiagnosed, and this can tragically lead to loss of life.
government_response_summary: NHS England provides diabetes care in children. Due to insufficient evidence supporting routine mandatory testing for paediatric type 1 diabetes it has no plans to introduce this at the current time.
government_response_body: Type 1 diabetes is diagnosed with a blood test that checks blood glucose (sugar) levels. It is the responsibility of the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) to provide guidance and quality standards on the treatment and care of diabetes in England. NICE NG18 guideline for type 1 and 2 diabetes provides clinical guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and care of children and young people. It states that clinicians should be aware of the signs of type 1 diabetes in children and young people, including:  •	hyperglycaemia •	polyuria (passing urine more often) •	polydipsia (excess thirst) •	weight loss •	excessive tiredness.  NG18 also recommends that children and young people with suspected type 1 diabetes are referred immediately (on the same day) to a multidisciplinary paediatric diabetes team with the competencies needed to confirm diagnosis and provide immediate care.  NHS England is not aware of there being any evidence for the feasibility and effectiveness of the mandatory offer of testing for type 1 diabetes in babies, toddlers, and young children as a routine part of medical assessments.  NHS England works closely with research charity Diabetes UK which has worked to raise public and health care professional awareness of the common symptoms of type 1 diabetes, known as the 4Ts: Toilet, Thirsty, Tired and Thinner. Further information of this campaign can be found here:https://www.diabetes.org.uk/about-diabetes/type-1-diabetes/symptoms  Early identification of type 1 diabetes through screening for antibodies prior to the onset of physical symptoms can provide clinical benefits, including helping to prevent diagnosis at the point of diabetic keto-acidosis (DKA). However, there is not currently a national screening programme in England.  The UK National Screening Committee advises the NHS on screening programmes and, in 2019 concluded that more research and evidence for the benefits of screening for autoimmune type 1 diabetes was required.  A National Institute for Healthcare Research-funded study called ELSA (EarLy Surveillance for Autoimmune diabetes) is currently underway in England exploring the feasibility and benefits of screening in children aged 3 to 13. NHS England is working closely with researchers and leading experts in this field to ensure that emerging evidence is considered in the development of future national guidance and is reviewed ahead of further decisions on the availability of screening.  Department of Health and Social Care

additional_details:

Currently, drivers over 70 only self-certify their fitness to drive when renewing their licence. This may lead to dangerous situations if vision problems go undetected.
Introducing mandatory annual eye tests for drivers over 70 would ensure early detection of issues, promote safer driving, and reduce the risk of accidents. This policy would be a reasonable safeguard to protect both elderly drivers and other road users, similar to measures in other countries.

action: Review possible penalties for social media posts, including the use of prison
background: We call on the Government to urgently review the possible penalties for non-violent offences arising from social media posts, including the use of prison.
additional_details: There is serious public concern about the proportionality of sentencing in cases involving opinion-based online speech. We believe imprisoning individuals for posts on social media sets a dangerous precedent and raises wider questions about freedom of expression, proportionality in sentencing, and the misuse of limited prison resources. We consider that alternative sanctions, such as fines or community service, would be more appropriate.
government_response_summary: The government is committed to ensuring penalties are proportionate and uphold freedom of expression.
government_response_body: Freedom of expression is a cornerstone of our democratic society. It is a long-standing tradition in this country that people are free to demonstrate their views, however uncomfortable these may be to the majority. The government is committed to protecting this right while also ensuring that laws are in place to address harmful, criminal behaviour.  The UK’s Online Safety Act 2023 (“the Act”) reflects this careful balance. It requires platforms to take proportionate steps to tackle illegal content and protect children from harmful material. At the same time, it has been designed to safeguard legal free speech, uphold privacy, and support innovation. The Act does not prevent adults from accessing legal content, nor does it restrict people from posting content that others may find offensive. It is not about individual posts. Instead, Ofcom will assess the systems and processes platforms have in place to manage risks and respond to harm. There are also protections against the over-removal of content, ensuring that lawful speech is not wrongly taken down.  Where an individual is convicted for an offence related to opinion-based online speech, the independent judiciary are responsible for determining appropriate sentences based on the facts of each case and the relevant sentencing guidelines.  The sentencing framework provides courts with a range of sentencing powers alongside imprisonment, including fines, community sentences, and suspended sentences. The law also makes clear that imprisonment should only be imposed where no other sentence would be appropriate.  The government commissioned a comprehensive review of sentencing powers through the Sentencing Review. This was a wide-ranging and evidence-led process that examined the full spectrum of sentencing options—from fines and community orders to custodial sentences—to ensure the framework is robust, proportionate, and fit for purpose.  The government has accepted the majority of the Review’s recommendations in principle and intends to legislate to implement them as soon as Parliamentary time allows. This includes targeted reforms to strengthen public protection and reduce reoffending.  We do not consider it necessary or appropriate to revisit the sentencing framework and we currently have no plans to review the penalties for these types of offences.  We are committed to ensuring that our justice system protects the public, upholds fundamental rights, and uses custodial sentences only where they are necessary and proportionate.   Ministry of Justice  This is a revised response. The Petitions Committee requested a response which more directly addressed the request of the petition. You can find the original response towards the bottom of the petition page (https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728715)

action: Review and fund improved detection and diagnosis of prostate cancer
background: Require PSA blood tests to be proactively offered to men at highest risk of prostate cancer. Review emerging evidence from the TRANSFORM trial to inform a future national screening programme for prostate cancer. We believe this will make the health system fairer and reduce inequality.
additional_details: Black men, men with a family history of prostate cancer, and men from socio-economically deprived areas are disproportionately impacted by prostate cancer. We believe that detecting and diagnosing prostate cancer is now safer and more accurate than ever. Prostate Cancer UK’s research suggests that harms of diagnosing prostate cancer have reduced by 79%. Yet it remains the second biggest cancer killer in men in the UK. We think it is time to review NHS guidelines on the PSA blood test and invest in an early detection programme.
government_response_summary: The Government has no current plans to require PSA blood tests to be proactively offered to men at highest risk of prostate cancer, because the evidence does not support this.
government_response_body: The Department of Health and Social Care is committed to providing the best care possible for men and we are taking the risks and impact of prostate cancer seriously. We are guided by the independent scientific advice of the UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC), and it is only where the offer to screen provides more good than harm that a screening programme is recommended. The UK NSC makes its recommendations based on internationally recognised criteria and a rigorous evidence review and consultation process. It last reviewed the evidence for screening all men for prostate cancer in 2020 and concluded that the UK should not do so.  Whilst it is recognised that the Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA) test can be a valuable diagnostic tool in certain contexts, such as for men who present with symptoms, its limitations mean that it is not currently recommended for population-level screening, i.e. screening men with no symptoms.  This is because elevated PSA levels can be caused by non-cancerous conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), prostatitis, or recent physical activity. This results in high rates of false-positive results, leading to unnecessary anxiety, invasive biopsies, and potential overtreatment. For example, a diagnosis via a biopsy and treatment (prostatectomy and radiotherapy) carries risks of life-changing harm, such as urinary and faecal incontinence, sexual dysfunction, as well as a smaller but serious risk of sepsis. Additionally, some prostate cancers may not produce elevated PSA levels, leading to false-negative results that provide deceptive reassurance. For these reasons, the UK NSC currently considers that these potential risks outweigh the benefits of population screening.  As part of its commitment to keep its recommendations under review, the UK NSC has commissioned a new evidence review for prostate cancer screening. This covers modelling of the clinical effectiveness and cost of several approaches to prostate cancer screening. It includes different potential ways of screening the whole population, and targeted screening aimed at groups of people identified as being at higher-than-average risk, such as black men or men with a family history of cancer.  The modelling and evidence reports are now complete, and are being considered by the UK NSC and experts. Subject to no further revisions being required, the UK NSC plans to hold a public consultation towards the end of 2025. After this the UK NSC will make a recommendation. Ministers will then be asked to consider whether to accept the recommendation.  In the meantime, however, recognising the importance of developing a better test, the Government have invested £16 million in working with Prostate Cancer UK (PCUK) to launch their £42 million TRANSFORM trial, a nationwide study that will compare the most promising tests to look for prostate cancer. It will be the biggest trial in prostate cancer screening for 20 years. It has been developed in consultation, and with the backing of, the NHS, the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) and the Government. It will ensure that 1 in 10 of the participants invited to take part in the trial is a black man, in acknowledgment of the higher risk black men have of being diagnosed with prostate cancer.   The UK NSC are engaged and working closely with TRANSFORM researchers and stand ready to receive findings as they become available. PCUK anticipate initial findings will be available in three years.  The Government agree that too many men are dying from prostate cancer. Any death from cancer is a tragedy, which is why this Government will publish a National Cancer Plan later this year. The Plan will have patients at its heart, with the goal to reduce the number of lives lost to cancer. The Government have been listening to and co-designing the Plan with members of the public, the health workforce, charities, academics and other partners. The Call for Evidence received over 11,000 responses. Officials at the Department of Health and Social Care are analysing those responses, to make sure every voice has been heard, to inform our Plan to improve cancer care.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Review all trade ties with Israel, suspend 2030 roadmap & impose trade sanctions
background: We call on the Government to review existing trade ties with Israel, suspend the 2030 Roadmap for UK-Israel bilateral relations and impose trade sanctions upon Israel.
additional_details: We are concerned that innocent people, including children, are suffering and dying in Gaza, and we feel the UK is not taking enough action. I oppose any violence against civilians and was horrified by Hamas's attack of October 2023. I believe Gaza's current Hamas leadership should be brought to justice but I believe this does not justify what is happening to ordinary people in Gaza. As UK citizens, we ask the Government to take action against Israel.
government_response_summary: We believe the quickest, most effective way to end the war and humanitarian crisis in Gaza is not through trade sanctions, but through ensuring the success of the peace initiative currently under way.
government_response_body: This Government came to power in July 2024 determined to secure an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, the release of all the remaining hostages held by Hamas, the unrestricted flow of aid into Gaza to tackle the escalating humanitarian crisis, and the restoration of a path to long-term peace and stability in the Middle East.  Over the last fifteen months, we have taken decisive action in support of these goals: restoring funding to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency; providing nearly £250 million in development assistance; coordinating international condemnation of the humanitarian crisis; and evacuating groups of sick and injured children to receive medical treatment in the UK.   We suspended negotiations on a new trade deal with Israel; suspended the export of arms and military equipment that could be used in Gaza; and imposed three rounds of sanctions on violent Israeli settlers and members of the Israeli cabinet.  And, after signing a landmark agreement with the Palestinian Authority to support their ambitious reform agenda, we took the historic step last month of formally recognising a Palestinian state, with no future role for Hamas, to protect the viability of a two-state solution and create a path towards a just and lasting peace, with security for the Israeli and Palestinian people alike.  We are now working tirelessly with our partners across the world to build support and momentum for the US peace initiative, which offers the quickest and most effective path to achieving the goals we have been working towards over the last year, and which – at the time of writing – is already creating hope of progress.  There is a long way still to go, but at this time, the efforts of all governments and all people of goodwill should be focused on supporting that effort to stop the bloodshed, release the hostages, end the humanitarian crisis, and restore a framework for peace.  The UK government does not believe that accepting the petitioners’ proposals at this time would contribute to that effort, and would risk punishing British businesses and workers without making any positive difference to the current situation in the Middle East, especially since the export of arms and military equipment for use in Gaza has already been suspended.  As a whole, UK exports to Israel were worth £3.3 billion in the twelve months ending March 2025, compared to £2.5 billion in Israeli exports to the UK. Those UK exports supported around 38,100 jobs in the UK in the last year for which data is available, particularly in advanced manufacturing.   Suspension of trade with Israel would not only put those jobs and businesses at risk, but would also damage the strong links between UK and Israeli scientists, who regularly collaborate on research and development projects, resulting in new technologies, medicines, industrial processes, and other products and services.  We fully understand the strength of feeling on this issue among the petitioners, but if their ultimate goal is to see an end to the war and humanitarian suffering in Gaza, then we hope they will in turn accept our sincerely held view that the quickest, most effective way to pursue that goal is not through trade sanctions, but through the current peace initiative, based on the months of groundwork that the UK has done alongside our international partners to give that initiative the best chance of success.   Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

action: Add a binding “VETO” option to UK election ballots to allow reruns if needed.

The VETO lets them formally withhold consent when the ballot fails to offer an adequate option. A majority VETO triggers a rerun, making consent a condition of election. This reform empowers voters and ensures no one takes office without real democratic legitimacy.

action: Do not implement the Independent Sentencing Review and hold further review
background: We want a further review of sentencing, looking at the impact on policing and public safety, and holding extensive consultation with the victims of crime. We think the impact on their mental health has not been addressed.
additional_details:
We think:
1. Rather than tackling prevention, prisoners are being released before they serve their full sentence.
2. Prison life needs to be more of a deterrent.
2. Insufficient consideration has been given to the impact on victims of crime.
3. Early release is not the answer, it is a get out of jail free card.
4. Reduced crowding should be addressed by building prisons, using vacant buildings, and more deportations of foreign criminals. 
5. We cannot pander to those already convicted and sentenced.

action: Election manifestos should be legally binding contracts with voters.
background: The electorate's votes for a general or local election should be regarded as entering into a legally binding contract based upon the manifestos. We cannot, any longer, subvert democracy by getting people to waste their precious votes on manifestos that are patently a tissue of lies.
additional_details: The Government/Parliament/Local governments should be subject to the same legals terms as any business entering into a contract. What they offer the electorate is the same as any tender from a business. The electorate vote on those promises or claim of intent. Therefore the electorate should be able to declare a breach of contract, after a year has passed, and get the courts to agree that a new election should be held.
rejection_details:

Require election & manifesto pledges to be implemented and legally enforced

action: Ban door-to-door sales to protect vulnerable people
background: We want the government to introduce a law that prohibits door-to-door sales to safeguard people who are at risk of exploitation and undue pressure.
additional_details: We are concerned that door-to-door salespeople often target elderly and vulnerable people who may feel pressured or coerced into buying products or services they do not need or cannot afford. These practices can lead to financial exploitation and emotional distress. We think a ban would help protect these individuals and promote fairer trading practices in our communities. Vulnerable people deserve to feel safe in their homes without the worry of unexpected and potentially predatory sales visits.

action: Increase eligibility UC period for mothers until the child reaches school age.
background: Raising Universal Credit eligibility from a child's age of 3 to when they reach school age would greatly ease financial pressure on mothers, especially single ones.
additional_details: It would reduce the burden of costly childcare fees, which are often high during school holidays, and prevent mothers from being forced into full-time work just to afford care. With nurseries mainly operating during term time, many mothers face financial and emotional strain during half-terms and holidays, particularly without family support. Extending support until children start school would provide crucial stability, helping mothers stay afloat and better care for their children.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

Currently, mothers of children aged 3 to 12 years old are eligible for Universal Credit; they are expected to work up to 30 hours per week or spend up to 30 hours a week on work-related activities. 

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/universal-credit-and-your-family-quick-guide/universal-credit-further-information-for-families#:~:text=If%20you%27re%20the%20main,child%20has%20exceptional%20care%20needs

action: Ban Single-Use Plastic Packaging for Fruit and Vegetables in UK Supermarkets
background: I am asking the UK Government to ban the use of single-use plastic packaging for fresh fruit and vegetables in all supermarkets and encourage the retail sector to adopt environmentally responsible alternatives.
additional_details: Plastic pollution is an environmental issue. Despite growing awareness, UK supermarkets package large quantities of fresh produce in single-use plastic. Contributing to plastic waste, which ends up in landfills, incinerators or our environment. There are sustainable alternatives, including compostable or reusable containers & loose produce options. The UK must follow in the footsteps of other countries, to reduce plastic waste, protect our environment, & lead the way to a sustainable future.

action: Change the pay of High level MP's including the PM to the national minimum wage.
background: Remove MP's expense account and change their pay to that of the national minimum wage, as they assure us that is enough to live on, so let's have them live by example.
additional_details: This would remove financial gain as a motive for attaining power and would therefore remove the desirability to those individuals that get into politics solely for financial gain and don't do an adequate job for those they supposedly represent in their constituencies. Let's at least try to keep the politics in this country honest.

action: Limit / ban AI generated & digitally altered content spreading false information
background: We need the government to review the potential impact these misleading information could place on young citizens and general public. There are no regulations that ban content that are misleading consumers (e.g. from companies) and potentially make wrong decisions because of it.
additional_details: Survey has revealed that a high degree of public concern surrounding online content in general, with 81% of respondents expressing worry about its trustworthiness, including digitally altered and AI-generated content. Photos and short videos are generated every second in the UK but there is no governance on contents that are sharing misleading information. Companies or individuals are using AI-generated content to 'flood' consumers without limit. Limit and ban should be placed.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions with a clear ask. We are not sure how you would like current rules to change. 

The Online Safety Act states that mis- and disinformation will be captured by the Act where it is illegal or harmful to children. Services will be required to take steps to remove illegal disinformation content if they become aware of it on their services.

You can read more about the Act here: 
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/online-safety-act-explainer/online-safety-act-explainer#how-the-act-tackles-misinformation-and-disinformation

Advertising rules apply regardless of how content is generated, edited, or targeted. You can read information about advertising rules by visiting the Advertising Standards Authority website: https://www.asa.org.uk/
