action: Abolish Penalty Points for Minor Speeding Offences
background: Abolish licence penalty points for minor speeding offences where the police issue Fixed Penalty Notices without going to court. I think fines should be kept for deterrence but penalty points reserved for serious or dangerous speeding violations which I think would reflect the level of risk involved.
additional_details: As most speeding offences are recorded by cameras and not actual police officers on the ground, in my view there is not enough context or discretion available when an infraction could be minor. I want the government to lower the voting age to 16 in all constituencies in the United Kingdom.

Lowering the voting age to 16 is a necessary and progressive step toward a more inclusive and representative democracy. Also Scotland and Wales voting age is 16 however England is not so what is the real difference between our great nations.

Hold a general Election.
A General Election is urgently needed to restore democratic accountability and give the people a chance to decide the future of the country.
additional_details: The current government must call a General Election due to the overwhelming lack of public trust and its repeated failure to uphold the promises made in the manifesto that secured its majority in the last election. The Prime Minister has lost the confidence of the nation and is no longer seen as an effective leader. action: Protect Children from Unlawful Religious Marriage Ceremonies in the UK
background: No CHILD should be trapped in a marriage under the guise of culture or religion. We urge Parliament to investigate and regulate underage religious marriage ceremonies, protect vulnerable minors, and ensure UK law applies equally to all—without exception.
additional_details: Behind closed doors, underage girls are being subjected to religious marriage ceremonies that violate UK values and law. This abuse hides behind the façade of culture and faith. It’s exploitation—nothing less. We demand accountability: anyone arranging such ceremonies should face prosecution, deportation if non-citizens, and placement on a national watch list to prevent further harm. UK citizens should follow UK law, no other regardless of religion. Enough is Enough! Stop enabling this!
rejection_details:

This includes non-legally binding ‘traditional’ ceremonies which would still be viewed as marriages by the parties and their families. You can find more information about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/legal-age-of-marriage-in-england-and-wales-rises-to-18

I also believe it will ensure we are well-prepared to defend our shores unlike some of our allies and friends.

action: Make CCTV mandatory in all taxis and private hire vehicles

action: Change foreign policy so the UK is neutral and not aligned with the 'West'.
background: We demand the government declare Britain a neutral state in what we see as a new cold war among global superpowers. We believe that neutrality will protect British interests, safeguard our national security, and uphold our tradition of diplomacy and peacekeeping in an increasingly polarised world.
additional_details:
We think the world is entering a new phase of global tension, with increasing confrontations between major powers. In our view the UK is at risk of becoming entangled in these geopolitical conflicts. We propose a neutral stance that would prioritise British security, protect our economy, and allow Britain to serve as a mediator, promoting diplomacy and peace on the international stage.

We think Britain is no longer a super power on the level of America, China, or Russia.

action: Ban "small-scale fracking" for onshore oil and gas
background: Fracking forces fluid into rocks to open cracks so oil or gas can flow out. It was banned in 2019 after being blamed for causing earthquakes in shale gas drilling. But the ban only covers fracking with large volumes of fluid.
additional_details:
We want the ban to be extended to cover activities with smaller volumes of liquid.

Extracting oil and gas will intensify the impact of climate change. There are companies who have submitted planning applications to use what we see as "small-scale fracking" to extract oil and gas. Little is known of the potential risks of this activity. We ask the government to close what we feel is a loophole to help protect communities from harm. We believe not doing so could slow the essential transition towards clean, renewable energy.
government_response_summary: We are committed to ending fracking for good. We are aware of local concerns regarding low volume hydraulic fracturing and are keeping this policy under internal review.
government_response_body: This Government is committed to ending new onshore oil and gas licensing in England. This will help make Britain a clean energy superpower to protect current and future generations.  On 1 October the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero announced legislation to end new onshore oil and gas licensing in England, including new licences that could be used for high volume hydraulic fracturing for shale gas (commonly known as “fracking”).  There is an effective moratorium on high volume hydraulic fracturing for shale gas (“associated hydraulic fracturing” as defined by the Petroleum Act 1998) in England, and this will continue to apply to existing licences. This is in place because of concerns around prediction and management of induced seismicity from this type of hydraulic fracturing. There are similar restrictions in place across other parts of the UK.  Low volume hydraulic fracturing includes activities such as “proppant squeezes”, which take place at lower volumes than the thresholds for “associated hydraulic fracturing” and in a variety of geological contexts. The small number of these activities are not currently in scope of the effective moratorium in England, which only targeted high volume hydraulic fracturing for shale gas extraction.  However, the government recognises concerns from local communities regarding low volume fracturing and the fact that it is currently treated differently, and is therefore currently reviewing the position with regard to low volume hydraulic fracturing.  Department for Energy Security and Net Zero This is a revised response. The Petitions Committee requested a response which more directly addressed the request of the petition. You can find the original response towards the bottom of the petition page (https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728912)

action: Cap airlines and resorts from inflating their prices during school holidays
background:
Airlines and resorts inflate their prices to double, or even triple the average price during the school holidays. 

I would like the UK government to put a cap on how much these prices can inflate during school holidays.
additional_details:
Going on holiday as a family isn’t a right, but it is a great privilege—one many hard working families miss out on due to unfair price hikes during school term time.

The government now punishes parents harshly for children missing a few school days for a holiday. Parents must either accept these hikes or forgo holidays entirely.

Family holidays are vital for making lasting memories, building stronger bonds, and offering learning beyond the classroom.

action: Modernise UK Education: AI, Digital Skills & Life Skills for All Students

Invest in inclusive education, teacher training, and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) to support all learners.
additional_details: The UK curriculum is outdated and does not prepare students for a world shaped by AI, automation, digital technologies, and global challenges. Countries like Singapore, Estonia, and Finland are already modernising their education systems. Without urgent reform, reducing outdated subjects, and proper investment in UDL, teacher training, and infrastructure, the UK risks falling behind, damaging our economy, workforce, and children’s futures. Failure to act now will cause long-term harm to society.

additional_details:
The means test should be abolished in favour of a universally paid, much higher State Pension, our politicians should be means tested for concessions and bar/restaurant subsidies should be abolished.

If ever there was a striking reflection of Britain's rich and poor divide, we merely have to note, how badly our elderly folk are treated compared to how well we look after our very rich MPs.

action: Increase regulation of parking signage
background: I call on the Government to increase regulations relating to parking signs to require councils to ensure they are made clearer and have clauses about what to do if there is, for example, an incorrect pay station in between the sign & the correct one.
additional_details: We believe that the current rules, which we feel are incredibly vague, mean councils can say their sign meets the guidelines, even if there are factors that may make the sign misleading. We believe that if the rules were more in depth and accounted for possible problems, councils would be forced to take responsibility for their misleading signage.
government_response_summary: Local authorities manage parking signs and machines and appeals are possible. The Government sees no need to change current sign regulations.
government_response_body: Traffic signs for use on roads in England are already regulated through the Traffic Signs Regulations and General Directions 2016. This includes those indicating parking bays and directions to payment machines.  Local authorities (LAs) are responsible for provision of on-street parking, including placement of payment machines and associated signing. It is for them to ensure that there is no ambiguity as to which payment machine relates to the parking bays in question.  The Department for Transport (DfT) publishes good practice guidance for local authorities in the Traffic Signs Manual. Advice on signing payment machines, including how to ensure drivers are directed to the correct machine where there is more than one, is given in Chapter 3 of the Manual, available at www.gov.uk/government/publications/traffic-signs-manual.   There is an appeal mechanism for drivers to use if they feel have been given a ticket unfairly. They can appeal to the local authority in the first instance, and ultimately to an independent adjudicator. The adjudicator may take into account the condition and placement of signs and the relevant guidance when considering appeals.  The Government believes that LAs are best placed to understand adequate sign placement for individual sites as they have detailed knowledge of their roads and the needs of residents and businesses.  The Government’s view is that the current Regulations covering parking restriction signs are adequate and has no current plans to make any changes.  Department for Transport

I want the government to make the vote for mayor of London a national vote.
I believe that our capital city should have a mayor that everyone in the country has had a chance to elect with the backing of the entire population behind them when they take office.
additional_details: I believe that the British people should have a say in who represents our capital city on the world stage.

The NHS needs more funding and OR  guidance on other forms of therapy (other than cbt) so that they stop turning people away when they deem them as “too complex” 

The government needs to look at how the nhs treats mental health conditions as a whole but especially those with CPTSD.

These are people who have tried to better themselves (with support from the nhs) but as they need therapy more specialised than your standard cbt are now being told the NHS cannot help them. 

This is life threatening, professionals have not been able to help these people but now they are shunned away left to fend for themselves.

action: Regulate recreational cannabis to protect UK users from contaminants
background: Create a legal framework allowing regulated recreational cannabis use for UK citizens. This would involve safety testing, eliminating heavy metal contamination, and preventing synthetic cannabinoid adulteration which we believe is causing health crises across Europe and America.
additional_details: Recreational cannabis users in the UK can face serious health risks from contaminated illegal products. There is research suggesting cannabis can contain toxic heavy metals which may cause cancer and long-term health problems. We believe that there has been an increase in these products which could cause medical emergencies. We think legal regulation with mandatory testing would help protect citizens from criminal suppliers who prioritize profit over public health.

action: Remove custody sentence for some offences from Standard & Enhanced DBS check
background: We think custodial sentence for certain crimes should be removed from Standard and Enhanced DBS check, crimes such as property damage, criminal damage (e.g. graffiti, throwing objects on windows) buying stolen items by mistake, minor theft etc especially if it’s their only crime in life.
additional_details: We think the government should get these kinds of crimes deleted from the Standard and Enhanced DBS check. We believe that the individual who only committed one crime in their life, which is also potentially a minor incident, a one off mistake in life, doesn't deserve to be embarrassed in a job application by this coming up as a reminder. In life this could have a mental impact and unnecessary stigma on them, or they may even be rejected in jobs which they deserve to work in.

action: Continue to allow Non stun slaughter as per the current legislation.
background: In the UK, legislation permits religious non-stun slaughter for Halal and Kosher meat production, primarily to accommodate the religious dietary requirements of Jewish and Muslim communities. We want this to be continued without any hinderence.
additional_details: We urge Parliament to recognise the deep importance of protecting our religious rights. For us as Muslims—and for our Jewish friends as well—faith and tradition are at the heart of our identity. We are truly grateful to the UK Government for respecting our right to non-stun religious slaughter, and we sincerely hope this understanding and support will continue. It is not just a matter of law, but of conscience, heritage, and the freedom to live our faith fully.
rejection_details:
On 9 June 2025, the Minister for Food Security and Rural Affairs stated that the Government "will continue to respect the rights of Jews and Muslims to continue to eat meat prepared in accordance with their beliefs" and that the Government "intend to continue to allow the religious slaughter of animals for consumption by Muslims and Jews."

You can read more about this here: https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2025-06-09/debates/27E94862-93C7-4D29-B0DA-F77F92D14161/Non-StunSlaughterOfAnimals

action: Scrap sponsorship requirements for overseas healthcare workers to switch jobs
background: We urge the Government to scrap the need for sponsorship for overseas healthcare workers already in the UK who want to switch jobs, so companies can give contracts of employment to people already here. Many people can’t switch to working for other companies as they are not offered sponsorship
additional_details: There are many care workers in the UK who do not have many working hours, and there are many jobs that are not being filled as many companies don’t offer sponsorships. There is also a lack of healthcare workers yet there are, what I believe, an adequate number of people to fill these jobs.

action: Designate the Mourne Mountains as a National Park.
background: Designate the Mourne Mountains as a National Park, with all the protections that such would entail.
additional_details: The Mourne Mountains are an hugely important fixture of the Irish landscape: intrinsically tied to the mythology of the Ulster Cycle, one of the oldest works of literature in Europe, and also made famous in modern song through the works of Percy French. NMD are obsessed with an incredibly unpopular policy of the farcically-named ‘Gondola’ project which would pollute the skyline of mountains with needless cable car. Having failed to build this in Newcastle, they now want to put it in Rostrevor.

action: Require unused website URLs to be made available after 12 months
background: We urge the Government to ban people hoarding or "squatting" on domain names (website URLs) without real use. We believe if a domain isn’t used for a live website, email or business within a year, it should be made available.
additional_details:
We believe this could help new businesses access domain names without high resale prices.

We believe many new businesses are struggling to get website names as many are bought and left unused. We believe this blocks entrepreneurs from building their brand online and can create unfair barriers. We believe domains should be for doing business—not profiteering. Releasing unused ones could support start-ups and fair competition. We believe domain squatting blocks entrepreneurs from launching with a meaningful domain, is digital gatekeeping, and stifles innovation.

action: Require companies to offer equal adoption and parental leave policies
background: We think adoptive parents should have the same parental leave and pay as birth parents. Some employers offer enhanced maternity pay but not adoption pay. We think this is unfair. We ask the Government to make equal leave and pay for all parents a legal requirement.
additional_details: Adoption is an equal route to parenthood. We think families formed through adoption face unique challenges and deserve the same support to bond and care for their child.

action: Home Office Personal Cultivation Licenses for Medical Cannabis Patients (CBPM)
background:
We call on the government to create a safe regulatory framework to ensure cannabis can be licensed/grown by patients at home, for those unable to afford thousands yearly on private healthcare or regulated pharmaceuticals.

Basic lab testing could be mandated to ensure safety and proper regulation.
additional_details:
Home-grown medical cannabis has been shown as a safe and appropriate substitute for regulated 'Cannabis Based Products for Medicinal Use' in numerous countries, whereby it's become a necessity for patients unable to afford the artificially inflated prices of commercial cannabis.

The current legal framework forces many prescribed patients to turn to cheaper illegal/illicit sources in-order to treat their conditions - instead many would safely and legally grow their own for <10% of the cost.

action: Ban surname changes for women after marriage
background: We want the government to legally ban the tradition for women to change their surnames after marriage or for any institutions to assume any name change for women after marriage.
additional_details:
We think this could challenge the patriarchal norm that women must give up their original surname in marriage and protect equality by law.

Changing your surname after marriage is seen as tradition, but we think it roots from patriarchal norms and imply erasure. I’ve seen women pressured to change their names just to appear “normal” after marriage, or because their company assumed a name change (which shouldn’t be allowed). We do not think a family’s unity is defined by sharing a surname; even if it is, a man is never expected to change his name. By banning surname changes for women, we think we can protect identity and challenge outdated norms.

background: Ban them. Make them a criminal offence in public. for no apparent reason.

action: Exempt medically discharged Commonwealth service people from immigration control
background: I would like automatic, continued exemption from UK immigration control for all Commonwealth citizens serving in the UK's armed forces, when they're medically discharged. I've personally experienced challenges of medical discharge from the Royal Navy, and feel compelled to advocate for change.
additional_details: I wish to highlight what I see as a pressing issue affecting Commonwealth servicemen and women who join the UK military. Many Commonwealth citizens like myself join, taking an oath to serve and protect the nation. However, when faced with medical discharge, they may find they have to leave the UK, despite having signed contracts and served honourably. Exemption from UK immigration control ceases when a person is discharged from the armed forces. I believe this can cause significant hardship, depending on the individual's circumstances.

background: Many people travel on buses for hours every day, sometimes having a frequent urge to urinate or defecate. We think this would also allow people with medical conditions to accommodate their needs.

action: Reverse the ban on XL Bully dogs
background: We urge the Government to reverse the ban on XL Bully dogs, as we believe the problem is with owners not the dogs themselves. We believe a ban on a dog breed due to some undertrained dogs is wrong and discriminatory.
additional_details: We are concerned about the impact the ban will have on the entire breed. We believe it is not fair on exempted dogs who have to walk with a muzzle, even when they are calm dogs. I have an XL Bully, and I can’t even get her to bite me if I tried, I put my hand in her mouth, and she just walks away! I believe it is unfair for them & the responsible owners. I think we should make sure all owners are responsible and have trained their dogs correctly.

action: Ban horse-drawn hackney carriages
background: I would like the government to ban the horse-cart hackney carriages to prevent the potential for some horses to be abused.
additional_details:
I believe some horses aren't resting at all, and that some owners are abusing them if they are not moving, hitting them with a whip.
Some horses might be overworked and could be taking loads that are overweight.
I believe they shouldn't be dressed up, be hit, or even used as an attraction for people.

action: Stop paying billions of pounds to the French government for stopping the boats.
background: I want our government to stop paying the French government billions of pounds when they clearly do not. The French police have been seen on more than one occasion letting mainly young men and sometimes children board these dangerous vessels.
additional_details: I want our government to put a stop to this practice as billions of pounds of our hard working money is being paid to people who are economic migrants and do not put any money into our economy. We should have s points system to bring in people we need. Enough is enough!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728872

action: End wage discrimination, standardise national minimum wage for all 18+ workers.
background: We want the Government to introduce a standard minimum wage for all adults aged 18 and over. The current pay gap between 18 and 21+ is unfair and discriminatory, despite both age groups often doing the same work and facing similar living costs.
additional_details: The pay gap between 18–20 and 21+ is a form of age-based discrimination. Many 18 to 20 year-olds are financially independent, paying rent, bills and supporting families. They deserve equal pay for equal work. A standard minimum wage for all 18+ is fair, just and reflects real-world responsibilities. Employers should not have the right to pay individuals less just because they are not yet 21.

Equalise the minimum wage for 18-20 year olds and 21+ workers

action: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR)
background: We urge the Government to leave the ECHR as we believe it will help protect British citizens.  We think this could give the Government more flexibility to make policies to help reduce the level of illegal migration to the UK.
government_response_summary: To achieve the Government’s goals to protect the UK’s border security and restore order to the asylum system, our priority should be to review the way the ECHR is interpreted, not withdraw from it.
government_response_body: The European Convention on Human Rights was formed in the wake of the Second World War, partly in response to the Holocaust and other horrors inflicted across Nazi-occupied Europe, and partly in reaction to the rise of totalitarian governments across the post-War Soviet bloc. British politicians and lawyers were among the chief architects of the Convention, and the UK was one of the first States to ratify it. We remain fully committed to protecting human rights both domestically and internationally as the essential underpinning of the liberties and democratic values that we all enjoy, and the ECHR plays an important role in that.  Our membership of the ECHR also facilitates and strengthens international co-operation on areas ranging from security to irregular migration. It is one of the foundations of peace and stability in Northern Ireland through its role in the Good Friday Agreement, it underpins law enforcement and judicial cooperation via the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement, and is also an important pillar of the devolution settlements. Since its introduction, the ECHR has made a positive difference to the lives and rights of those in the United Kingdom, including its role in the abolition of corporal punishment, ending the ban on LGBT+ people serving in the armed forces, and the continued abolition of the death penalty.  One of the ECHR’s most important provisions is the duty on states to protect an individual’s right to life. The families of the 97 football fans who lost their lives in the 1989 Hillsborough disaster relied on that right as they campaigned for the truth to obtain a new inquest, which concluded that the fans were unlawfully killed. Victims of the taxi-cab rapist John Worboys also used the ECHR to claim successfully that the Met Police had failed to investigate Worboys’ crimes effectively, and had thereby breached their ECHR rights to protection against ill-treatment.   Despite these two high-profile cases where victims of state failure were able to gain redress via the ECHR, the UK nevertheless has the lowest rate of applications to the European Court on Human Rights by population: in 2023 it was 3 applications per million persons in the UK. That compares to the rate for all Council of Europe member States combined, which was 47 per million people. In 2023, the European Court of Human Rights made only one adverse judgment against the United Kingdom out of the 176 applications assessed.  While the ECHR has played an important role in protecting the rights of UK citizens in the past, it is also true that no set of rules or multilateral institution is perfect; and neither the ECHR nor the European Court of Human Rights should be treated as impervious to change. Indeed, during the UK’s presidency of the Council of Europe in 2012, member states adopted a substantial package of reforms to the ECHR.  The Government’s 2025 Immigration White Paper (Restoring Control over the Immigration System) committed to bring forward legislation to strengthen the public interest test to make it clear that Parliament needs to be able to control our country’s borders and take back control of who comes to, and stays in the UK, striking the right balance between individual family rights and the wider public interest.  The government will bring forward a major package of reforms to the asylum system before the end of the year. We believe that reforms can be introduced to deliver our migration and criminal justice priorities without having to leave the ECHR, and this will remain our priority over the coming period.   Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

action: Close the border,Declare a state of national emergency & mass deportations
background: The country is being invaded by illegal immigrants . THIS MUST STOP !!
additional_details: Our sovereignty is being threatened and the labour government aren’t doing anything about it

action: Review Home Office Delays in processing immigration cases
background: Review the cause of delays in processing visa applications, including deadlines for processing, communication and updates to applicants, support for people affected by delays, and how the Home Office is held accountable. Review if current practices respect human rights and fairness.
additional_details: I believe the Home Office has repeatedly failed to handle immigration cases with due care and urgency, causing delays that have destroyed lives and futures. Even after legal appeals and decisions, some immigrants face indefinite waits for paperwork needed to work and live legally in the UK. I believe this is a systemic failure which undermines trust in the government and could violate basic human rights.

action: Recognise Non-stun slaughter as expression of religious freedom in UK
background: Parliment is debating soon on a ban of non stun slaughter but as its a free country and UK goverment respect all faith so Muslims and Jews who live in UK want a recognision Non-stun slaughter as expression of religious freedom.
additional_details: A small percentage of Halal slaughter is non-stunned here in the UK and all Shechita (Jewish) slaughter is non-stunned and All non-stunned Halal slaughter in the UK and EU is carried out humanely, in fully licensed and regulated slaughterhouses, adhering strictly to animal welfare laws. These practices take place in the same controlled environments and under the same rigorous standards as conventional slaughter, ensuring the highest level of care and dignity for the animals at every stage.
rejection_details:
On 9 June 2025, the Government Minister for Food Security and Rural Affairs stated that:

"The Government respects the right of Jews and Muslims to eat meat prepared in accordance with their beliefs. We therefore intend to continue to allow the religious slaughter of animals for consumption by Muslims and Jews."

You can read more about the Government's position on non-stun slaughter here: https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2025-06-09/debates/27E94862-93C7-4D29-B0DA-F77F92D14161/Non-StunSlaughterOfAnimals#contribution-BBC4DFF0-65DF-405E-BCE1-7031AC19086F

action: Urge Labour to Form a Coalition with Greens and/or Lib Dems
background: We, the public, call on the Labour government to enter into a coalition with the Green Party and/or Liberal Democrats. Our nation faces several challenges, one being the Cost of Living. This is leading to the far right gaining traction. A broader, morally consistent coalition would resolve this.
additional_details:
We cannot allow fear and division to dominate our Parliament or our future.
History will remember this. In times of global uncertainty, Britain must stand united with leadership that reflects compassion, sustainability, and justice. Germany's coalition model proves that progressive unity is not only possible. It works. We ask Labour to lead boldly by working with its progressive allies, not alone.
rejection_details: This issue is an individual policy decision for the political parties listed in the petition. The Government or Parliament is therefore not responsible for the issue raised in this petition.

action: Require car and phone makers to publish annual report of safety & repair issues
background: We want the Government to legally require car and phone manufacturers to report and publish all known repair and safety issues in their products, annually, broken down by model and year. We think this will help consumers make informed decisions and improve accountability across the industry.

action: Require nurseries and early years providers to make social media pages private
background: We urge the Government to pass a law which requires all nurseries and early years childcare providers to make their social media pages private. We believe this could help protect children's personal data, privacy and safety online.
additional_details: Many UK nurseries use social media platforms to share updates, activities and photos involving children. While this may help to engage parents, some of these pages are public and accessible to anyone online. We believe this creates serious risks; children may be identified, tracked or targeted, personal data may be exposed, safeguarding best practices may not be enforced in this context. We believe social media activity involving children should be secure and safe.

action: Make Stamp Duty payment flexible
background: Introduce Stamp Duty Land Tax payment flexibility: buyers choose between paying in full at completion or spreading the cost over 2-5 years via government-backed scheme. This could reduce upfront barriers to homeownership. Similar to other HMRC payment plans.
additional_details: We think the 14-day SDLT payment requirement creates affordability barriers for first-time buyers and homeowners. Buyers may have to save extra funds, on top of deposits, or increase mortgage borrowing, which could reduce purchasing power. We think short term solutions, such as temporary rate cuts create pressure for all parties in the moving process. We think a flexible payment scheme would be a sustainable solution, it would address affordability, while maintaining tax revenue, and improving housing market mobility.

action: Provide more funding for further biomedical research and education on CFS/ME
background: We want the government to provide more funding for further biomedical research and education on myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME)/chronic fatigue syndrome. ME Association UK estimates there are currently over 250 000 people in the UK with ME/CFS. Please help me and others who are suffering with ME/CFS.

I want a general election held, as the manifesto that was voted on has not be held. 
If labour do win it should be honoured for the next five years
additional_details: The manifesto has not been upheld and actually made a complete U-turn. It was voted on and not being adhered too so it is only right to present new manifestos from each government and let the people vote on those.

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Pause immigration until Home Office processes all pending asylum applications
background: Pause all legal and illegal immigration until those who are already in our country are processed correctly. Our resources are already stretched. We don't feel the present Government is doing enough. Enough is Enough!
additional_details:
Over 1000 people came into our waters illegally in one day. We believe as a country, we cannot cope with these numbers or the amount of money it costs to keep illegal migrants. 
 
We think the British people have had enough, we are scared, our bills keep rising, many of our veterans are on the streets, more people living in their cars. This country has been lost, are we the only ones that can see that? We need change, we need the boats to stop! We need to live, not just exist to pay taxes. We think this is a basic Human Right

action: Ban the sale of catapults and carrying catapults in public
background: We urge the Government to make carrying catapults in public places illegal, so that the police can arrest those carrying, especially in areas of known wildlife. We also urge the Government to ban the sale of catapults the UK, so they are not so easily accessible to children!
additional_details: I am a specialist of bird and believe we are currently in a wildlife crime pandemic. There have been reports of wildlife being attacked by young people carrying catapults and ball bearings. We think the law needs to change so that the Police has more powers to arrest those carrying catapults.

action: Ban industries serving food to the public from wearing latex gloves
background: We want latex gloves banned in all in commercial kitchens, restaurants, fast food chains, coffee shops, hotels, pubs, cruise ships, planes etc. We want the government to make it compulsory that anybody touching and preparing food must wear latex-free gloves if they wish to wear them.
additional_details: I have a latex allergy and latex proteins can migrate from gloves to food and potentially trigger allergic reactions in sensitised individuals. Sometimes I am afraid of eating or drinking out. I almost had a nasty experience when a member off staff was wearing latex gloves and I noticed when they were putting the lid on my coffee. Luckily I noticed it before I had a reaction. I think something needs to be done before someone gets hurt.

action: Allow pets to travel in the cabin on commercial flights to and from the UK.
background: Revise aviation regulations to permit small pets to travel in the cabin—safely contained—on commercial flights to and from the UK. Work with airlines to ensure clear, fair, and consistent policies, aligning the UK with practices in the EU, US, and other nations.
additional_details: Current cargo hold travel is stressful & potentially dangerous for pets. Allowing cabin travel significantly improves animal welfare. It's unfair that only private jet users currently have this option. Many countries (EU, US, Canada) allow it safely. Travel restrictions contribute to pet abandonment. Boarding/cargo is costly & stressful for owners. Solutions exist for allergies (limited pets/flight, HEPA filters, carrier rules, etc. This maintains all UK health/biosecurity standards.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a  similar action: 

Change rules to allow pets in airplane cabins going to and from the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727223

action: All new homes built in the UK to have Swift Nesting Bricks installed.
background: To impose a law that all new builds in the UK (homes and businesses) to have Swift Nesting Bricks installed to help increase the Swift population.
additional_details: Swift nest bricks provide safe, artificial nesting sites in buildings where natural cavities are lacking due to modern construction. By offering secure places to breed, they support higher breeding success and help stabilise or increase local Swift populations.
rejection_details: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727278

action: Require care settings to carry out basic nail care
background: We want the Government to require care providers in supported living, care homes and domiciliary care to provide basic nail care (such as nail trimming), unless there is a clear medical reason this must be done by a clinician.
additional_details:
Many care providers currently do not cut nails. We are concerned that as a result, vulnerable people are left with overgrown or painful nails, or forced to wait weeks for NHS podiatry appointments that may not be clinically necessary. This can lead to unnecessary discomfort and strain on NHS services.
 
We believe the government should require nail care to be part of personal care, not a clinical task — and that providers should be supported to carry this out safely with appropriate training and risk assessment.

action: Parliment to have an emergency debate on halting illegal immigration
background: I want the Government to have an emergency debate on immigration and to consider suspending immigration which includes allowing family members the right to live in the UK and deploying the Royal Navy to prevent illegal immigration until a sensible strategy is implemented.
additional_details: The country is a small island and we simply cannot fund the influx of immigrants without causing hardship to our own people.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:

Deploy the Royal Navy to help stop illegal immigrants entering the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/701998

action: Fund a National NHS Railcard for Healthcare Staff
background: Fund a National NHS Railcard to give healthcare staff discounted rail travel. This card could be similar to existing railcards for young people, veterans and seniors. We think this would ease commuting costs, support retention, and encourage public transport use.
additional_details: Many NHS professionals live far from their workplaces due to housing costs, and rail fares can exceed £300 per month.  A railcard would ease financial stress, support morale, support wellbeing, and recognise frontline workers in a practical way. It could also reduce car dependency and align with the UK’s environmental goals. We think is a fair, affordable step to value NHS staff, who keep our health system running.

action: Introduce a free UK visa or other evacuation route for refugees from Gaza
background: I want the UK Government to introduce and fund a free visa or evacuation route for refugees from the conflict in Gaza, including families, so that they can escape the violence and live in safety. I believe that thousands of lives could depend on action like this.
additional_details:
This petition is inspired by a family I know who are among those currently living in fear in Gaza, without any safe route out — a situation shared by many other vulnerable civilians.

I want to help peaceful civilians living in fear in Gaza, with no medical emergency, no relatives abroad, and no safe and legal way out. I want the Government to fund a visa or evacuation scheme to support these people, including families, on compassionate grounds.
 
We ask the Government to make this possible now as we fear more innocent lives will be lost.

action: Make using AI and generative language models in factual media a criminal offence
background: As a nation, we should make it a specific criminal offence to use any form of AI generated content or generative language model within any media that is presented as factual.
additional_details: I think British news, documentaries, and media are world-renowned. I believe it's essential that we draw a hard line in the sand when it comes to using AI and generative language models early on in their adoption. I believe this might not only help to stop the spread of disinformation but also help to restore public trust in the media. This, in turn, could help British factual media to maintain its good reputation.

action:
To stop the closure of Poole Hospital A & E
Services
background: There is a plan to shut Poole Hospital A&E department, and it will be transferred to Bournemouth Hospital. However it does not takes to consideration the travelling time that it takes to get from Swanage  and Wareham to travel to Bournemouth on a good day it takes 40 minutes, for heart attacks.
additional_details:
For people living in Rural Swange and Wareham and surrounding area, the travel time for emergency services to get from Swanage is 50 minutes and Wareham 40 minutes and that would be in 
Winter.
In the Summer when the area is a tourist influx doubles the population the traffic is stop and go at peak times who knows how long it would 
take.  This move to Bournemouth is totally impractical and should be cancelled.

action: I would like you to introduce flexiweek School holiday for parents and teachers.
background:
Take one of the school holiday weeks and make a flexiweek for parents/ teachers. This would help parents, teachers and the economy.
Ipads would be used so children can home study. This method can be used for a child who has been ill. It's a good way to teach a child to study themselves.
additional_details:
Good education is important but so is  happy childhood memories family time. Teachers should have a right to at least one week of their choice, this may help in recruitment.
 The population is about 69 million now, in 2050 the uk population is est to be 78m. We cannot continue cramming parents and teachers into a quarter of a year for holidays.
Some people cannot get time off during school holidays. 
People holidaying different times during the year would be good for seaside towns in th UK.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We don't know when you'd like the flexi-week to be. We're not sure if this would be an additional week of school during the year.

action: Fund mental health support for people who administered first aid
background: I would like the Government to provide funding for mental health support for all people who have administered first aid at a medical incident. This could be as simple as a call with someone who can give Mental Health support.
additional_details:
The reason I have put this petition together is that once the casualty has been taken by Paramedics, the person who administered first aid can have no idea 
about what happened to the casualty. This can start playing on the mind of the person who dealt with casualty, which can affect their mental health, and their personal life. We want the Government to fund mental health support for all people who administer first aid, to ensure they receive any support and advice they need.

action: Review punishments for young offenders
background: We want the government to review punishments for young offenders and decide whether they should receive harsher or lighter punishments.
additional_details: If an offender receives a harsh punishment, we are concerned that they could change in a negative way and suffer from depression. We are worried this could lead them to drug abuse or even joining gangs, which would only be negative for other peoples children as well.

action: Protect Legal Exemptions for Non-Stun Religious Slaughter in the UK
background: We call on the UK Government to uphold existing legal exemptions that permit non-stun religious slaughter under the Welfare of Animals at the Time of Killing (WATOK) Regulations, and to resist any proposals to remove or restrict these exemptions without compelling scientific or legal justification.
additional_details:
The UK recognises non-stun slaughter under the WATOK regulations, balancing animal welfare with the right to religious freedom, as protected by the the Human Rights Act 1998 and the ECHR.

When Religious slaughter is carried out properly, animals lose consciousness quickly. The FSA monitors these practices to ensure animal welfare.

Singling out non-stun is scientifically and ethically unjust and requires an inclusive approach towards welfare standards in general.
rejection_details: The Government has set out that this is already happening in its response to this petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/700557

action: Amend Section 27 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 to include all public highways
background: The existing Act deals with keeping dogs on a lead whilst on a road 'designated' by the local authority, but such roads are very rare and this legislation is seldom used.
additional_details:
Since the pandemic, dog ownership has surged along with attacks and other dog related incidents.
 
The Highway Code states 'Do not let a dog out on the road on its own. Keep it on a short lead when walking on the pavement, road or path shared with cyclists or horse riders' but this is not easily enforceable and a dog has to be 'dangerously out of control' before anything can be done. Very often this is too late and even if the incident is reported, only the gravest are dealt with fully. I think this change to the law could help protect the public and animals and enable faster enforcement.

action: Recall of MPs Act to cover MPs excluded from parliamentary estate for 60 Days+
background: Amend the Recall of MPs Act to trigger a recall petition for any MP banned from the Parliamentary estate and inactive for 60 days without in-person voting or participation in debates, questions, or committees, ensuring constituents can call a by-election.
additional_details: MPs excluded from the estate cannot perform all duties, which we believe leaves constituents unrepresented. We think including this provision would ensure that those unable to attend in person and inactive for two months can be recalled. We believe this helps to maintain democratic accountability and trust, and helps protect constituents' rights to effective representation.

action: Create a Fairer Immigration Policy for EU Citizens
background: We call on the UK Government to review and reform its post-Brexit immigration policy toward EU citizens. We ask that the UK recognises the unique relationship it shares with EU member states and creates a system that is fair, secure, and humane — not driven by fear or political rhetoric.
additional_details: The UK’s immigration debate has grown hostile and misleading. EU nationals contribute significantly to vital sectors like healthcare and social care. Post-Brexit, the UK should not treat EU neighbours the same as distant countries. We urge Parliament to reject misinformation and adopt a fair, secure, and compassionate immigration policy that recognises our historic ties and shared values with the EU.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly how you'd like the Government or Parliament to change the UK's migration policy for EU citizens.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Bring "Medical Exemption Certifictes" into the 21st century
background: We ask the Government to link medical exemption status directly to patient diagnosis using read codes in GP records. This would remove the need for separate applications, reduce admin burden for the NHS, and ensure patients access the care and medication they need without delay.
additional_details: The current medical exemption process creates unnecessary admin for patients and the NHS. Many with chronic conditions, like diabetes, are eligible but must still apply. By linking exemptions directly to diagnosis read codes already in GP systems, access can be automated, admin reduced, costs lowered, delays avoided, and patient care improved. This simple change uses existing data to make the system more efficient, fair and supportive for those who need ongoing care whilst crucially saving costs
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
Decisions about Medical Exemption Certificates are a matter for the NHS, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Ban In-Contract Price Hikes—Honour Fixed Full Contract Deals, Despite Inflation
background: We want the Government to ban all companies from raising prices during a fixed-term contract all together. We think a fixed deal should mean fixed price, and that  allowing mid-contract hikes is unfair, especially during a cost-of-living crisis.
additional_details: We believe allowing companies to raise prices during a fixed-term contract is unfair, even if the increases are advertised as per recent policy’s. Consumers enter fixed deals expecting stable costs. We think inflation shouldn’t justify breaking that trust. The Government must act to protect people from constant rising bills, especially ones where people are in fixed contracts. This should apply to all companies who supply contact based services.

action: I want you to re-think the proposal to change the parking arrangements around QE

action: Hold a referendum on leaving the European Court of Human Rights
background: We want the government to give our population the right to decide if we are to leave the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR). We think it is antiquated and not fit for the current world we live in.
additional_details: We want it to be replaced with a British Court of Human Rights. We think the government should give the British population the right to choose what matters to our people in our country and what our rules on human rights should be.
government_response_summary: Leaving the ECHR and the Court would be a costly, self-defeating move, undermining vital security agreements. Reforming it for today’s challenges is smarter than wasting £129m on a referendum.
government_response_body: The European Convention on Human Rights was formed in the wake of the Second World War, partly in response to the Holocaust and other horrors inflicted across Nazi-occupied Europe, and partly in reaction to the rise of totalitarian governments across the post-War Soviet bloc. British politicians and lawyers were among the chief architects of the Convention, and the UK was one of the first States to ratify it. We remain fully committed to protecting human rights both domestically and internationally as the essential underpinning of the liberties and democratic values that we all enjoy, and the ECHR plays an important role in that.  Our membership of the ECHR also facilitates and strengthens international co-operation on areas ranging from security to irregular migration. It is one of the foundations of peace and stability in Northern Ireland through its role in the Good Friday Agreement, it underpins law enforcement and judicial cooperation via the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement, and is also an important pillar of the devolution settlements. Since its introduction, the ECHR has made a positive difference to the lives and rights of those in the United Kingdom, including its role in the abolition of corporal punishment, ending the ban on LGBT+ people serving in the armed forces, and the continued abolition of the death penalty.  One of the ECHR’s most important provisions is the duty on states to protect an individual’s right to life. The families of the 97 football fans who lost their lives in the 1989 Hillsborough disaster relied on that right as they campaigned to obtain a new inquest, which concluded that the fans were unlawfully killed. Victims of the taxi-cab rapist John Worboys also used the ECHR to claim successfully that the Met Police had failed to investigate Worboys’ crimes effectively and had thereby breached their ECHR rights to protection against ill-treatment.   While the ECHR has played an important role in protecting the rights of UK citizens in the past, it is also true that no set of rules or multilateral institution is perfect; and neither the ECHR nor the European Court of Human Rights should be treated as impervious to change. Indeed, during the UK’s presidency of the Council of Europe in 2012, member states adopted a substantial package of reforms to the ECHR. That included reviewing the way we interpret ECHR provisions that impact asylum and immigration decisions in UK domestic law.   The Government’s 2025 Immigration White Paper (Restoring Control over the Immigration System) committed to bring forward legislation to strengthen the public interest test to make it clear that Parliament needs to be able to control our country’s borders and take back control of who comes to, and stays in the UK, striking the right balance between individual rights and the wider public interest.  The government will publish details of a major package of reform to the asylum system before the end of the year, including details of proposed changes to the implementation of the ECHR in the immigration system.  We believe that those reforms can be introduced to deliver our migration and criminal justice priorities without having to leave the ECHR, and this will remain our priority over the coming period, rather than delaying those reforms and instead holding an expensive referendum on the UK’s membership of the ECHR. According to the Electoral Commission, it cost £129 million to hold the referendum on membership of the European Union in 2016, so it would cost at least the same amount to hold a new UK-wide referendum on ECHR membership now.  The Government welcomes all efforts to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of multilateral institutions, including the European Court of Human Rights. The UK continues to engage with European partners on this issue, and the Prime Minister is leading efforts to build international consensus on strengthening the Convention system. A strengthened Court and Convention system ensures a focus on the most important cases, guaranteeing human rights as an essential element of the rule of law and protecting the dignity of all.  In view of Government’s support for the ECHR, it will not support the holding of a referendum on UK membership. However, commitment to the ECHR does not mean complacency. To retain public confidence in our policies on irregular migration, asylum and criminal justice, the ECHR and other instruments must evolve to face modern challenges.  Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

action: Deport all illegal migrants in the United Kingdom
background: We think an effective strategy is needed to identify, detain and deport all individuals residing the UK illegally.
additional_details: We think the cost to the taxpayer is crippling and needs to be addressed especially as more than 350,000 people in England are currently homeless. We think the UK is already so over-populated that the current government advocates building on low quality green belt land, or 'grey belt' land.
government_response_summary: The Government agrees that maximising the return of those unlawfully in the UK is essential to strengthening border security and restoring order to the asylum and immigration system.
government_response_body: The Prime Minister has repeatedly stated his commitment to reducing illegal immigration by dismantling the criminal gangs behind the trafficking of migrants across the channel and increasing the return of people with no right to be in this country. The Home Secretary has been clear on her priority to protect the UK border and explore all options to restore order to the immigration system.  The Government is bringing the full force of our laws to bear on these issues. Those found to have no right to be in the UK, including foreign criminals, should be returned as quickly as possible, through effective enforcement action where they refuse to depart voluntarily.   A systematic programme of work is focusing on delivering a major surge in immigration enforcement and returns activity. Immigration Enforcement staff are dedicated to making arrests, driving through decisions on individual cases, detaining people where necessary and getting them onto returns flights. In its first year in office, the Government returned over 35,000 failed asylum seekers, foreign criminals and other immigration offenders with no right to be in the UK, an increase of 13% on the previous year. This has included 66 charter flights, including four of the biggest returns flights in the UK's history, carrying more than 850 people.  There are significant and complex challenges that could impact on a person’s return as they move through the immigration system, such as new applications to regularise their stay, progressing through the appeals process or other litigation barriers, as well as changes in country situations. On 1 September, the then Home Secretary set out in Parliament a range of further measures for tackling abuses of the system that seek to prevent removal:   https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/strengthening-border-security-and-reforms-to-the-asylum-system  Strengthening international cooperation is also key to enabling quick and safe returns. Under the new treaty agreed with France in August - which allows the UK to directly return to France those who arrive in the UK on small boats - individuals can be detained immediately upon arrival at Dover, pending return. The first returns under this agreement began on 18 September 2025.  The Home Secretary agreed with Five Eyes partners to work even more closely to return those with no right to be in our countries by coordinating on measures like limiting visas for countries who do not cooperate. The Government is increasing detention capacity to support increased enforced returns, with work to establish two new immigration removal centres at Campsfield and Haslar progressing at pace.   Currently, there is a significant backlog in the First Tier Tribunal Immigration and Asylum Chamber, with an average wait time of 54 weeks. Whilst we have surged the average number of initial decisions made by 31,000 per quarter, delays in determining immigration and asylum appeals increase the pressure in the asylum accommodation system. That is why the Government announced plans to establish a new independent appeals body, which will be fully independent of government and staffed by professionally trained adjudicators, with safeguards to ensure high standards. It will be able to surge capacity as needed and to accelerate and prioritise cases, alongside new procedures to tackle repeat applications and unnecessary delays.  The Government has made a £1 billion investment in homelessness and rough sleeping services this year (2025/26), £233 million up on the year before, to prevent rises in the number of families in temporary accommodation and help to prevent rough sleeping.   The Spending Review protects this record level of investment to tackle homelessness and rough sleeping for the next three years and provides £100 million to fund increased homelessness prevention activity by local authorities.   The Government is committed to preserving Green Belts which have served England's towns and cities well over many decades. On 27 February 2025, it published updated Green Belt guidance, to ensure that a consistent approach is taken to the identification of grey belt land. More details can be found here:   https://www.gov.uk/guidance/green-belt.  The Government is taking forward an effective strategy for identifying and returning those with no right to be in this country. Further reforms will follow, but across Government, and led by the Home Office and Immigration Enforcement in particular, there will be a relentless focus on tackling the harm those here unlawfully cause to our economy and our society, building on progress so far and continuing to fix our broken system.  Home Office

action: Stop HMRC implementing making tax digital and enforcing quarterly submissions
background: HMRC is pushing ahead with Making Tax Digital: a scheme that requires all business to maintain digital accounts. Currently many small businesses use paper accounting records or spreadsheets. Small businesses may lack the skills, time and funding to maintain digital accounts.
additional_details: It is taxing enough for many of us to submit a yearly tax return to HMRC. But now we think this new implementation of making tax digital, using new software and quarterly submissions is taking things just too far.  Please stop making tax digital which is due to be started in April 2026. We think paying tax is hard enough but this is going to just add insult to injury.
government_response_summary: Making Tax Digital will help businesses stay on top of their affairs, boost productivity and ensure more of the right tax is paid. The Government will support users and has no plans to delay.
government_response_body: Making Tax Digital delivers value for money by increasing the amount of tax collected. This ensures that more money can go to funding vital public services, like the NHS, and supporting growth across the UK. Making Tax Digital for VAT has already been successful at reducing error and increasing tax revenues. HMRC’s published evaluation shows Making Tax Digital generated additional VAT revenue, as forecast, in the range of £185 million to £195 million in 2019 to 2020. Making Tax Digital for Income Tax  will build on this, and we expect it will result in an additional £1.95bn in tax cumulatively between its introduction and the 2029-30 financial year.   The Government is working with taxpayers, agents and software developers to ensure the introduction of Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from April 2026 is a success.  Making Tax Digital for Income Tax is a new approach that uses modern technology to helps customers stay on top of their tax affairs and avoid errors. It will build on successful introduction of Making Tax Digital for VAT which applies to over 2m VAT-registered businesses. Making Tax Digital for Income Tax requires sole traders and landlords to use software to keep digital records and send simple quarterly updates to HMRC. These quarterly updates are not tax returns. They aim to be simple and quick to complete, with software automatically drawing data from digital records.  From 6 April 2026, sole traders and landlords with a qualifying income over £50,000 must use it, where their qualifying income is their total annual income before the deduction of expenses or tax from self-employment and property. HMRC are introducing Making Tax Digital for Income Tax in phases, meaning that smaller businesses with qualifying income above £30,000 will be required to use the service from April 2027, with those above £20,000 brought in in April 2028.  The Government understands this is a big change for many taxpayers and agents, and it is committed to supporting them through the transition. It has worked with the software industry to ensure there is free and low-cost software available to support smaller and simpler businesses.  HMRC is also taking comprehensive steps to raise awareness by writing to affected taxpayers and agents, engaging widely with industry and tax bodies and launching a marketing campaign through social media and radio.   HM Treasury

Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly how you'd like MPs or the Government to be removed or the mechanism to carry out this specific action.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly how you would like the Government or Parliament to change the law to do this.

action: Launch a UK bottle deposit scheme to reward recycling and keep Britain clean
background: We urge the UK Government to fast-track a Germany-style bottle deposit scheme by 2026: eg £0.10–£0.20 deposits on plastic, cans, and glass, refunded at 20,000+ new return points. Reward recycling, cut 6.5B bottles in litter and keep Britain clean.
additional_details: UK’s single-use bottles litter streets, beaches, harming wildlife and costing millions in cleanup. Germany’s Pfand system, with £0.10–£0.20 deposits and 98% return rate, cuts waste and rewards recycling. We urge a UK scheme by 2026 with 20,000+ return points to incentivize sustainable habits, reduce landfill, save public funds, and protect our environment.
rejection_details:
In January this year, the Government introduced legislation to implement a deposit return scheme in the UK. You can find out more information here: 
https://www.gov.uk/government/news/government-to-clean-up-communities-with-deposit-return-scheme-for-plastic-bottles-and-cans

action: Abolish Section 21 'no-fault' evictions with immediate effect
background: We believe that despite repeated Government pledges to abolish Section 21, delays have left millions of tenants vulnerable. Landlords can give a Section 21 notice to evict tenants with just two months’ notice. We think it can often be in retaliation for requesting repairs or asserting legal rights.
additional_details: We call on the Government to speed up the passage of legislation and abolish Section 21 of the Housing Act 1988 now. It allows landlords to evict tenants without any fault from the tenant. We think this practice is outdated, unjust, incompatible with a fair housing system, and that it causes housing insecurity, unfair displacement, and retaliatory evictions. In our view, the Renters Reform Bill has been delayed for too long and Parliament must take immediate action to protect renters by terminating Section 21 now.

action: Seek free movement agreement with Australia, Canada & New Zealand
background: We want the Government to negotiate with the governments of Australia, Canada and New Zealand with a view to establishing the free movement of our collective citizens between these countries.
additional_details: Because we think the said countries have a great deal in common & it seems reasonable that because of our shared values, our systems of government, our shared heritage, our shared language, our shared systems of judiciary and our positive cooperation that we envisage greater freedoms of movement of people. We could enter into such agreements without political Union.

action: Lower the price of car insurance for learners / new drivers
background: the price of car insurance for new drivers is outrageous and with there being barley any jobs for young uk citizens to work at, especially in rural areas. me and 1000s of other young drivers would like the cost of insurance to actually be lowered to the £1200 depending on the score of driving test

We want this sorted. not all of us have £6000 spare.

background: Government to reassess reliance on US Treasuries amid dollar decline and trade volatility. Selling £60 billion of £690 billion owned, Parliament should adopt a structured divestment strategy to maximise returns. Funds should be reinvested in inflation relief, NHS, military expansion and others.
additional_details: Holding excessive US debt risks devaluing UK reserves. Trump's policies tariffs, deficit spending threaten Treasury values. With China offloading debt, the UK must act to protect its position and reinvest in infrastructure, inflation relief, NHS, tax relief, national expansion, and military growth. If Japan follows, Britain risks holding a declining asset. A structured selloff would fund transport upgrades, pothole repairs, energy security, defence, and economic recovery, ensuring stability.

action: Require galleries segregate artists' sale proceeds, protect them from insolvency
background: We urge Parliament to enact legislation requiring UK art galleries to segregate artists' sale proceeds into separate, protected trust accounts. We think this is essential to prevent commingling, ensure funds are not lost in gallery insolvencies, and safeguard artists' livelihoods.
additional_details:
This legislation must mirror laws like New York's, which we feel are a success.
 
In gallery insolvencies, artists' funds can be lost when commingled with gallery assets, resulting in their treatment as unsecured creditors with no recovery. We believe existing UK remedies are reactive, costly, and ineffective for artists, particularly in the absence of strong contracts. We see this as a systemic issue undermining artists' livelihoods and the British art market's reputation. We think that mandating segregation of the proceeds of sales of artists' work, as we believe has been successfully implemented in New York, is crucial preventative action to secure artists' incomes, foster trust, and ensure market integrity.

action: Raise the VAT threshold to £250,000 for small businesses
background: Raise the VAT threshold from £90,000 to £250,000 to support small businesses. We believe this could reduce red tape, encourage growth, and remove what we feel is an unfair penalty on growing businesses. We believe the current system discourages expansion and punishes progress.
additional_details: We feel the £90,000 VAT threshold hasn't kept up with inflation and the current system damages growth and profit. We believe that raising it to £250,000 could support sustainability, reduce admin, and boost the economy.

action: Do not change Access to Work scheme
background: I’m concerned that changes to Access To Work could take away the ability of many people with disabilities to be able to work independently. Often the payments are not huge, but they make a huge difference. This is not a benefit for those who do not work- quite the opposite!
additional_details: The payments can put disabled people on a level playing field, enabling them to make a valuable contribution to society and not have to claim other benefits. They can fund a range of support. We think it’s one of the most useful and fair ‘benefits’, disabled people WANT to work . Don’t disable!

action: Ensure All Aesthetic Practitioners Can Access Emergency Medicines
background: Allow all aesthetic practitioners, including non-prescribers, to hold and administer emergency drugs such as hyaluronidase and adrenaline. New NMC prescribing rules reduce timely access, increasing public risk. Emergency medication should be accessible and mandated for all to ensure public safety.
additional_details: The NMC’s prescribing changes (And those of the GMC/GDC) restrict non-prescribers from accessing emergency medications such as hyaluronidase and adrenaline. In time-critical situations such as vascular occlusion or anaphylaxis, delays can lead to blindness or death. This doesn’t improve safety, it compromises it. All qualified practitioners should be able to stock and administer emergency drugs to protect the public and uphold the highest safety standards in the aesthetics industry.

action: Ban or restrict hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) in cosmetic products
background: Ban or strictly regulate HEMA in consumer nail products. Require clear warning labels where HEMA is allowed and ensure salons offer alternative products without HEMA so consumers can make an informed choice. We also need to educate consumers and professionals on the risks of HEMA exposure.
additional_details: Hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) is a common ingredient in nail products but it’s also a known cause of severe allergic reactions, skin sensitisation, and long-term damage. Over the last 10 years, allergic contact dermatitis from acrylate-containing nail cosmetics (acrylic nails, gel nails, gel nail polish) has been reported repeatedly. Studies show up to 97% of allergic reactions from nail cosmetics are linked to HEMA and consumers are unknowingly exposed to this toxic ingredient.
rejection_details: Legislation is already in place which means that nail products containing HEMA cannot be placed on the market in the UK unless they are for professional use only. The nail products must be labelled “For professional use only” and “can cause an allergic reaction”.

action: Fund healthcare framework and pathways for adults with Cerebral Palsy
background: Adults with Cerebral Palsy face worsening symptoms and high rates of co-morbidities, yet there's no dedicated healthcare framework for them to ensure access to coordinated, specialist-led healthcare provision.
additional_details:
CP doesn’t end at childhood—lifelong, tailored support is vital. we need clear treatment pathways and referral routes to ensure adults with cp can access the healthcare they need, while upholding their dignity, health, and quality of life.

action: Make Play and Continuous Provision statutory in England's Key Stage 1 Curriculum
background: Revise statutory guidance for KS1 to make play based pedagogy a core part of the Key Stage One National Curriculum, extending the best practice that we see in Early Years to ensure all Key Stage One children continue to have a developmentally appropriate play based approach to their learning.
additional_details: The Early Years Framework highlights the importance of play. However, as children transition to Year 1 and throughout KS1, many may experience a stark shift to formal teaching strategies. We think this fails to reflect how young children learn best. We want our children to access a reformed education system that meets their developmental needs, supports wellbeing, allows for movement, communication, play and develops a true love of learning, enabling all children to thrive.
government_response_summary: We recognise play is critical to children’s wellbeing and development which is why the Department is working to make sure that all children have access to these enrichment opportunities at school.
government_response_body: The Department is working to make sure that all children and young people have access to a variety of enrichment opportunities at school, as an important part of our mission to break down barriers to opportunity. For some schools, these opportunities may be used to encourage children and young people to play.  We recognise that play is critical to children’s wellbeing and development, as highlighted in the Centre for Young Lives’ Everything to Play For report. This is reflected in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) statutory framework, which is clear that play is essential for children’s learning and development. The EYFS emphasises the importance of creating opportunities for indoor and outdoor play, and enabling environments and cultures for high-quality play.  Our expectation is for schools to organise the school day and school week in the best interests of their pupil cohort, to both provide them with a full time education suitable to their age, aptitude and ability, and to provide opportunities for schools to incorporate time for play and other activities.  We recognise the current key stage 1 curriculum requires reform. This is why the Government established an independent Curriculum and Assessment Review, to look into issues, such as this, and make recommendations to improve the curriculum for children. The Review Group is currently looking across the existing national curriculum and statutory assessment system, to ensure they meet the needs of young people in your area and across England.  The Review’s final report and recommendations will be published in autumn, at which point the Government will be in a position to consider any changes to the curriculum. The Government will consult with education experts, teachers, and parents to ensure the very best for children in England.  Department for Education

action: Create a statutory body to oversee university academic appeals
