background: We want the Government to waive the English proficiency test requirement for naturalisation applicants aged 18+ who have completed significant formal education in the UK, including primary, secondary, and ongoing further/higher education taught and assessed in English.
additional_details: We believe it is unfair and illogical to require young adults who have studied for sometimes over a decade in UK schools (primary & secondary) and undergoing undergraduate university education at the time of application, to prove English proficiency via an additional test. We feel this can place an unnecessary financial and emotional burden on families, devalue UK education, and ignores clear evidence of fluency already demonstrated.

action: Include asexuality as a protected characteristic in the Equality Act 2010
background: Include asexuality in the Equality Act 2010 to prevent discrimination
additional_details: Asexuality is not explicitly recognised in the Equality Act 2010 as a protected characteristic. While the Act covers discrimination based on sexual orientation, it defines this as attraction to the same sex, opposite sex, or either sex. Asexuality defined as the lack of sexual attraction, falls outside of this definition.

action: Ringfence revenue from Vehicle Excise Duty for roads
background: We call upon the Government to ringfence revenue from Vehicle Excise Duty (Vehicle Tax), with all monies raised to be solely used for the maintenance, repair, and improvement of Britain's roads.
additional_details:
Currently, Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) goes into general government revenues and is not specifically allocated to road upkeep.
 
Meanwhile, many British roads suffer from poor maintenance, potholes, and declining infrastructure. Many road users rightly expect that the taxes they pay for vehicle use should directly contribute to the condition and safety of the roads they travel on, without the cost of additional expenditure due to repairs on their cars from damage caused by pot holes which are unavoidable.

action: Ban local councils from requiring work permits for under 16s eligible to work
background: We would like the Government to ban local councils from requiring work permits for under 16s for any job, for those already eligible to work. We think this would help more under 16s get a job
additional_details: We don’t think you should need a permit to be able to get a good job between the ages of 13 and 16. We think under 16s should be considered for jobs on their personality and obvious determination for work rather than if they have a permit or not.

action: Increase foreign aid funding for children affected by war and conflict
background: Children caught in war are often denied education, healthcare, safety, and a chance at a normal life. This could be helped by funding education programs in refugee camps, and increasing humanitarian aid for children.
additional_details: I believe as a country that values human rights, the UK should lead efforts to protect the future of children affected by war and conflict.

action: Keep the UK Out of Any War with Iran and Israel.
background: I urge the UK government to stay out of any military action in the Iran-Israel conflict. No troops, no weapons, no war support. Focus on peace, diplomacy, humanitarian aid for civilians, and transparency in all foreign policy decisions to protect lives and promote stability.
additional_details: War risks British lives. Sending troops or weapons into conflicts that don’t directly threaten the UK drags us into danger with unpredictable consequences. History shows military interventions often make conflicts worse, causing more violence and suffering. The UK should focus on peace, diplomacy, aid to civilians, and invest taxpayer money in public services instead of costly wars abroad that divide us.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: 

Commit to no military involvement in attacks on Iran
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730360

action: Fund Social Services in Portsmouth to Protect Children from Abuse
background: We are urgently calling on the UK Government and Parliament to increase funding for children’s social services, review the impact of underfunding on child protection, invest in early intervention, and improve support for social workers to protect vulnerable children in Portsmouth.
additional_details: Children in Portsmouth are being left in unsafe homes due to underfunded social services. Overworked staff can't respond fast enough, and vital support is delayed or denied. Without urgent funding and reform, more children will suffer harm that could have been prevented. As someone who has experienced abuse firsthand, I know how it feels to be isolated and beyond rescue. But I want children across Portsmouth to know they are not alone — there is always someone ready to stand by their side and fight for their safety.
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: To get the government to supply sanitary products to women and girls in poverty
background: Supply areas of high poverty and homelessness with sanitary products as often individuals who are struggling financially have to ration their income thus meaning a simple need such as a tampon or a pad seems expensive.
additional_details:
The lack of period products often causes individuals to conform to using unsanitary products which leads to many health problems . Additionally it impacts education as girls have to miss school .it impacts the uk highly , it was found that 50% of girls said that they couldn’t afford menstrual products at some point in the past. 
This is a highly impactful topic and a real problem!!!!!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions, which call for similar action:

Fund increased access to menstrual products to address period poverty
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710759

Fund free period hygiene products via the NHS for all who need it
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/704841

action: Accountability for Animal wefare
background: We need the government to address the abuse and torture of Animals in abbatoirs or anywhere that deals with farm Animals. Also accountability of abuser.
additional_details: There are so many sensitive videos of Animal abuse especially in abbatoirs on Facebook it is sickening, something needs to be done not later it needs to be done now. What has happened to Animal welfare? Why is this being allowed to carry on? We need an MP that people can raise concerns to, not the amount of agencies that you have to go to.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. There are already laws that forbid animal abuse and cruelty, as well as regulations on how animals should be treated on farms and at slaughterhouses. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Grooming gang national enquiry to name officials and consider failures to act
background: To ensure that the culture within the Crown and Public Service, including but not limited to the Police, Social Work, Teaching, plus amongst elected officials, is one of accountability.
additional_details:
We think the National Enquiry must have the following elements:
 
1. Be an overarching investigation into child grooming gangs, that will name individual Crown and Public Servants that failed to act.
 
2. Where the race, ethnicity or religion of the offenders/victims is a underlying issue, identify what prevented officials from acting to prevent harm.
 
3. Identify what characteristics the victims shared that made them unlistened to, unbelieved and undervalued.

action: Force airlines to offer non-overbooked flight tickets
background: We think airlines should be forced to offer some tickets on flights that cannot be overbooked - "guaranteed boarding". An airline would then not be able to sell more of these tickets than there are actually available.
additional_details: Selling more of a product than a company is able to provide might be considered fraudulent in other settings. The justification by airlines is that selling extra seats means tickets are cheaper and planes are less empty. To maintain these benefits, ‘non-guaranteed boarding’ and ‘guaranteed boarding’ tickets could both be available to allow for passengers to accept the higher cost if they choose to. When someone has an event like a funeral to attend, they may wish to pay to guarantee their seat.

action: Students at secondary schools should be allowed to wear smart shorts as uniform
background: we would like the government to ensure that students at schools in the UK are permitted to wear smart shorts as part of their school uniform during the increasingly hot months.
additional_details: Many students feel as if they are boiling alive in their school uniform trousers, this is basic health and safety - there are students fainting and being unwell because of the excessive heat suffered in schools, many schools do not have air conditioning and temperatures in classrooms regularly hit over 30 degrees. Students will be able to work more efficiently in cool, smart shorts - shorts are a cheaper alternative to trousers, this would encourage improved attendance and happiness.
rejection_details:
School uniform policy is a matter for schools themselves.

The Government sets guidance on school uniform policy. This recommends that schools "take a sensible approach to allow for exceptions to be made during extreme weather – for example, allowing pupils to wear shorts in very hot weather or allowing trousers to be worn instead of skirts in very cold weather."

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/school-uniform/school-uniforms

You could reach out to a particular school to request they change their policy.

action: Review decision-making in asylum cases involving Ukrainian applicants
background: Since 2022, the UK has offered humanitarian protection to Ukrainians via the Ukraine Scheme and its subsequent extension. We think this shows the UK recognises it is unsafe to return. Yet, those seeking ASYLUM are routinely refused.
additional_details: We believe this contradiction creates a LEGAL PARADOX and leaves Ukrainian nationals in a state of deep uncertainty. It could raise concerns about the consistency of the UK’s protection policies.

action: Change law: OFWAT to block dividends & executive bonuses when rationing water
background: Change the Water (Special Measures) Act to require OFWAT to block executive bonuses and payment of shareholder dividends in the event of water companies declaring water rationing measures.
additional_details: Water companies have paid billions in shareholder dividends and bonuses while neglecting to make adequate investment in future proofing our water infrastructure to keep up with climate change or a growing population. We think the government should intervene and change the law to correct a market failure, by requiring OFWAT to apply financial penalties to shareholders and executives in the event of implementing water rationing.

action: Require key worker housing eligibility to include frontline charity workers
background: We believe key worker housing scheme providers should be required to include frontline charity workers in eligibility criteria for key worker housing schemes, in the same way as certain essential public sector workers.
additional_details:
Housing schemes for affordable or subsidized housing options are predominately available to essential public sector workers. We believe that frontline charity workers provide essential services and significantly support the public sector, especially in services like homelessness, mental- health and housing support. Therefore, we think their staff should be eligible, the same as certain public sector workers.
 
We think this could help charity frontline staff to address their critical needs for housing, to live closer to work and keep the most talented and dedicated staff in the charity sector.

action: Block BBC proposal to prevent households opting out of paying the TV licence.
background:
Rumours have circulated that the BBC is proposing enforcement of compulsory payment of the TV licence and charging higher rates for those in higher council tax bands…

This proposal needs to be blocked and prevented.
additional_details:
A large majority of the Nation do not consume live TV and ESPECIALLY avoid BBC services due to the constant propaganda and the ideological narrative pushed which doesn’t align with the values of modern British citizens. 

It’s wrong to force households to pay for services which they do not want or support. 

This fee is outdated and needs to be abolished.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730557

action: Grant Legal Right for Parents to Record All Interactions with Social Service
background: Legislate a clear legal right for parents to record all meetings, phone calls, and home visits with social services. This should ensure transparency, allow evidence to be used in proceedings, and prevent misrepresentation or manipulation of events.
additional_details: Many parents report feeling powerless and misrepresented in interactions with social services. Recordings would provide accountability, support fair assessments, and protect both families and professionals. It may reduce wrongful child removals and rebuild trust in the system. Failings from social services can have devastating consequences, including loss of life.

action: Rule out BBC licence fee being linked to council tax
background: There have been reports of the licence fee being linked to council tax, following a media interview from the BBC Chairman that covered future funding. For the reasons stated below, this petition asks that the Government should rule this out.
additional_details:
1. We think this would create complexities that requiring major legislative and bureaucratic overhaul and higher administrative costs.
 
2. We believe it could erode consumer choice, forcing payment regardless of usage.
 
3. We think it would disproportionately burden those on low or fixed incomes, especially those already struggling to pay C.T, and risk penalising everyone while ignoring media consumption or ability to pay.

action: Set out a pro-innovation strategy for blockchain and stablecoins
background:
Publish a strategy for blockchain & stablecoins. We want this to:
1. Drive a pro-innovation stablecoin & tokenisation regulatory regime e.g. support interest bearing stablecoins & preserve role as wholesale settlement asset
2. Explore Govt uses for blockchain
3. Appoint a blockchain & crypto czar
additional_details:
For centuries London was the centre of global trade and finance. We consider that the future is digital where equities, bonds and real world assets exist as tokens - tradeable 24/7, instantly, globally.
 
We consider stablecoins to be the basis of a tokenised economy; the US has ruled out CBDCs and is leaning into stablecoins. The UK is at a crossroads and we believe it will fall behind without a strategy. This is a question of national interest to preserve the competitiveness of the City and sterling’s global standing.
government_response_summary: The government published its Wholesale Digital Markets Strategy in July and will bring forward legislation for a financial services regulatory regime for cryptoassets this year.
government_response_body: The government recognises the transformative potential for digital assets and blockchain technologies to drive economic growth in the UK and increase efficiencies across financial markets. We are committed to making the UK a world leading destination for digital assets.     As part of this the government is bringing forward legislation for a comprehensive  financial services regulatory framework for cryptoassets by the end of this year. In April, the government published draft legislation for the core of the future regime, which includes provisions to support the development of UK GBP-backed stablecoin and facilitate effective market access for overseas-issued stablecoin.    The government is actively exploring the use of new blockchain technologies, and published a Wholesale Financial Markets Digital Strategy in July that sets out its approach to digitalising markets. The government has committed to:  1. Enabling the sector to test, scale and roll out solutions that tokenise financial assets and support the digitalisation of post trade processes. 2. Providing a regulatory and legislative framework that allows new digital solutions to be taken forward, and quickly putting in place permanent changes. 3. Ensuring there is a cross-sectoral approach to DLT adoption in wholesale financial markets, where the sector is able to identify the best DLT use cases and build cross-market coalitions to take forward live activity.  The government plans to appoint Digital Markets Champion, who will provide leadership for the sector on wholesale market digitalisation and join up work in the UK sector with other jurisdictions. Further updates will be announced in due course.  HM Treasury

action: Review support and payment for councillors in England
background: We ask the government to formally review the system of support and payment for councillors. We think this will help ensure this most vital of roles attracts and retains high quality candidates who are representative of the communities they serve.
additional_details: It's previously been reported that the average age of councillors in England is 60, 20 years older than the latest estimated median age of England and Wales' population. Government is overseeing a move to single-tier unitary authorities which is likely to mean fewer locally elected representatives. We think a review should look at reinstating the pre-2014 pensions scheme for local government and introducing parental leave as a statutory right, as well as consideration of an independent system to set allowances, loss of office payments and any other measures that may make it easier for people of all ages and backgrounds to stand.

action: Implement a 4-day work week
background: We are calling on the Government to legislate for a standard 4-day working week (32 hours) with no loss of pay. This change should apply across sectors where feasible, following pilot schemes and consultation with employers, trade unions, and workers.
additional_details: A 4-day work week can improve productivity, reduce burnout, and boost work-life balance. Trials in the UK and globally have shown that shorter working weeks can maintain or even increase output while improving employee wellbeing. A shift to a 4-day week could also help reduce unemployment by distributing work more fairly and support environmental goals by cutting commuting time. It's time to modernise our approach to work and ensure that technological progress benefits everyone.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government isn't responsible for the issue you raise. UK law places limits on the total amount of time someone can work during a week and the minimum amount they can be paid an hour, but it doesn't specify how many or which days of the week they have to work. This would be a decision for employers and the employee.

We could accept a petition calling for the legal maximum number of hours during a week to be reduced or a legal limit placed on the days that people can work, if this is something you would like to see happen.

action: Require all shops in England to sell alcohol in a separate, screened area
background: I call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring all supermarkets and retailers in England to only sell alcohol in a clearly separated and screened area.
additional_details: We believe constant alcohol visibility in stores can trigger relapse and distress for those recovering from addiction or struggling with mental health. We feel this measure would not restrict access for the general public but could help support vulnerable individuals, reduce harm, save lives, and ease pressure on the NHS and mental health services. It’s a simple change which we believe could have a meaningful impact.

action: Legislate to upgrade all B class license holders to include the C1 category
background: We urge the Government to pass a law where in the same way people with a B class (car/van 3.5 tonne) driver’s license are automatically entitled to a B+E category (car/van and trailer) license, people with a B class license can be automatically entitled to a C1 (7.5 tonne) license.
additional_details: People who passed their driving test in a car before 1997 automatically have C1 category on their driver’s license under “grandfather rights”. Those who wish to upgrade their license to include the C1 category may pay up to £1500 for tests and training. This includes ambulance workers who require C1 licenses as part of their job, or people who wish to drive motorhomes or removal vans. With long waiting test times, we think this could reduce pressures on test centres.

action: Mandatory collection and publication of certain child sexual offender data
background: Place a statutory requirement on councils, the police, the Crown Prosecution Service and all other related institutions to collect, record and publish the nationality, ethnicity, immigration status and religion of child sexual offenders, including gang based crime.
additional_details: To protect children and inform public policy, we believe it is essential to collect, record and publish the nationality, ethnicity, immigration status and religion of all child sexual offenders, including gang based crime. This data will allow for better understanding of offender demographics, ensure transparency, and support targeted safeguarding strategies. Without this information, critical patterns may be missed, weakening efforts to prevent abuse and protect vulnerable children.
government_response_summary: The Government is already taking action to increase the collection and transparency of data on the demographic characteristics of individuals responsible for group-based child sexual exploitation.
government_response_body: The Government is determined to protect children from the horrors of grooming gangs and other forms of sexual abuse and exploitation. In February 2025, the Prime Minister and then Home Secretary commissioned Baroness Louise Casey of Blackstock to evaluate the understanding of the scale, nature and drivers of group-based child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSEA), including assessing data on the ethnicity of perpetrators. Her National Audit was published on Monday 16 June, and can be found here – https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-audit-on-group-based-child-sexual-exploitation-and-abuse.    The Government immediately accepted the twelve recommendations from Baroness Casey’s Audit, which included making it a requirement for the police to collect the ethnicity and nationality data of individuals suspected of being members of grooming gangs or perpetrators of other group-based child sexual exploitation (recommendation four).    In July this year, the former Home Secretary wrote to all Chief Constables to set out the clear expectation that ethnicity data on child sexual exploitation and grooming gang suspects should be collected in every case, and to urge them to make sure they are fulfilling their obligation to collect suspect ethnicity data as part of the Government's commitment to transparency and accountability. The Home Office is closely monitoring data collection and provision from forces and continues to engage with individual forces on where improvements are required. If we do not see improvements, we will not hesitate to take further action.    In respect of nationality data, the Ministry of Justice already includes data on the nationality of persons within the prison system in its quarterly offender management statistics, here: https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/offender-management-statistics-quarterly.  In addition, the Home Office has committed to review the data that it collects and publishes regarding the nationalities and offences committed by foreign national offenders who are subject to deportation proceedings. Further details of that review process can be found here:   https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/statistics-on-foreign-national-offenders-and-the-immigration-system.   Recommendation four of Baroness Casey’s Audit did not include the collection of data on religion and immigration status. There is no current mechanism to collect such data on religion, other than through any declaration made by the perpetrator themselves, which would weaken both the accuracy and comprehensiveness of any analysis based on that data.   More broadly, as part of implementing the Casey Audit recommendations, we will nonetheless be looking at how safeguarding agencies (including the police, local authorities, schools and health services) are using information and intelligence to disrupt and prosecute those committing these terrible crimes and ensure victims and survivors are protected.   We will also continually seek to deepen our understanding of the drivers behind child grooming gangs and other group-based child sexual exploitation and abuse and ensure that as many as possible of the perpetrators responsible for these heinous crimes – whether non-recent or contemporary – are investigated and brought to justice.   Home Office  This is a revised response. The Petitions Committee requested a response which more directly addressed the request of the petition. You can find the original response towards the bottom of the petition page (https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730605)

action: Create a ‘Community First’ legal duty for charity legacy property sales
background:
Introduce a Community First Disposal Framework, which we feel will restore legacy justice to the charitable sector, including:
Before sale, public notice of assets, community right of first offer, social value assessments. Formal donor recognition & Charity Commission public register of disposal
additional_details: Often, people may leave churches, homes, land etc to charities believing they are serving their communities. These are gifts of trust and sacrifice, not assets to sell off in silence. We believe the Charities Act 2022 removed key protections, and that we now need the law to ensure donor's wishes are respected, protect local spaces and keep the money from property where it was meant to make a difference, in the community. We think we need a legal duty to protect donor intent, safeguard legacy spaces and keep wealth in the communities it was meant to serve.

action: Raise the marriage allowance to the full personal allowance of £12750
background: Currently the UK's personal allowance of £12570 offers individuals a significant tax free income.  We propose a crucial adjustment: enabling the full transfer of a non-working partner's personal allowance to their working spouse.
additional_details: This reform would effectively double a family's tax free income to £25140, providing much-needed financial breathing room and empowering families to choose for one parent to be a stay-at-home carer for their children.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Allow people to transfer all their personal allowance to their spouse 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727117

action: Allow pets to travel freely between the UK and Europe with proper documentation.
background: I urge the UK government to reconsider the current pet travel restrictions by permitting pets to enter and exit the UK from Europe with valid passports and health certificates, including proof of vaccinations and deworming. A pilot program at Liverpool Airport could facilitate this change.
additional_details: I urge the UK government to reassess pet travel restrictions that challenge pet owners. Allowing pets to travel between the UK and Continental Europe with valid health documentation would promote family unity and responsible ownership. A trial program at key airports, such as Liverpool, would be a valuable first step in modernising our approach to pet travel, reflecting the needs of today’s pet owners.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. Pets can already travel freely from the UK to a EU country, and return to the UK from an EU country, as long as certain requirements are met such as gaining an animal health certificate. 

You can learn more about these requirements and rules for taking pets into the EU here: https://www.gov.uk/taking-your-pet-abroad

You can learn more about bringing a pet back to Great Britain here: https://www.gov.uk/bring-pet-to-great-britain/which-pet-travel-document 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Require all social media platforms to verify identity of accounts
background: Make identity verification a legal requirement for all existing and new users on social media platforms. Nicknames could be used to maintain anonymity in the public eye, but accounts will be linked to real identities to help ensure social media users can be traced by authorities.
additional_details:
This could protect people against online hate and act as a deterrent to social media users writing hate online. Even with a nickname as a username, verification could mean a person can be traced and held responsible and deter people from writing hate and setting up fake accounts.
These extra layers of identification could also enable simpler identification of users, allowing action to be taken by platforms and authorities to deal with online hate.
We think this will create a safer online space for all.

action: Stop considering asylum requests for 2 years to control illegal migration
background: Suspend the asylum system for 2 years. We believe this could clear the asylum backlog and help the Government introduce a fairer asylum and welfare system, and suitable accommodation for genuine asylum seekers. We believe systems are abused, misused and broken.
additional_details: Under this suspension anyone arriving illegally by any route claiming asylum should be returned immediately to the country they travelled from. Many of us agree we have a migrant crisis. We think we should take ownership of our borders. We believe UK taxpayers cannot support everyone who arrives at our borders and demands asylum. We want this suspension so the systems change so they are sustainable, affordable and fit for purpose.

action: Broaden Grooming Gang Commission and ensure remit debated by MPs
background: We call on Government and Parliament to broaden the new Grooming Gangs Commission so it can compel evidence from central departments, national police bodies and politicians, make findings on their actions, and refer evidence to relevant bodies. Ensure its remit is debated by MPs.
additional_details: In the 16th June Govt response, the national inquiry section says “local” five times, never “central”. Evidence raises concerns about authorities' failure to act. I think survivors need an inquiry able to scrutinise central decisions, compel witnesses and gather evidence. I think a Commons debate on the remit will show independence and rebuild trust.

action: Make prescriptions free in England like Wales and Scotland
background: Make prescriptions free in England like Wales and Scotland, to make healthcare and medication more accessible.
additional_details:
Why does England have to pay for prescriptions when they’re free in Wales and Scotland? 
 
People are not getting their prescriptions because they can’t afford it. Why is this the current situation that we’re all living in?! We believe people should not have to choose between paying for prescriptions or something else. 
 
Make prescriptions free in England. This could save lives!

action: Creation of reperations and compensation fund for any foreign war
background: The UK to put in escrow 30 billion for post-war rebuild, additional £20k per family per person killed in affected countries. Commit an extra £20 billion to the refugeecare fund in Uk eg nhs. Money must be paid upfront apart from reparation for the dead must be paid within 1 year.
additional_details:
Cost of living is rising, our services are stretch and we are fighting wars at the behest of other then dealing with the refugees crisis while other take minimum load. 

This given money for rebuild quickly keeping people there but also enable our services to ramp up for influx proactively rather then reactively.

If we don't have the money then we sit out
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call for a clear action. You have explained you would like a reparations and compensation fund to be started, but we are unsure if you would like this to apply to all foreign wars, or only to certain wars (for example - where the UK is involved in a particular way).

You could start a new petition setting out clearly what you would like to happen.

action: Create widespread promotion for more eco-friendly writing options in school
background: Currently, an appalling amount of paper is wasted because of the use of paper workbooks and extra sheets in UK schools. This problem should be worked on within individual schools, but government involvement could help bring much needed awareness to what an issue this paper usage is.
additional_details: There are many ways that this can be tackled, but the best option of them all would be providing thin, flexible binders that children can attach writing paper and sheets to so there is not the excessive use of paper, purely used to stick down another sheet of paper. Large, cardboard binders will be impractical as they will be too big to have for every subject, but a thinner binder almost like the cover of a workbook could work very well for helping reduce the use of paper in schools.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call for a clear action from the UK Government or Parliament.

You have explained that you are concerned about paper usage in schools, but we're not sure what specific action you would like the Government or Parliament to take. You ask for "widespread promotion" but we are not sure exactly what you mean by this.

You could start a new petition setting out more clearly what action you'd like the Government or Parliament to take.

action: Calculate child maintenance from net pay, not gross pay
background: For child maintenance to be calculated from net pay not gross pay.
additional_details: We want reform to the current method used to calculate child maintenance payments, which is based on a paying parent's gross income. While we fully support the fundamental principle that both parents should contribute to the upbringing and welfare of their children, we consider that the current system places an undue financial burden on the paying parent by not accounting for their actual take-home pay. This often results in a situation where child maintenance payments are calculated on an amount that the parent never actually receives.

action: Develop government guidance encouraging councils to fly Pride & equality flags
background: We want Government to develop national guidance encouraging councils to fly inclusive flags, such as Pride, Trans, and Women’s Rights flags, during awareness events. We believe these flags show solidarity and support for marginalised groups and should be welcomed in public spaces.
additional_details: Some councils have banned the flying of certain flags, limiting displays to national and council flags. We believe such actions risk marginalising LGBTQ+ people and women. We believe there is increasing hostility, misogyny, and pressure on minority groups. National guidance could help ensure councils are free to show visible support for inclusion, equality, and the spirit of the Equality Act 2010.

action: Have full transparency on the Grooming scandal.
background: Have a true full inquiry which includes Councillors and MPs
additional_details: Because the country wants the full truth into this scandal, that was allowed for so many years, affecting so many young girls lives.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730653

action: Update the Highway Code Rule 243 to forbid parking/stopping on private driveways
background: Update Rule 243 of the Highway Code to forbid parking or stopping on private driveways. The rule currently pinpoints 12 places not to stop or park, but absent from the list is parking on someone else’s driveway.
additional_details: We think it is unfair to any property owners to have to take measures to prevent others from trespassing and parking vehicles on their driveways that they have not permitted. We want this to be covered in the Highway Code Rule 243.

action: Reverse Abortion Decriminalisation in England and Wales
background: We urge the UK Government to reverse abortion decriminalisation in England and Wales, voted by 379 MPs on 17 June 2025. Many believe this undermines life. Reinstate penalties under the 1861 Offences Against the Person Act to protect unborn children.
additional_details: On 17 June 2025, MPs voted 379 to 137 to amend the Crime and Policing Bill, decriminalising abortion for women ending their own pregnancies in England and Wales. We believe this opposes public values and the sanctity of life. We call for restoring criminal penalties while keeping the Abortion Act 1967’s safeguards for legal abortions.

action: Introduce Qualification exams to become an MP
background: I want to see a far higher standard of debate and decision making and bill consideration. We believe we need a higher calibre of MPs, with knowledge of Economics, Finance, History, Science. Anyone failing to pass these stringent exams would be barred from election.
additional_details: I believe there is a risible standard of debate today, aggravated by the obvious lack of subject matter expertise. I think this also means that undue time is spent on current social issues (which can be relatively easy to understand) rather than more germane forward looking issues.

action: Remove tax threshold creating 60%+ marginal rate for £100k incomes
background:
We urge the UK Government to revise the tax threshold causing an excessive marginal rate. Possible solutions include:  
- Removing the personal allowance taper for fairer taxation.  
- Creating a smoother transition for earners above £100k.Assessing effects on skilled professionals and incentives.
additional_details:
The £100k tax trap creates a 60%+ marginal tax rate due to the personal allowance taper, discouraging career progression and pushing people into salary sacrifice schemes and pensions to avoid excessive taxation. This reduces taxable income, meaning less government revenue and making the system counterproductive.

We urge the UK Government to revise or remove this threshold for a fairer tax system by:  
- Eliminating the personal allowance taper to restore fairness.  
- Smoothing tax transition beyond £100k.  
- Reassessing impact on skilled professionals and incentives.  

A reform would boost productivity, encourage growth, and end unfair financial penalties on hardworking individuals.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: 

Abolish personal allowance tapering
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/716530

You may also wish to sign the following petition:

Publish the economic impact of removing or raising the £100k tax cliff edge
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/718244

action: Allow Displaced Care Workers to work temporarily without a new sponsorship
background: We want the Government to allow Displaced Care Workers to temporarily, legally work full-time with another care company while they keep searching for a new Sponsor. Additionally, grant automatic renewal of their visas if expired and restrict them to care sector work only to help with staff shortages
additional_details:
1. Improve Workforce Retention in the Social Care sector and help tackle health and social care workforce shortages
2. Demonstrate the UK’s commitment to ethical labour practices and fair treatment of migrant workers.
3. Help ensure that vulnerable individuals, the elderly and disabled, continue receiving uninterrupted care, reducing pressure on hospitals and emergency services.
4. Help keep care workers economically active and paying taxes, contributing to the local and national economy.

action: Make property sales in England & Wales legally binding earlier, like in Scotland
background: The UK Government should reform conveyancing laws in England and Wales to mirror the Scottish system, where property sales become legally binding much earlier. This would reduce stress, financial risk, and delays for buyers and sellers.
additional_details:
In England and Wales, a home sale isn’t legally binding until exchange of contracts, which can happen months after an offer is accepted. This leads to frequent fall-throughs, gazumping, wasted legal fees.

In Scotland, once missives are concluded, typically after mortgage approval and survey, the agreement becomes legally binding, offering certainty and protection for both sides.

This approach would:

- Reduce collapsed chains

- Prevent gazumping

- Protect buyers & sellers from financial loss
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721744

action: Ban the Use of Mobile Phones by Members of Parliament in the House of Commons
background: Parliament to implement a clear & enforceable ban on the use of mobile phones during all official proceedings within the House of Commons. We believe this measure will restore focus, decorum, and accountability, ensuring MPs fulfil their duties with the seriousness and respect the role demands.
additional_details: We call for a ban on mobile phone use by MPs in the House of Commons. We believe phone use during debates distracts from serious decision-making, undermines public trust, and disrespects the role of elected officials. MPs should be fully engaged in representing the public, not scrolling or texting. For focus, accountability, and professionalism, we call for mobile phone use to be prohibited during all parliamentary proceedings.

action: Enshrine women's right to choose an abortion in law
background: Enshrine women's right to choose to have an abortion in law. We believe this will help protect women's right to choose from future governments and any religious influence.

action: RAAC Victim Justice – National Support Fund, New Legislation & public Inquiry
background: We are concerned that many families across the UK face homelessness, bankruptcy, and trauma after being forced from homes made unsafe by RAAC (Reinforced Autoclaved Aerated Concrete).
additional_details:
These homeowners did nothing wrong — yet are left to shoulder the burden of institutional failure and unsafe construction practices.

We believe many ex-council homeowners face bankruptcy and homelessness after RAAC was found in right-to-buy properties. We call for a national compensation fund and a public inquiry into government and council handling of RAAC. We seek laws mandating high-risk building registers, defect reporting by surveyors/solicitors, and 60-year developer liability. We believe mortgage interest should be banned on condemned homes, and first-time buyer status restored for affected owners. We want justice now.

action: Set minimum parking space width in car parks as 3.6 metres
background: We think car parking spaces are too small and don’t allow doors to open adequately for people to get in and out of their cars when other cars are parked either side of the defined parking zone. We want the Government to introduce a minimum width of 3.6 metres for car spaces in car parks.
additional_details: I am thin with a small car but I get enraged by tiny car park spaces. I literally have to hold my car door ajar so that it does not damage the adjacent parked car and squeeze/shimmy out of my car. It is demeaning and probably much worse for larger individuals. This needs to change. We think government need to set the minimum car park space dimension width as 3.6 metres, to accommodate not just the car but the actual people accessing their cars.

action: Introduce a bursary to help pay for uniform & equipment in year 10 and 11.
background: I'm a year 10 student with my active citizenship class. We are trying to help people who struggle paying for equipment and uniform.
additional_details: So people who are struggling can still afford new uniform and new equipment. Especially in year 10 and 11 because that's when you need the most equipment leading up to your GCSE exams.
rejection_details:
We can't publish petitions when the request is something that's already happening or something that has been announced since you started your petition.

Schools must follow legal guidance on the cost of school uniforms which includes making sure they’re affordable. Some schools may already offer support, and local councils may also be able to offer support. Contact your local council to find out if there is support in your area: https://www.gov.uk/find-local-council

action: Stop the Chagos Deal
background: We believe the Chagos Deal is a terrible disaster, and we find the cost unaffordable. We have concerns that it could harm the indigenous Chagossian people, and our national interests. We urge the House of Commons to block any legislation relating to this deal. We think MPs should stop it, all of it.
additional_details: We are concerned that the United Kingdom could pay billions of pounds over decades, which we find alarming at a time when there have been cuts to services for the vulnerable. We are deeply saddened that people across the United Kingdom are suffering economically. We oppose any increases in taxation, as well as cuts to expenditure, until this Treaty is cancelled. We find it unfair to suffer the cost of the Treaty, especially as many of the indigenous people oppose it. We cannot afford this Deal.

action: Mandate bilingual Gaelic/English and Scots/English driving licences in Scotland
background: We would like the government to mandate that in Scotland, fully bilingual driving licences and vehicle registration certificates be provided in Gaelic and English or Scots and English, as per the applicant's preferences.
additional_details: Driving licences and vehicle registration certificates issued in Wales are fully bilingual in Welsh/English. The Scottish Parliament has voted to establish Scottish Gaelic and Scots as official languages of Scotland. As such, we think the DVLA should issue fully bilingual licences in these languages in Scotland and accord them parity with their approach to the languages of Wales and England.

action: Prevent employment tribunals by introducing issue resolution into the process
background: I know from personal experience the vast majority of employment tribunals are avoidable. There are currently 49,800 backlogged cases and this is set to increase exponentially. I want the Government to step back and implement preventative and resolution measures, rather than recruiting more Judges.
additional_details:
Most employment tribunals could have been resolved without litigation. They cost the tax payer a fortune and this money could be spent actually resolving issues.

The biggest cost (exacerbated by time) is stress. The tribunal process causes an unnecessary, unimaginable and avoidable impact on the mental health and wellbeing of hundreds of thousands of people.

This is a huge productivity opportunity for the UK which will form a foundation for future productivity worth billions of pounds.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. There are four approaches by which the Employment Tribunals may encourage the parties to resolve their dispute by agreement. 

More information on alternative dispute resolution can be found here: https://www.judiciary.uk/courts-and-tribunals/tribunals/employment-tribunal/employment-tribunal-england-wales/other-ways-of-resolving-your-case/

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Stop VAT being added to Private school fees
background: Stop the charging of VAT on private schools fees. Government funds free schools, so therefore I think it should also be supporting private schools that hard working parents scrimp to pay for! I think supporting private schools increases places and facilities offered to state schools!
additional_details: Adding VAT to private school fees could mean some successful schools closing, which could impact the state sector/SEN provision. I think closures could also reduce parents' democratic right of choice. It could also cut superb teachers' jobs and the jobs of other competent staff, along with building heritage.

action: Change English Legal System for buying properties
background: Adapt the Scottish system for buying property in England. Millions of pounds are wasted every year due to English legal system. 30% of purchases fall through due to the lack of commitment, or issues with the chain and so many families suffer financially with chains falling through.
additional_details: Adapt the Scottish system for buying property in England
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:

Introduce conveyancing laws similar to those in Scotland, across England & Wales
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709395

action: Send the navy into the channel to help stop illegal migrants entering the UK
background: Send the navy into channel to help prevent illegal migration from boat crossings.
additional_details: To defend our borders.

action: Create a Public Accountability Act for Mismanaged Public Projects
background: Introduce a "Public Accountability Act" to ensure politicians and public executives responsible for catastrophic public spending failures face personal consequences. With legal duty of care for public funds, personal financial penalties or mandatory voluntary service and clawback contract clauses.
additional_details:
In any other job, if lots of money was lost, we would be fired. Ordinary people face consequences so should they.
 
This is about fairness, responsibility and protecting the public purse.

action: Legalise pepper spray for women
background:
1. For women over sixteen to be allowed pepper spray in their own homes

2. To introduce courses on pepper spray law & safety. Upon completion women receive a license to carry in public

3. Have refillable canisters with serial numbers registered to owners
additional_details: Crime statistics regarding women are partially as they are because women avoid being out at certain times & places, not as indication of how safe society is. Women therefore have less freedom than men & for this reason among others are rendered second-class citizens. Having pepper spray would give them greater peace of mind & the means to live alone safely.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legalise pepper spray as a method of self-defence
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/708964

action: Allow Skilled Worker sponsorship for graduate visa holders in entry-level roles
background: We ask the Government to allow Skilled Worker visa sponsorship for international graduates already in the UK who are working or seeking work in entry-level roles, particularly in sectors in NHS Expecting graduates to secure high salary roles is unrealistic and unfair.
additional_details: International graduates have followed all UK immigration rules, paid high university fees, and now work in vital entry-level roles like NHS admin and care. But the £38,700 salary threshold blocks us from being sponsored. We ask for a fairer visa pathway that reflects real job salaries and allows us to stay, grow, and contribute to the UK — the country we've invested in and come to call home.  Expecting new graduates to secure high-salary roles straight away is unrealistic and unfair.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. There are already different salary rules for recent graduates who wish to be sponsored for a Skilled Worker visa, and there is also a lower minimum salary for some healthcare jobs. 

More information on reduced salary requirements for the Skilled Worker visa can be found here, including the requirements that must be met: https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa/when-you-can-be-paid-less

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Create a pathway for overstayers with health or tech skills to regularise status
background: We ask the UK Government to introduce a route for immigration overstayers with essential skills in healthcare or technology to live and work legally in the UK, if they meet strict criteria including having no serious criminal record and a proven ability to contribute.
additional_details: The UK faces shortages in healthcare and tech staff, with many nursing and digital vacancies unfilled. Many overstayers have the skills to fill these gaps but cannot work legally due to their status. I think regularising their stay would boost the workforce, increase tax revenue, reduce exploitation, and support vital public services—offering a practical, fair solution benefiting both the country and these individuals.

action: Make large venues offer hygienic spaces for disabled medical needs
background: Change the law to require large venues to provide dedicated, hygienic spaces for disabled people to manage medical needs beyond just standard toilet facilities. This would include safe areas for tube feeding or medication use. We believe this will ensure dignity, safety, and accessibility for all.

action: Ban mobile phones in the Commons Chamber whilst Parliament is sitting.
background: MPs should not take mobile phones into the Chamber. If this is allowed then they must be switched off, not just put in silent mode. Texting and carrying on conversations whilst in the Chamber and debates are in progress should not be permitted.
additional_details: MPs are expected to pay attention to ongoing debates and discussions in the Chamber and it would appear that they are becoming a major distraction. This is disrespectful to both other MPs and the Electorate.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Ban the Use of Mobile Phones by Members of Parliament in the House of Commons 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730728

action: Fund free prescriptions for English university students
background: In Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, prescriptions are free. We think English university students should also be able to get their prescriptions for free too.
additional_details:
Currently, students in full time education can only access free prescriptions up to 18. This should be raised to university age (e.g. at least 21).
 
We believe everyone is feeling the impact of the current cost of living crisis, especially students - many of whom already sacrifice their studying to work. Prescriptions are an additional expense students could do without.
 
The age for English students in full time education getting free prescriptions should be raised from 18 to university age (at least 21).

action: The UK should not get involved with any conflict with Iran
background: The UK government should publicly commit to not getting involved in another needless war in the middle east. We already took action against Iraq against the wishes of the general public and we should not repeat this same mistake with Iran.
additional_details: We should be working with all parties to find a peaceful solution for this latest conflict.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Commit to no military involvement in attacks on Iran: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730360

action: Robert Blair Mayne to receive the VC
background: Nothing more
additional_details: It's because why we exist
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions that ask for someone to be given an honour.

The Government will only accept individual nominations, not petitions, so we can’t publish your petition.

To submit a nomination for an honour, visit: http://www.gov.uk/honours/

action: Reconsider the Decriminalisation of Abortion in the UK.
background: We urge the government to reconsider the decision made on the 17th June to decriminalise abortion, a matter of profound moral, ethical, and societal significance. The speed that this  decision was made raises concerns about the lack of debate, public consultation and democratic accountability.
additional_details:
The decision to decriminalise abortion was made with little notice or public debate. Regardless of personal views, such a significant legal and moral change should not be rushed through without full parliamentary scrutiny and public input.

This petition is not about division, but about democracy. We urge the government to revisit the decision, allow proper debate, and consider a public referendum so that all voices can be heard on this deeply important issue.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

National Referendum on the Decriminalisation of Abortion in England and Wales: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730832

action: Mandate that free roaming pet cats must be neutered
background: Change the law around free roaming pet cats so that all free roaming pet cats must be neutered. I also think rescue centres should be given powers to charge pet owners the vet bills that come with un-neutered cats fighting and mating.
additional_details: I work tirelessly along with many others to try and help cats and kittens on the streets. By changing the law that all pet cats that free roam must be neutered, I believe rescue centres can focus their attention on feral colonies and getting the population of feral cats under some sort of control.

action: National Referendum on the Decriminalisation of Abortion in England and Wales
background: Hold a referendum on decriminalising abortion up to birth, per the June 2025 amendment. Pause the law, consult the public, and review impacts to ensure it reflects Britain’s views. Safeguard women and unborn life.
additional_details:
We think the June 2025 vote to decriminalise abortion up to birth was rushed, it only had around 2hrs debate in the Commons chamber, and we don't think there was enough public input. Many will oppose it, fearing it undermines unborn life, lacks safeguards.
 
If a mother kills her child an hour after being born they would be charged with murder but an hour earlier they’re not.
 
We believe that a referendum, like Ireland’s 2018 vote, ensures democracy.
 
Pause law, review impacts, let the public decide.

action: Match the funding rate of childminders of 2-4 yr olds with current under 2s rate
background: Increase the hourly funding rate for 15/30hr early education & childcare places for 2-4-yr olds to the same level currently paid for under 2s. I believe current rates are financially unsustainable, contribute to some childminders leaving the profession, & lack of quality/flexible childcare places
additional_details: I believe current funding rates do not reflect the cost of delivering care for 2yrs+ under legally required ratios. Some childminders can earn below NMW delivering 15/30-hr funded places for over 2s. I believe some childminders are leaving the profession, and that it is unfair & discriminatory to a predominantly female sector. Equal pay for equal work should apply across all age groups. Every funded hour of EYFS care involves the same professional responsibilities, yet not all are paid the same

action: Restore the number of days campsites can operate to pre-2025 levels.
background: Review and reverse the recent restrictions on campsite operating days to support rural economies and public access to outdoor recreation, ensuring policies balance environmental protection with community livelihoods.
additional_details: 2025 regulations cut permitted campsite operating days, harming landowners incomes and restricting public access to affordable outdoor recreation. Introduced with no consultation, they threaten rural tourism, wellbeing, and local economies.As taxpayers and citizens we urge a fair review to balance environmental protection with preserving access to nature and supporting rural livelihood.Camping remains one of the few accessible forms of recreation and mental respite this right must be safeguarded
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. The law in England on campsite licenses does not restrict how many days a campsite can operate for, but a license is required if camping takes place over a set amount of days in a year. You can find more information about this here: https://www.gov.uk/find-licences/camping-licence-wales

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: When it’s 25 degrees or hotter boys can wear PE shorts in school
background: Allow boys to wear shorts when it gets too hot.
additional_details: When it’s too hot, it will improve concentration as it will be cooler for students.
rejection_details:
School uniform policy is a matter for schools themselves.

The Government sets guidance on school uniform policy. This recommends that schools "take a sensible approach to allow for exceptions to be made during extreme weather – for example, allowing pupils to wear shorts in very hot weather or allowing trousers to be worn instead of skirts in very cold weather."

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/school-uniform/school-uniforms

You could reach out to a particular school to request they change their policy.

action: Stop UK Government implementing Digital IDs and Currency. Protect Human Rights
background: Stop digital ID and currency in the UK as this will effect everyday life and personal freedoms . This breaches Privacy Governments gain enhanced ability to monitor, control, or limit access to services based on digital identity data, potentially infringing on personal freedoms
additional_details:
To protect and respect Human Rights and God given rights as human beings. This act is inhumane and unlawful as we are not even given a choice.
We believe that any move towards a mandatory digital ID must be thoroughly debated with public participation and legal safeguards to prevent abuse and safeguard our constitutional rights. We call on the government to halt any plans that compromise our privacy and freedoms until comprehensive consultations are held and appropriate protections are in place
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

action: Introduce drug testing for MP's
background:
MP's are the decision making centre of UK policy. 

It is of national and global interest that MP's are clean and sober when making any and all decisions. A breath/swab test should be implemented before entry to the hall. 

Drug testing should be carried out like they do in sport.
additional_details:
A lot of jobs have drug testing - sport especially as it has to be clean. 

Politicians should be clean. 

Decisions made in the house have not only national, but also global reach. It is imperative that the people elected by constituents are sober and drug free. 

Anyone failing a breath test or drug test should be barred from the house.

A law created that a by-election should take place. 

A WADA style doping system should be put in place.

action: Seek to join the European Free Trade Association (EFTA)
background: We think the UK should join EFTA, comprised of Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. We think this would be an ideal compromise between those who wish to be within the EU and those who don't.
additional_details: Parliament must consider that close to 10 years on from the Brexit referendum, the country is still talking about it. The government could negotiate a system where the UK can join EFTA but not be part of the EEA or Schengen Area. Government could work with EFTA countries to negotiate admission which works for both them and what is of paramount importance to the UK. We think it would then finally close the debate on the UK-EU's relationship.

action: A Request for a Footpath/Cycle lane between Heighington and the Eastern Bypass.
background:
For the safety of cyclists & pedestrians there is a much needed requirement for a Footpath/Cycle lane between Cliff lane Heighington and the Eastern Bypass along Heighington Road.
There are future plans in the Sustainable Urban Extension (Canwick Heath) for Canwick to the Eastern Bypass.
additional_details: I have written to the local councillor and she has just quoted the Sustainable Urban Extension (Canwick Heath) proposal; which doesn't include this request.
rejection_details:
You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

action: Ban the use of AI and electronic algorithms for filtering job applications
background: Ban the use of AI and electronic algorithms for filtering job applications so that organizations select candidates from applications manually. I think the problem in job searching is that all the electronic filters prevent people's CVs from even reaching the desks of their would be employers.
additional_details: As it stands right now,  some employers complain about not having workers, workers complains about not getting jobs, I think these problems are rooted in the fact that many applications don't make it to the employers desk due to various filters. I think employers need to go back to using the staff they can get and training their own staff in what they need if they aren't readily available. I and many others have applied to many jobs to only get a reply from a few of them.

action: Change the school week from 5 days to 4 day
background: We request the Government to make all schools make the school week four instead of five days- and to fit the 32.5 hour requirement, make school days 1.5 hours longer. There would also be an optional day for students to come in, to help families who cant take care of their kid(s) for the extra day.
additional_details: We need this to happen because from our evidence, 91.3% of people feel burnt out after 5 days of school, and you may think that extra 90 minutes may tire students, but 78.2% of students said a 4 day school week would prevent burnout. Along with this, 65.2% of students said that school is detrimental to their mental health. As well as this, teachers would have more time to prepare lessons, and 60% said their focus and grades would improve. We urge this to happen, and improve school life for all.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action:

Reduce the school week to four days a week
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727514

action: Stop the government banking with banks who invest in fossil fuel companies
background:
We want the Government Banking Service that supports the NHS to stop working with banks that provide finance to fossil fuel companies.
We want to prevent ill health caused by fossil fuel combustion.
We want an NHS focused on preventative healthcare from bank account to bedside.
additional_details:
Fossil fuel use causes climate change with more extreme weather events, loss of biodiversity, acidification of our oceans and pollution of air, soil and water.
These destabilise our ecosystems, reduce our food security, and could increase the risk of civil unrest and increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks.
Fossil fuels pollute the air which can cause heart and lung problems that shorten life expectancy.
We think that Government Banking cannot continue to use banks that finance fossil fuels that make our communities sick.

action: CPR training to be mandatory for all employees in the workplace
background: As a registered nurse, the knowledge and skills of Basic Life Support are taught throughout our training. However, I have seen how most of the general public do not have the knowledge or confidence to deal with a life threatening situation.
additional_details:
Teaching all employees CPR could save thousands of lives. Each year, thousands of cardiac arrests occur outside hospitals in the UK, and the majority of people don't survive.
 
If more people are trained in this skill, especially in workplaces, emergency responses may improve drastically. Making CPR training universal in employment can bridge the gap before paramedics arrive, reducing fatalities and building a life-saving culture across the nation.

action: Add Sickle Cell Disease to NHS Prescription Charge Exemption List
background: We ask the Government to add Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) to the NHS prescription charge exemption list as soon as possible. This will help ensure those affected by this serious condition, which can be life-threatening, can access essential medication and treatments without financial burden.
additional_details:
Sickle Cell Disease is a lifelong condition which can lead to other life-threatening health problems. It particularly commonly affects people with an African or Caribbean family background. Yet unlike many other serious illnesses, it’s not covered by NHS prescription charge exemptions despite being the most common genetic blood disorder in the UK. Many patients may not be able to work but still face monthly costs for vital medication.
 
We think this isn’t just unfair—it’s unjust. We urge the government to add SCD to the exemption list and take a stand against inequality in healthcare.
government_response_summary: The Government has no current plans to add sickle cell disease to the medical exemption list. Extensive arrangements are in place in England to ensure that prescriptions are affordable for everyone.
government_response_body: The Government has no current plans to review the list of medical conditions that entitle someone to apply for a medical exemption certificate, including relating to sickle cell disease.  There are extensive arrangements in place in England to ensure that prescriptions are affordable for everyone. Approximately 89% of prescription items are dispensed free of charge in the community in England, and there are a wide range of exemptions from prescription charges already in place for which those with sickle cell disease may be eligible. Eligibility depends on the patient’s age, whether they are in qualifying full-time education, whether they are pregnant or have recently given birth, or whether they are in receipt of certain benefits or a war pension. People on low incomes can apply for help with their health costs through the NHS Low Income Scheme. The Scheme provides income-related help to people who are not automatically exempt from charges but who may be entitled to full or partial help if they have a low income and savings below a defined limit. More information can be found here: https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/help-nhs-prescription-costs/free-nhs-prescriptions  People who need to pay NHS prescription charges and need many prescription items could save money with a prescription prepayment certificate (PPC), which allows people to claim as many prescriptions as they need for a set cost. A 3-monthly PPC (costing £32.05) or an annual PPC (costing £114.50) will save people money if they need four or more items in 3 months or 12 or more items in 12 months. To help spread the cost, people can pay for an annual PPC by 10 monthly direct debits. A holder of a 12-month certificate can get all the prescriptions they need for just over £2 per week. More information, and a link to purchase a PPC, can be found here: https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/help-nhs-prescription-costs/nhs-prescription-prepayment-certificate-ppc  The Department of Health and Social Care works closely with the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA), whose promotional activity on help with health costs regularly includes: •	Continuous organic social media promotion •	Paid social media advertising, directed at both patients and healthcare professionals (HCPs) •	Website content, directed at both patients and HCPs •	Media releases to relevant news titles •	Promotion to HCPs through relevant healthcare bulletins  The NHSBSA has also developed an online tool to help patients find out what help they may be able to get and where to apply for it. This is available on the NHSBSA website at: https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/dont-get-caught-out-penalty-charges/check-you-tick#:~:text=If%20you%20claim%20free%20NHS,Even%20if%20it%27s%20by%20mistake  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Review evidence and fund addition of Fabry disease to the newborn screening test
background: Provide funding to add Fabry disease to the newborn screening programme via the existing heel-prick test. Early detection could allow faster treatment and help identify affected families. Review the evidence and begin a process of funding the addition of the disease to the test.
additional_details: Fabry is a rare genetic disease that can cause life-threatening heart, kidney, and nerve damage. It often goes undiagnosed until it’s too late. Early detection at birth can save lives and allow families to access treatment sooner. Some countries and regions already screen newborns for Fabry and we think that we should too. As someone with Fabry, I know how crucial early diagnosis is. This change could transform care for future generations.

action: Petition that Abortion should be put to people of this Country in Referendum.
background: Petition that Abortion should be put to Country as Referendum and should not be left to MPs along, it must be voted on and Debated by people and voted by a Referendum.
additional_details: To let the Country and people vote on Assisted dying, by vote of a Referendum.
