action: Fund the installation of free public bike repair stations in cities & towns
background: We urge the Government to provide funding to install and support free public bike repair stations across cities and towns. We believe these stations should include tools and stands to allow cyclists to fix minor issues on the go.
additional_details: We think Germany's repair stations help cyclists stay mobile and safe. We believe our idea would support cyclists, promote sustainability, reduce car use, and improve public health. We believe it’s a low-cost way to make cycling more reliable and attractive for all.

action: Mandate and fund air conditioning units in all English state-funded schools
background: We urge the Government to fund and mandate AC units to be installed in all state schools in England.
additional_details: We believe rising global and annual temperatures, especially during the summer, can negatively impact a student’s ability to learn as well as perform in tests and in lessons to a high standard.

action: Stop Proposed PIP Changes: Protect Support for Individuals with ADHD and Autism
background: The UK government's new bill threatens PIP for those with ADHD/autism. It makes it harder to qualify and restricts how funds are used. We need Parliament to stop these changes, keep PIP flexible, and ensure fair assessments that recognise invisible disabilities.
additional_details: The UK government's PIP changes threaten vital support for ADHD/autism. Stricter eligibility, like needing 4+ points in one activity, ignores how invisible disabilities cumulatively impact daily life. Removing psychological distress from mobility assessments will isolate many. Restricting how PIP is spent undermines autonomy and access to therapies. This will cause immense hardship and must be stopped.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Stop PIP Cuts: Protect Support for Disabled People: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721918

action: Ensure the TV licence is not tied to council tax
background: On behalf of the british public, I would like the government to ensure that the TV Licence fee does not become tied to council tax upon the renewal of the BBC charter.
additional_details:
It would not be fair to expect the public who do not use live TV services to pay the TV Licence fee through their council tax.

Further more expecting those in a higher band home to subsidise the licence fee of others is unacceptable.

The BBC should be forced to move to an advertising or subscription model and stop harassing those of us who do not use their services or see value in them.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign:

Rule out BBC licence fee being linked to council tax: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730557

Scrap the BBC TV Licence & replace funding with adverts or paywall:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727365

action: Add the Progress Pride Flags to the flags that don’t require permission
background:
There are rules about the flags that can be flown without local planning authority consent.
 
The Rainbow Flag is already listed, subject to certain restrictions. We would like the Progress Flag & its Intersex inclusive version to be listed too, allowing organisations to demonstrate inclusiveness
additional_details:
Many organisations would like to demonstrate that all LGBTQ+ people are both welcome and safe doing business with them and entering their establishments. Sadly, we believe current public discourse leaves non-binary and trans people uncertain of their safety when the older rainbow flag is flown.
 
Adding both Progress Flags to the list of flags that don't require consent, alongside the rainbow flag, would allow organisations to freely choose which to display.

action: Create a regulatory body to regulate and oversee estate management companies
background: We call for the creation of a regulatory body to oversee estate management companies, to help ensure transparency, accountability, and fair service charges for leaseholders and freeholders. We think it’s time to better protect residents’ rights.
additional_details: Estate management companies operate without full oversight from a regulator. Many view them as often charging excessive fees, providing poor service, and leaving residents with no real recourse. Only Parliament can establish a statutory regulator with the power to enforce standards, resolve disputes, and protect homeowners. We believe a government-backed body would ensure transparency, accountability, and fairness—giving leaseholders and freeholders the rights they deserve.

action: Tunnel the A406 at New Southgate
background: Tunnel the A406 at New Southgate area to remove bottle neck caused by traffic lights and allow traffic  to be free flowing.
additional_details: Every hour of every day the section of the A406 by New Southgate is a traffic Jam. There is a primary school right there where the children breathe in the fumes all day. Tunneling and opening up the surface area could encourage property growth, commerce & more green spaces.

We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.
 
You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.
 
You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP
 
And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Government Funding for Nationwide Bluetongue Testing
background: We urge the Government to provide funding to cover all testing costs imposed on farmers relating to Bluetongue. DEFRA should fund this, as costs could burden farmers unfairly. Testing requirements vary across the UK; the Government should fund these costs or scrap testing altogether.
additional_details: Midges migrate across borders naturally, so we believe restricting animal movements and imposing further costs on farmers is unfair and ineffective. We are concerned livestock farmers could face financial devastation. We think the restrictions are illogical for a midge-spread virus and may further undermine food security.

action: The Government should not get involved in the war between Israel and Iran.
background: Parliament should vote against any British involvement in this war other than acting in self defense against either side.
additional_details: The war between Israel and Iran has nothing to do with the British and we should stay out of the conflict.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730360

action: Give Class D License Holders Class C1 and Class C License Holders D1 Entitlement
background:
Give Class D License Holders Class C1 Entitlement and Class C License Holders D1 Entitlement.

I Propose that Class D(PCV) License Holders should be given Class C1(7.5t LGV) entitlement.

And that Class C(LGV) License Holders should be given CLass D1(minibus) entitlement.
additional_details:
Making these changes would encourage drivers of different classes to working in areas not previously open to them with out additional costly training.

A Class D driver can drive a vehicle twice the weight of a Class C1 at present.

action: Stop the Decriminalisation of Abortion in England and Wales: Protect the Unborn
background: We urge the government not to pass the abortion decriminalisation amendment. It removes legal safeguards, puts unborn lives at risk, and sends a harmful message about the value of life.
additional_details: We believe this law is harmful as it removes vital safeguards and allows irreversible decisions to go unchecked. It diminishes the seriousness of ending a life and conflicts with the fundamental right to life, a right this law primarily denies unborn children.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Reverse Abortion Decriminalisation in England and Wales: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730690

action: Ban Second Jobs and Paid Gigs for Elected Officials, Including MPs
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation that bans Members of Parliament (MPs) and all other elected officials from holding second jobs or engaging in any other paid work or “gigs” during their term of office, regardless of whether payment is monetary, in kind, or indirect.
additional_details:
Elected officials are elected to serve the public. Second jobs or paid roles risk conflicts of interest, reduce public trust, and distract from their duties.

Serving as an MP or other elected official should be a full-time role. The ban should cover all forms of paid work, including jobs, consultancy, media, speaking gigs, and board positions, whether paid directly, indirectly, or through companies or trusts.

Public service requires full focus and accountability. This measure would help protect democracy and ensure officials serve only the people who elected them.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710565

action: Make a new business grant scheme for Neurodivergent Entrepreneurs
background: We call on the UK Government to launch a new business grant and support scheme for autistic, dyslexic, and other neurodivergent individuals who want to become self-employed or start small businesses.
additional_details: According to some estimates, there are over 2 million people in the UK with autism, dyslexia, or other neurodivergent conditions. Many have entrepreneurial skills but may struggle to access support, funding, and guidance. Other regions like the West Midlands already offer SME grant support. We ask for this to be implemented nationally and funded fairly for autistic and disabled entrepreneurs.

action: Save the sea Blobfish from extinction
background: Create more awareness about sea life and stop throwing out plastic
additional_details: They are really important to sea wildlife and the amount of plastic getting put in the ocean is killing all of are sea animals and wildlife.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

action: Review & amend school attendance guidance on the “S” code & introduce a new code
background: We urge the Government to review & amend the S code which grants students study leave for exams, so that it is excluded from negatively affecting attendance rates. We also urge the Government to introduce a clear code (e.g. L – Left or C – Completed Education) that won't affect attendance statistics
additional_details: We feel by not marking children’s attendance as “Left” or having attendance concluded, they are marked with the “S” code, indicating an absence due to study leave. This S code counts as an absence**, which can dramatically affect the student’s overall attendance percentage. This could negatively affect how parents view their child’s record, and in some cases, may impact students.

action: Ensure the Reception Baseline Assessment can be carried out screen free
background: We call on the Government to remove the requirement for the Reception Baseline Assessment (RBA) to be delivered on a digital device. We think teachers should have more flexibility to administer the assessment without screens, using printed or hands-on materials where appropriate.
additional_details: The RBA is currently carried out using a computer or tablet. Some parents and educators are concerned this introduces unnecessary screen time for 4-year-old children during a critical stage of development. There are concerns that digital delivery may interfere with teacher-child interaction, introduce bias based on digital familiarity, and fail to reflect best practice in early years education. We think schools should be given the flexibility to assess using age-appropriate, screen-free methods.

action: Create a UK-Wide Regional Equity Strategy to Tackle Systemic Inequality by 2030
background: Create and implement a UK-wide Regional Equity Strategy by 2030 to close the geographic inequality gap. We think this should include statutory investment targets, regional accountability, and a legal requirement to embed regional voices in national policy-making.
additional_details: Where you’re born in the UK still determines your access to opportunity. From transport to education, health to jobs, regional disparities hold millions back. This is not just a North/South issue—it affects overlooked communities in every nation and region. We think we need long-term, legally-backed change—not political soundbites.

action: Fund free music tuition for all secondary school children aged 11-16 in England
background: We urge the Government to full fund 1:1 music instrument lessons for all children aged 11-16 in all secondary schools in England. We believe this could close the “cultural capital gap” by ensuring all students can access these lessons regardless of their household income.
additional_details: We believe it could help music education flourish in schools. We believe access to instrumental music lessons should not just be for the wealthy or elite. We believe that if a child wishes to learn an instrument, they should be able to without any financial barriers. A UK Music report stated the music industry contributed £7.6 billion to the UK economy in 2023. We are concerned it could decrease if we do not invest in our youth. In 2021, the Scottish Government abolished these fees. We can do the same!

action: Set out how individuals will be held to account through grooming gangs inquiry
background: I would like the government to ensure that each and every person, regardless of position held, who may have covered up these crimes, will be included in the upcoming national inquiry and everyone found to have contributed into the cover up be held accountable.

action: Ban greyhound racing
background: Greyhound racing kills and injures dogs. From 2017–2023, 1,230 dogs died trackside, many more were destroyed, and there were over 31,000 injuries. We believe it’s time to follow Wales and ban this cruel sport.
additional_details:
The industry breeds more dogs than are needed for racing - approximately 15,000-20,000 dogs are bred in Ireland each year, and some are also bred in Britain. We are concerned that dogs live in poor kennel conditions, and overbreeding creates a surplus, overwhelming rescue centres.
 
A 2019 RTÉ documentary estimated up to 6,000 greyhounds are killed annually for not being fast enough. There are concerns about greyhounds being exported to countries with poor welfare laws.
 
We believe no animal should suffer for sport or entertainment.
government_response_summary: The government has no plans to ban greyhound racing. The government considers it a well-regulated sport and recognises the contribution it makes to many people’s lives as well as to the economy.
government_response_body: The government has no plans to ban greyhound racing. While the government recognises the concerns some people have about greyhound racing, there is legislation in place to protect the welfare of racing greyhounds in England and a regulatory body – the Greyhound Board of Great Britain (GBGB) – that has made many improvements to greyhound welfare.     The government also recognises the important contribution greyhound racing makes to the country’s cultural life and its rural economy, providing some 5400 jobs across Great Britain as well as being the sixth most popular sport in terms of viewership.    The welfare of racing greyhounds in England is covered by the Animal Welfare Act 2006 and the Welfare of Racing Greyhounds Regulations 2010. The 2006 Act allows action to be taken where there is evidence of cruelty to an animal or a failure to provide for an animal’s welfare needs. This includes where greyhounds are raced at tracks or kept at trainers’ kennels. Further to these general provisions, welfare standards at all English greyhound tracks are set by the 2010 Regulations.  The 2010 Regulations include the requirement that all tracks must have a vet present while dogs are running, who must inspect each greyhound intended to run in every race, trial, or sales trial to ensure that the greyhound is fit to run. Temperature-controlled kennelling must also be provided at the track, and all racing greyhounds must be permanently identified. Tracks must also keep records of any injuries sustained to greyhounds while at the track.   Standards in the 2010 Regulations can be enforced either by the local authority or by GBGB. GBGB’s ability to regulate track standards in the 2010 Regulations is allowed for in law because they are accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (UKAS). UKAS is the UK’s National Accreditation Body, recognised by the government as the sole UK organisation for the accreditation of certification and inspection bodies. UKAS provides independent, external oversight of GBGB’s performance as a regulator of track standards.    In addition, GBGB has also introduced several welcome welfare initiatives. In collaboration with animal welfare groups, the GBGB has developed a set of detailed welfare standards for trainers’ kennels, which are then verified at trainers’ kennels by independent auditors, with this process also accredited by UKAS. On average, GBGB licensed kennels will be inspected three times a year by GBGB staff, as well as by a vet and an independent inspector.    The GBGB has also introduced a Greyhound Retirement Scheme to contribute towards rehoming costs; as well as an Injury Recovery Scheme to provide financial support to trainers to treat career-ending injuries to greyhounds, where otherwise they might be put to sleep.     In 2022, the GBGB published its long term, national welfare strategy: ‘A Good Life for Every Greyhound’ (https://www.gbgb.org.uk/welfare-care/commitment-to-care/). The strategy focuses not only on further reducing risks of injury but also developing and implementing new management practices to improve the welfare of greyhounds throughout their lives, including after racing.    Since 2018 GBGB have published yearly, independently audited injury, fatality and retirement figures. The overall, long-term trend for injuries and fatalities for racing greyhounds since 2018 has shown significant improvements. For example: the total number of GBGB registered greyhounds reported to have died has declined from 1013 deaths in 2017, to 386 in 2024; and the total number of greyhounds put to sleep due to the costs of treating injuries has fallen from 333 in 2017, to 3 in 2024.  Given the work being undertaken to improve greyhound welfare, and the protections in place, the government does not believe it is necessary to ban greyhound racing. However, the government will continue to monitor GBGB’s progress and, should further measures and protections be required, the government will consider options that are targeted, effective, and proportionate.   Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs

action: Allow pupils in school to bring in school shorts during warm days over 25 °
background: Make it mandatory that schools allow pupils to wear school shorts.
additional_details: It’s much easier to focus and get work done when the room isn’t too hot. When it’s warm, most of us feel tired, uncomfortable, and distracted — it’s hard to concentrate when you’re sweating or just trying to stay awake. Cooler environments help us stay more alert and clear-headed, which makes studying and learning a lot easier. That’s why schools should let us wear shorts, especially when it’s hot. Dressing in a way that keeps us comfortable isn’t about breaking rules — it’s about helping us do our best. If we feel better, we’ll learn better too.
rejection_details:
School uniform policy is a matter for schools themselves.

The Government sets guidance on school uniform policy. This recommends that schools "take a sensible approach to allow for exceptions to be made during extreme weather – for example, allowing pupils to wear shorts in very hot weather or allowing trousers to be worn instead of skirts in very cold weather."

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/school-uniform/school-uniforms

You could reach out to a particular school to request they change their policy.

action: Ban electrically-assisted pedal cycles in shared pedestrian-cycle spaces
background: We want the government to ban electrically-assisted pedal cycles in shared pedestrian-cycle spaces. We think that the increasing use of electrically-assisted pedal cycles (EAPCs) in these spaces poses a growing safety risk.
additional_details: Shared pedestrian-cycle areas are intended to be safe and accessible particularly for vulnerable groups such as children, older people, and those with disabilities. EAPCs often travel at higher speeds and are generally heavier than conventional bicycles. We feel that current legislation does not go far enough in addressing this issue, leaving pedestrians exposed to unnecessary danger.

action: No War with Iran: Safeguard Britain’s Peace, Principles, and Prosperity
background: Refrain from any involvement—military, financial, logistical, or political—in the conflict with Iran. Suspend arms exports to Israel, oppose U.S. escalation, and adopt a stance of non-intervention and diplomatic restraint to protect UK security and interests.
additional_details: We express concern over the humanitarian, economic, and security consequences of UK involvement in a war with Iran. It will lead to increased refugee migration, rising living costs, and the threat of retaliatory attacks. The UK’s support for Israel risks damaging its global image and public trust.  We want the government to prioritize peace, diplomacy, and the well-being of its citizens. Any decision regarding the involvement in the war must go through a parliamentary debate.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions which call for similar actions:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730360

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729717

action: Chemical castration for all those convicted of child sexual abuse
background: We think that for all those found guilty in cases of child grooming and sexual abuse, along with a custodial period, they should be chemically castrated to help prevent repeating this behaviour.
additional_details: We want the government to introduce legislation so that the guilty persons are chemically castrated during their time in prison to help safeguard children from further harm and re-offending by prisoners.

action: Prohibit acts of harm or violence justified by religious belief
background: It shall be unlawful for any person, group, or institution to engage in or promote acts of violence, coercion, or discrimination on the basis of religion. This includes incitement to religious hatred or the justification of harm toward others based on religious doctrine.
additional_details: Violence, coercion, or discrimination justified by religion must not be tolerated. This law ensures freedom of belief while prohibiting harm in its name. By holding accountable those who incite violence or hatred through faith, we protect all religions and promote mutual respect in a diverse society
rejection_details:
Acts of violence, coercion, or discrimination justified by religion are already illegal under several laws. 

The Crime and Disorder Act 1998 enhances penalties for religiously aggravated offences, the Equality Act 2010 prohibits discrimination on the basis of religion or belief, and the Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006 criminalises inciting religious hatred.

action: Launch inquiry into missing children & create new national prevention strategy
background: Launch a public inquiry into long-term missing children, investigating patterns, causes, and institutional gaps, and create a new coordinated national strategy to prevent further disappearances and improve recovery.
additional_details: The latest annual data from the UK Missing Persons Unit, for 2022/23, shows at least 1,500 children in the UK were recorded as long-term missing. We believe these are not isolated cases but a systemic failure and that unlike more high-profile cases, most receive no attention. We need truth, accountability, and action — now.

action: Require all buses to have air conditioning
background: We want the government to make it compulsory for all buses to have air conditioning.
additional_details: We are getting hotter summers and we think having no air conditioning causes a risk to drivers who may have to sit in 30°c+ all day long. We are concerned that drivers could pass out due to the heat and cause catastrophic damage to passengers, other road user and themselves.

action: Stop arms sales and any military support to Ukraine and Israel.
background: We demand the government cease all arms sales to these countries along with any military support. We believe we should end our part in the pain and destruction inflicted by war, and that we should not support weapons but instead, invest the money in our own citizens and services.
additional_details:
We believe every penny spent on death and destruction should have otherwise been invested in hospitals schools and public services. Money it seems, can always be found for wars.

We believe that stopping war funding and redirecting money home, will improve our country. We think citizens are taxed, without having enough control over state spending and that it is more beneficial for the UK public to reap the benefits of their contributions, than funding what we see as foreign adventurism.

action: End funding for military interventions overseas and spend taxes in the UK.
background: We demand the government end the use of taxpayers’ money to fund military interventions, or providing military support for conflicts abroad. We believe that our taxes should be spent on improving public services, supporting communities and addressing urgent domestic issues rather than war.
additional_details:
We think the British public deserves to know, that their hard-earned money, is being spent responsibly and ethically, prioritising peace, stability and prosperity at home. We seek a foreign policy grounded in diplomacy and peace-building, rather than what can be costly and divisive military actions, that may have limited long-term success.

The financial burden of war is significant. The UK’s involvement in wars and military operations over the last two decades has cost billions of pounds.

action: Enforce tougher punishment for those who cause animal cruelty.
background: Once an animal has shows visible or emotional signs of abuse (whether in the home or in public) put in place a law where the guilty party is arrested and dependant on the extent of cruelty to receive a prison sentence.
additional_details:
More and more we hear about animal cruelty, cats having their ears cut off, eyes being injured and with dogs, throwing them off bridges, using them for dog fighting, an owner being neglectful and the dog being treated as a weapon/having to at times be put to sleep due to the carelessness of the breeders and owners.

This is happening far too often and some urgent action needs to be taken. This simply cannot go on!!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Increase maximum animal cruelty punishment from five years to eight years
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707848

Impose a lifetime ban on animal ownership for anyone convicted of animal cruelty
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/705772

Ban Private Dog Breeding and Strengthen Penalties for Animal Cruelty
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728177

action: Enact new Cybersecurity law that sets minimum standards and creates a regulator
background: To make the UK a resilient place to operate and reduce the destructive effects of cybercrime on businesses and the public, we want the government to introduce a new Cybersecurity Act that mandates minimum cybersecurity standards for ALL businesses larger than 20 staff or £2m annual turnover.
additional_details:
We think cybercrime is a pandemic. Effects on the mental health of it's victims, from business leaders to the general public, are huge. We think we need mandated defence.
 
We think a new cybersecurity law, modelled on previous Health & Safety legislation should be overseen by a new Cybersecurity Executive with powers of enforcement exercised centrally for large and government organisations and additional powers granted to local authorities responsible for monitoring and fining SME businesses headquartered in their areas.

action: Modernise treason laws to include terrorism and wilful betrayal of the state.
background: Treason legislation to be updated in line with wilful acts against the UK. Modern threats such as domestic terrorism, joining proscribed terrorist organisations acting against the UK, coercion with a hostile state to harm the UK and betrayal of public mandates all to be considered as modern treason.
additional_details: Whilst we believe it is essential to maintain treason as hostile acts against the Monarch, this does not encompass acts against the State and the UK population as a whole. As the Monarch could be argued to be a largely a ceremonial position, we think treason legislation must be updated to reflect the modern day make up of the UK to ensure hostile acts against the nation by its own citizens are likewise classified, and convictions reflected as treason.

action: Include play in the statutory national curriculum framework
background:
We want the government to recognise play and playful pedagogy in the statutory national curriculum for primary education. 
A reform of accountability measures to enable schools to embed play-based learning, support child development, well-being and skills essential for today’s society.
additional_details:
Play supports mental health, executive functioning, SEND needs, physical health, creativity, and learning. (See “Everything to Play For” Report)
Schools are currently under pressure to prioritise data over child development and childhood is being forgotten.
Embedding play helps address current crises, gives all children a joyful, meaningful education they deserve, alongside allowing the development of skills which are needed for the future (OECD and WEF).
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Make Play and Continuous Provision statutory in England's Key Stage 1 Curriculum 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729440

action: Reject Plans to Decriminalise Abortion: Protect Unborn Life
background: We urge the UK Government to reject proposals to decriminalise abortion. Every unborn child has value and deserves protection. Keep legal safeguards in place and strengthen laws to defend the rights and dignity of the unborn. Life must be protected at all stages.
additional_details: There are efforts to remove abortion from criminal law, allowing abortion up to birth with few restrictions. This risks undermining the value of life, removing safeguards, and ignoring unborn rights. We urge the Government to uphold current laws and even criminalise abortion , support women in crisis, promote alternatives, and protect both mother and child.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Reverse Abortion Decriminalisation in England and Wales
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730690

action: Further enforce littering in the UK.
background: I would like the Government to take action against littering by further enforcing the fine for the crime.
additional_details:
Littering is illegal in the UK. The fine for littering in many areas is £400 (£200 if paid within 10 days). If the fine isn’t paid within 14 days, individuals that
litter could face going to court and paying up to £2500. 

Unfortunately, it is hard to enforce, and many people continue to litter without facing said fines. I would like something to be done to prevent this crime, and to protect our environment.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund more bins, CCTV, enforcement staff and raise fines to prevent littering
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728466

action: Legislate to allow recall of MPs found to have deliberately misled the public
background: We think that if an independent body finds an MP has deliberately misled the public, their constituents should be able to trigger a binding recall vote. This could give voters the power to remove MPs who break their trust with the electorate, forcing a by-election.
additional_details: Trust in politics is broken. We believe that MPs can mislead the public and face no consequences, it suggests one rule for them and another for us. We think the current Recall of MPs Act 2015 is too weak, as it only applies after a criminal conviction with imprisonment or a suspension from the House of Commons of at least ten sitting days. Voters must have a proper mechanism to hold their own representatives to account for dishonesty. This is about basic integrity and giving voters a real say.

action: Cancel SLC debt for educators with degrees earned before teacher apprenticeships
background: We call on the government to introduce a student loan repayment forgiveness scheme for educators with 10+ years of service in public education. This could clear debt for those who trained before teacher apprenticeships, helping retain skilled teachers and ease financial burden in the sector.
additional_details: We think this would recognise their commitment. We are concerned that rising living costs have meant that many leave the profession or rely on financial support. We believe that clearing this debt could help retain skilled teachers and ease financial pressure. Currently, new training teachers can go through an apprenticeship scheme. However those pre apprenticeship can pay hundreds back a month to SLC and may struggle with the cost of living.

action: Fund new residential care centres for disabled children with complex needs
background: Fund and operate new residential care centres for disabled children with complex medical needs, to provide safe, specialist care when the level of support required cannot be met at home and local authorities are unable to commission appropriate provision
additional_details: I think that local authorities currently lack appropriate provision and families can be left with no safe options. I feel that more centralised, NHS-standard centres could offer trusted care and reduce long-term costs.

action: CatsMatter - Make Car Accidents Involving Cats a Reportable Offence
background: It is perfectly legal in the UK to hit a cat when driving and leave them scared, alone and in pain roadside. Cats are important, loved, valued family members and, as it does for dogs, the law should reflect this. Legislation currently leans toward encouraging unnecessary suffering, which must change
additional_details: We call upon lawmakers to implement stricter laws regarding hit & run incidents involving cats that will ensure drivers are held accountable if they fail to stop and report such accidents. Asking a bit of decency is legislated for by asking drivers be made responsible for seeking help for an injured cat should be a perfectly reasonable & simple ask. No more petitions, generic responses or excuses, people want action like legislation that recognises cats as a species worth helping if injured.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require drivers to stop and take cats to the vets if they hit them in their car
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728011

action: End all EU fishing rights in UK waters until France stops small boats
background: We urge the Government to end all EU fishing rights in UK waters until France stops small boats coming to the UK. We believe it is costing far too much money and cannot continue. If this is done, the Government could have more money to spend on other services and crime may decrease.
additional_details: We believe it could help our economy and our police if we have more money to invest in the UK. We feel the Government is not doing enough. We are also concerned that the UK is paying millions of pounds to France, and we believe the French police is not doing enough to combat small boats coming to the UK.

action: Do not fund the BBC through taxation or extend the licence to streaming services
background:
We call on the Government to protect individual choice by:
Keeping the BBC licence fee separate from Council Tax or any form of general taxation and not extending the BBC licence fee to cover streaming services 
I would like that the licence fee not to be included on other channels Like ITV UKTV
additional_details:
Funding the BBC through taxation (including Council Tax) removes the public’s ability to opt out and unfairly forces payment from those who may not use TV services. This turns the licence fee into a compulsory tax, which we strongly oppose. We also call on the Government to reject any proposals to extend the scope of the BBC licence fee to include the use of commercial streaming platforms like Netflix and others. 
People who do not use BBC services should not be required to pay a licence fee.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730557

action: Enshrine into law that the NHS cannot be privatised
background: We wish for a law to be created that prevents the NHS from being privatised by future governments.
additional_details: It is possible that future governments may make the choice to privatise the NHS and possibly move to a private model, like is seen in the USA, where a routine operation can cost thousands of dollars and routine prescriptions can often times be prohibitively costly to the patient as well. We see the NHS as a national institution and wish for it to be protected from privatisation, both now and in the future as well.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

The role of the NHS is set out in legislation already. If you would like changes to this, you could start a new petition about that.

action: Give funding to ice-cream vans to visit smaller villages
background: I feel that small villages are starting to become very quiet, without pubs or shops. I think having an ice cream van could allow people to buy cold drinks, instead of having to travel miles to purchase them.
additional_details: I think villages should have the same access to basic things as big towns and bigger villages do.

action: Ban gambling advertising on TV
background: We would like the government to step in and ban advertising on TV of all gambling and gambling sites. At present, it feels like there are so many adverts trying to get people gambling.

action: Bring forward the next general election
background: By the next election in 2029 the country will be drowning in illegal immigrants. We as British citizens should have a say in who comes into the UK. Why should we be paying for immigrants?? Let's vote now and send the boats back.
additional_details: It's wrong that British taxpayers who have payed into the system and especially the elderly don't get a fair deal yet immigrants get money thrown at them..free dental treatment, prescriptions, operations and now a free house. There's British people who can't get a council house or afford to buy these are the people the government should be helping not immigrants who we know nothing about. The government should be ashamed for not doing more for British citizens. It used to be GREAT Britain and now it's......?
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call an immediate general election: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Ban drinks manufacturers from tethering plastic caps to plastic bottles
background: Pass a law to ban drinks manufacturers from tethering plastic caps to plastic bottles. Return to having plastic caps unattached, separate and fully removable from all plastic bottles. I believe this will make plastic caps on plastic bottles more easily removable for elderly and vulnerable people.
additional_details: It currently makes opening and using the bottle difficult for many people, especially the elderly and vulnerable people with limited dexterity.

action: Prevent UK participation in any military or war conflict with Iran.
background: We call on the UK Government to commit to no military involvement in any conflict with Iran under any circumstances. This includes not sending troops, weapons, funding, intelligence, or logistical support.
additional_details: The UK should not support, directly or indirectly, any acts of war against Iran. We urge the Government to reject military escalation and instead prioritise diplomacy, de-escalation, and peaceful foreign policy in the region.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition:
 
Commit to no military involvement in attacks on Iran
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730360

action: Urgent Summer Support for Thanet: Police Presence & Infrastructure need now!
background: Take immediate action to protect the beaches and surrounding communities of Thanet—Broadstairs (Viking Bay), Margate Sands, and Ramsgate Sands—during the peak summer months of June, July, and August. They are lacking infrastructure and enforcement support  to cope with the intense influx of visitors
additional_details:
We are asking for immediate and nationally-backed intervention
1. **Significant Police Presence** – visibly patrolling Thanet's key beach areas and public spaces
2. **Transport Hub Monitoring** – Police present at stations 
3. **Litter and Environmental Enforcement Officers** 
4. **Support for Local Businesses** – protect shops, restaurants, and venues from vandalism and theft
5. **Structured Beach Management Plan** – A formal seasonal plan (similar to crowd management at events like Ascot)
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.
 
You could raise this matter with your local MP or the Government department responsible for policing.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find contact details for the Home Office here: https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/home-office

action: Review the application of KYC checks at online casinos
background: Urgently review enhanced Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements for UK online gambling operators. One study suggests current implementation has created a 522% increase in black market gambling, pushing vulnerable players to unsafe and unregulated sites.
additional_details: Some academic research shows KYC checks exclude vulnerable groups, and that affiliate sites have seen a marked decrease in online searches for licensed online casinos since the new KYC checks. Trends show growth in "no KYC casino" searches since 2023. Many self-excluded gamblers now access the black market. We believe current policy creates a two-tier system: privileged access regulated sites, working-class may face unregulated risks. We believe evidence-based reform is needed urgently.

action: Ban the sale of cruel caged eggs
background: Ban the sale of all caged eggs in the United Kingdom
additional_details: Animals give so much to us, they like us deserve comfort. It is time to ban this cruel, outdated practice of caging up animals for the sake of maximum profit.
rejection_details:
Battery cages were banned in 2012 but the use of enriched cages is still permitted. 

There is already a petition calling for a ban on these 'enriched' cages which you may wish to sign:

Make it illegal to use "enriched" cages in farming 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/716075

action: Declare a national emergency and stop all illegal boats entering British waters.
background: Return all illegal boards back to the nearest beach in France.
additional_details: The United Kingdom is under invasion by illegal immigrants and it needs to stop immediately.
rejection_details:
It is not clear what you mean in regards to declaring a national emergency and what sort of impact you would like this to have.

You could start petition calling for the Government to be given emergency powers to address illegal immigration, if that's what you'd like.

You may wish to sign the following petitions:

Publish a detailed plan to tackle illegal migration and stop boat crossings: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709678

Send the navy into the channel to help stop illegal migrants entering the UK: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730769

action: Keep Britain Out of War with Iran — No UK Role in Escalating Conflict
background:
We call on the UK Government to take a clear and immediate position that it will not participate in any military action related to the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran.

Commit to pursuing a diplomatic response aimed at de-escalation and regional stability.
additional_details: US forces have already bombed Iranian nuclear facilities, raising the real risk of a wider regional war. Iran has promised to respond, and there is serious concern the UK could be drawn into a devastating conflict that threatens civilian lives and global stability.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition:
 
Commit to no military involvement in attacks on Iran
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730360

action: Amend employment law to require additional pay for Sunday working
background: I’d like the UK Government to mandate that anyone who works on a Sunday gets a pay increase of time and a half, since Sunday is an unsociable day to work.
additional_details: Many people would rather be elsewhere than working on a Sunday, as I think there’s no incentive/benefit to working on a Sunday. I think there needs to be action for this to change to make employees want to work on a Sunday.

action: Funding and guidance for Equal Holiday Club Access for All SEN Children
background: Every child deserves the chance to enjoy fun, safe, and inclusive holiday clubs but we feel too many children with Special Educational Needs are being left out. We call on government to ensure equal access to holiday provision for all children.
additional_details:
1. Guarantee Equal Access to Holiday Clubs for SEN Children
Introduce national guidance and standards to ensure holiday clubs are inclusive and accessible to children with SEND across all local authorities.

2. Provide Targeted Funding to Support Inclusion
Allocate ring-fenced funding for holiday club providers to train staff, adapt environments, and provide 1:1 or specialist support where needed.

action: Decouple electricity prices from gas and commit to phasing out fossil fuels
background: We ask Government to break the link between electricity and gas prices, which we think keeps bills unfairly high, and commit to phasing out fossil fuels. In doing so, reform the energy market, boost UK investment in renewables and storage and publish a clear plan to phase out fossil fuels in the UK.
additional_details: The share of the UK's electricity generated from renewables, clean, often low-cost sources like wind and solar, has seen an overall trend of generally increasing over time, but bills remain high in part because prices are tied to gas. Continuing to use fossil fuels funds fossil fuel producers—some who may be in regimes linked to war or human rights abuses—while worsening the climate crisis. I believe that our money props up an outdated, polluting system whilst millions face fuel poverty. I think reforming the market in the way I've proposed would help lower bills, reduce emissions, boost UK energy independence, and align our values with a fairer, cleaner future.

action: Update food allergens list to include nightshade family foods on food labelling
background: Update the law so that nightshade ingredients must be included on food labelling and menus as allergens.
additional_details: Ingredients such as potato can get lost and are referred to as ‘starch’ or paprika as ‘spices’ thus ingredients can be missed in restaurants and in potential purchases

action: Create and fund third party regulator scheme for service charge disputes
background: Create a scheme where disputed service charges are payable to courts or similar body and only passed to landlords if they can prove the charge's legitimacy. Otherwise, the money returns to the tenant/leaseholder. The scheme would apply to all landlord types excluding self-management.
additional_details: Unreasonable and inaccurate service charges can cause immense financial and psychological strain on those affected (renters, shared owners and leaseholders). Although laws already exist specifying that charges must be accurate and reasonable, many people are expected to pay up then seek refunds. We feel this and other factors put people challenging charges at a huge disadvantage in the current judicial system. None of the proposed new housing laws address this enforcement gap.

action: Regulate the use of ultrasonic pest repellent devices in the UK
background:
1. Ban the use of ultrasonic pest repellent devices in shared residential buildings and public spaces.
2. Require disclosure and signage where such devices are used.
3. Promote other safe, science-based pest control alternatives.
4. Consider individuals with disabilities and sensory conditions.
additional_details: Ultrasonic pest repellents can cause headaches, dizziness, tinnitus, anxiety to some people. They’re often hidden, making exposure involuntary. I think these devices lack proven effectiveness and may harm pets and wildlife, and that the risks outweigh the benefits. I think they can cause great harm to individuals who are autistic or have chronic health conditions. Everyone deserves to live, work, and learn in an environment free of invisible, harmful technology. Let’s prioritise health, safety, and inclusivity for all.

action: Set the income tax personal allowance to £15,597 & higher rate to £62,379.02
background: Set the tax free allowance at £15,597, calculated via the Bank of England inflation calculator Vs 2021 when the current rate was set. The same for the higher rate, currently £50,271 set in 2021, this should be £62,379.02.
additional_details: We think this would give more people money in their pockets to pay their bills and rely less on government help. This could also mean more money being spent so more VAT in the governments pocket too. We are currently suffering fiscal drag because of this and the previous government chose to freeze thresholds but we think this is a stealth tax. As we pay more for goods, our tax free allowance stays the same meaning we're getting poorer.

action: End of double taxation on working parents whose children attend private schools.
background:
Since 1st Jan 2025, parents discharging their statutory duty via independent schools face double taxation paying full Income Tax and 20% VAT on fees.
This is fiscally inequitable, unfair and punitive.
We respectfully petition HM Government to revoke VAT or provide corresponding tax income relief.
additional_details:
Pursuant to s.7 Education Act 1996, parents must ensure suitable full-time education for their children.
Those opting for private education discharge this duty at personal cost, saving the taxpayer over £8,000 per pupil per year.
Imposing VAT on school fees constitutes disproportionate and discriminatory fiscal burden on a specific group, against the UK equality laws.
Other public sectors (health & transport) are VAT-exempt and many OECD nations exempt or offer tax relief on private education.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition:

Stop VAT being added to Private school fees: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730767

action: Stop laughing in Parliament. You have a very serious job.
background:
During all moments in Parliament, MPs should act with the highest probety.
The British public, whose lives are being debated, should not see any person of office- especially those in the Cabinet, laughing and joking during any session.
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker.

action: Make GCSE English Literature exams open-book
background: The exams should be open-book to encourage deeper understanding and critical thinking. This approach would allow students to engage with the text more analytically, focusing on interpretation rather than memorisation. It fosters long-term comprehension, preparing students for real-world application.
additional_details: Making the exams open-book would better apply skills needed in real-life scenarios, where people can access resources to inform their decisions. This would shift the focus from recall to analysis and deeper understanding of texts. Students would be encouraged to engage more with literature, using texts to support their interpretations, rather than relying on recall. It also reduces unwanted stress, allowing students to express their analytical abilities rather than their ability to memorise.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Replace GCSE and A-Level memory-based exams with open-book formats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730126

action: Change law so all service stations must provide at least one EV charging point
background: It should be a condition of having a licence to sell fuel in roadside service stations that at least one charge point is provided for electric vehicles.
additional_details: Change licencing law for service stations.

action: Legalise the use of e-scooters for under 16s on public roads
background: We think that e-scooters help young people get around cheaply and safely. With the right rules, we think they could be legal for 16s with no need for a licence.
additional_details: We think the fact that they're illegal for under 16s takes away a simple, fun, and affordable way for young people to get around. We think the government could set sensible speed limits, and make safe spaces to ride. Other countries let young people use them responsibly without bans or licences so why cant UK?

action: Introduce clear, enforceable national laws for responsible use of E-scooters.
background: We urge the Government to introduce consistent, national regulations for E-scooters, including speed limits, proper lighting, insurance requirements, age limits and rules on pavement and public road use to protect the public, prevent accidents, and support responsible use of this means of transport.
additional_details: Use of E-scooters is increasingly common across the UK, yet current laws are inconsistent and enforcement is limited. This has led to public confusion and contributed to rising numbers of injuries and complaints. Introducing clear and consistent national regulations will help protect pedestrians, support sustainable transport goals, and give police and local authorities the clarity needed to enforce safe use.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:

Urgently regulate e-scooters
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727359

action: Hold a referendum on Brexit on 23rd June 2026 as this is the 10 year anniversary
background: If one has not been held beforehand, to hold a re-run of the Brexit referendum, to be timed for 23/06/2026 with 2 options on the ballot paper. Rejoin the EU or Stay out of the EU
additional_details:
The political forces have told us over the years that a Brexit referendum is a once in a decade event and one cannot be held at any time beforehand.

We the undersigned feel that we have done what the political establishment have told us to do, and that is to wait for a full decade to pass. Once that timeframe has passed, this reasoning will no longer hold true and we hope that the Government, no matter who is in power will honour our request.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:

Have a new referendum on EU membership
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727964

action: Call a general election, faith in labour has been lost
background: Call a general election
additional_details: Faith has been lost in the current government, Our borders need to be closed, Disabled People need to be supported, not victimised by taking away PIP
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Raise ILR eligibility threshold to 15 years for future & current visa holders
background: Amend immigration rules to increase the minimum residency period for ILR to 15 years. This change should apply to all visa holders, including those currently residing in the UK, to ensure consistent and long-term integration.
additional_details: I believe the current ILR threshold does not adequately reflect a long-term commitment to British society, and that raising it to 15 years would better assess integration, contributions, and alignment with British values. I believe this policy should apply uniformly, including to current visa holders, to ensure fairness, reduce abuse the settlement process, and maintain public trust in the immigration system.

action: Require non-smartphone alternatives for real word services provided on apps
background: Many companies are using apps to fulfil physical services. For example, parking payment, etc. Some of these apps do not have a physical alternative.
additional_details:
We think any company offering an app to fulfill a physical service should be required to also offer a non-smartphone alternative, for accessibility.
 
There are many reasons why someone may not have access to a smartphone. Some studies show they're addictive and poor for mental health, and they're expensive. We think this excludes a lot of people.
We think being digitally underserved is an expensive inconvenience. We ask not to be shut out of modern society.

action: Ban button batteries from children’s toys
background: We think that all button batteries should be banned from being used in children’s toys to prevent fatal and tragic accidents due to them being ingested.
additional_details:
We trust that toys made for children are safe for them. But button batteries can be deadly, so we think they must be banned from these items.
 
Button batteries are extremely dangerous if ingested by children and currently they are not banned from children’s toys. While regulations state they must be secured, such as with screws, we do not think this is enough. Toys can be broken, giving children access to the batteries, or the compartments may not be replaced correctly due to human error, leaving the batteries easily accessible when the toy is handed back to the child. We feel that too many accidents can occur without a ban on using them in children’s toys.

action: Reduce Qualification Barriers to Mental Health Careers
background: Mental health services in NI and globally face a funding and workforce crisis. Many psychology graduates with bachelor’s degrees can't enter the workforce because a master’s degree is often required for mental health roles. This is a missed opportunity, given the growing demand for services.
additional_details:
We urge the Northern Ireland Executive and regulatory bodies to review entry-level requirements in psychology and mental health. Specifically, we ask that bachelor’s degree holders be given opportunities to pursue careers in this understaffed, underfunded sector.

Allowing psychology graduates to enter at various levels will expand the workforce, ease the burden on specialists, and improve access to mental health care in Northern Ireland.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Northern Ireland Executive and Northern Ireland Assembly is responsible for. 

If you want to raise this issue you could contact your MLA, or raise it with the Northern Ireland Executive.

You can find contact details for your MLAs here: http://www.niassembly.gov.uk/your-mlas/

You can find contact details for the departments of the Northern Ireland Executive here: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/government-departments-in-northern-ireland

action: Ban cycling on all public roads and fund the expansion of separate cycle lanes
background: Ban the use of all bicycles on public roads and fund expansion of cycling lanes, separate from public roads. I want cycling to be banned on all public roads as I think cyclists cause slower journeys for other road users, are a hazard and could endanger themselves by simply being on those roads.
additional_details: I want to expand bicycle lanes so that cyclists still have areas to cycle but in what I think will be a safer environment.

action: 30yr minimum sentence for all cases of murder & manslaughter involving a knife
background: We call for the introduction of a mandatory minimum sentence of 30years for murder & manslaughter cases where a knife or sharp object was used. We want knife crime laws changed with tougher sentencing for crimes of murder & manslaughter involving knives and sharp objects.
additional_details: I lost my son to knife crime in 2019. We think current sentences are not sufficient enough to deter violent crimes involving knives. We believe a mandatory minimum sentence of 30 years for all murder & manslaughter cases where a knife was used, including in cases where the perpetrator is under 18 years of age, would act as a stronger deterrent.

action: Require that the role of Police Chief Constable be elected by police and staff
background: Require the establishment of a voting system within Police Constabularies that allows police officers and police staff to vote on who their next Chief Constable will be.
additional_details: We believe that establishing a democratic system for electing people to the role of chief constable will help ensure chief constables and senior management within policing are held to account not only by the public but by the officers and staff who work for them. The aim of this proposal is to help reduce any divide between senior management and police officers and to help create a senior management team that police officers and staff alike can trust while they conduct their duties.

action: Ban All Face Masks and Face Coverings in Public Areas
background: We, the undersigned, call on the UK government to ban face masks and coverings in public areas, particularly at protests. This ban will enhance public safety, as visible faces foster accountability and deter criminal behaviour, including theft and vandalism.
additional_details:
By promoting transparency, we can restore trust and connection within our communities. Banning face coverings will also support law enforcement efforts, ensuring a safer environment during protests by encouraging peaceful dialogue. In a society that values openness, this measure can strengthen community ties and reduce crime rates.

We urge the government to consider this petition seriously for the betterment of all UK citizens.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Prohibit the wearing of all full-face coverings in public spaces
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/723131

action: UK to join the joint statement on ECHR interpretation
background: We believe delay on legal reform risks the same failings seen in the ECHR’s Swiss climate ruling. Nine democracies have published a statement supporting ECHR interpretive reform. We think the UK should act now to protect national law from judicial overreach and ensure democratic accountability.
additional_details: We think the ECHR’s Swiss climate ruling showed that governments can violate rights by delaying action on foreseeable risks. We think that if the UK ignores allies’ calls for ECHR reform, it risks ceding democratic legal control. Our view is that signing the joint statement now ensures clarity before judicial overreach becomes entrenched.

action: To place danger signs and fences and life rings along the river tees Darlington
background:
To factor in more off the dangers off the river tees Darlington. The river is so easily accessible to children teenegers and adults. 
There should be danger signs placed at the worst parts off the river with warnings not to swim there and liferings. Even if possible some fencing.
additional_details: We have lost far to many lives to the river tees I can recall 3 this year just from people I know and at the river tees there is no warning signs nothing to help someone if there stuck and far to easily accessible to young people
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.
 
You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.
 
You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP
 
And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/
 
You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Reduce the school summer break to 5 weeks and allow schools to authorise 5 days
background: It is very expensive to take children out of school during summer holidays. If summer holidays were reduced to 5 weeks and schools were allowed to authorise 5 days of holiday , this would allow parents to take their child/ren out during the term making it cheaper for parents and higher attendance.
additional_details: Help ease the financial burden on families who want to create memories with their children as holiday companies can not exploit the holidays to increase prices. This will allow parents a term time break without being punished financially when they are already struggling. Education won't be affected as the summer term would be shorter
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Allow parents to take their children out of school for 5 school days in a year
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728790

action: Introduce requirement for all dogs to wear humane basket muzzle in public spaces
background: We urge the UK Government to require that all dogs wear humane, breathable muzzles whenever they are outside their owner's private property. The basket muzzles must allow dogs to open their mouths, pant, breathe easily and drink water or have treats, while also preventing biting incidents.
additional_details:
No other type of muzzle can be used that does not fit these requirements.

We think this measure could reduce the increasing number of dog attacks on people, other animals, and livestock. It could be a proactive public safety step that respects both animal welfare and the concerns of the wider community.
 
Many responsible owners already take precautions, but unpredictable behaviour can occur even in well-trained dogs. Requiring muzzles in public places could help protect the public and reassure those who feel unsafe around dogs.

action: Fund and expand employment opportunities for newly qualified NHS nurses
background: We urge the government to support newly qualified nurses by creating more NHS-funded roles. We want them to offer preceptorships, ensure fair recruitment, increase trust funding, and reduce reliance on overseas staff.
additional_details: We feel that newly qualified nurses are being let down after years of hard work, training, and personal sacrifice. Despite a national shortage of nurses and growing pressure on NHS services, some graduates are struggling to find employment. We think this is a waste of valuable talent. We are concerned that the NHS spends millions on international recruitment, while some of our own graduates remain unemployed.

action: Make all private mental health treatment VAT exempt
background: We believe there is a mental health crisis. We want to improve access to mental health treatment by making treatment through counselling and psychotherapy exempt from VAT. This would mean those seeking treatment privately would only pay the fee, without an additional 20% VAT.
additional_details: Therapy waiting lists are long in the NHS and privately, and need is high. Private mental health treatments are not all exempt from VAT. We think this makes treatment unaffordable for many. We also believe this stops therapists from opening up slots to keep income under threshold, decreases patient access due to high fees and impacts recovery and rehabilitation. Registered psychotherapists are VAT exempt in Ireland.

action: Allow Wales to hold an independence referendum
background: We want the UK Parliament to allow and enable Wales to hold an independence referendum. We think the people of Wales must be given the chance to vote in a Wales independence referendum so they can choose to either stay a part of the UK or for Wales to be an independent country.
additional_details:
Some groups in Wales want Wales to be an independent country. An independence referendum could allow the Welsh people to decide the future of Wales. 
 
We want the referendum question to be "Should Wales be an independent country?" The people can then choose to tick Yes or No.

action: Ban all face coverings in the UK
background: Ban all face coverings in the UK those include religious coverings
additional_details:
Our ability to see people's faces is essential for maintaining public safety and ensuring that everyone feels secure.
While face coverings might serve various personal, cultural, or religious functions, in the public realm they can obscure identity and increase the potential for unlawful activities. Data from various safety reports suggests that places with visible face policies report fewer incidents of crime and greater community trust. Ban them all!!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Prohibit the wearing of all full-face coverings in public spaces
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/723131

action: Launch an inquiry into the application of the bruising protocol
background: We ask the Government to launch a statutory public inquiry into the application of the bruising protocol for infants.
additional_details: We request a national inquiry into the application of the bruising protocol by the NHS trusts, social services, and police. We believe that there is inadequate statutory oversight, a lack of uniformity across counties, and a lack of proportionality between medical measures (CT head scans and X-rays) and the evidence that suggests grounds for concern. We are concerned with the unknown long-term effects of ionising radiation (standard in the bruising protocol) on babies. We seek reform and protection for innocent families.

action: :Make vets affordable to everyone again,
background: Vet bills are up by more than 60% between 2015 and 2023, risen by another 5-10% since then. Minimum cost for a vet visit is usually £300. Only the very wealthy can afford to take their pets to the vets. We need affordable vet care for all animals in every household, no matter their income.
additional_details:
•More and more animals going into rescues •Rescues are unable to accommodate the rise
•local vet’s in the last 3 years from £28 to £65. For app. 

•scan was £300 during surgery hours, is now £1000. 

•more animals are being put to sleep
•owners avoiding going
•vaccinations down, spread of diseases 
•Dogs and cats are not being neutered, more unwanted pups, kittens 

•we are being taken advantage of. 
•many companies who own Vets, seeing animals as a commodity
•we just want to care of our pets
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do. For example, you could outline what measures you would like to be taken in relation to the affordability of veterinary care.

You may also wish to sign the following petitions:

Remove VAT from pet veterinarian bills
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/706056

Create a national pet health service for veterinary care

action: Require schools to let children use the toilet at all times in the school day

action: New Disclosure and Safeguarding Mechanism for At-Risk Children
background: We propose a statutory safeguarding framework that facilitates proactive information sharing where a child is at risk due to a parent or caregiver’s known history, even when current laws may not trigger disclosure.
additional_details:
•            Introduce a Child Risk Disclosure Scheme (CRDS) that operates similarly to Clare’s and Sarah’s Laws but is focused on the broader risk history of caregivers.
•            Require statutory services (police, social care, health) to disclose relevant past history to the child’s parent or legal guardian when a risk is identified.
•            Establish multi-agency response protocols, particularly where child contact, custody, or unsupervised access is being considered.
•            Empower professionals to raise safeguarding alerts and initiate family court safeguarding interventions where known risks exist, even if not currently under active investigation.
government_response_summary: We are delivering significant reform across children’s social care, policing and the family court system to better safeguard children and stop them falling through the cracks of services.
government_response_body: Keeping children safe is a priority for this government, and this is why we are delivering the most significant overhaul of children’s social care in a generation. We deeply sympathise with calls to more effectively safeguard children and we recognise that fostering a culture of proactive information sharing amongst safeguarding professionals is critical to the early identification of need and risk, hence the facilitation of better support provision to prevent escalation.   Through our landmark Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill, we have set out to improve multi-agency information sharing, introduce a responsive family help system, and sharpen the child protection system. These reforms, taken together, are intended to better safeguard children, and stop them from falling through the cracks.   It is only when safeguarding partners have a fuller understanding of a child that they can effectively assess risk and take the most appropriate action. Rightly, the proposed Child Risk Disclosure Scheme highlights the importance of empowering and encouraging safeguarding practitioners to proactively share information relevant to a safeguarding concern, including where information relates to a risk posed by another person in a child’s life. Whilst the Government is not minded to introduce the elements of a Child Risk Disclosure Scheme requiring police to disclose information to parents and guardians, proposals to strengthen multi agency responses and earlier safeguarding help are already included in the package of reforms we are taking forward.  We are introducing a new Information Sharing Duty as set out in clause 4 of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill. By legally obliging statutory safeguarding partners to share information across agencies where there is a concern relevant to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, we are ending misconceptions about when information can and cannot be shared. Crucially, this extends to the sharing of information about other individuals for the same purpose, enabling practitioners to act and inform families as appropriate.  We are also exploring means of reducing friction in sharing information across agencies through technological improvements. This includes delivering on our manifesto commitment to introduce a consistent identifier for children, to allow data to be shared more efficiently and accurately by linking records together to improve join-up across services.  Once needs are identified, our wider reforms will ensure children and families receive the appropriate support. Through the Families First Partnership Programme, we are committed to delivering the national rollout of Family Help – a new model of responsive early support that places children and families at the centre of its design, intended to prevent problems from escalating.   Where need does escalate, or concerns are of a greater gravity, we are sharpening the child protection system and ensuring strong multi-agency protocols on a local level through the introduction of Multi-Agency Child Protection Teams. These will bring experts together across agencies to better identify cases where children are suffering, or are at risk of suffering, significant harm. The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill places a duty on safeguarding partners to implement this on a local level, alongside measures to strengthen the role of education and childcare settings in safeguarding arrangements.  Alongside reforms to children’s social care and in recognition of the impact domestic abuse has on children, we introduced Operation Encompass in November 2025. This is a statutory duty that requires police to notify a child’s education setting where they have attended a domestic abuse incident in a child’s home, regardless of if they were present.  Regarding multi-agency protocols where child contact and custody are being considered, we affirm that the welfare of children is the paramount concern in family court proceedings. Established risk assessments and multi-agency safeguarding arrangements are already in place and we are taking a step further by delivering a package of reforms to the family court to enhance safeguarding of, and support for children. This includes our decision to repeal the presumption of parental involvement from the Children Act 1989, and our work to expand the private law Pathfinder model, which promotes safeguarding through multi-agency collaboration, early identification of risk and expert support in cases involving domestic abuse.   Through these reforms, we hope to bring about fundamental change – to lay the foundations for a system that is responsive, champions professional curiosity, keeps children safe and helps families thrive. We will continue to consider where we can go further to strengthen safeguarding arrangements and encourage good practice on a local level, either through future legislation or the implementation of these measures.   Department for Education
