background: Bottom trawling should be illegal in all areas of UK waters. Bottom trawling is a destructive form of fishing where a large net is used to scrape the seafloor, which destroys it, in order to catch fish.
additional_details: Bottom trawling is banned in some Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) but is still allowed in others. In order to protect ocean wildlife and to ensure the ocean is healthy enough to absorb carbon dioxide, it should be banned in all areas of UK waters. In 2024, MPAs suffered 20,000 hours of bottom trawling. If we include non MPAs, the number of bottom trawling incidents is far higher. This is completely unacceptable. Nature in our ocean must be protected from bottom trawling.

action: Remove VAT on veterinary fees for pets
background: Following reports of some pet owners not being able to afford vet fees, we believe it is time for the Government to remove VAT from veterinary fees for pets so that it is no longer charged on animal health care which is essential for their health.
additional_details: We believe pets are not a luxury but loved and valued companions and contribute to emotional and mental wellbeing for so many including the elderly. Some animal rescue centres may be full and unable to help, resulting in healthy animals being put down or left to suffer without basic care. We believe that if VAT is no longer charged on all veterinary fees, it could go a long way to rectifying this situation.

action: Raise the minimum wage across the UK and keep pace with inflation
background: We think the government should commit to raising the National Living Wage (NLW) to better reflect the actual cost of living. This could involve not just a nominal increase, but a substantial rise that keeps pace with inflation and ensures that low-wage workers can afford basic necessities.
additional_details: We think the UK government must raise the minimum wage to address widespread financial struggles. We feel that the current NLW fails to cover basic expenses, trapping low-wage workers in poverty and forcing reliance on public assistance. We believe that a higher minimum wage could stimulate economic growth by boosting consumer spending and benefiting young and precarious workers. We think it's a matter of social justice, ensuring fair compensation for hard work and promoting economic stability for all.

action: Do not require small businesses/micro-entities to file profit & loss accounts
background: From 1 April 2027, Companies House will require small businesses and micro-entities to publicly file their P&L in addition to the balance sheet. The option to file abridged accounts will be removed, making previously private financial information publicly accessible.
additional_details:
As an accountant working closely with small and owner-managed businesses, I am deeply concerned about the impact these changes will have on privacy, competitiveness, and entrepreneurial confidence.
 
I believe the most contentious issue is the requirement to publish the P&L account on the public Companies House register. This could expose key financial metrics such as turnover, gross profit, and operating profit to anyone — including competitors, suppliers, and even opportunistic scammers.

action: Fund mandatory neurodevelopmental screening for all children
background: Screening could take place in primary care, including GP appointments, health visitor reviews, and school entry health at key developmental stages. It should involve early, trauma-informed, and identity-safe screening tools, with clear referral pathways, follow-up support, and outcomes monitored.
additional_details:
We think mandatory neurodevelopmental screening could mean:
• Earlier recognition of children who need support
• Better outcomes in school, home, and mental health
• A shift from crisis response to prevention.

We believe Parliament must act now to protect future generations from preventable harm. Neurodivergent children deserve to be seen — not after a crisis, but from the start.
government_response_summary: The government recognises the need for early intervention and support for children. At present the evidence does not support neurodevelopmental screening for all children.
government_response_body: We know many people, including children and young people, with suspected neurodevelopmental conditions experience severe delays in accessing services, including assessments and support. We want to move to earlier identification and support. The government’s 10 Year Health Plan recognises the need for early intervention and support.  The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence’s (NICE) ADHD guidelines (NG87) recommend that ‘universal screening for ADHD should not be undertaken in nursery, primary and secondary schools’. Evidence underpinning the recommendation concludes that there is little to no effect in introducing a universal screening programme in educational settings on children’s ADHD symptoms. Similarly, the UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC) published a review of screening for autism in pre-school children under the age of five in February 2023. They concluded, based on the available evidence, that ‘the UK NSC does not currently recommend screening for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in pre-school children under 5 years’, due to concerns about the accuracy of current screening tools and a lack of evidence that children diagnosed through universal screening have better long-term health or social outcomes than those identified through clinical pathways.  We recognise that demand for neurodevelopment assessments has increased significantly in England, which means people of all ages are experiencing delays in accessing the help they need. Through the NHS Medium Term Planning Framework, published 24 October 2025, NHS England has set clear expectations for local integrated care boards and trusts to improve access, experience and outcomes for autism and ADHD services over the next three years, focusing on improving quality and productivity.  The government is currently carefully considering the recommendations made by the report of the independent ADHD taskforce, commissioned by NHS England in 2024. The report recommended improvements in the early identification of neurodivergent children and young people so that personalised support can be implemented to prevent escalating needs. The report is available at the following link: https://www.england.nhs.uk/publication/report-of-the-independent-adhd-taskforce/   Building on the work of the taskforce, the government is also working to better understand why demand is rising and how to make sure people get the right support at the right time. On 4 December 2025, the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care launched an Independent Review into Prevalence and Support for Mental Health Conditions, ADHD and Autism. This independent review will inform our approach to enabling people with ADHD and autistic people of all ages to have the right support in place to enable them to live well in their communities. The final report will be published in the summer.  Department of Health and Social Care

background: A large proportion of illegal migrants in the UK are economic migrants. We believe they must be returned to their country of origin to prevent further cost to the public purse.

additional_details: A new SL3 stop at the Townley Grammar school stop (where the 269 stops) would significantly improve safety and accessibility for hundreds of students who currently face long walks from existing stops, often in bad weather or dark conditions. action: Ban all types of wire snares
background: We think snares are cruel, outdated traps that cause immense suffering to wildlife and pets. They can be indiscriminate, sometimes catching non-target animals, including protected species. We think the government should ban the use, sale and possession of animal snares to prevent unnecessary harm.

action: Require a trained FLO to be assigned to families bereaved by suicide
background: We would like Jason's Law to be introduced which would Require all police forces to assign trained Family Liaison Officers to every family bereaved by suicide, which could help ensure consistent support, communication, and guidance during investigations, inquests, and the immediate aftermath.
additional_details: Thousands of families devastated by suicide may navigate complex investigations, inquests, and media attention alone, while homicide/road death families receive Family Liaison Officers. The Commons Health Committee identified this gap in 2017, noting suicide bereaved families lack standard FLO support. We think this requirement would end this inequality, mandating FLO support for all suicide bereaved families using existing resources fairly.

action: Introduce new Legislation for Light Commercial Delivery Vehicles
background: We call upon Parliament to enact legislation requiring all commercial pedal-powered and light electric vehicles (bicycles, e-bikes, tricycles, cargo bikes, rickshaws, and some other spoked-wheel vehicles), to meet mandatory safety, registration, and insurance standards.
additional_details: I believe government must act urgently to regulate commercial delivery vehicles as the current system has created what I see as a dangerous accountability vacuum that could put public safety at risk while undermining legitimate businesses. Accidents have increased alongside the gig economy boom. Unlike licensed vehicles, these operate with fewer safety standards. When accidents occur, victims cannot always identify the vehicle/operator, leaving them without recourse.

action: Stop the government from merging the TV license into council tax.
background: Keep the TV license as a separate entity as a minimum or better yet abolish it completely.
additional_details:
The current TV licence is a clearly defined, separate charge. If merged into council tax, it would become just another line in a complex bill. 
Right now, the BBC is directly funded through the licence fee, meaning the public has a clear financial relationship with the broadcaster. This structure encourages accountability. If the fee is buried in council tax, the BBC becomes further removed from the people who fund it.
Council tax is based on property value, not TV usage.

additional_details: The 2025 TfL consultation showed that 75% of users feel unsafe in pedicabs, 85% said fares are overpriced, and nearly 2,000 respondents called for a complete ban. Only 7% had ever used one. Most Londoners view them as a danger, a nuisance, and harmful to the city’s image. They should be removed, not regulated.

action: Introduce Molly’s Law: Shared Parenting by Default After Separation
background: We ask the Government to introduce Molly’s Law — a legal presumption of shared parenting following separation, unless there is clear evidence that such an arrangement would put a child at risk.
additional_details:
Molly’s Law would amend the Children Act 1989 to give children a legal right to a meaningful relationship with both parents post-separation.

Other countries (such as Sweden, New Zealand, and Australia) already use shared parenting as the legal starting point — and see reduced conflict, better child outcomes, and less pressure on family courts.

action: Hold a London-wide referendum on leaving the GLA, and giving the GLA more powers

additional_details:
We want the Government to legislate so the Greater London Assembly can block the mayor’s plans by a simple majority vote. 

As a voter in a London council, I want to vote for my council to leave the GLA and not be subject to the decisions of the Mayor of London. Over the past 25 years, I have been concerned about London mayors pursuing their own political objectives, regardless of public opinion, and a lack of means to challenge this.

action: New rules on online gossip sites

action: Amend terror law to remove "damage to property" as an element of terrorism
background: We think terrorism law should only be used for serious offences, not to police non-violent actions and protest. We think acts that only involve damage to property in ways that are not directly harmful to human health or life should not be governed by terrorism law.
additional_details: To protect civil liberties, we think the government should restrict the breadth of terrorism law. As it currently stands, we think terrorism law may be used to punish organisations for hurting the government's international standing.

action: Reverse increase in the rate of employer’s NI contributions for small businesses
background: Many small businesses are struggling under rising costs, inflation, rising wage costs and uncertainty. We believe many need relief from the increases in employer national insurance contributions for growth and job retention, and that the Government’s actions were counter-productive to growth.
additional_details: We want the Government to reverse this policy for small businesses as we believe it hampers businesses from employing, growing and generating profit, which raises corporation tax revenue. We believe it may cause small business to lay off staff as profit diminishes and avoid employing new workers. We are concerned it could burden the benefits system too. We believe the current policy is counterproductive and goes against economic growth. We urge the Government to make changes.

There is zero reason to permit motorcycles to create excessive noise for no reason other than the rider wanting their vehicle to be "noisier". It is pure anti-social behaviour and easily delay with by legislation.

action: Revoke Genetic Technology (Precision Breeding) Regulations 2025 & the 2023 Act
background: Revoke the Genetic Technology (Precision Breeding) Regulations 2025 & repeal the Genetic Technology (PB) Act 2023. They allow certain genetically modified organisms (GMOs), such as precision bred plants and animals, to bypass requirements related to the environmental release and marketing of GMOs.
additional_details: We feel these laws effectively declassify certain GMOs by exempting Precision Bred Organisms (PBOs) from existing GMO regulations. We are concerned this may weaken safeguards relating to health, environment, labelling, traceability & public transparency, and that deregulation could allow genetically altered organisms to be cultivated, released & marketed without adequate risk assessments or public oversight. We ask Parliament to revoke the legislation which we think will help ensure that all GMOs are subject to full regulation & scrutiny.

action: New protections and support for construction workers
background: We urge the Government to limit the hours of work on all construction sites (with limited exceptions) to 8 hours per day, increase the minimum wage for construction workers so they don't lose out, and fund more apprenticeships to encourage young people to enter trades.
additional_details: Many UK construction workers commit suicide each year. We think that long hours, poor working conditions and a lack of public respect contribute to this. We believe reducing construction hours can improve workers' work-life balance, leading to happier and more efficient projects. We believe the cost will be passed to clients and managed in preconstruction. We think it could also reduce unnecessary/vanity works, saving money and carbon emissions. Trades are vital and we must protect them.

action: Call 999 immediately, test for alcohol & drugs & tougher penalties post-accident
background: Require drivers in all traffic accidents to call 999 immediately, not after 24 hours or via non-emergency lines. Require police to test for drugs and alcohol at the scene & tougher penalties for drink & drug driving.
additional_details: Current law lets drivers involved in serious accidents wait up to 24 hours to report via non-emergency numbers, which may let them avoid immediate breathalyser or drug tests. We think this risks public safety and denies victims timely justice. We think requiring instant 999 calls and on-the-spot testing could help close these loopholes, ensure quicker police response, and hold drivers accountable, protecting everyone on the roads.

action: Age restrict the use of electronic bikes & scooters, and where they can be used.
background: Introduce a minimum age for using e-bike and e-scooters, and make it illegal for them to be used in public places (such as parks/playing fields) and pavements.
additional_details: Introduce the requirement of a provisional license and insurance in order to purchase and use an e-bike and e-scooter.
rejection_details:
There are already age restrictions on who can use e-bikes and e-scooters.

If you would like changes to the current age restrictions, you could start a new petition about that.

action: Stop all arms exports to Israel immediately and help to seek ceasefire in Gaza.
background: The UK must not be complicit in violence. Halting arms exports will pressure for peace and uphold international law. The Government should use all diplomatic channels to demand an immediate ceasefire, protect civilians, and support a lasting political solution.
additional_details: The UK must not enable actions that contribute to humanitarian crises. Exporting arms to conflict zones undermines our values and international law. Urgent action is needed to protect civilians, uphold human rights, and push for a just and lasting peace in the region.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729717

The UK Government has also issued a joint statement with international partners to urge for "an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire."

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/joint-statement-on-the-occupied-palestinian-territories

action: Hold a Referendum on Capital Punishment for heinous crimes
background: Hold a referendum on whether to reintroduce Capital Punishment, for heinous crimes in particular, to give those of voting age the chance to disapprove, abstain or support a penalty of removing life from a human being for heinous crimes.
additional_details:
The Referendum could contain a simple statement (based on the pure principle of reintroducing Capital Punishment for heinous crimes). In my view, the result would help show the collective feelings within our Nation and whether Capital Punishment should be a penalty within the legal system.
I believe that justice would be obtained for heinous crimes against the vulnerable and defenceless and that an element of closure may be obtained by those wronged.

action: Require invoices be sent for all charges in ANPR carparks without onsite payment
background: ANPR in carparks read numberplates on entry and exit. Many ask you to pay via a website or app within a short deadline. If you forget you may face a fine. Often people report receiving letters threatening action. Require that you must always be sent an invoice first and given a fair chance to pay.
additional_details: We feel this will then be more aligned with other processes for paying for services and help those of us who are happy to pay but whose lives are dictated by other priorities, such as kids, work, the excitement of picking up an old friend from the airport.

action: To make Vets bills exempt from VAT
background: To make VAT exempt from Vets bills
additional_details: The average cost of going to the Vets £100 which means each time I take my pet I have to pay the Government £20 for the privilege to of looking after my pet and with today high living costs this only adds to the maintaining the cost living
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731567

action: Increase the government limit on council parking fines
background: Increase the limit council can impose for illegal parking to fund more enforcement and keep our roads and pavements clear of bad drivers.
additional_details:
Illegal parking is incredibly common all over the country, we think the fines arent big enough to act as a deterrent and also not big enough to fund effective enforcement.
 
We think the current fine of £70 (or £35 if paid within 2 weeks) outside of London doesn't cover costs and makes recruiting wardens (civil enforcement officers) difficult due to low wages.
 
We think this means our streets are clogged with bad drivers abandoning their vehicles wherever they feel unlikely to get fined.

action: Require companies to employ minimum 70% UK nationals before sponsoring others
background: We believe 70% of employees in a company should be UK nationals. The government should set this as a requirement for any companies requesting a Sponsor License, Certificates of Sponsorship, or License renewals.
additional_details:
We urge the government to require all UK registered companies (excluding the NHS and Health Sector) to employ at least 70% UK citizens before sponsoring overseas employees on Skilled worker visas.

We believe this would help to reduce immigration, reduce employment rates and develop skills for locals.

action: Let people claim DLA past age 16 if caring for a non-Gillick Competent adult
background: Give the option for those who care for individuals with Severe, Profound, Complex Needs the option to remain on Disability Living Allowance beyond the age of 16.  We believe this is needed due to ongoing issues with PIP reform
additional_details: Since its introduction, PIP has caused undue stress, financial hardship, and harm to many disabled people and their families due to what we see as a flawed assessments and a point-based system that does not adequately reflect the complexities of many conditions.  The reforms could increase the flaws in the system and carers rely on DLA to support these children, and will need to continue to support them throughout adulthood.

action: Stop the BESS Madness - Review the current planning process
background: We call on the government to introduce more stringent central controls on the arbitrary planning applications presented to local planning authorities for the creation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS sites), most being on green belt land.
additional_details: Currently, applications for BESS sites are being approved by planning authorities on the basis that "the benefits to the community outweighs the harm done to the green belt". It is becoming increasingly clear that there's a lack of central control over these applications and empirical evidence is indicating that the goverments tragets for 2030 and 2035 have already been met by the applications that have already been approved, yet hundreds still remain in the planning pipeline. Stop this madness.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Review regulations on Battery Energy Storage Systems 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/723869

action: Introduce inclusivity pots of differing pens/pencils in primary schools.
background: As a children's Occupational Therapist I feel strongly that when it comes to writing implements, one type does not fit all. Primary classroom tables should have an inclusivity pot of differing pens/pencils/scissors and fidgets allowing children to chose their preferred writing tool from reception.
additional_details:
Children need to be able to explore different options to see what feels right for them in terms of ease of use, comfort, and manipulation. Not everyone holds a pen the same way, so a variety of pens/pencils should be available to allow children for chose what feels right for them without judgement.

Table inclusivity pots can then lead to the end of pen licences which are outdated, discriminatory, and uninclusive. 

Let’s teach handwriting at the right time with the right tools.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
Decisions about resources provided in the classroom are a matter for individual schools, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Mandatory records of bicycle (& component) serial numbers at sale & ban removal
background: Many bicycle frames, suspension forks, shock absorbers and other components already have unique identifiers from the factory. This is a petition to mandate record keeping of these identifiers for all new and used sales, on all platforms, for all those selling bicycles or parts.
additional_details:
Currently, there's no mandatory record keeping or declaration of unique identifiers. Stolen goods can easily be sold on online marketplaces and other platforms.
 
If it is mandatory to declare these identifiers when selling bicycles (and components) online, stolen goods may be harder to sell.
 
In addition, removal of unique identifiers should be made illegal. Possession of any bicycle (or component) that's had its unique identifier deliberately removed should be illegal.

action: Make stolen valour illegal in the uk
background: Bring the law from the US to stop people claiming to be ex and current service members.
additional_details: It is dishonest and quite frankly insulting to the name of current and ex servicemen and women. Arrest and charge those bringing the insult and dishonour to people that actually had the courage to sign up.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action:

Make "Stolen Valour" a Criminal Offence
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/716765

action: Cap cost of prison phone calls to 5p per minute & free weekly allowance
background: I want the Government to make prison phone calls affordable by capping costs at no more than 5p per minute and introducing a free weekly call allowance for all prisoners. Communication is a right, not a privilege — we feel that no one should be priced out of staying connected to loved ones.
additional_details: High prison call costs could force some families to skip essentials. Article 8 of the Human Rights Act outlines the right to respect for private and family life and UN Mandela Rules emphasise the importance of family contact. We feel providers profit from pain. Ministry of Justice research shows family visits cuts reoffending by 39%. We believe affordable calls could reduce isolation, improve mental health, and support rehabilitation.

action: Call an Emergency General Election Now in No10
background: The government should call for an emergency general election to restore public trust and the removal of the Labour Government. Recent scandals and policy failures have lost confidence in the current administration, leading to widespread dissatisfaction and protests.
additional_details: A general election would allow the public to express their views on these critical issues and choose representatives who can effectively address the country's challenges. Additionally, with significant shifts in public opinion and pressing economic concerns, a new election would provide a fresh perspective and the opportunity for a more unified and effective government. This would give the new government the legitimacy it needs to make big decisions. The UK won’t survive any longer with Labour.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Retain 5 Year ILR & Citizenship Route, Delay Public Funds Access Until Year 10
background: Retain the 5-year path to ILR and British citizenship for Skilled Worker migrants, but extend the no recourse to public funds period to 10 years. We believe this would balance and uphold the UK’s promise to migrants to make it their home via 5-year ILR path while easing pressure on public resources.
additional_details: We believe extending the ILR period to 10 years breaks trust with Skilled Workers who built and planned their lives around the 5 year route. To address public spending concerns, we suggest delaying access to public funds for a total of 10 years for those who have newly obtained ILR or citizenship. We believe this would preserve the original promise, deters misuse, and maintain public confidence. We believe it would also protect genuine migrants from reactive policy changes driven by rising net migration and spending pressures.

action: Teach the full history of South Asian people who fought for Britain
background: Add to the curriculum the full history of how the British Empire led to millions of South Asian people amongst other colonised people fighting for Britain during the world wars. We believe it is an important part of British history that is often left out.
additional_details:
In a world where social media dominates and a country where we are so diverse, we believe there is still a huge blank space, misinformation, racism and ignorance about the true history of the South Asian community's journey to Britain.
 
We think making it a compulsory part of the history curriculum would allow more engagement, inclusivity and interaction to British values and would shape the identities of the British Asian population. It could also help bridge divisions and bring us all closer.

action: Increase the maximum sentences for historical child abuse cases
background:
Currently, we think the law fails survivors of historical child abuse
We are calling for new maximum sentence that apply to historical child abuse cases prosecuted under the Children and Young Persons Act 1933 and the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022.
additional_details:
Under current legislation, courts must sentence offenders based on the guidelines that were in place at the time the abuse occurred, not the standards we hold today. This means that individuals who committed horrific historic acts of cruelty against children may receive a shorter sentence
Similar offences would now carry a longer maximum sentence. We think survivors of historical abuse are denied this justice simply because their suffering occurred before the law caught up.

action: Balance the need for housing in the SE with adequate infrastructure and services
background: Ensure that ALL future developments in Medway and Kent do not compromise the health, education and quality of life of the people who currently live there.
additional_details:
The population in Medway and Kent is growing. Affordable housing - good social housing is becoming more and more a need not a requirement. However, the population also needs schools, GP surgeries and hospitals that are big enough to cope.
Make it mandatory for developers to have in place a social policy to encompass the above and to secure staffing before planning permission is granted



We
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You may also wish to sign this petition which calls for strict infrastructure requirements before houses can be built:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710119

action: Change the way that car insurance policies are worked out for older people
background:
People over 70 renew their driving licence every 3 years. The DVLA should tighten up renewals starting with them asking for an opticians certificate to state the the persons eyesight is acceptable for driving.
This should help to keep insurance premiums down.
additional_details:
At the moment all elderly drivers are lumped together for insurance purposes, in my instance I am being penalised for my age. I am perfectly fit to drive without glasses and have all my faculties.
It would seem that all elderly people are classed as high risk as far as the insurance people are concerned, this is not so!
At the moment I have 14years no claims bonus.
The government needs to ask the insurance companies to work out a way of cheapening insurance for those safe elderly drivers.
rejection_details:
The way in which car insurance policies are worked out is a matter for individual insurance providers. 

Another element of this petition is covered by an open petition: 

"Require people over 70 have a compulsory eye tests every 2 years to drive"  https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725445

action: Abolish the Party Whip system in Parliament
background: We want Parliament to abolish its party whip system entirely. We think this would help MPs to feel freer to vote according to their conscience and their constituents' interests.
additional_details:
We believe any consequences for an MP’s vote, that may mean damage to their careers, should be treated as unparliamentary conduct.
 
We think that without enforcement by whips, there will be more need for party leadership to build consensus by proposing legislation that is consistent with the party's declared principles and current manifesto. We believe MPs will be more empowered to vote with integrity, guided by values rather than obedience.
 
In our view, abolishing whips will restore the independence, dignity and accountability of MPs and will let them vote with conscience and constituents in mind, while keeping party leadership anchored to core principles.

action: Set a limit on a temperature in which employees and contractors can work.
background: In extreme heat, it’s essential that there is protection for the health of people working and a safety net in place to prevent the NHS from being overwhelmed with patients affected by the heat.
additional_details: The majority of countries have these protections in place but it’s only in fairly recent years that the UK has begun to experience extreme heatwaves and that the problem has begun to arise in the workplace.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Introduce a legal maximum temperature to work - 25 degrees Celsius
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731468

action: Off-Peak prices for holidays for educational staff
background: We request off-peak holiday prices for all educational staff, including teachers, assistants, admin, and support roles. These prices should apply during school holidays, matching standard off-peak rates. Access should be simple, requiring only proof of employment in education.
additional_details: Educational staff dedicate their time, energy, and passion to shaping the minds of future generations, often working long hours beyond the classroom with limited flexibility for time off. Because they can only travel during fixed school holidays, they are unfairly subject to inflated peak prices, making rest and recovery unaffordable for many. This not only impacts their well-being but also affects morale and retention in a vital profession.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban holiday companies from charging higher prices in the school holidays
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730119

action: Make the Government aware Wisbech residents need clean air
background: I want the Government to legislate for a air quality monitor in every home
additional_details: With the Development of Medworth rather than letting MVV mark their own homework the residents of Wisbech want and need the faculty to monitor air quality 24/7 and not allow MVV to use their hindsight after an event
rejection_details:

action: Expand offence of attempted murder to include all knife crime
background:
We think Knife crime should carry a charge of attempted murder.
Carrying a knife
Using a knife
We think people carry a knife with intent to severely hurt or kill.
additional_details:
We think knife crime is rife in this country because the laws are too relaxed. We think knife crime has increased because the punishments are too lenient that degrades the seriousness of the crime.
We think that if you carry a knife you are going out with the intent to severely hurt or kill.

action: Review high street regeneration & local community empowerment
background: We call on the government to conduct a review of policies on empowering communities, regenerating high streets, and ensuring sustainable development of key town centre sites, prioritising local needs.
additional_details: We think that derelict town centre sites hinder high street vitality and sustainable growth and communities need a stronger voice in decisions about these vital assets. We feel that current policies often fail to ensure developments genuinely benefit local economies, foster local shopping, or align with climate goals by reducing car dependency. We believe government leadership is vital to empower towns and ensure public land serves community and environmental best interests.

action: Tarmac pump track, Allesley park Coventry.
background: Invest money into building the pump track.
additional_details: As the local citizens have been hoping for somewhere to ride there bikes, scooters and skateboards and for somewhere to socialize with others and make new friends.This would be a great addition to the park as it gives the community something to do and keeps them entertained.
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

action: Abolish the BBC Licence Fee – End Biased Broadcasting at Public Expense
background: Abolish the BBC licence fee and demand reform of its funding and editorial standards. The BBC must stop biased reporting and return to its duty of impartial, fair public broadcasting in a way that reflects today’s media landscape.
additional_details: The BBC is increasingly seen as politically biased, especially in its international coverage. Combined with rising fees and the removal of free licences for pensioners, many feel forced to pay for content they don’t trust or want. The public deserves a neutral, accountable broadcaster, funded fairly in a modern media environment.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Revoke the BBC's royal charter & right to charge a licence fee
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711434

action: Abolish the BBC licence fee and replace it with an optional subscription.
background: The current system forces hard-working people to pay for a service they may not use. It’s time for change. We call for a fairer, voluntary system where the BBC is funded through a subscription service.
additional_details: Britain is meant to be a free, democratic country – so why are people still being forced to pay a TV licence for a service they don’t want? The BBC has become outdated, expensive, and politically biased. It’s time to scrap the licence fee and let the public decide what they watch – and what they pay for.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Scrap the BBC TV Licence & replace funding with adverts or paywall
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727365

action: Revert to an opt in system for Organ Donation & advertising campaign to promote
background: The system has been changed over the last few years to mean someone who does not wish to donate their organs after death has to specifically notify the NHS Organ Donation team. We wish for the system to return to the old system where you had to opt in specifically.
additional_details:
While we recognise organ donation saves lives, we also feel uncomfortable about the new system where you specifically have to opt out, should you not wish for your organs to be donated. We think its not known to many people that this is the case and some people who did not wish to participate, may have their organs donated after death due to this lack of knowledge.

We wish for the system to be reverted to how it was and have an advertisement campaign instead to put forward the benefits of donation.

I would like parliament to understand the detrimental hit the industry is having, due to the extreme vat, electric, gas, fish industry, potatoes/farming, rising wages.

Eliminate VAT on hot takeaway food

action: Require DBS checks for delivery drivers
background: We call on the UK Government to make it mandatory for all delivery drivers—including those working for gig economy platforms—to undergo at least a Basic DBS check.  We believe this would help to prevent exploitation and protect public safety.
additional_details: We call on the UK Government to make it mandatory for all delivery drivers—including those working for gig economy platforms—to undergo at least a Basic DBS check. We are concerned that vulnerable people, including elderly, women, and disabled individuals, open their doors daily to strangers delivering food or parcels. It may then be possible for the driver to enter their homes. Most other drivers are required to have DBS checks; we believe the same should apply to delivery workers.

action: Change back cervical screening again from every five years to every three years.
background: The cervical screening period has changed from having a smear test every three years to every five years. This needs to change back to every three years as extending the time frame between smears will cost lives. It does not matter wether you have a clear test to then extend the time frame.
additional_details: I have a smear every three years and the last one I had I had HPV and abnormal cells, this was in a three year period imagine if I had to wait five years it could have been very different. I would have either had cancer that needed treatment or it might have been too late. We cannot let lives be lost just because someone decided it would be a good idea to extend the time frame. This is not moving forward in prevention it is taking a step backwards.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Review the NHS decision to make smear testing every 5 years if HPV negative
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729981

action: Force Accountability for Failed Parcel Deliveries Across the UK
background: We urge the UK Government to take action against failing delivery services, such as ParcelForce, by enforcing clear delivery standards, requiring proof of delivery, and establishing a regulatory body to investigate complaints and protect consumers from repeated service failures.
additional_details: Many face repeated delivery failures, with parcels falsely marked as “delivered” and no attempt to notify them. This causes confusion, distress, delays, and financial loss, especially for urgent items like medicine or pet supplies. Companies rarely take responsibility. We urge the Government to introduce regulation, enforce accountability, and protect consumers from ongoing postal and courier service failures.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707922

action: Require construction of data centres to be halted & find eco-friendly solution
background: We think as a country that has put much emphasis on ensuring our air and water is kept clean and accessible for the future of our children, it's imperative that the Government requires a halt in construction of all new data centres until more self-sustaining, eco-friendly, safe solutions are found.
additional_details:
Some recent research, for example from MIT, Forbes, and other institutions indicates the significant impact energy consumption by data centres can have on our climate.
 
Data centres can use a huge amount of energy and water daily. The associated emissions may contain large amounts of pollutants which have been reported to contribute to cancer and other serious health issues. Some communities in different parts of the world are forced to use plastic bottles of water to bathe or may find waste residue in their “clean” water supply, in part because of pollutants.
 
We think we need to set a global example of excellence and keep our Net Zero promise.

action: Require all nursing and care homes have to have air conditioning
background: We want the government to make it law that air conditioning must be installed in all nursing and care homes. With climate change and temperatures increasing, we feel we need to ensure the vulnerable are not left in uncomfortable, hot rooms.
additional_details: Each individual room should have its own portable air conditioning unit so that residents can choose what temperature they would like their own room to be. We think this would make life more comfortable for the vulnerable.

action: Stop TFL and partners raising the rent in the railway arches extortionately.
background: Stop the extortionate raises. Lower them to a price where people can make it work they don’t have to throw all those years hard work down the drain.
additional_details: The government are always talking about how they want to save small businesses, well now is the chance to save many. Hundreds of small businesses are closing by the week. Thousands of people out of jobs. Businesses that sometimes have been there over 40 years and was being handed to the next generation, suddenly gone with a click of their fingers. Please make it so it is compulsory for them to dramatically lower their prices and keep us all in business.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. It is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly. 

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Require child prices on tickets for concerts, events & holidays for under 16s
background: I want child prices on tickets for concerts or huge events and holidays to be exactly that. If you are under 16 and in education you are likely not earning a wage therefore I think should not have to pay adult prices for tickets.
additional_details:
I think some children over the age of 11 who are still in full-time education are unfairly excluded from receiving child pricing on tickets for events, holidays, and concerts.
 
I think this can place an additional financial burden on families and alienate many teenagers who are eager to participate in these activities. I urge the government to require businesses and services to provide child pricing to all under the age of 16 who are in full-time education.

action: Stop the building construction on farm land
background: Save the farm land from developers on building houses and looking into the infrastructure roads schools hospitals doctors etc
additional_details: It was green vent land not grey vent land homes and houses will be sold and bulldozed the farm has been in the one family for five generations plus the roads schools and doctors can not cope with the amount of houses on this land .

action: PROTECT MEDWAY AND GRAVESHAMS GREEN BELT LAND.  STOP DEVELOPMENT ON THIS LAND.
background: Stop councils from reclassifying green belt land for housing. Protect green spaces in Medway and Gravesham. Strengthen planning laws to prioritise brownfield development and preserve countryside, wildlife habitats, and community identity.
additional_details: Reclassifying green belt land threatens nature, increases pollution, and erodes community space. Once it’s built on, it’s lost forever. Wildlife habitats are destroyed, services overstretched, and green spaces vanish. We need homes, but not at the cost of our environment and quality of life.

action: Review how motorcycle licensing operates and is enforced
background: I want the government to review and change how motorcycle licensing operates and is enforced, including how to enable younger riders to achieve a full license, and cutting down on any illegal riders using delivery mopeds.
additional_details: I feel that after going through the licensing myself and seeing how expensive it was for me, not enough seems to have been done to have a more streamlined process for bike licensing and to curb what I see as the monopoly that bike schools have over the training industry.

action: Require all companies to declare microplastic levels in their food & drinks
background: We urge the Government to require all companies to publicly identify and declare the amount of microplastics in their food and drink products, so people can make an informed choice about whether to consume products that may contain high levels of microplastics.

action: Free childcare entitlements for adopted children while parent on adoption leave
background: Fund free childcare for adopted children whilst their parents are on adoption leave so they receive similar entitlements to working parents.
additional_details: You may not be able to apply for working parent entitlements until one month before returning to work from adoption leave. This means that adopted children cannot access funded childcare like other children and receive a funded nursery education. We think that this means their education is impacted by their adoption status.

action: Make SuDS mandatory for all new developments
background: We believe Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS) can help improve river water quality by reducing the amount of road surface water run off into the sewerage system, reducing flooding, and helping to recharge ground water.
additional_details: We think making SuDs mandatory for new developments, and the government  implementing Schedule 3 of the Flood and Water Management Act 2010 would provide a framework for the widespread adoption of SuDS and give local authorities the role of sustainable drainage approval body (SAB), with responsibility for checking compliance and approving their use.

action: Legislate to mandate offer of electronic pension transfers and higher standards
background: You can switch banks in a week and send money instantly, so why should pension transfers take months and be so stressful? Only the government has the power to change this, so we’re asking them to take action and set clear, enforceable standards for faster, electronic pension transfers.
additional_details:
63% of savers believe delays in pension transfers hinder effective retirement planning. Yet we think some providers persist with outdated, paper-based processes. At best, we think this may cause stress and confusion. At worst, we think it may deter people from moving their money, trapping them in poor-value, or unsuitable funds.
 
Some providers already offer secure, electronic transfers. We think it’s time to mandate this across the industry for fairer, efficient retirement savings.
government_response_summary: The Government recognises the importance of efficiency in the pension transfers system and is considering how to improve the pension transfer process while maintaining strong member protection.
government_response_body: The Government’s approach is guided by two objectives, supporting efficient transfers, and crucially, ensuring strong member protections, not least against scams. We acknowledge the calls for faster transfers, and we are exploring operational improvements to streamline processes, including the use of electronic processes which can drive real improvements.   Changes driven by mandation across the market, would however, require changes to Primary legislation. We would also need to be satisfied that any changes do not weaken existing member protections or present a heightened risk of pensions fraud. Ensuring there are robust safeguards to enable members to make informed transfer choices that lead to good retirement outcomes is essential.   The last government, in November 2021, introduced the Occupational and Personal Pension Schemes (Conditions for Transfers) Regulations 2021. The regulations were intended to better protect pension savers against the threat of pension scams by placing conditions on the statutory right to transfer, through a series of red and amber flags.  A review of the regulations was published in June 2023, as agreed with the Work and Pensions Select Committee. The review concluded that although the original policy intent remains appropriate, feedback from the pensions industry suggests that the practical application of some of the provisions may have contributed to delays in certain circumstances.   In response, the Government has been working with the pensions industry to consider changes that seek to provide a smoother transfer process and proactively respond to any developing risks. DWP is planning to consult on the outcome of this work in the coming months.   Department for Work and Pensions

additional_details: UK heatwaves are getting worse, yet there’s no legal max working temperature. Workers face unsafe heat, risking health and productivity. We need a sensible legal limit and measures like air con or breaks to protect people’s safety as our climate warms.

The law must be enforced equally and visibly, regardless of a person’s background, to protect the public and uphold UK values.

action: Recognise the UK State Pension as an Entitlement, Not a Benefit
background: We ask that the Government change its language to reflect that the State Pension is an entitlement earned through contributions—not a welfare benefit. The UK must follow the example of its European neighbours and treat the State Pension as the earned right it truly is.
additional_details:
Millions of UK citizens have contributed to National Insurance throughout their working lives with the clear understanding that they were paying into a system that would support them in retirement—and deliver a fair, secure income they could rely on.

The State Pension is not a handout. It is a contractual promise, based on years of contributions. Treating it as a “benefit” implies that pensioners are receiving something for nothing, which is insulting and unjust. It undermines their dignity and decades of hard work.

Catering services for the House of Commons are provided by an in-house team who do not provide a subsidised service, though the cost of running the service means that it runs at a loss. action: Reform social housing allocation with national, transparent, AI-assisted system
background: We want Parliament to introduce a national housing allocation system that is unified, transparent, and assisted by AI—replacing model that we think is a postcode lottery, controlled by councils and ensuring fair, consistent access to social housing for all.

action: Criminalise & legally require schools to tackle bullying in & out of school
background: We urge the Government to make repeated bullying over the age of 10 a specific criminal offence, and to make it a legal requirement for schools to act on all forms of bullying, inside and out of school, and mandate mental health reviews after bullying-related self-harm.
additional_details: Too many children are bullied in and out of school. We ask the Government for real consequences, urgent mental health intervention, and legal protection.
government_response_summary: Bullying is never acceptable. Schools have duties to prevent and address it, and we continue to promote best practice whilst also improving early mental health support for young people.
government_response_body: The Government is clear that all forms of bullying are unacceptable and recognises that bullying can have a devastating and long-lasting effect on individuals’ mental health. Tackling and preventing bullying in schools is essential to ensure that all schools are supportive environments within which pupils feel they belong and are able to achieve and thrive. The death of Willow Lee is a stark and tragic reminder of the potential consequences of bullying and of the need for schools to make both preventing and tackling bullying a priority, and to work with specialists to ensure that the right mental health support is provided at the right time.  The legal framework for this already exists and the Government is taking steps to improve both prevention and support. Schools are already legally required to have a behaviour policy. This should set out the policies and processes in place to prevent and deal with violence, bullying or harassment by pupils and be clear about the standards of behaviour expected in school or outside of school and the consequences or sanctions for such behaviour, which include reporting incidents to the police or taking legal action.   The Department for Education (the Department) provides schools with support to tackle bullying with its guidance Preventing and tackling bullying. The guidance is clear that schools should make appropriate provision for a bullied child's social, emotional and mental health needs. The guidance can be found here: Preventing and tackling bullying (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1069688/Preventing_and_tackling_bullying_advice.pdf)  In terms of criminal offences, while bullying in itself is not a specific criminal offence in the UK, a number types of harassing or threatening behaviour – or communications – can be a criminal offence, for example under the Protection from Harassment Act 1997, the Malicious Communications Act 1988, the Communications Act 2003, and the Public Order Act 1986. This means that there is a route to treat many specific instances as a criminal offence and Government guidance is clear that if school staff feel that an offence might have been committed, they should seek assistance from the police.  It is also vitally important that children and young people get early and appropriate support for mental health issues, including those that might be related to bullying. In particular, the Government is committed to supporting children and young people and others who have self-harmed or are at risk of self-harming through the targeted actions in the Suicide Prevention Strategy for England. These actions focus efforts on prevention and the provision of consistent high-quality care and support for self-harm. The Government continues to fund the Multicentre Study of Self-harm, whose work is vital in informing the development of policy, and of clinical practice across sectors.  More widely, the Government is providing access to specialist mental health professionals in every school by expanding Mental Health Support Teams (MHSTs), so every child and young person has access to early support to address problems before they escalate. Almost a million more young people will get access to MHSTs this year. One of the core functions of MHSTs is to give timely advice to school staff and liaise with external specialist services to help children and young people to get the right support. They also provide evidence-based interventions for early mental health issues.  The Department monitors young people’s perceptions of bullying through the annual National Behaviour Survey report, to develop our understanding of bullying prevalence and trends. The latest version (2023/24) is available here: National Behaviour Survey (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68a5ec7b8e2cb87576994d6f/National_behaviour_survey_AY_2023_2024_August_2025.pdf)  The Department is strongly committed to providing continued support for schools to tackle bullying and is procuring an expert- and evidence-led review into best practice on preventing and tackling bullying, as well as promoting good behaviour and reducing preventable exclusions. This will inform the creation of a practical resource for schools, to be tested in a range of schools before being rolled out nationally. This approach has been informed by recent engagement with a range of stakeholders, including teachers, parents, academics, charities and young people, to understand more about the issues around bullying.  The learning from the best practice review will inform the support to be shared across new Regional Improvement for Standards and Excellence (RISE) Attendance and Behaviour Hubs, which are being established across regions in England to focus on supporting senior leaders to develop safe, supportive school cultures.   Department for Education

additional_details:

action: Require fair access to PCN appeals and protect victims of number plate cloning
background: Require councils to offer direct Penalty Charge Notice (PCN) contacts, facilitate fairer appeals, and better protect victims of cloned number plates. We feel councils can issue PCNs with limited options for appeal or discussion.
additional_details: We think victims of number plate cloning are being unfairly fined by local councils through PCNs for offences they did not commit. The current appeal system is often automated, with no direct way to speak to a council officer, and can leave innocent motorists presumed guilty and threatened with bailiffs. We ask the government to make it a legal requirement for councils to provide direct, accessible contact for PCN disputes, and uphold the principle of innocent until proven guilty.

action: Formally recognise the killing of Armenians in 1915-1923 as genocide
background: We are calling for the Government to formally recognise the killing of an estimated 1.5 Million Armenians by the Ottoman Empire from 1915-1923 as genocide. The Government states that "any determination as to whether genocide has occurred is a matter for a competent national or international court".
additional_details: Raphael Lemkin (who coined the term “genocide”) said in 1949: “It happened to the Armenians, and after the Armenians, Hitler took action". We think the only reason we have not seen activity on this from the ICC is because it has no jurisdiction over crimes committed before its establishment, including genocide. Let’s overcome this technicality and join over 30 other countries in standing with our Armenian citizens and the descendants of genocide.

action: Scrap the 2026 £1 Million Cap on Business Relief for Inheritance Tax
background: We ask the Government to scrap the proposed £1 million cap on Business Relief for Inheritance Tax from 2026. We believe this policy may force the sale of family businesses and farms, penalising founders and heirs for owning illiquid, long-term assets tied up in active enterprises.
additional_details: We believe the 2026 changes to Business Relief mean that if a founder dies owning a business or farm, their heirs may face large tax bills with no liquid assets to pay them — which may lead to distressed sales that are below value. We believe it risks the loss of UK-owned businesses and farms, without raising meaningful revenue. The tax is calculated on death, even if the business later sells for less. We urge the Government to reverse this policy.

background: We urge the Government to restrict free access to public services, eg NHS and education, to UK citizens only. We believe illegal migration will always be an issue due to taxpayer-funded public services. By changing this, we believe we will lose appeal to asylum seekers.
additional_details: We believe that all non-UK citizens, including anyone that claims asylum should be charged for the use of the NHS for example. We believe this can provide the NHS and public services with much needed funding, while also being quite simple to manage.

action: Review contrail mitigation strategies in light of jet fuel chemistry changes
background: We ask the UK Government to review current scientific understanding of contrail mitigation, such as small altitude or route changes. Modern jet fuel additives may increase contrail growth, spreading clouds and affecting weather patterns. We urge the Government to update aviation policy accordingly.
additional_details: Recent studies show that modern jet fuel additives lower the humidity threshold for contrail-induced clouds to form, leading to more persistent and widespread contrails. This alters local weather, sunlight, and climate. We urge the Government to review current mitigation strategies and update aviation policies to reflect these changes in fuel chemistry. Implementing these low-cost mitigation measures could significantly reduce contrail-induced cloud cover and its impact on weather and climate.

We believe there are unethical practices which must be exposed, condemned, banned, and never repeated.

Government-commissioned documents like Mindspace reveal how fear, emotional priming, and perception manipulation can be used to steer public behaviour. These tactics can undermine informed choice, public trust, and democratic freedoms. The public must be protected from such unethical manipulation. These coercive psychological practices must be banned by law in all government advice and communications to safeguard individual autonomy, transparency, democratic accountability, and the right to decide with freedom.

For foster children in year 13 born early in the academic year, current regulations mean they face a change of legal status while still in education, and a loss of some allowances for which they may need to claim benefits. We believe the system is flawed, and that these kids are discriminated against on the grounds of age.

action: Introduce Statutory Menstrual Leave for People with Endometriosis & Adenomyosis
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce statutory paid menstrual leave of up to 3 days per month for people with conditions such as endometriosis and adenomyosis, following the model introduced in Portugal in 2025.
additional_details:
We urge the UK Government to implement a statutory menstrual leave policy similar to the one recently passed in Portugal. 

• Provide up to 3 days of paid menstrual leave per month for individuals with a valid medical diagnosis
• Require only a single annual medical certificate confirming the condition
• Ensure full employment protections, including no loss of pay, benefits or seniority
• Guarantee confidentiality and non-discrimination in the workplace
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to introduce menstrual leave for those with endometriosis or adenomyosis. We know the hardship they cause. Our employment rights reforms will help manage health at work.
government_response_body: We recognise the difficulty and pain many women with endometriosis, adenomyosis and other menstrual or reproductive health issues face. We understand that for some women, menstrual or reproductive health issues can have a significant impact on their physical and mental wellbeing, including their participation in education and the workforce.  The Government takes women’s health issues very seriously, and we are committed to tackling them and supporting women to balance work with wider life circumstances.  The Equality Act 2010 defines disability as a physical or mental impairment which has a substantial and long-term adverse effect on a person’s ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities. ‘Long-term’ is described as having lasted or likely to last for at least 12 months, or likely to last for the rest of a person’s life. ‘Substantial’ is defined as more than minor or trivial. Endometriosis and adenomyosis can classify as disabilities under this definition, and individuals with a disability are protected from discrimination and their employer is required to make reasonable adjustments.  Reasonable adjustments can include useful changes such as phased returns to work, part-time working or flexible hours. These adjustments ensure that disabled employees are not placed at a substantial disadvantage compared to their non-disabled colleagues. Therefore, the Government has no plans to introduce statutory menstrual leave for people with endometriosis and adenomyosis.  However, we are taking steps to support the wellbeing and positive work-life balance of all workers, including those suffering from both conditions.  If an individual’s symptoms result in them being unable to work, they may be entitled to receive Statutory Sick Pay. The landmark Employment Rights Bill boosts access to this by making Statutory Sick Pay available to all eligible employees and payable from the first day of sickness absence.  The Bill will also make flexible working the default except where not reasonably feasible. This will help workers with menstrual or reproductive health issues and their employers to agree solutions which work for both parties, ensuring they can access greater flexibility to balance their work and manage their condition.  As part of our plan to Get Britain Working, we have launched an external review to support and enable employers to promote healthy and inclusive workplaces. Sir Charlie Mayfield’s Keep Britain Working Independent Review is examining how best to support more people to stay in or return to work from periods of sickness absence, and recruit and retain more disabled people and people with health conditions. Sir Charlie Mayfield is expected to produce a final report with recommendations for government on how to support this agenda in autumn 2025.  It is unacceptable that women can wait an average of 4 to 10 years for an endometriosis diagnosis, and we have already taken action to address this.  The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) updated their guidelines on endometriosis in November 2024. Two new treatments have been approved, and we are investing £5.6 million into research and taking action to cut gynaecology waiting lists through our Elective Reform Plan.  We know that endometriosis, adenomyosis and other menstrual or reproductive health issues can affect women in different ways. We therefore believe that the best approach is to enable individuals to have an open discussion to determine what solution best supports their needs and the circumstances of the employer.  Department for Business and Trade
