action: Introduce a digital postage stamp to business emails
background: Introduce a micro-tax on business emails. This would apply a small charge per email sent. We believe this could help return to more efficient communication, reduce digital waste, and generate revenue for essential public services like housing, healthcare, and education.
additional_details: We think free, unlimited email causes inefficiency, digital overload, and environmental harm. We think a business email tax would reduce unnecessary messages, improve workplace wellbeing, and cut server energy use and the huge carbon footprint its responsible for. The revenue raised could support new schools, hospitals and homes—funded by waste, not wages, and business efficiency and UK growth will boom. We think our country must lead the way in digital reform to deliver a model for a truly sustainable global future.

action: Mandate businesses to accept card payment with non-compliance a criminal offence
background: Make it mandatory for businesses to offer card payment facilities as well as cash. We think this will improve consumer choice. Especially barber shops and take-aways. We believe that when money is traceable it will cut down on illegal activity.
additional_details: Make having a card machine a mandatory requirement. Not offering a card payment option should be a criminal offence punishable by a prison sentence and huge fine.

action: Restrict Engine Size & Power by Age & create super licence for high-powered cars
background: Legislate to limit car engine size/power for drivers aged 17–24 & 74+. Create a  "super licence" for high-powered cars, with age restrictions and advanced training to drive them. Align car licensing laws with motorcycle restrictions: we think this could reduce accidents & save lives.
additional_details: Young (17–24) and elderly (74+) drivers are more likely to be involved in accidents, yet can drive powerful cars without extra testing. High engine power needs skill & quick reactions, which we think develop with age and training. We want Parliament to restrict engine size/power by age and experience and require a “super licence” for high-powered cars. We think this could reduce accidents, deaths, NHS costs and protect all road users, making roads safer while promoting responsible driving.

action: Keep Sex Offenders on license and the register for life
background: Keep all registered sex offenders on license and on the register for life. We believe it will help protect survivors and potential victims.
additional_details: Some fixed-term offenders may finish their licence 3–5 years after release, depending on sentence length. Those on the register indefinitely can apply for removal 15 years after registering when they are released from prison. Many victims and survivors have spent their lives fighting to feel safe. Why should sex offenders be allowed to come off a register that can help keep children safe from them?

action: Improve accessibility standards in leisure vehicles, caravans and motorhomes
background: Legislate to improve minimum accessibility requirements within the caravan/motorhome industry. For example, a 750mm minimum habitation door width and bracketry to allow installation of a cassette lift/ramp.
additional_details:
I want improved accessibility standards put in place because at the moment I feel disabled people may be discriminated against within the industry. There have been regulations within the housing industry for years with regards to door widths, access routes, activity spaces etc so why not for the leisure industry?
 
There are electronic steps on many new caravans/motorhomes to assist non-disabled people to gain access, so why can't the same courtesy be extended to disabled people too?

action: Add VAT to university tuition fees to ensure consistency in education tax policy
background: Remove VAT exemption from university tuition fees. I believe the current approach is inconsistent and unfair, taxing only certain stages of education.
additional_details: I believe charging VAT on private school fees while exempting universities and nurseries is unjust. I believe this policy doesn't affect the wealthy but instead punishes aspirational families who can work multiple jobs to give their children a better future. Education is education. If it’s fair to tax it, then I believe it must be applied equally.

action: Ban any business from selling energy drinks to children under 16 years old.
background: I would like the Government to put a ban on energy drinks not to be sold to children under 16 years old.
additional_details: Energy drinks pose several health risks due to their high caffeine and sugar content, including cardiovascular issues like increased heart rate and blood pressure, and potential mental health effects like anxiety and insomnia. Furthermore, energy drinks exacerbate ADHD/ASD symptoms in children as, the high sugar content can also contribute to hyperactivity and mood swings, increasing poor behaviour in school or at home.
rejection_details:
As mentioned in the King's speech on 17 July 2024, the Government plans to "legislate to restrict advertising of junk food to children along with the sale of high caffeine energy drinks to children."

You can read the King's speech in full here: https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/the-kings-speech-2024

action: Ban UK insurance companies providing coverage to Russian vessels
background: We urge government to ban UK insurers from underwriting or reinsuring Russian-owned/Russian-flagged ships.
additional_details:
We urge the UK Government to lead by example and ensure that its financial and insurance sectors do not insure Russian vessels. We think strong enforcement and closing of legal loopholes are essential to uphold the rule of law and support our international commitments. 
  
We think failure to do so not only weakens the effectiveness of the sanctions regime but also damages the UK's international credibility and moral standing.

action: Review Maternal Vaccine-Induced IL-6 Responses on Foetal Brain Development
background: We call for an independent assessment of vaccination policies for use during pregnancy, focusing on vaccines that induce increases in IL-6.
additional_details:
With no safe maternal IL-6 threshold established, this assessment should be precautionary and review guidance to minimise vaccine-induced IL-6 elevation during pregnancy.

Vaccinations activate innate immune (DAMP) pathways that produce IL-6, a cytokine shown to influence foetal brain development. Studies in animals and humans demonstrate that elevated maternal IL-6 levels during pregnancy, not infection per se, can be associated with adverse neurodevelopmental changes in offspring. Maternal vaccination policies should fully account for these known biological effects, reflect the latest scientific evidence, and adopt a precautionary approach to protect foetal health.

action: Support newly qualified nurses in gaining band 5 roles
background:
Newly qualified nurses are struggling to find band 5 roles due to the job needing “experienced” applicants only and adverts being for only internal candidates only. 
Review on access to band 5 roles and improvement to support into practice.
additional_details:
Nurses train for 3 years to join into the NHS, but on qualifying some can’t get jobs. We feel there are too many internal job applications and not enough opportunities for new qualified nurses to have a chance. There are so many newly qualified and upcoming newly qualified nurses ready to care for patients but are being knocked down. 
This system is failing the NHS, patients and students
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Support newly qualified nurses: Review barriers to NHS jobs 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725928

action: Ban children under 16 years of age from using smartphones.
background: Ban children under 16 years of age from using smartphones
additional_details: It is very difficult for a parent to ban their child from using a smartphone when there is so much social pressure from the child's peers to be doing so. No one wants their child excluded socially because they don't  have a smart phone. However the risks to all children using social media are real and need to be addressed at a national level. This is why we need help from the government to ban smartphones below the age of 16 to help parents protect their children.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/714201

action: Create law that media outlets must refer to 'migrants' as 'migrating people'
background: Create legislation for all UK based media outlets where they must refer to 'migrating people' instead of 'migrants' in any published materials, to comply with the Human Rights Act 1998. Using the term 'migrants' dehumanises migrating people, and could lead to discrimination and a risk to safety.
additional_details: The Human Rights Act 1998 includes the right to life, freedom from torture and inhuman treatment, the right to a fair trial, and freedom of expression. It also protects against discrimination in the enjoyment of these rights for all. Mainstream media outlets consistently refer to migrating people as 'migrants'. This contravenes the Human Rights Act as it dehumanises people and can lead to unfair discrimination by those who consume the media. Creating this law will build a fairer, safer UK.
rejection_details: This issue is a matter for Ofcom, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Consumer compensation for fake delivery attempts or delays
background: Parcel companies often claim a package has had delivery attempted when it hasn't. This robs the public and businesses of time and vital goods on a regular basis. The public and businesses should be entitled to compensation.
additional_details: Either fine parcel couriers for delays and fake missed deliveries (they have GPS in their vans to prove it), or allow consumers to receive compensation.
rejection_details:
The following petition covers a very similar issue: 

Stricter laws for delivery companies: provide location info & access to parcels 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707922

action: Instruct the Bank of England to keep Sir Winston Churchill on the £5 note.
background: The Government should use its authority to instruct the Bank of England to retain the image of Sir Winston Churchill on the five pound note. If the Government does not have that authority, it should put a motion before the House of Commons urging the BoE to retain Churchill.
additional_details: Sir Winston Churchill’s leadership was key to the survival of the United Kingdom during the Second World War, and ultimately the defeat of Nazism. His image is emblematic of the national struggle for survival and the courage and sacrifices of that generation, to whom we all owe our freedom.  His place on the ‘fiver’ is a daily reminder to ordinary people of that pivotal moment in our history. The BoE proposes redesigns of our bank notes. Please let’s not lose Churchill in the process.
rejection_details:
The Bank of England is independent of the Government and Parliament.

You can find out more here:
https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/banknotes/banknote-characters

action: Permit anonymity in petitions where the petitioner faces credible personal risk
background: Introduce a process that allows individuals to submit petitions anonymously where there is credible personal risk. Cases should be reviewed individually, with oversight from an independent authority to ensure safety and data protection.
additional_details: The current system requires all petitioners’ names to be public. We think this excludes people at risk of harm for expressing their views, including whistleblowers and dissidents. Requests for anonymity should be assessed case by case. We think an oversight body such as an Ombudsman could ensure secure data handling and prevent leaks that could expose a petitioner’s identity. Participation in democracy must never come at the cost of personal safety.

action: Relocate and modernise UK pet entry checks to support in-cabin dog arrivals
background: Dogs aren’t allowed to arrive in the UK in-cabin, even though many airlines support it. Why? Inbound UK pet checks happen away from passenger terminals, forcing pets to travel as cargo. Yet pets can fly out in-cabin as checks happen inside passenger terminals. So pets can fly out, but not back in.
additional_details: We call on the UK government to relocate pet entry checks to the passenger terminals, so airlines can offer in-cabin pet travel into the UK, just as they do in many other parts of the world. Now is the perfect time for this petition, as it aligns with the UK’s reintroduction of the EU pet passport and supports government goals for tourism, animal welfare, and inclusive travel. This update would ease stress for pets, simplify travel for owners, and safeguard the UK’s high biosecurity standards.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727223

action: Call for children's trans books to be put back in Kent libraries child sections
background: Protect these books under the Equality Act and protecting literature for education. Reach out to KCC about this harmful issue. Keep these age-appropriate trans books in children's sections.
additional_details: The action is a reactionary attack on children's age-appropriate education of trans children, a library is for all members of the public to read all appropriate books and taking trans books away from children is taking education, causing harm and only affects those children whose parents would have let their children read them. Taking away trans resources only causes more hatred and violence to the transgender community and educating children through all life supports equality and understanding.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Reform Tax Rules for Everyone Earning £30,000 and Above
background: We call on the UK Government to urgently reform the tax and student loan system for everyone earning £30,000 and above. Fairer tax rates and lower student loan repayments are needed so hardworking graduates and workers can keep more of their income, pay off debt, & improve their financial security.
additional_details: Many students are encouraged to get degrees required for careers like healthcare, law, engineering, teaching, and mental health professions. These degrees come with significant debt and high costs. At £30,000 and above, nearly 20% of income is deducted through income tax, National Insurance, and student loan repayments. This system punishes ambition and makes it harder for people to pay off debt, save money, and build a stable future.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly how you'd like the Government or Parliament to reform the current tax and student loan systems.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly how you would like the Government or Parliament to change the current tax and student loan systems, as well as the specific changes you would like for them to make.

action: Fund work on pavements to make them more disabled friendly
background: I want the government to provide funding to have pavements resurfaced so they are more disability friendly. I think the state of pavements amounts to disability discrimination.
additional_details: I’ve just started using a mobility scooter and the pavements can be awful. Some aren’t straight and 1 curb in my area is so uneven it goes into a point. I think many are unsafe for any wheelchair or mobility scooter users and I think we need to have drop curbs on every junction.

action: All biological and intended parents to be named on birth registration & reform
background: I urge the Government to reform birth registration laws to protect every child’s right to know their biological and legal parents. Require both biological parents to be named, recognise intended parents in surrogacy, enable MORE record amendments.
additional_details: We think knowing biological parents is vital for medical history and self-identity. I grew up with absent parents but needed to know my origins. Current birth laws may exclude fathers if they refuse involvement or in surrogacy. Intended parents, especially same-sex couples, may face legal uncertainty without such birth recognition.

action: Revise Parental Leave Policies Now
background: Parental leave is vital for the well-being of newborn babies and for the mental and physical health of both parents. But the inability to financially support an extended leave period forces many parents, like us, to return to work prematurely.
additional_details:
We call on policymakers to revise parental leave legislation immediately! Extend paid maternity leave and offer equitable paternity leave to ensure all families can thrive. Prioritize legislative efforts that promote equal opportunities and healthy family dynamics, encouraging an inclusive policy that reflects the fundamental needs of a modern society.

Join us in advocating for a future where no family has to choose between economic security and spending vital early moments with their newborns.
rejection_details:
The following petitions call for similar actions: 

Improve statutory paternity leave in the UK to better support families
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/708707

Raise statutory maternity/paternity pay to match the National Living 
Wage 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/715292

action: Make MPs live on a middle-class income while serving in office.
background: We want legislation requiring MPs to live solely on a standard middle-class income during their time in office. No access to personal savings or luxury perks. This would create fairer, more empathetic, and accountable governance.
additional_details: We propose that MPs receive only a median UK income while in office, with no access to personal savings or luxury assets. Second homes, excessive expenses, and luxury travel would be restricted. A post-term bonus or pension would be awarded based on service quality, assessed independently. This reform would promote fairness, empathy, and rebuild public trust by ensuring MPs live under the same conditions as those they represent.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA) is responsible for deciding on MPs' expenses and pay. IPSA is independent of both Parliament and Government. 
 
You can find out more about IPSA here: http://www.theipsa.org.uk

action: Introduce a 30% tax on all non-stun slaughter produce
background: From field to fork, we believe the treatment of animals should be carried out in the most humane way possible.
additional_details: We think non-stun slaughter does not meet any welfare standards and the culling of animals in this way is far from humane. By introducing taxes on non-stun slaughter products, the revenue from this could be used for research into other animal welfare projects. We feel some eateries give you very little choice but to consume non-stun slaughter meat without advertising so. If the government can put a duty of tax on tobacco products, we think they can surely do the same in regards to non-stun slaughter produce.

action: Install Air Conditioning on London Underground Tube Trains
background: Install air conditioning on all Tube trains. Overheating puts pregnant people, asthma sufferers and the elderly at serious risk. Other cities like New York and Tokyo managed it — London must too. It’s a matter of health, safety and equality.
additional_details: The government must ensure air conditioning on all Tube trains because overheating is a public health issue. Pregnant people, those with asthma, and the elderly face real danger in extreme heat. Other global cities have solved this. Londoners deserve safe, accessible transport too.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The London Underground and Transport for London is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly. 

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Support newly qualified physiotherapists: Review barriers to NHS jobs
background: We think newly qualified physiotherapists are struggling to get NHS jobs due to experience requirements and internal-only adverts. Some apply for assistant roles or private jobs but may be rejected for being overqualified or lacking NHS experience. We want a review and better support into practice.
additional_details: We think physiotherapy graduates deserve fair access to employment and experience. Some applying for assistant roles to get experience may be rejected for being overqualified. Even private jobs may ask for NHS experience. We think this leaves graduates stuck and unable to start their careers. We’re calling for a review of Band 5 recruitment and better support to help newly qualified physiotherapists enter the workforce. We believe roles should be made more accessible to external applicants without NHS experience.

action: Change the First Past The Post voting system to a Ranked Choice system
background: The First Past The Post voting system should be scrapped, and constituencies should instead use a Ranked Choice Voting system in local and general elections
additional_details: First Past The Post is hugely unrepresentative, and other democracies worldwide make the UK look very undemocratic. A Ranked Choice Voting system would allow true representation of the people, and allow MPs to see what their constituents really want.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Replace First-Past-The-Post with Single Transferrable Vote & Alternative Vote 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727860

action: Suspend footballers under police investigation for serious criminal offences
background: Work with the FA and Premier League to require that players under police investigation for serious offences like rape or assault are suspended temporarily, and to create a national safeguarding code of conduct for all professional football clubs.
additional_details: Footballers under investigation for serious crimes can still play, earn full pay, and appear for their clubs — with no transparency or interim action. This would be unacceptable in education, healthcare, or law enforcement. Football must follow similar safeguarding standards. This is not about presuming guilt, but about protecting women, maintaining public trust, and ensuring football reflects the values we expect in every other part of public life.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
Decisions about suspending football players are a matter for individual clubs and the FA, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Cap the amount of times a person can be re-elected for London Mayor.
background: I would like the Government/Parliament to debate on whether a cap should be applied on the amount of times a person can be re-elected for London Mayor.
additional_details: I believe the current London Mayor has failed every person throughout London, Knife crime is up, Motorcycle theft is up, Mobile phone theft is up, the list of failings is endless. I believe that the people of London deserve better and deserve change.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Limit the number of terms an elected mayor can serve 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709729

action: Control domestic cat roaming to protect British wildlife
background: This petition asks the UK government to introduce limitations on the free, outdoor roaming of domestic cats. It requests that domestic cats are put on a lead when outdoors, and are not allowed to roam unsupervised. This is to stop cats from hunting wild animals whose populations are in decline.
additional_details: Regular surveys of British wildlife have shown a significant decline in small mammal, songbird and amphibian populations, including water voles, starlings and frogs. Domestic cats contribute to this decline by preying on these animals, and reducing prey for wild predators such as owls. They also endanger our native wildcats in Scotland by interbreeding with this species. Similar policies for restricting the free roaming of domestic cats have been successfully introduced in Finland.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Remove the ‘right to roam’ status applicable to domesticated cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725658

action: Mandate Ethical Rehoming for Lab and Breeding Animals by 2025
background: Mandate rehoming of lab & breeding unit animals as default by end of 2025. We want partnering with accredited rehoming orgs & a rehoming database, funded by licence fees & grants. We want to end unnecessary euthanasia & independent outcome monitoring for an ethical future.
additional_details: Demand the Government mandates rehoming as default for lab & breeding unit animals by 2025. Partner with UK rehoming orgs, and create a transparent rehoming database. Fund via licence fees/grants to boost rehoming rates. We want amendments to ASPA to end unnecessary euthanasia. We call for independent monitoring and reporting of rehoming outcomes to ensure success. We think this could establish the UK as a global leader in ethical lab animal rehoming and address public demand for compassionate welfare standards.

action: Investigate & reform Companies House procedures to help prevent potential fraud
background: Investigate and reform Companies House procedures to help prevent attempts to fraudulently register companies.
additional_details: We believe that Companies House's procedures are inadequate, and are putting the UK to shame for its efforts to address international anti-money laundering, identity theft and Financial Crime.

action: Pedestrian crossing outside of Perry Hall School, Colman Avenue, Wednesfield
background:
During drop off and pick up times there is a high volume of traffic.
There are people that drive at a dangerous speed up and down the road putting children and people in danger.
A pedestrian crossing should be an essential road safety measure outside any school.
additional_details: This should be essential outside any school. The safety of pupils should be at the forefront of the government’s mind.

background:
Allow land owners who own at least 1acre permitted development rights, to erect off grid housing on land which they own allowing change of use for area where living structure is.
As long as it doesn't ruin the surroundings, is kept clean and follows set rules during the development and onward.
additional_details: Housing is becoming unaffordable, councils not maintaining areas allowing them to fall into disrepair. If you own land you should be able to reside there whether it be off-grid or connected to the supplies. action: Give all British Citizens Overseas Access to Home Fees at English Universities
background: The Government should allow British citizens living abroad to qualify for home fee status at English universities, even if they have not spent the 3 years before the start of term living in the UK, or another eligible country.
additional_details: I think the current system penalises British citizens living abroad by charging international fees instead of home fees, even when many continue to contribute financially from overseas and maintain close ties to the UK. I think British citizens must be eligible for home fees, regardless of residence.

action: Fund councils to subsidise more mobility items for disabled and older people
background: We want the Government to make mobility scooters and powered wheelchairs more affordable for disabled and elderly people by providing funding for more subsidies. Everyone deserves the freedom to move and live independently.
additional_details: We think too many people are stuck at home, unable to get to the shops, doctors, or see loved ones because they can’t afford a mobility scooter. It’s heart-breaking and unfair. With better access, people could stay independent, connected, and live with dignity — not isolation.

action: Permit children with a EHCP up to 5 days of authorised absence from school
background: I believe children with an EHCP should be granted a 5-day allowance for holidays during quieter times, helping them avoid overwhelming and crowded environments.
additional_details: I kindly request that you consider allowing up to 5 days of authorised absence for children with an EHCP. This would greatly benefit those who find busy, crowded environments overwhelming. Every child deserves the opportunity to enjoy a break without the added stress of sensory overload or difficulty with self-regulation.

Fund more support for children with SEN & allow term-time holidays

Allow families with SEN children 10 days term-time holiday without being fined

action: Legal labelling of stunned and non-stunned meat throughout the food chain
background:
It is imperative that labeling of non-stunned and stunned meat be clearly and mandatory labelling throughout the food chain.  This includes, shops, supermarkets, suppliers, fast food and restaurants

This will include halal and Kosher labels clearly marked on every product available to consumers
additional_details:
The UK government should implement mandatory "method of slaughter" labeling for all meat products: "Stunned" or "Non-Stunned." 

This promotes consumer choice, especially for religious and ethical reasons, and enhances transparency. 

It requires broad consultation with stakeholders, practical industry support, and public education campaigns to succeed. Regular review is crucial.

No one should be forced to consume food which doesn't match their ethical choices and has the right to choose.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/704797

action: Reform property laws in England & Wales to match the Scottish home buying system
background: The home buying process in England & Wales is slow, uncertain and costly. Around one in three sales fail due to legal loopholes like gazumping & late stage withdrawals. Scotland’s system makes offers legally binding earlier, reducing fall-throughs and creating a more secure, fair process for all.
additional_details:
We ask the UK Government to reform property law in England & Wales to align with the Scottish model. This should include:
Making accepted offers legally binding earlier.
Introducing mandatory property information packs (e.g. Home Reports)
Preventing practices like gazumping and gazundering.
Setting time limits to complete transactions.
These changes would protect buyers and sellers, reduce wasted costs, and improve the housing market.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Introduce conveyancing laws similar to those in Scotland, across England & Wales

action: Implement a dynamic Land Value Tax
background: I think the government should implement a land value tax. It should account for the value of the land at the start of the tax year. This should apply to most land with some exceptions. rates should vary based on the way the land is used eg farmer owned farmland could be free but not rented farmland
additional_details: There's ideas of a wealth tax in the media but I think this has issues mostly wealthy people fleeing. I think a land value tax is easier and you cant move land and buildings the way you can with money and stocks. I think appropriate tax breaks are also more viable like self owned farmland, homes or economically helpful land use whilst also increasing rates on the opposite like development land not being developed, large warehouses pushing out small businesses or landlords hoarding homes at the expense of young people

action: Give people power to dismiss MPs – change the Recall of MPs Act
background: We think Parliament needs to change the Recall of MPs Act 2015 so that voters can start a recall petition at any time initiating a by-election, without needing certain circumstances to be met.
additional_details:
Right now, voters have no way before an election to remove an MP who stops listening, breaks promises, or ignores their local area.
We think this would give the public the right to remove their MP if they believe they are no longer doing the job properly.
Right now, voters have no way before an election to remove an MP who stops listening, breaks promises, or ignores their local area.
We think this change would give people the right to hold their MP to account between elections.
If 10% of voters in the MP’s constituency signed a petition, a by-election would be held.
We think this would make politics more democratic, fairer, more accountable, and give real power back to the public.

action: Limit the sale of fireworks to those running local council approved events only
background:
Ban the sale of fireworks to the general public to minimise the harm caused to vulnerable people and animals. Defenceless animals can die from the distress caused by fireworks.

I believe that permitting unregulated use of fireworks is an act of wide-scale cruelty to animals.
government_response_summary: The Government recognises the negative impact fireworks can have on some people and animals.  However, when used responsibly they are a source of enjoyment for many people.
government_response_body: The Government’s intention is to minimise the negative impact of fireworks and to support their considerate use, while reducing the risks and disturbances to individuals, animals, and property. The majority of individuals who use fireworks do so in a responsible and safe manner and there are enforcement mechanisms in place to tackle situations when fireworks are misused.  At this point in time the Government does not have any plans to ban the sale of fireworks to consumers. We have launched a fireworks campaign for this fireworks season to provide guidance on minimising the impacts of fireworks on animal welfare and encouraging responsible use. Lower noise fireworks are promoted in the campaign alongside encouraging people to consider going to a public display. Public displays are more likely to be well-publicised, providing people with an opportunity to prepare ahead of the display taking place. The campaign also includes new guidance for those running community fireworks events, and social media posts that emphasise the risks from the misuse of fireworks. This supplements existing guidance from Government and other organisations that is available to help people to use fireworks safely and appropriately. My safety: fireworks - GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/my-safety-fireworks) Organising non-professional fireworks displays - GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/organising-non-professional-fireworks-displays)  A regulatory framework currently controls the sale, availability, and use of fireworks to consumers. For example, there is an 11pm curfew in place for the use of fireworks, with later exceptions only for the traditional firework periods of November 5th, Diwali, New Year’s Eve and the Chinese New Year. Using fireworks outside the curfew hours is a criminal offence enforced by the police and can lead to imprisonment and a substantial fine.  There is also a maximum noise level of 120 decibels with many retailers also offering ‘lower noise’ and ‘no bang’ fireworks.  A number of animal welfare organisations, along with industry and local authorities, provide advice and guidance to enable people to minimise the negative impacts of fireworks on people, animals and our communities. We work closely with these organisations to amplify this messaging in the run up to, and during, key dates when fireworks are commonly used.    To inform any future action the Government will continue to engage with businesses, consumer groups and charities to gather evidence on the issues with and impacts of fireworks.    Department for Business and Trade

action: Review how mobility side of PIP is assessed for those that can drive
background: I would like government to review how the mobility side of PIP is assessed for those that can drive. Some disabled people who drive are being refused this lifeline due to being able to "plan and carry out a journey" etc. I think this is extremely unfair and needs to be changed.
additional_details: I am disabled. I am partially paralyzed on my left side and have just been denied the mobility side of PIP because I can drive my car which is automatic. I do not use my left side to drive and so don't need to grip anything with my left hand. I have read about lots of other people being refused the mobility side because they can drive and plan journeys etc. I feel we are being denied our independence for which PIP was intended.

action: Restrict non-emergency use of car horns in residential areas
background: We ask the Government to introduce clearer guidance and potential penalties for unnecessary car horn use in residential areas. Horns should only be used to alert to immediate danger, yet they are often used out of frustration, disturbing communities and contributing to noise pollution.
additional_details: The frequent misuse of car horns, especially during early mornings or late at night, negatively affects families, children, shift workers and vulnerable individuals. We believe public awareness campaigns, signage, and potential enforcement would protect community wellbeing and restore quiet to our streets.
rejection_details:
The The Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986 already restricts the use of car horns in the way described by this petition: 

https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1986/1078/regulation/99/made?view=plain

action: Spouses be entitled to partner state pension.
background: That spouses should be entitled to part if not all of their partners state pension if they die before pension age.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733964

action: Fund increased wage for Teaching Assistants
background: We feel that the role of a Teaching Assistant has changed dramatically over the years and the current salary does not reflect the hours and hard work they do. We think this need to be addressed and increased.
additional_details: As Teaching Assistants, we are not only teachers. We feel we often act as carers, support workers, counsellors and the only trusted adult in a lot of cases. We work tirelessly to provide love and care for every child and we think the salary associated with the role is totally out of date.

action: Make prisoners with life sentences never eligible for release
background: A life sentence is called a life sentence for a reason, yet some people may serve only 25 years. Make it law that if issued a life sentence, the convicted is not allowed release unless they are found not guilty until they die. Scrap parole for any life sentences.
additional_details: We think that if a rapist is let out after 25 years, nothing is stopping them repeating their offence. We think that rehabilitation may be a waste of public money and it could be easy for a criminal to pretend to learn that murder is wrong then repeat. We think life means life, so follow through.

background: Clear overgrown vegetation and trees on the banks of River Penk in Perton South Staffordshire that's causing stagnant water in the lakes and a reduced flow further down stream .

background: Before any UK government can donate more than £10 million to any foreign country there should be a UK national referendum held and the result should be legally binding.

action: Certify & Remove VAT on bee-friendly plants to support pollinator conservation
background: We call on the UK Government to certify and remove VAT from bee-friendly plants and seeds.
additional_details:
Pollinators are in crisis — with some studies warning of up to 50% species loss by 2050. In the UK, pollinator populations continue to decline due to pesticide use, habitat loss, and climate change.
 
We think many citizens want to help, but barriers remain. We believe that removing VAT from nectar- and pollen-rich plants would:
• Encourage people to grow pollinator-friendly gardens
• Support the UK’s Healthy Bees Plan 2030
• Align taxation with sustainability goals
• Empower households and communities to act

We think this small fiscal adjustment could lead to meaningful change for biodiversity, public engagement, and food security.
Please support a 0% VAT rate for bee-friendly plants.

action: Government to support the Elections (Proportional Representation) Bill
background: We call on the UK Government to support the progression of the Elections (Proportional Representation) Bill, ensuring time for a Second Reading in the Commons. Even if a vote were to fail, this is an important issue and deserves open debate and a free vote in both Houses.
additional_details: We believe the current electoral system (FPTP) often results in disproportionate outcomes and under-representation of many voters. We feel the Elections (Proportional Representation) Bill, which was introduced as a Private Members' bill, presents an opportunity to modernise our democracy by ensuring every vote counts more equally, and deserves fair consideration and debate.

action: Levy Water Companies to Fund Year-Round Water Testing to Safeguard Public Health
background:
Year-round, real-time water quality testing for all UK rivers, lakes, and seas.
Levy Polluting water companies to fund improved testing infrastructure, monitoring, and public alerts (“polluter pays” principle).
Enhance public health protections.
additional_details: There are growing numbers of reported illnesses linked to polluted water, including life-threatening infections. Real-time testing exists. We call on water companies to be levied to fund the Environment Agency to roll it out nationwide, all year round. We think winter testing is essential, as some of the largest sewage discharges occur out of season, when there’s likely to be less public awareness or monitoring. Set clear safety standards. Track and report illness. Provide care for those affected. Protect people, not profits. We think clean water isn’t a luxury, it’s a basic human right and a legacy we owe future generations.

action: Deport all asylum seekers that have broken the law

additional_details: We think the solution is simple and they should be deported.

action: Review how controlled substances are classified
background: The Government should review how controlled substances are classified under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 based on current scientific evidence of their actual harm and addictiveness. We think criminalisation of substances creates a monopolised illegal drug market that funds further criminal activity.
additional_details:
We think organised crime thrives on the illegal drug trade, using profits to fund violence and exploitation. We think many less harmful substances remain banned, giving criminals a monopoly over supply and promoting the development of  harmful substances like synthetic marijuana.
 
We think reclassifying drugs based on scientific evidence of actual harm would reduce criminal profits, support health-led interventions, and free up police resources.  We think adopting a harm-based approach to drug policy would reduce crime and protect the public.

action: Introduce tighter regulation of online crowdfunding sites
background: Crowdfunding sites can be useful to bring young projects to fruition, however we believe current regulations for consumer protection on crowdfunding sites are insufficient.
additional_details: We want the UK government to provide better consumer protection for citizens using these kinds of sites, which may be based in the USA, to help protect them from potential scams. UK credit card companies can help to a degree, but in some instances they might not be able to.

action: Require schools to allow students to wear skirts

additional_details:
We think uniforms shouldn’t be used to enforce conformity and banning skirts could limit self-expression and set a precedent for further restrictions. 
 
We think preventing students wearing skirts could:
Over-centralise control: Imposes blanket policies that ignore local community values.
Stifle debate: Eliminates parents’ and students’ voices in uniform decisions.
Erase individuality: Denies young people the choice to express themselves.
Distract from core education: Focuses energy on appearance over learning.
Mislabel conformity as equality:  True inclusion offers options, not bans.

action: Ban plastic hangers: help Save Earth, protect wildlife
background: We urge the government to ban plastic coat hangers. These single-use pollutants can harm the environment, fill landfills, and endanger wildlife. Promote sustainable alternatives like wood/metal.
additional_details:
We think this would be a vital step for a greener future, protecting our planet from persistent plastic waste for a healthier Earth.

Millions of hangers annually become non-recyclable waste and they can end up in landfills and polluting oceans for centuries, releasing toxins. They can also directly harm wildlife through entanglement and ingestion. Current recycling systems largely reject them, making disposal problematic. We believe that transitioning to sustainable alternatives like wood, metal, or recycled plastic, alongside robust reuse schemes, is crucial. We think a ban would demonstrate vital leadership in combating plastic pollution, protecting ecosystems, and fostering a circular economy, safeguarding our planet for future generations.

action: Review protections for important trees: amend Forestry Act & list heritage trees
background: Review and strengthen protections. Amend the Forestry Act 1967 to explicitly define and set a higher evidence bar for exempting any ancient tree felling from licences. Publish and maintain a list of heritage trees with protected status as proposed in the Heritage Trees Private Members Bill 2023-24.
additional_details:
We'd also like the Government to formally commit to implementing the recommendations of a DEFRA-commissioned report from the Tree Council (April 2025), which amongst other recommendations called for engaging key stakeholders within 12 months of publication, and the development of an ‘action plan’ for important trees. 
 
Ancient trees are irreplaceable habitats, and we believe they need better protection. The Forestry Act currently allows some to be felled without felling licences; we think there must be a more rigorous licensing requirement.
government_response_summary: Ancient and veteran trees and ancient woodlands are irreplaceable habitats in national planning policies. Tree Preservation Orders also prevent some trees from being felled or significantly modified.
government_response_body: As announced in the Spending Review, Defra is making the largest investment in nature in history, with over £7 billion directed into nature’s recovery, including our ancient woodlands and ancient and veteran trees. Ancient and veteran trees are listed as one of the eight ‘irreplaceable habitats’ by The Biodiversity Gain Requirements (Irreplaceable Habitat) Regulations 2024. The National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) recognises ancient and veteran trees and ancient woodland as irreplaceable habitats. We will continue to improve their protections.  Since January 2024, councils must consult the MHCLG Secretary of State if they are considering developments that might impact ancient woodland.  Local Authorities have the power to place Tree Preservation Orders, which prevent trees from being felled or significantly modified. The Ancient Woodland Inventory is being updated and is mapping smaller ancient woodland sites of 0.25 hectares. These updates, to be published by the end of Summer 2027, will increase the level of ancient woodlands identified, allowing them to benefit from their protected status as irreplaceable habitats.    We have reviewed the implementation and effectiveness of the NPPF for safeguarding ancient and veteran trees and ancient woodland. Whilst these habitats are strongly protected, the review identified implementation challenges. We are committed to finding ways to ensure that our ancient woodlands are protected in practice as well as policy.   Felling trees is a crucial part of woodland management. However, this doesn’t apply to ancient trees except in cases of overriding public interest, such as danger to life that can’t be mitigated. Done well, felling of non-ancient trees can let more light onto the woodland floor, encouraging ground flora and associated insect and bird communities to flourish. It can also support increased diversity within woodland canopies, supporting wildlife.  Felling licences under the Forestry Act 1967 are generally conditional on the owner maintaining woodland cover on site in the long term.  The Forestry Commission can refuse an application to fell growing trees for several reasons, including where they believe that the application fails to meet the interests of good forestry practice. This power may be used to protect ancient trees in woodlands from felling. As the criminal case for the Sycamore Gap tree has shown, our judicial system takes illegal tree felling seriously: those that cause illegal damage to trees, woodlands and the environment will be brought to justice.  The Defra-funded report led by the Tree Council and Forest Research provides a range of recommendations for improving the protection and stewardship of ‘important’ trees. The Government is carefully considering its recommendations, including their feasibility and potential impacts, balancing our approach with our existing priorities and statutory obligations. We will set out actions to protect important trees in the new Trees Action Plan, to be published in 2026.   Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

background:

action: Protect UK workers from US-driven cuts to workplace inclusion
background: We urge the Government to issue formal guidance protecting UK-based employees from the rollback of workplace inclusion initiatives by multinational companies responding to executive orders and political pressure from the United States. UK equality laws must remain fully upheld.
additional_details: Employees at US-owned companies in the UK are seeing inclusion programmes defunded, restricted, or removed due to presidential executive orders and political pressure from the United States. Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

If you would like to introduce mandatory D&I requirements then you could start a new petition setting out what you would like those requirements to be.

action: Make Premier League and Sports Broadcasting More Affordable for UK Residents
background: Make sports packages, especially Premier League coverage, more affordable for UK viewers. Prices are too high and many games aren’t shown. The British public should have better access to a sport that originated here and is loved across the nation.
additional_details: UK fans pay around £73/month for Sky, TNT Sports, and Amazon to watch Premier League games yet not all matches are shown due to the 3pm blackout. In Canada, fans get full access via FuboTV for just £14/month. The Premier League is a British institution, but home fans are priced out. Other countries enjoy more affordable and complete coverage. We urge the Government to investigate pricing, address exclusivity deals, so that football can be watched by more people in the UK, fairly and affordably.
rejection_details:
Decisions about the affordability of broadcasting packages are a matter for Ofcom.

You could start a new petition to make all football league matches a category A event so they are free-to-air.

action: Create a salary-bridging loan scheme for parents on parental leave
background: Allow working parents to borrow the difference between statutory leave pay and their normal salary as a 0% interest loan, repaid via salary sacrifice after returning to work. We think this would ease financial stress and maintain tax/NIC contributions.
additional_details: Introduce a government-backed, interest-free loan scheme to top up statutory maternity/paternity pay to a parent’s full salary during leave. This optional scheme would be repaid via salary sacrifice once the parent returns to work. We think it would ensure parents have financial security, help retain parents in the workforce, and promote shared parenting.

action: Provide support for aspiring drinking establishments entrepreneurs
background: We request that aspiring entrepreneurs wanting to get involved in the drinking industry have access to professional support, intended on revitalising and providing more avenues to the  industry.
additional_details: There has been an ongoing struggle over the last two decades regarding the inability of private businesses to thrive in the British economy. A substantial portion of British drinking establishments has either declared bankruptcy or silently stopped operations. We believe that there has been more boundaries than support, causing widespread vexation. Companies like BBPA has echoed this sentiment.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what kind of support you would like the Government or Parliament to provide to aspiring entrepreneurs in the drinks industry.

Additionally, your petition is about a devolved matter and would only apply to England.

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

action: Introduce Civic lessons in schools to help foreigners to adapt to our society
background: I think it’ll be a good idea to introduce Civic lessons in schools curriculum as this would help younger generations to learn how they should act as a member of our society. Also it’ll be a great opportunity for the foreign students to learn our society’s values in order to act in respect of them.
additional_details: I think the society will benefit from this initiative in the years to come. I also think that while multiculturalism have its own benefits, British culture with its moral and civic values must be understood and respected by anyone who lives in the UK
rejection_details:
Citizenship education is already a mandatory subject for pupils aged 11-16 in maintained schools in England.

You can read more about this here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study

action: Require all food products to show potassium levels on their packaging
background: Nearly 20% of the UK population aged over 60 are believed to have Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) and reducing potassium levels in one’s diet can be key to ensure your kidneys function. For some, working out potassium levels may require searching long amounts of time for individual ingredients online.
additional_details: I was diagnosed with CKD last year and I'm still struggling with what I can eat or what is best to avoid. I find that information online can be conflicting. I believe I could still enjoy some foods that I have been told to avoid if I could add up the amount of potassium in my diet each day.

action: Require delivery sites for HGV car transporters to provide parking/loading areas
background: We want the Government to require all commercial delivery and collection sites used by HGV car transporters to provide safe, designated parking and loading/unloading areas for drivers. We think this would improve road safety, reduce risk to workers, and prevent dangerous or obstructive stopping.
additional_details: We think many HGV and car transporter drivers face unsafe conditions because delivery sites often lack designated parking or loading areas. We think this may force drivers to stop in hazardous or obstructive locations, risking accidents, fines, and delays. We think the absence of proper facilities creates safety risks for drivers, other road users, and pedestrians. We think requiring safe, designated areas would protect workers, improve road safety, and support efficient deliveries.

action: Save EHCPs (educational health care plans) Protect Children and teachers.
background:
More funding for schools and local authorities to deliver EHCPs on time.
Significantly increased training places for Educational Psychologists so children aren’t left waiting years for an assessment.
Stronger accountability, Protection for the legal right to an EHCP.
additional_details:
EHCPs are not just paperwork they are a lifeline For over 560,000 children. Evidence shows that EHCPs work when they are delivered properly and work for everyone in the classroom. 
Without EHCPs, there would be no legal guarantee that specialist support will be provided. It’s not EHCPs that are the problem - it’s the system.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Retain legal right to assessment and support in education for children with SEND 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711021

action: Introduce higher tax on plastic gardening pots
background: We want the government to tax plastic gardening pots more highly. It is estimated that around 500 million plastic plant pots are produced every year and many end up in landfill. We think this is unsustainable and it's time we used natural alternatives to polluting plastics.
additional_details:
Plastic bag use at main retailers has dropped by 98% since the plastic bag charge was introduced in 2014. Government figures show the average person now buys around 2 single-use bags a year from these businesses - down drastically from 140 per year in 2014. Meanwhile, many plastic pots go to landfill each year. They can take hundreds of years to decompose.
 
We want the government to implement a new plastic plant pot tax.

action: Prohibit MPs From Using Phones During Parliamentary Hearings
background: MPs should not use personal phones during parliamentary hearings. It’s unprofessional and distracting. A ban should be in place, with an emergency contact system for families to reach MPs if needed. This ensures focus, respect, and proper conduct in Parliament.
additional_details: MPs should be fully focused during parliamentary hearings, not distracted by mobile phones. Their role is to represent the public and make crucial decisions. I urge Parliament to ban personal phone use during sessions, except when essential. In emergencies, MPs' families should contact a monitored line. This would uphold professionalism, mirror standards in other workplaces, and help restore public trust in the democratic process.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Ban the Use of Mobile Phones by Members of Parliament in the House of Commons https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730728

action: Make Political Education a compulsory part of the National Curriculum
background: In order to prepare young people for the lowering of the voting age, we deem it necessary to provide compulsory classes on politics to help people make informed choices on election days, increase voter participation, and help young people understand how political systems work and affect them.
additional_details: Although the notion to lower the voting age to 16 is great, it would be irresponsible to give younger people the right to vote without providing them with sufficient education and information on politics in order to help them make an informed decision on election day. Furthermore, there has been an increase in political disillusionment as well as more populist ideas amongst the youth, and this could be counteracted by giving them lessons from a young age on how politics works in the UK.
rejection_details:
Schools are already required to teach citizenship as part of the secondary national curriculum.

The citizenship curriculum includes content on how the United Kingdom is governed, its political system and how citizens participate actively in its democratic systems of government.

You can read the citizenship programmes of study for secondary school here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study-for-key-stages-3-and-4

If you would like to make a change to the current arrangements, you can start a petition setting out clearly what you would like to change, such as submitting a petition about making politics a core specific subject.

action: Fund and distribute a leaflet on climate change to every UK household
background: This leaflet would contain an evidence-based and impartial account of the reality of climate change. It should set out what is known of its causes and its likely effects on UK households under a number of scenarios for future levels of greenhouse gas emissions.
additional_details: We think there is a compelling urgency now for such a clear briefing (echoing the 'Brexit leaflet' sent to every household in 2016). This is underlined not only by the worsening condition of our environment, but also by recent reports of a spread of misinformation about climate change. We think the government has a duty to make us all aware of the reality of climate change, and the changes needed to reduce emissions and set in place measures of mitigation and resilience.

action: For Ozzy Osbourne to receive a Knighthood for services to music and Birmingham
background: To push for Ozzy Osbourne to receive a Knighthood for his dedication to music and founding a very important music genre! For also helping put Birmingham on the map
additional_details: Ozzy's battle with Parkinson's and still managed to arrange and a charity gig raising over £140 Million for three important charitys! (Parkinsons foundation, Acorns and Birmingham Children's Hospital) To do all this while battling with Parkinson's is amazing and he is such an important character in British Music History!

The Government will only accept individual nominations, not petitions, so we can’t publish your petition.
