action: Release all records from each census after 75 years instead of 100 years
background: A census gives the government a picture of households across the UK and is also used by genealogists to research family history. The UK has a longer waiting time for census records to be released, at 100 years compared to Canada's 92 and USA's 72. We'll have to wait until 2052 for the next release.
additional_details:
From the Inter-War period, genealogists in the UK have the information given to them about ancestors from the 1921 census and 1939 England and Wales Register.
 
However, the 1931 census was burnt in a fire in 1942 so that leaves a 30-year gap between the 1921 census and next available census from 1951.
 
Between the UK, USA and Canada, the UK has the longest wait for census records to be released, and I think that it should be lowered to 75 years instead.

action: Provide free bus travel for under-22s in England
background: Scotland and Wales already offer free or discounted bus travel for young people. We believe England should do the same to support equal access to transport, reduce emissions, and improve opportunities for young people.
additional_details: We urge the Government to provide free bus travel for under-22s in England. Scotland’s National Entitlement Card has shown that free youth travel increases mobility, reduces emissions, and improves access to education, work, and wellbeing. This change would support equality, sustainability, and young people’s independence.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund free bus travel and increase rail fare discounts for those 22 and under
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730337

action: Automatic rail fare cap, flexible season tickets & require smart ticketing
background: We believe current rail ticketing is outdated and penalises commuters with irregular travel patterns. Some Flexi Season tickets must be bought in advance, with no refunds if it is unused. Many commuters now travel 4–15 days a month and we believe existing options are too rigid or too expensive.
additional_details:
We call for the following changes: 
- Introduce an automatic fare capping system for rail operators like TfL’s model.
-  Develop season tickets or smartcard-based systems that apply discounts based on actual travel between fixed origin-destination pairs.
-  Require rail operators support smart ticketing that rewards loyalty and flexibility fairly.

action: Require a full licence to be eligible for business use motor insurance policies
background: Many food delivery riders on L plates haven’t passed a test; just a CBT every 2 years which shows they can move & stop a bike safely, we feel it doesn't show they have road safety awareness. We think they may be causing insurance premiums to rise due to the number of accidents they cause.
additional_details: Make businesses use motor insurance only available to full licence holders. We think this would ensure that anyone using their motor vehicle for business use are adequately licenced and qualified. We think the point of L plates is to learn how to ride/drive, not to let you run a business. We think the CBT makes it too easy for unlicenced (and often unqualified) riders to work for fast food delivery companies and conduct their business. We think they are involved in accidents which could be causing premiums for everyone else to rise.

action: I want the scrapping of the school term time fine for parents
background: I want this fine to be abolished completely.
additional_details: Parents are being punished for taking their children away and wanting them to enjoy the best part about being a child and that is learning to understand family & happy times are the most important part of life. They are punished in costs from the airlines and holiday companies. Teachers striking & taking training days also put into question the validity of this fine. Instead rules around the number of events/times children are removed should be implemented for a fine threshold ie 3/4 events.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop fines for taking children out of school on holiday
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727960

action: Increase funding for hospice care facilities
background: There are reports of hospice care charities being forced to cut staff and available beds for patients. We want the Government to increase the funding and support they’re allocated. Dying should be dignified and personal and hospices can provide this.
additional_details: So many end of life patients and palliative care patients rely on hospices to feel safe, to manage their pain and to provide a dignified and comfortable death. We think the NHS is already overrun, clearing beds as fast as possible, and under staffed. Many hospices are already up and running they just need additional funding.

action: Intervene through military means to get food and baby formula into Gaza
background: We want the UK government to intervene through military means if needed to feed Palestinians who are facing starvation. We especially want baby milk and special formula for neonates to be flooded into Gaza.
additional_details: There are reports that the blockade imposed by Israel has caused a shortage of baby formula, and that children have starved to death and many are suffering from serious malnutrition. It is not normal to see children as skin and bones. We want this Government to take meaningful action to stop children and babies starving.

action: Require public consultation before airfields and aerodromes can be closed
background: Airfields and aerodromes play a vital role in the UK's transportation network, economic growth, emergency services, and heritage. However, some sites may be closed and redeveloped, often without sufficient public consultation or long-term strategic consideration.
additional_details: We urge Parliament to legislate or amend laws such that no airfield/aerodrome is closed & redeveloped without formal consultation involving public, industry, and government. Each site’s strategic value should be assessed, with DfT input required. We think airfields should be recognised as critical infrastructure supporting aviation, emergency services, military, and economic growth. We think preserving them is vital for the UK’s role in the Advanced Air Mobility Revolution and emerging sustainable air transport.
government_response_summary: The Government recognises the importance of General Aviation and aerodromes, but decisions on a site's future use rest with the landowner and planning authorities through the planning system.
government_response_body: The Government recognises the important contribution that General Aviation aerodromes make to the UK’s economy, emergency services, skills base and aviation heritage.  However, most aerodromes and airfields are privately owned and decisions around their future use, including whether to continue aviation operations, are a matter for landowners, subject to the planning system. The National Planning Policy Framework already requires planning authorities to consider the role of airports and airfields in connectivity and economic growth and strategic infrastructure when considering development proposals.  While the Government values the role of General Aviation, it considers that the current balance between private property rights, local decision making, and national aviation policy remains appropriate. We will continue to support general aviation as part of our wider aviation approach.  Department for Transport

action: Require installation and maintenance of air conditioning in all HGVs and vans
background: HGV and van drivers may work long hours in dangerously hot cabs with no legal requirement for air con. We want the Government to require air con in all new HGVs and vans and require existing air con systems in older vehicles to be maintained and operational to protect driver health and road safety.
additional_details: Drivers can spend hours a day in cabs in high temperatures, especially in summer or when the sun hits the windscreen. This can cause fatigue, dehydration, and reduced concentration, putting safety at risk. Some drivers may spend days living in these cabs. With more heatwaves due to climate change, we think legal protection is urgently needed.

action: Mandate Tracking of hired Bikes, E-Bikes and Scooters & timed suspensions
background:
Many bikes, e-bikes and e-scooters (B,EB,ES) in British cities are hired.
These vehicles have been given extended rights and privileges, such as exclusive cycle lanes and superhighways to ensure they can ride safely.
additional_details:
However, we think some users are not complying with road laws.

Motorists, being in charge of more potentially dangerous vehicles, follow stringent training and rules set down in the Highway Code. CCTV and recording equipment is situated on roads to ensure compliance.

We think some users of B,EB,ES are not following road laws, making streets extremely dangerous for the most vulnerable of people - pedestrians, and for themselves. We think trackers in B,EB,ES with sensors in traffic lights, would catch those not complying, allowing for timed suspensions from hiring

action: Decided on a maximum safe to work temperature
background:
I would like the government to decide on a maximum work temperature. As the temperature is rising yearly in England many work places are not equipped to cope with the heat.
I would also like the government to consider heat compensation for staff of environments that rise above the chosen limit.
additional_details: The weather is getting hotter yearly and I think putting these measures into place early would encourage companies to provide adequate cool breaks or Aircon which will eventually be needed regardless as temperatures rise ..also staff would be fairly compensated for the hot work environment if safety measures are not met...i know some buildings hit over 50 degrees Celsius last year. We have no choice but to work so please make it safe.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731468

action: Deduct neo-natal leave from return to work date for childcare funding purposes
background: Currently, the 30 hours childcare scheme bases eligibility on the baby’s birth date and parent’s return to work. Neonatal leave delays some parents, which may cause them to miss deadlines and lose months of free childcare. We think the government must change this to stop families being penalised.
additional_details: For example, if a baby is born in January, they become eligible for 30 hours free childcare in September, when they turn 9 months old. However, if the mother takes 52 weeks maternity leave plus 2 weeks neonatal care and returns to work in February, the family will miss the January 31 funding deadline. As a result, they will not receive funding until April, losing three months of childcare support. This issue may affect many families using neonatal leave and we think it must be addressed by the government.

action: Funding for preventative NHS Mental Health Services & set minimum access times
background: We call on the UK Government to increase funding for preventative NHS mental health care. We think too many people are left to deteriorate while waiting for support. We demand legally enforced access times, and investment in early intervention and prevention — not just crisis response.
additional_details: We think too many people are left to deteriorate while waiting for mental health care. We think the NHS system focuses on crisis, not prevention. We call for legally enforced waiting times, and funding for proper follow-up after discharge and early access support services to stop people falling through the cracks before it’s too late. We think we need investment in prevention, not just emergency care. We think people deserve support before they break, not only after.

action: Fund school bus service for all Primary & Secondary state schools students
background: We propose the funding of a shared school transport service (e.g., buses/vans) to provide safe, efficient, and eco-friendly travel for all school children. We believe such a service would bring significant benefits to our community like it is in other countries.
additional_details:
We think funding school buses would:
1. Environmental Impact: Reduce carbon emissions by cutting down individual school runs.
2. Less Traffic: Decrease congestion near schools, improving safety and accessibility.
3. Social Benefits: Encourage friendships and bonding among children traveling together.
4. Weather-Proof: Offer a reliable alternative during extreme weather conditions.
5. Time-Saving: Free up parents’ time spent on daily drop-offs and pick-ups.
6. Child Safety: Provide a secure, supervised travel option for students.
7. Punctuality: Ensure on-time arrival, promoting regular attendance.
 
We think this service would benefit families, schools, and the environment. We urge authorities to consider funding this initiative for the well-being of our community.

action: Require a By-Election When an MP Changes Party Affiliation
background: Require that any MP who leaves the political party they were elected under must trigger an automatic by-election. Voters should not be represented by someone who no longer aligns with the party they originally supported at the ballot box.
additional_details:
Many voters cast their vote based on a party’s values, manifesto, and leadership — not solely the individual candidate. When an MP changes party or becomes independent mid-term, the political mandate given by their constituents is undermined.

This ensures accountability, maintains public trust, and respects the democratic process. A change of political alignment should be validated by the people who elected that representative.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Require AUTOMATIC by election if an MP changes party during a term of office
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711480

action: Make it a specific criminal offence to walk dogs on hot pavements and roads
background: Make it a specific criminal offence to walk a dog on hot pavements and roads, thereby risking burning the dog's paws. We think this problem simply isn’t being dealt with and that this change would assist the general public to help look out for it occurring instead of using overstretched resources.
additional_details: We believe that too many dogs are being walked during the hottest time of the day on scalding pavements and tarmac with no shade. A human may not be able to tolerate this heat so a dog shouldn't have to either. We think this is an act of cruelty and abuse and should be explicitly defined and criminalised as such in law.

action: Pause Liverpool Bay CO₂ storage until full environmental and legal assessment
background: We ask the Government to pause the Liverpool Bay marine CO₂ government storage project until a full independent safety and environmental assessment is completed. This site risks acid formation, seabed contamination, and long-term damage to protected marine ecosystems and aquifers.
additional_details: We are calling on the UK Government to pause the Liverpool Bay marine CO₂ storage project until a full, independent environmental and legal risk assessment is completed. Parliament’s own Public Accounts Committee has raised concerns about this technology. In their 2023 report, they stated that Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) remains “untested at scale” in the UK, and warned that its ability to deliver either value for money or climate goals is "still unclear".
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Reduce the salaries that MP’s are paid to reflect the current financial climate.
background: Parliament should vote reduce the salaries of MP’s by £19,960 each per year to make a total saving to the tax payer of £12,974,000 annually in solidarity with the people of the UK who are being asked to accept cuts proposed through policy put in place by the labour Government.
additional_details: The current average salary in the UK is £36,972. MP’s are currently paid £93,904. When the general public are being asked to live through a time where the government are proposing cuts to vital services to make savings and satisfy the Chancellors ‘fiscal rules’, Parliament should vote to reduce their wages by £19,960 bringing their salaries in line with twice the annual average income of a UK citizen as a sign of understanding that cuts effect us all and should be shared by all.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA) is responsible for deciding on MPs' expenses and pay. IPSA is independent of both Parliament and Government. 
 
You can find out more about IPSA here: http://www.theipsa.org.uk

action: Make the Freedom of Information Act apply to sporting National Governing Bodies
background: We call on the Government to require all sporting National Governing Bodies (NGBs) to be subject to the Freedom of Information Act. NGBs hold substantial authority over who can participate in grassroots and competitive sports.
additional_details:
We think NGBs make decisions directly affecting the lives and wellbeing of thousands of UK citizens. We feel they operate without transparency of public institutions, they are publicly recognised, receive public money, they impact communities, inclusion, and equality.
 
We think the public should have a right to access information from bodies that influence our daily lives and use taxpayer money. We think their decisions must be open to scrutiny.

action: Require companies to have a disability absence policy
background: Legislate to ensure that companies are required to hold a disability absence policy and enforce clearer and more transparent reasonable adjustments. Require large organisations to establish formal policies addressing disability-related absences.
additional_details: Currently, some companies treat disability-related medical leave as sick leave, which we think may adversely affect career progression for disabled employees. While reasonable adjustments may be available as "time off for medical appointments," there is no standard requirement for how such absences should be managed, which we think leads to disadvantages for disabled individuals.

action: Include AI in school IT curriculum
background: We want the government to make Artificial Intelligence a part of the primary and secondary school IT curriculum to encourage further growth in digital ability.
additional_details: AI has been incorporated into some jobs and professions in the last few years due to its useful nature in a workplace. I feel it can be used as a reliable work partner and as something that can increase productivity and overall create a better work environment.

action: Improve the standards of behaviour during House of Commons debates.
background: We want the Government to introduce formal behavioural standards or disciplinary procedures to address the immaturity, shouting, and disorder often seen in House of Commons debates. These behaviours reduce the quality of discussion and waste valuable parliamentary time.
additional_details: The behaviour displayed during debates in the House of Commons often falls far below the standards expected in any professional setting. Sessions that should be dedicated to rational, informed discussion are frequently disrupted by shouting, jeering, personal insults, and immature displays that do little to advance meaningful policy. This not only wastes valuable parliamentary time but also erodes public confidence in the institution and those elected to serve within it.
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker personally.

action: Ensure parity of esteem between mental and physical health services
background: The principle of achieving parity of esteem between mental and physical health services was established through legislation by the Health and Social Care Act 2012. We think that realising this objective requires more funding for mental health services, a goal that we think is far from being realised
additional_details: Mental health conditions account for approximately 28% of the overall disease burden and are associated with poor physical health and reduction in life expectancy. However, current allocation only gives 13% of funding to mental health services. We believe that addressing this disparity is essential to achieving equitable recognition and support for mental health. We think the government must commit to increasing investment in mental health services to ensure funding levels have parity of esteem with physical health.

action: Allow council estates in wales to put flowers out the front of their house
background: My nan was told by Carmarthenshire county council that she had a week to get rid of all her flowers from the front of their house in a “communal area” as it was a fire hazard! I want to allow them to have their flowers back!!

action: Ban on requiring an app to access purchased tickets
background:
The government should update relevant legislation, so digital tickets can always be accessed offline without a mobile app.
 
We think possible arguments regarding security do not outweigh the necessity of customer choice, access, and control
additional_details:

action: Save The Point Milton Keynes and protected landmark.

background: Create a “Stamp 0”style visa so UK residents can bring their dependent elderly parents to live with them if they fully fund their stay. background: We urge the Government to require all nurseries to allow parents to be able to use free, funded childcare hours at all times of the day and week, and to increase funding for nurseries to achieve this.

additional_details: To prevent misdiagnosis, recurring infections, potential impacts on future fertility, and life-threatening invasive infections such as Strep A, toxic shock syndrome, or sepsis, implement a mandatory dual-site swabbing protocol (internal and external) for all postpartum patients presenting with suspected suture/tear infections following vaginal delivery.

background: We want the government to instate a regulatory body to oversee doulas and birth keepers. We think there are people in this role offering  amazing emotional support. action: Reinstate the death penalty for serious violent crimes to reduce knife crime.
background: Knife crime is rising, causing many deaths and fear in communities. Current punishments aren’t enough to stop this violence. We ask the Government to reinstate the death penalty for the most serious crimes, including knife murders, to deter offenders and protect innocent lives.
additional_details: Knife crime is devastating families and communities across the UK. Too many lives are lost, and fear is widespread. Current laws and punishments are failing to stop violent offenders. Reinstating the death penalty for the most serious violent crimes would serve as a strong deterrent, ensuring justice for victims and helping to protect innocent people from future harm.

background: We call on the UK Government to urgently address the surge in phone and street theft in London. The Mayor of London has failed to protect Londoners. We demand increased police funding and national oversight to hold local authorities accountable when public safety standards are not met.
additional_details: Living in London is becoming increasingly dangerous. Street crime has become a daily threat, and many of us feel unsafe simply walking outside. The fear of being attacked, robbed, or targeted is real and constant. This is not normal. It’s the Government’s responsibility to step in, restore public safety, and hold those in charge—especially the Mayor of London—accountable for this failure. Without urgent action, confidence in policing and leadership will continue to collapse.

action: Review decision to abolish independent local Healthwatch
background:
We are asking the government to:
• Revisit its decision to abolish local independent services that speak up for the public
• Consult with the public to codesign a service which meets their needs and supports the NHS to realise its ambitions
• Invest in and strengthen independent services
additional_details:
Local independent services are rooted in their communities. We think they are well placed to support the 10-Year Health Plan by offering constructive challenge and helping co-produce solutions with those with the greatest health and care needs. We think trusted independent services that listen to local communities are essential to improving health and social care.
We listen without fear or favour and reach those whose voices are often ignored.
government_response_summary: The number of organisations monitoring patient experience is causing confusion and risks inaction. We will close some organisations like Healthwatch to allow direct patient feedback to care providers.
government_response_body: The Government asked Dr Penny Dash to carry out a review of patient safety across the health and care landscape. Dr Dash’s review focused on six key organisations overseen by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC): the Care Quality Commission, the National Guardian’s Office, Healthwatch England (and the local Healthwatch network), the Patient Safety Commissioner, the Health Services Safety Investigations Body and the patient-safety learning related functions of NHS Resolution.  Dr Dash found that there are many organisations carrying out reviews and investigations or looking at user experience. This can lead to an overwhelming number of recommendations which can cause confusion for patients and users. At the same time, customer experience is not given the attention that it deserves in the NHS. Dr Dash aimed to streamline, simplify and consolidate functions across the patient safety landscape to remove duplication and overlap, and make processes simpler and more effective for users and patients.  The report of the Dash review of patient safety across the health and care landscape was published in July 2025. In the report, Dr Dash made nine recommendations which the Government has accepted in full and aligns with the 10 Year Health Plan for England. As such no other options have been considered. We consider the Dash review to be thorough, with all the recommendations aiding to meet the overall objective.  The Government will abolish Healthwatch England (HWE) and Local Healthwatch (LHW) in their current form. A new patient experience directorate within DHSC, will bring patient voice ‘in house’. This will become a central function of the Department and ensure Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) and Local Authorities (LAs) incorporate the views of patients and users directly into strategic planning of services for health and social care.  ICBs will be responsible for the health function of LHW. They will ensure the functions are incorporated in provider organisations alongside existing patient engagement work such as Patient Participation Groups. LAs will be responsible for the social care LHW functions.  The overall objective is to simplify the patient safety landscape with the combined intended outcome to improve quality of care, including safety, by making it clear where responsibility and accountability sit at all levels of the system, and making it easier for staff, patients and users to directly feed into and access the system. And for the system to hear more clearly and so act on the views.  The Government aims for there to be fewer organisations in the patient safety landscape. Patients and users will have a clearer path to providing feedback, which will directly input into the centre, and the commissioners and providers of health and care. Their voices will influence policy, strategic thinking and planning with the aim of improving the quality and safety of care, both in their local areas and nationally.  To achieve the aims and outcomes, the Government must first make legislative changes to abolish HWE and LHW in their current form. Existing legislation will be amended or revoked with the functions currently held by HWE and LHW moving to the Secretary of State, ICBs and LAs.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Ban UK Border Force from picking up migrants in the Channel
background: We urge the Government to prohibit UK Border Force vessels from picking up and collecting migrants from the English Channel, and to only detain them once they land in the UK.

action: Levy per carcass to fund independent continuous abattoir CCTV monitoring
background: Effective, independent, real time observation required with costs funded by a levy per carcass.
additional_details: Reporting has demonstrated abuse in abattoirs yet we feel there have not been enough prosecutions. We think present legislation does little to protect animals from abhorrent abuse. We think more stringent regulations are needed and an independent committee established with no link to government or industry. We think costs funded by a levy per carcass would make this proposal financially viable.

action: Ban hotel accommodation for illegal migrants and require removal within 100 days
background: We want the Government to immediately stop using public funds to house illegal migrants in hotels and introduce a legal duty to remove all illegal entrants within 100 days of arrival unless their asylum case is resolved in that time.
additional_details:
The British public faces rising living costs, housing pressures, and NHS backlogs. Yet thousands of people who entered the UK illegally are being placed in hotels at an unsustainable cost — over £8 million per day.

This undermines trust in our immigration system. We believe those who enter illegally should not be rewarded with free accommodation, especially after travelling through safe countries.

We urge the Government to:

Ban the use of taxpayer money to house illegal migrants in hotels

Introduce a legal duty to remove illegal entrants within 100 days unless their asylum claim is resolved

This would reduce costs, deter illegal crossings, and restore fairness to our immigration laws.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Shut the migrant hotels down now and deport illegal migrants housed there 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/718406

action: Require the NHS to contract innovations that are successfully piloted
background: Require all NHS pilots of medtech and AI to include clear, evidence-based criteria for adoption, and a defined procurement pathway when those criteria are met — turning proven innovations into contracts, not abandoned trials.
additional_details: We ask Parliament to ensure that all NHS pilots of medical technologies, diagnostics, and AI tools include clear success measures and a set pathway to adoption. If a pilot shows strong clinical and economic results, we think the NHS should be required to move to contract the technology. We think this would stop proven innovations from being dropped and help patients benefit faster from safe, effective tools that have already shown they work in real NHS settings.

action: Review Section 47 of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861
background: We want the Government to review Section 47 of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861. We think it’s outdated and too broad. We think we need a fairer, modern law that reflects the severity and context of each case and avoids lifelong consequences for minor or provoked incidents.
additional_details: We think section 47 fails to reflect individual circumstances, leaving people with lifelong consequences for brief or provoked incidents. We feel it doesn’t account for self-defence, harassment, or mental health factors. We think a review is needed to ensure justice is fair, proportionate, and fit for today’s society. We feel it treats all ABH incidents the same, ignoring intent, context, and severity. People may face lifelong consequences for brief or provoked actions. We think we need a review for fair and proportionate justice.

action: Fund NHS dentists for all NHS staff
background: I want to the Government to fund access to an NHS dentist for all NHS staff.
additional_details: Some people find they have missed a couple of appointments, due to having to work or other appointments, and their Dentist has taken them off the system and they are told they will have to find a new dentist. Then they try and find an NHS Dentist without any luck.

action: Make it mandatory for MPs to wear badges of the organisations lobbying them
background: Mandate that MPs must wear badges representing individuals or organisations who lobby them, in a similar way to athletes wearing sponsors' logos on their kit. We think MPs should be more transparent with their politics and make it easier for the public to see whose interests they represent.
additional_details: We are very concerned about lobbying and know it is rife in politics. We believe publishing donations to MPs on the Electoral Commission website is not enough because many people are likely unaware that this resource exists, and the exact details and context around individuals and organisations lobbying MPs often requires intense research to find out who is donating to a party or individual and why that is significant. We think wearing badges of political sponsors should be made mandatory for MPs to wear to make this information more clear, and hold MPs more accountable.

action: Universal basic electricity allowance for all households, with usage thresholds
background: Set into law that all households be given free, basic electricity allowances, eg 4kWh daily, funded by energy companies through a series of energy use thresholds, where cost per kWh increases (for electricity, oil & gas). Capped for households with high energy use for legitimate health reasons.
additional_details: I think a basic free electricity allowance, for all 'on grid' households, would help thousands of people in fuel poverty. I propose the energy use thresholds (includes electricity, oil and gas usage), as I think there's a familiarity around income tax 'thresholds' and contributing more to society, the more you earn. I believe the initiative would encourage higher energy use households to make savings, invest in low carbon technology and help drive local jobs. I'd also propose households who require high energy use for health reasons (there may be other circumstances to include) are capped at a lower 'threshold'. This scheme could also be extended to small business owners.

action: Strengthening Democracy Through Participation.
background:
requiring all eligible citizens to vote in general and local elections, while preserving the right to formally abstain on the ballot. Those who fail to participate (without a valid reason) shall incur a modest fine, ensuring civic responsibility while respecting individual choice.
Why This Matters
additional_details: To improve on democracy overall, with full public engagement, this will be the best way to improve local and national turn out in elections.

Introduce compulsory voting

background: FORCE FAST FOOD CHAINS TO SELL PLASTIC STRAWS
additional_details: BECAUSE I HATE PAPER STRAWS

Unban the supply of plastic straws, stirrers and cotton buds

action: Remove the 20-hour work limit for sponsored care workers to ease staff crisis
background: We want the Government to remove or increase the 20-hour weekly work limit for sponsored care workers so they can take more hours with agencies when their main sponsor offers low or no hours. This will help ease the care staffing crisis and allow workers to support themselves.
additional_details: Care homes across the UK face severe staff shortages while many sponsored care workers want to work more hours but are restricted by the 20-hour weekly limit. Often, their main sponsor offers low or no hours, leaving them unable to earn enough while shifts go unfilled. Removing this cap will help workers support themselves, ease pressure on care providers, and ensure vulnerable people get the care they need. It’s a practical step to address the staffing crisis in health and social care.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728846

action: Hold a General Election once every twelve months
background: We believe that UK Governments do not deliver on their promises, that they do not listen to what we think the majority of the public want, and that they take their position of power for granted. We think it is time to make changes so our leaders can be held accountable through a yearly review.
additional_details: Under this system, once elected with the trust that politicians will form a government and run the country, they'd have 12 months to get on with it and start delivering for the public. If they do a good job, then they'd have nothing to worry about and should easily get re-elected. If they do a bad job, then the public would have the opportunity to swiftly replace them with a new government that would hopefully listen and do better if they'd like to remain in charge for longer than 12 months.

action: Reduce the recurring miscarriage threshold from 3 consecutive losses to 2
background: Reduce the defined threshold for recurrent miscarriage from 3 consecutive losses to 2, to allow families to access NHS funded testing and treatment earlier and to provide mental and physical support to women experiencing these tragedies.
additional_details: I believe fertility testing and treatment should be available to women and families who have experienced more than one miscarriage or pregnancy loss to reduce the physical and emotional impact that can contribute to severe trauma. Families should not be expected to experience 3 losses of life before the NHS funds explorative testing or preventative treatment.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
The definition of a recurring miscarriage is a matter for the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Fund wheelchairs and changing places facilities for beaches
background: We would like the government to fund better basic disabled facilities for beaches. By that we mean at least one beach wheelchair and a changing places toilet along with it. We have found some beaches have one or the other but a lot of disabled people need both.
additional_details: Many disabled children love being in the sea. Finding a beach that has both a wheelchair and a changing places facility can be hard work and some people have to drive long distances for this. Please help us fix this.

action: Compulsory AC for delivery drivers to be written in employee rights.
background: Delivery drivers drive unlimited miles in a year. Due to climate change, summer driving becomes impossible for those susceptible to the hotter temperatures.
additional_details: Today, I was exposed to 37C with no AC. It was unbearable with my health which contrubuted to fatigue, alertness and ability which is dangerous and may  contribute to RTC's on British roads. I spend a maximum of 10 hours on the road a day, in the hotter temperatures I CANNOT complete my job. I wish to make law and included in employment rights that all commercial and delivery vehicles must have air conditioning fitted to the vehicle to make a better environment for remote drivers.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Require installation and maintenance of air conditioning in all HGVs and vans

action: Seize boats used to transport illegal immigrants
background: It is possible that the same boats are being used over and over again. Seizing the boats prevents transporting more illegal immigrants.
additional_details: Government wants to stop the boats. Here is a straight forward strategy to do exactly that. Especially as the boats are usually overloaded with too many people on board which is very unsafe.
rejection_details:
The Nationality and Borders Act 2022 grants powers to Border Force to seize and dispose of vessels used to facilitate irregular entry by sea to the UK:

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/nationality-and-borders-bill-border-force-powers-to-stop-and-seize-small-boats-factsheet/nationality-and-borders-bill-border-force-powers-to-stop-and-seize-small-boats-factsheet

action: Improve regulation of letting agents including new statutory regulator
background: We believe there is an urgent need for better regulation of letting agents. We think the current system is broken, and that it seems to protect system abusers, not victims.
additional_details: We call on the UK Government to create a new statutory regulator for letting agents with powers to investigate financial irregularities, admit whistleblower evidence, enforce stricter penalties, and ensure more joined-up enforcement with local councils, police and Trading Standards. We think landlords and tenants should not be left alone to fight for justice, and that the system must protect them.

action: Call for a national emergency. End the small boat crossings.
background: We feel the British public are not being listened to, the government urgently need to get a grip on the ongoing small boat crossings in the English Channel. We feel now is the time to call for a national emergency.
rejection_details: It is not clear what you mean in regards to declaring a national emergency and what sort of impact you would like this to have.

action: Change the law to allow party members the right to enter party leadership races.
background: Change the law to allow any party member to run to be leader of their party just like Canada allows.
additional_details: This would give party members more control and raise the bar of competency in leadership positions.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

The rules for leadership elections in political parties are a matter for those parties. The Government and Parliament are therefore not responsible for the issue raised in this petition.

action: Parliamentary Debate on Government Failures in Welfare Reform and Immigration
background: We ask Parliament to debate the Government’s failure to reform welfare, tackle benefit fraud, and control illegal immigration through its deal with France, and to examine the wider consequences these failures have had on public confidence and political accountability.
additional_details: Citizens deserve a Government that delivers on its promises. Delayed welfare reform, rising benefit fraud costing billions, and a costly deal with France that returns few illegal migrants each week have led to public frustration and financial strain. These failures harm essential services, undermine trust, and threaten national security. Parliament must hold a full debate to scrutinise these decisions and hold those in power accountable through proper democratic processes.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do as a debate would be the outcome of a petition if it receives 100,000 signatures.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Change the English national anthem from God Save the King, to Jerusalem.
background: I would like Parliament to press for a change so that all the governing bodies of the various sports, at international level, and participating under an English flag, should be allowed to use Jerusalem, and *not* God save the king, as the official English national anthem.
additional_details: God Save the King is arguably one of the worst national anthems in the world. It is a depressing, tedious, tuneless dirge that utterly fails to inspire. National anthems should reach the *souls* of both direct participants and the watching crowd/fans. I would argue that William Blake's words, and Hubert Parry's music, combine in the most sublime way to produce something that becomes far more than merely the sum of its constituent parts.
rejection_details:
The use of the present National Anthem is a matter of tradition rather than having any legal status.

You can find more information about the history and status of the national anthem here:

https://www.royal.uk/national-anthem

action: Reverse the decision to remove funding from Midland Main Line Electrification.
background: Review the decision to terminate the next phases of Midland Main Line Electrification.
additional_details:
Railway electrification is strategic investment.   The Midland Main Line Electrification has so far been delivered to budget.   This is transformative investment in infrastructure that benefits the communities through which it passes. 
Investment had been earmarked and has recently been removed.  This is a poor decision and should be reversed.

action: Cap donations to political parties & politicians at £500 yearly, for each donor
background: Cap all donations to political parties and politicians at £500 per year, for each individual person or organisation making the donation—including unions and companies.
additional_details: We believe that our democracy is stagnating, and that what we see as entrenched funding from political donations can give political parties media and political dominance, starving the oxygen from any new or changed parties before they can surpass even an embryonic stage.

action: Prevent the closure of Crewkerne Community & other community hospitals in area
background:
Stop the closure of Crewkerne Community Hospital and other local community hospitals. 
Protect and invest in these vital services to ensure continued access to local inpatient care, rehabilitation and support for these vulnerable patients.
additional_details: Community hospitals like Crewkerne provide essential local care, reduce pressure on larger hospitals, and support patient recovery closer to home. Their closure risks increased travel, delays in treatment, and loss of trusted local services for elderly and vulnerable patients. These closures also force dedicated nurses and healthcare staff to be redeployed, creating uncertainty, breaking up local teams and worsening already critical workforce shortages. Please help us protect our hospital!

We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.

action: Seek to rejoin EU single market
background: I would like the UK Government to start discussions with the European Union to seek to rejoin the EU Single Market and to make rejoining the EU Single Market a priority for the UK Government, and to aim rejoining the Single Market within 12 months.
additional_details: In 2024, the EU accounted for 41% of UK Exports, and 51% of imports. The OBR estimates that both exports and imports will be around 15% lower in the long run than if the UK remained in the EU. We believe a reduction in income for the UK will inevitably force the Government to raise taxes and reduce spending on public services. We believe the EU referendum result could have meant people may have wanted a softer Brexit, which we think rejoining the Single Market could deliver.

action: Recognise & fund commemorations of the 1,100 Anniversary of England's Foundation
background: We urge the Government to officially recognise and fund commemorations for 4 September 2025 to celebrate the 1,100th anniversary of the coronation of King Athelstan in 925AD — the first King of a unified England. We believe this is a pivotal moment in British history and deserves commemoration.
additional_details:
We urge the Government to:
• Fund commemorative events and educational activities across England.
• Fund a permanent statute of King Athelstan to honour this foundational moment in English history.
 
We believe this is a rare opportunity to celebrate the unity and origins of England as a nation — rooted in culture, continuity, and Royal Patronage.

It needs to become an criminal offence not to follow through with what was promised to gain position of prime minster.

action: I want you to upgrade and improve the park for the kids. They have nothing.

action: Make feminine hygiene products free
background: To be able to make feminine hygiene products free for the people who struggle to afford the expensive of such things and the young girls out there. Women should not be having to pay for something that they have to go through monthly not because they caused it its a way of living
