action: Funding for finger-prick glucose test for all unwell children of any age in A&E
background: Fund all NHS A&E departments to do finger-prick blood glucose tests on all unwell babies, toddlers, and children, even if symptoms seem minor, specific, or common, to detect undiagnosed Type 1 diabetes and early DKA, preventing life-threatening complications.
additional_details: Many children with Type 1 diabetes aren’t diagnosed until they develop life-threatening DKA. We think early testing could save lives and prevent trauma.

action: Require police forces to provide preventative and ongoing PTSD support
background: Research shows almost 1 in 5 officers are estimated to have PTSD. The condition increases suicide risk and, if untreated, can cause impaired judgment, posing a safety risk to officers and the public. We want mandatory support & trauma training.
additional_details: We ask the Government to make it a legal requirement for police forces to provide preventative and ongoing PTSD support. We think officers face repeated trauma and are at far higher risk of PTSD than civilians or military personnel. Current schemes are not mandatory or consistently effective. We think legislation should enforce early intervention, mental health assessments, trauma training, wellbeing debriefs, and national tracking of suicide data. We think legislation is the only way to hold forces accountable.

action: Launch a review of the Domestic Abuse Protection Order system
background: We urge the Government to launch an urgent review of the Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) system in order to look into reforming the system. Currently, DAPOs can be issued where there is insufficient evidence to charge someone who is accused of perpetrating domestic abuse.
additional_details: We want this review in order to prevent possible misuse of the system. We believe that innocent people, particularly men, could be subjected to life upheavals by possible misuse of what we believe is a well-intentioned system and process. We believe the current system may disregard the possible likelihood of those who are accused of being victims themselves.

action: Ban all peanuts and tree nuts on all flights to protect allergy sufferers
background: Create legislation to ban all peanuts and tree nuts on all flights, including those served by airlines and brought by passengers. We think this would protect people with severe allergies from life-threatening reactions in a setting where emergency medical help isn't available.
additional_details: People with severe nut allergies may be put at serious risk when airlines serve or allow nuts on board. We think having to ask for an announcement every time is unreliable—crew often forget, and by then passengers may have already opened nuts. We think this leaves allergy sufferers feeling unsafe and vulnerable. We think a government ban would ensure consistency, prevent life-threatening reactions, and make flying safer for everyone.

action: Cap legal fees for divorce cases and remove or reduce VAT
background: Divorce can be stressful and costly. I think lawyers’ hourly fees are too high and should be capped, e.g. £250/hr. Legal help in divorce feels essential, so VAT should be exempt to ease the financial burden.
additional_details: Given that legal services in divorce are a necessity, it raises the question of whether VAT should apply at all. It would feel fairer if such services were either exempt from VAT or subject to a reduced VAT rate to ease the financial burden on those going through this difficult process.

action: Business Sale Exit Brokers publish success rates, Founder/Owners to be protected
background: Business sale exit brokers should publish true success rates. Founder-owners deserve transparency and protection when planning an exit, so they’re not misled about the real chances of selling their business. And/or Tax rate should be higher if no success.
additional_details: Business sale exit brokers should publish true success rates. Founder-owners deserve transparency and protection when planning an exit, so they’re not misled about the real chances of selling their business. Perhaps tax rules could change so brokers face a higher tax rate on fees if a sale isn’t successful, ensuring they share the risk and are motivated to deliver real results for business owners.
rejection_details:
We are not clear on what specific action you are seeking from UK Government or Parliament, for example whether this petition is calling for a new crime to be introduced, or an additional tax. 

You can start a new petition setting out more clearly what action you are seeking, and in what circumstances.

action: Review and reform education system based on Finland's to improve accessibility
background: I want the government to review, learn from and adapt principles and pedagogy from Finland's education system to reform our own. Remove standardised tests until age 16, relax the curriculum for more flexibility for individual schools and teachers, limit homework, increase play and exploration time.
additional_details: I believe the current approach to education is not conducive to accessibility and inclusion for disabled and neurodivergent pupils, with foundations in more Victorian-era approaches to having children sit still, quiet and eyes to the front. I'm also concerned about what I see as free market ideology principles reflected in education, such as in league tables and a set national curriculum. I am late diagnosed autistic/ADHD, I hated school and felt restricted.

action: Ban the sale of bottled water in plastic bottles
background: Ban the sale of all bottled water, as simple as that.
additional_details: We believe there is no need for selling water in bottles. There are reusable bottles people can use to fill up. We feel the sale of bottled water is completely unnecessary and it adds tons of plastic waste to an already huge environmental problem. We think individuals should use purifiers and filters if they have issues with tap water.

action: Fund NHS COVID boosters for Clinically Vulnerable people – keep covid boosters
background: 'Protect the NHS' and 'Save Lives' by continuing to fund NHS COVID boosters for Clinically Vulnerable people, including most previously shielded as CEV, rather than limiting them to over-75s, care home residents and those with severely weakened immune systems.
additional_details:
From autumn 2025 the Government will deny millions of Clinically Vulnerable people NHS vaccines including people with: diabetes, heart, lung or kidney disease and Down’s syndrome. They continue to face far higher health risks.

NHS vaccines are cheaper than private boosters at ~£100, and an ICU bed over £1,800 per day. We vaccinate the same people against 'flu because it also causes serious illness and death.
Keep NHS boosters.
Protect the vulnerable, the NHS, and save lives

action: Abolish waiting period to retake DVSA instructional ability test & add training
background:
When a PDI or ADI fails their part 3 or standards check for the third time, they can lose their badge and therefore their job, and must wait 2 years before retaking.

We think this should be changed to mandatory extra training and retesting.
additional_details:
The pressure people put themselves under can make it harder to pass with every attempt, knowing they could lose their job.

People can end up unable to pay their bills and may lose their homes. We believe this isn't fair and could lead to poor and dangerous mental health problems.

We believe mandatory training and a retest for people who fail after the third attempt is a much better option.

action: Require businesses to keep doors closed when using heating or air conditioning
background: Introduce legislation to prohibit businesses, including shops, from operating with doors left open while using heating or air conditioning to help reduce energy waste and greenhouse gas emissions.
additional_details: We believe that by requiring businesses to keep doors closed while using heating or air conditioning, we can significantly reduce energy waste and lower greenhouse gas emissions. We think this simple change could make a big impact on our environment, reduce energy bills for businesses, and contribute to a more sustainable future. In our view, it's a common-sense solution that doesn't hinder normal use of buildings or ships, as people would still be able to open doors momentarily to enter and exit.

action: Stop dictating the use of electric cars and taking away choice of vehicle type
background: Allow freedom of choice of vehicles whether ice or battery and stop dictating choice
additional_details: Adults should be allowed to make their own choices and not dictated to. If it is a policy then only some voted for it. Have a national vote asking what people prefer
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711554

action: Halt the Pylon Network Expansion & support underground & undersea cabling
background: We, the undersigned, urgently call on the UK Government to immediately halt and reassess the proposed expansion of the national grid network, which we believe could threaten irreversible harm to our natural environment, wildlife (including protected birds and bats), and rural communities.
additional_details:
We urge the Government to support underground & undersea cabling and alternatives which we think are less invasive. We believe this option is widely supported by the public. Some households do rely on natural wells which could be affected by the construction of pylons.
 
We call on the Government to:
-Suspend the pylon expansion plans.
-Conduct a more extensive environmental & public health impact review.
-Mandate the use of underground/undersea alternatives where feasible.

action: Petition for the Introduction of Mandatory Neutering of Cats over 6 months old.
background:
We urge the government to consider the introduction of legislation that would make the neutering of cats mandatory, mirroring policies already successfully implemented in several other EU countries. 
Rescues across the UK are now unable to cope with the sheer volume of unwanted cats that need help.
additional_details:
Uncontrolled breeding leads to:
•	An overwhelming number of unwanted kittens.
•	Increased burden on animal shelters and rescue organisations.
•	Higher rates of euthanasia for healthy animals
•	Spread of diseases among stray and feral cat populations.
•	Negative impacts on native wildlife through predation and competition.
The introduction of mandatory neutering is a proven, humane, and effective way to address these issues.
Let us follow other forward thinking countries who have implemented this
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Mandate that free roaming pet cats must be neutered 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730827

action: Change the criteria for NHS funded IVF cycles so that they are the same
background: Ensure equal access to NHS-funded IVF treatment across England by standardising the eligibility criteria.
additional_details: Currently, access varies significantly depending on where you live – a 'postcode lottery' that unfairly affects people’s chances of starting a family. All individuals should have the same rights and opportunities to access IVF, regardless of their geographic location.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Increase funding for IVF & fertility treatments to increase access.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711621

action: Protect Northern Ireland’s Dogs From Heat-Related Cruelty
background: Make it an offence in NI during extreme heat to walk dogs, leave them in cars, or outside without shade/water. Dogs are dying from preventable heatstroke. We need clear laws, enforcement powers, and penalties to protect them. Let’s make it law. Let’s protect our dogs.
additional_details:
Every summer, dogs in Northern Ireland suffer or die from heatstroke, a completely preventable cause of death. Walking dogs in high temperatures, leaving them in cars, or outside without shade and water is dangerous. 
There are no clear laws to stop this. I want enforceable heat protection for dogs, including safe temperature limits, powers for early intervention, and penalties for those who put dogs at risk. Let’s act before more dogs suffer needlessly.
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level. Animal welfare in Northern Ireland is a devolved issue which is the responsibility of the Northern Ireland Assembly.

You could ask your MLA to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MLA here: https://aims.niassembly.gov.uk/mlas/contacts.aspx

action: Cancel putting small business profit in the public domain from April 2027
background: From Apr 2027, Companies House intends to force small and micro businesses to publish their full profit and loss accounts online. This marks a significant and unnecessary intrusion into the financial privacy of hundreds of thousands of small businesses across the UK.
additional_details:
Publishing profits is a breach of privacy, like sharing a personal payslip with the country. 
It exposes owners to pricing pressure - customers could associate healthy profit with overcharging. 
It exposes owners to loss of business in tough times - loss of confidence could lead customers to take business elsewhere. 
Without context, figures are easily misread. 
HMRC already has access to this data, public disclosure serves no benefit. 
This policy harms, not helps, the UK's smallest businesses.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731571

action: Work with devolved governments to extend the grooming gangs inquiry
background: Work with devolved governments to extend the national inquiry into group based child sexual exploitation to Scotland and Northern Ireland. We think this is a form of group based child sexual abuse which has been significantly neglected, and which is at risk of becoming worse.
additional_details:
The Casey Audit noted that a ‘significant proportion’ of suspects involved in child sexual exploitation cases are non-UK nationals or individuals claiming asylum.

Any inquiry must include Scotland and Northern Ireland.

action: Reform school absence fines and restore parental authority.
background: Abolish school absence fines. Restore parental authority to decide family holidays. Remove schools’ power to deny reasonable requests. Parents should decide what’s best for their children, not schools.
additional_details: Fines penalise struggling working parents who already face high costs. The system unfairly criminalises families choosing affordable holidays during term time. Schools shouldn’t override parental decisions about family time. Parents work hard and deserve the right to make reasonable choices about their children without financial punishment.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Stop fines for taking children out of school on holiday
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727960

action: Require a Public Referendum Before Deploying Troops or Bombing Campaigns Abroad
background: Pass a law requiring a public referendum before any military action on foreign soil, including troop deployment, bombing, and covert operations. This would ensure real democratic control and help prevent unnecessary, harmful conflicts driven by political, corporate, and geopolitical interests.
additional_details: We want to ensure democratic control over all forms of foreign intervention. Involving UK citizens in decisions that could lead to war ensures we do not enter conflict without public consent. This could prevent future wars, reduce the human cost, restore democracy, foster peace, and ensure actions reflect the will of the people. By requiring a referendum before any military action or foreign intervention, we prioritise public involvement in matters of war and peace.

action: Require Ofwat to cap water bills during water shortages & increase reinvestment
background: We urge the Government to require Ofwat to cap water bills in unmetered households when water companies impose usage restrictions during water shortages.
additional_details: We believe it is unjust for water companies to pay huge dividends and bonuses to shareholders after increasing prices while imposing usage restrictions, which may be because the infrastructure does not support usage requirements if there is a lack of rain. We believe this money should be reinvested to enable the network to meet demands. We are concerned climate change creates these conditions annually and we believe things must change but not at the expense of households.

action: Increase funding for community mental health services and crisis lines
background: Increase funding for community mental health services to help cut waiting times and fully staff 24/7 crisis lines.
additional_details: We think too many people are failed by our mental health system. I’m calling for funding so people get early help, shorter waits for therapy, crisis lines that answer. This is about saving lives.

action: 75% of the UK support a wealth tax, the 2% over 10m in assets should be enforced
background: A 2% tax on assets over £10m could raise £24bn, helping plug fiscal black holes identified by Rachel Reeves. Reducing the need for future public service or benefit cuts, further tax increases, and would help the current economic climate when 50% of the wealth in the UK is held by 50* families.
additional_details: Wealth inequality hasn’t been this severe since the 1980s. Just 50 families hold more wealth than half the UK, while workers face the highest tax burden since WWII. Patriotic millionaires support a 2% tax on assets over £10m, which could raise £24bn and protect vital services from further cuts.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721409

action: Fund IV Fluid Treatment for POTS as a treatment option
background: IV Fluid treatment may be a last resort option for people living with POTS ( Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia syndrome). Some people with POTS are unable to work due to symptoms of extreme tiredness, fatigue, frequent dizzy spells and gastrointestinal issues.
additional_details: We think this treatment could reduce symptoms for some people living with the condition. There have been limited studies in the past where the treatment has worked on patients with POTS and still only remains a treatment if paying private. We think paying private for this treatment isn't an option if people can't afford it due to being too unwell to work.

action: Body cameras for all social workers to enhance accountability
background: We think requiring all social workers to wear body cameras would enhance accountability and transparency. We think this would ensure that all actions taken by social workers are just, honest, and free of personal bias or manipulation.
additional_details: We think this measure will not only protect families but will also protect social workers themselves from false allegations.

action: Extend parental bereavement leave to 4 weeks after the loss of a child
background: Currently, bereavement leave for parents after the loss of a child is two weeks. We believe this is not enough time to begin to grieve or plan and have the funeral before returning to work. We want to get the law changed so parents have more time to grieve after such a huge loss.
additional_details: We urge the Government to extend it by a further two weeks so that it is four weeks. This can ensure more time for parents to be able to start their grief process. We believe after the tragic loss of a child; two weeks is not enough time to bury or begin the grieving process. We believe there is no time limit on grief. We want this change to help parents feel like they matter.

action: Public mortgage scheme for first-time buyers with fixed interest & minimum term
background: We call on the Government to bypass the commercial banking system and use its sovereign power to create a scheme to directly to fund mortgages for eligible first-time buyers. These public mortgages should be offered at a 2.1% fixed interest rate with a 15-year maximum term.
additional_details:
We think the housing crisis may be partly fuelled by banks creating mortgage money for private profit. This proposal calls for the UK Gov to 'mint' its own funds to finance first-time buyers directly.
 
We think a 2.1% fixed-rate, 15-year mortgage could save the average buyer over £130,000 in interest vs a typical bank loan.
 
Crucially, all interest paid would become public revenue, not bank profit, which could create billions per annum for the UK once the scheme is fully established.

action: Recognise Junior Service (16 - 18) in HM Armed Forces as Pensionable Service
background: We think two years of junior armed forces training (ages 16–18) should count as pensionable service. In many other jobs, work from age 16 is recognised from day one. We think the UK should value early military service equally—it directly impacts pension entitlements for servicemen and women.
additional_details:
We think the UK government should recognise that military training from age 16–18 is as valid and demanding as any other form of work. These years should:
 
• Count toward armed forces pension schemes
• Be recognised retrospectively where possible
• Put service personnel on equal footing with their civilian peers
 
We think it’s not just an issue of pension contributions — it’s about respect, parity, and fairness for those who committed to service from a young age.

action: Raise Apprenticeship Minimum Wages for Fair Pay
background: Raise the apprentice minimum wage for all apprentices to match the National Minimum Wage for those aged 18 to 20. We think low pay blocks fair access to training and harms social mobility and our future workforce.
additional_details: We believe that low apprentice pay and limited benefits force many to quit or avoid training and that fair wages and support would help open apprenticeships to all, boost skills, and improve social mobility.

action: Automatic 1-year driving ban for using a mobile whilst driving
background: Driving whilst holding a mobile device in a vehicle can seriously distract drivers. We believe this problem is getting worse despite being illegal. We believe drivers who are guilty of using a mobile phone whilst driving should be given an automatic 1-year driving ban.
additional_details: We believe deaths and serious accidents will only get worse on our roads if this problem continues to escalate. The number of close calls that can happen with drivers using their mobile phones is astonishing.

action: Require clearer labelling of animal-derived ingredients
background: We want the Government to require food, cosmetic, and medical product labels to more clearly and explicitly disclose any animal-derived ingredients. This would include pork, beef, gelatine, insects, or enzymes. We think this would help protect religious, ethical, and dietary rights of consumers.
additional_details: Many UK consumers including Muslims, Jews, vegetarians, and vegans may unknowingly be consuming animal-derived ingredients because of labels which we believe are too vague. We think the current labelling regulations can deny informed choices, erode public trust, and violate religious, ethical, and dietary rights and beliefs. Requiring producers to state directly that the product contains animal-derived ingredients on labels of relevant products would better respect what we feel are basic rights.

action: Lower the MIR for family visas to the National Minimum Wage
background: At the beginning of June 2025 the Migration Advisory Committee recommended that the MIR should be lowered to national minimum wage of £23.000-25.000. We think the government should lower it and reunite families that are divided
additional_details: We think this would give more British Citizens the right and opportunity to live in their own country with their Foreign Spouse and Children without the stress of having to go through the worry and anxiety of finding a job that is outside of their expertise or the stress of having to find unrealistic amounts of money in savings. We think it would help to give equal opportunity to everyone who falls in love with a Foreign partner.

action: Average the income and study hours annually for carers allowance eligibility
background: Average the income eligibility and or study hours over the year instead of on a week by week basis.
additional_details:
Carers allowance eligibility is currently set at under 21hrs a week supervised study, or £196 per week income.
 
We think the DWP should use the amount per year and average it to avoid penalising students who average less than 21 hours per week of supervised study over the year but exceed that amount during term time.

action: Decriminalise the possession and use of marijuana & cannabis products in the UK
background: We urge the Government to review the classification of marijuana and decriminalise the possession and use of marijuana and cannabis-related products in the UK. We believe people shouldn’t be prosecuted or fined for what we believe is a private act of intoxication in their homes or public.
additional_details: Many opinion polls have found that many British people are in favour of decriminalisation of marijuana. We believe in a time of legal backlogs and pressure on the police, a change to the law could assist in alleviating these problems by possibly freeing up state resources and eliminating a climate of fear.

action: Remove Wirral council
background: Take the borough into central governments control until the council has sorted its administrative processes.
additional_details: Put the council into special measures
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

  

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Hold political parties legally accountable for discriminatory rhetoric
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation making political parties and candidates legally accountable for racist, sexist, or otherwise discriminatory narratives. This should include independent oversight, legal sanctions, and mechanisms linking political hate to rising hate crimes.
additional_details:
If political parties and their representatives contribute to an environment where hate is normalised, there should be legal accountability, not just PR management.
 
In a context where 70% of hate crimes in the UK are racially motivated, it is unacceptable that formal political parties, which shape public discourse, face no legal consequences for fuelling division or inciting hostility.

Hate speech and prejudice, when legitimised by public officials, normalise discrimination and violence.
rejection_details:
The Equality Act 2010 already legally protects people from discrimination, harassment or victimisation in the workplace and wider society in relation to their protected characteristics, including their race, sex, sexual orientation, and religion or brief.

In addition, crimes can be prosecuted as hate crimes if the offender has demonstrated or been motivated by hostility based on race, religion, disability, sexual orientation or transgender identity. These crimes are already covered by the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 and section 66 of the Sentencing Act 2020.

action: Revoke right to stay in UK for spouse visa holders who divorce.
background: We ask the Government to amend the Immigration Rules so that any person who enters the UK on a spouse visa and later divorces must return to their country of origin, unless there are exceptional humanitarian or legal reasons for remaining.
additional_details: Spouse visas are granted based on a committed relationship. If the relationship ends, the basis for the visa no longer exists. This change would help prevent potential misuse of the system and ensure immigration rules remain fair and consistent.
rejection_details:
Those on a visa that is dependent on a partner's UK visa or a spouse/partner on a family visa will already either need to apply to stay in the UK or leave following a divorce. More information on this can be found here: 

https://www.gov.uk/visas-when-you-separate-or-divorce

action: Fund a national memorial for those in unmarked / unnamed mental asylum graves
background: Thousands of people died in Victorian-era mental health hospitals and many of their bodies were not claimed by next of kin. Many were buried in unnamed pauper burial plots. Many burial sites are unmarked, neglected, or may even be sold, which we believe dooms patients to an eternity of anonymity.
additional_details: We urge the Government to fund a national memorial to show these people had value and deserve to be remembered. We believe it'll honour those who've died and been lost, returning dignity to their memory, and may act as a focal point to inspire communities who want to honour these gravesites locally, conduct historic research, and use public records to build a clear picture of who lies within them. We also believe it could help tackle historic shame and stigma and right a historic wrong.

action: Fund the creation of a single National Police Trust using proceeds of crime
background: We urge the Government to fund the creation of a National Police Trust with a committee that oversees grant funding for police charities and not-for-profit organisations which support the UK's police workers and their families including the bereaved.
additional_details: We want the Trust to be funded by allocating 10% of annual proceeds from Crime Act seizures. With officer assaults, ill-health retirement from injury, disability and mental health across all police forces, many police charities are struggling to provide support to officers, staff, volunteers and their families. Many police charities and organisations do not receive any government funding, and police workers may have to pay for their own treatment and recovery whilst in a cost-of-living crisis.

action: Require MPs and Lords to answer children's questions in a live debate
background: We ask Parliament to hold a livestreamed debate before each election where MPs and Lords answer live, unscreened questions from children and young people. Questions wouldn’t be shared in advance and would be moderated only for legal/safety reasons on social media platforms.
additional_details: We think this would promote youth political engagement, improve accountability, and give future voters the chance to question those in power directly. The event could be delivered through collaboration between Parliament’s Education Service, broadcasters, and major online platforms. We think this would help ensure impartiality, secure moderation, and wide reach. The process should involve no political filtering of questions, only legal and safety moderation.

action: Add professional employment mediation into the employment tribunal ADR process
background: Stop the plans to recruit more Tribunal Judges and Tribunal Members and instead implement professional mediation before judicial mediation which we think could resolve most issues. Invest the saved money into addressing the root cause by developing key resolution skills within organisations.
additional_details:
We think the vast majority of employment tribunals could be resolved through professional mediation. We think the current ADR steps are ineffective. By implementing professional mediation, successful mediation could reduce backlogged tribunals.

We think this would free up tribunals for cases which need them, organisations could be more productive, stress and wellbeing for employees could improve, and UK productivity could improve.

action: Fund free online access & release all historic birth, marriage & death records
background: We urge the Government to provide funding to make digital images of historic (100+ years old) birth, marriage, and death certificates for England and Wales freely available online, and to digitise and release remaining records as part of the national heritage.
additional_details: We believe these records are valuable for education, history, and family research. Other countries offer free or low-cost access. We believe the UK should treat these not as commercial products but as public records that are accessible to all.

action: Fund free period pads
background: We urge the Government to provide funding to ensure that period pads are free in England.
additional_details: Periods are a normal part of a woman's lives, and not all people can afford period pads or the basic tools that they may need to assist them with something that is out of their control. In Scotland, period products can be accessed free of charge, and we believe this shows that other countries have thought about this topic and decided that it is a good idea. We believe this policy change should be fulfilled.

action: Require Counselling and Mental Health Support for Blue Light Services
background: We want the Government to introduce a national policy requiring all Blue Light Services (Police, Fire, Ambulance, and Coastguard) to provide regular, mandatory counselling sessions and ongoing mental health support for their employees.
additional_details: Emergency workers may face trauma regularly, which may lead to PTSD, anxiety, and depression. We think support is inconsistent and often depends on self-referral, which many avoid due to stigma. We think requiring counselling would help protect mental health, improve wellbeing, and support vital frontline staff.

action: Make Healthy School Meals Free for All Children
background: For some primary school children going into year 3 in september, they will lose their free cooked lunch, for some children this is the only hot food they receive. Regardless of your threshold for houshold income, All children should receive a hot meal at the place they are expected to attend by law.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732029

action: Allow parents to take their children out of school for up to 10 days fine free.
background: We believe that parents should have the ability to take their children out of school for 10 days per year without a fine or a criminal conviction.
additional_details: We also believe that children need breaks sometimes due to stress, anxiety and much more as school can be a tough time for them. Another reason towards this is that families want to go on holiday during term time because of cheaper tickets.

action: Introduce mandatory prison sentences and lifetime bans for animal cruelty
background: Introduce mandatory prison sentences for animal cruelty offences, establish a national animal cruelty register, and implement lifetime bans for convicted offenders. Current penalties are too lenient - many cases result in small fines or suspended sentences that don’t deter repeat offences.
additional_details: Animal cruelty penalties are inadequate and inconsistent. Many serious cases result in small fines or suspended sentences that don’t deter repeat offenders. Animals are vulnerable and defenseless - they cannot escape abuse or seek help. Research shows links between animal cruelty and other serious crimes. The justice system must reflect the severity of these offences. Stronger deterrents through mandatory sentences, lifetime bans, and proper monitoring to protect innocent animals from suffering.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban Private Dog Breeding and Strengthen Penalties for Animal Cruelty
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728177

action: Require all public places to have allergy medication & EpiPens
background: We urge the Government to require all public places, such as cafes, restaurants, shops, businesses and schools, to have first aid boxes which contain EpiPens and allergy medication, as we believe allergic reactions are a life-or-death situation.
additional_details: Millions of children have clinically diagnosed food allergies and millions of adults may be still awaiting NHS allergy testing but cannot access testing due to backlogs. We believe medication must be accessible on hand at all places..

action: Allow all schools to choose their own holiday dates
background: We urge the Government to allow all schools in England to be able to choose their own holiday dates, such as being able to reduce usual holiday dates by one or two weeks and being able to set the equivalent time of holidays at their choice
additional_details: We believe this would enable families to have reasonably priced holidays and not have to pay extortionate prices or taking their children out of education for holidays, as well as allowing all members of school staff to access cheap holidays. We believe by enabling all schools to set their own holiday dates, there would be no disruption to children’s learning and families may be able to afford an affordable holiday.

action: Fund awareness & training for Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia Thrombosis
background: We urge the Government to fund a national campaign to raise awareness of Heparin’s potential side effects, and to fund training programs and continuous medical education which include comprehensive information on the drug’s side effects and their management.
additional_details: This condition, although rare, can be life-threatening and we believe it must be recognised by medical professionals swiftly to prevent unnecessary loss of life. We believe having informed medical personnel and immediate action can be the difference between life and death. We believe it is crucial that protocols for early recognition and treatment of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia thrombosis are established, and that NHS and all medical personnel have an awareness of the drug.

action: Make it law to call a by-election if an MP changes party or becomes independent
background: We ask the Government to introduce legislation requiring any MP who defects to another party, or leaves their party to sit as an independent, to automatically trigger a by-election. Voters should have the right to approve or reject their continued mandate.
additional_details: When MPs change parties or become independents, they are no longer representing the manifesto or values they were elected on. This undermines trust in our democratic system. Constituents should have the right to re-evaluate their support through a by-election, ensuring proper accountability and representation. MPs work for the public — not party leaders or themselves. This goes for every party in Britain, no exceptions. The people must have a voice.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/711480

action: Increase funding & penalties to tackle motorbike & bicycle thieves
background: We believe bike and motorcycle theft is out of control. We urge the Government to increase funding for more police resources, better bike parking facilities, to review insurance cover, and strengthen sentencing against robberies and the online resales of stolen bikes.
additional_details: We believe that some thieves are not being apprehended, and the police need more resources. Many owners face huge losses as insurance may not cover theft away from home. We believe more needs to be done regarding this is serious problem.

action: Require all wildlife rehabilitators to be licensed and regulated
background:
We are calling on the Government to:
 
- Introduce a national licensing scheme for wildlife rehabilitators
 
- Require basic training and access to veterinary support
 
- Implement welfare and hygiene standards
 
- Create a public register of approved rehabilitators
additional_details: We urge the Government to introduce a mandatory national licensing and inspection system for wildlife rehabilitators. This could help ensure consistent standards of welfare, training, hygiene, and accountability in the care of injured or orphaned wild animals. We think the current lack of licensing and regulation can lead to inconsistent animal care and pose a risk to both wildlife and the public.

action: Complete Phase 5 of the South West Rail Resilience Programme.
background: The Government has paused Phase 5 works of the South West Rail Resilience Programme - cliff strengthening of the railway between Dawlish and Teignmouth. If the cliffs collapse on to the railway, the region will incur huge - and avoidable - economic damage.
additional_details:
The cliffs between Dawlish and Teignmouth have long been recognised as the biggest risk to this beautiful but vulnerable railway.

It is the only railway connecting Plymouth including Devonport Dockyard, Torbay and Cornwall to the national network and is of huge economic, social, environmental and strategic importance. A major rockfall would close the railway for weeks, if not months, causing huge economic damage to the region. Reinstating these works will prevent that and help the region grow.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Fund access to tirzepatide on the NHS to help people with PCOS
background: We urge the Government to fund access to tirzepatide on NHS for patients suffering from Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
additional_details: I have personally heard many good things about tirzepatide in potentially helping people with PCOS and I feel PCOS is left behind in comparison to other women's hormonal disorders.

action: Allow 5 days off during school term per academic year!
background: Make councils authorise absence to children for 5 days off school per academic year for family holidays. Families need to be able to go away and have quality family time together and 5 days isnt going to cause any harm! If anything it will boost positivity in the children and a restart for everyone
additional_details:
There is no support for families when it comes to holidays.
You are either on benefits or very low minimum wage job and a week holiday cost during school holidays is ridiculously high,  its not affordable.
Then there is the issue for those that have a working parent/s and cannot get time off work during school holidays so they have no choice but to choose days during school term because its the only time they can get off work!
Families need more support on this matter as its not always by choice
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Allow parents to take their children out of school for 5 school days in a year
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728790

action: Require first aid training for all new drivers
background: We urge the Government to legislate to make first aid training a mandatory part of the driving test process. We believe new drivers should be equipped with basic life-saving skills to improve road safety and provide immediate help in emergencies.
additional_details: Making first aid training mandatory for new drivers could equip thousands with life-saving skills, increasing the chances of survival after road accidents. With more trained individuals on the road, we believe emergency response times can be improved, potentially saving lives before paramedics arrive. We believe this policy could promote public safety, align with road safety goals, empower citizens to act in critical moments, and increase cardiac arrest survival rates.

action: Support SAS Doctors: Allow Us to Work in GP Surgeries
background: We urge the Government to allow experienced SAS doctors to work in GP surgeries. With physician associates already in primary care although they are not fully qualified doctors, it’s only fair to create a safe, supported route for fully qualified SAS doctors to help ease the GP workforce crisis.
additional_details: GP surgeries face major staff shortages, yet experienced SAS doctors are barred from working in primary care. Many have years of clinical expertise, yet can't practice in GP settings while non-doctor physician associates can. We urge the Government to create a safe, supported route for SAS doctors to work in general practice and help ease NHS pressure.
rejection_details: According to the British Medical Association, SAS Doctors can work in GP practices: https://www.bma.org.uk/advice-and-support/international-doctors/life-and-work-in-the-uk/toolkit-for-doctors-new-to-the-uk/doctors-titles-explained

action: Keep the under 9s sex ed ban
background: Government are set to scrap statutory  guidelines for sex education for children under 9 years of age. This will mean a return to teaching children as young as 4 years old about sex education instead of leaving them to be children.
additional_details: We do not need sex education for children under 9 years of age and I want to prevent the Government from scrapping the current statutory guidelines banning sex education for children under 9 years of age.
rejection_details:
There is no statutory ban on sex education for children under 9, and the government is not mandating such education for very young children.

https://educationhub.blog.gov.uk/2024/05/new-rshe-guidance-what-it-means-for-sex-education-lessons-in-schools/

action: Make illegally entering the UK a criminal offence
background: Introduce legislation that makes it a criminal offence to enter the United Kingdom illegally (by any means) with a statutory prison sentence of 10 years. Early release will be available at 5 years for those that agree to return to their country of origin
additional_details:
We need to stem the tide of illegal entry to the United Kingdom and this will only be achieved by criminal prosecution of those that do so.
We must in parallel provide a legal route for genuine refugees and this should be done by having asylum application processes in place at UK Embassies.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. Illegally entering the UK is already a criminal offence.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/powers-and-operational-procedure/irregular-or-unlawful-entry-and-arrival-accessible

If you would like changes to this, you could start a petition about that.

action: Review the sale of over the counter codeine
background: A review could explore the feasibility of a system in which a notification is sent through to the patient's GP surgery. This way, there'd be a better audit trail for how many times someone purchases this medication. This could then be looked at if the patient is buying the medication regularly.
additional_details: I believe the current system for buying over the counter codeine is flawed. It seems easy to buy as I feel there isn't an effective audit trail. I think this could be contributing to opioid addictions. I believe that the pharmacy and the manufacturer have a duty of care to all patients purchasing this medication and that the system should be tightened up in order to help stop the misuse of codeine. I think this could ultimately save lives.

action: Introduce an automatic 2-year sentence for carrying a knife & fund prevention
background: We want the Government to treat knife crime like an emergency. We believe this means tougher sentencing, starting with the introduction of a mandatory 2-year prison sentence for anyone found guilty of carrying a knife.
additional_details: We also want the Government to fund prevention including youth services, education, and local policing. Many people are dying, and we feel it’s getting worse. We believe the current approach isn’t working as many are still carrying knives, possibly thinking they’ll get away with it or get a warning. We need the Government to step in and show that this won’t be tolerated. We believe this policy is about saving lives, making the streets safer, and giving communities like mine hope for change.

action: Designate all of Ukraine as unsafe to return to & accept all visa applications
background: We believe current Home Office policies for visa applications for individuals from the western regions of Ukraine are based on out-of-date information. We believe the war in Ukraine is escalating rapidly and the West is facing heavy attacks similar to other regions.
additional_details: We are concerned about reports of Ukrainian visa applications being declined on the basis that it is safe to return to Western Ukraine, including Ukrainians who may have not resided there before the war. Despite these allegations, the FCDO continues to advise against all but essential travel to those parts of the country. We believe that by recognising all of Ukraine as dangerous, Ukrainian immigrants could have a fair chance at obtaining a visa.

action: Call for a national referendum on Net Zero – a simple yes or no
background: We urge the Government to pass a law on holding a referendum on Net Zero, to give the people the opportunity to say whether they agree with this agenda or not, as we believe it could hurt the UK economy and people’s livelihoods.

action: Change the standard method for assessing local housing need to reflect real need
background: The NPPF insists on a method to calculate housing need that is not fit for purpose. It appears designed just to result in a target housing number in any given area that does not reflect the true, real need based on tangible issues such as population, demographics, etc.
additional_details: Planning is being negatively impacted by this standard method of calculation. This can lead to the wrong level of development in particular areas. Local areas know better than a formula what their local needs actually are.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.  

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to change in the current system.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to change.

action: Manadory arrest and jail for protests that damage, block public, attack public.
background: Write into law that illegal actions during protests such as gluing ones self to motorway or causing property damage or physical attacks on other results in immediate arrest and mandatory jail sentence.
additional_details: The public has been disrupted in going about their business, especially on motorways and emergency services can't get through during illegal actions during protests. Damage has been caused during protests or innocent people hurt. This is not protests but anarchy that the taxpayer or travelling public has to pay for. There seems to be little consequence for the protesters themselves.
rejection_details: Decisions on arrest are a matter for the police, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Support a law in Scotland for a two year sentence for carrying a knife
background: I want the Scottish Government to introduce a mandatory two year prison sentence for anyone caught with a knife. The current laws aren’t tough enough, and stronger action is needed to stop the rising violence in our communities.
additional_details: I want the government to act because knife crime is ruining lives, and current laws aren’t stopping it. A clear, tough sentence would deter offenders, protect the public, and show that carrying a weapon has real consequences.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.  
 
The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here:  

https://www.parliament.scot/chamber-and-committees/committees/current-and-previous-committees/session-6-citizen-participation-and-public-petitions-committee

action: Raise the income tax allowance from £12,570 to £18,000
background: A previous petition asking to raise income tax allowance to £20,000 was debated in May. The government said this would cost them funding to support hospitals, schools and other public institutions which I think sounds fair. I think raising it to £18,000 will leave the govt funding it still needs.
additional_details: In today’s time especially during inflation and higher prices, I think it’s unfair for the allowance to be £12,570. I think it’s extremely unfair and that minimum pay has not risen enough, which may result in Brits having to apply for even 3 jobs. I think this issue has caused some Brits to stop starting families and enjoy livelihood. Everyone should have the opportunity to work and enjoy life

action: Introduce Monthly Public Prime Minister’s Questions (PPMQs) Session for Citizens
background: Introduce a monthly Public Prime Minister’s Questions (PMQs) session where citizens—not MPs—can directly ask the Prime Minister questions, selected through an independent, transparent, and diverse process.
additional_details: Public PMQs would boost democratic engagement by giving ordinary citizens a direct line to the Prime Minister. An independent panel would select a diverse range of questions, asked live in a televised session. This open format ensures voices from all walks of life are heard, holds leadership to account, and builds public trust. It's a bold step toward a more transparent, inclusive democracy—one where power listens to the people.

action: Regulate drones under 250g to protect privacy and prevent misuse
background: Introduce legislation requiring all drones under 250g with cameras to be registered and subject to the same privacy, safety, and misuse laws as larger drones. This includes flight restrictions, penalties for harassment, and protection for private property.
additional_details: Lightweight drones are being misused to spy on people, invade private spaces, and fly over homes without consent. Current laws don’t cover these smaller drones properly, putting the public’s privacy and safety at risk. The law must close this loophole.
rejection_details:
Drones with a camera that weigh less than 250g are already subject to regulations that require the user to register for an Operator ID. You can find more information about registration requirements here: https://www.caa.co.uk/drones/getting-started-with-drones-and-model-aircraft/registering-to-fly-drones-and-model-aircraft/

If you'd like something else, you could start a new petition clearly explaining what it is.

action: Make two seater mobility scooters legal
background: I want the government to make two seater mobility scooters legal. I think two seater mobility scooters could help older people, blind people and people with Parkinson's disease get around more easily.

action: Protect Girls. Teach Women’s Rights and Abuse Prevention in Schools
background: Over 50% of students aged 11–19 report hearing misogynistic remarks weekly. We call on Parliament to require all schools to teach age appropriate modules on women’s rights. Embedding this in RSHE guidance and Ofsted inspections will ensure consistent delivery.
additional_details:
Although RSHE is statutory, it often lacks consistent focus on women’s rights. We urge Parliament to require that all UK schools teach age appropriate modules on:

- Women’s rights and gender equality

- Healthy relationships and consent

- Forms of abuse, including coercive and online abuse

These lessons help prevent violence against women and girls, an obligation under UK and international law. They are also key to the DfE’s preventative education agenda and RSHE review.
rejection_details:
On 16 July 2025, the Secretary of State for Education and Minister for Women and Equalities announced the publication of new statutory guidance for schools on the teaching of Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education.

The Secretary of State for Education and Minister for Women and Equalities stated: 

"The guidance includes significant new content to ensure that RSHE plays its full role in the prevention of violence against women and girls (VAWG), as part of our government mission to halve VAWG.

"This includes a focus on building healthy relationships skills from the start of primary. It includes an emphasis on opening conversations with young people about positive masculinity and femininity, and ensuring that nobody is stigmatised in these conversations. The guidance is clear that teaching about sexual ethics must go beyond teaching about consent, so that young people understand how to act with kindness and respect in all of their relationships."

You can read more about this here: https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-statements/detail/2025-07-16/hcws825#:~:text=The%20guidance%20includes%20significant%20new,in%20all%20of%20their%20relationships.

action: Protect babies lives once heartbeat detectable, except in extreme cases
background: Introduce a bill to protect babies in the womb once a heartbeat is detected. It bans abortion of healthy babies beyond this point, with exceptions for rape, to save the mother’s life, or if the child has a fatal foetal abnormality.
additional_details: Science makes it clear that the tiny being developing in the womb is genetically and biologically human. In 2022 over 250,000 of these human unborn babies were aborted in the UK. Several studies show abortion can harm women emotionally and physically. Therefore, to protect both mother and baby, we believe it is time we reviewed and reformed our abortion law.

action: Fund Specialist Care & Automatic NHS Continuing Care for dementia patients
background: We urge the UK Government to provide funding to ensure every dementia patient stays under specialist care and receives automatic NHS Continuing Healthcare. We think no one should face the heartbreak of dementia without proper care, support, and compassion.
additional_details: Dementia is a cruel disease that affects the whole family. Yet patients may be left in the care of GPs who lack the specialist training to manage their complex needs. Families may be left to cope alone, often without financial or emotional support. We call on the UK Government to provide funding to ensure all dementia patients remain under specialist care and automatically qualify for NHS Continuing Healthcare. Every person facing dementia deserves dignity, expert care, and support.

action: Ban lorries from overtaking each other on dual carriageway and motorways.
background: Pass a law that prevents lorries from overtaking one another on dual carriageways and motorways, following the examples of the Czech Republic and Germany.
additional_details: Lorries (trucks) should not be overtaking each other, as they are very slow (56 mph) and delay our journeys in vehicles such as cars and vans. It is also dangerous, causes traffic jams and increases pollution.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Restrict lorries to the left lane on dual carriageways and motorways 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/706409

action: Make those working in the education sector exempt from high price holidays.
background: I want those working in the education sector to recieve discounts on adult tickets during peak time holidays due to being unable to take time off during term time.
additional_details: As a Teacher I am unable to take Annual Leave during term time. Due to holiday companies boosting their prices during these periods it makes it impossible for many families with those working in education to afford holidays. I am petitioning for those who work in education to recieve discount on adult holiday prices due to not having the choice in taking time off during other parts of the year where prices are lower.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban holiday companies from charging higher prices in the school holidays
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730119

action: Re- open the approved plans for dualling 13 miles between Morpeth and Ellingham
background: Re- open the approved plans for dualling 13 miles between Morpeth and Ellingham in North Northumberland which have been cancelled after years of planning and acquiring property for the dualling to take place. It has to be completed for safely and business reasons.
additional_details: Discuss the matter in detail and approve the planned project - that just need to be started and as quickly as possible - due to volume of traffic and safety. There have be a lot of fatal accidents over the last 5 plus years and people just want the promised project to be completed and help secure this part of major road from England into Scotland for now and in the future. That will help avoid any further fatal accidents on this stretch of main 2 lane road into Scotland.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Govern animal rescues periodically rather reactively
background: In the light of 37 dogs found dead in a "rescue" in Essex, sadly not an isolated incident, periodic welfare checks by authorities such as RSPCA should be a requiremnt. Currently, it's reliant on reports and this is when it's sadly too late. Periodic welfare will ensure their havens are indeed safe.
additional_details: The 37 dogs found dead in Essex in a "rescue" is sadly not an isolated incident. Currently, there are no requirements or registrations needed for a "rescue" to set up and definitely no checks being made while they are operating and devastating discoveries like this can be avoided with welfare checks conducted by authorities to ensure they are following and abiding by the animal welfare act 2006.We are their voice, so let's speak up and ensure the lives of these precious animals are protected
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Introduce Licensing and Regulation for Dog and Cat Rescues to Protect Welfare 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/718660

action: Cap inflation to 3%
background: Currently, inflation has increased to 3.6% while benefits and wages have very small margins of change. Make the government take responsibility- cap inflation to 3% and improve the countries quality of life.
additional_details: The “cost of living crisis” is causing more poverty, negatively affecting peoples quality of life and effecting their mental health. Many people struggle with every day living costs (Food, energy bills etc.), and this appears to only be getting worse.
rejection_details: It's not possible for the Government to cap inflation is a measure of the cost of goods and services. The Government does set the Bank of England a target of 2% for inflation.

action: Why can schools take children on breaks during term time but parents can't?
background: It raises a significant question as to why schools are permitted to organise holidays or outings during term time, yet parents face criminal charges and fines for doing the same with their children.
additional_details: Regulations surrounding school attendance should be relaxed, particularly regarding penalties for parents who choose to take their children out of school for short breaks or day trips during term time. Imposing fines and criminal records for such actions is excessive, especially when these occurrences are infrequent and unlikely to significantly impact a child's education. A few days away from the classroom each year can provide valuable family experiences without detrimental effects on learning
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may wish to sign the following:

Stop fines for taking children out of school on holiday
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727960

Allow parents to take their children out of school for 5 school days in a year
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728790

action: Paid menstrual leave for endometriosis and adenomyosis
background: Follow in both Spain and Portugals footsteps by giving women an extra 3 day full paid sick leave every month when they are diagnosed with either endometriosis or adenomyosis
additional_details:
Endometriosis and adenomyosis are know to cause severe and debilitating symptoms and pain which largely impact daily life and for many women are constant.  They are more than just a bad period, And  during a period the pain and other symptoms can increase ato the point of being bed bound, hospital visits, fainting and migranes to name just a few symptoms.  

We should give these women additional sick leave so when the symptoms are at their worse they can rest and not worry about missing work.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Introduce Statutory Menstrual Leave for People with Endometriosis & Adenomyosis
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732342

action: Call for general election due to no confidence
background: Immediately start a general election.
additional_details: The public have lost all confidence in the current government, this is due to numerous U turns, broken promises and a weak prime minister. We were promised a dream and sold down the river. If the government has any shred of integrity left they will make way for a stronger government to take over and sort this country out.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Require accessible social housing to be available to disabled people of any age
background: Require social housing providers to allow all disabled people to access ground-floor flats/bungalows blocks, regardless of age.
additional_details: In parts of the country, young disabled adults face unfair barriers to ground-floor social housing. We urge the Government to require all disabled people, regardless of age, to be able to access ground-floor or accessible social housing.

action: Change the right to roam cat law.
background: To make cat owners responsible. Owning any pet, regardless of species should not be taken lightly. The right to roam law for cats is drastically outdated.
additional_details: Cats suffer illnesses, parasite infestation, accidents and at times death, keeping them contained on the owners own property is not "unfair" or "cruel" it is showing responsibility and care for the animal. Cats are also the cause of a very large decline in wildlife, wild birds in particular. Cats kill between 40 - 70 million birds annually in the UK.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Remove the ‘right to roam’ status applicable to domesticated cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725658

action: Allow Dental Therapist & Hygienist roles (3213) to be filled by migrant workers
background: We call on the government to reverse the decision to classify SOC code 3213 as below RQF Level 6, so that employers can still offer sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa route. If NHS practices are unable to continue to fill vacancies with migrant workers, services may suffer drastically.
additional_details: When RQF Level 6 was previously a requirement for a working visa, it was possible to sponsor these roles under the equivalent SOC code (2219). We think there is no justification to reclassify these occupations at a lower level within the Immigration Rules.

action: Ban Cyclists from Pavements, Introduce Strict Fines for Road Rule Infringements
background: Ban cycling on pedestrian pavements unless marked shared-use introduce fines for cyclists who break road laws such as riding through red lights, riding without lights or endangering pedestrians. Enforce existing laws, support local authorities launch a public awareness campaign on pedestrian safety
additional_details: Many pedestrians, especially the elderly, disabled, or those with children, feel unsafe due to cyclists riding on pavements. Though this is already illegal, enforcement is weak. Dangerous cycling behaviour like running red lights or riding without lights goes unpunished. As cycling increases, rules must be enforced to protect vulnerable pedestrians. We need fines, education, and stronger enforcement to ensure safer shared spaces.
rejection_details:
Cyclists can be fined for cycling on the pavement and must comply with the Road Traffic Act.

You can find more information here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/crime-and-policing-bill-2025-factsheets/crime-and-policing-bill-dangerous-cycling-offences-factsheet

action: Change to way house purchases are made
background: The whole process of purchasing a house is slow and overly bureaucratic. This needs to be streamlined with less emphasis on solicitors who are slow and drag out the process to maximise their fees.
additional_details: This would make purchasing homes easier and quicker. Offers need to be subject to penalty (as in other parts of the UK) if people just change their mind. A deposit at the time of offer would focus buyers and ensure serious purchases only. This would raise more money for the government because more sales would be made.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, such as changing the law around the transfer of home ownership, or setting out how you would like to see the process improved.

Introduce conveyancing laws similar to those in Scotland, across England & Wales 
 https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/709395

action: Reduce the working week for NHS Staff over 60
background: Working in the National Health Service can be both physically demanding and mentally stressful, particularly for those working full-time.  The reality is that many experienced staff members are retiring early because they cannot withstand the pressure.
additional_details: I strongly believe that introducing a reduced working week for NHS staff aged over 60 would encourage valuable and experienced personnel to stay longer in their roles, rather than opting for early retirement. A shorter workweek for these invaluable workers could significantly improve their quality of life while ensuring they remain a pivotal part of the healthcare system. By reducing their weekly hours but maintaining their current pay, we not only value their years of dedication and experience, but also mitigate the staffing shortages that are plaguing the NHS.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
Decisions about staff working hours are a matter for the NHS, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Ban the selling of peanuts from stalls in public areas
background: Approximately 1 in 50 children in the UK have a peanut allergy. Why does the UK still allow the most common allergen to be sold from stalls in public places? Peanuts can cause reactions that we think are completely preventable if we just stop peanuts from being sold in public spaces.
additional_details: Steam or smoke from cooking nuts on roasted peanut and almond stalls can carry enough protein to cause symptoms in some individuals. I have seen these stalls in public places, such as in front of an extremely popular museum for children.

action: Enforce existing laws to stop illegal gambling scams on Westminster Bridge
background: Deploy regular police patrols on Westminster Bridge to crack down on illegal gambling scams. Prosecute scammers who assault or intimidate witnesses. Coordinate with City of Westminster Council to implement deterrent measures and protect tourists from organized criminal gangs.
additional_details: Westminster Bridge hosts aggressive scamming operations that target tourists with illegal gambling tricks. When members of the public try to film these crimes, they face assault and intimidation. This damages London's reputation, makes visitors feel unsafe, and allows organized criminals to operate with impunity. Increased enforcement would protect tourists, support legitimate businesses, and uphold the rule of law in one of London's most visible locations.
rejection_details:
You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/
