action: Protect Family Farms and Family Businesses from Inheritance Tax Reform
background: An autumn vote is looming. We urgently call on the UK Government to halt or amend inheritance tax changes that threaten family-run farms and rural businesses, the heart of our rural communities. These reforms could inflict irreparable harm on rural heritage and food security.
additional_details: For generations, small farms have fed Britain and preserved our countryside. But removing Agricultural Property Relief (APR) on tenanted farmland and slashing Business Property Relief (BPR) for family businesses will saddle families with unaffordable 20% inheritance tax. Many will be forced to sell farmland or businesses held for centuries just to pay tax. Once a family farm or business is broken up, its legacy and local jobs vanish, weakening rural heritage and undermining our food security.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.  

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do, as we're not sure whether you would like the Government to stop or amend the changes to APR & BPR.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do. 

You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a 12 month amnesty on APR & BPR proposals: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721014

action: Make diplomatic representations to Israel to allow UK journalists to enter Gaza
background: Around 60,000 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since 2023 with at least 232 Gazan journalists killed according to Brown University Costs of War report. We are concerned UK journalists can’t get into Gaza. We urge the Government to make representations to Israel to allow UK journalists into Gaza
additional_details: We believe press freedom is a universal right, and that banning foreign media is deeply unethical. We feel the situation isn’t getting any better – many Gazans are recording it on social media. Blackouts occur which make it harder to report. We believe the Government and Parliament has a duty to help journalists capture the truth to the general public. We believe impartiality can’t exist if the truth is unknown.

action: Make it a legal requirement for wages to increase in line with inflation yearly
background: Protect the value of workers salaries by making it a legal requirement that all employers increase salary and hourly wage, at the minimum, in line with inflation annually.
additional_details: Because workers are often the ones most affected by budget cuts with promotions, pay rises and bonuses used to increase performance and then cut to save margin. If pay rises are not given in line with inflation then workers can essentially take pay cuts to stay in positions over a year. Money is worth what it can afford individuals and that should be protected.

action: Fund 30 hours of childcare per week for student nurses and midwives
background: We want the government to make it possible for student nurses and midwives to study and fund 30 hours of free childcare per week. We have to do long placement hours.
additional_details: We feel the learning support fund does not cover childcare. Student nurses can struggle to find paid work due to long placement shifts.

action: Make it a requirement for hotels to have ceiling hoists in accessible rooms
background: There are very few hotels in the whole of the UK that have ceiling hoists. This means non-ambulatory people can't go on holiday or rely on hotels as temp accommodation. We think this needs to change. Gov need to make it a requirement for hotels to include a ceiling hoist in accessible rooms
additional_details: Many people requiring temporary or emergency accommodation are not able to stay in a local hotel due to the lack of ceiling hoists. They may have to travel several hours between their work and the nearest accessible hotel. It also means if non-ambulatory people wanted to holiday in UK they cannot. We believe this needs to change so disabled people can have the same quality of life as non-disabled.

action: Unfair Dismissal Protections Should Start from Day One
background: We are calling on the government to introduce day-one protections against unfair dismissal. We think that no one should be left vulnerable to being treated unfairly just because they haven’t hit an arbitrary time limit.
additional_details: In the UK, you must work for 2 years before you're protected against unfair dismissal. That means if you're fired after just a few months, no matter how unjust, you have little to no legal protection. We think this outdated law leaves millions, especially new starters and temps, unprotected. In today's unstable job market, we think this must change. We think everyone deserves fairness from day one. Sign this petition to demand day-one protection, because we believe it could happen to anyone.

action: Regulate the use of brain-computer interfaces
background: We ask the UK Government to introduce urgent legal safeguards to the use of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), neural interfaces, or related neurotechnologies on individuals.
additional_details:
There are currently no regulations on the use of BCI systems — which may be capable of influencing, recording, or interpreting brain activity. Without clear legislation, we think individuals are vulnerable to potential misuse by both private and state actors.
This includes concerns about potential covert experimentation, neural surveillance, or unauthorised cognitive data access— all of which, we believe, could raise serious ethical and human rights implications.

action: Online age checks: do not use personal information & third party perform checks
background:
1) Prevent social media from requesting personal information (bank details and face ID).
 
2) Require age checks to be performed by a secure third party, to prevent the storage of personal information by unsecured websites.
additional_details:
We think social media's encroaching invasion of privacy is dangerous for both adults and children. We think being asked to provide your bank details, credit history, face, or ID is a danger to the security of all internet users, but especially to children.
 
We think it is vital that new legislation does not make it impossible to navigate the internet anonymously, both for the sake of safety, but also for the sake of freedom of speech.

action: Launch a National Inquiry into the MoD’s Afghan Data Breach and Its Consequences
background: The government must launch a full public inquiry into the Afghanistan data leak that exposed the personal details of thousands of Afghans who worked with the UK.
additional_details: This catastrophic breach put lives at risk, forced a secret £850 million evacuation scheme, and was hidden from the public under a superinjunction. We believe an inquiry is vital to establish how this happened, responsibility for this, what lessons were learned (if any), and to ensure full transparency over the use of public money and national security failings. We owe it to those Afghans and to the British public.

action: Prevent planning for  building and access through Elsbert Drive Bristol
background: Prevent planning for building as access is required which would block our road of 30 retirement bungalows causing congestion .Also blocking our views dust and contamination from works. Wildlife destroyed over 20 types including starlings.
additional_details: Green Belt Land choose a moe appropriate place to build.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. 
 
Decisions about local planning decisions are a matter for the relevant local authority, not the UK Government or Parliament. 
 
You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Ban the sale of second-hand power tools online & at car boot sales
background: We believe tool theft is very common and not enough is being done to prevent thieves profiting from stolen tools. We urge the Government to ban the sale of second-hand power tools to reduce thieves benefiting and profiting. We believe this could reduce the number of vehicles broken into.
additional_details: Many trades are suffering from financial difficulty due to the loss of tools and costs to repair vans. Millions of pounds worth of tools were stolen in the UK last year.

action: To create more jobs for youth (age 16)
background: We would like the Government to create more jobs for the youth to support the youth for skills that will be needed for the future.
additional_details: We would want the Government to make more jobs as the youth needs to learn skills of working for the future but as of right now,there  isn’t much of a choice for jobs for the youth widening the jobs for the youth may help to create a baseline for the youth for there future,  the youth may want to work more and also help create skills for the future to set them for the future and create a path for the future.

action: To serve at least 1 year in the armed forces before been classed as a veteran
background: Currently you can serve 24 hours as a recruit and class yourself as a veteran. We think this is insulting to those that serve longer.
additional_details: Veterans may be able to access medical treatment quicker along with a host of other benefits. We think that serving 1 day does not make you a veteran.

action: Require private nurseries to pay sick pay for employees at full wage
background: As practitioners working first hand with early years children, we sometimes pick up sickness bugs, conjunctivitis and flu. We can lose pay for being off sick and it can effect our Bradford score when the germs may have been passed to us while doing our jobs.
additional_details: I think we need more support and if we are ill from a bug that’s going around the workplace, the company should cover our sick pay at the same rate as our wages. I think that the staff are the heart of most work places.

action: Bring back the right to buy discount
background: I want the government to reinstate full Right to Buy discounts for long-term council and housing association tenants, making homeownership more affordable and giving renters a fair chance to buy the homes they’ve built their lives in.
additional_details: Many long-term tenants have paid rent for years and looked after their homes, yet they are now priced out of buying them because the Right to Buy discount has been reduced or removed. This policy helped millions achieve homeownership and financial stability. Bringing it back would give hardworking renters a fair chance to own the homes they’ve built their lives in, promote stronger communities, and make the housing market fairer and more accessible for everyone.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Bring back full Right to buy discount & give notice of future changes
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726223

action: Enforce Payments for UK Creative Professionals and Freelancers within 30 Days
background:
Introduce and enforce mandatory maximum payment terms for contracts within the creative industries, no longer than 30 days.
 
Implement effective penalties for businesses that (consistently) fail to adhere to these terms.
 
Support creatives to easily dispute and recover overdue payments
additional_details:
We think the payment practices within the creative industries in the UK are unsustainable for most creative professionals. They may frequently experience payment terms of 90-180+ days after invoicing the client.
 
This delay in payment and lack of penalties for late payers, creates financial instability.
 
We think the Government should protect the livelihoods of creatives, foster a healthier and more sustainable economy and ensure that those who drive one of our most successful sectors are paid fairly and promptly.

action: Review the family court system for removing children from their guardian
background: We urge the Government to launch a review of the family court system in England and Wales, and the guidance on when a child should be removed from there guardian.
additional_details: We are concerned that children could be removed from safe, loving homes. We feel children need their voices better heard and their welfare made paramount. We believe removing children from their mothers especially could cause significant trauma and lifelong problems. We believe a child's bond with their mother should be protected first.

action: Stop Public Bailouts of Water Companies and Nationalise the Water Industry
background: The Government must not use taxpayer money to bail out failing water firms like Thames Water. Decades of private failure and raw sewage in our waters demand action: bring the industry back into public hands and make it accountable to the citizens of the UK.
additional_details: We call on the UK Government to stop using public money to bail out failing private water companies, including Thames Water. Instead of rewarding mismanagement, the water industry should return to public ownership to ensure long-term investment, transparency, and clean water. The public should not pay for decades of failure or rising bills that benefit shareholders, while raw sewage continues to be pumped into our waterways, putting public health at risk.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727463

action: Add Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) patients to NHS Prescription Fee Exemption
background: IBD is a lifelong, incurable condition like Crohn’s and Colitis that causes chronic inflammation in the gut. It’s not currently exempt from NHS prescription fees, placing financial strain on patients who need constant treatment. Many must choose between daily essentials and vital medication.
additional_details: IBD patients often take immunosuppressants, increasing their risk of infections and need for antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals. Alongside long-term meds, they may need short-term treatments like iron for anaemia, pain relief, skin care, and GI support. Managing IBD involves multiple ongoing prescriptions, highlighting the need for NHS prescription fee exemption to ease financial strain and ensure consistent access to vital care.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Fund free prescriptions for people living with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725486

action: Introduce specific safeguarding regulation for extracurricular activities
background: Introduce safeguarding legislation and regulation for extracurricular activities. Ensure all staff and volunteers are trained, vetted, and members of an accredited awarding, governing or regulated body to safeguard vulnerable individuals.
additional_details: Children and vulnerable adults can face safeguarding risks in extracurricular activities due to a lack of specific legislation. These environments often operate without specific regulation or oversight. Requiring coaches, teachers, clubs and schools to be members of an accredited body would help establish minimum safeguarding standards.

action: The British Public have been betrayed, it is time for a vote of no confidence.
background: The UK faces rising public fury over lies, policy failures, from the Chagos deal and farming tax reforms, to Labour’s U-turns, migrant welfare strain, and secretive resettlements. With trust broken and 62% fearing national decline, a no-confidence motion is now a democratic necessity.
additional_details: A vote of no confidence must be debated due to widespread public outrage over two tier policing, broken promises, policy failures, and a collapse in trust. From the betrayal in Chagos to punishing farmers, U-turns on manifesto pledges, secretive immigration policies, and welfare cuts, 62% of the public now say the UK is on the wrong path. Parliament must act. Parliament is there to discuss the will and welfare of the public, this motion of no confidence is needed to restore public trust.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for Ministers to be sacked or for a vote of no confidence. 
 
If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

action: Make Carbohydrate content mandatory on restaurant and pub menus.
background: Require all restaurants, café's and pubs with 250+ employees to clearly display carbohydrate information on menus, alongside calories and Allergens.
additional_details:
Carbohydrate counting is essential for safe insulin dosing for many people with Type 1 Diabetes. Without this information, eating out can become dangerous. Many menus already include calories and allergens - carbs can be equally essential for those managing diabetes.

Having carbohydrates on the menus may not only make eating out safer for those with diabetes, but could also relieve stress on the NHS. Carb counting correctly can be essential to people keep glucose levels in range.

action: Require companies to clearly display a contact section with email & phone number
background: Make it a legal requirement for all UK companies to clearly display a “Contact Us” section with a working UK telephone number and email address on both their website and mobile app, so customers can easily get support from a real person when needed.
additional_details: We feel many companies make it hard to contact them, hiding contact details behind bots or buried menus. This can leave people - especially the elderly, disabled, or those less tech-savvy - frustrated and unsupported when things go wrong. Everyone deserves access to real help. We think clear contact info can help build trust, fairness, and accountability.

action: Apologize for the repatriation of pregnant Irish women from the UK to Ireland
background: I would like the government to apologize for the historic categorization by British authorities of pregnant Irish women as PFI, and the involvement of UK authorities in the deportation of these women to Ireland.
additional_details: The system of categorizing Irish women as 'pregnant from Ireland' and the discriminatory treatment of these women and their children in terms of access to healthcare and the welfare system in the UK was an abuse of their human rights. Their deportation often resulted in them being incarcerated in a cruel system of mother and baby homes in Ireland and the separation of women from their children.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Apologise to Irish women and their children who were repatriated to Ireland
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731382

action: Waive UK visa fees for overseas teachers coming to work in the UK
background: We believe the UK’s education sector is in the grip of a significant recruitment and retention crisis. Not all students have the subject specialists they deserve. We believe overseas teachers play a vital role in bolstering our falling teacher numbers; yet may be expected to pay to do so.
additional_details: We believe that any overseas teacher employed in the UK state education sector should have their annual working visa fees waived once their employment status is confirmed. Without their labour, we believe our education system would be in an even greater crisis. We believe they should not have to pay for the privilege of working here and educating our children and young people in the state sector. For many overseas teachers these fees cause financial hardship.

action: Label the Cruelty
background:
Introduce mandatory front-of-pack labels on all products tested on animals
Close the legal loopholes that allow animal testing to continue behind the scenes, particularly in supply chains
Invest in cruelty-free research and commit to a national plan to phase out animal testing
additional_details: Animal suffering should never be hidden. Let’s bring honesty to the label and lgive people the power to choose kindness.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Require clearer labelling of animal-derived ingredients
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733222

action: A change in UK law regarding planning priorities affecting the green belt
background: To enact in law that green belt development applications will be refused if there is no quantifiable & demonstrable local housing need or where brown/grey site alternatives are available within reasonable commuting distance; with the mandatory prioritisation of grey/brown field land over green belt
additional_details: The county in which I live, Surrey, has been overwhelmed by green belt planning applications since green belt was de-proritised by government, leaving a wide range of brown and grey belt opportunities untouched. This is not surprising: of course developers would prefer a virgin site in a beautiful area over something less attractive and perhaps requiring more work. As the tower blocks of the 1960s blighted lives, so too would the wholesale development of green belt land
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Prohibit and stop any building on our Green Belt Land 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724330

action: Add Asthma to NHS Prescription Charge Exemption List
background: The British government should make asthma medications like Fostair available for free, as they are essential and often lifesaving for those living with chronic respiratory conditions.
additional_details: Currently, a single prescription can cost around £80, placing a financial burden on people who rely on it daily to manage their health. The NHS is moving away from prescribing salbutamol due to environmental concerns, but the new recommended alternatives such as Fostair are significantly more expensive for patients paying out of pocket and often come with a short shelf life, making them even less accessible. No one should be forced to ration their medication or risk their health because of cost.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726704

action: Don’t lower the voting age to 16.
background: Do not proceed with plans to lower the voting age to 16 and keep it at 18.
additional_details: Many 16-17 year olds lack the maturity to vote in elections. They are also far more prone to radicalisation on social media. Many also lack enough political education to make an informed vote. If any member of the cabinet were to spend some time with a Year 11 class they would understand this.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Don't lower the voting age to 16
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733604

We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733679

action: Introduce mandatory political education for 14-17 year olds (KS4/5)
background: The government should introduce basic political education for 16-17 year olds (KS4/5) who have recently gotten the vote, so they may be informed when voting. Basic education includes: The voting system (FPTP), The Parties (minor and major), Functions of Parliament. Can take place with PSHE.
additional_details: We live in an era of disinformation and misinformation where opinions have become more prevalent than fact in elections. The only way to combat this, is to arm the new 16-17 years old voters with the knowledge of our political system, allowing them to resist the influences of social media and propaganda and focus on their own political interests when voting; Giving them the freedom to choose wisely as well as the incentive to carry on voting.
rejection_details:
Schools are already required to teach citizenship as part of the secondary national curriculum.

The citizenship curriculum includes content on how the United Kingdom is governed, its political system and how citizens participate actively in its democratic systems of government.

You can read the citizenship programmes of study for secondary school here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study-for-key-stages-3-and-4

If you would like to make a change to the current arrangements, you can start a petition setting out clearly what you would like to change, such as submitting a petition about making politics a core specific subject.

action: Pass a bill which holds political parties accountable for their promises.
background: A bill which requires parties to officially define their manifesto before general elections in a legally binding document. A new regulatory body established of impartial authority to determine whether governments have breached said document. In emergency situations an appeal may be made to alter.
additional_details: It has become far too easy for parties to lie to the people about what they will do after being elected with no real consequences for doing so. This situation renders our democratic system significantly compromised as we the people no longer have a say in what happens to our country, our vote becomes uniformed, and hence void. This bill will mean the power is given back to the people and their vote will once again stand for what they believe it to stand for, rather than an ulterior manifesto.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724417

action: Fund routine breast cancer screening from age 40 – early detection saves lives.
background: We want the government to lower the age of routine breast cancer screening in England from 50 to 40. The NHS Breast Screening Programme should offer regular mammograms to all women aged 40 and over to improve early detection and reduce late-stage diagnoses.
additional_details:
Thousands of women under 50 are diagnosed with breast cancer every year in the UK. Many are caught late because they fall outside the current NHS screening age range of 50–71.

Early detection saves lives, reduces the need for aggressive treatments such as mastectomy and chemotherapy, and lowers the long-term burden on NHS services.

Lowering the screening age to 40 would save lives, improve outcomes, and bring the UK in line with screening policies in other countries.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/720626

action: Make it illegal for 18+ adults to have sex with under 18s
background: Keep the legal age of consent at 16, but make it illegal for adults aged 18 or over to have sexual activity with anyone under 18. This could protect minors from grooming and adult exploitation while still allowing legal relationships between peers aged 16–17.
additional_details: We do not think that adults aged 18 or over should be allowed to have sex with anyone under 18. Although the age of consent is 16, 16–17-year-olds are still developing emotionally and mentally, and can be more vulnerable to grooming, coercion, and manipulation by adults. We believe this change could improve protection for teenagers, and align the law with existing safeguarding standards used in education and youth services.

action: Change the Law so you don’t get taxed on tips in hospitality
background: I think it’s an absolute disgrace that we should get taxed on our tips that customers have have us because of good service
additional_details: I want the government to abolish the law so we don’t get taxed on them anymore

action: Stop the persecution of older drivers.
background:
Stop the unfair proposed changes to the renewal of the over 70s drivers license.
The dangerous drivers on the UK roads are not the elderly but, the younger irresponsible people. 
They are the ones more likely to disregard the speed limit and othe highway code rules.
additional_details:
The proposed changes will require pensioners to pay privately for medical reports from GPs and opticians. Money that the majority can ill afford. 
For many the car is their only means of travel .
The only way to  visit family and friends or to attend appointments. 
It would take me hours on various buses to get to hospital should the need arise. A journey I could take in the car in 45 minutes. Without breaking any rules of the road
rejection_details:

action: Restrict access to NHS services to UK legal residents & taxpayers only.
background: Prohibit access to NHS services to anyone who is not a UK born citizen, or legal tax-paying foreigner who have paid into the system for a prescribed number of years - such as 5.This restriction to access would include illegal migrants, refugees & asylum seekers, & those in the UK on temporary visas
additional_details: The NHS is funded by UK residents. Its primary function should be to provide healthcare to those who contribute to the system. Offering free NHS services to illegal migrants, asylum seekers & non-tax paying foreigners undermines this principle. It is burdening a system that is already under immense strain with long waiting lists, understaffed facilities & funding shortages. It deprives essential resources from Britons who should be prioritised but who struggle to obtain quality & timely medical care as a result.
rejection_details:

Only allow UK citizens or residents with settled status to use the NHS

action: Don't lower the voting age to 16
background: We urge the Government not to extend the voting franchise to 16 and 17 year olds in all UK elections, including general elections. We think that the voting age should exist in line with the age of adulthood.
additional_details: We think the proposed changes to the voting age would be detrimental to democracy. We think 16 and 17 year olds are unlikely to have a wide range of experiences. Under law, they are deemed not mature or responsible enough to purchase alcohol, cigarettes, buy a lottery ticket, or marry. Many sixteen year olds may not be in employment, with many still at school. We think the proposed changes to the voting age would be arbitrary, unnecessary and could be harmful to democracy.

action: Amend the Party Wall Act 1996 to give adjoining owners stronger legal protection
background: Amend the Party Wall Act 1996 by introducing penalties such as fines for any breaches, grant local authorities powers to enforce compliance, create an affordable dispute tribunal, and establish a compensation scheme to protect any adjoining owners affected by unlawful or damaging works.
additional_details: We think the Party Wall etc. Act 1996 fails to protect adjoining owners when building owners ignore the rules. There is no enforcement procedure within the Act, and no automatic fines or right to stop potentially unlawful works. We believe this leaves innocent homeowners exposed to trespass, structural damage, and weather ingress, with no option but costly legal action to protect their property. In our view, the law unfairly favours those doing the work and urgently needs reform to ensure adjoining owners are properly safeguarded.

action: No more tax rises in this Parliament
background: We think the tax rises in the 2024 Autumn budget have been self-defeating, with unemployment rising. We think they will likely result in less tax revenue and lower growth. We believe that tax payers of all degrees pay enough already and the government needs to spend the money more wisely.

action: extend the free train fare for over 60`s in London to the rest of the UK.
background: Why cant the rest of the country have the same free travel as London for its senior citizens. There could be a National Transport Policy for senior citizens with photographic ID cards to prevent fraud.
additional_details: The current London free public transport for senior citizens is unfair to the rest of the population just because they live outside of London Boroughs. As well as being financially beneficial for the over 60`s nationally, it would remove a lot of vehicles off the roads and improve use of public transport, that the Governments have continually asked the public to do

action: Raise the voting age back up to 18

action: Cap the cost of bottled water in airports
background:
Water is a basic human right.
We think travellers in airports should not have to pay for bottled water at inflated prices.

action: Reform of petitions to include creating Citizens’ Assemblies at 500k signatures
background: Add a new mechanism to petitions so at 500k signatures and 5% of voters in at least five UK regions, it triggers creation of a Citizens’ Assembly empowered to deliberate, recommend policy, or call a binding referendum. Legal compliance check of the petition request before an Assembly is set up.
additional_details:
I believe this reform would increase accountability, encourage civic participation, and ensure petitions cannot be dismissed without due consideration. I think it would also be safeguarded against misuse through regional thresholds, legal review, and Citizens' Assemblies. 
 
I think the current system lacks democratic weight and that petitions, even with mass support, are often ignored.
 
I urge the government to strengthen public trust in democracy by making the petition process more participatory, representative, and effective.

action: Change School Uniform policies to be more relevant to working class standards.
background: Public high schools have set the standard of uniform too high claiming it is flexible, encourages identity and to prepares the children for the work place, however it is not relevant attire to most working class jobs, only a small amount of careers require such constrictive clothing
additional_details: Not many jobs require a person to wear such rigid uniform of blazers, jumpers, ties etc. These are costly and irrelevant to working class families. A higher % of children from public schools will end up in service-related industries or civil servant roles, which require a more reasonable, comfortable, flexible uniform such as Cargo pants, polo shirt, or smart casual. Uniforms stifle identity and individualism, forcing conformity during crucial years of self-discovery and expression.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/717040

action: Call for the Prime Minister to Resign Due to Loss of Public Confidence
background: We want Parliament to publicly acknowledge the growing loss of public confidence in the Prime Minister and urge him to resign from office.

action: Review extended determinate sentencing: reductions for rehabilitated prisoners
background: We'd like Government to review the use of extended determinate sentences (EDS) and consider allowing sentence reductions for prisoners who’ve completed their custodial term while demonstrating excellent behaviour and real rehabilitation.
additional_details:
We think the system should recognise reform and offer early release options.

We believe that the current system is unjust and that EDS prisoners who’ve done everything right — reformed, followed their sentence plan, behaved well — may still face long, fixed sentences. We think that they’re ready to rejoin society but are denied the same chances others get, and that their reform should be recognised and rewarded. In our view, this change would bring fairness, help reduce reoffending and support safer communities. We believe these prisoners are unlikely to face recall as they have fought for their release and that ultimately this could ease prison congestion.

action: We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds
background: We call on the government to hold a national referendum before extending voting rights to 16 and 17-year-olds in general elections.
additional_details:
We think this is a profound change to the democratic franchise, such a significant constitutional reform should not be without the direct consent of the British people.
 
We think the right to vote is one of the most consequential aspects of citizenship and expanding it to a new age group should not be decided solely by politicians, but by the electorate itself in a fair and open referendum.
 
The UK has held referendums on major democratic reforms, such as devolution (1997), the Alternative Vote (2011), and Scottish independence (2014). We think changing the voting age is no less significant and deserves the same public scrutiny.

action: Review of Gender Identity and LGBT Education in Schools
background: Initiate a formal review of how gender identity and LGBT content is introduced and taught in state-funded schools.
additional_details:
This should look at age-appropriateness in the delivery of such content, aligned with children’s developmental stages & educational guidelines. 
 
We also want this review to look at mandating that parents & guardians are consulted prior to the inclusion of such topics in the curriculum, and expanded rights to withdraw their child from all sessions deemed not suitable. 
 
We want development of balanced educational content.

This government was elected on a relatively small vote share and their views on the age of voting may not be reflective of the wider population. 

A referendum will deliver a clear result and build national consensus.

additional_details: Parent & Child bays are often misused, causing stress and safety risks for families needing space for car seats and prams. action: Implement policies to help provide affordable housing for all
background: We want our government to prioritise construction of affordable housing and improved affordability of existing housing so it's genuinely affordable for all. High housing costs, including rent and mortgages, are making it hard for many people and families to secure stable, safe, affordable homes.
additional_details:
We call for policies that incentivise the development of diverse housing options at prices accessible to those with moderate and low incomes. We see this as including exploring initiatives like Rent Control, Inclusionary Zoning in new developments and increased funding for Social Housing programs.
 
We believe that access to affordable housing is a fundamental human right, crucial for the wellbeing of our community and that it is time for action to ensure that everyone has a place to call home.

action: Reduce age limit for holding a full driving licence to 16 with restrictions

We think requiring this simple disclosure would promote transparency, reduce inequality in the job application process, and allow both employers and candidates to engage more efficiently and fairly.

action: Make the Industrial Strategy Advisory Council a Statutory Body

additional_details: While we welcome the Government’s new Industrial Strategy (2025) and its identification of key growth sectors, we think effective delivery requires stronger governance, clearer sectoral focus, and long-term coordination across skills, energy, infrastructure, and innovation policy.  We think a reformed ISAC must be empowered and have interdepartmental support to provide that as compared with Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry.

action: Make the Armed Forces pension tax free
background: Make the Armed Forces pension at age 60 tax free.
additional_details: We think this would balance out what we see as an injustice.
government_response_summary: The government hugely values the service of our armed forces but currently has no plans to make Armed Forces pensions tax free at age 60
government_response_body: We are profoundly grateful for the service of members of our armed forces, and therefore it is only right that they are entitled to a pension that ensures dignity in retirement. Members of the Armed Forces Pension Schemes do not have to pay contributions to their pension schemes. These are the only public service pension schemes that are non-contributory.   The government currently has no plans to make Armed Forces pensions tax free at age 60. The Armed Forces Pension Scheme provides tax-free lump sums to members on retirement. Other pension payments from the Armed Forces Pension Scheme are treated as taxable income under UK tax law. This tax treatment reflects the fact that pensions are forms of deferred income and as such are taxable. This same tax treatment applies to payments from all occupational pension schemes.  HM Treasury

action: Scrap legal aid for all convicted criminals and recent immigrants
background: Scrap all legal aid for all immigrants and convicted criminals. We think legal aid should not be available for immigrants who have paid less than 15 years tax and that repeat offenders should not have access.

action: Reforming the electrical industry to establish it as a professional sector
background:
Electrical Industry Regulatory Proposal

Limit public sales of electrical materials to basic items (e.g., sockets, switches, accessories).

Only accredited/qualified electricians may carry out electrical installations.

Introduce nationally recognized installer ID cards as proof of competence
additional_details:
Call for Electrical Industry Reform

Despite the introduction of Part P to improve domestic electrical safety, accreditation bodies have failed to enforce compliance effectively. A major body was recently fined by ACAS for inadequate assessments, reflecting deeper industry issues.

Unregistered electrical work continues to endanger lives and property. A stricter, centralized system—like New Zealand’s—is urgently needed to raise safety standards and remove rogue operators.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/713910

action: Lower the Age of Routine Mammograms to 40 Years Old
background: Breast Cancer is the most common cancer in women in the UK.  I was diagnosed at 45 years old.  The routine mammogram is from 50 to 70 years.  This NHS screening programme was set in 1988 and the lower age for being eligible has not been reviewed despite more and more younger women being diagnosed.
additional_details:
The Government needs to revisit and review the guidelines for Mammogram Screening to include women from 40 years old.  The earlier we detect, the better the prognosis and the better the survival rate.
Breast Cancer screening saves lives and needs to be available to more women.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/720626

action: Set minimum number of citizenship lesson hours, increase resources & training
background: We think the government should strengthen Citizenship education in secondary schools including a mandatory minimum number of teaching hours, alongside increased resources and teacher training, to give students the best chance to leave school politically informed and confident to vote.
additional_details: With plans to lower the voting age to 16, we believe effective political education is more urgent than ever. Research shows that knowledge increases participation but only 1 in 3 students recall learning about politics at school in the last year. Additionally, we think that as children’s risk of exposure to extremist and harmful content online increases, schools should provide regular, safe opportunities to discuss and debate political parties, ideologies, and current affairs in the classroom.

action: Reform the UK Driving Test Booking System
background: Learner drivers are struggling to book practical driving tests. Slots are often unavailable for months. Bots and third-party apps are abusing the system, making access unfair.
additional_details:
Increase driving test availability and examiner capacity.

Introduce measures to prevent bots and automated rescheduling tools from abusing the system.

Improve transparency and fairness in the booking process.

This is a national issue that affects young people, low-income families, and essential workers. Urgent reform is needed to restore access and trust in a service many rely on.
rejection_details:
The Government has consulted on reforms to the UK driving test system:

https://www.gov.uk/government/news/transport-secretary-acts-to-make-thousands-of-extra-driving-tests-available-each-month

And the DVSA has set out how it plans to reduce driving test wait time:

https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dvsa-sets-out-plan-to-reduce-driving-test-waiting-times

action: Ban the boiling of live crabs and other crustaceans
background: Ban the boiling or cooking in any form of live crabs, lobsters, and other crustaceans. Imagine being boiled alive with no escape. I believe it is savage.
additional_details: I believe that if boiling crustaceans alive continues it could escalate towards greater problems for humanity and the beloved creatures we share earth with. This way of killing creatures is breaking my heart.

action: Put Any Change to the UK Voting Age to a Public Referendum
background: Require a national referendum before changing the legal voting age, to ensure such a key decision is made by the people and not imposed by politicians or used for party advantage.
additional_details: Changing the voting age affects our democracy. It must be fair, transparent, and supported by the public, not pushed through by parties that may benefit. A referendum protects trust in the system.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733679

action: Ban scalping of collectable/hobbyist items
background: Legislate to penalise or fine people who hoard stock of collectable/hobbyist items in order to resell them at inflated prices. This impacts collectible item economies and can price out standard consumers.
additional_details: The practice of scalping collectable/hobbyist items such as games consoles, computer hardware, trading card games, and hobbyist books and merchandise, should be banned. Sellers who buy ridiculous amounts of stock just to resell at huge profit should be penalised. We think this practice often prices out regular consumers significantly, and sets a precedent within the marketplace that can lead to overall economic imbalance and destroys opportunity for some businesses.

action: Require all schools to provide mental health services to GCSE students
background: GCSE students can suffer from burnout and stress from the GCSE system. We want all state schools and academies to be required to provide mental health services to GCSE students.
additional_details:
Some studies have suggested 80% of young people reported academic pressure contributed to mental health difficulties.

We feel it is imperative that all state schools and academies are required to provide mental health services to all GCSE students.

action: Require schools to include both skirts and trousers in female uniform policy
background:
Require school uniform policy to allow girls the right to wear skirts or trousers.
 
I think control over the wearing of either item contravenes the Equality Act 2010 through direct discrimination of women.
additional_details:
I think the Department for Education should issue guidelines to schools regarding the implementation of uniform policy to require that inclusive uniform policy must permit both trousers and skirts, in line with societal and gender norms for women.
I think contradictory restrictions could be imposed on girls without government clarification of guidelines. I think such gender-based discrimination causes unnecessary distress, detracting from learning, and disengaging girls from education.

action: Mandatory politics education for secondary school years
background: On the 17th of July 2025, the Government announced plans to allow 16–17-year-olds to vote in all UK elections. The introduction of mandatory modern political education in PSHE would aid the next generation of voters with making an informed decision on polling days.
additional_details:
The aim of ‘boosting democratic engagement’ cannot truly be met without providing the appropriate political education in schools- of which should be up to date and unbiased.
Currently, teaching politics in PSHE is only a suggestion despite its ever-so increasing importance in British society following these recent election reforms.
Democracy cannot be achieved if citizens are unaware of voting practises and/or manifestos.
rejection_details:
Schools are already required to teach citizenship as part of the secondary national curriculum.

The citizenship curriculum includes content on how the United Kingdom is governed, its political system and how citizens participate actively in its democratic systems of government.

You can read the citizenship programmes of study for secondary school here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study/national-curriculum-in-england-citizenship-programmes-of-study-for-key-stages-3-and-4

If you would like to make a change to the current arrangements, you can start a petition setting out clearly what you would like to change, such as submitting a petition about making politics a core specific subject.

action: Conduct an Independent Evaluation of the Cass Review
background: We think the Cass Review has undermined trans youths' access to evidence-based and safe care.
additional_details:
We think its recommendations promote harmful practices, including:
• Restricting access to healthcare
• Promoting caution around social-transitioning
• Recommending 18 to 25-year-olds do not transfer to adult services
 
The Cass Review was commissioned in 2020 by NHS England, and led by Dr. Hilary Cass.
 
Many consider this review to be biased and harmful.

action: Stop all asylum from any country to the british isles that arent made off shore.
background: Ban all and any application for asylum from all natonalities  that arent made prior to entry of the uk.
additional_details:
The cause of an influx of illegal immaigtation and legal asylum application are weighing  a burden on the economy, benifit system, national health service,prison and juditial systems  And the cause of unrest amongs british citizens. 
 To eliminate foreighn criminal activity on british soil for protection of this and future generations.

action: Reverse the decision to Self-ID as Trans without diagnosis of Gender Dysphoria
background: Ban Self ID for trans people, Allow Photo ID with Gender Recognition Certificate for only Trans people who have had SRS/GRS.
additional_details: It is to protect females, preventing males entering female spaces in a state of undress. Preventing sex offenders identifying as Trans entering female spaces.
rejection_details:
It is not possible to self-identify as transgender.

You could start a new petition asking to require surgery to obtain a GRC.

action: Licence the sale of Class F3 and above fireworks & only allow sales at set times
background: I'd like the Government to bring in legislation to license the sale of the bigger classes of fireworks and only allow sale of the bigger fireworks at specific times ( Bonfire Night, Xmas, Dewali ect) to stop the anti social use of the bigger fireworks that continues all year around

action: Introduce minimum pricing threshold for alcohol for large hospitality chains
background: We think that large chains routinely slash the prices of their beers, wines, and spirits to levels independents often cannot match. They have massive buying power.
additional_details:
We are calling on the government to introduce a new legislative measure:

Any company in the hospitality sector with 50 or more outlets must adhere to a minimum pricing threshold for alcoholic drinks — including beers, wines, and spirits.
 
We ask that this be used to protect independents, who we consider are the backbone of Britain's hospitality.

action: Save Ashfield School theatre—protect arts, education, and community space.
background: We call on the government to save Ashfield School’s theatre—a vital hub for arts, education, and community. The DfE’s plan to remove it ignores its lasting value. We urge support to retain and integrate it into the new development, ensuring future generations benefit from this essential resource.
additional_details: Step in and save Ashfield School’s theatre, a vital space that nurtures creativity, confidence, and community spirit. The DfE’s plan to remove it as part of redevelopment overlooks its immense value to students and local residents. Preserving the theatre ensures continued access to arts education and performance opportunities. It supports young people’s development and strengthens community ties. We ask that it be retained and integrated into the new school design for future generations.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Do not sell seized cryptocurrency
background: There are reports the Government could sell seized cryptocurrency. I would like the Government to commit to not doing this.
additional_details: We believe crypto assets are a fast growing asset that should be held for the long term, not sold to plug a gap.

action: Keep the voting age at 18 and stop it being reduced to 16
background: Act responsible and keep the voting age at 18
additional_details: A person at 16 has limited life experience and is a very easy target to be lured into voting irresponsibly.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

action: Ban firms from using 'self employed' cycle couriers and increase requirements
background: Require food delivery companies to employ their couriers and provide insurance, training and compulsory safety equipment eg lights, helmet and high visibility clothing. Plus employment rights for couriers. Dis-incentivise fast food companies from using people who are working illegally.
additional_details:
We think this could result in many benefits:
 
Safer working.
Fewer people working illegally in this sector.
Make the work a more attractive and safer proposition for young people.
Drive up the price of junk food and as a consequence help to reduce the incidence of obesity and associated health issues.
Provide better accountability within this sector and so reduce the number of couriers who could be using food delivery as a cover for drug dealing.

action: Reverse the Decision to Lower the Voting Age to 16
background: We call on the Government to reverse the decision to give 16 and 17 year olds the vote. Voting is a vital civic duty that should be reserved for legal adults. At 18, citizens are more likely to have the maturity, independence and life experience to vote responsibly.
additional_details: Lowering the voting age to 16 undermines the seriousness of the democratic process. At 16, most young people are still in education, financially dependent, and lack the life experience needed to make informed political decisions. Voting should remain a right and responsibility of adulthood. We urge the Government to uphold the integrity of our elections by restoring the minimum voting age to 18.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Don't lower the voting age to 16: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733604

We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733679

action: Create a mtb track in Kintbury area, West Berkshire.
background: We want the west Berkshire council to make jumps in Kintbury area due to Kintbury lacking things to do for kids age 13+
additional_details: It will ensure happiness in the community, especially those aged 13+
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.

action: Ban OFSTED visits at the beginning of term and end of the academic school year
background: Ban any OFSTED visits and inspection of schools at certain times of year. Specifically, require them to not carry out visits and inspections during the first two weeks of a new term or the final two weeks of the academic year.
additional_details: I believe the mental wellbeing of school staff is a critical concern, particularly given the inherent stress that may be associated with an OFSTED inspection. I think that while such inspections are always demanding, scheduling them during the final two weeks of the academic year or the first two weeks of the new term significantly heightens stress levels. I believe it places additional pressure on staff during already challenging periods, potentially impacting their mental health and overall effectiveness.

action: Make Government & Politics a compulsory, core subject in schools
background: With plans to reduce the voting age for the next election to 16, we believe there's a greater need to introduce Government & Politics as a standalone, core subject in secondary schools.
additional_details:
We think this will help schoolchildren learn the fundamentals of British Politics and understand voting and how their vote matters.
 
We believe that without proper education, many will likely not vote or will get a majority of their information from social media platforms, which makes us concerned about the potential effects of misinformation and the impact on results at the next general election. In our view, the need for Government & Politics as a compulsory core subject in Secondary Schools has never been higher.

action: The EHCP System is Failing Our Children.The system is broken and needs to change
background:
Delays: Many families wait months — even years beyond the legal 20-week deadline.
	• Unlawful rejections: Councils routinely deny EHCP applications with little justification.
	•	Poor implementation: Even with a plan, children often don’t receive the help they were promised.
additional_details:
Mental health toll: The stress and emotional trauma of constantly fighting the system is breaking parents — and damaging children’s wellbeing.
	• Legal battles: Thousands of families are forced to take their councils to tribunal just to access their child’s legal rights.
rejection_details: You could start a petition which clearly states exactly what action you'd like the UK Parliament or Government to take related to EHCPs.

action: Keep the right to trail by jury.
background: Not to change laws regarding jury trials
additional_details: It's a British right to have a jury of piers hold judgement over someone at trail. A standard sent around the Globe.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Don't reduce the number of trials by jury
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710321

action: Require parents to pay child maintenance if the child is in Local Authority Care
background: We want the Government to make parents whose children have been removed from their care financially responsible by requiring them to pay child maintenance to the local authority until the child turns 18.
additional_details: When a child is taken into care by the state—whether placed in foster care or residential care—the full cost of raising that child is currently covered by the local authority using public funds. In many cases, the parents retain parental responsibility but are not required to contribute financially. We believe this is inconsistent with the principles of the Child Maintenance Service, which requires non-resident parents to support their children.

action: Discretionary life prison sentence
background: Inconsistency in Sentencing: Discretionary life sentences can lead to significant disparities in sentencing for similar crimes, depending solely on the judge’s interpretation and personal discretion. This inconsistency has raised huge concerns already in the uk with the IPP sentence.
additional_details:
1.	Establish clear guidelines for discretionary life sentences to ensure consistency and fairness in sentencing.

	2.	Implement comprehensive risk assessment protocols for all individuals facing discretionary life sentences.

	3.	Increase transparency in the sentencing process, allowing for public understanding and accountability.

	4.	Provide adequate resources for rehabilitation programs for individuals serving life sentences, focusing on reducing recidivism.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.  

We're not sure exactly what you mean by increasing transparency and risk assessment protocols.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do. 

There are also already guidelines from the Sentencing Council on discretionary life sentences: https://www.sentencingcouncil.org.uk/sentencing-and-the-council/types-of-sentence/life-sentences/

action: Allow State Pension to be passed to children, long-term partners, and dependents
background: We ask the Government to change State Pension inheritance rules so that individuals can nominate a beneficiary such as their child, long-term cohabiting partner, or carer – or offer them a lump sum – so it is not just a spouse or civil partner inheriting from the pension as at present.
additional_details:
State Pension benefits can only be inherited by a spouse/civil partner. Unmarried partners, adult children, or other dependents are excluded, even if financially dependent. Many may support adult children with disabilities, or are cared for by someone other than a spouse or civil partner.
 
We believe in having a system that recognises real-world relationships and dependency; allowing people to nominate a beneficiary, or offer a lump sum to dependents, could help protect vulnerable loved ones from financial hardship after bereavement.

action: Do not allow under 18 year olds to vote in the U.K.
background: Stop the Government from changing the voting age to 16 years old.
additional_details:
Children of 16 years old are still that, children. This is why they are still in education and protected by our laws as such.
Every Adult knows that at 16 years old most people are not capable of rational decisions and do not have enough experience of life to participate in an election.
This must be stopped.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Don't lower the voting age to 16: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733604

We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733679

action: Review UK laws and procedures relating to votes of no confidence
background: We call on Parliament to initiate a cross-party review of the laws and procedures for votes of no confidence, ensuring they are clear, modern, and fit for purpose following the repeal of the Fixed-Term Parliaments Act in 2022.
additional_details: Since the Fixed-Term Parliaments Act ended in 2022, we believe votes of no confidence now follow old, unclear rules. Without clear laws, things can get confusing, decisions may be inconsistent, and people might lose trust. We want Parliament to carry out a fair, cross-party review to make sure the rules are clear, modern, and help keep our democracy strong and trusted by everyone.

action: Regulate outbound medical tourism: mandatory accreditation, insurance, aftercare
background: Government should create an accreditation body for overseas medical providers advertising to UK patients, require them to offer complication insurance and UK-based aftercare, allow only accredited providers to advertise in the UK, and set up a national database to track clinical outcomes.
additional_details: In 2023, over 430,000 UK residents went abroad for medical treatment. Many of those who receive treatment abroad return with complications, and many medical tourism-related complications are managed on the NHS.  Some patients have died following medical treatment abroad. The Government must act to ensure patient safety, accountability, and reduce the financial and healthcare burden on the NHS by introducing clear legal regulations for medical tourism providers.

action: Legislate to create a threshold limit on parking charge increases by UK Councils
background: We urge the Government to legislate to create an annual threshold limit on parking charge increases made by councils each year to prevent large hikes. We feel current percentage increases of on-street parking charges could disproportionately affect vulnerable groups, neurodivergent and pensioners.
additional_details: We are deeply concerned about what we believe are unfair and excessive parking charge hikes imposed by councils. We believe increases have hurt local businesses, families, & vulnerable individuals, including those with neurodivergent conditions. We believe the Government must create a threshold for councils to abide by.

action: A petition for a national referendum on the reduction of the voting age to 16
background:
People younger than 18 years of age are consider by law to be children. 

This petition calls for a referendum of the current UK electorate on whether the voting age should be reduced from 18 to 16 years of age.
additional_details:
In the UK a person below the age of 18 is not allowed to make decisions on consuming alcohol or cigarettes and are banned from proscribed establishments such as sexually explicit entertainment venues.  People under 18 years of age are not considered adult in many sectors of the law, including employment and criminality.

The law implies that a person younger than 18 has not reached maturity and requires state protection and guidance.  This is incompatible with the proposed age reduction.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

We call for a referendum before extending voting rights to 16 & 17-year-olds: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733679

action: Fund spiking testing in A&E and in walk-in sexual health clinics
background: Fund greater access to testing for spiking victims, to allow the scale of the spiking cases to be quantified, truly analysed and tackled. We think this should be available in hospitals and sexual health clinics to help understand, deter and tackle spiking.
additional_details: Some victims don't know to call the police for forensic testing, so it’s unreported/ uncatalogued. With an estimated 90% of cases being unreported, the scale of spiking is unknown. How do you tackle a problem if you don’t understand even how big it is? We believe that without change, more people will, avoidably, be put into vulnerable, life-altering and potentially life-threatening situations.

action: Stop nasty comments and abuse on online platforms
background: There is a lot of negativity and nastiness on online platforms which makes using them unsafe for the current and future generation. The government needs to enable some sort of AI based detector that immediately disallows  individuals from posting any negative or nasty comments.
additional_details: Online platforms have become very popular with more and more individuals using them, but they have become places where negativity and hate is allowed. People can hide behind a keyboard, writing words that would never be said aloud to people’s faces. We need to think about the impact this is having on people’s wellbeing and mental health. Think, without nastiness or online hate, online platforms could be a much better/happier place, with more positivity spread to raise wellbeing.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action:

Require social media platforms to identify and remove all unsafe content. 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710557

action: Add Brazil as an eligible country for driving licence conversion
background: We think it would be beneficial to Brazilians to have their driving licences exchanged for British equivalent licences. We feel this makes sense with the lack of driving tests available in the country and the amount of Brazilians with full Brazilian driving licences living here.
additional_details: We believe this could alleviate the pressure on people with experience and qualifications as drivers. The Brazilian community greatly adds to the British society.

action: re-nationalise water
background: Nationalise the water industry. Water is a basic human right.
additional_details: Water companies should be not for profit. The water companies are failing in their duty of care to the environment and yet taking profits, giving bonuses and pleading for funding from the government when they get into financial trouble.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727463

action: Make private car parking company's charge per hour for illegally parking
background: Make all private land that has been designated as public car parking charge per hour for illegally parked cars and not a fixed fee of £60 plus. The fees per hour to be set by the councils in the area that the carpark is situated, and link the change of address to the driving licence the DVLA
additional_details: The motorists are being persecuted by these companies, causing stress and anxiety, there should be a warning sent first before a fine, pointing out the drivers errors, and it should be by recorded delivery, the commodity companies send warning letters before fines so should these companies, and make it mandatory that they have parking fees per hour on these car parks if they don't they cannot fine drivers.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Make machines, which take payment on exit, mandatory for parking operators
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/714398

action: Trigger Article 58 and begin withdrawal from the ECHR.
background: Invoke Article 58 of the European Convention on Human Rights and begin the formal process of withdrawal. Repeal the Human Rights Act 1998, replace ECtHR case law with domestic protections, and restore sovereignty to UK law and Parliament.
additional_details: Sovereignty means making our own rules and controlling our own laws without outside influence. The ECHR has repeatedly undermined the UK’s ability to protect borders, enforce immigration law, and uphold democratic decisions. British rights should be protected by British law, in British courts. It's time to restore legal and democratic control by triggering Article 58 and leaving the ECHR.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR)
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729027

action: Require anti-ableism training & improve transparency in social services
background: Require anti-ableism training in social services to support disabled parents, and improve transparency in safeguarding decisions.
additional_details: Children’s social services are meant to protect the vulnerable. We think that disabled parents and others from marginalised groups are too often treated with suspicion rather than supported. We think this may cause long-term trauma and diverts resources away from serious cases of child abuse. We think we need a compassionate, just, and inclusive system that helps families thrive.

action: Mass deportation of illegal migrants
background: The Government must implement a comprehensive national strategy to identify, detain and deport all individuals living illegally in the United Kingdom.
additional_details: The Government must take decisive action to address the serious issue of illegal immigration in the UK. Illegal immigration undermines our national laws, places a strain on public resources. A national strategy is needed to ensure that illegal migrants are identified, detained and deported. This strategy should include all necessary legislative, diplomatic, logistical, and financial resources to effectively enforce immigration laws and restore public confidence in the security of our borders.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729231

action: Keep 5-year ILR path for those already on Graduate Route visas in the UK
background: I’m on a Graduate Route visa, working legally and contributing to the UK. I chose the UK before ILR rules changed. It’s unfair to change the rules midway. Please exempt current Graduate Route holders from the 10-year ILR rule and keep the original 5-year path.
additional_details: I am on a Graduate Route visa, working legally, paying taxes, and contributing to the UK economy. I chose to build my future here before the new 10-year ILR rules were announced. Changing the rules partway is unfair and causes uncertainty for people like me who have invested in the UK. I ask the Government to exempt current Graduate Route holders from the new rule and allow us to keep the original 5-year path to settlement, recognizing our contributions and commitmen
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.  

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do as time on the Graduate Visa does not count towards Indefinite Leave to Remain.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Fund free menstrual products and access to drinking water in public
background: We want the government to fund period products so women and girls can access them for free. We also want them to guarantee access to clean, free drinking water in public and high traffic areas.
additional_details: People living unhoused or in poverty often can't afford pads, tampons, or bottled water. We think access to menstrual products and clean drinking water is a basic human right, not a luxury. Using the wrong products or no products in period cycles could cause infections and health problems.

action: Make a new Family Visitor visa for close non-EU relatives of UK residents
background: We urge the Government to make a new family visitor visa for close NON-EU relatives of UK residents who are visiting the UK for 6 months or less. We want it to be faster, cheaper, and recognise family ties - unlike the current Standard Visitor visa which we feel treats relatives like tourists.
additional_details: We feel the current system ignores family connections and can cause real stress. In the EU, family members of citizens are treated as a special category.

action: Pass a law which bans the reselling of practical driving tests
background: We urge the Government to pass a law which bans reselling practical driving tests and makes this practice illegal. We believe the lack of availability for booking a driving test in the UK is because people are openly booking and reselling practical tests.
additional_details: We believe people who are found guilty of reselling practical driving tests should be prosecuted. We feel it is unfair for pupils to have to resort to paying extortionate amounts to sit a practical driving test. We believe this is a public service and needs to be available to everyone in a fair manner and not exploited.

action: Childrens clubs have mandatory type 1 diabetes training in first aid.
background: Provide training for the clubs with their first aid training.
additional_details: This would make so many families & children with type 1 diabetes feel included and safe to attend camps that all other children can attend care free.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/
