action: Increase funding for PMDD, PME and menopause screening in mental health services
background: Increase funding to help ensure menstrual and menopausal health is included in mental health assessments, including crisis, talking therapies, specialist care & Mental Health Act assessments
additional_details:
We believe services should have adequate funding to track symptoms and create clear treatment pathways for PMDD (Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder) & menopause.
 
PMDD affects 1 in 20 women & people who menstruate, with some sources citing that almost a third attempt suicide. PMDD, PME (Premenstrual Exacerbation) & menopause can mimic psychiatric illness, leading to misdiagnosis, unsafe treatment, & preventable harm. There is no dedicated mental health pathway for PMDD. Neurodivergent women are disproportionately affected. Menopause will impact nearly all women. We think that including menstrual and menopausal health in assessments could reduce suicide risk, improve diagnosis, & ensure safer, more effective care.
government_response_summary: We have provided an extra £688 million this year for mental health and are expanding NHS Talking Therapies, which are available to women experiencing mental health issues and conditions such as PMDD.
government_response_body: The Government is committed to prioritising women’s health, and we are clear that women’s health, including mental health, will never be neglected again. We are taking steps to improve diagnosis and ensure safer and more effective care.  The nation’s mental health has deteriorated over the last decade. Lord Darzi’s investigation found that people accessing NHS mental health services are waiting too long, receive variable quality of care, and suffer from entrenched inequalities. We have already taken significant steps to stabilise and improve NHS mental health services. Total mental health spending for the 2025/26 financial year is expected to be £15.6 billion, an increase of £688 million from the previous year. Almost 8,000 extra mental health workers have been recruited since July 2024, against our target of 8,500 by the end of this Parliament.  We are expanding NHS Talking Therapies which provide psychological support for people with a common mental health condition like stress, anxiety, and depression. More than 670,000 people completed a course of Talking Therapies treatment last year, and through the 10 Year Health Plan, 915,000 people are expected to complete a course of treatment by March 2029. Women experiencing common mental health conditions and issues such as Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD), Premenstrual Exacerbation (PME) and menopause can self-refer to NHS Talking Therapies or be referred by their GP.  While menopause is a natural stage of a woman’s life course, symptoms are common, and for some women, menopause can have a significant impact on mental health. Low mood and anxiety are two possible symptoms of the menopause. In 2025, we announced that menopause questions will be included in routine NHS health checks for over-40s, raising awareness of symptoms and giving women the confidence to seek help. We are working with experts, including GPs, to design this content, to ensure women receive appropriate support for menopause symptoms.  In September 2025, we announced an “online hospital” – NHS Online – which will give people the choice of getting the specialist care they need from their home. Both menopause and menstrual problems will be among the first conditions available for referral to NHS Online from 2027. It will connect patients with clinicians across the country through secure, online appointments accessed through the NHS App. NHS Online will help to reduce patient waiting times, delivering the equivalent of up to 8.5 million appointments and assessments in its first three years, four times more than an average NHS trust, while enhancing patient choice and control over their care.  NHS England is also working on menopause workforce support packages for employees and developing a range of tools and interventions that will help to upskill more GPs in menopause care. This includes awareness of mental health symptoms during menopause and improved access to treatments.  The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) published their updated guidelines on menopause in November 2024 and recommended more treatment choices for symptoms. The updated guidelines support healthcare professionals by providing them with information they need to support evidence-based decisions about treatment choices, as well as information and support about menopause.  Menopause treatment options, including Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT), can be used to treat symptoms including mood problems and anxiety. NICE recommends that, for most women, HRT is a safe and effective treatment option. It is important that women are provided with accurate information and are able to make informed choices about their care, including treatment options such as HRT. The NICE guidelines also recommend that healthcare professionals should consider menopause-specific cognitive behavioural therapy as an option for symptoms associated with menopause in addition to HRT.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Fix Our Roads: National Plan on Dangerous Potholes Now
background: The Government must step in with a national plan: a dedicated pothole repair fund, strict repair deadlines for local councils, investment in more durable surfacing technology, and more transparency on spending. Safe roads are essential for communities, businesses, and daily life.
additional_details:
We believe it is long past time for the Government to step up and help local councils deliver lasting solutions to what we see as a pothole crisis. We think that for too many years, this issue has been left to drag on without sufficient action, leaving communities across the country frustrated and suffering the consequences.
 
We feel that residents are fed up with facing endless repair bills for tyres, wheels, and suspensions damaged by crumbling roads, and that it is also a serious safety concern.
government_response_summary: The Government is committed to tackling the poor state of local roads and has provided a record £7.3 billion for local highways over the next four years.
government_response_body: The Government recognises the importance of safe, well maintained local roads for residents, communities and businesses. We understand the frustration caused by potholes and other road defects, and the impact this can have on people’s daily lives, on the need for vehicle repairs, and on confidence in the local road network.  We also recognise that historic underfunding has meant local authorities have not always had the resources or tools they would want in order to maintain their roads to the standard we all expect. That is why this Government has taken significant steps to strengthen the funding, transparency and support available to local highway authorities.  This financial year, the Government has made available an additional £500 million for local highways maintenance. For the next four financial years, we have also confirmed a record £7.3 billion investment, providing the long-term certainty councils have consistently said they need to plan and deliver more durable and cost-effective highway maintenance programmes.  To support improvement, 25% of this financial year’s uplift is conditional on local authorities demonstrating compliance with clear criteria designed to encourage best practice in maintenance and asset management.  In January, the Government launched a new rating system for every local highway authority in England. Each authority has been assessed as red, amber or green. These ratings reflect factors such as the condition of their roads, how effectively they use the record Government funding available, and the extent to which they are applying best practice.  We acknowledge that some authorities face more challenging starting points due to historic underinvestment, and a lower rating does not necessarily indicate a lack of ambition or effort locally. Where authorities face particular difficulties, the Government will provide targeted support, including peer reviews carried out by sector experts.  This is complemented by wider resources to help authorities improve the durability and efficiency of their networks. We have extended the Live Labs 2 highways innovation programme into 2026/27 to support the adoption of new technologies and materials. We are also updating the Code of Practice for Well Managed Highways, to be published later this year, which will provide refreshed guidance on risk-based asset management and long-term planning.  Department for Transport

action: Make British Summer Time (BST) permanent year-round
background: We call on the UK Government and Parliament to keep the UK on British Summer Time (BST) permanently—by ending the bi-annual clock changes and remaining one hour ahead of GMT year-round.
additional_details:
We believe that:
1. Lighter evenings may improve safety, health and encourage active lifestyles.
2. Permanent BST helps avoid dark winter afternoons, which may make communities safer and more welcoming.
3. Ending clock changes may prevent disruption to sleep, work, travel and digital systems — potentially boosting productivity.
4. More daylight reduces energy use, helping households with bills and supporting climate goals.
5. Other nations have shown permanent daylight saving works, the UK should lead with a modern, consistent approach.

action: Create a Sikh regiment in the British Army
background: Historically, Sikhs have been very involved in the British (Indian) Army, serving in many wars and battles (WW1, WW2 and the Battle of Saragarhi). We believe opening a Sikh regiment in the UK army will help represent the previous bravery of Sikhs not just in the British Army, but in the World too.
additional_details: It could allow a true demonstration of the involvement of Sikhs in the British Army. Furthermore, it could promote diversity within the armed forces and may encourage more young Sikhs to be aware of it as possible career path. Not as a comparison, but as a consideration, there are already Gurkha units, which represents respect given to them due to their bravery in battle. Sikhs have represented honour and courage throughout history – having a Sikh regiment would highlight this.

action: Enforce the BBCs principle of due impartiality to ensure it remains trustworthy
background: Investigate current political news output for bias, contrary to the BBC core principle of due impartiality. Trust is the foundation of the BBC, and such trust is lost by the public when undue influence is seen to be applied
additional_details: The Bank Holiday weekend was the final straw in wall to wall coverage of Reform, a limited company with 4 MPs which attracted blanket coverage for days on every form of BBC news media, be it radio TV or website. A simple investigation into how this imbalance has occurred, together with a commitment from the BBC to create an action plan to redress the balance
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about the regulation of the BBC are a matter for Ofcom, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Mandate & fund the painting of all English zebra crossing with St George’s Cross
background: We urge the UK Government to mandate and fund all zebra crossings in England to be painted with the St George’s Cross to boost national pride and showcase English identity. We want funding to cover materials and labours, and exemptions can apply for historical or safety reasons.
additional_details: We want the UK Government to do this to foster national pride and unity. We believe the striking design would turn ordinary crossings into vibrant symbols of English identity, aligning with 2025 cultural events. We believe it could stimulate local economies by drawing tourists and creating jobs in painting and maintenance. Enhanced visibility may also improve road safety.

action: Make the State Pension equal to the national average wage at age 60
background: Parliament must legislate for a State Pension equal to national average earnings for all British pensioners, with the retirement age set at 60 for men and women. The pension should be a living wage, not a poverty trap, restoring fairness after decades of cuts and neglect.
additional_details: The State Pension was cut in value 40 years ago and has been left to wither. Pensioners have paid taxes all their working lives, yet are denied a fair share of national wealth. Women who raised families are not recognised for their contribution. Retirement at 60 for men and women is fair and just. A living State pension should reflect national average wages and rise accordingly. Fairness, not age discrimination, must guide our pension system.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Give State Pension to all at 60 and increase it to equal 48hrs of Living Wage
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728656

action: Make England/Wales/Scotland/NI painted flags compulsory 4 every mini roundabouts
background: I want the Government to make it compulsory for all mini-roundabouts in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland to be painted with the relevant national flag, to improve road safety and promote national identity across the UK.
additional_details: Mini-roundabouts are sometimes overlooked by drivers, leading to safety risks. Painting them with the relevant national flag would make them more visible and distinctive, helping to reduce accidents. This change would also promote national identity and pride by ensuring everyday spaces reflect the culture of each UK nation. I want the Government to require local authorities to adopt this approach across England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Signage and maintenance on roundabouts are a matter for the authority managing the road network on which the roundabout is situated. Depending on the roundabout in question, this could either be the local authority, or National Highways.

action: Make it a Criminal Offence to desecrate the Union Flag and UK National Flags
background: The Union Flag and the national flags of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland are powerful symbols of our shared history, values, and identity. They represent the sacrifices of past generations and the unity of our communities today.
additional_details:
We call on the Government to introduce legislation making it a criminal offence to burn, deface, or otherwise desecrate the Union Flag or the national flags of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

This law would send a clear signal that our flags deserve dignity and respect. It would not prevent legitimate protest or free speech but would ensure that our national symbols cannot be wilfully disrespected in ways that divide communities and dishonour those who have served under them.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Make destroying or vandalising the Union Flag a criminal offence 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/719227

action: Stop allowing immigrants to stay in our hotels free of charge.
background: I believe the Government should reconsider current immigration policies, mainly the provision of free accommodation and financial support for new arrivals. These resources could be directed towards addressing homelessness among British citizens, who are in urgent need of housing and assistance.
additional_details:
In summary, my position is that the Government should:
	1.	Re-evaluate the level of financial and housing support provided to new arrivals.
	2.	Place greater focus on supporting homeless citizens across the UK.
	3.	Ensure that immigration policy aligns more closely with the priorities and expectations of the British public.
rejection_details:
Shut the migrant hotels down now and deport illegal migrants housed there 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/718406

action: All newly elected MPs must complete a six month probationary period
background: All newly elected MPs should complete a six month probation. Unlike many other jobs, they can get a full term with what we feel is limited accountability. An independent panel should review performance, and MPs deemed unsuitable should face removal. We think this would help ensure MPs honour pledges
additional_details: We’re fed up with MPs who we think are making promises to win votes, and might then be able to dodge accountability for five years. We think a six month probationary period, reviewed by an independent panel, would help ensure MPs prove their competence and keep pledges. MPs deemed unsuitable by the panel could be removed. We think this would align politics with other jobs’ accountability standards. It could help rebuild trust, and help ensure MPs serve the public, not themselves.

action: Reduce the state pension age to 50 years old for men & women
background: We urge the Government to reduce the state pension age for men and women to 50 years old in the UK.

action: Trigger a by-election when an MP or MSP defects to another party.
background: Ensure that voters have an MP or MSP of the party  they voted for at the last election.
additional_details: The voters should be represented in parliament by a member of the party they voted for, not by a defector who prefers to change sides.
rejection_details:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party

action: Urgent Concerns - EU Entry/Exit System (EES) and its Impact on UK HGV Drivers
background: International HGV drivers to express my grave concerns about the implementation of the European Union's new Entry/Exit System (EES), scheduled to come into force on the 12th October 2025.
additional_details: I urge you to raise this issue with the relevant government departments in the EU and to advocate for a visa-free or exempted travel arrangement for UK professional drivers. Our work is essential for the UK . To avoid putting UK Companies and drivers out of business.   While EES may seem like a minor administrative change on the surface, its impact on professional drivers like me will be profound due to the "90/180-day rule."
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738267

action: Automatically grant UK citizenship to people affected by historical unfairness
background: We ask the UK Government to change UK nationality law to automatically grant UK citizenship to people who may have not been granted UK citizenship based on whether their British parent was their mother or father.
additional_details: Before 1983, British fathers could usually pass citizenship to children born abroad but British mothers often could not. Later reforms created application routes, but these are not automatic and may leave people disadvantaged. We ask the Government to legislate to ensure that UK citizenship is granted automatically to those who have been affected by this historic gender bias in UK nationality law.

action: MPs who wish to switch party should resign and stand for re-election.
background: Implement this change.
additional_details: Electors maty not be happy with the MPs new party.  So They should resign and stand for re-election under the new party banner.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Reducing The 6 Weeks School Holiday To 2 Weeks.
background: Reduce the six week summer school holiday to two weeks and spread the remaining four weeks across the year to improve learning, reduce childcare pressures and support families.
additional_details: 6 week summer holidays cause children to forget learning, widen the attainment gap and place huge childcare and financial pressure on families. Shorter breaks would keep children’s progress on track, support working parents and allow schools to better use teaching time. Long breaks create stress and high costs for families.
rejection_details:
Term dates are determined locally by schools and local authorities.

For maintained schools, community schools, community special schools, voluntary controlled schools, pupil referral units and maintained nursery schools, the governing body or local authority are responsible for setting term dates.

Academies, free schools, and other schools where the governing body is the employer of staff, such as foundation or voluntary-aided (church) schools, are free to set their own term and holiday dates.

action: Make politically motivated vandalism a specific offence with strong penalties
background: Make unauthorised painting of political markings or graffiti - particularly on roads, kerbs and road signs - a specific offence. Punishments should include high fines, community orders, rapid removal paid for by the offender and even custody for repeat or group offending.
additional_details: We think large paint symbols on roads and signs can create hazards, alarm residents and inflame tensions. They can be costly to remove and often reappear when enforcement is weak. We think creating a specific offence, with stronger penalties and rapid removal could deter repeat behaviour and protect safety and community cohesion.

action: Make funeral directors a regulated profession
background: We believe the funeral industry must be regulated as there are a lack of government regulations for setting up a funeral business, meaning owners don't need to meet specific requirements.
additional_details:
We urge the Government to make funeral directors a regulated profession, including introducing a legal code and qualification requirements.
 
Having experience and qualifications in the industry, I have visited many funeral homes, and many do not have the right facilities to care for “residents” in an environment which we believe should uphold their dignity. Standards in some places can be very low. Many funeral businesses may have no experience or qualifications when dealing with people who may be vulnerable after a personal loss. I believe after hearing so many stories, someone needs to advocate for the deceased and the bereaved.

action: Require conveyancing searches to include commercial noise & ban complaints
background: We urge the Government to legislate to require conveyancing searches to include commercial noise and ban any complaints from new residents about noises identified in the searches.
additional_details: We believe buyers should know about this when signing a contract, so new residents are unable to make noise complaints against local established businesses. We believe noise/nuisance from local established businesses should be highlighted so an informed decision can be made before contracts are exchanged. Public houses as an example: many are closing every week and it can become even harder to continue to trade, contribute to the economy and be a hub for the local community when a new resident moves in the vicinity and proceeds to complain.

action: Fund local authorities to build parks with wheelchair-accessible play equipment
background: We would like the Government to fund local authorities to build more parks with wheelchair-accessible equipment like wheelchair swings, wheelchair roundabouts, in-ground trampolines and lower basketball hoops so people with accessibility issues can play at the park.
additional_details: I am blind and have a wheelchair. I have 3 sisters who can walk, and I can’t. They get to play on the swings, slide and roundabout. I feel sad because my sisters get to play on the park. If the park had accessible equipment, I may be able to play too. There are lots of children who have wheelchairs who want to play at the park. They will feel happy if they get to play in the park.

action: Remove inheritance tax on all estates and their property worth under £1 million
background: Change the inheritance tax threshold from all estates from £325,000 to £1 million, so that no inheritance tax is levied on estates and the property within them up to a value of £1 million.
additional_details: With current inflation and property prices I feel it's only right that the threshold for paying inheritance tax should change from £325,000 to £1 million. So, there should be no inheritance tax on estates and their property under £1 million.

action: Scrap Marginal Energy Pricing To Lower Bills And Boost Clean Power Production.
background: We want the Government to end the marginal pricing system that pegs electricity costs to expensive fossil fuels. Replace it with a fairer model that reflects actual generation costs and supports cheaper, cleaner energy for households and businesses.
additional_details: Marginal pricing makes clean electricity artificially expensive, driving up inflation and punishing households already under financial stress. Scrapping it would lower bills, accelerate the green transition, and make heat pumps and EVs more accessible. This reform is urgent, fair, and backed by energy experts.

action: Establish ‘I Am Ukrainian Day’ to show solidarity with Ukraine
background: We ask the Government to establish “I Am Ukrainian Day” as a UK-wide day of solidarity. On this day, people would be encouraged to wear “I Am Ukrainian” T-shirts or display the Ukrainian flag, showing unity, raising awareness, and supporting Ukraine’s fight for freedom.
additional_details: We want the Government to establish “I Am Ukrainian Day” as a UK-wide show of unity. Free “I Am Ukrainian” T-shirts would be given out so everyone can take part, making support visible in schools, workplaces, and communities. This day would raise awareness of Ukraine’s struggle for freedom, strengthen solidarity, and show that the UK stands firmly with the Ukrainian people against aggression and injustice.
rejection_details: Decisions about this are not a matter that the UK Government or Parliament are responsible for.

action: I want the LatinAmerican community in the UK to be recognised as an ethnic group
background: I respectfully request that the Latin American community be formally recognised as an ethnic group in the UK. Over 450,000 Latin Americans live and contribute here, yet must still select “other” on official forms, leaving their identity unrecognised and invisible.
additional_details: I respectfully request that the Government recognise the Latin American community as an ethnic group in the UK. The movement “We are not ‘other’, we are Latinos”, which began in Elephant and Castle, highlights the lack of recognition on official forms, where Latin Americans must select “other”. This invisibility limits access to services and fair representation. Recognition would reflect decades of contribution and promote equality, visibility and inclusion.
rejection_details:

Require Latino/Hispanic option in the ethnicity section for official documents
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738829

action: Call on Government to support the hair, barbering, aesthetics & beauty sector.
background:
We call on the UK Government to hold a Parliamentary debate on how it can better support the hair, barbering, aesthetics & beauty sector.

The sector contributes £5.8 billion to the UK economy and supports over 275,000 jobs, yet it is too often overlooked in economic and social policy making.
additional_details:
We ask the Government to consider a range of support measures aligned with the NHBF’s Respect Our Sector campaign, including fairer VAT treatment, targeted skills & apprenticeship investment, employment cost reform and recognition of the sector’s social impact.

We urge MPs to recognise this sector as a skilled essential profession not just a consumer service and to debate how policy can help it grow, innovate, and continue to support the health, confidence, and prosperity of local communities.

action: Ban Bluefin Tuna sportfishing tournaments
background: We believe the Government must ban sportfishing of Bluefin Tuna as we feel it is unethical. It is reported these fish have only recently returned to British shores, and many are now being targeted by sportfishing.
additional_details: Some fishers are sportfishing and may harm these fish not for food but for their own entertainment. We urge the Government to ban this practice, or at a minimum, prevent sportfishing in shallow waters.

action: Pass a law that triggers an early General Election via a public petition
background: Right now, only the Prime Minister can request an early General Election. We believe the public should also have a clear democratic mechanism to do so.
additional_details:
We call on the Government to bring forward proposals to:

•            Pass a law where a petition signed by over 50.1% of registered voters can trigger an early General Election.
•            Allow public petitions which receive significantly large amounts of signatures to automatically trigger a no confidence debate in Parliament

Respect the previous petition calling for a general election by lodging a vote of no confidence in the cabinet
A lost vote usually results in dissolution,triggering a general election. 
The only actor that can call a general election is the PM.
Let the commons decide on the people's behalf

action: Make school dinners free for all children and young people under 18
background: The Government should provide free school meals for all children and young people under the age of 18 in education.
additional_details:
The law requires all children to remain in education until the age of 18, yet families are expected to pay for meals while children are in compulsory education. This is unfair.
Making school meals free would:

Ensure every child has at least one nutritious hot meal per day.

Ease the cost-of-living burden.

Improve concentration, behaviour, and learning outcomes.

Promote equality, as no child is disadvantaged.
If education is compulsory, access to food during that time should be guaranteed.

background: We urge the Government to pass a law which requires all public service broadcasters, including the BBC, to be required to give media coverage to political parties that is proportional to the number of MPs they have in the House of Commons.
additional_details: We believe that more fringe elements in Parliament have been given coverage and airtime due to their views rather than their level of support in Parliament. We believe that we constantly hear the opinions from a vocal minority, which outweigh the opinions of the majority. We believe reasonable party leaders are not platformed at all and that this gives an extremely skewed message to the public.

action: Replace income tax with a flat, standard annual payment
background: Abolish income tax and replace it with a mandatory annual payment to the Government that all UK residents must pay, regardless of their income, financial situation, etc. The payment will be the same for everyone.
additional_details: We believe income tax is unfair – people having to pay more simply because they earn more. It is their own money – we think they shouldn’t be penalised for earning more than others. With a flat, standard rate for everyone, we believe it will be much fairer, and ensure everyone contributes equally.

action: Open up Shaftesbury (Dorset) Police Station
background: Shaftesbury being a small town has very little police presence. The police station is closed and we would like to have it open again! Residents are starting to feel  unsafe and also fustrated due to antisocial behaviour, van/cars being broken into.
additional_details:
Help reduce the drug issues/ lower crime rates which are on an up. 
Protect local businesses and people's homes, cars and vans. General Property.
Make the residents feel safer. 
Help stop people wanting to move away. With more houses being built in the area we need our police station open

action: Commit to not increasing taxes or imposing additional taxes on landlords
background: We urge the Government to formally commit to not imposing tax increases or additional taxes on landlords to help protect current rental markets and tenants.
additional_details: We believe rental properties are essential. We are concerned there was a drop in the number of rental properties in Q1 of 2025. This supply shortage can lead to rental increases for residential properties. It was estimated that 42% of household income in London was spent on rent in 2024. We believe additional tax on Landlords will lead to the burden being passed on to the tenants. We believe it will lead to further increases in inflation and may lead to increases in homelessness.

action: Provide funding to subsidise school uniforms for all children
background: We want the Government to provide funding to subsidise free or significantly more affordable school uniforms for all school children to help families. We believe no child should be excluded or disadvantaged from education as their family can’t afford compulsory uniform.
additional_details: School uniforms are a compulsory cost for many families, yet many struggle to afford them, particularly during the cost-of-living crisis. We believe children should not face stigma, exclusion or disadvantage because their parents cannot meet these costs. As attendance at school is a legal requirement, we believe Government support is needed to ensure all pupils have equal access to education, free from financial barriers.

action: Review court system to address trial delays for rape and sexual abuse
background: We want the Government to review the court system in order to better prioritise and protect victims of rape and sexual abuse by preventing postponements of trial start dates. Victims can be left in limbo for months or years, which can cause further trauma and deny timely justice.
additional_details: Evidence from the Victims Commissioner shows that in July to September 2023, 21% of adult rape cases were rearranged on the day of trial.

action: Deploy UK forces to demilitarize terror infrastructure & weaponry from Gaza
background: We believe the UK should not endlessly criticise Israel’s actions unless it is prepared to offer a viable, operational alternative. The UK must demonstrate international leadership by taking upon itself to dismantle terrorist infrastructure entrenched in Gaza.
additional_details: The UK has repeatedly criticised Israel’s military methods. If the UK believes there's a better way, it should lead by example. British forces, known for their professionalism, should demonstrate how to neutralise terrorists without harming civilians or causing collateral damage. This would test the feasibility of disarming terrorists embedded in civilian areas, and would show that UK criticism is backed by practical solutions, not rhetoric.

action: Enable parents to register birth and death of babies carried beyond 24 weeks
background: We ask the Government to change the law so parents can register the birth and death of babies carried beyond 24 weeks, even if they passed earlier. Families deserve recognition and dignity, not the miscarriage label, for the babies they carried and gave birth to.
additional_details:
I lost my daughter, Winnie, during pregnancy the day before I reached 24 weeks. I knew my body and my babies’ movements, so I realised her heart had stopped. I carried her for another 8 weeks and gave birth to her via c-section at 32 weeks, alongside her siblings. Despite this, she was labelled a miscarriage. That word does not reflect the reality of carrying and birthing a baby after 24 weeks. It’s painful, dismissive, and denies families the recognition they deserve.
 
I want the Government and Parliament to change the law so that when a baby is carried beyond 24 weeks, parents have the right to register both the birth and the death, no matter when the baby passed. This change would bring dignity, acknowledgement, and comfort to grieving families.

action: Fix the poor service from TFL, particularly the district line.
background: Demand higher standards of service. Demand consistency and clear, accurate communication. 'Signal error' is over used and clearly inaccurate. Commuters on the district line are constantly late to work, important appointments and life events due to poor service.
additional_details: TFL are constantly increasing the prices and not providing the good service they are 'selling'. This affects thousands of people everyday and is simply not good enough.

action: Require watermarking of all AI-generated images and videos
background: We ask the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring all AI-generated images and videos to be clearly and permanently watermarked. This would help the public distinguish synthetic content from real media, reduce misinformation, and promote transparency in digital communication.
additional_details: As AI tools become more advanced, it is increasingly difficult to tell the difference between real and generated content. While these technologies offer incredible creative potential, they also pose risks, especially in news, politics, and social media, where realistic fakes can mislead or manipulate. Watermarking would preserve creative freedom while protecting public trust. It’s a simple, scalable way to ensure clarity in an increasingly synthetic world.

action: Pause UK offshore CO₂ storage projects and conduct full safety and legal review
background: We ask the Government to pause all UK offshore CO₂ storage projects until a full independent safety, environmental and legal assessment is completed. Some research suggests that injecting impure CO₂ can risk acid formation, toxic metal release, and long-term damage to marine ecosystems and aquifers.
additional_details: The Public Accounts Committee, Parliament’s own spending watchdog has already warned that Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology is untested at scale in the UK and has a mixed record globally. We think large-scale CCS is being advanced at speed despite major gaps in transparency, regulation, and public consultation.
government_response_summary: There are no plans to pause the development of UK Offshore CO₂ storage projects. Government works with regulators and the public to ensure CO2 storage regulations support the safe deployment of CCUS.
government_response_body: Carbon Capture, Usage and Storage (CCUS) enables CO2 produced across the economy to be stored safely and permanently deep beneath the seabed typically at depths greater than 800 metres, either in depleted oil and gas fields or saline aquifers. At these depths, CO2 is stored in offshore rock formations known as reservoirs, which are structured like a sponge and sealed by impermeable cap rock above. A typical geological storage site can permanently hold tens of million tonnes of CO2. (1) Geological CO₂ storage has been in operation globally for decades; although not yet deployed at scale within the UK, there are many examples globally of secure CO₂ storage. Norway, for example, has been storing CO2 offshore since 1996, with over 20 million tonnes of CO2 stored.(2)  To unlock sufficient CO2 storage capacity to meet Carbon Budget and Net Zero targets (3), potential CO2 storage sites will need to go through extensive appraisal, permitting and development activities. These activities increase confidence that a store can permanently and safely store CO2. If exploration and appraisal activity demonstrate that a site is suitable for CO2 storage, this site can then be permitted, developed and used pending commercial agreements.  Independent technical analysis commissioned by Government shows very high long-term containment confidence (4) with a typical project expected to retain over 99.9% of injected CO₂ over a 125-year period. Minor leak rates have a low probability of occurring whereas major leak rates have a very low probability of occurring. Therefore, the likelihood of damage to the marine ecosystem is considered to be very low. This is a central reassurance for the public and a key consideration in site selection and operational oversight. These assessments also consider risks associated with onshore and offshore CO₂ pipelines, which are regulated to the same high standards as other major hazard pipelines.  The UK has a comprehensive, multi-regulator regime overseeing the safe deployment of CCUS. The North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) is the technical regulator for offshore CO₂ storage and has granted permits for the HyNet and East Coast Cluster projects (5), issuing permits only where there is no significant risk of leakage or harm to the environment or human health. Before any permit is approved, the Offshore Petroleum Regulator for Environment and Decommissioning (OPRED), on behalf of the Secretary of State, undertakes the required Environmental Impact Assessment, including public consultation, which takes into account any potential environmental impact of the proposals including any impacts on marine protected areas. The NSTA cannot issue a permit without the Secretary of State’s agreement to OPRED’s assessment. The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) is the national regulator for workplace health and safety, covering offshore activities and the operation of pipelines, and regulates the health and safety of CCUS operations both onshore and offshore. Duty holders must identify and control risks, and HSE applies a goalsetting, targeted, proportionate and evidence based regulatory approach under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act, with interventions that support duty holders to meet their legal responsibilities. Alongside these controls, environmental regulators in England and the Devolved Administrations issue environmental permits for onshore activities ensuring robust environmental protection across all onshore elements of CCUS projects.  Storage site operators are subject to strict legal obligations to monitor stored CO2 and report on storage performance throughout the operational lifetime of a project and after sites are closed. The NSTA assesses proposed monitoring plans, which must, include monitoring during the operational lifetime of the project and the 20-year post-closure period once operations have ceased. In accordance with UK legislation, offshore CCUS infrastructure must be removed when decommissioned at the end of its operational lifetime, further reinforcing confidence in CO₂ containment for storage sites that receive a storage permit.  The UK does not plan to pause the development of CCUS, as full independent safety, environmental and legal assessments are already carried out for each storage site, and the UK has a strong regulatory environment to deploy CCUS safely.   Footnotes:  (1) Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (2018) (2) Equinor, Sleipner CO₂ Storage Project Overview (3) The Seventh Carbon Budget - Climate Change Committee (4) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/deep-geological-storage-of-carbon-dioxide-co2-offshore-uk-containment-certainty (5) Under Chapter 3, Part 1 of the Energy Act 2008, Ministers in the Devolved Administrations are the licensing authorities for CO₂ storage activities that fall within devolved competence, including onshore storage and, in Scotland, the territorial sea, while the NSTA remains the licensing authority for storage on the UK Continental Shelf.
