action: Include the Welsh Dragon in the Union Flag/Jack to represent Wales
background: We, the undersigned, formally request that His Majesty's Government makes provision towards amending the Union Flag/Jack in order to include the Welsh Dragon, or Y Ddraig Goch, within the centre of the flag.
additional_details:
Wales is the fourth Constituent Country of the United Kingdom, but is not represented within the flag which characterises the U.K.'s identity. When the flag was produced, only England, Scotland and Ireland were Constituent Countries, but the situation has since changed.

This change would make Wales feel an included and equal partner in this nation.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition that calls for the same action:

Introduce Y Ddraig Goch (The Red Dragon) to the union flag (representing Wales) https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742977

action: Fund not-for-profit NHS dispensing pharmacies in all UK towns
background: We urge the Government to fund not-for-profit NHS dispensing pharmacies in every town in the UK, including the re-opening of any pharmacy that previously closed as NHS dispensing pharmacies. We believe they are a lifeline for anyone in need of prescription medicine and drugs.
additional_details: We are concerned about dispensing pharmacies closing across the UK as they may be unviable, which can leave people, particularly the elderly and vulnerable, with no way of getting prescriptions. We believe additional goods for sale in pharmacies can be purchased elsewhere, but prescriptions which are vital for many people can only be supplied by qualified pharmacists, so we believe it is the Government’s duty that all UK citizens have access to one.

action: Close the ‘main residence’ loophole in UK property tax rules
background: Align the definition of ‘main residence’ across taxes and councils, require consistent declarations to HMRC and councils, and close loopholes that let people avoid stamp duty or council tax by claiming different main homes.
additional_details: Recent reports show people declaring different ‘main residences’ to HMRC and councils to avoid the 3% stamp duty surcharge and reduce council tax. With taxpayers facing high burdens and public services under strain, this undermines trust and fairness. Align definitions, require consistency, and close the gap.
rejection_details: You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Pause NHS Neighbourhood plans, protect local GP surgeries & hold consultation
background: Pause the rollout of Neighbourhood Health reforms. Hold a full public consultation, publish detailed implementation plans, commit to protecting GP surgeries, and formally commit to and guarantee that no contracts will be handed to private companies or overstretched hospital trusts.
additional_details:
We are concerned that the reforms could:
Lead to closing or merging local GP surgeries
End continuity of care with family doctors
Force patients to travel further for appointments
Bankrupt GP practices and force them shut as warned by the BMA
Hand contracts to struggling hospital trusts or private firms
Risk longer waits, poorer access and loss of trusted local care for patients
 
We call for an immediate pause, a full public consultation, protection for GP surgeries, and for the Government to formally guarantee that contracts will not be handed to private companies.

action: Amend the home buying process in England to align with Scotland
background: We ask the UK Government to reform property law in England to align more closely with the Scottish model. The process in Scotland makes offers legally binding earlier, which we think helps reduce fall-throughs and creates a more secure, fair process for all.
additional_details:
We believe the home buying/selling process in England is archaic, slow, uncertain and costly. Sales can often fail due to legal loopholes like gazumping & late stage withdrawals. We think these could be prevented by making accepted offers legally binding earlier, and introducing set timescales to complete transactions.
We believe these changes would help protect buyers and sellers, reduce wasted costs, and could mean the government will receive more taxes quicker.

action: Ensure Home Office needs planning permission for all hotel asylum accommodation
background: Amend the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999 and the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 so the Home Office must always seek local planning permission before using any hotels to house asylum seekers, ensuring local councils and communities are consulted.
additional_details: The Home Office has a duty to house asylum seekers who appear to be destitute. It can repurpose hotels for asylum accommodation if this does not represent a material change of use to a building or land. We think this undermines planning law and public safety. We want Parliament to require that any and all uses of hotels for asylum accommodation is treated as a material change of use needing planning permission and consultation with local councils, so communities have a voice and safety standards are upheld.

action: Review the Government’s housebuilding target & require infrastructure investment
background: We urge the Government to review their target to build 1.5 million homes. We want the review to focus on affordable houses and social housing over private sales.  We urge the Government to mandate that developments can only be approved with guaranteed investment for essential infrastructure.
additional_details: This includes schools, transport, GP services, shops & flood defences. We believe the current target risks a legacy of unsold private homes and destroyed communities. Without mandated affordable housing, we are concerned families remain unhoused. Rushing development without upfront infrastructure investment could overwhelm public services, erode village character and destroy the environment. We believe this approach fails on its own terms and sacrifices communities for a flawed numerical goal.

action: Take stronger measures to enforce payment of child maintenance arrears.
background: Take a stronger stance on non-paying parents related to Child maintenance and enforce more stringent measures to ensure they not only pay the regular payments due but clear any child maintenance arrears, especially when there's evidence the non paying parents can afford to do so.
additional_details: Of the Child Maintenance payments arranged through the Collect and Pay service, the total unpaid was £27.8 million. The government have the power to enforce collection but we think they aren't doing this adequately.

action: Opposition to table a Motion of No Confidence in His Majesty’s Government
background: We urge the Leader of the Opposition, and all opposition parties, to exercise their constitutional responsibility by calling a vote of no confidence at the earliest opportunity.
additional_details: This government has lost the confidence of the people through it’s bad management of the illegal migration situation in the country and has put the rights of the illegal migrants above the rights of the British population. Under the conventions of our constitution, it is the duty of Parliament to test whether the Prime Minister still commands a majority in the House of Commons.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

You might like to sign this petition:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Change CMS Child Maintenance Calculations to Be Based on Net Pay, Not Gross Pay
background: A formal government review into the fairness and accuracy of CMS calculations and to review and reform the way the Child Maintenance Service (CMS) calculates maintenance payments.
additional_details:
CMS bases assessments on a paying parent’s GROSS income, without taking into account the significant deductions that are made before a person actually receives their take-home pay such as Income Tax & NI.
This creates financial burden that's unfairly disproportionate for parents already struggling with the rising cost of living. Parents pay thousands of pounds a year in tax and National Insurance – money that is never physically seen. It is unjust to base child maintenance on the pre-tax figure.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for the same action:

Calculate child maintenance from net pay, not gross pay
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730665

action: Cancel the UK-India Free Trade Agreement due to Indian purchases of Russian oil
background: We urge the UK Government to cancel the UK-India Free Trade Agreement as punishment for India buying Russian oil, which we believe is helping fund Russia’s war against Ukraine. We believe the FTA should only be renewed if India halts all purchases of Russian oil.
additional_details: It is estimated that Russia has made over $130 billion in oil sales to India since 2022, which we believe has helped fund Russia’s war against Ukraine. The FTA is projected to boost UK GDP by £4.8 billion per year, but the UK has committed £21.8 billion to help Ukraine against Russia, which we believe is being supported by India. We believe this makes no sense, and that the sooner Russia is crippled economically, the sooner the war will end.

action: Stop the clocks from going back and forward and stick with GMT+1
background: In October every year the clocks are stopped for an hour and in April an hour is skipped. I think that it would be in the best interest of the people to stop this act and instead stick with the current timezone all year round; GMT+1.
additional_details: The most blaring reason is to help with depression caused by seasonal affective disorder, an hour would make a great difference to people especially during times when returning from school and work when it can be dark in winter. I believe that it will make most people happier in the winter, a time when depression is highest, gaining a feeling that the days are longer due to later sunsets and it will also allow more people to witness the sunrise, an equally beautiful moment.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/723945

action: Seek to form a free movement union and passport across CANZUK
background: We urge the UK Government to seek to negotiate a CANZUK Union passport with Canada, Australia and New Zealand to ensure free movement across the four nations. As key Anglosphere nations with shared heritage, we believe it would let citizens live, work and travel freely, while strengthening ties.
additional_details: We believe this proposal would strengthen political, economic and cultural ties, particularly as the USA grows into what we believe is an increasingly unreliable ally; fostering deeper cooperation, unity, and mutual opportunity across all four countries.

action: Campaign for shorter school holidays - reduce from 6 weeks to 4 weeks.
background: Consider shortening the summer holidays - this will benefit children as too long out of routine is not helpful and more time in education can only be a good thing. This will also benefit parents helping reduce stress, financial strain, improve work life balance.
additional_details:
Long breaks can disrupt sleep schedules, study habits, and daily structure.

Shorter holidays help maintain steady learning rhythms throughout the year.

Some children have access to enriching summer camps, travel, or tutoring, but others may not.

Long holidays can widen inequality because disadvantaged students may miss out on opportunities to learn or stay engaged.

Shorter, more frequent breaks spread throughout the year may be better for students’ and teachers’ well-being, avoiding the burnout of a long uninterrupted term while also preventing the boredom and isolation that can sometimes come with very long summers.
rejection_details:
Term dates are determined locally by schools and local authorities.

For maintained schools, community schools, community special schools, voluntary controlled schools, pupil referral units and maintained nursery schools, the governing body or local authority are responsible for setting term dates.

Academies, free schools, and other schools where the governing body is the employer of staff, such as foundation or voluntary-aided (church) schools, are free to set their own term and holiday dates.

action: Mandate a minimum 2-year prison sentence for benefit fraud & penalise offenders
background:
We urge the Government to pass a law that:
1. Mandates a minimum 2-year prison sentence for anyone guilty of benefit fraud.
2. Bans any further benefit claims for offenders for 5 years.
3. Removes criminals’ passports who travelled abroad with stolen money for 10 years.
additional_details: We feel there are disparities in the scale of fraud and sentencing. We believe too many criminals are given suspended sentences, including repeat offenders. We believe this undermines people in genuine need and alienates the taxpayers in supporting welfare. We believe the welfare budget is out of control with no deterrent to fraud. We believe there must be a deterrent to demotivate offenders and encourage them to find work to improve their lives, not steal from the taxpayer.

action: Ban excessive waiting times on customer service helplines
background: We want the Government to introduce a law that prevents companies from keeping customers waiting on hold for more than 30 minutes. Any company that offers customer support over the phone should be required to answer within a reasonable time or provide a free call-back option.
additional_details:
Many people are left waiting on hold for 30 minutes or longer when trying to reach customer service. This happens across many industries and wastes customers’ time, causes stress, and can be especially difficult for vulnerable people.

We believe companies should not be allowed to trap customers in long waiting queues. A legal maximum waiting time of 5 minutes, or mandatory free call-back service, would ensure fair treatment and better customer service standards for everyone.
rejection_details: It is unclear whether you want the government to mandate a 5 minute or 30 minute maximum waiting time. You could submit a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Require all public buildings in England to fly Cross of St George
background: We urge the Government to require all public buildings, including governmental and municipal buildings, in England to fly the Cross of St George. We want no other flags or signs to be flown with it, apart from the Union Flag and/or county colours.
additional_details: We support this proposal as we want to show the public’s support for the English flag and that we believe it is not racist to be proud of your country.

action: Lifetime ban on owning animals and prison for convictions of animal cruelty.
background: Change the law and sentencing guidelines to award a mandatory prison sentence and a lifetime ban on owning or caring for any animal for anyone convicted of animal cruelty.
additional_details: There are too many cases of animal cruelty going to court. In these cases animals are subjected to horrific injuries and torment, starvation, dehydration, abandonment and death. The sentences do not create enough deterrent or reflect the seriousness of the crime. The sentences handed out in most cases equate to a slap on the wrist particularly when solicitors use mental health issues as an excuse for the unacceptable behaviour.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Ban Private Dog Breeding and Strengthen Penalties for Animal Cruelty 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728177

action: Make builders liable for all costs associated with remedial cladding works
background: We urge the Government to pass a law which requires builders to pay for all costs associated with remedial cladding work, including increases in insurance premiums and service charges due to remedial work.
additional_details: Remedial cladding work on many developments, following the Building Safety Act 2022, has left many leaseholders out of pocket due to increases to their insurance premiums (which may be passed to leaseholders in their service charges). We believe the Government should require all builders to pay for all costs associated with necessary remedial work. We believe it can be easily calculated by looking at the trend in past insurance increases each year and making builders pay the difference.

action: Make a manifesto and pre election promises a contract that has to be delivered
background: Once elected a MP can do as they see appropriate and take action accordingly. This negates any pre election promise or manifesto since a party can promise actions but once elected  can completely change their minds. I call on the government to make a manifesto a form of contract that is enforceable
additional_details:
The public have lost faith in the people and parties that are running the country and this action I am asking would help restore faith in a system that can be used in appropriately.
A party can promise the public the earth yet once elected deliver the exact opposite, parties have access to facts and figures and should only promise that which they know they can deliver. If a party does not deliver that which it said it would do then serious action should be taken even including an election.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Require election & manifesto pledges to be implemented and legally enforced
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724417

action: Equalise maternity allowance with statutory pay & don’t reduce Universal Credit
background: We urge the Government to equalise maternity, paternity and adoption allowances with statutory maternity pay for self-employed workers and ensure that maternity allowance pay does not reduce Universal Credit pay. We believe families shouldn’t be penalised for being self-employed.
additional_details: Many women are self-employed or running their own businesses, yet we feel the maternity pay system has not kept up. Self-employed mothers only receive maternity allowance, which can be far lower and less flexible than statutory maternity pay available to employees. We believe this leaves many families financially vulnerable at a time when they should be supported and the current system is outdated.

action: Hold MPs accountable for distinguishing fact from opinion in public discourse.
background:
1. Introduce legislation requiring MPs to clearly identify between opinions and facts in all their public communications.
2. Establish a new offence of "Misleading the Public" to hold MPs accountable for spreading false or misleading information.
additional_details:
The current lack of transparency and accountability in public discourse is eroding trust in our institutions and creating division in our society. MPs presenting opinions as facts or spreading misinformation:
- Misinforms the public and their decisions
- Undermines the credibility of our institutions
- Fosters a culture of distrust and polarization
By supporting this petition, we can promote a more informed and engaged citizenry through a high standard of truthfulness and fact based discourse.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legislate to allow recall of MPs found to have deliberately misled the public
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731105

action: Make St. George's Day a bank holiday in England.
background: Make St. George's Day a bank holiday in England.
additional_details: Make St. George's Day a bank holiday in England.
rejection_details:
Make St George’s Day a Bank Holiday for people in England
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739078

action: Review potential impact of AI on employment opportunities for disabled people
background: I call on the Government to assess and regulate the impact of generative AI on employment opportunities for disabled people—particularly those with profound physical disabilities who rely on desk-based roles.
additional_details:
Some recent public statements from leading AI developers have suggested that generative AI could eliminate many white-collar and desk-based jobs. These may be the only viable employment options for some physically disabled people, who cannot work in manual or physical roles.
I believe this could create a foreseeable and systemic disadvantage for disabled people, which may constitute indirect discrimination under the Equality Act 2010 and a denial of right to work under the Human Rights Act 1998.

action: Change laws on tissue storage for unborn babies with genetic conditions
background:
Current legislation prevents parents from storing the tissue of aborted foetuses for future clinical use. 

However, technological advances mean it will soon be possible to genetically edit or silence genetic disorders identified in early pregnancy.
additional_details:
Changing the law to allow parents to store the tissue of aborted babies with genetic disorders will provide some hope that, in future, they will be able to give these children a healthier life once the technology to silence or edit these genetic disorders is freely available. 

Recent scientific advances suggest this technology could be clinically available in the not so distant future if the legalisative framework were to allow for it.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We think you may be referring to section 3A of the 1990 act which prohibits the use of eggs taken from aborted foetuses in fertility treatments. However, we are unsure.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Make divorces where a child is abused automatically eligible for legal aid
background: Someone who can prove they have suffered domestic abuse is able to access legal aid for divorce, but if the abuse was suffered by a child within the family, even if there are convictions, they have no automatic access to legal aid for divorce. We believe this needs to change!
additional_details: We believe in the event of a conviction of child sexual abuse in the family home, the other parent of the child may have to pick up the pieces and has no automatic access to legal aid for the divorce. After major trauma within the family and financial hardship that breakups can bring, one parent may be left legally tied to the predator that committed crimes against their child as they may be unable to afford the divorce. It can be truly traumatic.

action: Amend the Planning & Infrastructure Bill to ban wind farms on protected peatland
background:
We want the government to amend its Planning & Infrastructure Bill to:
1. Ban wind farms on peatland in the National Site Network and SSSIs in England, and
2. Require the restoration to good conservation status of peatland’s interlinked mosaic of habitats, including irreplaceable blanket bog.
additional_details: We believe these amendments are needed to protect peatland’s ecological integrity: benefiting climate, biodiversity, water quality and flood risk mitigation. We think that new energy policy statements increase safeguards for peatland, but aren't enough, and still greenlight development on shallower peat - which science warns against. There are concerns that the Sec of State may ignore potential damage to protected sites and approve 'Critical National Priority' windfarms on peatland subject to “compensation” - which we believe is impossible in a near timeframe.

action: Build Solar Farms on existing buildings not on Green Belt land.
background: The Govt should be promoting building solar farms on buildings such as govt/council buildings, hospitals, car parks, shopping centres, in fact any existing buildings suitable for this purpose, which are plentiful & adjacent to infrastructure, it makes no sense to build on Green Belt land, full stop.
additional_details: The govt has a green mandate, cut emissions, make our country self sufficient with renewable power and move away from fossil fuel, we have so many man made structures upon which solar panels could be erected, out of sight, not on our green belt & adjacent to existing infrastructure, why are we not implementing this, I do not understand?, please support this petition, thank you.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735942

action: Review family court legal aid for working mothers who've survived domestic abuse
background: We believe the legal aid means test is outdated, unfair and doesn't reflect the cost of living. We are concerned that women are being trapped in unsafe situations or denied justice as they earn slightly too much on paper. No mother should have to choose between safety and justice due to her salary.
additional_details: We're calling for a fairer system to protect mothers and children. Government should review family court legal aid for mothers who have survived domestic abuse. We urge Government to raise the legal aid threshold so more working mothers can access aid. Government should also introduce an emergency legal aid voucher scheme for survivors just above the threshold to contribute towards legal costs. The review should consider how the process for survivors to prove abuse and access legal aid can be simplified.

action: Align to Intl. Law to Protect Farming as Cultural Heritage & Nat’l SecurityAsset
background: To formally recognise farming/ farm stewardship as a protected element of the UK’s national cultural heritage, essential to national security, food sovereignty, environmental stewardship. Ensure  its protection in UK law under existing international human rights and cultural heritage obligations
additional_details:
We call on the UK Government to recognise farming/farmland stewardship as UK intangible cultural heritage under the UNESCO Convention, and within obligations under ICESCR & ECHR. Acknowledge farming as a strategic national security asset. Enshrine in law protections from CPOs, punitive tax, or non-farm use without overriding need, due process & fair compensation, safeguarding food security & heritage.

In times of global instability the UK must prioritise food security and our farming heritage.

action: Open an investigation into the use of VAR (Video Assistant Referee) in Football
background: We want an investigation into how VAR is being used within English football. We also want an investigation into how the FA and PGMOL are allowing this type of technology at football games and the affect it is having.
additional_details: We are seeking a ban into using the VAR technology within football. This technology is being delivered from a corrupt system. The use of VAR is not consistent and it is not fair. The PGMOL are clearly not trained in the use of the technology and are inconsistencies how the technology is used and which teams are being discriminated against with the decisions.
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Decisions about how to referee football matches are a matter for organisers and the football authorities, not the Government or House of Commons.

action: Reduce the sound of fireworks to under 80 decibels for humans and animals
background: I think fireworks are being used more frequently throughout the year and are becoming a nuisance. I want the government to mandate that fireworks should be reduced to below 80 decibels so they are safer for humans and animals.

action: Capital punishment for convicted pedophiles 11 years old and under.
background: Children that have no sex education or who are legally not allowed to be unsupervised that are subjected to pedophila are at risk of life long illness and self harm. I belive the convicted preparators should face capital punishment. If they have preyed and premeditated to engage in sexual activity.
additional_details:
Risks of pedophila;
Reoffending is high 
It is becoming normalised on social media and in the national press; then becomes a threat to police, cps, law firms, judges, medical staff and teachers who are innocent and involved as their is no faith or trust.
The industry of pedophila equals to sex trafficking, hostages, drug taking, long term prescriptions, loss of ambition, it ends careers for innocent child protecting roles when under investigation. 
Housing costs to rehouse offenders.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Reinstate capital punishment for those convicted of sexually abusing of a child
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739802

action: Make August the UK National Flag month.
background: The Government should declare that every year, the month of August is the UK’s National flag month. This is to further the expression of pride in all things British. Everyone should be encouraged to celebrate and fly flags traditional to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
additional_details: The UK’s National flag month is to further the expression of pride in all things British. In August everyone should be encouraged to celebrate and fly flags traditional to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, such as the Union Flag, the flags of St George or St Andrew, the Welsh Flag or the Ulster Flag. Councils will also allow residents and volunteers to celebrate all things British in style by flying these traditional UK flags on municipal property such as lamp posts.
rejection_details: The UK Government and Parliament are not responsible for creating national days or months.

action: Ban fish-shaped single-use plastic soy sauce dispensers
background: Plastic fish used in takeaway sushi and soy sauce are wasteful, non-recyclable, and contribute to environmental harm. Banning their use would reduce plastic pollution, protect marine life, and encourage sustainable alternatives, aligning with the UK's environmental goals and reducing excess waste.
additional_details: Following an Australian state's recent ban on these, single-use plastic fish in takeaway sushi and soy sauce packages are an unnecessary source of pollution. These items often end up in landfills or oceans, harming wildlife and ecosystems. As the UK strives to reduce plastic waste and meet climate goals, banning such items will help lower plastic consumption, protect marine life, and promote sustainable packaging alternatives. With growing awareness, it’s vital for the government to take action on this.

action: Make the wearing of Balaclavas in public places illegal
background: Grant the police the powers required to stop and forcibly remove from wearers and confiscate balaclavas.  The police should also be granted the power to forcibly stop all 2 wheeled bikes (motorbikes, ebikes, push bikes, surron electric bikes) where the rider(s) are wearing  balaclavas in public.
additional_details:
lawbreakers are adept at evading justice thanks to one simple but effective tool: the balaclava. It conceals their identities and transforms them into unidentifiable figures.

Balaclavas have gained notoriety as the accessory of choice for those who wish to commit crime without facing accountability. The anonymity provided by these garments is not just a minor concern.....it is a Major concern and the police must be granted powers to stop, forcibly remove these garments from wearers and confiscate them.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726978

action: Licence all dog breeders and limit litters to one per dog
background: We want the government to make it law that all dog breeders must be licenced and that each dog is only allowed a limited amount of litters in their lifetime.
additional_details: We believe that many dogs are overbred by inexperienced people seeking profit and puppies often go to unsuitable homes or shelters. We are also concerned that overbreeding and poor socialisation could cause aggression, increasing dog attacks. We think licencing and limiting the amount of litters per dog could help ensure dog welfare and public safety.

action: Call on the government to Re-Nationalise ALL water companies in England & wales
background:
Re-Nationalise Water – Stop Pollution and Profits Before People

For too long private water firms have polluted our rivers, taken massive profits, and rewarded their bosses—while we, the public picks up the bill.

We want the government to start the process to Re-Nationalise water now!
additional_details:
In the past decade, water company executives have pocketed over £112 million in bonuses—even as sewage pollution surged. 

In 2023–24 alone, £7.6 million was paid in bonuses despite widespread environmental destruction. 

Shareholders received more than £1.35 billion in dividends as sewage poured into waterways for over 3.5 million hours, equating to £377 per hour of pollution. Please sign this petition.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Nationalise all water companies
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727463

action: High achievers: let grade 9 mocks count as real GCSE results
background: Allow students who achieve a grade 9 in their official GCSE mock exams to have it count as their final GCSE, so they don’t need to retake the subject in summer. This would reward top performers, reduce stress, and free time for further study or enrichment.
rejection_details: Decisions about this are a matter for exam boards, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Change the system of governance
background: call a country wide vote for a new system of governance, dissolve perminently parliament, the house of lords and centralised power.
additional_details:
The public are fed up, of the corruption, of the lack of change, of the consistent degradation of our infrastructure and of our freedoms.

We call for a country wide vote on a new system of governance, I propose direct democracy, where each registered voter can vote on everything, is given all relevant information and is trusted to want the best for themselves and those around them.

Centralised power has failed, its time for genuine change, not just swapping out puppets.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may wish to sign the following: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/718906

action: Allow UK courts to enforce child maintenance when parents move overseas.
background: Close the loophole that stops the Child Maintenance Service enforcing payments if a parent is posted abroad by a UK employer. Use the UK–India Free Trade Agreement to secure a treaty so Sheriff and Family Courts can enforce maintenance internationally.
additional_details: Child maintenance is a child’s right, not a privilege. At present, when a parent is transferred abroad by a UK employer to a non-reciprocal country like India, enforcement stops. Mothers are forced into costly High Court cases. This loophole enables financial abuse. The UK–India FTA is a chance to fix this through a bilateral treaty.
rejection_details:
The arrangements you are requesting are already place, so we are not clear what action you are seeking. 

You could start a new petition with a clear request about how you would like the current system to change, or if you would like a review of enforcement arrangements.

action: Ban UK companies shipping and insuring all Russian Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG)
background: Russia is helping finance its illegal invasion of Ukraine by oil and gas exports, including LNG. The UK sanctions all imports of Russian oil and gas. It also sanctions the shipping and insurance of Russian oil sold above a cap. It must now sanction the shipping and insurance of all Russian LNG.
additional_details: Russia’s exports of oil and gas are its main source of foreign exchange, helping fund its criminal invasion of Ukraine. The extraction, production, shipping, and burning of Russian LNG are also significant contributors to Arctic and global heating. Some analysis has shown that since February 2022, UK-owned or insured vessels have carried around £45 billion, (76%) of Russia’s LNG exports - almost 4 times the UK's £12.8bn total aid to Ukraine up to February 2025.

action: Ban universities from using GCSEs for applications.
background: GCSEs should only be used to determine a student's next course in higher education, not further. This is not a call to undermine GCSEs, but a call to place emphasis on the capabilities of applicants at the time of their application, not two years prior.
additional_details: Using solely Level 3 qualifications for university applications employs students the ability to be placed in an environment where they thrive due to having complete control over their subjects. That being said their interest and competence should be prioritised over their Level 2 qualifications. This also reduces the level of demand for jobs that require certain degrees.

action: Repeal or amend the Online Safety Act to protect free speech and privacy
background: Review and amend the Online Safety Act 2023 to ensure compliance with UK GDPR, the Human Rights Act, and protections for privacy and freedom of speech.
additional_details: The Act requires intrusive age checks and monitoring that risk breaching data protection, privacy, and free expression. Citizens must be able to access lawful content without surveillance or censorship.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Repeal the Online Safety Act
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/722903

action: One wage should be enough - make tax fair for families
background: Introduce Optional Joint Filing for married couples and civil partners. Let households pool income, split it equally, and apply both partners’ tax allowances and bands. Keep individual filing as default so no one is worse off.
additional_details: The UK tax system penalises families where one parent earns most or all of the income. Two people on £33k each pay far less tax than one earner on £66k supporting a partner and children. Optional Joint Filing fixes this unfairness, makes one wage go further, reduces reliance on Universal Credit, and brings us in line with family-friendly systems like Germany and France.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727117

action: Mandate a (Less Scroll) More Soul Bank Holiday: An annual offline day
background: Britain needs a breather. An annual reset for our overwhelmed lives. A day where the nation logs off, looks up and reconnects. A government-enforced opportunity to not only build awareness for the grip tech has on us but remind us of what matters in a healthy society:  people, place and presence.
additional_details:
We are an addicted nation. An 18 yr old will spend 25 yrs of their life on a phone. Children spend less time outdoors (<1hr) than inmates. Loneliness, anxiety and polarisation are spiraling and all this before consideration of specific harms: exploitation, radicalisation, misinformation+

The UK has fewer bank holidays than almost anywhere in Europe.
One offline day/ year could provide a critical reset and reminder of what’s important. A day to reconnect with ourselves and our local communities.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726031

action: Remove option for family to object to deceased person's wishes to donate organs
background: We call on the government to amend the Organ Donation (Deemed Consent) Act (AKA Max and Keira's law), so donor decisions—recorded or deemed—are honoured without family or loved ones being able to object to the decision of the deceased person.
additional_details: We believe Max and Keira’s Law was a vital first step, but that family vetoes still block hundreds of donations every year, even when someone clearly chose to donate. Consent rates have fallen since 2020 and the waiting list is now the highest in a decade, with thousands waiting and hundreds dying whilst waiting for a donation each year. We should respect donor wishes, ease pressure on grieving families, and give patients the second chance they deserve.

action: Fund more affordable, accessible housing for families with disabled children
background: Create a national fund for affordable, accessible housing for families raising disabled children across the UK. We believe thousands of families with disabled children live in unsuitable or unsafe housing, paying sky high rents to private landlords.
additional_details: We think many face overcrowding, long waits for adaptations, and financial hardship. We urge the Government to fund more inclusive housing projects, to support local authorities to build homes specifically for families with disabled children. We believe every child deserves a safe, suitable home to thrive. Let this be their future.

action: All roundabouts in England, Scotland, Wales and NI decorated in countries flag
background:
The government should make it legal/possible for all county councils and local authorities to paint all roundabouts in the colours of the respective countries flag.

Our national flag and those of our United Kingdom family should be a source of pride.
additional_details:
The petition to do this should include some compulsory measures being enforced by government on councils to redecorate roundabouts in national flag colours when in need or repair or repainting.

This petition fits with the government’s own agenda of wanting to see more flags, and what better way to do this.

There should be no excuses, such as painting roundabouts make them unsafe, as clearly a colourful roundabout painted in the countries respective flag make the roundabout stand out much more.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Signage and maintenance on roundabouts are a matter for the authority managing the road network on which the roundabout is situated. Depending on the roundabout in question, this could either be the local authority, or National Highways.

action: Extend 30 hours free childcare to all working parents, regardless of visa status
background: As working parents on visas, we pay the same taxes as everyone else, yet our children are excluded from the 30 hours free childcare scheme. This creates inequality, adds financial strain, and denies children like ours the early education they need to thrive.
additional_details: Currently, families on visas with “No Recourse to Public Funds” cannot access the 30 hours free childcare scheme, even though they pay the same taxes as everyone else. Government guidance states that early education and childcare funding is not classed as a “public fund,” so children should not be excluded from the free childcare scheme on immigration grounds. Access should be based on work and contribution, not status, so all children have equal opportunities.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign the petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725832

action: Reinstate capital punishment for those convicted of sexually abusing of a child
background: Change the law to allow for the death penalty to be imposed to anyone convicted for raping or sexually abusing a child or vulnerable person.
additional_details:
We believe there surely is no more heinous a crime than this kind of physical and psychological damage imposed on our precious children. We believe that there are no success stories where full rehabilitation and ‘cure’ has taken place with regard to sexual attraction towards minors. These people are, in our view, the biggest blight on society.
 
We think that grooming gangs have further fuelled and highlighted the need for the gallows for such acts.

action: Introduce joint income taxation for a household
background: We would like to urge the government to revise the UK tax system to allow married couples, civil partners or cohabitants to file income tax jointly, enabling household-level assessment instead of individual assessment.
additional_details:
The current UK system penalises couples with unequal incomes. Joint taxation would benefit families, encourage financial equality and fairness. 
Avoiding the £100k personal allowance trap, this is especially attractive for families where one parent stays at home or works part-time. It would support family stability and child welfare, encourage workforce flexibility without penalising families, and improve labour market participation.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727117

action: Fund free rape alarms and make them available for everyone
background: We want the government to make rape alarms free and available to anyone who feels that they want one. We believe the country has become less secure and safe.
additional_details: We think making these available and free could help keep people safe and show compassion for those who have been affected.

action: MP must live in the area for min of 3yrs & within 10miles during their term
background:
MPs married or living in a relationship must share one home that has the tax relive on it! 
No second-home tax relief. This ensures MPs live among those they represent, understand local needs, and stop exploiting taxpayer perks.
additional_details:
This requirement would ensure MPs genuinely live among the people they represent, fully understand local needs, remain accountable to their community, and cannot exploit taxpayer-funded perks for personal gain.
The candidate’s main residence must always be within the constituency or no more than 10 miles outside it. 
To ensure fairness, reasonable exceptions may apply where constituency boundaries have recently changed.

action: Allow care worker visa holders to change employer
background: We want the government to replace the current visa scheme for care workers, where care worker is bound to the employers who have sponsored their visa, to a new scheme which allows the visa holders switch jobs freely still within the health sector without the risk of losing their visa.
additional_details: We believe that some foreign care workers under sponsorship by their employers are being unfairly treated and that some of these employers make it difficult for their staff to seek a new job. We think a new visa scheme will give care workers more freedom and stop exploitation.

action: Allow Displaced Skilled Workers Work At least 20 Hours To Sustain Themselves
background: The Government or Parliament should help repeal the law being restraining other employers from hiring any displaced skilled worker from working with them if they are not currently working for their primary employer, whose license is revoked or does not have the jobs promised the affected employees
additional_details: It’s simply because of the retinue of displaced skilled worker (particularly healthcare professionals) whose families are at the moment struggling to cope with cost of living here and there that I as a person have met and interacted with through my social media platform, and is now more like a community of displaced workers in the UK
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730717

action: Scrap Pubs Code 2016 and amend the Competition Act 1998 to ban tied beer lines
background: Scrap the Pub Code 2016 and amend the Competition Act 1998 to ban tied beer lines, giving pub tenants the right to buy and sell freely from any brewery, especially from independent and local UK producers.
additional_details: We think banning tied products could give consumers more choice and fairer prices, while helping pubs remain viable. It could boost the UK economy by supporting independent breweries, creating local jobs, and keeping money circulating in communities.

action: Stop withdrawing out of property transactions without valid reason.
background:
We ask to introduce accountability measures:
If a property transaction drags on for 3 months without exchange of contracts, and one party withdraws without a valid reason, there should be financial or legal consequences.
Valid reasons would be loss of employment or inability to secure a mortgage.
additional_details: It’s currently legal to withdraw from a property transaction before exchange of contracts, without facing any financial or legal consequences, unlike in Europe, Scotland, Australia, NZ, Canada and the US. This causes huge financial and emotional stress, including lost deposits, legal fees, and wasted time. This change would make property transactions fairer and more reliable, reducing wasted time, costs, and emotional distress for those genuinely committed to completing their purchase or sale.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721744

action: Change the DDA 1991 to end breed discrimination and focus on behaviour
background: To reform the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 by removing breed-specific legislation and replacing it with behaviour-based laws. Focus on responsible ownership, training, and education to improve public safety without unfairly targeting certain dog breeds.
additional_details: Breed-specific laws have not reduced dog attacks and unfairly punish dogs based on looks, not behaviour. Data shows aggression is linked to ownership and training. We need effective, evidence-based laws that focus on behaviour, enforce accountability, and support public education to truly keep people safe.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/716062

action: Enshrine core British freedoms and rights in law
background: Introduce a British Bill of Rights that protects core freedoms such as: speech, safety, dignity and due process. Shield these rights from repeal or erosion. Require national consensus for any changes. Uphold liberty and fairness through law. These rights belong to the people of the United Kingdom.
additional_details: Our core freedoms: speech, safety, dignity, and justice. Must be protected in law, not left to political whim. A British Bill of Rights ensures these values endure across governments and generations. I want government to safeguard the rights of the British people above all, and ensure that the promises Great Britain makes to its people are upheld.
rejection_details: It is not clear how a new law as described in this petition would change existing laws related to these issues, such as the Human Rights Act.

action: Ban smoking & vaping during working hours
background: We urge the Government to pass a law which bans people from smoking and vaping during working hours. We believe this would be better for the environment and allow more work to get done.
additional_details: We believe the ban could also help people become fitter and healthier. We believe it may also save companies, the NHS and the Government money, and result in more time working and less time not working. We also believe it may lead to more people actually giving up smoking and vaping.

action: Create a monthly, free personal carbon allowance to limit carbon usage
background: We urge the Government to create a monthly, free shareable, tradeable Personal Carbon Allowance (PCA) (in kgCO₂e) for those over 18 to limit and ration carbon usage. We want this allowance to include travel and energy use and reduce annually in line with Government carbon consumption targets.
additional_details: We believe global warming has been observed to be happening faster than predicted with serious implications if we continue with present policies. Experts believe the planet is absorbing more solar energy than before and warming may be accelerating faster than models predicted. We think a similar system should apply to businesses and other organisations, which we believe should be given appropriate monthly allowances.

action: Mandate all MPs and civil servants to complete Carbon Literacy training by 01/09
background: We believe MPs and civil servants deserve and need basic training tailored to their job roles and covering carbon emissions, climate change impacts and climate science.
additional_details: We want the government to develop and deliver an accredited Carbon Literacy course to provide 8 hours of learning on these essential topics. We believe politicians frequently make policies or pronouncements that show their lack of understanding of the basic science of carbon emissions and climate change impacts. We think this is severally hampering our ability to provide a liveable future for us and our children.

action: Petition for Parent/Child Parking Badges for children up to age 13
background: I call on the Government to introduce a parent/child parking badge for parents or guardians with children up to age 13.
additional_details: This age range reflects the ongoing need for safe, accessible parking for families beyond early childhood, especially when managing school-age children or those with additional needs.

action: Make the old and new pension schemes the same to eliminate the 2nd class status
background: Create a single state pension scheme by eliminating the old scheme. The administration savings would be beneficial. This petition is to reinstate the one that was cancelled by Parliament.
additional_details: Create a fairer scheme
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Increase New State Pension and pay to all, abolish the old Basic State Pension." https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728562

action: Fairer Toll and Parking Enforcement – Protect Drivers from Excessive Fines
background: All drivers must be allowed a fair period to pay original toll or parking fees before any fines are applied. Excessive, opportunistic fines must not be escalated to CCJs years later with added interest or fees, as this causes undue financial harm, stress, and long-term hardship for ordinary drivers.
additional_details: Car parks (private and council-run) must display clear signage showing payment is required and the maximum stay allowed. If machines are broken, signs must state the preferred alternative payment method or confirm no payment is required. Where signage is unclear or missing, only the original parking fee should be reclaimed. Penalties must be capped at £10–£20, ensuring fines are proportionate. Excessive fines for minor oversights, such as a £2 unpaid charge, are unfair.

Create a set of standards for private parking firms that ensure transparency
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/718339

action: Give chronically ill people more workplace protections
background: We call on the UK Government to impose mandatory workplace protections for chronically ill people, and to prevent businesses from subjecting them to strict absence policies that often result in punishment and dismissal. The Equality Act also needs to be more enforced.
additional_details:
Chronically ill employees require more time off work than their able-bodied coworkers, usually due to fluctuating symptoms, medical appointments and ongoing treatments. Despite this, chronically ill people are only allowed as much sick leave as someone who doesn't have to experience any of these things, putting them at an immediate disadvantage and leading to significantly higher rates of unemployment.

We need more protections to access and exceed in work, not to be forced out of it.

action: Make the US Honour UK–US Extradition Treaty & Protect British Nationals’ Rights
background: We call on the UK Government to ensure that the UK–US Extradition Treaty is upheld and that the rights of British nationals are fully protected. This includes ensuring evidence standards meet UK requirements, that detainees are told of their right to contact the British consulate,
additional_details:
and that no extra charges are tried beyond those approved in extradition. 

The UK must act to protect its citizens and ensure fair treatment, just as we do for US nationals in Britain.

action: Mandatory that TV broadcasters are to provide factual information to the public
background: Make it mandatory that TV presenters and TV programmers such as ITV and BBC are to inform their viewers of the factual information at the end of TV debates around politics to prevent misinformation being shared as it can be harmful and damaging whilst also encouraging hateful behaviour.
additional_details: Making it mandatory for broadcasters to provide factual summaries after political debates would help reduce misinformation, protect democracy, and prevent harmful or divisive narratives. It ensures accountability from politicians, supports public trust in media, and promotes informed decision-making. By clarifying misleading claims, broadcasters can limit the spread of hate and strengthen responsible, fact-based political discourse.

action: Recognise Latinos as an ethnicity in the UK census
background: Growing up I always had to tick “Other” when asked my ethnicity. Latinos are not “Other” and deserve proper recognition. I want the Government to add “Latino / Latin American” as an ethnicity option in the UK census and all official forms.
additional_details: Latinos are a growing community in the UK but are invisible in official data because we are not recognised as an ethnicity. Having to select “Other” denies us representation and makes it harder to understand our community’s needs. Recognition in the census and on official forms would ensure fair access to services, improve data on health and education, and give Latinos the visibility and respect we deserve.

action: Reinstate the policy to deport asylum seekers to Rwanda
background: On taking office this Government cancelled the Rwanda plan and promised to 'Smash The Gangs'. The annual number of illegal migrants crossing the channel was higher in 2025 than in 2023/24, and we think the gangs have not been smashed. We would like the Government to reinstate the Rwanda plan.
additional_details:
We think the Rwanda plan was working even before a flight had taken off. In 2024 the Irish Government attributed a rise in the number of people claiming asylum in Ireland to the Rwanda policy.
 
We think that it was and is a deterrent. British tax payers have paid for accommodation, which according to some reports is now being used by nations such as the USA.
 
We ask the Government to declare that they were wrong to cancel the Rwanda plan and to reinstate it.

action: Fund research and staff training on Mast Cell Activation Syndrome
background: Fund research into Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) and related mast cell conditions, and fund training for NHS healthcare professionals. We think this would improve recognition, diagnosis, and treatment, and give patients access to safe NHS care instead of potentially costly private options.
additional_details: There are many people in the UK live with disabling symptoms such as flushing, pain, digestive problems, and allergic-type reactions linked to MCAS, but NHS care is sometimes inconsistent and can often be unavailable. Without research and training, patients can be left suffering or forced to pay privately. We believe government support would help bring fairness, help reduce long-term health risks, and help many people get more timely diagnosis and treatment.

action: Create a voluntary physical national ID card
background: With the advent of the up and coming EES system in Europe, we are asking for a Government ID card system similar to current EU member state ID cards.
additional_details:
Since passport stamping will be a thing of the past in the EU post full roll out of EES, we think there will be no reason to have to use a passport only.

We believe these are the benefits:
 
1) This somewhat exists under the UK PASS card system
 
2) not everyone has a passport or driving licence
 
3) Post full roll out of the EES, we can see if the EU will allow for a UK ID card with travel purposes. This will require the art of deal making between the UK and EU to allow this to happen in the future.
 
4) in some EU countries you have to carry ID at all times. This way you can leave your passport in the hotel safe to prevent losing it.

action: Change the way the London Mayor is elected.
background: Allow all English citizens of voting age to vote in the election of all future London Mayors.
additional_details: London is our capital, and we want to restore national pride in that great city. Too many of us feel afraid or unwilling to visit London because of the crime rate, the poor public transport system, and the general run-down state of the once-proud city. We want tourists to feel welcomed and safe, and we want a say in major decisions affecting our capital, including new buildings, road systems and policing.The only way we can do this is by voting for the Mayor of our choice. Our City, our Mayor.
rejection_details:

Grant the vote for London Mayor to all UK Residents

action: Stop changing the clocks for DST and keep the UK on one time, preferably BST
background: We call on the Government to end the practice of changing the clocks twice a year for Daylight Saving Time. The UK should remain on a single, consistent time zone all year round, preferably BST.
additional_details: Clock changes twice a year disrupt sleep, health, and daily routines, and can increase accidents, stress, and reduced productivity. Energy savings are minimal, with a 2017 study showing only 0.3% reduction. A consistent time system would provide longer daylight in the evenings, improving safety, outdoor activity, and overall wellbeing. In a 2018 EU consultation, 84% of citizens wanted to abolish clock changes. Ending DST simplifies life and protects public health.
rejection_details:

action: Label ALL meat as Religiously Slaughtered or Non-Religiously Slaughtered
background: We want the Government to create a law requiring all meat to have a label, such as a simple RS (Religiously Slaughtered) or NRS (Not religiously slaughtered), that states whether it has been religiously slaughtered or not.
additional_details:
We think that labelling meat as ‘stunned’ or ‘not stunned’ is not adequate because when meat has been subject to a ‘recoverable stun’, the throat is slit and the animal may wake up in excruciating pain to hear the religious blessing, unable to vocalise its distress.

I am concerned that religiously slaughtered meat, using inhumane methods, is entering the food chain and is being sold to people who may object to the method of slaughter, without it being labelled.
government_response_summary: There are no requirements to label meat from animals slaughtered in accordance with religious rites. Where information of this nature is provided it must be accurate and must not be misleading.
government_response_body: The government encourages the highest standards of animal welfare at slaughter and would prefer all animals to be stunned before slaughter, but respects the rights of Jews and Muslims to eat meat prepared in accordance with their religious beliefs.   The first national legislative requirement for stunning before slaughter in England and Wales was the Slaughter of Animals Act 1933. The Act also introduced an exception from the requirement to stun when animals are slaughtered in accordance with religious rites, for the food of Muslims and Jews. A significant proportion of halal meat comes from animals that are stunned before slaughter.  There are detailed protections in legislation to ensure that animals are spared any avoidable pain, distress or suffering when being slaughtered. Animals are stunned to make them unconscious and insensible to pain and slaughtermen are required to check that animals do not present any signs of consciousness in the period between being stunned and death.  Official Veterinarians of the Food Standards Agency (FSA) are present in all approved slaughterhouses to monitor and enforce animal welfare requirements. When the FSA identifies breaches, they are fully investigated, and appropriate and proportionate action is taken to protect animal welfare.  There are no regulations that require the labelling of meat from animals slaughtered in accordance with religious rites. However, where any information of this nature is provided it must be accurate and must not be misleading to the consumer. It is for religious authorities to decide if meat is halal or kosher. The Government has no plans to introduce requirements for meat to be labelled according to whether it comes from an animal which has been slaughtered in accordance with religious rites.  On food labelling more generally, we recognise that while most consumers care about how their food is produced, the lack of consistency in food labelling makes it difficult for consumers to understand the animal welfare standards of their food and make informed purchasing decisions.  As set out in the Government’s animal welfare strategy, we are committed to ensuring that consumers have access to clear information on how their food was produced. To support this, we will continue working with relevant stakeholders, including the farming and food industry, scientists and NGOs to explore how improved animal welfare food labelling could provide greater consumer transparency, support farmers and promote better animal welfare.  Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

action: Introduce legally enforceable safe nurse-to-patient staffing ratios in the NHS
background: Make minimum staffing levels a legal requirement by introducing national nurse-to-patient ratios that can help guarantee patient safety and protect staff wellbeing.
additional_details: We believe recent government cuts have worsened understaffing issues, pushing services to a tipping point. Patients can be left waiting, care can be rushed, and harm can occur. There are reports of nurses burning out and leaving in record numbers. We feel unsafe care has become normal and is endangering both patients and staff. We think action is urgently needed to protect lives and sustain the NHS.
government_response_summary: There are no plans to make nurse-to-patient ratios a legal requirement in England. Staffing levels are determined locally, supported by national guidance and regulated by the Care Quality Commission.
government_response_body: Fixed nurse-to-patient ratios are not enforced in England. The responsibility for staffing levels remains with clinical and other leaders at a local level, responding to local needs, supported by guidelines set by national and professional bodies and overseen and regulated by the Care Quality Commission (CQC).   This is particularly important in community nursing settings, where a simple numeric ratio does not adequately capture the complexity of safe staffing. Unlike inpatient environments, community nurses work across dispersed caseloads, often as lone workers, with significant variation in patient acuity, geography, care complexity and travel time. A flexible, evidence-informed approach to caseload weighting and workforce planning is therefore essential to reflect the realities of community care delivery.  Providers must systematically determine and review staffing and skills to meet service users’ needs and ensure patient safety, following legislation and available guidance.  Reaching the right staff numbers and mix should depend on an evidence-based approach and the exercise of real-time, risk-assessed, professional judgements by day-to-day leadership and a multi-professional approach.  The CQC checks for compliance with regulations that require regulated providers to have enough suitably qualified staff, and can take enforcement action where incorrect staffing levels are having an impact on patient outcomes.  National Quality Board (NQB)  Guidance from the NQB entitled Safe, sustainable and productive staffing (2016, available online at https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/nqb-guidance.pdf) and Developing Workforce Safeguard (2018, available online at https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/Developing-workforce-safeguards.pdf) is designed to ensure a consistent, scientific and evidence-based approach to staffing levels and to improve governance and board accountability relating to staffing decisions.  The approach combines evidence-based tools, professional judgement, and outcomes to ensure appropriate staffing and minimise patient safety risks.  It is important to note that NQB guidance primarily addresses acute inpatient care. For community nursing, NHS England supports specific staffing tools to assess caseloads, and ensuring their widespread use is a priority.  While England’s approach to safe staffing is through a combination of locally led decisions, evidence-based tools, professional judgement, regulatory oversight, and national guidance instead of fixed ratios, the Government will continue to monitor international evidence for workforce planning.  The 10 Year Health Plan and staff  This Government is committed to publishing a 10 Year Workforce Plan to set out action to create a workforce ready to deliver the transformed service set out in the 10 Year Health Plan. The 10 Year Workforce Plan will ensure the NHS has the right staff, with the right skills, in the right places.  NHS staff told us through the 10 Year Health Plan engagement that they are crying out for change. Our new Workforce Plan will set out how we will deliver that change by making sure that staff are better treated, have better training, more fulfilling roles, and hope for the future.  For our staff to care for people, the Government must also support staff. We aim for a sustainable workforce, focusing on training, working conditions, and restoring pride and job satisfaction.  Nationally, we recognise that staff across the NHS have been under considerable pressure. We want to improve organisational culture and working conditions so that we can keep staff healthy and motivated and retain vital skills and experience in the NHS.  From April 2026, we will introduce new minimum staff standards, focusing on key areas for staff wellbeing. Developed with the Social Partnership Forum, these standards will put staff wellbeing at the heart of the workforce model.  It is important that NHS staff work in an inclusive, compassionate environment with support for their health and wellbeing. The 10 Year Health Plan will introduce Staff Treatment Hubs providing high-quality occupational health support, including for mental health and back conditions.  NHS staff needing specialist mental health support can access NHS Practitioner Health, a national service for complex issues like trauma or addiction.  NHS staff are dedicated to making a difference, so we must support them with training and ensure a rewarding, inclusive work environment.  NHS England’s retention programme supports staff with occupational health, flexible working, better culture and leadership, and guidance for managers, new joiners, and those experiencing menopause.  By prioritising staff wellbeing, development, and retention, we will build a resilient NHS workforce equipped to deliver outstanding care for years to come.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Seek to create pension agreements with India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, or refund NI
background: Negotiate reciprocal pension agreements with India, Pakistan and Bangladesh so migrants’ National Insurance payments count towards their pensions in their home countries. If agreements can't be reached, we think the UK should refund NI contributions when those affected return home.
additional_details: Migrants from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh are among the UK’s largest communities, and pay large sums in taxes and NI. Yet, when they return home, many may lose these contributions, with no increase to their pension, nor a tax / NI refund. We think this is unfair. We want the Government to either secure these agreements or refund NI. We feel it is unjust to take from immigrants and give nothing back.

action: Introduce a Pension Tax Lock to help protect retirement savings and incentives
background: The Chancellor should introduce a Pension Tax Lock: a commitment not to reduce the amount people can withdraw from their pension tax-free or the amount of tax relief given on pension contributions. We believe this would help ensure retirement savings are protected and people can save with confidence
additional_details:
We believe this simple commitment could put an end to the speculation seen ahead of every Budget – speculation which we think erodes confidence in long-term saving and can all-too-often lead to people making poor, sometimes irreversible, financial decisions.

We think this would come at zero cost to the Exchequer and would allow people to save for retirement with more confidence. We feel it could support the government’s twin aims of delivering pensions adequacy and boosting economic growth.
government_response_summary: The Government is committed to ensuring pensioners have security in retirement and has launched a Pensions Commission to look at what is required to ensure the system is strong, fair and sustainable.
government_response_body: The Government wishes to encourage pension saving, to help ensure that people have an income, or funds on which they can draw on, throughout retirement. The Government is committed to supporting savers at all stages of life. That is why, for the majority of savers, pension contributions made from income during working life are tax-free. This is known as 'pensions tax relief'. This relief is available at an individual's marginal rate. For example, contributions from a basic rate (20 per cent) taxpayer who contributes to a registered pension scheme in 2025/26 receives tax relief at 20 per cent. This makes pensions tax relief one of the most expensive reliefs in the personal tax system, costing £78 billion in 2023/24.  Investment growth of assets in a pension scheme is also not subject to tax. From age 55 (or when scheme rules allow a pension to be taken), up to 25 per cent of the pension can be taken tax-free (capped for most at a maximum of £268,275), depending on scheme rules. Pension income received (for example as a regular annuity payment or as income drawn down from a pension) is subject to income tax at an individual's marginal rate, to reflect the fact that pensions in payment are a form of deferred income and have not been previously taxed.  The petition proposes a ‘Pension Tax Lock: a commitment not to reduce the amount people can withdraw from their pension tax-free or the amount of tax relief given on pension contributions’.  At Autumn Budget 2025 the Government announced that it is changing how salary sacrifice for pension contributions works – from April 2029, the amount that is exempt from National Insurance contributions (NICs) will be capped at £2,000 a year for employee contributions made via salary sacrifice. More information on this change is available here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/changes-to-salary-sacrifice-for-pensions-from-april-2029  The government made no changes at Autumn Budget to the pension lump sum tax-free allowance, or to income tax relief on employee pension contributions. The Government keeps all aspects of the tax system under review as part of the annual Budget process, and in the context of the wider public finances, and does not intend to introduce a pensions tax lock.  The Government recognises the importance of promoting confidence in pension saving and is committed to ensuring future generations of pensioners have security in retirement. This is why the government announced a landmark two-phased review of the pensions system days after coming into office.  The first phase, the Pensions Investment Review, focused on reforming the pensions landscape to boost savers’ pension pots. These reforms will be delivered through the Pension Schemes Bill. The Pensions Commission will build on these foundations and make recommendations to the government on the broader questions of adequacy, fairness, and sustainability to guide the long-term future of our pensions system. The Pensions Commission will be undertaken by Baroness Jeannie Drake, Sir Ian Cheshire and Professor Nick Pearce.  More information on the Pensions Commission, including its Terms of Reference, is available here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/pensions-commission-terms-of-reference  HM Treasury  This is a revised response. The Petitions Committee requested a response which more directly addressed the request of the petition. You can find the original response towards the bottom of the petition page (https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740486)

action: Reform tax rules so rental income is taxed on profit, not revenue
background: Reform Section 24 so rental income is taxed on profit, not revenue. We think this would make new-build flats bought under Help to Buy or Shared Ownership more attractive to buyers and investors. We believe this could  allow first-time buyers to move on which could ease pressure in the rental market.
additional_details: Some first-time buyers using Help to Buy or Shared Ownership overpay for new-build flats. When they want to move, many may face negative equity and could be trapped in unsuitable homes, with savings spent repaying mortgages instead of funding a deposit. Renting may not be viable either, as S24 taxes gross rental income rather than profit. We think reforming these rules could help restore market mobility, boost rental supply, and make housing fairer and more affordable for tenants and homeowners.

action: Enhance NI with a secure biometric ID to protect citizens from identity theft
background: We want the Government to enhance the National Insurance system with a secure biometric ID card. Optional for most citizens; mandatory (employer-funded) for directors, regulated professions and Senior Management Function holders.
additional_details:
We think this could cut fraud, protect identities, strengthen security and build trust. Identity theft and fraud are growing threats and could be costing citizens and the UK economy billions every year. 
 
We believe that enhancing the National Insurance system with a secure biometric ID card could protect individuals, strengthen national security, improve efficiency, and build trust. It could ensure accountability where it matters most and fairness for all.
