additional_details:
MPs have privileged access to forthcoming laws and must not exploit this to gain for themselves or their families while the electorate bears the cost. Democracy relies on fairness, openness, and equal treatment under the law. Stronger rules on declarations, a public register, and powers to recover improper gains would deter abuse, close loopholes, and reassure voters that MPs act in the national interest, not for private advantage.
Laws should not be created which do not effect politicians alike

Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

MPs must register any change to their registrable interests within 28 days. Interests remain on the Register for twelve months after they have expired.

action: UK-wide 'National Appreciation Day' as a Paid Public Holiday for Migrants
background: We petition the government to establish an annual, paid public holiday, tentatively named 'National Appreciation Day.' This day would be granted to all migrants residing and working in the United Kingdom as a form of national recognition for their invaluable contributions to the country.
additional_details:
The UK's prosperity is built on migrants' tireless work in essential sectors like the NHS and hospitality. Their contributions drive economic growth and fill critical labor gaps, yet this is often overlooked.
A paid public holiday, 'National Appreciation Day,' would be a tangible expression of gratitude. This day would be for all migrants in the UK, granting them a paid day off.
This isn't just an extra day; it's a powerful precedent of national appreciation. By creating this holiday, the UK would formally acknowledge migrants' central role, fostering a more inclusive society that honors their hard work, sacrifice, and diversity.

action: Create an independent early years funding review
background: We ask Government to establish an Independent Early Years Funding Review Body. Similar to the School Teachers’ Review Body, it could take evidence from providers, parents and experts and recommend fair funding rates based on actual costs, not political decisions, for the Government to respond to.
additional_details: We believe that for too long, childcare funding rates have been set by HM Treasury and the Department for Education to meet policy goals, not providers’ real costs. When the Childcare bill 2016 was drafted it at one stage included an independent review, but this was removed before Royal Assent. We think the result has been chronic underfunding, nursery and childminder closures, and instability for families. Early years is the foundation of education and deserves the same independent, transparent process as teachers’ pay.

action: Keep the 5-Year ILR Pathway for EU Nationals under Skilled Worker Visas
background: We ask the Government to maintain the 5-year pathway to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for EU nationals on Skilled Worker visas, rather than extending it to 10 years. This would recognise their prior contributions under free movement, support family stability, and uphold the UK–EU relationship.
additional_details: The UK and EU have long shared deep ties of cooperation, friendship, and freedom of movement. For many years, EU nationals have come to the UK to work, study, and contribute to the economy. Many of those now on Skilled Worker visas are not newcomers, but people who had already built their lives here under these shared rights and values, demonstrated commitment and loyalty to the UK. To extend the ILR pathway to 10 years would disregard the trust and history of cooperation between the UK and EU.

action: Require coroners to find out if the deceased was a veteran and fund a database
background: Government should mandate coroners to establish and record whether the deceased has military/veteran status and to consider whether service-related brain injury (TBI) including blast wave and overpressure injuries, could be a contributing factor. It should fund a database to identify any patterns.
additional_details:
This is particularly relevant in cases of suicide where the state has enhanced investigative duties under Article 2 of the ECHR for deaths by suicide.

This could help coroners establish if TBI, including blast wave and overpressure injuries, could be contributing to deaths.  A centralised, anonymised database may help identify patterns and give families clarity, recognition and justice. We believe these reforms can help ensure investigations are accurate, meaningful, and serve public health.

action: Grant non-molestation orders based on past abuse, not just risk of future harm
background: We call on the Government to change the law so that non-molestation orders are always granted based on evidence of past domestic abuse, even if there has not been a recent incident. Currently, victims must prove not only that abuse has taken place but that there is an ongoing risk of future harm.
additional_details: Survivors are often refused non-molestation orders because judges say abuse is not "recent". This leaves victims exposed if abusers are briefly on "good behaviour" e.g. during court cases. Even some survivors of near-fatal attacks are told they must wait to be harmed again before getting protection. A lot of domestic abuse is cyclical so pauses don't remove risk. The law must recognise this & close the loophole: allow survivors protection based on past abuse without waiting for further violence.

action: Reform copyright law to treat music streaming like radio play
background: We urge the Government to reform copyright law so that music streaming is treated in the same way as radio play for royalty purposes. We believe artists and performers should be paid fairly for every stream, just as they are for every broadcast on radio.
additional_details: Many people now discover and enjoy music through streaming platforms such as Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube, rather than traditional radio. Yet, the law still treats streaming differently, which we argue results in a less fair deal for artists, songwriters and musicians. Radio pays per play, acknowledging each broadcast as a distinct use of music, and we believe streaming should reflect the same principle. Reform is needed to ensure fair pay for artists in the digital age.

Pets can enter the UK by car, ferry, or private jet under the same biosecurity rules but are banned from cabin travel on commercial flights. action: Regulate tattoo academies and training and introduce national licensing
background: We’re calling on the government to stop unsafe tattoo academies, make infection-control training mandatory, and introduce proper licensing at a national level. We think this could safeguard artists and clients alike and stop aspiring artists being exploited by scam courses.
additional_details: Tattooing is now mainstream, with 26% of UK adults tattooed. We think that tattoo academies are exploiting aspiring artists by charging thousands for sham training, resulting in unsafe practitioners who endanger clients. Wales has shown regulation is possible. We want the government to act to protect public health and the future integrity of the tattoo industry.

action: Introduce new tax code for state pensioners with double the personal allowance
background: We want the government to introduce a new tax code for state pensioners, set at double the basic threshold. If this was implemented, pensioners would receive a higher tax-exempt limit, but wealthier pensioners would still pay tax.
additional_details: We think that people with small private or workplace pensions are currently being taxed unfairly.
government_response_summary: The State Pension is the foundation of support for pensioners. The Government is committed to a fair tax system but doubling the Personal Allowance for pensioners would be untargeted and costly.
government_response_body: The State Pension is the foundation of support available to pensioners. The government is committed to the Triple Lock – one of the most generous State Pension uprating mechanisms in the world – for the duration of this Parliament. This will increase the basic and new State Pension by 4.8% next April, boosting pensioner incomes by up to £575 a year and strengthening retirement security.   The Personal Allowance is already the highest amongst G7 countries. Doubling this allowance for all pensioners would be costly and untargeted – disproportionately benefitting higher income pensioners.  As announced at the Budget, the government will ease the administrative burden for pensioners whose sole income is the basic or new State Pension without any increments so that they do not have to pay small amounts of tax via Simple Assessment from 2027-28, if the new or basic State Pension exceeds the Personal Allowance from that point. The government is exploring the best way to achieve this and will set out more detail next year.  HM Treasury

action: Mandate clear labelling of Coconut Oil and Palm Kernel Oil on food products
background: Clearly label MCTs (Medium-Chain Triglyceride), such as Coconut Oil and Palm Kernel Oil on products for consumption.
additional_details:
Whilst not clearly labelled as an allergen, people diagnosed with MCADD (Medium-Chain Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency) run the risk of consuming high amounts of MCTs without realising it, which could place their lives in danger.
 
Due to MCADD, individuals cannot metabolize MCTs and ingesting them can lead to a metabolic crisis, causing severe symptoms like seizures, comas, and even death. We believe that labelling MCTs clearly, just like allergens, is a crucial safety measure to prevent these life-threatening reactions and for those affected by this rare genetic disorder. It's a matter of necessity, especially where Coconut Oils and Palm Kernel Oils are concerned.

action: Recognise Hyperacusis as a disability.
background: Hyperacusis is a rare disorder, making it extremely difficult to tolerate everyday sounds, leading to debilitating levels of discomfort. It significantly impacts personal and professional areas of our lives. Despite its profound implications, Hyperacusis isn't officially recognised as a disability.
additional_details:
Hyperacusis should be acknowledged formally as a disability, and although there isn’t a validated outcome measure currently, subjective tools, in conjunction with an audiogram and patient history, should be sufficient to identify the condition accurately. 
We urge health authorities to implement formal processes considering subjective experiences to improve diagnostic criteria.

The absence of recognition means we are cut off from support to help manage symptoms and improve our quality of life.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. We're not sure exactly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do to "recognise hyperacusis as a disability".

The Equality Act 2010 defines disability as any physical or mental impairment that has a ‘substantial’ and ‘long-term’ negative effect on your ability to do normal daily activities.

action: Exempt students who arrived before July from changes to visa/settlement rules
background: Maintain the 2-year Graduate Route for students who arrived before July 2025 and allow transition to the Skilled Worker visa under pre-July 2025 rules, with a clear 5-year residency pathway to ILR.
additional_details: International students can invest over £30,000 in tuition, pay taxes, costly health surcharges, and upfront rent while using minimal NHS services as many are young and healthy. Many work in customer service, regularly pay landlords, and support housing and local economies. Yet we face ongoing uncertainty and repeated threats to leave if permits are not secured. We are not a burden but committed contributors who we think deserve fairness, stability, and the clear post-study pathway that was originally available.

action: Introduce a Sex Worker's Discrimination Act to safeguard sex workers
background: I want the government to introduce a Sex Worker's Discrimination Act. I believe new legislation is necessary to safeguard individuals working in the sex industry from discrimination, abuse and social stigma. I think this could help promote a fair, safe and more equal society.
additional_details: Sex workers are often subjected to prejudice, verbal abuse, and physical violence. These individuals are unfairly judged, which can lead to significant barriers in accessing basic services such as banking, housing and employment. I do not feel the current legal framework offers adequate protection, leaving them open to discrimination.

action: Stop Commonwealth Citizens voting in UK general elections unless mutual rights
background: The UK Government must end voting rights for Commonwealth citizens and replace them with fair, reciprocal agreements - if British citizens can’t vote in their elections, their citizens shouldn’t be allowed to vote in ours.
additional_details: Currently, Commonwealth Citizens from 56 countries living in the UK have the right to vote if they are 18 or over and have legal permission to enter or stay in the UK. This includes students, workers, and those with indefinite leave to remain. We call on the government to remove this right unless their country of origin allows UK citizens to vote in a reciprocal manner. Only UK citizens or citizens from countries with reciprocal voting such as Ireland should be allowed to vote in UK general elections.

action: Hold a vote in Parliament before any 'Bathroom Bill' style legislation is passed
background: We are asking that a Parliamentary vote is held, before any primary legislation is passed that mandates that transgender persons cannot use the toilets of the gender that they live as.
additional_details: We know that this legislation stands to be harmful to both trans people and gender non confirming cisgender (non transgender people) who some might confuse as being members of another gender.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. Bills that go through Parliament already have to be voted on.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: TV license to be free for all pensioners of 70 years of age and older.
background: I want our Government or Parliament to consider making the tv license free of charge for all pensioners of age 70 and older.
additional_details: Pensioners are staying at home more due to the cost of living. One of their enjoyments is watching television. If the tv license was made free of charge it may enable pensioners to get out of their houses and socialize more and spend some of the money that they save on the license fee. There appears to be more repeated programs especially on daytime tv. Over the last few months pensioners have suffered the brunt of spending cuts.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund Free TV licences for all pensioners.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728658

action: Abolish the VAT on Independent Schools implemented by the Labour government.
background: The government should reverse the imposition of its VAT policy on independent schools as this is tantamount to an attack on hard working families who make significant sacrifices and put great value on their children's education.
additional_details: Without such a reversal, this will only serve to widen the divide between independent schools and put greater pressure on state schools themselves, which will wipe out any savings generated from such a policy.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition that calls for a similar action:

Stop VAT being added to Private school fees - https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730767

action: Introduce a Safe Futures for SEND Act to fix the broken EHCP system
background:
Introduce a Safe Futures for SEND Act to fix the broken EHCP system. 
Protect medical diagnoses, enforce accountability, safeguard children’s placements, require transparency in EHCP drafts, and give all families free independent SEND advocacy.
additional_details: The EHCP system is failing. Children’s medical needs are being erased, deadlines ignored, and unsafe school placements forced. Families are left traumatised, with parents in constant fight-or-flight and children losing vital education. The law must change to protect children’s health, safety, and futures, and to restore trust for families navigating SEND. The impact is long-lasting, just like Covid reshaped a generation, the SEND crisis is reshaping ours, only without acknowledgement or urgency.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you are concerned about the EHCP system, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. For example, how would you like medical diagnoses to be protected?

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Reduce ILR qualification to 7 years for long residence visa
background: Reduce the qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain under the long residence route from 10 years to 7 years.
additional_details: We think this would create a clearer, fairer pathway to settlement. We believe a single 7-year route gives stability, predictability, and equal treatment to all who live and contribute lawfully in the UK.

action: Ban MPs and Lords from company stakes that pose conflicts of interest
background: Stop MPs and Lords from cashing in on the very industries they oversee. From arms to oil to big pharma and tech, politicians must divest or use blind trusts. No more hidden agendas -Parliament must put the public first and end financial conflicts of interest.
additional_details:
Democracy fails when lawmakers profit from the industries they regulate. It's not enough to "declare" interests - conflicts still corrupt decisions and fuel public distrust. Whether arms, oil, pharma or tech, private profit skews choices about our safety, health and planet.

To restore trust and protect democracy, Parliament must ban these financial ties or require assets in blind trusts, with strict penalties and full accountability for any illegal actions.
rejection_details:
We are unsure if you want MPs/peers to be banned from holding any shares in companies, except in blind trusts, or if you want them to be banned from holding shares in certain industries.

You can start a new petition setting out more clearly what action you are calling for.

action: Rule out military bases in Lincolnshire for asylum seeker accommodation
background: The Government should rule out using disused or active military sites in Greater Lincolnshire for asylum accommodation - especially where clear alternative plans are in place, like at RAF Scampton and Prince William of Gloucester Barracks.
additional_details:
Lincolnshire has many former RAF bases in rural areas, such as Scampton, Woodhall Spa, and Grantham, often far from hospitals, schools, and public transport. Using these sites for asylum accommodation risks isolating people, fuelling local tensions, and undermining regeneration, such as the £300m investment planned for RAF Scampton. Asylum provision should be in well-supported locations.
Lincolnshire people deserve better than more speculation, so we ask the government to be unequivocal.
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Reduce the school week to three days a week
background: Government and parliament need to lower children's school days per week from 5 to 3 to allow them to still enjoy their childhoods.
additional_details: We think that children's weeks in school are much too long and that this affects their childhoods, concentration and family relationships. The 5 day school week should be limited to a maximum of 3 days to allow children to still have a childhood and to allow children to learn at home too. Children from age 5 should not be forced by government and school bodies to be away from their homes and families for 5 days - up to 32.5 hours a week which is the equivalent in some cases to a full time job..

action: A month on minimum wage for all involved in setting it.
background: As a society we rely on a fair minimum wage, enough to support oneself and potentially their family. However those in charge of minimum pay may never experience it, and therefore be unable to properly understand the ratifications of their actions. I believe under a min. pay month we can reduce this.
additional_details: I am fully aware that the grounds of any member of parliament's pay is set by the IPSA and therefore in not the direct hands of UK parliament. However, I am preposing more specifically that total pay is to remain set by the IPSA, but it's distribution throughout the year is changed and written into law as minimum wage in a month and other than that month, all is else raised with the wage 'lost' from the month in name of making sure our government still receives a fair and independently run wage.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about MPs salaries are a matter for the Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA).

IPSA is an independent body, meaning that the Government and Parliament has no authority over its decisions.

You may wish to start a new petition asking Parliament to take back authority over MPs salaries from IPSA.

action: British public wish to force a vote of no confidence in our current government.
background: Active a vote of no confidence of the current labour government, in the name of the British people. Forcing an early general election.
additional_details:
The overwhelming sentiment of the British people, from all walks of life, is that we zero confidence in Keir Starmer and the Labour government to effectively represent our needs or wishes. We believe their inept leadership is, and will continue to have, an extremely detrimental effect on the UK. 
We cannot wait another 4 years until the next election, while they continue to destroy, divide and alienate our great nation.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

You may wish to sign the following petition:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Give the North of England a referendum to join Scotland as an independent North.
background: Give the North of England the right to have their say, allow a referendum vote for the North to have a voice and it's independence away from London
additional_details:
For too long, power and wealth in the UK have been concentrated in London and the South, while the North has been left behind. Despite our industrial heritage, natural beauty, and resilient communities, we face higher taxes, rising costs, and lower public services.

The North built Britain’s global reputation, yet decisions are made in Westminster without regard for our unique needs and identity. We lack the voice and agency we deserve. It’s time for the North to decide its future.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We are unsure if you would like an independent North of England, for the North of England to become part of a devolved Scotland within the UK, or the North of England and Scotland to merge as an independent country outside of the UK.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Abolish parking fees down Barry The Cold Knap
background: Barry Town Council have set up parking fees down The Cold Knap. This has never had fees, and the town of Barry have always used the Cold Knap as a place of serenity, peace and calmness. This has been taken away from everyone near and far. The local businesses around the Knap have seen a decline to.
additional_details: This will help the businesses around the knap as it’s already seen a change in the number of customers being lower than average. Staff are afraid of losing their jobs which they have had for yrs and local businesses fear closing down. People rely on the Knap as a place to relax and enjoy peace and quiet. A place where you can gather your thoughts after a hard days work. The only place in Barry that’s beautiful to look and and appreciate the sunset.

action: Require employers have monthly menstrual 1-3 day leave policy
background: We want the government to require workforces to allow women to have 1-3 days leave per month (outside of holiday and sick leave) during their menstrual phase.
additional_details:
Each month, many women suffer in silence at work during this phase, whether its pain, embarrassment, discomfort or handling emotions. Countries such as Spain and Japan along with others have menstrual leave policies. 
 
Menstrual leave could allow women to rest, restore and be in comfort without having to "show up" and "put a brave face on". It could also prevent any embarrassment in the office or any worry about needing to change clothes due to heaviness.

action: Require employers give employees 3 months sick pay when cancer is diagnosed
background: I want the government to have a policy in place to help all cancer patients financially. I feel that for the first couple of months, cancer patients need to focus on their diagnosis. Having 3 months of full sick pay in place could allow them to focus on what they are dealing with.
additional_details: It could also remove the added stress of money worries and allow patients to receive treatment and recover without losing income. This peace of mind when diagnosed will be a huge relief for most and will allow them to focus on their diagnosis, treatment and getting themselves fit instead of added financial stress.

action: Ban family houses from being converted into Houses of Multiple Occupancy (HMOs)
background: Introduce legislation to prevent property developers & private landlords from converting family homes into HMOs, especially ex-council homes. We think that there is already a dearth of family homes for low-income working families, & by converting them into HMOs, the situation is being made worse.
additional_details: We feel that rents for ordinary families are sky high, so converting houses into HMOs can create very difficult situations. I call on the government to help hard working, low income people.

action: Raise statutory maternity pay for parents with mortgage to help with costs
background: We believe home owners should be entitled to additional support during maternity leave.
additional_details: Many parents are forced to return to work for financial reasons, which can impact maternal health and infant development. We believe the Government should provide funding to further support new parents with mortgages.

action: INCREASE TIME FOR PEOPLE WHEN THE TRAIN CLOSES THE DOORS.
background: When the trains closes doors, The drivers should wait 10 seconds before fully locking the doors before departure
additional_details: I have seen soo many people in the overground missing Thier train because of a few seconds delay and have to wait 15 mins in the sufferget line. This makes me quite sad I as I couldn't do anything to help them. I believe this petition will hopefully help people get Thier train and reach on time for Thier journey.
rejection_details: This is a matter for TFL, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Make will writing a regulated practice for those charging for the service
background: We want will writing to be made a regulated practice for those who charge for the service.
additional_details:
There are reports of unregulated will writers giving incorrect legal advice and charging high fees for products that don’t deliver the protections they promise, including on social media. 
 
We believe regulating will writing for those who charge for the service would ensure higher standards of advice and stronger protections for consumers against harmful and costly misinformation.

action: Make a cappella choirs eligible for the Treasury's Orchestra Tax Relief scheme
background: The Orchestra Tax Relief (OTR) is offered to instrumentalist groups on public musical performances. I think the human voice is a versatile instrument capable of conveying emotion, rhythm, melody and harmony yet doesn't apply as a qualifying instrument for OTR, and this unfair definition must change.
additional_details: A cappella choirs can face the same financial challenges as traditional orchestras do in putting on paid public performances but are disqualified from claiming OTR because of Treasury rules. The opportunity to sing in public performances can promote mental wellbeing whilst also funding the choir's progress, so where is the commonsense in excluding a cappella groups from the ability to claim OTR ?

action: Make TfL accountable for Gallows Corner Flyover Roundabout works
background: Make TfL to commit to a clear date of end of Gallows Corner Flyover Roundabout works or open Gallows Corner roundabout for local traffic immediately.
additional_details: Overunning of the TfL's Gallows Corner Flyover Roundabout works with no clear end date in sight and with multiple road utility works taking place on designated diversion routes made Harold Hill and surrounding areas impassable for local traffic. Local businesse are closing and suffering, people late for work, kids late for school, how long this misery will last?

action: New National Anthem. "Land Of Hope And Glory".
background: Replace the current anthem which is dreary and outdated, hated by the Scots, and many English and ethnic people have little affinity with it, even Monarchists. Land Of Hope And Glory is a rousing anthem by a famous British composer and its words are far more inclusive for everyone to rally behind.
additional_details: I am myself a Monarchist and always sang the anthem out of respect for the late Queen, but have not sung it since and will not. The words are outdated and provocative to many, Whereas Land Of Hope And Glory is up there with Stars and Stripes and La Marseilles as something we can all rally behind. The national anthem doesn't have to be all about the Monarch, but about the peoples' hopes and aspirations in a free land.
rejection_details:
This isn’t something that the UK Government or Parliament would be able to do. The use of the present National Anthem is a matter of tradition rather than having any legal or constitutional status.

You can find more information about the history and status of the national anthem here:

https://www.royal.uk/national-anthem

action: Stop all overseas spending including foreign aid
background: The UK has a massive debt and we believe it is in decline, with a very high tax burden on its citizens. We think it is the duty of the UK government to put its citizens and the UK first and it is irresponsible to spend taxpayer's money on any overseas project.
additional_details: We believe we need to reduce the national debt and provide for UK citizens before any overseas aid is considered. We consider that the so called "Soft Power" that the government may hope to gain by giving away billions of pounds of taxpayers money is not an acceptable excuse for spending funds that are needed at home for the improvement of infrastructure, defence, education and health services. UK citizens must come first, we cannot continue borrowing money while giving money away overseas and struggling to pay the interest on the debt.

action: Introduce law to allow voters to recall local government councillors
background: At present only MPs can be recalled by their electors in specific circumstances. There is no mechanism for voters to remove local councillors. We think there needs to be legislation covering all elected local government representatives and have unacceptable non-attendance as a reason for a recall.
additional_details: We are concerned that it is possible to be elected to local government and not attend meetings/committees yet still be paid an allowance. Although the Local Government Code of Conduct allows for sanctions, there is no recall mechanism for electors.

action: Have military personnel assist law enforcement in urban areas with high crime.
background: Allow the military the ability to send patrols out from army bases to nearby urban areas which have hight crime rates in the hopes of deterring crimes, assisting in the arrest of violent criminals and assisting troubled civilians being harassed, stalked or threatened.
additional_details: The high crime rates in urban areas like London and Birmingham have been appalling and people no longer feel safe on the streets. It is clear the law enforcement agencies are under-staffed and aren’t able to effectively deter and deal with violent and petty crime. With a higher supply of law enforcement units regularly patrolling high-crime areas, there would most certainly be a spike in the arrest of violent criminals and save people from death, trauma and/or stalkers who harass them.
rejection_details:
Detecting and preventing crime is the responsibility of the police. It would be an operational decision for the police whether to request assistance. 

You can read more about deployment of the armed forces in the UK here: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-9601/

background: Call for a general election on the grounds of no confidence in the current government

Call an immediate general election

action: Ban CCJs for private parking fines from being included in credit files
background: We call on the Government to change the law so unpaid County Court Judgments (CCJs) relating to private parking fines cannot be included in credit files, as we believe their inclusion can unfairly block access to mortgages and loans.
additional_details: In our view existing CCJs from private parking should be removed from credit files as we think they unfairly harm access to mortgages, reduce buying power, and cause stress and loss of morale. We do not believe that parking disputes are the same as genuine financial mismanagement

action: Childless to be eligible for Residence Nil Rate Band for inheritance tax
background: Ensure that the childless have the same IHT allowances as those who have children, and benefit from both the 'Residence Nil Rate Band' of £175,000 and the Nil Rate Band of £325,000.
additional_details: We feel this is a deeply discriminating and offensive tax against the childless. Massive hikes in house prices have pushed what was once an average terraced home into price brackets nearing a million pounds in the South of England, with accelerating rates across the country. These are property values that can push people beyond the current inheritance tax Nil Rate Band and Residential Nil Rate Band, tax allowances. The childless are taxed at 40% on assets exceeding the tax allowance.

action: Call for a new General election
background:
I feel the current government have lost support of the nation .
It's time for the nation to speak
additional_details: The government needs to prove they have the support of the nation as I feel there's no confidence in the current government and a general election would let the nation speak
rejection_details:

Call an immediate general election

action: Restrict public access to birth certificates to help protect children’s privacy
background: We believe that it is too easy to buy a child’s birth certificate using only basic details, and this exposes children’s personal information to strangers.
additional_details:
We ask the Government to limit access to birth certificates for children under 18 to their parents/legal guardians, or authorised bodies, while keeping historic records accessible for research.

At present, anyone can obtain a certified copy of a child’s birth certificate if they know basic details (name, date of birth, place of registration, details of parents). This means sensitive personal information can be made accessible to strangers. This system has not kept pace with modern concerns about data security, child safeguarding, and identity fraud.

action: Celebration of the patron saint of  England
background: The government to legislate a public holiday to celebrate the patron saint of England,  St George. Which should be as near to 23rd April (St George's saint day) as possible.
additional_details:
The division within the English public gives credence to a lack of solidarity and direction. This has been evidenced by significant ventures in flag planting in public (roads n street lamps). Parliament needs to recognise, support, and nurture
future generations and their patriotism .
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739078

action: Introduce a public misconduct register for police accountability & transparency
background: Legislate to introduce a public misconduct register for police found guilty of misconduct or gross misconduct, including bullying and discrimination. We think this should be known as 'Isabelle’s Law'.
additional_details: We believe these changes could ensure that the public can request misconduct history of the officer/staff that's dealing with them, protect whistleblowers, and provide transparency for the public.

action: Allow patients with a medical cannabis prescription to grow for personal use
background: Allow patients with valid medical cannabis prescriptions to legally grow up to 6 plants for personal medical use. Require secure cultivation, LED lighting for safety, and registration with clinics to ensure safe, affordable, and regulated access to medicine.
additional_details: Patients with valid medical cannabis prescriptions often face high costs and difficulty accessing the correct strains. We believe allowing them to grow up to six plants at home would make treatment more affordable, provide consistent access, and offer therapeutic benefits from cultivation, while ensuring safety through secure growing conditions and LED lighting requirements.

action: Stop councils from removing English, Scottish and Welsh flags,
background: Encourage the nation to be proud of the country.....just like any other country in the world does.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban councils from removing the Union Flag and the flags of the four nations
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738423

action: Change the law to allow random breath testing (RBT) for drivers
background: We want the UK Government to allow police to conduct random breath testing, without the need for reasonable suspicion that someone has been drinking.
additional_details: A report has suggested that drink driving collisions represent 17% of all deaths on UK roads and this has increased over the last 15 years. By contrast, Australia introduced RBT in the 1980’s and has seen a significant and sustained drop in road fatalities since. It has been reported that the key ingredients for success appear to be continued, highly visible police enforcement together with extensive publicity. We believe we must adopt the same deterrent strategy.

action: Fund free NHS dentist treatment for all UK Citizens
background: During times such as the currently financial crisis many people including those who work full time are struggling to excess dentist treatment due to the cost. Make it free for all UK citizens to access.
additional_details: Every UK citizen should have the right the free dental treatment. Dental treatment can be very expensive and ultimately without such treatment it can have long term adverse implications that actually could cost the NHS and government more to resolve and care for. Just because someone is working full time it does not mean that they can afford to pay, and actually quite often working individuals are worse off due to the lack of support.

action: Require MPs who resign to immediately vacate their seat in the House of Commons
background: Change the law so MPs who resign also lose their seat and status. Currently they can remain MPs, causing confusion and undermining trust. Once they resign, they should no longer sit in the Commons or hold the title of MP. If an MP resigns they should leave Parliament
additional_details: MPs who resign should immediately lose their seat. Allowing them to quit a role yet remain MPs damages public trust. Resigning for misconduct or failure but keeping power and pay shows no real accountability. If their actions warrant resignation, they should leave Parliament. Anything less erodes faith in democracy and suggests politicians face different rules than the public.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a clear action.

We're not sure exactly when you'd like this to apply. For example, we're not sure if you are referring to MPs who announce their intention to stand down at the next election, or MPs who resign from ministerial positions. 

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like.

action: Create a separate MOT test classification for modified vehicles
background: I would like there to be a separate specific MOT test classification that can be done to verify a vehicle is roadworthy with aftermarket modifications.
additional_details: I believe the car culture of the UK to be a special one. People gather together that are car enthusiasts and show each other their cars. It’s a mix of creativity, passion and entertainment. To ensure that vehicles that are modified are safe and road worthy, we think it would be ideal to create a specific MOT test that can be done which involved an MOT tester inspecting the modification and ensuring they have been fitted or made in a safe and secure manner.

action: Enforce laws to stop racist and religious hate chants at UK public rallies
background: Rallies with racist or religious hate chants create fear and intimidation. We ask the government to enforce existing laws, give police clearer powers, and review permits to protect communities while upholding free speech responsibly.
additional_details: We ask the UK Government and Parliament to take stronger action to protect communities from racist and religious hate chants at public rallies. This includes giving police clearer guidance and powers to stop hate speech, enforcing existing public order and hate crime laws consistently, and reviewing rally permits where there is a risk of intimidation, ensuring free speech is exercised responsibly and safely.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call for a clear and specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do in regards to the current legislation in this area, or relating to the powers and enforcement responsibilities which sit with the police.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do. 

You can contact the police here to report a crime: https://www.police.uk/pu/contact-us/

action: Create a Cabinet Minister for Older People
background: We call the Government to create a new Cabinet-level Minister to represent older people and oversee policies affecting ageing, retirement, and wellbeing. Pensioners are around 18% of the population – a similar size to the 0-16 age population. We believe they demand the same representation.
additional_details: Several charities and the Minister of State for Work and Pensions have highlighted pensioner poverty. It is estimated nearly 1-in-5 pensioners are living in poverty. We believe this is a startling, shameful, figure. Without senior representation at cabinet level, we believe this and other issues like digital exclusion, scams, health conditions, loneliness, poor housing, age discrimination, lack of opportunity for paid work may never be addressed.

action: We urge the Government to reduce income tax on wages by at least 5%
background: We believe the Government should take urgent action to support workers and improve living standards by implementing this tax cut as soon as possible.
additional_details:
We urge the Government to reduce income tax on wages by at least 5% to help working people manage the rising cost of living. We believe a tax cut would increase take-home pay, reduce financial pressure, and boost the economy by encouraging spending.
We think millions of workers across the UK are struggling with inflation, high energy bills, and rising mortgage or rent costs, and that a reduction in income tax would directly benefit workers, increase consumer confidence, and stimulate growth.
We call for urgent and fair action to ease the tax burden on working people

action: Cut Politician Allowances to tackle the cost of living crisis in the UK
background: We call on the UK Government and the Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority to significantly reduce the allowances and expenses claimed by Members of Parliament and Members of the House of Lords.
additional_details:
We urge the Government and IPSA to:

Conduct a full review of MPs' and Lords’ allowances to identify and reduce unnecessary spending.

Cap or cut second home and travel expenses for MPs, especially where public transport or virtual meetings are viable.

Reduce the House of Lords daily allowance, or introduce means-testing and performance-based criteria.

Redirect savings from these cuts toward vital public services and support for low-income households.

We believe politicians should lead by example in times of national hardship. Even modest cuts would demonstrate solidarity with the public and help restore trust in our political system.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA) is responsible for deciding on MPs' expenses and pay. IPSA is independent of both Parliament and Government.

You can find out more about IPSA here: http://www.theipsa.org.uk

action: Stop Divisive Rhetoric Against Patriotic Citizens
background: It unfairly vilifies ordinary people and fuels an atmosphere where violence against them can be excused or encouraged. Patriotism is not extremism. Branding law-abiding citizens as “fascists,” “racists” or “far right” does not reduce radicalism, it risks inciting it.
additional_details:
Publicly condemn the use of such rhetoric.
Affirm that patriotism is not extremism.
Hold public figures and institutions accountable when they use language that vilifies ordinary citizens.
Words have consequences. The Government must act to prevent this rhetoric from endangering people and dividing communities.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly how you'd like the Government to condemn the use of certain language and how you'd like people to be held accountable.

action: Protect British Beer: Reserve 30 Percent of Pub Taps for Independent Breweries
background: We call on the government to legislate to require all pubs to allocate 30% of their taps to independently brewed British beer, and to support publicans with the guidance to implement this change.
additional_details: Independent breweries make up less than 10 percent of UK pub sales despite strong consumer demand. We believe that the tied pub system blocks access for small brewers, limiting choice and threatening local jobs. We think a 30 percent tap allocation would support small businesses, enrich pub culture, and ensure fair market access without removing existing agreements with large suppliers.

action: Make Misogyny a hate crime
background: The Government should make misogyny a hate crime by amending the Sentencing Act, introduce tougher laws for online abuse, train police and prosecutors, funding support for survivors in education, and tackle anti-feminist hate groups that target and radicalise young people online.
additional_details: Young women, especially students, face high rates of harassment, assault, and online abuse. Misogyny fuels this violence, yet current laws fail to address it directly. Recognising misogyny as a hate crime would protect victims, deter offenders, and send a clear message that gender-based hostility is unacceptable. It would also validate survivors’ experiences and help create safer environments in education and online, where young people are most vulnerable.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make misogyny a hate crime.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/722809

action: Withdraw from ECHR & stop processing asylum claims until Channel crossings stop
background: We call on the government to withdraw the UK’s membership of the European Convention on Human Rights and pause processing all asylum applications until illegal Channel crossings are completely stopped.
additional_details: We believe illegal Channel crossings are undermining border security and public trust, and that current membership of the ECHR prevents effective deportations and blocks government action. We think that by suspending ECHR obligations and halting asylum claims until crossings end, the UK can deter illegal entry, protect national sovereignty, and restore control of our borders.

action: In a government leadership contest for PM a general election should be called
background: If a government elects a new PM mid term then a general election should be called. The new incumbent has not been voted for and infighting is happening too much.
additional_details: Too often governments have changed Prime Minister within their term of office after considerable infighting. This is a distraction from real events that need urgent government attention. The new PM has not been voted into office. If a leadership contest for PM ocurres then MPs will think twice about a leadership contest if it means triggering a general election. All the unelected PMs have caused considerable issues such as May, Truss, and soon Starmer! Government has stopped governing!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737933

action: Require disabled toilets to have a fold down shelf for stoma users
background: There are often no facilities for stoma users in disabled toilets. Leaving us using the floor or the top of toilet seats for our appliances. This is not sanitary. I would like a legal requirement of a fold down shelf. This allows the shelf to be folded up so there is no impact on wheelchair users.
additional_details: I have reached out to supermarkets, coffee shops and various other places and very few are willing to make these changes. I have now started a social media campaign and have found many other stoma users have the same difficulty, including in hospitals! With a high risk of infection when the stoma is exposed for an appliance to be changed. How is this acceptable.

action: Include children not living with one parent in all benefits and housing claims
background: When applying for Universal Credit or Social Housing, you are only allowed to declare children that permanently reside with you. The government should amend the law to allow children that visit on a regular basis to be included in these calculations.
additional_details: Single people not living with their children cannot include children who stay with them regularly. This means housing allowance is capped at a 1 bed property, and any housing request to the local authority would also allow just 1 bedroom. This may have a negative effect on any parent who wants to ensure their children have adequate space to stay, and allow the parent to be able to afford to see them and feed them.

action: “Save the Tradition: Paper Tickets for Football Away Games”
background: I urge the Government to mandate football clubs offer paper tickets for away matches. Paper tickets hold deep sentimental value, preserving cherished memories and traditions. Ensuring fans have this choice respects their connection to the game and safeguards an important part of football culture.
additional_details: I urgently call on the government to act as digital-only ticketing excludes countless loyal fans and destroys a beloved tradition. Paper tickets are sacred keepsakes fans proudly collect, embodying unforgettable away days, shared passion, and lifelong devotion. Removing them risks severing our deep bond with football’s heritage. Preserving paper tickets is vital to honor supporters’ loyalty, ensure inclusivity, and protect the soul of the game.

action: Require urgent government intervention when councils fail SEND duties
background: Require urgent government intervention when councils fail their SEND duties. Strengthen the law so Ofsted and CQC must investigate and the Department for Education can act immediately where children with SEND are left without education
additional_details: Too many children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) are left without education because councils miss EHCP deadlines, remove provision unlawfully, or fail to secure Section F support. Families wait months for tribunals with no interim relief. This is a national crisis. Government must act now so no child loses their right to education through council failings
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740101

action: Remove the 2-Year Limit for CICA Claims for Sexual Abuse Survivors
background: We call on the Government to allow survivors of sexual abuse to submit CICA applications at any time, not limited to two years. This could give child survivors the chance to claim support when they are ready, without being penalised for delays caused by trauma, fear, or lack of awareness.
additional_details: Many survivors cannot apply to CICA within the current two-year limit because of trauma, fear, shame, or simply not knowing their rights. This rule can deny them access to justice, recognition, and vital financial support. Removing the time limit could give survivors a fair opportunity to claim compensation, feel validated, and begin to rebuild their lives after abuse.

action: Legislate that a by-election must be held when a representative changes parties.
background: Whether leaving one party to join another, or winning a seat as an independent but then joining a party or vice-versa, politicians at local, regional, and national levels in England should not be permitted to do so without giving constituents the democratic right to choose party and platform again.
additional_details: The Commons holds to an 18th-century convention that changing parties doesn’t force resignation and by-election on the principle that MPs are individually elected and free to develop their own agendas. Yet candidates and winners are supported, promoted, and controlled by parties/whips. Polls show citizens vote for parties &/or platforms. Those under the banner and manifesto of one party, or who promise independence but then join one, are not what was voted for. It is misleading and undemocratic.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Provide parking permits from pregnancy until the child is 12 years old or 135 cm
background: These permits will prevent others who are not entitled from using the small amount of spaces for baby and child parking. Care sets are a legal requirement so space should be provided in order to safely operate these.
additional_details: The amount of people parking in child spaces with teenagers or no children  causes serious problems for those legally obliged to use baby and child car seats. Baby and toddler seats especially require a fully open door to operate. People often use these spaces to be closer to the shops not caring that those with babies and toddlers really do need to be closer to the shops and have the extra space to safely operate legally required car seats.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739884

action: Make Anticholinergic Burden scores mandatory for all over 65
background: Require the Government and DHSC to recommend NICE mandate ACB scoring in all medication reviews for patients over 65.
additional_details: High Anticholinergic Burden (ACB) scores are linked to memory loss, confusion, falls, and premature death. Mandatory scoring during medication reviews could save lives, reduce harm, and empower families to ask the right questions. Funding should support prescriber training and awareness so patients and carers can challenge unsafe prescribing.

action: Fair Child Maintenance: Use Net Pay and Account for Outgoings of Paying Parents
background: Child maintenance reform is essential to ensure fairness for paying parents who actively support their children while managing their own living expenses. Current calculations based on gross pay disregard essential bills, placing an undue financial burden on responsible parents.
additional_details: The current child maintenance system is outdated and in need of urgent reform to reflect the financial realities of modern life. Calculations based solely on gross income fail to consider essential living expenses, placing an unfair burden on paying parents. A system based on net income and necessary outgoings would promote fairness, support children's needs more effectively, and help maintain financial stability and healthier relationships for both parents and children.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730665

action: Register stolen vehicles internationally as standard procedure
background: The current practice of using only the UK's national system to register stolen vehicles is not working. You would assume that when a vehicle is reported as stolen in the UK, it is marked as stolen in all countries. This is not the case and is something that needs to change!
additional_details: Since leaving the EU, the UK Police no longer register stolen vehicles on the international system, Interpol. Even if the French police pulled over your stolen car or motorcycle for speeding, they would have no idea that it was stolen. We are preventing international authorities from identifying stolen vehicles and giving thieves a free ticket. A vehicle can be on a ferry within hours no matter where you live in the UK, this is giving criminals an easy ride and making us a target.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We’re not sure exactly what you would like the UK Government or Parliament to do.

UK police forces can already access Interpol and record stolen cars on the Interpol Stolen Motor Vehicle Database, as the UK’s departure from the European Union did not affect its membership of Interpol.

You may wish to create a new petition which calls for the UK Government or Parliament to “seek an agreement with the EU for routine information sharing on stolen cars" if that's something you would like to happen.

action: Require all secondary schools to allow pupils to wear their PE kits on PE days
background: We want the Government to require secondary schools to allow children to wear their PE kit all day on days when they have PE, including allowing them to come into school wearing PE kits.
additional_details: We believe children always deserve the right to privacy and protection of their bodies. We believe schools should encourage children from early years to understand personal and physical boundaries. We believe it makes no sense to force them to undress in a public setting, and we feel communal changing creates an unsafe environment for pupils. Body insecurities, menstruation and physical comparisons may be highlighted, and peer judgment/bullying may result from children being exposed in this way.

action: Any mp crossing the floor should trigger a bye election in thier constituency
background: To change the law and make it compulsory to have a bye election  in the constituency of any mp changing his party

action: Require an election if 70% of the government manifesto isn’t delivered
background: Create a law requiring governments to deliver at least 70% of their clear, measurable manifesto pledges within a Parliament. If they fail, a general election must be triggered, with delivery independently verified.
additional_details: Manifestos are the basis on which voters choose who to elect, yet we think many promises are broken once in power. This undermines trust in democracy and leaves voters powerless until the next election. A 70% threshold, independently verified, would ensure accountability and restore faith that promises made during campaigns must be kept.

action: Make adaptive anti-dazzle headlamps mandatory on new road vehicles
background: Some manufacturers have developed headlamps that automatically change the shape of the light beam to avoid dazzling other road users. We want this technology to become a mandatory part of vehicle regulations, included in the MOT test.
additional_details: Light Emitting Diode headlamps have become common on road vehicles. LED lamps have the advantage of longer life than incandescent types, but can cause serious problems with dazzle. This is a potential road safety concern for all road users. Adaptive LED headlamps can be superior to manual or automatic dipped beam, if designed and calibrated correctly.

action: If an MP defects to another party, a by-election should be called immediately.
background: A new law should be introduced to ensure constituents, voting for a candidate who represents their chosen party defects, there should be a by-election to confirm the constituency still want representation from this individual.
additional_details: Very often constituents vote according to party preferences and may indeed vote tactically to ensure certain parties do not win a seat. It is therefore incongruent for an MP to decide to change allegiance without support from her / his constituents. A by-election should be called immediately.

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party

action: Include hair colour as a protected characteristic under the Equality Act
background: We want hair colour to be included as a new protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010, so cases of people being discriminated against due to having a different hair colour would not be tolerated or accepted.
additional_details: We believe this could change the way discrimination based on hair colour would be dealt with, by treating it such as any another situation based on another protected characteristic. An example of discrimination is that a 2014 study showed that around 61% of males and 47% of females with red hair have experienced discrimination in their lifetime due to their hair colour. We believe this shows that this is a serious issue and so it should be treated that way.

action: Introduce legal minimum ratios of care home staff to residents
background: We call on the Government to introduce minimum staff-to-resident ratios in all care homes, so every resident receives the attention, dignity, and safety they deserve.
additional_details: Currently, many care homes operate with staffing levels that are too low, which can leave residents feeling lonely, upset, ignored, or neglected. This can also place enormous strain on care staff and families, contributing to burnout, stress, and unsafe conditions. We feel it is time that dignity, safety, and companionship for care home residents are prioritised through clear, enforceable standards.

action: Review settlement routes for long-term adult residents in UK since childhood
background: Review the settlement and citizenship pathway for those born or raised in the UK from childhood. We believe many fall outside current routes due to law changes. The review should consider adding a new pathway resembling the Windrush scheme, giving rights to live, work, and contribute.
additional_details: We believe some people born or brought to the UK as children, who have lived here ever since, are not granted residency as adults through no fault of their own. Denied the right to work, study, or rent, they may face precarious situations, risking crime, exploitation, dependency, or poor mental health. Many fall outside current routes due to law changes and risk losing the right to remain.

action: Review UK food aid mechanisms to ensure it is prioritised by need
background: We urge the Government to launch a review into its current approach to providing humanitarian aid and ensuring global food security to ensure it is prioritised by need and not according to political or ideological considerations.
additional_details: Hundreds of millions of people face food insecurity across the globe, and we believe aid should be prioritised solely on humanitarian needs. Ensure rapid response mechanisms for regions facing acute malnutrition & famine & other high-risk areas, as well as to support independent monitoring & transparent reporting of food security crises to guide effective interventions. We believe political considerations must never override the urgent need to prevent starvation.

Treat all wars equally: give aid, diplomacy and attention across conflicts, including Ukraine, Sudan, Myanmar, Yemen, Ethiopia and the DRC. Uphold international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and condemn antisemitism and all forms of hate.
additional_details: The UK should show fairness in its foreign policy. At present, Gaza receives much attention, but civilians in other wars such as Ukraine, Sudan, Myanmar, Yemen, Ethiopia and the DRC also suffer greatly. Every civilian life has equal value. Focusing only on one conflict risks undermining trust and credibility. Equal attention, aid and diplomacy would demonstrate that the UK stands for peace, human rights and humanitarian law everywhere.

additional_details: Many children struggle in mainstream education due to unmet needs and rising mental health issues—around 1 in 5 aged 8–16 now have a probable mental disorder. additional_details: EDCs in everyday products are linked to infertility, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and pregnancy complications. Black women are disproportionately exposed and nearly 4x more likely to die during pregnancy. NHS guidance is silent on this preventable health risk, leaving women and babies unprotected. Early intervention can prevent harm, reduce health inequalities and close racial health gaps. This supports ongoing parliamentary inquiries into reproductive health reform.

action: Allow license holders to drive motorhomes up to 4250kg on UK Category B License
background: We want the UK to allow UK license holders to drive motorhomes up to 4250kg on UK Category B Licenses, in line with proposed changes from the EU.
additional_details: Current laws allow Category B car license holders to drive motorhomes up to 3,500 kg. We feel current laws restrict the size and weight of motorhomes, and many motorhomes just over 3500kg are automatic, which may be helpful for people with disabilities.
government_response_summary: The DfT keeps driving licence rules under review. The Government has not yet assessed the potential benefits of allowing Category B licence holders to drive motorhomes weighing up to 4,250kg.
government_response_body: On 5 November 2025, the European Union published the final text of the Fourth Driving Licence Directive (2025/2205/EU). This replaced the Third Driving Licence Directive and updates driving licence rules across EU and EEA countries.   The new Directive includes a range of changes, such as introducing digital driving licences, extending photocard validity from 10 to 15 years, updating driving instruction rules, and making changes to licence categories. One proposed change would increase the maximum weight of vehicles that can be driven on a Category B licence.   In 2015, when the UK was still an EU Member State, countries began negotiating a temporary exemption to support the uptake of low  and zero emission vehicles. This allowed Category B licence holders to drive vans weighing up to 4,250kg (instead of 3,500kg), without needing a medical, a Driver Certificate of Professional Competence (CPC), or to follow drivers’ hours rules. Drivers were required to complete five hours of training.   In June 2025, the UK Government extended these rules through the Motor Vehicles (Driving Licences) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2025. This change allowed all zero emission vehicles to be driven on a Category B licence, removed the training requirement, and permitted these vehicles to tow a trailer.   Under the Fourth Driving Licence Directive, EU countries will be able to allow Category B licence holders to drive motorhomes (referred to as “motor caravans” in the Directive) weighing up to 4,250kg. This would apply to petrol, diesel, and zero emission vehicles. This reflects the fact that many motorhomes exceed 3,500kg but weigh less than 4,250kg, and that some countries already allow heavier vans to be driven on a Category B licence.   This change would not be automatic. EU Member States must require either at least seven hours of training, a test (which does not have to be a full driving test), or both. Any training or test must cover key safety topics set out in the Directive. There is no requirement for drivers to have held their licence for a minimum number of years before driving a motorhome.   The Department for Transport published its Road Safety Strategy in January 2026. It was not possible to consider alignment with the new EU Directive before the Strategy was published.   The UK is already committed to introducing a digital driving licence. However, other changes in the Directive require careful consideration before decisions are made on whether to adopt them. The Government has not yet assessed the potential merits of changing Category B licence rules for motorhomes.   Any future changes to driving licence law would be subject to public consultation and a full assessment of their impacts.  Department for Transport

action: bring back physical tickets

rejection_details: Decisions about digital ticketing are a matter for individual retailers, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Stop large ticketing companies from using dynamic pricing
background: Ticketmaster have used dynamic pricing several times. To increase ticket prices during a sale because of the number of people queuing is awful. This happened with oasis and system of a down and presumably countless others. With soad tickets went from ~£100 to nearly £400 in less than hour.
additional_details: Stop them being able to do it. Tell people up front how many gigs there will be, and what prices the tickets will be. They should be fixed and dynamic pricing should be banned. Ideally those have overpaid should be refunded up to the price of the original ticket before dynamic pricing kicked in.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: "Ban dynamic ticket pricing for live events" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728612

action: Fund training in schools to support complex mental health conditions.
background: We call on the Government to increase funding and provide mandatory training in schools, colleges, and universities so staff are equipped to understand, identify, and support people with complex mental health conditions, including bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and personality disorders.
additional_details: Too often, severe mental health conditions go unrecognized in education settings, leading to stigma, crisis situations, and people being left without support. Staff lack the tools to respond safely and effectively. With proper funding and training, schools, colleges, and universities can reduce risks of harm, prevent exclusion, and create safer, more compassionate environments for those living with complex disorders.
rejection_details: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742545

action: Ban the testing of animals on all cosmetic products sold in the UK.
background: Ban the testing of animals on cosmetic products or make restrictions tighter on the welfare of animals.
additional_details: At the moment, many people use products without giving a thought at what is happening behind the scenes. Currently, animals are being forced fed and injected, basically being sentenced to death. From birth, animals are deprived of simple rights.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

End testing on dogs and other animals for development of products for human use
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736578

action: Free 30 hours weekly child care to 9 months child also to Welsh working parents
background: For the Welsh parliament to Implement the same law that has just been implemented in England, allowing working parents to receive free childcare since the child is 9 months old
additional_details: Because the way of living has changed and we don’t live anymore in an era where we can afford to have one parent only looking after the child in his early stage of their life,  and the other parent to carry the brunt of all costs. On average, childcare cost is equivalent to an individual’s average salary. The allowance that has just now been implemented in England was long due but regrettably this has not been the case in Wales or Scotland yet.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the UK Government or UK Parliament are directly responsible for. Decisions about childcare in Wales are a matter for the Welsh Government and Welsh Parliament.

You may wish to submit a petition to the Welsh Parliament's Petitions Committee: https://petitions.senedd.wales/help

action: Stop the Clocks going back in Autumn BST all year round!
background: When the clocks go back in Autumn, we lose that precious hour of daylight and we are lost to the darkness at 4:00! This madness has to end! because no nobody and I mean nobody wants it to get dark BEFORE they leave work/school!
additional_details: Well it might’ve been beneficial for some students in northern Scotland many years ago, there is infrastructure in place now to stop that being an issue so why are we still having to compromise!? I know everyone else thinks the same when we have to get up one hour earlier so help me do something about it!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Make British Summer Time (BST) permanent year-round
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739222

action: Downsize elders to smaller homes to create space for larger families
background: We ask Parliament to create safe, supported ways for older people to downsize into suitable homes. Many remain in large properties they no longer need. Helping them move can free up housing for growing families and ease the pressure on the overcrowded housing market.
additional_details: Family overcrowding is a growing crisis. Many live in cramped spaces, lacking privacy and comfort. Larger homes are in short supply, while many elderly people occupy homes too big for their needs. If downsizing is made easier for them, these homes can become available to families, easing overcrowding and improving quality of life.
rejection_details: We are not clear on what you would like the UK Government or Parliament to do. You can start a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Introduce mandatory business and entrepreneurship in secondary curriculum
background: I am deeply concerned that, in 2025, we continue to deliver a national curriculum designed for the traditional career paths of the 1980s rather than the technologies and opportunities of today.
additional_details:
Entrepreneurship should not be treated as an optional extra, but as a matter of strategic national importance.
 
With AI and automation already reshaping the workforce at speed, I think our young people risk being left behind unless significant modernisation is brought into our school curriculum.
 
The next great British founder could be sitting in a classroom right now but without guidance, inspiration and education on how to develop their ideas, they may never discover what they’re capable of.

action: Stop ALL legal aid for non British citizens unless worked in UK for 10 years
background: Stop Legal Aid for non British citizens exceptions would be if you have worked and paid Tax in the UK for at least 10 years continuously
additional_details: I believe that the British public should not be responsible for legal aid payments for non-citizens who haven't worked and paid tax in the UK. All visitors to this country should have insurance to cover both medical and legal expenses this should include both legal and illegal migrants

action: Change the Employment status of MPs and introduce a strong Code of Conduct .
background: Change the employment status of MPs which protects them from bad behaviour and introduce a Code of Conduct with a range of sanctions. Politicians are not capable of "policing" themselves and behaviour which shows a lack of integrity is not taken seriously.
additional_details:
Recent Governments and Political parties continue to be mired in controversy and this behaviour in some ways denies us a functioning democracy.
MPs refusing to clearly answer questions denies the electorate scrutiny.
The recent stamp duty case and the appointment of the UK ambassador to the US are among 2 of the latest scandals.
 Police officers would have been sacked  we see politicians act without honesty and integrity and face far less  sanctions. Take the inestigations away from politics
rejection_details:
