https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732555
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731105

action: Give everyone a day off work or school for their birthday.
background: People should be able to celebrate their birthday without having to take annual leave. Requesting a guaranteed day off.
additional_details: A day off would improve wellbeing, morale, and work-life balance. It would also ensure celebrated individuality.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/724372

action: Reduce NI payments for people not registered with an NHS dentist
background: As many people are unable to have an NHS dentist but pay full NI contributions. We think they should have a reduction in NI contributions to help with private dental care. Why pay the same as people who have an NHS dentist.
additional_details: Reduce NI contributions for members of the public that are not registered with an NHS dentist but pay full contributions.

action: To make wellbeing within schools a part of the education system.
background: To bring at least 1 lesson per week to focus on meditation, breathing exercises, understanding emotions vs thoughts and regulating those within the school environment for all children.
additional_details: Children go through many changes as they grow, emotional, mentally and physically, there is nothing to support these children through the changes, they are expected to cope regardless of the pressures of school work, thus pressure results in outbursts, bullying, lack of empathy towards each other, and has a knock on effect for some through life. If children understood and could hold their own emotions they could support each other’s better resulting in a happier school environment.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/721736

action: Change the DDA 1991 to end breed discrimination and focus on behaviour
background: To reform the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 by removing breed-specific legislation and replacing it with behaviour-based laws. Focus on responsible ownership, training, and education to improve public safety without unfairly targeting certain dog breeds.
additional_details: Breed-specific laws have not reduced dog attacks and unfairly punish dogs based on looks, not behaviour. Data shows aggression is linked to ownership and training. We need effective, evidence-based laws that focus on behaviour, enforce accountability, and support public education to truly keep people safe.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which asks for the same action: "Change the DDA 1991 to stop breed bans and focus on behaviour" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730292

action: Prevent blocking comments on social media posts from publicly elected accounts.
background: I want to stop those in publicly elected positions, such as the Mayor of London, from preventing comments on posts they make from official accounts on X, Instagram and other social media apps and websites.
additional_details:
The practice of blocking or limiting commentary on social media accounts reduces the opportunity for the public to provide feedback, context and air grievances to these elected officials so they can gain a wider understanding of the electorate, instead of existing in an echo chamber. This is increasingly important in such a divisive, digital age. 

Civic 'Town Square' discussion has been lost during the migration online. We must do something to ensure all voices can be heard.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731469

action: Fund free/discounted glasses & lenses for those who need them daily
background: Fund free or heavily subsidised prescription glasses and lenses for people who rely on them every day, similar to how essential medical devices are supported. We call on the government to help reduce the cost burden so no one has to struggle to afford the sight they need to live and work.
additional_details: We believe good eyesight is essential for daily life, work, education and safety, yet glasses and lenses are often expensive, and that people who rely on them have no choice but to buy them, unlike optional items. We think making them free or subsidised would ensure everyone can see clearly, avoid accidents, and take part fully in society without being held back by cost.

action: Change the laws to give dads the rights and access to their children
background: I want the government to make a law that protects us dads against having our children held captive from us during relationship break ups.
additional_details: All men and women deserve the right to be treated equally as a parent no matter the gender. Also every child deserves the right to see each of their parents and there’s no law to protect women keeping the children away from the man which should be legally speaking not just from her point of view. A lot of dads deserve justice and deserve to be around their children.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do. You may also wish to sign this petition: "More legal aid for fathers seeking access to their children" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/725169

The Government has guidance about making child arrangements if you divorce or separate: https://www.gov.uk/looking-after-children-divorce

Citizens Advice also provides guidance for making child arrangements: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/family/making-agreements-about-your-children/making-child-arrangements/

action: Remove or extend the 6 month time limit on prosecution for summary offences
background: Currently, summary offences must be laid before a court within six months of the offence. Once that time passes, no matter the evidence or the harm, justice is simply gone, and legal action cannot be taken. A review of this rule is urgently needed.
additional_details: We think the law surrounding summary offences lacks clarity, and the six month statutory time limit is deeply unjust. Victims and families deserve justice, regardless of how long it takes for evidence or offenders to come to light. This cut off silences victims and protects offenders. It sends the wrong message, a frightening one, that if offenders evade detection for long enough, they can walk away free. Victims deserve better. Families deserve better. Justice shouldn't expire.

action: End the practice of combining couples' Universal Credit into a single payment
background: Change how couples payments work to protect people who are in a relationship with an abusive partner. Currently Universal Credit pays couples into one account rather than two separate accounts. This can enable more abuse as the victim wouldn't be able to easily and safely escape an abusive partner
additional_details: To fix this you should remove the couples benefits and have the payment split over two accounts, or offer easier support that can't be tracked by the abuser to leave the relationship.

action: More funding to strengthen youth homelessness prevention methods
background: We call on the government to increase funding to support young care leavers.
additional_details: Including through family mediation, partnering with organisations to create specific employment opportunities for those leaving foster care, train school staff to recognise and respond to those at risk, create emergency temporary housing and dedicate consistent funding for these initiatives.

action: Make Holocaust denial and performing Nazi salutes a specific criminal offence
background: Parliament, with the backing of the Government, should legislate to make Holocaust denial (in speech, print etc.) and the performance of Nazi salutes a specific criminal offence in line with many countries in continental Europe and beyond.
additional_details: Holocaust denial is worthy of becoming a criminal offence as it is consistently used to debase historical fact in the pursuit of harassing, intimidating or otherwise harming groups persecuted in the Holocaust. Such activity only serves to empower extremist ideologies, and can breach numerous statutes protecting groups and their dignity in existing law. Likewise, Nazi salutes are not only a gross affront to our country’s history, but also intimidatory and hostile to these very same groups.

action: Regulations in beauty industries for Botox
background: I want the new regulations to be reviewed about face to face consultations
additional_details: Make amendments to the current regulations for asthetics consultations for Botox
rejection_details:
We are not clear what action you are seeking from Parliament and the UK Government. 

In Scotland this issue is devolved to the Scottish Parliament, which also has a petitions system which you can access here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/petitions/check

action: Make a local pump track in amersham for bikes
background: In Amersham a lot of people I know would like a local pump track near the Amersham train station for people who ride bikes
additional_details: I think this would be a great way for people to leave their homes and go out and about in this pump track and having fun introducing alltypes of new people to the area
rejection_details:
We have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: lessen the costs of public transport in london
background: lower tfl prices making public transport easier and more accessible for the general public
additional_details: this will not only benefit the general public but will also enable tfl to crack down on people who evade buying tickets, this will save the government money and also creates a more substantial revenue for the company, as of right now due to constant strikes the public are getting tired and angry, if action isn’t taken soon this will cause more harm than good.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. It is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly.

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Make First Aid and Seizure Training Mandatory in All Schools
background: Change the law so that all schools must provide age-appropriate first aid training, including seizure first aid, to all pupils. This training should include CPR, the recovery position, and how to respond to common emergencies. It should be practical, refreshed regularly.
additional_details:
No child should ever feel helpless watching a friend collapse, stop breathing, or have a seizure. Yet many young people leave school without knowing how to help in an emergency.A few simple skills learned early can save lives. First aid training gives children the confidence to step forward, not back, when every second counts. It empowers them, protects their friends and families, and benefits society as a whole.
Every child deserves the knowledge to save a life.
rejection_details:
We are not clear from your petition how you would like the current practice in schools to change. Information about the current practice is available here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/relationships-education-relationships-and-sex-education-rse-and-health-education/physical-health-and-mental-wellbeing-primary-and-secondary#by-the-end-of-primary-school

You can start a new petition setting out more clearly how you would like the current practice to change.

action: Establish instant lockdown alert system for schools, nurseries & parents
background: The Government should introduce a national instant alert system so schools, nurseries, and parents are directly notified by authorities when a lockdown is required and when it has ended.
additional_details: We believe that we need a national instant alert system so schools, nurseries and even parents are notified immediately, given clear information, and told when lockdowns have ended.

action: Make supermarket self service tills all accept cash as well as card payments.
background: Enforce supermarkets and businesses with self service tills ensure they all have the ability to accept cash which is legal tender and card payments so as not to exclude people who still deal in cash.
additional_details: Because cash is legal tender and should be accepted at payment points. Today in my local supermarket - 8 self serve tills and only one was able to accept cash. All self serve should have the ability to accept card or cash payments - not everyone wants to pay by card or wait long periods to wait for a cash till to be available.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which asks for a similar action: "Ban business from not accepting cash payments" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735459

action: Maintain the electric vehicle exemption to the central London Congestion Charge
background:
Transport for London (TfL) should be forced to maintain the full electric vehicle exemption to the Congestion Charge which is due to end on 25 December.

The 100% Cleaner Vehicle Discount is scheduled to end on 25 December and will be replaced by a 25% discount for electric cars.
additional_details:
TfL plans also include raising the Congestion Charge fee from £15 to £18 from 2 January 2026.

This means that people with an electric car would need to pay £13.50 every time they drive into central London, and traders with electric vans would pay £9.

Commuters face increasing cost of living pressures whilst businesses, hospitals and schools need deliveries and will still need to enter the Congestion Charge zone. This means they will no longer be inventivsed to use cleaner electric vehicles.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. It is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and Transport for London (TfL).

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Sever diplomatic, trade, and other relations with Israel and impose sanctions
background: Government should sever diplomatic relations with Israel, suspend all imports from and exports to Israel (including of military equipment & components), impose tight economic sanctions, cancel any contracts with Israeli firms (including UK subsidiaries) & cease any intelligence sharing with Israel.
additional_details: We think this is needed because of many concerns about Israel's actions. A UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry found that Israel has committed genocide.

action: Diabetes should not prevent someone serving in the British armed forces
background: Diabetics should be able to join the military due to the modern technological advances that occur everyday. Managing the condition is second nature to most diabetics therefore I believe it should not be considered a risk as those who are insulin dependent know how to handle it and live with it.

action: Review guidance for funded IVF
background: I want the guidance for same-sex couples accessing NHS-funded IVF to be reviewed to remove the requirement to prove infertility through costly artificial insemination. IVF should be funded for same-sex couples on the same terms as heterosexual couples.
additional_details: I want the government to review the guidance so that same-sex couples are treated equally. Right now, we may be denied funded IVF unless we can afford to pay for IUI first. This seems unfair and feels like a penalty simply for being in a same-sex relationship. Every couple deserves the chance to start a family, and that opportunity should never be taken away because of who we love.

action: Adopt Scotland’s wedding model in England & Wales
background: England & Wales still limit legal weddings to licensed venues or registrars. Scotland licenses celebrants, so couples can marry at meaningful locations. We want the same: authorise trained independent celebrants and allow legal weddings anywhere safe, fair, and dignified. Boosting local economies.
additional_details: Adopt Scotland’s officiant-based model. Let couples marry where their love has meaning—homes, gardens, hospices, community spaces—while keeping safeguards: notice, ID checks, two witnesses, and records. Licensing celebrants (trained, insured) cuts red tape, lowers costs, widens access, and drives spend across local venues, hospitality and creative suppliers, supporting the visitor economy year-round. It helps rural and urban areas alike, encouraging midweek weddings and sustainable growth.
rejection_details: On 2 October 2025, the Ministry of Justice announced reforms to marriage law: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/major-boost-to-economy-through-wedding-law-reform

action: Automatic By-Election for MP Defections to Another Political Party
background: If an MP leaves their elected party, they should be  required to hold a by-election. This would allow constituents to exercise their democratic right & ensure transparency in representation, as current political maneuvering undermines voters' choices. It's time to restore peoples faith in politics.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which asks for the same action: "By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Introduce subtitles in public environments, such as concerts & sports events
background: Implement subtitles in public situations, such as cinemas & theatres who can use technologies like subtitling apps aimed towards  hearing-impaired individuals. Concerts and sporting events can have screens displaying live-captioned text alongside the program to ensure everyone is included.
additional_details: As someone with a hearing impairment, I find myself constantly facing challenges in public spaces. Venues like cinemas, concert venues, theatres, and sports events are inherently reliant on audio, which poses a barrier for myself and the deaf and hard of hearing community. Without subtitles, the dialogue in films, announcements during sports events, and song lyrics at concerts become inaccessible, cutting us off from the full experience that everyone else enjoys.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about the use of subtitles in entertainment venues are a matter for individual businesses, not the UK Government or Parliament. If you'd like the Government or Parliament to set new requirements for venues about the use of subtitles, you could start a new petition clearly setting out what you'd like those requirements to be.

action: Review treatment of ARFID and access to NHS eating disorder services
background: In many cases, support from NHS eating disorder services is not given to people with ARFID. We think this support is crucial and should be mandatory. If left untreated, ARFID can be life threatening. People can miss out on education and life events, and can lack energy to do basic daily activities.
additional_details: I was diagnosed with ARFID when I was a teen. I was dismissed from the eating disorder team due to them not treating ARFID (an eating disorder). My BMI reached 13.9 and I was in and out of hospital. Due to not getting the support I needed while growing up the effects it had on me were iron deficiency anaemia, other vitamin deficiencies and borderline bone density. I am very lucky to be alive but I still face struggles and cannot get adequate support on the NHS.

action: Make School end in early June and get rid of the three half term holiday's.
background: I would like the government to make school end in early june instead of July, and remove the three one-week half term holiday's.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about school term dates are a matter for local councils, not the UK Government or Parliament. You can find your local council and its school term dates here: https://www.gov.uk/school-term-holiday-dates

action: Scrap the Old State Pension.  All pensioners to receive the New State Pension.
background: Pay the New State Pension to all pensioners eligible for a full state pension.
additional_details:
The basic cost of living is the same for all pensioners.   A good proportion of older pensioners will not have private or works pensions and find living costs hard to manage.
No-one who has worked all their life should have to decide between heating or eating.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728562

action: Stop energy/solar companies using NSIP legislation to bypass local planning
background: Energy companies should not be allowed to exploit the Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects (NSIP) process to override the authority of local councils in deciding the future of large-scale solar farms and other energy developments. Stop them scaling/linking projects to achieve NSIP status.
additional_details: The use of NSIP legislation to bypass local democratic planning processes undermines accountability, weakens community trust, and risks the imposition of industrial-scale developments on landscapes and farmland without proper scrutiny. While the transition to renewable energy is dedirable, it must be delivered in a way that respects local decision-making, balances environmental impacts, and ensures that communities, homes, businesses and agriculture are not destroyed in the process.
rejection_details:
We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.  

NSIP applications are decided by the Secretary of State not the local authority. The local authority are consulted as part of the NSIP application process. If you would like to call for energy projects to be ineligible for the NSIP process, you can start a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Increase Government funding for less commonly followed sports
background: I want the government to increase funding for less commonly followed and played sports at lower levels to increase peoples ability to play sports they love.
additional_details: I play international level roller hockey and despite representing GB everything is paid for by the players. This gives us a significant disadvantage when playing against other state funded nations.

action: Price lock re- sale event tickets to original price or less.
background: To stop people buying up event tickets to re sell only for profit. Reduce the use of bots and profiteering from genuine fans.
additional_details: Hear a bill in parliament mandating that event tickets cannot be re- sold for more than the original price.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: "Ban all ticket touting and reselling of tickets for higher prices" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734049

action: STOP THE BOATS!
background: Labour pledged to smash the gangs and stop boat crossings yet numbers continue to rise at an alarming rate putting pressure on our services and creating civil unrest in communities. We ask government to detain/return illegal immigrants and ban those who do this from seeking future asylum in the UK.
additional_details:
SOVEREIGNTY. We ask government to invoke Article 58 of the (ECHR) as UK common law and statute provides ample protection of civil liberties yet (ECtHR) judgements impact our politics and overrule our democratic governance.

We ask government to break links between British courts and the (ECtHR). Repeal the Human Rights Act and replace it with a "British Bill of Rights". Disapply roadblock treaties against deporting illegal immigrants and make our Supreme Court the final arbiter of UK matters.

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729231
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/723147

action: Bikes to have licenses and be fined or lose points for jumping red lights.
background: Cyclists to have the same rules as motor vehicles. When purchasing a bike, a license needs to be mandatory and road rules to be followed. Points taken, fines and loss of license if caught jumping the red lights
additional_details: Cyclists around school roads are jumping the lights when red, putting adults and children crossing the green man at risk. There have been a number of near misses and they do not show any sympathy or concern.
rejection_details: Cyclists to be licenced, registered to be on the road and have insurance: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729915

action: Create a recall law to remove the Mayor of London before the end of their term
background: Introduce legislation allowing Londoners to trigger a recall petition for the Mayor, similar to the existing process for MPs. If enough voters sign, this should require a by-election so the Mayor can be held to account mid-term.
additional_details: Currently, Londoners cannot remove the Mayor before the next scheduled election, leaving the office unaccountable for four years at a time. A recall law would give voters the same democratic rights they already have with MPs, strengthen trust in local democracy, and ensure that the Mayor remains answerable to the people throughout their term.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735260

action: Stop racism in school
background: Speak out on this topic as it is effecting the students learning as the racial comments said towards that have worried the students and effecting their mental health
additional_details: I believe they should this is because students are sometimes worried to tell the teachers holding their thoughts tight to themselves eventually effecting them and possible drop in their education
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you're concerned about racism in schools, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Automatically trigger a by-election following a defection to another party.
background: Automatically trigger a by-election following a defection to another party. This is to give constituents the opportunity to either re-elect the individual standing for their defected party, or vote for the political party they previously voted, but a different candidate following the defection.
additional_details: To ensure that politicians can’t just defect from a party that is unpopular to a party that is leading in hypothetical polls, to ensure they keep their elected seat at the next election. This is unfair to those local constituents who may have voted for the political party rather than the individual. Having a politician defect to a party that lost in a recently election isn’t democratic, nor fair for their local constituents.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Lower universal credit earnings threshold (the AET) for single parents
background: Many single parents are struggling to find more hours or new jobs that work around school holidays, resulting in pressure from the job centre with weekly phone calls / meetings. It is difficult to find holiday clubs for over 5’s in many areas which adds more pressure on the parent.
additional_details:
Administrative earnings threshold (AET) has risen significantly over the last 3 years:
2023 - £617
2024 - £892
2025 - £952!
Universal Credit Administrative Earnings Threshold (AET) keeps rising and so does cost of living! The cost of living is leaving many single parents struggling to make ends meet and falling into poverty.

action: Make impersonating military service/wearing unearned medals a criminal offence
background: I want Parliament to make it a criminal offence for anyone to dishonestly claim to have served in the Armed Forces, or to wear military uniforms or medals they are not entitled to wear.
additional_details: Serving in the Armed Forces is an honour involving sacrifice and service to our country. When people falsely claim to have served or wear uniforms and medals they have not earned, they disrespect genuine veterans and mislead the public. Current laws only cover fraud for financial gain or limited cases of unauthorised uniform use. A new offence is needed to protect the integrity of service and uphold respect for veterans.
government_response_summary: There are currently no plans for the government to introduce additional criminal offences for impersonation of military service or wearing unearned medals.
government_response_body: The term ‘Stolen Valour’ is emotive and is most commonly associated with individuals wearing medals that they have not earned or been awarded. In some cases, this appears to be veterans who are enhancing their own service record, in other cases it may be individuals who have no military service at all.  On some occasions, such behaviours may be associated with an attempt to deliberately defraud others for personal gain.  Serving personnel, Armed Forces veterans, and the public, are expected to adhere to the relevant laws and internal guidance regarding the wearing of medals. However, it is not currently a specific criminal offence for veterans, or the public, to wear medals to which they are not entitled.  It is an offence for a person not serving in His Majesty’s armed forces to wear the uniform of one of those forces without permission. The Uniforms Act 1894 also prevents the wearing of any dress having the appearance, or bearing any regimental or distinctive marks, of any such uniform. This does not, however, prevent individuals wearing a uniform for the purposes of a stage play or similar performance.  The Fraud Act 2006 (and common law fraud offences in Scotland) makes it an offence for someone to fraudulently wear uniforms or medals, or to pretend to be, or have been, in the Armed Forces, if it amounts to false representation for financial gain to themselves, or to disadvantage another person. This offence carries a sentence of up to 10 years’ imprisonment.  Where it is suspected that an individual maybe wearing a medal, or uniform, to which they are not entitled, in an attempt to defraud others, it is a matter for investigation by either the civil police, or the service police if the individual is subject to service law. In such cases, the MOD may be asked to provide information relating to an individual’s service record.   Since 2009, it has not been a specific service law offence for an individual to wear medals or decorations that they were never awarded. This change in the law was a result of the enactment of the Armed Forces Act 2006, which repealed section 197 of the Army Act 1955 and section 197 of the Air Force Act 1955, in which the offence was specified.   The MOD’s official position is that only those who were awarded medals are entitled to wear them. This applies to Service Persons under Joint Service Publication (JSP) 761, at para 12.25, but it does not extend to members of the public as it is an internal policy only.   Ministry of Defence

government_response_summary: In line with independent advice from the UK National Screening Committee, the Government does not intend to lower the age or increase the frequency of breast screens.
government_response_body: The Government is guided by the independent scientific advice of the UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC), and it is only where the offer to screen provides more good than harm that a screening programme is recommended. The UK NSC makes its recommendations based on internationally recognised criteria and a rigorous evidence review and consultation process.  As screening programmes can also cause harms, each of the adult screening programmes has both an upper and lower age range, within which there is good scientific evidence that the benefits of screening outweigh the harms.  Women younger than the age of 50 are not routinely screened for breast cancer due to the lower risk of women under this age developing breast cancer, and the fact that women below 50 tend to have denser breasts. The denseness of breast tissue reduces the ability of getting an accurate mammogram, the accepted screening test for breast cancer.  Due to this and other factors, there is a risk of over treatment and distress for women who do not have breast cancer but would be subjected to invasive and painful medical treatments and diagnostic tests.  The 2012 UK independent review of breast cancer screening (the Marmot review) estimated that inviting women aged 50-70 reduces mortality from breast cancer in the population invited by 20% and saves an estimated 1,300 lives a year. The Marmot review found that screening women outside the ages of 50-70 could lead to over-diagnosis (referring women for unnecessary tests) and over-treatment (operating on women with disease which is unlikely to cause serious harm to them).  We are in line with most European countries, most of whom screen women between the ages of 50-69.  Women with a very high risk of breast cancer (for example, due to family history) may be offered screening earlier and more frequently, sometimes using MRI rather than a mammogram.  The UK NSC keeps these age brackets under review. The Committee recognises that screening programmes are not static and that, over time, they may need to change to be more effective.  The UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC) reviewed the evidence relating to the provision of additional breast screening for women who have dense breast tissue in the summer of 2025 and invited stakeholders’ feedback on the findings to inform future work. In addition, the AgeX – age extension – breast screening research trial has been looking at the effectiveness of offering some women an extra screen between the ages of 47 and 49, and between the ages of 71 and 73. When the results are available, the report will be reviewed by the UK NSC.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: No to Digital IDs

We are already seeing alarming government overreach, with arrests for online posts and thousands of “non-crime” incidents recorded. Britain must not slide into a surveillance state. action: Recognise circus and fairgrounds in the UK inventory of ICH
background: The DCMS is drawing up an inventory of intangible cultural heritage (ICH) items following the signing of the UNESCO treaty on 'ICH'. We want circus and fairgrounds to be recognised on that inventory.
additional_details: Historic fairs and traditional circuses form an important part of the UK's cultural fabric and represent a way of life for travelling show people. This culture is not one of the 'protected characteristics' associated with visible ethnic minority or faith groups. Show people represent a diverse group but have in common the need to travel to present their entertainment offering. We feel only government recognition via the ICH inventory can provide the assurance for this way of life to continue.
government_response_summary: We welcome a submission on circus and fairgrounds to the inventories of living heritage, which will be included if it meets the published criteria.
government_response_body: As part of the implementation of the UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, the UK Government is working closely with the Devolved Governments to create inventories for each of the four nations in the UK; these will combine into one inventory of Living Heritage (or Intangible Cultural Heritage) in the UK.   Following a public consultation (www.gov.uk/government/consultations/2003-unesco-convention-for-the-safeguarding-of-the-intangible-cultural-heritage) on the inventory process, we have opened a call for submissions for communities to submit items of living heritage here: https://livingheritage.unesco.org.uk/.  The government would welcome a submission from the circus and fairground community on their living heritage. Subject to the submission meeting the criteria outlined in the consultation response, the item would be included.  Inclusion in the inventories of an item would provide recognition of the item's significance, contributing in part to the safeguarding of the item through greater awareness and understanding. The government will set out its approach to further supporting communities to safeguard their living heritage later this year.  Department for Culture, Media and Sport

action: Fund a new way to support young people with SEND in schools.
background: Update national policy and provide funding so schools and local authorities can offer hybrid learning (blended mainstream + therapeutic/vocational/community outreach) as a first-line alternative to full-time mainstream or exclusion/PRU, with clear safeguards and accountability.
additional_details: We are asking government to take three steps. First, introduce statutory recognition of Hybrid Education Packages within education and SEND frameworks, allowing schools and local authorities to commission blended provision lawfully and confidently. Second, create a ring-fenced funding stream for hybrid packages, pooled across education, health, and justice budgets, with outcomes measured in attendance, attainment, wellbeing, and reduced police contact. Third, establish a pre-exclusion duty requiring schools to evidence consideration of a hybrid option before a child is permanently excluded.

action: Set national planning rules to ban incinerators near facilities for children
background: We are calling on the Government to introduce national planning safeguards that prevent waste and clinical waste incinerators being built within a specific distance from schools, nurseries, and playgrounds.
additional_details: We believe children are the most vulnerable members of our society, and that their lungs, hearts, and immune systems are still developing, which makes them particularly sensitive to environmental pollution. There are currently no specific national planning safeguards that prevent hazardous or clinical waste incinerators from being sited next to schools, nurseries, or playgrounds. This is a gap in policy that urgently needs to be addressed.

action: Create a simple, fair route to citizenship for ILR holders.
background: People with Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) already live, work, and contribute in the UK permanently. But citizenship is costly, complex, and uncertain. This petition asks the Government to create a simple, fair route to citizenship for ILR holders — so families and communities can feel secure.
additional_details:
Why does this matter?
Because ILR holders already have permanent status: they work, pay taxes, and raise families here. Citizenship lets them belong fully and feel secure. ILR can be changed by governments. Citizenship is permanent and provides full rights and protections. Nurses, carers, teachers, families, all who hold ILR and already contribute to our society. It doesn't weaken border control, only affects people who already hold ILR, which requires years of lawful residence and contribution.
rejection_details:
It's already possible for people with Indefinite Leave to remain to apply for British Citizenship. We understand that you're concerned about the process to become a British Citizen, but we're not sure what changes to the process you'd like to see.

You could start a new petition explaining exactly what change you'd like to see.

action: Allow legal professionals to conduct litigation without being solicitors
background: Amend the Legal Services Act 2007 to recognise experienced legal professionals (e.g., paralegals or fee earners with 10+ years' experience) as eligible to conduct litigation without requiring full solicitor authorisation.
additional_details:
We ask the Government to create a pathway under the Legal Services Act 2007 that allows experienced legal professionals, such as paralegals and non-solicitor fee earners to obtain litigation rights. This would apply where individuals can demonstrate substantial, relevant experience, good character  and competence.
This could be achieved either by:
*Alternative authorisation routes for non-solicitors via the SRA or another regulator or;
*Expand the definition of “authorised person” under the Act.

action: Reduce summer break to 5 weeks and allow flexible school holidays
background: Reduce the summer holiday from 6 to 5 weeks and allow schools to use the extra week flexibly during the academic year, outside exam periods and excluding Years 10 and 11 to allow full exam prep.
additional_details: The six-week summer holiday is difficult for working parents to manage and costly for families. It can also make returning to school harder, especially for children with neurodiversities. A five-week summer break with a flexible week would ease childcare pressures, allow families to holiday outside peak times, and support smoother transitions for children back into school.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about term dates are a matter for academy trusts, local authorities or governing bodies.

action: Introduce a new word. "Waywordwithly"
background: Accept a new word into the English dialect and dictionary. the word would be "Waywordwithly" Definition: adjective: to be eloquent or to have a way with words.
additional_details:
This word does not exist and there have been multiple occasions where I needed precisely this word and I see no harm in and no reason why we shouldn't broaden our great dialect.

Thank you for taking the time to read my proposition.
Best Regards 
Will
rejection_details:
This is not the responsibility of the UK Government or Parliament. 

You may wish to contact the Oxford English Dictionary: https://www.oed.com/information/using-the-oed/contributing-to-the-oed

action: Suspend parliament and Call an immediate general election
background: Suspend parliament and call an immediate general election

rejection_details:

Call an immediate general election

action: We call on UK Government to provide sex crime victims with free legal support
background: We call on the UK Government to set out in statue that sex crime victims are a vulnerable group from first police contact, and grant them a legal representative at the taxpayer expense.
additional_details:
We believe this can help protect their legal and human rights in disclosure, any judicial process or damages retrieval post conviction.
Legal aid is afforded to the accused from the point of arrest, and we believe that giving the victims the same privilege will protect then during the judicial process, from any potential bias, gaslighting or other forms of anti victim prejudice and discrimination, and produce better prepared, more confident witnesses. Who feel safer whilst navigating the scary footpath to justice.

action: Inform patients if vaccine was developed from aborted human foetus cell lines
background: Call on the UK Government to ensure that information leaflets relating to vaccines state whether they were developed using cell lines originating from aborted human fetuses so that patients can make an informed decision, based on their conscience, whether or not to accept these vaccines.
additional_details:
The UK Government's policies relating to vaccination should comply with the European Convention on Human Rights. This includes the principle of making free and informed decisions whether to accept certain vaccines expressed in:

- The right to respect for privacy and family life (Article 8) ,

- The right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion (Article 9),

- The right to freedom of expression, which includes the right to hold opinions and to receive information (Article 10).

action: Hold a vote of no confidence in the current Government
background: We want MPs in the House of Commons to hold a vote of no confidence in the current Government. If the Government loses the vote, this should lead to a general election so the public can decide who governs.
additional_details: We believe the Government has failed to deliver on its promises and is not acting in the best interests of the country. A vote of no confidence would allow Parliament to decide whether the Government still has its support. If not, the people should be given the chance to choose a new Government.
rejection_details:
Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

Give the British Public the Right to Vote No Confidence in the Government

action: Withdraw the rollout of MTD ITSA planned for April 2026
background: We call on the Government to cancel the rollout of Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD ITSA) in April 2026. This policy will impose costly software, extra reporting, and harsh penalties on 4.2 million sole traders and landlords, damaging small business and the wider economy.
additional_details: MTD ITSA will hit 4.2 million sole traders and landlords with extra costs, red tape and penalties. Instead of one annual return, they must submit five, using software they are forced to buy. Many face errors, fines or closure. Sole traders are the backbone of the UK economy, creating jobs and vital services. At a time of high costs and weak growth, this policy risks driving thousands out of business, reducing tax revenues and damaging communities.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop HMRC implementing making tax digital and enforcing quarterly submissions: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729235

action: Let kids go to the toilet during lessons
background: Make teachers let kids go to the toilet during lessons, this is because if a kid needs the toilet and it’s an emergency they need to be allowed to go!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require schools to let children use the toilet at all times in the school day

action: Stop Slough Council’s Overspending: Residents Deserve Transparency Now
background: Appoint an independent financial overseer for Slough Council, require quarterly public audits, halt new charges or service cuts for residents, and investigate all council spending and recruitment practices to guarantee accountability and transparency for taxpayers.
additional_details: Slough Borough Council has a history of financial mismanagement, previously declaring bankruptcy and now facing an overspend of over £20 million this year despite government bailouts. Services have been cut and new charges added, but residents have no real say. We want the Government to enforce external audits, halt fresh charges, and appoint an independent overseer to restore trust and ensure all council spending is in the public interest. Residents deserve full transparency and accountability.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue.

action: Ban fines for free flow toll roads until after reminders are sent
background: Stop unfair fines when drivers simply forget to pay tolls. Require toll enforcement to only charge the toll itself. Fines should only apply if reminders are ignored. Drivers shouldn’t face £25–£50 penalties for a £2 crossing just because they forgot.
additional_details: Drivers are being fined £25–£50 for tolls costing just £2–£2.40, often because they forgot to pay online after using free-flow bridges. At the Mersey Gateway, around 20% of all money collected comes from fines, and at Dartford it’s around 40%. We think the system relies on forgetfulness to generate income. It’s right that people pay the toll, but honest mistakes shouldn’t be turned into excessive fines.

action: Replace Public Sector Pension schemes with a defined contribution scheme 4%/6%
background: Set up a defined contribution (DC) scheme for all public sector staff along the same lines as most private sector schemes (usually 4% staff & 6% employer contributions - staff can contribute more).
additional_details:
All new staff to join the scheme. Current staff transferred with enhanced terms (ie higher employer contributions) to compensate.
Public sector (PuS) pension costs are huge. The private sector (PrS) dealt with this a long time ago, which is why the vast majority of PrS schemes are now DC, not defined benefit (DB).
The Government recently attacked the PrS pension savers by pulling their pension pots into their estates. We think this is unfair when the PuS arrangements, which are vastly more beneficial to the Eee, remain untouched.
This strategy COULD help fill the "black hole" that has been talked about.

action: Require online platforms to remove misinformation targeting bereaved families
background: Introduce Jay’s Law: specific legislation obliging platforms to remove organised misinformation that targets grieving families after tragic deaths; require platforms to act on speculative, malicious content likely to cause serious harm; and work with Ofcom on enforcement and sanctions.
additional_details: Families who have suffered tragic deaths are being subjected to organised misinformation and malicious speculation online. This targets grieving families at their most vulnerable, causing severe additional trauma, distress, and emotional pain. Jay’s Law would place clear legal duties on platforms, backed by Ofcom enforcement and sanctions, to ensure all speculative, organised, and malicious content is swiftly removed, protecting grieving families’ privacy, dignity, and safety.

action: Lower the state pension age to 65 years old
background: Lower the state pension age to 65.
additional_details: We believe many people who work a lifetime and contribute to society all their lives need to retire earlier if they wish to enjoy their remaining years with a good quality of life at 65 years old. Many people don’t live to enjoy their retirement later in life, due to ill health and death.

action: Require providers to offer a dual fuel social tariff for disabled/low earners
background: Require all energy providers to offer a dual fuel social tariff for disabled or low income / benefits claimants.
additional_details: We feel the cost of energy in the UK is too high and that the cost of food / petrol / council rates have all increased. To heat our homes & keep warm should be more accesible to low earners and is enforceable by the energy regulator as a tariff for energy providers in the UK. We think an affordable social tariff needs implementing now

action: Make a law to protect ILR from abolition and retrospective changes
background: We want the Parliament to introduce primary legislation that guarantees Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) as a permanent route to settlement. ILR must not be abolished, withdrawn from holders, or replaced with visas. Any changes to ILR should apply only to new entrants from the date of implementation
additional_details:
ILR allows one to settle permanently in the UK, fostering integration into British society. Now this status is not protected by law: changes to it can be made by the Home Secretary at their discretion. The Act of Parliament should state that:
• ILR is a permanent immigration status
• ILR can't be revoked or converted into a time-limited visa
• Any future changes to ILR rules (including eligibility rules) must be for new applicants only, not retrospectively to those already on a settlement path

action: Ban aspartame in our food and drinks
background: I call on the government to ban the additive aspartame/E951 in food and beverages. I think that the precautionary principle should be key to safeguard public health.
additional_details: Whether it's soft drinks, desserts, chewing gum, or yoghurts; the use of the additive aspartame is common. The WHO's International Agency for Research on Cancer has classified this widely used sweetener as possibly cancer-causing, under some circumstances. Some research has also raised concerns about its long-term impact on weight control.

action: Lower the amount of years children spend in education
background: We want the amount of years children have to stay in a form of education in the UK to be lowered.
additional_details: This is because children should be able to learn work earlier insead of "work experience" which is within the school week. We want children to be legally allowed to pursue their dreams earlier.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you would like the amount of years children are required to spend in school to be lowered, but we're not sure by how much.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Implement an easily accessible public register of convicted domestic abusers.
background: Create a national public register of convicted domestic abusers, building on Clare’s Law. This register should be easy to access, updated in real time, and designed to help protect survivors, children, and communities.
additional_details: We believe survivors of domestic abuse in the UK are being left at risk. Police funding cuts, overcrowded prisons, and weak monitoring can mean too many abusers are released without proper oversight. We feel that measures like Clare’s Law and electronic tagging are steps in the right direction, but they don’t go far enough. We need a national public register of convicted domestic abusers to shine a light on repeat offenders, protect communities, and prevent future abuse.

action: Require that photo ID and fingerprints are taken prior to the purchase of knives
background: I feel the law needs to be changed regarding the purchase of knives. I believe that when purchasing a knife, photo ID should be held on record and finger prints taken, to reduce the lives lost to knife crime.

action: Prohibit sale of helium except for essential medical and scientific use.
background: Legislate so helium can only be sold for essential purposes such as MRI scanners and scientific research. Prohibit wasteful non-essential uses such as party balloons to safeguard this finite gas for healthcare and critical science.
additional_details: Helium is vital for MRI scanners that diagnose cancer, brain and heart disease. It is also essential in semiconductor and computer chip production — technologies society now depends on. Once wasted in balloons, helium is lost forever and cannot be replaced

action: Fund awareness campaigns on rape & sexual assault law for adults over 30
background: Fund national awareness campaigns to educate adults over 30 about rape, consent and sexual assault law so survivors can recognise crimes and seek support.
additional_details: We believe many adults over 35 grew up without education on consent or sexual assault law. Key legal changes may have come after they left school. Survivors often cannot report crimes they don’t recognise. The Government should fund national awareness campaigns to educate adults, so they understand consent, the law, and how to access support.

action: Hold General Elections every four years
background: Introduce a change to the law so that the maximum period between General Elections is reduced from five years to four years.
additional_details:
We think too much government decision making is done without clearly taking adequate representation into account. The current long gap between elections amplifies the problem.
 
Governments could be reenergised and gain better legitimacy by gaining a mandate from the people more frequently.
 
It could enable us to get rid of governments we think are bad quicker.

action: Ban Homework and reduce school hours.
background: The Government and Parliament must reduce school hours from 8:30 - 3:30 (on average) to 9:30 - 3:30 to help children get better sleep and to ban teachers or anyone to assign homework or to be set any task. Please make sure this can be sorted out by the end of the end 2025-26 academic year.
additional_details: Children and teenagers are suffering from anxiety, depression and also stress. This can lead to students facing a lot of pressure if they want to receive a good life. Homework is also not good for teachers as they will also have to spend time marking each homework and potentially grade them as well. This will help both children and teachers from exhaust.

action: Change the UK flag to quartered arms of Wessex, Mercia, Wales and Scotland.
background: We propose changing the UK flag to represent the ancient domains of our island - Wessex (Gold Dragon), Mercia (Symbolised by the Uffington white horse on a green field), Wales (Red dragon), Scotland (Red lion), quartered in heraldic fashion. We'll give Northern Ireland back to the Republic.
additional_details: We will do this to counter vandalism and nationally embarrassing racism, and because it will look sick. Our new flag will be much harder to paint on a roundabout, or on the face of someone trying to fight a hotel. We can and should be proud of our ancient past, and we should be mature enough to embrace the nuances of our history and acknowledge both the credit and debit in our heritage. Our new flag will be a symbol of this historical literacy and our ongoing commitment to national progress.
rejection_details: The future of Northern Ireland is a matter for the people of Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland, not solely the UK Government or Parliament. action: Government to use ‘Southwest Asia and North Africa' (SWANA) not Middle East
background: Government should stop using ‘Middle East’ in all its official business and communications. It is colonial, because it is 'Middle East' relative to Britain. We believe that Southwest Asia and North Africa (SWANA) is decolonial, inclusive and a geographically accurate way of identifying the region.
additional_details: The Government should lead in decolonising language it uses because if it changes, others may change by example. Language matters, because it influences how we think and conceptualise the world. With such turmoil in SWANA at present, it is more important than ever that language used is free from the colonial baggage of the past. Making this change could also demonstrate to everyone that the government and parliament acknowledge and distance themselves from the colonial mindsets of the past.

action: Reverse the decision of officially recognising a Palestinian State
background: The United Kingdom should not recognise a Palestinian State. We should not be communicating with Terrorist organisations and the embassy needs to be closed immediately. Cooperation with Palestine is traitorous to our Jewish population in the United Kingdom.
additional_details: The recognition of a Palestinian state rewards a terrorist organisation after the horrors of October 7th 2023. It is also fundamentally against international law with no formal border and no official governance. The state is currently under a Terrorist regime that is still holding many innocent hostages. This costly recognition for the taxpayer goes against the will of the British public and will have no impact on a ceasefire or peace solution.

action: The UK should reverse the decision to surrender the Chagos Islands to Mauritius
background: The United Kingdom should reverse the decision to surrender sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. This decision imposes a huge unnecessary cost to the British Taxpayer over 100 years and includes a strategic military base that we now have to lease.
additional_details: This advisory ruling from the International Court of Justice is not legally binding and will cost taxpayers £35 billion paid Mauritius, a close Chinese ally and despite Mauritius never having a claim to the island historically. The remote yet very strategic base of Diego Garcia is now unnecessarily leased for the next 99 years and faces falling into the hands of China. The people of Chagos had no consultation in this decision and this has the potential to set a precedent unless a U-Turn is made.

Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in UK men, with 52,000 diagnoses and 12,000 deaths each year. 

Currently there is no national screening programme, and access to PSA testing and MRI varies by region. Mandatory testing would end this postcode lottery, ensure equal access, and save lives through earlier detection and treatment. 

Any fears or concerns surrounding the accuracy of the current PSA test can be allayed by current trials underway for a more accurate one in due course.

We urge the Department for Education to act:
Make National Kindness Day a fixture in every school’s calendar. Embed kindness, empathy, and inclusion into PSHE and RSE curriculum guidance. Equip schools with the resources and training they need to deliver kindness-based education

background: The union flag is a flag designed to incorporate and represent all of the United Kingdom. background: We want the government to introduce mandatory registration and licensing alongside other regulations to align the system with what is in place for mopeds.

background: As the country seems to be getting very mixed feelings about the illegal asylum seekers we should have a referendum where the British voters can vote if they want or do not want their taxes being spent on the illegals,
additional_details:
Those who vote to opt out should pay less tax, those that want to help pay more taxes with a clause that if the offer to house these refugees their taxes would not be affected,
Thus freeing up the hotels cost,
As a democratic country surely the public should decide where their taxes are spent rather than having it forced on them to pay for something they do not want to,

UK citizens took part in experiments without appropriate protective clothing or proper consent, and we believe they have suffered debilitating illnesses and passed on congenital conditions to their children and grandchildren. In many cases they have only received a medal in recognition.

action: Cut VAT for local hospitality – for Pubs, Cafes & Restaurants
background: Across the UK, our cafes, pubs and restaurants are more than just businesses. They are the beating heart of our communities, the places where we celebrate milestones, share a quiet pint or coffee with a friend and create lifelong memories. And they're struggling to stay afloat.
additional_details:
We simply can't afford to lose another one of our favourite local spots.
 
Cutting VAT for hospitality could provide a desperately needed lifeline.
 
With the Autumn Budget approaching, we call on the Government to act now. Support the sector that brings our towns and villages to life and give our local hospitality a fighting chance.
government_response_summary: The Government recognises the importance of the hospitality sector across the UK. The Chancellor makes decisions on tax policy at fiscal events in the context of the public finances.
government_response_body: The Government recognises the significant contribution made by hospitality businesses to economic growth and social life in the UK. Pubs, cafes, and restaurants are at the heart of so many communities, and this Government wants to back them.  Since taking office the Government has taken a number of decisions on tax, welfare, and spending to fix the public finances, fund public services, and restore economic stability. This stability is critical to boosting investment and growth, and to making people across the UK better off.  Over 750,000 retail, hospitality and leisure properties will benefit from permanently lower business rates multipliers from April. This support is worth almost £1 billion per year.  At Budget, the Government announced a business rates support package worth £4.3 billion to protect against ratepayers seeing large overnight increases in bills. This means most properties seeing increases will see them capped at 15% or less next year, or £800 for the smallest.  In January 2026, the Government also announced that, from April, every pub and live music venue will get 15% off its new business rates bill on top of the support announced at Budget, ahead of their bills being frozen in real terms for a further two years. The new relief is worth £1,650 for the average pub next year and means that three-quarters of pubs will see bills flat or falling next year.   To consider the regulatory burden of alcohol licensing on hospitality venues, the Government has worked with the hospitality sector to announce the first National Licensing Policy Framework which sets a new strategic direction for licensing authorities and encourages them to have more regard to growth when reviewing licensing applications and decisions. Building on this, we are working with the sector to ensure local authorities are using it to ease licensing decisions ‘on the ground'. In another show of our commitment to the sector, we are pressing ahead with further licensing reform. All pubs and hospitality venues will be allowed to extend opening hours for Home Nation games in the later stages of the Men’s Football World Cup this summer. We will also legislate to increase the number of Temporary Events pubs and other hospitality venues can hold, whether that is to help them screen other national moments, or host community and cultural events. The Government will also explore further loosening of the planning rules to benefit pubs, helping them add new guest rooms or expand their main room without local the need for planning applications. We will continue to engage with the sector to ensure other retail, leisure and hospitality premises also have sufficient planning flexibilities.  Furthermore, the Government is more than doubling the Hospitality Support Fund, with £10m of further funding over three years. This fund will aim to help over 1000 pubs to diversify their business models, improve efficiency and productivity in the sector; and support people who are furthest from the labour market to move into jobs in hospitality. To support this, we are also bringing forward a new High Streets Strategy, to reinvigorate our communities. We will work with businesses and representative bodies to pull this Strategy together. It will be a cross-government strategy, and we will be look at what more government can do to support our high streets.  Turning to the ask to cut VAT for hospitality, the 20 per cent standard rate applies to most goods and services. Exceptions to the standard rate have always been limited and balanced against affordability considerations. VAT is the UK’s third largest tax, forecast to raise £180 billion in 2025/26, which pays for our public services. Tax breaks reduce the revenue available for those public services.  A reduced rate of VAT for pubs, cafes and restaurants would come at significant cost. The VAT relief for tourism and hospitality during the Covid-19 pandemic cost over £8 billion, and was introduced given the exceptional circumstances for the sector.    The Government makes decisions on tax at fiscal events in the context of the overall public finances.   HM treasury

action: Trigeminal Neuralgia diagnosis to qualify as a life impacting disability
background: Trigeminal Neuralgia is a life-debilitating condition causing unbearable pain, often referred to as the “suicide disease” due to the untreatable pain. We urge the UK government to recognise TN as a disability, so sufferers can access the support, protections, and resources they urgently need.
additional_details: Trigeminal Neuralgia is a severe, life-limiting condition leaving many sufferers housebound and unable to perform even simple tasks. We urge the UK government to recognise TN as a disability, provide access to pain relief, increase funding for research into a cure, and ensure patients receive the support and assistance they desperately need.
rejection_details:
We understand you are concerned about support for people with trigeminal neuralgia, but we're not sure what action you'd like the UK Government or Parliament to take.

Under the Equality Act 2010, someone is disabled if they have a physical or mental impairment that has a ‘substantial’ and ‘long-term’ negative effect on their ability to do normal daily activities. This could include people with  a Trigeminal Neuralgia diaganosis: https://www.gov.uk/definition-of-disability-under-equality-act-2010

Treatment for trigeminal neuralgia, including access to pain relief, is available on the NHS: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/trigeminal-neuralgia/treatment/

action: Fund free dental care for head & neck cancer patients
background: We want the Government to fund free dental care for head and neck cancer patients both during and after treatment to address the significant oral health challenges that survivors may face, and to improve their overall quality of life.
additional_details: Head and neck cancer treatments, such as surgery, radiation and chemotherapy, can result in long-term oral health issues, including dry mouth, tooth decay and infections. These conditions can severely affect survivors' quality of life, their self-esteem and ability to eat, speak. Providing free dental care could ensure patients have access to essential treatments, improve their health outcomes, and reduce the financial burden, similar to other cancer types already covered by healthcare services.
government_response_summary: We understand the importance of oral care for cancer patients. There are no current plans to extend free care to cancer patients, although those struggling with NHS dental costs can apply for help.
government_response_body: The Government recognises that patients with cancer, especially those with diagnoses of head or neck cancer, may be more vulnerable to oral health problems during and following their treatment. We are working across the system to ensure that patients who have a diagnosis of cancer receive timely, safe, and effective dental care.  Integrated care boards (ICBs) are responsible for commissioning primary care services, including NHS dentistry, to meet the needs of local populations and to determine the priorities for investment. NHS England has published guidance for ICBs to help ensure patients with a diagnosis of cancer can access oral healthcare in a timely manner. This guidance is available at the following link: https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/oral-healthcare-provision-for-cancer-pathways/. The guidance outlines an “oral health in cancer pathway” for patients with a diagnosis of head and neck cancer, patients awaiting chemotherapy or immunotherapy for any cancer type, and patients that will undergo bone marrow transplantation. This pathway could include oral health assessments, prevention, rehabilitation, and reconstruction in primary (NHS or independent), community, secondary, or tertiary care settings. This would be provided as part of a multi-disciplinary team care plan. Ongoing oral health management for the duration of the cancer therapy would take place.  Whilst there are currently no plans to extend free dental care to those with a diagnosis of head or neck cancer, for those who are struggling with NHS dental charges, there is a range of help available. This includes full exemptions from dental charges and, for those not eligible for exemption, support through the NHS Low Income Scheme.  Exemptions are currently available for those who meet the following criteria: •	people aged under 18, or under 19 and in full-time education •	people who are pregnant or have had a baby in the last 12 months •	people who have had a stillbirth in the past 12 months •	people receiving treatment in an NHS hospital from a hospital dentist (although these patients may still need to pay for dentures or bridges) •	people receiving War Pension Scheme payments, or Armed Forces Compensation Scheme payments, and for whom the treatment is for their accepted disability •	people in receipt of certain benefits  For those who are not eligible for a full exemption, either full or partial support with the costs of NHS dental treatment is available through the NHS Low Income Scheme, information about which is available at the following link: https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/nhs-low-income-scheme.  Further information on the help available can be found at the following link: https://www.nhs.uk/nhs-services/dentists/get-help-with-dental-costs/.  In addition, in the 10 Year Health Plan, the Government committed to providing more readily accessible, good quality care to those most in need. In line with this, we are working to transform NHS dentistry so it provides high quality care at the right time, and so nobody goes without because they cannot afford it.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Call a public inquiry into Russian influence on UK politics & democracy
background: We are concerned about reported efforts from Russia to influence democracy in the US, UK, Europe and elsewhere. We believe we must establish the depth and breadth of possible Russian influence campaigns in the UK.
additional_details: We believe recent events underscore the urgency of this issue.
government_response_summary: Russian interference threats to the UK will be examined as part of the Independent Review of Foreign Financial Interference. Review findings will be presented to the House for scrutiny in late March.
government_response_body: The Government shares the public's concern regarding the threat from Russian interference to UK democracy. The Government will not tolerate attempts to interfere in our politics from any foreign actor and we will take all measures necessary to defend our democracy.  The UK Government has already announced an independent review, in light of the deeply concerning evidence of Russia’s attempt to influence democracy in the UK. In December 2025, the Government commissioned Philip Rycroft to lead the independent review of foreign financial interference in UK politics, including efforts by Russia. The review will thoroughly assess current financial rules and safeguards, and provide recommendations to mitigate future interference risks. This will include an examination of recent cases of attempted interference in UK politics by a range of foreign actors, including events surrounding the conviction of Reform UK’s former Wales leader, Nathan Gill, for accepting bribes to promote pro-Russian views.   Review conclusions will directly inform the major reforms to protect our elections from foreign interference, which will be set out in a forthcoming elections and democracy bill, and support the Government’s Counter Political Interference and Espionage Action Plan, which aims to make UK politics a harder target for foreign threat actors.  Launching a new, parallel inquiry at this time would be premature as it would risk prejudging the conclusions of the ongoing review and duplicating its efforts. However, the Government will present the findings of the report by the end of March providing an opportunity for further scrutiny and debate.  Cabinet Office
