action: Make it an offence to carry a catapult in public without lawful defence
background: Change the law so catapult possession in public is an offence. Currently, police must prove intent or use to cause harm. We propose it becomes an absolute offence, like air rifles, without lawful defence. Rising attacks on people, animals, and wildlife show stronger powers are needed.
additional_details: Catapults are increasingly linked to assaults, criminal damage, and rising wildlife attacks. Making public possession an absolute offence like air rifles with age checks, and a licensing scheme for legitimate uses like angling, would give police stronger powers.
government_response_summary: There are laws that can already be used against individuals who use catapults as a weapon, but the Government understands the concerns and is actively looking at this issue.
government_response_body: The Government shares the concerns raised by the petitioners over the misuse of catapults, whether against people, property or wildlife.  There are a wide range of laws in place to punish those who misuse catapults. For example, under the Prevention of Crime Act 1953, if a person carries an offensive weapon in a public place or threatens a person with an offensive weapon, they may face up to 4 years in prison. An offensive weapon is defined as any article made or adapted for use for causing injury to the person or intended by the person having it with him for such use by him or by another person. The definition may include a catapult depending on the circumstances and facts of the case.   Where a catapult is used to harm a person, under the Offences against the Person Act 1861, it could be charged as assault occasioning actual bodily harm which carries a maximum penalty of 5 years’ imprisonment, However, depending on the gravity of the attack and the seriousness of the injury caused by the catapult, the offence of wounding or causing grievous bodily harm with intent could be committed, which carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment.   Under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 and the Wild Mammals (Protection) Act 1996, the police have powers to deal with offences concerning deliberate attempts to kill, injure or inflict harm on wildlife, and this would include cases where catapults have been used. It is also an offence under the Animal Welfare Act 2006 to cause an animal any unnecessary suffering. The Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021 increases the sentences available to our courts for the most serious cases of animal cruelty to, for example, pets and livestock by increasing the maximum penalty for this offence to 5 years’ imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine.  The Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 also provides the police, local authorities and other local agencies with a range of tools and powers that they can use to respond to anti-social behaviour including that involving catapults. This includes Community Protection Warnings and Notices (CPWs and CPNs), and Public Spaces Protection Orders (PSPOs) which can be used to prevent behaviour that is having, or likely to have, a detrimental effect on the quality of life of those in the locality. Through the Crime and Policing Bill we will also ensure that the police, local authorities, and other agencies have the tools and powers they need to deal with persistent anti-social behaviour and crime that is plaguing our communities. This includes increasing the maximum penalty for breach of a CPN or PSPO from £100 to £500, and the introduction of Respect Orders. Respect Orders will enable courts to ban adult offenders from engaging in harmful anti-social behaviours. This could, for example, see offenders banned from entering certain public places, where they have been behaving anti-socially.    This Government is focussed on putting neighbourhood policing at the heart of plans to reform policing, to both enforce existing laws and those that this Government is bringing forward. The Government has committed to delivering an additional 13,000 police officers, PCSOs and special constables in neighbourhood policing roles by the end of this Parliament and made £200 million available this year to support the first steps towards delivering this significant boost to neighbourhood policing.    The Home Office is providing funding this financial year for the National Rural Crime Unit as well as continuing its funding for the National Wildlife Crime Unit. This will help the units tackle those crimes that predominantly affect our rural communities.  There are a range of offences and powers that can therefore be used to prevent the misuse of catapults, but the Government is aware of continuing concerns about the problems caused by catapults. We are actively considering what more might be done, especially around enforcement.   We do not intend to accept the petitioners’ proposal at this time. However, public safety is a Government priority, and in view of the continuing concerns, we are actively looking at what more can be done to address the misuse of catapults.  Home Office

additional_details: Child Benefit is claimed and used by families/households, however, the HICBC is assessed on an individual income of £60K or more within any given household. That means a two-parent household could earn up to £120K (up to £60K each) before being eligible for the charge, however, a two-parent or single parent household that relies on the income of one parent earning anything over £60K is obligated to pay the HICBC. We think this is unfair and negates the value of claiming child benefit.

This means that consumers may be motivated to return containers for recycling as they could receive a reward for it. Therefore, more people may be willing to recycle. We ask the Government to work with IBMS, HCPC, and universities to ensure all biomedical science degrees include integrated registration portfolio training, so that graduates can enter the NHS directly. We believe this would create fairness across healthcare professions and remove unnecessary barriers for biomedical scientists, helping to address the shortage in pathology and diagnostics.

~Reduced stress – exams can put extreme pressure on students’ mental health.
~Fairer grading – continuous assessment may show true ability, not just exams.

Many places label food as “gluten-free” but cross-contamination makes it unsafe for those with coeliac disease, for example due to shared fryers and equipment.

action: Restore the Electoral Commission's Independence
background: We want ministers stripped of any powers related to the Electoral Commission’s budget and strategy. Parliament must restore the independence the Commission had pre-2022, and guarantee it can operate free from any political influence.
additional_details: The Electoral Commission exists to safeguard trust in elections. In 2022, the previous government introduced measures to allow ministers to direct the Commission. The current Government have not changed this. We view this as a betrayal, and feel it shows both main parties protecting their own interests. We think a greater degree of independence should be restored if the public are to have confidence that elections remain free and fair.
government_response_summary: The Government is taking decisive action to strengthen and protect the UK’s democracy and will continue to support the operational independence of the Electoral Commission.
government_response_body: The Electoral Commission is the independent statutory body which oversees electoral administration and regulates political finance. It is accountable to – and funded by – the UK Parliament via the Speaker’s Committee on the Electoral Commission.  The Strategy and Policy Statement for the Electoral Commission sets out the Government’s priorities for electoral policy and the role and responsibilities of the Commission in enabling the Government to meet those priorities. The Electoral Commission are required to have regard to the Statement. The existing Statement (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/electoral-commission-strategy-and-policy-statement/electoral-commission-strategy-and-policy-statement) was designated by the previous Government on 29 February 2024.  This Government is taking decisive action to strengthen and protect the UK’s democracy. Robust and proportionate enforcement of political finance rules is an essential part of this. That is why, as announced on 17 July in the Government’s Strategy for Elections (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/restoring-trust-in-our-democracy-our-strategy-for-modern-and-secure-elections/restoring-trust-in-our-democracy-our-strategy-for-modern-and-secure-elections), we are committed to strengthening the Electoral Commission’s powers and extending its remit to ensure that it can effectively enforce the political finance framework.  Given these changes, the Strategy for Elections also set out the intention to designate a new Strategy and Policy Statement for the Electoral Commission that reflects this Government’s priorities for elections and the Commission’s increased roles and responsibilities.  In doing so, we are clear that the Electoral Commission will remain operationally independent, and we will continue to support it to act without fear or favour in upholding political finance rules and stamping out foreign interference. Electoral Commissioners and the Commission’s executive leadership remain responsible for determining how the Commission should discharge its duties, including its strategic priorities and day-to-day operations.  Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

action: Amend the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022 to protect travellers
background: We want the Government to amend the Act so that Romani/Gypsy are excepted from the offence of residing on land without consent in or with a vehicle, to stop this law from being discriminatory against Romani/Gypsy travellers.

It has significantly decreased the amount of safe stopping spots and has made nomadic living even more strenuous. I believe this act adds more hardships to the lives of Romani/Gypsy peoples and therefore should be urgently reviewed.

action: National guidelines to standardise burial fees and ban non-resident surcharges

action: I would like to see a change in the labelling on meat sold to consumers in uk

action: Ban 20mph speed limits with limited exceptions
background: We believe anti car sentiment has become rife and 20mph speed limits are becoming commonplace in many towns and villages which just slows traffic and causes more congestion. There should be a national policy so 20mph limits are only used as the exception, e.g outside schools.
additional_details: Because we believe that we are becoming a society where we are ever more controlled rather than punishing those that do not follow the standard 30mph speed limit. Instead of punishing dangerous driving we inconvenience everyone.

action: Make mental health days official in the education system
background: I would like there to be official mental health days within the school system, it's important for developing children's mental health as school is a lot of constant pressure and it's good for children to have a break, I impose a day or two every month for this cause.
additional_details: Having mental health days could and would positively impact children's and teenagers mental health drastically, and even save students lives. It's important to protect the youth, mental health days should be a thing, children need and deserve time to themselves to take a break, wind down, relax, go outside, catch up on sleep and have a happy body and healthy mind.

Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

action: Hold a public inquiry into claims & information made in the EU Exit Referendum
background: We call on the UK Government to establish an independent, public inquiry into the claims and information presented during the EU Exit referendum. Many reports and studies suggest that misleading or exaggerated claims were made by both sides, which may have influenced public opinion and the result.
additional_details: We believe it is in the public interest to review the accuracy of the claims, the sources of funding for campaigns, and the role of misinformation in shaping voter choice. A transparent inquiry could provide accountability and help restore trust in democratic processes. Many believe the referendum was a turning point for the UK, and we believe the public deserves clarity on how it was conducted and the validity of the information that led to such a significant national decision.

action: Abolish the TV Licence Fee in the UK
background:
We call on the UK Government to abolish the mandatory TV licence fee and explore alternative funding models for public broadcasting.

The TV licence fee is an outdated mechanism that no longer reflects the way people consume media. In an era dominated by streaming services and on-demand content.
additional_details:
Many citizens—especially those on low incomes, students, and pensioners—struggle with the financial burden of the licence fee. 

Enforcement practices, including threatening letters and home visits, can be distressing and disproportionate.

Ending the TV licence fee would relieve financial pressure on millions of households and encourage innovation in how public media is funded and delivered.

additional_details:
When such language is used without evidence, it risks fuelling division, inciting hostility and puts individuals and communities at heightened risk of harm. It also undermines public trust in elected representatives and brings Parliament into disrepute.

Those in positions of authority should be held to the highest standards of integrity and responsibility. Parliament should debate whether reckless public accusations of racism are compatible with the standards expected of MPs.

additional_details: The United Kingdom has a problem with things like homelessness, domestic violence and under 18s within unsafe environments and this idea could bring about a change for the UK by providing a safe environment for them to start their lives as well as providing more jobs within the UK. It may also change views on rehabilitation and 'second chances'!

action: Turn the street Lights back on, make the streets safer for everyone.

action: Introduce the care home fees cap for personal care costs
background: A care cap was due to come into force in England in October 2025. It would have meant that no one would have to pay more than £86,000 in England for their personal care. This was postponed and finally abolished by the previous and current governments. I feel strongly that it should be implemented.
additional_details: I would like the government to implement a personal care cap as I find it unjust that people who worked all their lives and saved for their old age, but unfortunately are unable to remain living independently due to illness or disability, are obliged to pay 100% for their care until their capital falls below the means-test threshold of £23,250. A cap would mean that you still contribute to your personal care but people may be able to retain ownership of property or some savings.

action: Recognise Iron deficiency without anaemia (low Ferritin) as an illness.
background: Tens of thousands of people across the UK (predominantly young females) are suffering from debilitating iron deficiency, without anaemia. This illness is under recognised, under researched, and misunderstood. Resulting in misdiagnosis, mismanagement, and people desperately seeking treatment.
additional_details: The government must review this crisis. Ensuring iron deficiency (low ferritin levels) is correctly tested, managed, and treated. Including oral iron therapy being offered as first line of treatment, and if this does not work or is not tolerated, IV iron therapy is offered. These changes must happen across the board, in all areas of the NHS. Iron deficiency must also be considered, before conditions such as dysautonomia and POTS are diagnosed.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

The Government is not responsible for determining whether iron deficiency without anaemia (low ferritin) is an illness.

Diagnosis and treatment of patients is a matter for the NHS and individual clinicians. The Government is responsible for setting the rules for eligibility for benefits, but decisions about whether a person is eligible for particular benefits is an operational matter for individual decision makers.

We can accept petitions calling for the Government to fund additional support for people suffering from certain conditions. If you wanted to start a petition along these lines you would need to be clear what kind of additional support you want the Government to fund.

action: Change highway code rules relating to priority for turning right at junctions
background: Amend the Highway Code so vehicles turning right into a road must give way to vehicles turning right out of that road (except at dedicated filter lanes). This would establish a new junction priority system which we think would reduce driver confusion & frustration, & improve traffic flow and safety.
additional_details: We feel the current rules can cause daily frustration and confusion. Drivers turning into a road can often block those trying to exit, but we feel letting them out first wouldn't delay anyone. This can create unnecessary waiting, unpredictable behaviour, and potential safety issues when exiting drivers edge forward for visibility. We think the proposed change would improve traffic flow, simplify decision-making, and formalise courteous driving into law.

action: Stop the increase on immigrant workers’ minimum stay in UK before PR
background: Abolish the planned laws to increase to the minimum time and salary threshold that legal, trained, English-speaking, professional immigrants have to work in the UK before attaining a permanent residency.
additional_details: A lot of qualified professionals on skilled worker visas who have paid their taxes and immigration bills their entire time here are coming close to the end of their skilled worker visa. We were a compassionate nation at the end of WWII and rehomed a lot of holocaust survivors. Why can’t we do that now? The illegal immigration statistics should not affect the legal immigrants. If we lose legal immigrants the economy will collapse; the statistics say it for themselves. This will uproot their lives

action: Ban Open-Source Deepfake-Capable AI tools until further regulation is introduced
background: We call on the UK Government to ban open-source AI video generation models that create realistic synthetic videos, until further regulations are in place. We urge licensing, oversight and coordination with our partners, to control risks and prevent harmful applications.
additional_details:
We believe models available without licensing or guardrails, could pose serious threats to:
 
• National security (deepfake propaganda, surveillance, data harvesting, bias and disinformation)
• Personal safety (harassment, impersonation, non-consensual imagery, cyberbullying, identity abuse, criminal and terrorist use, fraud)
• Public trust (erosion of video credibility and news integrity, ‘Reality Decay’, Information overload)
 
Let's lead by example and help protect Reality!

action: Reform Child Maintenance Service enforcement to prevent repeated non-payment
background: At present, parents who fail to pay through Direct Pay can be moved onto a Deduction from Earnings Order (DEO), but can default back to DP even with a history of non-payment. Enabling repeated defaulting, leaving children and resident parents without financial support for upto 3 months at a time.
additional_details:
Ensure once a DEO is in place it remains until arrears are cleared and a consistent record of payment is established.
Prevent non-paying parents from defaulting to DP.
Strengthen penalties for persistent non-payment.
Enforcing maintenance obligations consistently and promptly, will protect children from financial harm.
Children are disadvantaged because the system allows repeated non-payment. 
Close the loopholes and ensure maintenance obligations are enforced effectively.
rejection_details:

Take stronger measures to enforce payment of child maintenance arrears.

action: Stop developing 2 wind farms next to MOD low-flying zone in Powys, Wales.

additional_details: Sennybridge Training Area (SENTA) is one of the UK’s most important military sites, used for low-flying jets, helicopters, parachute drops, drones and live-fire training. Wind farms at Garreg Fawr and Banc y Celyn fall inside a pre-agreed 10 km safeguarding zone and would pose a serious hazard to flight safety. If built, they would undermine vital training and compromise national security. The Government must enforce the 10 km exclusion zone and stop these developments.

action: Protect 5-year ILR and Reject Forced Renunciation of Citizenship

action: We want King Charles to step in and sack his government as soon as possible.
background: As King Charles is head of our Government we the signed call on him to dissolve this Government and force an early election.
additional_details:
I want this to happen because the current Prime Minister has absolutely no clue what the people of our great country want. All they do is blame everyone else apart from his own government.
They take no responsibility for the dire straights the country is in and how unhappy the great people of our country feel.

action: Remove VAT from all Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for construction workers
background: Remove VAT from all certified Personal Protective Equipment —not just certified safety boots and helmets—so every worker in UK construction is better able to afford the gear that keeps them safe, We think this would also support the government’s drive to boost building, skills and productivity.
additional_details:
HMRC already zero-rates certified protective boots and helmets, but other essential PPE (eye, ear, hand, respiratory, high-visibility and fall-protection equipment) is not zero-rated.
 
There’s precedent: During the pandemic the UK zero rated PPE. We think this proves it’s feasible to extend beyond boots/helmets.
The government’s success in building 1.5 million homes and expand the construction workforce hinges on costs. We think cutting VAT on all PPE aligns directly with these ambitions.

action: Raise the minimum age for social media accounts to 16 In the UK

additional_details: Social media is linked to rising rates of anxiety, depression, poor sleep, and harmful content exposure in children. Under-16s are especially vulnerable. Other countries, including Australia, are introducing stricter laws to protect children online. The UK must act now to prioritise child safety over corporate profit.

PPEMedpro has been ordered to repay £122m to the taxpayer for faulty PPE. Mone lied about being linked to the firm, which has now gone into administration meaning the taxpayer is unlikely to recover any money.

action: Don’t mess with existing skilled work visa holders & keep 5 years of route.

Affordable childcare is essential to enable parents to remain in work, support the economy, & give children the best start in life.

action: STOP PYLONS: Bury cables along existing routes to protect countryside & security
background: Require National Grid to deliver the National Grid Upgrade via underground cables, and route the line alongside existing infrastructure such as motorways. This avoids new pylons cutting through and destroying countryside and communities and reduces risks to national infrastructure security.
additional_details: Overhead pylons (an outdated technology first used in 1928) would permanently scar countryside, destroy wildlife habitats, damage heritage sites, and harm tourism and rural communities. They are also more vulnerable to accidents, sabotage, or extreme weather, posing national security risks. Under-grounding the lines along Motorway and A road corridor’s minimises environmental and visual harm, protects communities, safeguards landscapes, and ensures energy is delivered securely and sustainably.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Halt the Pylon Network Expansion & support underground & undersea cabling" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733182

action: Stop the Government taking more of our hard earned money through higher taxes
background: Rising taxes take more from hardworking families at a time when the cost of living is already unbearable. Instead of draining our pockets, the Government should focus on managing its spending responsibly and supporting growth, not punishing people for earning a living.
additional_details: Now is the time to stand together and say no. Enough is enough! You are taking from us, and we will not accept it any longer. REMEMBER WITHOUT US THEY HAVE NOTHING!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "No more tax rises in this Parliament" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733612

action: Ban any requirement to complete CPD for all on leave from work ie maternity
background: We believe it is a breach of the Equality Act when any professionals are required to complete CPD while on maternity leave, as is the case for Social work England. We have degrees and take job interviews we should not have to also do CPD when on leave or else loose our registration.
additional_details: I want the Government to require them to change policies to align with the law that no one on leave looses their registration because the body’s meant to support them want to make them do work when having much needed and legally protected leave.

action: Make sanitary products for menstruating age females free.
background: Make sanitary towels available without a fee to all menstruating age females ,as it is an expense that many simply cannot afford and they have no choice because it occurs to them.
additional_details: People who are not financially well off or who have Menorrhaggia have to buy these products which they have no choice in because it happens to us. Causing people to make decisions about buying them or food or paying bills. It is unfair to charge expensive ££ to females who have little money or who suffer with low self esteem mental health or suffering painful periods due to health problems which they have no control over. With many companies charging high prices they have to find the money for.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Fund free period pads" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733282

action: Ban LED vehicle headlights or regulate bulb wattage
background: We think LED headlights are dangerous and need banning, or a lower limit on the wattage of the bulbs in all vehicles needs to be enforced. We are concerned that LED headlights are far too bright and blinding to oncoming traffic and could easily cause an accident.

action: Introduce Legislation to Regulate Battery Energy Storage Sites (BESS)
background: Introduce national legislation to regulate all BESS sites, enforce strict safety standards with independent assessment, protect communities & countryside, use only brownfield sites meeting strict criteria, ensure developers fund all costs, keep energy prices stable, and mandate public consultation.
additional_details:
Lithium-ion batteries catch fire, releasing toxic & carcinogenic chemicals PFAs, risking future cancer epidemics (think Teflon Scandal)

Industrial BESS sites destroy landscapes, harm wildlife, threaten public health, disrupt communities & reduce residents quality of life

Limit BESS to brownfield, sites avoids industrialising rural areas

Taxpayers must not fund projects, energy prices must not rise due to BESS development 

Robust planning consultation & independent safety checks are essential
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Review regulations on Battery Energy Storage Systems
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/723869

action: Tell Us Once to inform NHS of deaths, review comms with bereaved people
background: We ask the Government to add the NHS to the list of organisations notified of deaths by the Tell Us Once service. We also want them to require a review of and improvements to all NHS services' communications to ensure communications with bereaved families are coordinated and informed.
additional_details: This must happen to ensure bereaved families are not sent appointments and treatment information for family members who have already passed away.

action: All Employment Tribunal awards must be paid in full to the claimant
background: If a claimant wins an award through an employment tribunal, they MUST get this money.
additional_details:
From my own experience I have realised an employment tribunal decision means nothing! 
The whole process is drawn out, stressful and even if you get an award - you still have to fight - and end up with nothing! 
This HAS to change.
rejection_details:
If a tribunal decides that compensation should be awarded, the employer is ordered to pay once the claimant has received a written judgement. If the employer does not pay within 14 days they will also need to pay interest. Claimants can report an employer to the government, go to court, or claim compensation from the government if an employer does not pay. 

More information on what happens once a tribunal awards compensation can be found here: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/work/employment-tribunal/employment-tribunals/the-tribunal-hearing/check-what-happens-if-you-win-your-employment-tribunal-case/

action: Employers to open 25% of job positions for parents 9.30am-2.30pm Monday-Friday
background:
Change/Create the law - every Employer in the UK have to open mandatory minimum 25% job positions for parents in between the times of  9.30am - 2.30pm Monday to Friday.

Make a scheme parents can apply to check eligibility ( in case they have a child with disability or special needs)
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about working patterns are a matter for individual employers, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Introduce Laws regarding the use and development of Artificial Intelligence
background: We would like the government to implement laws regulating the creation of artificial intelligence and potentially banning certain AI providers if they do not meet these requirements. and also implement stricter copyright against AI companies.
additional_details: For a long time the development of artificial intelligence has remained largely unregulated and this could pose a LARGE issue to the world, if we start drafting laws early and make them effective this can be shouldered we would like to propose a sort of interim laws until more can be known about artificial intelligence after the recent implementation of the online safety act we believe the government has the sense to read out petition and consider this in parliament.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand you're concerned about AI, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: This petition wants school meals for children to be free of charge.
background: We would like all school meals in the United Kingdom to be free of charge as some parents may not have enough money to pay the fee-this also helps children to prevent not eating because of their balance on their account.
additional_details: We want the government or parliament to do this  because it will prevent children from being hungry after Lunchtime , just because they dont have the right amount of money for a meal.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Free school meals for all children
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732029

action: Stop the council proposal of closing our schools
background: Consider as parents our thoughts about this decision and how this is going to affect our children.
additional_details: We, as concerned parents, carers, and community members, strongly oppose the council’s proposal to close schools. This decision would have a deeply damaging impact on our children’s education, wellbeing, and sense of security, while also placing our dedicated teachers’ jobs and livelihoods at risk. Schools are at the heart of our community, providing not only learning but also stability, support, and opportunity. We urge the council to reconsider this proposal.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue. You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Call a general election if a government breaks an election manifesto promise
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation that would trigger an immediate general election if a governing party breaks a commitment set out in its election manifesto.
additional_details:
Election manifestos are critical to the democratic process, providing the basis on which voters make informed choices. Once elected, a government’s manifesto is the contract between the electorate and those in power. If a government breaks the promises on which it was elected, this undermines democratic accountability.
 
To restore public trust in politics, the electorate should have the right to re-evaluate a government’s mandate through a general election if manifesto commitments are broken.

action: Provide Fully Funded Armed Security for Jewish Public Buildings
background: We call upon His Majesty’s Government to urgently provide funding for armed security (police or military presence) at Jewish public buildings – including schools, synagogues, and community centres.
additional_details: We are calling for this due to the rise in antisemitism in the UK and a recent terrorist attack in Manchester during Yom Kippur. Jewish schools, synagogues, and community centres face real threats, and we believe it is the state’s duty to provide permanent, funded armed security so that Jewish children and families can live, learn, and worship without fear.

action: Restrict access to public funds to UK citizens and permanent residents only.
background: We call on the Government to ensure that only UK citizens and those with permanent residency can access public funds, by tightening eligibility rules, improving enforcement, and preventing misuse of the welfare system.
additional_details: Public funds should be protected for those with full and lasting ties to the UK. Limiting eligibility to citizens and permanent residents ensures fairness, sustainability, and reduces pressure on welfare services.
rejection_details:
Restrict free access to public services to UK citizens only
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732256

action: Change how many DT subjects students can do for GCSE, A-Level, or BTEC
background: I want the government or parliament to change how many DT subjects students are allowed to do for GCSE, A-Level, or BTEC. For example,  if a student wants to do both food preparation and nutrition and hospitality and catering, even though they are very similar, they can.
additional_details: I want the government or parliament to do it because I think students should be allowed to do as many DT subjects as they want for GCSE, A-Level, and BTEC. Even if that means some schools that make students do PRS for GCSE say they don’t have to anymore. I just think it gives students an opportunity to learn more and develop essential skills, especially in the case of food, that will help them in later life.
rejection_details: This is a matter for individual schools and colleges.

action: Grant statutory right to leave for employees when a parent passes away
background: Introduce minimum statutory leave for employees after the death of a parent.
additional_details: Funeral arrangements can take 2-3 weeks to arrange. We think inadequate leave from employers can cause longer term damage pressuring an employee to return prematurely following the death of a parent. Arranging a funeral for a parent is very stressful, then the additional stress of closing that parents life down in terms of their finances and other business.

action: Stop digital ID that is optional in name but mandatory in practice.
background: Digital ID must not be introduced in a way that is optional in name but mandatory in practice. Forcing citizens to hand over biometrics to work or access services is coercion, insecure, and risks mass surveillance. Existing IDs already work without new threats.
additional_details: Digital ID that is optional in name but mandatory in practice is coercion. No system is unhackable; stolen biometrics can’t be changed. One login risks surveillance and exclusion. Before any digital ID, the UK needs a Digital Bill of Rights to protect privacy, limit overreach, and keep participation truly optional.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for a similar action: "Do not introduce Digital ID cards" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730194

action: Scrap VAT on labour and essential services like trades and childcare
background: VAT adds 20% to essential services like plumbing, childcare, and home repairs, making them expensive for families and small businesses. We think removing this tax would make vital services more affordable, easing financial pressure for households and supporting local trades.
additional_details: We think VAT on labour disproportionately affects low and middle income families and puts extra strain on small businesses. For example, a £500 home repair costs £600 with VAT, which can discourage people from hiring skilled workers. Scrapping VAT could boost small businesses, create jobs, simplify accounting, and make essential services accessible to everyone without reducing quality or availability.

action: Raise the motorway speed limit to 80mph
background: Implement a new motorway speed limit of 80mph
additional_details: Since 1965 the motorway speed limit has sat at 70mph since the temporary trial. Although there was a reduction in crashes due to the lower speed, this is not representative of the modern day. Average braking distances in 1965 at 70mph did not factor in modern tyres and anti-lock braking systems as well as technological advancements as we see in cars today such as Audi pre sense. I believe that the speed limit should be raised to 80mph as technology has advanced but the rules of the road haven't.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Increase dual carriage and motorway speed limit to 80mph
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738871

action: Ban Public Firework Sales – License Events to Protect People and Animals
background: We call for a ban on the sale of fireworks to the general public and the introduction of a licensing system, with a nominal fee per event. This measure would ensure responsible use of fireworks , while reducing the distress and harm caused to animals, vulnerable people, and local communities.
additional_details: Parliament should ban firework sales to the public and require event licenses with a minimum £100 fee. Funds could support emergency services and education on firework safety. This would protect animals, veterans, vulnerable people, and reduce anti-social use while still allowing controlled community celebrations.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Limit the sale of fireworks to those running local council approved events only" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732559

action: Revoke regulations that restrict promotion of high sugar/fat food and drink
background: Revoke the restrictions on selling sugary drinks and foods with high fat or sugar. Give the British people back their choice in consumption.
additional_details: We think the sugary soft drink refill ban, along with banning of deals for certain high sugar/fat foods, impede upon the liberty of adult citizens to make their own choices on their lifestyle. This act must be repealed to give the people the choice in the consumer market we deserve.

action: 🔒 Armed forces or trained armed security at every school entrance
background:
Present all day, every day during school hours and events. Professionally trained, licensed, and equipped. Specialised in child safety, crisis response, and de-escalation


 • Armed threats to schools are real and rising
 • Response time can save lives — deterrence is key
additional_details:
• Banks and government buildings get protection — so should our kids 

Help us demand action from:
📍 Local School Board or Council Name?
📍 Your MP or Education Department?

📢 Let’s keep our children safe — before it’s too late.

🖊️ SIGN TODAY — YOUR VOICE MATTERS!
rejection_details:

Fund security guards and CCTV on school premises & introduce new protocols 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738547

action: Petition to reverse their decision to follow through with digital IDs
background: I want the government to reverse their decision on the ‘Do not introduce digital IDs’ petition and to make government policy that they will not move forward with digital identification and they will not attempt again with digital IDs
additional_details: The petition to end digital IDs got 2.8 million votes it’s undemocratic for the government to see this and carry on with the policy which was not mentioned in their manifesto during the 2024 general election digital and other similar schemes have failed with the Brit card being repealed in 2011 and Churchill himself calling national identity cards unbrittish
rejection_details: The core ask of this petition is the same as an existing petition: "Do not introduce Digital ID cards" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730194

action: Stop UK Govt ILR Change: Keep 5-Year Rule for Skilled Workers Already in UK
background: We applied for Skilled Worker visas with the promise of ILR after 5 years. Changing this to 10 years for those already in the UK breaks that promise, disrupts families, and undermines trust. Keep the 5-year ILR route for existing visa holders.
additional_details: We ask the Government and Parliament to stop plans to extend ILR from 5 to 10 years for Skilled Worker visa holders already in the UK. Our visas promised settlement after 5 years. We have paid National Insurance and taxes, without taking a penny in benefits. Changing rules now is unfair, breaks trust, and harms families. We urge you to protect the 5-year ILR route for those who came in good faith under existing rules.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Keep the 5-Year ILR pathway for existing Skilled Worker visa holders" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727360

action: Pass a CBDC Safeguards Act before any introduction of a digital pound
background: Legislate binding legal safeguards before any central bank digital currency (CBDC) roll-out: guarantee continued access to cash, prohibit unilateral account freezes without judicial due process, require privacy protections for routine transactions, and create independent oversight and auditability.
additional_details: We call on Parliament to pass a CBDC Safeguards Act before any launch of a digital pound. Protections must include: cash guaranteed alongside CBDC; privacy for everyday payments; due process before freezing accounts; ban on expiry dates, negative balances or forced spending; and independent oversight. We also want it to include clear rules for stablecoins/DeFi to ensure safety, backing and consumer protection, protecting freedom and choice for all citizens. Safeguards must also ensure that no CBDC can be linked to any digital identity system without explicit primary legislation and clear public consent.

action: Mandate debates for petitions over 100k signatures, starting with Digital ID
background: Amend Standing Orders to mandate full debates for e-petitions over 100,000 signatures within 6 months of closing. Hold in main chamber or Westminster Hall; require ministerial attendance and substantive responses. Apply immediately to Petition 730194 (Digital ID cards) to restore fair accountability
additional_details:
E-petitions amplify voices but fail - Do not introduce Digital ID cards has 2.7M signatures vs privacy risks; Government dismisses it and PM pushes ahead.

Repeal Online Safety Act has 547K vs invasive rules; rejected Jul 28 and PM pushes ahead.

This platform erodes trust (14% trust pols). Petitions represent 99% engaged users - not "2% population." Dismissing petitions based on UK population and not engaged users is a misrepresentation.

We the people demand public debates on issues we raise!
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

The Petitions Committee has scheduled a debate on petition 730194 relating to digital ID cards on 8 December and petition 722903 relating to the Online Safety Act on 15 December. Both debates will be in Westminster Hall and start at 4.30pm. A government minister will attend the debate and respond at the end. You can find out more about petition debates here: https://committees.parliament.uk/committee/326/petitions-committee/content/194347/how-petitions-debates-work/

We could accept a new petition calling for changes to the current petitions system, as long as it was clear what you'd like those changes to be. For example, you could start a new petition calling for all petitions that reach 100k to be debated. 

We've published the following petitions which you may wish to sign: 

Make Government Petitions Legally Binding at a Threshold of Public Signatures: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736129

Give More Power to Public Petitions to Force the Government to take Action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736968

Reform of petitions to include creating Citizens’ Assemblies at 500k signatures: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733648

action: Remove the XL Bully from thelist of banned dogs
background: We call on the UK Government to remove the XL Bully from the li list of banned dogs under the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991
additional_details:
We believe that breed-specific legislation is ineffective and unfair. The vast majority of XL Bully dogs are friendly, safe, and well cared for by responsible owners. A dog's behaviour depends on its upbringing, training, and environment, not solely on its breed.
Banning XL Bullies punishes esponsible owners and leads to the unnecessary destruction of healthy, well-socialised dogs. Instead, the Government shol cus on promotina responsible ownershin
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Reverse the ban on XL Bully dogs" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729003

action: not needing ID for Energy drinks (Red Bull, Monster)
background: get rid of needing id to buy energy drinks
additional_details: some people ages 16+ dont have identification to purchase an energy drink
rejection_details: There is no legal requirement to produce ID to purchase any caffeine containing foods and beverages including energy drinks.

action: Do not change Indefinite leave to remain for family visa to 10 years
background: I want the government to reconsider and keep the current 5 year route for family visas
additional_details: Changing the route for family visas from 5 to 10 years is a drastic and unfeeling step. Many families, like myself have worked since coming to the UK, paying taxes and striving to integrate and make this country our own. The 10 year route is not just heart wrenching, it is a slap in the face. I have been working my fingers and soul to the core for this day- May 2026- to be free from worry, uncertainty and the financial burden that comes with renewing a visa and now that is being torn away
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Protect Legal Migrants: do not implement the 10-Year ILR proposal" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727372

action: Hold a referendum to decide whether or not digital ID cards should be introduced
background: Hold a public referendum to decide if the UK should have digital ID cards.
additional_details: The introduction of digital ID cards is a serious issue and should be decided by the British public via a referendum.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: ABOLISH THE TV LICENCE
background: Cancel the TV licence. People dont want to be forced to fund the BBC anymore.
additional_details: We are tired of having to fund a co-operation that publishes incorrect news.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Scrap the BBC TV Licence & replace funding with adverts or paywall
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727365

action: Fair NHS Care for Adults with ADHD in Scotland
background:
We call on the Government to:

Ensure funded ADHD medication titration and follow-up care are available on the NHS.

Expand adult ADHD services to reduce waiting times for diagnosis and treatment.

Guarantee equal access across Scotland so that care is not dependent on postcode.
additional_details: Adults with ADHD are being failed by the NHS. Waiting times for diagnosis are often several years, and many patients are then denied access to treatment. In some areas, adults are forced to pay privately for medication titration and follow-up, creating inequality in access to care.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

You may also wish to contact your local council and MSP who represent you about this issue. 

You can find the name of your local council and how to contact them here: https://www.mygov.scot/find-your-local-council

You can find the name of your local MSP and how to contact them here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps

action: Require local authorities to remove all flags from street furniture
background: Require local authorities to promptly remove flags that have been put up illegally in public spaces (under the Highways Act 1980), and encourage anyone wanting to display a flag to do so on their personal and private property.
additional_details:
The individuals who erected these flags did so without authorisation and this could amount to trespass and potentially criminal damage under the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
 
Continued inaction raises the danger that members of the public may attempt to remove the flags themselves. This could result in confrontations, injuries, or further property damage, all of which would expose the government and local councils to liability.

action: Require organisers and attendees to pay for policing of protests
background: We seek a change in the law, whereby any march or demonstration that requires a police presence, the cost must be borne by the attendees and the organisers, not the taxpayer.

action: Hold a referendum before introducing a mandatory digital ID system (“BritCard”)
background: We want the Government to commit to holding a national referendum before introducing any form of mandatory digital ID system. This would give the people the final say on whether such a scheme should become law.
additional_details: The Government plans to introduce a national Digital ID (“BritCard”), mandatory for Right to Work checks and potentially expanded to benefits, tax, and other services. This represents a fundamental change in the citizen–state relationship, raising serious concerns under Article 8 ECHR (privacy), Article 6 ECHR (fair hearing), and the Bill of Rights 1688. A referendum is essential to give the people the final say.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Recognise  the CST volunteers who saved lives at the Manchester Synagogue
background: The death toll from the terrorist attack on a Synagogue yesterday would have been far higher if it had not been for the incredible bravery and selflessness of the volunteer security guards from the Community Security Trust. We want that bravery recognised & rewarded
additional_details:
We have an honours system that rewards people for playing sport or being on television.
In this instance that system should be used to publicly acknowledge the bravery that stopped further deaths.
These rewards should extend to the police officers who approached a man that they believed had a bomb.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions that ask for people to be given honours.

The Government will only accept individual nominations, not petitions, so we can’t publish your petition.

To submit a nomination for an honour, visit: http://www.gov.uk/honours/

action: Require manufacturers to label caffeine content on all pre-packed coffee
background: Pre-packed coffee in the UK (instant, ground, filter) does not have to show caffeine content, unlike energy drinks or medicines with over 150mg of caffeine per litre. We feel consumers like pregnant women and heart patients therefore can't track intake safely.
additional_details: Recommended daily caffeine intakes are 400 mg for adults and 200 mg for pregnant women, but consumers cannot reliably use product labels to help track intake. Excess caffeine risks can include heart palpitations, anxiety, insomnia, and adverse pregnancy outcomes. We think mandatory labelling  would help empower safe, informed choices and protects public health. We want clearer caffeine labelling (mg per 100 g and per serving) to help protect health.

action: Police patrol when kids are on  school runs in the morning and after school
background: Our children to be safe from any danger and protected from any evil acts or strangers following them! Our children aren’t safe going to and from schools no more
additional_details: Because this country is not what it used to be no more, our children are having there childhood robbed from them due to the high level of violence and threats that have happened recently
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund security guards and CCTV on school premises & introduce new protocols
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738547

action: Regulate the sale and distribution of research peptides
background: We want the Government to regulate the sale of research peptides by creating a compulsory purchaser register. Only accredited buyers, such as universities, licensed research institutions, and registered companies, should be eligible to join.
additional_details:
To be included, buyers must provide valid identification and, where applicable, a company registration number. Sellers should be required to confirm that buyers are listed on the register before completing sales.

Currently peptides can be bought online with minimal oversight, creating risks of unsafe use and misuse. A regulated register with proper checks and balances would protect public health while allowing legitimate research to continue safely.

action: Recognise Jerusalem as the capital city of Israel
background: Given the appalling terrorist attack in Manchester on the back of rising antisemitism in the UK, I contend that it is time the UK government recognise Jerusalem as the capital of the State of Israel and move the UK Embassy and Consulate there.
additional_details: The Jewish people have a long and well established historical and religious connection to the Land of Israel. This is especially true of Jerusalem. We believe the PM and his government has neglected the rights and feelings of the Jewish community. We are sick of platitudes.

action: Call for a national referendum on the introduction of Digital ID.
background: I think the introduction of digital ID is a suitable subject for a national vote especially following the vast number of signatures on a recent petition against the government's plans.
additional_details: As this was never mooted in thus government's election manifesto, I would suggest that draconian changes to our civil liberties, such as the one proposed, should be a matter for national referenda now and in the future.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Stop income tax on employees' tips in hospitality industry
background: Tips help an industry already on its knees, desperately trying to keep staff willing to work in hospitality after the fallout of Covid and Brexit. Tips help small businesses keep hardworking teams employed when they can't afford to raise their wages due to spiralling costs and economic climate.
additional_details: Hospitality is a hard industry which many people couldn’t cope working in. We call for the Government to allow for some spontaneous gratuity of one human to another without a punishing tax that proportionally raises very little for the public purse yet is very detrimental to the hospitality industry and its workers.

action: Lower the GCSE grading system for children with SEND or EHCP
background: There should be some leniency on grading GCSE's or a lower pass grade for these children so they have a better chance to progress onto further education.
additional_details: It is hard for these children to cope academically in highschool. I have twins with EHCP's that struggle on a daily basis and it is heartbreaking to listen to them question why they are not able to transition onto certain college courses if they are unable to acheive the expected GCSE grades. They try their best everday but are still far off from the expected pass grades and will be sitting their exams soon. It is unfair that they are graded the same as a child with no learning disability.
rejection_details:
We also can only accept petitions from people who provide their full name.

You could start a new petition about a review of grade boundaries for children with SEND, but we would need a full name.

action: Equal Security Funding for Jewish Community Institutions: Protecting Community.
background: We call on His Majesty’s Government to allocate £117,000 over four years to enhance security for Jewish institutions across the UK. Jewish communities continue to face targeted attacks and threats, and we believe equal protection under the law must be reflected in equal funding for safety.
additional_details: This funding should match that given to Muslim communities and be used for CCTV, alarms, fencing, and paid guards to protect synagogues, schools, housing, and community centres from hate crimes.Jewish communities continue to face targeted attacks and threats, and we believe equal protection under the law must be reflected in equal funding for safety. We urge the government to act swiftly and justly to safeguard our community. No faith or group should receive preferential treatment.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Provide Fully Funded Armed Security for Jewish Public Buildings
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744965

action: change age of driving to 15/16 rather than 18

action: Hold an Immediate General Election to Restore Trust in Democracy
background: We are being consistently ignored, monitored and dismissed. Millions spoke out against digital ID, yet government presses ahead. The UK is sliding towards dictatorship. We demand an immediate general election to protect our freedom and our democracy. We have lost all trust.
additional_details:
We call on His Majesty’s Government to hold an immediate general election. Trust has collapsed as citizens’ concerns are disregarded and freedoms threatened. 

Democracy requires accountability. When petitions with millions of signatures are disregarded and surveillance measures continue to expand without transparent debate, confidence in our democratic system is lost. 

A new mandate is urgently needed to restore accountability and safeguard liberty.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Fund COVID booster vaccines for the general public
background: Give funding for the COVID-19 booster to be available for anyone who wants to get it.
additional_details:
With the offer of a COVID booster shot to certain groups, we think it is simply unconscionable not to offer this to the general public as well. Infections happen in crowded spaces such as schools, public transport and shops. 

Everyone should be able to protect themselves and others, regardless of whether or not they are already vulnerable.

action: STOP THE HOSUING OF ILLEGAL IMIGRANTS IN THE BOROUGH OF HILLINGDON
background: Cease housing of illegal immigrants in hotels,HMOs,and residential properties within Hillingdon.Protect the housing stock for those legally entitled to it,including vulnerable local families and residents Requesttransparency and accountability from the Home Office and other authorities involved in.
additional_details: We, the undersigned, are residents and members of the Hillingdon community who are deeply concerned about the ongoing use of local housing, hotels, and HMOs to accommodate illegal immigrants within our borough. We believe this practice: - Places additional strain on already stretched local services (including schools, healthcare, and housing). - Raises safety and safeguarding concerns, particularly in areas close to schools and residential neighbourhoods. - Is being done without full consultation of residents or transparency from national and local government. - Is unsustainable and unfair to local residents on housing waiting lists and those paying council tax
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

action: Hold a Referendum on whether or not to introduce a Digital ID system.
background: Hold a Referendum on whether or not to introduce a Digital ID system. The Referendum should be open to anyone that would or could have a digital ID in the proposed Digital ID system.
additional_details: The proposal to introduce a Digital ID system is controversial and should have the support of the majority of the citizens in a democratic society. Because of the potential for such a system to be a step towards mass surveillance and digital control the Government needs to ensure that the introduction of a Digital ID system is seen as a benefit to the majority it's citizens.
rejection_details:
Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action:
Stop Digital ID card plan.
Note risks of scheme to domestic abuse survivors.
background: We call on the UK Government to abandon the plans for mandatory Digital ID cards. Promoted as a vehicle to tackle illegal immigration, we are dismayed that narratives around this proposed scheme have not included any reference to the danger and risks posed to domestic abuse survivors.
additional_details:
Technology-facilitated abuse is rife. Digital ID cards, requiring smartphone-based digital identification, will fundamentally become additional weapons of abuse. 
They will: enable coercive control; compromise anonymity; exacerbate digital exclusion, and increase data vulnerability. 
The core safeguarding principles enshrined in UK law will be contradicted, and the Government's promise to halving violence against women and girls, broken.
Reject the cards to protect domestic abuse survivors!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not introduce Digital ID cards
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730194

action: Hold a public referendum over the introduction of Digital ID
background: The government should hold a public referendum as to whether Digital ID should be introduced or not. The people should have the final say on if we want this or not. It should not be forced on us by a government who have neither asked, nor consulted us. We live in a Democracy, not a Dictatorship.
additional_details:
Nearly 3 million people have signed a petition AGAINST the introduction of Digital ID's, and much like other petitions (i.e, one to repeal the so-called 'Online Safety Act') the government have looked at it and shrugged it off with a generic "We're doing it anyway" response, ignoring those people completely.

The people have made it as clear as we possibly can that we are vehemently OPPOSED to this and it is an insult to be ignored once again.

Let US, the people, decide if we want this or not.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Introduce a Presumption of Equal Parenting Time in Family Law
background: We want the Government to legislate to establish a presumption of equal parenting time following separation, unless there is clear evidence that it would not be in the child’s best interests. We think this would help ensure children maintain meaningful relationships with both parents.
additional_details: Current family law does not presume equal contact when parents separate. This can result in one parent having significantly less contact, despite research showing that children benefit most when both parents remain involved. One analysis of 40 studies found children in equal parenting arrangements consistently have better mental health, stronger relationships with parents and improved academic performance. We think that even in high-conflict situations, shared parenting leads to better outcomes.

action: A Successful Petition to Trigger a Binding Referendum on a General Election
background: Considering it is very difficult to design a different kind of electoral system that pleases the majority of voters, we demand a law that uses a government petition (I suggest a million signatories) to precipitate a binding referendum on whether to have a fresh General Election.
additional_details:
Too many people are feeling that their British way of life is badly threatened, in ways that were not declared during the General Election.
It is hard to understand, in what is intended to be a democracy, that just a few people, elected on a third of the vote, can have such an inviolable hold on power.
A referendum is the most honest expression of democracy.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Hold referendum if a petition reaches over 650,000 signatures
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743620

Give More Power to Public Petitions to Force the Government to take Action
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736968

action: Trial digital ID on new arrivals before UK citizens.
background: The Government has said digital ID is to tackle illegal immigration. We ask that it is first applied to all new arrivals only, for the remainder of this Parliament. Its effectiveness should be measured and published transparently before imposing it on law-abiding UK citizens.
additional_details: The justification for digital ID is tackling illegal migration. If this is true, we believe it should be trialled on new arrivals to the UK, who do not have citizenship, not imposed on the public. We think a trial until the end of this Parliament would prove whether the system actually works before asking citizens to surrender freedoms and privacy for an untested policy.

action: Existing skilled workers must be remained on 5 years route to gain ILR status.
background: Government should consider the existing hard skilled workers to be remained on 5 years rule. They contribute so much to society since  Feb 2022.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Keep the 5-Year ILR pathway for existing Skilled Worker visa holders" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727360

action: Safer Schools, primary and high schools
background:
Increased funding for school security systems (CCTV, secure entrances, panic alarms).

Mandatory terrorism response drills and staff training in every school.

Stronger coordination between schools and local police forces.

A review of current policies on emergency preparedness in schools.
additional_details: The safety of children and educational staff must remain a top priority, and I believe more can be done to support schools in protecting against potential threats.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund security guards and CCTV on school premises & introduce new protocols
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738547

action: Provide armed security for UK Synagogues and Jewish institutions.
background: The level of UK antisemitism is at its highest in recorded history. It is clear now after the Manchester attack that the current level of unarmed protection is not sufficient. Armed protection is the only way to provide real, effective reassurance and safety for the Jewish community.
additional_details:
10 Years ago,  after visiting Denmark and hearing about the Synagogue shooting attack there, I returned to the UK and created a petition to call for armed security at UK Jewish institutions, just like they have in most European countries.  At the time, it was believed it was not needed. The security situation since then has worsened significantly.
I repeat what I said then. 
It is impossible for a policeman  or security guard without a weapon to protect sites from terrorists who carry weapons.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Provide Fully Funded Armed Security for Jewish Public Buildings" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744965

action: Make it law that animal charities must obtain vets notes regardless of health
background: Make it a legal requirement that all rehoming and rescue charities obtain vets notes from previous owners when dogs are given up. This will show a full report of the animals health to ensure what the previous owner has disclosed is correct.

action: Allow BNO visa holders to work in sports and grassroots coaching
background: The BNO visa prohibits paid work as professional/semi-professional athletes or coaches in the UK, even at grassroots level. We ask the Government to remove this restriction.
additional_details: We believe this restriction harms youth athletes and qualified coaches from Hong Kong who are trying to build a life in the UK. It may stop young people from developing in sport and force experienced coaches to abandon their profession. Hong Kong is not a major sports labour exporter, and we feel BNO migrants pose no threat to UK athletes or the UK sports job market. On the contrary, we feel they can strengthen local communities and support grassroots sports.

action: Reform Home Buying so Agreed Sales Require A Deposit & Binding Commitment
background: We call on the Government to reform home buying in England and Wales so that when a sale is agreed, the buyer must place a deposit. If either party withdraws for reasons other than genuine exceptional circumstances, they lose the deposit.
additional_details:
This would bring the system closer to Scotlands where accepted offers are binding, reducing failed sales and giving buyers and sellers more certainty.
In England and Wales nearly a third of sales collapse after an offer is accepted causing wasted money, delays and stress. A binding commitment at the point of sale would:
Cut the number of failed transactions
Protect both buyer and seller form wasted costs
Make the process faster, fairer and more reliable
Its time to modernise home buying
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for a similar action: "Amend the home buying process in England to align with Scotland" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739512

action: Compel residential care homes in England to publish their tariff of room charges
background: We urge the Secretary of State to use their powers under the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, to compel residential care homes in England to publicly display an itemised tariff of fees for rooms and service charges, very similar to those displayed in hotels.
additional_details: Under consumer protection laws, businesses offering accommodation in England, Wales and Scotland must display a price list, including itemised information in brochures or websites, stating prices inclusive of compulsory service charges. This requirement currently applies to hotels but NOT residential care homes. We believe this omission limits competition and creates opacity in prices, which could allow the exploitation of vulnerable residents and their relatives by care homes.

action: Introduce the logging of suspects country of birth on arrest.
background: Introduce legislation to track the birth country of people committing offences in the uk. And make the information public.
additional_details: To enable citizens and authorities to be aware of the birth country of criminals.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. We're not sure if you want the Government to publish data relating to arrests or relating to convictions ('people committing offences'/'criminals'). You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

In respect of nationality data, the Ministry of Justice already includes data on the nationality of persons within the prison system in its quarterly offender management statistics, here: https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/offender-management-statistics-quarterly

In addition, the Home Office has committed to review the data that it collects and publishes regarding the nationalities and offences committed by foreign national offenders who are subject to deportation proceedings. Further details of that review process can be found here:
https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/statistics-on-foreign-national-offenders-and-the-immigration-system

action: Require train companies to allow passengers to sit in first class when it's busy
background: If a train is overcrowded, train companies should be forced to open up first class areas to standard tickets holders.
additional_details: People pay a large amount of money to travel by train, even though it is one of the most sustainable and efficient modes of transport. If a train is overcrowded, especially as a result of delays, it is unfair to make people stand when there is seating in first class available. It can also be less safe, prevent people from accessing the toilets and can cause further delays and discomfort as people struggle to reach the exits.

action: Review rules, policing and harm of marches
background: We want Government to review stricter permits for and costs of policing disruptive marches, penalties for organisers of protests where antisemitic or extremist activity takes place, and the policing, economic and community harm caused by protests.
additional_details: We think this is needed, especially after the recent synagogue attack. Repeated pro-Palestinian marches cost tens of millions in policing, cause major disruption to businesses and transport, and have coincided with rising antisemitism. The recent terrorist attack on a UK synagogue shows the risk to community safety. The public are fed up with disruption and fear.

action: Give British Citizens the right to bare arms!
background: Due to the continuous failure of the Police Force, Home Office, Secret Services, central and local government to protect British Citizens from life threatening crimes we want the RIGHT TO BARE ARMS re-instated so that we protect ourselves and meet fire with fire.
additional_details: Already stated above
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the UK Government or Parliament to take a specific action. We don't know what you would like a right to bear arms to include, so we're not sure what specific action you want taken.

At the moment, permission to possess or to purchase or acquire a firearm will be granted to an individual who is assessed by the licensing authority, the police, as not posing a threat to public safety and having good reason to own the firearm.

You could start a new petition clearly explaining what you'd like to happen. For example, you could start a new petition asking the UK Government and Parliament to make a specific change to firearm regulations, if that's what you'd like to happen.

action: Do not raise the retirement age to 67 due to life expectancy dropping.
background: Life expectancy has dropped since covid. Review required since it was raised because people were living longer. This is no longer the case...
additional_details: Reverse the decision to raise retirement age to 67
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop the State Pension retirement age rising to 67. Make it 65
