action: Hold a referendum / give the public a chance to vote on adopting digital ID.
background: It’s clear that despite a clear and huge divide amougnst the general public, the government are intent on bringing in mandatory digital ID. This is undemocratic as it wasn’t featured in the GOV’s manifesto and should be for the majority to decide, considering its impact on the whole UK.
additional_details: The UK public have not had a say on the adoption of digital ID, considering the impact this holds on every single individual in the UK, it’s only right that the public have the opportunity to vote. It’s already clear that a large amount of the population are not in favour considering the recent petition to scrap the idea completely, gaining support in the millions in a very short amount of time. The GOV must act accordingly and in the interest of the majority by allowing a vote to take place.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Do not decrypt and scan private messages
background:
There have been recent efforts to slowly and unnecessarily remove encryption from private messages online which is a huge invasion of privacy and disguised mass-surveilance. 

We call for change to cease all efforts by the government to erode or remove message encryption!
additional_details:
The vast majority of people have—at one point—shared personal/private details or experiences and scanning messages unnecessarily would be a massive invasion of our rights.

Not to mention putting all our private messages and information into databases would be a huge security risk as it allows hackers to see everything we sent with one data breach, essentially (for most of us) giving them blackmail material & access to private info we mentioned or sent in our messages.
rejection_details:
We understand you're concerned about encryption laws, but we're not exactly sure what you'd like the Government and Parliament to do. 

We could accept a petition calling the Government to change the law so that encrypted messages cannot be accessed by authorities such as the security services or police, if that's something that you'd like to see. 

For example, we previously published this petition which has now closed: 

Repeal the Investigatory Powers Act: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/717199

action: Require Government Ministers to hold sole British citizenship
background: Cabinet ministers make decisions of the highest importance, including on defence, foreign policy, and national security. Holding citizenship of another nation may create perceived or actual conflicts of interest and can undermine public trust in government decision-making.
additional_details:
We believe that by requiring sole British citizenship for these senior roles, we can safeguard national security, strengthen public confidence in Government accountability & ensure undivided loyalty to the United Kingdom.
 
We believe this measure will protect the integrity of government and ensure that the highest offices of state are held by those with exclusive allegiance to the UK. Exclusive UK citizenship ensures Cabinet decisions are free from potential foreign influence or divided loyalty.

action: Give the Home Secretary the same powers to ban static assemblies as marches
background: We are calling for a change to the law so that static assemblies can be banned by the Home Secretary where there is a serious risk of public disorder.
additional_details: Under section 13 of the Public Order Act 1986, the Home Secretary can ban a march if police believe there is a risk of serious public disorder that cannot be prevented by section 12 powers. Static assemblies do not fall under this category. The police can only impose conditions on assemblies or seek a ban on assemblies that involve trespass under section 14A of the Act.

action: Make Political Studies a Mandatory Subject for GCSEs.
background: Implement "Politics" as a subject that is mandatory, similar to Maths and English. With new voting laws, it is more important than ever that people truly understand the impact and meaning of politics and ideologies; only with an educated public can you benefit society.
additional_details: Implement Political Studies from either Year 9 or Year 10 as a mandatory requirement, like PSHE; but it adopts a similar form to the A-Level standard that is currently present. It may have to focus more on UK politics since its engineered to GCSE students but frankly its unfair that you let 16 year olds vote without many of them having a shred of political understanding, it would also help the youth to actually get involved in politics instead of just being commentators.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Make Government & Politics a compulsory, core subject in schools
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733942

action: Increase the fostering allowance to support fostered children
background: We want the government to increase the fostering allowance. We're concerned that some foster carers have had to cease fostering due to financial difficulty. We're worried that the increase of foster children and a lack of foster carers has meant children have not received nurturing homes.

action: Give the region of North England Autonomy & Devolution
background: As a Northerner I would like, my region North England to have powers like have it's own parliament and local government and even it's own laws too.
additional_details: As a Northerner who, cares about his region and his people I care about the working-class of this region to the fact that we up In North England are being neglected by Westminster and have our resources taken by Westminster. Not to mention poverty is a problem in North England and so is the cost of living and thanks to that it's hard to live and get jobs In North England due to work places, taken down due to deindustrialization. And health care has been a disaster for the people ever since 2020.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 
 
We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.
 
You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, including setting out more details about where exactly you would like this to apply and the area it would cover, and what powers you would like to be granted.

action: Introduce stricter controls and awareness campaigns to stop nitrous oxide misuse
background: We want tighter rules on nitrous oxide sales, stronger enforcement against illegal supply, and national awareness campaigns showing its dangers. We want the Government to act to protect young people and prevent more lives being lost to this potentially dangerous substance.
additional_details: Too many people don’t understand how dangerous nitrous oxide can be, or how easily it can kill. I want the Government to act now with stronger laws, clearer warnings, and national education to prevent more deaths. Please make real change so no families have to suffer the loss of a loved one.

action: Start a democratic public referendum for a digital ID.
background: The government should ask the people to choose if they agree to surrender liberty for a centralised digital ID card system. We should hold a democratic public referendum to get a real sense if the people really accepts the risks for the unapparent convenience.
additional_details:
Centralised personal data is a major security risk. Carrying all of our personal data and banking details on the same device while phone crime is soaring is a recipe for disaster.

The digital ID card cannot change anything the National insurance card and passports do already. The risk to reward ratio for this policy is too high.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Conduct a leadership review of Labour due to retrospective ILR rule.
background: We urge the government to pressure the Labour Party to conduct a formal leadership review and reconsider the retrospective 10-year ILR policy. This is essential to restore trust among refugees, migrants, and the public, and to ensure fair and humane immigration policies.
additional_details: The retrospective 10-year ILR policy has caused widespread loss of trust in the Labour Party, especially among refugees, migrants, and their communities. This policy undermines the promise of a fair and timely route to settlement and damages Labour’s credibility. A leadership review is necessary to hold the party accountable, restore public confidence, and ensure immigration policies reflect compassion and justice.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for elected representatives or public servants to resign or be removed from office.

We also can't accept petitions that ask for someone to be given a job, or to lose their job.

action: Increase the frequency of trains on the Elizabeth Line
background: I would like the Government and TFL to work together to increase the frequency of trains on the Elizabeth Line especially during peak times. As a passenger, I am very concerned about overcrowding and feel very unsafe. Passengers are tightly packed together which can lead to dangerous situations.
additional_details:
Increased overcrowding can lead to passengers being crushed, sexually abused and pick pocketed. As well as the increase of transmitting infectious diseases.Overcrowded trains can also make emergency evacuations more difficult.
In addition to this, I have witnessed passengers in altercations because of not being able to get on trains or being crushed. 
These concerns highlight the need for adequate train capacity and effective crowd management strategies before a serious accident occurs.
rejection_details:
Petitions must call for a specific action that the UK Government or House of Commons is responsible for. Decisions about London Underground operating times are a matter for TFL, not the Government or House of Commons. As a result it is not possible for the Government or House of Commons to take the action you have requested.

You may therefore wish to start a petition to the London Assembly, asking them to take this matter forward with TFL. You can find out how to do this here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Require bars/pubs to have CCTV covering areas surrounding toilets
background: I believe it should be a requirement for CCTV to cover all areas of the venue. This includes stairwells/corridors leading up to toilet facilities to monitor the safety of customers.
additional_details: This could help prevent spiking and other forms of assault.

action: Hold a general election & public vote on digital ID's.
background: The public of the UK want a general election and public vote on digital ID's, much like the process we had taken during the Brexit Campaign. There is a clear divide within and outside or parliament which requires a vote, not a forced decision made by one person.
additional_details:
Since the Labour party took office, it has failed to meet any of its mandates set out & is slowly implementing laws & acts set out to oppose freedom of speech. We are meant to be living in a free democratic society. The Labour Party does not represent this.

We want:

-An early general election with an additional public vote regarding the implementation on digital ID's. 

If the PM is so confident in his ability and decision making, call a general election, give the people what they want.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions, which call for the same action: 

"Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

"Call an immediate general election" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: Introduce a hand signal for pedestrians to indicate crossing at zebra crossings
background: Include in the Highway code a clear hand signal for pedestrians to indicate they are intending to use the zebra crossing. We think it would help motorists with clearly understanding the intentions of pedestrians at point of crossing; similar to cyclists indicating when turning at junctions.
additional_details: We think introducing a hand signal for pedestrians into the Highway code could save lives and save cost to the NHS. It could make it easier for drivers to gauge the intentions of pedestrians and help to share responsibilities more equally, reduce risk, and increase road safety. It could also strengthen social road user partnership through short and constructive interactions like signals.

action: Include British Citizens Studying Medicine Abroad in NHS Training Prioritisation
background: The Government should work to ensure the inclusion of British citizens who studied medicine abroad in NHS specialty training prioritisation, regardless of graduation date, so they are not treated the same as overseas applicants without UK ties.
additional_details: Some families have funded medical education abroad, expecting their children to return and serve in the NHS. Current proposals prioritise UK graduates and those GMC registered before March 2025, and we are concerned this may exclude British citizens still studying abroad. UK citizenship should be recognised in these proposals to ensure fairness, while strengthening the NHS with graduates whose training cost the UK nothing.

action: Keep Grove House open
background: Provide help to prevent the closure of grove house
rejection_details: We do not know which Grove House you mean. We also cannot accept petitions about things that are outside of the UK Government or Parliament's responsibility.

action: Let the public vote on introducing the digital ID cards
background: We the public have spoken but the government refuses to listen. If the government insist on going ahead with the "digital ID cards" then we the public demand that the government give us the opportunity to vote on whether we want it or not
additional_details: We live in a democracy and we should be allowed to vote on the matter, this will affect the public so the public should be alowed to vote.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Get rid of the 3pm kick off rule in England so we can watch epl games
background: To get rid of the blackout rule, what is the blackout rule? Its a rule where in england you cant watch a premier league game unless your in America i think we should be able to watch any game any time if were paying a subscription such as sky sports

action: Review law on disability-related dismissals and employment tribunals
background: Review law on employers disciplining or dismissing staff for disability-related absence. Review if employment tribunals are making reasonable adjustments, the speed of responses, and treatment of harassment cases and evidence examination. Mandate disability training for judges and panel members.
additional_details: We believe disabled workers are being punished for disability-related absences, some employers are not applying disability trigger points and other parts of the Equality Act 2010 to disabled people, leading to unlawful performance management processes harassment and unfair dismissal. Some self-represented claimants report ignored evidence, no adjustments, and years of delay, which is discriminatory. We feel stronger protections are needed so the law truly safeguards disabled people.

action: UK government to give the people a right to vote on Digital IDs.
background:
Give the people of the united kingdom the right to choose whether they want a digital ID when the majority of people already carry some form of ID.
A simple YES or NO vote let the people decide
additional_details:
We want the right to vote in a democracy and not be ignored by a government who doesn't want to allow people to have there say on the matter.
We don't live in a communist society the last time I checked we had freedom of speech, if a government  is in a position of power it is supposed to listen to and do the bidding of the people.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Allow citizens to carry pepper-sprays, and use it ONLY IN SELF DEFENCE.
background: It’s time to let UK citizens protect themselves! Every day, innocent people especially women walk the streets feeling unsafe. Allowing pepper spray for self-defence would give us a non-lethal, responsible way to deter attackers, and save lives. We deserve the right to feel safe within the law!
additional_details: Citizens of the UK deserve the right to protect themselves safely. Pepper spray is a non-lethal tool used worldwide to stop attackers and prevent violence. Current laws leave many, especially women, defenceless. We need sensible regulation, not prohibition. Sign this petition to support legal, responsible self-defence with pepper spray — for safety, freedom, and peace of mind!
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Legalise pepper spray in England" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742673

action: Reform the UK petitions system
background:
We think that the government doesn't take petitions seriously enough and don't listen to the voice of its citizens, and that the current system is undemocratic.
We think the petitions system should be overhauled to force the government to be held accountable by its people.
additional_details:
We see it all too often - a petition reaching hundreds of thousands, or even millions, of signatures and the government offering the same response outlining nothing more than that they have no plans to change anything. And even if a petition reaches one hundred thousand signatures, there is no requirement for a debate to be held - this is not okay.
We think that a new system should be put in place to give more democratic power to the people living in the country to decide how it's run.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining what specific changes you would like to see made to the e-petitions system.

You may also wish to sign the following petitions which call for similar actions:

Give More Power to Public Petitions to Force the Government to take Action 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736968

Make Government Petitions Legally Binding at a Threshold of Public Signatures

action: ​Hold a national referendum before introducing any form of mandatory Digital ID.
background: ​The UK Government must commit to holding a national referendum before implementing any mandatory Digital ID system. Given the immense public opposition (demonstrated by millions of signatures), this constitutional policy must be approved by the people, not imposed by Parliament.
additional_details:
​A referendum is appropriate because mandatory Digital ID is a profound constitutional change, not routine policy. It violates the UK's historic tradition of rejecting national identity schemes, fundamentally altering the citizen-state relationship and civil liberties.

action: Protect the Right to Live Without a Digital ID

There is currently no explicit legal safeguard to prevent digital ID from being over-relied on by either public or private organisations. Digital ID systems can shape access not only to essential services but also wider participation in society. Legal protections could ensure that people can choose without facing disadvantage or indirect compulsion.
government_response_summary: The Government is introducing a Digital ID system and will legislate for it to be voluntary, and free to access for anyone who wants it. The Government is consulting on the design of that scheme.
government_response_body: The Government has announced that it will offer a new national Digital ID system, free to access for anyone who wants it by the end of the Parliament. The use of Digital ID will be optional and there are no plans to change that.    On 10 March we launched a comprehensive consultation about the design of the Digital ID scheme, which will be open until 5 May. The consultation asks about how we can make the Digital ID a secure, convenient way for people to prove who they are. This will help the government reduce bureaucracy and build the intuitive, efficient, and responsive public services the UK deserves.    Following the consultation we will lead a national conversation about how Digital ID and digital tools can be used to make public services work better for you and to support innovation. The digitisation of government services by some estimates could save up to billions of pounds a year. Supermarkets, banks, retail companies have all chosen to move their services online to a greater degree because they believe it delivers better customer experience, and also because it provides better value for money.    More digital public services will also make them more efficient - because the status quo is expensive. There are costs of processing lots of paper forms, lots of manual payment systems, lots of duplication - every time you have to repeat your story to a different part of the state that’s a second, third or fourth cost to the taxpayer. The numbers across government are huge - the DVLA currently processes 45,000 letters a day, Defra uses 500 different paper forms, HMRC handles 100,000 phone calls a day.    We want you to help us build this, and we want people from all walks of life and from every part of the country to be involved. We want to hear from people about where we can make their lives easier and how we should design a Digital ID which works for them. The consultation on the national digital ID is open until 5 May, and you can complete it at   http://gov.uk/digital-id-consultation.   As we build the new Digital ID system, we are doing it based on three principles:  1. It must be useful: It needs to be easier than the old telephone and paper-based system.  2. It must be secure: It will use the latest security technology, like that used by your bank, will keep your data safer than traditional paper documents – all stored safely on your device, for you to use if you want.   3. It must be for everyone: We won’t leave people behind and will help you if you struggle with technology or can’t prove who you are with a passport, for example.   It will also make everyday interactions easier; from collecting a parcel to going to the cinema. You’ll be able to use your digital proof of identity across the wider economy - including for Right to Work checks. Digital Right to Work checks will be required by the end of the Parliament, tightening up a system that currently allows use of a variety of paper-based documents.   Robust digital checks will help challenge the perception amongst irregular migrants that it is possible to access work, services and benefits in the UK without lawful status. Anyone starting a new job will be able to use the new digital proof of identity for these right to work checks - or do a digital check of other documents such as your passport or eVisa if you prefer. A 2024 report found UK groundwater PFAS at 1,199,000 ng/L near a foam testing site, nearly 12,000 times England and Wales’ 100 ng/L limit. Many other countries have stricter standards. Prevention is cheaper than clean-up, which costs billions. Industry must be held accountable.

action: Remove all VAT on applicable Licensed Taxis
background: Remove VAT charges for all applicable licensed public-hire taxis, including London black cabs. Buses and trains are zero-rated for VAT under the VAT Act 1994. All licensed taxis, regardless of income, should receive the same treatment as public transport to support clean, accessible travel.
additional_details: Many taxi drivers are investing in electric, wheelchair-accessible vehicles that have been reported to have already cut London taxi emissions by 59%. The 20% VAT can add thousands of pounds to costs for self-employed drivers. Buses and trains get VAT relief; we believe taxis deserve the same to help keep cities clean and mobile.

action: Do not implement the Sugary Drinks Refill Policy
background:
The government has recently announced a ban on restaurants from serving bottomless sugary drinks in their menu e.g. Nando’s.

“To protect children’s diets”, when they could easily go into the nearest shop and buy an unlimited amount of sugary drinks. This ban would not benefit the UK at all.
additional_details: To either scrap the idea as a whole or perhaps implement it in a different way, as it can be easily flawed.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Revoke regulations that restrict promotion of high sugar/fat food and drink
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745031

action: Reduce the standard rate of VAT to 15%
background: We want the government to reduce VAT to 15%. We think this could help growth within the economy, put money back into the public pocket, boost business confidence and improve the cost of living.

action: Require gun sellers to verify firearms certificates with police before a sale
background: Create legislation that a gun exchange can only happen after a seller has verified the purchaser's firearm or shotgun certificate with police. This is a simple preventative measure that could help stop individuals with evil intentions purchasing guns with false documentation.

action: Raise the personal tax allowance to the state pension rate
background: Always raise the personal allowance to ensure state pension is free from tax.
additional_details:
We feel that living on just a state pension can be hard and under the current arrangement tax will be payable on the few pounds over the personal allowance.

To support those on state pensions and remove the requirement for tax returns in later years.

action: Put Christ back at the centre of British life.
background: To stand up for the foundations on which this country was built... the Word of God and His son Jesus Christ.
additional_details: Because Jesus is the one with all authority and the British government should submit to Him.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Allow UK Refugee Travel Document holders to obtain visas for Gulf countries
background: I want the UK Government to work with Gulf countries (Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, UAE, Saudi Arabia) so that UK Refugee Travel Document holders can apply for tourist visas and travel there like other UK residents.
additional_details: Most Gulf states don’t recognise UK Refugee Travel Documents, preventing refugees from visiting family or travelling for tourism. The UK should act diplomatically to remove this unfair restriction and ensure equal treatment for refugees.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about entry requirements for other countries are a matter for those countries, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Start school at 9 o’clock everyday

rejection_details: Decisions about the timing of the school day are a matter for schools, not the UK Government and Parliament.

action: Remove the triple lock commitment on pensions and tie increase to inflation only
background: We feel the triple lock on pensions is unaffordable and unjust. We think tying the increase in pensions to inflation only could ensure the living standards of those reliant on the pension are protected, and would be more affordable.
additional_details: Get rid of the triple lock on pensions. We believe it is unaffordable, unjust and unfair on those who pay taxes to fund it.

action: Fund review of access & use of Naltrexone for alcohol dependence & chronic pain
background: We want Government to fund a review into wider access to low-dose Naltrexone for Alcohol Dependence and as a treatment for chronic pain. Studies have shown it’s cost-effective, NICE-approved for alcohol dependency, and it could help reduce NHS strain.
additional_details:
We think wider access could help save lives and public money—act now to remove barriers.
We think low-dose naltrexone can help manage chronic pain and addiction, offering a safer, non-opioid option. Alcohol and drug misuse cost the UK over £32 billion annually. Drug treatment yields £4–£21 return per £1 spent. Expanding access could save NHS and social care budgets. Fair access is a public health and economic priority.

action: Fund and save the buszy and south bank diy skatepark in Milton Keynes

additional_details: Even just a few hundred would be enough too contact a ramp company and get a small half pipe or something similar.the most important point is just keeping them there though and not having apartments built, too lose the parks would be too lose years of skating history not too mention it would kill the opportunity for more people too enjoy the community and learn too skateboard

action: Priority to house homeless British people before illegal immigrants in hotels
background: Stop prioritising illegal immigrants with no documents over British people who are homeless whether they be veterans or those that have fallen on hard times
additional_details: Because these people are in Britain legally..can be identified and half of them have fought for this country!! Stop making illegal immigrants with no papers to identify them a priority!!

action: Make it illegal to keep or sell social animals like guinea pigs alone
background: We call on the government to introduce legislation preventing pet shops and breeders from rehoming social animals, such as guinea pigs or rabbits, without a suitable companion. Owners must keep these species in compatible pairs or groups, with exceptions only for bereavement or planned re-pairing.
additional_details: Guinea pigs and other social species need companionship to express natural behaviours and avoid stress or loneliness. In countries like Switzerland and Austria, keeping them alone is illegal. We should follow this example to uphold animal welfare standards and stop the sale of solitary animals. Limited exceptions could apply when an animal is adopted as a companion replacement or where the adopter commits to pairing within a set time frame.

action: Put some kind of speeding bumps or cameras on nuttall street.
background: I would like to get some sort of speeding camera or bumps on my street specifically the bend as my house is the first one that would get hit. But also because if they slow down there then there’s less chance of a crash because they would be able to see the road in front of them and have time to slow
additional_details: I would like to have the speeding solution in place because there has been a crash in front of my house where the car was crashed into another house. The drivers here drive way too fast and it will end in a fatality very soon!

action: Introduce knife arches in every secondary school!
background: I would like funding to be made to every secondary school to install knife arches.

We need to provide a preventative in school, 1 been educating them and the other been a knife arch to detect anything before any actions can be carries out. action: Stop teaching in depth and confusing sex education to under P7 school children!
background:
Stop teaching P3 and younger about the terminology lesbian, gay and bisexual. Stop showing videos like heartbeat of boys falling in love, these are children and should be allowed to remain kids as long as possible.

Stop teaching P4's in depth how babies are made, cared for and how to have sex.
additional_details:
Children should be children. Learning the indepth terminologies for gay, lesbian, bisexual is unnecessary and confusing. Kids are focused on playing, making friends, sports, gaming not dating or falling in love in primary school.

Why does any 8 year old need to know how babies are made, cared for or how to have sex? This is something P7 and above should know, stop trying to strip our children of innocence and make them curious about adult behaviour, its barbaric and enraging for parents.

Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.

action: Abolish Feudal Tenure and implement Allodial Tenure (same as Scottish Act 2000)
background: As they have under Abolition of Feudal Tenure etc. (Scotland) Act 2000, we demand all titles in England and Wales are amended to the "Allodial" Tenure and hold absolute title.

action: MPs and their families of eligible age be conscripted first before anyone else
background: Make it a condition of mandating or parliamentary voting on conscription, that all MPs of eligible age, and their children and families of eligible age, are conscripted first, and sent to the war zone, with evidence to prove this, before anyone else is conscripted.
additional_details: To concentrate the minds of those in authority, of the magnitude and the consequences of voting for the imposition of military conscription.
rejection_details: The Government has not announced any plans to introduce conscription.

action: Increase the £30,000 tax-free limit on settlement agreements
background: The £30,000 tax-free limit on settlement and redundancy payments has not increased since 1988. We think it should be raised to reflect inflation and indexed each year, to ensure fair treatment for workers facing job loss or redundancy.
additional_details:
We ask the Government to:

Increase the tax-free limit from £30,000 to a fair, inflation-adjusted level.

Automatically index the threshold to inflation each year.

We think this change would restore fairness, support people through job loss, and reduce the tax burden on those already under financial and emotional stress.

action: Bring back Birmingham's 40 mph Speed Limit!!
background: We want the council to bring back the 40 mph speed limit on major Birmingham roads, after this month's cut to 30 mph.
additional_details:
BCC has cut our 40 mph roads down to 30, claiming it makes us safer. Studies show dropping just 10 mph doesn’t make roads safer, it just causes traffic jams, longer commutes, higher fuel use and slower emergency response times. 

Our cars aren’t built to crawl at 20–30 mph. That strain damages engines, shortens vehicle life and the council won’t be paying our repair bills. 

Today it’s 30 mph. Next, it’ll be 20. BCC consulted residents, only 35% agreed and they still went ahead with the change!!

action: Grant UK Citizenship to Long-Term Residents Without Expensive Tests
background: Ask the UK Government to change its citizenship policy so that nationalised residents who have lived and contributed to society in the UK for years are automatically granted UK citizenship without needing to pass expensive tests.
additional_details:
Many of these individuals have built their lives here, paid taxes, worked in essential services, and contributed to our communities. Yet they face financial and administrative barriers to becoming citizens, including high application fees and the Life in the UK test.
People, effectively British should not be excluded by complex or costly processes. Recognising their commitment promotes fairness, integration, and  British values.
We call for citizenship for nationalised UK residents
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Exempt 10+ year UK residents/taxpayers from the Life in the UK Test
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729228

action: Increase minimum sentences for knife crimes including possession and use
background:
We would like the law changed and stiffer min sentences given out for knife crime:

- 5 years in prison for being in possession of a knife.
- 10 years in prison for using a knife to causing harm to a person.
- 25 years for taking a life with a knife.

action: Disallow fixed charges on fresh water and wastewater on water bill.
background: Many water companies have increased prices of supply without reinvestment in the system. Raw sewage has been pumped into the environment where the clean-up is again billed to customers as price increases. Bonuses and dividends should not come from such fixed or standing charges.
additional_details: Do not let the utility companies use the customers as their "cash cow". Customers should have value for money for the services provided where they are operated in a fair manner. Ban the practice of using fixed charges. We believe customers already pay the amount due and fixed charges are free income for the utility companies.

action: Apply the 10-year ILR rule only to new arrivals, not current residents
background: We call on the UK Government to apply the 10-year ILR rule only to new arrivals, ensuring that current residents can continue their path to permanent residency and citizenship under the existing 5-year rules.
additional_details: Applying the 10-year ILR rule to people who are already living in the UK would be unfair and disruptive. Many residents have built their lives, careers, and families here based on the existing 5-year rules. Retroactively changing the rules would create unnecessary hardship and instability. Implementing the 10-year requirement only for future arrivals protects the rights and stability of current residents while ensuring fair treatment for newcomers.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Make a law to protect ILR from abolition and retrospective changes" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742864

action: Review punishment of Child Sex Offences
background: Review sentencing to ensure penalties reflect the severity and long-term harm of child sexual abuse. Offenders convicted of child sexual offences must serve their full terms in Category B prisons or higher. There should also be mandatory lifetime registration and electronic monitoring.
additional_details: We call on MPs to act with integrity and courage. We believe silence and inaction in the face of injustice betray our nation’s moral duty. A report estimates that 1 in 10 children suffer abuse before turning 16, that is over 3 pupils per classroom. We feel victims’ suffering is overlooked by those in power and tolerated in the interest of budgeting. This must not stand. Protecting children is not negotiable.

action: End the weaponisation of abuse allegations in family court
background: We want the Government to reform family court procedures so that unproven allegations cannot be used to restrict a parent’s rights or contact with their child. Decisions should be based on credible evidence following fair and balanced investigation.
additional_details: In family court, allegations of harm or abuse can lead to immediate restrictions on a parent’s contact, even when no evidence has been verified. While protecting children from genuine harm is essential, safeguards are needed to prevent misuse. False or unfounded claims can cause lasting emotional harm to families and undermine trust in the justice system. In some cases, such allegations are used as a form of control, effectively weaponising the process against the other parent.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We're not sure what you mean by unproven allegations or what specific changes you'd like to see.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, giving more details about what kind of reform you would like to see.

action: Introduce a PM recall system to the UK
background: Introduce a PM recall system allowing the public to trigger a re-election if the Prime Minister loses significant public support, ensuring accountability and democratic choice between elections.
additional_details: Citizens currently have no direct way to remove an unpopular Prime Minister between elections. A recall system would allow a petition for re-election to trigger a no-confidence vote, requiring 1 million signatures on the petition and at least 65% public turnout on the vote, strengthening democratic accountability and giving the public a real voice.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions, which call for similar action: 

"Give the British Public the Right to Vote No Confidence in the Government" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734311

"Pass a law that triggers an early General Election via a public petition" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739383

action: Reform the petition system: Parliament vote at 1M signatures & referendum at 5M
background: Reform the petition system so that petitions reaching 1 million signatures trigger a parliamentary vote on the issue within 6 months, and petitions reaching 5 million signatures trigger a national referendum. This can help ensure the public’s voice leads to action, not just debate.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
additional_details: At present a digital ID petition has nearly 3 million signatures, the Online Safety Act petition exceeded 500,000, and multiple petitions on illegal migration and benefits have huge support - yet we feel the government has dismissed them all. Currently, ministers can ignore millions of concerned citizens after a brief debate. We believe mandatory votes at 1M signatures and referendums at 5M would force government to act on issues the public cares deeply about, restoring accountability to a broken system.

action: Invest in NHS supported Dental Practices
background: Provide NHS practices with full funding so ALL eligible citizens can gain access to required Dental procedures under NHS funding.  Increase NHS Dental Practices throughout the UK.  Current access to Dental Practices is almost impossible for eligible patients and we have the right to NHS treatment.
additional_details: This is a national crisis. Increased NHS funding to ALL dental practices must be provided to enable all lower income patients access to Dental Care.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Fund free NHS dentist treatment for all UK Citizens
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741025

Increase funding for NHS dentists and the NHS dentistry system
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743481

action: Put the decision of the new digital ID card to a public vote like Brexit.
background: Thiers alot of concerns towards the new digital ID card the main concern is that it could could potentially become a form of control so that being said i feel that the best way forward is to put it to a public vote the public vote being final it on my seems right as it is directly affecting the us.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Allow women to have smear tests from 18 if they choose
background: Lower the age limit from 25 to 18 for smear tests.
additional_details:
So many young girls/ women have problems, some have died before having a smear test.
Starting this at 18 and allowing women to have a choice to have this done earlier if they feel they have issues will give more women a chance to get ahead of health issues in that area.
Being told a a smear would not be looked at unless you are 25 and therefore they refuse to do them. This could potentially save womens lives.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Fund cervical screening every 3 yrs or more frequently, lower minimum age to 18" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730008

action: Limit benefits/police protection available to former Prime Ministers to 5 years
background: It seems obvious that ordinary people will be asked to give up more to reduce the deficit. We ask that Parliament also seeks to reduce the Public Duty Costs Allowance that former prime ministers (PMs) can claim once they leave office.
additional_details:
Ex-PMs can claim up to £115,000 per year, for the rest of their lives, to help with the cost of public duties. It is a huge lifetime benefit for a temporary role. This assistance should be limited to 5 years after a PM leaves office.
 
Ex-PMs also receive lifetime police protection. Protection when abroad is costly and - currently - can be provided even if foreign travel is undertaken for personal financial gain.  When ex-PMs travel abroad, protection should only be provided when travel is purely for official business, not for personal income.

action: Bring the retirement age for women back down to at least 62 yrs old
background: Drop the retirement age for women. We have suffered enough through life. What with menstrual cycles, babies, menopause, our bodies have been bashed. Most women I know, don't get a goodnight sleep due to menopause symptoms, hot flushes, mood swings, and many many more symptoms.
additional_details: So we can have a few years to rest, and enjoy life a little.

action: Immediately send millions in humanitarian aid to Gaza
background: We would like millions in aid to be sent to gaza, in light of the recent ceasefire agreement, the recognition of the palestinian state and the widespread evidence of starvation/famine from notable human rights organisations. enormous amounts of humanitarian aid is required
additional_details:
Everyone has seen the mounting evidence for starvation in the gaza strip, sending in humanitarian aid including food, medicine and infrastructure to help with what will undoubtably be associated refeeding syndrome.
The lack of action from this and the previous parliment has directly led to the worsening of these issues, reconciliation of this fact must start immediately with massive amounts of humanitarian aid.
Immediately sending £100m+ in aid would be a start (Aid to ukraine is £21.8b as now)
rejection_details:
The UK already plans to spend £101m aid in OPTs this year: https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2025-04-24/47670

You may wish to sign the following petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737736

action: Stop the proposed extension of public opening hours under the Licensing Act 2003
background: We call on the Government to abandon plans to extend the permitted opening hours of licensed premises under the Licensing Act 2003.
additional_details:
There are concerns that longer hours for pubs, bars and clubs could increase late-night noise and disturbance for nearby residents; heighten the risk of vandalism and rowdy behaviour; place further pressure on police and hospital services; and damage the broader economy through increased absenteeism and reduced productivity among working people.
 
We therefore urge the Government to maintain the existing licensing limits in the interests of public order, community wellbeing and economic stability.

action: Give homeless people living in nature legal status, address, work and healthcare
background: I want the Government to recognise people who choose to live in nature as citizens with full rights. They should have access to a legal address for documents, healthcare, benefits, and employment, without being forced into shelters or housing
additional_details: Many people choose to live in nature for personal, spiritual, or economic reasons, yet they lose access to basic rights like healthcare, work, and benefits. They are treated as invisible citizens. Recognising their way of life would protect their dignity, allow them to contribute to society, and reduce exclusion. Everyone deserves equal rights and legal recognition, no matter where or how they choose to live.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you're concerned about the rights of people without addresses, however we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. For example, we're not sure what specific changes you would like to see made or what you mean by recognising people as citizens. 

A fixed address is not required to claim benefits such as Universal Credit. You can find out more here:  
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/universal-credit-and-homeless-people/applying-for-universal-credit-information-for-homeless-people

Homeless patients are already entitled to register with a GP using a temporary address or the practice address. You can find out more here:
https://www.bma.org.uk/advice-and-support/gp-practices/managing-your-practice-list/patient-registration

The Financial Inclusion Strategy includes measures for homeless people to access ID and banking through pilot schemes. You can find out more here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/financial-inclusion-strategy/financial-inclusion-strategy

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do. For example, you could start a petition calling for the Government to fund post boxes for homeless people, if that's something that you'd like to see.

action: Stop changes to the large programme uplift funding to protect our education
background: The Large Programme Uplift (LPU) has been changed to only support the transition of students to "Priority Sectors" of industry. This Programme is being used by many state schools to support a variety of academic goals, not just "math".
additional_details: The government should focus on levelling up education, regardless if it is in academia, trade schools, STEM, or whatever pushes individuals to excel within their desires, goals, dreams and capabilities. Reorienting LPU impacts funding from other programmes, like the International Baccalaureate Diploma and we want to ensure funding remains in place.

action: Fund primary pupil assessments for ADHD before secondary school
background: Fund mandatory ADHD and learning-needs assessments for all pupils in England before they start secondary school, so every child’s learning profile is understood and supported early, improving education and wellbeing outcomes.
additional_details: Too many children with ADHD, autism, or learning differences go through education without being identified, especially girls and pupils from disadvantaged backgrounds. Early assessment could allow support to start sooner, help reduce exclusions, and help every child reach their full potential in education and life.

action: Introduce a Smartphone-Free Childhood Trial for All Children Under 16 in the UK
background: We urge the UK Government to launch a nationwide trial encouraging families to raise children under 16 without smartphones, protecting them from digital dangers and nurturing their mental and emotional development.
additional_details:
Children under 16 are increasingly exposed to the risks of phone. 
This initiative will:
✅ Protect children from online predators, trafficking networks, and harmful digital content
🧠 Improve mental well-being by reducing screen dependency and social media pressure
📚 Encourage reading, imaginative play, and outdoor exploration
🎨 Foster creativity and independent thinking
 🗣️ Strengthen family bonds through real conversations and shared experiences
😴 Promote better sleep and reduce anxiety
rejection_details:
We call on Government to urgently revise the mobile phone in schools guidance
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726477

action: Reverse Funding Cuts to IB State Schools
background: We call on the government to reverse the changes to the Large Program Uplift programme which cuts funding for IB state schools since from the 2026-2027 academic year the programme will only cover "normal maths and high value A level programmes"
additional_details: Removing funding from the IB means 5,000 students are losing access to programmes critical to future success. Without the LPU funding, it will be extremely difficult for state schools to get the funding to provide the IB, meaning it would only be available at private schools. The savings that the government would make from this change are minimal, but they would be affecting the lives of thousands of students and many schools who would have to remake resources and retrain teachers.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop changes to the large programme uplift funding to protect our education
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746219

action: Pause and review the use of EdTech in schools and early years settings
background: Pause all pupil-facing 1:1 device and EdTech use in schools and early years settings—except for children with specific technology needs—unless and until reputable, independent assessments confirm both net educational benefit and no unacceptable safeguarding, health or wellbeing risks for children.
additional_details: We feel that 1:1 devices and EdTech platforms have been rapidly adopted by schools despite virtually no evidence of net learning benefit. Reputable independent studies show device use can negatively impact academic attainment, particularly for disadvantaged children. Some 1:1 devices and platforms are linked to an increase in bullying, access to inappropriate content, safeguarding and data privacy issues and an array of negative physical, emotional and social health impacts.

action: Do not introduce road tax for classic vehicles.
background: Currently under the 40 year old rule, a range of classic vehicle types registered before 8th January 1985 are exempt from paying road tax with examples including cars, motorbikes and steam engines. The UK government must ensure and guarantee that this rule remains in place indefinitely.
additional_details: The Chancellor is considering scrapping vehicle excise duty (VED) or road tax exemption for classic cars to plug a fiscal hole in the treasury estimated to raise over £100 million per year and will affect over 300K road going cars alone according to the DVLA. These vehicle are insured for limited road mileage and mainly for summer shows. Enthusiasts will regard classic VED as yet another infringement on civil freedoms when most are already taxed on other vehicles. This exemption must be upheld.
rejection_details:
We think your petition is covered by Government or Parliament action already. 

The Government hasn't announced it will be introducing road tax for classic vehicles. 

Chief Secretary to the Treasury, James Murray MP responded to a Written Question on this matter in February 2025: 

https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2025-02-04/28704

action: Introduce minimum sentence of 5 years for sexual offences and ban appeals
background: Require that anyone who commits an offence relating anything sexual, including photos, gets an automatic prison sentence of a minimum of 5 years if found guilty. There should be no right to appeal.
additional_details:
Victims of sexual offences often don’t ever get over what’s happened to them and it does ruin lives. They have to live with it for the rest of their lives. 

Children are supposed to be protected by adults. Child victims have no choice and this can cause serious, life-changing trauma.

action: Increase speed limits back to 30MPH instead of the 20MPH
background: Take the 20mph zones and increase the limits back to 30mph as there’s no need to have 20mph anywhere that isn’t near a school it’s self and they have the flashing 20s which is sufficient
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Ban 20mph speed limits with limited exceptions 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744650

action: Make Housing Fair: Reform Unjust Bidding and Banding Policies for People in Need
background: I’ve waited years to return to Cheshire, where my support is. With disabilities and mental health needs, I ask the UK Government to make housing fairer and faster.
additional_details: We call on the UK Government to reform housing bidding and banding rules so disabled people, those with mental health needs, domestic abuse survivors, and people with real ties to an area are treated fairly and urgently. Current systems cause long delays and unfair outcomes. We need clear national standards, faster decisions, and equal treatment for all.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

The Housing Act 1996 governs the allocation of local authority housing stock in England. Local authorities must have an allocation scheme for determining priorities between applicants for housing which sets out the procedure to be followed when allocating housing accommodation. Local authorities set their own rules on banding and how housing is allocated, not the Government or Parliament.  

However, relating to this petition, local authorities are already required to give priority (reasonable preference) to: people who are homeless; people occupying insanitary or overcrowded housing or otherwise living in unsatisfactory housing condition; people who need to move on medical or welfare grounds (including any grounds relating to a disability); people who need to move to a particular locality in the district of the authority, where failure to meet that need would cause hardship (to themselves or to others) 

More information on housing allocation can be found here:
https://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/SN06397/SN06397.pdf

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Reform the Public Duty Costs Allowance for Former Prime Ministers
background: Reform the Public Duty Costs Allowance for ex-Prime Ministers. We do not think that taxpayers should fund what we see as lifelong perks for those who failed in their duty. We think reform will ensure only long-serving, responsible leaders get limited, justified support for genuine public duties.

action: Stop water rate hikes — hold investors & Directors accountable

additional_details:
Water companies successfully appealed and forced extra price hikes, despite OFWATS 2025-30 tariff limits.   The CMA has provisionally approved average additional rises, granting £556 million more in revenue. From CUSTOMERS, not the shareholders. This gives companies further power to burden customers rather than shareholders.
Failing water companies should be allowed to fail and be brought into public ownership. Shareholders must be held to account, not households. Enough is Enough
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about price controls for water are a matter for Ofwat, not the UK Government or Parliament.

Under the Water Industry Act 1991, Ofwat has a statutory duty to make sure that companies are able to finance the proper carrying out of their functions. In setting price controls Ofwat's aim is to allow for a return on capital that is no more than necessary for an efficiently run company to get the funding they need, and that ensures customers only pay for a reasonable level of financing costs.

You can find out more about Ofwat's price controls here:
https://www.ofwat.gov.uk/regulated-companies/price-review/

Abolish and replace Ofwat, and new legislation on investment in the water system

action: Change voting to a rank based system to allow complete freedom when voting.
background: Replace the First-Past-the-Post system for general elections with a preferential voting system. This would allow voters to rank candidates by order of preference, ensuring their vote is used to elect a candidate they support, even if their first choice is eliminated.
additional_details: First-Past-the-Post forces tactical voting and creates millions of "wasted" votes, leading to unrepresentative governments. A ranked system makes more votes count and allows people to vote for their true preference without fear of "spoiling" the result. action: Allow pharmacist-supervised over-the-counter access to asthma reliever inhalers

rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 
 
We're not sure how exactly you'd like the House of Commons to change its Code of Conduct. 

The Procedural Protocol states that the Commissioner cannot investigate complaints about MP’s “views or opinions, including those expressed on social media” unless he is investigating a breach of Rule 11 of the Code of Conduct. That says that “Members shall never undertake any action which would cause significant damage to the reputation and integrity of the House of Commons as a whole, or of its Members generally.” This is because, except for Rule 11, the Code of Conduct does not regulate MP’s views or how they express their opinions, and therefore the Commissioner cannot investigate complaints about their views or opinions.

action: Allow charities to rescue dogs with docked tails under the Animal Welfare Bill
background: We ask Parliament to include an exemption in the Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Bill for registered charities and approved, responsible rescue organisations to rehome adult, disease tested dogs, who were previously docked as working hunting dogs abroad.
additional_details:
Without an exemption, we can no longer rescue Italian Spinoni, and organisations cannot help many other working breeds like pointers, spaniels and griffons.
 
These dogs have sadly lost their tails, docked for working purposes, not fashion, and are often treated abroad as disposable hunting tools. We support this Bill and ask to help improve it in crafting legislation that protects welfare while preventing loopholes. Please involve us, and let us continue to help these dogs.
government_response_summary: We will work with stakeholders to consider appropriate exemptions as we deliver the relevant regulations. Exemptions will need to be finely balanced against the risk of creating loopholes.
government_response_body: As outlined in our manifesto, the government is committed to ending puppy smuggling. That is why we were pleased to support the Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act 2025.  The Act will close loopholes in the non-commercial pet travel rules that are abused by unscrupulous traders. It also gives the government powers to prevent the supply of low-welfare pets to the United Kingdom. This includes the power to make regulations prohibiting dogs and cats being brought into Great Britain with non-exempted mutilations, such as docked tails and cropped ears, and the power to specify appropriate exemptions in future regulations.   These prohibitions and any appropriate exemptions will be delivered via secondary legislation at a later date. We will continue to work with stakeholders and consider their feedback – for example, on the impact of the regulations on rescue and rehoming – to help shape these exemptions. The government is clear, however, that any exemptions to these measures will need to be finely balanced against the risk of creating loopholes that could be exploited by bad actors.  In the meantime, owners and importers can find up to date guidance on bringing dogs to Great Britain on the gov.uk website, available at: https://www.gov.uk/bring-pet-to-great-britain.  Department for Environment, Food and Rural

action: Keep 5-Year ILR and Restrict Access to Benefits for New ILR Holders
background: The Government should keep the current 5-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) and restrict access to government benefits for new ILR holders.
additional_details: Extending the ILR route to 10 years would unfairly affect thousands of Skilled Worker visa holders who moved to the UK based on existing 5-year rules, disrupting their plans, families, and financial stability. The Government should keep the 5-year ILR route and ensuring new ILR holders demonstrate financial independence before accessing public benefits. We think this protect fairness and stability.
government_response_summary: As set out in the Immigration White Paper, the default qualifying period doubles to 10 years. We welcome views on other measures, including access to benefits, via the earned settlement consultation.
government_response_body: Settlement in the UK is a privilege and not a right. It is a prerequisite for becoming a British citizen and brings lifelong benefits. It marks an important step in integrating and contributing to local communities and the wider country.  Under the current system, individuals qualify for settlement primarily on the basis of the length of time they have spent in the UK alongside a knowledge of life test which is used to verify knowledge of British customs, history, traditions, laws and political system.  These criteria alone do not reflect our strongly held belief that people should contribute to the economy and society before gaining settled status in the UK. Moreover, they fail to promote integration, which limits the wider benefit from long term migration into the UK and increases pressure on public services.  We therefore intend to fundamentally reform our settlement rules for the first time in over 50 years. The Immigration White Paper, published on 12 May 2025, set out that the default qualifying period for settlement would be increased from five to ten years. It also included proposals for a new ‘earned settlement’ model which are subject to consultation.  The consultation on the ‘earned settlement’ model launched on 20 November 2025 and will run for 12 weeks until 12 February 2026. It is open to anyone who wishes to share their views, including individuals, organisations and other stakeholders who may be affected by, or have an interest in, the proposed changes.  We are proposing to increase the baseline qualifying period for settlement to 15 years for those on the Skilled Worker route in a role below RQF level 6 (equivalent to a bachelor’s degree).   In the next five years, settlement volumes are forecast to increase significantly, due to the unprecedented level of migration to the UK in recent years. Between 2021 and 2024, there was significant growth in lower-skilled migration on work routes, particularly on the Health and Social Care visa, which is estimated to make up 47% of settlement grants in 2028.  Individuals will have the opportunity to reduce the qualifying period to settlement based on contributions to the UK economy and society.  Speaking English at degree level, earning a high salary and being employed in specific public service roles would result in a reduction. However, where a person has claimed public funds or committed immigration offences, they would face a penalty of extra years.   We are also proposing that benefits and social housing might not be available to new migrants granted settled status and that instead they should be reserved for those who have achieved British citizenship, easing the pressure on public finances.  For those who are on a pathway to settlement but have not yet been granted settled status, we are consulting on transitional arrangements for these individuals.   We would encourage anyone with an interest in the proposals, including the petitioners who have taken the time to sign this petition, to contribute to the consultation. We realise the significance of these proposals to people and we will listen carefully to what they tell us.  Further details on the proposals and the link to respond to the consultation can be found here: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement  Home Office

The IB says: “If the Department for Education carries out this plan, its savings will be minimal but there will be significant costs to students in loss of choice and opportunity in a globally competitive environment.” IB students are 3 times more likely than matched A level students to enrol in a top-20 higher education institution.

action: Ban plastic plants and flowers, except for in exceptional circumstances
background: Introduce legislation to prohibit the sale, import and public-sector procurement of artificial (plastic) plants and flowers. Exceptions could include situations where real plants cannot be used, for example in ICU/isolation rooms, transplant/haematology units and care homes.
additional_details:
Set a phase-out date of 24 months and support the reuse or repair of existing displays. Plastic plants create unnecessary and avoidable waste, produce microplastics, increase fossil-fuel demand, and mislead about greening.
 
Real plants clean air, support pollinators, can improve wellbeing and back British and European growers. A time-limited phase-out could cut emissions and litter, save disposal costs and make public spaces genuinely greener, without affecting legitimate medical or safety uses.

action: Reverse the change to International Baccalaureate funding for state schools.
background: I want the UK Government to reverse their decision on cutting funding for International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme in state schools because it does not bring back lots of money into the economy, degrades international education and removes an incentive for foreign students to learn in the UK.
additional_details: Funding the IB Diploma in state schools gives students access to a globally respected qualification that builds critical thinking, leadership, and global awareness—skills essential to the UK workforce. IB students are 3× more likely to attend top UK universities and 40% more likely to earn top degrees than A Level peers. Removing funding limits opportunity, reduces social mobility, and weakens the UK’s talent pipeline.

action: Abolish the 'tooth tax': remove VAT on children's toothbrushes and toothpaste.
background: Abolish the 20% VAT on children's oral care products like toothbrushes and toothpaste. Make these essential items zero-rated for VAT (like children's clothing). With an estimated 4.3 million children in poverty, this could ease pressure on families and reduce NHS costs from preventable tooth decay.
additional_details: We think children's oral health is in crisis. Tooth decay is the leading cause of hospital admissions for 5-9-year-olds in England. In 2022-23, 47,000 tooth extractions occurred in NHS hospitals for under-19s, costing £40.7m annually. Two-thirds of these were preventable. With many families unable to afford basic oral hygiene tools, removing VAT could ease financial barriers, reduce NHS pressure and improve access to essential oral health products. Prevention is better and cheaper than cure.

action: Keep the 5-year Indefinite Leave to Remain ILR for ex-Gurkhas & their families
background: We want the UK Government to keep the current 5-year Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) pathway, for ex-Gurkhas who left the armed forces post 1997, their spouses, and family members. Gurkhas have served Britain with loyalty and deserve fairness, stability, and respect for past commitments.
additional_details: Gurkhas have served Britain with courage and loyalty for over 200 years. Many have settled here with their families and contributed to UK society. We believe extending the ILR period to 10 years would cause hardship and break trust, and that the Government must honour its historic promise and keep the 5-year ILR route to ensure fairness, stability, and respect for those who have already sacrificed so much for this country..

action: Offer to cede the JFK Memorial site at Runnymede to the United States
background: We call upon His Majesty’s Government to explore, in consultation with the United States Government, the possibility of formally transferring sovereignty of the John F. Kennedy Memorial site at Runnymede to the United States as a unique and enduring symbol of Anglo-American friendship.
additional_details:
The JFK Memorial was presented to the United States in 1965 for perpetual use, commemorating President Kennedy’s legacy and the shared democratic values of our nations. While the site remains under UK sovereignty, it already functions as a perpetual gift and is maintained by the U.S. government.

A formal cession of this small parcel of land would have no practical impact on British territorial integrity but would represent a powerful diplomatic gesture, reaffirming the “special relationship”.

action: Allow a public vote on the laws on facial recognition cameras in public spaces.
background: Any British citizen, resident, or visitor, should have control to consent or opt-out to the scanning their biometric info in public. Private companies planning to trace this data should have no legal right to do so, and safeguards should be implemented urgently to protect how, and who can access it.
additional_details: The UK government and MET police have already trialled AI CCTV without public consent, and now installed permanent cameras in Coventry with no clear information on data protection, AI training, or a public vote. No third party can be guaranteed as secure, posing a major safety risk in the event of data breaches. People should be allowed in public spaces with the knowledge that their biometrics are not being stored, or used to train AI technology, which breaks the expectation of GDPR regulations.

We think children need both parents and it would help stop parental alienation, and having parents in a child's life helps them better progress in life.

This should guarantee at least partial pay for the full duration of sickness, so workers aren’t - in our view - financially punished for being unwell.
additional_details:

Many workers may use annual leave to cover sickness, leaving them without proper rest or holidays.
This can harm mental health and increases stress.

We think no one should have to choose between their health and paying bills. 
We believe mandatory enhanced sick pay would protect workers’ wellbeing and promote public health.

action: Legislate crimes motivated by misogyny are hate crimes, fund support & training
background: The Government should amend the Sentencing Act 2020 to record crimes motivated by misogyny as hate crimes and introduce tougher laws for online abuse, and fund the training of police and prosecutors, and support for survivors in education.
additional_details: We want the Government to tackle anti-feminist hate groups that target and radicalise young people online. Many young women, especially students, face harassment, assault, and online abuse. Misogyny can fuel this violence, yet we believe current laws fail to address it directly. Recognising misogyny as a hate crime could protect victims, deter offenders, and send a clear message that gender-based hostility is unacceptable. It could also validate survivors’ experiences and help create safer environments in education and online, where young people are most vulnerable.
government_response_summary: The Government has tabled an amendment at Lords Report Stage of the Crime and Policing Bill to extend the aggravated offences in the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
government_response_body: Hate crime legislation in England and Wales covers five protected characteristics: race, religion, sexual orientation, transgender identity and disability. Sex, or presumed sex, has not previously been covered, meaning that ‘misogyny’ currently falls outside the scope of the hate crime legislative framework.  Under the proposed amendment, sex will be added to the list of protected characteristics under the aggravated offences in the Crime and Disorder Act 1998, ensuring that offences motivated by hostility towards someone’s sex or presumed sex can be charged as aggravated where the evidence supports it. This amendment delivers the Government’s manifesto commitment to level up protections by expanding the aggravated offence framework so that hostility based on sexual orientation, disability, transgender identity, or sex or presumed sex attracts the same penalties as offences motivated by racist or religious hatred, thereby creating parity across protected characteristics.  Aggravated offences are crime types such as assault, criminal damage, harassment, stalking and certain public order offences where it can be proven that the offender was motivated by hostility towards a protected characteristic. These offences carry higher maximum sentences than their non‑aggravated equivalents. The offences mirror the (non‑hate crime) equivalents already covered under sections 28-32 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998. No new criminal offences are being created; the amendment simply extends the existing aggravated versions to additional protected characteristics.  The Government keeps hate crime legislation under review, strengthening it where necessary to protect those most at risk. As part of this ongoing commitment to ensuring the framework remains robust the Home Secretary announced the Independent Review of Public Order and Hate Crime following the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester in October 2025.   The purpose of the Review is to test whether public order and hate crime law remains fit for purpose, assess whether thresholds and safeguards are right and effective, and recommend reforms that improve consistency, protect rights and reassure affected communities. The Review is due to report its findings by the end of March.  Tackling violence against women and girls (VAWG) is a top priority for this Government. “Freedom from Violence and Abuse: a cross-government strategy to build a safer society for women and girls”, published on 18th December 2025, sets out the strategic direction and concrete actions to prevent violence and abuse, pursue perpetrators, and support victims, and to deliver our unprecedented commitment to halve VAWG in a decade.  Prevention and early intervention are fundamental to our approach. We will tackle the root causes of these crimes instead of only responding to the impacts, including supporting our education system to teach children about respectful and healthy relationships and consent.  We recognise the destructive role that misogynistic attitudes can play in society, including the impact they can have on men and boys. Tackling entrenched societal issues like misogyny requires a whole society approach, and we are working across government, public services, the private sector and charities to achieve our ambitions.   The commitments made by the Government through the strategy to tackle the root causes of these crimes can be found in “Freedom from Violence and Abuse: a cross-government strategy to build a safer society for women and girls Vol 2.”, available at https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/697c7e21aacd0dc9777b502a/31.260_VAWG_02_Action_Plan_Slip_FINAL_v3_WEB_290126.pdf   Home Office
