additional_details:
I want to hold this petition for reducing the likelihood of loud noise induced anxiety for animal wellbeing, as well as, people who find loud bangs distressing. Loud noises induced anxiety and distress in a wide group of humans and non-human animals. Providing laws around how and when they can be released, allowing scheduled events and specific times of year, reduces this stress significantly. 
By introducing laws and legislation people can be held accountable for their actions.

action: Fund lower train fares
background: I believe the prices of trains are horrendous and make it difficult for many people to use this to travel. It can be cheaper to travel by car for many, which can increase unwanted emissions.
additional_details: We want the Government to the fund lower train fares, particularly for younger people and students who may struggle to afford travel. Prices should be lowered to help reduce cost of living pressures, as so many people are struggling at the moment.

action: Grant interim exemptions to all seized dogs with no prior history of aggression
background: We would like for the Government to grant interim exemptions for all dogs seized from their owners under the XL Bully ban who have no history of aggression. This could allow for dogs to remain in the custody of their owners at home and not in kennels.
additional_details: We believe dogs deserve to remain in safe and loving homes whilst waiting for a decision from the courts. Many beloved pets may be kept for long periods of time in kennels, which can cost the owners thousands of pounds. Many dogs get no satisfactory interaction, and many have been returned home underweight, scared and uncared for. Many owners are scared to lose their pets to kennels for an unknown amount of time and having the interim exemption in place could see more owners come forward.

additional_details:
When SA’s are booked standard FAA or Equity contracts are used. 

Although productions sign up to this, often many of the rules are overlooked from the initial booking where they can cancel us up to 12pm the day before WITHOUT pay.

There is no direct union that looks after SA’s, although BECTU accept SA’s to join, none of them have no actual power to force the production from the correct pay and or standards. 

SA’s need a separate charter/union/bill of rights that enables SA’s better rights.

additional_details:
This includes allowing individuality through hair, makeup, and footwear choices that don’t impact learning or safety. Strict uniform and appearance rules can negatively affect children’s mental health, confidence, and sense of identity.

Every child should have access to professional emotional support and the freedom to express who they are — not be punished for it.

rejection_details:

additional_details: Too many children are being told they can’t go to the toilet during lessons, which can cause pain, stress, and health issues such as bladder problems or infections. It can also make school a place of fear or discomfort instead of safety and learning. Every child deserves dignity and respect. Allowing pupils to use the toilet when needed supports their physical health, emotional wellbeing, and basic human rights.

action: Review procedures to ensure terrorist regimes & groups don't receive UK funding
background: We call upon Parliament and the Government to conduct a review of procedures used to ensure no UK taxpayer funds, indirectly or otherwise, go to foreign governments, organisations, or groups known to support, finance, or engage in terrorism.
additional_details:
We think this is needed to help protect British taxpayers and uphold our nation’s commitment to peace and justice.
 
British taxpayers work hard to support their families and communities. Their money should not in any way contribute to funding regimes or organisations that promote violence, instability, or the persecution of innocent people. Any financial assistance provided by the UK must align with the values of peace, democracy, and human rights

action: Provide funding so every school can have a full-time school counsellor
background: We call on the government to require every school to have a school counsellor. Many young people face multiple mental health challenges in school and do not have someone to get help from. This must be changed. Children must not have to suffer in silence anymore.
additional_details: 1 in 6 children aged 5 to 16 have been shown to suffer from a mental health disorder. Early support and interventions in school can help save these children from suffering any longer. School should be a safe place to nurture and support children, but without a school counsellor to turn to they can far too often suffer in pain.

action: Ban electronic switch operated vehicle door releases on public safety grounds
background: Ban the rapidly emerging public safety issue of electronic switch operated interior door releases on vehicles where their failure can result in serious injuries or death. We think this formerly pure mechanical feature has been overlooked and potentially misunderstood by regulators.
additional_details:
A rising number of incidents have been reported globally where people including young children have been trapped in vehicles that have burst into flames before passersby, police or first responders could break the glass and rescue them.

Hidden 'emergency' releases are little use in a panic situation where instinct of the normal release method prevails and wastes critical time.

Young children in a car are reliant on others in the vehicle to escape and promptly remove them.

action: Limit Fireworks to 80 Decibels
background:
We the British people believe that fireworks used in the UK should be limited to 80 Decibels.
This would significantly reduce stress on wildlife, pets and vulnerable people and reduce social disruption caused by their increasingly frequent use.
additional_details:
We the British people want Government and Parliament to take a proactive approach to ensuring the well being of people and animals, both wild and domesticated, by lowering the legal limit of noise produced by fireworks to 80 decibels.
This will also improve social cohesion by reducing the potential for disruptive behaviour which can be caused by unnecessarily loud fireworks.
Fireworks are primarily a visual display and limiting them to 80 Decibels would not detract from the pleasure of their use

action: STOP Any 'One Off' or Any New Wealth Tax Being Introduced in The Next UK Budget!
background: The Government should rule out introducing any sudden or “one-off” wealth tax in the upcoming Budget,which measure would unfairly penalise those who have already paid tax on their income and savings,create uncertainty for investors and small business owners,undermining confidence in the UK economy.
additional_details: A surprise wealth tax could discourage investments & entrepreneurship at a time when the UK needs private sector confidence.Individuals have already paid income tax,capital gains tax,inheritance tax,and other levies — a further one-off charge would amount to double taxation.Sudden fiscal shocks risk driving capital and business abroad,reducing tax receipts in the long term and further deficit in the budget.Transparent,consultative policy-making builds trust in government and markets alike.

background:
Reverse funding cuts to arts and humanities subjects in higher and further education.
Increase funding to protect art schools and creative courses from closure.
additional_details:
Ensure more equal access to arts education.
Recognise creative education as vital to the UK’s innovation, economy, and cultural identity.

We urge the Government to reverse any cuts to arts and humanities funding, protect creative courses in schools, colleges and universities, and recognise arts education as essential to national culture, innovation and wellbeing.

action: Ban the purchase & delivery of alcohol via delivery apps
background: Ban the purchase, sale and delivery of alcohol via delivery apps to protect vulnerable and people who are underage.
additional_details: We believe that alcohol should only be sold through licensed premises with in-person age verification. The Government should pass legislation to implement this ban and work with local authorities and licensing bodies to prevent alcohol purchases, sales and delivery via delivery apps.

action: Allow family visa holders to include time spent on a skilled worker visa for ILR
background: The Government plans to increase the qualifying residence period for indefinite leave to remain from 5 to 10 years for skilled worker visa holders. We believe skilled workers on 5-year visas should be able to include time spent on their current visa if they switch to a family visa & apply for ILR.
additional_details: Skilled workers switching to family visas to re-enter a 5-year route to ILR cannot currently include the time they've already spent in the UK when applying for ILR.

action: Review the routine childhood immunisation schedule
background: We call on the government to conduct a review of the safety and effectiveness of the routine childhood immunisation schedule.  This should include considering the risks and side-effects of immunisations, and the process for obtaining informed consent before giving the immunisation.

action: Change school timings from 9:30am to 4:30pm Mon-Fri
background: Most people nowadays bunk school mornings because it begins too early, to combat this the government should make it mandatory for all schools to start from 9:30am to 4:30pm. additional_details: Studies show that children regardless on when they are advised to sleep they sleep at around 11-12pm and wake up at 7:30am. Making the school timetable 1 hour ahead would allow students to fit in more sleep in their schedule and allow them to be more on time. Other studies show that in countries where school starts at 9:30am their students actually come in and focus whereas in the UK most students do not come in the mornings exactly for this reason, "More Sleep".

action: Demand Immediate Action on Driving Test Appointment Crisis or PM's Resignation
background: The Government has failed to provide an effective solution to this crisis — is a clear indication of leadership shortcomings within the highest levels of Government.

action: Increase the number of bank holidays in England & Wales to 10 days
background: Bring the number of bank holidays in England and Wales in line with Northern Ireland, so that there are 10 ban holidays per year in England and Wales instead of the current 8.
additional_details: We believe that it would be reasonable and equitable to bring the number of bank holidays in England and Wales in line with the rest of the country, in order to promote consistency across the UK. action: Reclaim Our Pavements - End Dangerous Parking By Mandating Enforcement Of Fines
background: Legislate to mandate local traffic authorities to enforce endorsable fines for pavement parking within 24 hours of the offence, including when based on public photographic evidence. Fines should start at £100, escalate daily for ongoing offences, and rise annually with the Consumer Prices Index.
additional_details: Pavement parking is a direct threat to public safety. It forces vulnerable pedestrians—children, the elderly, wheelchair users, and parents with pushchairs—into the road and into the path of moving traffic. This selfish act turns our pavements into a dangerous obstacle course. The current slow enforcement process fails to protect people. We need rapid, escalating fines and penalty points to create a real deterrent, stop this dangerous practice, and make our pavements safe spaces for everyone.

action: Call for international halt to Artificial General Intelligence research

additional_details: AGI poses a serious risk to humanity. Aligning AI values with human values remains unresolved and may be impossible. AI systems can mislead, making alignment unverifiable. The SENDCo should be a separate role in schools. This is becoming more important with the ever growing need in SEN and schools.
additional_details: We believe it is important that the SENDCo has the time to fully commit to the role and complete the necessary jobs associated with this role. Currently full time class teachers are often given a small amount of time out of class to do this as an additional job to their class teaching job. With the ever increasing needs in SEN across the country it is vital we make this role separate to a class teacher.

action: Fund a pedestrian/cycle bridge as part of the A38 Upgrade in Somerset
background: We want the Government to fund installation of a low-cost pedestrian/cyclist bridge within the Somerset A38 upgrade project on the well-used Strawberry line path as the only real solution to remove a dangerous crossing and allows for easier traffic flow on a primary link to Bristol Airport.
additional_details:
We believe putting back a simple bridge at track bed level, at Shute Shelve makes life easier for wheelchairs, removes the road safety hazard completely & aids the flow of traffic - the £31M A38 upgrade’s aim.
 
We think the proposed solution, traffic lights, is of marginal benefit to users but seriously inconvenience motorists. It doesn't represent VfM. Somerset recognise enabling 158,000+ path users pa to cross this busy road safely is a priority, with a bridge as their preferred solution.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Introduce a law that makes it ILLEGAL for Businesses to refuse to take cash
background: Cash is Legal Tender - It should be against the law businesses to refuse to take cash
additional_details: Pass a law making it mandatory the business cannot refuse to take cash
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735459

action: Going to the toilet is a human right, it should be allowed during lesson.
background: There should be laws and legislation put in place for young people to be able to go to the toilet freely during class .
additional_details: Especially for young teenage girls not being able to go to the toilet when they need to is crucial and really should be a human right just as much as drinking water is , If you’re allowed to drink water in glass and you should be allowed to go to the toilet as well, it works both ways .
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require schools to let children use the toilet at all times in the school day
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731355

action: Add veterinary medicine to second-degree tuition loan exemptions
background: We ask the government to add veterinary medicine to the list of second-degree courses eligible for tuition fee loans. This would align it with medicine and dentistry, remove unfair financial barriers, and help address the UK’s critical veterinary workforce shortage.
additional_details: Veterinary medicine is vital for animal health, farming, food safety, and public health. Many graduates discover their passion later in life, bringing valuable skills, but face tuition costs of over £45,000 with no loan support. Adding vet med to the second-degree list would make the profession more accessible, support social mobility, and ensure the UK can train enough vets to meet growing demand.

action: Require councils to review social housing tenancies
background: People are being left without support, while some social housing tenants remain in subsidised homes despite earning high incomes or no longer meeting the need criteria.
additional_details:
I am calling for a review of social housing allocation and tenancy renewal legislation, to ensure homes go to those who need them most today.

Thousands of working families, single parents, and vulnerable people are being left homeless while councils fail to review existing social tenancies. Social housing should be a safety net for those in need, not a lifetime benefit without reassessment.
We urge the Government to:
	1.	Introduce a statutory review system (e.g. every 5 years).
	2.	Ensure councils publish transparent allocation data.
	3.	Re-prioritise housing resources for households in verified homelessness or severe housing stress.

action: Make pre-2006 student loans written off after 25 years, not at age 65
background: Change the repayment rules for pre-2006 student loans so they are written off 25 years after repayment starts, not when borrowers reach age 65. This will make loan terms fair and consistent for all borrowers.
additional_details: Many pre-2006 borrowers struggle for decades under growing interest, while newer borrowers see their loans written off after 25 years. This is unfair, causes stress, and traps people in debt for life. Updating the rules will bring justice, relief, and fairness to thousands who worked hard and now face endless repayments.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Write off all plan 1 Student Loans after 25 years 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743100

action: Adjust the £10 DWP Christmas Bonus introduced in 1972 to reflect inflation
background: Adjust the Christmas Bonus given to benefit claimants, from £10 - when it was introduced in 1972 - to reflect inflation (approx £180 in 2025). Make the uplift only available for British citizens, who have been claiming benefits for a minimum of 6 months.
additional_details: In the early 1970s, £10 was a valuable uplift for those without income, to help with the increased costs associated with Christmas time. It would have helped towards paying for heating and electricity, food and drinks or Christmas presents for kids. It would have been the equivalent of approximately £180 today adjusted for inflation. £10 today won't even buy a round of drinks, wouldn't pay for a quality Christmas pudding or buy a box of decent Christmas Crackers. £10 quite frankly is insulting.

action: Allow Skilled Worker Visa holders to work up to 40 hours in the same occupation
background: Allow Skilled Worker Visa holders to work up to 40 hours per week in the same occupation for licensed sponsors, instead of the 20-hour restriction, to give them flexibility and stability in employment
additional_details: Many Skilled Worker Visa holders face job shortages as some sponsors cannot provide enough shifts. This forces some to work illegally, harming the economy and reducing tax revenue. Allowing up to 40 hours per week in the same occupation instead of the 20-hour restriction, with any other company will increase productivity, boost government tax income, and reduce illegal employment in the UK. This change will also strengthen the UK workforce and economy.
rejection_details:
The 20 hour cap relates to secondary employment outside of the main role covered by the Skilled Worker Visa. 

If you work overtime in the job you’re being sponsored for, you do not need to update your visa. 

There’s no limit to how many hours of overtime you can do.

You can work up to 20 hours a week in another job or for your own business as long as you’re still doing the job you’re being sponsored for. 

You can find more information here: 

https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa/second-job#:~:text=If%20you%20work%20overtime%20in,one%20of%20the%20following%20conditions:

You may also wish to sign the petition below: 

Allow Skilled Worker visa holders to take unrestricted secondary work
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740003

action: Ban the use of private numbers for all NHS telephone correspondence
background: NHS use of private numbers can cause missed referral appointments, which can lead to missed diagnosis of serious health problems with potentially fatal outcomes. Many mobile phone users turn on private number barring to avoid spam or unidentified callers.
additional_details: Patients may not be aware missed calls from NHS referrals as they do not record as such. There may be many people missing appointments - being recorded as DNA - and being potentially exposed to further pain, distress and potentially fatal consequences because of a practice designed to protect the 'privacy' of a public health body. We believe the NHS needs to be transparent, it is funded by taxpayer money and should serve the people.

action: Give the people of the UK a referendum on Digital ID's let the people decide
background: I’m calling on Parliament to give the British people a choice a referendum on Digital IDs. This isn't a small policy change it’s a fundamental shift in our privacy, freedom, and identity. The government must let us decide if we want a future of digital control or the freedom to remain independent.
additional_details: Every citizen deserves a voice in shaping their freedom. Digital IDs may promise convenience, but they also risk mass surveillance, data misuse, and loss of privacy the foundation of democracy itself. The people of the UK must have the right to decide whether to trade liberty for control. A referendum isn’t resistance to progress, it’s a stand for choice, transparency, and the principle that government power should always remain accountable to the people.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Add an extra day to the week, a second Friday between Monday and Tuesday
background: Extend the week by one day, by adding a second Friday (Free day) where nobody has to work and can be spent with family, friends and people you care about
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

The Government is not responsible for creating days of the week.

action: Exceptional circumstances for children's leave from school
background: Include 'children's visit to see their expat parent overseas' as an exceptional circumstance for the granting of authorised leave from school
additional_details: I am a father of two children (both at secondary school) who currently works overseas in order to provide for his family. We have reverently had an application for leave rejected by our school on the basis it does not consistute exceptional circumstances. We are extremely careful of when we arrange family visits etc, however, and sometimes this does mean having to take our children out of school for a few ddays.
rejection_details:
Attendance policy is a matter for the school to decide. 

You may like to start a petition for the Government to introduce statutory guidance on when exceptional circumstances apply instead.

action: Fund another round of cost-of-living payments
background: Fund another round of cost-of-living payments in order to reduce the pressure on councils in supporting people on low incomes.
additional_details: We want the Government to do this to help low-income earners, many of whom are dealing with rising energy and food prices, as well as other cost-of-living pressures.

action: Request for Speed Cameras and Traffic Calming on the Priestland–Darvel Road.
background: Take immediate action to reduce vehicle speeds on the road between Priestland-Darvel. Residents have raised serious concerns about the excessive speed of cars, lorries, and trucks entering Darvel, which is causing noise, damage to nearby homes; as well as danger to pedestrians, children, and pets.
additional_details: Cars, lorries, and trucks are speeding into Darvel from the Priestland direction, creating a serious safety risk for residents and road users. The speeding causes loud noise, vibrations, and cracks in nearby walls, making life distressing for those along this stretch. A nearby bus stop used by children and families adds to the danger. The traffic speed and volume make it unsafe for pedestrians and uncomfortable for residents. Installing speed cameras or other calming measures would reduce speeding, improve safety, protect homes, and help prevent loss of life.

action: Suspend Astley Warehouses & Launch Independent Review of Wigan Council Planning.
background: The Government should commission an independent investigation into Wigan Council planning department's handling of the Astley Business Park warehouse development, examining its planning processes, competence, ethics, and oversight, and suspend further work until the review is complete.
additional_details:
Wigan Council forced through 18m warehouses towering over homes and a school - no Environmental Impact Assessment, no Landscape Review, no public consultation, and maps that erased local houses. 

Families are breathing dust & living in shadows. We have been subjected to pollution, noise, & health problems - & the warehouses will be open 24/7.

This is a systemic failure that demands independent investigation & accountability. Government must intervene and review how this was allowed to happen.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions which call for actions with regard to named individuals, organisations or businesses.

We also have to reject petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

action: Review enforcement of Section 132 of the Highways Act
background: We think council's around the country are not using their legal powers to fine people and remove graffiti and items that are unsafely attached to railings, lamposts and bridges that can cause dangerous circumstance if left unchecked.
additional_details: Councils around the country should be pressured to remove graffiti and other physical items to ensure safety and wellbeing of the community. Any unauthorised congratulatory/birthday banners, advertising for events or buisness or flags of any kind should be removed to guarantee the safety of road users and passers by and neutralising any public nuisance and disturbance of the peace. Councils should also be pressured to fine the people responsible, many of which have broadcast the acts online.

action: A debate on the Human Rights Act 1998 & ECHC the Conservatives want to repeal
background:
We do not believe that there ever was any intention to uphold the European Convention Human Rights. Because the government has been making new laws that totally go against the Articles ever since they were made.
Freedom of Speech, Freedom to Practice a Religion and the Right to Life all undermined
additional_details:
Every Article has been disregarded.
Scottish parliament took away freedom of speech in ones own home, the right to Prayer has been violated, and now the Right to Life of a baby in a womb. You clearly intended to this because the Blair Digital ID strategy can leave no right remaining in order for it to work, with permanent digital agent smart phones on everyone & the  Conservative party now want to finish off the job by repealing the Articles, which helps nobody but  Tony Blair.

It was a con

action: Proposal to open a Mental Health inpatient unit at Leighton Hospital  Crewe
background: To provide inpatient mental health services at MCHT site of Leighton Hospital working in partnership with Cheshire and Wirral Partnership to facillitate the unit, Providing 24 hour care provision when patients are acutely unwell and at risk of serious harm.
additional_details:
2010  the adult and older people's acute mental health inpatient services at Leighton Hospital were closed  The impact of this on patients and famillies is detrimental to all. Suicide rates increased.
As Cheshire East Suicide Rate Comparison 2024
Age-Standardised Rate (per 100,000)  North West (Region)	13.7

Cheshire East (Local)13.7 (3-year rolling average: 2022-2024)
Suicide rates are increasing exponentially and this requires an urgent review.

We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

action: Refurbish or destroy abandoned buildings
background: To start to refurbish or destroy abandoned buildings to save money over time

action: Introduce standing orders giving equal time at PMQs to opposition party leaders
background: We petition the House of Commons to introduce standing orders governing Prime Minister's Questions (PMQs) to ensure that the number of questions allocated to party leaders are shared equally among the leaders of all recognised opposition parties in the House of Commons, including smaller parties.
additional_details: All non-Government parties in the Commons constitute the collective opposition, and we think their leaders should all receive an equal number of questions and time in which to ask them.

action: Call for a referendum to call a general election
background: The outcry from the public not being heard is at its tipping point. If the current government think they are good enough then allow the public to decide whether a general election should be held.
additional_details: Call a referendum which will decide an early election
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for the same action: 

Introduce a mid-term referendum on whether to hold an early General Election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734396

action: Set mandatory minimum sentences for all child-related offences
background: We call on the Government to introduce mandatory minimum sentences for all sexual and violent offences against children.
additional_details: We believe children deserve the highest level of protection under the law. Yet, many adults who commit serious crimes against children, including sexual abuse, exploitation, and violent harm, receive sentences which we believe do not reflect the lifelong impact on victims. We want our justice system to send a clear message: crimes against children will be met with the strongest possible consequences.

action: Upgrade Melksham hospital to a minor injuries hospital
background: Put forward a motion to upgrade the current Melksham hospital to have an A&E facility or a minor injuries unit as a minimum.
additional_details:
Melksham has grown exponentially in the last decade and is still growing but the infrastructure hasn’t. 
The town sits between Bath and Swindon in Wiltshire but both general hospitals are at breaking point and people from Melksham need to travel an hour to get to the nearest A&E which is far too long plus when you get there you’re sitting for up to 7 hrs to be seen. This proposal would alleviate the need for urgent care in the area.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

action: Introduce a disabled bus pass without travel time restrictions for working age
background: Free restrictions for working age disabled person in order that they may travel for work , rather than rely on taxis or access to work . The disabled should not be discriminated against & afforded help , full flexibility to fulfill their potential.
additional_details: This should allow more disabled to get into work before 09:30 & travel after 23:00 shift work  , this would enable them more flexibility  & help the welfare bill reduce , I feel a small cost to relieve a bigger cost of welfare  , travelling is one of the biggest issues facing the disabled ,
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:  https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729326

action: Revoke a peerage of a serving Prime Minister.
background:
We the undersigned believe that a serving Prime Minister should not be able to hold a peerage. 
It causes conflict in our unwritten constitution with the House of Lords, and also it is a responsibility of the Prime Minister to represent his Country.
additional_details:
Being a Prime Minister is a hugely important role for representing the people against the Monarchy. To see a Prime Minister representing his Country while holding a title that makes her/him a serf to the King is laughable and makes a mockery of the Magna Carta.
Any person taking on this huge role representing his/her people on the World stage should immediately hand back the title in respect of the fact they are serving the people.
We the undersigned wish to see this implemented.
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions that ask for someone to be given an honour, or have an honour taken away.

action: Shutdown the petition's website
background: I want the government to shutdown the petitions website, time after time we have been shown to get incredibly high amounts of support for certain petitions. All of which have been responded with what is basically a no.
additional_details:
If the petitions website isn't even going to be used properly, why should we even have it? its a waste of space is it not? why should we waste our time saying something if all were going to get is a long response of the government saying "no."

Our time is saved by not having someone to be turned away, and your time is saved by not having to send us the same copy and pasted responses, its a win win.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Shut down the UK Government and Parliament Petitions system 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734870

action: Require schools to obtain consent for afterschool detentions & arrange transport
background: Pass a law which requires schools to obtain prior parental consent for after school detentions.
additional_details: We believe parents should be aware that their children are safe and looked after; and that they need to arrange transport for students to return home.

action: Change the law, so that UK citizens can force an immediate General Election
background: At present a vote of no confidence can only be called by parliament, leaving majority governments in an almost untouchable position. This means that governments can break promises or make decisions that are destructive to the country, and the electorate can do nothing until the next election.
additional_details: To act for the people in a true democratic position. Honoring the will of the UK citizens.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for the same action: 

Give the British Public the Right to Vote No Confidence in the Government
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734311

action: Review support provided to autistic parents involved in SEND tribunals
background: We think autistic parents are currently denied equal access to justice when representing their children in the Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) Tribunal, and call on the Government to review this as autistic parents deserve equal access to justice when advocating for their children.
additional_details:
The Equality Act 2010 requires public bodies to make reasonable adjustments for disabled people. However, autistic parents in SEND proceedings are often expected to manage complex legal cases without adjustments. We want a review of the system to include considering what reasonable adjustments can be offered to parents who declare a disability, and how tribunals can proactively identify and provide these adjustments rather than relying on parents to repeatedly request them.
 
We also call on the Government to extend legal aid to cover all SEND tribunals where the parent or carer is disabled and to create a SEND Equality Officer role to oversee the process to ensure it meets standards for accessibility, and that tribunals comply.

action: Scrap the cap on medical training & increase funding
background: We call on the Government to scrap the cap on medical training places. Abolish these limits and increase funding for more placements and trainers, and to widen access, reduce reliance on overseas recruitment, and ensure any needs are met.
additional_details: We believe Britain should train the clinicians it needs. Capped places could shut out talented young people, keep services short-staffed and push the NHS to recruit overseas which may impact poorer countries’ workforces. We back a sovereign, ethical workforce: scrap the cap, fund placements and trainers, widen access and retention, and phase down routine overseas recruitment. We want to be fair to British applicants, fair to patients, fair to the world.

action: Reform Universal Credit policies that disadvantage working claimants
background: Review and reform Universal Credit rules that stop working claimants from getting budgeting loans or advances when their income drops due to illness or hardship. Ensure fair access to help for those who have worked and paid into the system.
additional_details: The current Universal Credit policy discriminates against working people who have contributed through taxes and National Insurance. Those earning over £2,600 in six months are refused help, even when their income falls sharply. This punishes workers who rely on UC as a safety net when they need it most. Meanwhile, claimants who have not worked can access these payments more easily.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. 
We think that you're concerned about the surplus income policy, but we're not exactly sure what changes you'd like to see to it. For example, we're not sure if you want this to apply to anyone who has a fluctuating income, or only in specific circumstances. We're also not sure what loans and advances you are referring to. You can find out about the options for an advance of universal credit or other financial help here: https://www.gov.uk/universal-credit/get-advance-or-financial-support.

You can find sources for information about universal credit and how it works here: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/universal-credit-information-sources/

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Stop the proposed NMC fee increase
background: Nurses & Midwives currently pay £120 a year to hold a registration within the NMC, they are proposing to increase this. I feel due to the nature of the job and the sacrifices we make this should be stopped.
additional_details: The NHS has its struggles, however staff sacrifice so much to do the job they do, e.g. Christmas without their families to look after yours. Most individuals are struggling to live, so this will add an extra pressure to their lives.
rejection_details: The Nursing and Midwifery Council are an independent regulator, we can't accept petitions which call for actions with regard to named individuals, organisations or businesses.

action: Enforce rules and regulations for cyclists using the roads.
background: I want the government to reinforce rules and regulations for cyclists using the roads. Drivers, in any vehicle, have endless rules and regulations including the maintenance of their cars to ensure they are being safe for themselves and those around them. I believe cyclists should be held accountable
additional_details: Drivers must pay for lessons, theory and practical tests, and annual MOTs to ensure safety. They must wear seatbelts and avoid mobile phone use. Yet cyclists aren’t legally required to complete road safety training or follow the same strict regulations. They don’t need seatbelts or reflective clothing. Why are these rules enforced for drivers but not for cyclists?
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what new rules you would like the Government or Parliament to introduce for cyclists.

action: Allow electric e-scooters to be able to ride on pavements and roads
background: I don't understand why Parliament have made this rule, I think e-scooters, bikes and other e modes of transport are a good thing.
additional_details: Allow e-scooters e-bikes and any other e mode of transport to be able to be used on public roads and on pavements as they are electric so they are good for the environment and they are quick so they can get you to your location without you getting tired they also save on emissions as there are less cars on the road and more people on scooters under 16's should also be allowed considering the 15.5 mile per hour cap as the average person could cycle that easily.

action: Ensure council waste collection services meet high standards and accountability
background: Ensure council waste collection services meet high standards and accountability.
additional_details: Rubbish is piling up, bins overflow and streets smell because collections are inconsistent. Some workers are distracted or absent from duties. This harms the environment, lowers community pride, and reduces quality of life. We need reliable bin services we can trust.
rejection_details: Council waste collections is a matter for local authorities, and not something which the UK Government or Parliament is directly responsible for.

action: Stop quarterly MTD submissions as it will damage UK economy & small businesses
background: Stop HMRC implementing MTD regulations in April 2026 and reduce the red tape and future planned obligations on small businesses at a time when small businesses are struggling all round the UK.
additional_details: I want Government to free up the economy so that small and new startup businesses can flourish
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729235

action: Government to fund vorasidenib for NHS patients
background: We call on the Government to fund vorasidenib for NHS patients with IDH-mutant low-grade glioma, notwithstanding the NICE decision on whether to so or not.
additional_details: People with this rare brain tumour are often young and trying to live full lives. Vorasidenib could give them more time before harsh treatments, more time with family, more time to hope. It feels wrong to deny that chance when a safe, effective therapy already exists.

action: Ensure public energy and water infrastructure is protected from AI data centres
background: Water, energy and land expenditure for AI data centres has grown exponentially in the past 5 years. Government should make commitments now to protect public access to energy and water, set absolute caps on how much data centres can use, and ensure increased costs are never burdened on the public.
additional_details: Data centres are not going away, and the growth of their use worldwide has already placed a burden on water and energy infrastructure. These businesses should never be given freedom to expand data centres where that expansion reduces the availability or quality of energy and water supply to the general public, and it should be codified in law that all increased costs associated with greater strain on infrastructure should be burdened by the companies causing that strain.

action: Review NHS cancer treatment protocols
background: We want a review of the NHS cancer treatment protocols, including awareness and use of drugs not commonly used for cancer treatment but repurposed (so called off label drugs), and supplements.
additional_details: With chemotherapy alone costing the NHS at least £1.4 billion annually and the treatments still failing much of the time the time has come to consider funding robust clinical trials of off labels and supplements and ensure that oncologists are educated in their existence and usage.

action: Give All Citizens 3 Days Off To Celebrate Eid
background: I would like to start this petition so all citizens of the UK can have 3 days off. This is going to be to celebrate Eid and show that all cultures are welcome and are part of our community.
additional_details: I believe that if we can have many days off on other religious holidays such as Christmas, Halloween, Easter and more. This shows that Eid should be celebrated too as it is as important as other religious holidays. I also think that even though not all British citizens are Muslims, we should still respect it like we do with Christmas, Halloween and Easter.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729307

action: Automatically strip parents who murder children of parental responsibility
background: I would like the Government to strip people who are convicted of murdering children of parental rights and responsibility over their own children.
additional_details: We believe children should not have to go through court processes to remove the parental responsibility of biological parents who have been convicted of this offence and should not need to consult with their biological parent if they want to travel the World. All I ask is that once they are convicted, the parent is stripped of all parental rights and responsibility to their children.

action: Require schools to teach how to support vision impaired & disabled people
background: Implement high levels of education within the national curriculum about different disabilities, their impact and how to support people with these impairments.
additional_details: When I moved to a city, I knew I would come face-to-face with different individuals from all walks of life. However, one thing I was not prepared for was a severe lack of education about vision impairment and their impact on individuals. I have lost count of the amount of times that someone has grabbed me and dragged me across the road. I always explained to people that I’m capable but feel this very much falls on deaf ears. I would appreciate your support to improve education around disability.

action: Regulate and reform veterinary care
background: We call on the UK Government to establish regulatory oversight of veterinary care. This should include written treatment plans, itemised bills, consent safeguards, and accountability for corporate-owned practices which we believe profit from distress.
additional_details:
The CMA’s 2025 report highlights some widespread issues.
 
We believe we need urgent reform to protect families and pets, as we are concerned that families face potential financial coercion, missing records, and preventable deaths

action: Give children unrestricted access to toilets while in secondary school education
background: Create nationwide guidance that prohibits schools from restricting access to toilets. Allowing inclusion for all, without young people having to show proof of medical conditions. The current school policies discriminate against all young people without a medical condition.
additional_details: Medical research shows that it takes 30 minutes after eating and drinking for the effects of needing the toilet to present, this does not coincide with breaktimes. If a young person is holding their bladder or bowel they are not concentrating on the lesson which may impact on future exams. Young girls and transgender boys should not have to explain to teachers they need to use the toilet due to menstruation this can have detrimental impacts on their mental health and wellbeing.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require schools to let children use the toilet at all times in the school day
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731355

action: Reverse planned cut to LPU funding which limits UK state schools offering IBDP.
background: We hope to reverse the proposed cuts to large programme funding (LPF). The cuts limit UK state schools being able to offer the IB Diploma. Current students of the IBDP in a UK state school have organised this petition to ensure that the Government recognise the threat to the IBDP if the LPF is cut.
additional_details: As current students of the IB Diploma, we want to preserve it in UK state schools and understand that the LPU funding makes this possible for them. The IBDP requires us to study six academic disciplines, including Mathematics and at least one Science course. It ensures that we make competitive applications to world-leading universities. This programme allows us to access post-18 destinations which may not be possible on the traditional A Level route.

action: Review NHS policy on masks, safe air & ventilation to protect vulnerable
background: Vulnerable people — those with cancer, immune compromise, or chronic illness — should feel safe in NHS settings, not fearful. We’re calling for a 'do no harm' standard: an automatic right to treatment by FFP2/3 masked staff, safe air and ventilation in every setting and stronger infection control.
additional_details: The NHS was founded on the duty to 'do no harm'. That means protecting patients from preventable illness, not asking them to plead for it. We ask the Government and NHS England to adopt a “do no harm” infection-prevention standard by:  - Guaranteeing an automatic right for clinically vulnerable patients to be treated by staff wearing high-filtration masks (such as FFP2/3). - Maintaining safe air quality and effective ventilation across all health-care settings. -Reinstate masking in viral surges

action: Require a full and independent enquiry before any hospital job cuts

additional_details: Hospitals are complex structures. Roles such as HR, finance, clinical administration, and other corporate functions are crucial to keeping a hospital operating smoothly. We are concerned that current methods for making decisions about job cuts in hospitals don’t consider how cutting these jobs can destabilise the systems that frontline staff depend on, from A&E to maternity. We are also concerned about the cost of redundancies which can waste millions that could be invested in improving services. action: Remove power to cancel local government elections
background: Change the law to remove the power of the Secretary of State to cancel any further forthcoming local government, metropolitan borough, London borough or any other elections, for example, but not limited to, those due in May 2026.
additional_details: Ever since 1918, the right to vote is sacred and inalienable. 2025 Elections in some areas were cancelled this year. We believe any further cancellations would be voter suppression and undemocratic. The will of the people of the nation must be heard.
government_response_summary: The Secretary of State’s powers in this area are set out in legislation made by Parliament and used only with strong justification. The Government has no plans to amend these powers.
government_response_body: Parliament has conferred powers on the Secretary of State to postpone local elections under the Local Government Act 2000. While these powers sit with the Secretary of State, Parliament retains an oversight role through the statutory instrument process, ensuring democratic accountability. These powers are used infrequently.  Most recently they were used in February 2025 when a statutory instrument was made to postpone the ordinary local elections due to take place in May 2025 in East Sussex, Essex, Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Norfolk, Suffolk, Surrey, Thurrock and West Sussex. The instrument was made using statutory powers, laid before Parliament and debated and voted on by both Houses. The accompanying Explanatory Memorandum to the 2025 statutory instrument sets out the reasons for the decision: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2025/137/pdfs/uksiem_20250137_en_001.pdf  On 18 December 2025, the Minister for Local Government and Homelessness updated Parliament (https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-statements/detail/2025-12-18/hcws1215) that she had written to councils going through local government reorganisation that have elections scheduled for May 2026. She invited council leaders to set out their views on the postponement of local elections in their area and if they consider that postponement would release essential capacity to deliver local government reorganisation. No decisions have been made at this stage; all evidence and representations will be considered individually before any final decision. Any subsequent legislation would be subject to Parliament. The majority of local elections in 2026 are unaffected by local government reorganisation.  Parliament has also conferred powers on the Secretary of State to implement proposals for unitary local government under the Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007. These powers include provision for electoral matters. Again, while these powers sit with the Secretary of State, Parliament retains an oversight role through the statutory instrument process, ensuring democratic accountability. When these powers are used, it is typical to provide for elections to the new councils and to cancel any scheduled elections to predecessor councils that otherwise would take place at the same time. We have set out our intention to use these powers to implement the proposal for two new unitary councils in Surrey. We will bring to the House, for approval, a Structural Changes Order, which will establish East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council.  On December 4 2025, the Government announced it is minded to hold the inaugural mayoral elections for Sussex and Brighton, Hampshire and the Solent, Norfolk and Suffolk, and Greater Essex in May 2028, so that areas will have completed the local government reorganisation, and establish the strategic authority before mayors take office. This is because devolution is strongest when it is built on strong foundations and moving forward we will want to ensure strong unitary structures are in place before areas access mayoral devolution.  Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

Catering services for the House of Commons are provided by an in-house team who do not provide a subsidised service in the commercial sense of the word. action: Withdraw the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill immediately
background: Government to withdraw the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill immediately, because it downgrades education for all children, undermines educators and parents. We think it will cause harm to children, with their details being digitally stored for anyone to use without permission.
additional_details: We think the Bill is poorly drafted and is not supported by robust evidence. The impact assessments are inadequate. It will damage all children's educational opportunities. The Bill is silent on children’s voice and children's right to education. It undermines parents and school leaders. We think it forces a digital ID on children which is unethical and morally wrong. We do not want our children's personal and private details stored for anyone to use. This Bill is another form of control.
government_response_summary: The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill delivers on manifesto promises and will make progress towards the Opportunity Mission to break the link between young people’s background and future success.
government_response_body: This Bill is driven by the belief that every child deserves a safe, secure start in life and the opportunity to succeed. The Bill will reform both children’s social care and education to break down the barriers that hold children back, ensuring that at every stage of life, young people are supported to achieve and thrive.   Keeping children safe is a priority for this government. Practitioners supporting children and families must find, receive, and share relevant information to assess risks effectively. The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill introduces provision in law, paving the way for a consistent identifier to be specified and the organisations required to use it via regulations. The Department has initiated a series of pilots so we can establish how a consistent identifier can be implemented effectively and securely.   Upholding children’s rights, particularly in relation to respect for private and family life, are critical and that’s why all these measures operate in compliance with data protection legislation. The Department takes its data protection obligations seriously and is committed to ensuring high standards of information security, privacy and transparency. We have formally consulted the Information Commissioner’s Office  (ICO) on all Bill measures that will involve the use of personal data to ensure full alignment with data protection legislation and established best practice for safeguarding children’s information. We continue to engage with the ICO on the Information Sharing Duty and the Single Unique Identifier, as well as with multi‑agency safeguarding organisations, sector representatives and practitioners, to support the ongoing development of these measures. Separately, we are engaging with the ICO on the data protection impact assessment related to Children Not in School measures. This engagement helps ensure that all proposals are underpinned by appropriate lawful bases, clear limitations on access, and strict requirements for necessity and proportionality.  All data obtained or processed by the Department will be handled strictly in accordance with UK‑GDPR principles, including lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, and security. Access to data will be tightly controlled through Role‑Based Access Control, ensuring that only those with an operational need can view or use personal information.   Regarding evidence and impact assessments, the government has published Impact Assessments setting out the potential effects of the Bill and all its measures. These include regulatory impact assessments following the Better Regulation Framework for those measures that are in scope. These are published on gov.uk Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill: impact assessments - GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/childrens-wellbeing-and-schools-bill-impact-assessments). The department welcomes the Regulatory Policy Committee’s ‘Green’ rating for the Bill’s Impact Assessment, meaning that they have assessed it as being fit for purpose. The department has also conducted and published an equalities impact assessment, in line with the Public Sector Equality Duty. As with all legislation, these assessments are periodically reviewed and updated throughout the Bill’s passage considering any new evidence and feedback from stakeholders.   In addition to these, the department has also conducted and published a Child’s Rights Impact Assessment (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/695d3d1b4b69d216c438a137/Children_s_Wellbeing_and_Schools_Bill_-_Child_s_rights_impact_assessment.pdf), identifying where children are directly affected by policy and where certain groups of children and young people are more likely to be affected than others.   The Bill will create a floor for standards across our education system but no ceiling on innovation to bring all schools to the level of the very best. We are continuing to engage extensively with leaders from across the school system to ensure we drive collaboration and enable best practice to be shared up and down the country. For Children Not in School, the measures support local authorities to identify these children in their areas, so they can intervene in cases where a child is not receiving a suitable education or is at risk of harm. The government has tabled several amendments at Report stage to reduce the burden on parents of giving information for Children Not in School registers, improve the support package for families, and add touchpoints before or shortly after children leave school rolls to support early identification of children’s needs.  The government notes the issues outlined in this petition on the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill. We welcome views and engagement from the public, and continued parliamentary scrutiny, and are committed to working closely with stakeholders to ensure that the Bill improves outcomes for children and families.  Department for Education

action: Include glass bottles in the deposit return scheme (DRS)
background: The proposed DRS is set to cover single-use drinks containers made from plastic and metal (150ml to three-litre). It specifically excludes glass bottles. This petition asks the Government to extend the scope of the scheme to glass bottles.
additional_details: The Government mentions existing DRSs in other European countries in its motivation for the proposed DRS. Many European countries’ DRS include glass bottles. We believe this is for good reason: glass bottles could offer the advantage of being not only recyclable but also directly reusable. Reuse can offset issues with recycling, like the high energy use of the recycling process and the limited number of cycles for plastics like PET. Including glass bottles could also help kick off a culture of reuse.

action: Act now to end iodine deficiency in UK women and protect children’s IQ
background: We want the Government to introduce a national iodine strategy, including iodised salt or bread fortification, mandatory iodine in plant-based milks, national guidance for iodine supplements in pregnancy, and regular monitoring through the National Diet and Nutrition Survey.
additional_details: The latest national data show UK women of reproductive age have very low iodine levels (median 82 µg/L; 30 % severely deficient), below countries such as Ghana, Timor-Leste and Mozambique. Iodine is essential for healthy brain development in babies, and deficiency reduces child IQ and learning potential. Most nations now fortify salt or staple foods; the UK funds these programmes overseas but has none at home. This is a simple, low-cost fix with lifelong benefits. We need a policy and action now

action: We want a national referendum on the introduction of Digital ID.
background: We want the government to organise a national referendum on whether or not to introduce digital I.D cards.  This was never mentioned once in Labour's election manifesto and has just been announced as if it's a foregone conclusion. We, the people, have a right to vote on such a huge issue.
additional_details:
This represents a profound change for Britain and we, the people, have a right to vote on such a big issue.   There are passionate feelings both for and against the introduction of I.D. cards - so let the people vote.   Labour did not ONCE mention this plan as part of any of its campaigning, nor as part of its election manifesto.

The people of this country have a right to vote on such a vital topic.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition: "Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Give leaseholders a right to force a buy-back after serious mismanagement
background: To introduce legislation giving leaseholders the right to compel a freeholder, intermediate landlord or management company to buy back their property at the higher of the current market value or the original purchase price, where a tribunal finds serious breach of lease or mismanagement.
additional_details:
Some leaseholders feel trapped in properties that have lost value because of poor management, building safety defects or unremedied lease breaches. We believe that existing remedies do not restore financial loss or enable exit from untenable situations.

A statutory buyback right could protect homeowners from being financially ruined by others’ mismanagement and encourage responsible building ownership and management.

The buy-back should be at whichever is higher: market value or purchase price to prevent loss.

action: Recognise 1 May as Women’s Mind Health Day in the United Kingdom
background: We call on the UK Government to formally recognise 1 May each year as Women’s Mind Health Day — a national day dedicated to promoting awareness, education, and support around women’s mind health and wellbeing.
additional_details:
Women across the UK experience distinct mental health challenges linked to hormonal changes, life stages, caregiving roles, workplace pressures, and social expectations. Yet women’s psychological wellbeing remains under-recognised and under-researched, with many unable to access tailored support.

Recognising Women’s Mind Health Day would create an annual platform for education, open conversation, and positive action. The day would encourage employers, schools, healthcare providers, and communities to engage with women’s mind health
rejection_details: The Government is not responsible for designating national days.

action: Ban lootboxes in video games to anyone under the age of 18
background: Loot boxes should be banned for under-18s because we think they harm mental health and can cause addiction. There’s little protection for young players, and companies must take responsibility for the risks these present to minors through gambling-like game mechanics.
additional_details: The government should ban loot boxes for anyone under 18 because we think they negatively affect young people’s mental health and can easily lead to addiction. These gambling-like systems encourage constant spending for random rewards, yet there are no real protections for minors. We believe a government ban would help protect young gamers from addiction, stress, and financial harm.

action: Stop Over Development of Buckinghamshire - Fix infrastructure first!
background:
We ask the Council to:
1.	Reassess housing targets based on real local need.
2.	Fix infrastructure — before approving large-scale developments.
3.	Protect farmland and rural landscapes, prioritise brownfield sites.
4.	Restore local decision-making. Put Bucks residents first, not national quotas.
additional_details:
We, the undersigned residents of Buckinghamshire, call on Buckinghamshire Council and the UK Government to urgently rethink the scale and pace of development being imposed through the Buckinghamshire Local Plan and the Oxford–Cambridge Arc.
The current proposals would mean:
•	Buckinghamshire faces 372,000 new homes by 2050 as part of the Oxford–Cambridge Arc, plus another 95,000 under the Local Plan — government-driven targets far beyond what our local infrastructure can sustain.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Fund joined-up menopause care integrating neurodivergence & mental health
background: We call on the Government to fund menopause pathways with neurodivergence and mental health support, HRT access, specialist clinician training, sensory-aware appointments, and transparent data on outcomes and wait times.
additional_details: Women face inconsistent menopause services, amplified for neurodivergent or mentally ill patients. Fragmented care, postcode lotteries, and unsafe self-management could risk worsening health, mental distress, and inequality. We believe integrated services will improve safety, equity, and quality of life.

action: Do not increase University Tuition Fees in 2026
background: We call on the Government to reconsider the increase of the University tuition fee cap in 2026, and keep it at the current level rather than increasing it to meet inflation.
additional_details: We believe an increase in university tuition fees will further discourage young people, as well as mature students, from seeking higher-education pathways due to the rising costs and therefore the repayment implications once graduated. The government has published multiple plans to ensure UK students are securing graduate roles in integral sectors such as healthcare and engineering. Once again raising tuition fees directly challenges this sentiment.

action: Petition to ban those who missed the opening of parliament from being MPs
background: Ban anyone who skipped the opening of Parliament this year from being an MP. If they cannot take the time, they should not have the role
additional_details: It would make those who are in the position take it seriously. They have to attend their work to keep their job, like everyone else
rejection_details: There hasn't been a State Opening of Parliament this year (nor will there be one until next year) so it is unclear how the petition could be actioned.

action: Make English Literature GCSEs open-book
background: English Literature GCSEs are meant to give children the analytical skills they need for the future. The current predictable structure of exam questions and exams being closed-book means students just learn useful quotations for the sake of it and their accompanying explanations, making it nullified.
additional_details: The government should make English Literature GCSEs open book because it encourages deeper analysis rather than memorising quotes. It reduces stress, supports students with weaker memories, and reflects real-life skills where people refer to texts. Open book exams also create a fairer system and allow teachers to focus on understanding and interpretation, not just revision. This would make the subject more accessible and meaningful for all students.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730126

action: Stop Ltd companies offsetting loan interest or other expenses for rental income
background: We believe there’s a total disparity in an individual buying a house to rent and not being able to offset loan interest payments or refurbishments and updates to property that are considered ‘capital expenditure’ against rental income, whereas as Ltd company has these tax advantages.
additional_details: We want the Government to tax Ltd company rental income in the same way an individual gets taxed on property rental income.

action: Reverse increases in university tuition fees
background: The government must immediately reverse their decision to increase university tuition fees and maintainence loans in line with inflation. We believe that University should remain an opportunity for everyone, not just those who can afford it.
additional_details:
The government must financially support universities, not increase fees.

This government wants young people to be more educated and simulateously makes students pay extortionate amounts on higher education. This is particularly damaging in a time of economic uncertainty, a cost of living crisis and increasing graduate unemployment rate. We think there has been years of financial mismangement and the neglect of higher education by countless governments. The government must reconsider and commit to freezing fees and instead fund universities with government grants.

action: Mandate a 72-hour period before formal acceptance of a dog surrender document
background: The Government must institute a non-waivable 72-hour cooling off period before requesting a signature for any relinquishment form offered in lieu of seizure of a dog.
additional_details:
The police must complete and record a checklist to verify the owner's capacity, noting trauma or incapacitation, and confirming they have been advised of their legal rights. 

Currently, dog owners can be coerced into making an irreversible decision while distressed or mentally incapacitated. This practice risks breaching the Equality Act 2010 by failing to provide Reasonable Adjustment for owners with disabilities, mental health conditions, or learning difficulties. A 72-hour window is essential to allow owners, especially those who are vulnerable, the opportunity to seek legal advice and reach an informed decision.

action: Give men legal opt-out from parental responsibility in unintended pregnancies
background: Introduce a right for men to, within a set time frame after being informed of a pregnancy, legally opt-out of the parental rights and financial responsibility associated with it. This could promote fairness, equality and informed choices in reproductive decisions.
additional_details: Men currently have no legal way to opt-out of parenthood once a pregnancy occurs. We believe this creates inequality in reproductive rights and responsibilities. Allowing men to opt out of legal parenthood within a set time frame could promote fairness, equality and ensure parenthood is based on consent and choice.

action: Investigate UK citizens who served with the IDF since 7/10/2023 for war crimes.
background:
Investigate the legality of British citizens serving in the IDF under the Foreign Enlistment Act 1870. 

To have the police investigate all UK citizens who served with the IDF since 7th October 2023 for information on war crimes committed by any of serving member of the IDF.
additional_details:
‘Section 4 of the Foreign Enlistment Act 1870 makes it an offence for a British subject to enlist in the military of a foreign state at war with another foreign state with which the UK is at peace.’

As the state of Palestine has been officially recognised by the UK government today, and the government is not at war with Palestine, then the legal or criminal implications for anyone from the UK serving in the IDF are serious.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Investigations of potential crimes - including war crimes - are a matter for the police, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Reverse the cuts to International Baccalaureate (IB) funding in state schools
background: The Government should reverse its decision to withdraw funding for the International Baccalaureate (IB) in state schools. Removing this support without consultation will make the IB available only to private school students, undermining equality and access to a world-class education.
additional_details: Having studied and taught the IB, I’ve seen how it broadens horizons, raises aspirations, and builds global awareness. Cutting IB funding in state schools, with no consultation, makes it a privilege only for the wealthy, forces state pupils into a narrow British-centric curriculum, and could deepen social divides. It goes against the Government’s supposed principles of equality, opportunity, and levelling up that should underpin our education system. Reverse this decision now or be poorer for it

Throughout October to January, pet owners have to cope with petrified animals. Dealing with shaking, hiding underneath things, biting, toilet accidents, escaping animals and even paying a high vet prices for drugs.

We do a lot in this country to help SEN children and adults, but animals need help to, especially as they cannot advocate for themselves.

action: Ban the Sale of Fireworks and Restrict Use to Licensed, Low-Noise Events.
background:
Fireworks be available solely to licensed operators for use at approved events only.

Only low-noise or silent fireworks be permitted.

Local residents have the right to object to applications for displays based on noise, welfare, or environmental concerns.
additional_details:
This would reduce distress to animals, protect vulnerable individuals, minimise environmental damage, and improve public safety.

Existing regulations under the Fireworks Regulations 2004 do not sufficiently prevent misuse, noise pollution, and harm. Stronger controls are urgently needed.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732559

action: End the mandatory meat requirement in English school meals
background: Remove the mandatory requirement in the Requirements for School Food Regulations 2014 requiring maintained schools and academies to serve meat or poultry three days per week. We believe this rule conflicts with environmental goals and health guidance on reducing meat consumption.
additional_details: High meat consumption can increase the risk of obesity, heart disease, and diabetes in children. It is estimated that animal agriculture generates 14.5% of global greenhouse emissions and can drive deforestation. It can cause immense animal suffering—billions of chickens, pigs, and cattle confined in factory farms before slaughter. This regulation requires schools to support an industry which we feel is harmful to health, environment, and animal welfare. Schools should have freedom to serve sustainable, compassionate meals.

action: Commit to not deploying British Troops to Ukraine
background: Following recent speculation, we don't want the Government deploying British troops to Ukraine, even as part of a potential multinational force following a ceasefire or peace deal.
additional_details:
The UK has already provided significant financial and military aid for Ukraine, but committing British forces to deployment in Ukraine would risk entangling our country in a prolonged and unpredictable situation.

This could endanger the lives of our service members, escalate tensions with Russia, and divert vital resources from pressing domestic priorities such as the NHS, education, and cost-of-living support for British families.

Instead of risking further involvement in foreign conflicts, the Government should focus on diplomatic solutions, humanitarian aid, and strengthening UK defences and security at home.

action: Fund access for children from low-income families to go to after-school clubs
background: Many children cannot attend sport clubs as some parents cannot afford the high fees. We feel this is very unfair and we call for the Government to fund increased access for children from low-income families to attend after-school clubs.
additional_details: We want the Government put funding in place for children to go to after-school clubs, including sports clubs.
