action: Introduce legislation to ensure national marking of Remembrance Day
background: We call upon the House to debate and introduce a specific Act of Parliament to legally protect all established provisions and customs of the national Remembrance Day (11th November and Remembrance Sunday) events.
additional_details: This Act should ensure its cultural, historical, and solemnity be protected for future generations. We think Remembrance Day is of paramount national importance, ensuring we honour the sacrifices of our Armed Forces and maintain a collective national memory. While currently observed, its protections rely on convention and public will, making it vulnerable to future legislative or societal changes that could dilute its meaning. Dedicated legislation could provide a robust, statutory safeguard for its integrity and prevent the gradual erosion of this tradition of remembrance.

action: Introduce mandatory fines for people parking in parent & child bays without kid
background: We want the Government to introduce mandatory fines for people who park in parent and child bays who do not have children with them. This should be in the same way people are fined for parking in a disabled bay without a disabled badge.
additional_details: Many people park in parent and child parking bays on a day-to-day basis who do not have any children, which I find shocking. If there are no mother and child bays left, parents with children may have to wait for one to become available as it is physically impossible for many to get a baby out of the car in a normal space. Fining them could deter people from doing this whilst also making the Government money. It could be a win-win for everyone except the people who gain from parking there without children.

action: Stop the Social Care Immigration ban before services collapse nationwide.
background: We urgent the Government to reverse the proposed restrictions on overseas recruitment in Social Care. There is no backup plan to fill critical vacancies. Without immediate action, thousands on these services will go without care, providers will close and the NHS will  catastrophic pressure.
additional_details: Nearly one in three care workers in England are from overseas. The Government's plan to block international recruitment without a replacement strategy is reckless and dangerous. There's no domestic workforce ready to fill these roles. Services will collapse, hospitals will gridlock and lives will be at risk. The Parliament must act now.

Do not close social care visa to protect UK health and social care

action: Ban the teaching/encouragement of AI in Fine Art Courses
background: We would like the government to introduce new legislation to prevent the teaching of how to use AI in fine art courses as well as preventing universities from encouraging the use of AI.
additional_details: Students should not have to pay £9,500 a year to only be told to use AI software instead of actually working when we are already struggling with the high costs of degrees. AI Image Generation software is extremely harmful to the environment - 1L of water used for every 2 images generated - and steals from other artists work through using software to search the internet for picture references. It lowers our chances of employment in the industry, therefore has no place in university curriculum.
rejection_details: Decisions about the content of university courses are a matter for individual universities, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Introduce a non-taxable lunch allowance for employees to ease financial burden
background: I want the Government to introduce a law requiring all employers to provide a lunch allowance, which would be tax-exempt. We believe this would reduce financial pressure on employees, support workplace well-being, and ensure fair treatment across all industries.
additional_details: I want the Government to require employers to provide a lunch allowance exempt from being taxed. Employees often spend £5–£10 daily on meals, which adds up to significant costs. A non-taxable allowance would ease financial pressure, improve well-being, and promote fairness across workplaces.

action: Mandatory anti-spiking measures in all nightclubs and bars
background: Mandatory ID checks for everyone that enters a nightclub either manually or by an electronic system. Mandatory staff training for spiking awareness. Mandatory anti-spiking tools provided at every nightclub. Mandatory bag and pocket searches. Minimum of 1 trained welfare staff on shift at all times.
additional_details: Mandatory searches and ID checks can help prevent spiking and other crimes. It ensures there is a trace of every person in the nightclub to tighten security. This provides extra safety for everyone in the venue. The specially trained welfare staff would help those who have concerns of spiking and other crimes to ensure extra safety to the customers. Mandatory general awareness training for all staff members on spiking. Anti-spiking tools readily available ensures people feel safer in the venue.

action: Review consent law to protect neurodivergent people from miscarriages of justice
background: We ask the Government to review consent law to ensure courts and juries consider neurodivergence and relationship context when judging belief in consent. Neurodivergent people need fair legal protections to prevent miscarriages of justice in sexual offence cases.
additional_details: We believe current consent law does not reflect how neurodivergence affects communication, perception, and responses to questioning. Courts may overlook these differences, leading to unfair trials and wrongful convictions—especially in ongoing relationships. The law must ensure that neurodivergent people are properly understood and supported when consent or intention is in question.

action: Update business mileage allowance from 45p per mile (not changed since 2011).
background: The business mileage rate has been stuck at 45p per mile since 2011 – despite fuel, insurance, and maintenance costs soaring. It’s an unfair, outdated rate that penalises the self-employed and small businesses, effectively becoming yet another hidden tax on those driving the economy.
additional_details: The Government must urgently review and increase the business mileage allowance, frozen at 45p since 2011. Fuel, insurance, and vehicle costs have risen dramatically, leaving self-employed people and small businesses out of pocket every time they travel for work. This outdated rate unfairly penalises those who keep the economy moving. Updating it to reflect real-world costs would be a fair and practical step to support SMEs and freelancers facing growing financial pressures.

action: Provide equal NHS funding for all Hospices
background: Up and down the country, there is clear inequality within the NHS funding for palliative and end of life care. The aim of this petition is for a change to the funding so that all hospices receive the same amount.
additional_details:
People should not be denied care because their postcode. Some hospices in the country are fully funded by the NHS. Whereas, others provide the same standard of care but are partially funded, and are fighting to stay open.
 
There are concerns that if hospices close many people could die in unsuitable placements. We need to safeguard our hospices for the future.

action: Introduce an Emergency Legal Protection Certificate for domestic abuse survivors
background: Fund and provide state-funded legal advice and representation for domestic abuse survivors with verified police evidence via an Emergency Legal Protection Certificate, which will be provided to survivors and allow them to receive immediate protection and support while navigating the legal system.
additional_details: Domestic abuse survivors can face long delays, complex legal aid processes and financial barriers when trying to access urgent legal help. An Emergency Legal Protection Certificate could give anyone with verified police evidence immediate, state-funded legal advice and representation, which can reduce risk and trauma while easing pressure on charities that may be struggling to fill this gap.

action: Amend the way to book UK practical and theory driving tests
background: Booking a practical (or even theory) driving test is extremely difficult due to resellers, so making the reselling of tests should be illegal.Further by providing unique verification like a passport number AND PROVISIONAL (not full) licence number, and only allowing one test for each licence number
additional_details:
As a young driver, attempting to get any kind of driving test now is close to impossible unless you want to pay £300+ for a POTENTIAL slot, which a lot of the time is a scam.
This makes it more stressful and difficult for the learner driving population, and by amending the way you can book these tests, slots will be much more legitimate, and with only provisional license holders being allowed slots and reselling to be illegal, stops the crisis we currently have of driving tests in our country.

action: Why the UK Should Move Toward a 4-Day Working Week
background: I want the Government to act because only national leadership can make a four-day week a reality. Parliament can set the example, support businesses, and ensure fair implementation, creating a healthier, more productive, and sustainable society for everyone.
additional_details: A four-day work week boosts productivity and wellbeing without harming the economy. Trials show shorter hours improve focus, creativity, and health while reducing stress and burnout. Fewer commuting days cut emissions, ease traffic, and strengthen communities. The government should lead by supporting pilot schemes and adopting the policy to build a healthier, fairer, and more sustainable future for workers and society.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government isn't responsible for the issue you raise. UK law places limits on the total amount of time someone can work during a week and the minimum amount they can be paid an hour, but it doesn't specify how many or which days of the week they have to work. This would be a decision for employers and the employee.

We could accept a petition calling for the legal maximum number of hours during a week to be reduced or a legal limit placed on the days that people can work, if this is something you would like to see happen.

action: Keep Barking Driving Test Centre open until Lodge Avenue Flyover roadworks begin
background: There are ongoing rumours regarding the closure of Barking Test Centre. We want the DVSA to delay the closure of Barking Driving Test Centre until the roadworks on Lodge Avenue Flyover begin. This would allow learners and instructors to continue using the centre while access routes are still open.
additional_details:
Closing Barking Driving Test Centre now will cause major disruption for learner drivers in East London, as test waiting times are already extremely long. Many people will have to travel much further for tests, adding extra costs and delays when nearby centres are already overbooked.

Keeping Barking Test Centre open until the Lodge Avenue Flyover works start would help reduce pressure on the DVSA, learners, and instructors, and ensure fair access to driving tests during this period.

action: Do not include partner's income in calculation of disabled people's UC claims
background: We want the government to completely remove the policy that stops disabled people who are living with/married to their partners from receiving their out-of-work benefits. additional_details:
Under the UC system, choosing to live with/marry a partner could mean reducing or stopping a disabled person's benefits due to the total household income including their partner. This means disabled people MAY become wholly reliant on their able-bodied partners, losing their financial independence and putting strain on relationships.

This could put disabled people at an incredible risk of abuse and exploitation, and disincentivise disabled people from staying in relationships.

We demand the right to love.

action: Review care and support given to women facing ovary removal
background: Women facing ovary removal deserve clear information about surgical menopause, guidance on HRT/ alternatives, and proper follow-up care. Surgical menopause must be recognised as distinct from natural menopause, with individualised support reflecting its sudden, severe impact of hormone deprivation.
additional_details: Surgical menopause causes an abrupt loss of hormones that can trigger severe physical and psychological symptoms, yet women are rarely adequately informed or supported about the full impact it will have on their health and lives. One study showed that 95% of women leave hospital without HRT or follow-up care, increasing the risk of heart disease, osteoporosis, and depression. Surgical menopause must be treated as distinct from natural menopause, with informed, individualised care across the NHS.

action: Install metal detectors in all schools
background: Every child deserves to feel safe walking into school. Every teacher deserves to teach without fear. Installing metal detectors is a practical, visible step toward making that vision a reality.
additional_details: The safety of our children and educators must be a non-negotiable priority. Installing metal detectors in all schools is a proactive step toward creating a secure learning environment, free from the threat of weapons and violence. action: Change the burden of proof in the Family Courts
background: I want the government to change the law so that the burden of proof in the Family Courts changes from a 'balance of probabilities' to 'beyond reasonable doubt'. Especially when cases may involve the loss of contact between a child and their parent.
additional_details: Family Courts assess allegations on a 'balance of probabilities', or 'more likely than not' basis, and any allegations proven to this standard can then inform decisions about parental contact. Many of those who face family courts do so without legal aid and support, and can quite often face other parties who have legal aid and support. We feel this is grossly unfair on not just parents but children facing these life changing decisions. The law related to burden of proof must change.

action: Amend laws on parental titles on birth certificates
background: We believe UK law needs to be more flexible to allow parents to choose & amend the parental title recorded on their children’s birth certificates, to allow for two mothers/fathers. We think this is important to help formally recognise the realities of their lives and relationships.
additional_details:
We think this is especially for those within the LGBT+ community and their children. Lesbian and gay couples are required to go through what we feel are long and detailed processes to be registered on their child's birth certificate just as "Parent". We also believe laws on transgender parents in this context are not sufficiently specific for allowing them to be registered in line with their lived reality.
 
A similar approach to some EU countries could be adopted, allowing for 2 mothers/fathers.

action: Mandatory trauma-informed training and standards in the family courts service
background: We call on the Government to ensure mandatory trauma-informed training and standards for all professionals whose assessments influence decisions in the family courts, including judges, CAFCASS officers, social workers, and court-instructed medical experts.
additional_details: Trauma responses should not be labelled as mental health issues or illness; they should be recognised as symptoms of abuse – so, if a victim develops PTSD from domestic violence, it should be recorded and understood as a trauma response caused by harm, not a standalone mental health problem. Current guidance is inconsistently applied; there are huge gaps in professionals’ understanding abuse and mental health. We seek mandatory national standards, and a total reform on all current guidance and training.

Duty of Care in Governance.
additional_details: When those in power make decisions that lead to preventable harm — to children, to the vulnerable, to the public at large — and walk away without consequence, that is not democracy. That is failure without accountability are calling for a Public Office Accountability Act — a law that says no one, no matter how powerful, is above responsibility.

action: Establish a Royal Powers Review Commission
background: We ask Parliament to create a Royal Powers Review Commission to examine the monarchy’s constitutional role, consult experts and the public, and provide recommendations for possible, lawful, and measured reforms.
additional_details: The monarchy today is largely ceremonial, but it could provide stability during crises or deadlock. A Royal Powers Review Commission would allow Parliament to explore options lawfully, ensuring democracy, human rights, and parliamentary sovereignty are respected.

action: Ask NAO to investigate any errors in CMS arrears from system migrations

additional_details: We believe that system changes from CSA to CMS have caused incorrect arrears and enforcement actions against parents. We believe that data errors and unverified balances continue to affect families unfairly. We need an independent review to fix any false arrears and prevent any similar issues in future migrations. Enforcement should pause automatically when arrears are disputed or under review to protect families from harm.

action: Require women only carriages on public transport to improve passenger safety
background: We call on the UK Government to require optional women only carriages on trains and other forms of public transport nationwide. This measure could improve safety, comfort, and accessibility for women who experience harassment or unwanted attention while travelling.
additional_details: The petition aims to make women-only carriages a voluntary and protective option in the public transport network, offering a safer alternative to mixed carriages. There are successful examples in Japan, India, and Mexico. Women's safety is a concern, with harassment, followed, and groped incidents still prevalent on public transport, despite awareness campaigns and surveillance efforts.

action: Make Letterbox Contact a Legal Requirement for safe Birth Parents
background: We call for the reform of adoption laws to make letterbox contact a legal right for safe birth parents. This can bring reassurance & healing; for children, it can preserve identity, belonging & wellbeing. Some birth parents are allowed one letter a year, which, at present, is not legally enforceable
additional_details: Currently, birth parents may get to send and receive only one letter per year, and this is not legally enforceable. Letters may be left ignored and not responded to, which can leave families heartbroken and disconnected; precious bonds at risk, and children suffering in the long term. Some research shows that adopted children with steady birth family contact can grow up more secure and emotionally healthy. The court should be able to block contact if it wouldn't be safe for the child.

action: Make child abandonment by a parent a criminal offence
background: We call on the Government to update child protection and family law by making child abandonment by a parent a criminal offence.
additional_details: Abandonment is classed as neglect, but we believe absent parents face no accountability and scrutiny falls on the parent who stays. Making child abandonment by a parent a criminal offence could ensure the system is fairer and both parents are held equally responsible.

action: Legislate against online censorship of keywords related to women's health/bodies
background: Many legitimate discussions and educational content on women’s bodies and health are flagged as explicit or removed by major tech platforms. This widespread censorship limits access to vital information, harms businesses, and blocks products and services for women.
additional_details: We want the Government to make it illegal for tech companies to censor content about women’s health and bodies. They should set clear rules separating explicit material from legitimate health information, as well as create an independent panel to review censorship complaints, with the power to penalise discriminatory censorship. Algorithms can control what is restricted or amplified. We think that the censorship of words related to women's health amounts to digital discrimination and must be stopped by law.

action: Mandatory Life Skills and Financial Education in UK Schools.
background:
We’re asking the Government to:

1. Make practical life skills education a mandatory part of the national curriculum.

2. Provide mandatory neurodiversity training for all teachers and school staff, so they can properly support neurodivergent pupils.
additional_details:
Our school system is failing to prepare young people for real life. Children are leaving school without the basic knowledge they need to manage as adults things like how to open a bank account, budget money, apply for a mortgage, or find stable work. These are essential skills every person needs, yet they’re rarely taught in classrooms.
At the same time,neurodivergent children (those with autism, ADHD and dyslexia) are too often misunderstood, unsupported, or pushed out of mainstream education

action: Make it illegal to drive a moped without a full moped licence
background: The Government should introduce a law that requires all moped drivers to have a full moped licence to be able to drive on public roads.

They should be required to complete the Current Compulsory Basic Training Course as many times as necessary to pass both a theory and practical exam in order to qualify for a licence. 
 
The majority of moped drivers have not had an official exam to prove they are competent at being on public roads on a moped. Many apply ‘L’ plates, which show they have not passed their full moped test, and ride amongst experienced drivers. Delivery drivers are often using mopeds to work full time jobs, using the roads everyday, without having passed a full driving test. This is making the roads more unsafe for everyone. background: The Government should fund free school meals for children who are home-educated and who are medically unfit to attend school or are awaiting school placement. We believe no child should go hungry due to illness or lack of an appropriate school place.

These children miss out on Free School Meals, despite having the same needs as some of their peers. Extending support could ensure fairness, reduce hardship, and protect these vulnerable children’s wellbeing.

action: Publish data on NHS patients receiving ‘corridor care’.
background: Ask the NHS to publish the data for the number of patients receiving care in areas that are not designated as suitable for care, such as corridors, drug preparation rooms or hallways.
additional_details: The Royal College of Physicians and the Royal College of Nursing have both requested that the NHS publish data on the number of patients receiving ‘corridor care’. It is absolutely disgraceful and undermines the ability of staff to treat their patients. This data should be made freely available to the public in order to quantify the scale of the problem.

action: Protect and reform SEND and EHCP funding fairly — support real needs

additional_details:
Drivers face long queues and take unnecessary risks to themselves and other drivers. Notable accidents just this year 24 April, 18 July, 18 August. afternoon (October 6) after a pair of crashes in just over two hours. In other years: 7 aug 2023 5 people injured. action: Restore dental nurses to the Skilled Worker Visa List
background: The Government should restore dental nurses to the Skilled Worker Visa List and allow UK employers to sponsor qualified dental nurses already living here. This could help fill staff shortages, ease pressure on practices, and ensure patients get timely, safe dental care.
additional_details: The UK faces a national shortage of dental nurses, causing staff burnout, longer waits, and reduced access to care. Dental nurses are essential but no longer on the Skilled Worker Visa List, making recruitment and sponsorship difficult. Restoring them would help fill vacancies, ease pressure, and retain qualified nurses already in the UK, protecting the future of dental care.

action: DWP to classify tenants who claim housing benefit and keep it guilty of fraud.
background: Ensure  tenants who claim housing benefit that is paid to them is given to landlords and if tenants keep housing benefit money charge then with benefit fraud. Currently tenants can keep the housing benefit money with no repercussions. That is a disgrace and unfair on the taxpayer
additional_details:
Because there are tenants receiving tax payers money for their rent and not giving it to the landlord. Currently if rent is paid to the landlord, DWP can claim monies back from the landlord. If the tenants recieve the benefit and they spend it on living expenses then there are no consequences. That is legal
Loop hole that needs changing asap as taxpayers are funding these people. Classify it as benefit fraud
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. Housing benefit money is transferred directly to the claimant (or sometimes to landlord) to provide help paying rent. If a claimant goes into arrears for rent, or gives false information so they recieve more housing benefit than they are eligible to, there are already consequences and they may have committed benefit fraud.  

More information on this can be found here: https://www.nao.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/Housing-benefit-fraud-and-error-summary.pdf

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Keep school crossing patrols in calderdale west yorkshire
background: We were informed this morning by our lovely school crossing patrol lady that calderdale council are reducing the amount of school crossing patrols throughout the borough? I would like to help prevent this.
additional_details: The safety of our children is paramount! The journey to and from school, especially crossing busy roads can be extremely dangerous without someone to help guide them. Cutting school crossing patrols is disgusting and I would like to raise concern towards this happening in our town.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about school crossing patrols are a matter for your local council, not the UK Government or Parliament.

You could raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them, by entering your post code here: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Require Digital ID law to include direct democracy for public approval of bills
background: If the Government introduces Digital ID, it should also include a direct democracy system allowing verified citizens to approve or reject any bill before Royal Assent, ensuring laws reflect the people’s will.
additional_details:
Digital ID would give citizens secure online verification. The same system could enable nationwide votes on legislation before it becomes law. This would modernise democracy, increase transparency, and ensure that Parliament and the public work together in shaping the UK’s laws.

Such a system would strengthen democratic participation, increase government transparency, and ensure that future laws reflect the direct will of the people.
rejection_details:
Give UK citizens the right to veto laws by national referendum
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726955

action: Require period product packaging to include information about health
background: Make it a legal requirement for all period product packaging to include information to show that period patterns are an indicator of physical health. Clear information on warning signs of periods indicating potential underlying gynaecological diseases and cancer. Early recognition saves lives.
additional_details:
Millions of people in the UK experience symptoms — yet most do not realise these can be early signs of serious conditions and even gynaecological cancers.

This petition calls for the UK Government to:

1. Amend consumer packaging legislation to require all menstrual product packaging to include clear, standardised information about menstrual health.

It could improve early diagnosis rates saving countless lives and reducing long-term NHS costs.

Turning packaging into public health prevention.

action: Change the law of different sex siblings being allowed to share a bedroom
background: The law regarding different sex siblings sharing a bedroom hasn't been updated since 1935!! This needs reviewing immediately. I doubt everyone in government would allow their child to sleep in the living room if you only had a 2 bedroom house and a child of each sex.
additional_details: Review this law and allow people in social housing to have separate bedrooms for children of gender over a certain age
rejection_details:
The House of Commons Library states that there is no age at which it’s unlawful for siblings to share a bedroom, including siblings of opposite sexes.

You can find more information here: 
https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/does-the-law-set-an-age-at-which-children-cant-share-a-bedroom/

action: Ban councils from discharging housing duty if person refuses long distance offer
background: Ban local councils from designating people as “intentionally homeless” and relieving themselves of their duty if someone refuses an offer of housing more than 90 minutes away. Councils should be able to make long distance offers, but such offers would not discharge their duty.
additional_details: Many councils are under pressure to find housing for those who need it and may use “take it or leave it” offers, where people may be told that refusals could mean they are making themselves “intentionally homeless.” This can result in an offer of temporary or permanent housing over 200 miles away, where people may be forced to choose between being homeless or moving somewhere unfamiliar with no support, which may disrupt children's education and force them to quit their jobs.

action: Don't change current treatment of low-value imports
background: The Government is consulting on changes to low-value imports that currently could be seen to benefit companies such as Shein & Temu in China; but many people benefit from buying items from smaller companies in countries like Japan where they can buy exclusive items that can't be bought domestically
additional_details: The proposed changes in the consultation would be bad for the economy because they would add costs for working people and hurt small businesses that import goods that aren't necessarily from big companies in China, and would de-incentivise people from importing goods and also hurt trade.

action: Require medical history to be listed on horse passports
background: I want greater protection for horse welfare and for buyers from neglectful sellers within the equine world; where profit exceeds care. Legal requirement for all medical history to be listed on a horse passport to make it harder for sellers to be deceitful.
additional_details: Putting all medical history on a horse passport shows exactly what medical issues they've had and can prevent deception in the horse world. People are buying horses where there is no legal obligation to release medical paperwork and no way prospective buyers can check. Even after 5 stage vetting they may find the buyer has lied. This change can protect animal welfare and stops fraudulent sales and reduces the amount of cases going to court

action: Fund research into Desmoid Fibromatosis in children
background: I want the Government to fund research into Desmoid Fibromatosis in babies and children, including more research into the condition itself and treatment options.
additional_details: Due to a lack of research, many children die and are left with no options other than being made comfortable at a hospice. As the condition can be genetic, other children within families many carry the same gene and have the same condition. We believe there isn’t enough research for this condition, and it’s not good enough. There must be change.

action: Keep the UK in the ECHR and uphold fair, humane immigration policies
background: We ask the Government to commit publicly to keeping the UK within the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) and to reject any proposals for withdrawal. We also ask for continued support of fair, humane and lawful immigration policies that uphold dignity and equality for all residents.
additional_details: The ECHR protects fundamental rights like free speech, fair trials and freedom from inhumane treatment. Leaving it would weaken these safeguards and harm the UK’s global reputation for justice and liberty. Millions of lawful migrants and residents contribute to our society and deserve to live without fear of discrimination or arbitrary removal. Upholding human rights and inclusivity reflects Britain’s best values — fairness, compassion and respect for the rule of law.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. The Government has already said it is unequivocally committed to the European Convention on Human Rights

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Use legislation to expand the Network Railcard to cover all of Great Britain
background: Use legislation, including the Great British Railways Bill, in consultation with the Scottish and Welsh governments, to expand the Network Railcard to cover all of Great Britain so adults aged 30+ and off-peak groups can access discounted rail travel nationwide and fares are modernised fairly.
additional_details: The Network Railcard currently only covers London & the South East, leaving many adults over 30 without discounts. Expanding it would promote fair access, encourage off-peak travel, and modernise fares nationwide, either now or as part of the Great British Railways transition.

action: Make nursing an apprenticeship style course, where placement are paid.
background: Stop nursing courses going through university and have more option for work based routes.
additional_details: Nursing course are majorly based on placements, where student are wrongly being classed in staff numbers and treated as staff members, working full time shifts. They are getting a bursary solely for these shifts when doing near enough the same work as a qualified nurse and working the same, if not more hours.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund pay for student nurses and midwives for placement hours
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746707

action: Allow Visa-Free Access for Turkish Citizens travelling to the United Kingdom
background: We call on the Government to introduce visa-free entry for citizens of Türkiye for visits including tourism, business, family visits and long term stays. Turkish citizens are humans too and we think they deserve the same access rights as citizens of countries with visa-free entry to the UK.
additional_details: Türkiye & the UK enjoy strong diplomatic, economic & cultural ties. But we feel current visa requirements place a significant burden on Turkish citizens wishing to visit the UK for legitimate stays. Many comparable countries have introduced visa-free or simplified arrangements for Turkish citizens & the UK should too. We think introducing visa-free access for Turkish citizens would help strengthen all ties between the UK and Türkiye, boost economies/ease family reunions.

action: Review Coercive Control Law and Police Training
background: It appears that the current Coercive Control Law is not working and failing. Last year there were almost 50,000 offences of coercive control recorded by the police in England and Wales but only a very small number of these resulted in convictions. This conviction rate must be improved.
additional_details: The Government must review the application of the law and widen it to encompass more behaviours: severe lying, impersonating armed forces personnel, repeat infidelity, damage to vehicles. Adequate training must be provided to police forces and there must be a presumption in that training for women to be dealt with by female officers upon request.

action: The Domestic Abuse (Family Right to Act) Bill.
background: Give immediate family members the legal right to report and press charges for domestic abuse on behalf of victims.
additional_details: We call on the UK Government to allow immediate family members to report and, where evidence exists, press charges for domestic abuse. In the year ending March 2024 there were 360+ abuse-related deaths and 98 suicides. Victims often stay silent out of fear or coercion. This Bill would let families act early, prevent serious harm or death, and ensure police take proactive measures. If refused, we ask what steps will protect victims and save lives.
rejection_details:
It is already possible for family members to report concerns of domestic violence to the police. Decisions about investigations and charging people with offences are for the police and CPS.

We're therefore not sure exactly what change you'd like to see.

action: Create a law for changing the UK press's right to certain information & privacy.
background: Stop Photographs obtained by theft used as a daily display on Newspapers or news sites. Information printed about any person/persons obtained by hacking their mobile phone, personal computer, second hand rumours or via intimidating them or their immediate friends, family, colleagues/acquaintances.
additional_details: Scrutiny on biased reporting on Newspapers, live TV, news sites and an independent regulator will ensure fair unbiased reporting based around factual reports on live TV, news sites and in the newspapers. Misinformation as non-fact checked stories printed in Newspapers, published on News sites and reported on Live TV must allow a regulator to inform the police. The only way it can is with a new law to stop the press and ensure regulation of them and protect the public's right to privacy in UK.
rejection_details:
It is illegal to obtain information via hacking.

Complaints about the press are the responsibility of the Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO) and Independent Monitor for the Press (Impress), not the UK Government or Parliament. 

You could submit a new petition which sets out more clearly how your suggested approach to press regulation would differ from current arrangements.

action: Require utility companies to refund standing charge when no service
background: Government to require utilities companies through regulators like OFWAT and OFGEM to cancel daily service charge when companies fail to deliver service throughout the day.
additional_details: Many customers are suffering regular power cuts, interruptions to water supply, poor quality water and other failures to essential service. But, all utility companies still charge the daily service charge even when they are not delivering. We want the government and regulators to ensure daily charge is cancelled whenever there is a failure to deliver irrespective of length of failure or cause to provide contracted service.

action: Make an independent body to enforce elected politicians’ performance & behaviour
background: Create an independent body to monitor and enforce the performance and behaviour of elected politicians, and which has the power to take action when there are breaches or failures to act appropriately. We believe there have been many instances of corruption and failures not been acted upon.
additional_details: We believe this could ensure politicians at all levels behave appropriately and that action is taken by independent body when there are breaches. We also want the body to define the required number of meetings that elected politicians must attend and the minimum contractual hours they must work for, as well as monitor and enforce this. We would also like the body to monitor and ensure elected politicians listen, are honest, and do not avoid questions.

action: Fund therapeutic support service for women with suspected or late-diagnosed ADHD
background: We call on the UK Government to fund a nationwide therapeutic support service for women with suspected or late-diagnosed ADHD. It should offer trauma-informed care for RSD, emotional masking, and the impact of delayed diagnosis—tailored to women’s lived experience.
additional_details: ADHD in women is underdiagnosed and misunderstood, often missed until adulthood. Many struggle for years with emotional dysregulation, low self-esteem, and RSD, without support. Gendered expectations, masking, and lack of trauma-informed care worsen outcomes. We urge the government to fund a nationwide, inclusive therapeutic service for women with ADHD—designed with lived experience and focused on healing, identity, and wellbeing.

action: place employers at school establishment for 16+ for those looking for jobs
background: this would be easier for those looking for jobs after school or those currently seeking for jobs to get jobs as many people around the ages from 18-24 are on benefits this would also help the employer find employees
additional_details: this is helpful as it would decrease the amount of people on benefits as well as help those to get jobs with all this being mentioned if there is process for this schools should provide practice interviews or help with cvs if that’s needed for the jobs this is important to help the younger generation
rejection_details: This is a matter for each individual school and not something which the UK Government or Parliament is responsible for.

background: It should be necessary to teach children about rape culture and the true meaning of rape and consent from a young age. Many don’t understand that “no” means no, and early education can prevent sexual violence before it happens.

action: Introduce mandatory driving retests for drivers over the age of 70
background: We want the Government to introduce mandatory driving retests for drivers over the age of 70. We think this will make the road safer for everyone: motorcyclists, pedestrians and car users.
additional_details:
This petition seeks to implement regular assessments of driving ability in older drivers:
Full driving retests
Reaction time & hazards
Manoeuvring ability
Comprehensive eyesight examinations

We want the Government to introduce mandatory driving retests for drivers over 70, with regular assessments of driving ability, including full driving retests, reaction time and hazard tests, manoeuvring ability checks, and comprehensive eyesight examinations to help improve road safety for all.

action: Review guidance and fund training for psychiatric and mental health care staff
background: We call on the Government to conduct a review of sedation and chemical restraint policies in psychiatric hospitals and mental health care facilities.
additional_details: We want Government to fund mandatory training for psychiatric and mental health care staff in trauma-informed and compassionate care, and increased access to talking therapies, peer support, and non-medication-based interventions. We believe hospitals sometimes respond to mental health crises with heavy medication and sedation, which we think is wrong.

action: Save Britain’s Classic Cars – Protect the 40-Year Historic Vehicle Rule!
background: Protect the 40-year historic vehicle exemption and ensure no changes reduce or remove this status. Keep the right to register, own and use historic vehicles as part of Britain’s cultural, technical, and economic heritage.
additional_details: Classic cars are part of Britain’s living history and support thousands of skilled jobs in restoration, engineering, and small business. They are driven sparingly, have minimal environmental impact, and preserve vital heritage skills. Changing the 40-year rule would harm culture, jobs, and craftsmanship.
rejection_details:
We think your petition is covered by Government or Parliament action already.

The Government hasn't announced it will be introducing vehicle tax for classic vehicles. Including in the Chancellor's budget statement which you can read the statement here: 
https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2025-11-26/debates/0FD15A2E-84B6-49F0-939A-24B7AABFB798/FinancialStatementAndBudgetReport

Chief Secretary to the Treasury, James Murray MP responded to a Written Question on this matter in February 2025:

https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2025-02-04/28704

We only reject petitions that don’t meet the petition standards.

action: Grant citizenship to residents living in the UK for 15+ years & their children
background: Pass a law which grants automatic UK citizenship to individuals who have lived in the UK for at least 15 years on a continuous and lawful basis, and who have consistently worked and paid taxes and National Insurance Contributions.
additional_details: We also ASK for children born in the UK to these long-term residents be automatically granted British citizenship. This measure could acknowledge the long-term economic and social contributions of foreign nationals who have made the UK their permanent home. We urge the Government to establish a fair, transparent and automatic pathway to British citizenship for long-term taxpaying residents who have demonstrated commitment and contribution to the country over 15 years or more.

action: Urge the UK government to press Nigeria to condemn killings of Christians
background: Violent attacks on Christians in Nigeria have surged, killing thousands and destroying homes, churches, and villages. This violates Article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights 1948, which protects freedom of religion. Over 7,000 Christians have been killed since 2025 for their faith
additional_details:
The UK has a moral duty to defend human rights. Under Article 8 of the African Charter, freedom of religion must be protected. The Government must act to support Nigerian Christians by:
Urging Nigeria to protect Christian and vulnerable communities
Supporting justice for victims
Providing aid to displaced families
Promoting peace and religious freedom with global partners
Over 4 years 56,000 lives were taken due to religious beliefs. UK government has an obligation to provide support.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743829

action: Bring back pounds, shillings and pence
background: Replace the current system (pounds and pence) with the old system of Pounds, Shillings and Pence, where there are 12 pence in a shilling, 20 shillings in a pound, and 240 pence in a pound.
additional_details: The old system is part of our British heritage, and it is a distinctly British way of doing things. Bringing it back would encourage pride in our country's traditions.

action: Prioritise climate change action and stop producing fossil fuels
background: I want the government to stop production of fossil fuels, & introduce a detailed plan on how to stop climate change, instead of just setting goals & delaying them. More money & action must be put in environmental and conservational areas, and funding for fossil fuel production and deforestation cut
additional_details: Many studies have shown that we aren't doing enough to help our planet. I think we are all too consumed with wars and finances that we haven't paid attention to our environmental goals for 2030, or the years beyond. We can't just 'deal with it later', we must act now, and the Government is a huge factor on whether we save our planet or not. Time is money. And we are running out of time. Please do not say that you are already doing your part, many countries clearly aren't doing enough. Act now. Act more.

action: Review child maintenance service (CMS) process for accepting reduced payments
background: Currently, a paying parent can reduce their CMS payments by adding a partner’s child as a “relevant child,” even if that child is not biologically theirs and already receives support from their own parent. We want the Government to review this process.
additional_details:
We call on the Government to review the CMS process for accepting reduced payments to ensure that paying parents aren’t allowed to reduce their payment based on incorrect information. We want the CMS to:

• Require financial disclosure from both adults in the household;
• Verify that any declared dependents are genuinely financially supported by the claimant; and
• Exclude dependents who already receive maintenance from their biological parents.
We believe this will make the CMS fairer and prevent misuse of the system.

action: Include the Royal Family, Household & Duchies in the Freedom of Information Act
background: Legislate to bring the Royal Family, the Royal Household, the Duchy of Lancaster, and the Duchy of Cornwall within the scope of the Freedom of Information (FOI) Act 2000. We think this would help to modernise constitutional transparency, safeguard privacy and increase trust in the British Monarchy.
additional_details: Many parts of the monarchy receive financial support from the government, and carry out public functions. Yet they are outside FOI, and much information is secret by law. We think bringing them within FOI – while protecting personal data and security – would improve value-for-money scrutiny, prevent conflicts of interest, increase trust and transparency in an institution many of us support. We believe that if public money is used, there must be public accountability.

action: Change the national anthem from God Save the King to Mr Brightside.
background: Change the national anthem to something that everyone in the UK knows how to songs, ergo is more representative than the current tune, which is musically boring and unexciting, aswell as being poor at representing the UKs current multi-cultural society.
rejection_details:
The use of the present National Anthem is a matter of tradition rather than having any legal status.

You can find more information about the history and status of the national anthem here:

https://www.royal.uk/national-anthem

action: Require Public Consent for Major National Policies
background: We call on Parliament to introduce a law requiring verified public approval before any major policy affecting citizens’ rights or freedoms—such as a national Digital ID—can be implemented.
additional_details:
At present, governments can proceed without clear consent, leaving the public with no meaningful control over policies that affect them directly.
This law would ensure that the people remain the ultimate authority: no measure could proceed without a clear demonstration of public support.
Continuing with policies like Digital ID without such consent would show a lack of good faith in upholding democratic principle.
In a true democracy, the government serves the people, not the other way around.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do, and how you would like the Government or Parliament to obtain "verified public approval."

You may wish to sign these petitions which call for similar actions:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/726955
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Ensure UK Digital ID Remains Voluntary and Fully Transparent
background: We ask the Government to guarantee that any Digital ID system remains voluntary, with non-digital alternatives for essential services, and that no rollout occurs without full public consultation and a free vote of Parliament.
additional_details: Digital ID was not clearly presented in the 2024 election, yet new rules are making it effectively mandatory. This risks eroding privacy, consent, and public trust. Parliament must ensure transparency, open debate, and legal safeguards so citizens retain genuine choice and control over their personal identity data. We value innovation, but technology must serve people—not replace democratic consent or restrict access to work, housing, or public services.
rejection_details: Protect the Right to Live Without a Digital ID: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745717

background:
Older state pensioners are set to get £2,933 less in State Pension payments per year in 2026 compared to younger retirees thanks to the triple lock. Older pensioners have the same cost of living
to contend with. Its grossly unfair.
additional_details: Older state pensioners followed the rules as they were set yet they are being penalised.  Lots of pensioners don't want pension credit and all the form-filling that goes with it, they want fairness, they want to be able to cope with the cost of living the same without all the worry.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Increase New State Pension and pay to all, abolish the old Basic State Pension" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728562

action: Stop changing the clocks – keep British Summer Time all year round
background: We want the UK Government to stop changing the clocks twice a year and keep British Summer Time (BST) permanently. This means the clocks would no longer go back in October, and the UK would stay on BST all year.
additional_details: The original purpose of changing the clocks no longer fits modern life. It disrupts sleep, affects health, and causes confusion twice a year. Keeping British Summer Time permanently would give us longer, brighter evenings, improving wellbeing, safety, and productivity. It would also support tourism, reduce energy use, and make life more enjoyable for everyone.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition that calls for the same action:

Make British Summer Time (BST) permanent year-round

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739222

rejection_details: We are not clear what action you are seeking. You can submit a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Call for legal review into the decision to invade Iraq in 2003
background: We ask the Government to request an independent legal review of the 2003 Iraq invasion and refer any credible evidence of wrongdoing by officials to the relevant prosecuting authorities, including the ICC
additional_details: The 2016 Chilcot Inquiry found the case for war in Iraq was overstated and peaceful options had not been exhausted. 179 British service personnel and hundreds of thousands of Iraqi civilians died. The public deserves full accountability and transparency
rejection_details: It isn't clear from whom you are suggesting that the Government should request an independent legal review of the 2003 Iraq invasion, nor is it clear whether you are calling for this body to be UK-based or extra-territorial.

action: Protect our Pets from the impact of Fireworks
background: The Explosives (Fireworks) Regulations (NI) 2002 make it illegal to buy, possess, or use fireworks without a licence—and specifically ban “bangers”—every autumn sees unlicensed fireworks sold and set off at all hours, often without effective enforcement. We need a review of how this is enforced
additional_details: This issue not only affects pets but also has a serious impact on vulnerable people, including children and individuals with sensory sensitivities, who find these sudden noises distressing.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Northern Ireland Executive and Northern Ireland Assembly is responsible for. 

If you want to raise this issue you could contact your MLA, or raise it with the Northern Ireland Executive.

You can find contact details for your MLAs here: http://www.niassembly.gov.uk/your-mlas/

You can find contact details for the departments of the Northern Ireland Executive here: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/government-departments-in-northern-ireland

action: Require a referendum for any policy that breaches the governments manifesto
background: The government should not be able to act in away which goes against their manifesto pledges. We believe the manifesto is what drives the people to vote for government. If the government wishes to break the manifesto then we the public should have a vote in a referendum.
additional_details: Manifesto pledges should be adhered to by the democratically elected government. Introducing polices that break this should require the public to hold a referendum and hold the final say.

action: Ban smoking and vaping while walking or in transit in public spaces
background: The government should introduce a law prohibiting smoking/vaping while people are in transit,such as walking on pavements, crossing roads, or moving through public areas. Smokers and vapers should only be allowed to use designated stationary areas, away from others, before continuing their journey.
additional_details: Too often, non-smokers — including children, asthmatics, and people with respiratory issues — are forced to walk behind or through clouds of smoke or vapour in public. This is unpleasant, unhealthy, and unfair. People should be able to move freely outdoors without inhaling second-hand smoke or vapour.
