action: Instruct NHS England to revoke adoption of the IHRA definition of antisemitism
background: In October, the government asked NHS England to adopt the IHRA definition of antisemitism, without public consultation. Serious concerns were raised by Doctors in Unite and over 23 other organisations. We think the definition has serious flaws threatening freedom of expression and political debate.
additional_details:
We believe its examples are vague and conflate criticism of Israel or Zionism with antisemitism, leading to suppression of speech.
 
We think NHS England must uphold equality and freedom of expression under Art 10 ECHR and s.6 HRA 1998 and that adopting the IHRA definition which has been criticised for lacking legal precision – with some of its uses criticised by the original drafter – risks breaching these duties and chilling open discourse. UK law already protects Jewish communities from hate and discrimination. We urge the government to instruct NHS England to revoke the adoption, reaffirm its anti-racism stance, and consult diverse voices to ensure legal compliance and protect intellectual freedom.

action: Allow women to carry pepper spray with a licence for personal protection
background: Women deserve the right to feel safe. We ask the government to allow a license for pepper spray for self-defence. Applicants would need background checks and safety training, with strict penalties for misuse. A regulated system would empower women to protect themselves while keeping the public safe.
additional_details:
Every year in the UK, millions of women live in fear of harm in their own homes or on the streets. Around one in eight women experiences domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking in a single year.

These figures highlight a serious and persistent threat to women’s safety. Introducing a regulated licensing system for self-defence sprays would provide a measured, lawful means for women to protect themselves while maintaining strict public safety standards.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legalise pepper spray in England: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742673

action: Not use our military bases to house refugees who entered our country illegally.
background: Stop using military bases to house asylum seekers. These sites are for remembering our fallen heroes, teaching and honouring service, not residential use. The Government should find suitable civilian or purpose-built accommodation that meets needs while preserving our military heritage.
additional_details:
Military bases are old heritage which helps us remember our fallen heroes and teaching future generations. NOT housing. Using them undermines their purpose and heritage.

Our soldiers did not fight and die for this country to end up the way it has, and especially to have their bases took over by asylum seekers.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Stop asylum seekers being given housing in military establishments 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/748431

action: Urge Israel to permit regular humanitarian access to all Palestinian prisoners
background: We believe Israel is obliged to respect international humanitarian law under the 1949 Geneva Conventions which includes facilitating access by the International Committee of the Red Cross to all Palestinian detainees. We feel it's unacceptable that Israel continues to refuse access.
additional_details: We believe the UK Government should actively insist that there is no justification whatsoever for an alternative to the ICRC and that it must retain its uniquely vital and independent role in monitoring the conditions and treatment of all Palestinian detainees. The UK Government should actively promote and advocate for adherence to IHL and strongly insist that Israel immediately grants the ICRC regular access to all of its Palestinian detainees.

action: Require a referendum in the local area subject to a council being abolished
background: The current process allows Government to force top-down council reorganisations without a final, binding say from local residents. We believe that local consultations are often flawed. We demand the law be changed to give residents the democratic right to a referendum.
additional_details: Giving people a final say in a binding local referendum is the only democratic way to ensure reorganisations of local councils can only be done if there is support from the local people.

action: Provide government funding for early dyslexia screening in all primary schools
background: We are calling on the Government to provide funding for early dyslexia screening in all primary schools. Early identification allows teachers and parents to give children the right support from the start, improving literacy, wellbeing, and long-term learning outcomes.
additional_details: Many children with dyslexia are not identified early enough to get the support they need. Without early screening, children can struggle with reading and learning, lose confidence, and experience anxiety at school. Currently parents are expected to pay privately for testing which is not something that everyone can afford. Every child deserves the chance to thrive, and early dyslexia screening can make a real difference to their education and mental health.

action: Review penalties for fleeing the scene after causing a fatal collision
background: Review penalties for those found guilty of fleeing the scene after causing a fatal accident through dangerous driving. Penalties should be equal with murder. These changes could be called Abi's law.
additional_details: We believe victims families and friends are not getting the justice they deserve.

action: Hold a vote of no confidence in the UK Government - Failure to Protect Citizens
background:
We call on Members of Parliament to hold a vote of no confidence in His Majesty’s Government.
The Government has a duty to protect the well-being and security of its citizens. 

With multiple attacks, rapes and murders by migrants, we have lost confidence in them to protect us and our shores
additional_details:
We believe the Government has failed to act effectively in the national interest and no longer commands public confidence.
MPs should act to restore trust and accountability through a formal vote of no confidence.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Call an immediate general election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727309

action: End experiments on animals at the Charles River Labratories in East Lothian.
background: Protect the reputation of East Lothian and build a positive future without the stigma of animal experiments which take place at Charles River Labratories in Tranent.
additional_details: Having Charles River Labratories in Tranent, Edinburgh portrays a negative view of the area amongst residents, tourists and reflects badly on nearby businesses. Although the practice of animal experiments is already widely protested across the UK, the local residents of East Lotian and Scotland feel the practice has no place in our area and wish parliament to consider putting an end to the reputation it brings to East Lothian.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions which call for actions with regard to named individuals, organisations or businesses.

Your petition is also about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

You may also wish to contact your local council and MSP who represent you about this issue. 

You can find the name of your local council and how to contact them here: https://www.mygov.scot/find-your-local-council

You can find the name of your local MSP and how to contact them here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps

action: Fund Level 7 Apprenticeships for over 21s if a MSc Is Essential for Career Entry
background: Instead of capping funding for Level 7 apprenticeships for those over 21, we urge the government to distinguish between career entry and career progression and continue funding level 7 apprenticeships (regardless of age) in fields where an MSc is the minimum qualification for starting a career.
additional_details: We believe the age cap is unworkable and excludes students on longer degrees, placement years, or those who paused studies due to illness, caregiving, or hardship—disproportionately affecting disadvantaged and mature learners. With postgraduate funding and student finance rarely covering tuition let alone living costs, apprenticeships can represent the only accessible and inclusive route into careers where an MSc is essential.

action: Make the COVID vaccine universally available, free of charge, to protect us all.
background: Provide the resources required by the NHS, to ensure that the COVID vaccine is available for all who would benefit from it, regardless of their age.
additional_details: COVID continues to exert a serious toll on national health. Its impact is felt across the NHS, schools, businesses, and industry — with clear consequences for the wider economy. While COVID primarily targets the respiratory system, it can affect multiple organs and trigger a wide spectrum of symptoms and complications, some leading to hospitalisation and potentially life-threatening outcomes. Unlike many other countries, the UK still restricts access to COVID vaccines, despite their vital role in reducing severe illness and protecting public health.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Fund COVID booster vaccines for the general public
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745188

action: Investigate the UK military equipments used by RSF militia in Sudan conflict
background: A report by The Guardian highlights that UK-manufactured equipments, originally sold to the UAE, have reportedly been used by the RSF. It led into question the current effectiveness of our export control system. It is imperative to ensure British-made arms do not end up in human atrocities in Sudan.
additional_details:
we strongly urge the UK Parliament to take immediate action. We call for a thorough investigation into how UK weapons might have been diverted into the RSF's hands. There is an urgent need to review export licences granted to countries with a track record of diverting weapons to conflicts.  
We urge the UK Parliament to act now to investigate and prevent any further contributions towards atrocities in Sudan.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Prevent arms sales to the UAE following reports of UK arms being used in Sudan
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/748446

action: Removal of LED headlights in motor vehicles
background: More LED headlights are being used on the road. These LED headlights are very dazzling to other drivers causing heightened risk and nervousness in drivers. I want these headlights banned from use or updating legislation to prevent them from dazzling other drivers.
additional_details: I want Parliament to action this to prevent nervousness and danger to public safety. The Headlights are more efficient for power usage and are more economically friendly however they cause more danger to other road users due to their dazzling nature, especially when they are not dipped. Additionally, they look to be more like high beams than your standard nightime headlights which indicates rhat full beams may be fully blinding to other road users
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action: 

Ban LED vehicle headlights or regulate bulb wattage
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744882

action: Create independent body to investigate school complaints
background: We ask the government to create an independent body to investigate all school complaints from the start. The investigators must not be connected to schools, or Local Authorities, to help ensure fair, transparent outcomes and accountability for school leaders when serious issues are raised.
additional_details:
We are concerned that school complaints may be handled by school staff or school governors who know the headteacher well and who are often friends, which may lead to bias, cover-ups, and unfair outcomes. We believe many parents and students have faced ignored or mishandled complaints due to this issue.
 
We think an independent body would ensure impartial, fair, and transparent investigations, hold school leaders accountable, restore trust in schools, and help ensure they are properly protecting and supporting students.

action: Create laws for manufacturers to make adjustments to vehicle headlights
background: Vehicle headlights have changed over the years. With the switch to LED headlights, modern headlights have become quite dangerous for other motorists. New regulations should be made to make driving easier and reduce dazzling especially in the winter months where visibility is reduced.
additional_details: Vehicle headlights should be placed at a specified height to prevent glare and reduced visibility for motorists. There should also be a section in the driving tests which teaches new drivers how to adjust their headlights to prevent blinding oncoming traffic.
rejection_details:
Ban LED vehicle headlights or regulate bulb wattage
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744882

action: We the people have no confidence in the current government of the UK
background: This petition should show the government just how many people have no confidence in their ability to lead. We need a change and quickly, we need a government thats acts in the interest of the people who they represent. Currently we feel unheard and let down.
additional_details: This is an excersize to show you how many people want change and quickly. We want leaders who actually listen and care about the British people. This petition is acting as a voice for all that feel let down.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition: 

Give the British Public the Right to Vote No Confidence in the Government
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734311

action: Remove fines for parents taking children out of school up to 5 days
background: Remove the fines and criminal record threats faced to parents when they decide to take children out of school for a short period of time. There are many reasons why parents decide to do this and the schools/government should be working with parents not against.
additional_details: This puts a huge amount of pressure and stigma to parents facing the cost of living crisis and/or parenting a child of SEN that going away during half terms isn’t suitable. Other situations for example parents not being able to take annual leave during half terms restricts them spending time together. Then with the fine and criminal record can be devastating. The pressure of having a criminal record for this makes parents feel stuck.Trust that parents have the best intentions for their children.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action: 

Allow parents to take their children out of school for 5 school days in a year
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728790

action: End the UK's asylum system & right to asylum, use resources for border security
background: We want the Government to legislate to end the UK asylum system. Remove the right to claim asylum in the UK, withdrawing from treaties that compel us to take asylum seekers, and closing all asylum centres. Resources should go to border security and swift deportation of those who arrive illegally.
additional_details: We believe the asylum system is unsustainable, open to abuse, and undermines our sovereignty. We think Britain should not be required to accept asylum seekers, especially when safe countries exist closer to their origin.

action: Pay NHS staff for the full 40 hours we spend responsible for patients each week.
background: NHS staff spend 40 hours a week away from family, yet part of this time is unpaid even when we continue caring for patients during breaks. We want the Government to ensure staff are paid for any break time where duties continue, with proper recording of interruptions.
additional_details: Working through unpaid breaks causes fatigue and impacts patient safety. Paying for this time reflects the reality of our work and supports staff through rising living costs. It would improve fairness, wellbeing and retention across the NHS.
rejection_details: If you are being made to work through your breaks, we suggest you complain to your NHS Trust.

action: Legalise UK Citizens copyright to their own likeness & bio-data
background: Introduce legislation to grant every UK citizen full ownership of their likeness, including their face, retina, voice and body data to ensure no system or company can replicate or use these without consent.
additional_details: This law could ensure that no AI system or company can replicate or use these data points without consent. The call for this legislation comes amid the global rise of AI deepfakes, where hyper-realistic digital copies of people are used for scams, fake news, and even political manipulation. We propose a person’s appearance and voice is intellectual property, giving individuals legal grounds to demand removal or compensation if their likeness is misused.

action: Introduce measures to protect digital ride-share drivers from exploitation
background: We believe digital ride share drivers face growing exploitation from platform companies. They can take big commissions while paying little to drivers. Drivers work long hours but can earn less as fares and profits rise. Drivers now demand government action to end this unfair system.
additional_details: We believe that ride share companies profit while drivers carry all risk and cost. They change rates without consultation, leaving drivers struggling with fuel, maintenance, and inflation. We want new rules ensuring drivers keep at least 80% of fares, fair pay standards, and oversight of fare algorithms. The government must act now to protect hardworking drivers from ongoing exploitation and restore fairness in this essential industry

action: Legally require airports to be closed on Christmas Day for staff holiday
background:
We want all airport and airline workers to be granted Christmas Day off or a full 24-hour operational pause across the aviation network
 
- A national pause in commercial airport operations on 25 December
- A guaranteed full-day closure allowing every airport worker at least one Christmas Day off
additional_details: Airport and airline workers deserve Christmas Day off, just like other transport staff. Rail, bus, and ferry services stop, yet aviation continues, denying employees rest and family time. These workers keep the nation moving all year. The government should legislate to ensure a 24 hour pause on Christmas Day to promote fairness, wellbeing, and respect for those who serve the public every other day.

action: Release full crime statistics involving illegal immigrants and asylum seekers.
background: The Government must immediately release full, unedited crime statistics involving all undocumented migrants and asylum recipients. The British public, who fund asylum through taxes, have the absolute right to know the safety impact and financial burden — no delays, no excuses, full transparency now.
additional_details: Illegal immigration is out of control and the British public are being kept in the dark about its true impact. Crimes committed by those who entered the UK unlawfully threaten the safety of citizens and children. The government must release full data to restore accountability, protect the public, and uphold national security.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what statistics you'd like the Government to publish that it doesn't already publish.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You can find out more about what statistics the Government already publishes, here: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/statistics-on-foreign-national-offenders-and-the-immigration-system/statistics-on-foreign-national-offenders-and-the-immigration-system

action: Ensure post-adopted children are able to remain in contact with people they love
background: Ensure children who are adopted have the option to stay in touch with the people they love if it is safe to do so; such as Foster Carers, Siblings or Grandparents.
additional_details: Not staying in touch can re-traumatise the children who may have had trauma in their past. Foster Carers are encouraged to form strong attachments with children in their care and when these attachments are broken it can cause distress and feelings of mistrust for the children. We are concerned that foster carers are not being informed of current legislation around adoption orders and are unaware the court can decide who remains in contact.

action: Ban MPs from accepting any gifts or donations from businesses and individuals
background: Politicians are lawmakers and should be held to the highest standards of integrity. Yet MPs are currently allowed to accept gifts, hospitality, and donations from businesses and individuals. We think that even when declared, this can create a clear conflict of interest and undermine public trust.
additional_details: Other public servants — such as police officers, doctors, or members of the armed forces — are not permitted to accept gifts which may be perceived to influence their professional decisions. We think the same standard must apply to politicians. We think that declaring a gift doesn’t make it ethical, and that it’s still a form of influence. We call for a complete ban on MPs accepting any gifts, payments, or hospitality from private individuals, companies, or lobbyists

action: Fund and implement A Universal Basic Income (UBI).
background: We believe that we are in an era of economic uncertainty, growing inequality, and job insecurity and it is time for Parliament to introduce a Universal Basic Income (UBI). Some Economists argue, UBI is not just a welfare measure, it is an investment in people, and a foundation for economic security.
additional_details:
A guaranteed, unconditional income would empower individuals, providing them with dignity and freedom from financial precariousness. It could support entrepreneurs, artists, and caregivers, those whose work is often undervalued yet essential to our society. UBI could reduce stress, improve mental health, offer a safety net in an age of automation and unstable employment.

UBI is a progressive, pragmatic solution to modern economic challenges, in contrast to systems that oppress and humiliate.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Introduce Liveable Basic Income and repurpose Jobcentre buildings for community" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744058

action: Require Companies to notify candidates of their application status
background: Make it a legal requirement for companies to inform candidates that they haven't gotten through the application stage or that haven't received a position after an interview within a reasonable time period.
additional_details:
Thousands of people that apply for jobs in this country are getting no response about their job applications. Majority of those who get a response don't even get feedback or the opportunity to get feedback.

In Ontario Canada, a new law is coming January 1st 2026 to make it a legal requirement for companies with 25 or more staff to inform candidates whether the position they applied for has been filled within 45 days of the last interview.
rejection_details:
This is a duplicate of this open petition (below):

Require employers to send responses to all job applications: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742375

action: Require DBS checks for all staff in Soft Play centres.
background: We want the Government to amend safeguarding legislation so that all staff working in Soft Play environments are required to undergo DBS checks, ensuring consistent child protection standards across all childcare and play settings, and closing what we see as a clear safeguarding gap in current law.
additional_details:
Soft Play staff are not legally required to hold DBS checks, leaving a clear gap in child protection. Children often interact with staff beyond parents’ sight. 
 
An NSPCC report found that 1 in 20 children experience sexual abuse. The Government’s 2025 update on tackling child sexual abuse stated that every institution must help close spaces where children are vulnerable. DBS checks would align Soft Play with schools and close this safeguarding loophole.

action: Help Preserve Rothbury Estate for Wildlife and Future Generations
background: We ask the UK Government to match donations raised by The Wildlife Trusts for the £30 million purchase of the Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, securing this 3,800-hectare landscape for wildlife, restoring nature on a national scale, and protecting it for people and future generations.
additional_details: The Rothbury Estate is one of the most important opportunities in decades to restore nature on a landscape scale. By helping The Wildlife Trusts secure this land, Government can protect vital habitats for species like curlew, red squirrel and otter, support local communities, and leave a lasting legacy for nature, people and climate.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Establish review of risks to UK democracy from foreign influence on social media
background: We ask the Government to commission an independent review into the influence of foreign individuals and entities with significant control over major online platforms used in the UK. The review should assess potential risks to national security, democratic integrity, and the spread of misinformation.
additional_details:
Social media platforms have become key sources of news and political discussion for millions of UK citizens. We think that when these platforms are owned or controlled by individuals or organisations based outside the UK, there may be risks to democratic processes, public safety, and national security.
 
We believe recent events and inflammatory public statements by high-profile platform owners highlight the need for accountability, and safeguards against any manipulation of UK public opinion and political discourse.

action: • Build a significant amount of Green bridges across the UK to protect wildlife
background:
• There are a significant amount of animals killed on roads every day;
Annual road kill estimates
Foxes: Up to 100,000
Badgers: Up to 50,000
Deer: Up to 50,000
Birds: Approximately 30 million
Hedgehogs: About 29% of the population, which may contribute to their decline.
additional_details:
• Deer-vehicle collisions cause thousands of injuries and dozens of fatalities annually, with one source estimating around 74,000 deer involved in collisions each year. 
• Wildlife crossings significantly reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions by 85% to 95% with the help of fencing.
• For example, a highway in Colorado saw a 90% decrease in animal collisions after installing seven crossings, two overpasses, and five underpasses.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure what you mean by a "significant amount" of green bridges.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Abolish 0.5% Stamp Duty Reserve Tax on UK-Listed Equities
background: In order to promote more investment in UK industry by domestic & international investors the government should remove the current 0.5% Stamp Duty Investment Tax on UK listed Equities.
additional_details:
Removing Stamp Duty Reserve Tax will help the UK to be a competitive investment location when compared with other Countries where there is no equivalent tax levied.
Such reform could also encourage greater participation in share ownership by UK savers, align with the Government’s stated objective to revitalise the London stock market and reinforce the UK’s reputation as a leading global financial centre.

action: Require Fine-Issuing Bodies to Let People Check Pending Fines and Appeal Sooner
background: Require all fine-issuing companies and organisations to provide a service where individuals can check if a fine is being processed, enabling prompt appeals or peace of mind immediately.
additional_details: I often spend weeks worrying after parking or passing a speed camera—unsure if a technical error or a mistaken flash will lead to a fine. This uncertainty causes unnecessary stress that could easily be avoided. Fine-issuing organisations should be legally required to provide a service where people can check if a fine is pending. Such transparency would give peace of mind, reduce anxiety, and ensure people can promptly challenge any fines issued unfairly or in error.
rejection_details:
We are not clear whether this petition is asking for quicker processing of fines, or ability to check pending fines, and therefore it is not clear what action is being sought from the UK Government or Parliament.

You can start a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Require sanitary waste bins in all toilets regardless of gender
background: Change UK law to make it a legal requirement for businesses, public places and all social places with female, MALE and unisex restrooms to provide a safe and hygienic means for the disposal of sanitary waste to prevent environmental harm and maintain public health and hygiene standards.
additional_details: Following treatments relating to the removal of prostate cancers from men, the side effects can be very catastrophic and debilitating. We believe there is not enough emphasis, knowledge or awareness as to the requirements needed for men coping with their need to use sanitary products and the difficulty of disposal when facilities are not available.

action: Functional Neurological Disorder
background: We ask the UK Government to improve support and treatment for people with Functional Neurological Disorder (FND). This should include funding for specialist NHS clinics, mandatory training for healthcare professionals, and official recognition of FND as a serious neurological condition.
additional_details: We need the Government to take FND seriously by funding dedicated services, improving awareness, and ensuring those affected receive the same level of care and dignity as anyone living with a neurological illness.
rejection_details: We think this petition is very similar to yours: Fund better Functional Neurological Disorder care, treatment and support: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/727063

action: Ban training generative AI with creative works without artists' consent
background: The government should make it illegal for AI developers to train generative AI models on creative works - such as art, music, writing and film - without the creator's explicit consent. Artists deserve control and fair compensation for the use of their work.
additional_details: For too long, AI developers have gotten away with what we think is the effective theft of millions of creative works without permission, as a way of training their generative AI models. If a regular person redistributed this material, they could face thousands of pounds in fines. Artists deserve protection, control, and compensation for how their work has been used without their consent, while tech companies currently face no legal accountability.

action: Allow Women from 18+ to carry a form of protection. i.e pepper spray.
background: Allow Women from the ages of 18+ to carry pepper spray as a form of protection for self defence against predators and abusers.
additional_details: With the rising numbers of assault/ sexual assault against women and children and the appalling rate of which men are being caught and sentenced, I feel it fair to allow women to carry pepper spray as not only will it make women feel safer but also hopefully deter abusers/predators from attacking when they are faced with the possibility of a painful and uncomfortable retaliation. The idea of a woman carrying pepper spray will be far more feared than jail time as that rarely ever happens.
rejection_details:
We think this petition is very similar to yours: 

Legalise pepper spray in England: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742673

action: Abolish 10 year spouse route and replace with one 5 year route to ILR
background: Provide a single, UK Spouse visa path to ILR for all eligible couples; abolish the 5-year/10-year split and cap renewal costs. We believe this will be fairer.
additional_details: I urge the government to simplify the spouse visa process with a single 5-year route. We believe the current 10-year pathway is unfair, discriminatory, and overly complex, often necessitating expensive legal assistance. A streamlined process could alleviate financial and emotional burdens, promote equality, and enable families to settle and integrate more effectively, allowing spouses to contribute positively to society.

action: Abolish IPSA and set MP salaries to 160% of the 'National Living Wage'.
background: We want the government to abolish The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority pay settlement function and set MP pay at 160% of the 'National Living Wage'.
additional_details: We feel that Politicians have too many privileges currently and we think this will make them a little more sensitive to poverty in Britain.

action: Reopen Whitmore Railway Station
background: Reopen the former railway station in Whitmore, Newcastle, Staffordshire. Opened in 1837 and closed on 1952, Whitmore railway stations served thousands in the surrounding villages of Whitmore, Baldwins Gate, and others.
additional_details: Whitmore is less than a 10 minutes drive from many places, Madeley, Baldwins Gate, Ashley, Loggerheads, Butterton, Chapel Chorlton, and more. All of these places have to go to Stoke, Stafford, or Crewe for a rail link. The reopening of Whitmore would provide the almost 10 thousand residents of these villages a much needed rail link to the rest of the country.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level. 
 
You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this. 
 
You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP 
 
And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Tv-licence holders to be able to demand refund
background: We call on legislation to be introduced to enable tv license payers to be able to demand a 50% refund if the BBC is found to have breached its Charter and not provided an on-air public apology.
additional_details: This apology should be issued within a period of 24 hours following the airing of a programme, article or comment which has been found to have breached its Charter.

action: Leave the european conventionon human rights
background: Leave the ECHR
additional_details: Discuss  leaving the ECHR in order  for the Uk to make its own decisions on immigration and other issues in our courts.
rejection_details:
Leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729027

action: Reintroduce the death penalty for murder
background: We believe the death penalty for murder should be reintroduced based on key principles of justice and public protection.
additional_details: We think it could deliver ultimate justice, prevent future murders and be a stronger deterrent. We also think it could serve to align the justice system with a perceived need for ultimate justice.

action: Make Legal Aid available for UK Citizens ONLY
background: Ban Legal Aid for illegal migrants
additional_details: see above
rejection_details:
The action in the title and the action in the main text are not the same - action sought is unclear

There are two current petitions on this subject that the petitioner might wish to sign:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741349

and

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733844

action: Require companies to match board bonuses with employee-wide bonus distributions
background: Introduce a law requiring any company that awards a cash bonus or dividend to a board member or director to match that amount with a proportional bonus distributed across all employees.
additional_details: This change would ensure company success is shared fairly by everyone. In our view, too often, company profits reward only executives while workers see little benefit. We believe sharing bonuses fairly would improve morale, retention, and productivity, while boosting spending and reducing wealth inequality. We think that when employees share in success, businesses thrive, communities grow, and the UK economy strengthens. This simple reform could create a fairer, more motivated and balanced workforce.

action: Allow UK nationals living abroad to donate organs in the UK
background: Current UK organ-donation policy excludes British nationals who live abroad but die in the UK, even when they have indicated clear consent to donate. The residency restriction means willing donors are excluded, resulting in missed opportunities to save lives.
additional_details: We therefore ask the Government to amend legislation to allow donation in cases where explicit consent exists, regardless of residence status

action: On Thursdays, Friday and Saturdays have a late last C2C train from Fenchurch St
background: Provide a safe route home for people who end up missing the last train and have no way home back to Essex and cannot afford uber/taxi prices.
additional_details: After speaking to many people, and having many experiences myself - although you may leave time to make the last train home which is (usually 12.40am), the traffic in London to get from one destination to another safely makes it nearly impossible to make it to the station in time. additional_details:

We believe this is a vital step to make pet microchipping work. We call on the government to deliver the central portal now to make chips count.
government_response_summary: Defra is currently working with the Association of Microchip Database Operators to develop commercial solutions that will provide easier access to microchip records for authorised users.
government_response_body: Since the introduction of compulsory dog microchipping in 2016, the number of compliant database operators has risen from 4 to 24. Whilst the growth in the number of database operators has resulted in more choice for consumers, it has made it harder for approved users such as vets to access records quickly.    To address this, as set out in the Animal welfare strategy for England,   (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/animal-welfare-strategy-for-england/animal-welfare-strategy-for-england)   Defra is working with the Association of Microchip Database Operators (AMDO) to develop improvements to the way the microchipping regime currently operates.  AMDO is currently testing industry-led solutions that will enable authorised users to access information contained on the databases digitally through a single point of search.  Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

action: Hold an inquiry into CAMHS and NHS children’s mental health delays
background: Establish an inquiry into reported failures in CAMHS and NHS delays affecting children’s mental health, school attendance, and welfare outcomes.
additional_details: Many children face long waits for CAMHS and NHS mental health support, which can leave families without help and pupils unable to attend school. Access to care and GP prescribing of SSRIs can vary by postcode, which can create unfair treatment gaps. These failures can harm education and drive rising welfare costs. EHCP's are also being affected as we feel the H (Health) parts are not being addressed. This can cause further costs to cash strapped local authorities. An inquiry is needed now.
government_response_summary: The Government has no current plans to establish an inquiry. Multiple actions are in place to improve and reform NHS mental health services and provide children with timely access to appropriate care.
government_response_body: The nation’s mental health has deteriorated over the past decade. Lord Darzi’s investigation highlighted that people accessing NHS mental health services — including children and young people — face long waits, variable quality of care and persistent inequalities.  This Government has already taken important steps to stabilise and improve mental health services, but we recognise that much more needs to be done. Transforming the system will take time, but we are committed to delivering a fundamentally new approach to mental health care.  Progress is already being made. In the first 12 months of this Government, nearly 40,000 more children and young people accessed NHS mental health support compared with the previous year. This has been supported by the recruitment of over 7,000 additional mental health workers since July 2024, putting us on track to meet our target of 8,500 by the end of this Parliament.  We are also investing in innovation and evidence-based improvement. Since July 2024, more than £100 million has been awarded through National Institute for Health and Care Research mental health research programmes to improve treatments and care pathways. This includes £1.5 million awarded in October to 17 innovative health technology projects aimed at reducing waiting times for children and young people.  The NHS 10 Year Health Plan sets out an ambitious programme of reform to make the NHS fit for the future. Building on this, we will go further to ensure mental health services consistently deliver timely, high-quality care. It is clear that ‘more of the same’ will not suffice. We will continue to reform how mental health support is delivered, reducing waits, improving quality and embedding a whole-of-society approach focused on prevention and early intervention.  By spring 2026, up to 900,000 additional children and young people will have access to an NHS-funded Mental Health Support Team in their school or college. As part of our shift from treatment to prevention, we will accelerate rollout to achieve full national coverage by 2029. We will also strengthen workforce capability to better support young people with complex needs, including trauma, neurodivergence and disordered eating. To support this, we are investing £13 million to pilot enhanced staff training, informing future phases of the programme.  On 15 July, the Prime Minister set out plans to open 50 Young Futures Hubs over the next four years. Hubs will bring together services to improve access to opportunities and support for young people at community level, promoting positive outcomes and enabling them to thrive. The first eight Young Futures Hubs will launch by the end of this financial year, backed by a £2 million investment and targeted in areas with high levels of crime and antisocial behaviour, offering a lifeline to vulnerable young people. Work with these early adopters will inform the longer-term development of the programme, including how quickly we move to a greater number of hubs. We will set out more details in due course.  The Medium Term Planning Framework sets out how reforms from the 10 Year Health Plan will be delivered, including reducing the longest waits for children and young people’s community mental health services, improving productivity and tackling local inequalities and unwarranted variation in access.  Alongside this, the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care has launched an independent review into the prevalence of, and support for, mental health conditions, ADHD and autism. We are deeply concerned that too many adults, children and young people have been let down by services and are not receiving timely or appropriate support.  The review will inform our future approach to mental health, ensuring people receive the right support, at the right time and in the right place. It will also shape how we support people with ADHD and autistic people to live well in their communities. The review will examine prevalence, early intervention, treatment pathways and the challenges facing clinical services, as well as the evidence on diagnosis, medicalisation and outcomes.  It will also identify opportunities for alternative models of support and pathways, both within and beyond the NHS, that strengthen prevention and early intervention alongside clinical care. The review will be led by Professor Peter Fonagy, supported by vice-chairs Professor Sir Simon Wessely and Professor Gillian Baird, and guided by an Advisory Working Group of academics, clinicians, charities, epidemiological experts and people with lived experience.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Abolish "Polkey deductions" in compensation for unfair dismissal
background: The “Polkey deduction” lets tribunals reduce compensation for unfair dismissal by estimating the chance an employee would have been dismissed even if a fair process had been followed. We think this undermines the statutory right to a fair procedure and rewards employers who bypass due process.
additional_details: We ask the Government to amend the Employment Rights Act 1996 so that, where dismissal is found procedurally unfair, compensation is not reduced on “it would have happened anyway” grounds. Employers should bear the consequences of failing to follow a fair process. We believe this reform would restore the protective purpose of unfair dismissal law, vastly improve workplace standards, and provide clear incentives for lawful, respectful and fair dismissals.

background: Pass a law which strengthens male reproductive rights by making vasectomies more accessible for men and ensures contraception deceit invalidates consent.
additional_details: We believe men currently have limited legal protection over their reproductive choices. We think that doctors should not be able to refuse or seek to dissuade men from having vasectomies based on their age or parental status. Lying about your fertility or use of any sort of contraception to a sexual partner should be illegal and make the other person’s consent invalid.

additional_details: Families have suffered birth trauma, injuries, and loss due to unsafe staffing and overstretched maternity units. Many NHS trusts are not part of current investigations. We think a full national investigation and increased funding for midwife recruitment and training are urgently needed to ensure safety and accountability for all families.

additional_details: The government should refrain from taxing income earned through work. We believe people across all income levels are struggling, from those on minimum wage to higher earners. We believe wealth held in static assets contributes little to economic growth and can widen the wealth gap. In our view, a targeted wealth tax offers a fair and effective solution.

action: Legislate to make car insurance calculations transparent
background: We want the Government to mandate that car insurers must disclose how they calculate car insurance quotes. We would like to see detailed calculations, showing us all the factors, and where applicable the range of possible values for a given factor.
additional_details: Car insurance prices in the UK are among the very highest in the world. Providers are currently not required to disclose any level of detail of how they calculate our quotes. This puts the insurance industry in a very strong position. We believe it allows them to approach the public with a take it or leave it attitude, stops the public from understanding contributing factors and what can be done to improve the situation, stifles competition and creates possibilities for discrimination.

action: Require hospitality venues to offer in-person food ordering service
background: We would like to ask the government to mandate that all businesses serving food must provide the ability to order food in person, and to accept payments using traditional payment methods, being cash or card (no forced online-only payments).
additional_details: More and more places stop taking orders in person and require all customers to use a website or an app to place their food or drink orders. While we do understand that this is to streamline processes, optimise space and reduce costs, online-only orders discriminate against those among us who are not tech savvy (i.e. elderly), people with disabilities (affecting cognitively and visually impaired the most), or those who simply do not wish to give up their sensitive personal details to order food.

action: Allow adults to buy, possess, carry regulated pepper/PAVA spray for self-defence
background: People feel unsafe and unable to defend themselves. Current law bans all incapacitant sprays, leaving citizens defenceless. Allowing regulated pepper or PAVA sprays for self-defence, with training and strict penalties, would give law-abiding adults a non-lethal way to protect themselves.
additional_details: People are being attacked on public transport and streets, yet the law bans even non-lethal sprays for defence. Allowing trained, licensed adults to carry regulated pepper or PAVA spray would give them a lawful, safe way to protect themselves and others where there is an imminent risk to life, while keeping strict penalties and safeguards to prevent misuse.

action: Allow National Lottery funds to support social housing
background: Allow National Lottery funds to support social housing at social rent, whether provided by local authorities, community land trusts, housing co-operatives, or other not-for-profit providers. Change the rules relating to the principle of additionality to allow this.
additional_details: The National Lottery generates almost £2 billion annually for good causes, yet current rules prevent it funding social housing provided by local authorities or community-led, not-for-profit organisations despite the severe housing crisis. Many people wait years for a home, some in temporary or unsafe accommodation. Allowing lottery funds to support genuine social housing at social rent, regardless of provider, would unlock a vital, sustainable source of funding. It is unfair that a public resource cannot directly help those in need.

action: Make parental alienation a criminal offence
background: We want the Government to make Parental Alienation a criminal offence. We believe deliberately turning a child against a loving parent is emotional abuse. The law should make it an offence, train professionals to identify it, and hold offenders accountable to protect children’s rights.
additional_details: It was reported that parental alienating behaviours affect around 59% of separated families in the UK, and can be linked to child anxiety, depression, and long-term trauma. Many children grow up without a loving bond to one parent. We feel it remains unrecognised in law. Making it a criminal offence could protect children’s mental health, hold abusers accountable, and preserve the right of every child to love and be loved by both parents.

action: End all subsidies for food and drink for MP’s, Lords and all public servants.
background: The cost of buying basics like food and drink should be felt by all, especially those elected by and supposedly representing the public. The cost to MP’s, Lords and public servants of buying food and drink should not be subsidised at any time and wholly paid for directly without subsidies or gifting
additional_details: The entire nation is feeling the pinch of food and drink pricing. Whenever possible, those elected to represent the public or paid by the public purse must feel the same financial pressures as those they represent. To this end, food and drink must cost MP’s, Lords and public servants exactly the same as it would cost the average person in the same area/location. This might lead to better representation but most importantly is fair to the public and tax payer.
rejection_details:
Catering services for the House of Commons are provided by an in-house team who do not provide a subsidised service in the commercial sense of the word. Some venues make a profit, referred to as contribution because it contributes to reducing overall costs. In other venues, the cost of providing the service does exceed the income received in sales due to the irregular hours and unpredictability of parliamentary business. The contribution or cost of each venue is calculated by subtracting the food and operational costs from the catering sales. Rather than a subsidy, the House monitors the contribution or cost of each catering venue, which include cafeterias, dining rooms, restaurants and bars. Prices of food and drink are regularly benchmarked against appropriate external comparators.

You can read more about this here: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/freedom-of-information/information-we-already-publish/house-of-commons-publication-scheme/catering-services/house-of-commons-cost-of-catering/

We can't accept petitions about catering in the House of Lords as that is the responsibility of the House of Lords.

action: End gifting to MP’s, Lords and public servants

additional_details:
Firstly, the acceptance of gifts risks influencing the opinions and decision making of elected officials or those who have financial control of tax payer funding.
Secondly, MP’s, Lords and public servants should all feel the same financially pressures as those they represent. It is simply outrageous that people in such a privileged position seem fit to accept such gifts under the noses of those they were elected to represent.

action: Apply to Rejoin the EU as soon as possible to increase growth in the UK
background: We believe Brexit's not working. additional_details:
The OBR (Office for Budget Responsibility) March 2025 economic forecasts show the Brexit Trade and Cooperation Agreement will reduce long-run productivity by 4% due mainly to the increase in non-tariff barriers on trade with both imports and exports 15% lower, and that new trade deals will not have a material impact to offset this. Also that savings on payments to the EU have been absorbed by increased Government spending.

It's time to seek to rejoin the EU, remove those barriers and boost the economy.
government_response_summary: The UK will not be rejoining the EU, but this Government has reset its relationship with the EU with a new strategic partnership: A deal that is good for UK bills, borders, jobs and growth.
government_response_body: The Government was elected in July 2024 with a clear mandate to strengthen our relationship with the EU without rejoining the Single Market, Customs Union or returning to freedom of movement.   Since taking office, we have reset our relations with European partners in order to improve our diplomatic, economic, and security cooperation.  On 19 May 2025, at the first ever Summit between the UK and the EU, the Prime Minister announced a deal with the EU that will deliver on what the British public voted for last year. It’s good for bills, good for our borders, and good for jobs.  The deal we have struck will reduce trade barriers through the Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) agreement, increase energy efficiency through cooperation on electricity trading, and allow a cheaper transition to net zero through linking our Emissions Trading Schemes (ETS). These measures reduce costs for businesses, meaning better prices and more choice to consumers, and they will support British jobs and livelihoods.  Through this deal, the UK has unprecedented access to the EU market – the best of any country outside the EU or EFTA. The SPS and ETS linking measures alone are set to add nearly £9 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, in a significant boost for growth.  Our focus for 2026 is all about driving forward. Negotiations for the UK’s association to Erasmus+ in 2027 have concluded  and we are now working to conclude negotiations on the Youth Experience Scheme, establishing a common Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS)  Area and linking our Emissions Trading Systems (ETS) by the time of the next EU-UK Summit, so that businesses and consumers can benefit from the impacts of these agreements as soon as possible.   This Government is seizing the flexibility of Brexit - making the best choices for business and citizens from its position outside the EU, through significant deals with the US and India, and now a new partnership with the EU - each decision taken to support UK growth. This is making a Brexit that works for Britain.  Cabinet Office

action: Any form of personal tax rise,the public should demand a general election.

action: Abolish UK Mayors
background: We believe mayors represent an expensive, unnecessary layer of bureaucracy that duplicates existing council functions without delivering proportional value.
additional_details: We call on the Government to introduce legislation to scrap all mayors immediately and redirect any savings to frontline services like policing and education. We believe streamlined and empowered local councils would provide faster cheaper governance.

action: The right to hold referendum to vote on what happens to Staffordshire Moorlands
background: The residents of Staffordshire Moorlands want the right to hold a referendum to vote on the up and coming Government reorganisation plans.
additional_details: Staffordshire Moorlands residents are not happy with the proposed local reorganisation plans. We want the right to accept or reject proposals.

action: Allow people with coeliac disease to join the armed forces
background: I would like the Government to supply gluten free food/ration packs for people with coeliac disease so that people with the disease can join the armed forces.
additional_details: I want Parliament to support this decision because the armed forces are currently under recruited and there are low levels of employment for our country. There are many people that have coeliac disease that would love to join the army, including me, and I believe that allowing the ever increasing amount of people with coeliac disease to join the armed forces, would be beneficial for both them and our country.

action: Bring back weekly bin collections in Sandwell!
background:
We, the residents of Sandwell, are calling on Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council to reinstate weekly household waste collections. 
Since collections were reduced to a fortnightly schedule, our community has seen a clear decline in cleanliness and public hygiene.
additional_details:
Overflowing bins, missed collections, and rubbish left on pavements have become far too common. This is unacceptable and poses real health concerns for families and children. 
Residents pay full council tax and deserve a reliable, hygienic service. Longer gaps between collections are causing pest problems, foul odours, and make our streets unpleasant to live on. Every household deserves clean streets and a reliable waste service. The current system is failing residents.

additional_details: Knife and violent attacks are rising, leaving people defenceless. Other countries safely allow regulated sprays to help people escape danger. The UK should trust citizens with sensible, non-lethal protection to deter attackers and save lives.

additional_details: Schools can currently rewrite or summarise minutes of key meetings, leaving parents without an accurate record of what was said. Keeping word-for-word records would ensure fairness, transparency and accountability, and protect both children and schools from dispute or misrepresentation.

additional_details: I want Parliament to act because prohibition is failing to protect young people and communities. action: Ban unsupervised child contact during criminal investigations
background: Make it mandatory for all unsupervised child contact to be paused while an investigation into allegations of abuse, violence or coercive control by a parent is ongoing. If the police or CPS decide to take no further action, a Family Court Finding of Fact Hearing should automatically follow.
additional_details: When unsupervised contact continues during investigations, families can face preventable harm. A police or CPS “No Further Action” only means the criminal threshold wasn’t met. Any police investigation or CPS referral signals serious concern and requires heightened safeguarding. To protect victims, we think contact should, as a minimum, be professionally supervised during investigations, with a Fact-Finding Hearing afterwards, ensuring decisions are informed, evidence-based, and centred on safety.

action: Make it a legal obligation to keep election pledges or rerun election if broken.
background: Parties need to legally do any and all checks before making each election pledge, and then legally they have to keep those pledges. If the manifesto pledges are subsequently broken unless through entirely unforeseeable circumstances then the election needs to be re-run.
additional_details: It is immoral for a party to make pledges, secure votes from them and win elections, and then - as there's no legal requirement to keep  any of those promises - they aren't kept. It must be a legal requirement to perform auditable checks on whether they can commit to these pledges before they are made, and then to uphold those pledges if they win the election. Unless there are extraordinary, unavoidable, unforeseen circumstances, then if pledges aren't kept then the election needs to be rerun.

action: Introduce an independent appeals panel for school absences
background: As it stands, the decision whether a school absence is authorised or not lies solely with the headteacher or designated attendance officer. If this person deems the absence as not "exceptional" enough, or marks an illness absence as unauthorised, there is no formal right of appeal for parents.
additional_details: I'm proposing that the Government sets up an independent national appeals panel to allow parents to appeal a heads decision. This will prevent bias, ensure transparency, and put a stop to blanket policies within schools. Often, the nature of the absence means it should either be marked as authorised under code 'I', or authorised under code 'C' which is leave for exceptional circumstances. If a FPN is issued, parents are forced to risk court and a criminal conviction or accept liability by paying the FPN.
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to introduce an independent national appeals panel for school absences and believes there are already sufficient routes for parents to challenge inaccurate absence coding.
government_response_body: The Government has no plans to introduce an independent national appeals panel for school absences.  When determining the most appropriate attendance or absence code, teachers and headteachers should use their professional judgement of each pupil’s individual circumstances, context and educational needs, alongside the ‘Working together to improve school attendance’ guidance and information provided by the parent or guardian.  Existing processes including informal conversations, use of the school’s complaints procedure, local authority complaints procedures, Ofsted inspections and escalation routes to DfE and to the Local Government Ombudsman provide appropriate channels for oversight and raising concerns, negating the need for a separate appeals structure.  Parents have a legal duty under the Education Act 1996 to ensure that their child of compulsory school age (5-16) receives a full‑time education, either by attending school or otherwise. Where a child is registered at a school, parents must ensure they attend regularly. Parents can be penalised if their child is absent from school without authorisation.  We recognise there are situations in which a pupil is unable to attend school for a legally recognised reason. The Education Act 1996 sets out these situations in which an absent pupil will not be taken to have failed to attend school regularly. These include illness or other unavoidable circumstances, religious observance, where the school has given prior permission for absence, or where the local authority has not fulfilled any duty it has to help the child attend.  Schools must record attendance in line with the School Attendance (Pupil Registration) (England) Regulations 2024 and with regard to the DfE’s statutory guidance ‘Working together to improve school attendance’. Decisions about how an absence should be recorded depend on the individual facts of each case. Headteachers and school staff know their pupils well and are therefore best placed to decide how an absence should be recorded. In the vast majority of cases, a parent’s notification that their child is ill should be sufficient for the school to authorise the absence using code I (illness). Schools also have discretion to grant a leave of absence in exceptional circumstances and parents should speak to their headteacher and present their case where they feel that such an absence is required.  The Department has however made clear in statutory guidance that, generally, a need or desire for a holiday or other absence for the purpose of leisure and recreation would not constitute an exceptional circumstance. The majority of penalty notices (93% in the 2024-25 academic year) are issued for term-time holidays.  Introducing an independent appeals panel would be inappropriate, given the ‘Working Together To Improve School Attendance’ guidance states that parents, schools and local authorities hold responsibility for pupils’ attendance.  It would also create a bureaucratic process for thousands of routine attendance decisions made every day. This would generate significant administrative burden for schools, local authorities and any central appeals body, which would need funding, diverting time and resources away from teaching and supporting pupils.  The Government believes that existing routes already provide clear and fair ways for parents to raise concerns. Where a parent believes an absence has been wrongly recorded, they should discuss this with the school in the first instance. If they remain dissatisfied, they can make a formal complaint through the school’s complaints procedure. If they believe the school has acted unlawfully, they can also escalate their complaint to the Department for Education or, where relevant, the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman.  Local authorities also have established processes for reviewing evidence before issuing a penalty notice for unauthorised absence. Although there is no separate legal right of appeal, parents can challenge a penalty notice with the issuing local authority if they believe it was wrongly issued. Parents may provide evidence to support their case, and the authority must consider it carefully. If parents do not pay the notice and wish to contest it, the case may proceed to court, where they can present their arguments before magistrates. This provides an additional safeguard for parents who believe they have been treated unfairly.  For these reasons, the Government does not believe that a new national appeals panel is necessary or appropriate. The current system already allows schools to apply professional judgement, gives parents clear ways to raise concerns or challenge decisions, and ensures that local authorities act carefully and proportionately in enforcing school attendance. This approach helps maintain consistency while keeping decision‑making close to the pupils and families who are directly affected.   Department for Education

The suffering a person with MND has to go through is unimaginable. Causing  unbearable pain for them and their family caring for a loved one. The Government must do more to help.

action: Stop all legal immigration to UK for workers earning less than £80000 a year
background: Suspend all immigration to UK for at least 5 years for workers earning £80,000 or less to reduce pressures on the economy, social housing, the NHS, schools and other resources.
additional_details:
The Government should focus on training British nationals to undertake jobs where there are shortages using national initiatives instead.

We believe the UK has a huge burden upon it due to mass legal and illegal migration. It affects everything in society from housing, to schools, to healthcare as well as the economy, which we believe has become all for the worse based on per capita. We feel it is time for the Government to listen to the people of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. We want it to stop for at least a period of 5 years, to take stock and re-evaluate risks and benefits to UK.

action: Require domestic cats to be kept inside April-September and wear belled collars
background: We require domestic cats to wear quick release multi-belled harnesses or belled collars all the time, when cats are venturing outside, and/or be kept house bound between the start of April, right through to the end of September, annually.
additional_details:
This timescale is the most important period of the year for wildlife to breed, raise their young and maintain their numbers, without being predated.

We want legal protection of wildlife from cat predation. Domesticated cats predate through instinct alone, an estimated 270 million animals and songbirds annually in the UK. We think the loss of tens of millions of animals and songbirds each year through cat predation is an increasingly worrying sign of some species being unable to maintain numbers and becoming possibly extinct in the future. 

Over the years, birds have been suffering from habitat loss, climate change and the seriously declining insect numbers, the very food that most birds depend upon and cat predation only condenses the seriousness of falling wildlife numbers.

action: Give the George Cross to Samir Zitouni
background: Reward the selfless bravery of this man who nearly died trying to protect his train passengers.
additional_details: The man ended up in intensive care with life threatening knife wounds. Reward this brave man.

action: Cut rents by 50% keeping mortgage payments unchanged to make housing affordable
background: Reduce all residential rents in the UK by 50% while keeping mortgage agreements unchanged. This would rebalance the housing market, make homes affordable again, and allow fairer access for first-time buyers blocked by inflated rents and speculation.
additional_details: The current housing system unfairly rewards those who already own multiple properties, while trapping millions in permanent rent dependency. Rents have risen alongside interest rates and inflation, yet wages have not kept pace — meaning renters are effectively paying landlord's mortgages and profits. A 50% rent cut, with mortgages unchanged, would make housing fairer and encourage sales of overleveraged (debt fuelled) properties, opening opportunities for new buyers and reducing inequality.

action: Stop Combe Pafford School Changing its Primary  need of MLD to ASC.
background: We Require the Department for Education to stop local authorities from removing Moderate Learning Difficulty (MLD) school places without ensuring alternative provision, and to fund new Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) schools instead of redesigning existing MLD schools.
additional_details: For over 30 years, Combe Pafford School in Torquay has supported children with moderate learning difficulties (MLD). Torbay Council now plans to change its main need to Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC), leaving no local provision for MLD pupils. With 257 students and long waiting lists, this school is essential. We call on Torbay Council to keep Combe Pafford as an MLD school and build a new ASC school instead.

action: Fund free NHS dental care for people with epilepsy
background: We ask the Government to make NHS dental treatment free for people diagnosed with epilepsy
additional_details:
People with epilepsy often suffer dental damage caused by seizures or the long-term use of anti-epileptic medication. This includes broken or chipped teeth, gum overgrowth, dry mouth, and enamel erosion.
 
These problems are medical consequences of epilepsy, not lifestyle choices, yet dental treatment for them is not covered under NHS exemptions. Many people struggle to afford essential dental care while managing a lifelong neurological condition

action: Do not introduce the Vaping Products Duty
background: Stop the introduction of the Vaping Products Duty in 2026. We want the Government to halt any new tax on e-liquids and vape products, including 0mg nicotine-free options, to protect small UK vape retailers and manufacturers from closure.
additional_details: We are concerned this duty could cripple small vape businesses, raise prices for adult consumers, and push many back to smoking. Many independent UK brands already face high costs and regulation; an extra tax could destroy fair competition and jobs. We believe the focus should be on harm reduction, not punishment of responsible traders.

action: We dont think that pay per mile has legitimate aims of revenue only & oppose it
background: We oppose the Chancellors Pay per  Mile on the basis that it violates the right to privacy article 8 of the Human Rights act 1998 & therefore we do not want it introduced. The only legitimate aim of taxation is £ & there.is no need to implement our personal tavel details & information Into revenue.
additional_details:
On Page 103 of the Blackstones guide to the Human Rights Act 1998 by John Wadham & Helen Mountfield

It states these criteria for the test of article 8: 

(a) that an interference corresponds to a pressing social need (Sunday Times v United Kingdom); 

(b) that it is proportionate to the legitimate aim pursued.

There is no social need for pay per mile, the existing system works fine.
We believe the government has ulterior motives in addition to taxation moving us towards a China Gov model

action: Reduce the time of day that fireworks can be set off to between 5pm & 8pm
background: Reduce the time in which fireworks can legally be set off to reduce the nuisance & detrimental effect on animals & vulnerable members of the community.
additional_details: We think fireworks are a public nuisance and there are endless reports of people setting them off later in the evenings on & around bonfire night in particular. This causes distress & disturbances to many people & animals, resulting in health issues.

action: Make 5 November a bank holiday.
background: Make Guy Fawkes Night an official Bank Holiday for everyone.
additional_details: As there is limited days off in a year time. Especially between last bank holiday in August and Christmas. Can we all have an extra bank holiday in November. There is reasonable argument that people would gladly have one day extra off. Let's make it on 5 November.

action: Make sign language a compulsory subject in secondary schools across England
background: The government should make sign language a compulsory and recognised subject in schools, it could be taught alongside other languages such as Spanish, French or German and should be made into a GCSE subject.
additional_details: We think it is a helpful skill to have as it can be applied to everyday life, it also prevents the barrier that some people may have as they are unable to communicate with one another. Sign language is more beneficial than subjects such as Spanish or French as many people will have difficulties speaking and rely on sign language to communicate their thoughts. This could be an inclusive opportunity for children to learn the importance of BSL.

action: Fund supported living for all autistic adults
background: We call on the government to fund supported living for autistic adults and including those without intellectual disabilities (ID) who cannot sustain education, training, or employment without specialist help.
additional_details:
Many have workplace skills but need support to access jobs. Support should focus on promoting independence, inclusion, quality of life.

Some autistic adults without intellectual disabilities do not receive housing support, leaving them without vital support for independent living. This group can be highly vulnerable; their challenges are often hidden and poorly understood by professionals with potentially devastating consequences. Delivering dedicated supported living could enable them to thrive, achieve independence, gain employment, reduce reliance on benefits and deliver economic and social benefits while promoting equality and inclusion.

only allow the sale of fireworks to official, competent events organisers for the purpose of fireworks displays to the general public or events.

Every year pets and other animals suffer fear, distress and anxiety caused by fireworks,it’s not just the 5th of November, people consistently let them off on the nights leading up to the 5th and continue to do so for many nights after the 5th.
This surely is a form of animal cruelty and needs to be regulated correctly.

Incorrect by scientific empirical evidence not by typos 
and replace them with entirely new formulas that already available based on the theory of congruence.

Parliament must intervene the curriculum so that the younger generation becomes the pioneers of the CORRECT and ACCURATE also SOPHISTICATED fundamental science.

action: Allow People to Choose Their Parental Titles on Their Child's Birth Certificate
background: Change the law to give people the ability to choose whether they are listed as "mother", "father", or "parent" on their child's birth certificate, be that at time of registration of birth, or to change it at a later date, without the requirement of a Gender Recognition Certificate.
additional_details:
We think the legal definitions of "mother" and "father" are severely outdated, reflecting biological roles corresponding with creating a child, rather than the genders of parents.

 
Trans parents use the terms they feel most comfortable with in their personal lives, and we think they should have the right to those terms in formal writing too, be that trans men who have given birth being recorded as "father", trans women as "mother", or non-binary parents as "parent".

Amend laws on parental titles on birth certificates
