background: The Speaker should be responsible for ensuring ministers give clear answers and that MPs are heard without distraction, supporting transparency for both Parliament and the public.
additional_details: PMQs should provide meaningful scrutiny, not political point-scoring. When ministers avoid questions, the public lose faith in the process. Requiring clear answers and stronger moderation would improve respect, restore accountability, and ensure PMQs fulfils its purpose as a forum for democratic oversight.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. 

Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker personally, and Ministers are responsible for answers to questions.

action: Make false claims about serving in the armed forces a specific criminal offence
background: We think there is growing trend in the UK for individuals to claim they have served in the Armed Forces. These individuals undermine genuine current serving personnel and veterans.
additional_details: The UK Government should make it illegal for a person to make false claims about serving in the Armed Forces. The crime should be punishable with a custodial sentence to prevent these individuals from making such false and misleading statements.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741677

action: Revise the Current 'Right to Repair' regulations
background: We demand that the UK Government revise the current ‘right to repair’ regulations to include smartphones, cordless phones, tablets, and laptops.
additional_details:
Right to repair regulations make it law that when you buy certain products, you have a right to repair them when they break - but it does not include smartphones, tablets or laptops. This means that people are trapped in a constant cycle of replacing these pieces of tech.
 
This is bad for the environment, bad for your pocket, and only good for the profit of huge companies.

action: Require that there are trained disclosure officers in all spas and hotels
background: We want the government to require all spas, salons and hotels to mandate a trained independent third-party disclosure officer in every venue.
additional_details: Spa, salon and hotel staff have disclosed sexual assault or harassment by clients. There can often be no direct reporting pathway, and no requirement for an independent third-party disclosure officer. We need a safe, trauma-informed system to protect staff and guests. Creating a clear pathway to reporting could protect both staff and guests.

action: Make secondary school blazers optional to students.
background: Students and families don’t like to blazer. it’s centuries old and isn’t professional. it’s a problem that sparks concern in british secondary’s that has a simple solution to it. why should such a thing cause so many problems in schools.Even when it doesn’t benefit us in any meaningful way.
additional_details: Simply, the blazers should be removed. I’ll explain why in a few reasons. Blazers are expensive, with families on average spending £100+ per child on uniforms, with blazers up to £40+.  A solution for the schools should be to print the logo onto jumpers instead. Another reason is that the blazer affects children, with it being uncomfortable and children refusing to wear it. We shouldn’t be annoyed at going to school for such a little item of clothing that doesn’t affect us. Please consider.
rejection_details: Decisions about uniform are a matter for individual schools, not the UK Government or Parliament. Government guidance "strongly recommends" that schools "consider how comfortable the proposed uniform will be for pupils" and "take a sensible approach to allow for exceptions to be made during extreme weather".

action: Legalise pepper spray in Scotland.
background: Women and girls should be able to defend themselves in our country. Coming and going to work or college in winter months in the dark can be scary for women  travelling alone. Pepper spray could save so many women’s lives.
additional_details: Women should be able to defend themselves from being attacked . Legalising pepper spray could stop so many women from being sexually assaulted or murdered.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legalise pepper spray in England
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742673

action: Stop advertisement on TV and phones being louder than the programme
background: When the adverts come on, the volume is such considerably louder on purpose and triggering
additional_details: Prevent purposely loud decibels and other tactics used by advertising companies

action: Ban the Use of E171 (Titanium Dioxide) in Food Products in the UK
background: We call on the UK Government to ban E171 (titanium dioxide) as a food additive. Recent scientific assessments have raised concerns about the potential for titanium dioxide particles to cause DNA damage and accumulate in the body over time.
additional_details:
These risks are especially troubling because E171 provides no nutritional value and is used only for colouring and whitening foods such as sweets, chewing gum, and sauces.

Given the uncertainty surrounding its long-term health effects, we urge the Government to take a precautionary approach and remove this additive from all food products sold in the UK.

action: The Northern Ireland Troubles Bill should be withdrawn
background: We believe the Troubles Bill contains provisions which current and former service personnel will find insulting and should not be proceeded with.
additional_details: Withdraw the Troubles Bill permanently and allow our soldiers to do their jobs without the worry of one day being dragged into court over something they did while following orders from our Government. No soldier should have to worry about the enemy in front of them and now the lawyers behind them too.  We believe that only those who have never been involved with the military would think this Bill should be passed

action: Stop driverless cars coming to UK
background: Stop driverless cars from being introduced in the UK. We think they will threaten the jobs of over 300,000 private hire and London black cab drivers. We want the Government to block the rollout of autonomous taxis and protect drivers’ livelihoods.
additional_details: Driverless taxis could put over 300,000 private hire and taxi drivers out of work across the UK. Many drivers rely on this industry to support their families, pay rent, and manage rising living costs. The Government must protect workers, ensure job security, and prevent mass unemployment by stopping the rollout of autonomous vehicles.

action: Amend the Recall of MPs Act to include 'Systemic Refusal to Engage'
background: The Recall of MPs Act 2015 captures criminals but ignores negligence. Constituents have no recourse when MPs systematically refuse to engage or explain decisions. We must amend the Act to recognise 'Systemic Non-Representation' as a breach of duty, ensuring MPs cannot silence those they represent.
additional_details:
MPs rely on a 300-year-old precedent to act as "Trustees," owing judgment but not answers. This effectively legalises the attitude that "I am not accountable because I know better than you." Consequently, MPs can legally ignore constituents for years between elections.

We must amend the Recall Act to sanction "Systemic Non-Representation" (excluding abusive mail). We need a statutory "Duty to Account" to replace this aristocratic paternalism with a binding obligation to engage.
rejection_details: It is not clear how these suggestions have enough definite meaning to act as a triggers in the same way as the current provisions of the 2015 Act

action: Local Decision-Making for Local Planning, Local Involvement on National Projects
background: Promote and support local democracy by local council decision-making on all local planning development. On nationwide planning developments local council planning departments must be involved and not excluded or ignored. Final decision on Nationwide projects must be at Central Government level.
additional_details: 2200 housing units are proposed to be built in Bromley and Hayes on green built land in the centre of the borough. Central government are intending to remove the local council planning department from the decision making process by use of existing and proposed new laws. Local democracy requires our councillors to be accountable to the electorate for both the built environment and our natural environment. The Bromley and Hayes green belt project will set a precedent for all London Boroughs.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, such as changing part of a particular law that is currently in force.

action: Keep the 5-year pathway for all legal immigrants to apply for ILR
background: The Government should stop its plans to change the 5-year pathway for legal immigrants to apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain, potentially including immigrants who are already living and working in the UK and have already been on the pathway since 2021.
additional_details: Many of the immigrants who come to this country get jobs, pay taxes (sometimes at a higher rate than the average citizen) and health surcharges to help fund the NHS. We do not believe we should deter individuals and families who are coming here and contributing. We feel it would also be unfair to punish those who are already on the path to ILR and have already been making these contributions for years and may now be punished.

action: Stop Local Government Reorganisation in Gloucestershire
background: We, the Forest of Dean Independent Group, do not believe that Local Government Reorganisation, in terms of creating unitary authorities, is required or wanted by the people of not only the Forest of Dean but also Gloucestershire. The loss of local accountability and knowledge is unacceptable
additional_details:
As such, we demand the retention of our District, Borough and City Councils in Gloucestershire and that rather than a UNITARY Authority or Authorities, the people of Gloucestershire request The Creation of a Combined Authority made up of and with  each having equal status 
The Forest of Dean District Council, 
Tewkesbury Borough Council
Stroud District Council
Cotswold District Council
Cheltenham Borough Council
Gloucester City Council.

This is true devolution while retaining localness
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Give NHS Care Workers a 5-Year ILR Route in Recognition of service during covid
background: We ask the UK Government to reinstate a 5-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for overseas Care Workers and their dependants who have worked in the NHS or social care sector since 2021, especially those who served during the COVID-19 pandemic.
additional_details:
⸻

I want the Government to do this because overseas Care Workers played a vital frontline role during COVID-19, working directly with infected and vulnerable patients and supporting the NHS at its most critical time. It is unfair that they are now placed on a 10-year ILR route while nurses and doctors remain on a 5-year route. Care Workers deserve equal recognition, fair treatment, and the settlement pathway they were originally expecting when they came to the UK to help during the pandemic.
rejection_details:
The Government is currently holding a public consultation on reforming the current settlement system. This includes proposals on extending the standard qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain.

If you wish, you can find out more and respond to the consultation on the GOV.UK website: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/earned-settlement 

You may wish to sign the following petitions:

Keep 5-year ILR for Health and Care visa holders to protect the NHS
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745684

Allow all Care Workers and Senior Care Workers to Bring Dependants.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751718

action: Abolish all written/timed exams in every GCSE/A-Level & make them practical
background: Require DfE & Ofqual to reform every GCSE, A-Level & BTEC subject to 100% practical/portfolio/applied assessment, 0% written/theory, no exams. Grant all BTEC routes equal status in Progress 8/Attainment 8 and create dual academic/vocational pathways in every subject from 14–19 for inclusion.
additional_details: We believe timed written exams & theory components in every subject exclude neurodiverse students who can’t show true ability when forced to write fast or at length. Employers tend to recruit on practical skills, projects & portfolios — not exam-hall writing speed. BTEC proves 100% practical assessment works across dozens of subjects & is oversubscribed. We think the system is discriminatory, invalid, causes mental health crises & subject decline. Abolish timed exams — make every subject 100% practical now.

action: Stop the 10 or 15-year settlement route for UK care workers
background: We ask the Government and Parliament to scrap the 10 or 15-year settlement rule for care workers, restore a fair 5 year route, stop applying changes retroactively. Regulate employers—not punishing honest workers who support the UK’s vital care sector.
additional_details: The 15-year rule is unfair and punishes care workers who followed every law, paid taxes, and supported the UK during critical shortages. It creates insecurity, harms recruitment, and devalues essential work. Abuse in the system was caused by poor oversight, not workers. The government should protect honest carers, apply no retroactive changes, and create a fair, stable path to settlement.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Keep 5-year ILR for Health and Care visa holders to protect the NHS 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745684

action: Exclude Ancestry Visa Holders from the proposed amendments ILR rules
background: Specifically exclude ancestry visas holders holders from the planned amendments to ILR rules from 5 to 10 years.
additional_details: The core purpose of the Ancestry route is to acknowledge and preserve the longstanding familial and cultural links between Commonwealth citizens and the United Kingdom. Ancestry visa holders are literally the grandchildren of British citizens—people with direct lineage to the UK’s own citizens. They are re-establishing connections with a country that has shaped their family history for generations. To delay their official integration through ILR would undermine the spirit of the visa.
rejection_details:
This is in essence a duplicate of this petition (below) which you may wish to sign:

Keep 5 year route to ILR for Existing Ancestry Visa Holders
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743327

action: Do not extend ILR qualifying period for RQF6 & below workers
background: We believe the proposed extension of the ILR qualifying period from 5 to 10 years for RQF Level 6 and below skilled workers will cause severe financial hardship, heightened stress, and imbalance in work-life for ground-level employees contributing vitally to the UK.
additional_details: We feel these changes would inflict severe financial burdens—repeated visa fees drain of modest earnings—while spiking stress and shattering work-life balance. Like exempted doctors and nurses who served in the pandemic, many have toiled in essential roles, retail store, delivering goods and sustaining the economy. Exempt current visa holders to honour their commitment to Britain.

action: Call for Parliamentary inquiry into potential systemic discrimination of BNOs
background: We believe that the British National (Overseas) visa is only a partial remedy as it fails to correct historic injustice that stripped Hong Kong British nationals of the right of abode.
additional_details:
Parliament must amend nationality law so BNO holders and their descendants are treated as full British citizens, not as second-class nationals.

We believe that legal changes from 1962–2002 have resulted in the majority of British nationals who remain without full citizenship being predominantly of Hong Kong origin.  Parliament must investigate the backgrounds of those remaining without full citizenship to see if they are now predominantly of a single ethnicity. If so, this systemic exclusion may represent a profound injustice and risks another historic betrayal.

action: Protect Skilled Workers: Allow ILR After 5 Years With a “No-Benefits” Rule
background: We respectfully request that the UK Government avoid retrospective changes to immigration policy and maintain the existing 5-year ILR pathway for current Skilled Worker visa holders creating a “No-Benefits, No Public funds” Rule to prevent the misue of access to public benefits.
additional_details: We acknowledge the Government’s concern about the misue of access to public benefits. A fair transitional approach would be to allow Skilled Worker migrants already in the UK to complete ILR after five years under a condition that they do not access public funds. The proposal to extend the ILR qualifying period by another decade creates uncertainty, disrupts family life, exposes Skilled Workers to greater risk of exploitation, and causes significant emotional, financial, and practical hardship.
rejection_details:
This is substantively a duplicate of a petition we already have open, which you may wish to sign:

Keep 5-Year ILR and Restrict Access to Benefits for New ILR Holders
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746363

action: Open the garden again
background: I've heard someone complained about the garden being a pub garden one person complained
additional_details: I want the garden back open
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what garden you are talking about.

In any case, this is not the responsibility of the Government or Parliament.

action: Require defibrillator in all large public areas
background: I want Government or parliament to require all large public areas to require defibrillator and better with first aid kits
additional_details: I want Government or Parliament to do this as it would obviously benefit the health of the victim and for most serios illnesses the earlier the btter. It could take time for the ambulance to come and it would be common sense for first aid kits and defibrillators to be installed giving the victim a higher chance of survival. I specified "large public areas" because there is a higher density of people risking more people to fall victim to illness
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We are not sure how you are defining 'large public areas' where you would like this to apply to.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Allow disabled bus pass use at any time, not just after the morning rush hour
background: Stop the ban on disabled bus pass use before 9/9:30am
additional_details: The government wants to get more people back to work but we're unable to use our disabled bus pass to get there. Lots of disabled people are able to work some jobs but most work places need you to start at 9am. Not allowing use of the bus pass on a morning is putting an extra barrier in place where most people have no other option of travel like walking/cycling to a workplace.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Change England’s disabled bus pass so it can be used at any time on weekdays 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729326

action: Hold a referendum on banning housing developments in the green belt
background: Let the country decide what happens to its own green belt and historic villages and towns. Call a referendum on banning housing developments on green belt land.
additional_details: We believe we are losing too much historic character, green spaces and habitats to build houses that are not needed in these areas. We think the fair way to decide is to let the people vote.

action: Require mothers to list the father (if known) on birth certificate if safe to do
background: Require mothers to name the father on the birth certificate, if known and safe to do so, ensuring equal parental rights and responsibilities. Fathers with no criminal convictions or history of domestic violence should be granted equal parental rights from birth including 50/50 contact
additional_details: Many fathers face unfair barriers to seeing their child, despite having done nothing wrong. The current system forces them into costly legal battles and leaves children without equal access to both parents. Equal rights from birth - when it is a requirement to list the father on a birth certificate if known and safe -  can support children’s wellbeing, reduce conflict, and ensures parents are treated fairly and consistently.

action: Do Not Penalise Existing Care Workers - Preserve the 5-Year Settlement Route
background: Government must ensure fairness by keeping the original 5-year ILR route for current care workers. We have built our lives here, filled critical staffing gaps, and supported vulnerable people. Rules should not change retroactively for those already contributing.
additional_details: I want Parliament/Government to protect fairness for current care workers by keeping the original 5-year ILR route. Many of us came under agreed terms, made long-term plans, and dedicated ourselves to supporting the UK’s most vulnerable people. Changing the settlement pathway now is unfair and destabilising. The government must honour existing commitments and recognise our essential contributions.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Keep 5-year ILR for Health and Care visa holders to protect the NHS
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745684

action: Concern About Limited and High-Cost Non-Dairy Options in Supermarkets
background:
• Whether pricing disparities between dairy and non-dairy products can be investigated

• How supermarkets can be encouraged to offer more inclusive seasonal options

• What measures could help ensure essential non-dairy items are fairly priced and accessible
additional_details: Major supermarkets such as Morrisons, Tesco and Asda offer very few non-dairy alternatives, particularly for seasonal items like children’s advent calendars. While dairy versions come in a wide range of themes (e.g., Paw Patrol, Bluey), non-dairy options are usually limited to one or two generic products and are significantly more expensive.

action: Create a Fair Two-Stage ILR Model for Skilled Workers
background: Create a two-stage ILR model: an initial form of ILR that continues the “no recourse to public funds” restriction, followed later by full ILR.
additional_details: This approach is vital for preventing exploitation. Remaining tied to employer sponsorship for 10–15 years puts workers at serious risk, especially in sectors such as social care, where dependence on a sponsor can lead to unfair treatment. A two-stage ILR system would remove this vulnerability by allowing workers to leave restrictive sponsorship arrangements after three or five years, without granting immediate access to public funds.
rejection_details:
Your submitted petition appears to be calling for two separate things on which there are already petitions open, which you may wish to sign:

Retain 5 Year ILR & Citizenship Route, Delay Public Funds Access Until Year 10
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731835

Allow Displaced Care Workers to work temporarily without a new sponsorship
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730717

action: Reform UK Energy Standing Charges
background: Shift all non-infrastructure costs off electricity standing charges onto company profits or general taxation. Require Ofgem to separate policy levies from true network costs, make suppliers absorb bailout and policy expenses, and ensure foreign-owned firms reinvest profits into UK infrastructure.
additional_details: We believe households are being forced to pay for supplier failures, policy levies, and network costs that should come from company profits or taxation. Electricity standing charges hide these costs and tend to hit low-use and solar homes hardest. Foreign-owned firms extract profit from UK households while reinvesting less back. Parliament must shift these costs off consumers, make companies fund their own failures, and restore fairness to the system.

action: Disregard Transitional Protection when assessing Council Tax
background: We ask the Government to require all English local authorities to disregard transitional protection payments in full when assessing council tax. Transitional protection is temporary but counting it as income cancels out that protection.
additional_details: The Government should amend the Council Tax Reduction Schemes (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2012 so that the Universal Credit transitional protection payment is fully disregarded as income when calculating Council Tax Reduction. Transitional protection is designed to prevent households from being financially worse off when moved from legacy benefits to Universal Credit. Many councils count this temporary protection as income when calculating Council Tax Reduction.

action: Government to fund a public service campaign about not queuing in a line in pubs
background: Educate the public on how to queue in pubs. This should be around the bar, not in a long bus-stop style queue. Queueing around bars is traditional and sociable. Single file queuing destroys the communal nature of pubs. Regular public service broadcasts should raise awareness of queuing etiquette.
additional_details:
A Public Service Campaign for Better Bar Etiquette. The Government, through its relevant departments, to fund an engaging Public Service Campaign utilising digital media and print signage to educate the public on effective pub bar etiquette.
The campaign's core message should be simple: Do not form a single, long line. Position yourself around the bar area and respect the bartenders' judgment in serving the next customer.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about correct etiquette in pubs are a matter for individual pubs, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Urgent Action Against Illegal Waste Site on the banks of the River Cherwell.
background: Direct the EA to secure the site, and enforce action. Provide ring-fenced funds, a clear clean-up timetable, and full transparency. Protect the Cherwell and Thames from toxic gases, poisonous leachate, and escalating plastic pollution.
additional_details:
A site between the River Cherwell and the A34, on an active floodplain has become the dumping ground for tens of thousands of tonnes of illegal waste. 
The Environment Agency (EA) has been aware of this site since May 2025, yet the waste mound has been allowed to grow to catastrophic proportions. 
We are calling on the UK Government, Parliament, and the Environment Agency to take immediate and coordinated action to prevent further environmental, ecological, and public health harm.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Petition Against Retrospective Implementation of ILR on Skilled Worker Visas
background: I request the Government to stop ILR changes from applying retrospectively. Current Skilled Worker visa holders should keep the ILR pathway they were promised to, with any new rules applying only to future applicants to ensure fairness and protect those who have contributed to the UK in good faith..
additional_details: Because changing ILR rules retrospectively is unfair to legal migrants who built their lives in the UK based on the original promises. It would cause unnecessary hardship, break trust, and disrupt the plans of people who have contributed to the country in good faith. Many have invested years of work, under the expectation of stable rules, and sudden changes would create stress, insecurity, and financial strain. Keeping the original ILR pathway for current visa holders is essential to maintain fairness and confidence in the UK’s immigration system.
rejection_details:
Your petition is effectively a duplicate of this petition (below) which you may wish to sign instead:

Make a law to protect ILR from abolition and retrospective changes
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742864

action: Incorporate bible studies into the education curriculum
background: Add Bible studies to the school curriculum starting from primary school level at a beginner level and more advanced in secondary. This should not to replace current religious education (RE).
additional_details: We believe doing this will create religious awareness and knowledge of biblical fundamentals in our younger generations and bring the culture of Christianity back to the community. We believe this would resolve many of our current social issues. This will not affect diversity as RE can still continue to be taught and other religions can be studied.

action: Reform nurse education funding, cancel debt & reinstate bursaries
background: Abolish tuition fees for nurse training, reinstate the NHS nursing bursary, and forgive existing student loan debt for nurses working in the NHS.
additional_details: Newly qualified nurses in England often graduate with over £60,000 of debt. Research by the the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) and London Economics suggests that forgiving nurse student debt could retain nurses 7–10 years longer and save the NHS over £1bn. We believe that the current funding model dissuades people from entering nursing and worsens staff shortages.

action: Make University more cost friendly to people who may not be able to afford it
background: We want lower prices for everyone and to make it more accessible so that people can access it. We also want it to be cheaper because majority of people in University leave with debt and struggle to pay it back.
additional_details: We want this to be changed because it is extremely expensive and alot of people dont go for this reason however alot of jobs require degrees.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.Universities can charge what they choose up to the fees cap. 

We could accept a petition calling for the cap to be lowered, if that is what you would like.

action: Keep it fair: no retroactive settlement rules for Skilled Workers.
background: Ensure Skilled Worker visa holders already in the UK can complete their promised 5-year ILR pathway under the current rules, with no retroactive extensions or recalculations to their qualifying period when new settlement rules take effect.
additional_details: Applying new 10–15 year settlement rules to people already part-way through the 5-year Skilled Worker pathway is unfair and destabilising. Migrants relied on clear Home Office rules when planning their lives and families. Changing requirements mid-route undermines trust, creates hardship and harms the UK’s reputation. Transitional protection is essential for fairness and legal certainty.
rejection_details:
Your petition is in essence a duplicate of this petition, which you may wish to sign instead:

Make a law to protect ILR from abolition and retrospective changes
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742864

action: STOP APPLYING NEW REFUGEE SETTLEMENT RULES TO EXISTING 5-YEAR GRANTS
background: We oppose applying new 10/20 year settlement rules retrospectively to 5-year protection holders. This undermines legal certainty and creates pressure. Government must guarantee current holders complete their route.
additional_details: We oppose the retroactive application of new 10- or 20-year settlement rules to those granted five-year protection. Retroactively extending a pathway undermines legal certainty and the legitimate expectations arising from existing decisions. The new conditions create psychological pressure and exclusion for legal residents. We urge the government to ensure that existing protection holders can complete their pathways without the new conditions; this is vital for public trust and legal integrity.
rejection_details:
This is effectively a duplicate of a petition we have open - which you may wish to sign:
Make a law to protect ILR from abolition and retrospective changes
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742864

action: Work to prevent first bus from leaving cornwall
background: Offer more funding or implement a new policy that requires public transportation to be cheap and easily accessible in rural areas of the country such as Devon and cornwall.
additional_details: Because thousands of Cornwall residents rely on public transportation specifically first bus as they operate county wide and without them there would be minimal options such as the train or small unreliable private transport companies.
rejection_details: Matter for particular local authorities to fund and make operational decisions on

action: Government to create fund to support orphans in conflict zones
background: We urge the government to fund dedicated support for orphans in conflict zones, recognizing their extreme vulnerability and lack of access to basic necessities.
additional_details: We believe that by taking this action, the UK government can demonstrate its commitment to humanitarian values and inspire other nations to follow suit.

action: Stop MPs and Ministers from attributing extreme political views to the public
background: Add a rule to the House of Commons Members Code of Conduct and THE Ministerial Code setting out that MPs and Ministers should not attribute extreme political views to members of the public without clear evidence.
additional_details: Such extreme political views could include, but is not limited to, “racist”, “far-right”, “bigoted”, “fascist”, “Nazi” or similar. The rule should stipulate that if no evidence is given, the remark must be withdrawn.

action: Stop the cancellation of Local Elections to help uphold democracy
background: The Government must reinstate all cancelled local elections now.  Local communities need fair, timely elections, not political decisions made behind closed doors. We believe cancelling democratic votes without a national emergency is dangerous and undermines trust.
additional_details: We believe cancelling local elections is an unacceptable assault on democratic norms. There is no national emergency to justify suspending the public’s right to vote, and doing so sets a dangerous precedent that weakens accountability and concentrates power. Communities deserve timely, transparent elections. The Government must restore all local elections immediately and uphold the democratic standards this country is built on.

action: Stop High Powered 1.3g Fireworks being sold to retailers in the UK
background: Growing trends have seen a big growth in the sales of higher powered 1.3g retail fireworks, most of these type of products are dangerous and very noisy, totally unsuitable for the places where general public use them. If this was stopped most of the noise & safety issues would be dealt with.
additional_details: Government needs to legislate that 1.3g higher powered retail fireworks are only available to professional display operators, who should also have the correct storage license and insurance to use such products. This action would help local authorities including Trading Standards to deal with the problem at its root cause, which could then also be further focused towards the wholesale distributors & stop them supplying such products.

action: Do Not Punish Legal, Tax-Paying Migrants with a 10-Year ILR Rule
background: We want the Government to keep the ILR qualifying period at 5 years for migrants who arrived legally under routes that currently lead to settlement. Any change to a 10-year rule should apply only to new arrivals, not to people already living, working, and contributing in the UK.

action: Do not increase the time migrants with ILR need to wait to apply for citizenship
background: We ask the Government and Parliament not to amend the British Nationality Act 1981 to increase the qualifying period for migrants with indefinite leave to remain (ILR) to become eligible to apply for British citizenship.
additional_details: In its statement titled "A Fairer Pathway to Settlement", the Government announced its intention to remove certain benefits from migrants with indefinite leave to remain (ILR) and increase the baseline qualifying period for many migrants on pathways to ILR. Therefore, we feel that this could also make it harder for migrants to become eligible for citizenship (as described on p. 27 of the statement), and that this is unnecessary and unfair.

action: Streamline UK passport renewal so that citizens always have a passport
background: When renewing a UK passport, allow citizens to keep and use their old passport until the new one is issued, allowing for uninterrupted use. This is how Australia conducts its passport renewal process.
additional_details: Presently, when renewing UK passports, you have to submit your old passport. This means you can have weeks but sometimes months without a passport. For those with travel booked, or for those with family or friends abroad, this can be a big problem. You can pay for a faster service, but once you've made the standard application you can't transfer. UK should adopt the Australian model, where citizens can carry on using their old passport until the new one is issued, allowing for seamless use.

background: Don’t apply the new 10-year ILR rule to existing Skilled Worker/Ancestry  visa holders. We came in good faith, filled vital roles, paid taxes, and built lives here based on a 5-year pathway. Keep your promise —apply changes only to new applicants, not those already settled in the UK.
additional_details: Thousands of skilled migrants came to the UK in good faith, many from former colonies —working in vital sectors, paying taxes, and building lives on the clear promise of ILR after 5 years. Those who followed every rule shouldn’t be punished by shifting goalposts, and such changes will harm the UK’s reputation and ability to attract future talent.

action: Keep the 5-Year ILR route for refugees. Do not extend it to 10 or 20 years

action: Introduce a screening programme for prostate cancer, starting with high-risk men
background: We are calling on the Government to reassess the UK National Screening Committee’s (UK NSC) draft recommendation not to offer prostate cancer screening to anyone except men with BRCA1/2 genetic variants, and to introduce screening for all high-risk men.
additional_details:
Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in men yet has no screening programme.

We disagree with the UK NSC’s analysis of the evidence and the weight it has placed on avoiding unintended harms. We believe the Committee has fixated on potential harms that have already dramatically reduced, while under-weighting the very real benefits of early detection. The analysis has not kept pace with modern practice or acknowledged how this would be an improvement on the current inefficient and inequitable system.

Targeted screening for all high-risk men should be the starting point for building a screening programme that can ultimately protect all men. Early diagnosis saves lives.
government_response_summary: The UK National Screening Committee consulted on a draft prostate cancer screening recommendation and will make a final recommendation soon. The Government will then consider whether to accept it.
government_response_body: The UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC) makes recommendations to ministers and the NHS across the four nations of the United Kingdom, based on an assessment of high-quality, peer reviewed evidence on whether screening for a certain condition would do more good than harm at reasonable cost. The UK NSC considered the current diagnostic and treatment pathways and consulted on their findings. The evidence package can be found at https://nationalscreening.blog.gov.uk/2025/11/28/uk-nsc-opens-consultation-on-draft-prostate-cancer-screening-recommendation/   Screening is specifically for people without symptoms or a diagnosis. The process must therefore minimise harm, such as unnecessary treatment or anxiety resulting from false positive test results. This level of caution is less relevant for people with diagnosed conditions or already in clinical care. They have sought clinical care or advice for a problem. They are in direct contact with a clinician so they can discuss the merits or otherwise of tests and treatments, rather than simply being provided with generic information to read. They have symptoms or a reason for concern. This means their test is much more likely to represent a true positive result, unlike in screening when people have a greater chance of receiving a false positive result. People in clinical care expect follow-up and face a smaller risk of harm from predictive tests. The ethical position, the ability of an individual to discuss issues with a clinician, and the likelihood of having a condition, all therefore differ significantly between clinical management and screening. Screening can do harm, as well as good (benefit). It is also possible for someone to experience both the harms and benefits of screening at the same time. For example, a man may live longer due to their prostate cancer being identified and treated but also live with serious side effects of treatment.  The aim of prostate cancer screening would be to detect prostate cancer early to prevent death and reduce suffering from the disease. For men with aggressive and/or advanced prostate cancer, early intervention and treatment can allow them to live longer by preventing prostate cancer death. It can also reduce the chances of serious complications such as prostate cancer spreading to other parts of the body. Prostate cancer can spread to the area just outside the prostate (locally advanced or locally invasive cancer), and cause symptoms such as erectile dysfunction, difficulties emptying the bladder and pain. It can also spread further (metastatic cancer), most commonly to the bones and spine, where it can cause severe pain, fractures, or spinal cord compression. Just over one in ten (12% of) men diagnosed with prostate cancer in England have metastatic prostate cancer at the time of their diagnosis. These are important, serious outcomes that screening and treatment would try to prevent.  There have been very large research trials of population screening in England and the United States of America. These studies show that there is a very small reduction in deaths after 15 years from prostate cancer in screened men (two out of one thousand). There are also several harms associated with screening. These arise from the additional tests that men go through to get a prostate cancer diagnosis (including a biopsy of the prostate) and the treatment they may then receive. Harms can arise as early as two weeks after beginning treatment, and can persist for a very long time (six years or more, or possibly a lifetime). For example, after six months:  •	For men undergoing prostate surgery: o	19% (almost one in five) will be unable to control their bladder (moderate to severe urinary incontinence) o	3% will have moderate to severe impacts on their bowel habits o	66% (two thirds) will experience moderate or severe erectile dysfunction  •	For men undergoing radiotherapy: o	38% (nearly two in every five) will find it difficult to control their bladder o	6% will have moderate to severe urinary incontinence o	5% will have moderate to severe impacts on their bowel habits o	48% (nearly half) will have moderate or severe erectile dysfunction  The majority of men (c.80%) whose prostate cancers would be identified through screening would not benefit in terms of preventing prostate cancer deaths and metastasis. Many of these men would receive treatment they do not need and the harms of screening would quickly outweigh any benefits at a population level. The challenge is how to identify those men who have aggressive prostate cancer while minimising the risks of serious and long-lasting side effects for many other men. More information on how the benefits and harms of prostate cancer screening were considered within the prostate cancer screening model can be found in the UK NSC evidence papers.  The UK NSC will make a final recommendation soon, after which the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care will consider whether to accept and implement the recommendation.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
background: The MoJ plans to remove the right to trial by jury for either-way cases with a likely sentence of three years or less. We believe it is an ancient right allowing us to be judged by our peers and this right must never be lost.
additional_details:
The Magna Carta (1215) states:

“No free man shall be taken or imprisoned … except by the lawful judgment of his peers or by the law of the land”.

We believe that losing this right would be to break British Justice completely.

action: Ban the Shooting of Ptarmigans (Lagopus muta) as Game Birds
background: Pass a law to make the shooting of Ptarmigans as game birds illegal to prevent their extinction in the UK.
additional_details: Ptarmigans are red-listed birds restricted to high altitudes in the North-West highlands of Scotland. They are in severe decline and are one of the species most in need of conservation efforts. The RSPB estimates that their population could be as low as 2000 individuals. They used to inhabit the southern uplands and lake district, but they are now extinct in England and heading for extinction in Scotland due to humans and climate change. It makes no sense to anyone to hunt endangered species.

action: Hold MPs accountable for misleading statements and apply sanctions
background: Introduce a statutory mechanism to investigate and sanction MPs who make demonstrably false or misleading statements in Parliament or public communications. This should include an independent body empowered to review evidence, issue corrections, and apply proportionate penalties.
additional_details: Public trust in democracy depends on honesty and accountability. When MPs make misleading statements, it distorts policy debates and erodes confidence in government. Currently, there is no effective statutory system to hold MPs accountable for false claims. Introducing evidence-based sanctions will ensure transparency, protect democratic integrity, and prevent misinformation from influencing decisions that affect everyone.

action: Protect those already on 10 year FLR FP routes from new rules changes.

additional_details: The government's proposed immigration rule changes must include grandfathering protections for families—specifically,the partners and parents of British citizens—who are already on the 10-year route to settlement. action: Allow Class 3 mobility scooters to carry a disabled person and a passenger
background:
Change the law on mobility scooters (“invalid carriages”) so a Class 3 scooter may legally carry one disabled person plus one passenger at up to 8mph.

Current regulations only allow a single seat and make it unlawful to use a second seat on public roads or pavements, even at low speed.
additional_details: Mobility scooters are legally defined as single-seat vehicles, so two-seat scooters cannot be used on pavements or roads. Many disabled people cannot travel safely alone and may need a passenger for support, guidance, communication, medical needs or because they are parents who must bring their child. Allowing one passenger on Class 3 scooters (up to 8mph) would increase safety, independence and accessibility while keeping all existing speed and safety limits.

action: Launch a review of UK fishing laws
background: We urge the Government to launch a review of fishing laws, which looks into giving UK boats and anglers fair access, restricting foreign super-trawlers and fish stock management. We believe protecting our waters, rebuilding fish populations, and supporting coastal communities should be the priority.
additional_details: We believe our seas are under pressure, fish stocks are declining, and foreign super-trawlers take far more from UK waters than local boats and recreational anglers. Many coastal communities rely on healthy fisheries for jobs, tourism, and heritage. We believe we need fair, science-based rules that protect our waters, rebuild stocks, support British boats, and ensure future generations can enjoy the fishing we once had.

action: Mandate creation of a no-fly list banning air rage passengers for 5 years
background: We want the Government to pass a law to mandate airlines to create a no-fly list to ban unruly passengers from flying on any airline to/from the UK for a minimum of 5 years.
additional_details: We need to put in place a suitable deterrent for people who make the choice to become disorderly on an aircraft. While individual airlines have the power to ban said passengers from flying with that airline for a period of time (or even a lifetime ban), there is nothing to stop them booking onto another airline and doing it all over again. A 5 year no-fly list ban on all airlines will give the passenger time to reflect on their behaviour.

action: Do not apply ILR qualifying period changes retrospectively to ILR applicants
background: We, the undersigned, call on the UK Home Office and Government to ensure that the recent changes to the qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain announced on 20 November 2025 are not applied retrospectively to individuals who are already on the route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR).
additional_details: We believe applying the new, stricter rules retroactively is unfair to migrants who have already met current settlement requirements. Many have made important life decisions based on the existing system. We urge the Government to honour these commitments by exempting those currently on the ILR route and providing transitional protections. Retrospective changes could risk causing hardship, uncertainty, and financial loss, which may undermine fairness and trust in the immigration system.

action: Commission NICE to Review Guidelines on Chronic Pain
background: Around 15.5 million people suffer from Chronic Pain (Verus Arthrtis, 2021). A number of commonly used and vital treatments for pain relief and management are no longer recommended, and we believe the new guidelines do not meet the needs of people suffering from chronic pain.
additional_details: Experts warn that taking painkillers from those in severe need is a cruel health policy. The review should consider evidence from stakeholders and campaigners. Chronic pain has a devastating impact, and every available tool is needed. When patients are properly medicated, many can function, work, and rely less on benefits, reducing strain on public services.
rejection_details: Decisions relating to a review of medical guidelines are a matter for the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), not the UK Government or Parliament.

Then I have to carry my buggy back up because we haven't been provided us with a buggy shed with a lock on. We aren’t allowed to leave them downstairs because of fire safety rules.

action: Count waiting time from Covid-19 Home Office delays toward ILR 5-year residence
background: We call on the UK Government to count Home Office delays during the nearly two-year Covid-19 pandemic toward the 5-year residence requirement for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), ensuring fairness for long-term residents affected by delays beyond their control.
additional_details: During this period, visa extensions, asylum claims, and other applications faced months of delays due to lockdowns, staff shortages, cancelled appointments, and Home Office backlogs. Despite other protections afforded under Section 3C of the Immigration Act 1971, this waiting time is not counted toward ILR. We ask the Government to recognise these delays as extraordinary, count Section 3C periods toward ILR, and ensure no one is disadvantaged.

action: Perjury should be a victim-related crime not just an Offence against the State
background: To amend the entry at Column D row 550 of the HOSCR Notifiable Offences List to designate Perjury as defined by the Perjury Act 1911 section 1.1 as S/V not simply as 'S' rendering it either a 'state-based' crime without a victim or a 'victim-related' crime dependant upon the reported circumstances
additional_details: Currently, we believe there is an anomaly in law where a victim of miscarriage of justice secured by false statement cannot have the offence of Perjury recorded as a 'victim-related' crime. By rejecting a complaint of Perjury as a victimless Offence against the State the police may avoid recording a crime which may reveal incompetence negligence or reasonable lines of enquiry that could have, and should have, been pursued in the original investigation leading to the miscarriage of justice he complains of.

action: Require Local Authorities return children when original concerns no longer apply
background: We want the Government to change the law so that children cannot remain in foster care when the original concerns that led to their removal have been proven to no longer apply.
additional_details:
Families across the UK are experiencing long delays, incomplete assessments, or outdated worries being repeatedly relied on even after risks have been addressed.

We ask for a statutory duty requiring Local Authorities and social workers to promptly re-assess family members, prioritise family care, and return children when it is safe and proportionate to do so.

action: Create a Renewable Open Work Permit for Sponsored Workers
background: Create a renewable Open Work Permit for sponsored workers so they can change employers without needing new sponsorship. The Government says workers can change sponsors, but in reality few employers offer sponsorships. With ILR moving to 10–15 years, workers should not stay tied to one sponsor.
additional_details: Although workers are technically free to change sponsors, the reality is that very few employers are willing or licensed to sponsor visas. Some workers lose sponsorship through employer abuse or non-compliance and are left insecure for years. With ILR moving to up to 15 years, we feel this dependence is unsafe. A renewable Open Work Permit, similar to the open work proposals for asylum seekers, would give fair mobility and protect workers who support the UK’s economy.

action: A peaceful Restructuring of Nigeria into autonomous regional governments.
background: We respectfully urge the UK Government and Parliament to support and advocate for a peaceful, people-driven restructuring of Nigeria into autonomous regional governments. As a nation significantly shaped by the UK, the UK has historical responsibility to champion and ensure this is achieved.
additional_details:
We further call on Parliament to commission debates, hearings, and policy reviews highlighting the benefits of regional autonomy for conflict reduction, improved governance, and sustainable development in Nigeria. The UK should also support technical assistance, research collaborations, and peace-building initiatives that facilitate this restructuring in a lawful and democratic manner.

Our plea is for the UK to stand firmly for justice, self-determination, and stability.

additional_details:
Legal immigrants entered the UK under the explicit understanding that the 5-year route to settlement was the established pathway for permanent residence. 
Legal immigrants should not face unequal treatment in access to settlement simply because they entered under different visa categories.
This is a moral contract that the Government must honour. Extending the ILR qualifying period to 10 years is a retrospective change that breaks this promise

action: Ban the use of AI for image, video and audio creation
background: Legislate to ban the AI generation of images, videos and audio to protect the British public from misinformation, harmful and harassing content, and to protect jobs in the creative sectors.
additional_details: This ban should include AI tools from being used in the UK, as well as any foreign AI content to be banned on social media and television. This could help protect against things like false advertisement and fake or misleading content.
government_response_summary: The Government is focused on enabling the safe use of AI. We are taking steps to address harms, while recognising the positive ways in which AI can drive growth and improve lives.
government_response_body: The development of AI offers an opportunity to grow the UK economy and improve public services. It also poses risks – from the generation of misinformation and harmful content to the potential disruption of the labour market. The Government takes these risks seriously.  AI is already regulated in the UK through existing laws such as data protection, competition, and equalities legislation, and through forms of sectoral regulation. For example, services regulated under the Online Safety Act are required to have systems in place to address fraudulent advertising, illegal content and content harmful to children, including AI-generated content. Internet-based generative AI services that allow users to share content with one another, that search live websites to provide search results, or which produce pornographic content are regulated under the Online Safety Act.  The Government does not have any plans to legislate to ban the AI generation of images, videos and audio. Such a ban would block the UK from accessing the benefits that AI offers to people’s daily lives, public services and the economy.  However, the Government is committed to strengthening protections where required. Where existing laws are not enough to ensure safety, the Government will take action. We have already legislated to create new offences where needed, such as the a new offence covering the creation of non-consensual intimate images. The Government has also announced that it will legislate in the Crime and Policing Bill to ban ‘nudification’ tools – tools that use AI to turn normal images of real people into fake nude pictures and videos without their consent.   The Technology Secretary confirmed in Parliament that the Government is exploring how emerging services, such as AI chatbots, interact with the Online Safety Act and what further measures may be required.  The Government recognises the concerns of our world-leading creative industries. We are looking at how we can unlock the extraordinary potential of AI in this sector, while protecting the unique and important contribution human creativity makes to our economy and quality of life.  AI is transforming the world of work more generally. The Government is committed to ensuring that AI drives opportunity, not insecurity, for working people. We have established the AI and the Future of Work Unit which uses cutting-edge research and expert insight to stay ahead of risks and act early to support workers. The Unit works across government but is based in DSIT. It will help prepare the UK for AI-driven labour market transformation by researching and monitoring AI’s economic and labour market impacts, and providing advice on new policies to be implemented.  The Government is committed to supporting a free, sustainable and plural media landscape, as the best way to maintain a shared understanding of facts, and protect against the spread of disinformation. The government is taking steps to support a healthy news and information environment in the UK and strengthen and maintain a plural, thriving and trusted media sector.  The Government continues to work with a wide range of stakeholders to gather evidence, understand emerging issues and develop policy that carefully balances both the risks and opportunities of AI.  Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

action: PETITION AGAINST UNFAIR HOSPITALITY SERVICE CHARGE PRACTICES
background:
We, the undersigned employees, customers, and members of the public, respectfully submit this petition to raise urgent concerns regarding the unfair and non-transparent.

Across the industry, many hospitality businesses apply a mandatory service charge to customer bills.
additional_details:
We respectfully request that the Government:
	1.	Introduce or enforce legislation requiring 100% of service charges to be given to staff, with no hidden deductions.
	2.	Mandate full transparency.
	3.	Prohibit employers from retaining any portion of service charges, unless explicitly approved by law.
	4.	Introduce penalties for businesses that misuse or misrepresent service charges.
	5.	Require hospitality venues to clearly inform customers how service charges are handled.
rejection_details:
We cannot accept this petition as it calls for something which is already in place. 

The Employment (Allocation of Tips) Act was enacted in 2023, and sets out a legal obligation on employers across sectors to allocate all tips, gratuities and service charges which they are paid or which they exercise control or significant influence over ("qualifying tips") to workers without any deductions. The Act also requires employers to ensure that the distribution of qualifying tips between workers is fair, and provides a route for the worker to complain if the employer is not following the law. 

You can find the full legal text here: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/13/enacted
And the explanatory notes to the Act here: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2023/13/notes/division/1/index.htm

action: Oppose proposed statutory requirement that schools store or pouch smartphones
background: The Government should commit to not mandate nationwide phone storage systems in schools. The high profile movement to make this statutory should face proper scrutiny, in terms of costings, for example, and, instead, the far better alternative of banning smartphones from school premises be considered
additional_details:
Smartphones are not safe for children and are causing immense harm. Storing them is an option to better protect children during the school day. However, pouching smartphones:
Normalises children owning smartphones
Encourages parents of Year 6 to buy their child a smartphone
Is very expensive (see Ireland)
Promotes belief that schools cannot manage this themselves 
Makes complex what is actually straightforward
Locks schools into contracts with 3rd parties that they will find difficult to leave
rejection_details:
There are currently no reported Government plans to introduce statutory requirements for schools to store or 'pouch' phones. The current non-statutory guidance says that schools may develop their own policies to implement a no phones in schools rule. The guidance suggests the following systems that could be adopted:

No mobile phones allowed on the school premises
Mobile phones handed in on arrival
Mobile phones kept in secure location, which pupils do not access throughout the school day
Pupils may keep their phones but they are “never used, seen or heard

You can find out more in this House of Commons Library note: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10241/

We could accept a petition calling for the Government to ban schools from storing mobile phones, if that's something that you'd like to see.

action: Review access to cash in rural areas, require FCA to reform rules and criteria
background: Review access to cash in rural areas and require the FCA to reform its rules, and LINK’s criteria, so more rural communities like the Highlands can have banking hubs. additional_details:
I am concerned that across rural areas such as the Highlands, communities are losing access to essential banking services. I believe shared banking hubs have proven effective where local banks have closed, but that the current eligibility criteria is too narrow.

In my view, the current assessment process prioritises large retail centres, excluding many smaller towns and villages, despite these places acting as vital service hubs for surrounding rural communities.

To ensure fair and equitable access to banking services for all, I would like access to cash in rural areas, the criteria and FCA rules affecting it to be reviewed and reformed.

additional_details: Afghans who aided the UK's mission sacrificed and faced danger. We think a clear, expedited 5 year route, requiring successful completion of the Life in the UK test, English competency, good character, and no crimes, would honour allies, promote stability, and help treat long term residents more consistently.

action: Require Councils to Permit Cross-Pavement EV Charging

additional_details: We believe that many households cannot install EV chargers because they have no driveway and that councils often block cross-pavement solutions. We think allowing safe, discreet charging gullies would make EV ownership accessible to more people, encourage the switch to electric vehicles, support the UK’s climate goals, and ensure pavements remain safe and usable. I urge the Government to update planning rules to require councils to permit this.

action: Allow trained pharmacy staff to hand out checked medication if pharmacist absent

additional_details: Patients are regularly denied vital medication because current law forbids staff from handing out prescriptions if the pharmacist is absent, even when the medicine is already checked, labelled and ready. This leads to missed doses, withdrawal, worsening conditions and distress. Staff also face abuse and anxiety enforcing rules they did not create. Modernising the law would protect patients, support staff and reflect how pharmacies operate today.
rejection_details:

action: Cancel the clinical trial into puberty blockers & safeguard vulnerable children
background: The government is aware of the potential irreversible impact (physical and emotional) of puberty blockers, having acknowledged an 'unacceptable safety risk’ following the Cass Review. Yet, hundreds of children are about to be given puberty blockers under a government-sanctioned trial.
additional_details:
We want this trial to be cancelled. We believe that the answer for children feeling dis-ease in their bodies (many of whom are autistic) is the passage of time and natural progression of puberty, coupled with explorative therapy. We believe that the answer is never medicalisation that can harm brain development, bone growth, sexual functioning, and lead to infertility, and that to put children on a path towards such harm is the antithesis of safeguarding.
Let us not be written into history as the country that knowingly harmed vulnerable children.
government_response_summary: We are following the expert advice of the Cass Review to establish a clinical trial to determine the relative benefits and harms of puberty suppression in young people with gender incongruence.
government_response_body: It is essential for the Government and the NHS to be guided by expert clinical advice and act with caution and care when it comes to supporting children and young people living with gender incongruence. The independent Cass Review concluded that the rationale for early puberty suppression remains unclear, and that there is not enough clinical evidence for the safe and effective routine use of puberty suppressing hormones to treat gender incongruence in under-18s. For that reason, this Government supported and extended indefinitely the ban on their use outside of research. Despite these restrictions, some young people are going to great lengths to source these drugs from unregulated providers, in the absence of scientific evidence.  The Cass Review recommended that a programme of research be established to underpin the design and delivery of NHS gender care. It specifically recommended this include a clinical trial into puberty suppression in young people with gender incongruence. This recommendation addresses the lack of evidence about the relative benefits and harms of this treatment option, particularly when provided alongside an updated model of NHS care incorporating holistic assessment and a comprehensive and tailored package of psychosocial support.   The study protocol is available on the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) website: https://fundingawards.nihr.ac.uk/award/NIHR167530  The bar for a UK clinical trial to be approved is extremely high, with the PATHWAYS trial going through rigorous rounds of scientific, clinical, ethical and regulatory review. It was approved by an independent NIHR funding committee. The final protocol was subject to rigorous approval processes through both the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency and the Health Research Authority – including review by an independent Research Ethics Committee.   The Commission on Human Medicines also considered information on the trial in detail and made recommendations that were considered and adopted by the study team. With the strongest safeguards possible, a trial of this kind is the only way to build a sufficiently high-quality evidence base to inform decisions on the future use of this treatment option for this vulnerable and distressed group of young people.  Protecting and promoting the health and wellbeing of affected young people is the primary concern and there are strict eligibility criteria in place to join the PATHWAYS clinical trial. Parental consent is an integral component, with the parent needing to not only agree to their child’s involvement but also demonstrate sufficient understanding of the nature of the treatment, and what is currently known and unknown about its effects. Informed assent from the child will also be required. This will include the young person explaining in their own words to the clinician what the risks are and what they understand by those risks.   The only children to get to that stage will have already been diagnosed with gender incongruence for at least two years, will have received tailored psychosocial support, and will have been deemed clinically appropriate, within the context of the study, by both their NHS care team and the National Multi-Disciplinary Team. They will also have had to be assessed as being in stable physical and mental health.  Those young people receiving (or not receiving) puberty suppressing hormones will continue to receive other elements of routine support and treatment provided as part of newly established NHS Children and Young People’s Gender Services, whose practices have been shaped by the recommendations of the Cass Review. Participants can leave the trial at any time, at which point they would receive support in their withdrawal from puberty suppression as well as ongoing psychosocial support from NHS services.  Healthcare must always be led by evidence. Puberty suppression has been provided in the past with insufficient evidence, and young people have been left to go without the support and care that they need. This Government is determined to change that, and it is only through evidence-based research that we can determine the most effective way to support these young people. We believe that children and young people with gender incongruence have the same right to participate in ethically-approved research, and to receive evidence-based care, as any other group of individuals seeking the support of the NHS.  Finally, it is important to reiterate that gender incongruence is an internationally recognised disorder. It is defined in the International Classification of Diseases 11th Revision as “a marked and persistent incongruence between an individual’s experienced gender and the assigned sex”. It does not describe girls and boys experimenting with gender norms, which for many children is a normal part of growing up. These important differences are properly understood and reflected in the new model of care being provided by the NHS.  Department of Health and Social Care

action: Recognise ‘Veteran’ as a protected characteristic in law.
background: Make ‘Veteran’ a protected characteristic in the Equality Act 2010 to help ensure veterans aren't disadvantaged and that Armed Forces Covenant objectives are consistently applied. Require organisations to enable recording of veteran status with safeguards and prevent discrimination or disadvantage.
additional_details:
We are concerned that, without a clear legal duty to recognise and act on veteran status, avoidable disadvantage may continue across healthcare, housing, employment and the justice system. The Armed Forces Covenant sets important expectations, but without Equality Act protection there is not the same legal compulsion on public bodies and other organisations as exists for recognised protected characteristics. We believe recognising ‘Veteran’ as a protected characteristic would strengthen early intervention, fair treatment and better outcomes, in line with the aims of the Equality Act 2010.
 
For the purposes of this petition, ‘veteran’ is defined in line with the UK Government definition: anyone who has served at least one day in the UK Armed Forces (Regular or Reserve).
