action: Government apology and compensation for 1950s Women affected by pension changes
background: We ask Government to deliver a fair, timely, fully transparent apology that reflects ALL evidence based on what we think constitutes maladministration and discrimination; and addresses the financial, emotional and personal hardship experienced by 1950s women caused by pension changes.
additional_details: Many 1950s-born women have faced lifelong and historic discrimination, compounded by the Government’s failure to properly communicate State Pension Age changes. DWP Ministers have listened only to a group representing a fraction of those affected, leaving others feeling ignored. As many campaign groups unite, we think it is unacceptable that the Government continues to silence the majority. After decades of inequality, accountability and action are long overdue.
government_response_summary: We apologised for not sending State Pension age letters sooner. Deciding not to pay compensation and the Ombudsman’s report relate to that, not the petition’s “hardship...caused by pension changes”.
government_response_body: The Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman (PHSO) investigated the way State Pension age changes were communicated to women born in the 1950s and whether within a specific time period there was maladministration and injustice and if so, whether it warrants compensation. They did not examine the “financial, emotional and personal hardship experienced by 1950s women caused by pension changes” that the petition focuses on and which relate to the decision, first taken by Parliament in 1995, to equalise the State Pension age for men and women nor that to accelerate the increases in 2011 taken by the Conservative and Liberal Democrat Coalition.   The PHSO’s findings relate narrowly to a delay in sending letters over a relatively short period. The Ombudsman found that the Department’s communications met expected standards between 1995 and 2004. But that between 2005 and 2007 there was a 28 month delay in sending personalised letters to women affected and that this was maladministration.   On 29 January the Secretary of State announced the Government’s new decision on the Ombudsman’s investigation. He accepted that individual letters about changes to the State Pension age could have been sent earlier. He apologised for that maladministration in the House of Commons and in the document explaining his decision which has been published.   The Secretary of State recognised the importance that decisions on the State Pension age carry and the impact they have on people’s lives the need for government to weigh carefully any future changes. The Department is developing an Action Plan for the future.  The Secretary of State has set out the Government’s position in detail to Parliament, which can be found here - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-response-to-parliamentary-and-health-service-ombudsmans-investigation-into-womens-state-pension-age-communications-and-associated-issues.   There are legitimate and sincerely held views about whether it was wise to increase the State Pension age. In particular, whether the decision taken to accelerate equalisation and the rise to the age of 66 was the right thing to do or not. But this is not the issue the Ombudsman or the Government has been considering. Changes to State Pension age to equalise it to 65 and increase it to 66, 67 and 68 were agreed by Parliament and have been tested in the Courts.  In relation to the PHSO’s investigation, the Government took account of the views of 1950s women and people representing them, including Members of Parliament.   In the decision-making process, the Government considered the relevant evidence, including the PHSO's comprehensive report which itself drew on extensive testimony from affected women. The views and experiences of 1950s women were therefore part of the evidence base considered.  We are determined to ensure that all pensioners on lower incomes have a better life in retirement. The Government are now ensuring that more pensioners get that extra income with the biggest ever campaign to increase take-up of Pension Credit, which saw tens of thousands more Pension Credit awards in the year up to November than the previous 12 months.  In addition, our commitment to the Triple Lock for the entirety of this Parliament means that pensioners will see their state pension rise by up to £575 this year, with incomes up to £2,100 a year higher by the end of the Parliament. Indeed, overall spending on the State Pension is set to be more than £30 billion higher a year by the end of this Parliament than in 2024-25.   We are also putting record investment into the NHS, meaning that thousands more pensioners are getting the operations and treatment that they need, rather than being left in pain on waiting lists.  Department for Work and Pensions

background: We think the Government should bring in a law to make it compulsory to provide supporting documentation with estate accounts, so that executors and administrators can be held to account properly.

action: Keep the 5-year ILR route for health and social care workers
background: We want the government to keep the original 5-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for health and social care workers. This was the rule when we arrived in the UK, and it should not be changed to a 15-year pathway.
additional_details: We work on the front line, caring for vulnerable people every day, often in physically and emotionally challenging roles. We pay full tax and National Insurance, yet being called part of the “so-called Boris wave” feels unfair and disrespectful. Many carers are stressed and worried about their future because of the proposed 15-year ILR route. We ask Parliament to honour the 5-year ILR route we were promised, recognise our essential contribution, and treat care workers with respect and fairness.

additional_details: We think taxing only the income left after essential bills would ease cost-of-living pressures, reduce debt and create a fairer system. We urge the Government to review income tax rules so basic living costs are deducted before tax is applied.

action: Immediately Rescind David Lammy's Proposal to Conditionally Scrap Trial by Jury

background: The UK Government should require Invrrclyde, and local authorities in Scotland to maintain full overseas criminal record checks for all taxi and private hire driver applicants who were born outside the UK or have lived abroad for 6 months or more, and prevent councils from removing these safeguards.
additional_details: I want this because removing overseas criminal checks puts public safety at risk. If someone has lived abroad for years, the council would have no way to see serious offences committed elsewhere. Local drivers face strict vetting and every applicant should meet the same standard. Families, vulnerable people and the wider community deserve to know that anyone licensed to drive the public has been fully checked.

background: This petition seeks a constitutional rule requiring any government that breaks an explicit election manifesto promise—without compelling public-interest justification—to resign and trigger a General Election, ensuring accountability thereafter protecting democratic trust.
additional_details: I want a binding legal framework, impossible to evade or dilute, that compels any government which breaks an election pledge to resign and call a General Election.

action: Raise tax thresholds with inflation to protect incomes and support growth
background: Require all income tax thresholds, including the personal allowance, higher-rate bands and the £100k taper limit, to rise automatically each year in line with inflation. End the current freeze on tax bands and ensure the system keeps pace with the real cost of living.
additional_details: Since 2010, almost everyone in the UK has become poorer in real terms as prices have risen faster than wages and frozen tax thresholds have dragged millions into higher bands. People work harder yet take home less, leaving families struggling and the economy weakening. This hidden tax rise reduces spending, hurts businesses and increases reliance on benefits. Indexing thresholds to inflation would restore fairness, improve living standards and support real, sustainable growth.

Married couples do not pay this tax.
additional_details: We feel this is a totally outdated and unfair taxation on modern relationships and should be abolished.

action: Abolish plans to introduce a pay-per-mile tax on on electric and hybrid vehicles
background: The UK Government is planning on introducing a scheme whereby owners of Electric and Hybrid vehicles are going to be charged per mile travelled. Myself and many other EV and Hybrid vehicle owners including businesses feel this is is a disproportionate tax on environmentally friendly means of travel.
additional_details:
Cheapest EV biased home electric tariff (Octopus Go) is 6.5p per unit assuming you have access to a charger at home. 

Average EV achieves 4 miles per unit which is 1.6p per mile. Compared to ICE vehicles wavering at 10p+ per mile, it's a small incentive to switch. Adding 3p per mile increases this to 4.6p. Suddenly the incentive is diminished. 

On 12000 miles per year this adds £360 to your tax bill with no limit. 
Taxi drivers average 46500 miles per year, that is £1395.

Ban dogs walking around freely in public.

action: Cancel the planned '3p per mile' for EVs and Hybrids from 2028
background: Cancel the planned 2028 '3p per mile' tax for EV and Hybrid vehicles as this will not support EV take up for greener transport and it is essentially taxing EV owners twice as they already pay £196 Vehicle Excise Duty.
additional_details: The government needs to rethink the plan and/or remove the £196 VED  fee for zero emission vehicles, so that owners won't be hit two forms of taxation just to drive their vehicle.

action: Ban images and videos of children under 13 being shared online
background: Young children cannot consent to their image being shared. Yet parents sometimes share images of their children, building their digital footprint. This could make them vulnerable to abuse.
additional_details: We also do not think adults should be allowed to share a child’s image or monetise it for content before the child is able to consent to sharing. “Sharenting” can lead to a misuse of images in malicious ways such as deep fake child sexual abuse material. There is also potential for identity theft and fraud. Research estimates that by 2030, parents sharing images of their children online will account for two-thirds of identity fraud. Sharing your child’s location or school also makes them vulnerable to unwanted contact.

action: Apply the 1.5p per mile levy on hybrid cars only on electric miles driven
background: From April 2028, the UK Government plans to introduce a mileage-based road tax of 1.5p per mile for hybrids, alongside Vehicle Excise Duty. Hybrids will also keep paying fuel duty when using petrol, meaning they are taxed twice, through fuel duty and the new mileage levy on all miles driven.
additional_details: We feel this approach penalises hybrid owners who already pay fuel duty. Most hybrids use electric power for only a small share of their mileage (often 10–20%), yet the levy applies to all miles, not just electric ones. We believe this is unfair and discourages low-emission vehicle adoption, undermining the UK’s net-zero goals. We call on the Government to apply the 1.5p per mile levy only to electric miles driven, not total mileage, and ensure transparency and fairness in how hybrid mileage is calculated.

action: Reverse decision on pay per mile for EV and hybrid drivers
background: The 3p-per-mile EV tax adds about £255 a year for an average household, pushing up transport bills on top of loan, insurance, tax and charging costs. For many families this squeezes already tight budgets and leaves less money for essentials and savings.
additional_details: The government should cut or freeze the 3p-per-mile rate, introduce means-tested rebates or exemptions for lower-income households, and expand charging infrastructure to keep EV running costs affordable. Other countries like Norway and the Netherlands prioritise EV purchase grants, reduced toll fees and free parking over dedicated pay-per-mile taxes, making ownership easier. These approaches help families transition to cleaner transport without adding extra financial strain.

action: Protect children, families and genuine asylum seekers in new UK asylum reforms
background: Ensure new asylum reforms protect children, families and genuine asylum seekers by reducing delays, creating fairer settlement routes and allowing earlier legal work, while targeting criminal smuggling gangs—not vulnerable people—so the system stays fair, humane, safe and workable.
additional_details: The UK’s asylum reforms must stay fair, humane and true to British values of protecting the vulnerable. Families and children escaping danger face years of uncertainty through long waits and 10–20 year settlement routes. A better system needs faster decisions, early legal work rights, clear separation of genuine from non-genuine claims, and enforcement focused on criminal smuggling gangs—not vulnerable people simply seeking safety and stability.Every child deserves safety and hope.

action: Remove the EV and Hybrid pay per mile.

action: Provide winter and summer essentials for all primary school children in the UK.

In the summer pack we would like you to provide sunscreen, hat, water bottle and sunglasses. This would be for every child in the UK primary schools.
additional_details: By passing this law it will mean that all children will feel equal and not excluded. This will help all children to feel included and reduce bullying because of what they don't have. It will make sure that they are protected and healthy. The healthcare rates will decrease with less people having skin cancer, sunstroke or frostbite in the nearby future. This will save the NHS a lot of money. It can increase attendance in schools because children won't feel embarrassed to go to school.

action: Reverse VAT changes on Advance Payments for Motability Vehicles
background: We want the Government to reverse the changes it made to VAT on advance payments for Motability vehicles, as proposed in the latest Budget. These changes could result in people taking cars that are not suitable due to price increases.
additional_details: We are concerned scheme prices have been rising steadily lately due to the push towards swapping to EV. We feel the Government is unfairly targeting disabled people and that the Government is pushing people with different needs to either be unable to get a vehicle or get an unsuitable vehicle.

action: Review overtime taxation to make it fairer for UK workers
background: Many work overtime out of financial need, to make ends meet and do not do it always by choice, as it can reduce family time. Fairer overtime taxation could support workers, encourage extra hours in essential sectors, and help overstretched teams.
additional_details:
We ask the Government to launch a review into making overtime taxation fairer, as fairer taxation could reward personal sacrifice, reduce financial stress, boost the economy, and encourage staff to do extra in essential sectors like healthcare, and social. Clear eligibility rules could also ensure fairness. 
 
Overtime is usually taken because extra income is needed and, in some cases, is imperative for basic needs. This can often be at the cost of stress, fatigue, and family time. Taxing overtime at the same rate as regular pay can reduce money that is relied on.

action: Change the UK tax year to start on the 1st of January
background: The UK tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April, a relic of 1752 when Britain switched calendars and “lost” 11 days. That historical quirk made sense then - but today, it’s a barrier to simplicity and global alignment.  Let's modernise our system for ease and alignment with over 120 other countries.
additional_details:
•	Global Standard: Over 120 countries start their tax year on 1 January, including the USA, Canada, and most of Europe.
•	Simplification: Aligning with the calendar year would make payroll, budgeting, and reporting easier for businesses and individuals.
•	International Competitiveness: UK companies trading globally face unnecessary complexity because our tax year doesn’t match international norms.
•	Easier financial planning.
•	Reduced accounting costs.
•	Fewer errors and compliance headaches.

action: Maintain our constitutional right to trial by jury
background: Overturn the government's publicly stated intention to remove the right to trial by jury in all but the most serious cases and instead have government employed judges decide. We must maintain our constitutional right to trial by jury.
additional_details: Impartiality cannot be guaranteed unless a public jury decides the outcome. It is of no benefit to the British public to have this constitutional right taken away.

action: Create a coordination body for Nationally Significant Energy Projects (NSIPs)
background: We call on DESNZ to create a central body that adopts a strategic framework to assess projects collectively and ensure they proceed without environmental harm. We believe energy project cumulative impacts are a big issue, and a body is needed to coordinate competing schemes and explore alternatives.
additional_details: For example, within a 10-mile radius in East Suffolk, multiple major energy NSIPs are underway or proposed—including Sizewell C, the Friston Energy Hub, EA1N, EA2 and Sea Link and LionLink interconnectors—which are causing significant disruption for many residents. Yet there is no central body that assesses their combined effects on communities and the environment, the impacts on each project’s viability and delivery, nor why onshore siting is pursued when offshore alternatives exist. This should change.

action: Change the currency in Jamaica to Twenty Jamaican Dollars to One British Pound

additional_details: I believe as the King is Head of State and the highest ranking official, the Government who inturn works along side the King has the impetus to be able to implement change, the parliament can bring such urgent matters to the King's attention as Jamaica is suffering a crisis, the steadfast movement from parliament will be necessary and only parliament can address the King in such manner
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

The UK Government is not responsible for matters relating to the currency of another country.

action: Call a General Election now due to loss of confidence in the Government
background: We the public want Parliament to call an immediate General Election so the public can decide whether the Government still has a valid mandate. A new election would restore democratic accountability and ensure the country has leadership that reflects the priorities of voters.

A General Election is needed to give voters a say on the UK’s future direction and restore trust in national leadership.

action: Stop the Labour Government removing the right to elect trial by jury.

Despite being human rights zealots, David Lammy and Keir Starmer are politicising the courts with plans to remove the right to trial by a jury of our peers. This is the most important human right we have.

Without jury trials, defendants will be subject to a form of two tier justice that is akin to George Orwells 1984. It cannot be allowed.

This is the greatest attack on British democracy in history. It is anti-British and will also cost the taxpayer in legal challenges.

action: End the Personal Allowance Freeze – Raise It in Line with Inflation
background:
We want the Government to end the freeze on the personal allowance and restore annual inflation-linked increases.
The freeze has pushed more people into paying higher taxes despite no real rise in income.
We ask Parliament to up-rate the allowance fairly and transparently.
additional_details:
Freezing the personal allowance during high inflation means workers pay more tax without being better off in real terms.
More people are pushed into tax or higher bands even though their pay only rises to cover basic costs.
Ending the freeze would relieve pressure on working households and let people keep more of what they earn.

action: Fund self-defence for students and women, and legalise licensed defence tools
background: Introduce mandatory government-funded self-defence classes in schools for all students. Provide paid time off for women to attend government funded self-defence courses. Legalise regulated non-lethal self-defence tools for adults with licensing and training, such as pepper spray.
additional_details: Violence and sexual assault are growing concerns, particularly for women and vulnerable groups. Teaching self-defence in schools empowers young people, increases confidence, and promotes safety awareness from an early age. Paid time off ensures that adults, especially women, can maintain personal safety skills. We think regulated access to non-lethal self-defence tools allows responsible adults to protect themselves without increasing harm to others.

action: Arm all police officers with firearms
background: We call on the Government to ensure all police officers can carry firearms, not just authorised firearms officers.
additional_details: We believe having all police officers carrying firearms would make police reaction to emergencies that currently require specialist firearm unit to respond reduces the emergency response time as wouldn't have to wait for these units all officers could respond potentially save more lives

action: Fund provision of a tablet for every pupil in KS2 and above to support learning
background: To support educating our children in a technologically advanced world, fund the provision of tablets to learners, to access apps for educational purposes. Make these Government-issued devices available to learners from the moment they reach Key Stage 2.
additional_details:
We believe that there is a tech shortage in schools in an age where technology is relied upon heavily. It is important that our children remain up to date and technologically literate.
 
We think it would encourage learners to develop technology literacy and practise skills such as research, touch-typing, digital media amongst others. These skills would give our children a head start for future careers. In the long run, it will save on additional costs such as printing, laminating etc.

action: Keep Lifetime ISA for retirement savings & make a new ISA for first time buyers
background: I urge the Government to keep the current Lifetime ISA for retirement savings and reconsider scrapping or reforming it. We believe it is not a complicated product for those who use it to save for their future retirement and that first time buyers seem to be the ones having issues.
additional_details:
We want the Government to leave the Lifetime ISA in place for long-term savers and to instead consider starting a new ISA for first time buyers to save for their homes, as that seems to be where the issue lays.
 
We believe the current Lifetime ISA is a wonderful product that a lot of people rely on for saving for their retirement, and the talk of scrapping it is causing a lot of anxiety. Many people have invested their money in it since it started, and we feel the fact the Government may scrap it is unfair.

action: Reduce the age at which people can open Individual Savings Accounts to 16
background: At 16 people can work and get a passport without parental consent. We believe that lowering the minimum age for adult ISAs will send a strong, positive message to younger generations about the power of saving and investing as well as giving young people access to the full benefits of the ISA regime.
additional_details: People between the ages of 16 and 18 are some of the least likely to save or invest. If we support the new generation through education and opportunity, we can get them saving at an early age and build positive habits and outcomes.

action: Fund converting vacant Public & Commercial Buildings into Affordable Housing
background: We want the Government to identify vacant public and commercial buildings and fund their conversion into affordable housing which prioritises homeless people, young people leaving care and low-income families, so empty buildings help communities instead of standing unused.
additional_details: Thousands of public and commercial buildings in the UK sit empty while homelessness rises and families live in temporary accommodation. We believe converting these buildings into affordable housing is faster, cheaper, and greener than new builds. It could provide safe, permanent homes, support communities, and ensure public assets are used to help those who need them most.

action: Review job hunting and interviewee rights
background: Review the current protective measures in place to support those seeking employment, which includes looking into a new legal requirement to include salaries for all publicly advertised roles, and that interview tests or trials do not incur more than 1 hour of unpaid input from the interviewee.
additional_details: We also want the review to look into compensating interviewees for their time if it is more than 1 hour. It is current practice by many businesses to either not advertise salary or offer significantly lower than the market rate. Additionally, it's now very common for interview tasks or trials to either require significant amounts of time - 5 hours plus is common or sometimes for the work to then be used as part of the business without any compensation to the interviewee or acknowledgement of IP.

action: Ban the use of bots to make purchases on websites
background: Make bot-assisted online purchasing illegal by expanding the 2018 Breaching of Limits on Ticket Sales Regulations to cover all high-demand goods, including collectibles like sneakers, trading cards, and even essentials such as toilet paper.
additional_details: We believe hobbies like sneaker collecting and trading card games now resemble the stock market, with bots bypassing purchase limits to secure multiple items. We feel captchas are no longer effective as bots have evolved beyond them, creating a grey area under the Computer Misuse Act 1990. We also believe this practice is harmful and unethical, as it can inflate prices by allowing items bought at retail to be resold at a higher cost.

action: Bring back the 2 child benefit cap
background: The 2 child benefit cap needs to reintroduced.

action: Impose a freeze on all expenses paid to MPs and Peers, until 2031.
background: We would like members of both, The House of Commons (MPs) and The House of Lords (Peers) to take their share of the burden to reduce the UK National Debt and freeze their future expenses until 2031.
additional_details: Both the House of Commons (MPs) and House of Lords (Peers) should Lead by Example to those who pay both tax and national insurance.

action: Resuscitation and life saving taught in schools as part of national curriculum.

action: Fund Covid 19 vaccinations for those with progressive lung conditions
background: We call on the Government to fund Covid 19 vaccinations each year for those with progressive lung conditions, to prevent putting our lives at risk or shortening our lives due to the damage Covid and associated pneumonia can cause us!
additional_details: Government decided that those with progressive lung conditions, e.g, bronchiectasis are no longer eligible for free Covid 19 vaccinations. We think this is disgraceful and that this can put the lives of those with progressive lung conditions at risk, or in the case of survival means our lives can be shortened considerably by the damage Covid 19 and associated pneumonia can cause to our lungs. We should have a right to treatment that can prolong our lives and not leave us to suffer!

action: Reverse the freeze on income tax thresholds to stop stealth tax rises
background: Reverse the freeze on income tax thresholds and increase them with inflation. The freeze is a stealth tax that drags workers into paying more each year despite stagnant real wages. Uprating thresholds would protect working families from real-terms income cuts.
additional_details: Frozen tax thresholds mean workers pay more tax each year for doing the same job. Many of us are already struggling with rising living costs, and fiscal drag quietly reduces our take-home pay even when our wages don’t rise in real terms. This is a stealth tax that hits low- and middle-income families hardest. Thresholds should rise with inflation so people aren’t punished for small or necessary pay increases.

action: Stop proposed changes to the Motability Scheme

action: STOP the bill for Judge only trial's

action: Change speeding penalties to 1point for up to 25MPH on a 20MPH road
background: Drivers are currently penalised 3 points for travelling at up to 24mph in 20mph areas. This action is disproportionate. The current penalty treats these drivers the same as other drivers who speed at excessively dangerous limits.
additional_details: Change speeding penalties to 1point for up to 25MPH on a 20MPH road.

action: Debate the removal of the right of British citizens abroad to pay class 2 NICs
background: British citizens abroad will no longer be able to pay class 2 national insurance contributions to obtain a UK State pension. This has been in place until now, and UK citizens may have planned their future financial security around this scheme.
additional_details: Some British citizens abroad are in low paid jobs with local salaries, and may not have been in their country of residence long enough to accrue a reasonable pension there. We also believe that we carry out cultural diplomacy and promote Britain.

action: Protect the Right to Trial by Jury
background: We ask the Government to commit publicly to retaining the right to trial by jury in England and Wales. Trial by jury is a long-standing safeguard in the justice system, ensuring fairness, independence, and public confidence. We want the Government to rule out any proposals of this.
additional_details: We urge the Government not to pursue any reforms that would abolish or limit the right to trial by jury. Jury trials are a fundamental democratic protection, allowing ordinary citizens to take part in the justice process. Any move to weaken this right would risk reducing transparency and fairness.

action: Protect the right to jury trials for all eligible criminal offences

additional_details: Reports of plans to restrict jury trials threaten a core constitutional safeguard. Trial by jury protects the rule of law, limits state power and keeps justice in the hands of the people. Removing it would dismantle a centuries old protection and weaken public confidence. The backlog comes from years of under funding, not juries. Parliament must act now to defend this essential right.

additional_details: Just as cigarettes, alcohol, and gambling carry warnings, AI tools should disclose their artificiality and risks of dependency. We believe regulation is needed to protect public health and ensure ethical design.

action: Raise Bereavement Support Payment and extend beyond 18 months
background: Reform Bereavement Support Payment so families with and without dependent children receive help beyond 18 months, with annual uprating to reflect cost of living.
additional_details: BSP ends after 18 months and is not uprated, which can leave widowed families in financial hardship for years. I lost my husband in May 2025, gave up my career to care for him, and now earn less than 25% of our previous income while raising two young children. Previous Widowed Parent’s Allowance lasted until Child Benefit ended, offering stability. We feel that BSP ignores long-term income loss and emotional strain.
government_response_summary: Bereavement Support Payment provides valuable short-term help after a death. While we are not able to increase BSP at this time, longer-term support is available from other social security benefits.
government_response_body: The Government recognises the profound emotional and financial impact that losing a spouse, civil partner, or cohabiting partner with dependent children can have on families. We are grateful to the petitioner for sharing their experience, and we understand the challenges bereaved families can face during an already extremely difficult time.  Bereavement Support Payment (BSP) is designed to provide short‑term financial support to help with the immediate additional costs associated with a death. It consists of an initial lump sum followed by 18 monthly payments, with higher rates paid to those with dependent children. BSP is not taxed, does not count towards the benefit cap, and is paid in addition to any income‑related benefits the bereaved may be entitled to.  The petition asks the Government to extend BSP beyond 18 months for all families, and to uprate its value annually in line with the cost of living. BSP is not intended as an ongoing income‑replacement benefit, nor is it designed to match the duration of a family’s grief. The 18‑month duration reflects the policy intent to provide support during the acute period following a bereavement, when people may face sudden costs or short‑term disruption. Longer‑term financial support is instead available through income‑replacement benefits such as Universal Credit, which are usually uprated annually in line with inflation and designed to provide continuing support with everyday living costs.  We also recognise the comparison made in the petition to the previous Widowed Parent’s Allowance (WPA), which could be paid until Child Benefit ended. WPA formed part of a complex system of bereavement benefits which the previous Government reformed in 2017 to create a single, simpler, and more modern benefit. BSP was introduced to ensure a clearer, fairer, and more consistent approach across households.  On eligibility, BSP is currently available to surviving spouses and civil partners, and to cohabiting partners with dependent children. In 2023 the Government changed the law to extend eligibility to cohabitees with children following court judgments that found the previous rules discriminated against children on the basis of their parents’ marital status. This extension focused on families with children, to ensure they get the financial support they need.  On uprating, BSP is reviewed each year on a discretionary basis as part of the annual uprating process. In doing so we need to take into account the broader fiscal position and prioritise where government can most effectively deploy public money. Following this year’s review, it is proposed that BSP will stay at the current rate for 2026/27. Claimants on the standard rate will continue to receive an initial payment of £2,500 and 18 payments of £100, while those on the higher rate will receive £3,500 followed by 18 payments of £350. This allows BSP to help with the immediate costs of bereavement. There is a wide range of other financial support available to the bereaved, including Universal Credit where needed and Funeral Expenses Payments for eligible people arranging a funeral.  The Government keeps all benefits, including BSP under review. We recognise the significant impact of bereavement on individuals and families and remain committed to supporting people through the immediate period following the death of a loved one.  Department for Work and Pensions

action: Abandon any plans to curtail, in any way, the right to Trial by Jury
background: The government is concerned about the severe backlog in holding trials in the courts. The Law Society, Bar Council & other legal rights &  campaign groups have suggested a range of options for addressing this issue. But the Justice Secretary prefers the drastic remedy of ending trial by jury.
additional_details: The right to jury trial has been a core British value for centuries. It was  developed in Anglo-Saxon & Scandinavian nations, and is enshrined in Magna Carta: "No free man shall be...imprisoned, or deprived of his liberties [except] by lawful judgment of his peers". Experience across the world shows that keeping the right to jury trial (except for minor offences) is the most powerful protector of individual liberty. The government must find other ways of addressing the backlog in the courts.

action: Act to ensure Bills backed by MPs & public can complete all stages in Parliament
background: We want the Government to do everything in its power to ensure that when bills are supported by MPs & the public, they have the time to complete all their stages in Parliament. We believe this is important to uphold democracy.
additional_details: We believe the decision of MPs must be respected, especially on matters of social change, and that unelected Lords have a responsibility to scrutinise bills, not block them. With over 1,000 amendments tabled to the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, most by just a handful of Lords, we are concerned that it will run out of time. MPs have voted for it and a poll has found over 70% of the public back it. While the Government is neutral, it must uphold democracy. We believe it must act so the Bill can progress.
government_response_summary: Parliament is the supreme legislative authority in the UK and is responsible for making law. A Bill must be passed by both Houses of Parliament to become law.
government_response_body: Parliamentary sovereignty is a fundamental principle of the UK’s constitutional settlement. This means that it is Parliament, not the Government, that holds the power to make or repeal any law. The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill was introduced to the House of Commons as a Private Member’s Bill (PMB), and on the question of assisted dying, the Government has remained neutral on the Bill throughout its parliamentary stages.  The primacy of the House of Commons, as the elected House, is an established constitutional principle, and is reflected in the provisions of the Parliament Acts of 1911 and 1949, which reduced the House of Lords’ power to delay legislation against the will of the Commons.   The House of Lords is independent of both the House of Commons and the Government. The Government respects the important role played by the Lords in scrutinising legislation according to the conventions and procedures of the Lords.   As the Leader of the House of Commons has said, once the House of Lords have completed their scrutiny of the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, the Government will, if necessary, find time in this current session for the House of Commons to consider any amendments they propose.  Office of the Leader of the House of Commons

action: Introduce an NHS data opt-out & require a consultation for system expansions
background: Introduce a clear national opt-out for NHS data processed in the Federated Data Platform (FDP) and National Data Integration Tenant (NDIT) and require a full public consultation before any further expansion of these systems.
additional_details: The NHS is planning to move from multiple, separate systems to a new national data architecture. Technical documents show national processing of identifiable data, while public explanations may describe only anonymous or aggregate use. As these systems are still being rolled out, we believe the public should have transparency, a clear opt-out and the chance to respond before further expansion.
government_response_summary: The National Data Opt-Out does not apply to the NDIT or FDP as data use supports direct care, is legally required or is anonymised. National public engagement is shaping changes to the opt-out system.
government_response_body: The National Data Integration Tenant (NDIT) and Federated Data Platform (FDP)  Health and care providers already submit personal data daily that enables the NHS to run and manage services. NHS England is simplifying and strengthening that national data collection to support better care.  The National Data Integration Tenant (NDIT) is NHS England’s secure platform for collecting and managing national health and care data. It replaces multiple legacy systems with one unified, secure process, reducing burden for NHS teams while ensuring the right data is available at the right time to support faster decisions and safer care. Data is pseudonymised using Privacy Enhancing Technologies and then routed to the National NHS Federated Data Platform where it is used for analysis, insights and decision-making.  The Federated Data Platform (FDP) enables NHS England and NHS organisations to meet statutory duties for data processing, information sharing, planning and service delivery. Its legal basis for processing is set out in the Overarching Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA), which underwent extensive external review (including by the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) and National Data Guardian (NDG) to ensure lawful, fair and transparent processing.  DPIAs define the legal basis for each data flow and are assessed by the NHS FDP Data Governance Group (DGG) to ensure lawful processing. NHS England’s wider statutory responsibilities for data under the Health and Care Act 2022 require transparency, safe-haven standards, robust governance and public accountability.  Transparency and Public Involvement in the NDIT and FDP  The FDP programme demonstrates substantial, ongoing patient and public involvement, including around NDIT. Governance includes bodies established to embed public voice and provide challenge:  •	FDP Check and Challenge Group – strategic advice on transparency, ethics and public context. •	Health and Social Care Data Public Panel – ensuring clear, accessible public materials. •	NHS FDP DGG – national oversight of data processing and protection, ensuring lawful use. •	A public engagement portal enabling questions, feedback and participation opportunities, which can be accessed via the following link: https://fdp.england.nhs.uk.  The programme has a highly coordinated programme of engagement with a wide range of system stakeholders, including:  •	Trusts and integrated care boards through briefings, implementation support and proactive communications. •	Members of Parliament, national bodies and Arm’s-Length Bodies, kept updated throughout delivery. •	Clinical, operational and digital leaders via conferences, webinars and communities of practice. •	Ethics and regulatory bodies (ICO, NDG), through consultations and repeated DPIA review cycles with the DGG.  This intensive and diverse engagement helps ensure the FDP evolves with continuous feedback, scrutiny and co‑design across the health and care system.  In the future, user organisations may agree that FDP can be used to meet other use cases. NHS England has agreed to consult with patient groups and other organisations, including the NDG and the ICO, before any other Use Cases are agreed.  Patient Choice regarding the NDIT and FDP  The National Data Opt-Out (NDOO) prevents confidential patient information being used for research and planning purposes. It does not apply to direct care (i.e. patient care, for example when you are being treated by a doctor). It also does not apply where data is anonymised, or where the information is required by law. The public are able to make their choice online, or through non-digital channels. Further information on the NDOO is available on the NHS website at the following link: https://www.nhs.uk/using-the-nhs/about-the-nhs/opt-out-of-sharing-your-health-records/. Public engagement recommendations delivered in 2025 will shape changes to the NDOO.  NHS England carefully assesses all data processing within NDIT and the FDP. The use of patient data within the NHS FDP will always respect the NDOO and opt-outs will be applied in line with the policy.  The NDOO does not apply to NDIT processing because NHS England is legally required, under a direction from the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, to process this data to create national insights and dashboards. There is, therefore, no specific opt-out for the NDIT, or plans to introduce one, as the data processing occurs under a legal requirement.  The NDOO does not apply to the FDP because:  •	No confidential patient information is processed by any product in the national platform of FDP to which the NDOO would apply. •	Confidential patient information that is being used in a local platform of the FDP is only being used for the purposes of direct care, and therefore the NDOO does not apply.  Department of Health and Social Care

additional_details: We are concerned the April 2026 dividend tax rise places additional pressure on SMEs and founders already facing higher costs, tight margins and limited support. For many small businesses, dividends are part of how cash flow is managed, income is paid, reinvestment is funded and stability is maintained. Increasing the tax burden reduces the capital available for hiring, growth and resilience, ultimately discouraging entrepreneurship and weakening the UK’s small-business economy.

action: Introduce a Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) and MOT requirement for touring caravans
background:
Touring caravans are currently exempt from MOT testing and pay no Vehicle Excise Duty, despite:
 
Reports of being involved in thousands of road incidents each year
 
Causing an increase in vehicle CO₂ emissions
 
Making use of UK road infrastructure without contributing equivalent revenue.
additional_details:
A VED + MOT regime for touring caravans offers a high-value, low-disruption opportunity to enhance safety, reduce emissions, and generate significant public revenue (c.£95m per annum). Regular inspections will reduce mechanical failures - one of the top causes of caravan incidents.
 
With a fair and pragmatic rollout, this policy would modernise caravan regulation while supporting broader government goals in transport safety and environmental stewardship.

action: decrease strictness on school uniforms / ban school uniforms
background: The government can reduce uniform pressures by setting clear rules that limit expensive branded items and allow affordable generic alternatives. By giving flexible, low-cost dress codes, the government can help ensure families aren’t pushed into unnecessary spending and that all students are happy .
additional_details:
1. Financial Burden
Uniforms cost families unnecessarily. Most students already own suitable clothing.
2. Discomfort and Impracticality
Uniforms are often uncomfortable and unsuitable for changing weather. Students focus better in clothes they can move in.
3. No Proven Benefit
Research shows uniforms do not improve behaviour or academic performance.
4. Limited Self-Expression
Strict uniforms reduce students’ ability to express themselves, affecting confidence and wellbeing.
5. Fit Issues
Sizes often do not accommodate all body types, causing discomfort.
6. Environmental Concerns
Uniforms are replaced frequently, creating waste. Normal clothes are more sustainable.
We ask the school to adopt a flexible dress code that supports comfort, affordability, and student welfare.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban school uniforms
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742463

action: Scrap ILR B2 English requirements for people already in the UK on family visas
background: Scrap B2 level English requirements for ILR for people who are already in the UK on family visas. We believe the B1 requirement should remain place for people already living in the UK in this route. The B2 requirement only apply to applicants arriving after 2025.
additional_details:
Many people on family visas are residents who have come from countries where English is not the primary language and entered the UK under rules that required only B1 English proficiency for Indefinite Leave to Remain.
 
We believe people who entered UK on family visas should not have to face hardships after having previously entered the UK and meeting previous requirements. B2 level should only apply to people who come after 2025.
 
We believe B1 Level English is sufficient to integrate and participate in the UK.

action: Reintroduce the JobStart scheme instead of reintroducing 2+ child benefits
background: Instead of reintroducing child benefit for unlimited numbers of children in a family, use the money to fund an ambitious scheme to get young people into work by meeting half their wage costs.
additional_details: The JobStart scheme paid employers half the wages of young people to get them into work. Such a scheme is desperately needed now, as employers hesitate to recruit in the current climate and young people need to be in work for both personal and societal well being.
rejection_details:
The Jobstart scheme which you refer to seems to only have been available in Northern Ireland. 

There is already a petition open on keeping the two-child benefit cap which you may wish to sign: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/752621

action: Make punishments for people that abuse, endanger or murder animals more severe
background: I want the government to make the punishment for the people that chose to abuse, endanger or murder animals that are not of any threat to them much more severe
additional_details:
I do not feel that animal lives are taken as seriously and I feel that the punishment for animal abuse related criminal offences are not harsh enough.
I think people are significantly more careless when it comes to how they treat an animal in comparison to a human being despite them being more vulnerable (if the animal is not a current threat to them)

I think that making these punishments for animal related crimes would help put a stop to animal abuse
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stronger penalties for animal cruelty and stricter regulations on animal sales
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740729

action: Require mental health training for all HR staff, managers and directors
background: Introduce mandatory mental health training for all HR staff, managers and directors. Ensure the training is comprehensive, realistic and meaningful; to learn what it is like for an employee with a condition to work, struggle and cope within a workplace.
additional_details: Many adults experience mental health problems each year, yet we are concerned that workplaces often lack understanding. Employees can stay silent because they fear stigma, judgment or losing their jobs. This leaves countless people suffering in silence. Mandatory, meaningful training could help create safer, more supportive and informed workplaces for everyone.

action: Introduce a minimum age of 25 to work as a content creator in the adult industry
background: The minimum age to become a content creator in the adult industry should be raised to 25+ to protect the welfare of young adults and to work in alignment with the online safety act.
additional_details: Young people are vulnerable and the adult industry is not a line of work that should be seen as an easy way to make money. A human brain is not fully developed until 25 years old and decisions that are made before this could have a long term lasting effect on the mental health of these individuals. We think the current news headlines are becoming a danger to society. They are advertising and glamourising the industry, therefore, allowing young adults to think that certain behaviours are deemed normal.

action: Reject plans to cut jury trials and uphold the right to trial by jury.
background: Jury trials are a fundamental part of a fair justice system and protect defendants’ rights. Recent proposals to replace many jury trials with judge-only trials endanger centuries-old legal protections and risk miscarriages of justice.
additional_details: Record-high court backlogs should be addressed by improving court funding and resources — not by eroding the right to a jury trial. Removing or limiting jury trials may disproportionately affect vulnerable groups, reduce public confidence in justice, and undermine transparency and fairness.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Stop the government from changing jury trial formats
background: Keep things as they are!
additional_details:
By changing things in this way it will only exasperate the prison overcrowding or it will let criminals back onto our streets.
More emphasis should be on the efficiency and affectivity of the system as it stands.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases

action: Do not scrap trial by jury
background: The government has announced plans to scrap trial by jury for alleged crimes that carry a likely sentence of less than three years. I believe this is fundamentally wrong and that the government should not have the power to do so.
additional_details: Trial by jury is a cornerstone of the British legal system to remove this would be fundamentally wrong. Removing the right to a trial by jury is a step towards authoritarianism and leave the legal system open to huge corruption. This must be stopped and the Justice Secretary should resign.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases

action: Introduce mandatory filming of all non-jury court proceedings in England & Wales
background: Legislate for mandatory video recording of all non-jury criminal and civil court proceedings (eg. police body cameras), with footage available on request to any party receiving an adverse order, ensuring full transparency, accountability, and protection from judicial error or prejudice without jury.
additional_details: Current UK law on court filming is outdated (Supreme Court Act 1981 s.47; Crime and Courts Act 2013 s.32 – limited to Supreme Court and certain appeals, excluding lower courts). We believe mandatory filming would prevent potential prejudice, allowing parties to request footage and full public transparency in life-changing decisions.

action: Impose Sanctions on the U.S if it launches strikes on Venezuelan Land
background: Should the Trump Administration breach international law and launch strikes on land controlled by Venezuela, the UK must sanction any U.S military officers and members of the U.S government responsible. The UK should also summon the U.S ambassador to explain the actions of the United States
additional_details: By sanctioning the government and military command of one of its closest allies, the United Kingdom will be sending a powerful message that acts of aggression by its allies will not be supported. The UK as a major world power and one with monumental diplomatic weight must act to discourage another war started to affect regime change, particularly one initiated by the United States, whose interventions in nations such as Iraq have led to destabilising conflicts that have cost innumerable lives.
rejection_details: In this instance, what is already happening (or has already happened) is action in Venezuela by the US administration/armed forces.  So the petition as it stands can't be accepted.  There are some petitions that were submitted when US action commenced which should be opened shortly (we have a backlog of a few weeks, unfortunately) which you will be able to sign.

action: Require consent for child images in political or controversial articles
background: I want the Government to ban children’s images being used in political or controversial news stories without explicit, informed parental consent, and to amend media regulations so that consent can be withdrawn and children are better protected from online harm.
additional_details: Some parents have experienced their child’s photo being taken from one story and reused to illustrate a political article, which can remove anonymity and lead to online hostility and distress. I believe current rules do not adequately protect children from this type of repurposing and exposure.

action: Agree Prostate Cancer screening would save lives and have a screening programme
background: A recent decision by heath experts concluded that a screening programme would do more harm than good, but, if prostate cancer is detected early there is a better chance of living longer, and less long term pressure on NHS if it’s detected early
additional_details:
Reverse the recent study results which implies that it would be ‘more harm than good’ statement. If another study was to be done by prostate cancer patients, who never had any symptoms, or families of those who have passed away with this disease with no symptoms, I am sure opinion would change. Firstly think about the impact on individuals and their families. When you hear the word CANCER from the doctor, your world changes.  Early detection will save lives, and the NHS £££ 
Screening is a must
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751472 

In addition, your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

If you'd like your petition to apply to Scotland, you could start a petition on this topic on the Scottish Parliament website: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

action: Protect FCDO expertise on humanitarian, development and peace capacity from cuts
background: Pause FCDO plans to cut around 2,000 staff in the name of “agility” weakening UK diplomacy and response to crisis. Preserve expertise developed over the past years humanitarian, development, conflict and gender; and carry out humanitarian, climate and equality impact assessment before changes.
additional_details: Since the DFID–FCO merger, FCDO has already lost vital expertise and left many development adviser posts vacant. IDC Chair Sarah Champion warns that plans to cut 2,000 posts will cause an exodus of staff and put lives at risk. As other donors and agencies cut aid and staff, the UK should lead in diplomacy and multilateral crisis response by investing in humanitarian response, climate action, poverty reduction and protection of women and girls, not hollowing out the teams that deliver this.

action: Remove speed limits on motorways
background: We think it's about time the motorway speed limit was removed. Cars are safer than they used to be. We believe that driving at high speed is safer as you look at the road ahead far more.
additional_details: Germany has unlimited sections so we think we should be in line with them. We think this would bring England out of the Stone Age.

action: Remove VAT on all public utility bills
background: We believe VAT was never meant to be applied to life essentials and it was meant to be a BREXIT benefit. The UK has some of the highest electricity prices in Western Europe! We believe this is why so many citizens struggle whilst energy companies make huge profits, and why GDP is low.
additional_details: Remove VAT on public utility bills.

action: Guilt determined by peers to be a fundamental right
background:
Today David lammy announced an attack on a fundamental part of UK identity and justice announcing the right to trial by jury to be limited in all but the most extreme offences. 

This is a fundamental principle of British identity and uk justice.... Guilt decided by your peers.
additional_details:
Only 3% of cases go to a trial by jury so the reasoning behind jury trial removal is incoherent.... It will not clear court back logs. 

Further the potential for over reach and justice being met out without public consent is an abhorrent attack on British values
rejection_details:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases

action: Protect the Right to Jury Trial in England and Wales — Keep Justice Democratic
background: The Government should protect the right to jury trial, invest in courts and staffing to cut delays, and address the backlog through funding and reform — not by reducing public participation or weakening fundamental justice safeguards.
additional_details: The Government should act because jury trials protect ordinary people from bias, error and unchecked power. They ensure fairness through community oversight and strengthen trust in the justice system. Removing them would erode a core democratic safeguard. Real reform means investing in courts, judges and staff to fix delays without weakening our fundamental rights.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Launch a review into improving social housing provision for families
background: Launch a review into reforming social housing so families with young children aren’t trapped in unsafe, overcrowded flats. The review should look into creating fairer allocation rules, offering suitable downsizing options for older tenants, and ensuring families have access to a safe, healthy home.
additional_details: I want Parliament to take action because I believe the current social housing system is leaving families like mine trapped in unsafe, overcrowded homes with no realistic way out. Only Parliament can change the policies, funding and allocation rules that are causing this crisis. We believe we need national reform so every family has a fair chance at a safe, suitable home and older tenants are given proper options to downsize without being forced into poor-quality accommodation.

action: Keep the Ancient Right of Jury Trial Intact
background: The government and Parliament should not abolish the ancient right of Jury Trial -- the English and Welsh people should have a right to a fair trial, judged by a jury of their peers.
additional_details:
The Lord Chancellor has announced plans to abolish the right to a jury trial for criminal cases with potential prison sentences of up to three years.

For centuries the people of England and Wales have enjoyed the ancient right of Jury Trial. It is a necessary safeguard for individual rights to be judged by a jury of your peers, especially in cases of potential deprivation of liberty, including imprisonment.

The whim of one unpopular government should not be allowed to strip us of this right.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Include South Middlesex in the new West Surrey County name
background: This petition recommends “South Middlesex” be included in the proposed county name “West Surrey” as the current proposal does not reflect the geography, or composition of our area. South Middlesex identity remains important to residents and it should be recognised in this new county official title.
additional_details:
South Middlesex has a long-standing cultural and historical identity distinct from Surrey and identifying the county as “West Surrey & South Middlesex” acknowledges that heritage. A dual name supports alignment despite boundary reorganisation to 'preserve legacy' and prevent erasure of an area steeped in tradition and local history that government would do well not to ignore

Including South Middlesex follows 'established practice' for newly formed authorities with diverse historical identities.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

You could start a new petition calling for changes to the consultation process for the creation and naming of new unitary authorities, if that's what you would like.

action: For Parliament to discuss the proposed Chinese “mega-embassy”.
background: Parliament needs to scrutinise the proposed Chinese “mega-embassy” to address any potential national security concerns or other issues.
additional_details:
This decision to open this large Chinese embassy has attracted many concerns from across Parliament, security experts and international allies.
It deserves proper scrutiny in the Parliament as the effects will be long term and will extend far beyond this parliamentary term.

Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

action: Require Property Management Companies to Publish Management Annual Accounts
background: The Government should require all property management companies responsible for issuing service charges in residential apartment complexes to publish annual management accounts within 12 months of each financial year end and publish them on a publicly accessible portal, similar to Companies House.
additional_details: Leaseholders can face long delays or no access to management accounts, leaving them unable to see how service charges are used. We believe that requiring property management companies to publish annual accounts within 12 months on a central portal (similar to Companies House) could improve transparency, prevent misuse of funds, and ensure consistent, accountable financial practices. Failure to do so should results in fines, reimbursement of management fees, prison, or loss of relevant real estate licences.

action: Hold a Commons debate on whether the UK should introduce a statutory AI law.
background: Hold a House of Commons debate on introducing a statutory AI framework. The debate should draw on relevant parliamentary work on AI to help shape a clear and consistent national approach to regulating AI across the UK.
additional_details: The UK has no statutory AI law. Government relies on existing rules, regulators and the AI Security Institute. AI systems already influence decisions in work, education, housing, finance and services. A Commons debate is needed to consider whether the UK should move from a voluntary approach to a clear and accountable statutory framework.
rejection_details:
We are not clear what specific action you are seeking in regards to a law on AI.

You could submit a new petition setting out more clearly what you like an AI Act to cover.

rejection_details:

action: Keep the £135 customs duty relief on overseas imports
background: In the Chancellor’s budget, plans were announced to remove the £135 exemption by 2029, but many UK retailers are actively demanding this to be implemented sooner. The burden of this change could most affect UK citizens. Keep the £135 exemption and not put duties on goods under £135.
additional_details: We believe the only parties that will benefit from the exemption being removed are UK retailers, by shifting the burden of customs on UK citizens, and forcing them to consume UK retailer goods. This could cause catastrophic harm for small businesses and many citizens cannot be outspoken by the opinions of corporations. It could cause major delays in shipping times and delivery. People could be expected to pay £14 (customs + courier handling fees) on an import that only cost them £10, which we feel is distasteful.

action: Repeal the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991, introduce new laws on penalties & education
background: We want the 1991 Act to be repealed and replaced with new legislation mandating education on dog ownership at a young age, and specifying harsher penalties for any owners mistreating their dogs or who fail to prevent their dogs acting dangerously out of control and harming the public.
additional_details: We believe the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 is outdated and that many dogs have been wrongly euthanised and punished for looking a certain way. The law is partly focused on the physical appearance of a dog, whereas we think the focus should be purely on actual behaviour. A dog that is born a breed of dog that is not on the list of dangerous dogs may be taken, assessed and put on the list as another breed, limiting their life. Sometimes they don’t even make it out of the kennels.

action: Protect the right to trial by jury in criminal cases
background: Guarantee full access to trial by jury in criminal cases, and rule out introducing new limits or replacing juries with judge-only trials. Maintain the existing rights under which indictable and triable-either-way offences are decided by a jury of peers.
additional_details: Jury trials are a cornerstone of British justice, ensuring the state is held to account and that ordinary citizens play a central role in decisions that can remove someone’s liberty. Reducing access risks unchecked power, miscarriages of justice and the erosion of trust in the legal system. This fundamental safeguard must not be changed without clear democratic consent. Court backlogs should be tackled through proper funding – not by weakening vital protections.

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases

action: Keep University of essex southend campus open

additional_details: The government should act to keep Southend University Campus open because its closure would harm students, staff, and the local community. background: Maintain the right to trial by jury in English courts and reject any proposals that restrict or remove its availability, ensuring this essential safeguard of fair and transparent justice remains in place.
additional_details: Trial by jury is a long-standing safeguard that ensures fairness, public trust and democratic participation in the justice system. action: Require food manufacturers to show the presence of Ultra Processed ingredients
background: Modify existing food labelling laws to include the requirement for manufacturers to add a clear and appropriately sized and placed indicator of the level of processing that the ingredients of their product have undergone, using the internationally-recognised Nova Classification system.
additional_details:
A growing body of evidence suggests that ultra-processed foods are behind the modern increases in chronic health conditions, including alzheimers, cancer, obesity, diabetes and others. These conditions lead to many preventable deaths, the loss of quality of life for millions and costs the NHS millions every year.

Requiring manufacturers to clearly indicate the presence of UPFs will empower the public to make healthy choices and could save many lives and significant amounts of public funding.

action: Exempt the state pension from tax for everyone over the age of 67
background: Make the state pension taxable exempt exempt for every pensioner not just those on low incomes .

However, those who have worked and saved for an occupational pension (often without choice thanks to government legislation) will pay tax on both their occupational AND state pension - which is grossly unfair to those who have worked and saved
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746077

action: End postcode inequality in Child Performance Licence processing times
background: Children’s performance licence times vary wildly between councils, causing lost work and inequality. We want a national maximum turnaround of 10 days and a ban on “urgent” licences so productions plan properly and all children have equal access to opportunities.
additional_details: Current children’s performance licence times vary from 1–21 days, meaning some children are repeatedly passed over because their council is slow. Kids are even advertised by agencies for “fast licence turnaround,” creating postcode-based inequality. Opportunities are lost not due to talent but bureaucracy, costing children life-changing earnings and vital skills.

The shambolic state of the bureaucracy of Justice is no reason to change the rights of the citizen, it is a reason to change the shambolic bureaucracy.
We demand that the right to a Trial by Jury.

action: Address the funding crisis in UK HE to protect diversity of subject provision.
background: Reinstate government oversight of our publically-funded and vital sector. Protect diversity of provision and widening access by reinstating student number caps and requiring more democratic management structures. Address the financial crisis, including the impact of excessive senior leadership pay.
additional_details: Cold spots for degree-level subject provision are growing across the UK. Lack of government regulation of UK HEIs means no assurance of their continued provision of diverse subjects, as would align with Labour's Industrial Strategy, or that they enact their civic duties in locally-embedded ways. HE equips graduates with advanced knowledge, critical thinking, professional expertise. It drives innovation and economic growth, contributes to national security, enriches the social fabric. Protect it.

action: Halt aid to Tanzania & demand an investigation into violence against protesters
background: Suspend non-humanitarian aid to Tanzania and call for an independent, international investigation into reported violence against protesters. The UK should push for accountability, support democratic and electoral reforms, and ensure opposition voices and civil society can freely participate.
additional_details: We are concerned by serious allegations of violence against protesters in Tanzania raise urgent human rights concerns. We believe the UK should not continue unrestricted aid without an independent investigation. Suspending non-humanitarian aid and supporting an impartial, international investigation could help establish the truth, ensure accountability, and protect democratic freedoms. We believe UK action is vital to uphold human rights, prevent further abuses, and encourage fair political participation and credible elections.

action: Let First time buyers use their LISA to build a house
background: Currently Self builders can use their LISA to buy land, but they can't use it for the building itself. This disproportionately affects people who are looking to buy a cheaper land and have enough funds to buy the land outright, but need mortgage for the build itself.
additional_details: It would help people who would like to build their own house, which is important as we have a shortage of housing.

action: DO NOT cancel local elections in Chorley, Preston and Blackburn in May 2026
background: Ensure that local elections in Chorley, Preston and Blackburn go ahead in May 2026. The government must protect the rights of its residents.
additional_details: Cancelling the May 2026 elections would deny residents in Chorley, Preston and Blackburn their democratic right to choose who represents them. Proposals to create new larger "unitary" authorities in Lancashire are still uncertain and not due to take effect until 2028. Too much can change before 2028, and people deserve accountability and a say in their local elections and not be denied their chance to vote locally.

action: Ancestry Visas should not be affected by the proposed earned settlement changes.

additional_details: Ancestry visa holders should be exempt from the current White Paper proposal for earned settlement. If you hold an ancestry visa it is because you are a descendant of a British citizen and are returning to the country of your family’s origin. The requirements for this settlement route should not be changed/increased from what is currently required for this route.

Keep 5 year route to ILR for Existing Ancestry Visa Holders
