action: Do not base human rights on the outdated concept of biological sex.
background: We call on the government to rightly outlaw any attempt to segregate people and base human rights on the outdated, scientifically illiterate idea that all humans fall neatly into a binary based on the outdated concept of biological sex.
additional_details:
Calls to segregate society according to the wilfully ignorant idea of a biological sex binary are based entirely in ultraconservative hate, and have no foundation in scientific reality or the lives of real people.

The Supreme Court ruling on biological sex was entirely ideological and should be considered an international embarrassment to the UK in 2025.

The lives and human rights of gender diverse people should not be at the mercy of Stone Age beliefs like this in any modern country.
rejection_details:
We are not sure what action you would like the UK Government or Parliament to take.

The UK Government cannot change court judgements but could introduce new legislation about this.

You could start a petition about amending the Equality Act to define the terms woman and man not based on biological sex, if that is what you would like.

action: Require police to attend all welfare calls
background: I would like there to be a rule where police have to attend to people if they get a welfare call of someone vulnerable or in a bad mental state without judgement.

action: Create a primary care scrutiny committee to assess the current GP crisis
background: We call on the government to set up a parliamentary committee for General Practice for urgent cross party analysis.
additional_details: The committee should investigate the safety of the digital first approach which requires unlimited online consults throughout working hours. We believe that this is overwhelming GPs and putting patients in danger.  The Committee should also review GP contract negotiation and look at increasing GP funding from 7 to 11% of the NHS budget.

action: Repeal the The Bread and Flour (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2024
background:
The Bread and Flour (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2024 will require flour millers to fortify non-wholemeal wheat flour with folic acid. 
The people who have signed this petition demand that this act is repealed, or at the very least a referendum is held so the public may choose for themselves.
additional_details:
According to the gov.uk announcement in November 2024, the intention is to prevent 200 cases of debilitating brain and spine defects in babies every year. 
This represents less than 0.03 percent of the number of babies born each year and would rely upon the pregnant mother's of those babies affected eating non-wholemeal bread as part of their regular diet. 
Removing all choice from the entire UK population who choose to eat non-wholemeal wheat products is utterly ridiculous and a draconian move.
rejection_details: There is already a petition open on this subject, which you may wish to sign: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751401

action: Do not implement the business rate increases planned for April 2026
background: We call on the government to stop the planned business rate hikes. We believe this hike is going to drive prices up even further, result in more High Streets being abandoned by small and medium business and drown an already struggling pub trade.

action: Support kids with severe mental health who struggle with daily school attendance
background: Don’t punish parents for minors who struggle to attend school due to mental health issues. Support children and families having difficulty in coping with the overwhelming and sometimes intimidating pressures that attending school can bring.
additional_details: Should parents be fined for their children’s absence due to their mental health issues. In the current climate where the workplace is making strides in combatting neurodivergence and absence at work with more awareness it seems unfair that schools are not doing the same. Added pressure on parents financially especially those on low incomes makes no sense. Parents often have to have time off losing either holiday or pay to look after children who are off for this reason.
rejection_details: We understand they are concerned about support for children with mental health needs but we are not sure what action you would like the UK Government or Parliament to take. You could start a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Make comprehensive autism training mandatory for police officers
background: We want the government to require the police to provide mandatory, comprehensive, accredited autism training for all police officers. This training should cover communication differences, sensory needs, de-escalation strategies and appropriate responses during incidents involving people with autism.
additional_details: Autistic people can face misunderstanding during police encounters, which can cause unnecessary stress or escalation. Training is inconsistent, leaving many officers without the skills to recognise autistic traits or adjust their approach. Mandatory autism training could help officers communicate calmly, reduce risks, support vulnerable people, and ensure safer, more appropriate responses for everyone involved.

action: Teach mental health awareness and disability awareness In schools.
background: I want the government to make schools teach mental health awareness and disability awareness.  And also to teach about how to look after their mental wellbeing.
additional_details: I want the government to teach mental health awareness because I feel alot of people grow up not understanding it and for some not understanding themselves.
rejection_details:
It’s is compulsory for all schools to teach pupils about mental health and wellbeing as part of health and relationships education.

You may wish to start a new petition calling for the Government to review the current curriculum in relation to mental health.

action: Require dementia training for all patient-facing NHS staff
background: We believe that people with dementia face avoidable harm in hospitals due to inconsistent training and poor accountability. We need mandatory dementia training for all staff and national standards to ensure safe, compassionate, and consistent care across every NHS hospital.
additional_details: People with dementia face high risks in hospital, falls, delirium, long stays, and avoidable harm. We think this is because staff training and care standards vary. I want the Government to make dementia training mandatory and ensure every NHS hospital provides safe, consistent, compassionate care.

action: Change the mental health system
background:
staff re-training and new training for mental health 
More awareness for mental health
Improvements in inpatient care
additional_details:
too many young people struggling with mental health difficulties are losing their lives or are becoming traumatised from so called “care”.
CHILDREN are being left with ptsd in places they were told theyd be getting help.
Not enough is being done to prevent accidents/incidents and deaths due to mental health
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

Your petition is also about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

action: Review railway laws & regulations to ensure safer, reliable trains
background: Launch a review of all railway laws & regulations to ensure all train services enforce safe carriage limits, improve ventilation, upgrade signalling and infrastructure, train staff in crowd control, increase service reliability & build a fair, transparent compensation system for disrupted journeys.
additional_details: We believe delays and signalling failures are constant and services are unreliable, and that rail infrastructure is still far too easy for the public to access, which can lead to frequent incidents, serious disruption and loss of life. We feel this is a safety failure, not just an inconvenience. The Government should act to secure the network, modernise signalling, prevent harm and protect passengers.

action: Keep all jury trials
background: Do not introduce swift trials. Invest more in MoJ.
additional_details: Decades of court closures, chronic underfunding, and broken private contracts have left the justice system on its knees. Instead of working to fund and fix it this government is completely destroying it by scrapping our centuries old democratic fundamental right to jury trials dating back to 1220 and the Magna Carta. They have no mandate.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Headlight Glare Is Getting Dangerous — We Need Change!
background: I want to raise a growing safety concern regarding the increasing use of extremely bright LED headlights on vehicles. Over recent years, these lights have become noticeably more intense, and many drivers, myself included are experiencing significant difficulty and discomfort because of them.
additional_details: Reconsider these LED LIGHTS because they’re so bright that they leave dots in front of my eyes and many others eyes and even if it’s for a second that one second could cause a RTC and then who would be at fault? Those ones with the bright LED lights shining through your eyes and whole car or the person who’s driving and has the lights shining at them causing them to have dots in their eyes. Please reconsider this it causes my anxiety to go through the roof.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban LED vehicle headlights or regulate bulb wattage

action: Make cctv mandatory to all nurseries and schools
background: To force nurseries and schools to have cctv in operation for the safety of children
additional_details: Because the nursery management will never will to pay extra for things like this so the government must enforce this to all nurseries ans schools

You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require CCTV in all early years settings
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750797

action: Increase the Carer’s Allowance to equal 35 hours at minimum wage
background: I want the Government to appreciate unpaid carers who can’t work and to increase the Carer’s Allowance so it equals the minimum wage. Many unpaid carers are only paid around £333 a month for a minimum 140 hours care every 4 weeks, which works out around £2.50 an hour.
additional_details:
By being paid minimum wage, this could increase to around £1700 per month if they are paid the minimum wage.
 
We believe unpaid carers save the Treasury billions of pounds, many are paid around £2.50 an hour, which we feel is an insulting amount and only continues because many carers carry out social care out of love.

action: Fund and deliver a £60 million aid package for Sri Lanka
background: We write to express concern regarding the UK’s pledge of £675,000 to assist Sri Lanka after Cyclone Ditwah. We call for a £60 million humanitarian & recovery aid package for Sri Lanka to provide immediate relief food, medical supplies, temporary shelter, rebuilding of homes, hospitals, and schools.
additional_details:
The UK is home to a vibrant Sri Lankan diaspora, which is composed of highly skilled migrants, care workers, nurses and students. This community contributes extensively to the NHS, education, business, and public life.
 
In 2023, overseas aid was an estimated £15.3 billion, with over £50 billion spent from 2020-23. The UK has historically provided substantial disaster aid, £392 million after the 2004 tsunami and £10 million after the 2025 Myanmar earthquake.
 
We believe climate change is something the whole world should be responsible for, and that one country should not be left to suffer.

action: Reject & remove plans to abolish jury trials for offences under 3year terms
background: The Government plans to end jury trials for offences under three years, stripping citizens of their right to be judged by peers. This petition seeks the full rejection and removal of this proposal, which undermines open justice, concentrates state power, and weakens vital legal safeguards.
additional_details: We ask Parliament to halt this reform, hold a full debate, and require any change to jury trial rights to be approved either by primary legislation with constitutional safeguards or by a national referendum. Jury trials protect a core liberty rooted in Magna Carta, and no government should alter this without direct public consent.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Require major online retailers to state the recyclability of product packaging
background: We call on the UK Government to require large online retailers to clearly display the recyclability of all product packaging, including any boxing. Labels should state whether packaging is, for example: fully recyclable, partly recyclable, biodegradable/compostable, or not recyclable.
additional_details: Clear, standardised recyclability information would help consumers make informed choices, reduce waste going to landfill and incineration, and support the UK’s environmental goals. Current labelling is inconsistent, difficult to interpret, or missing entirely. A mandatory labelling standard would improve transparency, encourage more sustainable packaging design and help households to recycle correctly.

action: Require transparency and public explanation of how legal id is created at birth.
background: UK birth registration creates a legal identity used for rights, services, and duties, yet the process is unclear. Citizens need plain guidance on what a legal person is, how it relates to the living individual, what rights follow, how data is used, and how laws interact. Transparency is vital.
additional_details:
We are not asking to abolish birth registration or statutory law.
We are asking for:
	1.	A public review of the legal identity framework
	2.	Clear, accessible guidance explaining:
	•	The meaning of “legal person”
	•	The purpose and implications of birth registration
	•	How identity interacts with rights, responsibilities, and consent
	3.	Improved transparency so parents and citizens can make informed decisions
	4.	A public information notice issued by the Government to improve understanding
rejection_details:
We're not sure exactly what action you are seeking from the UK Government or Parliament.  

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Restart all local elections and by-elections
background: Due to the successional cancellation of local elections in potential Mayoral constituencies, parliament should reinstate local elections until 2028 when the Mayoral elections begin.
additional_details: To allow residents in their constituencies  to have a democratic choice over the local councils. Democracy delayed is democracy denied
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751384

action: Recognise 'femicide' as a specific crime within UK & NI's legal framework
background: Femicide is the misogynistic killing of women and girls, intrinsically linked to their gender. It encompasses not only intimate partner violence but also other forms of targeted gender-based violence, such as honour killings and the murder of women involved in sex work.
additional_details: Current laws fail to acknowledge the motive of gender-based hate in killings of women. Legal recognition of Femicide will expose the true scale of the crisis, send a clear judicial message that misogynistic murder is unacceptable, and provide the clarity needed for effective, life-saving prevention strategies across the UK.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Northern Ireland Executive and Northern Ireland Assembly is responsible for. 

If you want to raise this issue you could contact your MLA, or raise it with the Northern Ireland Executive.

action: Create a New Independent Skilled Worker Visa Route
background: This proposal recommends the creation of a new Independent Skilled Worker Visa (ISWV) that allows qualified foreign nationals to work in the UK without being tied to a sponsoring employer.
additional_details:
The purpose of this visa is to:
Address skill shortages more effectively
Reduce worker exploitation linked to employer-dependent visas
Enable non-citizens to contribute productively to the UK economy
Maintain clear safeguards to protect public resources and immigration control
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Create a Renewable Open Work Permit for Sponsored Workers 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751532

action: Mandatory Psychological Assessments for Childcare Staff to help protect children
background: We call on the UK Government to require annual private psychological assessments for all childcare and education staff, and introduce an early risk-identification support system, to better protect children and strengthen safeguarding nationwide.
additional_details: Introduce mandatory annual private psychological or psychiatric assessments for all childcare and education staff. Create a national early risk-identification and support system to detect emerging concerns. Review and strengthen all safeguarding procedures to better protect children across the UK.

action: Fund a national awareness campaign of suicide in the construction sector
background: We want an open and honest debate about this silent killer which we feel has been ignored in the sector. We want heightened public awareness, as we believe current legislation is not fit for purpose.
additional_details:
Construction workers help build nations’ futures, but many are being buried too soon, with more than one worker taking their own life everyday – we want help and change.
 
According to 2021 ONS stats, 507 construction workers took their own lives. The reasons are complex, but we feel the outcome is simple: we believe that without proper government intervention and reigniting the sector, nothing will change. Stigma and silence keep too many from seeking help and the crisis grows ever deadlier. We want the Government to acknowledge this issue and set about real change. We want to explore new ways to reduce depression and stress which sadly can lead to suicide.

action: Prevent Government from stopping the democratic right to vote.
background: Pass a law that establishes the requirement for Government to abide by the democratic right to hold ALL scheduled elections for all levels.
additional_details: Currently our local May elections have been postponed for 2 years and this is now to be extended for 3 more years.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Remove power to cancel local government elections" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747234

action: Stop utility shareholder dividend payouts until infrastructure upgrades complete
background: Pass a law which freezes utility and energy company dividend payouts to shareholders and requires payouts to only occur once infrastructure investment upgrades and repair work are completed. This should encompass water, gas and electrical companies.
additional_details: If investment is needed to upgrade infrastructure, we believe companies should be using all funds that are available to them, and if they have done so, only then should they be allowed to raise prices for consumers. We believe they shouldn’t be allowed to pay any shareholder dividends during this time. If the customer has to pay, we believe shareholders should as well.

action: Clear non-numeric labelling for Halal meat
background: I am requesting the Government introduce requirements for clear, non-numeric labelling on halal-certified products, including meat and processed foods. Supermarkets and suppliers rely on numeric identifiers to indicate slaughter methods/certification. These are not understood by the average consumer
additional_details: Use clear, front-of-label symbols or plain wording to indicate whether a product is Halal or non-Halal, so that consumers can make fully informed and confident decisions about the products they purchase, whether for personal, ethical, or religious reasons. Ensure consistent labelling standards across all food agencies and retailers to guarantee full transparency and fairness for every consumer.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Require non-stunned and stunned meat to be labelled accordingly 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737327

action: Reverse the decision to delay the Mayoral and other Local Elections until 2028.
background:
Reverse the undemocratic decision to delay the 2026 Mayoral and Local Elections by 2 years until 2028. This is undemocratic.

We want this debated by MPs in the House of Commons and asking the government to reverse the decision to delay local and mayoral elections.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751384

action: Ban the breeding of cats with extreme physical traits
background: Ban the breeding of cats with extreme physical traits or inherited conditions that cause suffering, such as Scottish Fold, Manx and dwarf-type cats. Require strict licensing, health screening and full disclosure of risks if breeding is permitted.
additional_details: These breeds face serious welfare issues. The Scottish Fold’s mutation causes lifelong cartilage and bone disease, while the Manx tailless gene can lead to spinal defects, incontinence and early death. Dwarf cats also suffer skeletal problems. Major registries refuse to recognise some of these breeds due to welfare concerns. Many countries ban these breeds, such as Australia and Austria. We believe legislation is needed to prevent avoidable suffering.

action: Give Early Years providers the same business rates relief as schools.
background: Exempt all Ofsted‑registered Early Years and childcare settings in England from business rates by creating a permanent relief scheme, funded centrally as for state schools, so that providers can reinvest this money into staff pay and quality.
additional_details: Early Years providers are an essential part of the education and childcare infrastructure, enabling parents to work and supporting children’s development. State schools have their business rates fully funded and many high‑street sectors get generous discounts, but most nurseries do not. Rising wages, energy and rents mean unfunded rates are pushing settings to close or cut staff pay. Scotland and Wales already give 100% business rates relief to registered childcare settings; England should too!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Stop Charging Early Years Nurseries Full Business Rates 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/752160

action: Require all schools to provide adaptive sports equipment for disabled pupils
background: Establish a statutory requirement for all schools to provide adaptive sports equipment, including a sports wheelchair, to ensure equal access to physical education for all disabled pupils and to promote inclusive physical education.
additional_details:
1. According to ParalympicsGB, only one in four disabled people in the UK regularly participate in PE and school sport.
2.  According to some reports, disabled children make up nearly 20% of the school population in England.
3. Some reports found that the lack of inclusive PE provision and adaptive equipment in schools is repeatedly identified as a major barrier preventing disabled pupils from participating in physical activity.

action: Provide a veterinary service funded by additional tax contributions
background: I want the government to consider introducing a voluntary additional tax to fund a free of charge veterinary service similar to the NHS.
additional_details: I’ve seen first hand how much veterinary bills cost, as well as seeing loved ones struggle with costly bills due to their pet already having an underlying health issue. We believe any responsible pet owner who works would volunteer a small deduction from their wage if it meant they never had to worry about paying for expensive vet bills.

action: Launch a review of the UK construction industry
background: Launch a review of the UK’s construction industry, including the work environment, wages and recruitment, and legislation that could protect earnings that may be lost as a result of weather conditions, along with any money owed.

action: Provide free childcare for working families&subsidised part-time for non-workers
background: Introduce free full-time childcare for working families and part-time subsidised places for non-working families to boost workforce participation, reduce childcare costs, and improve child outcomes, while ensuring fairness and efficient use of public funds.
additional_details: Rising childcare costs make it unaffordable for working parents, while families on benefits often get free places. This discourages workforce participation and limits opportunities for children. Providing free childcare for working families and subsidised part-time places for others promotes fairness, boosts productivity, and improves child development outcomes.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you mean in terms of providing free childcare for working families and subsidised, part-time childcare for those who do not work.

Under the Free Childcare for Working Parents scheme, working parents of children aged 9 months to 4 years old may be able to claim 30 hours per week of free childcare for 38 weeks of the year. 

Non-working parents may also be able to claim free childcare under the scheme if they fulfil certain eligibility requirements. You can read more about the scheme here: https://www.gov.uk/free-childcare-if-working/what-youll-get

You may wish to start a new petition calling for the Government or Parliament to increase the number of hours for free childcare entitlement or eligibility requirements to the scheme.

action: United Kingdom must ensure no government can cancel or postpone elections.
background: To uphold the integrity of the United Kingdom’s democratic system, it is vital to remove any possibility of a government cancelling or unduly delaying elections.
additional_details: In a democracy, the people—not the government—decide when change comes. The UK must guarantee that no government can ever cancel or postpone elections to serve its own interests. Strong fixed-term rules and independent safeguards are essential to protect our right to vote and keep power in the hands of the public.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition which calls for the same action:

Remove power to cancel local government elections 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747234

The deadline for the next General Election is five years from the start of the current Parliament (9 July 2024), plus the time required to run an election campaign. The Government has no plans to change this deadline.

action: Fund a universal Government Grant for all PGCE trainee teachers
background: I want the Government to fund a universal grant for all PGCE trainee teachers. This could ensure every subject is valued equally, remove financial barriers to entering the profession, and help address the national teacher shortage by supporting trainees throughout their training year.
additional_details: There is a growing teacher shortage, yet many PGCE subjects like Business, Economics, RE, Design & Technology, and the Arts receive no grants. Many trainees face heavy workloads and financial strain while shaping the future of education. Supporting all subjects with grants could ease hardship, widen access, strengthen recruitment, and affirm the vital role teachers play in society.

action: Role to be created or absorbed in parliament to ensure PM answers all questions
background: Currently, the PM often uses pre-planned script to answer questions in PMQ's, often without any attempt to answer the question. The MP does then not get an opportunity to challenge. The PM should have a responsibility to answer the question and somebody should be enforcing this, in real time.
additional_details: Good questions get asked and we, the general public, want to hear the PM's answer. Currently, the PM just says what he feels we want to hear instead of actually facing the challenge of the opposition.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker personally, and the Prime Minister is responsible for answers to questions.

action: Stop Wales becoming 'a nation of Sanctuary'
background: Stop the Welsh Government wasting tax payers money on a nation of sanctuary that nobody outside of the sennedd wants
additional_details: Because welsh Labour are not listenjngbtonthwnpeople of Wales
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Welsh Government is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.

The Welsh Parliament has its own Petitions Committee.

If you'd like to send your petition to the Welsh Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.senedd.wales/

action: Police officers should be paid more
background: Increase the pay for police officers so their job feels a bit more bearable and so they have a reason to come to work each day
additional_details: Being in the police is a dangerous and draining job. Many people put their lives at stake so that we can wonder the streets without worrying about everything. Police custody is a grubby, violent building filled with mostly nasty, drunken people. These brave warriors are not paid enough for their selfless efforts to help the country. Most of them do it for justice to the wrongdoers. I am not a police man. I just feel as though they deserve more pay for their efforts.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. The Government has already confirmed a 4.2% pay increase for police officers (https://www.gov.uk/government/news/42-pay-rise-for-police-officers-across-england-and-wales). We are not sure exactly how much more you would like police officers to be paid.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, such as specifying how much you would like police officer pay to be increased by

action: Fund free civil legal support for survivors of sexual violence
background: Create a Government-funded scheme that provides free, specialist civil legal support for survivors of sexual violence. This should cover legal advice, representation, and essential case costs, ensuring survivors can pursue civil claims regardless of income or financial barriers.
additional_details: Most rape cases never reach trial, leaving thousands of survivors with no legal route to accountability. Civil action is often the only remaining path, yet unaffordable for most. Free legal support would provide fair access to justice, reduce the impact of trauma, deter serial offenders, and lower the long-term social and economic costs associated with sexual violence.

action: Turn off the heating in the House of Common
background: I want Parliament to turn off the heating in the House of Commons to show solidarity with citizens facing rising energy bills. If households are told to cut back, MPs should lead by example and share the same discomfort, proving they are not above the standards they set.
additional_details: Heating the House of Commons at the taxpayer’s expense while millions struggle with rising energy bills is a symbol of hypocrisy. Citizens are told to cut back, wear extra layers, and accept colder homes, yet MPs enjoy constant warmth. Turning off the heating would force Parliament to share the discomfort ordinary people face, highlight the need for energy efficiency, and remind representatives they are not above the standards they impose.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about something that is an operational decision for a government or parliamentary body, rather than decision about policy or legislation that is made by the Government or Parliament.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: The UK Government to withdraw from Eurovision based on Israel allowed to compete
background: I would like the UK Government to debate if we should withdraw from the Eurovision next year based on Israel allowed to compete.
additional_details: Based on the atrocities that Israel have carried out in Gaza and the fact that even though here is a ceasefire there are still people being killed, the UK Government should join other countries such as Spain, Netherlands and Ireland and set an example for others to follow.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions as to whether the BBC takes part in Eurovision are a matter for the BBC not the Government or the UK Parliament. We also cannot allow petitions about individual productions that the UK Government or Parliament are not responsible for.

action: Tax all welfare and benefits at identical rates as earned income
background: Ensure all welfare and benefits payments, allowances and subsidies are subject to identical personal tax, national insurance rates and starting thresholds as earned and pension income
additional_details: We believe the fact that a working person has to pay tax and national insurance on very low income levels (just over £12,500 per year) whilst some benefits recipients can receive more than this (and some receive substantially more) tax free is an immoral outrage.

action: Review and Regulate AI to Protect Jobs and Prevent Mass Unemployment
background: We ask the Government to urgently review and regulate AI to protect jobs. Rapid AI advances could cause major unemployment across many sectors. We want an independent assessment of risks, safeguards for workers, and plans for reskilling so AI benefits society responsibly.
additional_details: Without regulation, we believe the rapid growth of AI could replace millions of workers, causing widespread unemployment, economic inequality, and social disruption. We urge the Government to introduce clear rules, invest in reskilling and retraining programs, and ensure AI is deployed to complement human work rather than replace it, protecting jobs, livelihoods, and the long-term stability of the economy.

action: Establish a Health & Care Commission on long-term NHS & social care reform
background: We ask the Government to establish an independent, cross-party Health & Care Consensus Commission tasked with creating a 10–15-year legislative plan for NHS and social care reform (including funding, workforce, system design, digital infrastructure and reform), to end repeated cycles of disruption.
additional_details: We believe the NHS and social care are trapped in a cycle of short-term reforms that change with every government. This can create instability, wasted resources, and poor outcomes for patients and staff. We feel that other countries, like Ireland and Denmark, have successfully used cross-party plans to achieve long-term improvement. We believe we need the same stability, to rebuild public and staff trust, and that without political cross-party consensus, all improvement and transformation attempts will fail.

action: Make Party Manifesto Commitments Legally Binding or Trigger a Public Vote
background: Require the Government to adhere to the key promises it was elected on. If a governing party significantly breaks commitments in its manifesto, this should be treated as a breach of contract with the electorate, triggering either a public vote on the changed policies or an automatic General Election
additional_details: The public vote in a General Election based on the manifesto commitments presented by political parties. These manifestos function as a form of contract: voters choose a government based on the promises made. When major manifesto pledges are abandoned, reversed, or significantly altered, the democratic mandate is undermined. This petition asks Parliament to create a legal or constitutional mechanism to ensure future Governments cannot obtain power and change promises voter approval.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Call a general election if a government breaks an election manifesto promise
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744946

action: Introduce 5yr Minimum Sentence for unlawfully carrying a Knife 3yrs Juveniles
background: We've a knife crime epidemic with too many people carrying knives in public; As a serving police officer I tackled many offenders carrying a knife & once almost lost my life when stabbed in chest arresting a burglar; too many parents are planning funerals instead of bright futures for their children
additional_details: We want the GOVT to introduce minimum sentences in order to act as a deterrent for carrying knives & blades in public; Knife homicides far outnumber gun homicides; yet carry a gun there is a 5 year Minimum sentence but carrying a Knife its often a community sentence. We believe communities live in fear of Knife crime & it has become a scourge on society and needs to be dealt with as a serious Health issue and a National Emergency as it is affecting the fabric of society & too often involving children.
government_response_summary: The Government is not planning to introduce minimum sentences for carrying a knife. The law already provides for minimum custodial sentences for repeat knife possession and threatening with a weapon.
government_response_body: Knife crime has destroyed far too many lives. That is why, as part of the Safer Streets mission, this Government is working to halve knife crime within a decade. We have a comprehensive, data-led and Government-wide approach to this goal.  The Government is not planning to introduce minimum sentences of 5 years for adults and 3 years for young people aged under 18, for carrying a knife.   Minimum sentences are rare in England and Wales. It is the function of the court to decide the sentence in each case subject to the maximum that Parliament has provided, and any relevant sentencing guidelines published by the Sentencing Council. Sentencing must also be proportionate to the offence committed, taking into account all the circumstances of each case.   The maximum penalty for carrying a knife is 4 years imprisonment. In recognition of the seriousness of offences related to knives, the law already provides for minimum custodial sentences for repeat knife possession and offences that involve threatening with a weapon. Adults face a minimum of 6 months imprisonment whilst young people aged 16 or 17 face a four-month Detention and Training Order.  Where someone is actually harmed by a knife or offensive weapon, there are a range of offences that they may be charged with, such as causing grievous bodily harm. These can result in lengthy sentences, up to life imprisonment. Murder is a very serious crime which carries a mandatory life sentence. This is the same for any murder, including those involving knives or guns.   In recognition of the importance of tackling knife crime, the Government’s manifesto committed to ensuring that every young person caught in possession of a knife would be referred to a Youth Justice Service and receive a mandatory plan to prevent reoffending. We are taking a significant step towards delivering this manifesto commitment and will shortly be publishing tough new guidance that sets out our expectations on how the police and Youth Justice Services should respond to knife possession offences committed by children.  On 24 September 2024, we implemented a ban on zombie-style knives and zombie-style machetes, and it is now illegal to sell, manufacture or possess these weapons. We also introduced new legislation to ban ninja swords, and since 1 August 2025, it has been illegal to sell or own these weapons.  In October 2024, the then Home Secretary commissioned Commander Stephen Clayman, the National Police Chiefs’ Council lead for knife crime, to conduct a review into the online sale and delivery of knives. The Independent End-To-End Review of Online Knife Sales was published on 19 February 2025. We are taking forward the most pressing recommendations and have announced “Ronan’s Law,” a range of measures which will include stricter rules for online sellers of knives. These include strengthening age verification controls and checks through a two-stage age verification system at the point of purchase and on delivery.   With measures in the Crime and Policing Bill, currently going through Parliament,  we are increasing the penalties for illegal sales of knives, creating a new offence of possessing a knife with the intention to commit unlawful violence, creating a duty on sellers to report bulk sales, and giving the police new power to seize knives when they believe they are likely to be used in connection with unlawful violence.  In February 2025, the Government committed to consult on plans to introduce a comprehensive licensing scheme for those who sell knives or other bladed articles, including importers, retailers and private sellers, making them subject to strict regulations and conditions. A public consultation was launched on 16 December 2025 to gather views on these proposals and consider impacts before making any legislative changes that would be required to introduce such licensing. The consultation is open until 24 February 2026 at: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/licensing-for-knife-sales  We have also introduced new legislation to provide the police with the power to require social media, marketplace, and search services to take down illegal knife and offensive weapon content. Failure to remove this material could result in significant penalties for both the company and a designated senior executive. This meets the Government’s manifesto commitment to hold the senior executives of online companies accountable for flouting rules around online knife sales.  Ministry of Justice

action: Update building regulations to require more women’s toilets in public buildings.

action: ​Mandate stricter childcare staff ratios: In-room presence & 2:1 qualified staff

additional_details:

​Staff-in-Ratio Must Be In-Room Practitioners: The staff-to-child ratio must strictly include only those practitioners physically present and actively supervising children in the specific room. Close loopholes allowing non-direct care staff (admin, management) to be counted.
​Minimum Qualification Ratio (2:1): Mandate a minimum of two qualified staff (Level 2+) for every one unqualified member in the statutory ratio. This guarantees consistent expertise and leadership, preventing burnout and ensuring the safe, high-quality care children deserve.

action: Allow child maintenance payslip deductions without notifying the paying parent

action: DEFRA Pursue UK Wide Monitoring & Publication of Farmed Salmon Safety & Welfare

additional_details:

action: Recognise garlic and onion allergies within UK food allergen regulations

additional_details: Garlic and onion allergies are common, yet they're not legally recognised. These ingredients are often invisible in meals, so people can’t detect them when food is served. action: Change Universal Credit so second parent earnings don't affect family’s payment

We believe the elimination of borders and territorial integration of the two regions will restore Tajik control and authority, improve human rights and inform future UK diplomatic and development policy.

action: Introduce a Kannada language GCSE

additional_details: Kannada is the administrative language of Karnataka, a southern state in India with population of approximately 70 million. It has rich tradition and history.
