background: I would like the Government to ensure that individuals seeking further education as an apprentice (e.g getting a level 3 qualification in childcare) can have a wage that is more appropriate for an their circumstances, as opposed to a single flat minimum wage for all apprentices.
additional_details: I am 19 years old. My parents are unfortunately dead, I am fairly estranged from my family. And so I have to pay rent. Some of my apprentice colleagues are on the same wage living with parents and do not have to pay a penny toward their living expenses, whilst I am left with almost no money every month.  I believe that it would be beneficial to apprentices with limited family support and higher living expenses many people living in circumstances such as this, and worse, to have a slightly higher hourly wage.

action: Limit council tax increases to the lowest of either inflation or 5%
background: Limit council tax increases to the lowest of either inflation or 5%
additional_details: How on earth the government can allow councils to take an extra 4.99% every year without fail when inflation is 3.6% meaning the majority are of the public are getting around the inflationary level yet the council keep taking more !

action: Repeal Section 127 of the Communications Act 2003
background: Repeal Section 127(1)(a) of the Communications Act 2003, which criminalises “grossly offensive” online communications. Replace it with clearer, narrowly defined legislation that seeks to protect the public from genuine harm while safeguarding freedom of expression.
additional_details: We believe the term “grossly offensive” is vague and subjective, giving the state excessive power to criminalise speech that is merely unpopular or provocative. This can undermine free expression, chill public debate, and can lead to inconsistent prosecutions. Harmful threats and harassment are already covered by more precise laws. Repealing and replacing this wording would, we believe, restore proper limits on state power while maintaining protections against genuine abuse.

action: Department for Transport to reconsider their rebrand of ‘Great British Railways’
background: Department for Transport have developed a new brand for the launch of Great British Railways which should be reconsidered to ensure it is fit for a long term future.
additional_details: This branding will represent the UK’s rail sector across multiple platforms and be the face that passengers see. It should be timeless and well considered to ensure it respects the heritage of our railways and leads us into the future. British Rail created the iconic Double Arrows in 1965 which has served as the de-facto identifier of the railway for 60 yrs. The proposed branding does not carry the same weight, and is weak on a world stage where Britain has continually set the standard for rail.
rejection_details: We are not sure what you mean by 'reconsider the rebrand'. You could start a petition to cancel the rebrand if that's something you would like to happen.

action: Consider implementations to law regarding adult bullying and harassment .
background:
Formally recognise the inappropriate use of cc’ing within work communications as coercive bullying and harassment. 

To create grounds to call out this behaviour and act with the support of clear legislation and guidance that will be written into policy for adult anti-bullying in the workplace.
additional_details:
Currently, the requirement for anti bullying and appropriate online communications is significantly under regulated, allowing margin for error and subjectivity. 
There is a need for a national response and a call to action against this behaviour which can, and does, affect many people within workplaces. Tighter restrictions with pathways to formal protections are required to reduce the misuse of this practice and to assert formalised ethical boundaries for online communication practices.
rejection_details:
A petition needs to be clear about what it asking of Government or of the House of Commons. Harassment and bullying, including when conducted by inappropriate cc'ing of people into emails, is already covered by legislation and guidance respectively. 

In that context it's not clear what else you are looking for the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Bobbles’ Law - legal requirement to stop & report all road collisions with cats
background: Cats are beloved family members, yet the law does not protect them as it does dogs. When a cat is hit by a car the impact on families is profound and immeasurable. However, drivers are currently not required to stop, seek help and report it. This silent gap in the law must change.
additional_details:
We propose updating Section 170 of the Road Traffic Act 1988, to make it a legal requirement for drivers to stop and report collisions with cats.

This urgent change to the law is required so that when a cat is hit by a car: Owners can be notified and seek immediate veterinary help; Cats have a greater chance of survival if treated promptly; Ensures driver vigilance and accountability

We feel it is time that the law reflected the value and vulnerability of all companion animals equally.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750612

action: Make abuse of school staff a specific offence
background: Make abuse of school staff by parents or adults a specific criminal offence. Adults banned from school sites for abusive conduct should face proportionate consequences, including review of government support.
additional_details: School staff deserve a safe workplace free from abuse. Aggression from parents or adults undermines wellbeing, disrupts learning, and sets a damaging example for children. Current measures do not deter such behaviour. Stronger legal powers and proportionate consequences will protect staff, uphold respect for education, and ensure schools remain secure environments where teachers can focus on supporting pupils.

action: Declare a national emergency over small boat Channel crossings.
background: We call on the UK Government to formally declare a national emergency in response to ongoing small boat crossings of the English Channel and to introduce stronger, lawful border control measures.
additional_details:
The rise in small boat crossings poses serious risks to public safety, border security and national capacity. Documented cases show individuals arriving via illegal routes being charged with serious crimes, including sexual offences against minors.

We urge the Government to declare a national emergency and introduce stronger lawful border measures, faster asylum processing and increased international cooperation, while upholding UK and international law.
rejection_details: It is not clear what you mean in regards to declaring a national emergency and what sort of impact you would like this to have.

action: Classify English Rail Projects as England-Only, Not England & Wales
background: We call on the Government to reclassify rail projects that are entirely in England as England-only, not “England & Wales”. This must apply retrospectively, including to HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, and all future projects so that Wales receives the proper Barnett funding it is entitled to.
additional_details: Wales currently receives no extra rail funding when the UK invests billions in England-only schemes like HS2 and Liverpool-Hull. We think Wales gains no benefit yet loses out on billions that could improve our railways, and that the UK Government must stop exploiting this loophole and give Wales the fair share it is owed.

action: Equal Definitions for All Faith Prejudices, Not Only Islamophobia
background: We ask Parliament to create official, equal definitions for prejudice against all faiths, not only Islamophobia, so Christians, Jews, Sikhs, Hindus, and others are equally protected under law and public policy.
additional_details: Only Islamophobia has an official definition, leaving other faiths unprotected. This creates bias, weakens equality, and risks inconsistent safeguarding. Parliament should establish definitions for all faith prejudices with the same strength as Islamophobia, ensuring fair treatment, legal clarity, accountability, and equal protection.
rejection_details: Under the Equality Act 2010, all religions including Christianity, Judaism, Sikhism, Hinduism, Islam, and others are protected equally as “religion or belief.”

action: Require vets to provide free lifesaving care for pets
background: If the pet is in desperate need of care, and the pet's life is on the line, the vets should have to give the animal free medical care, so the pet does not die.
additional_details: So the animals do not lose their life if the owner cannot afford the vet fees. The pets should not be able to make an animal lose its life if the owner cannot pay.

action: we should ban detention after school  especially in the winter
background: in winter it will be really dark and kids might get scared,they might be kidnapped /robbed.instead i think detentions should be happening in launch time or break time because in winter if kids are late parents get worried as well
additional_details: i think we should ban detentions everywhere after school in winter because of how dangerous it is for example my friend tanisha  was really scared to go home after detention.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban schools from giving after-school detentions
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734838

action: Create a UK Rights Charter to replace the EU Charter
background: Create a single, modern UK Rights Charter to replace the protections lost after leaving the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. Rights are currently scattered across different laws, and a unified charter would clearly set out the protections people can rely on today.
additional_details: After Brexit, no equivalent charter was created to replace the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. Modern protections were not brought together into a single, clear framework, leaving rights scattered across separate laws and creating uncertainty for citizens, workers, students, and researchers. A unified UK Rights Charter would provide clarity, accountability, and confidence in the protections people can rely on in the 21st century.

action: Windfall tax individuals and companies that profiteered from the Covid crisis.
background: We the undersigned call on the UK government to use every means necessary to recover taxpayers money lost through fraud and excessive profiteering during the Covid pandemic through the courts, wherever possible, but also by the introduction of a windfall tax on individuals and companies responsible.
additional_details: When people on very low incomes are persecuted and prosecuted for minor benefit infringements vast sums are deemed irrecoverable. This is unacceptable and government have a moral duty to recover our monies lost through individual or corporate greed and fraud at a time of national crisis. These spivs are no better than those that undermined our nation during WWII and must be held to account by being fined, taxed, named and shamed whoever they might be.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

You can find out what the Government is already doing to recover money lost through Covid fraud here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/covid-fraud-cost-uk-taxpayer-109-billion-reveals-independent-report

action: Stop the closure of Derby DrivAbility on 31/03/2026.
background:
This must be debated in Parliament.
It is fundamental to road safety to ensure that all road users are safe to drive following a DVLA notifiable condition. 
Government must maintain this service either by finding a new provider or supporting the UHDB NHS Trust to make a U-turn on their decision.
additional_details: We assess fitness to drive following medical investigations/diagnosis to determine whether a medical condition is affecting road safety. This closure will result in many clients/patients not being able to access the support they need, losing their freedom and independence, and negatively affecting their mental health and well-being.  It will also result in people continuing to drive that should have surrendered their license, impacting on their own safety and a danger to other road users.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Require health professionals to always inform partners of HIV diagnoses
background: I want the government to create a law to ensure partners of those with HIV are safely informed regardless of patient consent. I believe this would prevent HIV being used as a weapon and stop the spreading of HIV ensuring healthcare professionals manage cases with accountability and care.
additional_details: This law would close existing gaps by ensuring partners are always informed safely of HIV diagnoses, and healthcare professionals guide treatment to prevent harm to the public. This could be called Toni’s Law. No one should face a shock diagnosis or unknown risk of HIV alone; clear rules, trust and stronger prevention.

action: NHS to Prioritise HGV drivers who diagnose with sleep apnoea
background: I want the government order NHS and DVLA  to give priority for driver's who suffer from sleep apnoea
additional_details: HGV driver's job is dangerous and DVLA revoked licence. So we need a system to allow us to get treatment sooner than expected.
rejection_details: This is very much a clinical/operational decision - and there already exists advice within the NHS and DVLA about how to prioritise medical care for people with OSAS.

action: Make it illegal for DVLA to share vehicle keeper data with private companies
background: Make it illegal for the DVLA to share driver and keeper data with private companies. Drivers should not have their personal information released without consent, especially for use by private parking firms. DVLA data should only be provided to public authorities.
additional_details: The Government should stop the DVLA from releasing driver and keeper data to private companies because we feel motorists have no control or consent over how their personal information is used. Private parking firms rely on this data to issue charges we think are unfair and excessive. A public authority should protect personal data, not share it. Only official bodies such as police or councils should have access for legitimate legal reasons.

action: Make Medicine Prescriptions Free for Asthma Pump Users
background:
This petition is very simply calling for the UK Government to give all people with Asthma an exemption from paying the prescription fee.
More than three-quarters of people with asthma who pay for their prescriptions said they struggle to afford them, according to a recent report by Asthma UK
additional_details: The shocking reality is that an asthmatic may well reduce their use of the pump which could lead to devastating consequences. It is time the Government acted on this. Please sign and share this petition

action: Ban commercial dog breeding while rescues are over capacity
background: Introduce a temporary ban on commercial dog breeding while shelters remain overcrowded. Support adoption and fostering, and protect essential service-dog programmes, including assessing suitable rescue dogs for training where possible.
additional_details: Rescue centres are overwhelmed, with thousands of healthy dogs waiting months or years for homes, while profit-driven breeding continues to increase supply. This causes avoidable suffering and abandonment. Pausing commercial breeding could reduce pressure on shelters, improve animal welfare, and refocus efforts on rehoming dogs already in need.

action: Introduce a national information campaign informing expectant mothers about CMV
background: We want the Government to introduce a nationwide public information campaign to ensure all expectant mothers are informed about congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV), including how it is transmitted, how to reduce risk, and what support is available after diagnosis.
additional_details: Congenital CMV is a leading cause of childhood disability, yet most expectant mothers aren’t told about it. Simple hygiene steps can greatly reduce risk, but low awareness leads to preventable infections and missed diagnoses. We want the Government to launch a national information campaign to ensure all pregnant women receive clear guidance on CMV, its risks, and how to protect their babies by risk reduction.

action: Make it illegal to wear a face covering in public.
background: Gangs of youths are using face coverings to hide their identities and evade police and CCTV. Big groups of them at night time on bikes and e-scooters and are very intimidating. Face coverings that aren't being used for religious or medical purposes should be banned in public spaces.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make face coverings illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749103

action: Require all AI musicians and songs to have a visible AI notice
background: Petition to require all AI musicians, bands and songs to have a visible notice alerting the user to the fact it's AI created. Seeing AI music shooting past actual musicians in terms of streams is rather insulting.
additional_details: It's affecting the music industry and artists/musicians livelihoods and mental health when a computer is literally taking their job.

action: Ban airlines setting cabin bag size limits below overhead locker capacity
background: Create legislation preventing airlines from setting cabin bag size limits smaller than the overhead locker capacity of the aircraft. Bag dimensions should match what the plane can hold, stopping what we feel are artificially small limits used to generate extra fees.
additional_details: Airlines are increasingly restricting cabin bag sizes below what overhead lockers can hold, using rules we feel are unclear to charge passengers last minute. This drip pricing model can lead to stress, arguments at gates and confrontations between staff and travellers. In some cases staff appear incentivised to enforce charges, creating friction and damaging trust. A minimum size based on aircraft capacity would help reduce opportunistic fees, improve transparency and create a fairer experience.

action: Stop the government moving us closer to the EU without a general  election
background: We had a referendum on Brexit that wasn't fully implemented and now they want closer ties without the British people voting on this
additional_details: This is a very important topic that is going to effect everyone in this country and personally I think the public should have a say on  any of the decision made especially after we the voters were the one's who voted to leave .
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. It's unclear which policies in particular the public would be voting on.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Jury trials are so fundamental any change should require a referendum
background: The government should either drop any plans to limit trials by jury or should announce a referendum on the issue, allowing sufficient time beforehand for both sides to make their case to the public
additional_details:
The right to jury trial is rooted in Magna Carta of 1215; “No Freeman shall be .. imprisoned .. but by lawful judgment of his Peers“. Described as  “the greatest constitutional document of all times” jury trial rights globally stem from it.

‘Experts’ are wrong so often that justice is better served by individuals with common sense.

Justice is often neither ‘quick’ nor ‘cheap’, but this is no justification to alter an 800 year old fundamental right without public consent. Let the people decide.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Hold a referendum on planned changes to trial by jury
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/752114

action: Have Parliament support initiation of National Food Society modelled on RHS.
background: Facilitate public debate on the need for a large, well-funded, society for food enthusiasts of all ages, means, and gender, to share, learn about, and celebrate a love of food. Just as The Royal Horticultural Society exists to “involve, inspire, inform and improve” respecting those who love plants.
additional_details: Many people have told me this is a good idea, including members of the Guild of Food Writers. Whilst many charities exist to help with problems of nutrition and food poverty there is nothing which serves the needs of those who love food, cooking, and creativity but no longer have the opportunity to share and express that love. If there were a society such as I envisage it might alleviate problems of health, (both mental and physical), as well as mitigate social isolation and loneliness.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

You can find out how to set up a charity here: https://www.gov.uk/setting-up-charity

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue. You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

action: Fund more British Sign Language (BSL) interpreters in the emergency services
background: Fund more BSL interpreting services to ensure they continue throughout emergencies from start until finish. As it stands interpretation from BSL 999 ends when emergency services is dispatched, but there is often no interpreter during the emergency.
additional_details:
We want to ensure deaf people have equal access to emergency services without communication barriers and ensure the Equality Act 2010 and BSL Act 2022 are upheld.
 
Research has shown that many deaf people are dying young or have complex healthcare due to barriers. We want to prevent healthcare inequalities among the deaf community.

action: Review private parking regulation
background: Review and strengthen private parking regulation to stop unfair fines. Ban tickets for brief stops to read signs or turn safely. Require mandatory grace periods, automatic refunds for unfair charges, penalties and criminal liability for abusive parking companies so drivers are treated fairly.
additional_details: Drivers are being punished by confusing signage, tiny unreadable print and zero grace time. Some companies issue £100 fines within seconds even when drivers never leave their cars and stop only to understand the rules or escape safely. We think this system is unjust, predatory and damaging public trust. Urgent regulation is needed to protect motorists from abuse. These practices hit ordinary workers, families and vulnerable people the hardest and make driving stressful and unsafe.

action: Require prosecution of individuals who knowingly make false criminal allegations
background: We call on the UK Government to require police and CPS to prosecute individuals who intentionally make false allegations, including false claims of domestic abuse, rape, sexual assault. We ask for mandatory automatic referral to CPS, and penalties that reflect the seriousness of the harm caused.
additional_details:
False allegations destroy innocent lives. They create real victims — people who are investigated, judged, and sometimes lose their children, homes, employment, mental health and reputation, despite having done nothing wrong.
Knowingly making a false criminal allegation is not a minor mistake. It is a deliberate act that can devastate families, damage children, and consume huge amounts of police and social-care resources.  these cases are rarely investigated or prosecuted
rejection_details:
People can already by charged for perverting the cause of justice and wasting police time for making false allegations. We're therefore not exactly sure what further action you'd like to see. You can find out more here:

https://www.cps.gov.uk/legal-guidance/false-allegations-rape-andor-domestic-abuse-see-guidance-charging-perverting-course

action: All girls should be allowed to wear leggings instead of tights at school
background: Let girls be more comfortable in school uniform as tights may be uncomfortable for some students and teachers scold students for wearing leggings even though it does not effect our learning capability.
additional_details: Because girls need to be comfortable while in school to learn
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require schools prioritise comfort in uniforms & more personal choice for pupils
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751980

action: Amend VAT rates to Extend Zero Rating to include Educational Facilities
background: We call on the UK Government to amend VAT legislation so that construction, conversion, and major refurbishment work for educational facilities can qualify for zero rating when undertaken by or for Schools, Academy Trusts, Local Authorities, and Registered Educational Charities.
additional_details:
Specifically we ask for: 
Conversions of unused or non educational buildings into educational facilities to qualify for zero rating, supported by certification analogous to existing certification rules for “relevant charitable purpose” and other zero rated provisions. Alongside this allowing for remodelling, new build or major alterations whereby a net educational increase is seen should receive relief and not pay standard-rated at 20% VAT, aiding the spending within the public and private education sector.

action: Remove all social media and messaging platforms for under fifteens
background: I would like all platforms of social media to be banned to anyone under fifteen years of age
additional_details:
I feel that children are being brainwashed and not living in reality. Also screen time is not going to help the NHS with regards to bad eyesight.
They are also being withdrawn where normal day to day life is not being processed.
physical and mental health, causing digital eye strain, headaches, poor posture (tech neck), sleep disruption (due to blue light), obesity, and increased risks of anxiety, depression, and developmental issues in children by reducing real-world interaction, impacting brain structure, and interfering with social-emotional
This will put a unbearable strain on the NHS within the next ten years, in which they are already at breaking point
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban social media for under-16s to protect children
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/710283

action: Review traffic enforcement policies & mandate bolder signage & advance warnings
background: To protect vulnerable motorists the Government should require councils to consider hardship and mental health in traffic enforcement action. It should review current enforcement policies to ensure they are proportionate, humane, and safe.
additional_details:
I also want to ensure there is bolder signage & advance warnings for restricted roads. 
 
This petition seeks fairness, compassion, and a system that supports, not punishes ordinary people making honest mistakes. The pressure on low income families is immense, and we feel the impact emotionally and mentally can be disproportionate and inhumane.
 
Please support this petition so that no one else suffers financial hardship, emotional distress, or threat to their wellbeing because of PCN enforcement.

action: Increase the personal tax allowance for single adult households to £15,000
background: Revise the tax free allowance for single adult households increasing from £12,570 to £15,000.
additional_details: We believe by increasing the tax free allowance for single adult households will improve the living conditions for those living alone or raising a family alone. There is a rise in single households and with the increase in cost of living these individuals are unable to access other benefits as they are not considered a low earner however they are often living pay check to pay check which may impact mental health adding to the loneliness epidemic as they cant afford a coffee with friends or a day out.

action: Provide funding to dig out and clean all rivers
background: Provide funding for relevant bodies to dig out and clean all our rivers to make them deeper and cleaner allowing water to flow and rivers to to have greater capacity which may in turn reduce flooding of farmland and housing areas
additional_details: This should be government funded and should be done asap

action: Change the law that allows smaller supermarkets to charge more than larger ones
background: Change the law that allows smaller supermarkets to charge more than larger ones for the same items. This should not be allowed. Especially as there is less variety and stock available. The uplift in price is not justified. Stopping this will give all families access to cheaper and healthier food.
additional_details: Change the law that allows smaller supermarkets to charge more than larger ones for the same items. This should not be allowed. Especially as there is less variety and stock available. The uplift in price is not justified. Stopping this will give all families access to cheaper and healthier food. Everyone should have access to the same options. In the cost of living crisis this would go along way to supporting those in need. It would also save on fuel as people won’t need to travel to big stores
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We are unclear of the details of what you are asking for: whether you want a single price for a product across all shops, or whether you want to require companies to charge the same price for a product in all the shops they own regardless of their size (which could be different to other companies).

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Improve resilience and safety of the M4 PoW Bridge and the M48 Severn Bridge
background: Conduct a full review of the 9 December 2025 disruption, upgrade safety-critical infrastructure on both Severn bridges, strengthen wind-resilience, improve public communication, and publish a long-term strategy ensuring at least one crossing remains reliably open.
additional_details: The simultaneous M4 and M48 closures exposed a major weakness in cross-Severn travel. These bridges are vital, and full shutdowns disrupt commuters, businesses and emergency services. We need an independent review to improve maintenance, weather-closure protocols, contingency planning, and to invest in reliable alternative routes. Stronger infrastructure and clearer communication are essential to prevent future total closures and protect the region’s connectivity.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Require 1st and 2nd class postage to be combined and delivered 6 days per week
background: Require Royal Mail to combine 1st and 2nd class postage. We feel it's chaos now and there's hardly any difference in delivery times. Anyone wanting guaranteed next day delivery could use special delivery. This may enable them to deliver 6 days a week again, every week.
additional_details: We believe our postal service used to be the envy of the world. It should be improving not self destructing. The price of stamps has shot up and the delivery service seems to be dependent on which way the wind is blowing. Even knowing which days to expect a delivery seems to be impossible. We think it's time to combine the outdated system of 1st and 2nd class post and deliver 6 days a week again, every week!

action: Strengthen self-defence rights for adults who intervene to protect children
background: We call on the Government to amend self-defence law to give explicit statutory protection to any adult who reasonably and proportionately intervenes to protect a child from immediate assault, sexual assault, or grooming.
additional_details:
We would like:
- Rebuttable presumption that force used to defend a child was reasonable.
- Immunity from “excessive force” charges when honestly believing a child was in imminent danger and acting in good faith.
 
We believe that too many hesitate, fearing arrest. We think this could remove that fear and encourage intervention, while keeping force proportionate.

action: Lower the driving age to 16
background: Lower the driving age to 16 to allow people to drive to school, college, or work.
additional_details: It will allow students to drive to school, college, or work that they otherwise wouldn’t be able to do. This will therefore give them more opportunities.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Reduce age limit for holding a full driving licence to 16 with restrictions
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733742

action: Stop the Government restricting the right to a trial by jury
background: The public trust juries. We support leading legal experts – the Bar Council, Criminal Bar Association, JUSTICE, lawyers, retired judges, and politicians of all parties – in opposing Government plans to remove the right to elect for jury trial for 'either-way offences' with sentences up to 3 years.
additional_details: Justice needs juries. Curtailing jury trials in England and Wales will erode a deeply entrenched constitutional principle and risks undermining confidence in our criminal justice system. No concrete evidence has been made public that shows the difference this will make, and crucially this will not impact the current Crown Court backlog.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Fund local community litter crews and fund education around littering
background: Create and fund local “Litter Crews” in every community to help reduce litter, improve public spaces, and run education programmes that encourage people not to litter.
additional_details:
Litter is a growing problem in towns and cities. We feel that councils often don’t have enough resources to keep public spaces clean, and existing fines are not changing behaviour.
 
Government-funded Litter Crews could:
• Keep streets, parks and public areas clean
• Work with schools and community groups on anti-litter education
• Encourage pride in local areas
• Reduce long-term clean-up costs by changing behaviour
 
This could create cleaner, safer, and more welcoming communities for everyone.

action: Allow Conjugal visit in Northern Ireland
background: We want the government and parliament to recognize the importance of preserving family bonds and to implement legislation that grants eligible incarcerated individuals the right to conjugal visits in a safe and regulated manner.
additional_details: I want the government to allow conjugal visits because they help inmates keep family bonds, support mental well-being, encourage good behavior, and improve rehabilitation. Strong relationships reduce stress, strengthen stability after release, and lower reoffending. This respects dignity, creates safer prisons, and supports reintegration and stronger communities.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Northern Ireland Executive and Northern Ireland Assembly is responsible for. 

If you want to raise this issue you could contact your MLA, or raise it with the Northern Ireland Executive.

You can find contact details for your MLAs here: http://www.niassembly.gov.uk/your-mlas/

You can find contact details for the departments of the Northern Ireland Executive here: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/government-departments-in-northern-ireland

action: Review family planning support for parents who lose custody
background: Review support and intervention for parents who continue having children after losing custody. Strengthen safe-parenting programs, accountability, and access to voluntary or mandatory family-planning resources until they can provide a stable, safe home for the children they already have.
additional_details: I have worked in a children’s residential home for seven years and have seen a growing concern: many parents continue having children they cannot care for, causing significant emotional harm. Frequent placement moves lead to instability and educational difficulties. With the number of children in care rising, we need stronger measures that address root causes and provide better support for families.

action: introduce mandatory electrician licensing restrict sale of electrical materials
background: Introduce a national licensing system for electricians, require retailers to verify competency before selling key electrical materials, and strengthen enforcement of electrical safety regulations such as Part P.
additional_details:
Electrical work in UK homes can currently be carried out by anyone, regardless of qualifications. Untrained individuals, handymen and kitchen fitters are able to buy electrical materials freely and perform electrical installations with no formal training, assessment or accountability.

Qualified electricians must complete years of training, hold the 18th Edition wiring regulations, maintain insurance, and undergo regular Competent Person Scheme assessments (NAPIT, NICEIC,
rejection_details: Electric installation licence system & ban sale of materials to the unlicensed: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/728785

action: Vote for No digital ID to be implemented
background: On the 8th of December it was debated about digital ID. But it was not taken to a vote. All that happened was parliament discussing it and then continuing to move forward with their original plans. This solves nothing.
additional_details: I want the government not to implement any new sort of digital ID, it is invasive and ridiculous and without the consent of the public. There cannot be one rule for one person and another for everybody else. People will not follow along with the ridiculous notion that it is needed and will result in a revolt.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may also wish to sign the following petitions that call for similar actions:

Repeal the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 in full and stop Digital ID rollouts 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743698

Hold a referendum on introducing mandatory identity cards in the UK 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734246

action: Retain 5-year ILR Pathway for LGBTIQ+ Refugees in the UK
background: The Government’s new asylum policy proposes replacing the current five-year refugee leave with temporary 30-month grants and delaying eligibility for settlement to 20 years for those on the new core protection route. We believe these changes will disproportionately impact LGBTIQ+ refugees negatively
additional_details: The five-year ILR route lets refugees rebuild their lives, integrate and access stability. Replacing it with 30-month renewals for up to 20 years creates harmful insecurity, especially for LGBTIQ+ refugees who face heightened risks of homelessness, exploitation and discrimination. The proposed system adds bureaucracy, worsens backlogs and undermines effective protection and international humanitarian standards.

action: Change the Census Act to mandate a census every 5 years
background: Censuses have been held every 10 years since 1801, with the Census Act (1920) allowing governments to hold a census every 5 years, but placing no obligation to ever hold a census. The Act should be amended to place an obligation on the UK and devolved governments to hold a full census every 5 years.
additional_details:
We think the current practice and law is outdated. Since 1801 technological advancements have allowed data to be collected and analysed quickly with relatively minimal human intervention.
 
At the same time as these advancements, the pace of change in the country's demographics have accelerated, with immigration currently at record levels.
 
We believe it is therefore vital that we use the technology at our disposal to ensure we have the most up to date data regarding the demographic make up of our country.

action: Ban supermarkets from throwing away or destroying unsold safe food
background: Supermarkets should be made to either significantly reduce the price so food gets sold before closing time, or donate it to charities and food banks. They should be banned from throwing food into waste if there are other options, if the food is safe and hygienic under FSA guidance.
additional_details: This could reduce food waste, help families who are struggling and make supermarkets plan better to reduce overall food waste.

action: Ban private car parking companies
background: I want the government to ban private parking companies. They make thousands of pounds from parking fines. I believe many who are served fines are hard-working people either enjoying a weekend with family, or meeting friends to socialise in public places.
additional_details: I want people to enjoy their time away from work without the pressure of receiving a car parking fine. A fine of £100 for example, is a lot of money. That is nearly a weekly food shop for my family of three.

action: Require transparency on aircraft emissions and atmospheric activity over the UK
background: I want the Government to publish full details of all aircraft emissions and any authorised atmospheric activity in UK airspace. This should include independent monitoring, public reporting, and clear disclosure of any operations that may affect air quality or the environment.
additional_details: People in the UK are increasingly concerned about what is being released into the atmosphere and how it may affect public health and the environment. There is currently no clear transparency framework. Requiring disclosure and independent monitoring would build trust, protect public health, and ensure all activities in our skies are subject to proper oversight.
rejection_details:
Aircraft operators fall under the UK Emissions Trading scheme which means they  report on their annual emissions.

More information is available here: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6889f51c76f68cc8414d5b67/ukets01-mrr-general-guidance-for-installations.pdf

action: Hold a Government Inquiry into the poor standards of delivery companies.
background: Parcel theft has increased to an estimated £666.5m last year. Parcels are no longer left in designated spaces or with neighbours. Drivers themselves are routineley caught stealing. The government must hold an inquiry into the standards of delivery services to ensure improvements are made.
additional_details: Delivery companies failure to pay a suitable wage and their use of contracting employees has resulted in over worked drivers offering the lowest of quality of delivery services. This includes parcel theft, signature forgery, cases of public urination and other unnacceptable behaviours. Noticeable decline has occured since Covid, whereby parcels are no longer left in safe designated spaces, drivers are not attempting to deliver to neighbours, and forging signatures to leave parcels unnatended.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Review how delivery companies operate and standards
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735425

action: Demand Professional Standards in Parliament
background:
We, the undersigned, demand that MPs uphold workplace standards of professionalism.

In 2025, it is unacceptable for elected representatives to heckle, jeer, shout “Shame!” or wave papers like pantomime performers. In any other workplace, this behaviour would go to HR.
additional_details:
Such conduct undermines trust, trivialises debate, and turns Parliament into a circus instead of the heart of democracy. We call for reforms to enforce respect, civility, and serious discussion in the Commons.

Politics is not theatre. It is governance. MPs must stop the performance and do the job we elected them to do.
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker personally.

action: Ban the use of solid fuel/ wood burning stoves in residential areas
background: The UK ranks 101 out of 131 countries in terms of poor air quality (ranked from worst to best) according to the latest World Air Quality report in 2022. Domestic wood-burning is the biggest source of fine particle air pollution in the UK, contributing significantly to overall pollution.
additional_details: Wood burning in UK homes can harm public health and has been linked to 2,500 deaths a year in the UK. Recent research highlighting domestic fires as a major source of toxic fine particle pollution (PM2.5) has also estimated that treating health impacts linked to this pollution (like asthma, COPD, pneumonia, and cardiovascular events) costs the NHS about £54 million per year. Wood burning is therefore linked to thousands of new serious illnesses yearly, with most wood burning considered unnecessary.

action: Make life sentences mean life .
background: DNA evidence is so strong these days, that anyone proved beyond doubt of murder . Should get a full life sentence. Why should they only get 25yrs for taking someone's life??.
additional_details: Parliament should make it a life sentence mean life. If a teenager commits murder , they can be out on the streets before the age of 50 . This is so wrong. Just think if someone killed someone you know, they should never walk the streets again.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Replace life sentences with whole life terms for the most serious offenders
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732705

action: Ban the Burka
background: Ban the  Burka
additional_details: Because if I go into a shop bank football match ect I have to show my face I can't even wear a hood
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make face coverings illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749103

action: A long overdue rework to the British school system.
background: Rework how the school system works to accommodate the fact that many students learn differently. Right now the system can have a severe impact on mental health ( Standardized testing contributes a lot) and doesn’t even teach students relevant skills such as financial knowledge.
additional_details: Our world is changing faster than ever, yet schools are still teaching outdated material. Students need more than facts—they need skills like critical thinking, problem-solving, digital literacy, and adaptability to thrive in the future. If education doesn’t evolve, students will be unprepared for the challenges of tomorrow. It’s time to modernize the curriculum and equip young people with the tools they need to succeed in a rapidly developing world.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you would like a rework to the school system, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You may wish to sign the following:

Add critical thinking to the national curriculum
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741973

Add Economics & Business to national curriculum (for entrepreneurial skills)
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737807

Introduce mandatory business and entrepreneurship in secondary curriculum
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741347

action: Create one-off amnesty with extra tax obligation for undocumented people
background: Introduce a one-off amnesty for undocumented people currently living in the UK without a legal right to remain, granting them legal status to work. As part of this process those who are given the right to remain in the UK could pay a temporary additional tax to support the economy & public services
additional_details: We believe that a scheme like this, combined with a temporary extra tax contribution, would bring people into the formal workforce, increase revenue for the Treasury, reduce exploitation, and promote community safety. In our view, countries that have introduced similar schemes have seen economic and social benefits and we believe this would create a fair, practical, and compassionate solution for the UK.

action: Do not abolish the long residence (10-year) route to settlement
background: Please reconsider the total abolishment of the 10-year long residence route to settlement for individuals who have been legally living and working in the UK for a significant amount of time.
additional_details: I seek empathy and compassion from the Government/Parliament - to reconsider the abolishment of the long residence route to settlement for individuals who have been legally living and working in the UK for a significant amount of time (over 5 years/close to completing the 10-year qualifying period). Please consider the repercussions for individuals who are law-abiding, well educated, and have been contributing to the UK economy, whilst accruing time towards the long residence route. Thank you.
rejection_details:
We think this petition is very similar to yours: 

Do not apply new ILR rules to those who arrived before 2021 on a 10 year route: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751924

action: Make at least half of knighthoods about genuine acts of heroism.
background: Please discuss making knighthoods about what you actually picture a knight doing. It makes sense to recognise true courage in the face of real physical danger.
additional_details: A lot of modern day knighthoods are largely about political contributions which are often controversial. I personally envision a true heroic act being recognised as far less controversial and more deserving too.

action: Make all British passport holders eligible for university home fee status
background: British passport holders in British curriculum schools abroad already align with UK education. Treating them as home students is fair. It boosts domestic recruitment, strengthens global influence and gives UK universities a powerful, values based pipeline they can control and grow.
additional_details: British passport holders in British curriculum schools abroad already align with UK education. Treating them as home students is fair and removes an arbitrary financial barrier. It strengthens domestic recruitment, builds a reliable global pipeline and deepens the UK’s soft power by supporting families and teachers who already champion British education worldwide.
rejection_details:
Give all British Citizens Overseas Access to Home Fees at English Universities
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732511

action: Introduce Unlimited Stay & Work transitional visa for Existing Skilled Workers
background: A transitional arrangement of unlimited COS free stay and work visa for existing skilled worker migrants affected under the upcoming earned settlement model is essential to ensure safety, fairness, and genuine worker protection.
additional_details: This approach is vital for preventing worker exploitation. Remaining tied to employer sponsorship for 10–15 years places skilled workers at serious risk as dependence on a single sponsor can lead to unfair treatment.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751532

action: Falklands. Prevent the UK Government selling weapons to Argentina
background: Currently UK export rules ban weapons with British parts from being sold to Argentina, in place since the Falkland's War. The UK Government is considering lifting this ban.
additional_details: We the undersigned state this ban must not be lifted or diluted in any way especially considering the Falkland's Sea Lion oil field is due to begin exporting oil from 2028. It is strategic suicide for the UK to sell and/or permit weapons with British components to Argentina (either directly or indirectly), in light of Argentina's continued wish to gain sovreignty of the Falklands even before viable oil fields were discovered, and now due to be exporting in the near future.
rejection_details: We are not clear about the action that you are seeking, as the Government has recently denied that it is planning to sell weapons to Argentina.

action: Ban all convicted child sex offenders from using social media
background: I would like the government to introduce a law that prevents all convicted child sex offenders from using social media. It’s been proved time and time again that social media is used by paedophiles to target and groom vulnerable children.
additional_details: We believe we are encouraging this behaviour by not taking action on putting into place strict laws that stop these predators from abusing our children.

action: Require family court to refer findings of abuse & coercive control to the police
background: When the family court makes findings of Emotional Abuse (EA) and/or Coercive Control (CC), but the findings not accepted by perpetrators, these cases should be automatically referred to the police for further investigation. This should not be incumbent upon the victims/survivors.
additional_details: EA & CC are crimes (Domestic Abuse & Serious Crime Acts) yet we believe the family court allows perpetrators to continue to abuse with impunity. In our view, all abuse features EA; 1 in 4 people aged 16 years and over have experienced domestic abuse, according to the ONS. We believe that this country is never going to reduce these devastating statistics without proper consequences for the worst perpetrators, such as perpetrator programmes and other effective interventions before criminal proceedings might follow.  Our children need protecting so the cycle of abuse can stop.

action: Making the death penalty illegal worldwide
background: We would like government to take the idea of the death penalty being illegal worldwide to the United Nations the be put to a vote. We would like them to advocate the idea.
additional_details: We want the government to help abolish the death penalty due to fact innocent lives have been lost and people who deserve to suffer in prison are avoiding this.
rejection_details: The UK Government do not have the power to make the death penalty illegal worldwide.

action: Stop mental health, ADHD & autism services review. Adopt report recommendations
background: Scrap the review into rising demand for Mental Health, ADHD & Autism services. Instead fund & implement the recommendations of the 'Time to Deliver' (Autism Act Committee) & ADHD Taskforce Part 2 reports. This would help end systemic failure, poor health outcomes, & inequality in Autism & ADHD care.
additional_details:
New reports detail systemic failure, unacceptable delays & poor health outcomes, while providing solutions for these failures.
 
We think this review will not fix the failings, and could cause harm to those waiting for care.
 
We demand the government scrap the review & fund the recommendations in these reports to provide adequate care & end long wait times.
 
- NHS England's Independent ADHD taskforce report Part 2 (Nov 2025)
- House of Lords Autism Act 2009 Committee report (Nov 2025).

action: Remove NPPF Paragraph 11(d) and Footnote 8 to Help Protect Green Spaces
background: Remove Paragraph 11(d) and Footnote 8 from the National Planning Policy Framework to help stop developments proceeding where they may be contrary to local plans. This would help restore a genuinely community-led planning system and strengthen protection for green spaces.
additional_details: These rules can make it harder for communities to protect green spaces, which are vital for food production, wellbeing and climate resilience. We think removing them will not harm housing delivery: there are a million empty homes, major brownfield capacity, and developers already hold many unbuilt permissions. The issue in our view is affordability, not land supply.

action: Include BSL as a GCSE language option
background: To discuss it and work with exam boards AQA and Pearson who have decided against a GCSE BSL. A person in England is more likely to meet a Deaf person than a person from a second language, French, Spanish etc. .
additional_details:
British Sign Language is an official language, recognised by the UK Government in 2003. It should be offered to those in Secondary schools as an option. 

Raise Deaf Awareness and carry on the work in the BSL Act 2022. Please don't make the mistake made at the Milan Conference in 1880 where Sign Language in schools was outlawed and banned. 

The government needs to include Deaf people in campaigning and manifestos, make them available in BSL
rejection_details:
Make sign language a compulsory subject in secondary schools across England
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749914

action: Apply to re-join the Customs Union
background: We believe that re-joining the Customs Union would bring down the brexit trade barriers with the EU and would significantly help boost our economy and relations with EU partners. So we are urging the government to step up and pass a bill to apply to re-join.
additional_details: After Brexit, trade with the EU fell sharply and impacted our economy negatively making people worse off by thousands. Some analysis estimates that 90 billion of our tax revenue is lost because of Brexit and businesses are feeling the toll of this trade failure too. This is why we believe removing trade barriers with the EU through the customs union will put money back into people’s pockets and put an end to this badly negotiated Brexit deal.

action: Do not remove trial by jury
background: The Justice Secretary announced that trial by jury would be scrapped for crimes with sentences less than 3 years. We want the government to not do this, since it is a threat to democracy and to human rights.
additional_details:
Removing trial by jury would threaten democracy if a government were to come into power that arrests people for simply disagreeing with them. Trial by jury protects the human right of right to a fair trial by introducing unbiased members of the public.

Additionally, the reason of the "backlog" can be solved by more funding to courts/judges, and should at least have an end date if that were the reason, which is not present in the reforms, which is especially dangerous for the reason above.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: speaker of the House of Commons get prime minister to answer questions properly
background: I want the prime minister to actually answer a question put to him instead of the waffle and avoidance. I find pmq’s are a waste of taxpayers money because the prime minister doesn’t provide accurate answers tax payers are entitled to know.
additional_details: To hold the government to account for its actions and decisions
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker, and Members are responsible for their answers to questions.

action: Hold convention for complete UK constitutional reform process after the next GE
background: Hold independent convention for complete UK constitutional reform process after the next GE, with parliament, meritocrats, civil servants, & political experts voicing opinion. With the  aim of centralisation of a new constitution, and addressing the continuity of the HoL, FPTP, and executive powers.
additional_details: Grievances with government run deep; it's not just one thing, it's many: Our government is archaic inefficient & slow, and cannot address crises facing our nation. Governments currently & previously have abused power and been corrupt. The electoral systems and representative bodies of our country do not reflect the will of the people to our satisfaction; they are too subject to populism; not enough, to meritocracy. Our politicians are undeserving, incapable, cold, cruel, out of touch, overpaid.
rejection_details: We are not clear what specific action you are seeking from the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Strengthen and Protect Petitions to Hold Government to Account
background: New legislation, protecting stronger petition powers constitutionally, so they gain real democratic force. We suggest petitions of 250k+ signatures should trigger mandatory scrutiny, and petitions with 1m+ signatures should lead to binding public action such as a referendum or equivalent mechanisms.
additional_details: Public trust is damaged when governments can ignore huge petitions and act without meaningful accountability between elections. Once elected, no government should be free to push through policies the public overwhelmingly oppose. Strengthening petitions through legislation would provide a vital democratic safeguard. Giving 250k+ petitions mandatory scrutiny and 1m+ petitions binding outcomes ensures the public remain an active constitutional check on government power, not spectators to it.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you mean by "mandatory scrutiny".

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do, or you may wish to sign one of the following similar petitions.

"Give More Power to Public Petitions to Force the Government to take Action"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736968

"Reform the petition system: Parliament vote at 1M signatures & referendum at 5M"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746146

"Hold referendum if a petition reaches over 650,000 signatures"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743620

action: Add “accent” as a protected characteristic under Section 4 of the Equality Act
background: We believe accent bias harms regional speakers, working-class people and immigrants in jobs and daily life. It could limit opportunities and lead to harassment, yet the Equality Act offers no protection. Parliament should amend Section 4 to add accent as a protected characteristic.
additional_details: Accent can be a marker of socioeconomic status, yet we believe that UK law leaves regional speakers and many legal immigrants from non-English-speaking countries unprotected unless their accent links to nationality. Accent bias may block job opportunities, promotions and mobility, keeping Received Pronunciation (RP) dominant and limiting the UK’s talent potential. Adding an accent to section 4 of the Equality Act could close this gap and protect millions.

action: Make courier service disclosure mandatory in online transactions
background: Every day, countless consumers across the country are frustrated by failed delivery attempts, undelivered packages, or damaged/lost goods. We believe this frustration arises from a lack of transparency during online transactions, specifically about the couriers tasked with delivering our purchases.
additional_details: When we make a purchase, it's not just about the price or the product, it's about trusting that what we've paid for will arrive safely and on time. Yet, the reality is that some courier companies consistently fail to meet these expectations. We deserve the right to make informed decisions about whom we trust with our purchases. We want the government to legally mandate that online sellers and service providers should clearly disclose the courier service responsible for delivering our items before payment is made.

action: Make Nala’s Law: Require Drivers to Stop & Assist Cats Injured in Accidents
background: Require an amendment to the Road Traffic Act 1988 so cats are treated like other reportable animals. Motorists involved in a collision with a cat must stop, provide assistance, take the cat to a vet if possible, and report the incident to the police.
additional_details: My cat Nala, well known locally as the station cat, was hit by a vehicle and tragically died. I don’t know how long she lay there before being found, though a local business tried their best to help her. It makes little sense that cats - often similar in size to dogs and other animals that must be reported are excluded. The Road Traffic Act 1988 is outdated for modern pet ownership. With 230,000+ cats hit each year, requiring drivers to stop and report could save lives and prevent heartbreak.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750612

action: Protect Trial By Jury
background: We call on the government to retain trial by jury for all triable either way and indictable offences.
additional_details:
Trial by jury is a cornerstone of our justice system, giving ordinary people the power to decide the fate of the accused. Juries maintain fairness, democracy, and public trust, keeping the legal system grounded in the community rather than concentrated in the hands of a few.

Removing jury trials would erode democracy, place strain on judges, and increase criminal appeals (causing further backlog). Juries are not a problem to be fixed; they are the very safeguard of a fair legal system.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: Allow all ILR holders to bring parents and in-laws to UK as dependants
background: We want the UK Government to amend immigration rules to allow people with Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR)  to bring their parents and parents-in-law to live with them as dependants, even if they are not financially dependent or require long-term personal care.
additional_details:
Many ILR holders can’t return home due to financial pressures and work commitments, yet suffer deep emotional pain from being separated from their parents. We feel this separation harms both generations — parents face loneliness and declining health, while their children live with guilt and stress.

Families should have the right to stay united in later life.

action: Ban hunting with dogs in northern Ireland
background: Stop the use of dogs for hunting any and all wildlife. Bring about harsh punishments for those who break these laws.
additional_details:
Dogs have long been used as a method of sport to rip up and kill animals after a prolonged chase to complete exhaustion. It is contradictory to the long held views of the people of Northern Ireland who by large are highly conscious of animal welfare. 

People gaining joy out of the prolonged suffering of a defenders animal is not acceptable and it's time this barbaric practice was put to an end once and for all.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Northern Ireland Executive and Northern Ireland Assembly is responsible for. 

If you want to raise this issue you could contact your MLA, or raise it with the Northern Ireland Executive.

You can find contact details for your MLAs here: http://www.niassembly.gov.uk/your-mlas/

You can find contact details for the departments of the Northern Ireland Executive here: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/government-departments-in-northern-ireland

action: Ban exports of recyclable waste to non-OECD countries
background: The Government should ban the export of all recyclable waste (including plastics, paper metals, and mixed recyclables) to non-OECD countries, where weak regulation and limited waste-management infrastructure often result in dumping, open burning, or environmental harm.
additional_details: Exporting our recycling frequently shifts pollution to communities with fewer safeguards. Investigations show our waste ending up in rivers, open dumps, and informal burning sites in developing countries. This damages ecosystems, harms public health, and undermines trust in our recycling. We should process, recycle, or reuse our waste domestically or through environmentally robust OECD partners with strong enforcement guards.

action: Stop the ban on 3D, 4D & styled compliant plates; target ghost/stealth  plates
background:
Do not support BS AU 145e changes that would ban 3D, 4D or negative plates. Keep these styles legal when they meet BS AU 145e. 

Instead tackle ghost plates by stronger NIR tests and enforcement on IR-blocking films and sprays; Birmingham's "Operation Phantom" caught 4,300 ghost plates in 2 weeks.
additional_details:
Banning 3D, 4D and styled plates would wipe out a major legal product for 35 thousand plate makers and confuse millions of drivers who bought BSAU 145e plates in good faith.

"Stealth" plates are created by IR-blocking films and sprays, not raised characters. Police ANPR trials have already shown these plates can be detected!

Government action should target overlay films, uncompliant sellers and weak DVLA enforcement, while keeping tested 3D, 4D and styled plates legal when they meet BSAU 145e.
rejection_details: There is no evidence that there is going to be a revision of BS AU 145e anytime soon.

action: Extend the time limit to 10 years for medical negligence claims for ill patients
background: Extend the time limit to 10 years for patients who can prove they were too unwell to claim within the current 3 year period. This is to give sick patients a similar right for justice as patients well enough to claim in the shorter period.

action: Make it a Criminal Offence to make a false allegation about a Certificate Holder
background: There are a lot of false allegations made about a Firearm and Shotgun Certificate holders in the UK. Under public safety grounds this would make sense that the Police had the powers in place to prosecute someone to whom has been found guilty of making a false allegation about a Certificate Holder.
additional_details: Amend the Firearms Act to give the Police the ability and the powers to prosecute someone to whom has been found guilty of knowingly making a false allegation or accusation about a Firearm and or Shotgun Certificate Holder. My proposal would only improve public safety because the Police would at the start of any investigation fully explain the consequences if the allegations or accusations after being fully investigated are deemed and decided to be false.
rejection_details:
The request of this petition is already covered by existing laws related to public justice. You can find out more here: 

Public Justice Offences | The Crown Prosecution Service
https://www.cps.gov.uk/prosecution-guidance/public-justice-offences

action: Reclassify endometriosis & adenomyosis as chronic health conditions
background: Chronic disease classification, clinical approach toward non-reactionary care, immunology, gut health testing, providing non-hormonal/surgical investigations. Increased access to use of cancer-adjacent treatments, GnRH antagonists, selective progesterone receptor modulators on prescription etc
additional_details:
To ensure earlier and accurate diagnosis, reduce the chances of dismissal, broader treatment access, reduced surgical demand, improved fertility and quality of life.  
Proper classification would support earlier detection, continuous management plans, multidisciplinary care, better insurance coverage, and greater prioritization in research funding, reduce delays, and ease the heavy economic burden on patients, the NHS, the workforce and society at large.
rejection_details:
The Government's guidance on disability under the Equality Act 2010 states that you’re disabled if you have a physical or mental impairment that has a ‘substantial’ and ‘long-term’ negative effect on your ability to do normal daily activities:
https://www.gov.uk/definition-of-disability-under-equality-act-2010

There is not a list of conditions that meet this definition, but it is therefore already the case that under the Equality Act, anyone with a physical or a mental condition which has a substantial and long-term impact on your ability to do normal day to day activities is protected under the disability protected characteristic. This could cover people who have endometriosis or adenomyosis, where this has a a ‘substantial’ and ‘long-term’ negative effect on their ability to do normal daily activities.

We could accept a petition calling on the Government to fund additional research into endometriosis and adenomyosis, to improve understanding of these conditions and identify new treatments.

You may wish to sign the following:

Introduce Statutory Menstrual Leave for People with Endometriosis & Adenomyosis
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732342

Fund a National Endometriosis Registry and Audit to Help Improve NHS Care
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736164

action: Raise the standard tax-free Personal Allowance to £45,000
background: The Personal Allowance is the amount of income a person can get before they pay income tax. It stands at £12,570 in 2025. We would like the standard Personal Allowance raised to what we think is a more realistic figure of £45,00.
additional_details:
We think that the Personal Allowance, as termed by the government, has been kept unreasonably low for far too long, at the expense of the poorest, most needy people in our society.

We feel that the poorer majority should pay substantially less than the wealthy. We think that the tax system seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

action: Fund Free TV licences for all pensioners.
background: We want the Government to fund free TV licences for existing pensioners and those who reach the official retirement age. When people reach retirement age, we think they should receive a state-financed free TV licence.
additional_details:
Many pensioners live on the breadline with only the TV for company. With the cost of food soaring and utility bills ever higher, we feel there is a desperate need to provide all pensioners with at least this concession.

We feel it is a double outrage that those who have given their all to this country in taxes and raising children have to pay a TV licence fee and are only exempt if they receive means-tested Pension Credit. Meanwhile, some media figures draw huge salaries.

action: Mandate petitionable new elections if govt has under 25% UK electorate support
background: Introduce legislation requiring an immediate general election if a government is elected with support from less than 25% of the UK electorate, and at least 10% of UK electorate sign a verified petition calling for its removal, which would be binding.
additional_details: Governments can be formed with very limited support due to low turnout and the voting system. This, in our view, undermines democratic legitimacy and leaves many citizens unrepresented. We think setting a 25% UK electorate threshold ensures governments cannot remain in office without broad backing. We believe allowing the electorate to petition for removal strengthens accountability and gives people a direct way to act when dissatisfied.

action: Make First Aid Education Compulsory for All Secondary School Students
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce compulsory first aid training into the secondary school curriculum.
additional_details:
Young people are often the first on scene during emergencies and early action can save lives. Teaching essential skills such as recognising life threatening injuries, controlling bleeding, placing someone in the recovery position and performing basic CPR will give them the confidence and ability to act quickly.

First aid is a vital life skill. It empowers young people, reduces preventable deaths and strengthens our communities.
rejection_details:
First aid training is already part of the health curriculum for schools, which you can see on page 37 + 38 of the curriculum guidance here:

https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1090195/Relationships_Education_RSE_and_Health_Education.pdf

action: Residents want Twickenham Police Station to keep the public front counter open.
background: Pass our message to the police Commissioner and decision makers.
additional_details:
1. The elderly people may not know how to report crime online

2. People may can’t report crimes because they don’t have a phone (stolen)/Wi-Fi connection/ computer in emergency cases or are too poor to have one.

3. Foreign tourists who don’t understand English will not be able to report online

4. It is vital for keeping relationships and building trust between residents and the police

5. From discussions between locals, no matter how many issues we disagree with, we all agree on this one.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.
