action: Force ticket sale websites to enable resale at face value
background: Please force ticket sale websites to enable unwanted tickets to be relisted for sale and legitimately sold at face value. The pay out should be immediately upon purchase, not after the event.
additional_details: As popular ticketed events can be quite competitive, often multiple people from the same friend group will join the virtual queue to buy tickets. If everyone is successful you can end up with more tickets than you need. Please force ticket sale websites to enable these to be legitimately listed at face value with the pay out transferred upon purchase, not after the event. These websites are currently hoarding vast amounts of people's money for, in some cases, over a year.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban all ticket touting and reselling of tickets for higher prices
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734049

action: Force the government to call a referendum on re-joining the European-Union
background: Call a referendum and give us, the people ,the chance to vote on the UK re-joining the European-Union by applying to re-join under Article 49 of the Treaty on European Union
additional_details: Almost 10 years ago, In 2016, the public voted to leave the European-Union. Today however public opinion has completely turned on Brexit with many polls stating that the number of people supporting the UK re-joining the EU outnumbering people who wish to stay out almost by 2 to 1. Not to mention many analysts have stated the Economic disaster that is Brexit has caused with many stating that it costs our economy almost £2Bn per week. Many people are fed up with Brexit and want the EU again.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Commit to a referendum in May 2028 asking the next government to rejoin the EU
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747385

action: Commission a full Independent Review of Council Tax and Stamp Duty
background: We call on the Government to commission a full, independent review of Council Tax and Stamp Duty to deliver the fundamental, evidence-based reform the UK’s housing market urgently needs.
additional_details:
Council Tax arrears have risen to £8.3 billion, with more than two million households struggling to keep up. We believe a tax based on 1990s property values no longer reflects today’s homes or people’s ability to pay — and it fails to provide a stable way to fund essential local services.
 
We believe Stamp Duty remains a narrow, one-off tax that distorts the housing market and traps families in unsuitable homes.

action: Require airports allow taxis & private hires 15 minutes free access to car parks
background: We want the government to require airports to allow taxis & private hires 15 minutes free access to airport car parks.
additional_details: This could encourage travellers to use public transport to travel to and from airports and help prevent taxis and private hires from incurring excessive parking fees.

action: Remove the State Pension amount from HMRC Personal Tax Allowance.
background: If the State Pension amount was removed from the Personal Tax Allowance it would relieve financial issues from the majority of Pensioners thus reducing need for any Pension credits.
additional_details: To reduce financial pressure on UK pensioners.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign one of these petitions, which call for similar action:

"Raise the personal tax allowance to the state pension rate"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746077

"Introduce new tax code for state pensioners with double the personal allowance"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740671

action: Give the British Veterans who are on the street a place in a hotel.
background: I believe that the government should give the British people who are on the streets free places in hotels like they are giving to the illegal migrants that come over here daily. Thousands of British are left homeless when they have tirelessly worked for this country.
additional_details: I believe that every single person should never feel alone, especially this Christmas. So I think that the British people on the streets who have to beg just to get basic necessities should be allowed a place to call home.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: 

"Give British homeless same legal protection from destitution as asylum seekers" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731681

You may also be interested in the following petitions:

"New programme of support & housing for homeless veterans"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744230

"All UK homeless citizens should be prioritised for hotel accommodation"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/729887

action: Ban all face coverings on school grounds for the security
background: Ban all face coverings, including religious ones, on school grounds for the safety and security of children, parents and school staff.
additional_details: In this day and age we think it is a security risk.

action: Strengthen homeowner protection allowing clearer rights and non-lethal defences
background: Strengthen homeowner protection by clarifying self-defence laws, allowing non-lethal defensive tools in the home, and permitting safer pre-planned security measures. Create clear guidance on reasonable force and ensure priority police response to home intrusions to reduce risk to innocent people.
additional_details: Homeowners face uncertainty when defending themselves during break-ins. Current laws can leave innocent people afraid to act or worried about prosecution after acting in genuine fear. Allowing clearer rights, safer non-lethal tools, and stronger police response would reduce harm, deter intruders, and ensure families feel protected in their own homes. Modernising these laws prioritises safety, prevents escalation, and gives homeowners the confidence they need.
rejection_details: It is not clear what specific changes you would like to be made to the existing guidance on using reasonable force against intruders (https://www.gov.uk/reasonable-force-against-intruders). You could start a new petition setting this out more clearly.

action: Petition Plea: Automatic Deportation After Conviction
background: We petition for a change in immigration law: any non-citizen who is lawfully convicted of breaking our laws should automatically lose the right to remain and be deported, following due process. Respect for the law is a condition of staying in our country.
additional_details: I strongly believe this plea must be upheld to protect our country, defend the rule of law, and stand with victims whose lives are harmed by crime. Our communities deserve safety, justice, and accountability.
rejection_details:
Immediately deport foreign nationals who break the law
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732628

action: Put an immediate stop to the introduction of puberty blockers to children.
background: Wes Streeting needs to reverse his decision to allow experimenting on children.
additional_details:
Its an absolute disgrace that this government will allow the experimentation of puberty blockers on children as young as 8 years old. Children of this age have no real preconception of what puberty blockers will do and that it is irreversible.
Leave the children alone, don’t allow parents or the government to experiment on children, allow them to enjoy their young lives until such time they can make an informed decision in later life.
The government, in my opinion will face future legal battles.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Cancel the clinical trial into puberty blockers & safeguard vulnerable children
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751839

action: Review Working Hours Sponsorship Rules for Domiciliary Care Providers & Workers
background: Many domiciliary care providers rely on visa sponsored workers in their work to support vulnerable adults. We believe current Home Office rules unfairly punish normal hour changes, risking workers’ visas, and that a review to ensure clear, fair rules is urgently needed.
additional_details:
We call for a review of the Home Office sponsorship rules for domiciliary care providers and sponsored workers, and for the following amendments to it:
• Introduce a grace period allowing workers to retain their sponsorship when providers lose contracted hours.
• Protect sponsored workers’ visas when hours drop through no fault of the provider.
• Provide clear, consistent sponsorship compliance guidance.
• Introduce a transparent appeal or review process for licence suspensions or revocations.

action: Do not ban children from using virtual private networks
background: We call upon the UK Government to reject any calls or lobbying that propose to restrict or ban the use of virtual private networks ("VPNs") for children, because of the impact this would have on other VPN users.
additional_details: An amendment agreed by the House of Lords proposes an addition to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill: "Action to prohibit the provision of VPN services to children in the United Kingdom". The method and implementation would likely rely on 3rd-party facial scans or ID checks, which we believe are invasive. Thus, such a law would cause massive collateral damage for the millions of current users who rely on VPNs for privacy and security.

action: Organisation with 50 or more employees to report on inclusion and belonging
background: Introduce a statutory requirement for large employers (employing more than 50 people) to measure and report on workplace inclusion and belonging, alongside existing diversity reporting, with clear government guidance and a proportionate, standardised framework.
additional_details: We believe that current workplace reporting does not reflect how people experience their workplace, and that many people leave jobs due to poor culture, exclusion, or lack of psychological safety. We think that requiring large organisations to measure inclusion and belonging indicators would provide better insight into lived experience, support fair treatment, improve retention and wellbeing, and help create healthier, more productive workplaces across the UK.

action: Build a new acute hospital for East Kent,
background: We call for a new hospital to replace outdated sites, ensuring safe, accessible care for all East Kent residents. This must be centrally located, with full emergency services and future-proofed capacity.
additional_details: East Kent’s hospital system is fragmented, outdated, and unsafe for many. Lives are at risk due to delays, poor access, and lack of emergency services. A new central hospital is vital for dignity, safety, and future-proofed care. We’ve waited too long — action is urgent.

We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

action: Mandate public transport operators prohibit balaclavas except religious/medical
background: Require public transport operators (including TfL and National Rail) to amend Byelaws and Conditions of Carriage to prohibit the wearing of balaclavas and identity-concealing masks (excluding those worn for legitimate religious or medical reasons).​
additional_details:
Crime on public transport is rising, often facilitated by offenders wearing balaclavas to evade CCTV and intimidate passengers.

​Safety: Identifying offenders is currently impossible, rendering CCTV useless. ​Context: There is no reasonable need for thermal face coverings inside heated vehicles, distinguishing them from religious garments or medical masks. ​Enforcement: Police need clear powers to demand removal without a Section 60 order, making it a Condition of Carriage does this.

action: Extend the Recall of MPs Act to cover MPs who change or leave political party
background: We call on the Government to amend the Recall of MPs Act 2015 so that a recall petition is triggered when a Member of Parliament who stood for a political party leaves, is expelled from, or switches the political party from which they were elected.
additional_details: We believe that voters elect MPs based on both the individual candidate and the political party and manifesto they represent and that when an MP leaves, is expelled from, or switches party, the basis of that mandate changes. The Recall of MPs Act 2015 exists to protect democratic accountability. In our view, extending it to cover party defection would allow constituents to confirm or withdraw consent through an existing, voter-led process. This is the same democratic mechanism as in India.

action: Review regulation of crossbows and introduce licensing
background: We ask the UK Government to review existing legislation relating to crossbows and to introduce a licensing system to improve public safety and support effective policing.
additional_details: Weapon-related crime in the UK has been rising, raising concern about access to dangerous weapons. Crossbows are powerful, long-range weapons capable of causing fatal injuries. They can be used silently and from a distance, often without warning, which increases the risk to the public. Despite this, crossbows can be bought and owned with little regulation. A review was expected in 2024, but no change followed. This gap in the law should now be addressed as a matter of public safety and urgency.

action: Have a lifetime ban for voting on every illegal immigrant entering the country.
background: Prevent illegal immigrants having the right to vote in the UK.
additional_details: Because they do not hold the right to influence our way of life illegally.
rejection_details:
Illegal immigrants are already unable to vote.

You could submit a new petition requesting for people who do not pay certain taxes to be banned from voting in general or local elections, if that's something you'd like to happen.

action: All manifestos published for a general election must be legally binding.
background: To make it law that any party issuing a manifesto sharing their policies must be legally binding. These documents are used to showcase why people should vote for them. After they are elected they abandon these policies, anyone who voted was lied to and tricked.
additional_details: To hold all political parties to account and follow through on why they were voted for
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Make the government legally accountable for delivering its manifesto promises 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749381

action: Regulate the use of AI generated footage in the public domain
background: I would like legislation passed which forces anyone posting AI generated content to clearly show that the footage is AI generated, either by means of an AI logo clearly displayed throughout the footage or a disclaimer at the start of the footage with financial penalties for anyone found in breach.
additional_details: I feel that it has become increasingly difficult to tell fact from fiction. The potential for harm is considerable. We are often fed misinformation on any range of topics. Take recent examples like brexit where certain individuals twisted narratives to suit their own agendas. Also, fake footage showing police brutality/ineptitude which undermines public trust. Imagine the possible damage in the run up to an election or the potential damage caused to innocent people. This needs to be controlled.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions, which call for similar action:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736690

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747437

"Require all AI musicians and songs to have a visible AI notice"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/753997

"Require companies to disclose when they use AI for advertising"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744204

action: Urge Israeli Government to stop law allowing execution of Palestinian prisoners
background: The UK Government must act urgently to urge the Israeli Government to stop the proposed law which would permit the execution of Palestinian Prisoners, past, present and future.
additional_details:
We believe that such a law would constitute complete violation of the Geneva Convention and International Human Rights Law. UN experts have called for these proposals to be dropped.

We call on the UK Government apply considerable and substantial political pressure and the leverage of its international obligations to prevent the Israeli Government from passing this law.

action: Fund free bus travel for all post-16 students
background: We want the Government to fund free bus travel for post-16 students. We want free reliable travel for all post-16 students.
additional_details:
The Government has stated it wants to create 350,000 training and work opportunities but students are already disadvantaged if they cannot access a course because of cost of transport. We feel we have no choice but to go to college to enhance our earning potential - we are the future tax payers of Britain.
The government has said that no young person should be left behind but we feel that specifically rural students are being left behind.

action: Bring all social care into the public sector under the NHS & stop means testing
background: We demand the government bring all Social and Community Care under the NHS, fully funded by general taxation. We believe neither Social Care, Community Care, nor the NHS should be for profit, but remain free at the point of use.
additional_details:
We want to reverse the changes to Social Care, made over decades, which have resulted in parts of it being transferred to local government, privatised and/or means tested.

We believe that trends in local authority budgets and Social Care funding since 2010 have harmed the sector and that immigration policies have contributed to staffing problems.

action: Increase New State Pension and pay to all, abolish the old Basic State Pension.
background: We think the government should put all our elderly onto the New State Pension, increase the New State Pension to a good percentage of average earnings and abolish the old 'Basic State Pension'.
additional_details:
We believe those on the Basic State Pension should be paid the difference accrued, since the New State Pension's introduction, between the Basic State Pension and New State Pension.

Britain's basic State Pension is currently £176.45 per week.
Britain's New State Pension is currently £230.25 a week.
Britain's average weekly earnings (AWE) were estimated at £722 in March 2025, by the Office for National Statistics.

action: Implement a traffic light control crossing in Aspatria for the primary school.
background: The Aspatria community has consistently appealed to the council for assistance, yet they have neglected to install a safe crossing for our primary students. We urgently demand the installation of a traffic light crossing at an appropriate distance from the T-junction.
additional_details: The lollipop man was unfortunately removed from his duties at Richmond Hill Primary School in Aspatria following several troubling near-miss incidents. However, this decision has alarmingly heightened the danger for primary students, as their safety while crossing the road is now significantly jeopardized without the protective presence of the lollipop man. The Lollipop man himself has pleaded with the council for a safe crossing to be implemented Due to the dangers this road causes.

action: Make it a criminal offense to park across a drive or drop kerb
background: We want the Government to make it a criminal offense to park a vehicle across a drive or drop kerb.
additional_details: I'm classed as disabled. I have had people parking across my drive. I always ask nicely for them to not park there or to park somewhere else. Most days I've been late getting to work because of this. I think that it should be a criminal offense now as the Council Parking Enforcers do not seem to be able to stop it and often do not even show up when we have reported it.

action: Protect the Function of the Architect in UK Law
background: Protect the function of architects under UK law, not only the title. Review legislation and procurement to ensure that work affecting building safety, design quality, and regulatory compliance must be carried out or overseen by appropriately qualified and regulated architects.
additional_details: Although the title “architect” is protected, core architectural functions can be undertaken without proper regulation or accountability. We believe this creates risks to public safety, building quality, sustainability, and clear professional responsibility. Architects are trained and regulated to coordinate design, safety, and compliance. Protecting their function supports better building outcomes and aligns with post-Grenfell safety reforms.

action: Create and fund a national holiday and respite grant scheme for disabled adults
background: Create and fund a national grant scheme so disabled adults on low incomes anywhere in the country can get accessible holidays and respite breaks. This should be funding for several short trips or one longer holiday (UK or abroad) and can pay for more than one support worker’s travel & accommodation.
additional_details: I am a young adult, who is Deaf-Blind, Epileptic and I also have a serious neurological condition. To travel safely I need two support workers. I often pay for my own and my carer's travel and accommodation, therefore my one holiday can cost two or three times more than it would of a non-disabled person. I would like to be able to take short trips to Europe or maybe one further afield, but if staff changes are required mid-holiday, I also must cover the additional expense of those flights. Most charity help stops at 18 years old, so as a young adult there is almost no support.

action: Review the UK Novel Foods Regs to allow medical mushrooms for human consumption
background: Modernise the UK Novel Foods Regulation so traditional natural products with a history of safe global use can be sold without authorisation. The framework should reflect modern science, cultural diversity, consumer choice and fair access for small UK producers; not an arbitrary 1997 cut-off.
additional_details: Increasing numbers of people in the UK are choosing natural and traditional approaches to support their health and wellbeing. Products such as medicinal mushrooms have been used safely for centuries in other parts of the world, yet are restricted here due to the 1997 benchmark. This limits consumer choice, harms small businesses and fails to reflect modern science or cultural practice.

action: Include the Name “Fraser” on Personalised Merchandise at Garden Centres
background:
We call on garden centres and gift suppliers to include the name “Fraser” on personalised and novelty merchandise.

Many garden centres sell personalised items such as mugs, keyrings, pens, magnets, signs, and children’s gifts featuring popular first names. “Fraser” is frequently missing.
additional_details:
This petition is inspired by Fraser, an 8-year-old child, who has noticed that he can rarely find his name on merchandise when visiting garden centres. For children, seeing their name on an item can be exciting, affirming, and inclusive — especially when siblings and friends are able to find theirs easily.

We believe that:
	•	Fraser is a popular and recognisable name
	•	Children should feel included and represented
	•	Adding one more name is a small change that makes a big difference

We respectfully ask garden centres and their merchandise suppliers to add “Fraser” to their standard range of personalised and novelty products, alongside other common names.
rejection_details: Decisions about what stock to sell are the responsibility of individual businesses, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Require proof of license when selling speed pedelecs
background: Currently UK sellers of speed pedelecs are not obliged to confirm that a purchaser holds a valid moped or motorcycle licence. This needs to become a legal requirement. In addition the seller should record the buyer name, address, insurance & tax details before the purchaser can complete the purchase
additional_details: The use of speed pedelecs in the UK is on the increase for the purpose of collecting and delivering online takeaway food orders. Riders of speed pedelecs can achieve speeds of up to 28mph.  Sellers in the UK currently are not required to confirm if the buyer holds the required license and other legal documents. Sellers should be required to see these documents prior to the purchase and provide the buyer with a signed document of confirmation.

action: Scrap the TV Licence
background: Scrap the TV Licence and make BBC pay per view
additional_details: Get Rid of the TV Licence and make BBC pay per view as we believe it is out-dated and Biased

action: Retract the business rate rise for pubs
background:
Pubs are struggling more than ever since Covid, the damage Covid caused to hospitality is huge and no where near repaired yet ! 
Many once thriving pubs are now closing almost daily. Those still open struggling to keep prices affordable,
additional_details:
Not only are pubs taxed on absolutely everything but we’re having to deal with soaring energy bills on top. 
The rise in business rates is a kick in the teeth. 
Pubs are a big part of history and should be protected. A place to make friends/ relationships/ and keep lonely people occupied. 
The pub closures will cause a ripple of staff then companies that will be forced out of work. 
Have some humanity- retract the rates rise.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign these petitions, which call for similar action:

"Cut VAT, Slash Beer Duty, reform business rates and cap energy costs for pubs"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/734677

"Do not implement the business rate increases planned for April 2026"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/753272

"Reduce all taxes (inc. business rates, NI) for all pubs and restaurants by 5%"
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/731533

action: Stop the closure of pubs because of the business rates
background: Prioritise this issue as the impact on local communities and lively hoods ,which any closure would be devastating as once closed they will not reopen
additional_details: Because using a pub is an enjoyment that people like to do and is the core of a lot of small communities
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand you're concerned about the closure of pubs, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

Do not implement the business rate increases planned for April 2026: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/753272

action: Give parents the right to claim tax refunds for children's education expenses
background: As education is compulsory and fundamental in a society, parents should receive tax refunds for taxes paid on uniform, materials, tutoring, and school fees during all mandatory years education (5-16). It could help state school pupils, homeschooled and private educated children.
additional_details: Children over 14 pay VAT on school uniforms despite still being under compulsory school age. Parents of home-educated children fund state education via income tax, receive none of the £8k per-child entitlement, and pay VAT on tutors and materials. Parents of private school pupils similarly pay income tax and now pay VAT on school fees. We believe this is over-taxation. Education policy must be fair, accountable, and recognise that all children in education have the same rights.

action: Resurface the road through a housing estate with a school in the middle
background: Resurface the road through our Estate which is covered with potholes and very uneven surfaces due to poor pothole filling.  We have people of all ages and physical abilities crossing the roads to get to our school, the roads are a trip hazard.  Plus the damage this is doing to the vehicles.
additional_details: We are a Nursery, Infant and Junior School in the middle of a housing estate, the roads are in very bad disrepair, covered in potholes and extremely uneven where potholes have been badly filled.  Walking across the road to the the school is a trip hazard and we have people of all ages and physical abilities trying to cross the road without incident.  We have been asking the local council for the past 5 years to address the poor state of the road.

action: Fund Cervical Length Check at 12-Week Scan to Help Prevent Preterm Births
background: I lost my son in 2020 at 18 weeks when my cervix opened too early and I went into preterm labour. Including cervical length screening at the 12-week scan could identify risk earlier and help prevent devastating, avoidable baby loss.
additional_details: Preterm birth and pregnancy loss cause lifelong trauma for families. I lost my baby at 18 weeks due to undetected cervical insufficiency; nothing could be done in time. Evidence shows early cervical length screening can identify risk and allow simple treatments such as progesterone or cerclage. Including this in routine NHS 12-week scans could spare families unimaginable grief and save babies’ lives. Nobody should have to experience loss first to then be classified as ‘at risk’.

action: Scrap 5-year IPP licence cutoff & mandate victim support at release
background: Mandate specialist trauma support for victims during offender release. Automatically convert 'No Contact' licence conditions into permanent Civil Restraining Orders. Scrap the automatic 5-year termination of IPP licences to ensure high-risk offenders are monitored and victims are protected for life.
additional_details: Offender release can be a trigger for severe mental health decline, yet specialist support is scarce. The new 5-year IPP legislation creates a 'safety cliff': if a licence is terminated, vital 'No Contact' conditions vanish, leaving victims vulnerable to high-risk offenders without police monitoring. Protection should not have an expiry date. The state must prioritize guaranteed, lifetime safety and trauma support over administrative timelines to prevent further tragedy.

action: Abolish the effective Tax rate of 60% on income between £100,000 and £125,140
background: We want the Government to abolish the effective Tax rate of 60% on income between £100,000 and £125,140, replacing it with a Tax band of 45% on income over £100,000 and removing the tapered withdrawal of Personal Allowance.

action: Require faster eviction process, and improve protections for landlords in PRS
background: We petition the Government to amend the law for landlords by instituting a 6-week expedited court process for Mandatory Grounds s8/7A (arrears/Anti-Social Behaviour), creating a registered-landlord database of court-evicted tenants, and raising the deposit cap to adequately cover severe damage.
additional_details: The abolition of Section 21 under the Renters' Rights Act means evicting bad tenants relies solely on Section 8. Current MoJ data shows the average eviction takes over 27 weeks (6+ months). We believe this delay punishes law-abiding landlords via irrecoverable arrears and damage. We urgently need an expedited court process for mandatory grounds (ASB/arrears), a vetting database for repeat offenders, and a higher deposit cap to help sustain the rental market.
government_response_summary: Government does not support these proposals. From 1 May 2026, the Renters’ Rights Act will ensure landlords can continue to gain possession when necessary, while offering more security to tenants.
government_response_body: The Government has no plans to introduce an expedited court possession process for mandatory possession grounds, a tenant vetting database, or to raise the cap on tenancy deposits.  We value the contribution made by responsible landlords, who provide quality homes to their tenants and understand that landlords must have robust possession grounds where there is a good reason to take their property back.   The Renters’ Rights Act (RRA) will introduce a new tenancy system from 1 May 2026. These reforms will clarify and expand grounds for possession, allowing landlords to regain possession when necessary, for example to sell or move in. Where a tenant is at fault, landlords will be able to seek possession using relevant grounds, including where a tenant commits anti-social behaviour, is damaging the property, or falls into significant arrears. While we recommend landlords and tenants work together to address issues, these possession grounds are sufficient to take action when this is not possible.   Most tenancies end amicably without the need for landlords to take possession action in the county court. However, the Government recognises that landlords need a smooth and efficient process when taking possession action if needed. Currently, the median average time from landlord claim to a possession order being issued is 7.3 weeks, below the HM Courts and Tribunal Service target of 8 weeks. Of those landlord possession claims issued in 2024, only a minority (28%) required enforcement by bailiffs, meaning that most cases take less than 27 weeks to resolve.   The Government considers it important that tenants have the opportunity to attend a possession hearing if they wish to challenge an eviction. Vital statutory protections for tenants are built into the possession process, such as time available before a hearing to seek legal advice and reasonable notice before an eviction date. Safeguarding these tenant protections within the RRA is a key aspect of the Government's approach to ensuring landlords can reclaim their property when necessary, while ensuring tenants can challenge unfair evictions. A shorter ‘expedited’ process would not allow sufficient time for these protections.   We are working closely with HM Courts and Tribunal Service to develop a new digital end-to-end service for resolving all possession claims in the County Courts in England and Wales. The service will offer an online route for making and responding to possession claims, filing documents, and receiving updates and outcomes, offering improved user experience through guided journeys.   The Government does not believe that it is proportionate to create a database for tenants who have previously been evicted by a bailiff following a court possession order. Private landlords and letting agents already have a range of tools available to them to obtain references from their tenants, and may consider various factors when deciding to let to a tenant, including previous or outstanding rent arrears and credit checks.     With regards to increasing tenancy deposits, the Tenant Fees Act 2019 limits tenancy deposits to no more than five weeks’ rent where the total annual rent is less than £50,000, or six weeks’ rent where the total annual rent is £50,000 or above. This is in addition to a refundable holding deposit (to reserve a property) capped at no more than one week’s rent. We believe that this strikes the right balance between providing security for landlords and maintaining affordability for tenants.   Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

Delays in veterinary treatment can reduce the chance of survival. Requiring drivers to take cats they hit to a vet would improve animal welfare and save lives.

Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats

action: Require FCA regulation of proprietary trading firms operating in the UK
background: Proprietary trading firms offering funded accounts operate widely in the UK without FCA regulation. Many charge high upfront fees, impose restrictive conditions, deny payouts, and ban customers after taking thousands of pounds, using vague terms that allow payouts to be refused for almost any reason
additional_details: These firms market themselves to retail traders as legitimate opportunities but operate without FCA oversight or consumer protections. Customers risk losing large fees with no recourse when payouts are denied or accounts closed under vague terms. Regulation would improve transparency, prevent unfair practices, and protect UK consumers from financial harm

action: Amend the Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act for rescued pets
background: The Animal Welfare (Import of Dogs, Cats and Ferrets) Act 2025 restricts the importing of mutilated animals into the UK.
additional_details:
We believe that, with the best intentions, the Act is flawed and will prevent owners of rescued pets with previously docked tails from taking their pet to visit family in the UK. Or even preventing pets returning from holiday.

We think the act is unfair in the extreme to adopting pet owners who have done nothing more than rescue a badly treated animal to provide a caring & loving home. An amendment is required to exempt pets that have been rescued following mutilation.

action: Review laws around flying drones above and near all ports
background: Review rules around flying drones around ports. With growing threats from hostile states using drones, and the ease of flying drones near some ports, vital national infrastructure is at risk and requires stronger legal protection now to protect workers, trade, energy and safety
additional_details: We urge the Government and Parliament to require no-fly zones around all ports. Ports are critical national infrastructure for trade, energy and security. With increasing drone threats from hostile states and the ease of flying drones near ports, a review is needed to deter misuse, protect workers, prevent disruption, and strengthen national resilience. We think police and port authorities should have stronger powers to act quickly, improve safety, and reduce risks to the public and the economy

action: Introduce Politics as a mandatory subject for all Secondary School students.
background: To help students and young voters develop an understanding for the UKs political system.
additional_details: Help students develop an understanding for politics due to the new voting age of 16. Aims to reduce political bias and makes sure that voters vote using their own understanding of the UKs democracy and politics. With the new voting age coming into effect voters at the age of 16 could lack an understanding of our political system and could be bias or swayed into the wrong direction.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make Government & Politics a compulsory, core subject in schools
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733942

background:
Change the system

Put more funding available for private assessments for dyslexia and dyscalcula

Give schools more control and to do full assessments in school

action: Mandate green waste bins collected all year around
background: Introduce legislation to mandate councils to collect green waste bins every 2 weeks all year around. We think it is a shame that some people have to buy compost bins or dispose of it at a dump themselves, especially if you have poultry.
additional_details: I want green bins to be collected all year around as people with ducks chickens and poultry are struggling with the waste as they are not collected all year around in all areas of the country.

action: Give families an additional tax-free allowance for each child
background: Introduce a tax-free allowance for each dependent child under 18, in addition to the personal allowance, and ensure it is given to the parent with primary day-to-day care of the child.
additional_details: We believe that the cost of raising children has risen sharply, while tax thresholds have been frozen for years, leaving families worse off even when their income has not truly increased. We therefore  think that introducing an additional tax-free allowance per child under 18 years old would help parents support their children more fairly and reflect the real cost of raising a family.

action: Review and Reform the Use of Operation Brock on the M20
background: We call on the Government to urgently review and reform Operation Brock on the M20. Its frequent use causes severe disruption to residents, businesses, emergency services and the environment. Fairer, more effective alternatives must be developed and communities consulted
additional_details: We want the Government to carry out an independent review of Operation Brock, restrict its use to genuine emergencies only, and develop alternative traffic management solutions that do not place a disproportionate burden on Kent residents and businesses. The Government should improve coordination with ports and border agencies, properly consult affected communities, and ensure emergency services and local roads are not routinely disrupted.

action: Equal reproductive choice: let men relinquish parental rights & costs pre-birth.
background: Pass a law letting men sign a binding pre-birth opt-out that ends all parental rights and child maintenance. A woman can become pregnant and choose to keep or abort without the man's consent, yet men can still be forced to pay for 18 years. Make it fair.
additional_details: Current law gives pregnant people full control over whether a pregnancy continues, which is ethically correct, but men have no equivalent legal choice. A man can become a father without his consent and be forced to pay child support for 18 years, even if he never wanted a child or had no say in the outcome. This imbalance is unfair and outdated. The law should allow men a clear, pre-birth opt-out so responsibility matches choice, while abortion decisions remain solely with the pregnant person.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

End men’s financial responsibilities in cases of deceptive conception
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751119

action: Reform probate law to regulate executor powers & protect beneficiaries’ rights
background: Reform probate laws, including creating clear, legally binding timelines that executors must follow, mandatory will disclosure, and sanctions for delays or non-compliance. We believe beneficiaries need protection, transparency, and enforcement when executors fail in their duties.
additional_details: Many beneficiaries are having to fight. We believe executor laws are outdated and leave grieving families vulnerable. In the event that executors delay, hide information, or misuse their position, we feel beneficiaries have no real protection and no automatic remedy. Many are forced into costly litigation simply to access our rights. We believe reform is urgently needed to introduce timelines, accountability, and consequences so estates are administered fairly and families are not retraumatised.

action: All elected MPs, including Nigel Farage, must be allowed to speak in Parliament
background: We urge parliament to uphold democracy by ensuring all elected MPs, including Nigel Farage, can speak freely. Parliamentary free speech is a constitutional right under the Bill of Rights 1689 and applies equally to every MP, regardless of party size or political disagreement.
additional_details: We urge the House of Commons to uphold a core democratic principle: that all elected MPs have the right to speak and participate in Parliament. Nigel Farage was elected, has sworn the Oath of Allegiance, and holds equal constitutional status. Parliamentary free speech is protected by the Bill of Rights 1689 and long-standing convention. Restricting elected MPs undermines representation, debate, and public trust in democracy.
rejection_details: MPs already have the right to speak in Parliament under existing parliamentary rules. Nigel Farage MP has not been disallowed from speaking in Parliament.

action: Grant visas & scholarships for Palestinian students, collaborate with Gazan Unis
background: We demand that the Government extend the Gazan student evacuation policy that ended on the 31st December 2025 indefinitely, grant further scholarships for studies and facilitate twinning partnerships between UK and Gazan Universities.
additional_details: We demand the UK government establish an ongoing visa and evacuation scheme for Palestinian students from Gaza akin to the Ukrainian home visa scheme. In our view, the current inconsistent process has forced countless students to defer or lose university offers, pushing them to seek later intakes. We call for a long-term continuous safe passage corridor to ensure students can reach the UK, free from unrealistic financial barriers, by offering scholarships and accepting self-funded cases.

action: Apply the same restrictions on HFSS products marketing to alcohol
background: There is a restriction on promotions and marketing of products high in fat, sugar or salt. We think this should be also apply to alcohol.
additional_details: I lost someone close to me to alcohol. I think the promotion of something that can damage lives is harmful and irresponsible. In the initial summary the HFSS regulation was put into place for obesity prevention. I do understand how much of an issue this is for the government but I believe not promoting alcohol and not romanticising a serious addictive substance can also save lives and cut healthcare costs and justice expenses as well. It’s not a fix, but it’s a prevention measure, to reduce the drinking culture.

action: Ban all use of AI in the UK
background: I want the UK government to ban all use of AI in the UK. This should include all AI programs and models.
additional_details: I believe AI is contributing to destroying our planet very fast. Many places don't have clean drinking water but data centres feeding AI are using, and in my view wasting, gallons and gallons of it. I'm concerned that AI is also using artwork without permission from or compensation for artists who are struggling. I think our planet doesn’t have long left if we continue in the state we’re going, and that AI is just speeding it up.

action: Call a General Election immediately.
background: The people of this country voted in a referendum back in June 2016 to leave the EU with a majority of 17.4 million votes because of the restrictive Laws and rules that the EU imposed upon us, and the excessive amounts of taxpayer’s money given to the EU and its unelected organisations.
additional_details: Call a general election now so the people can decide the fate and future of our country.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

action: Do not remove the 10% wear and tear allowance for childminders from April 2026
background: Retain the 10% wear and tear allowance for childminders, or introduce an equivalent alternative that reflects the additional household costs of providing regulated childcare from home and helps ensure childminding remains financially sustainable.
additional_details: Childminders provide essential home-based childcare for families, including babies, siblings, children with additional needs, and parents needing flexible or wraparound care. They work from their own homes, so their workplace is also their family home. We believe the 10% wear and tear allowance recognises unavoidable household costs such as utilities, cleaning, equipment use, and general wear. We think removing it risks making childminding financially unsustainable and reducing childcare availability for families.
government_response_summary: Childminders, like any other business, can continue to get full tax relief on the business proportion of their expenses.
government_response_body: The Government is aware that childminders are concerned about changes to administrative arrangements from April 2026 in connection with Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax.  MTD for Income Tax, through digital record-keeping, aims to reduce errors and simplify tax returns. From April 2026, self-employed childminders with qualifying income over £50,000 must use MTD for Income Tax. The Government expects only a small proportion of childminders to use MTD for Income Tax from April 2026.  All childminders currently have the option to use alternative methods for some of their expenses and record-keeping responsibilities. In particular, all childminders can currently deduct 10% of their childminding income to cover wear and tear of furniture and household items, instead of deducting the actual costs of purchasing, repairing and replacing these items.  Childminders using MTD for Income Tax from April 2026 must use normal rules for expenses and record-keeping and so should deduct actual business costs for these items, in the same way as other businesses do. If an item is for both business and personal use the business proportion of the cost can be claimed, using a reasonable estimate if necessary. For example, if a childminder needs to replace kitchen equipment they use for meals for both their own household and the children they look after, and they estimate that 60% of the use relates to childminding, then they can claim 60% of the replacement cost.  The Government recognises childminders’ concerns about this method and so we will actively engage with childminders and stakeholders in the 2026 to 2027 tax year to review the impacts of moving from the 10% deduction to actual costs for wear and tear expense claims.  There are about 30,600 self-employed childminders in the tax system in the UK. About 2,500 of these will be required to use MTD for Income Tax from April 2026. In 2026-27, all other childminders can continue to use the alternative methods including the 10% deduction and are unaffected by these changes.  The 10% deduction only covers wear and tear of furniture and household items, not other costs including utilities, cleaning and non-domestic equipment. The actual business costs of these and any other expenses can be deducted, as well as the 10% deduction if applicable to those not in MTD. This is an important principle that the Government is aware may not have been fully appreciated by some childminders and childminding organisations. Childminders who have not been deducting these costs separately may get more tax relief by doing so, instead of only using the 10% deduction.  For utilities and other household costs, there is an alternative method to allow childminders to claim a proportion of their bills based solely on the number of hours of childcare provided per week. Childminders within MTD for Income Tax can also claim a deduction for a proportion of their bills, using the same rules that apply to all businesses based at home. The amount to claim is based on their own individual circumstances of how much of the property is used, and for how long. This ensures that childminders with exceptionally high household costs can get all the tax relief due to them.  These methods of deducting business costs together allow any childminder to reflect all the costs relating to providing childcare from their own home when calculating the profits of their business.  The Government is committed to supporting those childminders through the transition. HMRC has worked with the software industry to ensure there is free and low-cost software available to support smaller and simpler businesses. It is also taking comprehensive steps to raise awareness by writing to affected taxpayers and agents, engaging widely with industry and tax bodies and launching a marketing campaign through social media and radio.  HMRC has recently published updated guidance on GOV.UK for all childminders, including those entering MTD for Income Tax, and giving full details of the alternative methods for wear and tear, household costs, food and drink and record-keeping. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/claiming-expenses-and-keeping-records-if-youre-a-childminder   The Government engaged with Coram PACEY prior to the announcement of the changes at Budget 2025, as the original agreement in 1986 introducing the alternative methods was made with their predecessor. We will continue to work with Coram PACEY, the Scottish Childminding Association (SCMA), the Northern Ireland Childminding Association (NICMA) and other childminding organisations to help childminders with the transition.  HM Treasury

action: Stop the flats in Llandudno being refurbished to house asylum seekers
background: Stop the flats in Llandudno being refurbished to house asylum seekers and support local citizens instead. These flats are intended for asylum seekers whose asylum claims are being processed. This means they could be in these flats for years, whilst our locals continue to struggle.
additional_details: These flats should be prioritised for local people, including those experiencing homelessness or long waits for housing. Why are we always putting others first above our own local needs? This could be a very dangerous move, as these flats are on the seafront where many families visit every year. A lot of these people are unvetted, and could pose great risk to the local community. We have seen this time and time again, and it is still continuing every day.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Allow care workers to access 5-year ILR route like other health and care workers
background: Change settlement proposals so all care workers can earn settlement after 5 years like other health and care workers on Skilled Worker Visas. We believe care is skilled, essential work that helps people live safely, out of hospital, and their family to stay in work.
additional_details: We feel care workers should not be penalised. Care worker vacancies are estimated to be around 7% and overseas care worker recruitment has ended, while local recruitment remains difficult. Care work requires high-level communication, judgement, technical skill and compassion. Care workers work alongside nurses and other health staff but now could face a longer 15-year settlement wait. Many came to the UK expecting 5-year settlement. We believe recent proposals are unfair and risk workforce collapse. Government policy should stabilise the workforce, not drive skilled staff away.

action: Ban the use of all pest control methods against pigeons
background: Ban the use of any pest control on pigeons, as we believe it is cruel and should be against the law.
additional_details: I would like parliament to consider our past, and how pigeons have aided us. They carried messages during the war, they delivered them for us, they were like our telephones. But since real telephones came about, many feel we don’t need them anymore and they’re considered pests, which we believe is untrue and so unfair. We believe these birds deserve sanctuary for their service, and that it should be illegal to use pest control on them. I see birds trapped in nets and unable to feed their babies due to pest control methods.

action: Guaranteed West Yorkshire's Tram Network "spades in the ground in 2028"
background:
West Yorkshire has already lost two tram projects. Leeds in particular is too populated to not have a mass transit system. 

Guarantee the start of the project in good time, so the people of West Yorkshire can be confident it will eventually arrive
additional_details: A review few people expect has moved the expected delivery of the first line to the late 30s. Nobody understands why it takes so long. There's no good reason for it. Trams are a commodity. People deserve to be told why there's a delay - not why a report says we need a delay, but why there's no desire from Westminster to deliver infrastructure in The North
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that request action at a local level.  

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.  

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP  

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: Scrap the proposal of installing "tamper-proof" software to monitor devices
background: The Government should withdraw this amendment and reject any requirement for tamper-proof surveillance software on personal devices. Child protection must rely on targeted law enforcement, not blanket monitoring that undermines privacy, security, and encryption for everyone.
additional_details: The amount of control that the government is trying to take is quite frightening for some. If the amendment does get approved, it will be similar to North Korea (DPRK) and no one wants to be watched by the government whenever they feel like it as it induces a lack of privacy. It would be much more beneficial to not introduce this act, and it would also set a dangerous precedent for government overreach and reduce trust in the public.
rejection_details: The action is now unclear with the Lords having rejected the amendment in question last week.

action: Reverse the ban on selling Turkey Tail and Cordyceps mushrooms for human use.
background: Reclassify Turkey Tail and Cordyceps as traditional foods, not “novel,” and allow their sale as supplements or functional foods. Create an accessible approval pathway for small producers to meet safety standards without prohibitive costs.
additional_details: These mushrooms have been used safely for thousands of years in global herbal traditions. The ban harms public access to natural wellness options and disproportionately affects small UK businesses. Emerging research supports their immune and anti-inflammatory benefits. The “novel food” label ignores cultural history and scientific evidence
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition that has a similar ask:

Review the UK Novel Foods Regs to allow medical mushrooms for human consumption

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754498

action: “Restore democratic rights: run all postponed elections now.”
background: “Reverse the decision to postpone local and mayoral elections and reinstate them on their original schedule, ensuring democratic rights are upheld.”
additional_details: “Millions of voters are being denied their say because of election delays tied to local government restructuring. This is unacceptable. Reforms must not silence democracy. We demand the government reinstate these elections and ensure citizens’ voices are heard without further delay.”
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop the cancellation of Local Elections to help uphold democracy
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751384

action: Apply New ILR Rules Only to Future Arrivals, Not Current Residents
background: We want the Government to allow asylum seekers and their families who are already living in the UK to remain on the current 5-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain. Any new settlement rules, including a proposed 10-year ILR route, should apply only to people who arrive in the UK in the future.
additional_details: Individuals who have been in the UK for more than two years have established stability, community ties, and expectations based on the existing rules. Changing their path to indefinite leave to remain would be a retroactive change, creating uncertainty and disrupting their lives. We ask the government to uphold fairness and legal consistency by respecting the rules that were in place when these individuals entered the asylum system.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751517

action: Remove proposal to spy on UK citizens in the Children's Wellbeing & Schools Bill
background: Withdraw the new clauses following Clause 27 authored by a "Lord Nash", "Baroness Cass" and "Baroness Benjamin" on VPNs and monitoring software
additional_details: The monitoring software proposed is a massive risk to the security of the citizens of the United Kingdom. Spying on every mobile device in the United Kingdom is a massive breach of privacy, security and trust. These clauses define a child as 18, although many teenagers mature much before then into using technology on a daily basis, including VPNs. The clauses allow phones to transmit any data you record, anything you see or anything you do on your phone to the government—it is endangering to all
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. The action is now unclear with the Lords having rejected the amendment in question.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Expand the 'Enough' campaign to include violence against men
background: We feel that there are plenty of things in place for women in domestic violence situations not for men. There are men who have to suffer with the lasting effects of domestic violence and crimes against men are often unreported but shouldn’t be viewed as inferior or completely disregarded.
additional_details: Include men in the 'Enough' campaign. We think this will mean men get complete equality and better resources pumped into domestic violence as a whole. We think statistics on domestic violence against men are lower due to the amount of the crimes being unreported, but the effects are no less to a victim.

action: Let children be aloud to dye their hair any colour in secondary schools.
background: Make it so schools let children dye their hair any colours, without getting in trouble/consequences.
additional_details: Make it so children can show individuality and uniqueness in personalising themselves. It shows differences without hurting nor damaging anyone/ their education.
rejection_details: Decisions about allowing pupils to dye their hair are a matter for individual schools, not the UK Government or Parliament. You may wish to raise this issue with your school.

action: Review decision to end the ECO scheme, assess the economic and social impact
background: Review and pause the planned ending of the ECO scheme until a full impact assessment is completed, including effects on employment, industry capacity, fuel poverty and delivery of net-zero targets.
additional_details: The ECO scheme supports thousands of skilled jobs and underpins the UK’s energy efficiency supply chain. Ending it without a clear replacement or transition risks business closures, job losses, loss of specialist skills and higher fuel poverty. We believe a review is needed to assess economic, social and carbon impacts and avoid long-term damage.

action: Require all benefit claimants to “sign on” in person every month to get benefit
background: The Government should require all benefit claimants to show up in person and “sign on” every month in order to receive benefits. This could ensure that the person resides in the UK and has not returned to their country of origin.
additional_details: We are concerned that many people may come to this country, gain Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR), receive benefits, and return to their country of birth. We believe only people who reside in the UK should receive benefits.

action: Require Disclosure of All Pesticide Residues and Processing Aids on Food Labels
background: All residues and processing aids used at any stage of the food production and supply chain must be clearly and fully disclosed to consumers on product labelling, including the amount of agents used during farming, processing, preservation, or packaging that remain in or on the final food product.
additional_details: We believe that consumers have the right to know exactly what is present in their food to make informed and safe choices, including those with allergies, dietary restrictions, or ethical concerns. Transparency in food ingredients and residues promotes public health, trust, and accountability in the food industry.

action: Fund more NF1 specialists and regular monitoring and support for NF1 patients
background: Provide funding for more Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) specialists. Currently only two locations provide care. Monitoring is limited to yearly checks. My husband was diagnosed in 2018, had no follow-up, his NF1 tumour became cancerous (MPNST). He sadly passed on Christmas Eve 2025.
additional_details: I believe that the processes involved in my husband's monitoring of NF1 were lacking and accessibility to sufficient services would have benefited both him and further patients with the condition. More frequent monitoring would mean we could better track an ongoing condition and react quicker to any changes in anyone affected, meaning better survival rates especially in the cases of aggressive occurrences such as MPNST. More readily available specialists would further this possibility.

action: Increase domestic violence maximum sentences and penalties & reform bail laws
background: We call on Parliament to increase domestic violence maximum sentences and strengthen bail laws by banning bail to high-risk and repeat offenders. Increase penalties for repeat abuse and restraining order breaches to prioritise victim safety. Risk assessments should be required before release.
additional_details: We believe weak sentencing, routine bail, and failure to enforce restraining orders allow known abusers to repeatedly breach conditions without consequence. This can put victims at extreme risk and lead to preventable injuries and deaths. We believe laws must prioritise victim safety. Failures in domestic violence responses have cost many lives. We believe dangerous offenders are released despite risk, restraining orders are ignored, sentencing is lenient, and vital evidence is dismissed.

action: Government to require all car park operators to provide contactless payments
background: We want the Government to amend its code of practice so that people can pay car parking charges by card. Car park operators who only take payment through an app cause significant problems for many people who have issues with their mobile phone service.
additional_details:
The restriction of app only payment causes confusion and stress on people, particularly those advanced in age, due to the range of different apps required.
Making contactless payment options available will make parking payment simple.

action: Require government to secure consent by referendum to delay a local election
background: We think the present government is acting in an undemocratic way by continuing to delay some local elections. Any government wanting to delay any local elections should first have to put the question to a countrywide referendum and get public consent from the result.
additional_details: We believe the government is undermining the democratic process by delaying local elections. We want the government to pass legislation that will stop any future government delaying local elections without first getting consent from a referendum. We feel this will prevent the undermining of democratic process.

action: Stop the ability to delay 63 local council elections.
background: I would like the government to give us the right to vote in local elections.
additional_details: Having already had our local elections delayed it appears that the government is attempting to delay them again thus denying us the right to choose who governs us.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747234

action: Protect Children Without Turning Phones Into Surveillance Devices.
background: Amendments to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill would mandate phone monitoring and identity checks to use a privacy tools, crossing a serious civil-liberty line.
additional_details: Recent amendments to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill would require monitoring capability to be built into smartphones and could force people to prove their identity to access privacy tools. While protecting children is vital, embedding surveillance and identity-linking into personal devices by law creates permanent infrastructure that can be expanded later. This petition calls on Parliament to protect children without mandating phone monitoring or surveillance-by-design.
rejection_details:
The action is now unclear with the House of Lords having rejected the amendment(s) in question last week.

You could resubmit the petition in amore general form without reference to those amendments.

action: Raise the age to 18 for receiving Disability Living Allowance
background: Being 16 is still considered a child in the UK so how can a 16 year old take the responsibility of applying for PIP and to be knowledgeable about finances. To fill in complex forms is overwhelming for an adult let alone a 16 year old. You can’t drink alcohol until 18 so the laws should be the same.
additional_details: There’s many things you aren’t able to do at 16: playing the lottery, smoking and drinking alcohol. Would you allow a 16 year old to do this no we wouldn’t. 16 is just to young to take on the complexity of filling out many forms to claim a sickness benefit which is what the family would rely on. It’s simple: raise claiming PIP up to 18 so there’s no pressure on 16 year olds to become adults way to fast.

action: Make Christmas Eve a bank holiday
background: Christmas Eve is a magical time, but many people are required to work until 5pm or later, losing valuable time that could be spent with loved ones. Making Christmas Eve a bank holiday would allow workers more time to travel, prepare, and be together during the festive season.
additional_details: Only the Government has the authority to introduce new bank holidays, and doing so would reflect modern working patterns, support wellbeing, and acknowledge the significance of Christmas Eve for millions of people across the country.

action: Review use of abuse allegations in family court and immigration decisions
background: Allegations of domestic abuse can have serious consequences in family court and immigration cases, affecting housing, legal aid, financial settlements, parental access, reputation and mental health. Reviewing safeguards, standards and early fact-finding would help ensure fairness and due process.
additional_details: Allegations of domestic abuse can have serious and lasting consequences in family court and immigration-related cases, affecting housing, legal aid, financial settlements, parental access, reputation and mental health. While genuine victims must be protected, unproven allegations can cause irreversible harm. Reviewing safeguards, evidence standards and early fact-finding would help ensure fairness, due process and equal treatment before the law.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750199

action: Government to place limit on taxi licences and out-of-area use
background: We call on the Government to reform private hire licensing law by changing provisions that allow councils to issue unlimited out-of-area licences, introducing national limits and local connection requirements, and ensuring licensing reflects genuine local oversight rather than regulatory arbitrage.
additional_details: The current system allows councils to issue vast numbers of private hire licences to drivers who work almost entirely elsewhere. We believe this undermines local regulation and enforcement, creates unfair competition between drivers, weakens public confidence in licensing standards, and turns local authorities into de facto national licensing bodies without accountability. National reform is needed to restore fairness, consistency, and effective oversight.

action: Fund high-quality, non-partisan political and citizenship teaching resources
background: Youth Parliament UK urges the Government to invest in high-quality, non-partisan lesson resources that any teacher can use. It’s vital students are taught the skills for informed and active participation in society, but too often teachers don’t have the support, leaving students without consistency.
additional_details: This would help teachers feel more confident delivering these topics and ensure that lessons on democracy, government, citizens’ rights and responsibilities, media literacy, and more, are taught to a high and impartial standard in all secondary schools across the UK. With the proposal to lower the voting age, and in an age of AI and algorithms, it is essential we make high-quality, non-biased political and citizenship education a right, not a lottery.

action: Require clinicians to review full patient history before diagnosis or discharge
background: Legislate to introduce a new requirement for clinicians to review a patient's full medical history, when presenting with chronic or repeating symptoms, before diagnosis, discharge or treatment decisions.
additional_details:
This should be known as Faye's law and could improve patient safety and continuity of care.
 
We believe many patients can be misdiagnosed or dismissed because their full medical history is not reviewed. This can lead to missed warning signs, repeated errors and avoidable harm. Faye’s Law would require clinicians to consider full history before diagnosis or discharge, which could improve patient safety, safeguarding and continuity of care. It could also help prevent mislabelling, reduce preventable deaths and restore trust for patients and families.

action: Require schools to teach British Sign Language from Key Stage 2 & at GCSE
background: Require schools to teach British Sign Language from Key Stage 2 as it could promote inclusion, accessibility and ensure everyone is heard. BSL supports Deaf and SEN children, improves communication for all, and should be available at GCSE level like other language options.
additional_details:
We believe British Sign Language should be introduced in England’s primary schools, ideally beginning from Key Stage 2 in line with when languages such as French are taught. BSL is a legally recognised language in England, Wales and Scotland under the British Sign Language Act 2022.
 
The national curriculum should be updated to include BSL, as more people are using sign language than ever before. Early teaching could promote inclusion, support Deaf and SEN children, and improve communication and understanding for all pupils.

action: Local elections must go ahead in may 2026 without further delay
background: Uphold democracy and insist the elections go ahead in may 2026 unhindered
additional_details: We see this as an effort to deny us the public of our democratic rights to be able to choose who represents us and  more importantly not forcing us to be governed by unelected officials with absolutely no mandate from the electorate to govern.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Stop the cancellation of Local Elections to help uphold democracy

Remove power to cancel local government elections
