action: A UK nationwide ban on publicly chanting the slogan “globalise the intifada”
background: Introduce legislation and policing guidance to treat public chanting of “globalise the intifada” as a call to violence/terrorism. Prohibit its use at demonstrations and public events, and require organisers and police to stop it and take enforcement action where it intimidates, harasses or incites.
additional_details: After the Bondi Beach Hanukkah attack in Sydney, where 15 people were killed and authorities are investigating it as antisemitic terrorism, most UK Jews fear that tolerating this slogan normalises calls to violent “uprising”. The First and Second Intifadas included suicide bombings, stabbings and murders of Jewish civilians. Publicly chanting “globalise the intifada” can be understood as endorsing that violence and can embolden extremists and intimidate Jewish communities.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

The Government does not specifically prohibit certain words or phrases. Some language is already prosecutable as a hate crime or public order offence in certain circumstances. More information about this can be found on the Crown Prosecution Service website here https://www.cps.gov.uk/types-crime/hate-crime and here https://www.cps.gov.uk/prosecution-guidance/public-order-offences-incorporating-charging-standard

The Metropolitan Police and Greater Manchester Police issued a joint statement stating that they will "act decisively and make arrests" in response to placards and chants such as “globalise the intifada”. Several such arrests have been made. You can read their statement here: https://news.met.police.uk/news/joint-statement-from-the-commissioner-of-the-metropolitan-police-and-the-chief-constable-of-greater-manchester-police-504494

You may wish to sign the following petition: "Review rules, policing and harm of marches" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745282

action: Stop the NHS Pathways Experimental Puberty Blocker Trial for Children Aged 10–16
background: Abolish the NHS puberty blocker trial for 10–16 year olds. We believe children cannot legally or ethically consent to experimental medical trials with unknown lifelong risks. The Government must stop this trial to uphold child safeguarding.
additional_details: Children cannot consent to life-altering medical experiments. This trial subjects minors to hormones with unknown effects on fertility & bone health. History is full of medical trials on children that caused unforeseen harm; such research on minors is inherently high-risk. Government must prioritize safeguarding over experimentation and protect children from interventions where informed consent is impossible. We call for the abolition of this trial to ensure children are not used for research.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Cancel the clinical trial into puberty blockers & safeguard vulnerable children
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751839

action: Allow spouses to receive 3 years worth of their deceased partner’s state pension
background: If a spouse dies after retirement, surviving partners may be able to inherit up a part of their spouse’s pensions, sometimes up to 50%. However, most people cannot inherit their spouse’s state pensions based on their contribution record if their spouse dies before retirement age.
additional_details: Some work-based pensions allow for a named beneficiary to receive three years’ salary as a 'death in service' settlement, which we believe is reasonable. If a spouse dies before their SPA, even when both have paid thirty-five years’ worth of national insurance contributions, their partner cannot receive any part. We are calling for the Government to change this to allow a surviving spouse to receive a single payment equivalent to three years’ worth of state pension payments.

action: Increase deportations of illegal immigrants to five flights per day
background: I want the Government to significantly increase the number of deportation flights for those entering the country illegally. I am calling for a minimum of five planes a day to be used to return people to their home countries or a safe third country.
additional_details: I believe the current system is unfair to legal residents and those struggling with housing and services. By not deporting those here illegally, we are putting too much pressure on the UK's infrastructure. I want the Government to prioritize the safety and needs of its own citizens by ensuring that the law is enforced strictly through daily deportation flights.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about something that is an operational decision for a government or parliamentary body, rather than decision about policy or legislation that is made by the Government or Parliament.

You may also wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737105

action: Ban non-stun slaughter of animals in the UK
background:
We ask the Government and Parliament to introduce legislation to ban non-stun slaughter of animals in the UK.

The UK has some of the highest animal welfare standards in the world, built on the principle that animals should be protected from avoidable pain, distress, and suffering.
additional_details:
Mandatory stunning before slaughter is widely recognised by veterinary and animal welfare organisations as essential to minimise suffering. Allowing exemptions undermines the animal welfare protections that the UK has fought hard to establish and maintain.

We believe that all animals slaughtered in the UK should receive equal protection under the law, regardless of slaughter method, and that religious or cultural practices must evolve in line with evidence-based welfare standards.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban the non-stun slaughter of animals

action: Save Old Devonian/Celtic Devonian language by making it a protected language
background: Recognise Devon as a Celtic nation by making old/Celtic Devonian a protected language and make an effort to save its Celtic heritage and language.
additional_details:
I want the UK Government and Parliament to protect the Old Devonian/ Celtic Devonian language as we believe it represents an important but overlooked part of England’s Celtic heritage. Devon once had its own Brythonic language, closely related to Cornish and Welsh, but it disappeared without any formal recognition or preservation.
 
By granting it protected status, the Government could safeguard the remaining evidence of this language, support research into Devon’s Celtic past, and allow future generations to reconnect with a unique part of their identity. Recognising and protecting the language could ensure that Devon’s early history is not forgotten and is given the same respect as other Celtic regions in the UK.

action: Launch a review of eligibility for the Rural Fuel Duty Relief Scheme
background: At a time of ongoing cost-of-living pressures, we want the Government to urgently review eligibility for the Rural Fuel Duty Relief Scheme to ensure fairness, consistency and equal treatment for remote, rural and island communities, including those in Argyll.
additional_details:
The Rural Fuel Duty Relief Scheme is intended to address higher fuel costs in remote, rural and island areas where prices are consistently higher and alternatives to private transport are limited. Despite appearing to meet published eligibility criteria, we feel areas such as Argyll remain excluded. Fuel is essential for residents, local businesses and the delivery of services. 
 
We are concerned that possible exclusion may place additional pressure on households and local economies. The Government should review eligibility to ensure the scheme operates fairly and consistently.

action: Allow existing Dependent Partners & Children  qualify to ILR with Main applicant
background: Do not disrupt families. Allow existing Dependent Partners and Children to qualify for ILR with the main applicant. Adding income requirements for existing Dependent Partners unfairly disrupts the family unit, their right to family life and unjustly affects women, child welfare & child caregivers.

action: Allow school students to express themselves through appearance
background:
Remove all school rules about physical appearance (except for uniform) 
dyed hair, piercings, makeup, nails, rolled skirt etc.

It will not impact their learning and helps them discover their identity. People cant be slaughtered on are streets and be free in 10 years or less, it isnt good enough.

action: Create a Mass Transit System for Leeds
background: Parliament should commit funding and legislative backing for a fully integrated mass transit system for Leeds, enabling light rail or rapid transit, coordinated buses, and long-term operating support through West Yorkshire Combined Authority.
additional_details: Leeds is the largest city in Europe without a mass transit system, holding back productivity, jobs, and growth across West Yorkshire. Reliable rapid transit would cut congestion, reduce emissions, improve access to work and education, and support housing delivery. Investment would level up the North and give Leeds the connectivity expected of a major UK city.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

action: Recognise same-sex partners as legal parents of children born via surrogacy
background: Currently, UK law still recognises the surrogate as the legal mother (and their partner as the father if they have one), despite neither having any biological connection to the baby. This can lead to a lengthy court process costing thousands of pounds to be recognised as legal parents.
additional_details:
This means that same-sex partners who are using surrogacy to start a family aren’t automatically recognised as the legal parents once the baby is born, unless they go through a lengthy and costly court process.
 
We feel the current law leaves a baby effectively parentless and needs to be changed. We believe UK surrogacy laws are outdated and don’t reflect modern families.

action: Stop the media repeatedly targeting demographics with a protected characteristic
background:
The UK media has repeatedly and persistently been targetting a number of groups of people who have a protected characteristic for over a decade now.

The IPSO will not do anything about this because they cannot see a problem with it..
additional_details: Either get IPSO to do their job properly or put some other regulatory body or framework in place to prevent the media from running sometimes dozens of defamatory news stories each week about groups of people that are not only harassing in nature, but are also misleading or objectively wrong in content and, also calculated to get others to hate, abuse or attack these demographics.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you are concerned about some reporting by the news media, but we're not sure exactly what regulatory framework or offences you'd like the Government or Parliament to introduce.

We can also only accept petitions about things that the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. Decisions about the handling of complaints to IPSO are a matter for IPSO, not the UK Government or Parliament.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Repeal laws that restrict the right to free speech in the UK
background:
Repeal these laws where they create speech based offences:
- Public Order Act 1986
- Malicious Communications Act 1988
- Terrorism Act 2000
- Communications Act 2003
- Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006
- Terrorism Act 2006
- Criminal Justice & Immigration Act 2008
- Online Safety Act 2023
additional_details:
We believe these laws have been misused to prosecute supporters of legitimate political movements like criticism of the Israeli war in Gaza or republicanism. In our view words and ideas can't cause physical harm, harmful actions do. So, harmful actions should be prosecuted, not speech.
 
Britons have the least freedom of expression in Western Europe according to the 2025 Global Expression Report. If governments want to maintain that the UK is a free country then they should repeal these authoritarian laws.

action: Review safeguards to stop marriage fraud – to protect UK citizens from Visa scam
background: We call on the Government to review UK immigration law to ensure there are no loopholes or ways to exploit regulations to enable marriage and relationship-based immigration fraud, to better protect UK citizens from online grooming.
additional_details: We believe marriage and relationship-based immigration fraud is damaging lives, harming mental health, destroying livelihoods, and exploiting UK citizens. A review is needed to identify whether there are areas of weak enforcement and loopholes allowing the system to be abused, encourage further fraud, and create more victims, while British citizens are left unprotected and treated unfairly. In our view, this undermines public trust and the integrity of immigration protections meant for genuine cases.

action: Require all UK MPs and Ministers to take and pass the Citizenship Test
background: Suspend any MP who fail the test within 6 months of becoming an MP until they successfully pass. Ministers should be required to have passed before taking any role.
additional_details: This should be retrospective, and apply to all MPs currently in office.

additional_details: Democracy

Stop the cancellation of Local Elections to help uphold democracy

action: Increase driving test fees to £85 to pay for more examiners to clear backlog
background: We think by increasing the driving test fee to £85 from £62 (weekday) / £75 (evening, weekend, bank holiday), government could potentially raise millions, train an extra 300 examiners and increase salaries by £8000 per annum to make the job more lucrative from the current starting salary of £29,000.
additional_details: Currently the average wait time for a driving test is 5 months and government now predicts that the 7 weeks wait time won’t happen until 2027. By increasing the test fee to £85 this could potentially pay for another 300 examiners and also increase the starting salary to £36k, making the career more lucrative thus tackling the persistent backlog problem facing people waiting for a driving test.

action: Fund and Implement a 24/7 National Mental Health Crisis Response Service
background: Fund and implement a 24/7 national mental health crisis response service, integrated into the 999 system, so that people experiencing mental health crises are attended by trained crisis professionals rather than police or ambulance services where there is no immediate physical danger.
additional_details: Police and ambulance services are increasingly used for mental health crises, creating high costs and pressure on emergency services. A 24/7 national crisis response service, integrated into 999 and staffed by trained professionals, could significantly reduce avoidable A&E attendance, hospital admissions and Section 136 detentions, saving public money while providing more appropriate crisis care.

action: Strengthen enforcement against ghost and illegal number plates
background: We call on the Government to strengthen regulation and enforcement against ghost and misused number plates, require clearer standards for number plate manufacture and display, introduce penalty points for serious or repeated offences, and ensure police forces have the powers and resources to act.
additional_details: Ghost and misused number plates undermine road safety and law enforcement by allowing drivers to evade detection for speeding, red-light offences and other crimes. This creates unfairness for compliant motorists and weakens public confidence in traffic enforcement. Stronger regulation, clear penalties and consistent enforcement are needed to deter misuse and protect all road users.

action: Make Type 1 Diabetes Hybrid Closed Loop Systems available to all in the UK now.
background:
Make Type 1 Diabetes Hybrid Closed Loop Systems available to all in the UK now.

No more postcode lottery. No more unequal access.
additional_details: People with Type 1 diabetes deserve the same life‑changing technology wherever they live. It’s time to ensure fair, nationwide access to Hybrid Closed Loop Systems so that every person in the United Kingdom can manage their condition safely, confidently, and without discrimination based on their address.

action: Convene an inquiry into the targeted violence against Hindus in Bangladesh
background: Since August 2024, Hindus in Bangladesh have faced surge in violence, temple desecrations, and mob lynchings. Despite promises, the interim government has failed to protect this minority. We ask the UK to hold a formal inquiry into these atrocities and crimes against religious minorities.
additional_details:
Evidence includes the lynching of Dipu Chandra Das and thousands of attacks reported by ASK, Insight UK. MPs have raised concerns in Hansard about persecution of Hindus. Temples have been targets of arson, leaders face questionable charges. USCIRF notes extreme insecurity for minorities.

action: Fund accommodation for all prison leavers
background: We call on the Government to fund accommodation for everyone leaving prison so they are not released directly on to the streets and therefore put at a much greater risk of re offending.
additional_details: I run a homelessness charity and time after time we see clients released from prison straight on to the streets with nothing in place and their only option is to reoffend so they can go back in and have some where to stay. We think more needs to be done and put in place to help these people to rebuild their lives.

action: Introduce tougher sentences for crimes causing harm to many victims across UK
background: We call on the UK Government to review sentencing policy and introduce stronger sentencing uplifts where a crime causes harm to multiple victims, even when committed by a single offender or small group, and to work with devolved administrations to promote consistency across the UK.
additional_details: Crimes that harm multiple victims cause long-lasting damage to families, communities, and public safety. Sentencing should reflect the full scale of harm caused, not just the offender’s intent toward one person, to ensure justice, deterrence, and public confidence in the justice system
rejection_details:
Scotland has its own criminal justice system. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

action: Mandate Public/Open Domestic Abusers Register ( Butterfly Law)
background:
I am a domestic abuse survivor, Myself & many more would like to see an open & public domestic abuse register, similar to those for sex offenders.
One easy to access with factual & up to date information on both male & female offenders of domestic abuse
additional_details:
As part of a support group & soon to be charity -  Butterfly, filled with fellow female survivors of domestic abuse. We are all at different stages of the legal & healing process, but all have many similarities to our cases. Due to the volumes of  both men & women now suffering at the hands of a partner or ex. 
We would like to see an open/public domestic abuse register as we believe the current legislation in place does not go far enough, or takes too long to facilitate.

action: Stop the ban on trail hunting
background: Stop the plan to ban trail hunting!
additional_details: We believe trail hunting is a way of life and it generates so many jobs and helps rural communities and businesses. We therefore think that banning it will be a disaster.

action: Urgent review of CPS decision making for domestic abuse and coercive control
background: We call on the Government to urgently review CPS investigations and charging decisions in domestic abuse and coercive control cases, to ensure the law is being applied correctly and all forms of abuse are taken seriously, not just extreme physical violence.
additional_details: We believe that too many cases are dismissed despite clear evidence of coercive control, malicious communications, and sustained emotional, psychological, and physical abuse. Non-physical abuse causes severe and often irreversible harm, yet, in our view, victims are repeatedly denied justice because CPS practice prioritises visible injuries over ongoing patterns of control and harm.

action: Do not ban trail hunting and hunting in general. There is no need to!
background: Trail hunting especially is packed full of tradition and brings together people from all different backgrounds. It’s brings the community of equine, agricultural and hounds. There is no apparent reason why you have chose to do this now. All your doing is making yourself more hated and more protests

action: Require a referendum and 2 years' notice for any major constitutional changes
background: No government should be able to make major changes to constitutional structures without a referendum from the British people, including changes to elections or alterations to the powers or composition of Parliament. Proposed changes should have at least 2 years' notice to enable research & debate.
additional_details: Constitutional changes affect democracy and the way the British people interact with it. We believe changes should not be allowed to be made without permission from the British people and with an informed debate.

action: Repeal UK Laws Restricting Speech & Pass 'Free Speech Act' like US 1st Amendment
background: We call on the Government to repeal restrictive speech legislation - including sections of the Communications Act 2003 and the Public Order Act 1986 – and pass a “Free Speech Act” mirroring protections and rights guaranteed by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution.
additional_details: UK speech is a "qualified right" under the Human Rights Act, which we believe is often restricted by vague standards like “gross offence”. We are concerned that this could allow prosecutions for social media posts and unpopular opinions. We believe we must adopt an act modelled after the US "First Amendment" to protect all speech unless it incites imminent lawless action. We believe this could end what we feel is the "chilling effect" on debate and ensure the government cannot act as an arbiter of morality. The UK should move from a system of "permitted speech" to "protected speech."

action: Remove VPN restrictions and device-level surveillance from the Schools Bill.
background: Amend the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill to remove any clause on digital guidance that threatens encryption/privacy. Remove VPN ban for minors and all mandates for "tamper-proof system software" on personal devices. Prohibit any age-verification requirements for VPN and communication services.
additional_details: Restricting VPNs requires universal ID checks. This destroys privacy and autonomy and creates a loop where surveillance triggers workarounds, which are met with further control. "software" is a backdoor that scans messages and can result in false positives, also breaking encryption. This threatens whistleblowers & journalists who are fundamental to democracy. Who decides exemptions? It is authoritarian to treat all citizens as suspects. Police should use targeted stings, not mass surveillance.
rejection_details:
We are not clear what action you are seeking, as this part of the bill has already been considered by Parliament and some of the amendments you refer to have been rejected by the House of Lords so will not be part of the Bill. 

There is also a petition already open on not banning children from using VPNs https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754408 that you may wish to sign. 

We cannot accept petitions that ask for the same or very similar actions to a petition that is already open.

action: Require vets to inform owners if medicine is available cheaper elsewhere
background: I would like Parliament to legislate that any agency issuing prescriptions for animals must advise people if a cheaper option is available to purchase from another source. And if they do not do that people should, by providing evidence, be reimbursed the difference by the prescription provider.
additional_details: My vet prescribed and issued a prescription for my dog. They charged £36.39. The same drug is available online for £5.39. This is extortionate.

action: To stop the ban on Trail Hunting
background: To consider what impact banning trail hunting will have on the economy, livelihoods, horses, hounds and also the loss on traditional values. Trail hunting uses humans to lay the scent, not foxes!
additional_details: To truly analyse the impact than enforcing a ban will cause. Local hunts provide so much to each of their local economies, from pub breakfasts, charity fund raising events and not mention horse industry businesses who heavily rely on the season. That's not to mention what would happen to thousands of hounds and horses whose jobs are specific to trail hunting. It is a way of life passed down through generations, a sport who welcomes everyone irrelevant of class, upbringing or financial stature.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Stop the ban on trail hunting" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/755123

action: Mandate CPI-Linked Coverage Increases for Existing Pet Insurance Policyholders
background: We want Government to oblige Insurance Companies to raise maximum cover values in line with CPI. Premiums continue to increase for pet owners each year. Not to mention the cost of appointments, prescriptions & procedures have risen; yet the maximum cover assigned to owners isn't subject to review.
additional_details: The breakdown of maximum cover values that are disclosed within policy documentation should be amended in line with inflation. If premiums are increased each year, even when owners have not submitted a claim, and the cost of procedures increases, members should too have their maximum cover amounts increased to reflect this.

action: Provide adequate funding to support British inland waterways
background: Given that another breach of a canal has happened on the Llangollen canal today, the UK government should provide adequate funding to maintain and enhance the inland waterways to support canal liveaboarda, canal users, tow path users and support and increase mental, physical and emotional health.
additional_details: Funding to the Canal and River Trust has decreased massively over the previous few years yet the costs are increasing as a lot of the inland waterways are centuries old. If this was a physical building or highway, more would be done to maintain it so the same should be demanded of the government for the canals and navigable rivers of Britain.

action: Condemn Thai actions against Cambodia & support Cambodian sovereignty and peace
background: We ask the UK Government to condemn Thailand’s attacks on Cambodia, publicly support Cambodia’s sovereignty, and urge for a peaceful resolution. additional_details: We believe Thailand’s actions against Cambodian territory, including the suspension of the peace deal, has caused civilian casualties, displaced nearly half a million people, and has reportedly destroyed civilian infrastructure and cultural heritage sites. action: Review rising costs & financial pressures on the UK hospitality sector
background: We call on the Government to launch a review into rising costs facing UK hospitality, including National Insurance, minimum wage, VAT, business rates and supplier costs. We are concerned these pressures could threaten jobs, high streets and the survival of hospitality businesses.
additional_details: The UK hospitality industry is vital to the economy, employing millions and providing accessible jobs, particularly for young people entering the workforce. It generates significant tax revenue through VAT, income tax and National Insurance, supports local supply chains, boosts tourism and creates employment opportunities across the wider economy.

action: Keep the Five year-ILR Pathway for UK Ancestry Visa Holders & Their Dependants
background: The existing UK Ancestry visa route should be retained in its current form. This includes the eligibility of individuals with British-citizen grandparents to live and work in the United Kingdom for a five-year period, followed by eligibility to apply for ILR after completing those five years.
additional_details: Preserving both the route itself and the five-year qualifying period for ILR is essential to provide certainty and fairness for applicants who make long-term personal, professional, and financial commitments based on this established policy. Any change to these arrangements would undermine confidence in the immigration system and risk disadvantaging individuals who have planned their futures in reliance on the current framework.

We demand: 1) mandatory whole-life orders for deliberate knife-related murders, 2) no parole or release, 3) strict penalties for knife possession in violent situations. Knife attacks destroy families and communities. We believe the punishment must reflect the severity of the crime.

action: Make it a legal requirement for dog owners to have insurance

additional_details: Vet bills after dog attacks can be very high and if victims are unable to cover the full costs of vet bills, owners having third party insurance could cover the remaining costs. action: End the practice of placing children for adoption in NAI cases
background: We call on the Government to end the practice of placing children for adoption in cases involving alleged or proven non-accidental injury (NAI), and instead prioritise family-based care and long-term safeguarding solutions that preserve a child’s identity, relationships, and welfare.
additional_details:
We are concerned that adoption permanently severs their legal and emotional ties to their birth family, siblings, culture, and identity, which can compound trauma rather than resolve it.

We believe that in many NAI cases, risk can be safely managed through alternative measures such as kinship care, special guardianship orders, or long-term fostering with continued family contact. These options could allow children to remain connected to their family while ensuring their safety.

action: Require review hearings for all Child Arrangements Orders
background: Legislate to require all Child Arrangements Orders to be subject to compulsory, automatic review hearings in the family court, for example at three-month and six-month intervals, with an expectation that both parents adhere to and engage with the process by law.
additional_details: This review process should be free to the parties and built into the original order, so that distressed parents, often fathers, are not forced to issue fresh applications to the court at great emotional and financial cost simply to enforce an order that already exists. The aim is to ensure orders are working in practice, not just on paper, and to reduce the mental health strain caused by prolonged exclusion and repeated litigation. We think this would better protect children’s relationships with both parents.

action: Amend avian flu regulations to allow the vaccination of swans and wildfowl

additional_details: Swan populations in the UK are being decimated by the H5N1 virus. These populations are static, live in localised areas that they don’t usually stray from and as such should be treated like birds in zoological collections. action: Introduce prison sentences for deliberate cruelty to wild birds including pigeon
background: We call on the UK Government to amend existing wildlife and animal welfare legislation to introduce custodial prison sentences for any individual who deliberately goes out with the intention of injuring or killing wild bird, specifically including pigeons, using catapults or similar weapons.
additional_details: Under current law, deliberately killing or injuring a wild bird is already a criminal offence, yet penalties often fail to reflect the seriousness of the act or act as a sufficient deterrent. Deliberate acts of cruelty carried out for amusement or gratification demonstrate a clear disregard for animal life, public safety and the law. Despite the protection under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 section 1(1)(a) individuals who target and kill pigeons face minimal or zero consequences.
government_response_summary: There are existing laws to prohibit killing or injuring wild birds, including pigeons, which can carry a custodial sentence. The government is actively considering the issue of misuse of catapults.
government_response_body: Pigeons, like all wild birds, are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, which makes it an offence to kill or injure them, including with the use of a catapult.   Significant sanctions are already available for judges to hand down to those convicted of wildlife crimes. Anyone who commits an offence under existing legislation, such as the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, could face up to a six-month custodial sentence and/or an unlimited fine.   Sentencing of those convicted of wildlife crimes remains a matter for judges, and these decisions are rightly taken independently of government.  It is also an offence under the Animal Welfare Act 2006 to cause an animal any unnecessary suffering. The Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021 increased the sentences available to our courts for the most serious cases of animal cruelty to pets, livestock and wild animals under human control by increasing the maximum penalty for this offence to five years’ imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine.  In the government’s Animal Welfare Strategy published in December 2025, a commitment was made to review and look to strengthen penalties for cruelty against wildlife more generally so that a disparity is addressed and they are consistent with the higher levels of sentencing available for animal welfare offences against pets and livestock.   Wildlife crime is unacceptable. Defra supports the National Wildlife Crime Unit (NWCU), which helps prevent and detect wildlife crime (including crimes involving misuse of catapults) by obtaining and disseminating intelligence, undertaking analysis which highlights local or national threats and directly assisting law enforcers in their investigations. Defra is providing £494,000 for NWCU in the financial year 2025-2026.  The NWCU attended the first of a new series of “Operation Lakeshot” meetings in January 2026. Operation Lakeshot is a working group which meets quarterly to bring together police and charities to raise awareness of the problem of wildlife crimes being carried out with catapults and will be working with partner agencies to prevent people from engaging in this crime and to support law enforcement.   The government recognises that misuse of catapults is causing great concern to some local communities whether the targets are wild or domestic animals, other people, or property. The government is clear that catapults should not be used against wildlife, property or people and is, for example, convening a roundtable to understand the problem better and to identify what more can be done.  It should be noted that certain birds, including pigeons, may be killed by an authorised person in certain licensed circumstances (such as to prevent serious damage or to preserve public health and safety) but this should not involve the use of catapults.   Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

action: Bring back 75% business rates relief for retail, hospitality & leisure sectors
background: Business rate increases and business rate relief reductions come into effect in April 2026. We urge the Government to increase business rates relief back to 75% for retail, hospitality & leisure. We are concerned increases could lead to business closures, substantial job losses & empty properties.
additional_details:
Just under 300,000 businesses closed in 2025, the number of payrolled employees fell by 171,000, and the unemployment rate increased to 5.1%. A substantial amount came from retail and hospitality.
 
An increase on business rates could put substantial pressure on an already struggling business market and result in significant business closures, and possible job losses in 2026 if support and relief is not put into place. We believe these increases are not sustainable and that these sectors need support.

action: Ban the sale of rope toys for animals
background: Ban the sale of rope toys for animals. String and rope are classified as foreign bodies which are dangerous and can cause blockages and death in animals.
additional_details: There is no official, government-mandated ban on the sale of rope toys for animals in the UK. As the toy frays or is chewed, animals can swallow the individual threads or larger pieces of rope. These linear foreign objects can travel along the intestines, causing severe internal damage, blockages, or a potentially fatal "drawstring" effect where the intestines are damaged. It was too late for our little two year old boy dog "Chip" the rope had severed his intestines and bowel. Please ban them.

action: Fund green spaces for communities impacted by major infrastructure developments
background: Communities affected by developments like HS2, New Road and commercial developments deserve environmental and social investment. We call for funding to create a high-quality natural park or walking space for wellbeing, young people, and nature recovery — not more car-led retail infrastructure.
additional_details:
Many areas, including our own, have already experienced serious environmental disruption from HS2 and New Road developments, including loss of green space, habitat damage, increased pollution, traffic and noise. Despite this, we feel further planning approval has focused on drive-through retail, supermarkets and car parks that primarily benefit commuters and commercial interests.

We are concerned that local young people are left with fewer free, natural places to go, which may worsen mental health pressures and reduce access to nature. We are calling for policy-led environmental compensation via government funding of projects such as  protected, high-quality natural parks or walking spaces that restore biodiversity, support wellbeing, and give something meaningful back to communities.

action: Require able-to-work benefit claimants to participate in community work schemes
background: Require all benefit claimants who are able to work to participate in mandatory local community work schemes. We believe continued receipt of benefits should depend on regular participation in approved local tasks, with exemptions for disability, illness, caring responsibilities, or education.
additional_details: We believe the welfare system should protect those who genuinely cannot work while expecting reasonable contribution from those who can. Community work schemes could improve local environments, reinforce fairness for taxpayers, help claimants maintain routine, confidence and basic skills, and reduce long-term dependency. Visible contribution in return for public support could increase trust, social cohesion, and public confidence in the benefits system.

action: Ban water company bill hikes & reduce shareholder dividends to fund repairs
background: We ask the Government to require Ofwat to ban water companies from increasing charges for customers for historic underinvestment where profits were paid to shareholders. Repairs to be paid by reducing shareholder dividends before bill increases.
additional_details: Water companies operate as regulated monopolies, meaning customers can find it difficult to switch provider or avoid price rises. In the last year, many customers have faced sharp bill increases to fund infrastructure repairs following long-term underinvestment. Where profits were paid instead of investment, we believe it is unfair for customers to fund these historic failures. Regulation should prioritise affordability, fairness and consumer protection.

action: Give Local councils more funding & new powers to evict council house tenants
background: We call on the Government to provide funding and new powers to local councils to ensure they are able to carry out evictions of council house tenants for repeated, evidenced antisocial behaviour.
additional_details: We believe local councils must be given these powers and funds to better balance supporting vulnerable tenants with protecting communities. Where antisocial behaviour is persistent and well documented, current eviction processes can often be slow and complex, allowing harm to neighbours to continue. We ask the Government to reform the law to empower local councils to take swifter action in these cases, while retaining safeguards, so councils can act proportionately, protect residents, and maintain safe communities.

action: Fund & require new, stronger gates at train stations to stop fare evaders
background: We feel current train station gates are too easy to force open and can allow criminals from entering unchecked. This can facilitate fare evasion and can put staff at risk when they try to stop fare evaders.
additional_details: We want the Govt to fund and require tougher, high-resistance barriers that cannot be pushed through by force. We believe current "paddle" gates are too weak, allowing many individuals to barge through or "tailgate" with minimal effort. This can bypass security, facilitate fare evasion—costing taxpayers millions—and create a dangerous environment. Station staff may face abuse or physical assault when trying to stop these individuals. We want the Government to mandate and fund new and upgraded barriers that use high-resistance, reinforced designs that cannot be forced open, ensuring a safer, fairer rail network.

action: Revise the eVED Taxation on Plug-in Hybrid Vehicles (PHEVs)
background: We call on the Government to revise the proposed eVED charge to prevent 'unfair' double taxation. PHEV drivers pay a flat 1.5p/mile even on petrol miles, where they already pay 53.95p/L fuel duty. We believe this discriminates against those who adopted hybrids in good faith to reduce emissions.
additional_details:
We request specific revisions to the PHEV eVED:
1. "Fuel Duty Credit": Allow owners to offset pump duty against their eVED bill.
2. Exempt Non-Electric Miles: Use onboard tech to apply eVED only to zero-emission miles.
3. Adjust the Rate: Reduce the 1.5p PHEV rate for short-range vehicles (e.g., 20-30 miles).
4. "Grandfathering Protection": Exempt existing PHEV owners - early adopters - from the new charge.
We believe these changes would ensure fairness for those who invested in transitional green technology.

action: Allow radio operators to install antennas & masts without planning permission
background: Reform planning laws to allow licensed amateur radio operators to install antennas and masts without planning permission, to support innovation, skills, and emergency communications.
additional_details: Amateur radio is an experimental and educational hobby for many, and antennas may need to be changed to suit varying atmospheric conditions. We believe current planning rules make this costly and impractical. We request planning law reforms for permitted development rights for licensed amateur radio operators to erect up to two antennas, to a maximum height of 15 metres or 5 metres above roof height (whichever is greater), and a maximum width of 8 metres. We would like reforms stipulate that only larger installations require planning permission. A modest antenna licence fee, payable to local councils, could support this concession.

action: Create a law that all Governments (current & future) stick to their manifesto
background:
I urge the government to create a new law that forces all Governments (current & future) must stick to their manifesto.

If the Government wanted to bring in something new not on the manifesto they would ask the public to vote, if 60% of voters vote yes, the Governments plan is brought in.
additional_details:
This new law would help all British citizens and Members of the public be shown true transparency when voting. 

If the law is created and the Government breaks it by not following the manifesto or not announcing a public vote on their plan they should be fined personally (not government or party).

Any Party or Government should be in favour of this suggested law as at the end of the day why shouldn’t they be speaking truth of what change they want in our county before we vote them.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Require a referendum for any policy that breaches the governments manifesto" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/748234

action: Make fireworks illegal to the general public.
background: Fireworks should be made available to those who have a valid license. Members of the general public without a license should not be able to purchase fireworks. Fireworks should be used as a display, in safe areas, with notice. Fireworks should not be used in built up areas due to safety precautions.
additional_details: A license should be held to purchase fireworks as they are an explosive. Its becoming increasingly dangerous for members of the of the general public to purchase fireworks as these can be set off anywhere. Due to the increasingly large numbers of fireworks being let off in built up areas, more residents are at risk. If a license is required for shotguns, cartridges and riffles, bullets; why is a license not needed for fireworks? They are all explosives. The volume of incidents is concerning
rejection_details:
We already have petitions open on this:

Limit the sale of fireworks to those running local council approved events only
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732559

Licence the sale of Class F3 and above fireworks & only allow sales at set times
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733895

action: Legislate for the statutory regulation of 'Counsellor' and 'Psychotherapist'
background: Legislate to make ‘Counsellor’ and ‘Psychotherapist’ protected titles regulated by the HCPC. The Government should also review how this could include influencers and life coaches offering mental health services, ensuring all are subject to mandatory fitness-to-practise oversight.
additional_details: We believe that current voluntary regulation fails to protect the public. Anyone can legally use these titles without training. Unregulated 'influencers', 'life coaches' and in some cases negligent practitioners can cause iatrogenic harm and family breakdown without, in our view, proper accountability. We believe some struck-off practitioners can rebrand without oversight. Statutory regulation could end the 'Wild West,' restore public confidence, and protect the integrity of the profession by ensuring all practitioners meet national safety and ethical standards.

action: Introduce a progressive system of penalties for speeding offences in 20mph zones
background: We call on the Government to amend sentencing laws and reduce the minimum penalties for speeding in 20mph zones, so that a first offence between 20-25 mph only results in 1 point, a second leads to 2 points, and a third leads to 3 points.
additional_details: We believe too many urban drivers are accumulating points and getting disqualified for marginal and minor offenses. A progressive system could send out the same message but avoid automatic disqualification being imposed too quickly.

action: Ban all supermarkets from throwing away edible food & require their donation
background: Everyday, UK supermarkets throw away tonnes of edible food while millions of people rely on food banks to survive. We believe this is wrong, and that food that is safe to eat should not end up in bins when many families, pensioners, and workers are going hungry.
additional_details:
We call for the Government to ban all supermarkets from throwing away all edible food, and require them to donate any surplus food that is edible and is approaching the best-before-date or with minor imperfections to be donated to food banks and local charities. Ending food waste could reduce hunger, cut environmental damage, and show real social responsibility.
 
No one should go hungry while good food is thrown away.

action: Require fireworks to be sold only through the fire service with registration
background: Require consumer fireworks to be sold only through the fire service, with purchasers registering in advance using valid photo ID. Profits from these sales should go towards support for firefighters and their families.
additional_details: Fireworks are widely available despite their potential for misuse, antisocial behaviour and harm. Communities, animals, veterans and people with sensory sensitivities are frequently affected by unpredictable and prolonged fireworks use. Emergency services regularly respond to fireworks-related incidents, placing strain on limited resources. We think that introducing controlled access would improve accountability, reduce misuse and support safer, responsible celebrations.

action: Stop deducting carers allowance/ Carers support payment from Universal Credit
background: Unpaid carers are being pushed into poverty by deductions of Carer’s Allowance from Universal Credit. If a carer earned £83.30 from work it would not be deducted, yet carers are penalised for providing essential unpaid care.
additional_details: The government must stop deducting Carer’s Allowance and Carer Support Payment from Universal Credit. Unpaid carers should be treated fairly and not penalised for providing essential care. Ending these deductions would reduce poverty and recognise the vital role carers play
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/752032

action: Revive the National tradition of Ringing in the New Year instead of fireworks.
background: As ringers and/or lovers of the sound of church bells, we believe it is important to keep the British tradition of ringing in the New Year alive. We would like to see the use of fireworks on New Years Eve replaced by environmentally friendly, mental health enhancing church bell ringing.
additional_details:
Church bell ringing is quintessentially British. This tradition and important skill must be kept alive. Bell ringing is fantastic for mental health and agility, and great for physical health. It has many social and community benefits and can be enjoyed by ringers and listeners alike. The music of the bells brings communities together and is a reassuring sound for many people.
The bangs of fireworks terrify people and animals. They are uneconomical and unfriendly to our environment.
rejection_details: Decisions about New Year traditions are a matter for individuals, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Intro: ‘Citizens Initiative’ law for the public to trigger a general election.
background: Introduce a ‘Citizens’ Initiative Act’ to let the public trigger a general election by official petition. If a verified high percentage of voters (e.g., 20%) signs it, Parliament must vote on an immediate election. This provides a direct public check on government power between scheduled elections.
additional_details: The public must hold the government directly accountable, not just MPs. Popular sovereignty needs a safety valve for when a government loses national confidence on fundamental issues. This high-threshold tool, for profound discontent only, empowers citizens, strengthens accountability, and rebuilds trust for all future governments.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739383

action: Mandate the installation of panic alarms in all licensed pubs, bars & clubs
background: We believe this could make the workplace a lot safer for the staff members and customers in the premises.
additional_details: Many pub employees have seen some awful things that may have been resolved more quickly if there was an instant button connecting us to the emergency services. For example, stabbings, fights, people being run over and many more. On many occasions, staff have to deal with it themselves. This can not only put the staff in danger, but customers too. We believe that lives are being put in danger by wasting time on the phone to the emergency services to get help for staff members.

action: Launch a cross departmental review into school term times, holiday care & work
background: We call on the Government to launch a joint review by the Department for Education, Work and Pensions and HM Treasury into school term times and better aligning them with childcare provision and modern working life.
additional_details:
The review should include looking into piloting alternative term patterns and expanding affordable wraparound and holiday childcare.
 
For millions of working families, staying in work depends on school and childcare logistics as much as pay. Long school holidays and limited wraparound care can create gaps for some parents, who may have to fill them privately. For many households, especially single-parent families, this could mean using annual leave, paying for holiday clubs or taking unpaid leave. This may push parents out of work and leave families absorbing costs that the system creates. We believe any term time date changes must protect teacher workload and be properly funded through pilots.

action: Mandate use of motorway cameras and technology to catch lane hoggers
background: The Government must ensure that cameras, sensors etc on motorways are used effectively to catch lane hoggers in the same way they are used to catch people who speed.
additional_details: The motorway network has a significant amount of cameras and sensors which can recognise numberplates, speed of vehicles, even weights of HGVs. As the UK moves to an AI approach and incorporates cameras for mobile phone usage and seat belt usage, there needs to be investment to catch and punish lane hogging, which causes great frustration and increases the chances of accidents on the UK roads.

action: Introduce a refundable deposit for booking NHS appointments
background: Introduce a flexible, refundable booking deposit for NHS appointments, where patients would pay a small amount (e.g. £5) when booking and is refunded if they attend or cancel within a set notice period (e.g. 48 hours). The deposit would be kept by the NHS only if they do not attend or cancel late.
additional_details:
Missed NHS appointments cost hundreds of millions of pounds, with estimates of up to a billion each year. It can also waste limited clinical capacity. A small refundable deposit could encourage attendance without charging patients for care.

We believe similar systems work in the private sector. With clear exemptions for vulnerable patients, this could reduce no-shows, free up appointments faster, improve efficiency, and protect NHS resources for those who need them most.

action: Fund a new government-backed animal cruelty policing unit
background: Fund a government-backed Animal Cruelty Policing Unit that has legal authority to seize animals, enforce fines and force entry in cases where there are reasonable grounds to believe that an offence against a protected animal has occurred under Section 9 of the Animal Welfare Act 2006.
additional_details: Animal welfare charities, such as the RSPCA, have no legal powers to seize animals or force entry into properties, and we believe the police seldom act on cruelty cases due to being a low priority for them. This dedicated unit could effectively bridge the gap between animal welfare charities and the police by enforcing welfare laws without burdening police forces.

action: Review ways for children with ECHPs to go to mainstream schools and colleges
background: Mainstream schools and colleges often hesitate to accept a child with an EHCP. We want these schools to actually give these children a chance because it can be really hard to get into education with an ECHP. They can lose time waiting to be put into a school or college.
additional_details: No one should have to go through this experience.  It can be very depressing and children can feel like no one wants them. Special schools aren't always the best for children. Many can do better in a mainstream setting.

action: Withdraw from jurisdiction of European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR)
background: We believe the ECtHR is outdated and does not look at the rights of both sides, and will overlook the rights of everyone it effects while it blocks dangerous people being deported.
additional_details: We believe the ECtHR is an outdated body which has no place in modern society.  The UK should immediately disassociate itself from it as we feel it places our citizens in danger and has a significant financial impact on UK tax payers.

action: Require NHS to start priority triage & discharge pathways for dementia patients
background: Make NHS hospitals implement priority triage and faster discharge pathways for people with dementia when the medical condition is treated & home or community care is available. Formally recognise that delay in discharge can cause rapid deterioration and should be treated as a clinical risk.
additional_details: People with dementia can deteriorate rapidly in hospital due to unfamiliar environments, delayed discharge due to fragmented processes and sequential signoffs. NHS England recognises that admission can trigger distress, delirium, and functional decline. The Parliamentary debate in March 2024 on inequalities in dementia services acknowledged that existing dementia initiatives can fall short and more must be done. We believe faster, dementia informed discharge pathways would reduce harm, distress, and unnecessary hospital stays, freeing up beds.

action: Hold a national referendum on whether the UK should rejoin the EU
background: We call on the government to begin the necessary steps toward rejoining the European Union and to hold a national referendum so the public can decide whether the UK should rejoin.
additional_details: Ten years ago, the public voted to leave the EU, but voters were not fully informed of the consequences. Since then, Brexit has contributed to a £20 billion loss in productivity in the UK’s financial sector, with firms relocating to EU cities such as Frankfurt and Paris. It has also increased the cost of living, adding nearly £6 billion to UK food bills in just two years. Despite this, little has been done to address or reverse these impacts.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747385

action: Make domestic battery installations mandatory for new homes under the FHS
background: Please do not cave-in to pressure from housebuilders to increase their profits and back down from making it mandatory from them to install domestic batteries for new homes under the new Future Homes Standard soon to be adopted.
additional_details: Batteries are absolutely cruicial to maximising benefits to home owners/renters of low carbon energy efficient systems with solar PV, heat pumps and building insultation. Without a battery installation, the full energy efficiency savings of £1350/year (3 bed home) will not be realised to help people combat the cost-of-living crisis. Taxpayers/consumers will instead need to pay more to deliver the equivalent of two nuclear power stations in new electricity generating capacity. Please stand firm!

action: Ban electronic shelf labels in shops
background: Ban the use of electronic shelf labels and the possibility of dynamic pricing via these electronic shelf labels in shops.
additional_details: We are concerned behaviour surveillance technologies and AI may be used to charge people more based on their circumstances and habits. This could exacerbate inequalities as more economically desperate people could be charged more for essentials. We believe this is an affront to a free and open society and democracy. We believe any claims of saving carbon are a non-starter as this has such a minuscule impact to be useful.

action: Ban the Sale of Fireworks to the General Public – Restrict to Professionals Only
background:
We call on the UK Government to:

Prohibit the sale of fireworks to the general public.
Restrict fireworks use to licensed, professional organisers for large-scale, controlled displays only.
Fireworks may look beautiful, but for pets, livestock, and wildlife, they’re terrifying.
additional_details:
Fireworks cause significant stress and harm to animals, including pets, livestock, and wildlife. Loud explosions and bright flashes can lead to anxiety, injury, and even death for vulnerable animals.

This change would reduce animal suffering, improve public safety, and ensure fireworks are enjoyed responsibly.

Sign our petition to ban the sale of fireworks to the general public and restrict them to licensed professional displays only.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Limit the sale of fireworks to those running local council approved events only" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732559

action: Require all healthcare services to provide free parking for medical students
background: We call on the Government to require all healthcare services to provide free parking for medical students.
additional_details: We think that doing this will show that the Government and the healthcare services care about students who will be the future of all our medical needs in the future.

action: Make Saint George’s Day a bank holiday in Great Britain
background: I would like the government to make Saint George’s Day a UK bank holiday . As other countries in the world Celebrate there patriotism to there Saints with a Bank Holiday I think the UK should as well
additional_details: This would show the people of the country that the government shares the British people there patriotism for our country . This would also boost morale amongst the population
rejection_details:
Make St George’s Day a Bank Holiday for people in England
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739078

action: Stop the sale of fireworks to the general public.
background: Stop the sale of fireworks to the general public. Only council organised displays on the 5th November & 31st December.
additional_details: Fireworks are the cause of misery to millions of animals and humans. Wildlife, live stock and mostly pets. Causing illness and death. Also humans with ptsd soldiers, people suffering with mental health and even those who suffer from fits. Use drone displays like a lot of forward thinking countries. Fireworks are used as weapons and basically you allow anyone to buy and use them. Dogs die from the fear of the noise. Humans would if they weren’t sedated. Puts chemicals in to our environment
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732559

action: Introduce UK Safe Haven Laws & fund baby boxes
background: Pass UK Safe Haven laws and fund the provision of baby boxes to protect abandoned babies. Every week, a baby is left vulnerable. We urge the Government to introduce these compassionate laws to provide a safe space for desperate parents to surrender their baby, ensuring care and support.
additional_details: When babies are abandoned in unsafe places, they're at risk of hypothermia, injury, and even death. Safe haven laws and baby boxes could provide a safe space for parents to surrender their baby, where parents know their babies will get medical attention and care. Many of these parents are facing unplanned pregnancies, lack of resources, or emotional distress. This could be a safe and anonymous surrender option where parents would know their baby is safe. This law could show that the UK values life and cares for its most vulnerable.

action: Review March 2024 rule on migrants bringing dependants to UK
background: We call on the UK Government to launch a review into changes to migration rules made on 11 March 2024 relating to bringing dependants to UK, as we believe they are separating legally married couples - especially those experiencing infertility, have no children and lived in the UK before the changes.
additional_details:
We respectfully urge the UK Government to review the migration changes introduced on March 11, 2024, which restricts the ability of migrants to bring or retain their legally married spouses as dependants.

For many couples, infertility is not a choice. It is a medical and emotional struggle involving years of treatment, testing, and financial sacrifice. We feel the current policy forces such families into an impossible decision.

action: Ban Hootananny Jools Holland
background: Axe the show as it is a waste of the licence fee
additional_details: It makes me ill to watch and know it's aired using my tax money

action: Fund the NHS to provide all services free at the point of use
background: We demand the Government to provide NHS funding to ensure all services are free to all and are based on clinical need rather than an individual’s ability to pay. We want the NHS to be free at the point of use for all for any medical, mental, age-related, optician and dental services.
additional_details:
We believe it’s time to recognise the holistic nature of all health aspects, from mental and physical health to elderly care, providing robust services that cover these areas comprehensively.

Some health services, such as dental and optician care, require fees or private contributions, making them inaccessible to many. Expanding the NHS to cover these areas comprehensively could ensure that healthcare needs are met equitably across the population.

action: Create a rising tax rate system and set an effective maximum income level
background: We would like the current tax band system in this country to be abolished, in favour of a formulaic system, where tax is calculated from a starting income of £45,000, rising to a maximum income figure of around £250,000.
additional_details:
Any income above this amount would be taxed at 100% in order to set a 'maximum income'.
 
We feel that there have been years of gross inequity in Britain, which have promoted a tax system that seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

action: Require all forms of public transport to have compulsory quiet areas
background: I would like the Government to require all forms of public transport to provide enclosed, quiet areas with doors where passengers are prohibited from using mobile phones and other electronic devices with the speaker on.
additional_details:
I feel it has become a regular occurrence now on public transport where a small group of people think it is acceptable to use their electronic devices on speaker. I believe this is disruptive and disrespectful for other passengers, and the content can sometimes be inappropriate.
 
I feel we should all be entitled to have a quiet area where we do not have to be subjected to this antisocial behaviour.

action: Stop Firework Displays
background: This petition is to advocate for the ban of Firework displays. In the 2025/26 new year’s eve celebration alone, the UK spent £30-40 million on fireworks.
additional_details: Fireworks pose significant distress to the vulnerable, including our pets, children, and veterans with PTSD. Furthermore, our environment. Firework displays can result in uncontrolled fires, and cause pollution. For these reasons, I urge you to consider the negative side of these “beautiful” fireworks, and think of your community, country, and Earth.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Ban both private and public use of fireworks & replace with cleaner alternatives" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750214

action: Require prisons to separate visiting children from all sex offenders
background: We want the Government to require prisons to run separate, safeguarded visiting sessions for prisoners convicted of sexual offences so that children visiting other prisoners are not exposed to them during visits.
additional_details: Children visiting parents in prison should be protected from exposure to prisoners convicted of sexual offences. Visiting arrangements allow many offenders with sexual convictions to attend visits at the same time and same space as children, causing distress to families. We think this is a serious safeguarding concern. Prison visits should be safe, child-appropriate environments. We are calling for mandatory separation of child visits from prisoners convicted of sexual offences to protect children’s safety.

action: Reform Child Maintenance Service, strengthen processes to protect paying parent
background: Reform CMS by calculating maintenance using net income, tax maintenance as income for the receiving parent, allowing reductions for denied contact, mandatory auditable arrears explanations, cease liability at 16, ensure due process before deductions, prosecute false declarations by either parent.
additional_details: We think the CMS lacks transparency, proportionality and due process and that it operates in favour of the receiving parent. Calculated on gross income, weak due process and opaque enforcement can disproportionately impact paying parents. Unexplained arrears, deductions and reasons can cause financial distress, instability and documented mental health issues. Reform is needed to align with basic tax principles, administrative justice, and accountability, while preventing misuse of the system.

action: Ban public use of fireworks on New Year’s Eve & promote quieter alternatives
background: We ask the Government to ban the use of fireworks by members of the public on New Year’s Eve, and to promote safer, quieter alternatives for celebrations, such as professionally organised drone light displays accompanied by music.
additional_details: Fireworks on New Year’s Eve cause severe distress to animals, especially dogs, and pose public safety risks. Loud explosions may trigger fear, panic, and injury; pets may escape or suffer medical emergencies. Cats, small pets, wildlife, and farm animals may also be affected. In London, animals may not be able to escape the noise.

action: Require employers to pay unused annual leave or carry it over to the next year
background: Every year 1000s of workers do not claim their full annual leave entitlement for many reasons. It should be law for employers to pay all unused holiday at the end of each year or carry it over. Employers budget for it and should not benefit from those who are happy to work rather than have time off.
additional_details: Only Parliament can create this law. We should not be in a use it or lose it system. I personally would love to see 2 weeks of unused holiday in my paycheck at the end of the year rather than being forced to take time off I'd rather not have.

action: Make sanitary products freely available in all public toilets in the UK
background: Require all publicly accessible toilets in the UK to provide free sanitary products, in the same way that toilet paper is provided, to ensure basic hygiene and dignity for all who need them.
additional_details:
Sanitary products are essential hygiene items, not luxury goods. Periods are unavoidable, and lack of access to sanitary products in public toilets can cause distress, missed education or work, and health risks.

Toilet paper is provided free in public toilets because it is necessary for basic bodily functions. Sanitary products serve the same purpose and should be treated equally.

Scotland has already made period products free by law, demonstrating that this policy is practical and effective. However, access across the rest of the UK remains inconsistent.

Making sanitary products freely available in all public toilets would reduce period poverty, improve public health, and promote dignity and equality.
rejection_details:
This is a duplicate petition of this one which you may wish to sign instead: 

Fund free female sanitary products in Public Restrooms
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741219

action: Make melatonin easier to obtain and prescribe in the UK
background: Make melatonin easier to obtain and prescribe by reclassifying it or enabling pharmacist-led supply. Currently, prescribing is difficult, often requiring conditions like an ADHD diagnosis, limiting access for many who need it.
additional_details: Melatonin helps regulate sleep and is used safely worldwide. In the UK, it’s hard to access and often requires a prescription, causing delays. Easier access could improve sleep health, reduce pressure on GPs, and provide a safer alternative to stronger sleep medications.
rejection_details: Decisions about the classification of medicines are a matter for the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), not the UK Government or Parliament. The MHRA is operationally independent from the Government.

action: Petition to Increase International Student Working Hours to 24 Hours per Week
background: We urge the UK Government to increase the term-time working limit for international students from 20 to 24 hours per week to protect the sustainability of UK universities and maintain the UK’s competitiveness in the global higher education market.
additional_details: Recent immigration policy changes, particularly the removal of the international student dependant visa, have reduced the UK’s attractiveness to prospective students. Declining enrolments have caused financial strain and redundancies across universities. A controlled increase in working hours would support students facing high living costs, ease labour shortages, stabilise institutions, and help the UK remain competitive with global education leaders.

action: Require all new magistrates to hold a law degree or independent legal experience
