action: Review the evidence and fund the addition of SMA to the Newborn Screening Test
background: We urge the UK Government to fund and help fast-track the process to add SMA to the NHS newborn heel-prick test. SMA is a rare genetic condition with devastating consequences if not treated early. Every baby should be screened at birth to allow early diagnosis and access to life-changing treatment.
additional_details: SMA was one of the leading genetic causes of infant mortality: up to 90% of untreated babies either died before age two or required permanent ventilation. It is now treatable, but treatment is most effective before symptoms appear. Early diagnosis can give babies the chance at a life without severe disability. Without screening, many babies are diagnosed too late. The damage already caused to their mobility, breathing and swallowing cannot be reversed. Scotland has committed to piloting SMA newborn screening this year. All babies should have the same chance. No child should suffer avoidable harm.
government_response_summary: The NHS is planning an in-service evaluation offering SMA screening to newborn babies in England. This will inform a decision on whether to extend the NHS newborn blood spot screening programme.
government_response_body: The Government is grateful to campaigners who have made a powerful case for doing more on screening for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). We are committed to seeing more children with SMA not just surviving but thriving.  Ministers and the NHS in all four nations of the United Kingdom are advised on all screening matters by the UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC), an independent scientific advisory committee which is made up of leading medical and screening experts. Where the Committee is confident that to offer screening provides more good than harm, they recommend a screening programme. Ministers in each of the four nations then make a decision on whether to accept the recommendation.  As recommended by the UK NSC, we are working at pace to roll out an In-Service Evaluation (ISE) in NHS screening services in England. An ISE is used where a change in screening policy is justified by strong evidence, but important evidence gaps still remain that can only reasonably be filled by evaluation in a live NHS setting. The UK NSC uses ISEs to support its screening recommendation process and inform wider policy decisions about screening.  There are a number of areas where evidence gaps exist which an ISE of newborn screening for SMA will help to fill:  1.	Feasibility The ISE will test the optimum clinical pathway and test methodology within the context of a nationally delivered newborn blood spot programme in the NHS, ensuring the safe movement of babies through the screening pathway. This includes testing the logistics of administering a programme that is delivered consistently by multiple geographically separated and commissioned screening and genetics laboratories, treatment referral centres and IT systems, including the establishing of sustainable data collection systems for longer-term outcomes.  2.	Acceptability Work is required to understand the acceptability and experience of families of screened babies and the healthcare professionals involved in the screening pathway, for example with regard to the timing and mode of delivery of results. This will support future decision making on the optimal screening pathway.  3.	Effectiveness Screening for SMA aims to screen, diagnose and treat babies before they have symptoms. The ISE will evaluate the timescales that can be met by UK services at important stages of the screening pathway, such as for result availability, clinical referral and the start of any treatment. The performance of SMA tests in an NHS environment needs to be evaluated to ensure the screening programme demonstrates test characteristics, such as accuracy, reproducibility, resilience and operational utility.  As the drugs to treat the underlying biology of SMA are quite new, there is no evidence on their long-term clinical effectiveness, so evaluating this within the context of the NHS Newborn Blood Spot Screening Programme is important. Gaining more data on short-term outcomes will contribute evidence as to how clinically effective screening in the UK is.  As the long-term effectiveness of novel treatments is currently unknown, the ISE will allow for sustainable longer-term health outcome monitoring systems to be established. This will provide an essential capability for assessing the effectiveness of the screening programme. This includes metrics such as health states, quality of life, mortality and psychosocial outcomes.  4.	Cost-effectiveness The economic model commissioned by the UK NSC estimates that SMA screening in the UK is likely to be cost-saving or cost-effective. However, there are important uncertainties that could affect the accuracy and conclusions of the model. The ISE will therefore identify further information to allow both clinical and cost-effectiveness to be assessed, using real world UK data. This includes:  •	costs involved in screening  •	clinical effectiveness of presymptomatic and symptomatic treatment and the impact of diagnostic delay on presymptomatic babies •	long-term effectiveness of treatment •	how accurate the screening tests are  •	which treatments patients receive and how effective these treatments are  •	incidence of SMA in the UK  The research component of the ISE is being commissioned via the National Institute for Health and Care Research. A decision on funding is expected in spring 2026.  The Secretary of State has asked NHSE to look at what can be done to move faster on the rollout of the ISE, and whether it would be feasible to extend the ISE to the whole of England.  The planning and development of the ISE is being overseen by a partnership board that includes:  •	screening experts from the four UK governments and from the NHS •	stakeholder organisations interested in newborn screening for SMA •	clinicians •	academics •	genomic experts •	patient and public voice representatives  SMA can have a devastating impact on individuals and families, and we are committed to working with all our stakeholders to progress this work in the UK.  Department of Health and Social Care  This is a revised response submitted by the Government. You can find the original response towards the bottom of the petition page https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/755980

action: Make all court and tribunal transcripts available free of charge
background: Make all court and tribunal transcripts available for free. Currently, fees can reach thousands, creating a "paywall" for justice. All legal records should be public property to help ensure transparency, allow for fair appeals, and support victims. Access to the law should not depend on wealth.
additional_details: High transcription costs can create a prohibitive paywall for justice. Private companies can charge thousands for transcriptions, which can effectively bar small-claims litigants from pursuing fair appeals or accessing their own trials. Full transcriptions of the longest trials can cost £20k. Access to the law mustn't be a luxury for the wealthy. We ask the Government to end the private-pay model and provide free digital access to all transcripts to help ensure transparency and equality.
government_response_summary: The Government is already increasing transparency in the courts, including expanding free access to Crown Court sentencing remarks.  Going further now would place even more pressure on the system.
government_response_body: The Government is committed to strengthening transparency across the justice system and is already taking significant steps across all jurisdictions.  In the Crown Court, sentencing remarks are now published online in cases of significant public interest, and judges can also permit broadcasters to film Crown Court sentencing remarks, ensuring greater public visibility of judicial decisions. Victims of rape and serious sexual offences and bereaved families of victims of homicide, manslaughter and fatal road accidents are already entitled to free transcripts of Crown Court sentencing remarks. These can be requested here: Apply for a transcript of a judge's sentencing remarks: Form EX107H (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/apply-for-a-transcript-of-a-judges-sentencing-remarks). From Spring 2027, the Government is expanding free access to Crown Court sentencing remarks to all victims, ensuring these remarks are provided in time to support any application to the Unduly Lenient Sentencing Scheme. The Government's ongoing reform of the criminal courts will further enhance transparency by making sure all hearings in magistrates courts are recorded.  In the family court, the Government has also been working to support the judiciary to increase the number of family court judgments that are published in anonymised form, while ensuring the privacy and protection of children and families involved in proceedings.  On more targeted transparency measures, the Government is working with the judiciary to roll out new provisions relating to Transparency Orders across England and Wales, providing a clear framework for reporting where a journalist or legal blogger has attended a family court hearing. Since 29 September 2025, provisions relating to Transparency Orders have applied to all children’s cases.   In civil proceedings, litigants in England and Wales do not need to pay for the written order or judgment relating to their own case; this is sent to all parties involved, setting out the court’s reasoning for the decision, which parties can refer to if they wish to appeal that decision.  In tribunal proceedings, any judicial decision and the reasons will be provided to the parties unless there has been an order restricting that. Many of the major tribunal chambers also allow parties to proceedings to request fuller written reasons for tribunal decisions for no additional cost.   The Ministry of Justice is also working with the judiciary and His Majesty’s Courts & Tribunals Service to consider the procedural, operational and resource requirements of implementing the publishing of written reasons for decisions in the Immigration and Asylum Chamber of the First-tier Tribunal, to improve transparency and public understanding.  While the Government remains committed to continuing to improve transparency across the justice system, this has to be balanced against our capacity to deliver existing priorities and commitments. Making all court and tribunal transcripts available for free would create significant financial and operational pressure at a time when we are focused on rolling out free sentencing remarks for all victims, and when the wider justice system is under considerable pressure. Producing an accurate court or tribunal transcript is a resource-intensive process. Full hearing or trial transcripts are particularly expensive due to their length and the level of quality assurance required to ensure they are accurate and safeguard personal data. Ensuring compliance with reporting restrictions is also central to the release of any court transcript, including vulnerable parties are protected and sensitive details are not inadvertently released.  The Government is committed to upholding the principle of open justice, including embracing AI and exploring the opportunities it offers to produce court and tribunal transcripts more quickly and cost-effectively, while still meeting the necessary accuracy and safeguarding standards. additional_details: A public inquiry could assess whether the public received accurate information, whether Brexit implementation was sufficiently prepared using thorough analysis and fact-finding, and whether institutional capability matched the scale of the policy. action: Fund routine blood test at 6-8 weeks for post partum mothers
background: We call upon the Government to fund routine blood testing for all post-partum mothers as a mandatory component of the 6–8 week postnatal check.
additional_details: Some symptoms of postnatal depression can actually be due to physical issues such as anaemia or thyroid dysfunction. By correcting these biological imbalances, we believe that we can ensure mothers are physically and mentally equipped to care for their babies during the critical postpartum period. While the NHS provides extensive prenatal checks for the baby, the lack of similar investment in maternal recovery is in our view a type of health inequality. When a mother’s health and wellbeing is considered and supported; her entire family benefits.

action: Stop kier starmer taking us back into the EU
background: Stop England rejoining the EU
additional_details: Because I want England to remain a sovereign country
rejection_details: The Government has not announced any plans to rejoin the EU.

action: Reduce age required for historic/classic vehicle status from 40 to 30 years
background: Historic/Classic vehicle status in the UK can be applied for when a vehicle becomes 40 years old, whereas many European countries allow this status to be applied for when a vehicle is 30 years old. We want to bring the UK rules into alignment with most of Europe.
additional_details: We feel that owners of historic and classic vehicles in the UK are penalised for a whole ten years more than most of our European cousins. Make “Historic/Classic” vehicle status available for vehicles when they are 30 years old. Many owners of classic vehicles have collections of multiple cars, and each one is required to go through annual MOT tests and pay road tax, even though owners really only use one vehicle at a time on UK roads. We believe this makes preserving British historic vehicles unfairly expensive.

action: Let low-income parents take kids on short term-time holidays without fines
background: Let low-income families take children on short term-time holidays without fines. We believe this would reduce inequality, help struggling families afford a break, and support children’s wellbeing, while keeping overall attendance rules in place.
additional_details: School holidays are expensive, making breaks unaffordable for many low-income families. Many children from wealthier families can travel, while poorer children miss out or parents face fines for taking them out of school in term-time. We think allowing limited term-time holidays for low-income families would reduce inequality, support children’s wellbeing, strengthen family bonds, and still protect overall school attendance.

action: Create a west midlands/ Birmingham transgender nhs clinic.
background: I want a nhs transgender clinic in the west midlands to serve the high volume of trans individuals in Birmingham and surrounding areas.  At the moment individuals have to choose between London and Nottingham and thats HOURS of travel, thats not fair or easy accessible. So I say let's build one.
additional_details:
With the government's assistant it can be built as it would be an nhs facility. One where educated doctors can help the queer individuals in the area.
Grants, building permission and hearty catalogue of doctors.

action: Mandate testing to stop PFAS and toxic chemicals in products sold across the UK
background: Research shows forever chemicals (PFAS) and VOC (volatile organic compound) contamination in UK products from food packaging to fresh produce, and everyday items. We call on the Government to mandate testing for all products before they reach consumers, ensuring only safe goods are sold.
additional_details: We believe consumers lack the expertise, equipment and resources to test for toxins like PFAS and VOCs, and that these checks require accredited labs and regulatory knowledge, making it impossible for individuals. We call on the Government to mandate that suppliers test any product they place on the UK market, as PFAS and VOCs can enter supply chains without the supplier’s knowledge. Suppliers should be required to verify whether a product contains PFAS or VOCs via UK accredited lab tests and maintain a national certificate register, ensuring safety before sale and giving consumers optional transparency.

action: Change The Legal Gambling age to 16
background: I think that the legal gambling age should be lowered to 16, especially when you can get a job at 15.

action: Abolish the Office of the Children’s Commissioner
background: We call on the government to dissolve the Office of the Children’s Commissioner. We think it is not independent enough from government and risks becoming politicised.
additional_details:
We also disagree with its promotion of the vision of children’s rights reflected in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). We think it is a threat to private and family life.

We believe there are two visions for our children's future: one respects the family, protecting its integrity, privacy, and freedom. The other, in our view, undermines it, believing that the state should direct the formation of our sons and daughters and the character of family life through global mechanisms such as the UNCRC. We reject this agenda and call for the abolition of the Office of the Children’s Commissioner.

action: Replace age verification process set out in Online Safety Act to voucher system
background: We the undersigned wish for the government to change how online age verification is currently handled because we have serious concerns about online security and the potential for fraud as a result of the current implementation requiring websites to do their own checks, often with data sent abroad.
additional_details: We believe the current system of going to a website and then being redirected to another website to share your ID, or a likeness, puts users at greater risk of fraud or impersonation online because often, these third party companies are sending users data outside of the UK and EU. There's already been examples of data leaks as a result of this. We call on the Government to instead set up a central database and allow people to verify their age in exchange for a voucher which could be used online without their ID being stored.

action: Call for a referendum to block joining the European Union
background: I would like to block the govermen from any negotiation on rejoining or getting closer ties with the European Union  by calling for a referendum in which only British  voters can vote
rejection_details: Petitions need to call on the UK Government or Parliament to take action. We are not clear on the action sought in your petition as the Government is not in the process of joining the EU.

action: Petition for UK recognition and  legal protection of the Benjamnist religion
background:
We therefore call upon the Government to:
*   Affirm that this religion may be formed and practised in the UK
*   Ensure equal legal protection for followers of newly established religions
*   Uphold freedom of religion without discrimination based on the age or size of a belief syste
additional_details: This Benjamnist religion is founded on principles of the Benjaminic Creed, the glory of the saviour King Ben, the balance of aura, and respect for others. Its followers seek the same legal protections and freedoms already afforded to existing religions, including the ability to gather, practise beliefs, and bet treated equally under the law.

action: Require banks to allow customers to set maximum caps on Direct Debit payments
background: Amend the Payment Services Regulations 2017 to require banks to provide a "Customer-Defined Cap" for Direct Debits. If a withdrawal attempt exceeds this cap, the bank must automatically block payment and notify the customer. Payment should only proceed when authorised and a new cap is set.
additional_details:
Current rules allow organisations to vary Direct Debit amounts with minimal notice, often too late for customers to act. For services like energy and water, estimated increases can often be overcalculated, causing financial hardship.
 
We believe this proposal ensures:
Protection: Customers are shielded from large or erroneous withdrawals.
Transparency: Organisations must provide clear calculations for any increase.
Control: Customers must approve increases or cancel before funds leave their account.

action: Ban HGV overtaking on motorways to help improve safety and traffic flow
background: The Government should introduce a ban on heavy goods vehicles overtaking on motorways, with exceptions only for passing stationary or broken-down vehicles. This should be supported by clear signage, effective enforcement, penalties, and alignment with road safety practices in parts of Europe.

action: Fully support Ukraine against Russia both financially and with our armed forces
background: Stand up to the Russian threat to the free world by giving Ukraine stronger support. Do not bow to the Putin threats. Engage with European partners and give Putin an ultimatum, back off or we join Ukraine against you. Do not make same mistakes that led to World War 2.
additional_details: Millions of men, women and children did not die by and suffer in WW11 so that the next generations could squander what they fought for. If we continue to show weakness against aggression by Putin it will, and has, emboldened him. Parliament and the government need to show some backbone. The country may have to pay a high price but we will prevail and be able to, as we did post WW11 come out of the situation knowing we did the right thing. God save the King.

action: Use Dartmoor Prison in the short term to house illegal asylum seekers.
background: Open Dartmoor prison to house asylum seekers in the short term while waiting to be processed instead of using hotels and houses of multiple occupancy.
additional_details: The cost of millions per week at the tax payers expense.
rejection_details: You could start a different petition calling for parts of the prison estate across the UK that are currently not being used to be made available for this purpose.

action: Require schools to accept part-time working requests for people with children
background: I would like the Government to legislate so all schools must accept part-time working requests from people who have had children and want to return to work by doing part-time working hours.
additional_details: I feel it is unfair that some schools allow these requests, while others refuse and may not provide a full explanation. I believe mothers should be able to put their own family at the forefront of their lives, whilst giving so much of themselves to other people’s children. Many schools do not allow part-time, and I believe it is unfair because many other schools do, despite them having the same job. I feel this is a huge part of the crisis in the retention of teachers.

action: Protect Workers and Contributors from Unfair Systems
background: We call on the Government to reform Employment Tribunal enforcement, government support services, and benefit entitlement rules to ensure fairness and proper support for individuals who have worked, paid taxes, and complied with the law in the United Kingdom.
additional_details:
We call on the Government to reform Employment Tribunal enforcement, government helplines, and benefit rules. Claimants should receive awards directly, with the state recovering money from employers. Helplines must provide practical guidance, and individuals who have paid taxes and National Insurance for years should receive support in their own right, not based on a partner’s income.
Conclusion:
Current systems place the burden, cost, and risk on law-abiding individuals while allowing employers and institutions to avoid responsibility. Reform in these areas would promote fairness, restore confidence in public systems, and ensure justice and support are real and effective.
rejection_details:
We understand that you are concerned about the operation of employment tribunals, but it is not clear exactly how the changes called for in this petition would differ from existing arrangements in this area. 

If you want the Government to pay any compensation arising from a tribunal case, then recuperate the money from the employer, then you could resubmit your petition to focus on that. 

You may find the following information helpful: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/work/employment-tribunal/employment-tribunals/before-you-go-to-the-tribunal/check-what-compensation-you-can-get-for-unfair-dismissal/

action: Introduce a team that specialises in civilian privacy and anti-censorship.
background: The UK government has been pushing its reach over legislation related to privacy and censorship without any sort of vote or two-sided conversation to discuss what UK residents would like. There needs to be a team dedicated to pushing back in favour of protecting the liberties these threaten.
additional_details: Digital ID has received the largest pushback of anything in the UK since 1990. People are familiar with the story of 1984 and are rightly terrified of the possibility of Orwell's story becoming reality. There needs to be a dedicated team that works, with the government, to protect citizen privacy and fight censorship. Organizations like Big Brother Watch are an inspiring example that stand up for these causes. Imagine what a similar team could do with government inclusion and funding.

action: Make government provide financial help to pubs and restaurants
background: We need the government to reverse the business rates increases and provide a VAT break to pubs and restaurants. If they don't then maybe people should consider spending the money for their tax payments in pubs and restaurants instead!
additional_details:
Pubs and restaurants are closing at an unprecedented rate and unless the government provides assistance to them by the time of the next election we will have lost too many.
The government need to provide assistance now or step down before they do irreversible damage to our hospitality sector. Let's hope the public spend money in pubs etc instead of paying their tax bills and also that all pubs, restaurants etc ban Labour MPs so they can sample what life will be like for us all in 2029!

action: Condemn attacks on Kurds in North Syria & use diplomatic pressure to bring peace
background: We want the UK Government to condemn attacks on Kurds in Northern Syria and use diplomatic pressure to stop any violence and work with international partners to promote lasting peace and stability and provide protection to Kurdish areas in accordance with Chapter VII of the UN Charter.
additional_details: Kurdish civilians in Northeast Syria have faced violence, displacement and instability from military operations. After years of conflict, we are concerned their situation risks getting worse without international pressure. We believe that the UK has a responsibility to uphold human rights and support vulnerable communities. Acting now could help protect Kurdish lives, reduce suffering, and promote long term peace and stability in the region.

action: Increase Personal Income Tax allowance to £14,000 to cover the State Pension
background: Raise the income tax personal allowance from £12,570 to £14,000 to cover the State Pension. This will put all State pensioners, including older pensioners who have paid into SERPS or the State second pension, on an equal footing until the end of this Parliament.
additional_details: We believe The Chancellor’s proposals that only those receiving the new State Pension will not face additional tax demands because of the Triple Lock are flawed in that they favour pensioners retiring since 2016 with the benefit of the New state pension and thus create an unfair system. We feel that older pensioners who in the past have paid into SERPS or the second state pension will be discriminated against by the Chancellor’s proposals.

action: Make the BBC a subscription only service.
background: Parliament must scrap the licence fee and make the BBC a subscription only service. Any form of UK taxpayer funding is totally unacceptable.
additional_details: The licence fee currently makes the BBC totally independent of public opinion or requirements. Whatever the BBC says or does its income is theoretically guaranteed by the iniquitous legally imposed licence fee. It is clearly insulting for TV viewers to have to pay a fee to the BBC so they can legally watch GB News, Sky News or ANY other live TV programmes. Objectors face prosecution with a fine or prison sentence by refusing to pay the licence fee.

Rename ‘BBC licence fee’ to ‘BBC subscription’

action: Require cooling off period with no-fee cancellation for UK flights
background: Introduce a regulation framework in respect of flight cancellation fees charged by airlines for flights to and/or from the UK, which is currently very unfair to the consumers. A cooling off period where no cancellation fee is incurred should be introduced for all UK flights and ticket types.
additional_details: Many airlines charge cancellation fees even minutes after booking, weeks before departure—often exceeding the ticket price. With near-zero digital processing costs, we think these fees are disproportionate and unjustifiable. This practice harms consumers and demands government protection; introducing fairer consumer regulations is paramount.

action: Make it mandatory for horse riders to wear body protection and helmets
background: Make it mandatory for all horse riders when on a horse wear body protection and helmet.
additional_details: My mum died from falling off horse - in the paperwork it was noted she was suitably dressed for horse riding including a helmet. There was no mention of body protection - which is available but not mandatory - if she was wearing this there is a chance her injuries may not have been life ending.

action: Use a permanent implanted tracker for murderers released on licence
background: I would like to see a permanent implanted tracker in perpetrators of murder released on licence, and an app that those affected by their crimes can use to track their whereabouts at all times.
additional_details: When perpetrators are released, those affected by their crimes may have constant fear of repercussions for the rest of their lives. I think if perpetrators on a life licence had a tracker permanently implanted it could help those affected to have a little bit of peace of mind to have the access to the whereabouts of the perpetrator.

action: Establish a legal right to have a bank account
background:
Because of societal changes and how we pay for goods and services over the last decade plus, I think the right to have a bank account should be enshrined in law.
In this modern age it is a necessity to have a bank account as it directly effects day to day lives of everyone.
additional_details:
I understand there may be circumstances to de-banking someone - for instance, criminal behaviour but there needs to be a limit on banks’ powers.
So I ask the Government to enshrine a legal right that at least a basic bank account should always be attainable. Where business accounts are concerned if there is no criminal reason to close them then they should also be protected as this could impact the employees that are connected to a business.
Protections must be put in place so people can live and work.

action: Ban the UK & constituent nation flags’ use for political purposes
background: Pass a law so no political party is allowed to use the national or constituent flags for any political purposes in any way. We want it to be a criminal offence to use, modify, alter or change the appearance of any national flag from the UK for political purposes.
additional_details: We believe the flags of the UK and constituent nations are being used by political parties and activists to suggest that they represent the values inherent in these flags. We feel this is dangerous, as we believe that our flags belong to all citizens, irrespective of their political views, race, gender, age or other descriptor. The flag should be a symbol of unity – the common denominator that reflects shared values. We believe they are too precious to be used to become a symbol not of what we share, but what divides us.

action: Say No to another HMO, within a tiny cul-de-sac
background: Yet again, another person making his money at the expensive of the local residents. We have been informed that there has been a planning application for a HMO, which will be to house 6 complete strangers.
additional_details: Within Yew Tee Road, homes have been within families for generations. Everyone living there have built a strong family community. We have Mom's/dads, Sister/brothers,sons/daughters,grandkids and grandparents living within Yew Tree road and the surrounding area. This like many parts of Smethwick is now at risk of losing this bond. Please help us stop this HMO

action: Approve dualling scheme for the A120 between Marks Tey and Braintree in Essex
background:
This petition calls on the government to put the A120 dualling scheme for the stretch between Braintree and Marks Tey back on the table.
This follows the strength of public opinion following the launch of the Colchester Gazette's newspaper campaign A120: Road to Safety.
additional_details:
The A120 continues to impact lives and livelihoods in north and mid Essex and our readers have told us how improvements are desperately needed. 
Why? It's simple.
* People are continuing to lose their lives due to the poor road conditions
* Residents’ lives and their homes are constantly blighted by the traffic
* The county’s economic growth is being stunted by lack of a suitable highway
Action must be taken NOW.
To support, please sign the petition. Together we can make change happen.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Ban private fireworks to protect animals
background: Introduce legislation to ban the sale and use of private consumer fireworks, restricting fireworks to licensed public displays, in order to protect pets, livestock and wildlife from distress, injury and long-term harm.
additional_details:
Fireworks cause severe distress and harm to animals each year. Pets, livestock and wildlife can experience panic, injury, escape attempts and long-term trauma due to loud explosions.

Private fireworks are used unpredictably over extended periods, making it difficult to protect animals. Restricting fireworks to licensed public displays would reduce suffering while allowing celebrations. The Netherlands has approved a nationwide ban on private consumer fireworks to protect animals.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Limit the sale of fireworks to those running local council approved events only

action: End the Ban on In-Cabin Air Travel for Small Pets dogs and cats Entering the UK
background: We ask the Government to amend UK pet travel regulations to permit in-cabin air travel for small pets on approved routes, subject to defined weight limits, approved carriers, pre-travel certification, microchipping, rabies vaccination, full compliance with UK biosecurity.
additional_details:
Allowing small pets to travel in the cabin would:
1.Improve animal welfare and reduce travel-related stress and trauma
2.Increase safety by keeping pets under direct supervision
3.Align the UK with international best practice
4.Support responsible pet ownership and family reunification
We ask the Government to review existing regulations and work with airlines, veterinarians, and animal welfare organisations to introduce a controlled and safe framework for in-cabin pet travel for small animals.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Allow small pets to travel in the cabin on flights entering the UK

action: Abolish the Old Basic State Pension — Give All Pensioners the New Pension
background: We urge the UK Government to end the unfair two-tier State Pension system by abolishing the old Basic State Pension and awarding the full New State Pension to all pensioners. The difference between the two grows each year. It is unfair and increasingly it a source of grievance.
additional_details: Many older pensioners now receive significantly less income purely because of their date of birth, despite having paid National Insurance for decades. This injustice leaves some of the oldest members of society struggling to meet basic living costs while others receive higher payments under newer rules. Equalising the State Pension would restore fairness, reduce pensioner poverty, simplify the system, and ensure every pensioner can live with dignity and security. End this unfairness now.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754460

action: Stop the government taking our country back into Brussels by stealth
background:
I would like the government to stop ignoring the referendum to withdraw from Brussels, we had a referendum to remain a sovereign nation.
This needs to be upheld, the government needs to stop taking us back by stealth, this is unacceptable on every level. The people of Great Britain have spoken.
additional_details: the government are ignoring the referendum, we voted clearly to stay a sovereign nation, Kier Starmer does not have the right or mandate to ignore the referendum result.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. The Government have not announced any plans to re-join the EU.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Do not introduce 6 month rule before learner drivers can take a test
background: Do not introduce rule that new drivers must wait 6 months before taking a test. There is a standard set by the government to pass a test. If it's passed by a new driver, it should be accepted as by the standards. Crash courses should be allowed.
additional_details: New young drivers can have a difficult world to enter, leaving home, renting and the difficult task of saving for a home and on often low wages. To drain them for a further 6 months of their hard earned money isn't right. How are they expected to get to work? This proposal could cause desperate youngsters to drive illegally or fall out of work.

action: Don't lower the blood alcohol levels for driving in the New Road Safety Strategy
background: Keep the blood alcohol levels at 80mg in the New Road Safety Strategy rather than lowering them to 50mg. We believe putting more effort into enforcement of the current levels (and also of detecting drug drivers) would be far more effective at making the roads safe.
additional_details: We do not think that drivers who drink one pint are high risk drivers or responsible for a high number of accidents (especially when compared with drug drivers). We are concerned that lowering the blood alcohol level to 50mg will kill off many social activities where people go for one drink after an event, and it will kill off Country pubs at a time the govt. is meant to be encouraging the hospitality industry. We believe that if we can't drive after having one pint people will not bother going and society, our social lives and pubs will suffer.

action: Ban AI chatbots while they are capable of creating Child Sexual Abuse Material
background: Generative AI chatbots on social media platforms have been fulfilling requests to make Child Sexual Abuse Material. Such chatbots must be banned, disabled or otherwise removed from public access until such a time as the government has received assurances that such material can no longer be produced.
additional_details: It is unacceptable that while the AI chatbots and their social media platforms are being investigated over the production of this material, that the Child Sexual Abuse Material is continuing to be produced, and at an alarming rate. The Government must immediately intervene to protect its citizens from the current and continued exposure to such material while waiting for the AI chatbots’ functionality to be fixed.

action: UK must act now & condemn the killing of Kurdish civilians in Rojava & Rojhilat
background: We urge the UK Government to act immediately to try to stop the killing of Kurdish civilians in Rojava and Rojhilat. The UK must condemn these attacks, raise them at the UN, press Syria and Iran to halt violence, support investigations, impose sanctions, and protect civilians.
additional_details: Kurdish civilians in Rojava and Rojhilat are facing deadly attacks, displacement, and fear. Entire communities are being targeted simply for who they are. The UK has a moral and legal duty to speak out, protect civilians, and act to prevent further bloodshed and humanitarian catastrophe.

action: Keep dogs on leads at all times to protect people, wildlife and other dogs
background: Requiring dogs to be kept on leads at all times would improve public safety, protect children, elderly and disabled people and reduce dog attacks. It would also safeguard livestock and wildlife, prevent road accidents, and give clarity to owners, councils and the public through one clear rule
additional_details: Keeping dogs on leads at all times will significantly improve public safety & animal welfare. Uncontrolled dogs can cause serious injury, distress & pose risks to children, people undertaking sporting activities (runners), elderly people & those with disabilities. Leads also protect livestock and wildlife, reduce road traffic incidents, and prevent conflicts between dogs. A clear nationwide rule would remove confusion, support responsible ownership, and help councils enforce safety consistently
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require all dogs to be kept on leads in public places
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750056

action: Change the amount of Sparx Reader Points required to complete homework to 200.
background: Lower the amount of Sparx Reader points you need to complete the assignment on Sparx Reader.
additional_details: Because many people spend hours a day trying to complete this assignment and most pupils want to lower the required amount to atleast 200 SRP.
rejection_details: This is a matter for Sparx, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Create a national database of convicted animal abusers
background: The database should be accessible to relevant authorities and regulated organisations, including local councils, animal welfare charities, veterinary professionals, licenced breeders, rescue centres, and organisations responsible for rehoming animals. Animal cruelty is a serious offence.
additional_details: Its purpose would be to prevent convicted animal abusers from owning, working with, breeding, or having unsupervised access to animals. It would also improve enforcement of animal disqualification orders, support safeguarding efforts, enhance public and animal safety, and strengthen existing animal welfare legislation. Appropriate safeguards should be included to ensure compliance with privacy and human rights laws. At present enforcement relies on fragmented records and inconsistent checks.

action: Fund new-born screening and more treatment for MPS Hurler syndrome
background: Improve early diagnosis and access to treatment for children with MPS Hurler syndrome, including clearer referral pathways and new-born screening, so children are not diagnosed too late to benefit from treatment.
additional_details: My son died at two and a half years old from MPS Hurler syndrome, a rare genetic condition. From an early age, we raised repeated concerns with GPs and hospitals but he was diagnosed very late. By the time treatment began, the disease was widespread and he passed away. Early diagnosis is critical for children with MPS. Clear national pathways could prevent other families experiencing the same loss.

action: Require panels of lay people to review abattoir CCTV footage for potential abuse
background: Since 2018, it's been mandatory for CCTV to be installed on all areas of abattoirs where animals remain alive. The recordings made being available to "official vets" only. This has not ended reports of animals being abused prior to slaughter, most of these reports coming from unofficial sources
additional_details: Recently, on 7 March 2025, the BBC reported on the Food Standards Agency’s investigation of an incident at the T&S Abattoir in Arley, Warwickshire. The local MP had raised the issue in the House of Commons the previous day, saying people were horrified by a video, posted online by an animal rights activist, that apparently showed hours of abusive behaviour at the facility in her constituency. More cases have been recorded by the Animal Justice Project, Animal Equality UK & others.

action: Require that all vehicles (except emergency services) are limited to 70mph
background: We want the government to require that all road vehicles are limited to 70mph using a speed limiter. The maximum speed for road users is 70mph and therefore no vehicle (other than emergency services) require a vehicle to exceed this speed.
additional_details: Reduce road accidents. Save tax payers money with less crashes.

action: Protect Kurds and Alevis in Aleppo – Stop Targeted Attacks Now
background:
We call on the UK Government and Parliament to act now to protect Kurdish and Alevi civilians in Aleppo and northern Syria from targeted attacks by extremist groups.
These attacks threaten innocent people because of their ethnicity and religious identity.The UK should not remain silent human rights
additional_details:
We ask the UK Government to:
	1.	Condemn these attacks publicly.
	2.	Provide urgent protection and humanitarian aid.
	3.	Support international accountability for those responsible.
	4.	Work with partners to prevent further violence.

If this petition reaches 100,000 signatures, Parliament will be asked to debate this urgent issue.

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756339

action: Increase waterway dredging to help prevent flooding
background: Increase dredging of our waterways to assist in preventing flooding. We view dredging as essential to enhance the water-carrying capacity of our rivers & streams. By increasing this capacity, we could significantly help reduce the risk of flooding, which threatens businesses, homes, & lives.
additional_details:
Riverbeds accumulate silt and debris over time, restricting water flow. Dredging can remove these obstacles, helping to improve waterways' capacity to handle heavy rainfall and to reduce flooding risks.

While some worry about the impact on flora and fauna, we think the greater threat lies in blocked waterways, which can suffocate aquatic life and disrupt ecosystems. We view dredging as vital for community protection & wildlife preservation. We urge decision-makers to prioritize dredging efforts.

action: Require the issuance of new death certificates for those containing errors
background: We call for the Government to require the issuance of new death certificates for death certificates that contain errors and need to be corrected, rather than issuing an amended certificate.
additional_details: When my wife passed away, the registrar made a mistake where she noted that my wife was my HUSBAND.  This error was not only deeply upsetting for me and my family, but also remained visible on the certificate. The only adjustment was an amendment at the bottom of the certificate, which I feel undermined the dignity of my wife's memory. We propose new legislation to require the issuance of a new certificate with the amendment in the correct place in order to preserve the dignity of loved ones who have passed away.

action: Direct train from Manchester Airport to Rochdale
background: There is a direct train from Manchester Airport to Leeds. I think is a bit useless that we have to make a stop in Victoria to then take a train (to Leeds) to arrive to Rochdale.
additional_details: Rochdale is the new  Town of Culture for 2025-26 I'm Greater Manchester. Adding this line from the Airport will bring more people and easier.
rejection_details:

action: Save the mountain bike jumps at Dartford Heath
background: to express concern over the repeated removal or destruction of the local mountain bike jumps in Dartford Heath. The jumps are not only a recreational feature but an important part of our community’s mental health, especially for young people and those who benefit from outdoor active lifestyles.
additional_details: Mountain biking provides a safe and healthy outlet for physical activity, creativity, and social connection. For many of us, the ability to ride and improve our skills in a natural environment is more than a hobby—it’s a crucial part of managing stress, anxiety, and overall mental health. These jumps are built by riders who take pride in their maintenance and use them respectfully and responsibly.

action: Publish a decision on the Park Home Sales Commission in 2026
background: We call on the Government to publish a final decision in 2026 on the future of the 10% sales commission charged to park home residents.
additional_details:
Over a decade of delay in Governments making a decision on this matter leaves older and vulnerable homeowners unable to plan their finances, move home, or pass on assets.
 
We urge the Government to:
Publish a clear decision in 2026 on whether the 10% commission will remain, be reduced, or be abolished
Set out a timetable for any legislative changes
Explain how consultation evidence has been assessed
Park home residents deserve certainty, fairness, and action, not more delay.

action: Stop solar farms being built on farmland and place them on all rooftops instead
background: Stop permitting solar famrs to be built on farmland of any type and instead place them on the roofs of all public buildings, tall buildings over 5 storeys and all carparks including building a roof on ground level carparks to hold the panels. Stop forcing farmers to sell their land for solar farms.
additional_details: As an island, and a once indepedant island, we need to our farmland to produce food. Raising meat, growing crops and feeding the british people with british food, we cannot eat solar panels. There is more than enough roof top space in cities and towns to accomodate enough solar panels. Stop placing them in farmland and put them on the roofs of all public building, buildings over 5 storeys tall, all large capacity buildings and all carparks
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban solar panels on farmland & require new build homes to have solar panels
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735942

action: After USA action in Venezuela the UK should’nt go to the World Cup & Olympics
background: I want the government to withdraw from the Olympics and World Cup to protest UK behaviour in Venezuela
additional_details: Because the US behaviour contradicts decent diplomatic behaviour
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

It is up to the Football Association, not the Government or Parliament, whether to take part in the World Cup. Deciding whether to participate in the Olympics is a matter for the British Olympic Association.

action: Make Carbohydrate Labelling Mandatory in all Restaurants and food establishments
background: Please consider advocating for legislation that makes the display of carbohydrate content compulsory for restaurant meals, in the same way that calorie labelling is currently mandated. This practical change would make eating out safer and more inclusive for thousands of people across the country.
additional_details: People with Type 1 diabetes must calculate and administer insulin doses based on the amount of carbohydrates in their meals. Without access to accurate carbohydrate information when eating out, they are forced to guess, which can lead to serious health consequences such as hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia.

action: Do not remove trial by jury for offences with sentences of three years or less
background: The Government should withdraw proposals to restrict jury trials for either‑way offences with likely sentences of three years or less, and should guarantee that such offences will remain eligible for trial by jury in the Crown Court.
additional_details: Trial by jury is a core safeguard rooted in Magna Carta 1215 and centuries of English constitutional practice, protecting the right of free citizens to be judged by their peers rather than the state alone. Curtailing jury trial in a wide range of criminal cases is difficult to reconcile with the fair‑hearing guarantees in Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights, as applied by the Human Rights Act 1998, and risks eroding public confidence in the justice system. No government should use a temporary majority to dismantle long‑standing common‑law constitutional rights without clear consent from the electorate. Parliament and the Government should therefore protect the availability of jury trial in serious and either‑way offences and drop plans for routine judge‑only trials
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Do not remove trial by jury for certain cases
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751480

action: STOP the construction of a 24hr waste and recycling plant in Wollaston NN29 7PR
background: The plant building will be 12m high & cover the area of half a football pitch. It will run 24 hrs a day and be visited by 25 trucks a day. It is 500m of a SSSI and nature reserve, harming rare migratory birds. It will affect local residents on a 24hr basis. Cyclists will be at risk of being hit!
additional_details: The SSSI is only 500m away from the proposed area. Pollution, noise, light and air from the proposed 24 hour operation at the plant will endanger the rare birds at the SSSI and the wider nature reserve. The area is a prime birdwatching location, and is home to rare birds like the Egyptian Goose and expanding species like the Little Egret. The area supports many transient and breeding birds. Traffic caused by trucks will increase the likelihood of a road traffic collision with local cyclists.

action: Change the term "lifetime sex offender registration” to reflect it is reviewable
background: We want the Government to amend legislation and guidance so that the term "lifetime sex offender registration” is reviewed and changed to reflect the term’s real definition and prevent victims or members of the public from being misled by this terminology.
additional_details: The term "lifetime" registration is widely understood by many to mean permanent registration for the remainder of an offenders’ life. In reality, individuals subject to lifetime notification requirements may apply to be removed after a qualifying period. We believe this mismatch risks misleading victims and the public, and undermining trust in the justice system.

action: DO NOT SEND BRITISH TROOPS TO UKRAINE
background: We ask the Government to reconcider its policy to send British troops to Ukraine,  sending British troops to Ukraine would be a disaster and could lead to a war with Russia nobody wants as well as leading to deaths and casualties never seen since the first World War.
additional_details: The idea of EU troops on Ukraine territory is not favoured by all NATO countries, Hungary, Poland, Chechia, Spain, Slovakia and Italy have all said they would not send troops to Ukraine so there is a deep split in NATO on this subject.  The only way for peace is for Europe including Britain to have sensible dialogue with Russia on ways to come to a permanent peace.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Commit to not deploying British Troops to Ukraine
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747668

action: Have a general election
background: Dissolve the government and have a general election.
additional_details: The country has lost any confidence that it had in this government and requires a general election in preference to open rebellion.
rejection_details:
We already have a petition open on this subject which you might like to sign:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

action: Make Grade 3 a pass in England
background: Make Grade 3 a pass in England since the youth are struggling with their mental health if they aim lower they are not burnt out about able to achieve more in their education and later career
rejection_details: This is a matter for schools and exam boards.

action: Let Scottish Fontan Patients Stay Home for Life-Saving Heart Transplants
background: I was born with Tricuspid atresia unventriculated heart disease. I survived because of the Fontan heart bypass and Extra Cardiac Fontan heart surgery. Fontan circulation is not a cure it fails. When it does a heart, lungs and/or liver transplant is the only way to live.
additional_details:
Scottish Fontan patients are forced to leave Scotland for life saving transplants separating us from family and support at the most terrifying time of our lives. This is not choice it is a failure of the system. NHS Scotland must allow Fontan patients to be assessed and transplanted in Scotland.
Let us fight for our lives at home. 
We are not numbers or referrals. We are people terrified of dying far from home, asking for the chance to live — with dignity, love and support — in Scotland at Home.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

You may also wish to contact your local council and MSP who represent you about this issue. 

You can find the name of your local council and how to contact them here: https://www.mygov.scot/find-your-local-council

You can find the name of your local MSP and how to contact them here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps

action: Remain neutral in foreign conflicts
background: We demand the government declare Britain a neutral state. We believe that neutrality will protect British interests, safeguard our national security, and uphold our tradition of diplomacy and peacekeeping in an increasingly polarised world.
additional_details:
We think the world is entering a new phase of global tension, with increasing confrontations between major powers. In our view, the UK is at risk of becoming entangled in these geopolitical conflicts. We propose a neutral stance that we think could prioritise British security, protect our economy, and allow Britain to serve as a mediator, promoting diplomacy and peace on the international stage.

We think Britain is no longer a super power on the level of America, China, or Russia.

action: Withdraw UK commitment to 2030 UN Agenda for Sustainable Development
background: We demand that the UK Govt. immediately withdraws its commitment to the UN 2030 Agenda’s sustainable development goals, to ensure the UK’s withdrawal before 2030, and the reversal of any steps or agreements that align with the 2030 UN Agenda.
additional_details: We believe the 2030 UN Agenda is a terrible plan and we are concerned that it will be the citizens of individual UN member states who will suffer, with their freedoms curtailed and lost.

action: Call on Denmark to invoke NATO's Article 4 due to USA's statements on Greenland
background: The UK must call on Denmark to lead NATO consultations under Article 4 and subsequently issue a new joint statement rejecting the USA's statements. Push more strongly for clear NATO unity and greater respect for international law. Make the UK’s position known more loudly.
additional_details: This is about security. NATO exists for collective defence and trust under Article 5. This matters. We think the USA’s statements on Greenland weaken that trust and put UK security at risk. Article 4 allows allies to consult when territory or independence is threatened. When a powerful ally makes threats, the alliance is undermined. If the UK is silent other members may doubt support. We think a new united message would strengthen NATO unity and protect UK defence interests.

action: Create a formal appeal process for Coroners’ inquests
background: We want the Government to introduce legislation creating a clear right of appeal against Coroners’ inquest conclusions, allowing families to challenge findings where there are errors of law, procedure, or failures to properly examine state involvement or evidence.
additional_details: At present, there is no effective way for families to challenge Coroners’ inquest conclusions, short of judicial review or with the Attorney General’s consent, even where there are serious errors, procedural failings, or failures to properly examine state involvement. We believe this leaves families without accountability or redress and risks public confidence in the inquest system, particularly in deaths involving detention, healthcare, or state care.

action: Protect Access to Lawful Digital Platforms
background: Call on Parliament to respect that UK governments are elected to serve the people, not to control lawful speech. Adults must retain the right to access legal digital platforms, with any restrictions subject to democratic consent and full parliamentary scrutiny.
additional_details: In the UK, governments are elected to serve the people, not to rule them. Their role is to protect stability, rights, and public trust—not to decide which lawful information adults may access. If the people oppose a policy, that voice matters. Banning a lawful platform would undermine democratic consent and set a precedent where public will is overridden by executive control.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We don't know what you mean by "lawful digital platforms".

action: Lift the ban on regulated sales of raw (unpasteurised) drinking milk in Scotland
background: Urge Govt & Food Standards Scotland to lift ban on raw (unpasteurised) milk/cream sales. Allow regulated direct sales (farm-gate etc) with testing, hygiene & warnings, as in rest of UK, for informed adult choice like alcohol/cigarettes.
additional_details:
Scotland completely bans raw (unpasteurised) milk/cream sales, unlike England, Wales & NI which allow regulated direct sales (farm-gate, markets) with testing, hygiene, TB-free herds & warnings.
Informed adults deserve choice for raw/organic milk (taste, benefits), similar to cigarettes, alcohol, gambling & energy drinks despite risks.
Review to permit safe, controlled sales, balancing health & farmer support.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/
