action: Student discount at major grocery stores
background: Impliment madatory student discount at grocery stores, percentage off whole shop as opposed to vouchers or deals currently available. Students find it hard to pay for accommodation as well as the university fees and groceries. Let alone anything else.
rejection_details: Pricing and discounts in supermarkets are a matter for the supermarket in question.

action: Stop Armed Services Pensions from being Taxed
background: To cease taxing Armed Service Veterans pensions.
additional_details: Review the whole of the armed services pensions. Keep them free from taxation. Remember many armed service veterans have had to put up with Poor accommodation, Poor Pay & poor conditions during their service careers. It is a total insult to tax these pensions. They should not be taxed. Armed service personnel are not respected or looked after in this country & never have been. Charities have to fill the gaps that Governments should be fulfilling. No wonder its hard to recruit,
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Make the Armed Forces pension tax free
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/733797

action: Require tax agents to share liability for errors in tax returns they prepare
background: Introduce legislation so that any person or company preparing and submitting tax returns on behalf of others is jointly liable for penalties, interest, and losses arising from errors caused by their negligence, misrepresentation, or failure to meet professional standards.
additional_details: Taxpayers are legally responsible for their returns even when they reasonably rely on paid professionals to prepare and submit them. This creates an imbalance where individuals bear the full consequences of errors they did not make or understand. Shared liability would improve accountability, protect consumers, raise professional standards, and strengthen trust in the tax system without penalizing compliant advisers.

action: Allow those with a freedom pass to enter the transport system before 9am
background: Allow those with a freedom pass to enter the transport system with their pass before 9:00am and not have to wait until 9:00am to get on the bus or tube with their pass
additional_details: I want the government to do this because those with a freedom pass (mainly O.A.P’s) have hospital and or doctors appointments before 9:00am at times. Appointments sometimes cannot be changed and this doesn’t help with their independence when they then rely on someone else to have to take them because they can’t afford to pay for the bus.
rejection_details:
This is not a central Government responsibility but a local/London responsibility GLA/TfL

If you want Govt funding for free bus passes nationwide for over 65s to apply at peak as well as at non-peak times you could submit a petition on that subject.

action: Ban councils from using third party litter enforcement companies
background: Councils often employ third party companies to hand out fines for the dropping of litter. These companies are driven by profit. We want this practice to end and councils must employ their own enforcement employees.
additional_details: Companies hold contracts for litter enforcement in our cities. They have huge amounts of complaints regarding the way they approach litter enforcement. We are concerned that for some companies their income is generated by how many fines they hand out, which we think brings into question the honesty of these unregulated enforcement officers.

action: Make Children’s Zip Oyster Cards Available Digitally
background: We want the Government to work with TfL to introduce a digital option for children’s Zip Oyster cards, allowing them to be used on phones. This should include proper checks and remain optional, so physical cards are still available.
additional_details: Children rely on public transport daily for school, activities, and getting home safely. Physical Zip Oyster cards are easy to lose or forget, which can lead to fines or children being unable to travel despite being entitled to free or discounted travel. This also causes accidental fare evasion. A digital Zip card would reduce stress for families, prevent unfair penalties, and modernise the system to reflect how people travel today.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. It is the responsibility of Transport for London, the Mayor of London and the London Assembly.

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Join the EU Customs Union
background: There was a ten minute motion voted on in Parliament on the 9th December 2025 that got more votes for yes (Joining the Customs Union). We as everyday citizens wish to see the UK rejoin the EU Customs Union to boost trade with our closest trading partner.
additional_details: The UK economy has not done so well over the last 10 years. Some of this can be attributed to the financial costs associated with Brexit. Rejoining the Customs Union will be a move that will help grow UK GDP and show a willingness to the EU that we are a nation that is keen to reset the relationship with the EU.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: 

Apply to re-join the Customs Union
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754234

action: School should start at 9:15 and end at 2:30 to boost student well-being.
background: School should start at 9:15 and finish at 2:30 to support student well-being. Later start times help teens sleep properly, improve focus, and boost morale, while shorter days reduce stress and create a healthier, more productive learning environment for all students.
additional_details: We want Parliament to support changing school hours to 9:15–2:30 because student well-being is a national concern. Teens need adequate sleep to learn effectively, stay healthy, and maintain morale. By adjusting school hours, Parliament can set a positive example, reduce stress, improve focus, and help students across the country reach their full potential
rejection_details:
Decisions about what time the school day starts and ends are a matter for schools, not the UK Government or Parliament.

You may wish to sign some of the petitions that we already have open about the school day.

action: The right to sack Members of Parliament
background: Give us the right to remove MPs that are not properly representing their constituants and deviating from their manifesto promises.
additional_details:
For too long MPs have blatently lied to the public to get elected and either gone back on election pledges or just done the opposite, this cant continue, MPs should be accountable to the public for their bad policies, the public need the right to easily remove bad MPs.
If 35% of the turnout of the previous election demand it a new election should be called in the constituancy.
rejection_details:
Give people power to dismiss MPs – change the Recall of MPs Act
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732555

action: Review category tyre fitment to vehicles specific to seasonal conditions
background: Winter tyres or all season winter categorised tyres greatly outperform Summer tyres in snow and ice. Most new cars are fitted with Summer tyres which give very little traction/grip in snow or ice. Summer tyres actually lose a great amount of traction/grip in temperatures around 0 Degrees C.
additional_details: Having the correct tyres on a motorcar for the UK climate conditions such as All season winter categorised tyres (which can be used all year safely) or summer tyres only during warmer months and Winter tyres during colder months could result in a huge reduction in delays on roads during snowfall saving lost time and money from the U.K. economy. It could make roads safer and possibly save lives. Some new cars are fitted with Summer tyres and these are not designed to work in winter conditions. We call on the Government to take action on this matter.

action: Revoke recognition of the United States Declaration of Independence 1776
background: Bill to be passed stating the UK no longer recognises the legal status of the USA as an independent country, and the original Thirteen Colonies to be legally returned to The United Kingdom of Great Britain.
additional_details:
The Declaration of Independence is only legitimate if other countries accept its legal status. What is the basis of their territorial claim to this land except a piece of paper.  
It can be agreed that nobody is going to fight the United Kingdom militarily over the future of America.
For the future security of NATO and the West, It is imperative that these Thirteen Colonies are brought under the control of the United Kingdom. 
We cannot allow a failed project to continue for another 250 years.
rejection_details: We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

action: End Default Religious Slaughter Without Choice
background: Require clear labelling of halal and kosher meat, end its default use in public institutions, guarantee a non-halal/non-kosher alternative, and ensure informed consent and consultation so that all religious, ethical, and moral beliefs are respected equally.
additional_details:
Religious freedom for all religions should be protected, but problems arise when religious slaughter standards are introduced as a default without clear labelling, consultation, or the ability to opt out. Clear information, genuine alternatives, and consent are essential for fairness, choice, and public trust.
Consent, respect, and genuine choice must apply equally to all religious, ethical, and moral beliefs which currently is sadly lacking
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require non-stunned and stunned meat to be labelled accordingly
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737327

action: Stop Violent Suppression of Peaceful Protesters and Internet Blackout in Iran
background: Condemn the violent suppression of peaceful protesters in Iran, impose targeted sanctions on individuals and entities responsible for human rights violations, and work with international partners to restore internet access and protect civilians.
additional_details: Iranian security forces have reportedly used lethal force against unarmed civilians during nationwide protests. At the same time, authorities have imposed a full internet blackout, preventing families from contacting loved ones and blocking the documentation of human rights abuses. The UK must act to defend human rights and protect civilians.
rejection_details:
The Government is already taking steps in this direction.  See this recent Urgent Question: 
https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2026-02-03/debates/9CF7A5A9-1F44-44AD-917F-15F55C597CE6/Iran

The UK Government has indeed condemned the violence and brought in sanctions against an increasing number of individuals and entities in Iran (some had been sanctioned before the current unrest began):
https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-announces-sanctions-against-perpetrators-of-human-rights-violations-in-iran

action: Legislate protective laws around trans people consequential to the court ruling
background: I have seen friends and acquaintances, marginalised, harassed, and bullied for their gender identity, and now this new supreme court ruling has further increased the threat that trans people continue to face. Developing laws to protect trans people would help support these individuals greatly.
additional_details: Those who do not identify with their assigned gender at birth make up only around 0.5% of the population. The number of hate crimes against trans people in England and Wales has risen in the past ten years from 607 annually in 2015, to 4120 in 2025. Transgender people are entitled to the same human rights as gender conforming people, and shouldn't face invalidation from their own government. Please, support this beautiful minority, by making new legislation, education, healthcare, and support.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We understand that you would like more laws in place to protect transgender people, but we're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly exactly what you'd like those laws to do.

action: ​Increase 'Expensive Car Supplement' threshold to £50,000 for Hybrid vehicles.
background: ​We call on the Government to raise the threshold for the Expensive Car Supplement (the "luxury car tax") from £40,000 to £50,000 for all petrol and diesel hybrid vehicles, matching the upcoming threshold increase for fully electric vehicles.
additional_details:
Stop the unfair "Luxury Tax" on family hybrids! 
​The £40k tax threshold is outdated. While EVs get a raise to £50k in April, hybrid drivers are being left behind. We’re calling on Parliament to raise the limit to £50k for all hybrids to keep green motoring affordable.
​Sign & share to tell the Govt to fix the Expensive Car Supplement! 
​
rejection_details:
Review the Expensive Car Supplement
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738766

action: Repeal Net Zero targets & Climate Change Act. Stop Renewable energy expansion
background: We think Government MUST immediately revoke ALL Net Zero Targets & The Climate Change Act 2008. Since this became law numerous scientists up to Nobel Laureate level have jointly declared "There is NO climate emergency". The raised energy prices are impacting the UK's living costs & economy.
additional_details:
Current policies are based on just one side of what we consider to be a two-sided scientific debate, as we do NOT believe there is a consensus among scientists that human emissions cause or influence climate change.
 
We think this is not a basis for significant UK legislation. We think that Net Zero & renewable energy targets cause UK's economy & citizens to suffer high energy costs & that expanding renewable energy takes good farmland. Net Zero MUST end & be reconsidered with evidence from ALL sides.

action: Hold an inquiry into Healthcare Professionals dying by suicide.
background: To help us understand potential reasons for healthcare professionals dying by suicide. To make recommendations to governing bodies and workplaces on how to reduce suicides and improve staff mental wellbeing, and ensure adequate funding is in place to carry out the recommendations adequately.
additional_details:
There is evidence suggesting that on average, one nurse dies by suicide a week and one doctor every 3 weeks. That is not taking into account other healthcare workers.

It is a tragedy that we are losing healthcare staff in this way. This loss needs to be understood in depth, along with moral injury, safe staffing and psychological safety. Effective strategies and funding must be put in place to support staff and create accessible systems that are safe for staff and patients.

action: Allocate share of per-pupil education funding to support home-educated children
background: We believe home-ed families should receive a share of per-pupil funding to support resources as home-ed children are entitled to a suitable education, yet families currently receive no direct funding, despite the state saving thousands of pounds when a child is educated outside the school system.
additional_details:
Home-ed families must fund all educational materials, exam fees, group learning spaces, and enrichment activities themselves. Many home-ed children benefit from shared learning environments, such as home ed groups, co-operatives, and community classes. 
 
We ask the Government to introduce a fair, accountable funding mechanism, such as:
Education grants or vouchers for registered home-educated children. Proportionate per-pupil funding that follows the child, not the institutions.

action: Fund free NHS dental treatment for injuries from domestic abuse or violence
background: The Government should provide dedicated funding and require the NHS to provide for free any dental treatment needed because of injuries caused by domestic abuse or violent assault, and issue clear national guidance stating that such injuries be recognised as medical and trauma-related, not cosmetic.
additional_details: Survivors of domestic abuse and violent crime are often left with visible dental injuries caused by violence. We are concerned that many may be told the treatment they need is “cosmetic” and must be paid for privately, even though the damage was inflicted through abuse or assault. These injuries can affect mental health, confidence, work, and daily life, and can be constant reminders of trauma. Injuries caused by violence are not cosmetic. Survivors deserve NHS-funded dental care that recognises trauma and supports recovery.

action: Give children 5 school days of "bookable" leave per academic year
background: To enable children to spend time away from school with family. These could be for day trips, holidays that are affordable or just to reinforce the love and care that children need from their guardians, as we believe families are crucial to a functioning society and supporting those bonds is key.
additional_details:
We seem to have a society that punishes families for spending time together. Local authorities can fine parents for making memories with their children.  Some businesses profit from this by raising prices for many things during school holidays. 
 
Allowing children 5 school days per year to book off, like employed people do, will, we feel, allow families time together to bond and build relationships with their children that will benefit them forever. Society benefits from healthy happy families. We would extend this to people employed by schools, so they too can take advantage and enjoy these days with their own children.

action: Set a maximum 6‑month diagnosis target for endometriosis
background: With diagnosis of endometriosis taking on average 8-10 years, I am calling for a national 6‑month diagnosis target, supported by mandatory GP training, a clearer NHS process for assessment and referral, and increased investment in specialist services.
additional_details: Endometriosis affects 1 in 10 women, yet many wait years for a diagnosis. These long delays cause avoidable pain, disruption and distress, often affecting daily life and the ability to work. Earlier diagnosis would improve wellbeing, reduce long‑term harm and avoid the £12.5 billion annual cost to the NHS and wider economy. A 6‑month diagnosis target supported by better GP training and clearer assessment and referral, is essential to improving the welfare of those with symptoms of endometriosis.

action: Increase the Local Housing Allowance and freeze private rents
background: In London, private tenants may pay around £2,500 per month for a three-bedroom home, compared to around £700 for council housing. To address this gap, the Government should fund increases to the Local Housing Allowance annually and rent freezes.
additional_details:
We believe Local Housing Allowance (LHA) should increase annually in line with inflation, and private rents should be frozen. Many people cannot access social or council housing due to long waiting lists, leaving private renters with no choice.
 
In London, council tenants may pay around £700 per month for a three-bedroom home, while private renters could pay about £2,500 for the same property. We feel this is unfair and places severe financial pressure on private renters, and that the Government should fund LHA increases and rent freezes.

action: Ban MPs from foreign interference to focus on domestic duty and national unity.
background: I propose a new Diplomatic Neutrality Act to restrict backbenchers from "freelance diplomacy." MPs should be barred from private lobbying of foreign courts or governments, ensuring foreign policy remains the sole remit of the Executive while refocusing parliamentary efforts on domestic issues.
additional_details: The Act would mandate that all international engagements by MPs be pre-cleared by the Foreign Office to prevent "dual-track" diplomacy. Crucially, it would include a social media ban on commenting officially or privately on the internal legal or political affairs of sovereign states. By prohibiting foreign-funded lobbying and digital interference, we protect national security and ensure MPs prioritise domestic duties over global grandstanding and online partisan conflict.

action: Make Post Separation abuse a specific offence
background: As survivors we call for mandatory post-separation abuse training across all statutory bodies; extension of Claire’s Law after separation; PSA as a stand-alone offence; automatic restraining orders; extended survivor protection; and PSA education in all prevention and perpetrator programmes.
additional_details: Post-separation abuse is one of the most overlooked forms of domestic abuse. For many survivors, leaving does not end the harm — it escalates. Perpetrators use child contact, the courts, finances and ongoing harassment to maintain control. Without recognition as a specific offence, this abuse is minimised and misunderstood. Naming post-separation abuse in law would validate survivors’ experiences, close dangerous gaps, and ensure accountability where it belongs.
rejection_details:
Controlling or coercive behaviour is a crime in England and Wales under section 76 of the Serious Crime Act (2015). This law highlights that domestic abuse is often a purposeful pattern of behaviour.

The Domestic Abuse Act (2021) for England and Wales extended this offence to include post-separation abuse. This changed the law so that controlling or coercive behaviour can now potentially be prosecuted as a criminal offence even if the parties are no longer in a relationship and are not living together.

Parents may be forced to choose between paying IHS fees and meeting basic household needs such as food. Changing this could strengthen social cohesion, reduce poverty, and uphold the UK’s values of fairness and opportunity for all.

action: Fund free oral health checks for people with diabetes as part of NHS care
background: We want the Government to integrate free, routine oral health checks for all diagnosed diabetes patients into NHS diabetes care pathways. This could be delivered through NHS dental services or commissioned screening programmes, with appropriate referral pathways for further treatment where required.
additional_details:

action: Stop any inclusion of financial penalty clauses in future UK–EU agreements

Such clauses could bind future electorates to decisions they did not vote for and restrict the ability of elected governments to respond to changing public mandates. International agreements should allow lawful withdrawal without punitive financial penalties.

action: Press for international action to restore internet access in Iran
background: We ask the UK Government to work with international partners to oppose internet shutdowns in Iran and support the restoration of full internet access, so people can communicate safely and human rights abuses can be reported.

action: Replace RPI with CPI in the calculation of interest added to student loans

additional_details: This could reduce the speed at which debt increases. We believe young people should not be saddled with large debts if we want to see young people go to university to get better qualifications and better jobs, and to assist students from low-income families to escape poverty. We are concerned loan debts could hold them back financially in the property market and cause children of low-income families to borrow more and have larger debts. Changing RPI to CPI, backdated to 2011, could help reduce the accrued debt from interest additions.

action: Review the digitisation of UK telephone lines
background: Copper land lines, while ‘old technology’, provide resilience and mitigation for poor cellphone signal in many rural areas, and work during power cuts. We think digital rollout is a national strategic risk and should be subject to a review.
additional_details: Storm Goretti left many Cornish households without electricity for up to 4 days. Digital phone lines do not work during power cuts, leaving people unable to seek help when their homes are damaged by storms or check on vulnerable relatives. We believe land lines need to be independent of electrical supplies and function during power cuts.

If a dog kills livestock, another dog, or injures a person, laws are stronger but dog attacks on cats are not specifically covered. Often a dog can kill without consequence. This is unfair and outdated.

Cats deserve the same protection as other animals if not more. Their emotional value is immense. Let’s make the law reflect that.

action: Sever UK-Iran ties, withdraw recognition of Iran’s regime & expel all diplomats
background: We urge Parliament to severe all diplomatic ties with Iran, withdraw recognition of the regime as the legitimate government of Iran, and expel any Iranian diplomats from the UK, in the wake of recent events and reported human rights abuses that have been committed there.
additional_details: We believe the Islamic Republic of Iran has neglected the needs and will of its people for 47 years. Now, people are in the streets demonstrating against the regime and calling for a transition to democracy. Rather than listening and accepting their demand, the regime has decided to cut internet access, phone lines, and other means of communication with the outside world, and are reported to be suppressing protesters with live ammunition, which have killed thousands.
government_response_summary: The Government condemns Iran’s destabilising actions, but believes relations are essential to protecting British nationals, holding Iran to account, reducing escalation and supporting diplomacy.
government_response_body: For decades, Iran’s behaviour across the region has caused instability, fear and suffering. Its nuclear programme remains of significant concern. The regime has used violence to suppress the Iranian people and also pursued activities that endanger peace beyond its border.  In the UK, a number of Iran-backed plots have been disrupted over the past year.   We are clear about the seriousness of the domestic threat and are taking the necessary actions to counter it. Iran’s ongoing reckless attacks on countries in the region are unacceptable, and we condemn them in the strongest terms. We have been clear to Iran: it must put an end to these activities.  The petition calls for the UK to sever ties, withdraw recognition and expel Iran’s diplomats. We understand why people might support these steps. However, the Government’s responsibility is to protect British lives and interests while working for a safer and more stable Middle East.  Our priorities remain: preventing Iran from developing a nuclear weapon; supporting regional stability and protecting UK economic and security interests; protecting the UK against state threats from Iran; providing support for British Nationals; and preventing the regime from using violence to suppress its people.  We believe that maintaining our diplomatic relations, and the ability to apply firm and coordinated pressure on Iran, is essential to pursuing these objectives. Our relationship allows us to deliver clear messages directly to the regime. We still believe that a negotiated outcome is the best way to address the nuclear issue and reduce wider regional risks. Keeping channels open preserves important diplomatic leverage. Cutting ties would narrow the options available to us.  This also applies in the context of the current conflict. The UK has not been involved in the strikes on Iran. We have taken the decision to accept the US request to prevent Iran firing missiles across the region, thereby helping to prevent attacks that could kill innocent civilians, put British lives at risk and hit countries that have not been involved. We urge Iran to urgently choose a different course, cease its reckless attacks, and demonstrate willingness to reengage in a diplomatic process. The Government will continue to press for diplomacy.  Iran currently poses an unacceptable level of threat to people in the UK. These threats stem from the activities of the Iranian Intelligence Services, including of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the Ministry of Intelligence and Security, and the criminal proxies and enablers they use to carry out their work. Maintaining diplomatic relations enables us to deliver robust messaging directly to the regime to stress that this behaviour is unacceptable.  Consular support and crisis response rely on having channels of communication. Withdrawing recognition and expelling diplomats would severely limit our ability to assist British nationals in Iran or respond to urgent issues affecting their safety. Even when relations are strained, having a channel to demand access, raise concerns and work with partners can be critical. Ending diplomatic ties would weaken our ability to support British nationals in Iran and advocate for those at risk.  The UK condemned Iran’s deliberate and appalling use of violence and brutal killing of protestors, arbitrary detention, and the use of intimidation tactics by security forces against demonstrators. We have demanded the Iranian authorities respect the fundamental rights and freedoms of their citizens.  Maintaining diplomatic relations strengthens the UK’s ability to hold Iran to account for its treatment of its people. It enables direct and unambiguous communication with those in power, allows the UK to raise concerns about the treatment of protesters and minorities, and supports coordinated pressure with international partners.  Our actions at the UN Human Rights Council in January to highlight these abuses – together with the targeted sanctions imposed on 2 February on those responsible for human rights violations – carries greater weight when we are able to engage directly with the Iranian authorities.  The UK’s position is firm. Iran’s regime is responsible for appalling actions and must never be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon. The Government will remain engaged, apply pressure, and work closely with allies to constrain Iran’s dangerous activities. We will continue to condemn reckless attacks, promote civilian protection, support the security of partners across the region, and take all possible steps to keep British nationals safe. The future of Iran should be for the Iranian people.  For these reasons, the Government does not intend to sever diplomatic ties with Iran. Maintaining relations – while being firm, coordinated and clear about our objectives – offers the best prospect of advancing British interests, supporting stability, holding Iran to account, and preserving the possibility of a diplomatic solution.  Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office

Create and maintain ideas.parliament.uk, an Ideas Commons where people can submit and support ideas that create solutions for life in the UK and everywhere our decisions reach.

What if the nation’s huge, untapped wealth of imagination and practical ideas had a place where they could be heard, supported and acted on?

action: Pause Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill for consultation with children
background: I believe decisions about children should include children. I want the Government to ask the Children’s Commissioner to consult children on the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill, and pause the Bill until the consultation finishes, including on data privacy & protecting the home as a safe space.

The Children’s Commissioner should listen directly to children, including on wellbeing, data privacy, and protecting the home as a safe and private space. action: Reduce Vehicle Excise Duty by 50% for vehicles aged 20 to 39 years
background: Introduce a 50% VED reduction for cars aged 20–39. High taxes force functional vehicles to be scrapped, creating a "disposable" culture. Keeping existing cars is greener than building new ones, as it preserves embedded carbon. This "Young-Timer" bracket supports the circular economy and UK heritage.
additional_details: Manufacturing a new car creates massive carbon debt. We must move from a "disposable" car culture to a circular economy. Keeping a functional 20-year-old car on the road is often greener than building a new one, as it preserves the embedded carbon already spent. Current VED rates force many well-maintained cars to be scrapped prematurely. We call for a 50% "Transition to Historic" tax discount to encourage repair, support the UK heritage industry, and reflect the low mileage of modern classics.
government_response_summary: The Government has no plans to reduce Vehicle Excise Duty liabilities for vehicles aged 20 to 39 years. The Government keeps all taxes under review and the Chancellor makes decisions at fiscal events.
government_response_body: Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) is a tax on vehicles used or kept on public roads. Different rates apply to cars, vans, and motorcycles, and the rate for each vehicle is calculated according to a range of factors, such as its date of first registration, weight, or CO2 emissions.    Cars registered before 1 March 2001 pay VED annually based on engine size. Since 2001, the tax system has encouraged the uptake of cars with low carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions to help meet the UK's legally binding climate targets. Cars first registered between 1 March 2001 and 31 March 2017 pay VED annually according to CO2 emissions.  From 1 April 2017, a reformed VED system was introduced for new cars. The changes in April 2017 were applied to new cars only, meaning that the tax treatment of existing cars was not impacted.  The majority of an internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle's emissions come from fuel production and tailpipe emissions. The Department for Transport's 2022 lifecycle analysis shows that the manufacturing emissions for a medium sized petrol or diesel car are estimated to be less than 20% of the lifetime emissions of the vehicle (2020-2030 scenarios). The lifecycle analysis can be found here:   https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/lifecycle-analysis-of-uk-road-vehicles.   At Budget 2014 the Government at the time announced that it would introduce a rolling 40-year exemption from Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) for classic cars. This means that currently vehicles constructed before 1 January 1985 are exempt from paying VED. From 1 April 2026 vehicles constructed before 1 January 1986 will become exempt from VED.  The law does not specifically define a vehicle as historic or classic for registration purposes, and it is widely recognised that there are many factors other than age which influence whether a car is considered classic. The Government at the time therefore set 40 years as being a fair cut-off date to distinguish classic cars from older cars.   Revenue from motoring taxes helps ensure we can continue to fund the vital public services and infrastructure that people and families across the UK expect. For example, by 2029/30, the government will commit over £2 billion annually for local authorities to repair, renew and fix potholes on their roads – doubling funding since coming into office. This record level of funding will enable the government to exceed its manifesto commitment to fix an additional 1 million potholes per year by the end of the Parliament.    While there are no current plans to reduce VED for cars aged 20 to 39 years, the Government keeps all taxes under review, and the Chancellor makes decisions on tax policy at fiscal events.  HM Treasury

action: Abolish interest charges on student loans
background: Cancel interest charges on all student loans. We believe placing this burden on the backs of those that want to succeed in life is abhorrent and short-sighted. These charges penalise our brightest and best, the very people that contribute the most to society.
additional_details:
Charging interest on student loans burdens graduates with growing debt, often £50k+ while many never fully repay due to income-contingent terms.
We believe that abolishing interest would make higher education truly accessible, without a lifelong financial penalty and also boost social mobility and productivity by freeing young people from debt drag. Education benefits society; taxpayers already subsidise it—we want to remove this unfair tax on ambition.
government_response_summary: Student loans are heavily subsidised by government. To be fair to taxpayers and low earners, those who financially benefit should contribute to the cost. Adding interest to loans is one way to do this
government_response_body: The student finance system removes upfront financial barriers for students entering higher education and remains a deliberate investment in our young people. The Government does not make a profit on the student loan system, rather the student loan system is heavily subsidised by government.  To ensure that the taxpayer, many of whom have not gone to university, are not subsidising an unfair proportion of the cost of student loans, and to protect borrowers  who do not go on to be high earners, the student loan system is designed to ensure that those who financially benefit most from their education make a fair contribution towards its cost. Applying interest to student loans is one way that we manage this.  Applying interest in line with inflation ensures that student loans maintain the real value of the loan over the loan term. Removing interest completely would mean that borrowers who go on the repay all, or nearly all of their loan, would repay less, in real terms, than they borrowed.  While interest rates impact the overall amount borrowed and therefore the length of time spent in repayment for borrowers who go on to repay all, or nearly all, of their loan in full, they do not alter the monthly repayment amount for borrowers. Most borrowers are not forecast to repay their loans in full and therefore do not repay the interest accrued on their loan balance. For example, for undergraduate borrowers starting in academic year 2024/25, the average loan balance at the point the borrower becomes eligible to make repayments is £45,600. The estimated average lifetime repayment in real terms is £28,000. Interest rates typically only affect the total amount repaid by mid to high earning borrowers and those with small balances, who will pay back more of their student loans.  This is a conscious decision in the design of the student loan system.  It means that if a borrower goes on to be a high earner, they will contribute more to the cost of their education, while low earners are protected by calculating repayments based on their income and cancelling any outstanding debt, with no detriment to the borrower or their family, at the end of the loan term.  Removing interest rates from student loans would mean that the taxpayer had to subsidise a greater portion of the student loan costs while those who have benefited most from higher education pay less towards its cost.  We inherited the student loans system, which was devised by previous Governments, and we are looking for ways to make it fairer.  Department for Education

action: Ban VAR in football.
background: Legislate to outlaw the use of Video Assistant Refereeing (VAR) in domestic football matches, with the exception of goal line technology.
additional_details: VAR is ruining the beautiful game, particularly for the match going fan. It is interfering in instances which are not clear and obvious errors, taking far too long to reach decisions, and in many cases still getting decisions wrong. It should be abandoned (or banned), and matches should be officiated how they were, mostly successfully, for 150 years.

action: Commission an independent inquiry into social care and social work
background: We call on the Government to commission an independent inquiry into the delivery of social work and social care services before making further progress on the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill.
additional_details: This review would assess the current system, and the impact of the Bill on any existing issues in the system. In our view, social work and social care systems are under severe pressure, resulting in delayed, unsuitable or denied support for children and families, including children in care. We believe these are systemic issues, not isolated cases or individual failings and that proceeding with major reform without independent scrutiny risks entrenching harm rather than addressing it. Given the significance of this we think Parents and grassroots organisations must be central to this inquiry.

action: Scrap the UK Digital Identity Programme in Its Entirety
background: Scrap the UK digital identity programme in full, including all voluntary, optional, or future digital ID systems. Pausing compulsory use is not enough. Parliament must commit in law to never introducing a national digital ID. Anything less than full abolition is disingenuous.
additional_details: Recent claims of a “U-turn” do not address the central concern: the digital identity programme is still being pursued. While some compulsory elements are paused, the infrastructure and long-term intent remain. Digital ID is introduced gradually, framed as “optional”, then expanded until refusal becomes impractical. Voluntary in name, mandatory in practice. A centralised digital ID carries inherent risks to liberty, autonomy, and privacy. It should be scrapped entirely.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Do not roll out digital IDs" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757131

action: Demand UK Action to Condemn the Islamic Republic and Support the People of Iran
background: Publicly and unequivocally condemn the actions of the Islamic Republic of Iran. Acknowledge the severity of the human rights crisis in Iran. Take practical action to support the Iranian people, including diplomatic pressure, targeted sanctions, and support for independent investigations.
additional_details: The people of Iran are facing extreme violence and repression. At least 12,000 people have lost their lives according to official figures, with credible reports indicating the true number is far higher. Despite the scale of these atrocities, the response from the UK Government—and Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer—has been disturbingly quiet. Silence in the face of mass suffering is unacceptable. The UK has both a moral and international responsibility to respond to this genocide.
rejection_details: We already have a petition open calling for similar action, which you may wish to sign: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756775

action: Ban AI-generated images in the advertising of beauty and cosmetic products
background: Introduce legislation banning AI-generated or AI-altered images in the advertising of beauty and cosmetic products, requiring realistic, truthful visuals that show real results on real people, to prevent misleading claims, protect consumers, and stop the spread of visual misinformation.
additional_details: AI-generated images in beauty advertising can create unrealistic and unachievable results, misleading consumers and distorting expectations around skincare, cosmetics, and ageing. When synthetic images are presented as product outcomes, consumers cannot make informed choices. We believe regulation is needed to prevent visual misinformation, protect consumer trust, and ensure beauty marketing reflects real products on real people.

action: Stop the increase of residents parking permits in Southampton.
background: The increase in residents’ parking permit charges in Southampton is causing financial pressure on local households. I want the Government to require local authorities to stop these rises, reduce current costs, and make residents’ permits free where possible.
additional_details: The proposed increases to parking permits in Southampton raise costs sharply for residents, from £30 to £45 for a standard permit and from £6 to £12 for visitor scratch cards. This comes at a time when many households are struggling with rising living expenses. These changes risk making essential parking unaffordable. Lower or free permits would reduce financial pressure and support local residents.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

action: Mandate enforceable standards and timeframes for police investigations
background: We call on the Government to introduce a statutory right to a timely and effective police investigation for victims of crime, including enforceable standards, defined timeframes, and accountability where those standards are not met.
additional_details:
Victims of crime in England and Wales can experience delayed or ineffective investigations, including missed evidence or closure without proper inquiry.
There is no statutory mechanism enabling victims to require compliance with investigative standards or timeframes.
Concerns are generally addressed retrospectively through complaints or oversight processes rather than through enforceable rights at the point of failure.

action: Call an early General Election in 2026 so voters can renew or withdraw consent.
background: Millions have already signed petitions calling for a General Election, yet debates avoided the core issue: whether the Government still has a democratic mandate. The Prime Minister should request dissolution so the public can judge policies introduced or changed since the last election.
additional_details: Early elections have been called before to renew legitimacy when trust breaks down. The Government says it needs time to fix an “inherited mess”, yet has introduced major tax rises, policy reversals and measures not clearly set out in its manifesto. Repeated U-turns and mandate drift have damaged public confidence. An early General Election would let voters decide whether this Government should continue.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

background:
Medway Maritime Hospital is unable to adequately serve the growing population and is unsustainable and necessitates immediate action.

This investment in healthcare would benefit the entire community. 
We call on the government to prioritise this essential project and investing in a new hospital.
additional_details: People of Medway and the surrounding area who use Medway Maritime Hospital are receiving inadequate care due to the growing population of Medway and is the only hospital in Medway, which provides emergency care and other services to the population in Medway and surrounding areas, Medway Hospital is unable to cope with the capacity. Something needs to be done to alleviate the demands on Medway Maritime Hospital. It is not sustainable for central and local government to keep building new homes.

action: Make Manifesto Pledges Legally Binding or Require Accountability
background: On 4 July 2024 Labour won on promises of no tax rises on working people, pensioner protection, secure borders and economic stability.Since then the Government has made major unpromised changes, including winter fuel cuts for pensioners, impacts on farmers, and others that have disappointed voters.
additional_details:
We call on the Government to legislate that:
• Major post-election policy changes must be foreshadowed in the manifesto or face mandatory public consultation and parliamentary vote.
• Failure to honour core manifesto commitments triggers an automatic independent review and stronger democratic accountability mechanisms.
This restores trust, stops voter deception, and ensures elections mean something. Our democracy demands honest government—act now.
rejection_details:
We have a number of petitions already open that reference issues relating to manifesto promises - yours is effectively a duplicate in what it is requesting of a  couple of these - you can find them at this link (you may wish to sign one or more of them):

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions?state=open&q=manifesto

action: Make British politics compulsory in the secondary school curriculum
background: British politics should be compulsory in secondary school to help prepare young people for the responsibility of voting in elections. The fundamentals of British politics and how to vote: we think these things which are lacking in the British education system.
additional_details: We think teaching the fundamentals of British politics and how to vote are vital to producing informed voters. We would like every young person to learn, as a compulsory part of the curriculum, the basics of British politics and how to vote. These materials already exist as part of the resources from the UK parliament education department. Government intervention could ensure the consistency of experience and understanding of British politics across Britain for all future voters.

action: Review NHS Guidance to Protect Vulnerable Adults in Community Care
background: We are calling on the Government to review NHS guidance to ensure current practices prevent deaths caused by systemic failures in emergency triage and community healthcare coordination.
additional_details:
We would like the guidance to set out a “checklist” of expected care to ensure no other family suffers preventable tragedy:
1. Mandatory Clinical Triage Review
2. Mandatory Inter-Agency Welfare Checks

My mother’s death was not just a medical event; it was a failure of the safety net. We think this NHS wide guidance will turn "missed opportunities" to provide excellent care in community settings into "mandatory actions" which can save the lives of the most vulnerable members of our society.

action: Allow Reform UK the right to ask questions and respond during PMQs
background: Reform UK has a membership which clearly places them as an equal party such as Lib Dem, Conservative and Greens therefore the party and its Leader should have the courtesy enabling it to respond to direct attacks during PMQs and also the democratic right to ask the PM questions.
additional_details: To show the country that our democratic process is transparent, fair and equitable. That no political party , its leader or its members should suffer personal attack without the right to reply, defend itself, put forward explanation or refute allegations in open parliament.
rejection_details:
Any Member of the House of Commons - of any party or none - can table a question for Prime Minister's Questions (PMQs) or attend PMQs and indicate that they wish to speak.

You can find out more about how MPs participate in PMQs here https://www.parliament.uk/business/commons/the-speaker/speaker-and-the-chamber/prime-ministers-questions-and-the-role-of-the-speaker/ and here https://guidetoprocedure.parliament.uk/collections/nPylcSv3/prime-ministers-questions

PMQs is an opportunity for Members of the House of Commons to put questions to the Prime Minister. Only the Prime Minister answers questions at PMQs.

action: Improve access to Parliament’s work for people with learning difficulties
background:
We want the Government and Parliament to change so that we can participate in their work.

We want to change the law in the Equality Act so that this must happen.

See this petition in Easy Read: https://www.inclusionlondon.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Parliament-E-petition.pdf
additional_details:
We find it very hard to have a voice in Parliament when they want our views about the following
 
• new laws
• Government departments’ work
• Big issues that Government and Parliament should know about
 
We want the Government to work with people with learning difficulties led groups to look at how we can access information and tell the government what we think about:
 
1) new laws
2) Government departments’ work
3) Parliament’s work 
4) big issues that Government and parliament should know about

action: End the blanket ban on diabetics serving in non-frontline UK Armed Forces.
background: Review and modernise Armed Forces medical policy to end the blanket ban on people with diabetes, allowing medically fit individuals to serve in non-frontline, specialist and support roles in line with modern diabetes care and technology.
additional_details: The Armed Forces apply a near-blanket ban on people with diabetes, a policy that no longer reflects modern medicine or military roles. Advances such as continuous glucose monitoring and insulin pumps allow safe, reliable management. Many non-frontline, technical and specialist roles do not pose the same risks as combat. A role-specific, evidence-based approach would be fairer, safer, and strengthen recruitment without compromising operational effectiveness.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Diabetes should not prevent someone serving in the British armed forces
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741445

action: An immediate General Election
background: I want an immediate general election because the current government no longer has a clear or credible mandate from the public. Major decisions are being made that affect people’s lives, livelihoods,and future, yet voters have not had a recent opportunity to express how they feel.
additional_details: I want the Government or Parliament to call an immediate general election to restore democratic legitimacy and public trust. Major decisions are being made without a clear, current mandate from voters, and public confidence has been undermined by political instability and broken promises. Parliament’s role is to represent the people, not preserve power. An election would allow voters to hold leaders accountable and choose the direction of the country
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which is currently open:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

action: Modernise School Uniforms: ban the Requirement for restrictive blazers and ties
background:
Build on the 2026 cap on branded items by issuing statutory guidance that phases out the requirement for restrictive blazers and ties in all state funded schools. 
Schools should adopt practical, comfortable, inclusive, and affordable uniforms and prioritise pupil wellbeing.
additional_details:
There is no proven link to better outcomes and formal uniforms. Instead it creates unnecessary barriers to education and wellbeing.

Restrictive clothing causes discomfort and distraction for many children but especially those with SEND, including sensory processing differences.

It is an outdated expectation that does not align to the workplace expectations of today. 

The large financial burden that comes with blazers costing £40–£60 and require frequent replacement as children grow.
rejection_details:

Require schools prioritise comfort in uniforms & more personal choice for pupils

background: Require MPs to provide clear and relevant answers to serious questions and discourage the use of jokes, deflection or avoidance during parliamentary scrutiny, so debates are conducted with seriousness and respect for the British public.
additional_details: We ask UK Parliament to strengthen standards of conduct so MPs provide clear and relevant answers to serious questions. Parliament should discourage the use of jokes, deflection or avoidance during scrutiny, ensuring debates are conducted with seriousness, transparency and respect for the British public.

action: Require a by-election if MPs / Councillors change parties or become independent
background: The Government should legislate to require a by-election to be held if an MP or Local Councillor switches political party in the middle of the parliamentary term so affected constituents get the opportunity to vote in an election to decide who represents them.
additional_details: Many people vote for people they believe will represent them best and for candidates which represent the values of a particular political party. We believe it is not fair or democratic for voters who vote for an elected official who switches party, or becomes independent, and does not have to stand again in an immediate election. It stands to reason that some will not support the values of the new party, but to be balanced, some will, but this is assumptive and we believe it should be ratified via an official election.

action: Review the laws relating to driving and prescribed medical cannabis use
background: I want the government to investigate the impact on driving of prescribed medical cannabis because at the moment there are arguably a lot of people driving around impaired.
additional_details: Arguably medical cannabis users have an unfair right to be impaired whilst driving. This could place many people in danger from those that choose to medicate and take the wheel.
rejection_details: Under the Road Traffic Act 1988, individuals who are legally prescribed medical cannabis are allowed to drive as long as they adhere to their doctor’s guidance and are not impaired at the time of driving.

action: Cap failed payment fees for individuals and small businesses
background: Introduce legislation to cap fees associated with declined direct debit and late payments so that do not exceed the administrative cost of handling the late payment. We also call on the Government to require grace periods and fair payment alternatives for those unable to pay.
additional_details: In our view fees associated with declined or late payments are automated charges that often far exceed the administrative cost of handling the late payment, and disproportionately affect people and small businesses in financial difficulty. We believe that such fees increase arrears, worsen debt, and trap vulnerable customers in a cycle of charges instead of encouraging payment. The Government should review the regulatory oversight of such fees to prevent these charges being used as a revenue stream. We think that in a cost-of-living crisis, allowing firms to profit from failed payments is unfair and counterproductive.

action: Ban the use of electronic device loudspeakers in public & require headphone use
background: Ban any use of electronic device loudspeakers in public places, such as using your loudspeaker for phone calls, private conversations, videos, music, social media, etc, to protect others who don’t wish to listen to the content they’re playing.
additional_details:
Require the use of headphones to listen to this content in public spaces. I believe it’s an invasion of one’s downtime / travel time / private time / personal time when members of the public play whatever they want on their electronic devices on loudspeaker in spaces where they can wear headphones to listen to their content of choice.
 
It is invasive for many around them, can be rude and embarrassing if they are having conversations on phone calls which the whole train carriage of people may not wish to hear.

action: Change the benefit cap for those who claim childcare
background: Exempt the Universal Credit childcare element from the Benefit Cap. It is a work-related expense, not a benefit. Stop penalizing parents who work 40+ hours only to be poorer than non-working households. Ensure the 2026 child element increases actually reach working families, not just the capped.
additional_details: Exempt the Universal Credit childcare element from the Benefit Cap. It is a work expense, not a benefit. Currently, the system punishes full-time work; my £1,770 childcare cost exceeds my £1,687 wage, and the Cap steals the "child elements" meant for my children’s survival. While non-working households will benefit from the April 2026 changes, working families will see every extra penny "capped off." Stop making it more profitable to stay home than to work 40 hours. Make work pay for us too.
rejection_details:
We are not clear what action you are seeking, as childcare cost are not subject to the benefit cap. 

You can find more information here: https://data.parliament.uk/DepositedPapers/Files/DEP2023-0365/020_Benefit_Cap_V22-0.pdf

action: Seek a joint UK-French force to counter illegal migration & fund joint training
background: We want the Government to fund military training with France and to seek the creation of a joint UK-France peacekeeping force to combat the illegal migration of migrants who are trying to leave France, a safe country, which may put themselves and English Channel shipping in danger.
additional_details: The UK Government has announced £200 million to train our military for the possible deployment of a combined French/UK military peacekeeping force in Ukraine. By training on French beaches together, we could make it easier for our French allies to understand English orders and help both countries' military to learn how to deal with illegal migrants. It could also encourage combined camaraderie.

This is not unusual,I know of 8 people this has hsppened to and infact most people you talk to have had this experience. It is time it was resolved and will be supported by estate agents and house purchasers alike.

action: Put diplomatic pressure on Syria & Turkey to protect Kurds & other minorities
background: We want the UK Government to help protect Kurds and other minority communities in Syria and Turkey by applying diplomatic pressure on both the Syrian and Turkish Governments to stop any attacks, ensure civilian safety, and uphold human rights for all affected minority communities.
additional_details: Recent attacks on Kurds have put civilians at grave risk, with shelling, displacement, deaths, injuries, and many people missing. It has been reported that Kurds, Syria’s largest minority, have faced repeated violence and rights violations. We believe the UK Government should apply diplomatic pressure on the Governments of Syria and Turkey, and urge them to protect Kurdish civilians, ensure humanitarian access, and uphold human rights.

action: Do not roll out digital IDs
background: We do not want digital IDs. We are concerned about total control by the government. Do not spend our money on this system!
additional_details: The government already dropped its mandatory right to work requirement for digital IDs, however we wish to avoid all doubt and stop this being introducing though the back door. We require the government to completely scrap this idea. Do not spend our money on this idea that the public clearly do not agree with.

action: Ban companies from charging single people higher prices for holidays
background: I would like the Government to change the law to prevent companies charging single people travelling alone higher prices for holidays.
additional_details: Single persons who wants to go on holiday to have a break will see good deals advertised per person. However, it has been my experience that as soon as you put that you are travelling alone you have to pay for a second person too to get that deal or face a higher price if only paying for one person. I think this is very wrong and I think it's discriminating for single people and the companies shouldn't be allowed to do it.

action: Require social workers to use body-worn cameras during statutory visits
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation requiring social workers to use body-worn cameras during statutory home visits, child protection investigations, and formal assessments.
additional_details: Social workers make life-changing decisions that can remove children from their families and lead to court action. These decisions have permanent effects on children’s wellbeing and family stability. Social workers are not required to use the body-worn cameras frequently seen on police officers or front-line staff. This can limit evidence, increase disputes, and reduce protection for children and families. Body-worn cameras could improve transparency, accountability, and public trust.

action: Remove the Reverse Charge VAT for trade contractors and subcontractors
background: We ask the Government to remove the Reverse Charge VAT for trade contractors and subcontractors and to implement alternative, targeted measures which in our view could prevent VAT fraud without damaging legitimate businesses or causing widespread cash-flow pressure across the construction industry.
additional_details: We believe the reverse charge VAT has fundamentally damaged cash flow across the construction supply chain, particularly for small and medium-sized subcontractors. In our view it has removed vital working capital while businesses still face upfront VAT on materials, labour costs, CIS deductions and long payment terms. We believe this has increased insolvencies, reduced competition, and unfairly shifts the funding burden onto legitimate firms. We call for reform to protect cash flow while still preventing VAT fraud.

action: Allow qualified driving instructors to also act as examiners to cut test backlog
background: Create a unified Level 4 qualification for both examiners and instructors to standardise education. Allow instructors to test students (not their own) via a "local swap" system. This clears backlogs, ensures impartial assessment, and uses shared data to improve road safety and pass rates.
additional_details: We call on the Government to create a "Dual-Certification" framework. This would require both driving examiners and instructors to undergo the same Level 4 standardized training to unify assessment criteria. Once qualified, instructors should be permitted to conduct driving tests for candidates they have not personally taught. This "local swap" model will use shared performance data to address fail hotspots, eliminate the test backlog, and maintain impartiality through DVSA-led audits.

action: Amend standing orders: give right of reply to any MP/party mentioned in Commons
background: Amend the standing orders to give an automatic immediate right of reply to any MP or any party mentioned in any statement, question or answer in the House. We think this will deter MPs and Ministers from using parliamentary business to attack opponents.
additional_details: We believe we have seen PMQs used to attack opponents rather than answer questions, and that without a right of reply this causes an unfair and undemocratic advantage. There needs to be balance. Accordingly, any MP or party mentioned in any way in parliament should have an automatic immediate right of reply.

action: Introduce a law for mandatory visible disclosure marks on AI-generated media
background: Introduce legislation requiring all AI-generated images and videos to carry a clear, visible label embedded in the content. The label should remain visible when shared across platforms, helping the public identify AI-generated media and improving transparency, trust and online safety.
additional_details:
AI-generated images and videos are being used to harass, humiliate and impersonate people. This harm has been linked to young people taking their own lives and is an urgent safeguarding issue for children, adults and society. Clear labelling would help prevent harm and protect everyone.
While we wait for corporations to act responsibly we are all at risk and our government has the power to protect us.  The time is NOW!

Ban personal use of AI and require AI watermarks

action: Cap student loan interest rates at a fair and affordable level
background: Reduce or cap interest rates on UK student loans so that repayments are fair, affordable, and allow graduates to meaningfully reduce their debt.
additional_details: UK student loan interest rates significantly exceed inflation and continue to grow even when graduates earn modest incomes. As a result, many borrowers see their debt increase despite making regular repayments. We believe the current system discourages social mobility, places long-term financial strain on graduates, and disproportionately affects lower and middle earners. The Government should reduce, cap, or reform student loan interest rates so that repayments genuinely reduce debt.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to make a clear ask of the Government or Parliament.

We are not clear if you are asking for a reduction, cap, or reform of student loan interest rates. You can submit a petition setting out more clearly what action you are calling for.

action: Tighter control and ban the use of artificial flavouring and colouring in food.
background: Change policy and to treat artifical flavouring and colours like allergens on food labelling.
additional_details:
Carcinogenicity:Some flavorings, like certain smoke flavorings in the EU and chemicals.
Genotoxicity: Substances that damage DNA (genotoxic) are a major concern.
ADHD & Allergies:Artificial colors and flavors have been suspected of causing hyperactivity and allergic reactions, particularly in children.
Neurological & Metabolic Issues:Research suggests potential links between artificial additives and long-term health problems, including neurological disorders.

action: Require energy companies to allow changing from smart meter to traditional one
background: We don’t feel like people are being told the truth about smart meters – although they have been found to be safe some people could be sensitive to the radio waves they emit. Customers should have the option to have these meters removed.
additional_details: We therefore think that companies should allow customers to change from a smart meter to a traditional one, if they want to. People who move into a bought home or rented property that already has these smart meters installed are unlikely to be able to change it. Some people experience sensitivity towards the radio waves they emit and, in our view, must be protected under the Equality Act 2010. We think people should be given the choice.

action: Reinstate supply of triamcinolone injections in the UK for keloids & alopecia
background: In 2025 DHSC & NHS discontinued the supply of Triamcinolone injections, which has resulted in there being no stock left. I want the supply chain to be reinstated to the UK so patients are able to be treated with this medication.
additional_details:
We believe Triamcinolone injections are essential, evidence based treatment for keloids and alopecia, affecting over 127,000 people in the UK. 
We understand that the UK is now the only country denying patients this proven therapy, creating an unacceptable health inequality and leaving thousands without effective care.
We urge the Government to immediately reinstate the supply of triamcinolone injections for NHS and private patients

action: OUR VOTE, OUR RIGHT: Democracy Delayed is Democracy Denied
background: We call on the government to make postponement of elections impossible except in a genuine national emergency, and that any such postponement must be approved by Parliament, ensuring no Prime Minister or minister can delay elections on their own.
additional_details: In history, leaders who feared facing voters delayed, cancelled, or hollowed‑out elections to stay in power. Castro, Hitler, and Stalin all did this. Recent UK actions allow councils to delay votes for reorganisation, undermining people’s right to vote. Elections must happen on schedule; reorganisation can wait for the next cycle. The right to vote must come first — never postponed for convenience.

action: Require & fund all public sector buildings to be fully wheelchair accessible
background: Require and fund the renovation of all public sector buildings to be fully wheelchair accessible, so they are required to install elevators and / or wheelchair accessible ramps in all public sector buildings, including train stations and museums.
additional_details: Many people in wheelchairs go through life struggling with accessibility, a lack of equality and discrimination at times. I believe they are being overlooked and would greatly benefit from feeling equal in terms of accessibility, which at the moment in some places, is not possible. Train stations are a particular example and I believe many need to be renovated to ensure full wheelchair accessibility.

action: Expel Iranian diplomats, proscribe IRGC, and sever relations with Iran’s regime
background: We call on the UK Government to expel Iranian regime diplomats from the UK, formally proscribe IRGC as a terrorist organisation, sever diplomatic relations, and apply maximum political and economic pressure to hold the regime accountable for human rights abuses and protect protesters’ lives.
additional_details:
Iran’s regime has committed serious human rights violations, including killing and imprisoning peaceful protesters, journalists, and dissidents. Thousands have died during nationwide protests.

The IRGC plays a key role in repression, while internet shutdowns are used to conceal violence.

We urge the UK to expel regime representatives, proscribe the IRGC, downgrade or sever diplomatic relations, and apply all available pressure to prevent further atrocities and protect civilian lives.

action: Don't introduce essentials-only benefit cards and protect claimants’ freedom
background: Do not introduce benefits payment cards restricted to “essentials only” and keep benefits paid as normal money via bank accounts or cash access. Address fraud through targeted enforcement rather than blanket restrictions that affect all claimants.
additional_details: Restricted benefit cards could stigmatise disabled people, carers and low-paid workers, treating them as a lower class of citizen. Cash benefits are spent locally, supporting jobs, VAT and GDP. Evidence shows cash payments are not widely misused. Real-world essentials like transport, bills and repairs cannot be reliably restricted without causing hardship.

action: Replace ban with regulated license system for certain dog breeds
background: We feel the current ban on certain dog breeds punishes the animal not the owner, and is distressing to owners of well behaved dogs. We believe the problem is poor training. Instead of bans, there should be a license system to own certain dog breeds, just like the gun license system.
additional_details: We feel a licensing scheme will be fairer and could give opportunity for people to change their negative perceptions and stop demonising all dogs because some people are bad owners. Many large dogs are well-trained and friendly, and could be kept by responsible owners who have passed a course and DBS check to gain a licence. To keep their license, the owner would have to prove they have paid for professional training for their dog. There could be regular checks on the dog's welfare too.

action: Include GMC accredited degrees from UK medical campuses outside of the UK
background: The Medical Training (Prioritisation) Bill should be amended to include GMC accredited medical degrees from UK medical campuses outside of the UK within the definition of UK Primary Medical Qualification.
additional_details: We believe the current Bill irrationally discriminates against British citizens or other third country nationals, funding equivalent GMC-validated UK University degrees abroad at UK university campuses, potentially breaching equality or legitimate expectation principles. We are concerned students having funded five years of medical studies could be discriminated against by failure to accept their qualifications for the purposes of prioritisation for Foundation Training as resident doctors.

action: Reassess the housing allocation for Broughton Astley village.
background: A further 550 homes should not be built until infrastructure constraints are properly resolved. Broughton Astley is a low-lying village with a watercourse running directly through it, where natural gradients already cause surface water to pool and rise.
additional_details: Drainage limitations and an overstretched sewerage system mean these issues are worsening rather than improving. Local infrastructure is under strain. There has been repeated flooding in specific areas, and residents have seen first-hand how the sewerage network struggles during heavy rainfall. Available data indicates the treatment works is near capacity, with frequent sewage spills affecting the watercourse and, at times, homes and gardens. Drainage and sewage infrastructure must come first.

action: Parental Bereavement Legislation on par with UK Maternity/Paternity Legislation
background: Every parent who loses a child should have the time and financial support to grieve — just as parents are supported when welcoming a child. UK law provides only 2 weeks statutory parental bereavement leave (often unpaid), leaving parents to return to work far too soon after unimaginable loss.
additional_details:
We call on the government to amend the law so all parents who lose a child, regardless of age, receive statutory leave and pay equal to maternity/paternity leave. This would give bereaved parents the time, dignity, and support they need to grieve.

Society recognises the birth of a child as life-changing — it must also recognise child loss as equally profound. In the UK, maternity leave can be up to 52 weeks, yet bereaved parents currently get only 2 weeks. This is not equality — it must change.

action: Supermarkets edibles food waste
background: For five months I have investigated supermarket food waste and found large amounts of edible food being discarded. This is unacceptable during the cost-of-living crisis, worsens food insecurity, harms the environment, and shows the need for urgent government action.
additional_details: The government should introduce stronger regulation to reduce food waste in supermarkets. This should include mandatory requirements to prioritise redistribution of edible surplus food to charities and community organisations before disposal. Supermarkets should be required to report food waste levels publicly, meet clear reduction targets, and face penalties for repeated failure. Government support should also expand food redistribution infrastructure nationwide.

action: Negotiate exemption to the 90/180 Schengen travel rule for professional drivers
background: We call on the UK Government to negotiate an exemption from the Schengen 90 days in any 180-day period rule for UK professional drivers, including HGV (lorry) drivers and PCV (coach and bus) drivers, when travelling for work purposes.
additional_details: UK professional drivers regularly need to enter EU and Schengen countries to carry out essential transport services such as freight haulage, international coach travel, and tourism operations. The current 90/180 rule was designed for tourists and short-term visitors, not workers who cross borders as part of their job, specifically for licensed professional drivers travelling for commercial and work-related purposes only, with appropriate documentation.
