action: Do not ban social media for under 16s
background: I think the government shouldn’t ban social media for under 16s. This is because for many young people social media is how they communicate with their friends. Some people view social media as a lifeline. A community, a supportive network. This is why I think the government shouldn’t ban it.
government_response_summary: The government recognises the benefits of digital technologies, including social media, for children. We are consulting on how to ensure children have an enriching and positive experience online.
government_response_body: I would like to thank all those who signed the petition on this important issue. The government is committed to harnessing the benefits of technology to shape a future that works for us all, particularly for children. To do this, people must have confidence that their children are protected online.  The Online Safety Act (the ‘Act’) is one of the toughest regimes globally in protecting people from illegal content and activity, and children from harmful and age-inappropriate content. Since the Act has come into effect, the government has ensured keeping children safe online remains a priority and have always said we will take further action as necessary.  We know parents are grappling with how much screen time their children should have, when to give them a phone, what they are seeing online, and the impact all of this is having. We also know there are growing concerns among parents, carers and those that work with children about AI, including children forming relationships with chatbots as if they were real people.  Every child deserves the strongest possible start in life, full of love, learning and play. Technology can open up huge opportunities for young people and social media can help children communicate with friends and feel part of a wider community. However, in the age of smartphones, children’s lives are changing rapidly – sometimes faster than families, schools or support services can respond.  There are calls from across the UK for the government to take action, including calls from many to enforce a social media ban for under 16s. However, as is evident from this petition, opinions on a possible social media ban are divided – with some of the most prominent voices believing that social media ban is not the right answer. This demonstrates that, while there are calls for the government to take action, there is still no consensus on how.  The government firmly believes that policy making must give proper consideration to a range of views and be rooted in the best available evidence. That is why, on the 2 March 2026, the government launched a consultation to seek further evidence and views on these issues and possible solutions, including on whether there should be a minimum age for social media, and if so, what age would be right. The responses to this consultation will also help shape decisions on: •	Whether platforms should be required to switch off addictive features that keep children hooked late into the night - like infinite scrolling and autoplay; •	Whether mandatory overnight curfews would help children sleep better and what age they should apply to; •	How age verification and age assurance technologies can support effective implementation and; •	Whether the use of mobile phones in schools should be put on a statutory footing.  This will be a short, sharp consultation of three months, closing on 26 May 2026, allowing us to hear all perspectives, build consensus where we can, and then act decisively. There will be no delay, and government will explain our next steps by the summer.  We welcome views from all those with an interest in this issue, including parents, children’s organisations, bereaved families, industry, and children themselves. Alongside the consultation, today we are launching a child‑ and parent‑friendly version to ensure voices in this debate are properly heard. To access the consultation, consultation survey, and child and parent friendly versions of the consultation survey, please follow this link: Growing up in the online world: a national consultation - GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/growing-up-in-the-online-world-a-national-consultation).  Alongside the consultation, we are launching a wide-ranging national conversation and piloting potential interventions to ensure future decisions are informed by real-world evidence. We will also look closely at the experience in Australia and their ban for under 16s.  This consultation is the next step in the government’s work to ensure children’s experiences online are safe and enriching. Together, we are shaping a digital world that reflects our values and protects our children while preparing them for the future in an age of digital technologies and rapid technological change.  Department for Science, Innovation & Technology

action: Mandate a "One-Click to Cancel" button for all online subscriptions
background: We want the Government to use the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 to require companies to provide a prominent, one-click cancellation button for any subscription purchased online.
additional_details: Currently, many companies make it easy to sign up but force customers through "dark patterns"—multiple pages of warnings, phone calls, or hidden menus—to cancel. While the 2024 Act requires "straightforward" cancellation, we believe it is too vague. We want the law to state that cancelling must be as easy as signing up: if it took one click to join, it must take no more than one click to leave.

action: Ban abortions after 24 weeks due to Down's syndrome diagnosis
background: Amend laws relating to abortion to equalise the 24 week limit for abortions in cases where the baby has been diagnosed with Down’s syndrome. We believe that the law should affirm the equal value and dignity of all lives, ensuring that every child has a fair chance to make their mark in the world.
additional_details: In our view, the law as it stands creates a discriminatory double standard where babies diagnosed with Down syndrome can be terminated much later than those without. We believe this late-term allowance is not only unjust but perpetuates a societal view that individuals with Down syndrome are less worthy of life. There’s countless stories of individuals with DS who thrive and contribute significantly to society. We think changing the law will foster greater acceptance and support for these individuals and their families.

action: Fund more research into gynaecological health from current 2.4%
background: Only 2.4% of public research funding goes to women’s gynaecological health and childbirth. I would like to see this massively increased and much more importance placed onto it.
additional_details:
Women make up 51% of the UK population, yet so many continue to experience reproductive health challenges. Many women live with painful periods, fibroids, or ongoing pain with no clear diagnosis. These experiences are too often dismissed due to such little research, which desperately needs to be increased.
 
Addressing misogyny within the healthcare system is essential. When women’s pain is not taken seriously, the consequences can be severe and life-threatening.

action: Fund more reasonable adjustments in NHS primary care for autistic people
background: We want the Government to provide funding to strengthen and enforce more reasonable adjustments in NHS primary care. This could include flexible appointments, longer consultations, quieter options, remote consultations, and home visits where surgery attendance is not possible.
additional_details: Many autistic people, including children and adults, face barriers accessing GP services due to sensory environments, rigid appointment systems, and communication difficulties. These barriers can prevent access to essential healthcare. More reasonable adjustments could reduce health inequality.

action: Review requirements of reversing test in HGV class 1 training
background: Since Brexit, the UK has struggled to fill thousands of class 1 HGV jobs due to a shortage of drivers. At present, there is funding available for training to become a class 1 HGV driver, however, we feel the course does not cover reversing that will be involved whilst in the real working world.
additional_details:
I propose to update the current reversing module, known as 3a, to include actual real world reversing in bays. Another option is to add an additional day or two, which is dedicated to being able to reverse into loading bays, safely and accurately.
Many training schools have the availability of such space to be able to implement this. These measures could also help improve employment chances.

action: Make it compulsory for children to wear gloves ice skating
background: I'd like to for the law to be changed so children are only permitted to ice skate if wearing protective gloves to protect their hands. The blades are so sharp.
government_response_summary: The safety and welfare of those taking part in ice skating is absolutely paramount. We have no plans to change the law. The terms and conditions for ice skating are decided on a venue-by-venue basis.
government_response_body: The safety and welfare of everyone taking part in sport and recreational activities is absolutely paramount. The Government understands the concerns of those who wish to ensure that recreational activities are as safe as possible for participants, including children and young people.  Temporary and permanent ice rinks are vital attractions that pull diverse audiences into the heart of our high streets. These ice rinks go beyond providing recreation; they ignite the local ecosystem, fueling secondary spend in nearby restaurants, shops, and hotels. By enriching a destination’s visitor offer, they turn a simple visit into a memorable experience, sustaining the vitality of our regions.  The Health and Safety Executive advises people to not take part in a recreational activity if it is believed that activity is not safe. However, individuals have the right to make their own choices, and parents and guardians are free to exercise that right on behalf of the children and young people they are responsible for where appropriate.  The terms and conditions for ice skating are decided on a venue-by-venue basis. The Government has no plans to change the law to make it compulsory for children to wear gloves while ice skating.  The majority of ice skating activity does not take place in a structured sporting environment. However, for sport skating, participants should refer to safety guidance issued by the relevant national governing body. British Ice Skating is the national governing body for ice skating within the United Kingdom.  The Government will continue to discuss participant safety with sports and other stakeholders to ensure that everyone, including children and young people, can take part in sport as safely as possible.  Department for Culture, Media and Sport

action: Review staff ratios for educational and early years settings based on need
background: Review existing funding framework across education and early years and introduce guidance that allows ratios to be adjusted based on assessed needs to ensure adequate funding and staffing resources to support differing levels of need.
additional_details: We also call on the Government to do more to recognise professional judgement in determining safe and effective staffing. We are calling on the government to take action because we believe the current statutory ratio system in early years provision does not reflect the realities of today’s settings or the increasingly complex needs of children. We speak on behalf of many professionals working across the early years sector who are committed to delivering safe, inclusive, and high-quality care and education. In our view, under the current framework, staffing ratios are determined solely by numbers, not by need.

action: Introduce clear statutory rules and guidance on rent abatement
background: I think the law on rent abatements (rent reductions due to disrepair) is unclear. Landlords can refuse rent reductions even where serious repair issues may exist, forcing tenants to go to court. I propose statutory rent reduction bands, similar to Vento bands used in employment law.
additional_details: I believe current rent abatement law is complex and unclear, and can allow some landlords to take advantage of tenants and cause lengthy legal delays. Introducing clear rent abatement bands would protect tenants, promote consistency, fairness, and help landlords comply with the law.

action: Amend laws permitting telecommunications infrastructure installation

additional_details: Such action should include, but not be limited to, amending the Communications Act 2003 and planning rules to prevent telecommunication infrastructure obstructing small businesses, introducing requirement for more extensive consultation in these cases, a review of the impact of Ofcom’s enforcement role, and to fund remediation and compensation for long-term harm for business impacted. We believe the Government should act to ensure infrastructure is deployed proportionately, with proper consultation, clearer enforcement, and fair routes to redress.

action: End funding for military interventions overseas and spend taxes in the UK.
background: We demand the government end the use of taxpayers’ money to fund military interventions, or providing military support for conflicts abroad. We believe that our taxes should be spent on improving public services, supporting communities and addressing urgent domestic issues rather than war.
additional_details:
We think the British public deserves to know, that their hard-earned money, is being spent responsibly and ethically, prioritising peace, stability and prosperity at home. We seek a foreign policy grounded in diplomacy and peace-building, rather than what can be costly and divisive military actions, that may have limited long-term success.

action: Not Ban Social Media for Under-16s
background: Banning social media for under-16s oversimplifies a complex issue. It cuts off connection, creativity and support, pushes use underground, and fails to teach safe digital habits. Education, safeguards and guidance work better than bans for young people today. This helps teens grow responsibly online

Extend the responsibility to declare a medical condition to the DVLA to include any medical professional who confirms the diagnosis. Enhance control of the regulatory management of Driving Mobility Centres.

action: Create a legal entitlement to two weeks’ paid bereavement leave for employees
background: We call on the Government to create a legal entitlement to two weeks (10 working days) of paid bereavement leave for employees, which can be taken flexibly and in separate periods where needed, to ensure consistent protection for bereaved workers across the UK.
additional_details: Bereavement leave policies vary widely, and can leave many workers without pay or forced back before they're ready. Cremations & funerals can take 10–14 days to arrange & death admin is often only possible in working hours. One report suggests grief costs the UK economy an estimated £23bn a year. A legal entitlement to two weeks’ paid bereavement leave could support people when they need it most, reduce financial stress, benefit the economy and help us all when we inevitably go through loss.

action: Allow all share owners to be named on the share register after dematerialisation
background: We wish for the government to seek a solution that allows shareholders to buy sell and hold shares recorded under their own official name instead of having to use nominee facilities post digitisation task force (when paper share certificates no longer will be used).
additional_details:

We are concerned that there will be no contest as to who owns what, unlike a pooled nominee account.

We recognise the Government's desire to withdraw paper share certificates from use, however we are asking for the Government to develop an alternate solution for shareholders to hold shares with their own name on the register.

background: Right now in the UK cat cafes are unable to buy any form of medical insurance for the cats within their care because they are not classed as pets. The government needs to change this so all cats legally owned by the business/business owners are also classed as pets and not just treated like stock.

Even small bills for things like check ups add up over time when you have several cats, and cats that need surgery lead many cafes to turn to funding pages in order to try and help pay for it. The government needs to change the law so that cafe owners are able to buy insurance, which I believe is a basic right for every cafe cat.

additional_details: Many instructors and third parties bulk-book driving test slots and resell them at higher prices, forcing learners to overpay or wait months. action: Allow visually impaired people to drive with bioptic glasses
background: We call on the Government to allow visually impaired people to drive with bioptic glasses.
additional_details: In our view, visually impaired people can encounter more challenges in their life compared to people without visual impairments person. So allowing them to drive with bioptics could make their life so much easier. Driving is often a requirement in day-to-day lives, and allowing visually impaired people to drive with bioptic glasses could boost their sense of independence. For example, they could do jobs further away from their house, or even work jobs like delivery drivers etc.

action: Require permanent road repairs instead of pothole patching.
background: Roads across Cheshire East, including Knutsford, Alderley Edge, Wilmslow, Holmes Chapel, Middlewich, Northwich and Mobberley, have become dangerously damaged. Potholes are deep, unavoidable and repeatedly damaging vehicles, with many residents forced to replace tyres and wheels.
additional_details:

This situation is not just damaging vehicles but poses a serious risk to public safety, particularly to motorcyclists, cyclists and drivers who may lose control or be forced into oncoming traffic. Without proper resurfacing, it is only a matter of time before someone is seriously injured or killed.

additional_details: Democracy relies on regular, guaranteed elections. When elections can be postponed by law, voting becomes a privilege rather than a right. A Constitution of Democracy would protect voters by making the right to vote absolute and preventing future erosion of democratic rights.

action: Ensure Peaceful Protesting Outside Animal-Testing Facilities Is Not Criminalised
background: We call on the Government to repeal the recent amendment to the Public Order Act 2023 which, in our view, could effectively ban peaceful protests at animal-testing facilities.
additional_details: We believe such protests shouldn’t be a crime when they pose no threat or intimidation, and we consider animal testing is an area of open ethical debate & the ability to protest against it should be protected. Regardless of your stance on animal testing, it should be the right of every citizen to stand up and peacefully express their ethical concerns in an organised fashion, including for animal rights at an animal-testing facility. We believe suppressing peaceful dissent does not protect science or public safety: it erodes our fundamental democratic freedom, and the list of "banned protests" will only grow longer. In our view a peaceful protester is not a criminal for trying to protect puppies.

Providing change to climate policy, taxes, regulation & planning changes. & providing grants.

We were once the forefront of manufacturing and innovation. We need radical policy change to restore our industry, so Britian can be industrial hub of the world again.

action: Require all LAs in England to publish why children enter elective home-ed
background: The Government must mandate that LAs in England record & publish why children have moved into elective home-education (EHE), including whether they have an EHCP or S19 alternative provision was requested or provided & how long they were out of school before deregistration.
additional_details:
This anonymised data should be published annually. Children are being recorded as EHE even when they have been pushed out through lack of suitable provision. Families are often EHE due to unmet SEND needs, EBSA, failure to deliver EHCP provision, reduced timetables & placement breakdown.
 
Government must require LAs to record and publish the reasons children move into EHE, so that children educated at home by choice are not merged with children forced out by systemic failure.

action: Nationalise water companies to make water a non profit publicly owned asset
background: To make water a non profit making national asset that ensures we have a secure water infrastructure that ensures our water security for future generations.
additional_details: We believe it has become very clear that funding capital infrastructure improvements has been a lower priority than shareholder profit and CEO salaries and bonuses by all the privatised water companies. Therefore, to ensure that our citizens water needs are met, now and in the future, water companies should be re-nationalised to ensure our country's water security in the future.

action: Ban client side scanning (CSS) of private communications on personal devices
background:
We ask the government to:
- Prohibit any requirement for client side scanning on consumer devices.
- Reaffirm its commitment to safeguarding democratic freedoms, protecting human rights, and preserving the security of its citizens’ digital communications.
additional_details: In our view, CSS is mass surveillance that could scan every private message, eroding the privacy rights protected by the European Convention on Human Rights and undermining democratic liberty. We believe that technically, it creates a universal backdoor: any state or malicious actor could exploit the on device scanning technology, exposing personal, financial and health data. We do not believe that enabling scanning technology that only targets illegal content is possible; once the code exists, it can be repurposed, and our privacy no longer exists.

action: Make Period Products Free of Charge in England
background: Period poverty is a pressing issue which the government must tackle. Following the success from Scotland's Period Products Act 2021, the Act should be enrolled across the UK so that women and girls can have access to menstrual products with dignity whenever needed.
additional_details: According to a survey by ActionAid (2023) 1 in 5 women in the UK struggle to afford menstrual products, equating to 2.8 million people (the equivalent of Greater Manchester's population). action: Make adultery illegal

action: Ensure no-one "ages out" of dependent status during parents' 10-year ILR route

action: Review levels of pay for Teachers' Maternity Leave

action: Stop the closure of Fareham and Gosport’s homeless shelters.
background: The funding for the homeless organisation, Two Saints, was redirected and they are now having to close two of the homeless hostels within the local area. Meaning an est. 30 individuals and their pets will be put on the streets. We want the government to please review this and give the funding back.
additional_details: These are peoples lives that are being messed with. People who have hit rock bottom and found help and charity from this organisation, and are now having to face the streets once again.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

Breach of

action: Ban palm oil in all food that is sold and manufactured in the UK
background: We call on the government to introduce legislation to ban palm oil as an ingredient in all foods manufactured or sold in the UK. This should include a phased transition period for businesses to reformulate products using more sustainable and locally sourced or low impact alternative oils.
additional_details: Palm oil is high in saturated fat, and when consumed in large quantities can make the nation even more unhealthy. This affects poorer households disproportionately as they can't usually afford healthier options putting more strain on an already broken NHS.

action: Expand the MP Recall Petition Process to include party defections
background: When MPs defect to another party during a Parliamentary term, they betray the trust of constituents who supported them. Voters elect MPs as local representatives, but party affiliation and manifesto commitments almost always drive that decision. Our political institutions must recognise this.
additional_details:
The Recall of MPs Act 2015 should be reformed to include voluntary party defections as a trigger condition. 

Some may ask why not instead mandate automatic by-election upon defection. While this approach has its merits, by-elections cost taxpayers an average of £240,000, so it makes sense to only hold one when there is clear constituent demand. Some MP defections, such as Lee Anderson's in 2024, reflect shifting voter preferences - in such cases, automatic by-elections can prove unnecessary.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Extend the Recall of MPs Act to cover MPs who change or leave political party 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754418

action: Introduce national support standards for autistic children with PDA
background: We urge the Government to recognise the growing cohort of autistic children with a Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA) profile who are unable to attend school safely.
additional_details:
We believe that in demand-heavy, compliance-led settings, they may face escalating crisis, including increased risk of self-harm and suicidal ideation.
 
In our view PDA is inconsistently supported across education, health and local authorities, resulting in many children experiencing preventable crisis. For some children, proximity to mainstream environments triggers crisis; without timely access to low-arousal or alternative learning pathways, risk increases. We ask the Government to strengthen partnerships through improved awareness of PDA-related needs, supported by training and accountability, so children are not required to fail first.

action: Abolish the tv licence
background: To abolish tv licences, for the whole of the UK
additional_details: We already pay for streaming services and channels. For those people who struggling it makes it harder for us to simply just relax and watch a bit of tv.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Scrap the TV Licence
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754524

action: Review Child Maintenance Service (CMS) rules on reduced income claims & arrears
background: Review CMS rules and processes for accepting reduced income claims, managing arrears, and allowing special expenses deductions. The review should ensure decisions are properly evidenced, consistently applied, and prioritise children receiving the correct level of financial support.
additional_details:
Current CMS processes allow paying parents to repeatedly reduce payments, renegotiate arrears, and submit special expenses claims with limited scrutiny. 
Errors, delays, and inconsistent calculations are leaving children without the financial support they are entitled to for long periods. 
Arrears can be prolonged for years, undermining confidence in the system and causing financial strain for receiving parents. 
A review is urgently needed to ensure fairness, accuracy, and accountability.
rejection_details:
Review child maintenance service (CMS) process for accepting reduced payments
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/748156

action: Provide funding to partially cover costs of private healthcare
background: Provide funding for any NHS patients to access private treatments for procedures that the NHS typically covers, covering the costs equivalent to what the NHS would normally pay if the treatment were conducted through the NHS. Patients would then only need to cover the difference in cost.
additional_details: This approach would not only reduce waiting times significantly but also lessen the pressure on NHS resources, helping it focus on emergencies and those in critical need.

action: Introduce a statutory duty to acknowledge and support menstrual health.
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce new legislation placing a statutory duty on schools, colleges, training providers and employers to recognise, accommodate and support menstrual health and period-related impacts for girls and women, from adolescence through adulthood.
additional_details: This duty should apply universally, without requiring proof of severity, medical diagnosis or disclosure. Menstrual health affects girls and women from early education through working life. Symptoms vary month to month and are a normal biological reality, yet many face stigma, penalties or lack of support in schools and workplaces. A statutory duty would promote equality, dignity, educational attainment and long-term participation without medicalising a natural process.

action: Investigate the service performance of couriers & enforce minimum standards.
background:
Investigate courier service's performance and complaint handling.
Introduce and enforce minimum standards for courier services.
Apply penalties or corrective measures where standards are not met.
Ensure customers have meaningful protection and recourse.
additional_details:
Across the UK, customers regularly experience lost, delayed, damaged, or misdelivered parcels, alongside an ongoing lack of customer support. Customers report being unable to speak to real people, receiving generic automated responses, or having legitimate complaints closed without resolution.
Repeated service failures should trigger regulatory scrutiny, companies must be held to enforceable standards, and customers should have access to human customer support and fair compensation processes.
rejection_details:
Ensure couriers are fully responsible for delivery issues & introduce penalties 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747939

action: Align foreign & trade policy with EU and set steps towards closer integration
background: The Government should formally reassess the UK’s foreign and trade strategy and commit to a much deeper political, economic and regulatory alignment with the EU, going beyond, what we consider vague, “closer ties” and setting out clear, time-bound steps for stronger integration.
additional_details: Such steps could include considering another referendum of whether to join the EU. We believe the global political landscape has changed fundamentally and that the US can no longer be relied upon as a stable or predictable partner, as shown by recent tariffs imposed on allies. We believe Labour’s current EU policy, based on a limited “reset”, is already extremely outdated and that the UK’s economic security, trade resilience and international credibility now depend on a decisive shift back towards Europe rather than continued drift. In our view, this is no longer just politics, our security and safety depends on action and now.

action: Bring back the BBC sitcom Goodnight Sweetheart. A cultural petition.
background: We call on you to debate the cultural value and public support for reviving the sitcom Goodnight Sweetheart. The show originally aired from 1993 to 1999 with a revival episode in 2016, remains popular through repeats and streaming, and a new continuation has been written and is ready for production.
additional_details: We believe Goodnight Sweetheart remains culturally significant, celebrates British television history, and continues to resonate with audiences across generations. We therefore ask Parliament to debate the value of encouraging the BBC to consider commissioning new episodes of the programme, reflecting public interest in the return of this iconic series.

action: Remove 6 year limit on paying voluntary NI Contributions to repair gap in record
background: Anything less than 52 weeks' worth of NI contributions results in that whole year not being counted, so you get nothing if you didn't get NI credits. Currently it is only possible to pay voluntary contributions for gaps from the last 6 years. It's unfair, and this limit should be removed.
additional_details: Hard working people are already contributing with taxes and NI contributions to our society so we deserve something back. We don't want anything for free, we are happy to pay voluntary contributions to have the years with gaps recognised. It should be allowed, they are not gift years, we are happy to pay. Why should we lose whole years for only a few weeks' gaps? We believe it is very unfair, so we don't want handouts, we want to be allowed to pay voluntarily to have the years recognised.

action: Make Rape Prosecutions and Convictions a Priority in UK Law
background:
Rape is a serious violent crime in England and Wales, only a small proportion of reported cases result in charge or prosecution.
 Many survivors face :long delays, cases dropped without explanation, and a lack of faith in the justice system, fear, trauma, & previous experiences of being ignored.
additional_details:
We call on the UK Government to:
Make rape investigations and prosecutions a clear priority for police & prosecutors
Improve charge & conviction rates through better forensic investigation, evidence handling, and specialist victim support
Review sentencing guidelines to ensure penalties reflect the severity and lifelong impact of rape
Ensure timely investigations and trials so survivors are not subjected to prolonged trauma
Invest to encourage reporting and reduce stigma around sexual violence
rejection_details:
We're not entirely clear what you are calling for that might not already be happening or just have happened recently:

CPS has made rape prosecutions a priority:
https://www.cps.gov.uk/publication/cps-annual-rape-scrutiny-report-october-2025

Sentencing guidelines were toughened in 2023 
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/sentencing-bill-2023/sentencing-bill-factsheet-serious-sexual-offences-sentencing-and-release-arrangements

action: Provide safe accommodation and support for people experiencing homelessness
background: We call on the UK Government to provide guaranteed, safe accommodation for people experiencing homelessness, alongside proper mental health, addiction, and employment support. Current systems often fail those with complex needs, leaving them excluded from help rather than supported.
additional_details: Take urgent action to end rough sleeping by funding emergency accommodation, reopening unused buildings, and ensuring support services are accessible to people with complex needs.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

National rough sleeping programme: permanent, safe accommodation and support
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747196

action: Ban No Caller ID phone calls
background: I'd like to ban the use of No caller ID phone calls, as well as measures to ensure that when a person blocks a phone number, that number can't still contact your number through no caller ID even if they're blocked.
additional_details: I think that if you block a phone number, they shouldn't be able to contact you again. It's an invasion of privacy and blocking a phone number means you don't want to talk to that person any more. The fact that they can still contact you through No caller ID mode on their mobile phone defeats the whole point of being able to block somebody. No caller ID should be made illegal for people's privacy and could also help to stop bullying within teenagers/ adolescent people.

action: Allow full-time students who provide 35+ hours care to receive Carer’s Allowance
background: Amend the eligibility rules for Carer’s Allowance so that people in full-time education who provide at least 35 hours of care per week can receive Carer’s Allowance, provided all other conditions are met.
additional_details: Many students provide 35 hours or more of unpaid care each week for disabled parents or relatives but are excluded from Carer’s Allowance solely because they are in full-time education. This forces carers to choose between education and financial support, even though the care must still be provided. The rule is outdated and unfairly treats student carers differently from others providing the same level of care. Eligibility should be based on hours of care, not education status.

action: STOP Inverclyde council raising council tax once again to line their own pockets
background: Stop Inverclyde from raising council tax once again, it was raised last year by 8% however the council had the utter audacity to the give their councillors an 8 % pay increase which is utterly deplorable.
additional_details:
One of the most impoverished area in Inverclyde and yet the council continue to take from people’s
Pockets to line their own pockets with corrupt council leader.
rejection_details: This is a local issue that doesn't fall under the responsibility of the UK Government of or Parliament, so I am afraid we can't accept it. You may wish to petition the Scottish Parliament instead.

action: To issue guidance to prevent glorification of British Somaliland.
background: We ask the UK Government to formally acknowledge Britain’s role in creating the Somaliland Protectorate and issue clear guidance to councils, institutions, and venues. This will ensure colonial history is not misused to justify political claims or romanticise “British Somaliland
additional_details: Some members of the UK-based Somaliland community are increasingly organising local events glorifying British Somaliland and its colonial legacy. These activities misrepresent historical facts and perpetuate British colonial frameworks that have no contemporary legal or political legitimacy, risking division within British communities. We ask the Government to clarify historical facts, issue formal guidance or policy, and support community-led engagement and lawful oversight.
rejection_details: The Government has no power to direct local councils on this issue, nor private community groups. Nor does it have a role in determining historical facts.

action: Nationalise water companies now.
background: Nationalise water companies within the next two parliaments.
additional_details: Access to clean drinking water is a most basic  human right and companies should not be profiteering off it.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757426

action: Mandate Standardised Bricklaying Pay Rates Across the UK
background: Establish national standard bricklaying pay rates for use by housebuilders and mandate payment for all work done. We believe this will stop unpaid tasks, prevent undercutting, protect apprentices and help fix the construction skills shortage.
additional_details: We also believe bricklayers face widespread underpayment due to rates being set too low, unpaid extras, and income lost to delays outside their control. This causes financial stress, mental health issues, and drives skilled workers out of the trade. Fair, transparent national rates would stabilise earnings, support apprentices, prevent undercutting, and help maintain a reliable workforce needed to deliver housing across the UK.

action: Create a health ID card for emergencies
background: The government should create a card similar to an ID card that includes a chip, a picture, and all relevant health details. This could help people who have accidents and can't communicate with the ambulance crew properly, such as about their allergies.
additional_details: This card could be used as an ID and can help ambulances give the correct and fastest first aid. This will enable them to identify the patient more easily and provide assistance more quickly and course in the correct way. To achieve this, the government needs to update the database and integrate it with the ambulance tablets and card reader.

action: Review of mandatory cat microchipping and informed consent requirements
background: Review the current law for compulsory microchipping of cats in England. A review could consider introducing microchipping as optional, or setting clearer requirements to ensure cat owners are informed of recognised but rare risks, including the potential for injection-site sarcomas.
additional_details:
This could be known as Princess' law.

Injection-site sarcomas are a documented but uncommon adverse outcome of any injections in cats & may be aggressive in nature.

For context, my cat, Princess, later developed an injection-site sarcoma & was ultimately euthanised to prevent further suffering. This submission does not allege negligence or misconduct by veterinary professionals, but seeks a proportionate review of existing policy to balance animal welfare, owner autonomy, & public policy objectives.

action: Reduce roadside littering: penalty points, increase fines, fund litter picks
background: Allow authorities to impose penalty points on drivers for discarding litter from a vehicle. Increase minimum on the spot fines for littering and awareness through TV/online campaigns. Insist businesses take more responsibility in anti-litter campaigns. Increase budget for highways litter picks.
additional_details: Roads are increasingly becoming covered in litter. This is no longer just an urban problem - it affects all roads from motorways to rural country lanes. The issue appears to be worsening, and it seems little is being done to stop it. The problem not only blights our country, but also poses a danger to wildlife and, on occasion, other road users. The visual pollution negatively impacts citizens but also presents our country unfavourably to overseas visitors.

action: Revoke the Declaration of Independence and assert British rule over the USA
background: The Americans in 1776 signed the declaration of independence declaring America independent of the Kingdom of Great Britain. Since then, they have made a hash of it. They can't be trusted anymore so we should take control back.
additional_details: Trump's MAGA movement is proving to be a danger to the rest of the world. First Venezuela, next Greenland. Then, the world. It's time we used Trump's own words to the effect he wants. The British landed in American and claimed it as their own when in reality it should have been owned by the Native Americans. It's time to put Donald Trump into a care home and fix the mess that's left of the USA.
rejection_details: It is a matter for the Government of the US of A to revoke what is their own declaration.

action: Review the mandatory fortification of non-wholemeal wheat flour with folic acid.
background: We call on the UK Government to review and remove the mandatory fortification of non-wholemeal wheat flour with folic acid. We ask the Government to ensure that unfortified flour remains available and that flour products are clearly labelled so consumers can make informed dietary choices.
additional_details:
The UK Government introduced mandatory folic acid fortification of non-wholemeal wheat flour as a public health measure.

What We Want the Government to Do:
Review the current requirement for mandatory folic acid fortification
Remove the blanket mandate and allow unfortified flour to be produced and sold
Require clear labelling of flour products indicating whether folic acid has been added
Consult with consumers, health professionals, and food producers when reviewing the policy
rejection_details:
There is already a petition open on this subject, which you may wish to sign:

Ensure access to non-whole meal flour without folic acid fortification
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751401

action: Protect Iranian Civilians and Hold the Iranian Regime Fully Accountable now
background: We call on UK Government to protect Iranian civilians by condemning Iran at UN, expanding sanctions on officials responsible for killings, repression, downgrading diplomatic relations, taking measures affecting the Iranian Embassy if abuses continue,supporting UN investigations & assisting refugees.
additional_details: Recent protests in Iran have been met with mass arrests, arbitrary detention, and violent suppression. Many face torture, unfair trials, and possible execution without urgent action. The UK has obligations under UN Charter Arts 1 & 55, Genocide Convention Art I, ICCPR Arts 2, 6 & 21, and UK Human Rights Sanctions Regulations. Immediate measures are needed to uphold human rights, protect vulnerable civilians, prevent further widespread civilian deaths and suffering, and support basic freedoms.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition which is already open:

Sever UK-Iran ties, withdraw recognition of Iran’s regime & expel all diplomats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756775

In the time since you submitted your petition, the UK Government announced on 2 February that it was applying sanctions to several individuals and one organisation in response to those whom it said have committed human rights violations in Iran. You can read more here if you wish: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-announces-sanctions-against-perpetrators-of-human-rights-violations-in-iran

In January, the Foreign Secretary made a statement to Parliament, in which she condemned the killing of Iranian protestors. You can read the statement here: https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2026-01-13/debates/94D92574-B962-41F2-BD4C-B290EC113BC7/Iran

On 23 January, the UK's Ambassador for Human Rights gave a speech at a UN Human Rights Council Special Session. The Ambassador stated that the Iranian authorities must be held accountable and that the UN’s Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, must be renewed, which it subsequently was.

You can read her speech here: https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/un-human-rights-council-special-session-to-address-the-deteriorating-human-rights-situation-in-the-islamic-republic-of-iran-23-january-2026

And you can read the Council's resolution here: https://www.ohchr.org/en/media-advisories/2026/01/human-rights-council-adopts-resolution-extending-mandates-fact-finding

Further information on this topic can be found in the House of Commons Library's briefing on the UK and international response regarding the 2026 Iran protests: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10462/

action: Introduce mandatory email route for customer feedback for companies which email
background: We call on the Government to introduce a mandatory requirement to provide email route for customers to respond via, on to all companies that use email to contact customers. Companies should be required to provide public complaints email address, instead of online portals or lengthy phone queues.
additional_details: We believe that many companies use email to communicate with customers but refuse to accept emails in return, breaking the principle of fair, two-way communication. In our view, by forcing customers into complex portals or long phone queues, poor customer service is often hidden behind barriers to contact. Requiring a public complaints email could restore symmetry, simplify communication, and make accessible, accountable customer service the norm.

action: Review suitability of NHS mental health services for Neurodivergent people
background: At present, I believe people with Autism, ADHD and other Neurodivergent conditions do not receive appropriate Mental Health treatment and care they need and deserve through NHS Mental Health services. All NHS Mental Health services must be suitable for Neurodivergent people.
additional_details: I believe NHS Mental Health services are not fit for purpose for Neurodivergent people. Treatment methods are inadequate for many Neurodivergent people due to some not recognising that Mental Health issues affect Neurodivergent people differently to non Neurodivergent people. Many Neurodivergent people find CBT (Cognitive Behavioural Therapy) doesn’t work for them and have to go to private mental health support. There must always be reasonable adjustments to treatment.

action: Rework the OSA with features like Government provided age verification
background: I think it's unlikely for the UK Government to repeal the Online Safety Act. However it should be their responsibility to help cover things like non-affordable age verification and/or offer help with reducing collected user information that should be private.
additional_details:
The Online Safety Act has been poorly thought through and implemented. In order to change this I would like to see things introduced such as a privacy-respecting Government issued ID (verifying you are 18+ without any private information). Alongside implementing this ID system for smaller business/websites paid for by the Government allowing companies to more easily remain accessible and suitably private in the UK.

If this act is to be around for the foreseeable future it needs an overhaul.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736140

action: Enshrine the current status of Greenland in UK Law
background: The President of the United States, Donald Trump wants Greenland to become part of the USA. I believe this is wrong due to it being imperialism. The future of Greenland is for Greenlanders and the Kingdom of Denmark to decide, nobody else. The current status of Greenland must be enshrined in UK Law.
additional_details: I believe Greenlanders overwhelmingly want to stay part of the Kingdom of Denmark, with the possibility of Greenland becoming a fully independent country in the future. This is a matter for Greenlanders and the Kingdom of Denmark only, nobody else. The UK Government must Legislate for the current status of Greenland to be enshrined in UK Law.
rejection_details:
Whatever is said about a foreign country in UK law only applies in the UK and has no bearing on the action of foreign states.  We don't know what you are otherwise trying to do in this petition.

There is an existing petition on Greenland which shares some of your concerns and which you may wish to sign:

Call on Denmark to invoke NATO's Article 4 due to USA's statements on Greenland
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756560

action: Public inquiry: NHS care standards for the elderly, disabled & chronically ill
background: Commission an independent public inquiry into NHS care standards for elderly, disabled, and chronically ill patients, including access to treatment, safeguarding, discharge practices, clinical decision-making, and whether financial pressures are compromising patient safety and dignity.
additional_details: There is widespread public concern about delays in treatment, premature discharge, inadequate safeguarding, and failures in clinical decision-making affecting vulnerable patients. Many families report avoidable harm and poor outcomes. An independent inquiry is needed to establish the facts, restore public confidence, and ensure patient welfare is never compromised by cost pressures.

action: Review need for a national standard of care for children with cerebral palsy
background: NHS England introduced a Cerebral Palsy Commissioning Framework in 2025, but it has only been piloted in some Integrated Care Boards and not adopted nationwide.
additional_details:
We call for full implementation of a national minimum standard of care, guaranteeing access to therapy, orthopaedics, complex movement clinics, named care coordinators, early intervention, clear waiting times, and support for UK research including stem cell trials. These changes could be known as Frankie's Future. 
 
Many children still face a postcode lottery for care, with families forced to fight for support during crucial early years.

action: End the Saturday Football Blackout in the UK
background: Abolish the 3 pm blackout, allowing fans to watch live top-flight football legally at any time. Modernise broadcasting rules to reflect today’s digital, on-demand viewing habits. Protect both fans’ rights and the sustainability of football by encouraging legal, accessible ways to watch games.
additional_details: The 3 pm Saturday football blackout is outdated and largely ineffective in the modern era. Originally intended to protect lower-league match attendance, it now has limited impact and often drives fans to watch Premier League games via illegal streams. With digital platforms and on-demand services widely available, the blackout restricts fans unnecessarily and fails to achieve its original purpose, making it time for a modernised approach.
rejection_details: Decisions about when to hold and broadcast football matches are a matter for the FA, the Premier League and the Football League, and broadcasters, not the Government or House of Commons.

action: Review the student loan system and explore alternatives
background: Consider options for abolishing the current system and alternatives such as a progressive graduate tax, scrapping interest rates, or writing off existing debts to address its unfair and burdensome impact on graduates.
additional_details: The student loan system requires some graduates to repay 9% of earnings above a frozen threshold, with debts written off after 30-40 years. We feel this functions like a horrifically high graduate tax that can destroy living standards, especially amid low incomes, and is a drag on the economy. We believe it disproportionately disadvantages students whose parents cannot afford to pay fees upfront, trapping them in a loan system while wealthier families can opt out entirely.

action: Nationalise the water industry or reorganise as not for profit organisations
background: It is time to ensure that the water industry is run for the benefit of people, by renationalising the water industry or the creation of purely not for profit organisations capable and duty bound to ensure proper investment into water and sewerage treatment infrastructure
additional_details: Given the disgraceful management of water companies, ongoing water supply issues and continuous marine pollution events it is time to cut off the gravy train of unfathomable shareholder and board payouts and to ensure that the water industry is run for the benefit of the consumer, for whom safe and continuous water supply and clean marine environments is nothing less than a right and an entitlement
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757426

action: Make a taco bell in Taunton
background: Make a taco bell in taunton

action: Allow small pets to travel in aircraft cabins when entering the UK
background: Review and update UK rules that require pets to travel as cargo. Introduce a controlled system allowing small cats and dogs to travel in aircraft cabins when entering the UK, under strict health, safety and biosecurity conditions, with airline discretion.
additional_details: “The UK is one of the only countries requiring pets to travel as cargo when entering the country, causing unnecessary stress, welfare risks and high costs for owners. Many UK families living abroad are forced into long, complex journeys to avoid cargo. Other countries allow in-cabin pet travel safely with strict controls. A regulated UK system would improve animal welfare and support returning families without increasing disease risk.”
rejection_details:
We already have a petition open on this subject which you may wish to sign:

Allow small pets to travel in the cabin on flights entering the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750817

action: Sort out potholes in Newport, south wales.
background: Fill in the potholes and uneven road surfaces and smooth them over for suitable vehicle use. Redo the road if necessary.
additional_details: Cars in Newport city are being damaged due to the amount of potholes in the city. We pay hundreds a year in vehicle tax to “pay for the roads” but why should we pay to have our cars on unsuitable roads? They are a MAJOR hazard and need action. We have our cars safety checked to be able to use the road, but why isn’t the road safety checked for the cars? These potholes are causing crashes and injury. Sort it out or we take action ourselves.

action: school pupils not have to wear  school uniforms instead
background:
School kids do not like uncomfortable uniforms they like to dress how they want
To be more comfortable
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.

Government guidance states that "It is for the governing board of a school to decide: rules about appearance; whether there should be a school uniform policy and, if so, what that should be". You can read the full guidance here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/school-uniform/school-uniforms

We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. You could start a new petition explaining clearly what change you would like the Government to make to its guidance to schools.

action: Protect the Abraham Lincoln memorial in Manchester, relocate the migrant camp.
background: Work with Manchester City Council to relocate the encampment from Lincoln Square, safeguard the Grade II listed Abraham Lincoln statue and plaques, and fund humane alternative accommodation and support for those affected. Relocate the migrant camp humanely; protect the memorial and plaques.
additional_details: Lincoln Square is a commemorative site centred on the Grade II listed Abraham Lincoln statue and inscriptions, linked to the 1862 address from Manchester working people and Lincoln’s reply. An encampment around the monument risks damage, blocks access, and undermines the dignity of a public memorial. I want government to help council services move people on safely, with proper housing, sanitation, and outreach support.
rejection_details: We cannot accept this petition as it is a local matter, and not the responsibility of the UK Government or Parliament. You may wish to contact Manchester City Council.

action: Ringfence 75% of all VED revenue raised to be reinvested in road system
background: The Government must allocate a minimum of 75% of all monies raised through Vehicle Excise Duty to be reinvested in the building, maintenance and repair of the road system in the UK.
additional_details: The revenue raised by the Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) in 2023/24 amounted to £7.8 billion, of which 25% (£1.95 billion) was reinvested back into the building, repair and maintenance of the road system of the UK. We believe the amount that is currently allocated to the roads is clearly inadequate, and as a result has rendered our roads 'dangerous': this manifests itself as a direct danger to pedestrians and all road users causing death, injury and damage.

action: Raise VED road tax for cars registered before April 2017 to at least £195 a year
background:
We believe that we all need to pay for road tax in a fair and consistent way.
Pre 2017 vehicles only pay £20-£30 if their emissions are low.
In our view, the minimum road tax should be £195 for all vehicles.
additional_details:
We think it's unfair to pay less tax for a car just because it's a bit older.
The road network in the UK needs improvement and the lack of funds to maintain and build new roads is becoming an issue.
Everyone needs to pay their way into the system if you plan to use the public road network.

action: Transition the UK Nuclear Deterrent to Full Strategic and Technical Independence
background: Government to initiate a long-term programme to decouple the UK nuclear deterrent from United States technical and logistical support; invest in the domestic development of missile delivery systems & maintenance infrastructure to ensure the UK possesses a truly sovereign "Life-of-Type" capability.
additional_details: The UK’s deterrent relies on the US-managed Trident missile pool and technical support. Relying on a third party for critical security infrastructure can create a strategic vulnerability. To ensure national safety regardless of shifts in foreign politics, we believe we must achieve full technical sovereignty. We call for a transition to a domestic delivery system and maintenance framework, ensuring the UK possesses a truly independent "Life-of-Type" capability similar to France.

action: Make it a specific criminal offence for an MP to lie in Parliament.
background: Debate whether Members of Parliament who knowingly lie in Parliament should face legal consequences, or be treated as having committed serious misconduct, in line with the standards applied to other public office holders such as police officers, judges, and civil servants.
additional_details: Public trust depends on honesty from those in power. Although mechanisms such as the Ministerial Code, parliamentary standards processes and correcting the record exist, they are political rather than legal and are widely seen as weak and inconsistently enforced. Other public officials can face criminal or professional sanctions for dishonesty, yet MPs are largely protected when making false statements in Parliament. We ask the Government to debate reforms to ensure deliberate deception by MPs is subject to meaningful and independent accountability, through criminal law or a clear offence of serious misconduct in public office.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

MPs cannot be prosecuted for what they say in the House of Commons during Parliamentary proceedings because of Parliamentary privilege. You can find out more about privilege on the Parliament website: https://guidetoprocedure.parliament.uk/articles/szEQlFBF/freedom-of-speech

action: Cap student loan interest rates at inflation (CPI), do not apply retrospectively
background:
We ask the Government to:
Cap student loan interest at inflation (CPI), and
Ensure future changes are not applied retrospectively to existing borrowers.
We think this would restore fairness, transparency, and confidence in the student finance system.
additional_details: We call on the Government to reform student loan interest rates so borrowers have a realistic chance of repaying what they owe. Current student loan interest rates exceed inflation for many graduates, meaning that despite making regular repayments, balances continue to grow rather than fall. For many borrowers, this can make the loan effectively impossible to repay in full. Student loans were intended to be a fair, income-contingent contribution to education — not a debt that increases indefinitely.

action: STOP Water Companies charging a ‘Fixed Charge’ on all household water bills.
background: Stop all Water Companies charging a daily ‘Fixed Charge’ on household bills.With the cost of living crisis consumers cannot afford these charges,the standing charges which in some cases be more than the cost of the actual bill is an unfair system & gives no incentive for households to save water.
additional_details: To abolish daily Fixed Charges by Water Companies.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746127

action: Require MPs who defect to another party to face a by-election.
background: Require legislation so that when an MP defects to another political party during a Parliament they must seek a fresh mandate through a by-election. This would protect voter trust, prevent unapproved shifts in representation, and ensure democratic legitimacy.
additional_details: When an MP switches party mid-Parliament, voters may end up represented by a party they did not choose. Many people vote based on party, manifesto and leadership, not just the individual. Defections can therefore erode trust and alter the political balance without consent. Requiring by-elections for party defection would give constituents a democratic say and help maintain legitimacy and accountability in our parliamentary system.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

background: For the safety of road users Queens Head Junction, Oswestry to have average speed cameras or 40mph speed limit put in place.
additional_details: There's been so many accidents at Queens Head Junction, myself included due to people's speed coming out of Junction and the turning across 60mph road. There's been fatalities there, road is cambered and greasy surface. Its renowned for its dangers. Speed should be reduced to 40mph or have average speed cameras to regulate people's speed and ensuring safety for the road users.

action: Ensure all food and product packaging clearly states any high risk additives.
background: Research on high-risk additives points to inflammation, endocrine and gut issues, and carcingenocity, cause of cancer. Many foods, such as crumpets/ wraps/ pancakes, nuggets, hand wash, pastas and many more contain many high risk additives. This needs to be clearly shown to the consumer.
additional_details: The consumer should be made aware when a product contains a high-risk additive. These are harmful and can cause terminal illness if consumed regularly everyday. If the high-risk additives are clearly visible on the packet, name and how many, consumers then have a choice whether to purchase and consume. The nutritional value is clearly shown green/amber/red. An indication if what you're consuming is healthy or not. However a 'green' product can still contain high risk and therefor is not healthy.

action: Disregard compensation paid to injured service personnel from UC calculation
background: Introduce legislation to disregard any payments made to ex-service personnel in the form of injury or income compensation from Universal Credit (UC) calculations, no matter in which manner this payment has been paid out (lump sum or ongoing payments) indefinitely.
additional_details: Some service members and ex-service personnel who are permanently injured lose Universal Credit after 12 months because their Armed Forces Compensation Scheme (AFCS) payments, and War Pensions are treated as capital. We believe this is disproportionate, forcing some families to spend money meant to cover long-term injury, illness, or loss of independence just to survive.

action: To not ban social media for under 16's
background: I would like the parliament to rethink the decision of banning social media for under 16's. Social media is a way for people to find new interests, teach you things such as how to sing or dance and more. With this ban, people under 16 would be unprepared to use it as social media is developing.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Do not ban social media for under 16s" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757233

action: Legislate for the repair of potholes within a time frame in the UK.
background: Set legislation for National Highways and local councils to repair and make safe every pothole found on roads, dual carriageways and motorways, within a specific time frame. This should link to a transparent public national reporting system to track progress and accountability.
additional_details: We pay significant taxes for road use and fuel duty. In 2023–24, the Government raised £32 billion from road-related taxes. Motorists also maintain roadworthy vehicles via MOTs yet face extra damage costs from poorly maintained roads. We believe it is time for road maintenance to become a national priority for the public’s wellbeing. Funding needs to be ring-fenced so that we have a well-maintained road network to reflect the UK’s commitment to a more sustainable society that supports economic growth.

action: Require teachers to follow the school uniform standards as pupils
background: Introduce guidance requiring teachers in secondary schools to follow the same or equivalent uniform standards as pupils. We think this would ensure fairness, consistency and non-discriminatory enforcement of school dress codes.
additional_details: Many secondary schools strictly enforce uniform rules for pupils, issuing, in our view, sanctions for minor breaches. However, teachers are often exempt and may wear clothing that would not be permitted for students. This inconsistency can feel unfair and discriminatory to pupils, undermine respect for rules, and negatively affect wellbeing. We believe applying equivalent standards could promote equality, consistency, and positive role modelling in schools.

action: Stop purchasing American goods until threat of extra tariffs are removed
background: Advise UK citizens to boycott purchases manufactured in USA
additional_details: America is threatening all of Europe with more tarrifs due to standing up to them over purchasing or invading Greenland
rejection_details: unclear as to whether threat of tariffs still exists or has been removed

action: Introduce a 10 year minimum sentence for manslaughter
background: My brother was killed, and I do not think that the sentence that his killer received was long enough. We think the minimum sentence for all manslaughter cases should be 10 years time served, to provide justice for victims and their families. This should be known as Andrew's law.
additional_details: We don’t want any more families to have to go through what we have. We also want the crime of manslaughter to be taken more seriously. Bringing in a minimum served sentence of 10 years will in our view be the first step in acknowledging the seriousness of the crime and the debating consequences it has on the families of the victim when lives are taken.

action: Strengthen regulations for parcel delivery companies to protect consumers
background: The Government should introduce stronger regulations for parcel delivery companies to ensure reliable service, proper handling of parcels, and fair treatment for consumers. Clear standards would help reduce missing items, improve accountability, and create a more consistent delivery experience.
additional_details: Stronger regulation is needed because unreliable parcel delivery affects both consumers and small businesses. Missing or damaged parcels create financial losses, harm customer trust, and increase operating costs for small companies. Clear national standards would improve reliability, protect consumers, and support small businesses that rely on consistent delivery services.
rejection_details:

action: Government to advise monarch to refuse/cancel state visits with hostile powers
background: The Government should advise the Monarch against facilitating a ceremonial head of state visit where a foreign state is engaged in hostile activity - whether economic, diplomatic, military or otherwise - that is directly contrary to UK interests and/or the rule of international law.
additional_details: The Monarch acts on the advice of the Government of the day when deciding whether to facilitate the considerable honour of a ceremonial head of state visit with the UK. We think it is not appropriate to offer such an honour in cases where the foreign state concerned is engaged in taking or promoting activity directly and seriously contrary to our national interests. A state visit is even more inappropriate in situations where the head of state is personally directing any such hostile action.

background: MPs who change parties mid term should face an automatic by election As the people who voted for the MP did so because they like their parties policies

action: Save Blackpool heritage Rigby Road Depot and heritage trams from destruction!
background: Blackpool was the first & last place in the UK to have trams. Been here since 1885. Since 2011, modern trams were introduced & heritage & illuminated trams have run together. The local council is threatening to pull down the old depot, leaving the heritage trams to cease running forever in Blackpool
additional_details: We, the people of Blackpool, the tourists, the tram enthusiasts want the depot saved. Volunteers have primarily run it as a visitor attraction, putting countless hours of work into restoring and running the trams and raising money for it's preservation. Without the depot the trams have nowhere to go but be scrapped or sold off. Blackpool illuminated and heritage trams are as part of Blackpool as the Tower, piers and Pleasure Beach is! action: Do Not Scrap the 1265 Directed Time Provision for Teachers
background: We are concerned about reports that the 1265 directed time policy for teachers may be scrapped. We feel teachers have faced real terms pay cuts, and view 1265 as the only thing protecting staff from even more unpaid and excessive workload. Recruitment and retention is already critical. We say no.
additional_details: Our school staff and young people deserve better. We oppose trying to run state schools on the cheap. There is a cost of living crisis and many teachers and support staff have 2nd/3rd jobs, which they wont be able to commit to. Scrapping 1265 in favour of unregulated and unpaid hours will lead to more poverty and burnout of staff. This will not help our young people. We want to attract people into the profession, not expect them to be 'on call' at the whim of CEO's/ Leadership - unpaid.

action: Fund improvement to PCOS, Endometriosis, and Fertility Health care and treatment
background: We believe PCOS, endometriosis, and other fertility conditions are poorly understood, often dismissed, and leave patients in chronic pain with little hope. We urge the government to fund improvements in medical training and research to ensure earlier diagnosis, and provide proper long-term support.
additional_details: I’ve suffered from PCOS and other fertility conditions—heavy periods, hair loss, chronic pain—and felt dismissed by doctors. I help others by sharing my story online, but I shouldn’t have to. No one should feel scared, alone, or left without answers. I’m starting this petition to urge the government to fund research, improve diagnosis, and provide real support so people like us finally get the care we deserve.

action: BAN ON INDOOR USE OF ALL FIREWORKS, SPARKLERS, AND PYROTECHNICS IN PUBLIC VENUES
background: The British Burn Association, LSEBN and CRG are concerned with the safety of fireworks, sparklers and pyrotechnics in public venues following the recent tragedy in Crans-Montana, where 40 people lost their lives and more than 115 were seriously injured in a fire during New Year’s celebrations.
additional_details:
This catastrophe is not an isolated event. Over recent decades, repeated incidents linked to indoor pyrotechnics and unsafe celebratory practices have caused devastating loss of life in public venues across Europe — including nightclub fires in Volendam (2001), Bucharest (2015), and Kocani (2025).
In the last 50 years, over 550 people have died and more than 1,500 have sustained severe, life-changing burn injuries in similar incidents in Europe.
rejection_details:
We already have a petition which has just opened on this subject, which you may wish to sign:

Ban the sale and use of indoor fireworks
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/755883

action: Make children eligible for Bereavement Support Payment after death of a parent
background: Review Bereavement Support Payment so children who lose a legal parent are not left without help. Bereaved children should be supported in their own right regardless of their parents’ relationship status or who the deceased lived with.
additional_details: My partner died suddenly under tragic circumstances. Although we were in a loving, committed relationship, because we did not live together neither I nor our children received bereavement support payment. My partner contributed substantially to their upbringing. Upon his death this financial contribution vanished. Our experience shows why bereavement support must focus on children, so no family faces financial hardship alongside such a devastating loss.

action: New criminal offence for paedophile hunters to post online before a conviction
background: Make it a criminal offence for online paedophile hunters to post anything regarding the people they accuse before that person has been convicted.
additional_details: This is due to the number of innocent people being accused by these groups. Many people have had their lives ruined because their face and in some cases addresses have been posted online by these groups claiming them to be paedophiles, This is vigilantism at its finest and this must stop. Their influence to affect people’s decisions is extraordinary.

action: An immediate by-election to be called if an MP defects to another party.
background: A by-election after an MP defects is essential to democracy. Voters elect a party and its values, not just an individual. Changing allegiance breaks that mandate. A by-election restores trust, accountability, and gives constituents the right to choose their representation again.
additional_details: The government should introduce a clear legal requirement that any MP who defects from the party they were elected under must trigger an automatic by-election. This would protect democratic mandates, uphold voter trust, prevent political opportunism, and ensure constituents always have a direct say when their representation fundamentally changes.

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party

Broadcast on BBC for deterrence & justice. This stabilises society amid uncertainty.

Prison is no longer a deterrent and offers comfort, prisons are offering better life than Middle East, proof in reoffending.

reinstate public executions for convictions since 2000. 

Amend Human Rights Act 1998 & related laws to allow forfeiture of rights for rapists/murderers. Withdraw from ECHR Protocols 6/13 if needed. Broadcast on BBC for max deterrence.

Hold a referendum on the re-introduction of capital punishment for murder
