action: Fund and distribute first-period boxes through schools and healthcare settings
background: We ask the UK Government to fund the provision of first-period boxes with essential menstrual products for girls, through schools and healthcare settings. We believe this could help educate and provide products to girls in less fortunate settings.
additional_details: We believe many girls do not have access to a trusted or appropriate adult to discuss menstruation with, or may not feel comfortable doing so. Therefore, in our view, first-period boxes allow girls to access clear, reliable information privately and at their own pace, supporting understanding and confidence during this stage of development.

action: Rework a social media ban to u13 instead of u16.
background: The government in all likelihood is going to introduce rigid social media restrictions, and it should be a more rigid ban on u13 instead of u16.
additional_details: Children age 14-16 are undertaking GCSEs and there are many useful resources, especially on YouTube that assist in learning. Also, many teenagers use social media as an online space to make friends and interact with a community. People in Y10/11 have taken lessons and courses in social media safety in school and there is an element of trust in them to be safe. A 13 year old is far less mature and unaware of the risks of certain things online. Finally, all voting on this aren't affected at all.
rejection_details:
We already have a petition open on this which you might wish to sign:

Government ban on social media to be for under 13s only
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757849

action: Require primary legislation & referendum for any council restructure proposal
background: Amend the law so creating combined authorities, re-organising local authorities into “super councils”, or cancelling local elections can't be done by secondary legislation. Primary legislation should be passed for any proposal, requiring binding local referendums before it comes into force.
additional_details:
We believe that democratic control of local government is a core part of our constitution and that people are seeing large “combined authority” and “super-council” deals that move power away from their town halls, sometimes abolishing or merging councils with little scrutiny. We think doing this without proper parliamentary scrutiny and clear local consent is a breach of the trust on which government power is held.
 
There should be a national framework setting clear principles, such as when restructuring can be proposed, minimum consultation and evidence standards, and the requirement for referendums.

action: Protect Skilled Care Workers Affected by Sponsor Licence Revocation
background: Grant care workers affected by sponsor licence revocation a 1–2 year transition visa to secure alternative sponsored employment, with no recourse to public funds, and protect housing and children’s education during this period.
additional_details: Care workers on Skilled Worker visas lose their status through no fault of their own when sponsor licences are revoked.Short curtailment periods lead to sudden job loss, housing insecurity, high visa fees, forced relocation, and disruption to children’s education.These workers have filled critical shortages and served communities diligently. A time-limited transition visa would be fair, prevent exploitation,reduce family hardship, and retain skilled carers in a sector already facing challenges.

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!

action: Require employers to give employees a paid day of leave on their birthday
background: I believe that no one should ever have to work on their birthday. I ask the government to consider requiring employers to give employees a paid day of leave on their birthday.
additional_details: I think that thereby allowing the British workforce the ability to enjoy the day, and stay in bed a little longer if they wish on the anniversary of their birth, would be a special thank you for their devotion and commitment to working hard and paying tax.

action: Government ban on social media to be for under 13s only
background: Any government ban on social media that is introduced should be for under 13s only. We want people 13+ to be able to use social media. Not just 16+, as we believe 13 is reasonable as you are officially a teen and responsible for yourself.
additional_details: We want this to happen as many teens in the UK will be affected by the ban and we believe the proposed age limit for the ban is too high and want to lower it to apply to under 13s only.

action: Introduce Romanian into the GCSE Curriculum
background: Require the Government to approve Romanian as a GCSE subject, and help fund exam development and the training of  teachers, to allow students to study and sit Romanian GCSE alongside other modern foreign languages.
additional_details: There are now over half a million Romanian-born people living in the UK according to the latest census, making Romanian one of the most spoken foreign languages here and reflecting a significant community that could benefit from access to Romanian GCSE education. We believe that Including Romanian in the curriculum would support linguistic diversity, help children from Romanian backgrounds connect with their heritage, and better serve a large and growing population group in schools.

action: Fund £1,500 towards a first car for everyone who passes their driving test
background: Fund a scheme to offer new drivers £1,500 toward their first car after passing their test. I think this support could improve access to work and education, reduce financial barriers for young people, and encourage safer driving habits.
additional_details: Fund a scheme to offer new drivers £1,500 toward their first car after passing their test. I think this support could improve access to work and education, reduce financial barriers for young people, and encourage safer driving habits.

action: Require HMRC to issue a mandatory questionnaire on how taxes should be spent
background: We believe UK taxpayers are dissatisfied with how public money is spent and the state the country is in. Require HMRC to issue a mandatory questionnaire, with penalties for non-completion, to those born in the UK or who have paid UK tax for 10+ years, asking how they want their taxes spent.
additional_details:
We propose that it includes questions on whether taxes spent on access to benefits, NHS care, council housing should be limited to UK-born citizens & long-term contributors only (e.g. 10+ years of paying UK tax). Supporters might argue that this could reduce health tourism, prioritise essential services, and ensure fairness to taxpayers.
 
We believe that due to some wider concerns about national identity this should also prompt questions about how they want their taxes spent on measures related to tighter borders & clearer entry rules.

action: Allow mortgage interest to be deducted when calculating taxable rental income.
background: Allow mortgage interest to be treated as a deductible business expense when calculating taxable rental income, in line with standard UK business taxation principles and generally accepted accounting practice, helping support stable rental supply and avoid upward pressure on rents.
additional_details: Current rules tax rental income before mortgage interest costs, with only a basic-rate credit applied afterwards. This can result in tax being charged on income not received in real cash terms. Most UK businesses can deduct financing costs when calculating taxable profit. The current approach for rental businesses departs from this principle and can discourage investment and reduce the supply of compliant rental homes, particularly where costs are rising.

action: Create power to permanently remove vehicles from dangerous/undocumented drivers
background: Enact a Law to give Magistrates and Police powers to remove vehicles permanently from those not entitled to be on the road or whose actions on the road endanger the general public. Those vehicles would then be crushed or sold (if viable) and the value returned to Police services and victim funds
additional_details: Thousands are maimed or killed every year by drunk, speeding, unlicensed and uninsured drivers. We think bans don't work, fines don't work, and unpaid work orders don't work. Remove their cars and we believe behaviour will change. Losing your car, your status symbol, will hurt. The more you can afford, the more expensive the car will be, so the pain will be relative but fair. Give the Police some real support and protect the public.

action: Include more modern and diverse authors in the GCSE English curriculum
background: I want the Government to review the old existing texts and plays and to include some authors written by women and people who come from a diverse background. One report suggested 1% of GCSE students have studied a book written by an author of colour.
additional_details: I think the texts are outdated and not relevant for the growing world. Also that students find these particular texts boring and they are particularly uninterested in something they may not particularly relate too.

action: Change the way sexual offences are dealt with in the courts system.
background: I would like the government to make positive changes to sexual offences. EG: A male was caught masturbating,  indecent exposure in a bus infront of women and children and all he got was £170 fine and released back into the public the next day.This consequence not going to make them stop offending.
additional_details: I would like the government to take a look at how sentencing is handled for such cases as I do not believe the court system does enough for perverts however people who do petty crime get years in prison. So where is the protection for women and children in our system and processes ?

action: The UK education system must improve to better support children.
background: I want the Government and Parliament to review the UK school education system. Many children, in primary and secondary schools, are not receiving enough support from teachers. Greater focus is needed on children’s learning, wellbeing, and especially their mental health
additional_details: Over 1 million under-18s in England were in contact with NHS secondary mental health services in 2024-25 — more than double compared with 2020. I think this says more than anything.
rejection_details: You could try and start a new petition setting out more clearly what they would like the review to consider.

action: Ban people with any criminal conviction from standing for Mayor
background: We believe a Mayor is a position of responsibility, and will have dealings with vulnerable parts of the public including children, and they will be in charge of public finances.
additional_details: Therefore we call on the Government to ban anyone with criminal convictions from standing for Mayor.

action: Create independent body to regulate pay practices for private hire drivers
background: We ask the Government to create an independent regulatory authority for the private hire sector. This regulation should ensure fair pay structures for drivers, set fair minimum fares, cap commission, and protect drivers from unfair practices by private hire operators.
additional_details: We are concerned that many private hire drivers are affected by unregulated pricing, including low pay, high commission, insufficient protections, and lack of transparency.

action: Public Voting Forum on Naming Storms, Top One Wins!
background: We would like the UK Government to back an initiative to create a public forum that constantly updates real time for the voting of storm names. This will introduce public creativity and better awareness about developing storms turn a bureaucratic process into an efficient voting system.
additional_details: The reasoning behind this is the current system would have 1000s of more creative names and options that get swept away by the MET Offices' final say in the yearly storm names. This is both inefficient and boring. When a storm needs to be named, the bureau can take the top voted name resulting in the public having a majority say in the matter. The goal is to have more creative, funny, interesting and memorable names that the people enjoy. Follow stormy.mcstorm.face on Insta for more...
rejection_details:
Decisions about naming storms are a matter for the Met Office, not the UK Government or Parliament.

You can find out more about how storms are named here: https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-storm-centre/index

action: Increase The Lifetime ISA House Price Cap to Reflect Inflation
background: The LISA house price cap of £450,000 set in 2017 does not reflect the current financial landscape, with inflation adjusting this sum to around £625,000. I believe the cap should be adjusted to this figure, and re-adjusted annually or bi-annually, in line with trends of inflation.
additional_details: This change would allow more FTBs to benefit from the scheme, reducing a barrier to entry in the housing market and encouraging home ownership.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757202

action: Students keep phones on and near them
background: Students not to have their phones removed from them in school. Students should be able to check their phones at break and lunch to see if there is anything that is going on at home or their parents need to get ahold of them. If students caught on phone in lesson phones may be taken for the rest
additional_details: Of the lesson. There have been past story’s of families dying or going into hospital while students are in school and parents have not been able to  contact children.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Pass a law that schools cannot prohibit the use of personal devices
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735449

action: Lower the ban on social media for under 16s to be under 13 years old
background: Lower the ban age from 16 years old to 13 years old
additional_details: People between 13 and 16 should not be banned from using social media
rejection_details:
We already have a petition on this which is open and which you can sign:

Government ban on social media to be for under 13s only
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757849

action: Close all US Military bases in the UK
background: End all agreements and leases that allow the US access to military bases on UK soil.
additional_details: The US is no longer a reliable ally and represents a security risk to the UK
rejection_details:
This petition is substantively a duplicate of one we already have open on the petitions site, which you may wish to sign:

Expel all US military personnel and close all US military bases in the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756133

action: Government to commence the Medical Training (Prioritisation) Bill in 2027
background: The Government must ensure that the provisions of the Medical Training (Prioritisation) Bill once enacted come into force in 2027 not 2026, as the selection process is already underway for this year and a 2026 commencement would retrospectively affects this year’s process.
additional_details: Resident doctors have spent significant amount of time and financial resources for this year’s application process which closed in November/December for Specialty Posts. The long listing and shortlisting process have already happened so the bill once enacted would retrospectively affect the process. Also, the role of significant NHS experience has not been reviewed for this year but will be for next year which we believe presents an inequality in the application of the law between years.

action: Immediate ceasefire and stop slaughtering Kurds people in Syria
background: immediate and unconditional implementation of a ceasefire throughout the territory of Syria and demand an end to all unlawful acts of violence and  punishment directed against the Kurdish people. All parties must comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law.
additional_details: We formally call for the immediate and unconditional implementation of a ceasefire throughout the territory of Syria and demand an end to all unlawful acts of violence, persecution, and collective punishment directed against the Kurdish people. All parties must comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law and international human rights law.
rejection_details:
Condemn attacks on Kurds in North Syria & use diplomatic pressure to bring peace 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756339

UK must act now & condemn the killing of Kurdish civilians in Rojava & Rojhilat
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756419

action: Stop the closure of the Derby DrivAbility centre at Kingsway hospital DE223LZ
background: Speak with the NHS trust responsible for decision to close this facility
additional_details: This facility is needed to assess the ability of someone with a driving license that has had a medical illness or injury that could restrict their mobility and ability to drive safely on today’s roads. Anyone who needs this but cannot attend it in Derby would have to travel to Birmingham, or Leeds  The NHS says it’s a cost cutting measure of affordability but taking this away from people could mean many continue to drive when they’re not safe. Putting themselves and others in danger on the roads
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: All advice centres should receive statutory funding from local authorities
background: There needs to be a change in Law so all local authorities must fund all advice centres in their districts who request funding. The local authorities should not discriminate against small local providers. Local authorities must give statutory funding to all providers who request it.
additional_details:
Advice Services Can Save Lives. They save money for the public purse, support local authorities and in a more complex world advice services are needed more than ever.
We think it is also the right thing to do when advice services are closing up and down the country due to lack of funding.

action: Fund crisis support signs on motorway and railway bridges
background: Fund signs with local crisis support info and helplines on motorway and railway bridges. Work with relevant campaigns and organisations to ensure signs are safe, effective, and help people in crisis find local, face to face support.
additional_details: People are dying from jumping from motorway and railway bridges, deeply affecting families, drivers, and whole communities. These incidents cause huge trauma for witnesses and exponential costs to emergency services. Signs with crisis support info could save lives, and prevent horrendous suffering.

action: Ban the use of Prong collars and Electric Shock Collars on Dogs and Cats in UK
background: Ban the use of Prong Collars & Electric Shock Collars for use on Dogs and cats in the UK. We believe they are inhumane, inflict pain, fear and anxiety leading to potential physical and psychological damage, while punishment tools can increase aggression leading to more bites and risk to the public.
additional_details: Prong collars & Electric Shock collars are sometimes used on Dogs & Cats to control behaviour, as a punishment or used as part of training. Both collars inflict pain, fear & anxiety, leading, we believe, to potential physical injury (e.g. to the thyroid) & psychological damage, and they also can increase aggression leading to more bites & risk to the public. The Royal Kennel Club, British Veterinary Association, Dogs Trust, RSPCA, PDSA, Blue Cross, Battersea Dogs & Cats Home all support a ban.

action: Do not ban social media for under 16s
background: Do not ban social media for under 16s
additional_details: Don’t ban I because there is also good stuff that you can do on social media and good wins over bad
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Do not ban social media for under 16s" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757233

action: Restrict the Lumens LED lights can have on Headlights on cars
background: LED Headlights on newer cars even on the regular light setting are a risk to health as they are blinding to drivers and passengers in oncoming vehicles. The Lumens need to be restricted to lower levels.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Ban LED vehicle headlights or regulate bulb wattage" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744882

action: Introduce lessons on neurodivergence to the curriculum for all children
background: Every child should have the chance to be understood. I want the curriculum to require that all children be taught about neurodivergence. This should include teaching on Autism, ADHD, Dyslexia, Dyspraxia (DCD), Dyscalculia, Tourette's Syndrome, and sensory processing disorder, to name a few examples.
additional_details: I believe this should be taught in school as every school is likely to have neurodivergent children with one or more of these conditions, and I feel these lessons would help children understand their peers better. I think this would open up a whole new world for children because they can help support their peers that are neurodivergent, and it could help children with neurodivergent siblings or parents to better understand and support them.

action: Reassess the ‘Special Relationship’ with the United States.
background: We call on the UK Government to distance itself from the United States’ current foreign policy platform and prioritise strategic alignment with European partners. As part of this reassessment, the Government should request the full withdrawal of United States Visiting Forces (USVF) from the UK.
additional_details:
The UK must take action due to:
US rhetoric regarding military intervention in Greenland—a sovereign territory of our NATO ally Denmark—threatens to collapse the North Atlantic alliance. The UK should not host forces for an administration that contemplates using military or economic coercion against fellow NATO members.
The Government must end the policy of appeasement and acknowledge that the UK's future lies in a sovereign, independent path aligned with Europe.
rejection_details:
There are already petitions calling for these actions: 

Expel all US military personnel and close all US military bases in the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756133

Align foreign & trade policy with EU and set steps towards closer integration
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757542

action: Don’t ban social media for under 16s
background: either not make the social media ban to come in effect or make it so that it’s under 13s as most apps don’t allow under 13s
additional_details: because it’s some people’s jobs and get paid for doing it and it helps kids mentally with school work and life
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for the same action: "Do not ban social media for under 16s" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757233

action: Review of guidance parents receive after a Patau’s syndrome diagnosis
background: I ask the Government to conduct a formal review and consideration of updates to the guidance parents receive if their baby is suspected of or diagnosed with Patau’s syndrome, to ensure they are always accurately informed that some children may survive Patau’s syndrome, and that outcomes may vary.
additional_details:
I was personally told my baby would not be compatible with life. I believe parents shouldn't be given any impression that the condition is universally “incompatible with life,” as there are some children who may survive beyond birth and in rare cases for longer.

The review should examine how medical professionals communicate any uncertainty and present choices to parents so they are always clearly informed and can make fully informed decisions. It should consider the emotional and practical support they're offered after diagnosis, ensuring families always receive balanced, evidence-based information and support regardless of their decisions.

action: I would like to create a national Callum day
background: To allow the name Callum to be celebrated on a dedicated day like majority of others are when searched on google. I believe this name is equally important as any other
additional_details: There is no other way to allow this to occur unless a petition is made

action: Make drivers who run over cats stop and seek help, like they do with dogs.
background: Put a law in place that prohibits drivers from conducting a hit and run on cats. They are household pets just like dogs
additional_details: Cats are beloved household pets, and should be treated with equal regard as dogs do
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750612

Legally require drivers who hit a cat to take them to a vet
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751525

action: Establish lawful regulation for electric unicycles and personal EVs
background: We ask the Government to create clear legislation for electric unicycles and similar devices. They are treated as motor vehicles but cannot be registered or insured, making compliance impossible. A proportionate framework with safety standards and lawful routes to compliance is needed.
additional_details: Because electric unicycles sit in a legal grey area where ownership is lawful but compliance is impossible. This creates uncertainty for the public and enforcement bodies, discourages innovation, and leads to disproportionate outcomes. Clear rules would improve safety, fairness, and legal certainty.
rejection_details: We are not entirely clear what you mean by compliance in this context - compliance with what? Is this about their being driven on public highways?  You may want to start a petition that makes the issue of compliance more clearly.

action: Require all social media platforms to verify identity of accounts
background: Make identity verification a legal requirement for all existing and new users on social media platforms. Nicknames could be used to maintain anonymity in the public eye, but accounts will be linked to real identities to help ensure social media users can be traced by authorities.
additional_details: This could protect people against online hate acting as a deterrent to social media users writing hate online. Even with anonymous username, verification could mean a person can be traced and held responsible and deter people from writing hate and setting up fake accounts. These extra layers of identification could also enable simpler identification of users, allowing action to be taken by platforms and authorities to deal with online hate. We think this will create a safer online space for all.

action: Create an Education Travel Tax Relief scheme to offset peak holiday costs
background: Create a tax-relief framework (like 'Cycle to Work') where travel providers receive tax credits for offering capped 'Term-Time Equivalent' pricing to state education staff. Additionally, launch a review into the affordability of travel for education staff at peak times.
additional_details:
State school staff are uniquely penalised by their contracts, which forbid term-time leave. We feel that travel companies exploit this captive market, charging premiums compared to term-time prices.
 
This can act as a de facto pay cut for public servants.
With the current recruitment and retention crisis in education, pricing staff out of affordable rest is unsustainable. If the Government cannot raise wages, it must intervene to lower the cost of living for those serving our schools.

action: Introduce 5-year ILR route with mandatory volunteer service for UK graduates
background: Introduce a structured five-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain for international graduates of UK universities who have done 6 months mandatory voluntary service, employment, or established a business.
additional_details:
Create an accelerated citizenship option for those who serve in the Armed Forces or UK security services.

In our view the UK invests heavily in educating international students, but we believe forcing them to leave after graduation wastes skilled talent during shortages in healthcare, education, public services, technology, and security. This petition proposes a five-year settlement route for UK-educated graduates, requiring six months of voluntary public service, followed by employment or business creation, with accelerated citizenship for those joining the Armed Forces or security services.

action: Make it easier to book driving tests
background: Reform the DVSA driving test booking system to reduce excessive wait times (often over 3 months). Add nationwide availability views, accurate nearby-centre searches and an automated cancellation system so candidates can easily find and book earlier test slots.
additional_details: Many people struggle for months to secure a driving test, disrupting work, family responsibilities and career progression. I experienced this while helping an NHS consultant who depends on driving for her job. These delays are driven by an inefficient booking system that limits visibility of cancellations, forces users to manually check centres one by one, and releases slots at fixed times that overload the website. Better design would reduce stress, wasted time and unfair access.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Review the driving test booking process, ban resales at inflated prices & bots
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736594

action: Increase funding for NHS counsellors and review current referral pathways
background: I want referral pathways from GPs for mental health issues to be reviewed, and improved. There is a need for a robust recruitment drive for actual counsellors and specialists in the NHS, and for better observance of the principle that mental health should be treated like physical health.
additional_details: I recently lost my son - he and many thousands of people are suffering living with only limited access to the correct help they require, a lot of people are contacting services which can only help the scars, not the problems. There is a grave lack of counselling in the NHS & there needs to be a robust recruitment drive. An improvement is needed for pathways to be accessible from GPs. It’s needed now!

action: Ban MPs from having second jobs except in NHS
background: MPs should not have other jobs outside of Parliament unless they are qualified doctors, nurses or other healthcare professionals and actively work in the NHS
additional_details:
Parliament should ban any sitting MPs from having second jobs as we feel it is a conflict of interest.
 
The only exception to this rule are if the MPs are qualified doctors, nurses or other healthcare professionals who actively work within the NHS.

action: Shorter Weeks Inclusive of Independent Schools
background: The parliament debated to reduce the school week from five days, to four days. Although, this would only apply to state-funded schools, we want it to apply to independent schools.
rejection_details: Operational schooling/teaching arrangements for private/independent schools lie outside the Government's direct responsibility.

action: Formal recognition of climate-displaced people within the asylum system
background: Amend immigration and asylum law to establish a clear legal status for people displaced by climate change, provide access to protection comparable to refugee status, and create defined humanitarian pathways and resettlement schemes for climate-displaced people.
additional_details: Climate change is already driving mass displacement, with estimates of over 30 million people forced from their homes each year by climate-related disasters. The World Bank warns up to 216 million people could be displaced by climate impacts by 2050. UK asylum law offers no protection for those displaced by climate change. As a historic high emitter and global leader, we feel the UK has a moral responsibility to respond through clear legal recognition and safe humanitarian pathways.

action: Ban atmospheric geoengineering in UK
background: Prohibit all atmospheric geoengineering and weather-modification in the UK. These practices could raise environmental and public health concerns and lack transparency. We call for independent research, democratic oversight, and clear law.
additional_details: Atmospheric geoengineering and weather-modification may pose serious risks to public health, air quality, ecosystems, agriculture, and weather stability. The public deserves clarity about activities that could affect the environment and well-being. Precautionary action is needed to prevent harm, protect public trust, and ensure environmental decisions are evidence-based, accountable, and safe.

action: Ban employers from requiring job applicants to have an address
background: In the UK, it's difficult for the homeless to find work, as employers  may dismiss their applications as there is no address. We want the government to make it illegal for employers to dismiss these applications for not having an address.
additional_details: Homeless people already struggle with finding jobs, we want to make it easier for them to find a job and financially support themselves to eventually make it out of homelessness. Without a permanent or temporary address, and the employers potentially dismissing their applications as a result, homeless people can't get back on their feet and are left to suffer on the streets. Homeless people should be given a chance to get back on their feet, and live the life they've wanted.

action: Increase funding for information on dangers of high blood pressure in pregnancy
background: Allocate more funding to information about the dangers of high blood pressure during pregnancy. Detailing every single symptom to look out for, and highlighting the dangers, which if missed can sadly lead to fatalities of both mother and child. Placental abruption due to high bp is serious!
additional_details: For example, leaflets detailing all and every single symptom especially the dangers of high bp to be put in maternity packs for appointments. Posters detailing all and every single symptom especially the dangers of high bp in pregnancy be put in all maternity units across the uk. Placental abruption can be a cause of high bp which can cause the baby to have less oxygen and can also result in bleeding heavily which can be fatal for mother and baby. All women need to be made aware!

action: Seek to negotiate recognition of licences exempting dogs under the DDA across UK
background: Dogs banned under the Dangerous Dogs Act are legally required to hold an exemption. Currently England & Wales, Scotland and NI manage their own exemption schemes with no cross recognition. This means dogs cannot be brought to another part of the UK for example to visit for leisure.
additional_details: In our view, dog owners who have taken the responsible decision to comply with the law are unduly affected because the government are not taking steps to address the lack of cross border recognition of exemption certificates. I call for the government to start the process to recognise the certificates for those of the devolved nations and to negotiate their recognition of exemption certificates issued in England & Wales.

action: Allow self-builders to use their LISA for building costs not just land purchase
background: Right now self-builders can use their Lifetime ISA (LISA) for land purchase if they have a mortgage. We believe this punishes those who can buy a cheaper land outright, but still need a mortgage for the build itself.
additional_details:
Allowing self-builders use their LISA for building costs might help people financing their self-builds, which would be helpful in the housing crisis, especially in places with lower land prices. 

A LISA can be used for both the building and land when buying an already built house, so it should be the same for self-builds too.

action: Reform Universal Credit to reduce long-term benefit dependency and costs
background: Reduce Universal Credit by applying stricter eligibility for work-capable claimants. Pay standard Credit only for a defined job-search period (e.g. 3 months). After this, reduce payments and make them conditional on accepting suitable work, approved training/placements or community work.
additional_details: Over 8 million now claim credit, including many work-capable adults who remain on benefits for years with no automatic end point. In some cases, people can receive more on benefits than by working, reducing incentives to work, effectively rewarding unemployment, while undermining fairness for working taxpayers who help fund the system. Time-limiting support and tightening capability criteria would reduce dependency, lower costs, restore confidence while protecting those genuinely unable to work.
rejection_details:
We are not clear on the specific action that you are seeking or how this would apply to Universal Credit claimants who are already in work. You can start a new petition setting this out more clearly.

You may also wish to sign this open petition which is calling for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/752728

action: Increase HMRC Mileage Allowance to 70p per mile
background: The 45p per mile mileage allowance has been static for fifteen years. Since April 2011, prices in the UK have increased by around 49.2% according to the Bank of England. We want the allowance to increase to 70p a mile.
additional_details:
Employers set their mileage allowances using the 45p HMRC rate, which we feel is now unrealistically low. We believe drivers aren't just affected by not having extra tax relief, but by being underpaid for their work associated travel costs, are effectively subsiding their employers out of their own pockets.
 
For someone claiming the maximum 10,000 miles of work or business travel the difference between 70p and 45p equates to a loss of £2,500 a year. Someone driving just 1,000 miles a year would be £250 out of pocket.

action: Reform oversight of Private Parking Enforcement and trade associations.
background: Introduce independant oversight of private parking enforcement, require trade associations to follow enforceble complaints processes, and ensure the DVLA investigates non-compliance where accredited bodies fail to act.
additional_details: Private parking enforcement relies on trade associations to regulate their members. When they fail to investigate complaints or follow their procedures, there is no effective esculation route. The DVLA and Department for Transport decline to intervene, leaving motorists without protection. This disproportionately affects the eldarly and vulnerable, who often pay unjust charges due to confusion, poor signage, or inaccessible appeal processes. Independant oversight is needed to close this gap.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Review private parking regulation
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754025

action: UC must cover housing costs following marriage breakdown in forces accommodation
background: Following marriage breakdown in families living in in forces accommodation, the party occupying the property while seeking alternative accommodation can be classed as a 'trespasser', and may therefore be ineligible for support with housing costs through Universal Credit.
additional_details: This can make it incredibly difficult for spouses going through a marriage separation. The word 'Trespass' means Universal Credit will often not help with the housing element of Universal Credit, so the spouse is eligible for the full cost. The spouse is given a breakdown of this cost for example water, council tax, garage rent, house rent and are expected to pay this rent and charges. This can leave families in financial difficulty, in debt when already struggling.

action: Government must act to help stop Christian persecution in India
additional_details:
We believe that being a Christian in India today has become increasingly difficult, unsafe, and distressing. Under the present political climate, incidents of persecution, discrimination, and violence against Christians have risen at what we believe is an alarming rate.
 
We believe that the Government’s voice, influence, and moral leadership can make a meaningful difference. History reminds us that when injustice is confronted with courage and compassion, change becomes possible.

action: Restrict the sale of fireworks and act on this issue, stop fobbing us off.
background:
Improved regulations on the sale and use of fireworks are backed by a wide range of MPs, charities and organisations and has huge public support.

The distress and trauma caused is very well known to the medical profession, emergency services, human and animal welfare groups AND the Government.
additional_details: Stop ignoring this issue and take action. Restrict fireworks to licensed public events only or only sell no noise fireworks to the public.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Limit the sale of fireworks to those running local council approved events only
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/732559

action: Abolish Secure Borders UK
background: ICE in the US has deported and killed American citizens, and I’m worried the same thing will happen here. Those who have been detained by ICE have also been kept in inhumane conditions. I want the government to abolish Secure Borders UK before people are unjustly deported or killed.
additional_details: I want the government to abolish Secure Borders UK because its existence makes marginalised groups such as people of colour and LGBTQ+ people feel unsafe; again, I am also worried about people wrongfully being deported or even killed just because of the colour of their skin or where they work, for example.
rejection_details: Action unclear because hypothetical.

action: Limit the amount of News Broadcasts for the sake of the Nations Mental Health
background: Call for a review on why it is deemed necessary to have news every half hour on the radio in particular. Also, why is only negative news deemed news. Why is there no balance?
additional_details: I believe the amount and frequency of negative news is out of proportion with what is necessary. I believe it is having a detrimental effect on the Nation’s Mental Health and it spreads fear mongering.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions related to which news to report and the frequency of reporting are not a matter for the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Fund a mandatory NHS wide digital patient record across all NHS hospitals
background: Patients may experience fragmented or delayed care because NHS trusts use different record systems. We want a single mandatory NHS-wide digital patient record to help prevent errors or lost information, and stop patients being triaged or treated without full medical history across all NHS hospitals.
additional_details: I am starting this petition based on lifelong personal experience navigating NHS care for myself and while advocating for my family. Over many years we have repeatedly seen vital medical details lost, delayed, not recorded, or not shared correctly between trusts. In our experience this has led to fragmented care, repeated assessments, longer waits, unsafe triage, and clinicians making decisions without full context. We believe a single mandatory NHS-wide digital record would help improve safety, efficiency, and patient outcomes.

action: Limit the use of fully autonomous AI systems to make high-risk decisions
background: I want the Government to introduce clear limits on where fully autonomous AI systems can be used. Such systems must be auditable, accountable, and reversible before deployment.
additional_details:
Meaningful human oversight should also be present, particularly in high-impact public and private uses, such as in healthcare triage and treatment, or criminal justice and law enforcement. 
 
Current AI systems can appear confident while remaining uncertain, difficult to audit, and prone to rare but significant failures. The immediate risk is not whether AI systems are sufficiently intelligent or wise, but that decision-making power is being delegated before reliability, uncertainty handling, and accountability are sufficiently understood. Delaying action increases the likelihood that unsafe practices become embedded and their effects harder to reverse.

action: Make carrying of a knife a mandatory 10 year Prison Sentence.
background: Anyone caught carrying a knife or dangerous weapon, get an automatic 10 year Prison Sentence.
additional_details: Agree to make it a mandatory 10 year prison sentence.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Increase minimum sentence for carrying a knife to 10 years
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750758

action: Expand free school meals provision to cover all school children
background: I would like the Government to expand free school meals to cover all school children up until the end of sixth form.
additional_details: The cost of living crisis can be addressed by giving free school meals to all children. Families will save at least £250 per child every year and could help alleviate the cost of living crisis. It would give families more disposable income.

action: Introduce penalties for MPs who deliberately mislead the public.
background: Introduce rules so MPs who knowingly provide false or misleading information face consequences. This should include independent investigation and proportionate sanctions. Wales has committed to introduce similar measures to address deliberate political deception.
additional_details: Public trust in democracy depends on honesty from elected representatives. When MPs deliberately mislead the public, it undermines confidence in government and weakens democratic accountability. Voters rely on truthful information to make informed choices. This proposal would not restrict free speech, debate, or political opinion. It would apply only to knowing or reckless falsehoods, ensuring transparency, fairness, and higher standards in public office.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions which call for similar actions:

Hold MPs accountable for misleading statements and apply sanctions 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751495

Make it illegal for politicians to use false information and statistics 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742718

action: Scrap stamp duty on share transactions bought within an ISA
background: By reducing cash ISA limits to push stocks and share ISA's, government will take more in tax than from traditional interest. 20k means multiple stamp duty payments of £100 if stocks are traded. If the government are serious about people investing to better their savings, scrap stamp duty in an ISA.
additional_details: It is an absolute disgrace that government is penalising savers by increasing tax to 22% on interest whilst reducing cash limits in ISA's and pushing people into stock market investing where the government takes 0.5% of every £ invested regardless, of that being in an ISA / SIPP or regular account, and regardless of whether the investment makes a profit or loss. Stamp duty is a tax and as no place in an ISA wrapper.

action: Introduce a framework for multiple approved gas engineer registration bodies
background: Introduce a regulated framework allowing multiple approved registration bodies for gas engineers. Set consistent standards, independent oversight, and a clear appeals/reinstatement process when administrative errors occur.
additional_details: Gas engineers rely on registration to work legally. When one body controls registration, mistakes or poor admin can wrongly remove engineers, which can cause lost income and reputational damage with little accountability. We think allowing multiple approved bodies would create choice, improve service standards, strengthen fairness and transparency, and still protect public safety through regulation and auditing.

action: Fund provision of defensive equipment for paramedics due to attacks sustained
background: Fund the provision of defensive equipment like pepper spray or stab resistant clothing for paramedics.
additional_details: The 2024/25 figure for violence, aggression, and abuse against paramedics was 22,536 (14.8% increase from 2023/24). With these rates of violence, and the severity of violence increasing paramedics need better protection in order to be able to continue doing their job whilst keeping themselves, their patient(s), and members of the public safe. Additionally, these acts of aggression aren't just from combative patients, some are from members of the public forcing paramedics to work in fear.

action: Ban public sale of rodent poisons to protect wildlife and pets
background: Ban the public sale of rodenticide poisons and restrict their use to trained, licensed professionals only. Ensure that all pest control methods available to the public are humane, wildlife-safe, and environmentally responsible.
additional_details: Rodenticide poisons cause slow, painful deaths and lead to secondary poisoning of wildlife such as owls, foxes and hedgehogs, as well as pets. These poisons contaminate ecosystems and food chains. Humane alternatives exist, including live traps, proofing and deterrents. Restricting poisons to licensed professionals in cases when absolute necessary will protect animal welfare, biodiversity and public health.
rejection_details:
We already have a petition open on this which you might wish to sigh:
Ban the sale and use of rat poison due to the negative impact on wildlife
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/753779

action: Classify all sexual offences as violent crimes and end automatic appeal rights
background: We want the Government formally to reclassify all sexual offences as "Violent Crimes" in legislation to ensure sentencing and rehabilitation reflect the violence of these acts, also amending the Magistrates’ Courts Act '80 to remove the automatic right of a defendant to an appeal in the Crown Court
additional_details: Current law separates sex offences from violent crimes, which we believe downplays trauma and may contribute to poor rehab and high reoffending. Furthermore, the automatic right to appeal from Magistrates’ Courts can allow offenders a "practice run" forcing victims into a "Double Trial Trap" with years of delays. Loopholes can be gamed to ignore court deadlines, leaving victims in procedural limbo. We demand a system that prioritises victim recovery over offender convenience & treats sex offences as violent acts.

action: MPs repeatedly failing to disclose financial declaration on time to be suspended
background: Reform MPs’ financial disclosure rules so repeated late declarations automatically trigger Standards Committee referral and suspension. We believe this would ensure patterns of non-compliance have real consequences, including recall where thresholds are met.
additional_details: In our view, recent cases show that MPs can repeatedly fail to declare large sums on time without serious sanction. We think treating multiple breaches as “inadvertent” undermines trust and creates the impression of unequal standards. We therefore call on clear, automatic escalation to restore accountability and allow voters to decide when confidence is lost.

action: Clear up the excessive litter at the side of Britain's motorways and laybys
background: Establish a taskforce with national highways and local councils to immediately begin to address the excessive litter plaguing Britain's roads and laybys. Also consider installing ANPR cameras on motorway slip roads and in laybys to catch and fine roadside litter louts and deter further littering.
additional_details: The sides of motorways and major A roads in Britain are in a disgusting state. Miles of discarded cans, bottles, coffee cups and plastic bags cover the sides of the roads and whilst some ignorant individuals continue to throw rubbish out of their vehicles, the council and national highways continue to make no effort to clear it up, so it keeps accumulating. This affects wildlife who choke and get caught in the waste, and makes our roads look untidy and more comparable to a third world country.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Reduce roadside littering: penalty points, increase fines, fund litter picks" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757624

action: Make road safety lessons a mandatory part of the curriculum
background: I want the Government to introduce road safety education as a mandatory part of the curriculum in all schools. This should include lessons on crossing safely, cycling awareness, and understanding road signs. The aim is to reduce accidents involving children and improve long term public safety.
additional_details: Because many young people walk or travel to school every day, improving road safety education would help prevent accidents and save lives. Teaching these skills early creates safer habits for life and reduces pressure on emergency services.

action: Require Members of Parliament to have min 15yrs work experience outside politics
background: Ensure the elected representatives of the people have the relevant real world experience necessary to make more informed decisions.

Anyone sitting in parliament should have a minimum of 15 years PAYE outside of politics
 
We feel career politicians cannot truly comprehend and manage something they may have no real world experience of.
 
Much like someone studying very hard for many years academically then being let loose as a brain surgeon!

action: Fund urgent replacement / refurbishment of Central Line trains.
background: We call on the UK Government to work with TFL to urgently fund the replacement or major refurbishment of the Central Line’s 1992 ageing rolling stock, improve service reliability, and implement a short-term stabilisation plan to reduce severe delays, train failures, and dangerous overcrowding.
additional_details:
The Central Line is one of the most unrealiable parts of the London Underground, with near-daily severe delays, repeated service suspensions, train defects and unsafe overcrowding. This is largely due to the ageing 1992 rolling stock which is no longer reliable enough to support a stable timetable. 

Passengers routinely experience long gaps between trains, repeated suspension of entire branches, dangerously overcrowded platforms, affecting work, childcare, education and healthcare.

action: Take action to support Kurdish people in Syria
background: Kurdish forces were critical in the defeat of ISIS - they lost more than ten thousand people in the process. Kurds are currently under attack by Syrian forces. Recent attacks by the Syrian army have also led to ISIS fighters escaping from prison.
additional_details:

If ISIS re-emerges in the region, it could endanger the UK and the rest of the world. If there is no support for the Kurds, it’ll lead to weakening of a great ally in the fight against terrorism, and many innocent civilian Kurds could lose their lives and be displaced.

action: Set policy that exam boards should give students notice of GCSE exam topics
background: I want the government to allow pupils to know what topics (not questions) will come up on GSCE exams for each subject to save them from stress and feeling like they cannot achieve the grade they want to achieve. If this happens it would allow students to focus on understanding rather than guessing.
additional_details: Many students revise large amounts of content for their GCSEs, often all at once. This creates high levels of stress, particularly when topics they focus on do not appear in the final exam. By giving students every topic (not question) that will come out on the GCSE exams from 2026, it gives them the opportunity to succeed and achieve the grades they want. additional_details: I was born with a cleft lip/palate I struggle a lot with my appearance like many others do! I suffer with confidence issues and low self esteem. action: Uni Students with Coeliac Disease to be eligible for enhanced bursary

additional_details: Delaying elections damages trust in local democracy and risks setting a precedent that election dates can be moved for political or administrative reasons. Even where reorganisation is planned, voters should still be able to choose who represents them and oversees services and budgets during any transition. Regular elections are a cornerstone of democratic legitimacy and should not be treated as optional.

action: An MP that is in multiple breaches of the MP’s  code of conduct, should resign.
background: Multiple breaches of code of conduct should trigger an investigation and suspension of an MP; if guilty the extent of the breach should merit whether an apology should be made, or if they should be called to resign their position.
additional_details: Parliamentary rules need to be updated and modernised; when a member of parliament betrays the privilege of their position of service and the trust the public put in them with breaches of the MP’s code of conduct, the extent of the breach should warrant whether an apology or resignation is in order, especially if in excessive multiple breaches of the conduct of conduct, or the seriousness of the breach.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action. 
 
We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do. We are unclear whether you want MPs found to have breached the Code of Conduct to be forced to resign, to be automatically suspended, or if the sanction should be based on the extent of the breach(es). 

The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards is responsible for investigating complaints that a MP has breached the Code of Conduct. Where a case is referred to the Committee on Standards and they find that there has been a breach they can recommend sanctions ranging from requiring an apology, through suspension and up to expulsion from the House depending on the seriousness of the breach. The Procedural Protocol relating to the Code of Conduct sets out the process in more detail and is available here https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5803/cmcode/1084/report.html 
 
You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Establish a 'Less Scroll, More Soul' Bank Holiday: An Offline 'In-Community' Day
background: We think the country urgently needs a breather: an annual reset for our overwhelmed, disconnected lives. A day to log off, look up & reconnect. A government-backed opportunity to build awareness of the grip tech has on us & remind us of what matters in a healthy society: people, place and presence.
additional_details:
We are an addicted, distracted nation. There are studies suggesting 67.4 million hours a day are lost to scroll and that children spend less time outdoors (<1hr) than inmates. We think loneliness, anxiety and polarisation are spiralling & all this before consideration of specific harms: exploitation, misinformation & more.
 
We have fewer bank holidays than almost anywhere in Europe.
 
One offline day a year could provide not only a critical reset but an opportunity for charities to showcase community volunteering opportunities.

action: Urgent Review and Reform of the CICA Scheme

Implement a Digital Progress Portal
Improve Guidance
Modernise processes on medical information

action: Add mental health therapy training to school curriculum
background: Government to mandate that schools teach Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and or Dialectical Behavioural Therapy to give our children the skills they need to deal with modern life and the challenges of social media.

action: Hold public inquiry into racial hatred in England since 2012
background: We think public attitudes have shifted amid a constant stream of misinformation about minorities and immigration, and that politicians, public figures and so-called "news" channels now lie with impunity.

We call for an inquiry into why racial hatred appears to be on the rise, and how the Government should tackle it

In 2012 we hosted the Olympics and displayed true British values of welcome and tolerance. Since then, in our view, Britain has become insular and xenophobic. We think individuals, so-called "news" organisations and social media have all been instrumental in the direct incitement of racial hatred, to the point where our national flag is widely abused on lamp posts in order to intimidate minorities. We need to address the root cause of this shift in public "values" before it's too late.

action: Write law that a referendum is required for the UK to be able to leave the ECHR

additional_details:

action: Increase the Personal Allowance to £16,000 and link it to inflation
background: We call on the Government to increase the Personal Allowance from £12,570 to £16,000 and automatically uprate it each year in line with inflation (CPI), so people on low and middle incomes don’t pay more tax in real terms when living costs rise.
additional_details:
The Personal Allowance has remained at £12,570 for several years while prices and wages have increased. This means more of people’s earnings become taxable over time, even when tax rates do not change.

We believe that raising the allowance to £16,000 and linking it to inflation would help protect living standards, make taxation fairer, and provide clear, transparent support to working households.

action: Make non-fatal strangulation an attempted murder offence or increase charges
background: Parliament must strengthen UK domestic violence laws with harsher sentences. Non-fatal strangulation should be charged as attempted murder. Putting hands around someone’s throat restricts air and blood flow and can kill. This must not be treated as minor assault.
additional_details: Domestic violence is rising and victims deserve stronger protection. Non-fatal strangulation is not “minor” assault, it is a life-threatening act. If someone puts their hands around another person’s throat, they are restricting airflow and blood flow with the intent to cause serious harm or death. Strangulation is a key predictor of future homicide. Laws must change so non-fatal strangulation is treated as attempted murder with stricter sentencing.

action: Fund history teachers free/discounted entry to historical sites

action: Fund access to private health care for all injured British veterans
background: Injured British veterans often live with lifelong physical and psychological conditions caused by service. NHS pathways can involve long waits and limited specialist care. We think guaranteed private healthcare would provide timely, expert treatment and fulfil the nation’s duty of care.

NHS care can involve long waits and limited access to specialist treatment. We think guaranteed private healthcare would provide timely, expert care and fulfil the UK’s duty of care to those injured serving their country.

action: Include more financial education in secondary school curriculum
background: Introduce some mandatory focus on basic world-applicable financial skills including but not limited to: long-term investment, pension planning, risks of debt and borrowing, budgeting and taxation. We do not believe teenagers are being aptly prepared for financial independence.
additional_details: We think the majority of 17/18 year olds coming out of the school system feel overwhelmed by the imminence of independent life. A major contributor to this feeling could be a lack of financial literacy. We are concerned that there is widespread inability to properly manage personal finances, resulting in a lack of monetary growth, often paired with overpaying for financial services. 1 in 6 UK adults have no personal savings, and only 23% hold any stock market investments. Financial education needs to improve in the school system.

action: Require disclosure before publishing covert recordings of direct interactions
background: Introduce legislation so that when recordings of direct interactions filmed using hands-free or concealed body-worn devices are published and individuals are identifiable, the publisher must show the person was informed they were being recorded, unless publication is in the public interest.
additional_details: Reports show women being secretly filmed with smart glasses during conversations and posted online without their knowledge. This has led to abuse, unwanted exposure and loss of control over how they are represented. The law allows public filming but offers limited protection when covert recordings of direct interactions are published and people are identifiable. Requiring disclosure during covert filming allows people to choose how they’re shown online while protecting existing freedoms.
