action: Amend Dangerous Dogs Act to recognise and fund rehoming of non-dangerous dogs
background: We call on the Government to amend the DDA1991 to allow non-dangerous dogs deemed prohibited under Section 1 to be recognised as such, and for their rehoming through approved rescues under a behaviour-based licensing system to be funded.
additional_details: Amend the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 to establish a behaviour-based rehoming scheme for dogs prohibited or seized under Section 1 where no dangerous behaviour has been demonstrated. This should apply to strays, disclaimed dogs, and dogs seized due to owner unfitness or unrelated criminal matters. Dogs would be rehomed via approved rescues, preventing unnecessary euthanasia while retaining powers for genuinely dangerous dogs.

action: Sellers who take house off the market to be liable to repay expenses of buyer
background: We call on the Government to make house sellers who withdraw their property from the market at short notice, after title searches and builders surveys have been completed at the buyers expense, to be liable to repay any expenses incurred by the prospective buyer.

action: Update law to help protect over-60s from social media algorithms amplifying hate
background: Review and update the Online Safety Act to include specific recognition of over-60s as a vulnerable group and require platforms to assess and mitigate any algorithmic amplification of hateful and extremist content that may disproportionately harm older adults, without restricting lawful speech.
additional_details: We believe older adults can be disproportionately affected by social media systems that we feel prioritise divisive and hateful content to maximise engagement. Factors such as loneliness and lower digital literacy can increase vulnerability, yet the Online Safety Act provides no specific recognition of these risks to over-60s. We want the Act to be updated to specifically require platforms to assess and mitigate any foreseeable algorithmic harms to over-60s in particular, without restricting lawful speech.

action: Legislate to enforce timely payment of workplace pensions
background: We call on the Government to legislate for timely payment of workplace pensions, including a guarantee of the first payment to be paid within 31 days of someone retiring. This period must commence on the agreed date of retirement, including the payment of lump sums.
additional_details: We believe without this change many people will continue to be impacted by the poor management of workplace pensions, in the public and private sectors. It can negatively and significantly impact financial security and wellbeing of those retiring from work, as well as on occasion negatively impacting mental and physical health. Not paying pensions, sometimes for months, cannot be allowed to continue.

action: Commission a statue of King Athelstan to mark England's 1100th anniversary
background: We call on the Government to commission a permanent bronze statue of King Athelstan, England's first king, for the Fourth Plinth of Trafalgar Square. This would mark the 1100th anniversary in 2027 of Athelstan unifying England as a single kingdom in 927 AD at Eamont Bridge
additional_details: In 927 AD, King Athelstan united the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms into the nation we now call England. Summer 2027 marks 1100 years since this founding moment—yet there is no major national monument to Athelstan. The Fourth Plinth has hosted rotating contemporary art since 1999, but was always intended for a permanent statue. Honouring England's founder on this milestone anniversary would be a fitting use for one of London's most prominent sites.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about the use of the Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square are a matter for the Fourth Plinth Commissioning Group and the Mayor of London, not the UK Government or Parliament.

You can find out more here: https://www.london.gov.uk/programmes-strategies/arts-and-culture/current-culture-projects/fourth-plinth-trafalgar-square

action: Repeal Mandatory Folic Acid Fortification in UK Bread Flour
background: We call on Parliament to repeal mandatory folic acid fortification of UK bread flour, protect consumer choice, respect informed consent, and replace mass medication with targeted education and voluntary supplementation for those who need it most.
additional_details: Synthetic folic acid can accumulate as unmetabolised folic acid, with concerns including masking vitamin B12 deficiency, potential cancer progression in some groups, and side effects such as headaches, anxiety, sleep and digestive issues. Genetic variants like MTHFR may impair metabolism, increasing risk. Mandatory fortification removes choice despite uneven benefit.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ensure access to non-whole meal flour without folic acid fortification
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751401

action: Add Sickle Cell Disease to the NHS Prescription Charge Exemption List
background: Living with Sickle Cell is a journey which can be defined by unrelenting unpredictability and hardship. This is not an abstract issue or a distant statistic - it is my life. I am not just writing about Sickle Cell; I am living it. The health scares are constant, and the uncertainty never rests.
additional_details:
Beyond the physical pain and emotional toll. The cost of medication. These medicines are not optional. They are life-sustaining that allows patients to manage complications, and maintain a quality of life. We think it is both strenuous and unjust to expect individuals already battling a debilitating genetic disorder to also shoulder such overwhelming financial strain.
 
Proactive healthcare is essential to managing it. Access to medication should not depend on income, geography, or circumstance.

action: Scrap the idea of a Police Licence to Practise
background: Scrap the idea of a Police Licence to Practise. We do not think it would solve the issues that police are currently facing. We believe there is no realistic possible way to implement this to have a positive impact on policing.
additional_details: Police Officers hold a warrant card which confirms their legal authority. Officers have already undergone basic training, tutor periods and some have completed degrees as well as already doing yearly reaccreditations for skills that they have obtained. We think all the license will do is cause a higher wastage of police funding as you'd have to pay people to create and monitor it.

action: Call on the UK Government to protect Kurdish rights in North East Syria
background: We urge the UK Government to put political pressure on the Syrian government to protect Kurdish rights in North East Syria by upholding the ceasefire, ensuring Kurdish participation in political processes, preventing harm to civilians, and allowing humanitarian aid to reach affected areas.
additional_details: Kurdish-led forces were the main partner in defeating ISIS, helping remove its territorial control and reduce its global threat over many years. Their role contained security risks in North East Syria and prevented wider displacement. Recent shifts in control risk renewed instability, civilian harm and disruption of humanitarian access. UK action urging respect for the ceasefire and pressure on the Syrian government would help prevent further conflict and support regional stability.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions:

Put diplomatic pressure on Syria & Turkey to protect Kurds & other minorities
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757124

Condemn attacks on Kurds in North Syria & use diplomatic pressure to bring peace
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756339

action: Review the sentencing standards for carrying a bladed article in public
background: Following yet a other mindless, needless murder of a teenager, with a bladed article, I wish for the Government to increase Police powers of stop and search enabling them to identify those who carry bladed articles in public and enforce a minimum 5 year custodial sentence on those found carrying one
additional_details: As a Father, I do not wish to see any child, of any age, being needlessly killed by other children. I genuinely believe that the Government owes it to every family who has lost a child in this manner to start making an example of those who do carry bladed articles in public and prevent them having the opportunity to take someone's child's life.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Introduce 5yr Minimum Sentence for unlawfully carrying a Knife 3yrs Juveniles
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/753568

action: Protect Kurds in Rojava (North & East Syria) and prevent further atrocities
background: We urge the UK Government to protect Kurds and civilians in Rojava (NE Syria) by condemning attacks, backing UN monitoring/investigations, imposing targeted sanctions on perpetrators, boosting humanitarian aid, and working with allies to ensure stability and civilian protection.
additional_details: Kurdish forces and communities in Rojava (North & East Syria) were key allies of the UK and partners in defeating ISIS. Many Kurdish civilians now fear renewed violence, displacement and persecution amid instability and conflict involving the new Syrian authorities and other actors. The UK should not stay silent. We urge the Government to defend human rights, support stability, prevent ISIS returning, and act through diplomacy, coordination and lawful sanctions.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions:

Put diplomatic pressure on Syria & Turkey to protect Kurds & other minorities
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757124

Condemn attacks on Kurds in North Syria & use diplomatic pressure to bring peace
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756339

action: Legally require all councillors & mayors to speak proficient English
background: There’s no legal requirement for councillors/mayors to be proficient in English. This can lead to communication barriers in meetings and with constituents. This petition calls for mandatory English fluency for these roles.
additional_details: In recent years, viral media clips have raised concerns about English proficiency among some ceremonial mayors and councillors. Discussions question if limited fluency impairs public communication. These cases support calls for mandatory English proficiency and English-only official meetings for clarity and accessibility.

action: Debate the Impact of Higher Taxes on Workers Despite Promises to Protect Them
background: We believe Parliament should debate whether this definition accurately reflects the UK workforce, whether recent tax decisions are consistent with public commitments made to voters, and whether further action is needed to protect working people from rising financial pressure.
additional_details:
We call on the UK Parliament to hold a formal debate on the rising tax burden faced by UK workers and to review the Government’s definition of “working people” used to justify recent fiscal policies.
many workers have experienced higher overall tax and contribution costs through changes. These increases have reduced take-home pay for millions who rely primarily on wages or salaries. The Prime Minister has repeatedly stated that “working people” would be protected from higher taxes.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call for a clear action from the UK Government or Parliament. You could submit a new petition calling for a specific change in tax policy, if that's something you would like to happen. You could also sign petitions on this issue, such as: 

We urge the Government to reduce income tax on wages by at least 5%
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741071

End the freeze on income tax thresholds & adjust annually, indexed to inflation
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749467

action: Propose the creation of a new defence treaty in Europe as an alternative to NATO
background: We call on the UK Government to support the creation of a European defence treaty which can remain dormant until the day the United States could no longer uphold the North Atlantic Treaty. It would need no secretariat or integrated commands until those of NATO become available for use by Europeans.
additional_details: We, the undersigned, are concerned about the legacy of this US administration’s policies toward Greenland, Ukraine, Europe, and international law in general. We question the ability and the will of the US to defend both Europe and the Far East in the future. We believe only a legitimate treaty could ever replace NATO and that no current European institution is fit. The EU & UK already have many times the population and GDP of Russia. We believe only the political will is needed.

action: Expel all US diplomatic and military personnel from the UK
background: We urge the UK Government to expel all US diplomatic personnel from all US diplomatic missions in the UK, alongside expelling US military personnel and aircraft from RAF and other UK military bases.
additional_details: We believe that due to recent actions from the US, the UK should consider severing diplomatic and military relations with the United States. Many consider the US' presence in our military bases to be dangerous, contributing to the US’ military actions against other sovereign countries, and benefiting from the service and accommodation provided by UK military bases.

action: Fund and Deliver Overground & Tube Extensions South of the River Thames
background: South of the Thames is still under-served by the Underground despite long-standing TfL plans. This has led to overcrowding, longer commutes and unequal investment. We call for funded Tube extensions or rail conversions and a clear timetable for delivery.
additional_details:
South London (and beyond) is home to millions of residents, key town centres and growing communities, yet remains largely excluded from the Underground network. Despite years of TfL plans, no proper new Tube stations have been delivered south of the Thames. We deserve fair investment, better connections and Underground-standard services to support jobs, housing and sustainable travel.

Overground lines would be incredibly helpful considering there’s already National Rail lines in place.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. It is the responsibility of the Mayor of London and the London Assembly. 

The London Assembly has its own petitions process. You can find out more about how to petition the London Assembly here: https://www.london.gov.uk/about-us/london-assembly/petitions

action: Take action to immediately stop the decline in hospitality venues in the UK
background: Urgently review the impact of the last two UK Budgets on the hospitality sector, including rising employment costs, energy prices, supply chain inflation and business rates. The current business model is unsustainable. We ask the Government to bring targeted support or reform where necessary asap.
additional_details: It’s simple - at the current rate of decline the number of pubs and hospitality businesses will continue having a massive impact on employment, business growth, supplier impact,  communities and social well being. If action is not taken immediately community hubs will be lost and never return. VAT in hospitality is the highest in Europe, business rates are not calculated on profit. Young people support is non existent.
rejection_details:
Review rising costs & financial pressures on the UK hospitality sector
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/755209

action: Prevent MP's from changing party during a Parliament without a bi-election.
background: Ensure that the practice of crossing the house stops so that MP's either continue to represent the party they were elected to by their constituents or they resign and stand in a bi election for their new chosen party.
additional_details: Constituents vote for prospective MP' on the basis of the party they stand for and or the policies of that individual and that party. If they change party clearly they no longer represent their constituents on the basis on which they were elected.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Apply diplomatic pressure on Syria to protect and grant self-rule to Kurds
background: We ask the UK Government to apply diplomatic pressure on Syria to halt military advances into Kurdish areas to protect Kurds and support a constitution which guarantees the Kurds’ right to self-rule.
additional_details: We believe the Kurdish people have been vital to regional stability, yet recent military advances may threaten to undo years of local governance and safety. Without UK diplomatic intervention, we are concerned there is a high risk of mass displacement and ethnic persecution. We believe a stable Syria requires an inclusive political settlement that respects Kurds’ right to self-rule.

action: Review and increase expense rates for employees traveling outside the UK
background: HMRC sets scale rate expenses for subsistence paid to employees who travel outside the UK, such as Cabin Crew. We feel the rates are not reflective or the real costs for people whose work takes them abroad, and that the way they are put into blocks of 5/10 or 24 hour blocks is completely unfair.
additional_details: We want these rates to be reviewed by HMRC so they are up to date with the current cost of living. If a flight is delayed by an hour this can mean dropping from the 24 hour payment down to the 10 hour payment so essentially working 12 hours without a payment, this is a common occurrence in air travel, hence crew being penalised for something out of their control. We believe the scale rates need to provide a wider range of rates and time blocks so that if you fall between rates you are not penalised.

action: Call on MPs to table a vote of no confidence in the government
background: We want Members of Parliament to table and debate a motion of no confidence in the current government, allowing the House of Commons to formally consider whether the government still has the confidence of Parliament.
additional_details: We believe the government has demonstrated repeated failures in judgement and decision making on behalf of the UK population. There is widespread public concern about leadership, competence, and an inability to act consistently in the public interest. These concerns have led to a loss of public confidence that should be addressed through proper parliamentary process.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help#standards

If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

action: Review the way media outlets inc online/social media report about suicide deaths
background: Conduct a review with the aim to protect the welfare of families left behind after someone dies by suicide and consider what legislation is necessary.
additional_details:
Currently, some media outlets and reporters attend scenes/inquests and report what they like. Sometimes information can be factually incorrect, which can cause further harm and suffering. This can include children. 

Any new law in relation to this could be called "Levi's Law".

action: Allow Mayors to stand in any future leadership contests
background: People who have been democratically elected into such positions of authority such as Mayor should be allowed to stand for their given party in any leadership contest. As they can demonstrate their ability to govern at a high level.
additional_details: People such as Mayors are elected and are representatives of their parties they are also members of their parties. In sight of recent events allowing this would eliminate any abuse of power, thus stopping any future blocking of potential candidates. This Petition is about democratic fairness.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about eligibility to stand for offices within a political party including party leader are a matter for individual political parties, not the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Lower decibel limits for vehicle exhausts and monitor with noise cameras
background: Fund the nationwide roll-out of acoustic noise cameras and set stricter, lower enforceable decibel limits for vehicle exhausts.
additional_details: It is estimated that over 15% of the UK population is neurodivergent (including, but not limited to: Autistic, ADHD, and SPD). For those with diverse neurotypes, modified exhausts can be a sensory assault. Sudden, explosive noise can cause physical pain and trauma, especially for children. We have a right to access public spaces, yet avoidable noise can make our streets "no-go zones." We call on the Government to mandate national acoustic camera enforcement to help protect all neurominorities.

action: Stop the ban for under 16’s and change it to 13 or 14
background: If your wanting to do a ban put it on under 13’s or for under 16’s make it have a screen time limit on the certain apps like 1-2hrs a day and then the rest of the time they can’t have it till next day as a lot of over 13’s are more mature then 16’s so either don’t do the ban or do a screen limit
additional_details: A lot of teenagers rely on social media to message there friends and family so by taking it away it will make stuff worst and a lot of teenagers struggle with mental health and social media is there way of coping so by taking all that away it could end someone’s life. Yes relying on social media isn’t a good thing but if you put a screen time it may help
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Government ban on social media to be for under 13s only" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757849

action: Reject a social media ban for under-16s and change the minimum age to 13 instead
background: We call on the Government to reject proposals to ban under-16s from social media. The Government should maintain the  digital age of consent at 13 and focus on enforcing the Online Safety Act instead of implementing a blanket ban that removes digital autonomy for 14 and 15-year-olds.
additional_details: A ban for under-16s risks isolating teens who rely on social media for community and education. At 13, teens should begin developing digital literacy under parental guidance, not state prohibition. The Government is currently consulting on this, and we believe education and safety features are better solutions than a ban that restricts the rights of millions of young people.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Government ban on social media to be for under 13s only" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757849

action: Advocate for Kurdish civilians and women’s rights in Syria
background: The Government should use diplomatic & legal channels to protect Kurdish civilian rights in northeast Syria, ensure aid access, defend women's rights in peace talks, oppose forced displacement, gender-based violence & support independent monitoring of ceasefire arrangements and human rights abuses.
additional_details: Although a ceasefire was announced in January, Kurdish civilians in northeast Syria continue to face insecurity and displacement, with humanitarian reporting showing urgent needs for food, shelter and medical care. Women and girls are especially vulnerable to violence, exploitation and exclusion when conflict disrupts legal protections and essential services. In our view, the UK has obligations under international humanitarian law and the Women, Peace and Security agenda to protect civilians and women in conflict.

action: Make spitting on the streets in public illegal
background: Ban spitting on the streets.
additional_details: I am worried that spitting in public places could spread infectious disease. Saliva and mucus contain live pathogens responsible for tuberculosis, influenza, COVID-19, pneumonia, and meningitis. Once expelled onto the ground, these pathogens can contaminate shoes, hands, dust, and water runoff — creating multiple pathways for transmission, especially in dense urban areas. I want the government to make it an offence to spit in public.

action: Ban all e-bikes & electric scooters in public
background: Fully ban e-bikes and electric scooters in public, in order to prevent accidents and stop people from using them to commit crimes.

action: Mandate paper towels in public toilets for sensory-sensitive people
background: Require public toilets (including shops, restaurants, and public buildings) to provide paper hand towels as an accessible alternative to electric dryers. This could support proper hand drying and hygiene for people with sensory sensitivities, such as autistic individuals distressed by dryer noise.
additional_details: Electric hand dryers terrify some autistic children. They can cause them to panic, cry, cover their ears and wipe their wet hands on their clothes. Autism affects 1 in 100 people in the UK; many with noise sensitivities avoid toilets or outings. We think paper hand towels as a quiet alternative are simple, low-cost and effective. They can reduce anxiety, and make public spaces inclusive for autistic children and adults.

action: Mandate recognition of primary caregiver in family court decisions
background: Amend Children Act 1989 to require courts in disputes about child arrangements/parental responsibility to identify parent providing most daily care and create presumption giving greater weight to that parent’s views in decisions, unless another arrangement better serves the child’s welfare.
additional_details: Parental responsibility is obtained through marriage or birth registration regardless of caregiving involvement. In many families one parent carries most of the day to day responsibility for a child’s care, routine and stability. However, courts are not required to formally recognise this when resolving disputes about arrangements or parental responsibility. This can leave primary caregivers managing the realities of raising a child while legal influence remains equal.

action: A New Years wish: make Britain Great, for once...
background: We call on Parliament to: stop funding wars, legislate the closure of all American military bases in the UK and apply to join BRICS trading nations. We believe that Britain has been in the shadow of it's distant transatlantic neighbour for too long and that it's time to break free.
additional_details: We believe that, America has been effectively occupying Europe, since the end of WW2, whilst costing the UK tens of £billions in contributions. America seems to have swapped it's self appointed role of 'world policeman' for the more overt role of international piracy, not out of strength, but in desperate fear of economic collapse. We feel that the 'promissory notes' of such a country, cannot be trusted, let alone for them to be used as the main international trading currency

action: Bring in baby loss certificates to Wales, Scotland and Ireland
background: Baby loss certificates for babies lost before 24 weeks were introduced for England ONLY in 2024 but not available in Wales, Scotland and Ireland. We would like the government to make them available for people in the whole of the UK, and not just people in England
additional_details: I would like the government to make baby loss certificates available for the whole of the uk. I’ve read a few articles saying that wales and Ireland will be doing it but no date has been set for this. This is something that should be available for everyone in the UK not just England. I’ve spoken to a few people that feel this would help massively and bring comfort to parents that have lost a pregnancy/baby before 24 weeks
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Welsh Government and Welsh Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.

The Welsh Parliament has its own Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Welsh Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.senedd.wales/

You may also wish to raise this issue with your local Members of the Senedd who represent you. You can find out who your Members of the Senedd are and how to contact them here: https://senedd.wales/find-a-member-of-the-senedd/

action: Incorporate self defence classes into PE lessons throughout schools
background: Incorporate self defence classes into PE lessons for primary&secondary aged school children.
additional_details:
The world is rapidly changing. In many places, individuals, especially women & young people, are facing risks of physical harm or harassment within their communities, it is imperative that we equip our next generations with the skills necessary to navigate these dangers effectively.
Incorporating self-defence classes into the Physical Education (PE) curriculum for primary & secondary school-aged children is a forward-thinking solution.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Introduce self-defence lessons into the PE curriculum in all secondary schools
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749166

action: Ensure Government Listens to Public Concerns, Including Privacy & Digital Rights
background: Im asking the Government to genuinely consult the public, improve transparency in decision-making, and review the Online Safety Act to ensure it does not undermine personal privacy, data protection, or freedom of expression, with stronger safeguards, accountability, and democratic oversight.
additional_details: Many people (myself included) feel ignored by the Government on issues that affect daily life, from the cost of living to public services and civil liberties. A healthy democracy requires ongoing public engagement, transparency and accountability. Concerns about the Online Safety Act highlight the need to protect privacy, free expression and data rights, and ensure policies are developed with public consent and safeguards.
rejection_details:
We are not sure what specific action you are seeking from the UK Government. You can start a new petition setting out more clearly what you would like the Government to do. There is also a open petition which may be interested in signing:

Call for full scrutiny & a 6 month public consultation on Digital ID
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743425

action: Urgently implement all Cumberlege Report recommendations and reform the MHRA
background: We call on the Government to fully implement all the recommendations of the First Do No Harm report; they must undertake a radical overhaul of the Medicines & Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) to ensure it is more patient-focused & transparent, & provide full redress for victims of harm.
additional_details:
The 2020 First Do No Harm report exposed decades of avoidable harm from Pelvic Mesh, Sodium Valproate, and Primodos. Key recommendations remain unfulfilled.
We urge the Government to:
Reform the MHRA: Overhaul the regulator to ensure it is patient-centric, transparent, and prioritizes safety over industry interests.
Redress Schemes: Provide financial support for victims
Transparency: Enforce a mandatory register of interests for all doctors.
Thousands of families are still waiting for justice.

action: Provide free period products for all girls and women via the NHS
background: Provide free period products via the NHS for all girls and women, ensuring access through GP surgeries, pharmacies, hospitals and schools, to reduce period poverty, support menstrual health, and promote equality.
additional_details:
Access to period products is essential for health, dignity and equality. Many girls and women cannot afford these products, leading to missed school or work, poor menstrual hygiene, and negative health outcomes.

The NHS already provides essential healthcare free at the point of use. Providing period products through the NHS would help prevent period poverty, support menstrual health, and reduce health inequalities, aligning with Government commitments to women’s health.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund free female sanitary products for all women and girls
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756958

action: Adjust Child Maintenance Payment assessment to account for living costs
background: We urge Government to revise child maintenance calculations to reflect net incomes after essential living costs. We believe this would ensure a fair and balanced system that supports both children and non-resident parents.
additional_details: In our view, current calculations often impose financial strain on non-resident parents, risking mental health and housing stability. Reforming the system to consider net income after essential costs could promote consistent support for children while safeguarding parents’ well-being. We believe this change is crucial for a fairer approach to child maintenance.

action: Create a central body to manage the maintenance and development of all roads
background: The maintenance and development of all roads currently managed by local authorities should be centralised. Responsibility should be removed from local authorities and handed to an independent, properly funded and governed, competent, professional, central body covering the whole country.
additional_details: The establishment and maintenance of an effective transport infrastructure is a key measure of a successful first world country. We believe it is readily apparent that the majority of local authorities across the UK have wholly failed in this duty with regard to the road network over decades and that the problem is getting measurably and rapidly worse. Government should redirect the responsibility and funding to a new body with the sole responsibility for managing the road network.

action: Cease prosecution of any veteran who served in northern Ireland.
background: Reverse and put in place legislations that will stop the witch-hunt of many of our armed forces from being prosecuted.
additional_details: It was the government who put soldiers in difficult positions which meant young men had to make difficult decisions in the face of a terrorist organisation that used sneaky tactics to kill innocent civilians. It was the UK government who gave many known terrorists immunity while offering nothing to our veterans who are being hounded right up to veterans who are in care homes suffering from dementia.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751251

action: Block the construction of the Peak Cluster Pipeline on the Wirral peninsula
background: Block the application of the Peak Cluster Pipeline on the Wirral. The Wirral has a population of over 300,000 people and is far from rural land. CO2 pipelines bring completely different risks as compared to natural gas or other pipelines and the risk to life in the event of a leak is high.
additional_details: The proposed Peak Cluster Pipeline, like all other 'Carbon Capture' technology, is merely a greenwashing attempt to push continued burning of fossil fuels at industrial scale. CO2 pipelines pose considerable safety risks should a leak form near an urban area. A leak in Satartia, Mississippi with a population of just 40 almost cost several lives when cars stopped working due to the lack of oxygen - proving the risk to life is considerable. The rush to net zero should not mean cutting corners.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Give teachers time off to attend their own children’s school events
background: Give teachers a formal option to attend their own children’s school events during school hours. Even a few hours per year, paid or unpaid, would ensure all teachers can participate in assemblies, sports days, and performances, regardless of individual school policies
additional_details: Teachers currently have no formal way to attend their own children’s school events during school hours, unlike other employees who can use leave. This creates inequality, affects wellbeing, and forces parents to miss key milestones. A formal option, even limited or unpaid, would ensure fairness, support teacher morale, and allow teachers to participate in their children’s lives.
rejection_details: Annual leave policies are a matter for the individual school, and is not the responsibility of the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Make it illegal to secretly film and publish personal information online
background: Introduce laws to make filming people secretly and elucidating personal information for the purposes of publishing online content a crime.

action: Tougher sentencing for pedophiles and child rapists
background: We want tougher sentencing for pedophiles/child rapist/child abusers, having indecent images of children, anything to do with harming innocent children.
additional_details: As a nation we want tougher sentencing for all of the above. Some are getting 27 months for having indecent images of children, that’s not justice, nothing will ever be justice for these sick individuals. They deserve to be in prison for life. No child should ever suffer abuse and feel like there predator is roaming free. The sentencing needs looking at and changing. These people destroy children’s lives.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Review punishment of Child Sex Offences
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746131

action: Make all MP's who change from one party to another, have to have a bi-election.
background: MP's who change party mid term, have to resit their seat.
additional_details: With our party system MP's are voted in as they are part of a party system, if they now change the party they support, they should go for re-election.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Require employers to pay carers for travel time and all hours worked
background: Many carers are not paid for travel time between service users, even though it is part of their working day. This means some carers work long hours but are only paid for contact time. We think this is unfair, lowers real pay and risks carers' salaries falling below minimum wage.
additional_details: Unpaid travel time and insufficient mileage payments are widespread in the care sector and can result in carers working long hours without being paid for all the time they work. We believe this practice is unfair, risks bringing pay close to or below the minimum wage, and can contribute to staff shortages and burnout. Paying carers fairly could improve retention, quality of care, and sustainability of the care system.

action: That a by-election be triggered immediately if a serving MP changes party.
background: Hold a by-election immediately if a serving MP changes party affliation.
additional_details: When voting in a general election, one considers which party and which individual candidate would best serve the constituency and, probably, the country as a whole. I suspect that in a general election, the party counts for more than the individual. There has recently been a spate of MPs changing party mid-term and joining parties which their constituents *did not choose*.
rejection_details:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party

action: Replace use of hotels for asylum seekers with a risk-based accommodation system
background: The Government should introduce legislation to replace long-term use of hotels for asylum seeker accommodation with a risk-based processing system, including rapid assessment, time-limited decisions, and UK-controlled processing facilities where identity or security concerns remain unresolved.
additional_details: The Government should introduce primary legislation to replace long-term use of hotels for asylum seeker accommodation with a risk-based processing system. This should include rapid individual assessment, time-limited decisions, differentiated accommodation based on risk and vulnerability, and designated UK-controlled processing facilities for cases with unresolved identity or security concerns, subject to judicial oversight.

action: Allow children and teens to have an extended amount of time off school when sick
background: Extend time off for the wellbeing of children and teens
additional_details: Children and teens who are sick only get to have 5 days off school out of the year until they are fined so this time should be extended to 2 weeks or 3 out of the year has children and teens are forced to go into school sick causing more youths to gain sick and be fined placing payments on parents  who are on benefits who cant suppourt the payment
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

5 days is the threshold for fines for unauthorised absence, not sickness.

Schools may request evidence for repeated illness, but they cannot fine parents for legitimate sickness.

action: Enforce By-elections in constituencies where the MP defects to a different party
background: Discuss in parliament enforcing by-elections in constituencies where the MPs defect to another party.
additional_details: Romford,Newark,Fareham & Waterlooville and any other constituencies that have their MP change party should have to hold By-elections. MPs are voted in largely on their alignment with a party's view not just the individual.

You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party

action: Ban AI in the UK
background: I would like the government or parliament to ban AI of all kinds in the UK.
additional_details: Artificial intelligence (AI) is actively destroying our planet, using massive energy and water consumption for training models in Data Centers, increasing carbon footprints, reliance on fossil fuels, intensive hardware manufacturing (mining rare minerals, e-waste), and exacerbating social inequalities through pollution in vulnerable communities, all while potentially hindering climate action through misinformation. Malicious use: People could intentionally harness powerful AIs to cause widespread harm. AI could be used to engineer new pandemics or for propaganda, censorship, and surveillance, or released to autonomously pursue harmful goals.

You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban all use of AI in the UK

action: Kurds in Rojava, Northeast Syria, facing genocide
background: To use their power to call an urgent meeting within the international community to stop the genocide taking place in North-eastern Syria against the Kurds in Rojava.
additional_details: We urge you to fulfil your humanitarian and moral obligations and for the British government to raise awareness, as a powerful nation within the United Nations, to take immediate action against these crimes committed against the Kurds in North-eastern Syria.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

UK must act now & condemn the killing of Kurdish civilians in Rojava & Rojhilat

Condemn attacks on Kurds in North Syria & use diplomatic pressure to bring peace

action: Link MP wages to GDP growth per annum
background: Link an MP's annual salary increase to the GDP growth of the previous year. This creates an incentive structure so that politicians can focus on delivering pro-growth policies that benefit the country while increasing their own pay.
additional_details: A member of parliament currently makes £93,904 a year which is almost three times the average annual salary. Linking it to GDP growth would mean that MPs could focus on delivering growth so that they can reap the rewards of their efforts. This is the right thing to do to restore the trust in Britain's economic policy.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA) is responsible for deciding on MPs' expenses and pay. IPSA is independent of both Parliament and Government.

You can find out more about IPSA here: http://www.theipsa.org.uk

action: Create a superloop bus from Bluewater to Lewisham
background: A lot of people face a daily struggle commuting between Kent and Central London for work. Travelling long distances from Kent to London has become the norm, and now more than ever, efficient and cost-effective transportation is critical for the thousands of workers who make this journey every day.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

action: More enforcement action and consequences to non payment of child maintenance
background: More power to be given to child maintenance service. The current system lacks effective enforcement, and the repercussions for those who fail to pay for their children are minimal. This places an undue burden on the parent who is rightfully entitled to receive these essential funds
additional_details: Enforcement actions and consequences for not paying child maintenance could potentially improve things by ensuring that parents meet their financial obligations to their children. Stronger enforcement might lead to more consistent payments, which can significantly improve the well-being of children and reduce the financial strain on custodial parents.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Take stronger measures to enforce payment of child maintenance arrears.
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739525

action: Legislated online age verification should not be provided by the private sector
background: Online age verification should be provided directly by a government agency like HMRC who already has the necessary data. The data transmitted to platforms during the age verification must be limited to a simple yes/no answer that they are old enough. The precise age must remain private.
additional_details: Private age verification is collecting too much sensitive data and poses a significant identity theft risk, especially to children. There have already been several known leaks. Privacy policies already cover how verification data is used for targeted advertising. The "Unless absolutely necessary" retention law is too broad. Smaller platforms cannot afford the costs of compliance and have to close, which ensures only big tech remains in the market. A public service would solve these issues.
rejection_details:
This is very similar to a petition which is currently open, which you may wish to sign:

Replace age verification process set out in Online Safety Act to voucher system
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756256

action: Make parking on footpaths illegal in England
background: Make parking on footpaths illegal for the whole of England.
additional_details: We believe footpaths are exactly as described for the public to freely walk without hindrance from parked vehicles. Keep car parking away from footpaths, with enforcement powers given to local councils to punish those who do block footpaths.

action: Reduce the age that the cbt can be done for 50cc to 14 years old
background: Reduce the age from 16 down to 14 like 7 other eu countries for learner moped riders wanting to get on the road and do there cbt which would help parents and the teens gain experience on the road earlier on in their developing life
additional_details: The government should do it as many young people are eager to get on the road, reduce their burden on their parents and have a small amount of ownership and responsibility. Another reason is that it has already been proven by 7 eu countries that the 14 year old age requirement is working and makes more sense having then had 3 years of road experience before then moving onto a bigger motorbike or car

action: Link the pay of MPs and Civil Servants to people's average disposable income
background:
Total remuneration (pay, bonuses, expenses, etc.) should be linked to median disposable incomes of the population (after taxes, housing costs, energy bills, etc.).
If disposable incomes rise, MP and civil servants are rewarded; if they drop, then MPs and civil service remuneration is cut by double.
additional_details:
For at least three decades, governments have made decisions that have made UK citizens poorer. House prices, insane rents, energy prices, expensive food, high taxes, rampant immigration, and more are governments decisions that make us poorer.
In order to ensure that our politicians are genuinely working for the benefit of the people of the UK, we need to align incentives: if politico decisions make people poorer, then they should be made poorer too.
Align politico pay incentives to our benefit.
rejection_details:
We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. The Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA) is responsible for deciding on MPs' expenses and pay. IPSA is independent of both Parliament and Government.

You can find out more about IPSA here: https://www.theipsa.org.uk/

action: Allow the legal sale of raw milk in Scotland with clear consumer choice.
background: Raw milk is currently illegal to buy/sell in Scotland, despite being legally available in the rest of the UK. It is not the government's right to remove this choice from the Scottish people. Take note from the rest of the UK and restore our freedom of CHOICE.
additional_details: Adults are trusted to buy alcohol, cigarettes, vapes and ultra-processed foods, yet are not trusted to choose whether to consume raw milk. This decision is clearly not about health. We call on the UK Government to legalise the sale of raw milk, subject to clear labelling and hygiene standards, so adults can make informed choices about what they consume. In other words, call off the dairy cops, it's pathetic. It's a matter of personal freedom, transparency, and consumer choice.
rejection_details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

You may also wish to contact your local MSP who represent you about this issue. 

You can find the name of your local MSP and how to contact them here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps

action: Fund lowering the age for a smear test to 16 years old
background: I would like government to fund the NHS so the minimum age for a smear test is lowered, to prevent women from having cell changes at a younger age leading to cervical cancer or even vulva cancer.
additional_details: I have had ongoing abnormal smears and cell change since the age of 25, I am now 36 and still being treated for abnormal cells, at 25 I had the highest grade of abnormal cells (CIN3) if I hadn’t had my smear when I did I may not be here now, so I think the age should be lowered as this could prevent women reaching to higher grade cell change. Many young women become sexually active at the age of 16 which puts them at risk of getting HPV which can lead to cell changes, and the wait is far too long to be able to be screened for abnormal cells, this could prevent so many women from getting cervical cancer or even vulva cancer, lowering the age for a smear test could help so many women.

action: Fund vape bins to cut litter, protect wildlife, and promote cleaner streets
background: We urge the Government to fund local authorities to pilot dedicated, fire-resistant vape bins in public spaces and near schools to reduce litter, prevent lithium battery fires, protect wildlife, lower clean-up costs, and enable safe recycling of over 1 million disposable vapes discarded daily.
additional_details: Disposable vapes create litter, pollution, and fire risks from batteries. We urge the Government to fund a pilot for secure vape-only bins in public areas. Councils showing the most dedication to proper disposal of vapes would receive additional funding for schemes like tree planting, reducing litter, enabling recycling, and promoting safer, cleaner streets.

action: Legislate for automatic by-elections when a standing MP decides to defect.
background: Bring in legislation that will trigger an automatic by-election when a standing MP decides to defect from the party they represented when elected, to another political party during the life of that parliament.
additional_details: MPs are elected based on the political party that they stand to represent at an election, and its policies.  If they consequently decide they no longer agree with the policies of that political party and wish to defect to another, then there should automatically be a by-election to allow the people who voted for them, to decide whether or not they are still a suitable MP.  Until that by-election they should continue to act for the party for which they were elected or stand down immediately.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Reduce UK partner/spouse visa minimum income from £29,000 to £25,000 per year
background: I am asking the Government to lower the minimum income for UK partner/spouse visas from £29,000 to £25,000. The current rule prevents many citizens from bringing partners to live with them and is higher than the average salary. Reducing it would make family reunification fairer and more achievable.
additional_details: The current £29,000 minimum income for UK partner/spouse visas prevents many citizens from bringing partners to live with them. Reducing it to £25,000 would make family reunification fairer, more achievable, and less financially burdensome for ordinary earners.

action: Introduce mandatory paid menstrual leave of up to two days per month
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation for employees whose menstrual symptoms significantly affect their ability to work, with protections against discrimination to support health, dignity, and workplace equality.
additional_details: This policy would align the UK with international best practice and support employees’ long-term participation in the workforce. We believe menstrual leave should be treated as a legitimate workplace health accommodation, similar to other temporary health-related leave, and should not disadvantage employees in hiring, promotion, or performance assessment.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require employers have monthly menstrual 1-3 day leave policy
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740839

action: Push for mental health services, because a lot of people really need support.
background: Advocate for mental health services!  We need more money, facilities, and support workers. People are suffering immensely and often turning to suicide. Please advocate for this invisible illness. We need more funding to support the vulnerable.  #MentalHealth #Support #Funding #Advocacy #Awareness
additional_details: It is imperative that we comprehend the profound impact of mental health across all demographics. Enhanced education and awareness are crucial, as a transformative shift is urgently required. We currently face significant challenges, including insufficient diagnostic resources, extended waiting periods, missed opportunities to provide essential medication, and an overwhelming demand for counseling and support services. Implementing systemic changes is critical to preserving lives.
rejection_details: It is not clear from the text of the petition exactly what the Government is being asked to do beyond what it already states its intention is.

action: Overhaul the UK driving test system to ensure fair access to local test centres.
background: Review the driving test booking system to ensure learners can book tests at their local centres within a reasonable timeframe, and prevent third parties from bulk-booking and reselling tests at inflated prices.
additional_details: An unprecedented number of learner drivers are competing for too few tests, often having to turn to third-party resellers. Availability is so limited that many remain stuck in the system indefinitely, without a fair chance to pass their driving test.
rejection_details:
Review the driving test booking process, ban resales at inflated prices & bots

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/736594

action: Request verified numbers of protesters killed, injured and hospitalised in Iran
background: Ask the UK Government to formally request verified information from Iranian authorities on protesters killed, injured or hospitalised, including injury severity, since 28 December 2025, and to seek assurance that all injured protesters are receiving appropriate medical care.
additional_details: Families deserve truth, not silence. Transparent reporting of deaths and injuries is essential to honour those who have lost their lives and to ensure the wounded receive proper medical care. This is a humanitarian request. Verified information protects human dignity, enables medical oversight, and helps prevent further loss of life.

action: Commit £30m to community cycling facilities
background: We believe that community cycling facilities help children, families and adults become active, improving health and wellbeing while reducing pressure on the NHS and that existing programmes have delivered proven results. Government backing is needed to expand this model across the UK.
additional_details: Community cycling facilities help tackle physical inactivity, improve mental health, and support children, families and under-represented groups to be active. One independent analysis of British Cycling's Places to Ride programme linked it to over £13m in estimated NHS savings and £100m+ in social value. Scaling proven models would deliver long-term health, transport and community benefits across the UK. This supports national prevention, active travel and social prescribing priorities.

action: Issue immediate travel warning for the USA due to human rights concerns
background: Human rights must be applied consistently, or they cease to have meaning. The United States should not be exempt due to its political influence or alliance status
additional_details: The United Kingdom has a stated foreign-policy commitment to upholding human rights and has historically taken the position that it should not maintain uncritical alliances with states that fail to adhere to those principles. We think the US, through the documented actions of ICE and related agencies, is currently falling short of internationally recognised human-rights standards, including the right to life, freedom from arbitrary detention, and protection from cruel or degrading treatment.

action: Government must increase practical elements in Drama GCSE guidelines
background: I want the Government to change the drama GCSE curriculum to be 70%+ practical, as currently it is majority written work. This is unwarranted as the subject is a practical piece of work. We believe this can demoralise students and possibly make them fail.
additional_details: As a GCSE drama student I am appalled by the written work forced onto people, and I believe that making drama a majority practical subject can not only improve grades, but improve work ethic and people who are taking the subject. Many people may also be encouraged to participate more.

action: To stop cars from parking outside primary schools in newham
background: The parking around schools in newham is getting dangerous especially primary school the main hot-spot is vicarage lane east ham. They double park out the school with a bus route that also going down it so dangerous a child will ended up killed before newham council does anything about it
additional_details: Make it a non traffic zones during the schools hours like the rest of London
