action: Orthopaedic Practitioners to be recognised as registered professionals by NHS
background: I would wish for the Government/Parliament to help ensure that Orthopaedic practitioners registered with the British Orthopaedic Association, are recognised as registered professionals within the NHS, and are offered the opportunity to develop as part of the NHS multi-professional framework
additional_details:
In order to be employed as an orthopaedic practitioner, one must undertake on the job training, followed by a further 6 weeks at Stanmore hospital for academic teaching, and subsequent practical/verbal examination. 

On completion of this training, the student is rewarded a level5/6 certificate, and is signed onto a professional register for orthopaedic practitioners under the British Orthopaedic Association.
rejection_details:
We are not clear that this is a matter for the Government, it falls in part under the HCPC's remit which in turn falls under that of the PSA. 

I also am not clear that the steps you set out to become an orthopaedic practitioner  are comprehensive - I believe you also need an undergraduate medical degree and think training at Stanmore isn't obligatory (it can be taken at another hospital/institution as geographically appropriate - forgive me if I am wrong on this last point).

action: Review National Safeguarding Standards for Licensed Chaperones
background: Align chaperone regulation with comparable roles by reviewing national safeguarding standards for vetting, training, and oversight, ensuring children in performance receive consistent protection regardless of where they work.
additional_details: Licensed chaperones undertake a safeguarding-critical role with children in performance, yet oversight of licensing, renewal and accountability can vary widely by location. Centralised national oversight, with clear minimum standards and local delivery, would reduce inconsistency, strengthen safeguarding practice, and ensure children and professionals are protected regardless of where work takes place.

action: MPs that defect to another party should trigger an immediate by-election
background: Change the rules so that when a sitting MP defects to a different party, a by-election is immediately triggered
additional_details:
so that the electorate of the relevant constituency get a chance to be represented in parliament by an MP that represents them and the manifesto the majority initially voted for.
The votes should not follow the MP, as by definition of defection, the MP no longer represents the voters that put the MP in parliament, and the only way to check this is to have a by-election
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Reform child maintenance to be fair, balanced and reflect modern families
background: Base child maintenance on net income and exclude non-guaranteed bonuses, factor in essential living and housing costs of paying parent, and protect meaningful access to both parents by discouraging withheld contact and supporting cooperative parenting except where safeguarding concerns exist.
additional_details: The current child maintenance system focuses on gross income and often fails to account for disposable income, income stability, or unavoidable financial obligations of the non-resident parent, including continuing to pay the mortgage on the former family home. In some cases, it creates financial incentives that discourage shared parenting, causing hardship, reducing cooperation, increasing conflict, and producing outcomes that may not serve the child’s best interests.
rejection_details:
The following petition calls for a similar action: 

Reform Child Maintenance Service, strengthen processes to protect paying parent
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/755824

action: Protect bricklayers with fair pay, safety rights, and career support
background: The Government should set legal weather limits for outdoor work, guarantee winter pay when sites close, enforce safety standards, fund heated facilities, to strengthen worker rights and support apprenticeships to attract and retain skilled bricklayers.
additional_details: We believe the Government should introduce national winter working regulations for bricklayers, including enforceable temperature and weather limits, mandatory welfare facilities, and paid weather stoppages. By improving job security, fair pay, health protections, and funding training and apprenticeships, we believe bricklaying can become a safer, more attractive long-term career, helping address labour shortages and strengthen the construction industry.

action: Fund cold capping for all chemotherapy patients where clinically appropriate
background: Access to cold capping during weekly chemotherapy should not depend on postcode, and whether or not a particular hospital can offer that treatment. All patients should be offered the choice where clinically suitable, ensuring fairness, dignity, and equal cancer care for all.
additional_details: The government should end the postcode lottery by making cold capping available to all patients undergoing weekly chemotherapy where clinically appropriate. This requires national guidance, guaranteed funding, and consistent implementation across all NHS trusts, so access is based on patient choice and medical suitability—not on their postcode.

action: Stop the Chagos deal
background:
We have got to stop politicians giving away our hard earned wealth without it being agreed on .
It should be in a manifesto minimum or a referendum
additional_details: Stop this going through now
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop the Chagos Deal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/730757

action: Empower / entitle residential flat leaseholders to pursue commonhold ownership
background: To debate the merits of further strengthening of the Commonhold aspect of the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill, with the purpose of introducing further legislation to empower all leaseholders with the rights to pursue the Commonhold ownership for a fair and equitable settlement.
additional_details:
The freehold system is out of date and grossly unfair to leaseholders. It is abused by unscrupulous freeholders and their property managers, who hide behind unclear legislation to exploit their position of power and control to excessively inflate service charges, for their gain, without accountability and transparency.

Parliament should now establish a straightforward and clear path to Commonhold ownership to enable leaseholder an equal say in the control and cost management of their building
rejection_details:
It is already possible to pursue a commonhold conversion and the UK Government is currently considering changes to the process. More details here: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/commonhold-white-paper

You could start a new petition setting out more clearly what you think the UK Government or Parliament should do differently from what it is currently doing.

action: Make CCTV compulsory on all SEND transport
background: For the safety of our vulnerable children, CCTV should be mandatory on all transport to ensure our vulnerable children and adults are protected from any abuse that may occur by drivers and escorts
additional_details: There have been many occasions where vulnerable adults or SEN individuals have been hurt on SEND transport. CCTV would protect our children and adults from potential abuse, As it stands it is not yet legally required for CCTV to be in place on SEND transport and staff take advantage of this, especially to very vulnerable individuals who don't have the capacity to explain what happened. This would also protect staff from said allegations if they're innocent.

action: Platforms to provide free opt-out option for targeted ads on social media
background: We believe UK users should be able to opt out of personalised ads on social media sites without paying. In our view the “consent or pay” model pressures users and undermines GDPR rights. We urge the Government to require platforms to provide a free, genuine opt-out from targeted advertising.

action: Schools should prepare students for the real world
background: Year 7+ students must be taught business, finance, and entrepreneurship alongside life skills like tax navigation and household management. This curriculum should progress from basics to adult economic readiness, ensuring UK students can navigate the workplace and real world confidently.
additional_details: Parliament must mandate this curriculum to end the "postcode lottery" of financial literacy. Relying on parents or luck leaves thousands vulnerable to debt and unemployment. By formalising business, accounting, and tax education, the Government ensures social mobility and national economic resilience. We cannot expect a 21st-century economy to thrive if the next generation enters adulthood without the basic tools to manage a payslip, start a business, or navigate a professional workplace.
rejection_details:
The following petitions call for similar actions: 

Introduce mandatory business and entrepreneurship in secondary curriculum 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741347

Replace the RSHE curriculum with life skills 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750580

action: Fund support for UK companies to create more internships & jobs for young people
background: We urge the Government to prioritise helping young people with the job market in the UK by funding financial support for UK-based companies to create more internships and job positions for all, but especially young people.
additional_details: We believe the current UK job market is brutal for young people. The unemployment rate for people aged 16-24 is around 16%. Although the government has promised more internships for young people, we feel this is not enough and more needs to be done urgently. We feel the job crisis is causing young people to be pushed into poverty and worsening the mental health crisis. We believe young people have been most affected by the pandemic and economic crisis, and we want the Government to urgently act.

action: Review financial support for parents if child maintenance payments can't be made
background: Review financial support available to single parents if the other parent is unable to pay their child maintenance payment. We believe more needs to be done to support single-parent households by introducing a government-backed income or interim payment when the other parent cannot contribute.
additional_details: Single parents can be placed in severe financial hardship when the other parent cannot pay child maintenance due to for example unemployment, illness, absence or avoidance. The financial burden can then fall entirely on the primary caregiver, forcing families into poverty and instability. This directly affects children’s wellbeing, development and access to basic needs. In our view there is currently no safety net to ensure continued financial support. We believe that government intervention is necessary when these arrangements fail.

action: Restore Britain’s EU Membership for a Stronger Future
background: I want the UK Government to explore rejoining the EU to restore stability, protect our economy and strengthen alliances, especially as global politics feels increasingly unpredictable and the US becomes more volatile.
additional_details: I want the Government to begin an open process exploring the UK rejoining the EU, including honest discussions with EU partners and clear information for the public. Many people feel global politics is becoming unstable, with rising uncertainty in the US, so the UK should strengthen its alliances. Rejoining the EU could support our economy, improve opportunities and give people a meaningful say in our future.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Apply to Rejoin the EU as soon as possible to increase growth in the UK
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749128

action: Stop price increases by water service providers failing environmental standards
background: The Government to direct Ofwat to block price rises by water providers until they meet strict environmental & service standards, including binding pollution targets, independent monitoring, stronger fines, & a ban on executive bonuses until performance & customer trust are restored.
additional_details: Southern Water has, for example, repeatedly failed customers and the environment, including illegal sewage discharges and regulatory penalties. Despite this, bills continue to rise while senior executives receive high pay and bonuses. Households face cost-of-living pressures and should not fund poor management and environmental harm. Government action is needed to protect customers, enforce accountability, and ensure bill rises only follow real service improvements.

action: Ban all plastic in food and drink packaging
background: Ban plastic packaging.
additional_details: The Government must put a plan in place to remove plastic packaging.

action: Mandate GP surgeries to be open seven days a week
background: Unlike many other NHS services that operate seven days a week, many GP surgeries do not, and we feel this does not reflect current demand. As the population continues to grow, we believe this mismatch has reduced access to primary care and increased pressure on other parts of the NHS.
additional_details: Opening GP surgeries seven days a week, in line with NHS hospitals, walk-in centres, and NHS 111, could significantly improve access to primary care. Greater appointment availability could allow more patients to be seen by their GP at an earlier stage, reducing the number of people attending hospitals for non-emergency issues. This could help shorten hospital waiting times, improve patient flow, and reduce pressure on overstretched hospital doctors while distributing workload more effectively.

action: Provide Separate, Compassionate Spaces for NICU Mothers and Pregnancy Loss
background: Introduce national NHS guidance and funding to ensure hospitals can provide separate, private rooms for mothers whose babies are in NICU, and separate waiting and ward areas for women experiencing miscarriage, to ensure compassionate, trauma-informed care.
additional_details: Mothers with babies in NICU are often placed on shared postnatal wards surrounded by newborns, causing severe emotional distress at an already traumatic time. Likewise, women experiencing miscarriage are frequently made to wait alongside pregnant women or families with babies, which can intensify grief and trauma. These practices can cause avoidable psychological harm and lack compassion and dignity.

action: Get central government to increase funding to improve our roads/highways
background: Government to increase funding to improve our roads. They have been in a steady decline over the last 10+ years. Recently our roads (locally & nationally) have become dangerous to drive on. We have a legal obligation to make sure our vehicles are road worthy, yet the roads are not safe to drive on.
additional_details: The roads are horrific to drive on. I feel that there will be a fatality due to the unsafe conditions of our roads. Especially for vulnerable road users like cyclists or people on motorbikes. The pothole repairs we see last only a couple of weeks/months, such a waste of tax payers money. The contractors should be held accountable for their work.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition that calls for the same action:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739014
Fix Our Roads: National Plan on Dangerous Potholes Now

action: Add a 20% deposit to takeaway food & drink to pay for the clean up of litter.
background: Join me in urging our legislators to enact a law that will profoundly impact our environment's health and cleanliness. Please sign this petition to push for a cleaner, safer country, where takeaway packaging no longer clogs our beautiful landscapes. Share this petition widely please.
additional_details:
The escalating levels of litter on roadsides and countryside is ruining the beauty of our environment. Despite the efforts of local councils, they lack the funding to address this issue and the problem is worsening.

Our country is at risk of being overwhelmed by the vast amounts of waste from takeaway packaging. This is not just an eyesore but a threat to our natural habitat, wildlife, and the overall health of our environment. It's time for us to take proactive steps to keep our nation clean.
rejection_details:
We are not clear whether you want a 20% surcharge on takeaway food to be used for clear-up or an actual deposit worth 20% of the value of the purchase which can be reclaimed if the takeaway packaging is returned (which is what a deposit usually means - something reclaimable).

We suggest you may wish to resubmit your petition making this clearer.

action: Put abuse survivor voices, including youth, at the heart of UK support services.
background: We ask Parliament to make sure abuse survivors, including young people, are consulted when creating or changing support services and policies, so real experiences help improve systems and ensure survivor voices are genuinely heard.
additional_details: Abuse affects thousands of people across the UK, including young people. Survivors often feel unheard and unsupported, and current services can miss real needs. A Parliamentary debate would highlight survivor experiences, encourage better-informed policy, and help improve support systems nationwide by ensuring lived experience is part of decision-making.
rejection_details:
A petition must seek clear action from the UK Government or Parliament, and we are not sure what action you are seeking in this petition. 

You could submit a new petition setting out more clearly what you would like the UK Government or Parliament to do, and how it is different from what it is currently doing.

action: Make it a legal requirement to stop and act when you hit or run over a cat.
background: I want it made a legal requirement to at least stop and act if you hit a cat, or run over a cat. Theirs laws for dogs so why not cats? They are loved pets just as much, they deserve that dignity just as much! Stopping, taking action & reporting should be a legal requirement!
additional_details: 500 words is no where near enough. I am utterly heartbroken, my cat was hit at speed and left like last nights rubbish. She sustained horrific, traumatic injuries, she did not make it after fighting for her life. I had to see that, whilst people were eating tea we were digging a hole in the ground. It’s disgusting that someone can do that, cause that hurt and just go about their day & life. Why dogs and not cats?
rejection_details:
We are very sorry to hear about your cat.

You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750612

Legally require drivers who hit a cat to take them to a vet
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751525

action: Reformation of DWP Child Maintenance Service. Redress Legality, Virtue & Justice
background: Mandate Judicial Care Before Enforcement; Legally Enforce Protected Earnings; Assess Eligibility Factors of Mothers & Fathers. End Coercive, Pejorative Threat-Based Dehumanising “Paying Parent” Language. Stop the Enforcement of Disputed Cases. Restore Proportionality, Legal Principle and Due Process
additional_details: Current Practice Violates Justice Causing Severe Financial & Psychological Harm to Family. Safeguards Fail to Prevent Ultra Vires Deductions by Breaching Statutory Protected Earnings Leaving Parents Without Sufficient Means of Provision. Enforcement Is Applied Without Independent Judicial Oversight. Calculations Disregard Ability to Pay & Exceed Lawful Authority Which Undermines Dignity & Stability. A Just Government Must Never Destroy Its Citizens Livelihoods to Claim Support. Reform Is Vital.
rejection_details:
We are not clear what action you are seeking from the UK Government or Parliament.

You can submit a new petition setting out more clearly what action you would like to see.

action: Require community-based recruitment in public services using national statistics
background: We want the Government to introduce a national framework for community-based recruitment across public services, including schools, NHS, councils, and other public-sector bodies, based on official national and local statistics.
additional_details:
Using nationally recognised data—such as census, labour market, and demographic statistics—would ensure community-based recruitment is fair, transparent, and evidence-led.
Aligning recruitment with local population data can improve representation, public trust, safeguarding in schools, service effectiveness, and workforce stability, while creating local employment opportunities without undermining merit-based selection.
rejection_details: We cannot understand from the text of the petition exactly what it is that you want the Government to do.

action: Cap baby formula price
background: I would like the government to legislate for a price cap on baby formula. Many people have been affected by rising prices across various areas such as tax fuel and energy bills, and this cap could help support lower and middle-class families.

action: Mandatory whole life order for murder
background: If a person has taken a life and there is concrete evidence to support this then they should be given a whole life order. It should be life for a life. Imprisonment until they die. Regardless of if a person pleads guilty or if there are mental health issues.
additional_details: I've watched a fair few crime documentaries based on fact. And the judicial system makes absolutely no sense to me. In some cases, pleading guilty to murder may result in less punishment. The same can happen for those with mental health issues or a history of abuse. I believe they're all dangerous and shouldn't be allowed back into society to potentially reoffend. If due to mental health there should be a facility provided for them rather then jail if needed. Same for those with a traumatic history.

action: Extend the Driving Theory Test Expiry date
background: We believe learner drivers are being penalised having to retake their driving theory test due to long waiting times for practical Driving Tests. The Government needs to extend the 2-year rule, or consider abolishing the expiry altogether.
additional_details: Learner drivers are being told that the 2 year rule keeps their knowledge current but we have seen no evidence that doing this test every two years keeps anything current. Extend or Abolish the 2 Year Rule now to give learner drivers hope.

action: Treat non-fatal strangulation as equivalent offence to attempted murder
background: Amend section 75A of the Serious Crime Act 2015 so that non-fatal strangulation is treated as seriously as attempted murder, reflecting the intent and potential lethality of the act and ensuring perpetrators face appropriate sentencing of up to life in prison.
additional_details: Non-fatal strangulation is one of the strongest predictors of homicide and can cause life-altering injuries days or weeks later. We believe survivors are often left without justice as the severity and intent of the act is minimised. Treating this offence as equivalent in seriousness to attempted murder would better reflect the reality of the violence, improve victim protection, and act as a stronger deterrent.

action: Allow part-time teachers to have set working patterns
background: Change the part-time contracts/flexible working requests for teachers to allow for set day working requests. For example, 3 days as opposed to the current 0.6 offering.
additional_details: Part-time contracts in teaching disproportionately affect women, specifically working mothers returning from maternity leave. Current part-time requests are for a reduction in hours as opposed to days. This means that teaching staff are being expected to work reduced hours but stretched over the full week, incurring extra costs for childcare and time travelling, without the pay. Allowing teachers to put in flexible working requests for a specific amount of days would improve retention.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

Decisions about flexible working arrangements are a matter for individual schools, not the UK Government or Parliament. Teachers are already entitled to request flexible working arrangements or different working patterns, and it is the responsibility of individual schools to consider these requests and decide whether to allow them or not.

action: Impose criminal penalties on companies advertising Ghost Jobs
background: The government should impose criminal penalties on companies advertising ghost jobs. I have applied for roles that were never real, wasting time, effort, and money. This is deeply unfair when so many of us genuinely want jobs. Graduates are tired of applying and we are getting nowhere.
additional_details: The rise of ghost jobs means many adverts don’t lead to real hires, with estimates showing around 30% of UK postings may be ghost listings and not filled, wasting jobseekers’ time and energy. Scams tied to fake job ads have surged, with advanced-fee job scams up 237%, costing victims on average £1,420. We need penalties to protect people seeking genuine work and stop exploitation.

action: Stop the Syrian invasion of Rojava and the massacres committed by them.
background: Ban of arm sales to the Syrian transitional government and imposing sanctions towards them until the Unjust invasion of the Rojava area is stopped.
additional_details: The Kurds  (SDF)  helped the international coalition in defeating isis and captured most of the territory from them and successfully captured Raqqa their capital from them effectively ending the Islamic State, the group is a major NATO and coalition  partner.  SDF have demonstrated to the world their democratic and fair values in the creation in the North Eastern Autonomous Region  of Syria where they have created a fair and free society between the many minorities there
rejection_details:
The following petitions call for similar actions: 

Condemn attacks on Kurds in North Syria & use diplomatic pressure to bring peace
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756339

Put diplomatic pressure on Syria & Turkey to protect Kurds & other minorities
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757124

UK must act now & condemn the killing of Kurdish civilians in Rojava & Rojhilat 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756419

action: Schools to allow absence exceptions for students with mental health struggles
background: We call on the Government to mandate that schools must make exceptions to absence policies for children who struggle to attend school because of mental health issues, including due to recovering from trauma or due to SEND. In our view, schools must replace punishment with support.
additional_details: We think we must stop penalizing parents and children for school refusal caused by mental health, trauma, SEND or abuse. The Government must fund timely mental health support, alternative education, and school-based support; ensure courts consider abuse, trauma, and disability before fines or imprisonment; and train schools and local authorities in trauma-informed approaches.

action: vote of confidence, given that Labour have gone against their pledges.
background: Vote of confidence
additional_details:
Voters place their trust in political parties based on the commitments made during an election campaign. When a government departs from those commitments after taking office, it risks undermining democratic accountability and public trust.

Many people believe that current Labour policies are having a damaging impact on the UK economy. Working people are finding it increasingly difficult to stay afloat, as rising taxes and living costs affect households across the country. If these issues are not addressed, there is growing concern that vital parts of the UK economy — including working industries, high streets, and the hospitality sector — will continue to decline.
rejection_details:
We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for a vote of no confidence in the Government. This is set out in the Committee's standards: https://petition.parliament.uk/help

If you're concerned about a particular policy or decision that's the responsibility of Government or the House of Commons, you could start a petition about that.

You might like to sign this petition:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

action: Introduce justice and protection to prevent conflicts of interest
background: We ask the Honourable Parliament to strengthen safeguards and transparency to prevent conflicts of interest in public institutions, including clear disclosure requirements for private memberships, and to ensure victims of crime receive fair treatment and protection without institutional bias.
additional_details: British democracy is widely respected, yet recent injustices raise serious public concern. Lack of transparency and disclosure within councils, the NHS, policing, and public institutions undermines trust and leaves victims unprotected. Strong rules on disclosure, accountability, and victim protection are essential to prevent bias and ensure equal treatment.
rejection_details:
We are not clear what specific action you are seeking from the UK Government or Parliament.

You can submit a new petition setting out more clearly what action you would like to see and who it would apply to.

action: Review Handling of Abuse Reports Where Women Are Subject to Counter Allegations
background: We call on the Government to review the procedures followed by police forces in England and Wales when responding to reports of abuse against women and girls, particularly where counter-allegations are made by the alleged perpetrator.
additional_details: In our view, women and girls reporting domestic abuse or sexual violence often face inadequate police responses, especially when perpetrators make counter allegations. We do not think that these tactics, recognised in coercive control guidance, are not applied consistently, leading to victims being wrongly treated as suspects. This can result in delays, poor investigations, and loss of trust. Victims must be able to report abuse without fear; better police responses are essential for safety and justice.

action: Reform Home Office enforcement powers to prevent abuse.
background: We call Parliament to reform Home Office immigration enforcement powers by requiring body-worn cameras, strict procedural safeguards, access to legal advice, interpreter support, and clear legal limits on powers of entry, detention and questioning, to prevent abuse, coercion and unfair enforcement.
additional_details: Home Office enforcement officers exercise serious powers of entry,detention and questioning, yet unlike police officers they are not required to wear body cameras or follow legal safeguards. This lack of transparency allows abuse, coercion and unfair practices to go unchecked. Individuals and businesses face penalties on flawed investigations. Parliament must act to introduce body cameras to all officers, legal warnings, access to legal advice, interpreter,and clear limits on enforcement powers.
rejection_details:
Body-worn cameras are being rolled out (announcement of December 2024) to 1,200 enforcement officers:

https://www.gov.uk/government/news/huge-increase-in-migration-returns-and-illegal-working-arrests

Immigration enforcement officers also appear already to follow strict procedural/legal safeguards: 

https://www.bing.com/search?q=%20%20home%20office%20immigration%20enforcement%20officers%20legal%20safeguards&qs=n&form=QBRE&sp=-1&lq=0&pq=%20%20home%20office%20immigration%20enforcement%20officers%20legal%20safeguards&sc=0-63&sk=&cvid=5B70C7481EE444DDB0966E820EA2F693

In this context it is not clear what you are asking for that is not already being done.

action: Stop the move to mandatory weekly food waste collection
background: I want the Government to reverse its decision to mandate weekly food waste bin collections.
additional_details:
The cost to the taxpayer of this weekly collection will be significant. No one asked whether we wanted this. It’s been imposed. I know nobody who thinks this is needed.
We believe the money to do this could be better spent on helping our vulnerable veterans on the streets and providing better social care for the elderly and learning disabled.

action: Reduce VAT on hospitality to 10%: protect jobs, communities & UK competitiveness
background: Reduce VAT on hospitality to 10% to prevent closures & protect tax revenue. When venues close, HMRC loses 100% of its VAT, business rates, PAYE & corporation tax, reducing employment & supply chains. We believe a lower VAT rate would keep viable businesses trading, securing jobs & ongoing revenue.
additional_details:
Hospitality businesses operate on very tight margins and struggle to absorb 20% VAT alongside rising food, energy, wage and rent costs. We believe a permanent reduction to 10% VAT would save jobs, keep venues open, support apprenticeships and skills, and strengthen high streets – it would help businesses survive and continue contributing billions to the UK economy.
 
This would protect local jobs, keep pubs and restaurants open, and help high streets, tourism and communities survive.

action: Make constitutional changes for party-switching MPs and Local Councilors
background: Instigate a constitutional change to the parliamentary and local government systems, that mandates any standing Member of Parliament or local councilor who changes their political allegiance from one registered party to another to stand down and trigger a by-election or re-election.
additional_details:
The current political system is unfair, unethical, and outdated. This betrays the trust voters place in their representatives to reflect their views honestly. Voters lose their democratic right to elect someone who represents their views under the current system.

Enforcing such a measure, will promote transparency and accountability in our political system. Voters can reaffirm their choice based on the current political stance of their representatives.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Mandate by-elections for Councillors who change parties post-election
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749622

By-elections to be called automatically when MPs defect to another party
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/737660

action: Require public access defibrillators on all new housing developments
background: Make it compulsory for all housing developers to install a community public access defibrillator on all new housing estates for planning permission to be approved. Costs should be covered by estate management fees.
additional_details: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is one of the leading causes of death in the UK, often occurring at home or in residential areas. Survival falls by around 10% for every minute without defibrillation. We therefore call for community defibrillators to be mandatory in all new housing developments. Installed at build stage, they are low cost, reduce health inequalities, strengthen communities, and save lives.

action: For latinos to be included in ethnicity option when filling a form.
background: Latinos in the UK share distinct cultural and historical roots, yet are excluded from ethnicity options on official forms. Recognizing Latinos as an ethnic group ensures visibility, accurate data, and fair access to services and representation.
additional_details: The Government should formally recognise Latinos as an ethnic category on all UK official forms, including the Census, NHS records, school forms, and equality monitoring. This change would ensure accurate data collection, proper representation, and fair access to public services for the Latin American community.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/738829

action: Government to review local authority fees for grassroot football
background: We believe grassroots football is a vital pillar of British life. It is fun, builds essential physical fitness, and acts as a lifeline for the nation’s mental health, preventing thousands of cases of depression annually.
additional_details:
We want a reasonable pitch fee to be the standard across the county that is affordable to everyone.
 
However, we feel that extortionate pitch hire fees from local councils are pricing us out. In some regions, costs have jumped 130%, making the "people’s game" a luxury. We urge the Government to review and consider regulating these costs to protect these community hubs before more clubs are forced to fold.

action: Change your definition of carers allowance to “carers supplement”.
background:
I want carers allowance to be put in a different bracket from a “base benefit”.
I believe it keeps carers in poverty because currently you cannot get two base benefits at once. State pension & bereavement allowance are also base benefits.Right now, carers allowance is removed if you claim either.
additional_details:
I am coming up to pensionable age. I learnt, when I apply for my pension, my carers allowance will be removed! I will still be looking after my son for the 133 hrs I currently do, so why/how can it be right to remove this.
When my husband died, my carers allowance was removed because I claimed bereavement allowance for the following year even though I was still looking after my son. How is this fair/right?
Please recognise the work we carers do and the money we save the government. Value us!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition which calls for the same action:

Exempt Carer’s Allowance in benefit calculations 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/755554

action: Implement a national education framework to help students affected by cancer
background: I want Government support to address a serious, overlooked gap in our education system: the lack of a consistent national policy to protect the educational outcomes of 14-24 year olds diagnosed with cancer. Cancer is treated as an individual problem while COVID was treated as a collective emergency.
additional_details: Currently there is no right to alternative assessment, no national framework for education continuity during cancer treatment, and no automatic protection of future progression in the education system. Fighting cancer should not forfeit an education. Implement a national policy allowing teacher-assessed/predicted grades for students undergoing cancer treatment; this will safeguard education & health simultaneously.

action: Reset the Windrush Compensation Scheme with free legal assistance for victims
background:
We call on the Government to:
1. Move the Windrush Compensation Scheme out of the Home Office to a fully independent body.
2. Provide guaranteed, non-means-tested legal assistance for all claimants.
3. Expand the scheme to include all losses, like military pensions.
additional_details:
The Windrush scandal remains a profound state failure. Yet, victims are denied the same justice as Post Office and Infected Blood scandal victims.
 
Their compensation scheme is run by the Home Office – the department that caused the scandal. It is slow, complex, and denies victims legal assistance, resulting in low offers and delayed justice.
 
It is time to end this two-tier system of justice. The Windrush generation built Britain; they deserve the same dignity and esteem.

action: Stop East Herts Council imposing high car parking charges
background: Reverse the decision that is extortionate charges for the small high street that will greatly negatively affect small local business, workers and residents
additional_details: East Herts council never consider residents objections in their biased and unfair decisions, with revenue being their only reason
rejection_details: Not central Government's or Parliament's responsibility.

action:
Ban deepfakes and image making AI in the UK
ex: character AI, Grok AI etc...
background: We would like for the government to ban the use of generative AI in the UK, due to the amount of people being cyber harassed and violated due to these AI bots. Bots are also capable to make inappropriate images of people, and post it online. Young people are mainly impacted due to this problem.
additional_details: We believe the government should do more about this by banning the use of generative AI due to the environmental impact, (eg, water wastage, electricity, pollution) and the impact this has on the people being used against, with these bots. (such as celebrities, innocent people, and those being exploited). The evidence we have, is that water is being used in millions of gallons every year to cool these machines, and this water CANNOT be recycled. We would like this issue to be addressed.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban Open-Source Deepfake-Capable AI tools until further regulation is introduced
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744724

action: Use of lie detector tests in rape cases
background: In rape cases, it should be made a right for the accused to be offered a lie detector test. If the accused’s test comes back as truthful, the accuser should be asked to take a lie detector test; they can refuse.
additional_details:
If the case goes court, the facts of the truthful test and the accuser's refusal can be used in court.

We believe offering this legal right will help set the investigating officers on the right path to the truth, upholding the law to protect the innocent, by not needing the accuser to take the test. This will help protect the victim. A test early will decrease the length of time needed to investigate the truth, saving time, money and resources. Not blocking evidence in court will be fairer, and maintain our human rights to a fair investigation and trial.

action: Fund education on gender-based violence and misogyny in schools
background: We call on the Government to fund mandatory education on misogyny, gender-based violence, and respectful relationships in schools, from primary through to secondary education.
additional_details: I am asking Parliament to make education on misogyny and gender-based violence mandatory in all schools from primary to secondary level. Prevention must start early. Without education, harmful stereotypes and abusive behaviour can go unchallenged and become normalised. I believe teaching children about respect, equality, and consent will help reduce violence, protect young people, and build a society where everyone can live free from fear.

action: All military veterans to be exempted from tax on their military pensions
background: Studies show that some people leave the forces without access to adequate benefits, placing immense pressure on families and, in some cases, leading to homelessness or suicide.
additional_details:
This policy proposes a holistic approach: tax exemption on military pensions, so veterans receive the dignity & care they deserve.

Veterans have dedicated the best years of their lives to serving and protecting the nation, with many making the ultimate sacrifice. It is the Government’s moral obligation to ensure that those who have served are afforded dignity, security, and a better quality of life in their later years. This policy proposes that all military pensions be exempt from taxation, recognising the unique contribution and sacrifices made by veteran. We believe this would also help with retention and recruitment.

action: Review sentences for sexual violence
background: We would like the UK Government to review the sentences for people who are involved in sexual violence related crimes, to better protect women.
additional_details: We would like the government to increase the sentence for people who commit sexual violence crimes as we do not believe they are long enough. This, in our view, can lead to women not report such crimes, as the sentences aren’t long enough.

action: Legislate to stop headlight flashing by cars with ultra bright LED headlights
background: Ultra bright LED headlights may be of benefit to drivers of these cars to the detriment of other road users, particularly at night time. Showing another driver a courtesy should not result in being stabbed in the eyes by LED headlights on full beam, thus instantly spoiling one’s night time vision.
additional_details: In the interests of road safety and driver comfort we believe this LED headlight flashing menace should be actively discouraged. As a happily retired former ADI (approved driving instructor) I previously encouraged students to momentarily dip down (i.e. switch from dipped headlights to sidelights for a moment). This signal to other road users is perfectly clear and no discomfort is caused by this "come on" or "thank you" signal.

action: Introduce legally protected menstrual leave for women with debilitating periods.
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legally protected menstrual leave for women with debilitating symptoms, ensuring they do not have to work through severe pain and that their health is recognized in employment law.
additional_details:
Menstruation is not a minor inconvenience. Many women experience severe pain, fatigue, nausea, and other symptoms that significantly impair daily functioning. Yet women are expected to work through these symptoms without recognition or protection.
Current employment law does not acknowledge menstrual health, leaving women to choose between their health and their job. Legally protected menstrual leave would ensure women can manage their health safely while maintaining their dignity and productivity.
Periods are not optional, and neither should workplace protections be — women’s health matters, and it’s time the law reflected that.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require employers have monthly menstrual 1-3 day leave policy
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740839

action: Build a stronger teacher union: fair pay, manageable workload, real support!
background: We call on Parliament to strengthen teacher unions, fund fair pay rises, reduce excessive workloads, and recognise unpaid marking and planning hours. Teachers’ free time is consumed by work with no compensation. Either raise pay or trial a four-day week.
additional_details: Teachers are overworked and underpaid with excessive workloads extending far beyond school hours. Marking, planning, and admin regularly consume evenings and weekends with no extra pay. Teacher unions must become stronger and refocus on protecting teachers pay, time and wellbeing. Parliament must fund fair pay rises, reduce unnecessary workload demands and recognise unpaid labour. If workloads cannot be reduced, teachers deserve higher pay or a four-day working week to protect work life balance.
rejection_details:
We can only accept petitions about things the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for. Unions are private organisations, and decisions about what they should focus on are not things that the Government or Parliament are directly responsible for.

You may wish to start a new petition specifically about pay or working patterns of teachers

action: Subtitles in Cinema: An Essential Accessibility Feature
background: We call on the Government and Parliament to make subtitles mandatory for all movies shown in cinemas. Subtitles are essential for Deaf and hard-of-hearing people, non-native language speakers, and many others. Access to cinema should be inclusive and equal for everyone.
additional_details: We ask the government and parliament to act because only they can guarantee equal access to cinema for everyone. Subtitles are essential for Deaf and hard-of-hearing people and others who rely on them, yet availability is inconsistent and depends on individual cinemas. We believe accessibility is a human rights issue, not a choice. Government action can set national standards, ensure fairness, and prevent exclusion from cultural life.

action: Make the destruction or scrapping of UK military medals a criminal offence
background: Make it a criminal offence to destroy or scrap officially issued UK military medals. Rising silver prices and a lucrative collectors' market mean medals are being melted down for profit, engraved names erased and service details and irreplaceable records of those who served destroyed forever.
additional_details: Scrapping or damaging medals erases personal and national history. These honours deserve legal protection to stop their permanent loss for furure generations.

action: Automatic 50/50 Parental Custody Rights for Responsible Divorced Parents
background: We, the undersigned, call on the government to ensure that, in cases of divorce, both parents who are responsible, loving, and capable, with no history of abuse, neglect, substance misuse, or other harmful behaviors, are automatically granted equal parenting time with their children.
additional_details:
Making equal custody the default encourages fairness, reduces parental conflict, and ensures children have strong connections with both mothers and fathers.

We urge the government to update family law to reflect these principles, establishing equality, fairness, and the best interests of children as the foundation of custody decisions.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Automatic 50/50 custody for separated parents without a criminal conviction
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746439

action: Reform the Blue Badge parking system: more side hatching bays
background: People with mobility difficulties need parking that allows safe and dignified access. Some people need bays close to entrances to minimise walking distance. As a wheelchair user, I do not need to be close to the front, but I do rely on side hatching markings to safely get in & out of the car.
additional_details: Without such spaces, I can’t transfer into my Wheelchair.  I feel the current Blue Badge system does not reflect these different needs. There should be a mix of parking provision, with standard bays near entrances for those with limited mobility & wider bays with side hatchings in suitable locations: the back or sides of car parks, for those who rely on wheelchair/pram access/adaptations. We shouldn't be excluded due to poor parking design. It needs to be more inclusive and better reflect real life mobility needs.

action: Instruct MP’s to behave like adults in Parliament and actually answer questions.
background: Parliament has become an embarrassment - name calling and insults instead of properly debating matters. People in power acting like children and refusing to answer actual questions. I would like MP’s to be made to grow up and actually act like adults (especially in PM’s question time)
additional_details: These people are meant to be running our country. The Speaker needs to take control of the MP’s and the house needs to take some pride in what they do. No more jeering and abuse. Answer the questions and no more insulting each other. It is, quite frankly, immature, embarrassing to the people of the country, and pathetic.
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament as a whole aren't responsible for the issue you raise. Order in the Commons is the responsibility of the Speaker personally.

action: Review medical testing standards & process: use optimal ranges & cellular tests
background: Review whether symptomatic patients should be assessed using optimal ranges and cellular tests instead of standard reference ranges and serum tests. We are concerned that current tests might fail to reflect cellular or neurological dysfunction.
additional_details: We are concerned that standard reference ranges and serum tests often fail to detect cellular or neurological dysfunction. Many symptomatic patients may be dismissed as “normal” despite significant impairment. This can lead to delayed diagnosis, preventable harm, disability, and rising healthcare costs. We believe symptom-led care using optimal ranges and cellular testing reflects modern science and protects patient safety.

action: Mandate education on female hormone brain health and ADHD in medical training.
background: We want the Government to require UK medical schools and postgraduate training programmes to mandate training on the effects of female hormones on brain function across the lifespan including how hormonal changes can affect ADHD and other neurodivergent women and how this may present in females.
additional_details: Female sex hormones affect every woman’s brain across the lifespan, influencing cognition, mood, attention, stress regulation and emotional processing; not just reproduction. Yet medical education focuses largely on fertility and pregnancy, with limited teaching on hormone-related brain effects. This gap leads to missed recognition, misdiagnosis and delayed care, particularly during perimenopause and in women with ADHD (often un recognised) whose symptoms often worsen with hormonal change.
rejection_details: Medical education is the the responsibility of the General Medical Council and other professional bodies. We can therefore not allow your petition as it is not the responsibility of the UK Government or Parliament.

action: Harsher sentencing and mandatory prison for all child sexual abuse
background: Introduce mandatory custodial sentences for all child sexual abuse offences, including child abuse image offences, and end the use of suspended sentences. Ensure harsher punishments for all pedophile cases, prioritising child protection and victim justice over offender mitigation.
additional_details: People convicted of child sexual abuse, including making, possessing, or distributing indecent images of children, are given suspended or minimal sentences. These crimes are not victimless—every image and offence represents a child being abused. Lenient sentencing fails victims, prioritises offenders over children, and undermines public confidence. Children deserve real protection, and offenders should face harsher punishments in all pedophile cases, reflecting the severity of their crimes.

action: Review GP training and diagnostic guidance for gut-related conditions
background: Require a review of GP training, ongoing certification, and diagnostic guidance to ensure modern, evidence-based assessment of gut, microbiome, and related systemic conditions, including appropriate referral and testing pathways within primary care.
additional_details: Peer-reviewed research increasingly links gut microbiome imbalance, bile dysfunction, histamine intolerance, and hormonal stress markers to chronic symptoms. However, GP diagnostics often rely on limited testing. Updating training and guidance to reflect current evidence would improve early detection, reduce chronic illness burden, and lower long-term NHS costs.

action: Remove Interest from UK Student Loans
background: We call on Parliament to remove interest on UK student loans. In 2024–25, £15.2bn in interest was added while only £5bn was repaid — roughly 3x as much. Graduates enter repayment with average debts of around £53,000, and around 75% are expected to never repay in full.
additional_details:
• Lower and middle earners often pay mainly interest, while high earners clear loans more quickly. In 2024–25, 67% of those repaying student loans added more interest than they paid, and 2.2m people now owe £50k+.
• Repayments add 9% on top of tax and NI, pushing marginal rates towards 60%. The Times reports graduates typically need to earn ~£66k before reducing the balance.
• Unlike other debts, student loans cannot be cleared through bankruptcy and are repaid via the tax system for 30+ years.

action: Amend the Terrorism Act 2000 to allow proscription of state-backed entities
background: We want the Government to amend or introduce legislation that enables the proscription of hostile state-embedded organisations as terrorist entities. The current law should be updated to address groups that operate with the practical definition of a terrorist or hostile entity.
additional_details: The current framework under the Terrorism Act 2000 was designed for non-state actors. This creates a legal barrier to designating entities formally embedded within a foreign state, such as the IRGC, even when they engage in regional proxy activity or threats against dissidents in the UK. Relying on sanctions alone limits accountability. Closing this legislative gap is essential for national security and to ensure the UK can act decisively against all forms of terrorism.

action: Review existing safeguards for UK national crew working on cruise ships
background: Review safeguarding and reporting requirements which should protect UK crew members working on cruise ships, ensuring serious incidents reported by crew are independently recorded, investigated, and referred to appropriate authorities.
additional_details: We are concerned that serious safeguarding incidents through internal channels are not always formally recorded or escalated, leaving people without protection or recourse and allowing the failure to go unaddressed. We feel a review is needed to ensure independent safeguarding and reporting requirements to protect UK crew members working in the cruise industry.

action: Provide funding for body armour for frontline operational ambulance staff

additional_details: Operational staff members have had knives pulled on them when attending addresses deemed safe. They have no protection or adequate personal defence training. They feel genuine fear for their lives, and they can have young families at home. These types of incidents are on the increase.

action: Mandate teaching about discrimination of women in Afghanistan in curriculum
background: I want the Government to make it compulsory for schools to teach the issues Afghan women are facing and the pressure the Afghan government is enforcing on them.
additional_details: We believe it is important that young pupils are taught about the issues faced by Afghan women as they are the new future and can spread awareness even further; possibly growing a large interest in the topic. Awareness means that change can be made and that is exactly what Afghan women need. Awareness needs to be made for Afghan women who are unable to leave the house without a man, bans on education and full-body burqas.

action: Exempt all female hygiene products from tax
background: We think it's unfair that there can be a price difference between male and female hygiene products. Females often have to pay more for hygiene products because they are targeted towards women with pink and purple packaging. We therefore call on the Government to exempt such products from tax.
additional_details: Gender-based pricing, also known as “pink tax,” is an upcharge on products traditionally intended for women which have only cosmetic differences from comparable products traditionally intended for men.

action: Fund a trial for children and young people denied NHS access to medical cannabis
background: We call on the Government to support children and young people on private prescriptions for drug-resistant epilepsy, still unable to access medical cannabis on the NHS, despite it being legally available in the UK since 2018, by establishing a funded observational trial.
additional_details: Hannah Deacon’s campaign was critical to legalising medical cannabis in 2018. But children and young people with drug-resistant epilepsy are still denied NHS access. Forced to pay privately, families fundraise whilst caring for their sick children. Sophisticated trials are planned but take years and are unsuitable for those already on medication. We urge the Government to fund a simple Observational Trial for this cohort.

action: Secure the Future of Teignmouth Pier for the Community
background: We ask the Government and Parliament to raise the discussion of public ownership of Teignmouth Pier to secure its long-term protection, accessibility, and future for the community. Teignmouth Pier is a historically significant structure and an important part of Devon’s coastal heritage.
additional_details: Continued private ownership places it at risk from neglect, commercial pressures, and closure. Public ownership would allow the pier to be managed transparently in the public interest, prioritising heritage conservation, public access, and community benefit. We call on the Government to explore legal and financial mechanisms, including support for acquisition by a local authority or community trust, to safeguard this irreplaceable asset for future generations.

background: We want the Government to cancel the planned freeze of Plan 2 repayment thresholds and instead increase the threshold from April 2026 in line with average earnings. additional_details: Blackpool’s heritage trams and their engineering base are a nationally significant example of living transport heritage. The Rigby Road site is a rare surviving working tram depot and the specialist workshops, equipment and skills are essential to keep historic trams safe, operational and accessible to the public. If the tram shed and engineering works are demolished or lost, the damage would be irreversible and could end the long-term future of this unique heritage attraction, along with its educational, volunteering and tourism benefits. We want Government-backed protection and a funded plan to safeguard the depot and workshops for future generations.

At present, men must actively request a PSA test or wait until symptoms appear. 

Routine screening would:

Detect prostate cancer earlier
Improve survival rates
Reduce the need for intensive late-stage treatment

Early detection saves lives, and would save the NHS money.

action: Ban use of filibustering against Private Members' Bills relating to Human Rights
background:
Government need to evolve parliamentary procedure to stop filibustering tactics to block compassionate legislation. 
• Human rights bills—such as dignity in dying—face failure.
A freedom of belief shouldn't be used as a tool to block the choices & rights of others or stall official proceedings.
additional_details:
• Existing Rules allow for "filibustering"—where MPs talk for extended periods to prevent a vote. While the Speaker can stop it (Standing Order 42), this is rarely used.
• Previous Efforts: A 2019 petition to "Stop Filibustering in Parliament" noted that bills regarding sexual harassment (upskirting) were delayed by these tactics. 
• The UK government has stated that while religious freedom is fundamental, it does not override the state’s obligation to protect the rights and freedoms of others.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or the House of Commons to take a specific action. 
 
The House of Commons and House of Lords have their own separate rules of procedure. We can only accept petitions relating to issues that the Government or House of Commons are responsible for. We, therefore, cannot accept petitions relating to procedure in the House of Lords.  

There are existing procedures in the Commons that can prevent “filibustering”. These include SO No. 42, but also, for example, the ability to bring a debate to an end via a closure motion, the ability of the Speaker to select which amendments are debated and voted on, the ability of the Chair to impose a time limit on speeches, and the ability of the House to agree a programme or allocation of time order to apply to a Bill which can limit the time that can be spent debating a Bill before any decisions are made. We are not clear how you would like these rules to be amended or supplemented.  
 
You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do.

action: Ban anyone convicted of terrorism offences from standing for public office
background: Introduce a new legal disqualification so people convicted of terrorism offences (in the UK or abroad) cannot stand as candidates or hold elected office, including local councils.
additional_details: This is needed because current local election disqualification rules focus mainly on recent imprisonment thresholds (for example, being sentenced to 3 months or more within the last 5 years) and therefore may not prevent individuals with serious historic convictions from standing today. The Electoral Commission notes that the returning officer cannot confirm whether a candidate is disqualified and candidates self-declare their eligibility when submitting nomination papers.

action: Introduce new regulations for driving instructors and cap the price of lessons
background: Additional regulations to ensure that learners are able to afford driving lessons. With new restrictions coming in each year and new proposed rules it is the hardest it's ever been to be on the roads, this can isolate young people entering the workforce as public transport costs increase.
additional_details: Lay out new guidelines, allow a new and improved system to help learners report inappropriate behaviour from instructors, such as charging extra when a driving lesson accidentally runs over or randomly hiking prices without making this clear to learners. Additionally, capping prices so they may not charge more than a reasonable price (adjusted when necessary) e.g £50, with intensive courses having additional allowance before a cap.

action: Phones allowed in schools
background: Allow students to bring their phones to school.
additional_details: I think we should have our phones because there are many educational apps and students can access their timetable and homework on their phones. I don’t think that this law is very fair at all.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Pass a law that schools cannot prohibit the use of personal devices
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/735449

action: Make the roads car worthy,as cars have to be road worthy.Pot holes are dangerous
background: Get all councils to fix the roads, as they are becoming like a 3rd world country roads.
additional_details: Fix the roads, too many cars are getting damaged
rejection_details:

Fix Our Roads: National Plan on Dangerous Potholes Now

action: Save Wellington House Daycentre in Brighton
background: Wellington House ,the last council run daycentre in Brighton that meets the needs of 20 plus service users with behaviour that challenges .The workers have years of experience and training . The service is recognised for its skills base. The effect of closing this service would be devastating.
additional_details: Step in and help to save the service and not allow this council to target our cities most vulnerable people .
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

action: Install fences and barriers on bridges over motorways to help prevent suicide
background: Suicides or attempted suicides can create traffic chaos, which can then create more mental health issues. Install fences to keep people from attempting suicide from  motorway bridges.

action: Scrap interest on student loans
background: I believe that university loans should not have an interest rate applied to them, or should have lower rates. Too many young people are refusing higher education due to its sheer cost and potential for debt. Therefore, I want the government to reduce or scrap interest rates on student finance loans.
additional_details: As a sixth form student, I know myself and my others have had to rethink our higher education over financial cost. For a loan that comes directly out of a pay-check, so many people are never able to pay it off. With tuition now rising every year, university is becoming more and more unaffordable for even well off students. While I understand the economical reasoning behind interest, a loan you take out at 17/18 with little to no choice should not have to damage you financially as an adult.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756832

action: Unblock the North West Rail: Upgrade our Castlefield Corridor for Reliable Rail.
background: We urge the Government and Parliament to upgrade the Castlefield Corridor, removing the single-track bottleneck, increasing capacity, and improving reliability on the Manchester-Liverpool line so commuters and businesses in the North West have faster, safer, and more dependable rail services.
additional_details: The Castlefield Corridor is a major bottleneck on the Manchester‑Liverpool line, causing frequent delays, overcrowding, and unreliable service for commuters and businesses also from Blackpool, Crewe and North Wales. Upgrading it would increase capacity, reduce travel times, support economic growth across the North West, and make rail a dependable alternative to road travel, reducing emissions. The Government/Parliament must act to invest in this critical infrastructure for the region’s future.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

action: Reverse the freeze on the student loan repayment threshold for Plan 2 loans
background: The Government should reverse its decision to freeze the student loan repayment threshold from April 2027 for Plan 2 loans. It should also consider reducing the repayment rate from 9% and increasing the repayment threshold immediately.
additional_details: In the 2025 Autumn Budget, the Government announced that the student loan repayment threshold would be frozen from April 2027. This use of fiscal drag will mean graduates on Plan 2 loans in England who earn above the threshold repay more of their income during a cost of living crisis and on top of the tax threshold freezes. This Labour government should ease the burden of student debt, not increase it.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759293

action: Ban driving insurance companies from charging more because of a drivers age
background: The Government should ban car insurance companies from charging higher premiums based solely on a driver’s age. Insurance prices should be based on individual risk factors such as driving record and claims history, not age-based assumptions.
additional_details: Age-based pricing in car insurance is unfair and discriminatory. Many young and older drivers have clean records and drive safely, yet are charged more purely because of their age. Premiums should reflect individual behaviour and risk, not broad assumptions that penalise responsible drivers and limit access to work, education, and independence.
rejection_details:
We already a have a petition open on this subject which you may wish to sign:

Ban higher car insurance premiums for young drivers
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742967

You may also wish to sign this petition, which is on a related subject:

Require car insurance companies to insure the car, not the driver
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/740323

action: More help and support for SEN children & parents
background: Offer mainstream schools more help and support to understand SEN children. To help each individual child with their individual needs and not penalise them for having different needs or a disability.School should be a safe place where children grown not be failed!
additional_details:
I have just pulled my son out of mainstream school he is nearly 14 he has adhd and is on the autism pathway. He has been failed immensely by his school and has been made to feel he is crazy and worthless! He has been penalised because of his disability! This should NOT be happening ! How are these schools getting away with this?
I don’t just speak on behalf of my son I speak on behalf of every  SEN child and their families. Every child and their families. 

Every child has a right to an education!
rejection_details:
I'm afraid this petition is unclear about exactly what you want the Government to do that it is not already doing (or says it's doing).  

We do have some petitions already open on SEND issues which you may want to look at and possibly sign:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750793 - Provide more funding for children with SEN in schools

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746871 - Provide funding for all schools to have a full time dedicated SENDCo

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746351 - Mandate all teachers in mainstream schools receive SEN & mental health training

action: Ban the use of AI in schools
background: The government needs to stop schools from cutting corners by AI generating lessons and setting homework on AI sites.
additional_details: Schools have been using AI to: make revision sheets that are often inaccurate; generate random posters for revision (my school even used AI to generate a poster for the eco committee); setting homework; and sometimes to plan the whole lesson. This is clearly wrong in many ways as it is harming our education aswell as the planet.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund information campaign for secondary school teachers about generative AI
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756733

action: Abolish the concept of marital duty to have sex
background: Abolish the concept of marital duty to have sex. Bring consequences for sexual coercion and abuse within marriage and enshrine it within UK law.
additional_details: So many women in marriage have sex not because they want to, but out of an obligation and a duty within marriage. This leads to things like sexual coercion, rape and women don’t have a voice. Marriage should not mean sex is expected. Consent is always required. Protect women in marriage. A woman’s body does not belong to her husband and no should always mean no. France has done this, we should too.
rejection_details: There is already no legal requirement or obligation to have sex during marriage.

action: Add more female scientists to the National Curriculum
background: We would like the Department for Education to add more female scientists to the National Curriculum and make it mandatory for every exam board to include them in the specification.
additional_details: The reason we are bringing it to the Government is because we want to make it mandatory for every exam board to include female scientists so that every student, in every school has the chance to learn about women in STEM. We think it's important for young girls to have a role model to look up to and encourage them into careers in Science.

action: Raise the retirement age of MP’s in line with the state pension age.
background:
Improves fairness and equality in society by ensuring those changing legislation affecting millions of pensioners are subject to the same changes. 
Reduces the cost of funding to the government as a pensionable age of 60 years is now unaffordable according to the government.
additional_details:
Reflects modern longevity and working lives. Fairness and consistency as aligning  MP’s pensions  with the state pension avoids a perception that MP’s are treated differently from the public they serve.
Retains experience and expertise.
Improves representation: An age-diverse Parliament better reflects the full spectrum of society.
Encourages merit over age.
Stability in governance.
Supports mentoring and leadership development: 
Signals respect for older workers nationwide:
rejection_details: The normal retirement age for MPs has been the same as the state pension age since 2015 as this library note on the issue shows: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/sn06283/

action: We would like the law to change for cats been killed on the road to be reported
background: We would like to government to consider our petition for all our pet cats across the uk to be recognized been reported when hit by any vehicle on the uk.
additional_details: It is already in place for when dogs are hit by vehicles on the road to legal be reported and so with this petition we would like the same rule in place for our cats as they are domestic pets and family too thank you.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750612

action: Make History compulsory at school until 16 to protect the future
background: We call on the Government to make History a compulsory subject for all students in England until the age of 16, and to examine the merits of  extending this to age 18, so that young people gain strong historical knowledge, critical thinking skills, and a deeper understanding of civic responsibility.
additional_details:
The decisions young people make today will shape Britain for decades. Yet many in England can stop studying History at just 14 — before they’ve developed the skills and critical thinking needed to understand society, politics, and global events.
 
We believe that History helps children recognise misinformation, learn from past mistakes, and navigate a divided world. Making it compulsory until at least 16 would, we believe  help create informed, thoughtful citizens who can protect democracy and build a fairer, stronger society.

action: Review and strengthen enforcement of welfare laws for animals in street begging
background: We want the UK Government to review and strengthen enforcement of animal welfare laws by supporting routine checks and microchip scanning of dogs used for begging, and giving authorities powers to remove animals at risk of fear, distress or exploitation.
additional_details: We want the Government to strengthen enforcement of animal welfare laws by supporting routine welfare checks and compulsory microchip scanning of dogs used in street begging. Clear guidance should allow authorities and the SSPCA to remove animals where there is evidence of fear, distress or exploitation, even if physical injury is not visible

action: Force the government to repair the potholes and unsafe road surfaces in the UK
background: Engage contractors and/or councils to repair and make good all roads.
additional_details: Because it is causing a danger to people driving on roads that should be, at the very least, driveable.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fix Our Roads: National Plan on Dangerous Potholes Now
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739014

action: Apply changes to the driving theory test to help learners with dyspraxia
