background: We would like the Government to change the theory test for learners with dyspraxia by: giving extra time for the hazard perception clips, providing alternative hazard perception formats (e.g. still frames + questions), the ability to pause or replay clips, and reducing penalties for early clicking.
additional_details: We would also like the test to have a dyspraxia-specific adjustment category. I want the Government to do this because I believe it is unfair for people with dyspraxia to struggle when completing the theory test. Also, I believe the current theory test reduces their confidence, may discourage them from wanting to learn to drive, and cause them to be more dependent and reliant on other people or public transport.

action: Ban employers from making changes to employment contracts once signed
background: We call on the Government to introduce new protections to prevent employers changing the employment contracts once the employee has signed their employment contract.
additional_details: In recent times we have seen how many companies reduce benefits such as paid breaks or over-time payments. We think the Government should introduce protections for workers, so that employers are banned from making any changes to employment contracts once they are signed.

action: Legally ringfence Vehicle Excise Duty revenue for transport infrastructure only
background: Vehicle Excise Duty was originally established to fund road maintenance and construction. Since the ending of its hypothecation in 1936, revenue has no longer been exclusively allocated to road-related projects. We believe VED should be ring-fenced solely for road construction and maintenance.
additional_details:
Poorly maintained roads pose a serious risk to public safety. Potholes, degraded surfaces, unclear markings, and failing infrastructure can increase the risk of accidents, vehicle damage, injuries to motorists, cyclists, and pedestrians, and emergency service call-outs, affecting vulnerable road users and the wider public.
 
Ring-fencing VED for road infrastructure could improve transparency, ensure motorists’ contributions directly benefit the road network.

action: Bring the teaching of Key Word Signing in to all nurseries and schools
background: Key Word Signing is very common in special education settings, but we believe it needs to be brought in to all nurseries, primary schools and secondary schools, being taught alongside languages. In our view it has the potential to become a universal language and everyone would benefit.
additional_details: Key Word Signing can greatly support those with learning difficulties and communication needs, and also people whose first language is not English. It can encourage a sense of community, interaction and inclusion. Everybody can benefit from learning it.

action: Review CPS disclosure practices and prosecution processes
background: We call on the Government to commission an independent review into the Crown Prosecution Service’s training processes and competency standards for prosecutors handling disclosure obligations, and the disclosure regime under the CPIA 1996.
additional_details: In our view recent cases suggests there are widespread CPS failures to disclose evidence, causing wrongful convictions and collapsed trials. We believe victims and defendants suffer when prosecutors inadequately understand or ignore disclosure duties. We think current training appear insufficient to prevent repeated mistakes, and that the disclosure regime requires urgent examination to ensure fair trials, protect the innocent, and maintain public confidence in criminal justice.

action: Allow Women to Legally Carry Pepper Spray for Self-Defence
background:
Review current legislation on self-defence weapons
Legalise the carrying of pepper spray for women for personal self-defence.

Introduce sensible regulations, and guidance!

Put women’s safety first by giving them lawful, practical means to protect themselves.
additional_details:
Women across the UK face an unacceptable level of risk in everyday life. Despite repeated assurances, violent crime particularly against women remains a serious and ongoing concern. 

Many women feel unsafe walking alone, travelling at night, or simply going about their daily lives. 

Currently, UK law prohibits women from carrying pepper spray, leaving them legally defenceless while expecting them to rely solely on after-the fact policing and prosecution. 

This needs to change!!!
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Legalise pepper spray in England
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/742673

action: Increase highway funding & ringfence fuel duty & road tax for road maintenance
background: We want the Government to increase capital highway funding for local authorities and ringfence a fixed percentage of revenue from the Fuel Duty Tax and Road Tax to meet the “steady state” maintenance requirement and allow for a permanent structural repair.
additional_details:
We believe the current funding model is failing. Motorist taxes make around £30 billion annually; the 2024 Autumn Budget allocated only around £1.6 billion for local highways. We feel this disparity has left parts of our road network in poor condition.
 
Nottinghamshire County Council has inherited a backlog of around £391 million. To stop roads deteriorating further, we need higher government grants to ensure repairs do not fall short.

action: Abolish the Casey Commission into adult social care
background: We believe the Casey Commission is a barrier to desperately needed social care reform, a delaying mechanism and a waste of taxpayer’s money. We want the Government to abolish the commission and instead focus on resolving the social care crisis, preferably on a cross-party basis.
additional_details: Social care is in crisis. It is estimated that around 2 million people over 65 are not getting the support they need and estimates of around 11% of hospital beds filled with people ready for discharge. We feel the Commission was never needed, as there have been at least 25 other inquiries since 1997, with multiple public consultations. We feel all the options for reform and funding options are already in the public domain. The Government should abolish the Commission and act now.

action: Reinstate the death penalty for Treason
background: Treason strikes at the very heart of a nation’s survival. Those who knowingly betray their country, aid its enemies, or undermine its security and place every citizen at risk.
additional_details: Until 1998, the ultimate seriousness of this crime was recognised in law, but Tony Blair’s Government abolished the death penalty for treason that year. There is a strong argument that such an act — deliberate betrayal of the state — should once again carry the gravest possible consequence, both as justice and as a clear deterrent to foreign and domestic traitors.

action: Amend ERA 1996: replace the ‘reasonable responses’ test with objective fairness
background: Amend Section 98(4) of the ERA 1996 to end the 'Range of Reasonable Responses'. Employers and tribunals should be legally required to judge the objective merits of a worker’s intervention in emergency or crime situations.
additional_details: We believe section 98(4) of the ERA 1996 lets firms too easily sack staff for technical breaches during crises. This prioritises rigid policy over human safety. Employers use 'safety protocols' and 'potential disrepute' as catch-all excuses to sack often heroic employees who intervene in thefts, violent crimes, or life-saving incidents. We believe the Government must mandate independent appeals and shift the legal test from a boss's 'belief' to the objective necessity of a worker's intervention to prevent harm.

action: Replace First Past The Post with a transferable voting system
background: We ask for the replacement of the current voting system with a transferable where the electorate will indicate preferences for up to 3 candidates and candidates are eliminated until one has over 50% of the remaining votes. This could ensure all votes cast are fully counted and be more representative
additional_details: This could stop elections where the winning candidate has only 25% of the votes cast, leaving 75% of the votes spread over the various other candidates. We also believe it could help prevent extreme candidates from gaining elected positions with minimal votes. Under this new system, all candidates MUST gather 50% of the elected votes to be declared a winner.

action: That all water companies should be put back into public ownership.
background: As there is no competition within the domestic water industry the government should bring all water companies back into public ownership.
additional_details: The water companies, some more than others, have failed to maintain infrastructure but in the meantime have paid dividends that bear no relationship to the true profitability of the business's. Competion that was the incentive to privatise doesn't exist and so the state has created water monopolies who have taken advance of the situation to the complete disadvantage of the citizens of the United Kingdom. The cost of this mismanagement is now being borne by the bill payers and no doubt an element
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Nationalise water companies to make water a non profit publicly owned asset
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757426

action: Change rule Britannia to our National anthem
background: This change marks significance as it expresses our National Identity, those who were born and came here alike who represent the british values proudly everyday.
additional_details: The Country needs something to unite us all,as hightening tensions consume the very nature of what it means to be British.This celebrates our nation while also giving us the patriotic  morale we all need.
rejection_details:
The use of the present National Anthem is a matter of tradition rather than having any legal status.

You can find more information about the history and status of the national anthem here:

https://www.royal.uk/national-anthem

action: Give kinship carers equal financial & legal support to foster carers
background: We want the Government to ensure kinship carers are not pushed into poverty for keeping children out of care by ensuring kinship carers are entitled to equal financial and legal support enjoyed by foster carers, including benefits, housing protections and legal aid.
additional_details: Many kinship carers step in during crisis to keep children out of foster care, often following bereavement or family breakdown. Despite saving the state significant costs, we feel many are denied financial and legal support based solely on the court order used. We are concerned that this creates a postcode lottery, may force carers into hardship, and may disadvantage children who deserve stability and equal support.

action: Ban employers & recruiters asking about candidates’ salaries when recruiting
background: Change employment laws so that employers and recruiters are prohibited from asking candidates about their current or previous salary at any stage of the recruitment process.
additional_details: We believe a person’s salary history reflects past circumstances, not their skills or suitability for a role. Allowing employers to ask this question could lock people into lower pay and carry forward past underpayment throughout their careers. This affects workers at all wage levels and may limit fair pay progression. Banning salary-history questions could support fairer recruitment and ensure pay is based on the role and the candidate’s capability.

action: Allow small roof ridge increases for attic conversions in terraced houses
background: Update national planning and permitted development rules to allow small increases to roof ridge height on terraced houses where attic space falls marginally below required headroom, provided there is clear street precedent and no adverse impact on neighbours or the street scene.
additional_details:
Many families living in terraced houses face rising living costs, growing households and limited ability to move home, making it increasingly important to adapt existing properties rather than relocate.

Current planning rules prohibit any increase to the highest part of a roof, even where attic space falls short of required headroom by as little as 20–50mm. This disproportionately affects terraced houses, particularly Victorian terraces.

Homeowners are therefore forced to lower internal ceiling heights to comply, creating cramped and poorly proportioned rooms without providing meaningful benefit to neighbours. Many streets already show variation in rooflines, and modest ridge increases would allow better use of existing housing stock while preserving street character.

action: For Under 13's to be banned from social media
background:
. Make sure all Under 13s only have access to media like YouTube and WhatsApp so they are still able to communicate and watch entertainment.
. All short form content to be banned for Under 13s as it designed to shorten attention spans.
. All Social Media apps required to have facial recognition.
additional_details: Recent debates discussing a potential Parliamentary ban on Under 16's being banned from social media is the wrong age range. As a current 16 year old I belive it would be more beneficial for them to ban all Under 13s from social media and for all apps to have face id to verify that children are not using there guardians birthdays or IDs. I believe no child ages 13 and Under need social media and all they would need is apps like WhatsApp and YouTube inorder to communicate.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Government ban on social media to be for under 13s only" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757849

action: Ban schools from issuing absence fines to both parents if they’re separated
background: We want the Government to change the rules so that school attendance fines are not automatically issued to both parents if they are separated, and only to be issued to the parent who arranged or agreed to the unauthorised absence.
additional_details:
Currently, local authorities may issue penalty notices to each parent with parental responsibility, even where parents are separated and one parent had no knowledge of, involvement in, or ability to prevent the absence.
 
We believe this is unfair and causes unnecessary conflict. We want the system updated so that fines are only issued to the parent responsible for the decision, or so that parents can be exempt if they can show they did not agree and could not reasonably stop it.

action: Ban anyone convicted of serious criminal offences from standing in elections
background: People with serious criminal convictions are allowed to stand for election for councillor after five years and once they leave prison, for MP. This includes terrorism, violence, sexual offences and fraud. We believe public office is a privilege, not a right, and should meet higher moral standards.
additional_details: Many public roles — including police, teachers and security-cleared civil servants — permanently exclude people with serious criminal convictions. We feel elected politicians currently face a lower standard. This petition calls for permanent disqualification from elected office for anyone imprisoned for terrorism, violence, sexual offences, violence against women and girls, or serious fraud, whether in the UK or abroad.

action: Increase funding for investment in 3G football pitches
background: Many grassroots football fixtures have been postponed due to grass pitches being in poor, unplayable condition. Many grassroots clubs do not have enough facilities available to accommodate the games.
additional_details: We believe it is an absolute must that investment is made into this sector and needs to come from the Government. I speak for many when I describe the impact it is having on our children, when we are all looking forward to a game on the weekend and then it is called off following a pitch inspection. Some teams go weeks without playing a single game and it’s upsetting for many kids who mentally rely on this social interaction. Please consider our children and our future.

action: Overhaul the Child Maintenance Service to ensure assessments are sustainable.
background: CMS formulas cause financial crisis by ignoring high living costs and care expenses. This leads to unmanageable debt and 20% fees that compromise a parent's survival. The system must balance child support with a parent’s right to a stable life and financial reality.
additional_details: Current CMS formulas ignore high living costs and care expenses, causing unmanageable debt and financial crisis for many. The system must balance child support with a parent’s ability to survive and afford a stable life.
rejection_details:
There is another petition already open that appears to ask for what you are seeking, which you may wish to sign instead: 

Reform Child Maintenance calculation: include daytime care and actual costs
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746377

action: Make It Law: Donors Have the Right to Know Where Their Charity Money Goes
background:
We give £5, £10, or £50 believing our money is helping someone in need — feeding families, supporting the homeless etc. 

But most donors never actually know where their money goes.

How much reaches the cause?
How much goes to administration?
How much is spent on salaries and marketing?
additional_details:
We are calling on the UK Government and the Charity Commission to introduce a law that requires:

• A clear spending breakdown for all registered charities
• Percentages showing how much goes to the cause vs admin and salaries
• Simple, plain-English reporting that donors can easily understand

Transparency builds trust.
Trust increases donations.
And more money reaches the people who truly need it.

Sign this petition to make charity giving honest, open, and accountable.
rejection_details:
Guidance from the Charity Commission states that charities are required to produce an annual report, a set of accounts and submit an annual return to the Charity Commission.

All charities must keep accounting records, and prepare annual accounts which must be made available to the public on request.

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/charity-reporting-and-accounting-the-essentials-november-2016-cc15d/charity-reporting-and-accounting-the-essentials-november-2016-cc15d--2#section4

action: UK to mandate "zero plastic pellet loss" in line with new EU law ASAP
background: The EU recently formalised its Plastic Pellet Loss Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2025/2365), which mandates risk management plans and independent audits for large handlers. We want the UK to follow suit with its own equivalent law.
additional_details:
The EU recently formalised Regulation (EU) 2025/2365, which mandates risk management plans and independent audits for large handlers of plastic pellets. UK NGOs and the Scottish Government have called for similar binding legislation in the UK.
 
Nurdles (3-5mm plastic pellets) are raw materials for nearly all plastic products. A major source of microplastic pollution, estimated up to 445,000 tonnes spill into the natural environment per year during transport or manufacturing, a large proportion of which ends up in the seas and oceans, causing severe harm to marine life.

action: Ban estate agents from soliciting buyers to bid more on an offer
background: The Government should ban estate agents from soliciting potential buyers to bid more on properties, as we believe this is pushing property prices up and pushing buyers to even spend more than their budget. Everyone should be able to afford a place to live.
additional_details: As a couple who have been actively looking to buy a property, we believe it is unacceptable for estate agents to force you to bid more on an offer that you already put on. Some estate agents claim that there are many offers and you should bid more to get the property, they don’t always disclose how many offers or how much. We feel this is an irresponsible money-making practice that is pushing property prices up to a point where no one can afford a place anymore. People shouldn’t be having to fight to buy a home.

action: Review traffic penalty laws to protect victims of driving licence identity fraud
background: We call on the Government to conduct a review of traffic penalty laws and how take into account the risk of accused drivers being the victims of identity fraud.
additional_details: Someone could steal your name and driving licence number, commit a speeding offence, and give your details to the police. You then receive the penalty notice even though you were not there, did not drive the car, and were not insured on it. In our view, the time which a victim of such crimes has to try to rectify matters with the relevant agencies are too short and deadlines are not paused when such fraud has been reported. We call on the Government to conduct a review to ensure victims are protected and offenders face serious action.

action: Automatically remove parental responsibility for parents convicted of abuse
background: We want to change the law to automatically remove parental responsibility from parents convicted of abuse. We feel children being required to see their abusive parents and allowing them to still make decisions regarding the child's life is abuse in itself and may cause more suffering.
additional_details: We believe many children are failed by the system and may be left with lifelong trauma and PTSD. Foster parents should been given full parental responsibility instead.

action: Investigate and revoke Tier 2 sponsorship to sell sham visa / human trafficking
background: Home Office urgently Audit all Tier 2 sponsors for shell company activity. Revoke licences immediately where no genuine business exists its director charging individuals large sums for visa sponsorship. Refer directors to Police, NCA-FU, HMRC, SFO, OISC, ROCUs, GLAA, HOIE, AF, CH, HMRC-TF, UKVI-SC
additional_details: Licensed Tier 2 sponsors are operating as shell companies with no real customers or suppliers. Directors are charging up to £30k per visa and placing victims on fake payrolls.There is no genuine work or employment relationship.This exploits vulnerable people and undermines the immigration system and human trafficking.Currently no clear, fast route for victims to report this. Dedicated reporting system would allow Immigration Enforcement to act swiftly before more people are harmed and exploited.
rejection_details:
It is already unlawful to operate a sham business to sponsor visas. If you think a company is breaking immigration laws, you can report them here: https://www.gov.uk/report-immigration-crime

You can find out more about the Government's enforcement of immigration laws for companies here: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/record-numbers-of-visa-sponsor-licences-revoked-for-rule-breaking

action: Fund the construction of more special education schools
background: We believe the Government must fund the construction and opening of more special education schools as we feel there are not enough spaces in schools for children with special educational needs.

action: Ban interest on student loans above RPI and reform loans system
background: Cut interest on student loans to a maximum of RPI including retrospective calculations; make first PHD part of first degree debt not a second payment; no interest to be added to the debt all while completing the degree; make loan education mandatory as part of studies.
additional_details: We believe the current generation is systematically being disadvantaged. Education used to be free for UK citizens. Current older graduates had these benefits and no debt to pay off but the system has now been changed to going back to a place where degrees will only be accessible to the rich or poorer people will be saddled with a lifetime of debt. The system needs changing for the youth of our country.

action: end tax payer money being used to subsidise mp's food and alcohol in Westminster
background: No tax payer money should be used to fund any alcoholic drink and food in any Westminster bars they should pay like any person would .
additional_details: Normal working people don't get subsidised food or drink this is clearly a freebie why should we the people have to put up with this any longer we don't live in the middle ages anymore this needs to stop.
rejection_details:
Catering services for the House of Commons are provided by an in-house team who do not provide a subsidised service in the commercial sense of the word. Some venues make a profit, referred to as contribution because it contributes to reducing overall costs. In other venues, the cost of providing the service does exceed the income received in sales due to the irregular hours and unpredictability of parliamentary business. The contribution or cost of each venue is calculated by subtracting the food and operational costs from the catering sales. Rather than a subsidy, the House monitors the contribution or cost of each catering venue, which include cafeterias, dining rooms, restaurants and bars. Prices of food and drink are regularly benchmarked against appropriate external comparators.

You can read more about this here: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/freedom-of-information/information-we-already-publish/house-of-commons-publication-scheme/catering-services/house-of-commons-cost-of-catering/

We can't accept petitions about catering in the House of Lords as that is the responsibility of the House of Lords.

action: Transitional period for international medical graduates working in NHS
background: Provide transitional relief period for international medical graduates for the 2026 medical recruitment cycle. Clearly define significant NHS experience for 2027 recruitment cycle onwards as a minimum of two years of NHS employment to ensure pre-entry procedural fairness & informed decision-making.
additional_details: Changes to UK medical graduate prioritisation were introduced after recruitment processes had already begun. We believe this undermines procedural fairness and effectively applies rules retrospectively. In our view “significant NHS experience” has not been clearly defined, preventing doctors from making informed career decisions. International medical graduates form a substantial proportion of the NHS workforce, and we think uncertainty or exclusion risks workforce disruption and undermines the contribution they make to patient care.

action: Allow financially independent EU retirees to join their family members in the UK
background: Open a visa pathway for financially independent, retired parents of EU citizens to join their family members in the UK. Currently no dedicated route exists for EU settled status holders to bring a parent to the UK, and the retirement visa no longer exists.
additional_details: EU citizens with settled status in the UK, who can either fully financially support their parent or whose parent is fully financially independent, should have the right to bring the parent to live with them in the UK. We believe thousands of families are suffering because of the non-existent possibility to provide company and/or care to a retired parent, who in turn could provide childcare assistance where needed. Retirees who pose no burden to public funds should have a visa entry route.

action: Compulsory minimum wage for class 1 HGV drivers of £18 per hour
background: We call on the Government to set minimum wage of £18 per hour for HGV class 1 drivers, due to the high risks these drivers are exposed to and the risk of fines. We also believe it would improve safety of others on the road.
additional_details: We think a minimum wage of £18 per hour would better reflect the pressure and stress HGV drivers are under.

action: Ban puppy yoga, puppy Pilates and other “puppy cuddle therapy”
background: We call for a ban on puppy yoga, puppy Pilates and other “puppy cuddle therapy” to help in bringing an end to an alarming rise in the number of businesses offering alternative therapy classes which use puppies as part of their sessions.
additional_details: We believe that puppies as young as 8-weeks-old are being exploited for needless gimmicks by businesses. In our view, using puppies when they are at their most impressionable, placed in an unnatural environment where they are continually handled by strangers and are expected to perform hour after hour to entertain paying customers, is done without regard for their safety, their well-being, or recognition of the emotional damage being caused.

action: Only apply capital gains tax to gains above the rate of inflation
background: We call on the Government to reform capital gains tax so that it is payable only on the gain above inflation, as we believe it is unreasonable not to take into account inflation.
additional_details: We believe taxing citizens on the asserted gain in value of an asset caused purely by inflationary effects is completely unreasonable because there is no actual gain. When you are taxed on an asset because it has allegedly risen in value because of the effects of inflation, we feel it unfairly takes away from people as we believe you haven't actually made any gain unless it goes up by more than inflation. We feel it is a totally unreasonable tax in its current form.

action: Introduce regulated conjugal visits in UK prisons
background: I am asking the Government to introduce regulated conjugal visits in UK prisons. These visits would allow eligible prisoners in verified long-term relationships to have limited private visits with their partner under strict rules and security measures.
additional_details: Current prison visitation rules make it difficult for prisoners to maintain healthy intimate relationships, which can negatively affect mental wellbeing, family stability, and rehabilitation. Evidence from other countries shows that supporting stable, committed relationships can reduce reoffending and improve reintegration. Regulated conjugal visits could benefit prisoners, families, and wider society while maintaining prison security.

action: Reduce VAT for hospitality from 20% to 13% permanently
background: Reduce the standard rate of VAT applied to hospitality businesses (including restaurants, cafés, pubs and accommodation) from 20% to 13% on a permanent basis, to reflect the sector’s cost structure and to support business viability following recent fiscal changes.
additional_details: The Autumn Budget increased cost pressures on hospitality through higher employer National Insurance contributions and changes to business rates relief. The removal of the Covid-era 40% rates discount, combined with revaluations, has in our view materially increased fixed costs. A targeted VAT reduction could directly improve cash flow, protect employment, and reduce closures across high streets, including businesses excluded from current pub-only reliefs.

action: Fund free dental care for all under-18s, regardless of NHS dentist availability
background: Guarantee free dental care for all under-18s. Where NHS practices are full, the Government must fund private check-ups and essential treatment. No child should be denied healthcare or left in pain because their parents cannot afford private fees. End the "dental deserts" now.
additional_details: We believe this is an educational emergency. The national "Belonging and Thriving" agenda fails when children are left in agony. Students cannot learn while suffering chronic pain or sleep deprivation. They cannot "belong" when ashamed of their smile or missing school for extractions. For families locked out of the NHS, private fees can be impossible. If the NHS cannot provide a space, the state must fund private care. We must end this two-tier health system.

action: Create a Heathrow residents’ commissioner to protect residents in the area.
background: Following the precedent set by the HS2 residents' commissioner, the residents of Hillingdon wish to have representation to protect their rights during the proposals for a third runway. The commissioner would monitor the proposals with the four tests set out and aim to secure more for all residents.
additional_details:
The residents surrounding Heathrow have been through decades of threats to destroy their homes. HS2 has a commissioner who stands up and protects residents.

https://www.hs2.org.uk/about-us/independent-hs2-commissioner/

We want to have our own independent commissioner to help vet proposals for any Heathrow expansion. We want the government and parliament to look at proposals on this and explore how to serve the residents' voices better. This is on behalf of the Hillingdon Herald.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Remove VAT on all veterinary care services & fund new support for vet services
background: Remove VAT on all veterinary care services. Increase funding for veterinary services, including means-tested support for low-income pet owners struggling with veterinary bills, funding for registered rescues, and subsidised neutering to cut unwanted litters and long-term rescue intake.
additional_details: We would like this new funding to go towards a government-backed pet insurance, per-cat hardship intake financial support, and incentives for vets to aid rescues.

action: Fund £10,000 armed forces funeral grants & pension inheritance rules
background: We believe veterans who serve for decades deserve dignity and pension protections like some other pensions. Many don't receive death payments to help with funeral support and often pensions can’t pass to dependent adult children, leaving families insecure and reliant on charities.
additional_details: We feel this is out of step with some other pensions in the Civil Service, NHS, and private sector. We urge the Government to fund an automatic £10,000 funeral grant for deceased armed forces pensioners and reform rules to expand inheritance rights, so veterans can leave their remaining pensions to their dependent adult children. This could provide dignity in death, reduce charity reliance, improve fairness, and modernise rules and align military schemes with other schemes.

action: Allow UC claimants with start-up-businesses to receive payments for 3 years
background: Change the law to allow people on Universal Credit who start and run a business to continue to receive payments for 3 years. This could give them time to build income and stability before benefits are reduced. This could encourage self-employment, growth, and independence from Universal Credit.
additional_details: Currently, people on Universal Credit risk losing benefits after 12 months, making it difficult for many to move forward. A 3-year grace period could let them build sustainable businesses, increase confidence, and create future jobs. Many may later leave Universal Credit altogether, saving money long-term and giving people real opportunities to succeed.

action: Increase funding for better security in the Prison Service
background: Target increased funding at the Prison Service in order to improve security in and around prisons as well as avoid administrative errors including, but not limited to, accidental prisoner releases which have increased by around 120% in the past few years, as well as relieve overcrowded prisons.

action: Eject US Armed Forces personnel from bases hosted by UK & apply to join BRICS
background: We call on the Government to eject all US Armed Forces personnel from bases in the UK and apply to join the BRIC (Brazil, Russia, India, China) foreign investment strategies grouping. We believe that Britain has been in the economic grip of America for too long.

action: Make it a criminal offence for government officials to lie to the public.
background: Introduce a law which would hold the PM, MP's and partie candidates criminally responsible for lying to the public.
additional_details:
Voters cannot make an informed decision on which candidates to vote for in elections if candidates lie about their promises.

Politicians lying repeatedly to the public in order to secure a seat in Parliament and gain power. We've seen this happen with Brexit, Nigeria Farage and Kier Starmer. If political parties or politicians cannot gain the poplar vote without deceiving the public they are not fit to govern a country and should be penalised for placing the country and its people in danger
rejection_details:
This appears to be asking for the same thing as a petition we already have open, which you may wish to sign instead:

 https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/746833

action: DONT LET AI TAKE OVER OUR JOBS!!
background: Us public want too be able to keep our jobs, and educate ourselves. Without a job there’s no money? WE DONT WANT AI TAKING OVER OUR JOBS!!!
additional_details: Us public need to be able to afford our taxes / rent, food ect and we need to be able to have a structure in our life’s. There’s gonna be a loss of skill if AI takes over. AI is NEVER gonna be as better as us humans.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petitions, which call for similar action:

Review how to protect jobs from being taken by AI technology
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/707509

Make AI job replacement illegal
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/753745

action: Launch a review into airport terminal drop-off charges
background: We want the Government to a launch a review into UK airport drop-off fees which looks into giving the CAA powers to audit and cap all airport drop-off fees. The review should look into ways to abolish profit-making from forecourts, a 10-minute free grace period, and preventing cost manipulation.
additional_details: In Heathrow, fees rose to £7. We are concerned that “cost recovery” claims lack transparency and that the fees are a “stealth tax” on the public, especially the elderly and disabled. The Government should ensure these fees are independently audited and capped to protect the public from monopoly pricing.

action: Uprate Plan 2 repayment threshold and cap student loan interest.
background: Change Plan 2 student loan rules so the repayment threshold rises each year with average earnings, and cap Plan 2 interest at inflation (RPI) for existing and future borrowers. Reverse the 2027–2030 threshold freeze.
additional_details:
Freezing the Plan 2 repayment threshold at £29,385 from April 2027 for three years increases repayments through fiscal drag, especially for low and middle earners.
​
Plan 2 interest can be RPI plus up to 3%, so balances may grow despite repayments.
​
Student loans are presented as a contract; retrospective-style worsening of terms may be legal but feels unfair and undermines trust.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action:

Restore Plan 2 student loan repayment threshold increases from April 2026 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759293

action: Any person Convicted of a crime should not be allow to stand to become a MP.
background:
Ensure the potential and sitting MPs are of the highest moral standing whilst in public office. Any person who has been convicted of a crime should be bared from becoming an MP or if in office should be removed as a MP with loss of benefits of having been a MP.
This should be embedded in law.
additional_details:
The general public has lost faith in British  politics they make statements which are clearly not going to be possible with no  consequences to misleading the public.
If they lose an election most will just walk across to the other benches and carry on as normal, there is no consequence to failure at any level.
MPs should be of the highest moral standard and be above reproach.
rejection_details:
We are not clear the specific action this petition is calling for, including what is meant by "benefits" and whether the action sought would be retrospective.

You may instead wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:
'Prevent people convicted of serious crimes standing or serving as MPs'
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744197

action: Amend Tobacco and Vapes Bill to restrict vapes like cigarettes, and limit access
background: We call on Parliament to amend the Tobacco and Vapes Bill to restrict access to vapes using a similar generational ban as it has for cigarettes, and restrict it for other people by making it available via prescription only and restricting available flavours.
additional_details: We have witnessed how bad vaping can be, especially among teenagers and those in schools, but in fact vaping has INCREASED in prevalence. We must follow Australia's lead and restrict vapes to pharmacy and doctor prescriptions ONLY as a smoking cessation support, as well as restricting flavours

action: Parliament: End MPs subsidised bars restaurants & perks
background:
While their constituents have been forced to endure austerity cuts, low wages, & meagre state pensions, our MPs are not suffering at all. This disparity has to stop!

If ever there were visual evidence at one of the pinnacles of our massive rich and poor divide rotten class system, this is it.
additional_details:
Austerity has never been an economic necessity, it has always been a political choice made by the right wing, to take from the poor, and give to the rich.

Our MPs are elected to parliament to work on behalf of their constituents, and not to feather their own nests at our expense. 

We have a race to the bottom competitive deregulated low waged, free market system.

While our MPs live a working life of tax payer subsidised luxury.

Its time it was ended.
rejection_details:
Catering services for the House of Commons are provided by an in-house team who do not provide a subsidised service in the commercial sense of the word. Some venues make a profit, referred to as contribution because it contributes to reducing overall costs. In other venues, the cost of providing the service does exceed the income received in sales due to the irregular hours and unpredictability of parliamentary business. The contribution or cost of each venue is calculated by subtracting the food and operational costs from the catering sales. Rather than a subsidy, the House monitors the contribution or cost of each catering venue, which include cafeterias, dining rooms, restaurants and bars. Prices of food and drink are regularly benchmarked against appropriate external comparators.

You can read more about this here: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/freedom-of-information/information-we-already-publish/house-of-commons-publication-scheme/catering-services/house-of-commons-cost-of-catering/

We can't accept petitions about catering in the House of Lords as that is the responsibility of the House of Lords.

action: Let Type 1 Diabetics join the British Forces.
background: I want the Government or Parliament to review the rules that prevent people with Type 1 diabetes from joining the British Forces. Many with Type 1 diabetes can meet the same physical and mental standards as non-diabetic recruits and should have the same opportunity to serve their country.
additional_details: I want the Government or Parliament to review the rules preventing people with Type 1 diabetes from joining the British Forces. Many with this condition are just as fit, capable, and committed as non-diabetic recruits. These outdated rules unfairly block willing and qualified individuals from serving their country. Updating them would ensure fairness, recognise true ability, and let all dedicated applicants contribute to our nation’s defence.
rejection_details:
We already have a petition open on this subject which you may wish to sign: 

Diabetes should not prevent someone serving in the British armed forces
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741445

action: Review education about nutrition and responsible farming in schools
background: We call for a review of the national curriculum to consider how it could better include nutrition and responsible farming to teach people about the journey their food takes from farm to fork. We believe good wholesome homemade food can ward off sickness and obesity so also protecting NHS.
additional_details: In our view, the current food education within schools is basic and doesn't provide enough education in respect of where our food is from, which food is nutritional and locally produced. This, we believe, can continue to adulthood as there are adults who have no idea what they are consuming and the nutritional values.

action: Fix Northampton Potholes
background: On behalf of Northampton people and on behalf of driving instructor community as im one of the driving instructors. I would like to draw the government attention to fix the potholes in northampton. It is one of the worst in the world. Nobody can travel safely and this costing us a lot.
additional_details: The government must push the Northampton council to keep the roads safe and legal. Every single person pays road tax and council tax, what for ? We are losing our cars and people cannot drive safely from one point to another without losing a tyre or damaging their cars. This ruins the image of the town and the whole nation and government.

action: Governing parties must show real progress on their manifesto commitments
background:
This petition calls for a simple, fair rule: governing parties must show real progress on their manifesto commitments within six months—or face consequences
If they fail without good reason, Parliament should be able to remove the Prime Minister and prevent them from holding any government position
additional_details:
This assessment should take into account economic conditions, national emergencies, legal constraints, and other exceptional circumstances, and should be supported by transparent reporting to Parliament
Politicians win elections on promises, but far too often, once in power, those promises are abandoned.
Election promises should mean something
It’s time to restore trust in our democracy.
Additionally, all politicians should undergo enhanced CRB checks to ensure those in power are properly vetted
rejection_details:
We're not sure how this is different from existing Parliamentary scrutiny of the Government and its manifesto, and Parliament's ability to hold votes of no confidence.

You may be interested in the following petitions:

Call a general election if a government breaks an election manifesto promise
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744946

Make the government legally accountable for delivering its manifesto promises
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749381

Require an election if 70% of the government manifesto isn’t delivered
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741176

Ban party to put forward candidate if it has broken manifesto commitments
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749686

action: Expand CAMHS assessments to include neurodivergent children in severe distress
background: Expand CAMHS assessment criteria so neurodivergent children in severe distress can access timely mental health assessments and support, without needing to self-harm or reach crisis point.
additional_details: Many neurodivergent children experience severe anxiety, emotional dysregulation, school refusal and family breakdown, yet are unable to access CAMHS unless they self-harm or reach crisis. This delays early intervention, increases long-term harm, and places additional pressure on families, schools and emergency services. Early assessment improves outcomes and reduces future costs.
rejection_details:
We understand that you are concerned about how neurodivergent children access CAMHS but we are not sure what you would like to change. 

You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759345

action: Introduce Pet Licence for cats and dogs and require reporting cat collisions
background: Introduce a national Pet Licence scheme for cat and dog ownership, linked to microchipping and responsible care. Amend the Road Traffic Act 1988 to make road traffic collisions involving cats legally reportable, like collisions involving dogs and livestock.
additional_details: Microchipping improves traceability but does not prevent abandonment, neglect or irresponsible ownership. A Pet Licence scheme would improve accountability and support enforcement and animal welfare. Drivers must report collisions involving dogs and livestock, but not cats. Making cat collisions reportable would help injured cats receive assistance, allow owners to be informed via microchips, and support road safety by identifying collision hotspots and speeding issues.

action: Make all government services & payments fully digital & reduce reliance on cash.
background: We want the Government to commit a gradual transition towards fully digital system for all government service & payments & to significantly reduce reliance on physical cash in economy.We believe a modern inclusive & secure digital system will benefit citizens, businesses & the UK economy as a whole.
additional_details:
The UK is a highly digital society, yet many public services and transactions still rely on physical cash and offline processes. This increases costs, slows services, and limits transparency.
Expanding fully digital and online payments would help reduce tax evasion and cash-related crime, improve accountability through clear transaction records, and make public services faster and more convenient for citizens and businesses.
Reducing reliance on cash would also save public money, support environmental goals, and encourage innovation in financial technology. Any transition should be gradual and inclusive, with support for those who face digital barriers.

action: Remove interest from all UK student loans to stop unfair graduate taxation
background: Remove interest from all student loans and freeze balances in real terms so repayments reduce debt instead of inflating it. Student loan repayments already function as a graduate tax and should not grow through interest.
additional_details: Student loans now operate like a second tax on graduates, taken directly from pay. High interest means balances grow even while people repay, trapping them for decades. This reduces take-home pay and makes it harder to save, including paying into pensions, leaving graduates paying two forms of tax for education.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the same action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756832

action: Discontinue the TV license.
background: The TV licence needs to be discontinued. In this day and age it is no longer needed. The general consensus of the general public is that it is a waste of peoples money and in fact robbery.
additional_details: Minimal people still watch live TV with the majority using streaming. If the BBC want income then introduce adverts.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Scrap the TV Licence
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/754524

action: Fund travel reimbursements for families of children with lifelong conditions
background: Provide funding for travel reimbursements for all families of children with lifelong conditions who are attending specialist centres for their conditions, similar to the scheme for paediatric cancer patients.
additional_details: Long term health conditions, such as heart conditions and other unique conditions, mean that families may have to travel miles to specialist centres. These costs can be crippling if your child needs regular hospital admissions and outpatient appointments. We want the Government to fund reimbursements of these costs to families who are affected.

action: Change the age in which a car becomes a classic and therefore VED and MOT exempt
background:
I would like the government to bring down the age at which a car becomes a classic, from 40 years to 30. 
Making younger cars also VED and MOT exempt.
additional_details: 40 years is far too long. Through purchase and 30 years of running, the country has had far more than the value of the car in tax.
rejection_details:
We appear already to have a petition open on this which you may wish to sign instead:

Reduce age required for historic/classic vehicle status from 40 to 30 years
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756228

action: End Stealth Tax raise the Personal Allowance & threshold in line with inflation.
background: The government needs raise the Personal Allowance (currently £12,570) and the Higher Rate threshold (£50,270) in line with inflation (CPI)
additional_details: It prevents "fiscal drag" from eating into your take-home pay every time you get a cost-of-living raise. A petition for this targets the "hidden" tax rises that hit workers harder than those on fixed benefits.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/749467

action: Introduce mandatory ankle and feet checks by school nurses in school
background: When nurses come to check children’s height and weight, we think this should include a mandatory check to see if these children have any issues with their ankles and feet - eg, having flat feet, or in- or out-toeing.
additional_details: We believe feet and ankles should be checked due to their consequences on health, and if a child is to have these problems they should be allowed access to aids such as special shoes insoles and ankle braces to correct these issues. In our view, this limited measure could cause a long term decrease of strain on the NHS.

action: Change the statutory term ‘Special Educational Needs’ to more inclusive language
background: Change the term “Special Educational Needs (SEN)” in education legislation and statutory guidance to more inclusive, modern terminology such as “Additional Learning Needs” or “Learning Needs”, including in the SEND Code of Practice and relevant education law.
additional_details: We believe the term “Special Educational Needs” is widely seen by many as outdated and stigmatising. We are concerned it can reinforce deficit-based views of children. More inclusive terminology like “Additional Learning Needs” is used in Wales and we feel it reflects a modern understanding of neurodiversity, child development and inclusion. Updating this language in England could reduce stigma, increase inclusivity in school culture, and align with current research and best practice.

action: Make 12 July 2027 a Bank Holiday for 1100th anniversary of the birth of England
background: Make Monday 12th July 2027 a bank holiday in England to commemorate the 1100th anniversary of the birth of England, so that all the people of England celebrate this occasion. The Government should also support organising celebrations for that day.
additional_details: It is recognised by many that the meeting arranged by King Æthelstan on 12th July 927 at ‘Eamotum’ in Cumbria represents the original unification of the English people, it is rightly described as the Birth of England. After this date King Æthelstan styled himself as Rex Anglorum - King of the English. We believe the Government, by creating a bank holiday on that day, would indicate its recognition of this significant day in England's history and could allow most people in England to join in the celebrations.

action: Make a public animal abuser register & automatically ban ownership
background: Create a public register of all offenders convicted of animal abuse and introduce an automatic, lifetime ban on animal ownership for anyone convicted of animal neglect or abuse. This register should be searchable by vets, breeders, charities and the public to prevent repeat offending.
additional_details: I clean homes for free for people in need and regularly witness animals suffering under owners with a history for animal neglect or abuse. Currently, bans are discretionary and there is no public register. Abusers can continue acquiring animals. A mandatory ban and register could prevent repeat cruelty and break cycles of harm. Additionally, an immediate automatic lifetime ban could prevent animal ownership being at a judge’s discretion.

action: Abolish fees for passport name changes
background: Abolish fees for people who change their name on their passport due to marriage, divorce, gender reassignment, estrangement, or escaping domestic abuse, where the change is supported by official documents such as a marriage certificate or deed poll.
additional_details: People changing their name must pay the full passport fee on top of the cost of marriage certificates, divorce certificates or deed polls. We feel this disproportionately affects women, who are more likely to change their surname after marriage. Changing a name on a driving licence is free, which we believe creates an unfair inconsistency across official ID. Accurate ID is essential to avoid travel issues or accusations of fraud.

action: Allow cancelled passports to be reactivated if found within reasonable timeframe
background: Once a UK passport is reported lost, it is cancelled and cannot be used, even if later found. We ask the Government to allow reactivation within a reasonable timeframe, with security checks.
additional_details: When a UK passport is reported lost, it is immediately cancelled, even if later found, forcing holders to pay £94.50 unnecessarily. Allowing reactivation within a few hours or a day, with strict security checks, would save money, reduce hassle, and be fair, while keeping border security intact.

action: Automatic review of parental responsibility for perpetrators of abuse
background: Change the law so domestic abusers and stalkers face tougher punishments, and any conviction of abuse - no matter how “minor” - triggers an automatic review to remove or restrict parental responsibility to protect children and victims.
additional_details: Domestic abuse, stalking, and coercive control put victims and children at serious risk. Many perpetrators keep parental rights even after convictions, and there are hundreds of abuse related deaths each year in the UK. We feel tougher sentences and automatic review of parental responsibility, no matter the severity, would protect survivors, children, and prevent repeat abuse.

action: Strengthen and enforce rules to stop scam emergency trade call-out adverts
background: Require search engines to verify emergency trade advertisers before allowing paid adverts. Only allow adverts from trusted, accountable providers and ban “bait and switch” pricing. Remove scam adverts quickly and stop repeat offenders from returning.
additional_details: We’ve been told the Online Safety Act (OSA) 2023 already requires search engines and platforms to prevent paid-for fraudulent adverts and remove them when reported. But it isn’t working. Rogue emergency trade adverts still appear at the top of search results, pushing reputable local businesses out of view. Complaints keep rising and recent BBC coverage shows the scale of harm. “Bait and switch” pricing (cheap advert, inflated bill) misleads consumers in emergencies and is still happening.

action: Do not introduce a mandatory learning period for new UK drivers
background: The Government must withdraw its proposal to introduce a minimum learning time requirement for new drivers in the UK.
additional_details: The suggestion that individuals applying for a driving licence in the UK must undertake a compulsory learning period of up to 6 months will, we believe, directly prevent certain groups (immigrants, elders who have to reapply, and those unable to afford private lessons) from getting onto the road and will lead to the already terrible learner driver environment to become even more unreasonable in terms of wait times for lessons/tests/etc, and will increase the number of drivers without a licence.

action: Protect Children Online: Require ID for Social Media Accounts
background: “Introduce legislation requiring social media platforms to verify users with government-issued ID (such as a passport or driving licence) to prevent fake accounts, underage access, child grooming, and to support criminal investigations.”
additional_details: “Social media currently allows anonymous and fake accounts, enabling child grooming, underage access, harassment, and repeat offending. Requiring government-issued ID would reduce fake profiles, protect children, improve accountability, and help law enforcement investigate serious online crimes while keeping personal details private.”
rejection_details:
Your petition is effectively a duplicate of one we already have open, which you may wish to sign:

https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/757983

action: Re open cardonald public library
background: Funds where approved for building work to go ahead in april 2025 to make safe and reopen cardonald library i have posted on cardonalds local page and alot of people are interested when this will be happining the community needs it it is a joke how long it has been closed now to be honest
additional_details: Sort the problem and have the library opened as soon as possible

action: Change the tax & welfare systems so WORK PAYS for low and middle income earners
background:
DON'T increase welfare spending, funded by ever more taxation; INSTEAD change the systems to :
Encourage and fairly reward the strivers of this country
Encourage all who can to contribute to society by working
Discourage welfare as a lifestyle choice
Allow us to support those in genuine need
additional_details:
The planned budget changes will increase tax further for many working people BUT still find the money to increase welfare payments.
Recent reports suggest that soon 1 in 4 workers in full time jobs would be better off staying at home on benefits - often by thousands (and even tens of thousands) of pounds.
This is madness !
Our tax and welfare systems have to show people that their work is valued and it has to be financially worth working - if not, more and more will choose to stop.
rejection_details:
We understand that you are concerned about low and middle income earners but we are not sure what changes you would like to see. You could start a new petition setting out clearly what changes you would like to happen. 

Or you could sign petitions we already have open. For example: 
Increase the personal tax-free allowance to £26000 https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745558

action: Increase the UK inheritance tax gift allowance in line with the US
background: We call on the UK Government to reform the current inheritance tax gift rules (where only £3,000 is exempt each tax year before the seven-year rule applies)
additional_details: So that UK residents can give larger lifetime gifts without inheritance tax implications — aligned more closely with the US annual exclusion of ~$19,000 per recipient. We believe this would help families support loved ones during their lives and modernise UK tax policy.

action: Keep B1 English ILR requirement for those already in UK on family/spouse visa
background: Do not change to the B2 English requirement for ILR which has been proposed in the November 2025 immigration white paper. This change will not be possible to achieve for those planning to apply for ILR in 2026 as there is insufficient time to achieve B2 English level for some on the family route
additional_details: This change needs a transition period until at least 2027 applications for ILR. Some of those applying for ILR in 2026 will not be able to meet the proposed new B2 standard level which means they will have to apply fir an additional FLR visa at an additional cost of circa £4500. This creates uncertainty for families and spouses of UK citizens unnecessarily.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751572

action: End the Plan 2 threshold freeze and review unfair interest rates
background: The Government should end the Plan 2 repayment threshold freeze immediately and review the whole post‑2012 loan system. Interest rules should be changed so balances don’t keep rising while borrowers make regular repayments, ensuring a fairer and more sustainable system.
additional_details: The Plan 2 system is fundamentally unfair. The repayment threshold freeze forces graduates to pay more each year during a cost of living crisis, while high interest rates make balances grow even when people repay. It’s placing huge pressure on a generation already struggling to build secure futures, delaying milestones like saving, housing and stability. Ending the freeze and reviewing the system is urgently needed.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759316  


You may also wish to sign this petition: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759293

action: Fund all payment fees for EpiPens and asthma inhalers
background: Fund all payment fees for EpiPens and asthma inhalers to make them free of charge. These medicines are critical for managing life-threatening conditions and are required for immediate emergency treatment. We believe it is unreasonable for such essential medication to come at a cost.

action: 10 pence charge to plastic bottles to encourage recycling
background: I would like the government to implement a 10 pence charge to plastic beverage bottles which will be returned to the consumer when the bottle is recycled at an appropriate station; this is similar to programs in Australia
additional_details:
I want to implement a 10p deposit return scheme for plastic bottles. this policy shifts the economic incentive transforming what is currently perceived as litter into an asset. It will ensure that empty bottles are returned to the supply chain rather than being discarded in nature.
The benefits of such a system are great as millions of tonnes of plastic are lost to landfills annually a 10p charge creates a circular economy. The consumer incurs no cost, while the polluter pays.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fund a £0.10 deposit scheme for recycling single-use beverage containers
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/744300

action: Recognise OET as proof of English language skills for naturalisation
background: We urge the Government to recognise OET (Occupational English Test) as proof of proficient English, skills for applicants who have done this test for the purposes of their healthcare worker visa, when applying for citizenship
additional_details:
We believe this will align the English language requirements across many healthcare professions’ professional registration, long-term settlement (ILR), and citizenship (Naturalisation).

The OET is a high-level English test already accepted by many healthcare bodies for the Skilled Worker Visas. Excluding it from Naturalisation is an unnecessary inconsistency. We think this forces highly skilled healthcare migrants to take a redundant, costly second test despite having proven their proficiency to practise medicine in the UK.

action: Make GCSES affordable for Home education families
background: The government should support home-educated students by funding or reducing GCSE exam fees. Parliament should ensure fair access to exam centres, clear GCSE arrangements, and equal treatment so home-educated learners are not disadvantaged compared to school students.
additional_details: Home-educated students face high GCSE exam fees and limited access to exam centres, while school students take exams with no extra cost. This creates unfair barriers and can affect future education, apprenticeships, and career opportunities. The government should fund or reduce fees, provide clear guidance on exam arrangements, and ensure equal access so home-educated learners have the same chances to succeed academically, socially, and personally.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/743064

action: Allow humanitarian medal to be awarded retrospectively
background: We would like the operating principles of the Humanitarian Aid Medal to be amended so that it can be awarded retrospectively, so that it could be awarded to those involved in Operation Rescript the military operation to provide support during the Covid-19 pandemic.
additional_details: In our view, the Covid-19 pandemic crisis is an obvious and extreme example, of the selfless commitment made by the armed forces when called upon, with many having worked in unfamiliar, potentially dangerous circumstances, sacrificing personal freedoms to support civil authorities and serve the public. We believe these efforts should be formally recognised by the public and state in the form of a medal.

action: Scrap interest on all student loan repayments
background: We are calling on the government to remove interest from student loan repayments. Graduates are charged interest of up to 3% above inflation, meaning they repay far more than borrowed. This creates a ‘graduate tax’, leaving many in debt for 30 yrs & making this far more expensive than original cost.
additional_details: Student loan interest means graduates often repay far more than they originally borrowed. With interest charged at up to 3% above inflation (currently around 7% total), a typical 3-year degree costing ~£27,000 can grow to over £40,000 in real debt before repayment even begins. Many people remain in debt for 30 years despite regular payments. Removing interest would make repayments fairer and reduce long-term financial strain.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Abolish interest charges on student loans
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756832

action: To have a 4 day school week
background: To reduce the school week to 4 days, either a Monday or Friday and have a 3 day weekend.
additional_details: I want the government to do this because I believe it will improve mental health of the younger generation and increase attendance rates during the 4 day week, which would result in better GCSE results.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Reduce school to 4 days a week and have optional extra activities
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756710

action: Fund free therapy access for students in all schools
background: We would like the Government to ensure students have full access to therapeutic help if they are struggling with their mental wellbeing or anxiety due to stress placed upon them from any exams, such as mocks or GSCEs, by providing funding for free therapy.
additional_details: Certain studies have shown that depression or mental loneliness have been rapidly increasing due to pressure from teachers or bullying. All this stress can build up within students and result in tensions with bullies, resulting in fights which can lead to detentions and negative social consequences. We feel this doesn’t help as punishments can then take up time which could be used for revision.

action: Ban holiday companies from implementing price hikes during school breaks
background: We feel that families (be that single parent families, one income families or other less fortunate families) are being squeezed by holiday companies with price increases in the school breaks. We feel this is unfair.
additional_details: We want to make memories with our children that will last a lifetime. Many of us can’t due to the price of holidays. Teachers can also suffer financially for this reason.

action: Provide protection and support for individuals falsely accused of serious crimes
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legal and employment protections, as well as financial support, for individuals who are accused of serious crimes and are unable to work while investigations are ongoing. Those convicted would have to pay any support back.
additional_details: Individuals who are falsely accused of serious crimes often face severe consequences despite not being convicted of any offence. While investigations are necessary, there are currently limited safeguards to protect the livelihoods and wellbeing of those who are later found to be innocent or where no charges are brought. The presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle of justice, yet we believe false accusations can effectively punish individuals without due process.

action: Less Stricter Uniform Policies In Secondary Schools
background: I would love for the parliament to keep school uniform, but make the rules say that you can wear shorts and a T-shirt in summer or coats in the winter
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require schools prioritise comfort in uniforms & more personal choice for pupils
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/751980

action: Ban multilevel marketing businesses
background: I would like the government to ban MLMs.
additional_details:
MLMs often convince people to spend a lot of money, promising huge profits, which is often very exaggerated. On top of this, it can often cause strain between the individual and their friends and family as they are encouraged to sell to those first.
 
Members are often vulnerable and may be manipulated in to continuing to spend money, while also being encouraged to be slightly mysterious as to what they are doing and will often get angry if someone tries to warn them.

action: Require all local authorities to have a youth advisory panel
background: Pass a law that requires all local authorities to have a youth advisory panel. These panels could allow young people to voice their opinions, raise concerns, and offer ideas, while allowing councillors to better understand the needs of younger residents.
additional_details: Youth advisory panels could attend selected meetings, submit recommendations, or be consulted on policies that impact young people. They could also contribute to council meetings and consultations. Many council decisions directly affect young people, including those relating to education, transport, public spaces, community safety, and youth services, yet we believe young people often have limited opportunities to formally share their views.

action: Ban individuals convicted of terror or hate offences from holding public office
background: Introduce legislation preventing anyone convicted of terrorism offences or hate‑motivated crimes from standing in local elections or holding any public office or local elections.
additional_details: People convicted of terrorism or hate‑motivated offences pose a risk to public trust and democratic integrity. Those who have promoted violence, extremism, or hatred should not be permitted to represent communities or hold public authority. Clear rules are needed to protect public safety and confidence.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban anyone convicted of terrorism offences from standing for public office
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759385

action: Make it mandatory for all MPs to complete an enhanced DBS check
background:
I want the government to debate this issue and hopefully bring all MPs into line with other persons that are subject to having to complete DBS in order to carry out their work. 
I feel it is unsatisfactory that they should be excluded in this day and age.
additional_details: Members of Parliament occupy positions of exceptional trust, power, and access. They make laws that govern the lives of others, routinely interact with vulnerable individuals, and enjoy privileged access to schools, charities, care settings, and constituent casework involving children and adults at risk.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756785

action: Expedite delayed January intake student visas and ensure fair, timely decisions
background: Prolonged delays in January intake student visa processing led to missed enrolments and financial loss. We urge the Government to improve processing capacity, set transparent timelines, provide remedies for affected students, and prevent future intake disruptions.
additional_details: Delays in processing student visas for the January intake disrupted study plans, caused financial losses, and harmed student wellbeing. Clear, consistent processing timelines and increased capacity would restore confidence in the UK’s immigration system and uphold the UK’s reputation as a fair, competitive destination for international students. We ask Parliament to implement durable reforms to avoid future intake failures.

action: Align Plan 2 student loan interest rates with Plan 5 (RPI only).
background: We call on the government to remove the +3% 'real' interest rate from Plan 2 loans and cap interest at RPI, as is the case for students who started after 2023.
additional_details: Plan 2 graduates are the only cohort charged interest above inflation, creating an unfair 'middle-earner trap' where balances grow despite regular repayments. Furthermore, the government has frozen the Plan 2 threshold at £29,385 until 2030. As wages rise with inflation, this acts as a stealth tax. We ask that the threshold also be adjusted annually in line with the Retail Price Index (RPI).

action: Ban anyone convicted of a terrorism offence from running for Councillor/MP
background:
Introduce legislation to permanently disqualify anyone convicted of terrorism from standing for or holding any public office in the UK, including as an MP, councillor, mayor, or other elected roles.
Current UK law does not impose a specific, automatic, or lifelong ban for terrorism convictions.
additional_details:
This change would protect democratic integrity, ensure public confidence in elected representatives, and prevent those convicted of terrorism from gaining platforms of influence.
We urge the Government and Parliament to act swiftly to legislate this safeguard.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Ban anyone convicted of terrorism offences from standing for public office
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759385

action: Bring back the Beat Bobby
background: Bring back proactive policing in the U.K.
additional_details: Criminals are making the most of no Police presence
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what you'd like the Government or Parliament to do.
