If you would like the Government to fund more Police presence on the streets, you could start a petition about that.

action: Raise care infrastructure funding for adults seeking gender dysphoria treatment
background: Increase funding for care infrastructure for adults seeking gender dysphoria treatment to ensure that there is sufficient capacity, expanded care, assessment bottlenecks are tackled, standardised care, and greater investment in workforce training.
additional_details: Waiting times at gender dysphoria clinics in the UK are between 5-8 years, and demand is increasing. We believe it is time for an improvement in infrastructure and greater funding to significantly speed up wait times and help struggling staff.

action: Scrap the underoccupancy charge for public housing
background: Scrap the underoccupancy charge (also known as the bedroom tax), for low income families, for the sick disabled and unemployed.
additional_details:
We believe the bedroom tax is totally unfair because it puts a strain on peoples low finances and those wishing to move down to a smaller property where there isn’t any. It’s an unfair tax that people can’t afford to pay.
 
It can impact on disabled people the most if they need an extra room but yet people still feel punished for being disabled but yet get their benefits reduced. How is that fair?

action: Sack Eddie Howe immediately
background: Sack Eddie Howe
additional_details: Eddie Howe is anti football and tactics have went stale

action: Cap individual net worth at £1 billion & use excess wealth to fund NHS
background: We call on the Government to cap individuals’ net worth at £1 billion, and to tax all wealth above this threshold at 100% to fund the National Health Service. We believe this is an ethical act of governance and could be an opportunity for the UK to set a global & historical precedent.
additional_details: We believe extreme concentrations of wealth undermine democratic accountability, distort public life, and enable undue influence over policy and institutions. We believe no individual accumulates £1,000,000,000 without reliance on public infrastructure, labour, and stability. A wealth cap could act as a safeguard against corruption and hoarding, while redirecting excess wealth to the NHS could strengthen a vital public service and return value to the society that helped to enable such accumulation.

action: Require all social housing providers to publish floor plans for accessible homes
background: We call on the Government to require all social housing providers and local authority housing registers to publish floor plans and key accessibility measurements for any property advertised as accessible or suitable for disabled applicants.
additional_details:
Many properties are currently labelled as “wheelchair accessible” or “suitable for an indoor wheelchair user” without providing room sizes, doorway widths, or turning space dimensions. Disabled people therefore have no way of assessing whether a property is physically usable before bidding. We believe publishing floor plans and accessibility measurements is a simple, practical step that would remove these barriers and ensure accessible housing is genuinely accessible.
We ask the Government to introduce national standards requiring:
 
• Mandatory floor plans for all accessible social housing adverts
• Published accessibility measurements for properties labelled accessible
• Consistent accessibility classifications across housing providers

action: Recognise smear campaigns as abuse and strengthen legal protections for victims
background: Recognise smear campaigns as a form of psychological abuse and strengthen legal protection for victim survivors, including consideration of criminal accountability where smear campaigns are used to silence, intimidate, discredit or retaliate against disclosures of abuse. Smear campaigns cause harm.
additional_details: Smear campaigns are a harmful practice used against victim survivors after disclosing abuse. They occur not only in intimate partner relationships, but also in workplaces, professional settings and communities, where false allegations, reputation damage, and isolation are used to silence and punish disclosures. These actions cause serious psychological, professional, and social harm, yet are often dismissed as civil disputes instead of criminal. Victims need stronger recognition and protection.
rejection_details:
It's not clear how what the petition is calling for are any different than the protections already available under statute law, such as under s1 of the Protection of Harassment Act 1997

https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/40/section/1

action: Ban Police sharing footage obtained by police, for commercial purposes
background: We want police forces to be banned from sharing recorded footage such as bodycam footage, with companies which use it for commercial gain. We believe that such footage should only be used and shared for law enforcement.
additional_details: I want the Government to restrict UK police forces from releasing bodycam footage to companies for commercial gain. For example, a police force recently released footage to an entertainment streaming platform which was used to produce a documentary, which in my view does raise some concerns over potential privacy infringement and exploitation. Footage should only be used for law enforcement purposes, ensuring transparency and protecting individuals' rights.

action: Update UK e-bike laws: allow 750W, 20mph limit and throttle use.
background: Modernise e-bike law by raising motor power to 750W, increasing assisted speed to 20mph and permitting throttle control. Update regulations so e-bikes remain legally classed as bicycles, without licences or insurance, while keeping safety rules and existing road standards.
additional_details: Current UK limits are outdated and restrict practical use of e-bikes. Higher power and a 20mph limit would make e-bikes safer in traffic and more useful for daily travel. This is vital for the economy as many rely on e-bikes to transport goods and services, including food delivery couriers, parcel couriers, handymen and builders. Modern rules would reduce congestion, support green transport, create jobs and help small businesses operate more efficiently and economically.

action: Call a public inquiry into any foreign influence on UK politics & democracy
background: It’s clear that we have numerous issues with covert foreign interests attempting to influence British political parties. In order to ensure British democracy is preserved by the next election, we believe we should understand how embedded foreign interests are in British politics.
additional_details: We are concerned about reports of some British politicians’ links with overseas figures and foreign nations. We believe we cannot have a free democracy while foreign interests influence our Parliament and our democracy.

action: Ban abortions after 12 weeks
background: Ban abortions after 12 weeks. Babies can survive after 21 weeks, and we believe it is wrong to be able to have an abortion after 12 weeks.
additional_details: There are alternatives people can turn to if they do not want their child. There are many people who can’t have children and who would be over the moon to be able to raise a child. Stop allowing abortions after 12 weeks – we believe every child deserves a chance in life.

action: Ban foreign media ownership, enact a social media levy & new regulatory reform
background: Pass law to ban foreign & offshore ownership of UK media, enact a social-media levy to distribute media ownership across society & fund independent, local & cooperative-owned media. We believe democracy is failing as the media & political power are owned by a tiny rich elite.
additional_details: We also call the Government to introduce new regulatory reforms, including requiring all media in the UK to be members of a statutory regulator and requiring media-covered think-tanks to report donations in real time. We believe we need to take back control of media ownership for the British people and that media should be free from offshore ownership and think tanks who accept dark money. Media ownership should reflect ALL of society not just the rich.

action: Stop accommodating asylum seekers in ex-military camps in local communities
background: The current practice and policy of using ex-military camps in local communities is causing increasing pressure on local communities. In at least one case an asylum seeker has absconded after a serious sexual offence. Asylum seekers are unvetted and such a practice is high risk to vulnerable groups.
additional_details: The placement policy needs urgent action. It appears that asylum seekers are ‘bussed in’ on entry to Uk, to any of a number of such camps. With the potential mass increase as border pressures themselves are susceptible to open penetration the continued use of this policy needs ceasing. Apart from single cases of absconding, in general the home office own data suggests that it is not possible to keep asylum seekers in any location local communities of families and vulnerable groups need safety.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Stop asylum seekers being given housing in military establishments
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/748431

action: Stop individuals with Terrorism Convictions from Standing in UK Local Elections
background: I am calling on the UK Government to close this loophole and introduce clear legislation preventing anyone with a terrorism conviction from standing in local elections.
additional_details: Public office requires the highest levels of trust, integrity and public confidence. Allowing individuals with terrorism convictions to run for elected positions undermines that trust and poses an unacceptable risk to democratic institutions.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for the a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759385

action: Require that the media refer to sexual abuse victims under 18 as "children"
background: Media outlets can refer to victims of sexual offences under 18 as “young women”. We feel this language is inaccurate, risks minimising child sexual abuse, and conflicts with safeguarding and child protection principles.
additional_details:
We ask the Government to require accurate, child-appropriate terminology in media reporting.

In UK law, anyone under 18 is a child. Referring to children as adults in reporting on sexual offences can distort public understanding of these crimes and undermine child protection and safeguarding. Anyone who is a child and a victim should be reported as a child. Not a young adult. Not a young woman. Not a young man. A child.

action: Review the use of retrospective rule changes by the Home Office
background: Consider whether the Home Office should have the authority to bring forward any proposals or rules with Retrospective effect. If this practise is fair? And once a precedent is set, who stops the Home Office from exercising their powers over and over again affecting thousands of families.
additional_details: We believe the recent Immigration White Paper 2025 is more Authoritarian rather than Humanitarian. There are concerns that if this goes through once, future governments will do this as well and there will be No Stopping of rules applied in Retrospection. We think the Home office is mixing Illegal migration with Legal Tax payers who came here with a set of rules, that if followed had a clear goal post.

action: Fund homeless shelters specifically for under-25s
background: We call on the Government to provide funding for local councils to fund shelters specifically for under 25s. Some young people experiencing homelessness face risks that adult shelters are not designed to handle, and may avoid existing shelters because they feel intimidated, or unsupported.
additional_details: Such funding must be used to ensure such shelters are safe, welcoming, and youth-focused, with trained staff who understand trauma and youth needs. We want these shelters to provide wraparound support, including mental health services, education and employment assistance and pathways into stable housing. We also believe that unnecessary barriers such as strict curfews or excessive entry requirements that prevent young people from gaining help should be removed. We are concerned that young people who do not get support via shelters sleep rough, couch surf, or remain in dangerous situation including abuse, exploitation, and trafficking.

action: Subsidise the Isle of Wight ferries so they are affordable to Island residents.
background: The Isle of Wight is in the bottom quartile of the UK economy with higher than average levels of poverty. The ferries provide a critical lifeline but are unregulated, and fares have now risen to unaffordable levels for many. We need the Government to step in and subsidise fares for IOW residents.
additional_details: Unregulated private equity companies have pushed up ferry fares. Residents of the Isle of Wight, making personal visits to the Mainland, are now in need of financial support - in the form of a Government subsidy - to afford access to essential visits to the Mainland. Establishing this subsidy would be a useful objective for the newly formed Cross Solent Transport Group, to deliver value for Island residents as well as the ferry companies; facilitating economic growth through increased travel.
rejection_details:
We can’t accept petitions that call for action at a local level.

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

And you can find out how to ask your MP to present a public (paper) petition here: https://www.parliament.uk/get-involved/sign-a-petition/paper-petitions/

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

action: Impose a 40% import duty on all Japanese goods
background: Impose a 40% import duty on Japanese imports to show that the UK does not tolerate the killing of pilot whales and dolphins in Japan. This could significantly increase UK revenue by billions of pounds.
additional_details: We believe the UK should do something about the slaughter of cetaceans in Japan every year, and the capture of cetaceans as part of the aquarium trade. Whales and dolphins hold valuable importance to our ocean ecosystem, and we feel they are being put at risk due to the hunts.

action: Ban compulsory purchase orders in redevelopment: protect homes & communities
background: We want the Government to ban compulsory purchase orders in redevelopment schemes, protect residents’ rights to stay in their homes, and ensure regeneration is based on voluntary agreements and genuine community-led decision-making that strengthens, not dismantles, local communities.
additional_details: We believe Compulsory Purchase Orders are being misused to displace families, pensioners, and long-standing residents for profit-driven redevelopment. This practice destroys communities, erodes human rights, and causes severe stress, especially for the vulnerable. Homes should not be treated as commodities. The Government must act to protect dignity, security, and ensure regeneration is voluntary, fair, and community-led, so redevelopment strengthens rather than dismantles neighbourhoods.

action: no yonder punches at barlby high school for prom
background: let barlby high have a yonder free prom
additional_details: for memories because it is a once in a lifetime event

action: Strengthen protection of DA victims and how their testimony is treated in court
background: Introduce Tianne Olivia's Law so evidence given by domestic abuse (DA) victims while alive is not dismissed as hearsay after death. Improve monitoring of high risk perpetrators, and prevent future deaths. Fund support when victims leave the perpetrator.
additional_details: Tianne gave evidence about her abuse while she was alive, yet after her death it was treated as hearsay. We call on the Government to introduce a law to prevent this, and for it to be known as Tianne Olivia's law. Clare’s Law allows the disclosure of information about previous history of abuse, but we think this must include active monitoring by the police of high-risk perpetrators. We also call on the Government to strengthen protections for domestic abuse victims, including introducing robust support packages for the victims who leave the perpetrator of the abuse should also be considered to ensure the victims’ mental and physical health does not deteriorate.

action: Mandate a national referendum for any petition reaching 1 million signatures
background: Introduce legislation to require a national referendum for petitions with 1m+ signatures, open to UK citizens and residents with settled status.
additional_details: Currently, petitions reaching 100K signatures can only lead to a debate, often leading to no action from the Government. We think a 1m signature threshold represents a huge mandate that deserves a binding vote. Residents with settled status (ILR/EUSS) pay taxes and are permanent members of our society; they must have a say in major national changes. To manage costs (historically £75m–£130m per vote), referendums should be bundled into one annual “Decision Day” or held during elections. We think this would turn the petitions site into a tool for real democratic change.

action: Ban trail hunting
background: Ban trail hunting as it can be another excuse for fox hunting.
additional_details: We would like the government to stop all trail hunting. We think this could prevent fox hunting permanently.

action: Student loans should be made interest free.
background:
Stop all interest payments on student loans we paid for the education they were happy to lend us the money. 

Increase the starting earnings repayment threshold annually.

Reduce repayment from 9% to 5% over threshold

Reverse the threshold freeze

Ensure repayments actually reduce the debt
additional_details:
Graduates in the UK have signed student finance contracts. The Government have retrospectively changed the terms of these contracts. This is unfair for graduates who have sought higher education. 

Private loan providers may face challenges if they did this. 

People who attended university or other higher education who hope to improve their outcomes and earning potential are having any improved income taken away by what can be seen as a "Graduate Tax" which is not the purpose of the loan.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Abolish interest charges on student loans
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756832

action: Reduce the tax burden on healthcare workers

action: Stop the Houses of Parliament renovation: Spend it on our NHS instead
background: Cancel the "Restoration and Renewal" program. Instead of spending up to £39bn on the Houses of Parliament (Palace of Westminster), the Government should build a modern, cost-effective seat of democracy for a fraction of the cost. Savings must be diverted to the NHS and public services.
additional_details: In our view, the possible £39.2bn cost is an insult to taxpayers during a national crisis. We are told "there is no money," yet billions are found for a Victorian relic. We believe that common sense must prevail over sentimentality, and that a purpose-built building could save tens of billions and be more efficient. The British people should not bankroll a multi-billion-pound fossil while our hospitals and schools are crumbling. Put public need before old stones.

action: Make the 15th June 2026 a bank holiday for England and Wales
background: We want the UK Government to grant a bank holiday on 15 June to England and Wales to recognise Scotland’s participation in the World Cup.
additional_details: His Majesty the King has already granted Scotland a bank holiday to mark its participation in the World Cup, as proposed by the Scottish Government. As this is a major sporting event followed across the UK, it would be fair and inclusive for the Government to extend the bank holiday. This would boost morale, support local businesses, and allow everyone to share in the celebration.

action: Legalise Wild Camping In England
background: I ask the Government and Parliament to create a legal framework that allows responsible wild camping across England
additional_details: I want the Government to allow wild camping in England because it would give everyone the chance to experience the outdoors, explore forests and hills safely, and learn important skills like bushcraft, self-reliance, and caring for the environment. Right now, most areas are off-limits, which prevents people of all ages from connecting with nature, enjoying small, controlled campfires or taking part in outdoor activities responsibly. Scotland and other countries show that this can be done safely

action: Ban the use of facial recognition software & require consent for biometric data
background: We call for a law to make the use of facial recognition technologies by all actors, including police and security services, illegal. Such a law should require written consent for the collection of any biometric data, with full right of deletion preserved.
additional_details: We believe individual liberty and the rule of law are cornerstone British Values and they're what make Britain the country that it is. We think a tolerant country which values individual liberties and rule of law does not collect, or allow anyone to collect, biometric data of its citizens without their full, prior, informed consent. In addition, we think there are also pragmatic objections, in Britain and the US there are myriad instances of people being wrongly identified. The EU has taken steps to regulate this technology.

action: Prioritise construction and review policies for affordable housing
background: We want our government to prioritise construction of affordable housing and improved affordability of existing housing so it's genuinely affordable for all. High housing costs, including rent and mortgages, are making it hard for many people and families to secure stable, safe, affordable homes.
additional_details:
We call for policies that incentivise the development of diverse housing options at prices accessible to those with moderate and low incomes. We see this as including exploring initiatives like Rent Control, Inclusionary Zoning in new developments and increased funding for Social Housing programs.
 
We believe that access to affordable housing is a fundamental human right, crucial for the wellbeing of our community and that it is time for action to ensure that everyone has a place to call home.

action: Call a public inquiry into US influence on UK politics and democracy
background: Hold a public inquiry to examine potential US influence in UK politics. We want the inquiry to investigate financial and other forms of support from the US for political figures and groups in the UK, as well as possible US influence during the Brexit Referendum.
additional_details: Reports indicate that prominent groups in the US with significant financial resources have been actively encouraging, supporting, and funding political activists and activity, including anti-EU supporters, in the UK.

action: Review & Regulate Veterinary Care so it's Affordable & Accessible
background: Government action is urgently needed to review and regulate veterinary pricing, improve transparency, and explore measures such as fee caps, subsidies, or support schemes, so that essential animal healthcare remains accessible and preventable animal suffering and loss can be reduced.
additional_details: Veterinary fees have risen to unsustainable levels, pushing pet ownership beyond the reach of many responsible owners and creating a growing animal welfare crisis. The cost of routine and emergency care now far exceeds what many households can afford, even though pets play a vital role in family life and mental wellbeing. As a result, increasing numbers of animals are surrendered to shelters or euthanised solely due to unaffordable veterinary costs, not because they are unwanted or neglected.

action: Minimum fare regulation for PHVs to support sustainable driver pay
background: Private hire drivers face falling real-terms pay due to unregulated fares and high platform commissions. Government should empower TfL to set minimum per-mile and per-minute fares, as with black cabs, to ensure fair pay, sustainability, and service standards.
additional_details: Private hire fares are unregulated, allowing platforms to increase commission and suppress driver earnings. In London’s high cost-of-living environment, this undermines workforce sustainability and service quality. Parliament should amend transport legislation to grant TfL explicit statutory powers to set minimum per-mile and per-minute PHV fares, aligning regulation with the licensed black cab model.
rejection_details: This petition is local (London area only) and concerns TfL for whom the Government do not have direct responsibility.

action: Introduce mandatory 24-hour CCTV in all NHS Neonatal units
background: Babies in neonatal units are extremely vulnerable. We believe making 24-hour CCTV mandatory would strengthen safeguarding, support accountability, reassure families and staff, and ensure consistent protection across all NHS neonatal units, with strict data protection controls.
additional_details: In our view recent legal cases have exposed serious safeguarding failures within neonatal units and highlighted the need for stronger oversight to protect vulnerable babies. Mandatory 24-hour CCTV could act as an additional safeguard, support early detection of harm, strengthen accountability, and help prevent future tragedies, while operating under strict privacy and data protection rules.

action: The removal or death of a PM should trigger a general election
background: We call on the Government to introduce legislation which would mandate a general election if a Prime Minister is removed or resigns from post, or if the Prime Minister dies.

action: Introduce regulations governing media reporting of abuse of women and girls
background: Abuse, assault and harassment of women and girls is a serious issue, one that has been described as a "national emergency". One in 12 females in the UK are victims, and a staggering 97% of women aged 18-24 have been sexually harassed. Yet media reporting of the issue normalises and trivialises it.
additional_details:
Regulations must prevent media reports from using incorrect terms that trivialise these crimes. There is no such thing as an "underage woman" - that is a child. "Underage sex" between an adult and a child does not exist - sex with a child is rape. The word "sex" should never be used to describe rape ("sex scandal", "accused of sex with").
 
This language normalises rape and child abuse, creating a culture where these are minimised and ignored. Laws must enforce correct terminology to clarify the severity of these crimes.

action: The vaginal and C/S birth numbers required by the NMC for student midwives
background: We would like the requirements to change according to the increase of caesarean section births accounting to almost 50% of births. Student midwives provide intense care and support during a caesarean section and currently these births are not included in our required numbers.
additional_details: Many of us, nationally, are experiencing difficulty in gaining the required numbers to graduate. When the caesarean birth rate is so high, this means less opportunity for vaginal births of which some are instrumental deliveries, which students cannot count. We are having to work extra hours to attempt to reach these numbers including over allocated annual leave or study time. We feel the numbers required should be 30 vaginal births and 20 caesarean sections.
rejection_details:

action: Review educational provision for children with SEMH needs
background: We would like an independent review into the currently available educational provision for children with Social, Emotional, and Mental Health needs, and whether it is fit for purpose
additional_details:
We call for investment in trauma-informed training, and for truly therapeutic and nurturing provision to be rolled out in all SEMH settings. Children present with SEMH needs for a host of reasons, such as neurodiversity, infant trauma, and ongoing difficult home situations. Tough starts in life that deserve care and understanding. 
 
We think the opportunities for children with challenging behaviour such as aggression or absconsion are concerning. They include settings that can be loud, chaotic and with punitive behaviour policies and physical restraint. The opposite of the nurturing and therapeutic settings needed to feel safe and learn.

action: Review and revise age of consent in light of advances in science
background: In light of scientific evidence, showing the human brain (prefrontal cortex) is not fully developed until between 21-30, l am asking the UK Government to review & revise the law to protect to our vulnerable children from emotional, physical, and mental harm.
additional_details: Currently UK law allows adults to engage in sexual activity with a child of 16 upwards, including adults of 20, 30, 50 and 60. Scientific evidence shows the prefrontal cortex (the decision making part of the brain) isn't fully developed. 16-year-olds are still learning grasping life-long decisions and consequences. This leaves them vulnerable to manipulation, sexual exploitation, unwanted pregnancies, STDs and spiritual harm. The consequences of the harms of this are real and can have lifelong effects.

action: Make a statutory requirement for schools to have a bereavement policy for pupils
background: A bereavement policy is necessary for well-being but should not be watered down or muddied by a mental health policy as grief is significantly different. We believe the policy for it should encompass a pupil passport for the longevity of a child's entire education to support learning and retention.
additional_details: We are concerned that the required equitable support for bereaved children is not currently in place. The time, emotion and even financial impact that parents can have to undergo in order to have to repeat the same conversations to multiple staff year after year is both exhausting and unnecessary. We think a passport system which is supported with a sturdy bereavement policy would work and this could change school retention for children.

action: Maintain current fireworks regulations and the 120dB maximum noise limit
background: Keep current firework laws and the 120dB limit. Existing rules balance tradition, safety, and public joy. We believe that further noise cuts are unnecessary and would harm the UK firework industry and businesses.
additional_details: The current 120dB limit is strictly regulated and fits outdoor celebrations. Dropping this to 90dB would effectively ban rockets and traditional displays, ruining the sensory experience the public expects. We believe such restrictions would devastate the industry and seasonal retailers. Instead of punishing responsible users, authorities should focus on enforcing existing laws against misuse. Since low-noise fireworks are already available, market choice should prevail over a restrictive blanket mandate.

action: Independent body to run extensive background check on all Members of Parliament

Therefore we believe that a new independent body which has the power to run background checks on Members of Parliament is needed to retain public trust in Parliamentary systems. We can’t brush over issues so lightly and in our view there needs to be more scrutiny in the way our Parliamentarians are acting.

action: Hold MPs Accountable: By-Elections if They Lie or Mislead the Public 3 Times
background: I want MPs held fully accountable for lying or misleading the public in any context - on social media, in interviews, speeches, or Parliament. Each lie could incur a fine, be logged in a public register, and if an MP accumulates three lies, a by-election could be triggered to protect democracy.
additional_details: Lies by MPs erode public trust, spread propaganda, and threaten democracy. Misleading statistics, selective facts, or partial truths can be as harmful as outright lies. Holding MPs accountable through fines, a public register, and mandatory by-elections after repeated offences could ensure honesty, transparency, and that elected officials treat voters as their true employers. Truth in politics must be non-negotiable. There must be zero tolerance; any deliberate deception must have real consequences.

action: Government to support the Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Bill [HL]
background: I want the Government to support the Bill proposed by Lord Holmes on the regulation of Artificial Intelligence. AI is Already Impacting, yet key questions around data use, liability, copyright, safety standards and transparency remain unresolved. If passed, the Bill will help with this.
additional_details: We believe this lack of resolution is bad for trust, bad for competitiveness, and bad for the UK’s ambition to lead in responsible AI. “Wait and see” isn’t a strategy. If the UK Govt wants growth, trust and sovereign capability, we believe we need to move from confusion to clarity, consistency and coherence and enable meaningful, sustained public engagement and participation, as citizen, consumer, creative, cross-society, cross-business. Such an approach is far more likely to deliver legislation fit for the AI age. Our data, our decisions, our AI futures.

action: Introduce a contribution-based asylum scheme for residents with 3+ years in UK
background: I want the Government to Introduce a contribution-based asylum route for people living in the UK for 3+ years, including long-pending asylum families, legal entrants who later overstayed, UK-born children and their parents, subject to identity checks, good character and proof of residence.
additional_details: Introduce a contribution-based asylum scheme for residents with 3+ years in the UK: asylum pending families, visa overstayers who entered legally, and parents of UK-born children. Tiered pathways: 3 years standard, 2 years for families with children or essential workers. Require identity verification, good character checks, and payment of fees/NHS surcharge. Grant temporary work rights leading to settlement after 5 years, reducing hotel costs and generating = annual tax revenue.

action: Do not extend the ILR qualifying period for Skilled visa holders to 10 years
background: We call on the Government to keep the current 5-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for Skilled Worker visa holders and not extend it to 10 years.
additional_details: We call on the Government to retain the 5-year route to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for Skilled Worker visa holders and not extend it to 10 years. Skilled workers already contribute through taxes, National Insurance, and high visa fees, while paying the Immigration Health Surcharge despite limited access to public funds. If benefit access is a concern, ILR should remain at 5 years, with public funds restricted until British citizenship.

action: Require companies to test all batches of baby formula before sale
background: Require all companies making baby formula to test all batches prior to them leaving the factory.
additional_details: Multiple baby formula companies have recalled their products on basis of suspected or potential toxins, and for some companies, the presence of toxins has now been confirmed. Multiple babies have become sick and it's not right that this has been allowed to happen. Companies should be taking more responsibility for their baby products. I have had to switch formula twice, be worried about sourcing new formula and worried whether the new one will also make my baby sick...again!

action: Lower the cost of British Citizenship applications to £800
background: We think the current cost of applying for British citizenship is disproportionately high and creates a real barrier for people who have lived, worked, and paid taxes in the UK for many years.
additional_details: The actual administrative cost is around £575, yet applicants are charged £1605. Citizenship should reflect integration and contribution, not financial privilege. Reducing the fee to £800 would be fair, transparent, and just make it easier to apply for many people.

action: Restrict HGV's to first two lanes of smart motorways to improve flow of traffic
background: HGV's can often reduce the flow of traffic in the 3rd lane of smart motorways, essentially creating a bottleneck. The Government should restrict HGV's to the first two lanes. During busy times smart motorway signals can be used to restrict access to the third lane.
additional_details: Varying speed limits on motorways is a helpful way of controlling the flow of traffic, but we believe that the fact that HGV's swap lanes to overtake slower vehicle creates a rolling roadblock for other road users, restricting line of sight for everyone else in order to adjust their driving for traffic movements ahead.  Restricting HGVs to the first two lanes could be run as a trial on selected motorways to determine the impact.

action: Provide funding to repair severe potholes and compensate drivers
background: Provide funding to resurface and properly repair affected roads. Ensure local authorities have adequate resources to maintain roads safely. Review compensation processes so drivers are not left out of pocket for damage caused by neglected road infrastructure
additional_details: Many vehicles have been damaged due to severe potholes, costing people hundreds or even thousands of pounds in repairs. Potholes can not only cause financial hardship but also create a serious safety hazard for road users. No one should have to risk an accident or vehicle damage simply by using a public road. Prompt action is needed.

action: Require essential services to have phone and face to face options
background: The Government should require essential services, including the NHS, banks, utilities and public bodies keep telephone and in person access. Digital only systems risk excluding older, disabled and low income people who cannot reliably use online services.
additional_details: As more services move to online only, many people are being locked out of vital healthcare, banking and public support. Not everyone has the skills, confidence or connectivity to use digital systems, creating barriers to medical care, financial security and daily needs. We urge the Government to require essential services to offer staffed phone lines, face to face access and protections for those unable to use digital systems.

action: Bring back mortgage relief for landlords on rental properties.
background: Labour's policies don't work; they made it completely unworkable. All for helping good tenants find good landlords. They pushed out both, bringing back tax relief on mortgages for landlords, which would help more properties return to the rental market. Stop giving corporations the advantages.
additional_details: Help landlords and tenants, Labour's policies don't work; they made it completely stupid. All for helping good tenants find good landlords. additional_details: Some consumers are increasingly interested in less processed food and in supporting small and local dairy farmers by allowing licensed sales of unpasteurised milk in supermarkets, with proper safety standards and clear labelling, would make it easier to access, while ensuring public safety and allowing adults decide to make their own informed decisions and respecting people's freedom to choose. This would also help shift sales into a properly regulated system.

action: Hold media outlets responsible

Media Truth Law
