In addition to this, the department shall have the authority to award mandatory compensation, to similar levels, the individual or company would have received had they pursued legal action.
rejection_details:
We are not clear how this would be different to the role currently carried out by OfCom and IPSO. 

You could start a petition focused on mandatory compensation outside the court system.

action: Make school libraries statutory in all secondary schools
background: We think all secondary schools should have a school library with a dedicated full-time librarian, and that this needs to be compulsory for all secondary schools and not simply an optional "bolt-on" depending on how individual headteachers feel about libraries and literacy provision.
additional_details: If we are serious, as a society and as a government, about tackling educational inequality, barriers to literacy and poor reading levels (which naturally affect other areas of communication and self-expression for our students), then, in our view, a staffed library is an essential tool in that endeavour. Students and parents deserve to know that these facilities and opportunities will always be available to them in school, and not taken away in the name of "funding cuts."

action: Create Lilo’s Law to require reporting after hitting pets
background: Introduce legislation known as “Lilo’s Law” to require drivers to stop and report when they hit a domestic pet, including cats, and to make it an offence to leave an injured or deceased animal on the road without reporting it.
additional_details:
There is currently no legal requirement for drivers to stop or report collisions involving domestic pets such as cats. As a result, injured or deceased animals can be left on the road, causing unnecessary suffering and distress for both animals and their owners.

Introducing a legal duty to stop and report would improve animal welfare, encourage responsible driving, and give families clarity and closure when incidents occur
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition, which calls for similar action: "Legislate to require drivers to report collisions with cats" https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750612

It is already a requirement to report collisions with dogs: https://www.gov.uk/report-dead-animal

action: Create a single national opt-out from secondary use of personal data
background: Create a legally enforceable, single national system allowing individuals to opt out of non-essential or secondary use of their personal data by public bodies and their external technology contractors. The opt-out must be simple, universal, and transparently enforced.
additional_details: As public services become more data-driven, personal data is often used beyond its original purpose, including by external technology contractors similar to high-profile analytics firms. While such use can support planning and research, people should retain meaningful control. A single national opt-out would strengthen privacy, improve trust, and support UK GDPR principles while allowing essential services to continue safely.

action: Launch an independent inquiry into foreign influence & dark money in UK politics
background: We urge the Government to investigate and report on foreign-linked funding, dark money networks, and lobbying influence affecting UK political parties and senior political decision-making.
additional_details: Recent public concerns have highlighted the potential for foreign states, wealthy individuals, and offshore-linked entities to exert influence through political donations, indirect funding routes, lobbying, media support, and pressure surrounding major political appointments. We believe existing safeguards may be insufficient.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:

 https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/760050

action: Add Politics & Economics lessons to the secondary school curriculum
background: We would like the government to enforce mandatory education about how politics and economics work within a society. It could start in secondary school in year 8 and teach the basics of society. It could cover how Parliament works and the economy (stocks, investing and shares etc).
additional_details: The cost of living crisis is increasing rapidly. 62% of adults in Great Britain reported that their cost of living had increased in the period from 1 October 2025 to 4 January 2026. Now, if you imagine young adults going into this world of inflation, politics and taxes with no prior knowledge how would you expect them to survive? we think the simple answer is they wouldn’t. We need to teach this so that people can live adult life. Furthermore, the voting age is looking to be lowered to 16 soon, so it is more crucial for young people to have knowledge on this area.

action: Extend Mother and Baby Units to admit mothers with babies older than 1 year
background: Currently Mother and Baby Units admit mothers until their baby is 1 years old. We want the Government to review this and extend this past the 1-year mark.
additional_details: In our view, some mothers are being discharged from Mother and Baby Units while still severely unwell, leading to prolonged postnatal mental illness. I was discharged while actively suicidal, and my recovery took almost four years. As the postnatal period is recognised as lasting up to two years, specialist MBU funding must extend to reflect this clinical reality.

action: Bring Netball into the Olympics
background:
We would like the Government to speak to the International Olympic Committee about adding netball to the Olympic games.
We have all played netball since we were in year three and since then we have played and trained netball at high standards. We would love to see netballers reach Team GB.
additional_details:
Students at many schools enjoy being able to expand their career in netball. Other sports will be in the Olympics, and the sports enjoyed will be showcased.
Other elite athletes get to train and get to compete in the Olympics but netball players only have the leagues, cups and titles. Other sports teams get to compete in the leagues, cups AND the Olympics. It is unfair that other sports get more opportunities. 
Netball, like many other sports, is beneficial to your physical and mental health.
rejection_details: We can't accept your petition because the UK Government and Parliament aren't responsible for the issue you raise. This is a decision for the International Olympic Committee.

action: Review Dangerous Dog Act 1991 and bring in dog ownership license and dog tagging
background: I want the Government to review Dangerous Dogs Act to bring in stricter penalties for out of control dogs, and require by law that all dog owners hold a dog owner license and that all dogs are tagged.
additional_details: We believe ensuring ALL dog owners have a licence will help prevent harm, neglect and abuse towards animals and to ensure animals are in safe hands. Animal victims of attacks should be tackled more seriously to keep them safe. Animals should only be given to an owner who has a valid dog owner licence. Any evidence of harm towards animals should have their licence removed to further prevent harm and abuse.

action: Ban the sale of Paan on health and environmental grounds
background: Pan masala is a toxic mix of areca nut and lime that is directly linked to oral cancer and mouth disease. It is often sold as a freshener, but its use can lead to addiction and a hazardous "red spit" habit. A national ban is vital to protect UK citizens and reduce the growing burden on our NHS.
additional_details: Beyond health, the habit causes massive environmental and financial damage. The "red spit" permanently stains pavements and buildings, requiring councils to spend thousands of pounds on specialist high-pressure cleaning. This is a direct waste of taxpayer money that should fund schools or social care. We believe a government ban is the only way to stop this biohazardous littering at the source, ensuring our public spaces remain clean and that local council budgets are protected from these avoidable costs

action: Include benefit income in Child Maintenance calculations
background: We call on the Government to reform Child Maintenance Service (CMS) rules so payments are based on a parent’s total income, including benefits, not just earnings.
additional_details:
Currently, a working parent earning around £2,000 per month may pay about £240 per child, per month while a parent receiving a similar amount through benefits pays only a flat rate of around £7 per week. This creates unfairness and reduces the financial support children receive.

The cost of raising a child does not change based on where a parent’s income comes from. CMS calculations should reflect the full financial position of both parents to ensure fairness and better support for children.

action: Reduce Interest on Student Loans & Cap Total Debt at One Year’s Average Salary
background:
We call on the Government to:
1 Reduce interest on student debt
2 Cap total student debt to one year’s average UK salary to ensure:
- No graduate leaves university with an unmanageable debt
- Repayments proportionate to earnings
- Public servants with lower incomes are not financially penalised
additional_details: As a graduate of 2003, I'm appalled that today’s graduates have university debts larger than the cost of my first home. In our view higher education is essential to the UK’s future prosperity, and free or affordable education has always been the backbone of advanced, socially mobile societies. I believe ours entrenches inequality through a disproportionate financial burden: those of lower income, disabled, ethnic minorities, female, transgender carry the heaviest burden. I believe this is unjust, unethical, and economically short sighted.

action: Set up an independent inquiry into West Indian children placed in ESN schools
background: We want the Government to commission an independent inquiry into the unfair placement of West Indian children into Educationally Sub Normal (ESN) schools from the 1950s to the early 1970s. This inquiry should closely examine assessment practices, institutional biases, and local authority decisions.
additional_details: Research shows that many children were mis-assessed, misunderstood, or discriminated against, leading to significant negative effects on their education, employment, and overall well-being that persist from the 1950s until 2026. We believe more research is required to understand why this happened to intelligent Black children back then to understand why Black children are more likely to be labelled with special educational needs today, setting the groundwork for acknowledgment, healing, and reparative actions.

action: Require & fund the assignment of a caseworker to every domestic abuse victim
background: Victims of domestic abuse are often required to navigate police, courts, housing and family law alone. Many are penalised for not understanding complex legal systems or procedures. A dedicated case worker could provide continuity, guidance and support from first disclosure to case conclusion.
additional_details: Without consistent guidance, victims of domestic abuse may face confusion, delays and repeated trauma. Many make mistakes simply because they do not understand legal or administrative systems, which can affect safety, housing and child arrangements. A dedicated case worker could reduce harm, improve outcomes, and ensure survivors are supported rather than disadvantaged. We believe protecting victims of domestic abuse from further harm is essential for a fair and safe society.

action: Abolish interest on university tuition fees and maintenance loans in England.
background: We call on the Government to abolish interest on university tuition fees and maintenance loans in England. Charging interest disproportionately targets working-class students who rely on loans to access higher education, deepening inequality and entrenching classism in our education system.
additional_details: Abolishing interest on university tuition fees and maintenance loans is necessary to ensure higher education is fair and accessible. Interest inflates debt far beyond what students borrow, creating long-term financial pressure that discourages participation and limits social mobility. Removing interest would make repayment fairer, reduce inequality, and support economic stability in England.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756832

action: Give the public the right to vote for a new Government. Call a General Election.
background: Call a general election. The public has no confidence in this Government.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

action: Make Solar Affordable: Tax Relief, NI Deduction, 0% VAT
background: Families who want to install solar panels still face high upfront costs. With energy bills rising and households under pressure, the Government should support people who are trying to reduce their costs and reduce demand on the national grid.
additional_details: We are calling for: Income tax relief, NI deduction and permanent 0% VAT rate on all domestic solar & battery installations, similar to the incentives that helped EV gain widespread adoption. This would reduce cost by 20-45% and bring the return on investment down to 4–6 years, making clean energy affordable for ordinary families. These changes would help households save money, strengthen the UK’s energy security and accelerate progress toward net‑zero, without requiring large government grants.

action: Make A ICE (Immigration Customs Enforcement) In The United Kingdom
background:
Make A ICE (Immigration Customs Enforcement) In The United Kingdom. 

So ICE can deport immigrants from the United Kingdom back the there original country for back to a different country. 

We call upon the government to take this very seriously to make sure this is done properly.
additional_details:
The streets are getting out of hand with crimes committed daily by illegal immigrants and others.
You put them in hotels that barely a British citizen can afford to stay in for a week this needs to stop NOW.
rejection_details:
Petitions need to call on the Government or Parliament to take a specific action.

We're not sure exactly what clear action which is not currently happening that you'd like the Government or Parliament to carry out.

The UK already has Immigration Enforcement (IE), which is an operational arm of the Home Office and responsible for removing people who have illegally entered the UK.

You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you would like the Government or Parliament to do in relation to immigration enforcement in the UK.

action: Scrap the planned VED increases on 20 year old vehicles
background: The government is planning to roll out VED increases on older cars, which in our view, are barely worth the amount in tax they want to impose on the public even though no one has voted for it. £760 for a 20-year-old car, we think constitutes daylight robbery.
additional_details: This was not voted on by the public. We think it’s a constant war on motorists to fulfil an agenda the public hasn’t directly voted for. In our view this will hit the poorest and force millions of older cars off the roads, cars that are MOTd and serviced and are in good order, cars that have already been taxed to death and with little financial worth but a lot of worth to the owners.

action: Limit Repeat Abortions
background: We call on the Government to set a limit on the number of abortions someone can have, except in cases of abuse, rape or medical need.
additional_details: This petition calls for compassionate regulations to limit repeat abortions, while fully protecting access in cases of rape, abuse, coercion, or serious risk to the woman’s or baby’s health. In our view abortion should not be used as a substitute for contraception. We believe greater safeguards, education, and access to effective contraception are needed to support women, reduce repeat procedures, and protect life through responsible, trauma-informed care.

action: Introduce amnesty for migrants already in the UK without visa
background: The government should introduce a carefully designed amnesty for approximately 500,000 + migrants without visas already embedded in the UK economy. In our view, this would not be about encouraging new arrivals, but ensuring those already here could find work.
additional_details: Some modelling suggests that such an amnesty could be positive for the UK economy as it could increase labour market participation. Tax receipts could also rise as wages could move from cash-in-hand to formal contracts subject to income tax and National Insurance. In our view, these gains align with the Migration Advisory Committee's findings that working-age migrants in employment make substantial net positive contributions, particularly when benefit access is initially limited.

action: Only require disclosure of role-relevant convictions to employers and regulators
background: Reform the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act so employees are only required to disclose to employers and licensing bodies criminal record information that is directly relevant to a role.
additional_details: We feel the current disclosure system allows employers to see irrelevant convictions, enabling hidden discrimination against rehabilitated people and undermining the purpose of criminal justice. This can limit employment, increase reoffending, and waste talent. Restricting disclosure to role-relevant convictions could improve fairness, support rehabilitation, boost productivity and tax revenue, and protect public safety.

action: Fund NHS access to Omaveloxolone for patients with Friedreich's Ataxia
background: We call on the Government to fund NHS access to Omaveloxolone in the UK.  We believe the drug should also be considered under the HST programme, which we feel is the only appraisal route which reflects the realities of Friedreich's Ataxia. This is a degenerative disease & time is of the essence.
additional_details: Friedreich's Ataxia patients need access to the drug Omaveloxolone, the only drug available for this disease. Without treatment, this degenerative disease can get worse. Patients & families may have to see their loved ones deteriorate when they are aware there is a drug available to stop the progression of this disease & in many cases, to improve the symptoms. The drug is available in EU countries & America. It passed the safety test in April 2025 and we believe it should be available on the NHS!

action: Change the law to give pedestrians priority at unmarked crossings
background: Change the law so pedestrians have clear legal priority at unmarked crossings, including dropped kerbs and pedestrian islands, wherever crossing infrastructure exists, including at side roads and in residential and urban areas.
additional_details: Many crossings are clearly designed for pedestrian use but lack zebra markings, meaning drivers often do not stop. This can create unsafe and confusing situations and make pedestrian priority feel optional. We believe where crossing infrastructure exists, pedestrians must have priority by default, especially in busy urban and residential areas, including near parks and schools.

action: Ban spitting by players and staff in professional football stadiums
background: To work with The FA, the Premier League, and other football authorities to introduce rules banning spitting by players and coaching staff anywhere within professional football stadiums, including the field of play, touchlines, and technical areas, with appropriate sanctions during matches.
additional_details:
Spitting is normalised in professional football. Bodily fluids within these environments pose H&S risk to everyone working in close proximity.
footballers & coaches are visible role models. Spitting during TV matches encourages imitation by children at grassroots level. 
The IFAB already punish spitting at another person. This should be extended to all spitting within football. Other elite sports have high standards of conduct without spitting & football should meet the same expectations.

action: Change the law on intestacy rules
background:
I would like the law around intestacy rules to change, I feel that a lot of people don't realise how this law can affect people's lives.
A half brother, sister, aunt who has known the deceased person may be excluded due to finding a person who did not know the deceased existed classed as full blood
additional_details:
I feel that the law is outdated and wrong that someone who never knew a deceased person existed can come before the people who have loved and taken care of said person all their lives.
Half blood Aunt who brought up the deceased could lose out to a full blood decendent who knows nothing about the deceased.
If this is the case I'm sure most people would rather the government have it than a complete stranger.
rejection_details:
We understand that you want to change how current intestacy rules work, but we're not exactly sure what change you'd like to see. 

You could start a new petition explaining how you'd like them to be changed. For example you could start a new petition calling for half blood relations to be treated the same as full blood relations within intestacy rules. You could also start a new petition calling for knowledge of the deceased to be taken into account in some way within intestacy rules.

action: Launch an inquiry into road maintenance & publish road tax spending
background: We would like the Government to launch an inquiry into awful road conditions and what can be done to make them more reliable in the future. The inquiry should investigate the materials and companies involved in building roads, and finding better solutions, as we feel our roads are not suitable.
additional_details: Road tax statistics should also be published to show where they money is being used. Many people all over the UK experience the same issues with roads falling apart and not lasting a significant length of time. Potholes are rife and are causing significant damage to vehicles in many areas. The cost of living is already high for many and having more reliable roads could mean less money being spent on car repairs that are becoming more expensive to fix.

action: Reduce Student Loan Plan 2 interest rate to be that of Plans 1, 4 & 5.
background: Reduce Student Loan Plan 2 interest rate to be the same as that paid by students on Plans 1, 4 & 5. This would reduce the interest rate to 3.2%, from 6.2%.
additional_details: We think that this will permit younger people to be able to repay their loans to the UK Government, reducing the overall national debt. In addition, this will empower the financial freedom of those on Plan 2 (c.640,000 people), and combat current challenges they face, such as the graduate labour market and astronomical housing costs, in turn boosting the UK economy.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759969

action: That it be a requirement that all members of Parliament publish tax returns.
background: That to remain a Member of the House of Lords and the House of Commons, said members must publicly publish full details of their Tax returns. Any Member failing to comply within 30 days of the end of said tax year will be expelled from the respective House.
additional_details: All Legislators acting on behalf of and in the interest of the people of the United Kingdom should be open and transparent. We the people of the United Kingdom have the right to know what and who’s money is being given to our Legislators.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Require parliamentary candidates publish five years of tax returns
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750212

action: Require all emergency services to record staff suicides
background: There is no mandatory system for recording suicides among emergency service staff, which could lead to underreporting and opportunities for prevention. Mandatory recording could reveal the true scale of the problem and enable effective, evidence-based support to protect those who protect the public.
additional_details: I want the government to do this because without mandatory recording, I believe the true scale of suicides among emergency service staff is hidden, patterns are missed, and opportunities to prevent deaths are lost. I believe accurate data is essential to create effective mental health support, policies, and protections for those who risk their lives to protect the public.

action: Extend Paid Maternity Leave to 18 Months to Support Child Development.
background: We, the undersigned, respectfully petition the Government to extend paid maternity leave until a child reaches 18 months of age, and to provide parents with the opportunity to remain at home with their babies for longer during this critical period of development.
additional_details:
The first 18 months of a child’s life are a crucial period for physical growth, emotional security, brain development, and attachment. Extensive research shows that stable, responsive caregiving in early life lays the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and wellbeing.
Despite this, many parents are currently required to return to work well before their child even reaches 12 months, often due to financial necessity rather than choice. This can child development & parental mental health.

action: Donations to a political party capped at £500,000 per individual or organisation
background: Donations to political parties, from an individual or organisation, should be limited to £500,000 across total donations. We think this could reduce the influence of unelected and foreign individuals on UK politics.
additional_details: Currently, in our view, too many domestic and foreign individuals and companies are using money to secure their own interests within our parliament. The population of the UK should be parliaments primary concern, our well-being should be the nations priority. We believe politics has become an industry, where influence is bought and sold through political donations, and that it is unhealthy for our four nations and breeds distrust in those we elect to govern us. We believe a cap on donations is required to restore trust.

action: Stop illegal immigrants getting council houses
background: The government should not be giving illegals council houses to get them out of hotels, the government should return them to their home country
additional_details: Illegal immigrants should not be given council or social housing, the illegals must be returned to their home country, the government should also stop these illegals from entering British territorial waters amd return the boats back to France by whatever means necessary,  council housing should only be given to the British people and not to illegals
rejection_details:
We're not sure if you want all those who arrive illegally to be deported and not allowed to apply for asylum, or if you want to stop the government scheme through which councils can apply for grants to build council housing for asylum seekers. You could start a new petition explaining clearly what you'd like to happen. 

You may wish to sign these petitions which are currently open: 

Withdraw from ECHR & stop processing asylum claims until Channel crossings stop: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741099

Deport asylum seekers from safe countries & review current asylum seekers: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/741209

Detain anyone arriving in the UK illegally: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759367

action: Restructure child maintenance payments
background: Many families struggling financially while non-paying parents evade accountability. There needs to be stronger enforcement powers, improved tracking methods for non-paying parents without fixed addresses, thorough income verification, realistic arrears repayment, and strengthen enforcement action.
additional_details: Non paying parents should not get away with not paying support for their children.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739525

action: Ensure fair access to suitable vehicles under the Motability scheme
background: I’d like the Government to allow Motability customers to access luxury vehicles just as a person who can work can.
additional_details: I believe that if people who are capable of working are able to make enough money to buy luxury cars, then it is fair for Motability to allow disabled people to buy luxury cars. Motability customers still had to pay a large deposit for those cars so it’s not as though they were getting them for free. And the only reason they’re unable to work and earn the money to purchase these kind of cars themselves is because of restrictions due to their disability.

action: Grant an Open Work Permit after five years on the Skilled Worker route
background: Introduce an open work permit for Skilled Worker visa holders after completing five years on the route, if the settlement qualifying period is extended to ten years, allowing workers to change employers while remaining subject to immigration control and no access to public funds
additional_details: Skilled Worker visa holders entered the UK based on a clear commitment that settlement would be available after five years. Extending this to ten years without flexibility is unfair and restrictive. An open work permit after five years would reduce exploitation risks, support career progression, protect mental health and family stability, and allow workers to continue contributing to the UK economy through employment, taxation, and business creation.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/747176

action: Allow mothers to stay with children in foster care when parenting isn’t the risk
background: Introduce and expand mother-and-child foster care placements where children are removed due to external risks such as domestic abuse, housing issues or crisis situations, but where the mother has not been found to pose a safeguarding risk to the child.
additional_details: Many children are placed into foster care due to circumstances such as domestic abuse, housing problems or lack of support rather than poor parenting. Separating children from a safe and loving parent causes unnecessary trauma. When children are removed despite no evidence of harm from the parent, it can lead to emotional distress, attachment difficulties, anxiety and poorer long-term outcomes, even in safe foster placements. Keeping families together with support would better protect children.

action: Increase funding for veteran-led organisation supporting veterans into work
background: We call on the Government to fund and support veteran-led organisations delivering training and employment for veterans who have fallen outside transition support, enabling them to move into sustainable work and reducing long-term reliance on welfare and crisis services across the UK.
additional_details: We believe many veterans miss or fall outside existing transition support and later face unemployment or instability. In our view, veteran-led organisations provide structured training and direct employment pathways but struggle to access funding due to rigid commissioning systems. Increased government funding could allow these programmes to expand nationally, helping veterans into long-term work while reducing reliance on welfare, housing and crisis services.

action: Repair and resurface the road due to severe pothole damage
background: We want the Government to ensure the local authority inspects the road, carries out proper repairs, and resurfaces it where necessary. Temporary patching is not sufficient, and long-term repairs are needed to make the road safe.
additional_details: The road has multiple deep potholes that are damaging vehicles, increasing repair costs for residents, and creating safety risks for drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. The poor condition of the road has been ongoing and requires urgent action to prevent accidents and further damage.
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign this petition which calls for similar action:

'Provide funding to repair severe potholes and compensate drivers'
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/760312

action: Add ‘Security Officer’ to the recognised profession list on GOV passport website
background: The position of ‘Security Officer’ should be added to the recognised profession list in order to be able to countersign for passport applications.
additional_details: All Security Officers in the security industry are licensed and have a clean criminal record and are trusted to keep the public safe. They should be a recognised profession.

action: Give private vehicle owners access to diagnostic tools and repair information
background: Extend existing Right to Repair rules so private vehicle owners can legally access manufacturer diagnostic software, service procedures, and repair information on a paid, regulated basis, with appropriate safeguards, similar to access already available to independent repairers.
additional_details: Modern vehicles rely on software for fault diagnosis and routine maintenance. Private owners are excluded from official diagnostic access despite owning their vehicles, increasing repair costs and limiting consumer choice. This also encourages reliance on unofficial or unverified tools, creating safety, cybersecurity, and reliability risks. Legal, regulated access would support safe repairs, reduce waste, and strengthen consumer ownership rights.

action: Reduce vehicle tax rates by 50% for vehicles registered up to 31 March 2017
background: Reduce vehicle/road /VED tax by at least 50% for cars registered up to 31 March 2017. In our view, the current costs are not realistic, unfair, and extortionate and further promotes the disposable, uneconomic car culture that results from serviceable vehicles being scrapped.
additional_details:
We think the current vehicle tax amounts are extremely illogical, unrealistic, and 
extortionate.

As stated the current associated cost within this band further promote the ‘throw away’ culture, costing (otherwise perfectly serviceable) older vehicles off the road. Manufacture of new vehicles creates massive economic (resource and emissions) debt. Keeping an older vehicle well maintained and running is greener than manufacturing a new one. We would like the tax rates to be reassessed logically and fairly.

action: Sort out the uk roads ! Or we stop paying road tax !
background: Sort out 90% of the uk roads as the potholes are beyond ridiculous !
additional_details: Because we all pay road tax and the roads are getting worse ! You make us get an MOT to ensure our cars are ok for the roads .. yet the roads aren't good enough for our cars
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Fix Our Roads: National Plan on Dangerous Potholes Now
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/739014

action: Guarantee in law that the NHS can never be abolished
background: The NHS is one of the greatest achievements of any government, anywhere in the world. Please enshrine in law that it will never be abolished or replaced unless by an absolute overall majority in a national referendum
additional_details: The NHS protects the most vulnerable in our society from the costs we see in societies such as the United States where citizens have to choose between priortising healthcare or paying household bills/putting food on the table. Whilst it currently has flaws and is underfunded it should be an unalienable right for all UK citizens, morally and compassionately it should be a fundamental human right.
rejection_details: It's unclear how this could be accomplished as one Parliament cannot bind its successor as both are sovereign bodies in their own right.

action: Investigate the failures in the administration of Civil Service Pensions
background: We call on Parliament to investigate the ongoing and systemic failures in the administration of civil service pensions. These failures have left thousands of current and former civil servants in limbo, waiting excessive periods for pension payments they are entitled to.
additional_details:
The delays have caused significant financial hardship, emotional distress, and insecurity for individuals who have planned their retirements in good faith.

Parliament should scrutinise Capita’s handling of pension administration, the government’s oversight of the contract, and what immediate action is required to resolve outstanding cases, prevent further harm, and provide redress to those affected.

action: Make failure to indicate a specific road safety offence
background: Introduce clearer enforcement, fines and penalty points for drivers who fail to indicate when changing lanes, overtaking or turning. Treat failure to signal as a specific road safety offence, except where indicating is genuinely unnecessary.
additional_details: We believe failure to indicate is a widespread and dangerous behaviour that causes collisions and near misses. Motorcyclists, cyclists and pedestrians are especially at risk as they rely on clear signals to react safely. Indicators are a basic driving requirement, yet lack of enforcement means many drivers ignore them. Proper penalties could improve road awareness, reduce accidents and save lives.

action: Start a general public petion to call a general election urgently
background: No confidence in this Labour Government the country needs a general election urgently
additional_details: As explained above
rejection_details:
You may wish to sign the following petition, which calls for similar action:

Dissolve Parliament and call a General Election now!
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/750050

action: Ban AI translation
background: Ban AI translation applications. Highly trained and qualified translators are losing pay and even their jobs due to the rise of AI translation, despite humans accurately translating language and culture-specific nuances which machines cannot fully grasp.
additional_details: The amount of jobs available for translators is rapidly decreasing, and those which are available are mostly post-editing, which takes the same amount of time or longer, often for less pay. We feel this is an unnecessary threat to a crucial industry which helps connect people across the globe. Furthermore, AI produces lower-quality translations, resulting in the purpose and meaning of source texts being inaccurately conveyed. This can be damaging for the creator of the source text as well as the target audience.

action: Raise the Expense rates for salary Sacrifice Electric Vehicles
background: We ask Government to raise the expense rate for public EV charging on salary sacrifice vehicles, as we believe the current 14p per mile is unrealistic as public charging costs continue to rise, leaving drivers out of pocket simply for doing their jobs. Fair rates are essential.
additional_details: The Government has in our view mistakenly classified Salary Sacrifice cars as company vehicles, restricting mileage expense claims to HMRC mandated company car rates of 7p for home charging and 14p for Public Charging. Unlike conventional company cars, salary sacrifice employees cover the lease, maintenance, insurance, and BIK tax, while employers only cover minimal admin costs. We think treating them the same penalises drivers for choosing greener transport and risks discouraging EV uptake.

action: Remove all interest from Plan 2 student loans and recalculate balances
background: Remove all interest from Plan 2 student loans and recalculate outstanding balances as if no interest had been applied since the loans were issued.
additional_details: Plan 2 student loan borrowers are charged high interest while studying and after graduation, causing balances to grow even when repayments are made. Many graduates will repay far more than they borrowed or never clear their loan. In our view, borrowers had no choice over being placed on Plan 2 or its terms. We think removing interest and recalculating balances would restore fairness, improve trust in the student finance system, and ensure repayments reflect the original cost of study.

action: Registered keeper to be held responsible for hit & runs if driver not identified
background: We want registered keepers to be held responsible for hit and runs if the driver fails to admit liability.
additional_details: The registered keeper is held responsible for most things including parking tickets,  maintaining the vehicle, insuring and taxing. To avoid unnecessary stress, eliminate blaming and for responsibility to be taken, I believe this will have a significant change so in the event of a hit & run, the registered keeper is held responsible.

action: Classify Organised Grooming and Rape Gangs as Domestic Terrorism under Law
background: Organised rape gangs operate through systematic sexual exploitation, coercion, violence, & intimidation, primarily targeting vulnerable children and young people. These crimes are not isolated offences but coordinated, ongoing campaigns that instil fear, silence victims, to undermine public safety.
additional_details:
These activities meet many of the key elements we think commonly define domestic terrorism, including organised criminal action, the use of violence and intimidation, and the deliberate targeting of a civilian population to exert control and silence: 
Multiple perpetrators
Structured roles
Long-term operations Intimidation & control
Threats, violence, blackmail
Victims and communities living in fear
Systemic harm sometimes on racial or religious grounds
Repeated offences over years
Institutional failures to intervene

action: URGENT: Call for Review of Child Sexual Offence Sentencing and Prison Expansion
background: Review sentencing for all child sexual offences now. I urge mandatory prison for all child sex offences and whole life orders for physical child sex abuse. The government must build more prisons to ensure capacity and end leniency. Child predators can NOT be rehabilitated.
additional_details: Child abuse causes lifelong psychological trauma that current sentences often fail to reflect. Mandatory prison terms are essential to provide a true deterrent and ensure justice for victims. For those who have physically abused children, whole-life orders are necessary to eliminate the risk of reoffending and protect the public permanently. We must build more prisons so that capacity never dictates justice. Child predators can NOT be rehabilitated.

action: Allocate more childcare funding for working parents
background: The government makes extra funding available for childcare costs and holiday clubs if: parents are in work and claiming Universal Credit; and if the child is eligible for free school meals respectively. This funding should also be available to working parents who fall outside these criteria.
additional_details: Offering extra funding has multiple benefits: it would allow more parents, carers and guardians to take up full time work without worrying about high childcare costs, care givers are currently working to pay nursery and childcare fees. During the school holidays, they are left finding childcare or forced to take the little annual leave they have left whilst holiday clubs are funded for children on free school meals, whose parents may be on benefits. Open this funding up more widely.

action: Lower pension age for physically demanding jobs to 62
background: Introduce a reduced state pension age of 62 for people who have worked long-term in physically demanding occupations.
additional_details: Many workers in construction, care, manufacturing and similar roles experience physical decline earlier due to years of manual labour. A flexible or reduced pension age would recognise the physical toll of these jobs and support fairness in retirement. Workers who have contributed over 35 years in physically demanding jobs should be eligible to claim there state pension at 62 without financial reduction.

action: Call general election amid collapse in public confidence in PM & Government
background: We ask the Government to call an immediate General Election so the public can decide whether the current Prime Minister and Government still have a democratic mandate to govern.
additional_details: Public confidence in the Prime Minister has significantly declined due to ongoing political instability, internal division, and lack of clear leadership. At a time of major economic and social challenges, the UK needs stable leadership with public consent. A General Election is the appropriate democratic mechanism to restore trust and legitimacy.

action: Halt the deletion of Court records and preserve open justice
background:
We call on the Government to immediately halt the deletion of court records held by Courtsdesk and to preserve this archive in full pending independent review.
It was created as part of a government-approved pilot to improve transparency and media access.
additional_details:
The Ministry of Justice has ordered the deletion of this archive on data protection grounds, yet no specific breach has been publicly identified. 

Deleting the entire archive is an irreversible and disproportionate response when less extreme options, such as redaction or restricted access, are available.

Destroying these records would permanently erase evidence of how the justice system has operated, prevent scrutiny of past decisions, and undermine public confidence in the courts.
rejection_details:

action: Ban engagement-driven algorithms that push provocative content on social media
background: Introduce laws to severely limit engagement-driven algorithms that push emotionally provocative news and political content. Require simple, non-algorithmic or chronological feeds by default, and give users a clear option to turn off behaviour-influencing content ranking.
additional_details:
In the past, people chose when to watch the news. Today, social media places a permanent stream of news, arguments and outrage in our pockets, driven by algorithms designed to trigger emotional responses.
 
These systems use the same psychological techniques once used in advertising to sell products, but now apply them continuously to beliefs, emotions and identity. We believe that this constant exposure is harming mental health, increasing division, and affecting how people think and vote, without meaningful consent or an off switch.

action: Automatically suspend PR when a parent is convicted of child murder/serious harm
background:
Current legislation ensures the automatic suspension of parental responsibility (PR) in cases where one parent murders another.
 
However, there is currently NO automatic suspension of PR when a parent is convicted of seriously harming or murdering their child.
additional_details:
I'm asking the government to create 'Charlie's Law' to spare families the pain of perpetrators being able to maintaining influence and power over their children from prison.
 
Please support my campaign for Charlie’s Law and sign and share this petition.

action: Require employers to manage psychosocial risks like stress & poor mental health
background: Introduce a legal requirement for employers to identify, assess & manage psychosocial risks like stress and poor mental health caused by work due to for example workload, job design, management practices & workplace culture. This could raise the importance in line with physical health & safety risks
additional_details: Work related stress and mental ill health are major causes of sickness absence, reduced productivity, and lives lost. In our view, current laws in this area are unclear and inconsistently applied, leading to reactive responses rather than prevention. We believe clear legislation in this area could protect workers, give employers certainty, support enforcement, and ensure mental safety is managed as seriously as physical safety.

action: Implement compulsory voting in General Elections
background: Make the voting mandatory for everyone or they will have to pay a fine for not voting because a lot of people are not voting, and the percentage of people voting in the UK is decreasing. To maintain democratic freedom of choice, this should include a 'None of the Above' option on all ballot papers.
additional_details: It will help to increase voter turnout (higher % of citizens voting) in General Elections as low voter turnout risks legitimacy of our democracy. With compulsory voting more people will be politically active so that will make the Government represent everyone as people of all ages (above 18) are voting so the Government party will want to reflect the will of the entire nation

action: Make Religious Education optional for students from Year 7 to Year 13
background: We want the Government to reform the school curriculum by making Religious Education an optional subject for all students between Years 7 and 13 to allow non-religious students to have their own beliefs and not have religion enforced on them.
additional_details: We feel that religious education is not necessary for student education, could make anyone at a school feel uncomfortable with their own religion (non-religion) and ensure inclusivity towards all.

action: Ban the use of choke chains and choke leads on dogs
background: We call on the UK Government to ban the use, sale, and promotion of choke chains, choke leads, and other aversive restraint devices on dogs, due to their proven risks to animal welfare and wellbeing.
additional_details:
Choke chains and choke leads tighten around a dog’s neck and can cause pain, injury, and distress. They may damage the trachea, spine, and neck, and can increase fear, anxiety, and behavioural problems.
 
Veterinary and canine behaviour experts support humane, reward-based training methods, which are safer and more effective. Harnesses and flat collars provide suitable alternatives without causing harm.
 
Despite this, choke leads remain legal and widely available. This is inconsistent with modern animal welfare standards and puts many dogs at unnecessary risk.
 
We ask the Government to introduce legislation to ban these devices and promote humane dog training.

action: Mandatory pausing of civil court actions during domestic abuse investigations
background: Introduce a requirement to pause or restrict civil family court actions, including occupation and financial orders, where there is an active domestic abuse criminal investigation or prosecution, unless there is a clear safeguarding necessity
additional_details: Victims of domestic abuse are often re-traumatised when alleged perpetrators use civil courts to continue control through housing, finances, or children while criminal proceedings are ongoing. This can create an imbalance of power, increase harm, and undermine justice. We believe safeguards are needed to prevent further abuse until criminal matters are concluded.

action: Seek a global ban on superintelligence and to agree safe AI development path
background: We call on the Government to seek a global agreement that bans the development of artificial superintelligence and to encourage the establishment of a globally accepted safe path for developing advanced AI, ensuring strong safety standards and international coordination.
additional_details: Some leaders of major AI companies and top experts have warned that advanced AI could pose significant risks. Some companies are actively pursuing superintelligence despite these warnings. The UK Government should act now to help prevent a dangerous global race and work with other nations to seek a safe, internationally coordinated approach to advanced AI development.

action: Conduct review of treatment of teachers in schools & colleges & mitigations
background: We believe there needs to be a review of the treatment of teachers in schools, and consideration of whether new policies and frameworks could better protect them from abuse.
additional_details: We believe cameras in class rooms, independent audits of administrative practices and school leadership processes could help provide teachers with a better work environment. The Government should conduct a review and present its findings to Parliament. I have chosen to share my story openly through a short film called Swallow exposing harsh realities rarely seen on screen.

action: Give Leuchars Station back to RAF Control.
background: I want the Government to recognise the historic and strategic importance that RAF Leuchars held for nearly 100 years, and to consider returning Leuchars Station to RAF control.
additional_details: RAF Leuchars was one of the most important RAF bases in the UK when it was under RAF control. Leuchars also hosted a major airshow, which brought in income for the base and organisation, as well as tourism for the local area. Bringing Leuchars Station back under RAF control would help ensure that local businesses could benefit once again. Leuchars Station also served as a major part in helping aircraft cross the Atlantic, as it is in a strong geographic position for transatlantic flights.

action: Make insurance cheaper for new drivers
background: Place some kind of limit on the amount of money that can be charged for new drivers for their insurance and help new drivers buy insurance and be able to drive.
additional_details: Some of us are very responsible new drivers and because of irresponsible and reckless drivers our insurance quotes just go up by horrendous amounts or no one wants to insure us. Increase the insurance of the reckless drivers, and not responsible ones.

action: Make the student loan system fairer for young people
background: Reverse the upcoming Plan 2 repayment threshold freeze, and restore it to the level it would be if it had risen each year with earnings growth as promised. Set student loan interest rates at CPI inflation, and reduce the repayment rate from 9% to 5%.
additional_details: Successive governments have made retrospective changes to the Plan 2 loan terms. Repeated threshold freezes alongside high interest rates for Plan 2 loans mean many will pay back far more than they borrowed. These proposed changes will remove the unfair above-inflation interest as well as helping to address the high marginal tax rates which are disincentivising young people. The changes will also give young people more ability to invest into the economy and their futures.

action: Fund a new dedicated Good News channel to air daily
background: We call on the Government and Parliament to recognise the impact that constant negative news coverage has on public mental health, social cohesion and trust in media. Provide funding for a dedicated Good News free broadcast channel within public service broadcasting frameworks.
additional_details:
We ask Government and Parliament to act because they already shape broadcasting standards. Constant negative news harms mental wellbeing and trust. We feel public institutions can support a balanced, independent Good News channel that serves the public interest.
 
Imagine turning on the news and instead of your nervous system going into fight-or-flight, it does the opposite. People might start the day calmer. Less fear, less doom-scrolling, more perspective.

action: ILR after 5 years for main applicants, their dependants ILR after 10 years
background: We ask the Government to allow main applicants on family and work visas to be able to apply for ILR after 5 years. Their dependants can remain longer routes, including the 10-year route. We believe this gives stability to working families, improves integration, and maintains immigration control.
additional_details: In our view, many main applicants are already working, paying tax and meeting strict visa rules. Allowing them to gain ILR after 5 years could provide stability, reduce exploitation and help families integrate. We think dependants could still remain on longer routes to ILR, so this change would be fair, controlled and beneficial to the UK economy.

action: Bring back the death penalty for the most serious of crimes involving children.
background: I want the Government and Parliament to introduce legislation to allow the death penalty to be applied in the United Kingdom in the most serious cases involving crimes against children.
additional_details:
This would apply only to the most severe offences, where guilt has been proven beyond doubt through the full legal process, including appeals. The aim would be to ensure the strongest possible punishment is available for the worst crimes and to act as a deterrent.

I believe sentencing policy should reflect the seriousness of these offences and prioritise the protection of children and the public.

action: Forgive Plan 2 Student Loan Debt
background: Review whether Plan 2 Student Loans have been mis-sold under false terms and false advertising, and forgive the debts accordingly.
additional_details: It was falsely advertised that the repayment threshold would rise with inflation and that the debt would be a sensible, worthwhile investment. Instead, the repayment threshold has been repeatedly and unilaterally frozen. Extreme interest rates apply, more than typical mortgages, and beyond the understanding of an 18 year old. RPI is used when the UK gov typically uses CPI (lower). It was not accurately represented that the loan would become a 9% additional tax for our entire working lives.

action: Ban the Production and Sale of Lab-Grown Meat
background: We call on the UK Government to introduce legislation banning the production, sale, and importation of lab-grown (cell-cultured) meat for human consumption, following the precautionary approach already adopted by countries such as Italy.
additional_details:
We urge the Government to prohibit the commercial production, sale, and importation of lab-grown meat for human consumption in the UK in order to:
- Protect traditional livestock farming and rural economies
- Uphold high food safety, animal welfare, and transparency standards
- Apply the precautionary principle to novel food technologies

action: Abolish real interest rates on Plan 2 student loans.
background:
Over 5 million people who began university between 2012 and 2023 have a Plan 2 Student Loan. Many of these loans accrue interest at up to RPI + 3% (currently 6.2%).

The Government should abolish real interest on all Plan 2 student loans so that they only accrue interest at the rate of inflation.
additional_details:
Graduates with Plan 2 Student Loans must repay 9% of everything they earn over £28,470.

However, because of the high interest rates a typical graduate has to earn £66,000 just to keep pace with the interests. Most graduates are trapped into 30 years of debt and many will pay back far much more than they borrowed.

It would be fairer to align interest with the rate of inflation - as is the case for those who went to university before 2012 or after 2023 - so no-one pays back more they borrowed.

action: Reduce VAT to 5% on Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO), an alternative to Diesel
background: HVO is a viable alternative fuel to Diesel. Using it we believe that we can reuse our existing fuel infrastructure and vehicles and make use of a product to support an orderly transition to net zero in realistic timescales without reliance on imported electric vehicles made overseas.
additional_details: It’s green, proven to cut up to 90% of net CO2 emissions and it can be made in the UK but it’s charged at 20% VAT. So let’s encourage use and reduce VAT to 5%. A straightforward VAT reduction from 20% to 5% will bring it into closer parity with diesel prices. If home-based charging for electric vehicles is charged only 5% VAT, why should HVO be stuck at 20%?

action: Prohibit the Use of Mobile Devices During Formal Parliamentary Proceedings
background: We want the House of Commons to adopt rules to restrict MPs from using mobile phones and tablets during formal parliamentary proceedings. Clear guidance and appropriate sanctions should ensure compliance and maintain professional standards.
additional_details: Parliament sets the standard for public life. When MPs use personal devices during debates, it gives us the impression of distraction and a lack of seriousness. Most workplaces expect full attention during formal proceedings, and elected representatives should meet at least the same standard. We believe that restricting device use would reinforce professionalism, improve public confidence, and show respect for democratic debate.

action: Require offside adaptive headlights be fixed when driving over 50mph
background: We call for the Government to require offside adaptive headlights be fixed when driving on all dual carriageways and motorways and at speeds over 50mph.
additional_details: Lorry drivers can be dazzled because of their higher driving position and the cars' sensors may not see incoming traffic due to the safety barriers. Unregulated rules for adaptive headlights can impact drivers' eyes health and being dazzled can put other road users at risk.

action: Remove Business rates for Pubs and Restaurants

action: Should Shabana Mahmood step down over changes affecting migrants’ ILR rights?
background: We call on the Government to halt any mid-journey changes to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) rules and protect migrants who began their lawful settlement pathway under previous criteria. Fairness, legal certainty, and transitional protections must be upheld.
additional_details: Migrants who entered a lawful pathway to Indefinite Leave to Remain did so based on clear rules and legitimate expectations. Changing eligibility mid-journey undermines trust in the UK’s legal system, creates uncertainty for families, and risks unfair hardship. Policy reform should not penalise those who complied with existing requirements. The Government must uphold fairness, legal certainty, and transitional protections.
rejection_details: We can't accept petitions about appointments, which includes calling for elected representatives or public servants to resign or be removed from office.

action: Require building of fully wheelchair accessible homes in all new developments
background: We believe accessible housing isn't a luxury & is essential for independent living & equal participation in society. The UK cannot meet the obligations of the Equality Act or the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities without addressing the crisis of a lack of accessible housing.
additional_details:
• Make wheelchair accessible (Category 3) homes a mandatory requirement in all new housing developments
• Set a national minimum percentage of wheelchair accessible homes for every development
• Strengthen and enforce building regulations so developers cannot opt out of accessibility requirements
• Increase investment in accessible social housing
• Create a national accessible housing register
• Improve funding and processes for home adaptations

action: Keep 5-Year Settlement for Students who switched to Health & Care Visas
background: We ask the Government to maintain the current 5-year qualifying period for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) for all Health and Care Worker visa holders who hold a UK university degree.
additional_details: Thousands of students entered the UK through legitimate, highly-regulated routes. Many first contributed significantly to the UK economy as international students, paying high tuition fees to UK universities. UK graduates have already spent years integrated into British society, mastered the English language, and adopted UK professional standards.They chose to stay and serve in care sector based on a genuine passion for public service, with a legal promise of a 5-year path to settlement.
rejection_details: You may wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/745684

action: Fund free parking for key workers at their places of work
background: I want to speak about fairness, recognition, and practical support for the people who keep our communities running: our key workers. Key workers are not a luxury. They are a necessity. They are nurses, paramedics, teachers, social workers, carers, police officers, firefighters and support staff.
additional_details: For shift workers, public transport is not always a viable option. Early morning starts, late-night finishes, carrying equipment, travelling between sites, or responding to urgent calls often make driving a necessity — not a choice. Some councils already provide concessions for residents, businesses, and visitors in various circumstances. We think free parking permits for verified key workers is both administratively feasible and socially responsible.

action: Stop child sex offenders living near schools & within victims’ communities
background: Children deserve to feel safe in their homes, schools and communities. Allowing convicted offenders to live close to schools or within the same town as their victims can cause fear, trauma and undermine public confidence in safeguarding measures.
additional_details: Victims of abuse can experience long term trauma. Knowing their offender lives nearby can cause fear, anxiety and further trauma. Restrictions can help survivors feels safe in their own communities. Other children within the community also deserve protection. Limiting where sex offenders can live could reduce opportunities for contact with potential victims and help create safer environments around schools and youth facilities. We believe parents need confidence that that their children and safeguarded.

action: No confidence in Labours ability to govern. Go to a General Election

action: Require contractors to guarantee all roadworks for 2 years
background: I call on the UK Government to require a two-year guarantee on all roadworks by contractors and utility companies. Any defects such as sinking, cracking or potholes within that period must be repaired at their expense to protect taxpayers and improve standards.
additional_details: As a taxpayer, I am frustrated by poor value for money. Roads are left to deteriorate until nearly undriveable, and when repairs are finally made they often fail within months. Councils and utility companies repeatedly dig up roads, yet reinstatements sink or crack, causing potholes and costly vehicle damage. Motorists already pay fuel duty and Vehicle Excise Duty. We are effectively paying twice. A two-year guarantee could help ensure accountability and longer-lasting repairs.

action: Fund dedicated housing for men with shared custody of their children
background: We call on the Government to provide dedicated funding to support single dad's to be homed with their children if they have 50% custody of their children as it impacts the children's lives to not be able to live with their parent.

action: Do not apply income tax to our statutory annual holiday pay
background: I want the Government to introduce a law to prevent income tax being applied to employees' statutory holiday pay.
additional_details: I believe that If income tax was removed from employees' holiday pay, it would be a vote winner and also encourage more people into employment reducing the Government's astronomical cost for universal credit each year.

action: PLEASE make Keir Starmer resign. He is a disgrace to the UK.
background: Don't leave us floundering with Keir Starmer as our Prime Minister. He needs to resign or be subjected to a vote of no confidence. He won the last General Election not because we wanted him, but because the Conservatives were broken. Labour is now more than broken, and is positively destructive.
additional_details:
So many reasons we need this resignation: the Lord Mandelson scandal, the economy is dying, the immigration crisis continues...
Starmer needs to take the accountability he keeps talking about and stop using the Conservative party's failures as a cover for his own inability to run the country. He measures his own effectiveness against them too often, refuses to answer questions and blames all his innumerable mistakes on ignorance or other people. This will not do. Starmer has had his time.

action: Cap working age benefits at the same level as the state pension
background: Ensure that no working age individual on benefits receives a higher basic income than a pensioner living solely on the State Pension. Review benefit levels to bring them in line with the income the Government has deemed sufficient for pensioners.
additional_details: We believe this would create a fairer system that does not disadvantage older people who rely entirely on the State Pension. Pensioners should not be placed at a financial disadvantage compared to working age benefit claimants.

action: Require NHS to offer routine third trimester pregnancy ultrasound scan
background: As a mother of a baby born via emergency c-section due to missed foetal compromise I urge the Government to require the NHS to offer a routine third trimester ultrasound scan. I think this could reduce emergency c-sections, stillbirths and lifelong disabilities due to missed foetal complications.
additional_details: Currently the NHS offers two routine scans, one at 12 weeks and one at 20 weeks. After this the baby's health is relied upon fundal height, parent blood pressure, dipstick urine tests, and a minutes-worth of doppler use every 2-4 weeks. I believe that not only are these methods outdated, but can also miss growth restrictions, reduced foetal heart rate and placental issues. I therefore call for the NHS to offer routine third trimester scans, which could detect issues earlier, medical intervention can be involved sooner and emergency c-sections reduced.

action: Stop Labour from removing our monarchy from the UK
background:
Address the parliament with the public's genuine concern.  The UK is being taken over by Labour who intended to strip our King of overall power. 
This is the continued work of Tony Blair just in the form of Kier Starmer, once the gov have full control public freedom will end
additional_details: Put this choice to public vote, the people will not be controlled by government. The king needs to step up and save our country before it's too late and our history fades.

action: Make littering from a vehicle a driving offence with penalty points”

action: Protect BTEC qualifications and inclusive post 16 pathways.
background: We are asking the government to stop the removing and defunding L3 BTECS and keep them alongside T and V Levels. This keeps post-16 routes open for students with lower GCSE grades and teenagers with learning difficulties who may not be supported by exam sources and succeed in practical coursework.
additional_details: Removing the BTEC qualification risks limiting opportunities for many young people after Year 11. Students with lower GCSE grades and for example teenagers with disabilities or learning differences, may struggle to meet the academic and placement demand of the T Levels or V Levels. BTECs offer practical, coursework-based pathways that support a range of learners. Keeping BTECS promotes and gives inclusion, fairness and equal access to education and employment.

action: Increase Statutory Paternity Leave to a minimum 12 weeks paid leave for fathers
background: Amend employment law to extend Statutory Paternity Leave to at least 12 weeks for fathers, paid at a meaningful rate. This should be a protected entitlement separate from maternity leave and not dependent on Shared Parental Leave. with protection from workplace discrimination and financial penalty.
additional_details: The UK provides only 1–2 weeks of low-paid paternity leave. Postnatal depression affects around 1 in 10 mothers and up to 10% of fathers. Early paternal bonding improves child development and family stability. The UK ranks near the bottom among OECD nations for father-specific leave. Fathers should not be forced to use annual leave or unpaid time to support their families. Investing in fathers early reduces long-term social and economic costs. Modern policy must reflect modern families.

action: Exempt all military families from school fines — let them be with family.
background: We call on the government to exempt military families from school attendance fines. Military parents often live away from home and are deployed for weeks or months at a time. These families make extraordinary sacrifices. They deserve flexibility and compassion when spending precious time together.
additional_details: We believe that it is unjust that armed forces members sacrifice their safety and family life, often living apart even outside deployment, yet face restrictions on time together when they return. A strong relationship with a serving parent is vital for a child’s wellbeing. “Exceptional circumstances” are not guaranteed and remain at a headteacher’s discretion. A government that relies on the commitment and sacrifice of its armed forces should not then dictate when those same families are permitted to reunite.

action: Give students the legal right to unrestricted toilet access in school
background: We are concerned about “zero-tolerance” toilet policies in schools which can force children to wait for escorts or deny toilet breaks and can cause physical harm (retention/bowel distress). We believe it violates the Equality Act, and we call for a legal right to toilet access at all times.
additional_details: We believe many schools use "zero-tolerance" toilet rules that ignore physical health. We feel this system fails children by possibly causing urinary retention, UTIs, and bowel dysfunction. We believe it also discriminates against students with IBS, Crohn’s, or Autism through humiliating "escort" policies and compromises menstrual dignity. We request a mandate ensuring: 1. Toilet access is a basic legal right, not a privilege. 2. Students with medical needs have immediate, unescorted access. 3. Ending "collective punishment.

action: Continue PR for severely disabled adults instead of costly CoP Deputyship
background: Amend the law so Parental Responsibility continues beyond 18 where a capacity assessment between the ages of 16-18 confirms the young person severely and permanently lacks capacity, with oversight safeguards, removing the need for families to apply for costly, Court of Protection Deputyship.
additional_details: When the person is 18, parents of young people who severely and permanently lack capacity lose legal authority and can be forced into costly, complex and often unsuccessful Court of Protection deputyship. In our view, families who have safely cared for their child for life should not face an adversarial process to continue protecting them. A safeguarded continuation framework could provide stability, reduce court burden and better protect vulnerable adults.

action: Update school uniforms, encouraging a shift away from formal business attire.
background: The traditional UK school uniform is no longer fit for purpose. While the intent of uniform is to provide equality and identity, the current "formal" execution creates unnecessary barriers to learning. Suits are outdated. We need sensory-friendly, inclusive active-wear that fits the modern world.
additional_details:
Traditional "suited & booted" uniforms are outdated relics. Rigid blazers, scratchy uniform fabric & ties create "sensory load" for neurodiverse kids and body confidence issues during puberty. If teachers don’t need suits to work, kids shouldn’t need them to learn.

We propose a shift to "active" uniforms: soft, breathable jersey fabrics, hoodies, joggers, and polo shirts. Let’s prioritise student wellbeing and focus on education, not enforcing uncomfortable fashion.

action: Fund a time-limited childcare scheme for all parents with cancer
background: Fund a national, time-limited funded childcare scheme for parents undergoing active cancer treatment to cover nursery and before/after-school care during treatment and short-term recovery. Eligibility would not depend on employment status.
additional_details: Cancer treatment often prevents parents from working, yet most childcare support is linked to employment. Families can face sudden income loss while still needing childcare to attend treatment and maintain stability for their children. There is no national scheme providing childcare based on medical need. A targeted, time-limited support scheme could reduce financial strain and protect children’s wellbeing during treatment.

action: Review self-defence laws to allow regulated non-lethal deterrents
background: Conduct a formal review of UK self-defence legislation to assess whether regulated, licensed non-lethal personal deterrents should be permitted for individuals at higher risk of gender-based violence, including women and trans people.
additional_details: Women and gender-diverse people face disproportionate levels of harassment, assault and violence. Current UK law prohibits most effective non-lethal deterrents, leaving many feeling unprotected. A formal review could explore carefully regulated, licensed options while maintaining public safety. Safety policy should reflect lived risk and modern realities.

action: Increase the £100k childcare income cap in line with inflation
background: Increase the £100,000 per-parent childcare eligibility income cap to restore its original real-terms value, and automatically uprate it each year in line with inflation to prevent further fiscal drag and unfair loss of childcare support.
additional_details: The £100,000 cap has been frozen since the 30-hours childcare scheme began in 2017. Since then, CPI inflation has risen by around 35%, meaning £100,000 now has the real-terms value of roughly £135,000. Earnings have increased while the cap has not, pulling more families over the limit each year. The per-parent cliff edge also produces unfair outcomes between households with similar or lower total incomes.

action: Require schools to record  and report SEND pupils placed in behaviour rooms.
background: Require all schools and academies to record and report data on SEND pupils who are removed from lessons or placed in behaviour rooms or internal exclusion, including how often this occurs, how long pupils are removed, and what support or reasonable adjustments were attempted first.
additional_details: Many children with SEND, including those with ADHD and autism, are regularly removed from lessons and placed in behaviour rooms instead of being supported. There is currently no national requirement to record this data, meaning pupils can spend significant time out of education without visibility or accountability. Recording this information would help identify patterns, safeguard children’s mental health, and ensure support is provided rather than punishment.
