action: Legalise and regulate cannabis for adults across the United Kingdom
background: Introduce laws to legalise and regulate cannabis for adults in the UK. This should include licensed production and sale, strict age limits, product testing and labelling, restrictions on advertising, and taxation to fund the NHS, education and addiction services.
additional_details: Cannabis is widely used in the UK despite being illegal, which allows the black market and organised crime to profit. Regulation would improve public safety through age checks, quality control and education. It would also reduce criminal records for minor possession and raise tax revenue for the NHS and support services.

action: Review Existing and Proposed Low Traffic Neighbourhood (LTN) Schemes
background: Conduct an independent review of existing and planned LTNs to assess their impact on congestion, emissions, local businesses and all residents. Require transparent consultation, proper impact assessments and consideration of alternative safety measures before further schemes are approved.
additional_details: Many LTNs appear to displace traffic onto main roads, increasing congestion and potentially raising emissions in those areas. Not everyone can rely on public transport due to cost, reliability, work or caring responsibilities. Some residents and businesses report reduced accessibility. A national, evidence-based review would ensure policies are proportionate, fair and effective before expanding further schemes.

action: Hold a referendum: Replace FPTP with Proportional Representation through STV
background: Legislate for a UK-wide referendum on the voting system for House of Commons elections, with two options: Replace First Past the Post with proportional representation using the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system, or keep First Past The Post. Include a potential timetable for implementation.
additional_details: FPTP is an unfair voting system. It can produce large majorities in the House of Commons from a minority of votes and makes voters' influence depend on where they live. In 2024 the largest party won 63% of seats on 33.7% of votes, while smaller parties won far fewer seats than their vote shares, that meant ~24k votes per Labour MP, ~461k votes per Green MP, and ~824k per Reform MP. PR-STV makes votes count more equally, keeps local representation and reduces the need for tactical voting.

action: Introduce targeted coastal trawling bans to protect ecosystems & reduce erosion
background: We call on the Government to establish 0–6 nautical mile exclusion zones for bottom-contact fishing in key UK coastal areas. We think this will allow kelp and seagrass recovery, strengthen natural defences like saltmarsh and dunes, and reduce coastal erosion and flood risk sustainably.
additional_details: Seabed disturbance from bottom trawling can increase turbidity, destabilise sediments, and undermine nature-based defences. There is evidence showing passive recovery after trawling bans outperforms planting alone, protecting coasts at lower cost than repeated restoration or hard-engineered defences. We think targeted bans will benefit ecosystems, fisheries, and coastal communities while adapting to climate change.

action: Ring-fence 100% of VED  for mandatory road maintenance targets
background: The Government must ring-fence 100% of Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) for road infrastructure. We call for a National Plan that mandates local authorities to meet strict repair deadlines and safety targets, ensuring road tax is used solely to eliminate the pothole crisis and improve road quality.
additional_details: Motorists pay billions in road tax, yet the infrastructure we see is crumbling, causing dangerous conditions and costly vehicle repairs. Only a fraction of VED is currently spent on roads. By ring-fencing this tax and setting legal repair targets, we believe the Government can ensure accountability and safety. This petition is not about tax cuts; it is about ensuring that the money we already pay is used as originally intended to create a road network that is safe, efficient, and fit for purpose.

action: Traffic Calming and Speed Reduction Measures Outside Cockshutt School
background: Reduce the speed limit on the main road through Cockshutt to 20 mph and implement appropriate traffic-calming measures outside the school to improve safety and enable pedestrians to cross the road more safely.
additional_details: Reducing the speed limit to 20mph outside Cockshutt School, supported by traffic calming measures, is essential to protect children and improve road safety. Children cannot reliably judge vehicle speeds and may act unpredictably near roads. At 20mph, drivers have more time to react and stopping distances are significantly shorter, reducing both the likelihood and severity of collisions. Measures such as raised tables and clearly marked crossings help ensure drivers slow down consistently. A safer environment encourages walking and cycling, reduces congestion and noise, and supports the wellbeing of pupils, families, and the wider community.

action: Repair Our Roads Now! We need an urgent repair Plan on Dangerous Potholes Now!
background: The Government must step in now with an urgent action plan: necessary funding, strict repair deadlines for local councils, investment in more resurfacing where needed, and full transparency on spending. Safe roads are essential for the national economy, communities, businesses, and daily life.
additional_details:
We believe this is now an Emergency. The Government needs to urgently step up and ensure local councils are delivering lasting solutions to what is now a crisis. This issue has been left to seriously deteriorate, leaving people across the country frustrated and suffering the consequences. In particular Cyclists and Motorcyclists face a daily danger of death as a result.  

We face endless repair bills for tyres, wheels, and suspensions damaged by crumbling roads. During a cost of living crisis!

action: Allow more flexible clothing choices in UK school uniform policies
background: We want the Government to review school uniform policies in UK schools. Students should have more flexibility in what they wear, including different trouser colours, optional uniform items, and the possibility of using a small school badge instead of strict full uniforms.
additional_details: Many students feel current uniform rules are too strict and do not reflect modern student life. Some students may feel uncomfortable or stressed by strict clothing rules or specific colours. Allowing more flexibility would help students feel more comfortable and confident while still allowing schools to identify students through small badges or school logos.

action: Commit to building the Aylesbury Spur of East West Rail now.
background: Provide immediate funding and a fixed start date for the Aylesbury-Milton Keynes section of East West Rail. The "Aylesbury Spur" must be restored to the core project plan to ensure our town isn't left as a dead-end with outdated diesel trains.
additional_details: The town of Aylesbury is currently being treated as a "dead-end" in the UK’s rail strategy. While the Government and East West Rail (EWR) Company celebrate the progress of the Oxford-to-Milton Keynes link, the vital Aylesbury-to-Milton Keynes "spur" has been sidelined into "passive provision." This is a failure of planning that leaves a town of over 90,000 people isolated from one of the UK’s fastest-growing economic hubs.

action: Restore the British Empire to its largest & become the worlds strongest empire
background: Parliament must pursue a national project aimed at expanding Britain’s power and influence to match the full reach once held by the Empire, rebuilding strength, asserting authority abroad, and restoring the nation to a dominant position on the world stage.
additional_details: I want to restart the British Empire because, in my view, this country has been run into the ground by our new Prime Minister. Britain has become an international laughing stock, with declining global influence and a military that no longer reflects our historic strength. I believe a renewed national vision is needed to restore pride, stability, and a sense of purpose.

action: Creating a national register for those found guilty of Animal welfare offences.
background:
Create a registry for those convicted of Section 4 animal welfare offences. 
This would be disclosable on a DBS check. This register should also be checked when a Claires Law disclosure is being considered.
additional_details:
Causing unnecessary suffering to animals is precursor to other violent offences. Having a disclosable register would allow the police, housing, agencies and employers to include this information in any risk assessment they are making regarding an individual. 

This would also protect animals from further harm. Those convicted of offences and who have received banning orders can still live in the same household as family pets. This is not classed as a breach of that court order.

action: Access for Halton residents 60+ to the Merseytravel concessionary travel scheme
background: Call on Halton Borough Council to include Halton residents aged 60 +  in the Merseytravel concessionary travel scheme.
additional_details:
Halton Borough Council and Merseytravel to work together to include Halton residents aged 60 and over in the Merseytravel concessionary travel scheme.

rejection_details: This is the responsibility of Merseytravel and local councils, not the UK Government.  It is also a local issue.

action: Improve Safety at WestHill and EastHill, Hastings -to deter Accidents & Suicides
background:
We are calling on Hastings Borough Council to take urgent action to improve safety at WestHill and EastHill by installing protective fencing, cliff edge warning signs, and mental health support signage.
We need protective measures put in place to prevent further deaths.
additional_details:
We respectfully ask the council to:
Install protective fencing in high-risk cliff edge areas.
Place clear and visible warning signs highlighting the danger of the cliff edge and
Add mental health support signage with contact numbers in prominent locations, for those feeling suicidal, this could help deter people that are going through a crisis. 
These simple measures could help prevent accidents, deter suicide attempts, and save lives. 

- This petition is in Memory of Simon Boobyer
